speaker: Jotun Warrior
en: Obey your master, or I'll melt you into a sword, you bastard!

speaker: Havi
en: It can't be. Gullinbursti...?

speaker: Jotun Warrior
en: Dwarven junk! Nothing but scrap metal that thinks it's alive! It's a long way back to Asgard, piggy! So shut up and do as you're told! You won't listen? Rah! Rah! You like that?!

speaker: Jotun Warrior
en: Tremble before my might!

speaker: Jotun Warrior
en: Yah! Run away, Æsir! You cannot defeat us both!

speaker: Jotun Warrior
en: You stand no chance against my mighty boar!

speaker: Havi
en: You dare steal what is mine? You will die this day!

speaker: Jotun Warrior
en: Agh! Curse you, Aesir!

speaker: Havi
en: You will pay for harming Gullinbursti!

speaker: Havi
en: There-there Gullinbursti. You're alright, you're alright. I'm here now... and I am in need of your aid, if you will offer it. Be calm, old friend. I am your master now.

speaker: Aelfwyn
en: O Lord, forgive not these men their trespasses. Send them instead to the same Hell they brought upon our land. If their blood does not cleanse them of their sins, send them to Hell with the others. O Lord, forgive them not, forget them not.

speaker: Aelfwyn
en: This is not your place, heathen. Leave, before you draw the wrath of our Father.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you kill these men?

speaker: Aelfwyn
en: These defilers killed themselves by despoiling this sacred ground. God told me the full tale. Then he told me to chastise them. And he has told me much about you, too.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand down, Saxon! I mean you no harm!

speaker: Aelfwyn
en: I warned you to leave! Now God guides my hand!

speaker: Aelfwyn
en: May God strike you down!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me again. What did your God say about me?

speaker: Aelfwyn
en: My God names you the Crow-Eyed Devil. And He sends out his angels to find you and kill you. And then they will fling you into the pits of Hell, demon.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would say, well met, brother, but I cannot shake off the needle-itch of dread. Is something wrong?

speaker: Basim
en: I followed the here, kept him in my sight. But the monks, his servants, I have seen nothing of them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dead?

speaker: Basim
en: I do not think so. But there is no good here in this grave-hush.

speaker: Eivor
en: And where is the abbot now?

speaker: Basim
en: In his quarters. Come, and be on your guard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Does this have the stench of betrayal to you, brother?

speaker: Basim
en: Why would the godly shepherd ally with the heretic?

speaker: Eivor
en: Cynebert is a man who craves power and position. With Tedmund dead, he must find it somewhere else.

speaker: Basim
en: There is truth in that. Keeps your eye and blade sharp.

speaker: Fulke
en: Cynebert, your guests have arrived.

speaker: Fulke
en: Come. Supper's ready. The dear abbot sent me an invitation. Said my friends were eager to meet with me. It's early for supper, I know. But Cynebert's ale goes so well with roasted lamb and cinammon-blueberry-peas. I couldn't resist!

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is my brother?

speaker: Fulke
en: Is he... is he not here? Mon Dieu (My God). I never told him.

speaker: Basim
en: Kill her, and we'll never find Sigurd.

speaker: Fulke
en: Sit, Eivor. Eat. And let me tell you the tale of a man who talks with gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mock me. I have killed for much less.

speaker: Fulke
en: Of course you have. Isn't that the way of this ugly world? We cull the sheep and thin the flock as we see fit, you and I. Most who walk the earth are little more than talking blood-bladders. Wasted flesh. But not Sigurd. Sigurd is something else. Sigurd has been touched. He is deified. The gods, they speak through him.

speaker: Eivor
en: You lured him with that lie. Your words are bile and blight.

speaker: Fulke
en: You should have listened, Eivor. I tried to tell you. The gods are real. And their power is within our grasp.

speaker: Fulke
en: You will never find him. Not 'til I have had my fill. To old friends.

speaker: Fulke
en: This really is delicious, Cynebert. Is it cloves I taste?

speaker: Fulke
en: Well that concludes supper.

speaker: Fulke
en: Kill them. And bring their bodies to my sanctum in Canterbury.

speaker: Basim
en: They will be upon us soon. Maybe there is another way out?

speaker: Basim
en: Steel yourself Eivor. Or Sigurd is lost to us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your god waits on the edge of my axe, Saxons!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: You heard the lady! Leave no one alive.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke let slip that her sanctum is at Canterbury.

speaker: Basim
en: She did, and with no cause. I'd approach the place with caution. It may be a lie.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be, but it's the only lead we have.

speaker: Basim
en: I hope all of this innocent sacrifice is worth the trouble.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's Sigurd. My brother. Of course it is.

speaker: Basim
en: Then come, let us dive into the maw of death. I was never keen on seeing my winter years.

speaker: Basim
en: This will not be for nothing, Eivor. We will find Sigurd.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not just him. I want Fulke to suffer!

speaker: Basim
en: This land of summer, mists, and forests dreaming darkly. I see secret, and I want to know England. All of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: And yet it rounds on us at every turn, snarling like a cornered dog. I begin to despair of ever settling here.

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps the stars write your path, and you will never have a home here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you miss the land of your birth?

speaker: Basim
en: I have long been away. But it is fiercely beautiful beneath the vanity, arrogance, and pettiness of men.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should like to see it.

speaker: Basim
en: You could if you wish. My father was an architect, a builder of wonders. The of Samarra, his masterpiece. Another man, who played the caliphate's game better took the credit. He was exiled and died in poverty.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your faith sours. What of loyalty, shared stories around the hearth? Warm nights, bodies, and the tender love of another?

speaker: Basim
en: There are some who are worthy, a scant few that tower above the sullied mass. Men and women of vision and valor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd is one such man?

speaker: Basim
en: He is. Fulke isn't wrong on that score.

speaker: Eivor
en: I fear for him, Basim. I cannot rest until he is free.

speaker: Basim
en: Nor will I, my friend.

speaker: Basim
en: The practice of learning has waned considerably in England since the days of the Romans. What books they still have, they keep locked away in their churches, hidden from the eyes of common folk.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thralls and ceorls cannot read. What would be the point?

speaker: Basim
en: They could learn. The Church could teach them. So much of human history would be opened to them. Aristotle, Pythagoras, Euclid... ancient knowledge lost to all but a few hard-headed men of the cloth.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have studied these works yourself?

speaker: Basim
en: In my youth, I was consumed with a passion for understanding. I spent many hours a day in the House of Wisdom in Baghdad.

speaker: Eivor
en: A seminary?

speaker: Basim
en: A great library, full of the greatest learning on mankind. For a boy seeking answers, it holds many riches. One day, I was sitting cross-legged, devouring a study by the great astronomer al-Khwarizmi. With a swiftness belying his years, the papers were plucked from my grasp by the great man himself. His presence stole my voice. He was kind and openhearted. He showed me such scientific wonders.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what did you learn there?

speaker: Basim
en: Calendars and calculations placing the sun, moon, and five planets. Equations that crackled and sparkled with divine intelligence. I asked the great man, "Is this what it is to know God?

speaker: Eivor
en: You saw your God's hands in the runes?

speaker: Basim
en: I found wisdom. And I have been searching for more ever since. There is great vastness outside ourselves, Eivor. Most only notice a few grains of the sand. But some, like Sigurd, I believe, see the endless flow of the hourglass.

speaker: Eivor
en: What you see in Sigurd... is that what Fulke sees as well?

speaker: Basim
en: I believe it is.

speaker: Basim
en: We will find no friends in Canterbury, so try not to draw attention.

speaker: Eivor
en: This place reeks of the piety of priests.

speaker: Basim
en: This place swarms of Fulke's people. Sigurd will be well-guarded. Caution, and subtlety should be our path.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ready? Follow me.

speaker: Basim
en: This is a trap. Why would Fulke give us her sanctum?

speaker: Eivor
en: She baits us. Cocksure and arrogant. But she cannot see failure in her path.

speaker: Basim
en: Her fearful wit would say otherwise.

speaker: Basim
en: Whatever we find there, keep your head.

speaker: Eivor
en: You chastise me like a child, Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: I guard you like a father. Nothing is served with your brutal end. You have much to do in this life, I know it.

speaker: Eivor
en: More riddles, sly tongue

speaker: Basim
en: No riddles. I sense a greatness within you both. Your destiny is not to stain the stones of this God-house with your blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: To arms, Basim!

speaker: Basim
en: So we are to blunder in like an ox?

speaker: Eivor
en: If she is still here, I will burn this Christ-house to the ground.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: For the Order! For the Glory of the Ancients! Do not let these infidels find its secrets.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be the way to Fulke's sanctum.

speaker: Basim
en: Then let us go.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Guards! To arms!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: They have entered the cathedral! To arms!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke! I'm here! Face me!

speaker: Basim
en: Have a care, Eivor. You will play into her hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does it mean, these word-tangles that speak of elves and demons?

speaker: Eivor
en: By Odin, this is a sick tapestry she wove. For every drop of his blood she spilled, I will take a mead-horn more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Details on The Order of the Ancients. Fulke ranks high among them, but is not their head.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Gospel of Mary Magdalene. Hm.

speaker: Eivor
en: The plans to the great fortress in Wessex. Is there something here we can use to breach it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd...

speaker: Eivor
en: No!

speaker: Basim
en: Eivor, what is it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me that you found something. Anything we can use.

speaker: Basim
en: I may have. A fortress in Suthesexe. The Order trains soldiers there.

speaker: Eivor
en: We must be sure. Sigurd is running out of time.

speaker: Eivor
en: Anything else?

speaker: Basim
en: Documents of interest to the Hidden Ones. Hytham will surely want a look. But for Sigurd, Portcestre is our only lead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm.

speaker: Basim
en: If he is in Portcestre castle, we'll need a massive army to crack its walls.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have many friends in England now. If I call on them, they will come.

speaker: Basim
en: They will.

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim... she severed his arm clean off. Can a man survive such a loss?

speaker: Basim
en: Physically, he can. Mentally, it's hard to say. So much stress can drive a man to despair.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you suggest that he might take his own life as Tedmund did, banish that idea.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must tell my people at the settlement that their jarl remains a captive. They will not take it well.

speaker: Basim
en: We will not fail again, Eivor. I'll scout ahead, and send word to the settlement when I know more of Portcestre. Be ready.

speaker: Dag
en: Eivor! Eivor! Face me, Eivor!

speaker: Dag
en: Stop there, Wolf-Kissed. This ends now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag. Turn around and walk away.

speaker: Dag
en: Your habits are not my own, Eivor. I do not flee responsibility for the sake of my glory. I stand firm with my people.

speaker: Dag
en: For many months, I have stood at your side, keeping faith in Sigurd's judgment. Because I believed in him and his vision. Do as Eivor commands, he told me. And I have. Against my better judgment, I did as you have asked me. And where has that left us? Without a jarl, without a purpose, watching you chase glory around this land like a spooked hare.

speaker: Eivor
en: You could have come to me in confidence, Dag. But that offer is gone.

speaker: Dag
en: I have no need of it. My mind is fixed.

speaker: Dag
en: Hear me, all! I challenge Eivor for the leadership of this clan until Sigurd is safe home!

speaker: Eivor
en: Walk away, Dag!

speaker: Dag
en: No. We fight to the death.

speaker: Eivor
en: I accept. We settle this now.

speaker: Dag
en: Ah! A final act of courage. Very well...

speaker: Eivor
en: This is madness, Dag. That I do not accept.

speaker: Dag
en: This is not a question, Eivor. Come.

speaker: Eivor
en: You spew nonsense, Dag. This is absurd.

speaker: Dag
en: Enough!

speaker: Dag
en: Let the circle be made.

speaker: Randvi
en: Please. Please, both of you!

speaker: Dag
en: Is that the best you can do?

speaker: Eivor
en: You walk a fool's path, Dag. This does not need to happen.

speaker: Dag
en: A coward to the last. Have courage, Eivor. I will make it quick.

speaker: Dag
en: Pathetic!

speaker: Randvi
en: Stop!

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not want to do this! Walk away.

speaker: Dag
en: What's the matter, Eivor? Are you scared?

speaker: Eivor
en: Only for what I must do.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you not see what you do? There is no honor in this.

speaker: Dag
en: What do you know of honor that Sigurd did not teach you? You suckle at his teat and then leave him to die.

speaker: Dag
en: You should have listened! You might have saved yourself!

speaker: Eivor
en: I would grant you exile. Leave this place, but go with your life.

speaker: Dag
en: Spare me your pity and fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: So be it. You leave me no choice.

speaker: Eivor
en: You could have waited. You could have come with me! You're a fool, Dag. You see where it's gotten you?

speaker: Dag
en: Silence!

speaker: Dag
en: You... you...

speaker: Dag
en: Eivor... you... you

speaker: Odin
en: If I had any pity, I would not lavish it on this poor fool.

speaker: Eivor
en: He forced my hand.

speaker: Odin
en: Yes. And the cost of disrespect is death. You said it yourself.

speaker: Odin
en: All he demanded, you gave him. That should be enough, for I have no need for one so fragile in my hall of heroes.

speaker: Eivor
en: He fought for what he believed in. Does that not count for something?

speaker: Odin
en: Does it? You killed him all the same.

speaker: Odin
en: What is the true cost of disrespect? The choice lies with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: It should have not come to this, old friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take this, and fly to Odin's hall. Whatever you sought in this life, may you find it in the next.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you gave no quarter in life. And you will receive none in death.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go to your homes. I will lay him to rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go to your homes!

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag accused me of betrayal. He accused me of breaking my oath. And this, this is the answer I gave him! Now you will hear the truth unvarnished. None, none more than me wishes for Sigurd's safe return. You know this, you know this, all of you! And I will burn the fields and dredge the rivers of Wessex to find him! That... that is my oath! That is my oath.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find Sigurd. You will not be without your jarl. This I promise.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag. You lived as you died, proud and defiant. I cannot begrudge you for that.

speaker: Eivor
en: I miss hearing you tell your stories, old friend. But I remember them well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wherever you now roam, I wish you well. I'm sorry that such a fire grew between us.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Even when Dag was younger, he had a streak in him. Hate to see it go that way, but you did the right thing. Can't imagine what you are feeling. Anyhow... you probably need something, eh?

speaker: Hytham
en: I am sorry for what happened with Dag. It could not have been easy. May he rest in peace.

speaker: Reda
en: Men like Dag litter every clan, city, and century. The prideful ones. Men who never know when just enough is still too much.

speaker: Randvi
en: How do you feel, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: I... I would rather not talk about it.

speaker: Randvi
en: I understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: I wonder what became of you. If anything remains of so strong a spirit. We think of you often, Dag. I do hope Sigurd knows how much he meant to you. We are beyond the time of telling of such things now.

scene: A Brief History of the Hidden Ones
speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham. I have the codex pages you asked for. Six in total.

scene: A Brief History of the Hidden Ones
speaker: Hytham
en: Ah, wonderful! We have so little writing from the original Hidden Ones. This will grow our understanding immeasurably. These documents may have been inked by the founders of the Hidden Ones, in fact. But their names are unknown to us, lost to history. A deliberate choice on their part, I think. I'm hoping these documents may shed some light on that mystery.

scene: A Brief History of the Hidden Ones
speaker: Eivor
en: I could not say. They are written in a language I do not understand.

scene: A Brief History of the Hidden Ones
speaker: Hytham
en: You know, the black market merchant Reda has an old piece of writing from the same era as the codex pages you found. Speak with him if you are curious to see it.

scene: A Brief History of the Hidden Ones
speaker: Eivor
en: Reda. Hytham says you have an old piece of writing from the early Hidden Ones.

scene: A Brief History of the Hidden Ones
speaker: Reda
en: O, that old scrap? Yes, it's just a short letter from one Hidden One to another. One of my rarest artifacts.

scene: A Brief History of the Hidden Ones
speaker: Eivor
en: How did it find its way to you?

scene: A Brief History of the Hidden Ones
speaker: Reda
en: A friend gave it to me, for safe keeping. Bayek was his name. Egyptian fellow. Very kind. Haven't seen him in a long time. A very long time. Anyway, the letter is written in , so it may not mean much to you. But you're free to have a look.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yes. Yes, this feels familiar. Eivor, we will press on. The rest of you, wait here!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Follow me! Into this kingdom of snow!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, can we not wait for this to pass?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ah, the sting of ice on skin! Revel in this, Eivor. We walk the footpath of the gods!

speaker: Eivor
en: To where? More glaciers and deserts of snow?

speaker: Sigurd
en: To glory!

speaker: Eivor
en: Could we not wait until this tempest quiets down? With the ship, where we have mead and food to warm us?

speaker: Sigurd
en: No! We must confront the omens and honor the gods. They will not seek or find you. We must go to them.

speaker: Eivor
en: We would be poor company with frozen bones and ice pellets for eyes.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You need not fear the cold, Eivor. Where we are going the winds and snows cannot touch!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. It is bitter cold. As wind from Nifelheim!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Keep steady! It should not be far now!

speaker: Sigurd
en: It must be near. I know the shape of these rocks! Yes, we are close.

speaker: Eivor
en: For the sake of frozen fingers, I hope so.

speaker: Sigurd
en: There, that frozen lake. This must be it. And ahead lies a cavern.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will you not say where this leads?

speaker: Sigurd
en: You will see soon enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: And too late to turn back, I fear.

speaker: Sigurd
en: There! The cave! Within hides the sacred gate.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The ice looks fragile. Can you clear it?

speaker: Eivor
en: A strange find... a spear like Odin's.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gungnir... is it you?

speaker: Sigurd
en: My heart races. This is it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods, this door. Have you seen this before?

speaker: Eivor
en: The space above. The Saga Stone sat there, did it not?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Long, long ago, yes. Now stand clear. zrhwachày nàgkwat nsmæ br trrhwndi kwardæ, I sorhwlàs vras chnàkodi de, nsm huchràs réyzdéràæ chaz zàwomsi. (When the destruction and death threatens before us, and the solar flare is reaching, to the calculator of futures we run.)

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you do this? Where did you learn these words?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I told you, Eivor. My visions are memories. Of a life once lived. Come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods! What is this place?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Over here, this plate will lead us onward.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Hoærhàsi! (Activate!)

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, I... I don't know what to say. This is all so strange.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Trust this place, Eivor. This old and sacred place.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where does it lead?

speaker: Sigurd
en: To the hall of the slain and the golden fields. To Valhalla.

speaker: Eivor
en: This vessel. Was it crafted by dwarves?

speaker: Sigurd
en: It is finely made, that much is true. I doubt Gunnar could hammer a piece any finer.

speaker: Eivor
en: And this cavern... so deep, and humming with magic.

speaker: Sigurd
en: There! The old tree! The tree of life!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this...?

speaker: Sigurd
en: See how proudly she sits. How beautiful she gleams. Here, all the roots of life run together.

speaker: Eivor
en: The skalds would cry to behold such a sight.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And there's more to come. I swear by all the names of the All-Father, this is only a taste of what I have in store for you. For my visions go further. To Odin's great hall.

speaker: Sigurd
en: There! Do you feel that? The sacred energies?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have never seen something so grand.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This shrine is ours. It will open for us. Watch and see for yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: How do you know these things? Was all this in your vision?

speaker: Sigurd
en: All this and more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that... Is that Svala? Valka's mother? How did she come to be here?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yes, it is returning to me now. This ancient shrine is set alight by this sphere of metal. And these shining arms, these branches. They will grant us access to the refuge of the Gods. To Valhalla. Are you ready?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, take great care. We should not tinker with the tools of the gods.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You speak for yourself, Eivor. For I am no mortal. I see that now. I know it.

speaker: Eivor
en: What lies beyond all this? Where does this lead?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Take your place at the center there, and you will see.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd...!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hail, you givers... a guest has come.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this place?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: There you are!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Hail, drengr (warrior)! Welcome!

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: The Havi returns to lead us to victory!

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Lead us to glory, Havi!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: We are proud to serve you, Havi!

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: Whet my lips with another horn of mead, Brother!

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: Drink for strength! Fight for glory!

speaker: Norse Warrior 8
en: Yesterday is gone, tomorrow never comes!

speaker: Svala
en: Eivor. Týr said you would come. Welcome.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you... are you Valka's mother? Svala?

speaker: Svala
en: You have a keen eye, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Sigurd
en: After all this time, Eivor! We have arrived! Now raise a horn with Freyja here and sing a victory song!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, what is all this? Your arm has returned... and your vigor as well.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Glory eternal, Eivor! Here we dine in the great hall of the slain. At long last! O, I want to scream with joy!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is... this is all so beautiful.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your visions were... they were real.

speaker: Norse Warrior 9
en: The battle horn blows! Come, Týr!

speaker: Norse Warrior 10
en: To the field! Fight with us!

speaker: Svala
en: Go, Eivor. Enjoy the fight. You have earned your place here.

speaker: Eivor
en: The strength I have!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ha! You are finished! Look at me, Sigurd! Ah, the music of the battle-din! (howl) This is incredible!

speaker: Norse Warrior 11
en: All hail the endless battle!

speaker: Norse Warrior 12
en: For Odin!

speaker: Norse Warrior 13
en: Die, dung worm!

speaker: Norse Warrior 15
en: Face me, drengr (warrior)! Show me what you are made of!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Don't be a coward, Eivor! Come fight me! Eivor! Over here! Eivor, join me when you have tired of crushing mice! Fight me! Now the real dance, here! Come fight me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, this place is incredible.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Enough with those sword-flies. You and I must fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: The battle we never had.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And hold nothing back. For here we need not fear a thing.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Spill the eternal blood of Valhalla.

speaker: Eivor
en: At last, I share the din of infinite battle with a true... Troll-arse!

speaker: Sigurd
en: You will taste a meal of iron before the day is out!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Come on, Wolf-Kissed! Let me cut you a new scar!

speaker: Eivor
en: You will beg for Fulke when I have done with you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Swine!

speaker: Eivor
en: Cur! Honor-drunk fool!

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Worry not, Eivor. For we earn no scars here. Only battle wisdom.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The day is done!

speaker: Eivor
en: What just happened?

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: The Havi returns to lead us to victory!

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Lead us to glory, Havi!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: We are proud to serve you, Havi!

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: Whet my lips with another horn of mead, Brother!

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: Drink for strength! Fight for glory!

speaker: Norse Warrior 8
en: Yesterday is gone, tomorrow never comes!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd... your arm has grown back.

speaker: Sigurd
en: It was never gone, Eivor. Not truly. Nothing is permanent here, I told you. Nothing save the courage and the reputation of its warriors.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are we immortal in this place?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Let us discover that together!

speaker: Eivor
en: A new day?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ha! Bit to the marrow's bed!

speaker: Eivor
en: Again you've lost your arm.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And again it will return!

speaker: Eivor
en: Father.... Is that you?

speaker: Eivor
en: That cannot have been my father...

speaker: Sigurd
en: Skal! (Cheers!)

speaker: Svala
en: Take your horn. Join the battle cheer.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Dearest skald of war and verse, how do you like this frenzy so far?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is... it is quite something.

speaker: Svala
en: Raise your horn, Eivor. What stops you?

speaker: Eivor
en: My father... Varin. Have you seen him in this hall?

speaker: Svala
en: I have not. Should he be here?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, he died a coward. Yet by Odin's eye, I swear I have seen him.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Cast aside your cares in Valhalla. Let seeking go, we have earned our joy. The journey is complete!

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw you, Father. Where are you? Show yourself.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: The Havi returns to lead us to victory!

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Lead us to glory, Havi!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: We are proud to serve you, Havi!

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: Whet my lips with another horn of mead, Brother!

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: Drink for strength! Fight for glory!

speaker: Norse Warrior 8
en: Yesterday is gone, tomorrow never comes!

speaker: Eivor
en: Great warriors, have you seen Varin?

speaker: Norse Warrior 16
en: Who?

speaker: Eivor
en: Varin. My father.

speaker: Eivor
en: Varin? Father?

speaker: Eivor
en: Blast! Where is he?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ha! Next time I lose this fucking arm, I'll beat a man to death with it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you not tire of these injuries?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Never!

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait... Father!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, you have a guest!

speaker: Eivor
en: You should have knocked first...

speaker: Sigurd
en: Nonsense. I brought you someone. Look!

speaker: Varin
en: My Eivor! There you are! What a warrior you have made of yourself. I am overfilled with pride!

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you find your way here?

speaker: Varin
en: You remember our great battle? You remember how we fought, side by side, with your mother and Sigurd and our clans united?

speaker: Eivor
en: We fought, Father. But you did not. You died a coward.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, enjoy this! Your father has returned.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Have you lost all your love for life?

speaker: Eivor
en: That was not my father. That was a lie.

speaker: Sigurd
en: That was not a lie, that was my gift to you. I have power here. And I can do as I please. You wished to see your father. I made it happen. As easy as breathing.

speaker: Eivor
en: By Odin's laws, my father is not allowed in this place. I do not wish to see him where he should not be.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Your father died doing what he hoped would save you. He died to protect you. And his clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, he...

speaker: Sigurd
en: This is the end of our road, Eivor. This is Valhalla, the eternal golden field. Now come... battle beckons!

speaker: Eivor
en: How is all this possible?

speaker: Eivor
en: How are the slain brought here?

speaker: Svala
en: The Valkyries know this, only them.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, that cannot be true. None of this feels right.

speaker: Svala
en: Do not despair, Eivor. Look. Your friends are here. Everyone you could ever want is here beside you.

speaker: Eivor
en: No. They are not real.

speaker: Eivor
en: This place is a lie.

speaker: Svala
en: This place can be whatever you wish it to be, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not want it. Not like this.

speaker: Svala
en: You would resign yourself to an empty death?

speaker: Eivor
en: The ecstasy I feel here is an illusion. I'd sooner caw like a Raven than sing a false song.

speaker: Svala
en: Illusion or not, here there is no death, no pain, no loss... no betrayal. Not like out there.

speaker: Eivor
en: You want this? To live inside a lie?

speaker: Svala
en: I am an old woman with a broken body. What life I had left was brief. So I bid farewell to my dear Valka and came here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I wish you well, Svala. But this is not for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must find Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The arm! The arm! Always the fucking arm!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, this is an illusion... a trick. Leave with me now and return to England. Our people need us.

speaker: Sigurd
en: No. I am no one in that world. I am somebody here. Powerful, capable, a god. Here I may live forever. Here I cannot die.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cows die, family die, you must die. The only thing that never dies is the reputation of the one who's died. in here, you have no reputation. But out there, it's not too late.

speaker: Eivor
en: Every day the same empty war, the same hollow victory. Spilling blood that tastes of water and smells of grass. You have known real battle, real glory. But this is not it. You know this, I know you do.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother... it is time to leave.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Am I destined to follow you everywhere? 'Til the end of my life?

speaker: Sigurd
en: All right. We go.

speaker: Odin
en: No! You stay!

speaker: Odin
en: I do not give you leave to go!

speaker: Odin
en: Why leave this place? A glory you fought so hard to find?

speaker: Odin
en: Walk with me.

speaker: Odin
en: I am humbled to walk with you, Eivor. Your reputation is a song warriors will sing forever.

speaker: Odin
en: You are the Wolf-Kissed one, who lingered at the edge of death, yet fought back.

speaker: Odin
en: You spilled the raven-wine of battle to paint whole kingdoms red.

speaker: Odin
en: You have killed kings and crowned them as you desired, bowing to none.

speaker: Odin
en: You stood tall where your brother stumbled, yet you still came to his aid.

speaker: Odin
en: You have felled many great foes in your brief time.

speaker: Odin
en: You have earned your place here, Eivor. Seize it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand aside! My people need me!

speaker: Odin
en: I have given you everything you wanted. Everything you needed!

speaker: Eivor
en: You gave me nothing! It was all me!

speaker: Odin
en: Yet I cleared your path. I guided your axe!

speaker: Eivor
en: You were a fly, buzzing in my ear!

speaker: Odin
en: How dare you deny me!

speaker: Odin
en: Everything you believe in stirs before you! Yet you question all! You question the very gods!

speaker: Odin
en: Fight me! Do not diminish yoursef!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your corpse hall is nothing but a dream!

speaker: Odin
en: Nothing but a dream? A dream is as real as anything in this world! Do dreams not inspire? Do dreams not make us fearful? Do they not push men to their greatest glories?

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I am done with dreaming!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor! Stand!

speaker: Randvi
en: Join us. We are here for you.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Back on your feet!

speaker: Valka
en: Rise up, warrior.

speaker: Randvi
en: Up, Eivor! Up!

speaker: Soma
en: Rise, drengr. This is not your end.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This way.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Put your weapon away. There is no need to fight.

speaker: Odin
en: You are mine! Do not turn away! Why do you flee from the truth! Your place is here! With me! Come back! Do not flee your destiny! You are a leader of Einherjar! Fight upon my command!

speaker: Odin
en: What are you doing? Take up your axe! Wield it like a true warrior!

speaker: Odin
en: Take up your axe!

speaker: Odin
en: Coward of cowards!

speaker: Odin
en: Beggar's bastard!

speaker: Odin
en: Stand and face me, you feeble-armed thrall!

speaker: Odin
en: Leave me now and you are nothing! With me you have wisdom! Glory! Power! What more do you need!

speaker: Eivor
en: Everything else.

speaker: Eivor
en: S-Sigurd... are you... are you with me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd?

speaker: Basim
en: Ah! The hanged-one awakes! Feet upon the ground once more!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor! Be careful!

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim? What is this?

speaker: Basim
en: Come closer, Eivor. Let me get a better look at you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Leave him be, Basim!

speaker: Basim
en: For too long, I stared at the sun! It blinded me to the truth. That it was you. It was you I wanted all along.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you track us here? Like a cowardly fox, concealed in the brush?

speaker: Basim
en: You widowed my destiny, Wolf-Kissed! You broke all my hopes!

speaker: Sigurd
en: He's mad, Eivor! Silence him.

speaker: Basim
en: Come, Eivor! Come save your crippled prince of dead ravens!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Sigurd
en: It is nothing, go! Kill that bacraut (asshole)!

speaker: Basim
en: You must suffer. A thousand times what I suffered.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this about?

speaker: Basim
en: My son, Eivor. This is about my son!

speaker: Eivor
en: You speak nonsense, Basim!

speaker: Basim
en: Forgiveness is impossible.

speaker: Eivor
en: We shared so much in England. Fought and bled together.

speaker: Basim
en: Dig, Eivor. Into the wellspring of your memory!

speaker: Eivor
en: Speak your grievance! Show yourself! I do not wish to fight with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does battle serve? Let us speak!

speaker: Basim
en: I have waited countless ages for this moment. No more talk! I hunger for this kill.

speaker: Basim
en: Show me your neck! Show me!

speaker: Basim
en: The kiss of the wolf takes my prize! Of course!

speaker: Eivor
en: Yah!

speaker: Basim
en: Rise!

speaker: Basim
en: My son will not have suffered in vain!

speaker: Eivor
en: You spout nonsense. Like an alehouse drunk!

speaker: Eivor
en: If you are resigned to this, so be it.

speaker: Basim
en: You will not die in peace. You will never see your home or your people again!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this what you wanted?

speaker: Basim
en: I want you to suffer!

speaker: Basim
en: When I have finished, you will be a sack of blood and shattered bones. And my conscience will be clear.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, damn!

speaker: Basim
en: Let us make this more interesting. We'll drag Sigurd into the fray!

speaker: Eivor
en: Coward! Face me! Fight me here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Be on your guard, Sigurd!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd! Be careful! He's coming for you!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Oath-breaker! You'll die here!

speaker: Basim
en: This brings me no joy, Justice-Bringer. You were always so kind, but you chose the wrong side.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am your prize, Basim. Come.

speaker: Basim
en: You are, indeed.

speaker: Basim
en: Will you not die?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not here. Not by your hand.

speaker: Basim
en: I will leave you here to die! Like a rotting fruit on a dying tree! You died once, you will again! (scream)

speaker: Sigurd
en: Stun him within the circle!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah!

speaker: Basim
en: Ah!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd! Stop this thing! Douse its fire!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd?

speaker: Eivor
en: Does he still live?

speaker: Sigurd
en: He does. But in darkness.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. The bastard...

speaker: Eivor
en: For how long has Basim been planning this treachery?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I dare not guess.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Gods! Am I to be hounded by a parade of blood-minded traitors the whole of my life? There is no end to this.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have something you want to say? Then say it.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I... I need some time to breathe. Let me sit a moment.

speaker: Sigurd
en: That man's anger. His rage. It had a familiar sting that I... I cannot place.

speaker: Eivor
en: He was raving, Sigurd. Without sense or reason. Pay it no mind.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I am not mad, Eivor. These things I see and feel... I know they are true.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know, Brother. Now more than ever. You always spoke true. We should cast our eyes towards home. It's a long journey and I am... not well.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Home. Eivor. On our journey here, I had much time to think. On the ecstasies and agonies of our friendship.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I am not the man I was. My time as the jarl of our clan has run short. You must lead us now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you mean this?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I cannot return to England with you. That is not my home... not now.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you saying?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Randvi told me of your bravery, your courage, your wisdom. In my absence, you were a pillar of stone. She admires you.

speaker: Eivor
en: And I her. But that cannot be the only reason.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I know about you and Randvi. A lover's tryst, in spite of me. I should challenge you for such a betrayal, but I'm... I'm not fit for such a fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: I... I understand. Is that all?

speaker: Sigurd
en: When Dag called you out and challenged you to a duel, you let him die with honor... in spite of his betrayal.

speaker: Eivor
en: He did what he felt was right. And I honored that.

speaker: Sigurd
en: When Dag called you out, as he felt he must... you refused him honor, did you not? A cowardly act, one I abhor. Dag acted out of love for this clan. That is not worth the shame you inflicted on his name.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw things differently then.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I recall our days in Oxenefordscire, our search for the Saga Stone. You disagreed with my orders. But you followed them. You questioned my methods, my aims... but you did not disobey.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Do you recall the day we stood before Eadwyn, searching for the Saga Stone? You struck Basim, you lashed out at me, you made a fool of us all. That is not a leader I wish to follow into death and glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: You were being secretive then. Foolish, I thought.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And when I passed judgment on Holger, you let my sentence lie, though I knew you disagreed. The look on your face said all.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And when I returned to the settlement, your pattern of disobedience continued. I made a judgment... and you openly defied me!

speaker: Eivor
en: I believed you were wrong then. I still do.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And I remember and admire the way you guided us from Norway to England. You kept my anger in check, my ambitions focused.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was a trying time.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And my grievances go back further still. You stole my father's riches. In my haste to leave, I should have stopped you then... A true leader would have stopped that thought before it took form. You were selfish.

speaker: Sigurd
en: In all my days away, in my fog of confusion, you have shown great wisdom and strength and leadership. Where you go, Eivor, I will follow. Our clan is yours to lead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Brother. I... I won't let you down.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This is not a decision I make lightly, Eivor. You are family. You were my drengr (warrior). But here our paths must diverge.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother, please stay. Your place is with us. In England. Our home is your home. My road forward has been a muddy one, slick with blood and tears. But we can reach its end together. Let us face new foes and greater glories together.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Since my captivity, I felt you were cold and distant. But here your words glow with heart-fire and kindness. All right... all right... I will come. But only if I may counsel you from time to time, to be better than you are.

speaker: Eivor
en: I expect nothing less.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand your anger. I would be too if I had suffered these insults. But there is no need to abandon what you have worked so hard to achieve. Return with me, and show me how best to lead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fate has drawn you here, Brother. Back home. Where you belong. Have no worry for what you leave behind.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You have a stormy look.

speaker: Eivor
en: Years ago, before we left for England, I saw a vision. A vision that foretold of betrayal. That I would betray you. I refused to believe it. I would never do such a thing, I told myself. But in the years since... I have robbed you of your dreams. Of England, of Valhalla... If you feel I have wronged you, Brother, I will make it right.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We cannot unweave our fates, Eivor. All is laid before us, from the day we are born. To be angry at this would be like... like wrestling the ocean. A pointless struggle.

speaker: Eivor
en: We two ragged ravens... what a we have inscribed together.

speaker: Sigurd
en: A tale for the ages.

speaker: Sigurd
en: England is too infected with ugly memories. I will stay here, in the land that gave me life and strength.

speaker: Eivor
en: Just as the prophecy warned me.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Prophecy?

speaker: Eivor
en: Years ago, before we left England, I had a vision. A prophecy that I would... that foretold the course of my life, up to this moment.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You never told me this. And has your prophecy come to pass?

speaker: Eivor
en: I... I do not know. I think it has... but not because I chased it.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Well... I hope for your sake, that you grow well into the role you have earned today. That hope is all I have left.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will try. I promise.

speaker: Eivor
en: What in the nine realms was that?

speaker: Eivor
en: Careful, grandmother. Something fell from the sky to earth like it has been thrown by Odin himself.

speaker: Hildiran
en: A strength he no doubt wished he possessed. No danger remains but look, it revealed something hidden in the mountain side.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hmm. Looks almost like a door.

speaker: Hildiran
en: If it is, then it's the door to something I have long been searching for. May I ask you for a kindness, drengr?

speaker: Eivor
en: My name is Eivor of the Raven Clan, and that depends on how kind you need me to be.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Will you grant me a home while I investigate the door, Eivor of the Raven Clan?

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't make a habit of sheltering strangers.

speaker: Hildiran
en: My name is Hildiran. There, now we are no longer strangers. Please. If I am right, then this is Freyja's Gate. Allow me to stay and I will help you discover the treasures that lay on the other side.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very well. I'll give you a small piece of land to make a home on and supplies from our raids to build with.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Thank you, kind Eivor. The gods smile on you!

speaker: Eivor
en: I may be kind but I am no fool. Everyone must pull their weight and I expect no less from you.

speaker: Hildiran
en: A fair rule and one I can easily follow.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Eivor the Kind! A welcomed visit. Like what you see?

speaker: Eivor
en: You've certainly made this space your own. But how does this help you open a stone door?

speaker: Hildiran
en: It is a shrine to Freyja. We will need her favor if we wish to reveal the hidden treasures.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, it's "we" now, is it?

speaker: Hildiran
en: I told you, Eivor, you will want to see what is on the other side. Now come, Freyja demands combat before she will aid us.

speaker: Eivor
en: For a moment I thought you meant for me to fight you.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Fear not, I can handle myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot possibly fight you. I would kill you.

speaker: Hildiran
en: You could try. Attack me.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Now get up and let's give Lady Freyja a fight!

speaker: Hildiran
en: Fight harder, Eivor! Yes! Give me everything you have!

speaker: Eivor
en: This old woman fights like a young jomsviking!

speaker: Hildiran
en: Your form is sloppy! You can do better. You're leaving yourself open to attack.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Good. Now watch.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Come at me again!

speaker: Eivor
en: What magic is this? And how do you fight with the strength of a berserker?

speaker: Hildiran
en: I can teach you, Eivor. But first, we fight!

speaker: Eivor
en: These aren't my weapons.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Are you already making excuses, drengr?

speaker: Eivor
en: You fight with a fury I have not seen in Mercia.

speaker: Hildiran
en: As will you, after my training.

speaker: Eivor
en: How is this possible?

speaker: Hildiran
en: Calm your mind of questions and concentrate on battle!

speaker: Hildiran
en: Good. That was good.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have seen many strange things but nothing like this. What magic do you possess? I've not seen a fight like that.

speaker: Hildiran
en: I am no seer. I am what you see before you, an old warrior with a knowledge of secrets.

speaker: Eivor
en: If that was not magic, then what was it?

speaker: Hildiran
en: That was a battle meditation. You entered Hugrheim, the mind's realm. It is a secret form of training that not many know. You can attack full force with no fear of injury.

speaker: Eivor
en: And yet you know this training?

speaker: Hildiran
en: You're glad to have let me stay now, aren't you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Very much! Tell me, what part does the amulet play?

speaker: Hildiran
en: It is a vessel. It needs to be filled with the energy created in battle.

speaker: Hildiran
en: But it will only work with this type of shrine. They can be found all over Mercia.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have many questions still.

speaker: Hildiran
en: I promise you will get answers. But first, I have marked a shrine location on your map. Once there, enter a meditation. The amulet will pull you into Hugrheim.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what happens when I finish my training?

speaker: Hildiran
en: Then you return to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: ...very well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you met Valka? Something of you reminds me of her.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Go now, kind Eivor, and train!

speaker: Eivor
en: This looks like the shrine she told me about.

speaker: Eivor
en: By the gods! It's as though I'm dreaming while awake.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can this truly be the work of my mind?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not finished with my training.

speaker: Eivor
en: My training is complete. I should return to Hildiran.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Eivor, you return.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here. I am done.

speaker: Hildiran
en: You have done well. I have collected many treasures in my lifetime. I am willing to part with them, but only to drengr I deem worthy.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'd be honored.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Feel free to return. As you continue your training by visiting more shrines, I will be able to gift you more powerful treasures.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: Rest easy, friend. You will be avenged. Our bodies may be broken, our pouches may be empty, but our souls will thrive. You will be remembered.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened here?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: An attack gone awry. We found more of Constantin's Picts than expected. The rich have their numbers... both in coin and spears. My men were not ready, and we were overwhelmed. But I'm afraid it's not over. They know I still live.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: Hark! Pict reinforcements! To battle! The spirits of my men are with me, and my spirit with theirs. Owooo!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: We will kill every king, even yours, for they squander the nobility they've been birthed to. Owooo!

speaker: Eivor
en: The threat is gone.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: What a fight! The Pict King Constantin will feel a little lighter in the purse tomorrow. Thank you for your aid, uh...?

speaker: Eivor
en: Call me Eivor.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: The name is Ryce, Ryce Sherwin. You know, we could use someone like you in our band of merry rogues and knaves. The poor get richer and the rich get poorer thanks to us. We've a hideout in the woods. Drop by sometime, share an ale maybe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe.

speaker: Ryce
en: Well, until we meet again!

speaker: Eivor
en: A hideout in the woods. Sounds interesting.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Ey! He's back! How was...?

speaker: Ryce
en: Not good. Our friends will be remembered. But now, I need to plan for our next target. You lot can get back to training.

speaker: Ryce
en: Welcome, friend, to our neck of the woods! You are free to join us any time.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is is that you do here?

speaker: Ryce
en: We borrow some coin from the ones who have plenty, and give it to the ones who need them. We took silver from King Aella, jewels from Aethelwulf. I like to call it balancing the scale.

speaker: Eivor
en: A small gesture for their cause.

speaker: Eivor
en: A small gesture for their cause.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, you missed the opening act. Kjotve's forward camp melted like a spring thaw at our approach.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is from here we launch our attack?

speaker: Guthorm the Wise
en: We do indeed, and we are ready to fight. King Harald's forces are well in place. Only give the word.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I will. But before we strike, I have a request.

speaker: Guthorm the Wise
en: Name it.

speaker: Sigurd
en: That Eivor may give challenge to Kjotve at the gates of his fortress. A battle to the death in single combat.

speaker: Guthorm the Wise
en: Is...is this what you want?

speaker: Eivor
en: Kjotve robbed my father of all honor and dignity. I will win it back.

speaker: Sigurd
en: When honor is at stake, let none interfere. And if Kjotve should die before the battle begins, all the better for our chances.

speaker: Eivor
en: Today my blade must do the work of Skuld's sharp scissors and cut short the cord of Kjotve's fate.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Well said, my sharp-tongued warrior-skald. May we all live to hear that sung.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have waited years for this, but I will not risk losing it through rashness. We should wait until the time is right.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We set sail when you are ready.

speaker: Basim
en: Eivor, a word.

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim. Hytham. This feud is not yours, yet you fight it all the same. I find that strange.

speaker: Basim
en: You find it strange because you are wrong. Our clan, the Hidden Ones, have been fighting with Kjotve's Order for centuries.

speaker: Eivor
en: You came from Miklagard to kill Kjotve yourself?

speaker: Basim
en: We did. Or rather, we came so that Hytham could kill him. My apprentice has been studying this target for many months

speaker: Eivor
en: Is Kjotve's reputation so great outside Norway?

speaker: Basim
en: Not his reputation alone, but the order to which he belongs. Something of a rival clan to our own.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham, I mean no disrespect to you or the Hidden Ones, but Kjotve is mine. My family's honor is at stake.

speaker: Hytham
en: I understand. All that matters is that Kjotve dies this day.

speaker: Basim
en: On that, we are agreed.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: KJOTVE! KJOTVE! KJOTVE! KJOTVE! KJOTVE! KJOTVE!

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: Sigurd Whoreson! You slink around my walls like a thief in the night! Face me here, now!

speaker: Eivor
en: The fight is mine, Kjotve. Sigurd is only here to watch me feed your innards to my raven.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: Look at this! Once again, Eivor Wolf-Kissed appears to take a swipe at me!

speaker: Eivor
en: This ... this is my father's shame! Today I take back the honor he lost.

speaker: Eivor
en: I call a ' (duel)! Here against the oath-breaker.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: I will make you beg as your father begged, Wolf-Kissed! Squeal as your mother squealed!

speaker: Eivor
en: You destroyed my life. I will take yours.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: You are weak like your father was weak. I need no weapons but these hands. You dance better than you fight.

speaker: Odin
en: Rise Eivor. This is not your day to die.

speaker: Kjotve
en: Why do you refuse to die?

speaker: Eivor
en: We are not alone, Kjotve. The All-Father watches.

speaker: Eivor
en: My blade will drink your blood.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: Your flesh will feed my wolves.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham!

speaker: Hytham
en: Ah!

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: A shameful trick, Wolf-kissed. You are your father's child.

speaker: Odin
en: Rise, Eivor... and awaken.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin?

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you want of me?

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: You've won your prize, Wolf-Kissed. The glory of my death.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: All for this...

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: ...your coward father and his empty sacrifice.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: Heed the price of our war, Wolf-Kissed. The harvest of three dead generations. All their names, unknown. It all means nothing.

speaker: Eivor
en: No. My clan will not be forgotten!

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: I fought as I did, as hard as I did, to survive. For I know what awaits us in the end.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: Only darkness.

speaker: Gorm
en: Raven Clan! Your lives are forfeit! Come forward if you must, into the crucible of your doom!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your father is dead, Gorm! His debt repaid! Open the gates and you will be spared!

speaker: Gorm
en: Wallow in shit, Wolf-Kissed! Archers, take aim!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ravens! Show no mercy!

speaker: Gorm
en: Archers... Fire!

speaker: Eivor
en: Forward to glory!

speaker: Dag
en: Get those ladders up, you soft pricks!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Get over that wall and take down that gate!

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin is with us!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hew their heads and spill their blood!

speaker: Sigurd
en: The cowards hide behind yet more walls! Onward! Eivor! Gorm fled into the church!

speaker: Gorm
en: A blind pursuit of vengeance has made you predictable.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are a shadow of your father, Gorm. Weak and witless.

speaker: Gorm
en: And you will leave this place as ashes on the wind.

speaker: Eivor
en: The coward Gorm flees. His father dies twice today.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor! We have the day. Let the coward go.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor! The breath-of-battle rises from my brow! The skalds will sing of this night!

speaker: Eivor
en: We have won the day, but Gorm escaped. He fled north, to King Harald's domain.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Let that bruised piglet run where he may. His father is dead, his clan is no more. We are the masters of Rygjafylke!

speaker: Eivor
en: A toothless cub may grow to be a dangerous wolf.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, stop. And listen. You have reclaimed your honor. Enjoy the night's victory, tomorrow we will celebrate.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're right, Brother. You are always right.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Guthorm! Relay news of our victory to your nephew, the king.

speaker: Guthorm the Wise
en: I have done so already, Sigurd. He'll be more than pleased, and will ensure you pride of place at his (clan gathering) at Alrekstad.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Tell him we will come! Battle flushed and singing songs of glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep company with kings and you will soon have a crown of your own.

speaker: Sigurd
en: If the fates have spun it so. Linger here and loot what you can. I will bring news of our victory to Father before he leaves for Harald's Althing.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know, Sýnin. Another time...

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Has anyone seen a hunter? He is tall, his hair is like mine... and he uses a bow! He was last seen hunting near the woods to the west. He should be back by now.

speaker: Eivor
en: A lonely end. Luck skipped his turn.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take you back to Nyhofn? A tall ask for a corpse.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have some weight on you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Almost there.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Brother? Brother!

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Brother...! You should have listened to me... You have always been too selfish, reckless! Even Mother said so!

speaker: Eivor
en: Blame not the adventurer, for the pull of blood-song can tempt even the gods.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Wh-where do I go now, without you to guide me? Wh-what should I do? L-lost... I am l-lost...

speaker: Eivor
en: His path is in front of you, child. He would want you to follow it, to do what he can no longer do.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: H-his bow... I could teach myself how to use it... I could, couldn't I?

speaker: Eivor
en: Remember your brother and all that he is. Bring home his tales and let his legacy be grown. That is all we are... words and song.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: I will hone my bow-craft, and he will smile upon me from above. He will be proud.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Th-thank you, for bringing him back. Thank you.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: I'm going to be the best hunter ever, just like you, Brother. Wait and see, I will shoot that elk in the eye.

speaker: Eivor
en: Just like breathing, death is a constant. The sooner you learn and accept, the sooner you become stronger.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Wh-what are you saying...? You want me to forget my brother?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not forget, child

speaker: Norse Woman
en: No! I don't care about your stories! Thank you for bringing my brother back, but please, go away!

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Brother... O... what would Mother say... Brother... I miss you. Why did you leave us...!

speaker: Eivor
en: Remember your brother and all that he is. Bring home his tales and let his legacy be grown. That is all we are... words and song.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: I will hone my bow-craft, and he will smile upon me from above. He will be proud.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Th-thank you, for bringing him back. Thank you.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: I'm going to be the best hunter ever, just like you, Brother. Wait and see, I will shoot that elk in the eye.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Frey! Wh-wha? N-no... is that?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: He is in the halls now.

speaker: Norse Man
en: I... I am sorry, Frey. He died by prey, but he will rest a hunter.

speaker: Hrorek
en: The jarl needs help! Come, if you have courage!

speaker: Eivor
en: Which jarl?

speaker: Hrorek
en: He has been taken by bandits. Come, quickly!

speaker: Eivor
en: A jarl taken by bandits?

speaker: Hrorek
en: If you are as brave as you appear, you will come.

speaker: Hrorek
en: The jarl will be grateful, trust me! We are almost there! Hurry, or they will kill him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kill him? Do they not want a ransom?

speaker: Hrorek
en: Just hurry. We are near. Go on, they are up ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: You know where they are. You lead.

speaker: Hrorek
en: Fine. Follow me.

speaker: Bandit
en: Kjotve has no power here!

speaker: Eivor
en: This pathetic gamble has cost them their lives.

speaker: Hrorek
en: They threatened to kill me if I did not help.

speaker: Eivor
en: So to save your life, you led others to their death.

speaker: Hrorek
en: Our village was burned by Kjotve the Cruel. We had to flee to the forest. Those who survived grew mean and desperate. Olaf, one of the men you killed, said we had to fight for our land. But he only wanted to kill for silver.

speaker: Eivor
en: You picked the wrong fight. I am of Raven Clan and Kjotve's sworn enemy.

speaker: Hrorek
en: Then we share a common foe, and I was wrong to use you like that.

speaker: Eivor
en: There was no need for this fight. Kjotve is dead by my hand. I have lifted his boot from your neck.

speaker: Hrorek
en: Olaf, you lifeless fool! You almost murdered our rescuer!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your second mistake was choosing me as your prey.

speaker: Hrorek
en: That was not a mistake. You looked like a good fighter. I was hoping you would kill or weaken Olaf so I could escape.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are young and still foolish, so I will spare you your life. But cross me again or harm anyone I cherish, and you will join your friends in Helheim's foul forests.

speaker: Hrorek
en: Y-you will never see me again! I will be a white rabbit in the snow!

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like something is happening near Valka's hut. Perhaps I should take a look.

speaker: Edyt
en: Eivor! I can hardly believe it's you. The one fated to save my people.

speaker: Eivor
en: That woman seems to know me.

speaker: Edyt
en: Oh, it's you! Valka said we would meet, but I can hardly believe the great Eivor is fated to save my little Isle of Skye!

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are you?

speaker: Valka
en: Ahead of yourself as always, Edyt. Eivor, Edyt is an old friend and a seer. She contacted me for advice. Her people are plagued by nightmares to the point madness.

speaker: Eivor
en: I wasn't aware people settled on the Isle of Skye.

speaker: Edyt
en: There are small settlements, but it is a place of passage for many, making it perfect for dreams to wreck havok.

speaker: Edyt
en: Until now, I've mostly been deciphering whether my cousin's feasting on feathers in her dreams means she should marry a farmer or a baker

speaker: Eivor
en: You've lost me again.

speaker: Valka
en: Edyt needs your help. And it's not just her people being affected.

speaker: Valka
en: As someone deeply in tune with the spirit realm, I have also begun to lose sleep. I fear it may spread to out settlement soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will investigate, but it is not as if I have experience chasing away bad dreams.

speaker: Valka
en: There is more. You're not going to like this, Eivor, but I believe somehow... Randvi is involved. Perhaps even responsible.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know Randvi's whereabouts better than most and she isn't—Er, what I mean to say is she couldn't do something like this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka, you've really gone mad this time. Randvi would never do something like this. Nor could she! She's always here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka, you know I trust your wisdom, but... Randvi is my... friend. How could she threaten the settlement like this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka, you know I trust your wisdom, but... Randvi is my friend. How could she threaten the settlement like this?

speaker: Valka
en: Ever since the nightmares started, I began asking the spirits for clarity and a vision came to me.

speaker: Valka
en: Though it was cloudy, I know what I saw. You will find Randvi amidst a scene of death on Skye Island. The two of you will fight before you're forced to part ways forever.

speaker: Eivor
en: That just can't be true.

speaker: Valka
en: Believing is your choice. The only way to find the truth and stop the nightmares from spreading is if you go to Isle of Skye. I must tend to my duties, but Edyt can take you when you're ready.

speaker: Edyt
en: So? Are you ready? My people can't go without sleep any longer.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll find out what's plaguing your people. Whatever or whomever it may be.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need some time before we head out. I'll come back when I'm ready.

speaker: Edyt
en: Please, don't wait too long. My people need you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I knew Valka was wrong. Randvi's here, like always. Time to find out what's actually plaguing Edyt's people.

speaker: Edyt
en: You're back! Are you ready to go to Skye now?

speaker: Edyt
en: Here we are. The Isle of Skye. Beautiful, isn't it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Any idea where I should go first?

speaker: Edyt
en: Investigate Kiltaraglen first. It's where complaints of nightmares began. My hut is there, too, if you need to find me.

speaker: Woman in Distress
en: O, my ickle Dandelion! Where are you, Dandy? Here girl! Come out, Dandy-do! You'll burn! Burn to a widdle crisp! Come out!

speaker: Eivor
en: What has happened?

speaker: Woman in Distress
en: Dandelion Puff upset dome kindling. Bad girl! Everything burst into flames! I barely escaped.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dandelion Puff?

speaker: Woman in Distress
en: My widdle doggie-woggie! She's still in the house! I rushed out, but she didn't follow me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Dandelion? Uh, Dandy-do?

speaker: Eivor
en: Dandelion Puff, you're no dog.

speaker: Eivor
en: This way, girl! Let's get out of here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your mistress is this way, Dandelion.

speaker: Woman in Distress
en: Dandelion Puff! You live! That was wrong to stay in the burning house. Wrong, wrong, wrong!

speaker: Eivor
en: She's lucky to be alive.

speaker: Woman in Distress
en: Friend, I soon will sleep in the comforting arms of the Lord. Can you please look after my widdle doggie-dog?

speaker: Eivor
en: Dandy is no dog. She is a fox.

speaker: Woman in Distress
en: A fox? How silly I've been! So that's why you love the forest so, eh, Dandy Puff!

speaker: Eivor
en: But yes, I will find a place for her.

speaker: Woman in Distress
en: Bless you, I die in peace. Goodbye, my Dandy-Dandy-Dooooooo...

speaker: Eivor
en: Dandy.

speaker: Eivor
en: We need a place for you to stay. Would you like to join my settlement?

speaker: Eivor
en: Dandy! I am happy to see you.

speaker: A Fated Encounter
en: was a virtual representation of one of Eivor Varinsdottir's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan in 2020 through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Thrall (female 1)
en: No sense trying to change fate. What counts is how you face it.

speaker: Thrall (male 1)
en: My father was a thrall, as is my wife, as will our children be.

speaker: Thrall (female 2)
en: If there is another life beyond this, I hope it is a better one.

speaker: Thrall (male 2)
en: Toil and drudgery is our lot.

speaker: Jotun (female guard 1)
en: War brings glory, but there is no greater joy than a plump harvest.

speaker: Jotun (female guard 2)
en: From earth we came, and to the earth we will return.

speaker: Jotun (male guard 1)
en: The Æsir may have beaten us back at Asgard, but our time is coming.

speaker: Jotun (male guard 2)
en: Rock and snow, stone and squall, Utgard's walls will never fall.

speaker: Jotun (male guard 3)
en: Suttungr is always thinking. Don't trust anyone that thinks that much.

speaker: Jotun (male guard 4)
en: These walls are strong, but I long for the peace of the Ironwood.

speaker: Suttungr
en: You are small to my eyes, stranger.

speaker: Havi
en: Small in stature but great in deed. I am the one they call Havi, the High One of Asgard, and I come bearing a great gift.

speaker: Suttungr
en: Your name is known to me. But what could mighty Suttungr want that a little thing like you could provide?

speaker: Havi
en: Your great cauldron, stolen by Hymir's sons. Let this offering be a beginning to the end of our hostilities.

speaker: Havi
en: Such a small thing, yet so much deeper than it seems. Appearances can be deceiving, can they not?

speaker: Suttungr
en: Well spoken, Havi. Our people may be enemies, but you have earned your welcome here. Thralls! An honored guest has come! Prepare a feast!

speaker: Havi
en: I hope also to meet your daughter, Gunlodr. I have heard much of her skill in the mystical arts.

speaker: Suttungr
en: She will be toiling at her work, as ever. But be forewarned, she shuns the company of others.

speaker: Havi
en: I could summon her to the feast, if you like. We might discuss matters of alchemy on the way.

speaker: Suttungr
en: That would please me. You will find her in her grotto, up the path, within the circle of stones. Have a care, though. You are safe in my presence, but you wander Utgard at your peril.

speaker: Havi
en: I will be discreet.

speaker: Suttungr
en: And Havi... be kind. Gunlodr is... different from you and I.

speaker: Havi
en: The vault is still closed. When will Suttungr open it?

speaker: Havi
en: Utgard, ancient keep of the Joiner. Suttungr holds sway within those walls.

speaker: Havi
en: I promised to bring Gunlodr to the feast. I should not keep Suttungr waiting.

speaker: Havi
en: Here is the stone circle, but no way into the sanctum. Another illusion!

speaker: Havi
en: The way inside is revealed.

speaker: Havi
en: Gunlodr? What is this place?

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Some time ago, we made powerful magic here. We sought to see all futures. But every road led to Ragnarok. Father does not visit here anymore. He sees no profit in it. But I am not yet ready to give up.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: You are Æsir.

speaker: Havi
en: I am.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: I have seen images of the future. Heard the voices of those who will come after us.

speaker: Havi
en: Voices from... in there?

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Yes. I leave them words. Little packets of possibility, waiting for unknown ears, many ages hence.

speaker: Havi
en: What do these future voices say?

speaker: Gunlodr
en: They seek the wisdom of the past. They speak of things to come. But even they cannot turn the tide of Ragnarok.

speaker: Havi
en: There is to be a feast in my honor. Your father sent me to fetch you.

speaker: Havi
en: It may be you need a break from your toil, Gunlodr.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: There is no time for rest. Ragnarok will be upon us soon. My people rely on me.

speaker: Havi
en: There is to be a feast in my honor. Your father sent me to fetch you.

speaker: Havi
en: There is to be a feast in my honor. Your father sent me to fetch you.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: No, not yet. Listen. I want you to hear the voices.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Are you there, prophet? Can you hear me?

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Perhaps another day. Another thread. Come. We must not keep Father waiting.

speaker: Hushed Voice
en: Who are you?

speaker: Havi
en: Winter's knife cuts deep and sky-pearls fall thick in this land.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: It... it is cold out here!

speaker: Havi
en: How can that surprise you?

speaker: Gunlodr
en: I haven't been outside in... hm, I don't know how long.

speaker: Havi
en: You are devoted to your work.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Not my work. My responsibility. My people ignore the disaster bearing down on them. Someone must do something. We have long searched for a solution, until the burden of it has bent my mind. I do not think as clearly as I once did.

speaker: Havi
en: I have heard there is one method still untested.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: There is. But to activate it would mean defiling our well of knowledge, from which all of Midgard drinks. There is no telling the change it would wreak on humankind. It would bring chaos at the least. And I do not wish to hurt them.

speaker: Havi
en: Even if it means the death of all Jötnar?

speaker: Gunlodr
en: We will find another way. We must.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: This land is quite beautiful. I had all but forgotten.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: The vault, wherein our greatest discoveries are kept. Such things would do great harm in the hands of evil people.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: No stone walls will defend us when Ragnarök comes. All we have built here will be swept away.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: For so long we made magics there in that tower. Enchantment has seeped into its very walls. The wind and snow have gnawed that tower to the bone. Soon we will knock it down.

speaker: Suttungr
en: Havi, your feast is prepared. I hope it pleases you.

speaker: Havi
en: You are generous and hospitable indeed, great Suttungr. None can say otherwise.

speaker: Suttungr
en: And see, your gift stands in pride of place, brimming with freshly fermented mead. Enough for a hundred Jotnar and more!

speaker: Havi
en: This is... an unexpected honor. You have filled it already with mead from your vault, then?

speaker: Suttungr
en: No need! It has filled itself. Such is the magic of the cauldron.

speaker: Havi
en: Impressive. But what if it should run out of mead?

speaker: Suttungr
en: Do you hear this? Havi fears he will drink us dry!

speaker: Suttungr
en: My cauldron is deep, but my vault is deeper. Do not worry about my stores of mead. I have plenty to go around.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Father, you know revelry does not suit me. Must I attend this feast? I have work to do.

speaker: Suttungr
en: Your work can wait, my daughter. Take a moment, enjoy yourself.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Father, we have very little time

speaker: Suttungr
en: Enjoy yourself. I insist.

speaker: Suttungr
en: Havi, the guests are uneasy. They see an Æsir, but they do not know you. Will you address them?

speaker: Havi
en: I am ready.

speaker: Suttungr
en: Now we will hear from our honored guest! The Lord of the Æsir has come in peace, and has brought us a mighty gift. Attend!

speaker: Havi
en: Havi, I am called, whose axe is never slaked! The blood of my enemies is my mead, their skulls my pillow!

speaker: Suttungr
en: You brag well. They were ever pleased by violence.

speaker: Havi
en: I am Havi, deft of tongue and quick of wit, here to spin you a tale!

speaker: Suttungr
en: Your stories are wasted on them. They respect deeds, not hollow talk.

speaker: Havi
en: I am Havi, dreaded hunter of your kind! One hundred Jotnar I have slain.

speaker: Suttungr
en: You tread on dangerous ground, Æsir.

speaker: Havi
en: You are all brothers and sisters to me!

speaker: Suttungr
en: Do not be too familiar. Jotnar are slow to trust.

speaker: Havi
en: Though our people are enemies, I come here to do you honor, for I know that none feast, nor fight like Jotnar.

speaker: Suttungr
en: Your words are well chosen.

speaker: Havi
en: Great Jotnar, I stand here in awe of your might and majesty.

speaker: Suttungr
en: They do not respect weakness. Show some backbone!

speaker: Havi
en: I offer a toast to great Suttungr!

speaker: Suttungr
en: They do not love me as much as they love to feast.

speaker: Havi
en: Now I will sing you the lay of Idunn, whose apples gave life eternal!

speaker: Suttungr
en: Those with rumbling bellies will not stand for long tales.

speaker: Havi
en: I could go on, but who wants to hear words when there's meat and mead to be had?

speaker: Suttungr
en: You know your audience well, it seems.

speaker: Havi
en: Now we will drink deep and eat heartily!

speaker: Suttungr
en: Let the feast begin!

speaker: Havi
en: What can I do to get them to drink faster? The guests are not drinking fast enough. Perhaps I can speed things along. I need to empty that cauldron. Then Suttungr will open his vault.

speaker: Jotun (female 1)
en: Two of my brothers died in the attack on Asgard. Now we throw a feast for Asgard's lord? Is Suttungr under a spell?

speaker: Jotun (female 2)
en: Patience. They cannot outlast us. You will have your chance at vengeance.

speaker: Havi
en: Is there any sweeter music than the clash of drinking horns?

speaker: Jotun (male 1)
en: Ægir's cauldron has come to Utgard? I'll never be sober again!

speaker: Jotun (male 2)
en: A feast is for meat and mead, not empty chatter.

speaker: Jotun (male 3)
en: Suttungr keeps strange company. Strange company indeed.

speaker: Jotun (male 4)
en: Must we drink to our enemies now?

speaker: Jotun (female 3)
en: An Æsir? I think I've lost my appetite.

speaker: Jotun (female 4)
en: Raising our horns to an Æsir? I never thought I'd see the day.

speaker: Jotun (female 5)
en: Cold winds howl and snows may fall, but the mead is always warm in Suttungr's halls.

speaker: Jotun (male 5)
en: What is an Æsir doing here?

speaker: Jotun (male 6)
en: Humble foes are thralls in waiting. Give me an enemy worth the swing of an axe!

speaker: Jotun (male 7)
en: You can measure a warrior by the notches on his blade.

speaker: Jotun (male 8)
en: Tales and songs are naught but wind and clamor. It's deeds that matter here.

speaker: Jotun (male 9)
en: Suttungr is keen of mind, but he does not have our hearts. We need a warrior to lead us!

speaker: Jotun (male 10)
en: This Havi must be mighty indeed, if Suttungr honors him so.

speaker: Jotun (male 11)
en: Is that Gunlodr? Not often you see her dragged away from her work.

speaker: Jotun (male 12)
en: Aaah, better out than in.

speaker: Jotun (male 13)
en: Ale dulls both mind and blade. What if the Æsir should attack right now?

speaker: Jotun (male 14)
en: Does anything bring you joy?

speaker: Jotun (male 13)
en: The feel of my opponent's skull giving way beneath my axe.

speaker: Jotun (female 6)
en: You know, you are not so repulsive when I'm drunk.

speaker: Jotun (male 15)
en: More mead here!

speaker: Havi
en: Ægir, mighty friend to the Æsir! Are you not sorry to lose your cauldron?

speaker: Ægir
en: It was never mine by right. Thor won it from Hymir so he might feast in my hall. I only kept it on his behalf. And after that bloody business with Hymir's sons, well, I'd as soon be rid of it! I'll have no strife beneath my roof.

speaker: Havi
en: The end of strife. I'll drink to that!

speaker: Ægir
en: And I'll drink to anything!

speaker: Havi
en: Is that Loki there? Surely he would not dare...

speaker: Havi
en: Loki?

speaker: Thokk
en: Not me, friend. My name is Thokk.

speaker: Havi
en: Forgive me. I... I thought you were someone else.

speaker: Thokk
en: Too much drink in too little time. The cure for that is sleep.

speaker: Havi
en: The right food will inspire thirst. I should head to the kitchen.

speaker: Thrall (kitchen)
en: No guests in the kitchen! Out!

speaker: Havi
en: The kitchen. Here I might find some way to make the guests thirsty.

speaker: Havi
en: Hot spices call for a cooling drink. Now how can I use this?

speaker: Thrall (kitchen)
en: No guests in the kitchen! Out!

speaker: Havi
en: These guests will drink more with fire in their mouths.

speaker: Jotun (music-seeker 1)
en: What is a feast without music? I want to dance!

speaker: Jotun (music-seeker 2)
en: I've seen more life in a grave mound.

speaker: Havi
en: I see musicians... but where is the music?

speaker: Havi
en: Somber souls will only sip at their drinking horns. Conjure us a tune to raise their spirits.

speaker: Thrall (musician)
en: We are keen, but my harp has been stolen. We cannot play without it.

speaker: Havi
en: Who would steal a song-bringer's instrument?

speaker: Thrall (musician)
en: There was a group of children playing round us earlier with mischief in their eyes.

speaker: Havi
