en: I will get your harp back. And then you will play.

speaker: Havi
en: Thralls. Humans kept in bondage, bred to serve. Such is the fate of the lowly.

speaker: Thrall Child 1
en: Give it to me! I want a go!

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: Get your grubby paws off my harp!

speaker: Thrall Child 3
en: My turn! My turn!

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: Not you too! You'll break the strings with your sausage fingers!

speaker: Havi
en: That harp does not belong to you, little thief. You should give it back.

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: What are you going to do? Fight me for it?

speaker: Havi
en: Why don't you give me a real challenge?

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: All right, you want this harp, go dive in that mead! Climb as high as you can, though! I want a big splash!

speaker: Havi
en: Watch and learn.

speaker: Thrall Child 1
en: Bet they won't do it!

speaker: Thrall Child 3
en: How many broken bones, you think?

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: Fifty at least. Maybe a hundred!

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: Did you see that? He flew!

speaker: Havi
en: There. Now give back the harp, so the musicians may play.

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: Ymir's hairy balls, that was amazing! You must be half raven!

speaker: Havi
en: Who taught you such language?

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: Mother. Why?

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: You jump next!

speaker: Thrall Child 3
en: No, you!

speaker: Thrall Child 1
en: I'm not going, no way.

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: Coward.

speaker: Thrall Child 1
en: I don't see you jumping.

speaker: Thrall Child 2
en: I'm... I'm not ready yet!

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: Who will challenge our champion? Who among you is brave enough? Who is in the mood for a brawl? Don't be shy! Test your fists against the champion!

speaker: Havi
en: They are calling for challengers to face their champion. A fight would make them drain their horns faster.

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: Havi! Show us your might! Beat our champion, and we will drain our horns in your honor.

speaker: Havi
en: Bring me this champion, and I will shine my knuckles on his jawbone.

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: Behold!

speaker: Havi
en: Do you mock me? I will not fight a withered old crone.

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: If you are too afraid to face her, well, that is that...

speaker: Havi
en: If she is truly your champion, then so be it. I will try not to break her brittle bones, but I promise nothing.

speaker: Jotun (male spectator 1)
en: Can you not beat an old woman? My lambs hit harder than you!

speaker: Jotun (male spectator 2)
en: Don't be scared of that crumble-bones! Is she too strong for you?

speaker: Jotun (female spectator)
en: Perhaps a babe would be more suited to your strength.

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: Indeed, you are mighty! You have fought old age and won. No one has ever done that before.

speaker: Havi
en: Drink to me, then, as you promised you would.

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: All of you! Empty your horns for Havi!

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: A brave try, but you have failed.

speaker: Havi
en: She is more formidable than she seems.

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: Do not be downhearted. You may battle old age, but old age will win in the end.

speaker: Havi
en: I'm back.

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: Found your courage, have you? Are you ready to face our champion now?

speaker: Havi
en: I will not underestimate her this time.

speaker: Havi
en: This challenge is beneath me. I will not dance for your amusement.

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: Scared of an old hag? Well, come back if you change your mind.

speaker: Havi
en: I'm back.

speaker: Jotun (pit-master)
en: Found your courage, have you? Are you ready to face our champion now?

speaker: Jotun (female spectator)
en: They beat the champion? Nobody's ever beaten the champion!

speaker: Jotun (male spectator 3)
en: Drink in the name of Havi!

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Come, give it a try! What's the worst that can happen?

speaker: Jotun (bow contestant)
en: Last time I played your game, I got so drunk I shot my brother in the leg.

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: What's the second worst?

speaker: Havi
en: I should try the archery contest. No doubt they will toast my prowess if I succeed.

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Greetings, Havi! Will you test your arm at archery? You must hit three targets in a handful of heartbeats.

speaker: Havi
en: I can shoot the wings off a wasp.

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Ah, but can you do it while mead-addled? Before each attempt, you must take a drink.

speaker: Havi
en: I'll take your challenge on one condition. For every drink I take, you take two!

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Ha! That's a condition I'll gladly accept. Are you ready?

speaker: Havi
en: Show me those targets.

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Then take a drink, and let fly!

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Did you forget your mead? Drink from the cup and start again.

speaker: Jotun bow-heckler 1
en: Let us hope you hold your beer better than you hold a bow!

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Fine shot! Now have a drink and try another.

speaker: Jotun (bow heckler 1)
en: Close your eyes, your luck will improve! (appears to be a random call with the other lines)

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Steady eye, now! The last one is the hardest.

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Not so easy after supping at the brook of the cheer-cup, eh? When you feel ready, take a drink and try again.

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: You return! Keen to stretch your bow string?

speaker: Havi
en: Show me those targets.

speaker: Jotun (bow heckler 2)
en: You look a bit wobbly there. Careful!

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: You are a keen shot, Havi! Your hand grows steadier with drink, where others lose their eye.

speaker: Havi
en: Another round?

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Not for me. My belly roils like a knot of eels... and I see three of you. I think I should walk this off...

speaker: Havi
en: We can do this later.

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: Not so easy after supping at the brook of the cheer-cup, eh? When you feel ready, take a drink and try again.

speaker: Jotun (bowmaster)
en: You return! Keen to stretch your bow string?

speaker: Havi
en: Gunlodr looks glum, and she has not touched a drop of mead. Maybe I can raise her spirits.

speaker: Havi
en: You are not drinking, Gunlodr.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: I do not care for it. Drink is the heron that steals away one's memory.

speaker: Havi
en: Some would say it frees the spirit of worry.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: We call those people drunks.

speaker: Havi
en: I see your wit is as sharp as your intelligence.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Wit? I was simply stating a truth.

speaker: Havi
en: Let us play a game. Ask me some riddles. I will see if I can guess them.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: I enjoy a good riddle. How did you know?

speaker: Havi
en: All great minds enjoy riddles. You fashion order from disorder. Sense from nonsense.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: You have me at that. Very well, I will play.

speaker: Havi
en: Give me an easy one to begin.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Would that I had now what I had yesterday. Find out what that was. Mankind it mars, speech it hinders, yet speech it will inspire.

speaker: Havi
en: The answer is courage.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: No, the answer is ale. I thought you would get that, as you seem so fond of it.

speaker: Havi
en: It is ale, of course.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: A child could have solved that one.

speaker: Havi
en: It must be gold.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: A worthy guess, but wrong. The answer is ale.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Would you like another?

speaker: Havi
en: All right. I'm ready.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Who is that shrill one who rides a hard road and has fared that way before? He kisses hard who has two mouths and goes only on gold.

speaker: Havi
en: It is a hammer.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Well done! I hope that wasn't just a guess?

speaker: Havi
en: An arrow, surely?

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Arrow fly shrill and kiss hard. But two mouths? Gold? The answer is hammer.

speaker: Havi
en: A river has a mouth, and sometimes flows on gold.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: A good try, but the river's kiss is soft. It is a hammer.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: One more?

speaker: Havi
en: I feel good about this one.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Be prepared. This is the hardest yet. White haired women, servants two, bore ale-tub to the larder. No hand turned it, nor hammer beat it. But there, outside the island, the upright one who made it.

speaker: Havi
en: Snow on the trees.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: You have a poet's heart. But you should have used your mind. It was swans and eggs.

speaker: Havi
en: It can only be swans and eggs.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Very clever, Havi. Yes.

speaker: Havi
en: Old age is the answer.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Old age? I think age is slowing your brain. The answer is swans and eggs.

speaker: Havi
en: Well, now the game is over. Have I raised your spirits at all?

speaker: Gunlodr
en: That was disappointing. Perhaps you'd better find someone more suited to your intelligence.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: I feel a little better. You are kind to attend to me, Havi. Most have given up trying.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: I feel better. Much, much better. I might even go and have a drink!

speaker: Havi
en: I've had enough.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: O. Very well.

speaker: Havi
en: I have changed my mind. Riddles bore me.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Did I do something wrong?

speaker: Havi
en: Enjoy the feast.

speaker: Havi
en: The mead is half gone. Then Ægir's cauldron can be drained!

speaker: Havi
en: The cauldron is empty. I should tell Suttungr.

speaker: Havi
en: Great Suttungr, your guests thirst for mead yet the cauldron is dry.

speaker: Suttungr
en: All gone? I never would have thought it possible! Gunlodr!

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Father?

speaker: Suttungr
en: Open the vault. Instruct the thralls to bring more mead for my guests!

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Do they really need more, Father? Several are unconscious already.

speaker: Suttungr
en: Do as I ask, Daughter. Give them all they can drink.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: As you wish. I will open the vault.

speaker: Suttungr
en: None will say that Suttungr is less than generous.

speaker: Havi
en: None will be capable.

speaker: Havi
en: Finally, the vault is open. The Mead awaits within.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Havi! I heard a noise, and I... What are you doing here?

speaker: Havi
en: I wanted to speak with you, away from the others. I brought something for you. A gift.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: For me? Thank you, but... why?

speaker: Havi
en: Fate, Gunlodr. We are helpless to escape it. And we were fated to be here now, together.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: You and I? How? It makes no sense.

speaker: Havi
en: The Nornir spin their patterns, and we can only surrender. We are entwined, spun together. There is perfect sense in that.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Your words, your gift, your eyes when you look upon me. You bewilder me, Havi. I do not understand you.

speaker: Havi
en: Listen and attend. I will show you all you need to know.

speaker: Havi
en: Fate, Gunlodr. We are helpless to escape it. And we were fated to be here now, together.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: You and I? How? It makes no sense.

speaker: Havi
en: The Nornir spin their patterns, and we can only surrender. We are entwined, spun together. There is perfect sense in that.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: No. You tease and mock, but I do not believe your lies. Your only desire is the Mead! You are a thief and an agent of chaos. I'll see you pay for this deceit. Guards!

speaker: Gunlodr
en: The Mead is no treasure for the ignorant!

speaker: Gunlodr
en: You're here to steal our secrets!

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Don't do this! You cannot know the consequences! No one can!

speaker: Havi
en: I have come for the Mead, and neither you nor your father will keep me from it.

speaker: Gunlodr
en: You are a thief and an agent of chaos. I'll see you pay for this deceit. Guards!

speaker: Gunlodr
en: The Mead is no treasure for the ignorant!

speaker: Gunlodr
en: You're here to steal our secrets!

speaker: Gunlodr
en: Don't do this! You cannot know the consequences! No one can!

speaker: Havi
en: The Mead. By this strange magic, might the Æsir evade our doom?

speaker: Havi
en: Hyrrokin has promised answers at the Well of Mimir.

speaker: Suttungr
en: Havi!

speaker: Loki
en: There! See! The robber caught red-handed!

speaker: Suttungr
en: Betrayer! Deceiver! I treated you as an honored guest, and this is how you repay me?

speaker: Havi
en: I saw you at the feast, Loki! Small wonder you disguised yourself, after all you have done!

speaker: Havi
en: Loki? You should have the sense to stay far away from me, after what you did.

speaker: Loki
en: Someone needed to warn my people of the treachery in your heart. Suttungr, show this Æsir how the Jotnar deal with thieves.

speaker: Suttungr
en: Come. Embrace your death!

speaker: Loki
en: You are not going anywhere, Havi!

speaker: Suttungr
en: Deceiver! False-tongue! Dishonorable trickster! You would gamble with uncountable lives! What have you done with my daughter?

speaker: Havi
en: Suttungr's ice... it looks unstable. That ice looks fragile.

speaker: Havi
en: Ah! I should take cover. Need to get out of this.

speaker: Loki
en: Are you getting weak, Havi? Is the strength in your arm fading?

speaker: Suttungr
en: I have lived too long to suffer one such as you!

speaker: Suttungr
en: Your bones will splinter beneath my boots!

speaker: Havi
en: Be thankful it was me who took your Mead and not Loki. What I do, I do for the safety of the Æsir and Vanir.

speaker: Suttungr
en: You will change countless fates, Havi, but not your own.

speaker: Havi
en: We will see.

speaker: Havi
en: Hyrrokin said to find her at Mímir's Well. I will deal with that venomous trickster another day.

speaker: Havi
en: One of Freyja's statues. Who put you up here, little cat?

speaker: Havi
en: So that's how it is. Lead the way, nimble one.

speaker: Havi
en: Where are you leading me?

speaker: Havi
en: Nowhere to go but down...

speaker: Havi
en: I have it. Who knew you could capture a sound?

speaker: Eivor
en: A message has come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Whatever this, beast or monster, defeating it would only add to my reputation. I should meet this abbess, Wulfhilda.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Those raiders killed our cattle!

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Danes did not do this! It's the Devil's work!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: We know it's the Danes. It's always the damn Danes. Make them pay wergild (penance) for the dead that now litter the fields!

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Show sense, please! What would the Danes gain from the slaughter of poor farmers?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Look! There's a filthy Dane now! Why don't we ask!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: You slaughtered my best milk-cow, you beast!

speaker: Eivor
en: I did not touch your herd.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: You fools are making this worse!

speaker: Eivor
en: These Saxons fight like mad dogs to protect their own. I cannot blame them.

speaker: Eivor
en: They hit hard for farmers and country folk.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Thank you for staying your hand, stranger. What is your name?

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor. Of the Raven Clan in Mercia.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Wulfhilda, Abbess of Barking and inquirer into mysteries.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are we here for the same reason, I wonder?

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Aye, to look upon Devil's work. But why would a Dane from upriver care what happens to Saxon farmers?

speaker: Eivor
en: If there is a rabid wolf or bear on the prowl, I would see it dead. Blame often falls on my folk for such carnage.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Well and good, Eivor of the Raven Clan. Take a look at the maulings and tell me what manner of rabid beast did these things.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could start with the dead cows.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bite marks, but not from any beast I know. And the corpse is covered in a strange mold, though the wounds are fresh.

speaker: Eivor
en: You there. What befell this poor beast?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Danes befell it.

speaker: Eivor
en: How can you be sure?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: It was Hrothgar's war-band! They're holed up in that old church, working their misery upon us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Warriors do not often go about slaying milk cows. Besides, I have heard talk of a beast on the loose.

speaker: Eivor
en: Blood. Still wet as dew. Where does it lead?

speaker: Eivor
en: By the gods! What manner of beast flung that poor creature up here to its doom?

speaker: Ashildr
en: A Jotun did this! I saw it, all big and hairy, staggering across the moor!

speaker: Cedl
en: Giants aren't real. You saw the Devil himself, taking his tithe to Hell!

speaker: Eivor
en: You are brave ones for getting so close to this awful sight.

speaker: Ashildr
en: I saw it, warrior, I did! The night it happened, I saw it all!

speaker: Eivor
en: What did you see? A wolf, a bear? Maybe a rabid hound?

speaker: Ashildr
en: It was a Jotun! As great as a tree, and it laughed while it ripped and teared. It yelled out its name, Grendel!

speaker: Eivor
en: What sort of beast leaves glistening mold over freshly killed prey? Yet that woman blamed Hrothgar and his band of Danes? Were the killers men? Whoever it was, they were mighty enough to get a mauled beast-corpse onto a rooftop. But that little girl said the creature was a giant, calling itself Grendel. This may be the work of a band of drunken Danes, or something far, far worse. I should discuss these clues with Wulfhilda.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wulfhilda. I have learned all I can from the villagers. And those dead beasts.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: And what is your take on the mystery? Still believe a wolf or bear did these things?

speaker: Eivor
en: This is not the work of a woodland creature. The bite marks. The mold. Most odd.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: So, you admit this is the Devil's work? Or one of your wooden dragons come to life?

speaker: Eivor
en: A few maulings do not make for a devil or a dragon. It must be a man or a pack of them. The girl mentioned a name. Grendel.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: No ... no mortal hand could rend flesh in such a way. Surely you see that.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have seen the worst the hands of men can do. Deeds bloodier than this.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: And these men stalk the night, slaying cattle as they go?

speaker: Eivor
en: True. This thing, I cannot explain.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Three times these attacks have happened. Each time bite marks, broken bones, and streaks of mold. Something wicked walks in East Anglia. Some other animals were attacked in the woods northeast of here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let us go.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: This way. We may find more clues.

speaker: Eivor
en: Theotford has answered the call. I should join Finnr at our forward camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: The King's Bury horn has inspired more than a few farmers to action.

speaker: Eivor
en: You did this?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Aye. We heard the horn's call, as in times past. Are we to rise against Rued's dogs?

speaker: Eivor
en: Theotford will rise. And Northwic. And Elmenham.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Then we will too. Oswald drew first blood taking Rued down. We will finish what he started.

speaker: Eivor
en: We meet at the ruins north of Burgh Castle.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: We're only hog farmers, but we'll fight as hard as we're able. Let's go. There's a long road ahead for us!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Let me go, heathens! Have you not taken enough from us already?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Shut your hole, shit-stain.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rued's wretches spared you. You're lucky.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: God be praised! We were lambs before their blades, ready for slaughter.

speaker: Eivor
en: You draw breath still.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: I heard the horn's call, but I thought I was dreaming. I will join the fyrd. Just name the place.

speaker: Eivor
en: We gather at the ruins northeast of Northwic.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: I'll be there.

speaker: Eivor
en: That horn came from Elmenham. Valdis must have got to them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those men must have heard the horn's call. The people of East Anglia have more courage than I imagined.

speaker: Eivor
en: The brothers' fleet, gathered and ready.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: Can we really do this? We're just farmers and merchants!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 5
en: Have faith, brother. God protects the righteous.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Finally, we put my longship to use again. I was tired if it gathering dust.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Our ships are sturdy, but Burgh's walls are sturdier. This plan of Finnr's is mad.

speaker: Finnr
en: Eivor! Word of your actions in Theotford has spread like wildfire! Men are pouring in from across East Anglia. And our ships stand ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: Theotford's reeve is with us. His men will be here soon.

speaker: Finnr
en: More than his. The King's Bury horn has inspired men all across this kingdom. We will have the army we need. It seems Oswald got what he wanted in the end. Saxon and Dane, united in common cause.

speaker: Eivor
en: A pity he's not here to see it.

speaker: Finnr
en: The forces will be ready soon. Are you ready to start the assault?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am.

speaker: Finnr
en: Our target is Burgh Castle, said to be impenetrable.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Let them have their false confidence.

speaker: Finnr
en: By cover of night, Valdis will lead the at the front gates. With Rued's men distracted, our forces move on the sea gate from the black waters at their backs.

speaker: Eivor
en: And once we're in, we'll leave no gate closed in that castle. Rued's men cannot be allowed to dig in further. Your longship. Is she ready?

speaker: Finnr
en: She awaits her own special glory.

speaker: Finnr
en: They need your words, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald was a man who did not hesitate when you sought him for favors. A man who was fair and strong. A man who gave his life for his kingdom. Honor him today. Honor his memory and fight with the same extra courage he showed.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Men
en: For Oswald!

speaker: Eivor
en: For a long time you lived in fear. Your houses razed, your fields scorched. Now your chance has come. Fight to be free of this pain. Fight to be free of fear.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Men
en: Freedom!

speaker: Eivor
en: This land you call home is on the verge of ruin. Burned and pillaged by Rued's clan, it bears the scars of an age of endless war. But today we will reclaim her. Today we fight for your land. And tomorrow, we rebuild.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 6
en: For East Anglia.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 7
en: For East Anglia.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now is the time. Today, we rid East Anglia of Rued's clan, once and for all.

speaker: Finnr
en: You remember the dream I spoke of?

speaker: Eivor
en: You sailed through Helheim on a ship of fire.

speaker: Finnr
en: Here, it may come to pass.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dreams. Life. It may be they are one and the same.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tonight I ride the flaming sea-steed, rushing for the spear-din. A alight on water's wake, another glory I will keep.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ready yourselves! Rued's shit-stains will see us coming!

speaker: Finnr
en: We've been spotted.

speaker: Eivor
en: Steady! Hold course!

speaker: Finnr
en: Ready yourself to brace, men! We bring Helheim to our enemies!

speaker: Finnr
en: How nice, they greet us with some of their own from the air! Arrows!

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Brace!

speaker: Finnr
en: Odin's hand! May his sword-maidens take them swiftly.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Close one, that was!

speaker: Finnr
en: Keep your shield arms limber! Harden yourselves, men!

speaker: Eivor
en: Steady your hands! Hold for impact! Hold!

speaker: Eivor
en: Now!

speaker: Eivor
en: Forward! Get that ram in place! We need to open these gates!

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: Charge!

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: For Oswald!

speaker: Finnr
en: Put that glorious ram to use! Rued's dogs are all bark! Prepare to cut them down!

speaker: Brothir
en: This is for Oswald!

speaker: Broder
en: Come and die on my blade!

speaker: Eivor
en: The ram could push through.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could break the gate from behind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now to the final gate! Get the ram to the gate and push! And keep pushing! East Anglia depends on it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Our battle plan has legs! Keep the pressure!

speaker: Eivor
en: The fyrd has broken through. These merchants and farmers can fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need help with this gate!

speaker: Eivor
en: Valdis, well met!

speaker: Valdis
en: Onward everyone! Onward!

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald... He lives.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald lives!

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor! Is that you?

speaker: Rued
en: Shut your arse, twig-spine!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand fast! This will be over soon.

speaker: Oswald
en: Worry not for me! You must stop

speaker: Rued
en: Silence, fool!

speaker: Rued
en: So this is what it comes to, Wolf-Kissed? Two Danes fighting over a filthy Saxon whoreson? If this swine is your prize, come and get him!

speaker: Oswald
en: The people of East Anglia have spoken, Rued. Give yourself over.

speaker: Rued
en: Taken prisoner to a Saxon? To you? Never. You think yourself above the Danes?

speaker: Oswald
en: I think no such thing. Only God is above us, of both Saxon and Dane alike.

speaker: Rued
en: You and your slaver god. Pathetic! You'd dare try and bed my Valdis!

speaker: Oswald
en: She's not yours to do with as you please.

speaker: Rued
en: Of course she is. Just as East Anglia is!

speaker: Rued
en: You dare call yourself drengr (a courageous warrior)! Face me, battle-swine! I'll take your head for a trophy!

speaker: Rued
en: The Saxon-lover comes to fight!

speaker: Eivor
en: A miserable clan you lead, Rued.

speaker: Rued
en: Yes, and one that has bled this country dry for two summers!

speaker: Oswald
en: You are finished here, Rued!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your battle is not yet won, Oswald.

speaker: Eivor
en: Flee Rued, while pity restrains my blade.

speaker: Rued
en: Not 'til I have taken all these shores have to offer.

speaker: Eivor
en: East Anglia will have its king, and it will not be you!

speaker: Rued
en: That groveling worm in a cage? You must be blind to stand with such a man. Danes fighting for a Saxon King! The sagas will scorn this day!

speaker: Eivor
en: For all your efforts, only the cold dark of Niflheim awaits you.

speaker: Rued
en: Valhalla is my destiny. But that fate will not be met today. This land is rife with weakness, and you are just another blighted blot upon it. Nothing a little fire cannot purge!

speaker: Rued
en: They should be ruled, Wolf-Kissed! Made thralls, (slaves), not treated as equals. We are better than this! Than all of them!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not drag me down to the sewage you wallow in.

speaker: Rued
en: I will enjoy this! Why does a Dane fight tooth and nail for a Saxon? This Saxon of all?

speaker: Eivor
en: He has in abundance that which you do not. He is fit to rule, fit to lead. You are naught but a murderous plunderer.

speaker: Oswald
en: Thank you.

speaker: Rued
en: You'd throw in with these wastrels, these ' (cowardly) swine? For what, a scrap of land and a promise of peace?

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor! No! He should be tried before God. A lawful assembly.

speaker: Oswald
en: I won't have my reign begin with more blood spilt than is needed.

speaker: Odin
en: Another screeching scold.

speaker: Odin
en: This man must die for the damage he has wrought. The old laws are clear.

speaker: Eivor
en: These are Oswald's lands, to rule as king, as he sees fit.

speaker: Odin
en: Does Eivor bow to kings?

speaker: Eivor
en: To defy a king would shame him. East Anglia cannot heal without his honor intact.

speaker: Odin
en: And what of your honor, Eivor? How much are you willing to lose?

speaker: Eivor
en: He deserves death, Oswald. That's our way.

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor, please...

speaker: Oswald
en: Blood for blood leaves no warmth in the hearts of men, Eivor. None at all.

speaker: Eivor
en: The rightful King of East Anglia has spared your life today. And so it will be.

speaker: Oswald
en: Compassion is a virtue suited for anyone, Eivor. Including you. Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should speak with Oswald... see if he is well.

speaker: Norse Soldier 8
en: Rued's finished.

speaker: Norse Soldier 9
en: To the ships.

speaker: Norse Soldier 10
en: Praise the All-Father. Oswald lives!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 8
en: You fight well, heathen.

speaker: Norse Soldier 11
en: Not bad yourself, Saxon.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 9
en: We did it! I can't believe we did it!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 10
en: And Oswald yet lives! God is truly merciful!

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor...

speaker: Eivor
en: Saxon and Dane. We fought well, side by side.

speaker: Oswald
en: If there is to be a future for both our kind, people like you and me will have to change the most to live with it. Even if that makes us... uneasy.

speaker: Eivor
en: When you are crowned king, the laws of this land will be yours to decide.

speaker: Oswald
en: Thank you for heeding me, Eivor. I know the worth of such a gesture.

speaker: Oswald
en: All this is...is like a dream.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you are not asleep.

speaker: Finnr
en: Well fought, well fought! The both of you!

speaker: Oswald
en: You came as well, old friend?

speaker: Finnr
en: If I had known you were still alive, I would have stayed in Northwic.

speaker: Eivor
en: Look around you. A happy occasion. And a glorious victory.

speaker: Oswald
en: And soon, something more grand to take place. Our wedding, my love...if you will still have me, that is.

speaker: Valdis
en: And why would I not?

speaker: Oswald
en: I fought poorly. I melted under the heat and anger of that brute. And I never

speaker: Valdis
en: Oswald, stop. You fought. With all your heart and soul. That is all you need ever do.

speaker: Oswald
en: Come, then. We have much to prepare for.

speaker: Finnr
en: A bride to wed and a kingdom to lead. What some men wouldn't give for such things.

speaker: Eivor
en: Countless men have died for them. And you, Finnr? Are you jealous of such things?

speaker: Finnr
en: Hardly. My heart is afire, but my body aches. I desire only...a long nap.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw a bale of hay back there.

speaker: Finnr
en: Later, Eivor. For now, I must see to the wounded.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I will see you at the wedding.

speaker: Finnr
en: Aye, of course, you will.

speaker: Finnr
en: Victory was hard won, but we did it. Rued's clan is blown to ash.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should return to Elmenham. Oswald's wedding will soon begin.

speaker: Everold
en: Eivor? Child of Varin? Eivor Wolf-Kissed? Is that you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Do I know you?

speaker: Everold
en: You were too young to remember me but I stayed with your household many years ago.

speaker: Everold
en: This is for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Mead Horn of Suttungr! How is this possible? Can you conjure things from dreams?

speaker: Everold
en: It's only a model. I fashioned it from a story, told to me by your father. But since he's dead, I offer it to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is exactly like I saw it... in my head... as Varin described it to me. Have you made other things from stories?

speaker: Everold
en: Only if the storyteller is very good. Your father was. He would have made a good skald.

speaker: Eivor
en: Could you do it from dreams or visions? Bring something into this world from another?

speaker: Everold
en: Not all dreamers speak, and fewer yet speak clearly. Seers talk too much and cloud your vision with

speaker: Valka
en: What's this about bringing things into this world from another?

speaker: Everold
en: Hmmm. More like imagining it into our world. When I have the image, its design speaks to me in a language I do not know and yet understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is Suttungr's mead horn, Valka. From Jotunheim. As Varin described it to him.

speaker: Valka
en: I do not like the business of trafficking in visions, but if it revives good memories of your father, there may be value in it.

speaker: Valka
en: I will bring you a potion that will let Eivor dream and speak clearly. If you take advantage, your death will be painful.

speaker: Everold
en: Nah, you need not go to so much trouble. You could give me the recipe

speaker: Valka
en: I will bring you a potion.

speaker: Valka
en: Do not dig too deeply. We do not know the true cost of this.

speaker: Eivor
en: There'll will be no cost to the gods. You heard him. He does not take things from their realms. He imagines them, then crafts them.

speaker: Valka
en: Not the cost to the gods. To you.

speaker: Everold
en: I will get the workshop ready. Come by when you want to get started.

speaker: Everold
en: You'll be safe in my care. Valka has promised that any harm you suffer will be visited upon me tenfold.

speaker: Eivor
en: She is protective of her people.

speaker: Eivor
en: But I must exact a promise from you. You must not speak of this to anyone... whatever happens...

speaker: Everold
en: I swear upon my life, I will not speak of this to any but you.

speaker: Havi
en: Munnin!

speaker: Havi
en: When you're near, dear raven, my memory's sharp, my aim unmuddled. Down there, in Niflheim, things are... less clear...

speaker: Havi
en: You know I cannot take you. I can barely get myself through the Warding Wall, and only then by abandoning my trusted weapons.

speaker: Havi
en: Do not sulk. I will not risk you, for who then would remind me of my purpose?

speaker: Havi
en: Yes. Baldr. My son. The Light of the World, locked away in Hel's dark castle.

speaker: Havi
en: He was taken too soon. Stolen from us! I shall not rest till I have denied destiny and brought Baldr back from the dead.

speaker: Havi
en: You're right, Munnin. If it is to be done, best it were done quickly. It is time to go to Hel.

speaker: Havi
en: You think you can keep me out? I pulled your realm out of Ymir's ass! I will send it hurtling back to the Void if I have to!

speaker: Thor
en: I do not think they can hear you, old man.

speaker: Havi
en: Have you come to lend us aind, my son?

speaker: Thor
en: I have news from home. War rattles the gates of Asgard while you dally in this dream of rescuing Baldr.

speaker: Havi
en: My whole life I have defied expectations by doing the unthinkable. How could I do any less when your brother's life is at stake?

speaker: Thor
en: My step-brother is dead! There is no life at stake! You are full of advice to all who will listen but deaf to anyone else.

speaker: Havi
en: Can you name anyone with more wisdom than I? Who has fought and fallen and sacrificed more than I have?

speaker: Thor
en: No.

speaker: Havi
en: Then I hope you will understand, Son, why I do not take counsel easily.

speaker: Thor
en: So, you are going back. Back to Niflheim.

speaker: Havi
en: As many times as it takes.

speaker: Havi
en: Have we met before? There's something familiar about you.

speaker: Nar
en: Ah. You may have met one of my brothers.

speaker: Havi
en: Do they live around here?

speaker: Nar
en: Haha! In a way, in a way. They're dead. Doomed to Niflheim for... well, let's just say they got into some nasty business.

speaker: Havi
en: And now you come here to pay homage to them?

speaker: Nar
en: Ha! I pay them nothing! I come to earn! You see, I have a bond with my brothers, like you with your ravens, but deeper. When I stand at the edge of Niflheim, I can see what they see. Hear what they hear, smell what they

speaker: Havi
en: I understand. But how can this profit you? Or benefit me?

speaker: Nar
en: I have learned some secrets of the dead. Charms and spells that I offer to you as... Favors. Are you interested? Can I tempt you with a favor?

speaker: Havi
en: That depends. What are you offering?

speaker: Havi
en: TBA

speaker: Havi
en: Each time you cast me out will only make me stronger!

speaker: Havi
en: You sharpen my will like a dwarf-forged blade! I will slice you from tail to ti–

speaker: Thor
en: Enough! I've heard this too many times! I cannot bear it any longer!

speaker: Havi
en: The problem with children is their utter lack of patience.

speaker: Thor
en: How can you say that? And who needs patience? When did patience ever win a war?

speaker: Havi
en: Almost every single time! When preparing for battle–

speaker: Thor
en: No... No, no more of your... words of... wisdom, just... Please, Father... release me from my oath!

speaker: Havi
en: Oath? What oath?

speaker: Thor
en: If I tell you, I will... break it.

speaker: Havi
en: So break it, if your need is so great. If you swore to be my wet-nurse, to coddle me, then I free you from your bond.

speaker: Thor
en: I swore upon the head of Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent, and the... glorious death it will know at my hands.

speaker: Havi
en: Then tell me true. Will your words cause me to doubt my deeds? Sow suspicion in my thoughts?

speaker: Thor
en: I cannot say.

speaker: Havi
en: In that case, I am sorry, Son. I have no wish to burden you with my grief, but you are here, and Baldr is not.

speaker: Thor
en: Aye.

speaker: Havi
en: You do well to hide behind your monsters, daughter of Loki! If you were here, I would tear you–

speaker: Freyja
en: No need to grab your weapon, Husband. It is not that kind of visit. We need to talk about Baldr.

speaker: Havi
en: How honorable! Seems your oath does not stop you from complaining to your mother.

speaker: Havi
en: So, this troll-tosser told you about Baldr, did he? Or have you been spying on me through your mirrors and pools?

speaker: Freyja
en: I need neither Thor nor magic. You are on the edge of Niflheim and look like shit. Of course this is about Baldr. Jötunn are talking with Muspels. Týr thinks they will move on Asgard together.

speaker: Havi
en: Týr will know what to do, he was War Lord once.

speaker: Freyja
en: He will take that title again if you are not careful.

speaker: Havi
en: What care I for titles? Or Jötunn or Muspels? I saw Baldr's body! His light snuffed out! How can I see that same light seated on Hel's dark throne and not take action?

speaker: Freyja
en: You saw him on Hel's throne? I did not know you had reached her castle.

speaker: Havi
en: No... I–I did not think I had... I could not remember...

speaker: Havi
en: Perhaps it was a vision!

speaker: Freyja
en: You are many things, Lord of Lords, but a seer you are not.

speaker: Thor
en: His wits are curdled! We should take him home!

speaker: Freyja
en: I sense a mystery not easily untangled. Asgard will not fall today. I'll stay and learn more before passing judgement.

speaker: Havi
en: Thank you... for believing in me.

speaker: Freyja
en: I shall believe what I see. Thank the Fates for gifting me patience.

speaker: Thor
en: She seeks a vision to help with your quest.

speaker: Freyja
en: I see a foul creature, half living, half dead... who feeds on the dead... or roots in their stead...

speaker: Thor
en: Could that be Hel?

speaker: Freyja
en: I see a great throne in a room dark as night.. a king or a queen, their heart filled with light...

speaker: Thor
en: That is like the vision you had! Baldr on a throne!

speaker: Havi
en: Be quiet!

speaker: Freyja
en: A sacrifice made, the price to be paid... one prince will be found, another one bound...

speaker: Freyja
en: Ah... did you learn anything useful?

speaker: Havi
en: You confirmed what I expected. I will need to face Hel to find Baldr.

speaker: Thor
en: And the part about the sacrifice. Do not forget that.

speaker: Freyja
en: A sacrifice?

speaker: Havi
en: What do you expect? I am the King of Sacrifices.

speaker: Freyja
en: And I am too tired to give argument. Do what you must do, but make sure you strike a good bargain.

speaker: Freyja
en: What happened down there?

speaker: Havi
en: I penetrated deep within Hel's defenses but her forces pushed me back. Why do you ask? Did you sense something?

speaker: Freyja
en: There was a... a push. From Niflheim. I do not know how else to describe it.

speaker: Havi
en: You felt this in your body?

speaker: Freyja
en: No... more like I... I felt it in my '. A forceful presence, but far away. Like a great wind blowing from a distant land.

speaker: Hel
en: Ahh!

speaker: Hel
en: No need for timidity, I cannot do much harm. Yet.

speaker: Thor
en: Then why bother at all, witch? This feeble display is laughable.

speaker: Hel
en: Testing the waters. I too have found a crack in the Wall, a crack that could telease the flood...

speaker: Havi
en: You will only put yourself in more peril by dragging out our dispute. Release Baldr and we can end this here.

speaker: Hel
en: End it? But there is so much more to learn about you... and your lands... all the soft places...

speaker: Freyja
en: Begone!

speaker: Freyja
en: Once I identified the right root, it was a simple thing to push back.

speaker: Freyja
en: But she was right. She will continue prodding that barrier until Hel breaks loose.

speaker: Havi
en: I gambled with the fate of the Nine Worlds and may lose them to the forces of chaos.

speaker: Freyja
en: Perhaps, and maybe Hel will be the harbinger of that doom, but I sensed something... unintended. She was afraid.

speaker: Havi
en: Afraid? Of who? Of me?

speaker: Freyja
en: Do not act coy. Of course she fears you. Or what you might discover.

speaker: Thor
en: So, what are you saying? I should continue on this course? Even if it weakens the Wall?

speaker: Thor
en: If anything gets out of that wicked realm, I will send it back. I need some exercise after all this waiting.

speaker: Havi
en: Well then, I should go get your step-brother.

speaker: Freyja
en: My love...!

speaker: Freyja
en: Can you speak?

speaker: Havi
en: Hel has grown strong since we last met... I simply need a moment... to catch my breath...

speaker: Thor
en: You reached her? You fought? Was it glorious?

speaker: Havi
en: It was... a challenge. But now that I've taken the measure of Hel, and her hound, I will cut her to the quick.

speaker: Thor
en: Hound?

speaker: Freyja
en: No, my husband, you must not return. I fear Niflheim has infected us with a madness that will only worsen the longer we remain.

speaker: Havi
en: Freyja, I cannot stop now. Not when I have gone this far.

speaker: Freyja
en: And what has it gotten you? You have been to Hel and back and yet you are still no closer to Baldr.

speaker: Havi
en: But I know he's there... I have seen him!

speaker: Freyja
en: The vision you spoke of?

speaker: Havi
en: It was no vision! It's... It is a... It is a memory! I cn recall it more clearly now...

speaker: Havi
en: I saw him, as clear as I see you, seated on a throne...

speaker: Havi
en: When I reach for more detail, the image grows cloudy... as though covered by layers of some concealing veil.

speaker: Freyja
en: Could this be some illusion? An effect of Hel's magic?

speaker: Havi
en: No. If anything, it is a fragment of a deeper truth. A truth someone is trying to hide from us. I lost Baldr once, and may be a fool trying to undo destiny. But someone seeks to rob me of his memory, and that I cannot allow.

speaker: Freyja
en: I will not question your resolve, but I need to step back. I am too exposed to the perverse energy bleeding from that realm.

speaker: Havi
en: I will not think you weaker for it. Return to Asgard and let Týr know he has my gratitude but that you hold my trust.

speaker: Freyja
en: Good luck to you, Husband. I hope your efforts bring you some measure of peace.

speaker: Thor
en: Enjoy the fight, Father.

speaker: Thor
en: What was it like among the shameful dead? How is it with the worst that the worlds can offer?

speaker: Havi
en: Not all down there are deserving of their destinies. Some simply suffer from ill luck, or a cruel twist of fate.

speaker: Thor
en: You have that look you get when you've been fighting wolves. Did you meet a match for Loki's son?

speaker: Havi
en: Hel has bred some dreadful creatures, but none can compare with the wolf, Fenrir.

speaker: Freyja
en: A Helish fog clouds my vision...

speaker: Havi
en: You remember Hjalmgunnar? The King of the ? He has become a misshapen monster, twisted by hate.

speaker: Thor
en: You were too hard on Brunhild over that one. Hjalmgunnar was a rotten bacraut (idiot) while he lived. He deserves a dark fate.

speaker: Thor
en: You stink of dragon turds. Have you met Nidhogg? He must be old and toothless by now.

speaker: Havi
en: He sustains himself with the sap from Yggdrasil's roots, but cannot fully stave off the rot as Chaos reaches to reclaim him.

speaker: Freyja
en: Some say corruption springs forth from Nidhogg. In truth, it is his weakening of the World Tree that lets the rot seep in.

speaker: Thor
en: Why does your hate for Hel burn so bright?

speaker: Havi
en: I do not hate her, I simply want Baldr. But I feel I have created a monster that could unleash an apocalypse.

speaker: Freyja
en: The very best and worst of the dead find their way to Hel's castle. Be wary of both.

speaker: Thor
en: You have been to Hel and back. Did Garmr fight at her side? Is he truly the best of hounds?

speaker: Havi
en: They share a bond stronger than Munnin and I. Garmr is formidable because Hel lent him life and earned his undying loyalty.

speaker: Freyja
en: Do you regret how you treated Hel? Trying to trap her in Niflheim?

speaker: Havi
en: Aye. Hel, Fenrir, Jörmungandr... Loki's entire line is like a string of curses.

speaker: Havi
en: Niflheim's riches are doubly defended. I must kill the guards before disarming the shield.

speaker: Havi
en: The shield surrounding this prize must have been tied to its defender's life... or death.

speaker: Havi
en: No going back now.

speaker: Havi
en: That skulking figure has the demeanor of a thief. Who better to lead me to things of value?

speaker: Havi
en: I must move carefully.

speaker: Havi
en: My patience has been rewarded.

speaker: Havi
en: Luck was not on my side.

speaker: Havi
en: The air appears to shimmer here. Much in the way it does when the jötunn weave their illusions.

speaker: Havi
en: I shall make better use of this than Hel's officer would.

speaker: Havi
en: Elk shrines are known to be places of healing.

speaker: Havi
en: That looks like a warrior of rank. Perhaps he carries some prize on his person.

speaker: Havi
en: Hospitality without a host. Are these drinks for the dead, or might anyone partake? That note may shed some light.

speaker: Havi
en: Which one shall I choose?

speaker: Havi
en: By my loins! I feel refreshed!

speaker: Havi
en: That is an excellent drink.

speaker: Havi
en: Búri's bile! It burns my throat!

speaker: Havi
en: I'll not take a drink at this time, lest it muddle my purpose.

speaker: Havi
en: Only one drink per visit. Generosity has its limits.

speaker: Havi
en: I'm discovered, and the roots would rake my reward!

speaker: Havi
en: One must be quick in the land of the dead.

speaker: King of Thieves
en: The King of Thieves welcomes all who wish to bargain fairly and freely.

speaker: Havi
en: Can I expect fair treatment from one holding so dubious a title?

speaker: King of Thieves
en: I was once a common thief, fighting over scraps, picking corpses clean of all that could be bartered or sold. But now, as their sovereign, the rogues of Niflheim trust me with their traffic, and you may do the same.

speaker: Havi
en: I may offer trade, but my trust is not easily earned.

speaker: King of Thieves
en: Fine by me. I'm not looking to make friends, only deals. Are you interested?

speaker: Havi
en: Show me your stock.

speaker: Olver the Unsettled
en: Why go to some other shop when my shop will come to you?

speaker: Havi
en: You carry your whole shop with you? That is quite a feat.

speaker: Olver the Unsettled
en: Anything can be negotiated if you have the means, even this difficult land. Would you like to see what I have?

speaker: Havi
en: Let us get down to business then.

speaker: Havi
en: I have a memory of an elk shrine here... or does some Helish magic muddle my wits?

speaker: King of Thieves
en: Ah, the wary bargainer returns.

speaker: Havi
en: Show me your stock.

speaker: Olver the Unsettled
en: Looking for a deal?

speaker: Havi
en: Let us get down to business then.

speaker: Hel
en: Leave, lest I make a monument of your bones.

speaker: Havi
en: I granted you this realm, child, but I will unmake it if you deny me Baldr.

speaker: Hel
en: You gave me a barren world filled with the dishonored and other undesirables. I gave them purpose.

speaker: Havi
en: What purpose? An afterlife of constant death?

speaker: Hel
en: No, a new kind of life, one free from the fear of death. All who serve me shall have their rebirth.

speaker: Havi
en: I have lost all appetite for boar.

speaker: Hel
en: I cannot train my pets if you are too weak to play.

speaker: Hel
en: Why have you returned, Old One?

speaker: Havi
en: Why do you not face me, Queen of the Shamed? Or better yet, give me back my son and I shall leave you in peace.

speaker: Hel
en: I can shape dead flesh into new life, summon an army with a whisper. What makes you think you still have power over me?

speaker: Havi
en: Then why would you not show your true self? What is it you fear?

speaker: Hel
en: My fear is beyond your imagining. Your fear, however, is well known among the dead.

speaker: Havi
en: Far from my first wolf, and it will not be my last.

speaker: Hel
en: You are good with animals.

speaker: Havi
en: I am skilled at killing all manner of things.

speaker: Hel
en: Leave, lest I make a monument of your bones.

speaker: Havi
en: Like your dead, I will keep coming back, Learning, growing stronger until I take back what is mine.

speaker: Hel
en: You know nothing of my dead. Not all I do is driven by war. But quite a lot is.

speaker: Hel
en: I cannot train my pets if you are too weak to play.

speaker: Hel
en: Why have you returned, Old One?

speaker: Havi
en: You think me afraid of your creations? I have had nightmares more terrifying.

speaker: Hel
en: What an interesting thought. If one can harvest memories, could one not plant a dream?

speaker: Hel
en: You are good with animals.

speaker: Havi
en: I am skilled at killing all manner of things.

speaker: Hel
en: Leave, lest I make a monument of your bones.

speaker: Havi
en: I am bound to see this through.

speaker: Hel
en: I cannot train my pets if you are too weak to play.

speaker: Hel
en: Why have you returned, Old One?

speaker: Havi
en: Ah, I cannot resist a good fight.

speaker: Hel
en: You are good with animals.

speaker: Havi
en: I am skilled at killing all manner of things.

speaker: Havi
en: Better hury. This place grows hotter.

speaker: Havi
en: The air appears to shimmer here. Much in the way it does when the jötunn weave their illusions.

speaker: Havi
en: Impressive attire! I shall add it to my wardrobe.

speaker: Havi
en: Only one of us leaves in one piece!

speaker: Havi
en: The last of that lot...

speaker: Havi
en: More drinks on offer. Will the result be any different?

speaker: Havi
en: Which one shall I choose?

speaker: Havi
en: By my loins! I feel refreshed!

speaker: Havi
en: That is an excellent drink.

speaker: Havi
en: Búri's bile! It burns my throat!

speaker: Havi
en: I'll not take a drink at this time, lest it muddle my purpose.

speaker: Olver the Unsettled
en: Looking for a deal?

speaker: Havi
en: Let us get down to business then.

speaker: Havi
en: Another thief... another opportunity.

speaker: Havi
en: My patience has been rewarded.

speaker: Havi
en: Luck was not on my side.

speaker: Havi
en: Are you...?

speaker: Dar
en: No, no. I'm sure you're thinking of someone else. Perhaps one of my cousins.

speaker: Havi
en: Right. And I take it you are also involved in the family business?

speaker: Dar
en: Ah! If you want a fair deal, look no further!

speaker: Havi
en: Let us get down to business.

speaker: Dar
en: I am always open for a friend of the family!

speaker: Havi
en: Let us get down to business then.

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: All-Father!

speaker: Havi
en: Be thou one of Hel's experiments gone awry? What shameful crime could have earned so twisted a fate?

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: It's not the Nornir, but you and that bitch Brunhild who made me thus!

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: Have you betrayed so many Goths, Oath-Breaker, that you no longer recognize their king?

speaker: Havi
en: Hjalmgunnar? Why has Hel raised you as this grotesque monstruosity?

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: I rebuilt myself from abandoned appendages and discarded flesh. A labor of loathing, fuelled by vengeance and driven by hate.

speaker: Havi
en: I would feel worse about Hjalmgunnar if he was not such a bacraut (asshole).

speaker: Hel
en: Hjalmgunnar has got his revenge.

speaker: Dwarf Rebel 1
en: Look everyone! The Giant Slayer has returned! Hjalmgunnar's bane is back!

speaker: Havi
en: News travel swiftly down here.

speaker: Dwarf Rebel 1
en: Not just any news! We have been waiting for a sign like this. Proof the giant can be beaten.

speaker: Havi
en: I'm glad to have given you hope. Now you must seize your destiny with both hands.

speaker: Dwarf Rebel 1
en: Oh, we will! Thanks to your example, we will never be enslaved again!

speaker: Dwarf Rebel 2
en: What I wouldn't give for a real mug of mead right now...

speaker: Dwarf Rebel 3
en: Hjalmgunnar must die the true death!

speaker: Dwarf Rebel 4
en: TBA

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: All-Father!

speaker: Havi
en: Your fate shames me, Hjalmgunnar. I would have given you the victory I promised had the Nornir not tied my hands.

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: I don't give a rat's turd about your shame. I lost my life and my kingdom, and I won't rest till I've destroyed yours.

speaker: Hel
en: TBA

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: All-Father!

speaker: Havi
en: Whatever wrong was done you, giant, your actions have cancelled my debt.

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: Honor won't be restored until I have ground you underfoot.

speaker: Hel
en: Hjalmgunnar has got his revenge.

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: All-Father!

speaker: Hjalmgunnar
en: I'll tear you apart!

speaker: Hel
en: TBA

speaker: Havi
en: One would boil, bathing in that.

speaker: Havi
en: Thrym's house once stood here, before ruin came upon it.

speaker: Havi
en: Cold enough to freeze the breath in your body.

speaker: Havi
en: Loki often tells the tale of how Thrym stole Thor's hammer. It seems his account of Thor's rage was no exaggeration.

speaker: Havi
en: Ah! Thor's bridal circlet. This would be a gift worthy of Gunlodr's attention.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now to find Nolwenn, the smuggler Toka told us about. If there is a weakness to the island, she'll know it.

speaker: French Man 1
en: Not even Odo's warriors patrol these ruins. We are left to rot in squalor.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: On the bright side, there's nothing left for the Northmen to steal.

speaker: French Man 1
en: Everyone, come bask in my wife's comforting words of wisdom. Her cheerful quips will warm us this winter. Her playful words will feed us! Her sharp tongue will defend us!

speaker: French Woman 1
en: You're awfully sarcastic for a ditch-digger, Henri.

speaker: French Man 2
en: That smuggler owes me wine! Guard my warehouse, she says. And I'll give you a jug of wine. I have been guarding that pile of rocks for three hours already. Bring me my wine! Curse you, Nolwenn! You left-handed child of a Breton thief!

speaker: Eivor
en: Pardon, friend. Did I hear you speak of a smuggler named Nolwenn?

speaker: French Man 2
en: I did. That damned thief promised a jug of wine to guard her warehouse.

speaker: Eivor
en: O? And where is her warehouse?

speaker: French Man 2
en: It's, uh... over to the east somewhere. Got a plague cross painted on it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, my friend. Perhaps you should sleep it off before going back on guard duty.

speaker: French Man 2
en: All right, good idea.

speaker: Eivor
en: Food, herbs, healing wraps. I wonder who these are meant for.

speaker: Eivor
en: Arrowheads. Whetstones. Smuggled goods, meant for the Île de la Cité.

speaker: Eivor
en: It seems the Queen knows the smuggler. Maybe Richardis can help me find Nolwenn.

speaker: French Man 3
en: Behold, a wonder in heaven! A red dragon with seven heads, ten horns, and seven crowns upon his seven heads! Are these not the seven heads, the seven sons of Ragnar Lothbrok, and all that heathen horde? It is written that the dragon's tail shall tear one third of the stars from heaven and cast them upon the earth. Have not the heathen armies ravaged a third of Francia and slain that many of her people? There shall be a war in heaven, and Michael and his angels shall fight against the dragon! The angels shall prevail and cast down that old serpent, the Devil, Satan, which deceiveth the whole world.

speaker: Richardis
en: Let us pray in the words of Our Savior. "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you." "Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

speaker: French Man 4
en: A heathen monster, bearing weapons on our holy ground!

speaker: Richardis
en: A trusted friend. Good people, do not break the peace of our church.

speaker: French Man 4
en: Who can trust a pagan diable? How many have you killed, fiend?

speaker: Richardis
en: Friends, remember. "When the saw the beaten man, he had compassion and bound his wounds.

speaker: Eivor
en: You keep busy, Queen.

speaker: Richardis
en: Someone must tend to those who fall in battle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Plague did this, not war.

speaker: Richardis
en: War breeds plague, Eivor. I am not yet ready to return to Charles, if that is what brings you here.

speaker: Eivor
en: No. I seek a Breton who resides in this ward, name of Nolwenn.

speaker: Bernard
en: I know her! A freelance thief.

speaker: Richardis
en: A disreputable woman, although not without... talents. To those who can pay.

speaker: Eivor
en: They say she can smuggle goods and messages over walls and past guards.

speaker: Richardis
en: Yes... So why do you seek this woman's help?

speaker: Eivor
en: Better we take this city before it starves. We will not harm the commoners if I can help it.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is a friendship between us, but I cannot share everything. Yet I promise, our goals are the same.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have urged a truce on all sides, without success. But I can still try.

speaker: Richardis
en: But Sigfred the Frank-killer leads this army, not you. He inflict vengeance upon us, town by town.

speaker: Eivor
en: Because the Franks killed his brother.

speaker: Richardis
en: How many Northmen must die so Sigfred can avenge one man? Should his niece die too? Should you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot stop entire armies. Only urge reason and a truce on all sides. I do what I can.

speaker: Richardis
en: You did save my life. I must take that first step and trust you, my Good Samaritan.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, queen. I am in your debt. I mean that. So, where is this Breton?

speaker: Richardis
en: Alas, I do not know. She visits from time to time.

speaker: Bernard
en: I know! I know the way to Nolwenn's hideout! Please, let me show Eivor!

speaker: Richardis
en: From the mouths of babes! Very well, but hurry back, Little Bear.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not so fast, little prince. This place is not safe.

speaker: Bernard
en: Nowhere in Francia is safe now! Mother Richardis says so.

speaker: Eivor
en: How is it you know where this smuggler works?

speaker: Bernard
en: Yesterday, I went on an adventure and followed her! But she saw me and waved. I felt silly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, I have been down this way before. Thank you Bernard, get back to the queen.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like the place. Thank you Bernard, best you return to the queen.

speaker: Bernard
en: Bye, Eivor. Have fun and let's have another adventure soon.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Back off, you rat bastards!

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Why so sour, my sweet?

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Farewell, vermin. And you, my friend, just who are you?

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Bonjour my brave friend, but I do not have any silver.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not here to take your silver. I have no quarrel with you.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Praise the saints! And I thank you for your fine and timely blade, but I must go.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, you see, I'm a friend of Richardis, Queen of Francia.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: And I am married to the pope. Long may he reign.

speaker: Eivor
en: They say you walk through city walls. I need your help.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: I am no ghost, just a simple bard from Brittany that has lost her way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Look, you are a smuggler, all Paris knows it, even the Boy-Prince does. I need your help.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: And if I know a thing or two about all that, what is it worth to you?

speaker: Eivor
en: You saw how well I fight. Would you like to see it again?

speaker: Nolwenn
en: No, friend. You helped me, it's only right I repay the favor. Such is my free and generous nature.

speaker: Eivor
en: At last. We understand each other.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this enough silver to loosen your tongue?

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Ah, sweet silver, the bane of Judas. It will do.

speaker: Eivor
en: Silver makes fools of even the wise, and the rich make greater fools than the poor.

speaker: Eivor
en: My friend Toka wants her necklace back. This I know.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: There is her chain, friend. Tell her to find me in Nantes when this is all over.

speaker: Eivor
en: Toka shall hear your words.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: All is well. So, what do you need, Northerner?

speaker: Eivor
en: I seek a weakness in these walls. Is there a hidden tunnel, a secret door, something like that?

speaker: Nolwenn
en: No, no, not so simple, the Franks sealed the city well. But take this key, it will open the bridge-door.

speaker: Eivor
en: The bridge? I can reach the bridge from outside. What I could use is a way to take it down.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: A little silver birdie told me that the bridge's foundations are in dire shape.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see. And if we can take that bridge down, the longships can encircle the city.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: You did not hear this me from me. Farewell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is this bridge? It must be near.

speaker: Eivor
en: The smuggler was right. Some jars of grease will bring this bridge crashing down. I will set the jars so we can destroy the bridge later, during the attack.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Tell me to scout the Northmen's army by myself? What do I want with their suicide mission? Let's see how well they hold their city without their precious bridge. Bastards.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Hey, you don't belong down here. Though to be honest, neither do I.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then let us pretend we're both elsewhere.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Eh, why not? We are all doomed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe if I moved something I could get across.

speaker: Eivor
en: There, the trap is set for the siege of the island. Better return to the others.

speaker: Eivor
en: Knud? What are you doing in here?

speaker: Knud
en: Eivor! We need your help!

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is "we"?

speaker: Knud
en: Sylvi and Eira are in trouble! We went into the woods and... and... there's no time to explain! You need to come with me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are they alright?

speaker: Knud
en: No! They're hurt! A-and badly!

speaker: Eivor
en: Take me to them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are they?

speaker: Knud
en: Not far! We need to hurry!

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened? Are they still in danger?

speaker: Knud
en: Not if we get there soon!

speaker: Eivor
en: Which way now?

speaker: Knud
en: This way, we're almost there!

speaker: Knud
en: Come on, Eivor! Can't you run any quicker?

speaker: Eivor
en: Knud, you have to tell me what has happened.

speaker: Knud
en: I can't! You won't understand, even if I do! Just trust me!

speaker: Sylvi
en: I think he did it.

speaker: Eira
en: Shhh, she's coming!

speaker: Eira
en: You did it! You brought Eivor!

speaker: Sylvi
en: Good work, Knud!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this about?

speaker: Knud
en: Sorry, Eivor. We had to trick you. But it wasn't my idea, it was Eira's!

speaker: Eivor
en: Lying is not a good way to get my attention, children.

speaker: Eira
en: But we found a dog that needs your help! She's caught in a trap down there!

speaker: Sylvi
en: We thought you wouldn't come if you knew it was just a dog.

speaker: Eivor
en: O! That is not the sound of a dog, Eira. That is a wolf.

speaker: Knud
en: But a wolf is a kind of dog, yes? My mother told me that.

speaker: Sylvi
en: Of course it's a kind of a dog! Listen to that sound! Awoooo! Pure dog.

speaker: Eira
en: Eivor, if you won't help us free her, we must do it ourselves.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is no need. Let me see what I can do.

speaker: Eira
en: We must help her. She could be starving!

speaker: Knud
en: Poor her!

speaker: Knud
en: She's crying, we have to help!

speaker: Sylvi
en: Her family probably misses her!

speaker: Eivor
en: This house needs a key. If I am lucky, there is one nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: The children must have missed you, poor fellow. Or they might be singing a different song. It looks like something attacked you. An animal.

speaker: Eivor
en: No key here. I should look around.

speaker: Eivor
en: A bloodied boar. I think we have found our killer.

speaker: Eivor
en: A shame Wallace isn't here to butcher you. But I need to see if you are carrying a key.

speaker: Eivor
en: And there it is. Along with your last meal.

speaker: Eivor
en: A key to the front door. I must be cautious opening it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll free that wolf. And pray to Tyr that I needn't slay it in front of the children.

speaker: Eivor
en: The table is set. He never made it home. At least his end came quickly.

speaker: Eivor
en: These skulls bear teeth marks. The wolf must have helped him take them down.

speaker: Eivor
en: The man liked his trophies. At least he leaves that legacy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Easy... easy... You have a kind look to you. I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait! Easy now!

speaker: Eivor
en: Deceived by children and shouting at wolves. I was a warrior once.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you all right? Did you see the wolf?

speaker: Knud
en: Yes! You freed her! You're amazing, Eivor!

speaker: Eira
en: But she ran away! And didn't even say thank you!

speaker: Sylvi
en: She's going back to her family, maybe! Her mum and dad were probably very scared.

speaker: Eira
en: Or her wolf-husband!

speaker: Knud
en: Maybe her wife! We don't know!

speaker: Eivor
en: But we do know it is time to get you three back to the settlement. Before your parents think you were eaten by wolves.

speaker: Knud
en: O, all right...

speaker: Eivor
en: Chin up, Knud. You were very brave today. All of you.

speaker: Eivor
en: In future, you should not be exploring the woods alone. You understand?

speaker: Sylvi
en: But you go off on your own all the time!

speaker: Eivor
en: Because I am very wise. And you have a lot to learn.

speaker: Eira
en: Yes, but there are three of us. That balances everything.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is not quite how it works.

speaker: Knud
en: Ah! More wolves! And not our new friend!

speaker: Eira
en: Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand back!

speaker: Sylvi
en: Look there, that's her! Our wolf friend!

speaker: Knud
en: She's coming to save us!

speaker: Eira
en: We love you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you alright?

speaker: Eira
en: Thanks to our hero! This dog-wolf!.

speaker: Sylvi
en: Dwolfg!

speaker: Knud
en: What?

speaker: Sylvi
en: Duh-wolf-guh. It's like dog-wolf.

speaker: Knud
en: No, I don't like that at all! We should name her Mouse.

speaker: Eira
en: That makes no sense. I think we should call her... Chewy. Because she chews things.

speaker: Sylvi
en: What do you think, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Dwolfg. It has an absurd sound, just like all of this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mouse. That's a... a strange choice. But it works.

speaker: Eivor
en: Chewy, I suppose. Good as any other.

speaker: Knud
en: She's our best friend!

speaker: Eivor
en: Now we need to get home. All five of us.

speaker: Knud
en: Fine...

speaker: Eira
en: We only wanted to have an adventure like you, Eivor.

speaker: Sylvi
en: And we did! And we got a new friend!

speaker: Eivor
en: Part of adventuring is learning a good lesson, did you know that?

speaker: Sylvi
en: Yes. The boring part.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well... have you children learned anything about wild animals today?

speaker: Eira
en: Hmm... maybe!

speaker: Knud
en: Yes! Befriend them at any cost.

speaker: Sylvi
en: They are perfect companions. And very kind.

speaker: Eira
en: My mother always told me to avoid wild animals. Shows what she knows!

speaker: Eivor
en: How about we think quietly on what we have learned. Just until we get home.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think she's quite fond of you.

speaker: Knud
en: I know she is! We saved her!

speaker: Sylvi
en: She'd be rotting away by now! Just like that boar you killed, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: You saw that?

speaker: Eira
en: We see everything.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's not tell your parents, all right? Now scamper off home. And take your new friend with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must find Cynon before I am spotted. The longhouse is a good place to start. Festivities haven't started yet. There is still time to search for Cynon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are you, Cynon? He isn't here. But, someone else may have seen him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brigid is here. I shall polish my ears in hopes that a word of clarity will slip through them.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Eivor, finally you have returned.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Brigid, it is good to see you.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Eivor! What has becomme of Tewdwr? Did you find his body?)

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have found Tewdwr alive, and safe. I need to speak with Cyn−

speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar is well?

speaker: Brigid
en: (Silent about your whereabouts, but loud about missing festivities.)

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Brigid! I found an abandoned bird's nest in the rafters. I'm going to take home to Mother.

speaker: Brigid
en: (If you leave it, then the babies will come back and lay their own eggs there, Gwen.)

speaker: Gwenydd
en: It's you again. The Samhain Butcher!

speaker: Eivor
en: The Samhain Butcher? Never mind. Gwenydd. I'm looking for Cynon. Have you seen him?

speaker: Gwenydd
en: He's busy with the festival and shooed me away to Brigid. Would you like to see some magic I've been practicing?

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you show me to Cynon if I say yes?

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Just one trick and then I can show you around. Um, okay, so reach into this pouch...

speaker: Gwenydd
en: And the number of stones you're holding is... three!

speaker: Eivor
en: Wonderful magic, Gwen. But now I really need to find Cynon.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Festival time!)

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Come on, let's go find him!

speaker: Gwenydd
en: There are the church ladies. They don't like the festival, but mama says they come anyway to cluck-cluck like hens. Do you want to see another trick? I can pull an acorn from your ear!

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to find Cynon. It is important.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Your loss, Butcher.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would know more about you, Gwenydd. You're certainly an odd little bird.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Mother says there'll be no one like me in the whole of creation. From the dawn to dust to the end of sorrows.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your mother trusts you? Lets you run about on your own?

speaker: Gwenydd
en: She spends the holiday blessing hermits and old rocks. What fun is that?

speaker: Eivor
en: And your father, Gwenydd? Where is he?

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Well, it's not to be spoken of, but I was born from the union of my mother with the horned king of the forest, Cernunnos.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're close with Brigid?

speaker: Gwenydd
en: She's like a big sister. But it's not like I'm gonna get to see her much anymore once she leaves with you and Gunnar.

speaker: Eivor
en: How do you spend your days, Gwenydd?

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Collecting dead things for Mama's spells. I have quite a collection: birds, mice, erm... beetles. And I dance, and I can talk to cats.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should find Cynon.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Please go get Tewdwr fast. My wedding depends on his rescue.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Why is that woman wearing a striped mask?

speaker: Gwenydd
en: That's a badger! All the festival ladies in charge wear one.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you seen Ealdorman Cynon?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O! That unholy visage startled me. It's past sundown, so Cynon has retired to the church for prayer.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have business with him.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Even if you have business with him, it will have to wait until the morning. Locked 'imself in, only Geva has the key.

speaker: Eivor
en: Would Geva let me in?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: She's been instructed not to. Not that I can see her following a task so simple. Girl'd forget her own head if it weren't attached.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you for your help. I will speak with Cynon tomorrow.

speaker: Eivor
en: The key is held by someone named Geva. I must find her.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you seen Cynon?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Hey, it's the Mari Lwyd! Rhyme with me, Mari Lwyd.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: On Samhain night, all out to flyt, some to fight... O, I've messed up the rhyme!

speaker: Eivor
en: The man tries to write with all his might.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Ha! Didn't take much to outwit me. You're really good, good enough for a reward.

speaker: Eivor
en: Many thanks, enjoy the festival!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sorry, friend, I have other matters to attend to.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: You're no friendly spirit at all!

speaker: Eivor
en: I am looking for Glowecestre's ealdorman.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Well, the one who still draws breath is in the church.

speaker: Eivor
en: How do I get in?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: You're not supposed to get in. No reason to enter that dump anyway. Fuck, you'd have to get me very drunk to show you inside.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sounds like some ale will loosen his tongue.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: I've been praying to God and St. Kenhelm alike for poor Tewdwr's soul.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: The whole thing's been eating away at Cynon. Have you seen how gray and drawn he's been?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Should go and comfort him. All he's got to keep him company are his thoughts, and that daft girl, Geva.

speaker: Eivor
en: You harbor a personal grudge against the Church?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: I hate this town more than I hate the building, or Lord forbid, God himself. Damn kids here keep ruining my offerings in His glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: Offerings?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Windows! Do you know the work, the artistry that goes into making a sheet of glass into a martyr?

speaker: Eivor
en: The pretty glass pictures? They do break easily.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Yes, they do! Moons of painstaking works! Shattered by one foul stone sent by pagan ruffians.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am very sorry for the loss of your work. I must get going.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Wait! Wait! One last drink before you go. A toast... to Ealdorman Cynon... or a toast to Samhain. One to the Mari Lywd. One to... to... glass.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I break the glass window, I can get into the church.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you seen Cynon?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 4
en: He's gonna be in the wicker man.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cynon?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: For you, love, I could be.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where's Cynon?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: Mari Lwyd! Come dance with me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you seen Cynon?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 5
en: The Mari Lywd! O goodness, you are so frightening. What are you doing after the festival?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for Cynon.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 5
en: Right! Right. Yes. He's in the church. Actually, if you're headed that way, this crate needs to be delivered to him. Just tell Geva I sent you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course. What does Geva look like?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 5
en: Badger mask, same as me. Should come running when she sees you. Best of luck, and Happy Samhain!

speaker: Eivor
en: Geva is waiting for this delivery to the church, that's my way in.

speaker: Geva
en: Righ', gotta keep my eyes peeled for that crate delivery. O no, I shouldn't have had that tea.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you Geva? I need to entry to the church. I have important business with Cynon.

speaker: Geva
en: Hmm. I'm not supposed to let anyone in, spirit. I'm sorry, but everyone is counting on me to do a good job of keeping Cynon undisturbed.

speaker: Geva
en: Ah! The crate! Yes, yes, come this way. Good you come by, Sarah was supposed to drop it off ages ago.

speaker: Cynon
en: What was that noise? Saint Kelhelm, my boy, if you've any mercy to spare, grant it to this old sinner.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cynon is inside. I must find a way to get in.

speaker: Eivor
en: There you are, snake-tongue.

speaker: Cynon
en: Eivor! Have you... have you been enjoying the festivities?

speaker: Eivor
en: We are done with this shadow play. Tewdwr is safe, and I know of your plan to sacrifice him in your stead.

speaker: Cynon
en: You think I mean to escape the flames? I go to the wicker man gladly. But I will not leave Glowecestre in the hands of the Christian zealot.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then what? Leave your people without a leader and an angry Church ready with holy fire?

speaker: Cynon
en: They won't be without a leader. Modron will sit upon the horned throne.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you telling that Modron lied?

speaker: Cynon
en: Ha! We've turned you in circles like a dog, haven't we? Modron was the architect of Tewdwr's murder, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: All to take control of Glowecestrescire for herself? It would be a hard grasp to hold, surrounded by Christians on all sides.

speaker: Cynon
en: There was no other way. She had a vision, Tewdwr framed by flames, and burning... everything we created together.

speaker: Eivor
en: Everything...? You and Modron. Then... Gwenydd?

speaker: Cynon
en: A man must get his house in order before his death. Feather his nest for his children.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then make peace with your God, Briton. For shitting on my name and drugging me is an offense I kill for.

speaker: Cynon
en: I'm to be dead within the wicker man by Samhain's end. I beg you, let me die for my people!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your grand scheme has collapsed into sand at every step, Cynon.

speaker: Cynon
en: I know. I never should have trusted Gwilim and his merry band of fuckwits to kill one man!

speaker: Eivor
en: You and the witch, this was your plan? To make me dance your merry tune. So you could build a legacy for your daughter?

speaker: Cynon
en: I always desired Modron, so when she asked me to take the part in a fertility ritual, of course I agreed. Our union conceived not only Gwenydd, but a united Glowecestrescire. One that Tewdwr would stamp out.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is where you failed, Cynon. Tewdwr is a changed man. He straddles the same line as you.

speaker: Cynon
