en: Tewdwr? The boy has the head of a mule. You taught him reason?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not just I, the kindness of bandits and strange Britons. He embraces Christ and Cernunnos alike.

speaker: Cynon
en: Shit. Prophecy is a strange web, is it not? Tewdwr's reformation just needed a kidnapping and a dedicated Dane.

speaker: Cynon
en: Eivor. Modron would have taken Tewdwr to her forest temple. If you make haste, you might be able to stay her blade. I have much to attend to here, otherwise I'd lead you myself. Go now, unless you plan on killing me first?

speaker: Eivor
en: You should not have fucked with me, Cynon.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are already a dead man. I will not make your people suffer for your actions.

speaker: Cynon
en: Thank you, Eivor. Your mercy will be rewarded, I'm sure.

speaker: Mad Monk
en: The Grim Rider approaches!

speaker: Mad Monk
en: All falls into place. The pattern comes into focus...

speaker: Eivor
en: Does it now?

speaker: Mad Monk
en: A rune of writ large on the longhouse, the restless put to rest, and a people prepared for the hunt.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think you're less mad than you let on, monk. But I have to disappoint you. There will be no hunt.

speaker: Mad Monk
en: Will there not? Even now, powerful forces gather. We're not out of the woods yet!

speaker: Braun
en: The gods are angry! I'll never doubt you again, Uncle!

speaker: Sunniva
en: Did we do something wrong?

speaker: Alwin
en: What does it mean?

speaker: Thyra
en: The Wild Hunt.

speaker: Eivor
en: Everyone, listen! The Wild Hunt will not come for us this night!

speaker: Ake
en: How do you know that?

speaker: Eivor
en: Because I've seen the courage and skill of our people. We've come together, Norse and Saxon alike, to meet great challenges... And because I know that when people are united and strong, they earn the respect of the gods!

speaker: Sunniva
en: The gods are with us.

speaker: Meiri
en: Look, don't be embarrassed. If you've lost the key, just say so.

speaker: Batr
en: I'm not bloody embarrassed. It's like I said! The damn fish took it from me!

speaker: Meiri
en: You were robbed... by a fish! C'mon, get serious!

speaker: Batr
en: I am serious!

speaker: Meiri
en: So, what? The fish reached into your pocket and just took the key?

speaker: Batr
en: What? Don't be stupid. I... uh, gave it the key.

speaker: Meiri
en: You 'gave' our key... to a fish?!

speaker: Batr
en: An exceedingly persuasive fish, yes! You want it back, you go talk to it!

speaker: Meiri
en: Look, just... tell me again, exactly what happened.

speaker: Batr
en: So I was gonna catch the fish, right? Well... it had other ideas. Told me to drop everything I had in the water. So, um, I did.

speaker: Meiri
en: Right. Good. That clears that up, then.

speaker: Havi
en: You there. What's this of a fish-based robbery?

speaker: Meiri
en: According to my brother here, the damned fish that guards these waters has now taken to petty theft.

speaker: Havi
en: It guards these waters? Surely a terrifying creature of the deep!? All teeth and tentacles, and eyes all over its monstrous head, yes? A challenge fit for the Lord of Asgard!

speaker: Batr
en: No, no. Just a normal, y'know, fish.

speaker: Havi
en: But huge, at least... Yes?

speaker: Meiri
en: No. Not especially.

speaker: Batr
en: But it is cunning! No dwarf has caught a fish here in months, and all because of that one fish!

speaker: Havi
en: ...Indeed. And... what of the theft?

speaker: Meiri
en: It managed to charm our hard-fought key right out of my stupid brother's pocket, he reckons.

speaker: Batr
en: It was most persuasive.

speaker: Meiri
en: Listen, stranger. Catch this fish, you can keep our key and the treasure it unlocks. We just want that one fish gone. What'd you say?

speaker: Havi
en: Perhaps. Let us see what this beast is capable of.

speaker: Batr
en: Us? Oh no. I'm staying well away. You want it, you get it. I'm off.

speaker: Meiri
en: Yeah, there must be somewhere decidedly less dangerous to go fishing...

speaker: Havi
en: Come, fearsome creature of the depths! No more shall you torment those who visit these waters. Face your end at the hand of the High One!

speaker: Havi
en: Have at you!

speaker: Havi
en: This feels different! You... you are the guardian fish! Come here!

speaker: Kjoptr
en: My mouth! What are you playing at? You don't see me barging into Asgard and dragging you out of your house!

speaker: Havi
en: So, not a fish at all!

speaker: Kjoptr
en: No, and not an enemy. I was there when you came to Jotunheim, and drank enough mead to kill a man. I saw what you did to Suttungr that day, damn near beating him to a pulp single-handedly. Only a fool would challenge you. But, you have bested me fairly when no other could. And believe me, many have tried.

speaker: Kjoptr
en: You want this key, I assume.

speaker: Havi
en: That, and for you to leave these waters.

speaker: Kjoptr
en: That I will not do. I have made a home here. Dwarves repeatedly intrude. Make attempts on my life, and those of my aquatic neighbors. I won't stand for it. So I impede them, harming nothing but their pride. I daresay you would defend your lands from invaders more vigorously?

speaker: Havi
en: Aye, I would, and I see your point, as strange as this all may seem.

speaker: Kjoptr
en: Then have your prize, and I shall have mine. Life as a fish is full of wonder you'd never imagine, so I shall protect these waters for as long as I live.

speaker: Havi
en: Very well.

speaker: Havi
en: After all that, let's hope this chest was worth the bother.

speaker: Kjoptr
en: I just want to swim in peace. No concerns. No burdens. Just movement, and flow. You hear that, brothers? Sisters? Our lake is safe again! ...Hm. Conversation is the one thing I miss, mind. I shall guard this lake, and all who dwell within it. It is an honor and a privilege. Feels strange, having legs again... I found the most remote lake in Svartalfheim, and yet dwarves flock here like there is no invaders in their lands.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: Welcome, traveler, to our lush and fertile shores!

speaker: Eivor
en: I did not expect to find anyone on this island.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: And why not? This is England. Home to a nation of Saxons and Danes. Our shores are open for trade.

speaker: Eivor
en: England? It is not what I expected.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: Many from Norway find the trip dizzying, but fortunately, you have me to guide you. I know the land better than my own son.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you all right?

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: My son. Nesting with the Picts north of Hadrian's Wall. Who knows what schemes they are hatching...or the sort of people they might send to spy on me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You said something about a tour.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: Of course, of course, a tour. Follow me.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: This is the city of Lunden, first built by the Romans during ancient times. We have not seen builder like that since.

speaker: Eivor
en: I guess they had to work with what they had.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: These are the Dover Cliffs, famous for their blue birds.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hmm.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: Here is Jorvik, the Dane city of trade. Keep this between us, but King Alfred has a plan for Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: This is Hadrian's Wall. Our last line of defense against the barbarous Picts.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: It is a line of sorts.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: At the end of the tour is Wincestre, the heart of Wessex, where — Where is King Alfred? Those honorless Picts! They have taken the king! We must seek them north of Hadrian's Wall!

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: Where are you my king?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am sure he is somewhere.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: Do not worry, my king! I am coming! Do not worry, my king! I am coming!

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: My king! What happened? Why won't you speak?

speaker: Djon the Woodsman
en: Who in Hel's name are you? Why are you going through my things? Thor's balls, you found it! Why did you take it back? You set him off again.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: Traitor! The king won't speak to me! You cut off his tongue!

speaker: Djon the Woodsman
en: He has no tongue!

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: Because you cut it out!

speaker: Eivor
en: You are his son.

speaker: Djon the Woodsman
en: Do not feed this fantasy. His wits wither and become those of a babe. I took him here to ease his madness, but it grows worse. I try to use reason or playing along, but he hears what he wants to hear.

speaker: Eivor
en: "Only what he wants to hear", hm? I have an idea that could help...if you let me. Old man, your king is worn out from his ordeal. I can hear him speak, very softly. He is praising you. He wants to thank...

speaker: Djon the Woodsman
en: Hysing.

speaker: Eivor
en: He wants to thank Hysing for his loyalty to the crown.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: What else does he say?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Picts, terrified at word of your approach, will pledge themselves to the crown if you spare their lives.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: They will?

speaker: Eivor
en: And they agree to pay a daily tribute of food and other goods in exchange for free passage through your lands.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: It is a good deal and greater news. Thank you. You may leave the king in my care now.

speaker: Djon the Woodsman
en: This will only lead to further delusion.

speaker: Eivor
en: You will know at least he eats every day. And maybe, someday, the fog will lift.

speaker: Djon the Woodsman
en: Forgive my ill will. I knew this would be a difficult end, but sometimes the weight bears down heavily.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is courage and honor in what you do and the gods know it. Good luck to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like England is united.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: The Picts have been fine subjects. King Alfred is pleased.

speaker: Djon the Woodsman
en: The peace holds. For now.

speaker: Eivor
en: You walk in a dream. It is time to wake.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: What are you saying?

speaker: Eivor
en: What is real may not be pleasant as a fantasy, but you have people in this people who honor you.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: It does not matter what you tell is real. This is what I believe. I believe Alfred has sold us out to the Picts! You betrayed your nation and your people! I denounce and dethrone you!

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a harsh choice, but sometimes you must put fire to a wound to heal it.

speaker: Djon the Woodsman
en: Forgive my ill will. I knew this would be a difficult end, but sometimes the weight bears down heavily.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is courage and honor in what you do and the gods know it. Good luck to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Still at war with England?

speaker: Djon the Woodsman
en: That tough old fox is still hanging on. I admit I am impressed.

speaker: Hysing the World-Wise
en: Tell your Pictish master that you will never take England!

speaker: Eivor
en: I would not think of it!

speaker: Settlement Renown 1
en: After building the Blacksmith's forge, Eivor consulted the Settlement Status letter from Randvi in her room.

speaker: Eivor
en: Raiding is the surest way to find treasures and supplies for building up our settlement.

speaker: Rowan
en: Eivor, my stable is a bit spare just now, but if you can build me something better, I promise you the finest of beasts.

speaker: Eivor
en: A bustling stable would be a great boon here. I will see what I can do.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me about what you do here.

speaker: Rowan
en: As a stablehand and gameskeeper, I am happy to help you with any matter concerning your horses or your raven. But for the moment, I'm a little stuck. If you could build me a stable, I can set up shop.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you come to have such an affinity for horses, Rowan?

speaker: Rowan
en: They were my best friends growing up. I was a sickly boy with a stammer, and the horses were the only ones who never teased me. Over time, I suppose I came to understand them as well as you may understand people. I listen when they speak, and vice versa.

speaker: Rowan
en: That's a damn fine stable we have now. Lord, look at it!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it you do here, again?

speaker: Yanli
en: I buy and sell all manner of items. What's more, I am connected to a wide network of other traders, meaning I have access to nearly everything you could want, right here. But I cannot do much of anything if I don't have a place to work. If you can build a place for me, I can get started right away.

speaker: Yanli
en: There we are. Nice to have a more permanent spot.

speaker: Eivor
en: We have talked so little since our first days, Yanli, and I know nothing about you. How did you come to live in England?

speaker: Yanli
en: I wish I had a more intriguing story for you. I came from Zhongzhou, far from here. For no real reason. Curiosity, I suppose. It is not an exotic story. A young woman, excited by the prospect of travel, granted passage on a trading boat.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you miss your home?

speaker: Yanli
en: Yes, often. I intend to return one day, or perhaps coax some friends and family to join me here. But I am in no hurry.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, you are most welcome here.

speaker: Yanli
en: O, I should soon have a few spices from the East to add to our feasts. As much as I love your hospitality... your food is... Well, you are doing your best.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me about what you do here.

speaker: Eydis
en: If you want to deal with your raiders, you come through me. I'll make sure they're ready for you, and keep them in fighting shape. You need to build some barracks. Otherwise, these raiders are going to get soft. And we can't have that.

speaker: Eydis
en: Ah! with this we can recruit more warriors. Now I can build the most vicious crew ever to sail the rivers of England.

speaker: Eivor
en: Our warriors now have a place to rest and train.

speaker: Eydis
en: A fine shelter, it is. When word gets out, it should attract many Jomsvikings to fight with us. Which reminds me. A few of your raiders are chomping at the bit in hope of becoming your second. You ought to pick one.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it you do here again?

speaker: Svend
en: If you need something tattooed, you come here and I do it. And you can bring me whatever designs you come upon, too. But of course, no shop, no tattoos. Build something for us when you can and then we'll get working.

speaker: Svend
en: O thank you, Eivor. This... this is the place we needed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me about what you do here.

speaker: Tove
en: If you would ever like to get a new tattoo, you can come to me. I'm open to inspiration, as well, so feel free to bring any designs you find.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you remind me what you do here?

speaker: Gudrun
en: Whatever you need for your longship, my husband and I are happy to help. We have quite an eye for these things. But right now we're more concerned with you building us a place to do our work. Get on that soon, won't you?

speaker: Gudrun
en: This is perfect, Eivor! You really are a generous one.

speaker: Octavian
en: Salve, Eivor! We have not yet been introduced. I am Octavian Claudius Britannicus, a collector of Roman relics.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite a name you have.

speaker: Octavian
en: If you are wondering what good I will bring to the settlement, you need only look to the greatest empire the world has ever known.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I have seen their great ruins. Always impressive.

speaker: Octavian
en: But you have not seen them restored to their former glory! And I can help. Of course, I will need a place to store my collection.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will build you something when I can. Have patience.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you remind me what you do here?

speaker: Octavian
en: If you find any Roman artifacts out there in the world, bring them here. I'll appraise them and see they're given a good home. With me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must take my leave. So long.

speaker: Octavian
en: Bonum Fortunam in your travels, Eivor! Die dulci fruimini!

speaker: Octavian
en: Hmmm. I suppose it will do for the moment. Though it lacks the grandiosity of the Empire at its peak.

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't like it?

speaker: Octavian
en: It's not that. It's just not terribly Roman. It needs more. More relics, more statuary, more... Rome! If you happen to find any distinctly Roman artifacts on your travels, bring them by. We can make something of this mess yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here you are. More relics for your collection.

speaker: Octavian
en: Show me what you found. What have you brought for me? Let me see what you have.

speaker: Octavian
en: Wonderful! And here is something for you!

speaker: Octavian
en: I want more of these artifacts. There should be more like this out there. I could use more artifacts like this. Bring me more like this.

speaker: Octavian
en: Wonderful! This should complete my collection.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it you do here again?

speaker: Wallace
en: When you hunt any animal, bring it here for trade. And if you get something really special, I'm happy to mount it. That said, though, I can't do much until you build me a place to work. It won't do tanning hides on makeshift tables and dirt.

speaker: Wallace
en: Thank you for this. Whether fur, meat, or bone, we will provide only the finest.

speaker: Petra
en: And if you intend to go hunting... consider bringing us your kills. We will prepare the hides and heads.

speaker: Wallace
en: Aye. I've been mounting Petra's trophies for years. And she's a discerning woman.

speaker: Petra
en: In all things.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll keep that in mind. Enjoy your new home.

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor. You seem to be someone with a penchant for... trophies.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do like victories, but I rarely keep a record of them.

speaker: Petra
en: Your weapons show the marks of great battles. And you walk with a pride that speaks to your triumphs. Am I wrong?

speaker: Eivor
en: You are not. Why do you ask?

speaker: Petra
en: To bolster our trade, of course. Wallace is the finest and in all of England. If you wish the tales of your hunts to outlast you, there is no better way than making trophies of your kills. If you defeat a rare and worthy creature, bring it to us. We will display it for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: A good idea. Keepsakes to adorn the longhouse. Thank you, Petra.

speaker: Petra
en: O, and before you go, could you spare a moment? For a small favor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not have the time at the moment, but I will return.'

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you remind me what you do here?

speaker: Arth
en: We're fishermen, my granddad and me, and we can help you with anything you need! Bring us fish you find out there and we'll pay you for 'em! But if I'm being honest, we can't do a think until we have a place to work. If you've got time, we'd love it if you could build something.

speaker: Arth
en: Thanks for the good work, Eivor! Got a real little fishery going here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you the man in charge?

speaker: Arth
en: It's my grandfather, really, but he says the best way to learn responsibility is by working. Besides... between you and me... I'm better at it. More of a "people person," you know?

speaker: Eivor
en: I do. It's good to have you. Both of you.

speaker: Valka
en: Hm. This will do. Thank you Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Anything to help you feel at home.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me about what you do here.

speaker: Olsen
en: I've travelled this great country and found all manner of secrets, plus a few points of interest. For a price, my maps can be yours. If you want access to my maps, I need access to a workshop. If you can build me something, I'd appreciate it.

speaker: Olsen
en: This is fine work, really. Thank you for seeing this done.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Mmm. Quite delicious.

speaker: Eivor
en: A Saxon noble. He's a long way from home.

speaker: Eivor
en: What about Lincolnscire?

speaker: Randvi
en: A rather boisterous man named Hunwald arrived recently, wishing to speak with you. On a matter of great importance, he said.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is he now?

speaker: Randvi
en: Down at the docks, carousing with my scouts and scaring the fish from the river. He waits for you with great eagerness.

speaker: Eivor
en: He sounds charming. I will meet him at once.

speaker: Randvi
en: Protect your ears.

speaker: Hunwald
en: This is true happiness, isn't it, men? Life in the rough, in the company of friends, sitting beside a carefree river!

speaker: Norvid
en: I'm here for the mead, Lord-Boy.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I just adore the laughter of the water, the spice of the mead in the nose, the spittle of shouting Danes!

speaker: Svanhildr
en: Norse, you troll-wart!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Norse! Yes, forgive me. Norse...

speaker: Hunwald
en: *Coughs* Ah! Ahem. Went down the wrong pipe!

speaker: Svanhildr
en: Caution, lord.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Mm. This is strong stuff. I taste a pinch of clover in the mead. Am I wrong?

speaker: Hunwald
en: You may think this odd, but our lively chatter here has inspired in me a short poem. May I recite it for you?

speaker: Norvid
en: Go on, Lord-Boy. Make me tremble.

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, indeed. I shall try! I call it, "Ode to a Hungry Flame.

speaker: Eivor
en: Another skald come to join us?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Me? O, goodness no, I'm no skald. No. Just a humble nobleman with an interest in versification! An amateur really...

speaker: Hunwald
en: Shall I continue...?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not here to judge your poems, lord. Speak your purpose or down your mead.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Y-yes, sorry. I have come at the hope of meeting Eivor, the great warrior of this clan... if such an audience is possible.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're talking with her now. And you are...?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ah, by God's blood. my day begins with a lash of good fortune!

speaker: Eivor
en: Every warrior in this clan deserves a song or , lord? Why Eivor?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Because her name alone dries the tongues of my enemies. If such a hero fought beside me, I'd fear nothing.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is your name, lord?

speaker: Eivor
en: You must understand that Eivor has more enemies than friends in Mercia, lord. Before I drag you off by your knob to meet her, I'd like to know your name.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes, forgive me...

speaker: Hunwald
en: I am Hunwald, loyal son of Lord Hundbeorht, the current Ealdorman of Lincolnscire, may God keep and cure him. You see, my father is ailing. And in his delirium, evil men have corrupted his judgment. A secret and powerful order, if the whispers are true. Only a month ago, without forewarning, Mercian soldiers chased me, his only son, from my home. I know not why, but I do know my father would never have ordered my exile.

speaker: Eivor
en: Outcast from your family, that is a hard road to walk.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Could one of your clan help me return to Lincoln? March beside me through the city gates and set me at my father's noble feet once again.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be we can help you. But we'll want something in return. An alliance between our clan and yours.

speaker: Hunwald
en: And you shall have it! My father is a great friend of the Danes, in spite of the recent wars.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I knew my father was ill or beyond saving, I would ready myself to take his place. Will you take his burden should he fall?

speaker: Hunwald
en: O banish the thought that such a great man should perish. But, if he were to pass... yes, yes I believe I could. I must!

speaker: Eivor
en: The ealdormen in Mercia are as changeable as the seasons. Why should we care what happens to your father? Someone will take his place.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Because my father is honest. And a friend to all people, Saxons and Danes alike. If you offer an alliance in good faith, he will honor it.

speaker: Eivor
en: You sing a sad song, Hunwald of Lincolnscire. A son robbed of his father's protection, now desperate to prove his honor. How far will you go to regain it? To a bloody end?

speaker: Hunwald
en: O indeed! I will plunge into the heat of battle to defend my father, knowing our cause is a righteous one!

speaker: Eivor
en: All right, young lord. My clan has need of me just now. But when I'm ready, we'll find your father together. And right the wrongs you've suffered.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ah! You are the chieftain, here! I suspected as much.

speaker: Hunwald
en: God praise you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I won't be leading you into the heart of a shield wall, but there will be danger. I want your word, you will follow my orders to the rune.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I am yours to abuse!

speaker: Eivor
en: If it comes to that...

speaker: Hunwald
en: I'll wait for you in my safe haven. Botolphston to the northeast. From there, we shall make our way to Lincoln.

speaker: Norvid
en: Goodbye, Lord-Boy! Safe travels!

speaker: Hunwald
en: God bless and keep you all!

speaker: Eivor
en: I fear I may be escorting that boy to his own execution.

speaker: Svanhildr
en: That might shut him up.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: You see Hunwald's back? Drinking and jabbering as always.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Hun-who?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Hunwald, son of our ealdorman. Thinks himself a real wonder, slouching with the common folk. Ponce!

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Ah, leave him be. If a man wants to drink in the dirt, let him."

speaker: Eivor
en: So this is Hunwald's "safe haven"?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Caught me a sturgeon on the river, yestermorn. Rare as teeth on a rooster, they are.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: A round of mead here! And be quick about it.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Though we be a Mercian shire today, tomorrow the Kingdom of Lindsey will rise again. As free as the wind on the back of my neck.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Your line of kings died long ago, Hunwald. We're in Lincolnscire now. Do you need a map to remember?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Aelfgar, my dear man, I do not need a map to prove what my bones know for truth.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Hunwald. Who is this stranger?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Eivor! Come! Sit!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Bread and ale please, ale-wife!

speaker: Hunwald
en: I have been discussing my delicate situation with Aelfgar here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lord.

speaker: Hunwald
en: He is a nobleman like me, one of Lincolnscire's sturdy thegns.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Hunwald's idea of sturdy is a mug of ale that won't tip over.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Aelfgar has pledged his loyalty to my family, the house of the ferocious swan!

speaker: Hunwald
en: With his influence and your might, we shall rid Lincolnscire of the ruffians who plague this land, once and for all.

speaker: Eivor
en: We're going to see your father, Hunwald. That's all.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Indeed, Eivor! With speed and purpose! You are the axle to my wheel. The spark to my tinder!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald, your father is ill and your enemies have every advantage under the sun. Do you have a plan, or have I come all this way to watch you drink this watery piss?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Of course, my friend. I am a man of action above all else. Ready to leap and dance and fight!

speaker: Eivor
en: I can only bring you as far as your father, Hunwald. You are the man who must reach his heart and lead him to reason.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Are we talking about the same man? Your father is a spendthrift, Hunwald. He ran this shire into the muck.

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, Aelfgar, you jest!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald, I don't know your friend here. And not knowing him, I don't trust him.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: I'm his voice of reason, Eivor. And I've told him a thousand times, it's too dangerous for him in Lincolnscire.

speaker: Eivor
en: Listen. I've come to escort you to your father's side. We go now, or I walk.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ah, yes, to Lincoln! Away! But with care. The road between here and there is teeming with brigands who wish me dead.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: You daft lump of lard. A single Dane will not protect you against the whole of Mercia's army.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I think you are wrong, Aelfgar. And here she'll prove it.

speaker: Cearl
en: I am hot for a fight, snow-dog! Give me half a chance, and I'll stove your heathen face right in!

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. A quick brawl to get familiar with the local dregs.

speaker: Cearl
en: I'll vomit on you, Dane! Won't think twice about it!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Nothing welcomes us more into the day than a swift bruising!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that what it means to be your friend?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Rip a lung out!

speaker: Hunwald
en: We shall triumph, Eivor! We shall win this ugly row!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: You're losing ground, you drunken sot!

speaker: Hunwald
en: You're a fool to challenge this one!

speaker: Hunwald
en: By all the saints and martyrs, Eivor. You are a beast! Even Beowulf never fought so well!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Eivor! My bladder is bursting! I must step outside for a long deserved slash! Keep them dancing 'til I return!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald, do not wander!

speaker: Cearl
en: I bleedin' love a good toss-around. Gives me life!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Forget the pain, Cearl. Shake it off!

speaker: Cearl
en: Lord, give me strength!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Clear out, all of you! Before you kick up a fire!

speaker: Cearl
en: Jesus, my bones are aching. Could use a dip in the sea.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Shut your hinge, Cearl. And stop dripping blood in my hall.

speaker: Cearl
en: A worthy tussle, Dane! Give this one a cup of mead! They are not the dogs we take them for.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's not break our bones without some alcohol to dull the coming pain. Ale-wife, for these stout Saxons, a round on me!

speaker: Cearl
en: Well, that's, uh... that's kind of you. Unexpected like.

speaker: Cearl
en: Cheers to this Dane! One who knows the true worth of silver!

speaker: Hunwald
en: You canny fox. That was incredible! Like watching a captain navigate the roiling waters of an angry river. I must void my bladder, Eivor. Then we shall set forth in search of adventure new!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: You travel with a marked man at your side.

speaker: Eivor
en: He's with me. He'll be fine.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: If I had a scribe jot down all the occasions I'd warned that stupid boy, I'd be the most written about man in history.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfgar... the boorish nag of Lincolnscire.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you ever seen a blood eagle, my Saxon friends?

speaker: Cearl
en: A what?

speaker: Eivor
en: A blood eagle. A raw, magnificent bird I'll tear from your guts.

speaker: Eivor
en: First, I crush your ribs. Then, I pull out your lungs, and stretch them into wings. So you can fly to your heaven as fast as possible.

speaker: Cearl
en: Jesus. Fucking heathen.

speaker: Hunwald
en: You canny fox. That was incredible! Like watching a captain navigate the roiling waters of an angry river. I must void my bladder, Eivor. Then we shall set forth in search of adventure new!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: You travel with a marked man at your side.

speaker: Eivor
en: He's with me. He'll be fine.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: If I had a scribe jot down all the occasions I'd warned that stupid boy, I'd be the most written about man in history.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfgar... the boorish nag of Lincolnscire.

speaker: Eivor
en: I told Hunwald to stay near. Where did he wander off to?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Did you hear that scream? Sounded like Hunwald. He went out that side door.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald's in trouble.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: They call this patsy whelp a lord?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Look at him! Soft as unbaked bread.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Villains! Leave me be!

speaker: Eivor
en: Leave him be!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: Jesus! He's brought a bloody Dane!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: This ain't worth the silver they's paying us!

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, I have been struck down! Pruned within an inch of my life! But I will survive, I must. Continue as you would, Eivor! And if I should expire, avenge me!

speaker: Hunwald
en: I live! I'm alive. Heaven have mercy!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Unbelievable! The Battle of Botolphston will be remembered for years to come! Aelfgar! We have won our first great victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald, are you hurt?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Never better, I...

speaker: Eivor
en: We should get to Lincoln as quickly as we can.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes... yes, you're right. Let's depart.

speaker: French Man
en: Late last week and again this week. I do not see him being late when drink is cheap at the tavern.

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem to be waiting for someone.

speaker: French Man
en: Everyone is waiting. For resolve, for courage, for love...

speaker: Eivor
en: For wares to be delivered under the cover of night. I have the supplies you're waiting for.

speaker: French Man
en: Ah, finally! The medicine! The children have been waiting for days. Day and night, I have prayed all I can. But their fevers do not subside... Hand the wares over, quickly!

speaker: Eivor
en: Coin first, and throw in a bit more for my trouble.

speaker: French Man
en: Wha... outrageous! This... these are mine! I will only pay you the coin owed, not any more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you want them or not?

speaker: French Man
en: Fine. Here, that is more than a fair price.

speaker: French Man
en: What happened to the lad who used to bring these here?

speaker: Eivor
en: Replace him. Goodbye.

speaker: Eivor
en: Coin first.

speaker: French Man
en: Did they replace the last courier? He had more tact. Here, the coin owed. Now, give me the medicine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take them.

speaker: French Man
en: Thank you. Now, here is the coin owed...

speaker: Eivor
en: No need. To die from fever is not something I would wish upon my worst enemies. Heal your sick. May fate grant them an honorable death.

speaker: French Man
en: I do not follow your customs, Northern One, but I appreciate your kindness. Godspeed to you.

speaker: Mad Monk
en: Who tramples wildflowers in my wood? Another Dane with blood on their hands. God will punish you, heathen. I see your stained soul, murderer. You cannot hide from His eyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: This tomb has been opened. It looks like someone lives here.

speaker: Mad Monk
en: I still see their glassy stares when I sleep. I buried them all. My friends. My fellows. Do you remember Chertsey Abbey? The deadly sin committed there? Bone and sinew, tooth and nail. People splinter apart like dead branches.

speaker: To God and the Many Martyrs
en: To Our Mighty Lord above, I have ninety-nine vengeances I must carry out. For such is the Holy Work. I swear to you I will not fail. I counteth ninety and nine souls of Heaven taken by the invading heathen horde. All good monks, whose dirty knees did prostrate for Him and Mary and Jesus. I must feed the memory of lost saints. For each I have named, for each I have a cross an a lashing upon my body. The ninety-nine marks on me are for the ninety-nine that died and the ninety-nine more I shall take. Praise be to God and every branch of His making. Brother Largworth of the Ninety-Nine

speaker: Psalm Scroll from Desperate Monk
en: Lord, Today I am sending more Danes for you to judge. Let their deaths cleanse their sins. May your will guide my hand so I keep this holy work to avenge my brothers. Praise Be To the Deliverer from Evil

speaker: Mad Monk
en: I was a man of peace, but you taught me a killer's ways! All Danes must die! You butchered my brothers! Ninety-nine graves I dug in the hard earth for those you killed. The abbey at Chertsey was a holy place! You defiled it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hatred has driven you mad! I have done you no wrong! How many have you murdered in this wood? You are mind-sick! Whatever you have suffered, it was not at my hands!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your thirst for vengeance led you here. Rest now.

speaker: Eivor
en: The monk lived in this tomb. Perhaps he wished we were dead, like his brothers.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is where the monk inflicted his dark vengeance upon his victims.

speaker: Eivor
en: The monk's victims. No more Norse will be murdered on his account.

speaker: Bragi
en: Steady, Eivor.

speaker: Tove
en: Eivor... Sigurd.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tove.

speaker: Tove
en: Welcome home.

speaker: Eivor
en: We missed a great feast, it seems.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor...

speaker: Sigurd
en: Sit a moment... and rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: For me.

speaker: Randvi
en: Gifts of the gods, you are back!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Safe and standing tall.

speaker: Randvi
en: Did you... did you find what you were looking for?

speaker: Sigurd
en: We did, we did. But it was not for us.

speaker: Randvi
en: What is this?

speaker: Eivor
en: I, ah...

speaker: Tove
en: Eivor! You've returned. Is... is Sigurd with you?

speaker: Eivor
en: No... not for now, Tove.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor, is that you?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is.

speaker: Randvi
en: Is Sigurd not with you?

speaker: Eivor
en: He stayed behind. To begin anew.

speaker: Randvi
en: Stand up.

speaker: Eivor
en: What?

speaker: Randvi
en: Stand. This seat is yours.

speaker: Randvi
en: It suits you.

speaker: Tove
en: Eivor's returned! Inside, at the hearth! Come!

speaker: Randvi
en: Your secret is no longer safe.

speaker: Gudmund
en: Eivor? Randvi? What is this? Is everything all right?

speaker: Randvi
en: Our jarlskona has returned to lead us forward into an uncertain future. Will you speak to your people?

speaker: Eivor
en: For love and joy, words can jade. Our souls must sound in a heartful song. And when... no, no...

speaker: Eivor
en: You are less mine than I am yours. And I ask of you only this, keep me honest in the times to come.

speaker: Bragi
en: Hearken well, in hall of kings On ocean-steed my words gain wings.

speaker: Group
en: Odin's mead, I forth will bring, For noble deeds, thine honor sing. We beat and blazed our trail of red Till Odin gazed Upon the dead Then horns resounds the mighty hall. For those who fight For those who fall. For those who fight and those who fall. Then horns resounds the mighty hall. For we who fight For we who fall.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd...

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor. Before you say more, I must tell you something. Randvi and I have... have ended our marriage.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am sorry to hear that.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ah, do not be. We adore one another dearly, but our marriage was not built on love. We were brought together as an act of peace. I was pledged to her well before I knew her. And though we have tried to settle our differences and find love in our faults... it has not worked out. And so we have dissolved our bond. Yet as a clan, we will grow together.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I'm glad for you both. And for the rest of us. This place would not be the same without you two.

speaker: Eivor
en: So this is what you chose?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Did I choose this? Or was it thrust upon me? I find it difficult to see the difference sometimes.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be a little of both.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Time will tell. And one day, sooner or in the far future, I may return to England to witness what you have made.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope you will. And I hope you will see that I have not led us astray.

speaker: Sigurd
en: May we endure this pain until our hearts guide us back to each other again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Farewell, brother.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Between you and me, Eivor? Always knew you'd be a good jarl.

speaker: Octavian
en: Eivor, have you ever been in Love?

speaker: Eivor
en: Why do you ask?

speaker: Octavian
en: I wonder if you know the feeling of having your very heart pulled from your chest as it pursues the elusive object of your desire? I wonder if you have ever known the bitter agony of seeing your beloved in the arms of another? I have known such a pain. And Maximus was its source.

speaker: Eivor
en: One of your lovers?

speaker: Octavian
en: O gods, no! No no no! Maximus is a snake and a leech! A slime-encrusted bloodsucking viper of a man! He stole from me my beloved ... a perfectly-preserved statue of a legionnaire. It is all I desire in this world. Last I heard, Maximus was holed up in and around Lunden. Holding my beloved captive, leering and pawing at it no doubt! If you should ever see him, give him my regards. By that, I mean spit on him, then recover my statue!

speaker: Eivor
en: Octavian... I have something that may interest you.

speaker: Octavian
en: Hm?

speaker: Eivor
en: Maximilian sends his regards.

speaker: Octavian
en: What? He... he gave this to you? That perfect little wretch, how did he bring himself to part with it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ask no questions, hear no lies. I only hope you enjoy it. And that neither of us have to see that man again.

speaker: Octavian
en: O, thank you, Eivor! Thank you!

speaker: Sunniva
en: I've never heard tell of any "River Champion." Not sure what to make of that. But you're welcome to ask Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sunniva. And stranger. What brings you to our shores?

speaker: Sunniva
en: Vagn and his crew claim to be raiders of great treasures. They seek to join Ravensthorpe.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you seek to join us, we only ask for hard work and loyalty. No need of silver or gold.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Wouldn't say no to it, either...

speaker: Vagn
en: It is good to meet you, Eivor. And there is more in this for you than precious metals. We may seem weary and ragged... But we know secret routes of England's coasts where you will find a wealth of resources for Ravensthorpe.

speaker: Eivor
en: You seek to share them with us? Why?

speaker: Vagn
en: When the table is laden with too great a feast, you gather friends 'round to enjoy. We seek friends and feasting. Let me show you. I will take you out on a raid ... once we repair our ship.

speaker: Eivor
en: I appreciate the offer and accept it.

speaker: Eivor
en: And? How do you judge our dock?

speaker: Vagn
en: Ah! Now that's a dock worthy of our longship! Come and talk to me whenever you are ready to leave.

speaker: Vagn
en: Are you ready to set sail?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am ready. On to the raid.

speaker: Vagn
en: We will use my crew for this first outing. Easier for me to show you what lies beyond the river bank. Later, you are welcome to send your own Jomsvikingr along the paths we travel. Mine could use the rest.

speaker: Vagn
en: This river does not appear on many maps. Few know how to navigate it. But the Jomsvikingr have been learning its currents. An old friend said it was a smuggling route for Roman traders. She claims it was useful in hiding their tracks. In fact, it is so well-hidden, you could raid your very neighbours and they would never know it was you. Something to think about.

speaker: Vagn
en: Look there! Villagers! Not hoarders of wealth, mind you, but well worth the trouble if you are seeking rations for the crew.

speaker: Vagn
en: Remember, my crew is like a pack of trained wolves. They will respond to your orders. Give them freely and loudly.

speaker: Eivor
en: That seems to be everything. We should return to the ship.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've had tougher fights in taverns.

speaker: Vagn
en: Well, stay alert. The smoke from the flames will alert camps downriver. The fighting will get tougher as we go.

speaker: Vagn
en: There! Military camp. You will find foreign supplies and even gear if you are lucky. They will put up a fight, but so be it, ja?

speaker: Eivor
en: This looks valuable. I should take it back to the settlement.

speaker: Eivor
en: I thought you were a fighter, yet you didn't join the battle. Biding your time for bigger fights?

speaker: Vagn
en: More of a captain these days. Odd, isn't it? A raider who doesn't raid. Turns out spending years getting damn near chopped in half leaves you with enough aches and stiff muscles to keep you boat-bound. Now come, let us go.

speaker: Vagn
en: I don't know about you, but I am ready to return to Ravensthorpe. Let the crew know when you are ready.

speaker: Vagn
en: Monasteries are a great boon! Packed with as much knowledge as riches. Brains as full as coffers.

speaker: Vagn
en: That was invigorating! And as lucrative as I promised, ja? Think we have got enough supplies here to put something together?

speaker: Eivor
en: Something like what?

speaker: Vagn
en: A place to stay where we can stretch out. A hall. Wouldn't want to bother Eydis and the rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: You know Eydis?

speaker: Vagn
en: Er ... I—I know of Eydis. Her reputation as a fighter and as a trainer precedes her. Simply wouldn't want to get in her way.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see... Well, we have space for a hall, and with enough supplies, we can make something in due time.

speaker: Vagn
en: Welcome to the Jomsviking Hall, Eivor! Been a long time since we've had a permanent place to gather and share stories. Come here to hire more Jomsvikingr for your raids. With time, it will attract some impressive fighters. Real talents.

speaker: Flann
en: Eivor, come in. Sichfrith tells me you've been hunting pirates in the North?

speaker: Eivor
en: Allies of Armagh, providing weapons and other supplies. I've cut them off.

speaker: Flann
en: God is truly with us! Eogan is weakened and will soon taste God's justice.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you have the men to take Armagh?

speaker: Flann
en: We do, thanks to Sichfrith. He has rallied Vikings from every corner of Ireland.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you convince the Norse to fight for you?

speaker: Sichfrith
en: I told them of a monastery full of silver to be looted.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your father would not have made such a promise.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: And he would have not raised as many men.

speaker: Flann
en: We cannot win the goodwill of the people by destroying their homes. Or their church.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: But, my lord... these men came expecting a raid, if we deny them that...

speaker: Eivor
en: If I may? I think in this case, some burning might be useful.

speaker: Flann
en: Tell me how.

speaker: Eivor
en: When we were attacked by Clogher, Eogan didn't stop there. He burned Cashelore as well. To send a message. It is our turn to light up the land with fire and smoke to let the people know that Armagh has fallen.

speaker: Flann
en: Burn what you must, but keep your warriors leashed. Kill only those who oppose us, and spare the church.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: As you command, my king.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's something else. Abbot Eogan leads the Children of Danu.

speaker: Flann
en: So ... the poisoning, the ambush... they were all part of Eogan's nefarious schemes. We'll cleanse Armagh of this unholy filth. Sichfrith and I will prepare our men. Join me when you're ready.

speaker: Flann
en: Choose a good view, dear poet. It'll be a battle for the ages.

speaker: Ciara
en: Thank you for not saying anything about... my past.

speaker: Eivor
en: The past is past and not our future.

speaker: Ciara
en: I swear, Eivor, you really are like a hero out of folk tales. Do I have permission to sing your song?

speaker: Eivor
en: You do, once I've had a chance to finish it.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's good to see you take command. It suits you.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: It feels heavy and stiff like this new armor. I envy you, Eivor. When battle is done, you can move on to what you like.

speaker: Eivor
en: I go where my destiny takes me, Sichfrith. None of us are free from that. There are worse fates than being a king.

speaker: Flann
en: Our forces are replenished, thank God's good grace.

speaker: Eivor
en: Some part of those thanks should go to Sichfrith, lord.

speaker: Flann
en: Aye, I'll not forget his role today. He's a good man, but he lacks his father's seasoning.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then you must show him what it is to lead, lord, in the court and on the field.

speaker: Flann
en: Come, let us flush out this false abbot without delay.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, Eogan must answer for his actions.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hold a little longer. I need more time to prepare.

speaker: Flann
en: My warriors are restless stallions champing at the bit. Shall we begin this battle?

speaker: Eivor
en: There are few defenders than I expected.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: They cower behind their walls. Let's strike while we have the advantage!

speaker: Flann
en: We'll move forward but remain alert. God will guide the right.

speaker: Flann
en: We have no other choice. Breach that gate!

speaker: Sichfrith
en: My Norsemen are ready! Smash them an opening!

speaker: Flann
en: The bridge is down! Onward and across!

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: Leave the barbarian to me!

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: God will give me strength!

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: Brothers! To me!

speaker: Flann
en: If they don't plead mercy, kill them to a man!

speaker: Flann
en: Take care! They have artillery! They attack from above! Clear the ramparts!

speaker: Flann
en: Unleash God's wrath on these sinners! These are soldiers, not farmers! Don't hold back!

speaker: Sichfrith
en: We're trapped like rats!

speaker: Flann
en: We must raise that portcullis to go any further.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Cover Armagh in flames! Light up the sky for all to see! Torch the rooftops!

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Soldiers coming!

speaker: Flann
en: We cannot advance until we clear the area!

speaker: Flann
en: There's only one way! Through that gate!

speaker: Sichfrith
en: They fall back!

speaker: Flann
en: Gather your breath, but remain at the ready!

speaker: Eivor
en: King Flann! Are you near?

speaker: Irish Soldier 3
en: For Saint Patrick!

speaker: Irish Soldier 4
en: They mustn't breach the gate!

speaker: Eivor
en: A trap. I knew it looked too easy.

speaker: Flann
en: We cannot advance until we clear the area!

speaker: Irish Soldier 5
en: For the Abbot of Armagh!

speaker: Flann
en: Eivor! I need help with the door!

speaker: Eogan
en: Leave this house of God, Flann Sinna, or be cursed with His wrath eternal!

speaker: Flann
en: You desecrate this holy place with foul corruption. You are a sickness to be purged.

speaker: Eogan
en: God will be my judge, not you. You act the Christian king, but let pagans and wolves do your dirty work.

speaker: Flann
en: Do not preach about playing both sides. I know you lead the Children of Danu.

speaker: Eogan
en: Do you? Then you should know you cannot win. My Children are everywhere. Even in your court.

speaker: Flann
en: Who do you mean?

speaker: Eogan
en: Ciara had the makings of a High Priestess, but she was careless. Dabbled with forces she could not control.

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't listen, Flann. He tries to cloud your judgement.

speaker: Eogan
en: Small wonder why she charmed her way into your court. She's always been attracted to men of power.

speaker: Flann
en: You lie, devil!

speaker: Eogan
en: Ah ... "Love conceals blemish and evil." It's easy to lose sight when you're following a woman's backside.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is no shame in keeping your hands clean of this filth. Let me do your dirty work.

speaker: Flann
en: It's God work.

speaker: Eogan
en: Protect your abbot!

speaker: Flann
en: Take the guards! Leave Eogan to me!

speaker: Eogan
en: "You shall not let your cattle breed with a different kind ... You shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed..."

speaker: Flann
en: Do not quote Scripture to me, devil. May your tongue burn for eternity while your throat is pierced with jagged glass.

speaker: Eogan
en: No ... you would rather have a song from your ... pagan poetess... If she didn't tell you ... about the Children of Danu ... what other secrets does she keep?

speaker: Eivor
en: He tries to poison your mind with his dying words, lord. Don't let them in.

speaker: Flann
en: But could he speak truth?

speaker: Eivor
en: The best liars mix truth with lies. If she was part of that cult, she isn't anymore.

speaker: Flann
en: You are right, of course. This fetid air befouls my thoughts. Let us step out into God's cleansing light.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a beautiful land.

speaker: Flann
en: We are a blessed people.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Word of our victory spread like fire in a dry field. I couldn't stop all the looting, my king, but I made certain the people were spared.

speaker: Flann
en: They will sing of the High King who cleansed the church of Armagh and the King of Dublin who fought with honor at his side.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: And the hero who came from the Land of Heroes who helped them win the day.

speaker: Eivor
en: All will be remembered. The living and the dead.

speaker: Offerings for Valka
en: 2 chickens from Snaefrid to annoint her crops 1 sheep from Thora for her child's blood-blessing 1 goat from Dag for more skin salve

speaker: Valka
en: Hamu-ram... Hamu-ram...

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka?

speaker: Valka
en: Hush. I need silence to hear the songs of nature. Hamu-ram... Hamu-ram...

speaker: Eivor
en: Svala?

speaker: Svala
en: She gives praises, and she is greeted.

speaker: Valka
en: For your hearing, I harken, O Ancient Ones! Great Odin, great Freyja, I give you thanks for your gift of seidr (magic).

speaker: Svala
en: She gives thanks, and she is blessed.

speaker: Valka
en: Eivor, it has been some time. What brings you so far to see me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I... I have come for your advice. On a private matter.

speaker: Valka
en: Come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is your mother well?

speaker: Valka
en: Her mind is a jumble. She speaks to spirits. I fear her final winter has come. But she has me. Now let us speak to your needs.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have had a vision. A powerful vision. It may have been my battle lust, or a delirium caused by the cold but...

speaker: Valka
en: Describe it for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: After seventeen years, I saw my father's axe again. And when I touched it, the vision came on fast. There was a wolf, howling and fierce. And then a figure. A graybeard in a cloak with a single eye. He bid me follow him.

speaker: Valka
en: Ah! The High One! He calls to you. Perhaps he means to speak with you. Deliver a message. Only through seidr will you see more clearly and unravel the threads that sit tangled upon your mind. This will not take long.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you brewing?

speaker: Valka
en: An elixir to loosen your hugr (mind) and unwind your thoughts. You will enter a waking sleep and journey to the world of dreams.

speaker: Valka
en: It may confuse or disorient you, but you must take note of all you see.

speaker: Eivor
en: Whatever happens, whatever I see, whatever you foretell, it must stay between us.

speaker: Valka
en: We cannot change the fate we are bound to. What matter who know and who does not? The outcome will be the same.

speaker: Eivor
en: It matters to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you used this sort of magic before?

speaker: Valka
en: Have no fear. It was not my seidr that made her like this. Her condition inspired the elixir.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did it help her?

speaker: Valka
en: For a time. It opened her up to visions. Strange, unreadable things. Then she returned to her current state.

speaker: Valka
en: Drink... if you seek true understanding.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm? I saw nothing, Valka. Felt nothing.

speaker: Skuld
en: Havi! Havi! Havi!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do I walk among the dead?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd...? Sigurd. Brother... When did you arrive?

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this?

speaker: Urðr
en: Hrm-mah-mr-mah, hrm-mah-mr-mah... Hrm-mah-mr-mah, hrm-mah-mr-mah...

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd? Brother? What is this?

speaker: Sigurd
en: There was no other way, Havi. Our fates are fixed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd! What has... what has happened?

speaker: Sigurd
en: This was not for you, Havi.

speaker: Eivor
en: No!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ahhh! Ah!

speaker: Valka
en: Steady, Eivor. It is Valka. I am here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods, I thought I... wh-what was that?

speaker: Valka
en: Tell me everything.

speaker: Eivor
en: I-I-I was on a mountain in a violent blizzard, climbing towards the summit, following a wolf.

speaker: Valka
en: Hm hm.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw Odin. And the Nornir, spinning the threads of fate. They were watching me.

speaker: Valka
en: Hm. Not watching. They were showing you the way forward. Your life. Your path. What lies before you, and where it ends.

speaker: Eivor
en: And the wolf was eager for my attention. As if it were... beckoning me to follow.

speaker: Valka
en: You are the Wolf-Kissed, fated to carry its mark for life. In this case, it might represent your ambition... or your fear.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw the gates to Odin's hall of slain champions. They opened for me.

speaker: Valka
en: Shades of Valhalla. For which you are destined.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not know what else to say. M-my memories are faint, hazy.

speaker: Valka
en: Did you reach the summit of this mountain?

speaker: Eivor
en: I did, yes. Sigurd was there. Wounded, in pain. His fighting arm was missing. Then the wolf reappeared, the size of a dragon, twisted and terrible. It fixed its eyes on me and struck! Then I awoke.

speaker: Valka
en: The gods favor you, Eivor. They always have. You will have your glory, and you will earn your place in Valhalla. But these portents carry a darker truth. The missing arm, the trail of blood, the beast. You will betray your brother, Sigurd. That is the meaning of your vision.

speaker: Eivor
en: That cannot be right. I would never betray Sigurd. He's my brother, my family.

speaker: Valka
en: The Nornir have spoken, and this is their message.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, this is wrong. Or you misunderstand. That cannot be right!

speaker: Valka
en: You will betray Sigurd.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin fought against his fate. It can be done.

speaker: Bárid
en: Flann is inside.

speaker: Eivor
en: Relax your shoulders. He has as much to gain from this as we do.

speaker: Flann
en: Bárid. We welcome you to Durrow. It has been a long time.

speaker: Bárid
en: Thank you for meeting with me, lord. I trust our gift was well received?

speaker: Flann
en: Exotic spices, all of which are foreign to me. I am impressed.

speaker: Bárid
en: Only a taste of things to come. Dublin will soon be known as the pillar of Ireland's trade. To a long life and prosperous reign, my king.

speaker: Flann
en: Such fealty. You honor me.

speaker: Flann
en: You must be Eivor. My gratitude, for your selfless actions in what preceded my coronation.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lord.

speaker: Flann
en: It seems my enemies could not wait for my reign to begin before trying to put an end to it. An old tale between Northern and Southern Uí Néill, I'm afraid. But it's one whose ending I will be the author of.

speaker: Eivor
en: Planning a war?

speaker: Flann
en: A High King should have control over his land. And I shall. If it takes a bloody war, I must be prepared for it.

speaker: Bárid
en: Dublin's trade has plenty to offer, and plenty of stout fighters. Eivor included, ready to fight alongside you.

speaker: Flann
en: I appreciate your desire to strengthen the ties between Meath and Dublin. And as much I find myself in need of aid, it appears you find yourself undermined by your own people.

speaker: Bárid
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Flann
en: During the coronation, a monastery was raided and a Christian text was lost. The Book of Kells. Dublin Danes are to blame. Your support would be of great help, let me be clear. But this capriciousness will sooner harm me than help me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I take it the book is important.

speaker: Flann
en: Authored by monks by the monastery of Iona some eighty years ago, it was. After the Danes first reached our shores. It was meant to preserve the Christian faith in uncertain times. Today it is a symbol of that perseverance.

speaker: Eivor
en: Whoever these Danes, they acted alone. It has nothing to do with Bárid.

speaker: Bárid
en: It does not matter. They are Dubliners who threaten the holiness of the land. It would be unbecoming to ally with their leader.

speaker: Flann
en: It is as simple as that.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I retrieve the book, set straight the ones who did this, would you welcome Bárid into your court?

speaker: Flann
en: It would help.

speaker: Eivor
en: These Danes, you know where they are?

speaker: Flann
en: In a bog of Inchroe, just north of here.

speaker: Bárid
en: Eivor, this is my responsibility.

speaker: Eivor
en: Remain here. I will see it done.

speaker: Eivor
en: Inchroe's Bog. These are the ones who stole the Book of Kells. I should search their stashes for it.

speaker: Eivor
en: This confirms Flann's information. The book should be here somewhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not what I'm looking for.

speaker: Thorstein
en: Ah! O! It's you!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's you? Thought we told you to leave, Thorstein.

speaker: Thorstein
en: Ah ah! "Leave Dublin." Correct me if I am wrong but... this is not Dublin.

speaker: Eivor
en: You did not understand you were not to be seen again?

speaker: Thorstein
en: O, come now! How was I to know you would find your way out here? Why are you here?

speaker: Eivor
en: Looking for a book you stole. You raided a monastery recently.

speaker: Thorstein
en: It was several monasteries, actually. These new friends of mine do not tire easily.

speaker: Eivor
en: The book is important to the Christians. I need it back.

speaker: Thorstein
en: The Christians? Hah! See? You are an Irish lapdog.

speaker: Thorstein
en: I... I do not have it.

speaker: Thorstein
en: Are you upset? Please, do not be upset. You are upset, hmm?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am running out of reasons to let you live.

speaker: Thorstein
en: I know where it is! Boyne Tombs. Some strange folks offered me this hoard for it. I could not resist! Could you?

speaker: Thorstein
en: See? You understand! We are very alike, you and I. I could just as well be your brother, I... Do not kill me...

speaker: Eivor
en: Thorstein... your blood is not worthy of my steel.

speaker: Thorstein
en: I could not agree more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now vanish. I mean it this time. A third encounter, you will not walk away from.

speaker: Thorstein
en: O, I am through with Ireland. My ankles ache for how I must dance around all these kings. It offers nothing!

speaker: Thorstein
en: Except for this. I will just take this... and this...

speaker: Eivor
en: Boyne Tombs. Thorstein said I could find the Book of Kells here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Need to tread carefully. These must be the people who bought the book from Thorstein.

speaker: Eivor
en: Blocked.

speaker: Eivor
en: An underground cavern. Whoever these people are, they're secretive.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Book of Kells. Now, to get out of this ghastly grotto.

speaker: Eogan
en: It is a violation of the highest degree.

speaker: Bárid
en: This will be remedied soon enough, abbot. You have my promise.

speaker: Eogan
en: The book, have you found it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Its popularity is ever increasing.

speaker: Flann
en: This is Eogan, Abbot of Armagh. The book is for him.

speaker: Eivor
en: I remember. From the coronation.

speaker: Eogan
en: I pray you did not have to endure much to reclaim this.

speaker: Eivor
en: A small price to ensure the high king's patronage.

speaker: Eogan
en: What's this? Lord, you are chosen High King by God Almighty. These are pagans.

speaker: Eogan
en: I mean no disrespect.

speaker: Eivor
en: We Norse have hardened shells, abbot. It is why we are liked by so many.

speaker: Eivor
en: You hear that, Bárid? You can save their lives, protect their religion, and still they treat you like dog shit.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have no say here. This is between the two kings.

speaker: Eogan
en: I only mean to warn Flann of the possible implications, nothing more.

speaker: Flann
en: And I am well aware of them, abbot.

speaker: Eogan
en: I have spoken past what is right. I will take my leave. Lord, please excuse my clumsy intrusion.

speaker: Flann
en: No need. I am gladdened to see the book back in good hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: He is colorful.

speaker: Flann
en: I do not blame the abbot for raising alarm. History dictates he has every reason to. What is your report?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have dealt with the leader in the bog. You'll have no more problems coming out of Dublin.

speaker: Flann
en: Then we shall turn our eyes to the problem at hand. Ulster is using its power to sway Connacht. An allegiance that must be snuffed before it takes flame. For that, we need to gain support from the other kingdoms. Speak with Ciara. She will guide you in this.

speaker: Bárid
en: I shall return to Dublin to gather men and resources for the march.

speaker: Flann
en: I welcome them. When we are strong enough, we will meet at Knockfree and devise a strategy.

speaker: Bárid
en: You were gone some time. What happened?

speaker: Eivor
en: The book was in the hands of a strange cult. They procured it from Thorstein.

speaker: Bárid
en: I was weak to spare him. My own son knew better.

speaker: Eivor
en: Chin up, Bárid. We have come into favor with the High King.

speaker: Bárid
en: I will feel better the day Flann's trust in me is not shadowed by doubt. Back to Dublin I go. Talk with Ciara. We must gain favor with the other kings quickly.

speaker: Norse Man
en: I am one with the earth! With the air and water, and fire, and... What is the other? Clouds! Tree bark. What is that smell?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Do you think you can stop him? Because I cannot. Some help over here? This skald had the bright idea to alter his mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Easy, friend. I think you may have eaten something that did not agree with you

speaker: Norse Man
en: Today my saga is writ! Glory! Ah! A brave steed has swept me up! Onward, to my loyal companion!

speaker: Eivor
en: If I don't stop him, something or someone less forgiving will. I should stay close by, wait for him to tire.

speaker: Norse Man
en: I have the strength of one thousand Thors! I cannot be stopped!

speaker: Norse Man
en: This victory I will add to my growing saga!

speaker: Norse Man
en: I may throw up, I may throw up, ugh! I will take on any challenger, be it on two legs or four! Show yourselves to me, if you dare! Am I crying? There is no fight I will flee! And should the gods answer my call, so be it! They too will feel my wrath!

speaker: Eivor
en: You keep this up, you're going to get yourself killed. Are you hearing me?

speaker: Norse Man
en: Yah! Loud and clear! Now stand aside so that I may fulfill my destiny! Yah!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm going to have to drag you back myself, eh?

speaker: Norse Man
en: Jeska. Where are you? I must find my way back to you!

speaker: Norse Man
en: O, if my mother could see me now... My saga is complete and it is the envy of all who came before and all who are yet to come!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your skald.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Gods! Is he dead?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, but he should be. Seems the gods disagree this time. Splash water in his face, and keep your distance. He'll throw up something fierce.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Thank you for the advice, and for your trouble... which is now my problem...

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Such carnage I've never seen. That twisted bishop must pay the devil his due.

speaker: Eivor
en: What news?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: We have learned that Herefrith occupies the fort at Anecastre, south of here. An eager fyrd awaits my voice to lead them into battle. Will you ride with us?

speaker: Eivor
en: I've gone some days without a proper siege. Lead on.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: To the camp then, and onward to Anecastre! Follow if you will!

speaker: Hunwald
en: A bold attack. And in broad daylight! The hatred that eats at that man must be ravenous.

speaker: Eivor
en: What news, Hunwald?

speaker: Hunwald
en: We've learned that Herefrith rode for the fort at Anecastre following the massacre. I have assembled a fyrd there. Quite a large one, in fact. They eagerly await your orders, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mean your orders, ealdorman.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ah, yes, that's right! My orders. Which are... which are what exactly?

speaker: Eivor
en: Who can say? Ride with me to your camp and we'll find out together.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Herefrith was a friend of my father's, and always so dear to me. I don't understand what possessed him.

speaker: Eivor
en: He invoked the name of an ancient order before his men attacked. I know exactly what possessed him.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Do you?

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not a story for now.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: This will send waves of disgust through all the parishes of Mercia. Herefrith is a new and ugly stain on the Bishopric.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your Christ was an interesting man, if a little soft. But stranger still... I've met so few Christians like him.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Today has been a boon, Eivor. In spite of everything, I now know my father's spirit still burns within me. It's thanks to you I know this. When songs are sung of the day Lincolnscire was saved, your name will ripple through every stanza.

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't be hasty, Hunwald. One verse of our song remains unsung. The din of battle beckons.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: You pagans and your appetite for battle. I certainly don't share it. I worry what diabolical feast the bishop has in store.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Don't let that poxy bishop worry you. With Eivor beside us, he'll be vittles before long. How has Acha taken all this? She and Herefrith were so close.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: She must feel as though the Devil himself attacked her monastery, the poor lady.

speaker: Eivor
en: We spoke briefly. Her spirits were low, but her work carried on. I think she'll be fine.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Manipulated by a man who should be God's gladdener.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Our camp is just here. When the fyrd is ready, we'll attack with speed.

speaker: Eivor
en: The sooner the better. Herefrith will entrench deeper with every passing hour.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Here's the camp, do you see? The fyrd will soon be ready for action!

speaker: Eivor
en: Give them mead and let them rest. There is hard fighting ahead.

speaker: Randvi
en: Something troubling has come. A letter from Aelfgar in Lincoln. It seems the new ealdorman, Herefrith, has turned on them. When you are able, you should visit with him. See what this is about.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me more about Lincolnscire. What has become of their ealdorman, Herefrith?

speaker: Randvi
en: He has turned on his people. And what's more, Hytham has learned his true allegiance. The Order of the Ancients.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods. This is my doing, Randvi. I voted to install Herefrith as ealdorman.

speaker: Eivor
en: Indeed. And now Aelfgar asks that you return and right the wrong you brought to life. He is waiting near Anecastre with his fyrd (peasant army). Will you go?

speaker: Eivor
en: I must fight beside Aelfgar and make this right.

speaker: Randvi
en: Be careful. Herefrith may be more than he seems.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Our camp is just here. When the fyrd is ready, we'll attack with speed.

speaker: Eivor
en: The sooner the better. Herefrith will entrench deeper with every passing hour.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfgar.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Eivor. I must say, I expected a rather different outcome. But... no matter. You cannot un-throw a stone from a creek.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Who's fetching the turf this time? Eh? Don't want to freeze to death here!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: We are the men of Lincolnscire. Remember it!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: My ancestors fought with the ancient kings of Lindsey. It's for their memory we fight today.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: This battle will be fucking Hell, and my boots have holes the size of chestnuts. Jesus.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Such carnage I've never seen. That twisted bishop must pay the devil his due.

speaker: Hunwald
en: A bold attack. And in broad daylight! The hatred that eats at that man must be ravenous.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: Our war-smith has arrived. The fyrds are ready to fight.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Chieftain Eivor. Can we win this battle with the small number you see assembled here?

speaker: Eivor
en: If they fight as strongly as they smell, we'll claim victory.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Then we'll have no cause for worry. We should attack soon, before the bishop can muster more troops. What do you think, Eivor?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Chieftian Eivor. Can we win this fight with the men you see assembled here?

speaker: Eivor
en: If they fight with the bravery of double their number, we may.

speaker: Hunwald
en: And is there room in your Valhalla for a ferocious swan?

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course. Let fly your glorious banner.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Are we ready, then?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Chieftain Eivor! We are ever so glad you came.

speaker: Eivor
en: How could I not? It was my vote that got you into this mess.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: The bishop caught us unaware. Claims to have taken this shire in the name of some sort of religious order.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Order of Ancients?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: That's the one. Do you know what he means?

speaker: Eivor
en: I may.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: As our hastily elected ealdorman, I advise we attack quickly, before he can rally more troops.

speaker: Eivor
en: We attack now. Ready the fyrd.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: Our first task will be to breach the outer wall. Then we deal with the troops inside.

speaker: Eivor
en: We're not ready. The battle din must wait.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: Are you ready now? The fyrd is itching for a fight.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: For the glory of Lincolnscire!

speaker: Hunwald
en: To me! Holy warriors of Lincolnscire!

speaker: Eivor
en: The best way to breach is with a battering ram. I should help it along.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: The gate is down! Leave the ram, we don't need it.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Fight, men! Fight until your livers hang from your mouths!

speaker: Eivor
en: Need to find a way past that palisade. An explosion could do it, or I can try hitting it with a springald.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Lower the drawbridge!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Hunwald! Watch your arse!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ah! I... I got him! My thanks, Aelfgar!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Thank me when the bleeding is done!

speaker: Hunwald
en: A moment's rest is all I needed.

speaker: Eivor
en: A challenge at last.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 6
en: I'll stick you like a pig!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods! Herefrith has gone mad!

speaker: Eivor
en: You... point me to the bishop. No one else need to die today.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: He's... he's in the chapel there. Hiding away. Scabrous coward.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let no one leave that church without facing judgment.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Some respite, lord, please. Our battle is lost.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Continue the work of God, my boy. Kill this pagan.

speaker: Herefrith
en: I died the day I hid behind these robes, this cross. To bring the light of my order to a wider view, I debased myself. Clawed my way to the top of this common religion, full of common men. I should have lived as the ancients did.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's the folly of mankind, Herefrith. We wallow in our failures like happy pigs in a sty of shit. You should have learned to enjoy it.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Eivor, you fought as one possessed by a demon today.

speaker: Eivor
en: Herefrith may yet have allies in Mercia, members of his secret order. But the immediate danger is passed.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: You have my deepest thanks, Eivor. To you, I owe all my future happiness and prosperity.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a good fit for ealdorman, Aelfgar. Just make sure you put the shire's needs above your own.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Of course. I'd not be the man I am today without this land, these people.

speaker: Eivor
en: I did this to secure the alliance between us, Aelfgar. Not to bring you personal prosperity.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Yes, of course, you did. Forgive me. I'm not yet accustomed to the size of the task before me.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a shame Hunwald was not fit to don his father's boots, but he can bring joy to the people here. Treat him well.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Yes, about that... I believe that he has a somewhat different idea of his future. You should talk to him.

speaker: Eivor
en: About...?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Until next we meet, Eivor. The strength of Lincolnscire is yours, should you need it.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are bonded now, your people and mine.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I have found better friends in Danes to be honest. Swanburrow is my love, and you are a better friend to me than any here. Would it be an imposition to ask... well, could we live with your clan? Swanburrow and I? It would mean so much to her... and to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course you may. We would be happy to host you, Ferocious Swan. And your charming Dane. Come when it suits you.

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, yes, I'll pull my weight, I promise! And fight when needs be. And I won't drink more than I'm allotted.

speaker: Eivor
en: You fight with us, Hunwald. And you can drink as much as you like.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Thank you, Eivor. This means... it means the world to me.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I... I can't believe I survived that!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: I mean this with the utmost love, my friend: neither can I.

speaker: Hunwald
en: The blood and splinters, flying through the air! The blood... and viscera... absolutely poetic...!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: There there, Hunwald, take deep breaths. Perhaps I can find you a jar to take the edge off.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Eivor. Is he... is the bishop dead?

speaker: Eivor
en: He bled too little and talked too much. Now he's gone.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I won't miss him, but Acha will need some time to grieve.

speaker: Eivor
en: You fought well, Ferocious Swan. Notched a few scars in your baby fat today.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes, but they will heal. And stronger than before.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lincolnscire is yours to lead, ealdorman. The hardest fight begins now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be careful in the coming weeks. There may be others who wish you harm. Herefrith was not the only member of his Order in Mercia.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I shall hold on to my friends with every fiber of my constitution and watch my back for iron daggers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lincolnscire is yours to lead, ealdorman. The hardest fight begins now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lincolnscire is yours to lead, ealdorman. The hardest fight begins now.

speaker: Hunwald
en: The din of battle still rings in my ears. I think I now know what it means to be a leader.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I would ask a favor, if I could.

speaker: Eivor
en: Name it.

speaker: Hunwald
en: As ealdorman, my life may be a dangerous one. For a time anyway. Would you allow my Swanburrow to take refuge in your settlement? At least until I feel all danger has passed.

speaker: Eivor
en: We'd be happy to have her.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Thank you, my sturdy Norse berserker. The meadhalls of my shire will be lonely without you stomping about.

speaker: Eivor
