en: Our people are bonded now. We must look out for one another.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Blast it, I am a horror with goodbyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: It'll do for now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, it seems the wind calls me back to Randvi. Best tell her the good news.

scene: A Tale of Ice and Fire
speaker: Havi
en: Let me tell you the story of how I bested Muspel and Jotun both! Next, fate steered me into the path of a mighty Muspel, and battle was joined! I encountered my next enemy unsuspecting, and moved in for the kill. After that, I came face to face with a Jotun of extraordinary size! My foes were mighty indeed, but of course... I prevailed!

speaker: Randvi
en: At one time, the title Jarl referred to a man second only to the king. But that use has softened. Now a jarl may be a chief, a leader, or a man with broad wealth and influence.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: The world is bigger now, and broken into many pieces. It seems our language must do the same to keep up.

speaker: Randvi
en: An interesting thought.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert, your father sent you here to learn, not teach.

speaker: Randvi
en: Then you must start, Eivor. Give us a summary of our recent gains, for instance. The clan is thirsty for knowledge.

speaker: Eivor
en: You want me to give a speech?

speaker: Eivor
en: Right.

speaker: Eivor
en: My friend, hearken to me! And hear a tale of triumph and toil. I have traveled far since we landed, and seen much on the roads and fields of this new England. And for all my travels, strong alliances we have gained. The honorable Ceolwulf, King of Mercia, now calls us friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: And to the south, Soma Jarlskona and the Danes of Grantebridge have pledged their oaths to us.

speaker: Eivor
en: By Sigurd's hand and my own, we have strengthened the ties of

speaker: Dag
en: You seat yourself as Sigurd's equal in these tales of yours. Would Sigurd do the same if he were here?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd knows what I have achieved. And he would celebrate it more roundly than I have. But this takes nothing from you, all of you. For I sit among some of the staunchest wills and strongest fighters I have ever known.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not claim to be Sigurd's equal. But I will not shy away from the triumphs I have fairly won, Dag. Let glory seek and find those who have earned it. If that means me, so be it. If that means you, any one of you, all the better.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hush, Dag. Or would you steer us into a storm, even as the seas are calm?

speaker: Dag
en: I only say what I feel, that being a hot wind blowing from your ass!

speaker: Eivor
en: Breathe deeply, Dag. You may benefit from the air.

speaker: Eivor
en: And so I raise my horn! First to Sigurd, may he return to us soon. And to the Raven Clan, the best of friends and fighters.

speaker: Randvi
en: To Sigurd!

speaker: Dag
en: To Sigurd! May he return and relieve us of you!

speaker: Eivor
en: And may all of you enjoy the ale as much as Dag has. Skal!

speaker: Raven Clan
en: Skal!

speaker: Dag
en: You think me drunk, Eivor? Would it soften my blows if I was?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your words are blunt enough. But it would explain your boldness.

speaker: Dag
en: My eyes are clear and open. And I see before me one eager to claim a piece of Sigurd's glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is enough glory in the world to go around for all who earn it. And I have no doubt how much I am owed.

speaker: Eivor
en: All you say is nonsense, Dag. Have I done something to raise your ire?

speaker: Eivor
en: If you're not drunk yet, you should be. This is a feast and a celebration of Sigurd's leadership. Enjoy it.

speaker: Dag
en: Just as I thought! You

speaker: Sunniva
en: Attackers from the river! They look to be Danes!

speaker: Eivor
en: Danes? How many?

speaker: Norvid
en: Too many! Now come! The battle roars already!

speaker: Dag
en: Bloody curs! What quarrel have Danes with us?

speaker: Eivor
en: Those who can fight, take up your weapons! All others, stay here!

speaker: Eivor
en: With me!

speaker: Oswald
en: That's silver, livestock, and a trophy from our slain enemy. What more do you want?

speaker: Broder
en: Who said we wanted anything, Saxon?

speaker: Broder
en: No battle-dented Dane would ever follow this lump of lard into battle! I don't care how many shields he brings me!

speaker: Oswald
en: You mean to say you refuse my gifts, Broder?

speaker: Broder
en: I don't have time for this!

speaker: Valdis
en: It's a generous offering, Brother. You'd be a fool to turn your back.

speaker: Eivor
en: Refuse this and your shame will stain the name of your sons, and their sons beyond.

speaker: Broder
en: Stay out of this Wolf-Kissed!

speaker: Brothir
en: Take the gift! We have bigger problems.

speaker: Oswald
en: One of Rued's men?

speaker: Brothir
en: Aye. Sniffing around the outer walls, looking for an easy way to slip a few dozen men inside.

speaker: Valdis
en: If there's one scout, there will be more. Something you might have learned if you kept him alive.

speaker: Brothir
en: I was passing water when he surprised me. It was either him or my plow-sword!

speaker: Eivor
en: Valdis is right, there will be others.

speaker: Brothir
en: If I had seen any more, I would have killed them too.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where did you find this one?

speaker: Eivor
en: You did what you had to, Brothir. This one's better off dead.

speaker: Oswald
en: We'll have to act fast if we expect to find others.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where did you find this one?

speaker: Eivor
en: Where did you find this one?

speaker: Brothir
en: Just outside the Northwic walls, by the water's edge.

speaker: Eivor
en: They'll be looking for points of entry, to sneak a herd of raiders through.

speaker: Oswald
en: Jesus. Find another scout, we'll question him.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll look around. The rest of you stay here and out of sight. If I find anyone suspicious, I'll bring him here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rued's scouts would be camped near their boats outside the city walls. One of them will talk.

speaker: Brothir
en: We spotted this one on a boat. If there are others, they might be by the river. Look for anyone suspicious outside the city walls.

speaker: Eivor
en: There. Looks like one of Rued's men.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Wait, wait! What are you doing? I'm just a pig farmer.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're awfully well armed for a pig farmer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay down muck-worm. I have some friends who'd like to speak with you.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Put me down! I tell you, I'm a cow farmer! Let me go, Dane.

speaker: Eivor
en: You said you were a pig farmer just moments ago.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: It... it is not beyond reason. I tend to many livestock!

speaker: Eivor
en: You are as Dane as I am. Save your breath, liar.

speaker: Oswald
en: Did Rued send you too? Speak now and you may live to see tomorrow.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Argr (cowardly) swine.

speaker: Oswald
en: That won't make you any friends here.

speaker: Broder
en: A scolding like that is a mortal offense, boy. I'd kill the bastard. Don't give him time to act again.

speaker: Oswald
en: I'll ask once more. Why were you lurking around Northwic's walls?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: I came to pay my respect, lord... to Oswald, the simpering Saxon ergi (weakling) of East Anglia!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell him why you're here and you may walk free with your head on your neck.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could do that all day, you drooling blood-bladder. Only give me a reason.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have scolded this man twice with forbidden words. It's now his right to kill you.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Lick... my... dung-hole.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here's the tongue I use for licking.

speaker: Eivor
en: How does it feel against your arse?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: When the brazier's lit at Dunwic, Rued and his men will rally. They mean to attack Northwic by its weakest wall.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: You English Danes are soft as butter now. Rued sends his blessing, lady. He'll see you again very soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've served your purpose. Time to die.

speaker: Oswald
en: You promised he'd go free!

speaker: Eivor
en: That's enough to go on. Time to die.

speaker: Oswald
en: That wasn't necessary.

speaker: Eivor
en: He insulted you before everyone gathered here. Don't ever let that go unanswered.

speaker: Eivor
en: He may still be of value to us if he

speaker: Valdis
en: Any man who questions your courage and feels no shame... that's your answer.

speaker: Oswald
en: I will not have blood spilled needlessly in my kingdom! This has to end!

speaker: Eivor
en: Alive, this man was a risk.

speaker: Oswald
en: Valdis. This man spoke as if he knew you.

speaker: Valdis
en: Rued was my husband.

speaker: Oswald
en: Your husband! You're married already?

speaker: Valdis
en: I was. We've been apart for five summers. I never expected to see him here, and I never wanted to.

speaker: Oswald
en: East Anglia's prosperity depends on our safety and unity. With Rued's clan stomping around, neither is possible. I must speak with him myself, man to man. There's no place for him in East Anglia. He must hear it from me.

speaker: Finnr
en: Right. I'll start looking for a new king tomorrow. It was good to know you, lord.

speaker: Broder
en: Rued will eat your lungs for supper, Oswald. Steer clear of him.

speaker: Oswald
en: If I'm to be a worthy king, I must meet the man who bedevils us. I'll light the brazier at Dunwic and face him when he comes.

speaker: Eivor
en: You sure you want to do this? Meeting Rued in the open comes with many risks.

speaker: Oswald
en: It's the only way. We must face him head on, and we cannot waiver.

speaker: Valdis
en: Come, Oswald. We make for Dunwic.

speaker: Eivor
en: And of course, I will see the lot of you there as well, else the songs of your cowardice will ring out over the generations.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sure you're heading to Dunwic any moment.

speaker: Finnr
en: We'll be there, Eivor.

speaker: Broder
en: You don't speak for us, steward.

speaker: Finnr
en: Need I remind you wags what Halfdan will do with us if East Anglia falls into Rued's hands?

speaker: Eivor
en: Dunwic... Rued's men tore through it.

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor, you made it.

speaker: Oswald
en: Dunwic...

speaker: Valdis
en: It is time to light the brazier.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll light it. You do the talking.

speaker: Broder
en: Brothir, Valdis, and I will scout the dock, make sure there are no surprises.

speaker: Finnr
en: Oswald and I will hold here until the brazier is lit.

speaker: Valdis
en: The front gate is heavily guarded. You'll not be walking in.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll find my own way.

speaker: Oswald
en: We'll be watching your back.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dunwic... Now to clear out Rued's men, and light that brazier.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: How long 'til the scouts return? I want to be out there, raiding and pillaging. Not here, scratching my thighs.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: If I know Bjorngeld, he'll be drunk and sober six times before he's back.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Is it true Rued wants that whore Valdis back?

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: You watch your mouth. I would like to see you call her that when she's back. Remember Frode?

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Aye, she had him flogged and laid bare in the square for disrespecting her.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Then shut your mouth before you get us both flogged.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's the last of them. Once the brazier is lit, the rest of Rued's men should arrive.

speaker: Rued
en: Odin gifts me a bargain! A few dead men at my feet in exchange for a ripe East Anglia and my wife returned. What a day!

speaker: Rued
en: You... I don't know you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor of the Raven Clan. The clan your men attacked before I fed them to the crows.

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't need to know my name. You will not have a use for it beyond today.

speaker: Eivor
en: Any questions you have, you ask the King of East Anglia. And bend the knee while you do.

speaker: Rued
en: Who called for me? Was it you, Valdis... my love?

speaker: Valdis
en: Why would I call you now, after five happy years away from your stinking balls?

speaker: Oswald
en: I called you, Rued.

speaker: Rued
en: You? Oswald, the hopeful king of East Anglia?

speaker: Oswald
en: And Valdis's husband-to-be.

speaker: Oswald
en: Take your men and go. East Anglia is strong with Saxons and Danes united. It will not fall to raiders.

speaker: Rued
en: Must I set sail for Denmark with nothing to show for the journey? After coming all this way?

speaker: Oswald
en: You'll have my weight in silver. And an abundance of livestock and grain.

speaker: Rued
en: I've taken ten times that already. What's the real prize? I'll make you an offer, pig-foot. A , just you and me, for the future of your kingdom.

speaker: Oswald
en: I accept. I accept! A fight to the death!

speaker: Rued
en: East Anglia's the prize, let it be heard!

speaker: Rued
en: The hazel is laid! The square is made!

speaker: Oswald
en: When you see a chance, lead Valdis and the brothers to safety. They must not fight today. East Anglia needs them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me be your champion.

speaker: Oswald
en: No. He called on me.

speaker: Rued
en: Whenever you're ready, king of sheep shit!

speaker: Oswald
en: I'm ready.

speaker: Rued
en: Another Saxon king has bent the knee!

speaker: Rued
en: Call me king before I gut you!

speaker: Rued
en: Fighting dirty, are you?

speaker: Rued
en: King Rued commands you to die!

speaker: Valdis
en: Oswald!

speaker: Rued
en: Call me king!

speaker: Eivor
en: Go! Now!

speaker: Eivor
en: Run for the bridge!

speaker: Brothir
en: Go! Go! Go!

speaker: Valdis
en: Move!

speaker: Finnr
en: I'm going!

speaker: Eivor
en: They're breaking off...

speaker: Valdis
en: They've given up for now.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's put some distance between us. We can rest a moment.

speaker: Broder
en: By Thor, he fought well. Raging like a bonfire.

speaker: Finnr
en: We should go back!

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald may have survived. Rued as well.

speaker: Brothir
en: It's possible.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not hold to hope. Few could survive such a fall.

speaker: Broder
en: None could, not from that height.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rued's men will press their advantage. We must be ready when they attack.

speaker: Finnr
en: We'll go to Northwic. Meet me there when you can.

speaker: Valdis
en: He died a hero, there's no doubt. If his god won't take him, Odin's sword-women will.

speaker: Valdis
en: Elmenham will not recover. None of us will.

speaker: Eivor
en: This was Oswald's...

speaker: Valka
en: Eivor! What a pleasure to see you! O dear! It feels like it's been so long!

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka, my friend. You're most welcome here. Are you well?

speaker: Valka
en: Better than well. I am present.

speaker: Eivor
en: And... your mother?

speaker: Valka
en: My mother has found her peace at last. She walks through a world seen only in dreams, and will forevermore.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is all any of us can hope for.

speaker: Valka
en: Indeed. Come.

speaker: Eivor
en: How was your passage?

speaker: Valka
en: Exhilarating. The waves and wind were with us from the start. We flew like seabirds. And how are you? In spite of your stoic look, there is a brightness in your eyes that warms me.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be a kind of hope. Our settlement is growing, the people are happy, and I am... looking forward to more.

speaker: Valka
en: And your visions?

speaker: Eivor
en: They come and go. But leave all that aside. Let me help you with your things.

speaker: Eivor
en: This way. We found a fine spot for you at the foot of the hill.

speaker: Valka
en: Hm... every hour we traveled, I tried to conjure in my mind some vision of this place.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how close were you?

speaker: Valka
en: I saw the trees and the water and the rolling hill. But I could not foresee so much... green! It is magnificent and calming color. A balm for sea-salted eyes.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Valka! Gods above, what brings you? Hope there isn't a curse on the settlement or some such.

speaker: Valka
en: Ha! The only curse on this place is their great lout of a blacksmith.

speaker: Valka
en: It is a rare feeling to travel across the sea and still find oneself at home. This place feels powerful. Alive.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you foresee great things for us?

speaker: Valka
en: No need for foresight. I feel it in my heart.

speaker: Randvi
en: Is that Valka I see? What took you so long to follow?

speaker: Valka
en: Wanted to ensure the place was up to snuff. We must talk again soon, Randvi, once I'm settled.

speaker: Eivor
en: And before my arms fall off. What is this I'm carrying?

speaker: Valka
en: My heaviest reagents, of course. Lead, whalebone, flecks of gold.

speaker: Randvi
en: Put this one to honest work, that is what I like to see!

speaker: Valka
en: All these people you have brought here, this life you have built on these stranger shores. Does it please you?

speaker: Eivor
en: It does. To know that I have built this place and kept these people safe is a gift.

speaker: Valka
en: You speak first of yourself when I ask this question... which says more than you intend, I think.

speaker: Octavian
en: Salve, Eivor! Ad meliora! (Towards better things!)

speaker: Eivor
en: Good day!

speaker: Valka
en: And who's that fellow?

speaker: Eivor
en: Octavian. A strange man. I think you'll like him.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no idea.

speaker: Valka
en: Well, the town must be bustling.

speaker: Eivor
en: You see there, your home is just ahead.

speaker: Valka
en: Tell me about your visions.

speaker: Eivor
en: They are as they have always been. Little has changed, save their clarity. With every return, the things I see feel less like dreams and more like memories.

speaker: Valka
en: And does the All-Father still appear before you?

speaker: Eivor
en: From time to time, yes. He speaks to me as well, but... it feels mad to say such things aloud.

speaker: Valka
en: I understand. You can put those just there, thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: And here we are.

speaker: Valka
en: Lovely, just as you promised. As soon as I am set up here, we can return to the matter of your visions.

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka, please...

speaker: Valka
en: You are touched, Eivor. A conduit for godly tidings. Please... let me help. I may know a way to clarify these visions. An elixir that may open the door of your mind into the realm of the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you think it would help, I can finish your home myself. Only give me some time.

speaker: Valka
en: I would be grateful. Thank you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course. And... welcome home.

speaker: Vili
en: This is an excellent shield, Sunniva. Gunnar's craft never disappoints.

speaker: Eivor
en: And here, from the Raven Clan

speaker: Vili
en: An impressive shield!

speaker: Eivor
en: It is good, but it needs a touch of grandeur. Something personal for your father. A sigil, I think. A mark to adorn the front. We need an artisan. Is there one in the village?

speaker: Vili
en: I know a man. A master craftsman in exile. He lives in a cave northeast of Hemthorpe. I would take you there myself, but I have Isbjorn to retrieve.

speaker: Eivor
en: Isbjorn? Your father's spear? Did he not wield it at Ulkerthorpe?

speaker: Vili
en: He lost it some winters back on a bear hunt. He hit the beast hard, but the spear stuck and the bear fled into the forest.

speaker: Eivor
en: And after all these winters you hope to find it again and present it to the pyre? The odds are narrow to say the least.

speaker: Vili
en: Fret not, friend. I have a nose for these things. Seek out the exile. He'll see to your shield.

speaker: Vili
en: Head on to the cavern, Eivor. Isbjorn awaits me elsewhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be the cave Vili mentioned. Who would live here?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Exile must value his solitude, living in a hole such as this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin's beard.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a difficult man to find.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hemming Jarl is dead.

speaker: Hermit
en: Hm.

speaker: Eivor
en: I was told you're a master craftsman. I seek an etching on this shield, to celebrate the life and death of Hemming Jarl.

speaker: Hermit
en: The stones... Hemming Jarl possesse a steady hand and steady heart. Do you possess the same?

speaker: Hermit
en: Your heart is not yet steady.

speaker: Eivor
en: How could it be at such a time?

speaker: Hermit
en: Hemming Jarl's heart never wavered.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. Hemming's heart was as steady as it was large.

speaker: Eivor
en: In life, it did not. But in death, it lies as still as a stone.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are you? A friend of Hemming's? Or man exiled by his order?

speaker: Hermit
en: It does not matter who I was. I am nameless now. I am no one.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have not yet answered me. Will you help with my etching?

speaker: Hermit
en: Hm...

speaker: Hermit
en: How will you remember him?

speaker: Eivor
en: By his unraveled prowess on the battlefield.

speaker: Hermit
en: Ah. Gungnir, then. Odin's faultless spear. A symbol of power. Is this your choice?

speaker: Eivor
en: By his wisdom, always an inspiration.

speaker: Hermit
en: The Web of Wyrd then. Nine lines that write our fates. Past, present, and future entwined. Is that what you desire?

speaker: Eivor
en: By his determination to keep his clan safe and his people celebrated.

speaker: Hermit
en: The marks of . Sights never lost. Is this your decision?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I choose this one.

speaker: Hermit
en: I will begin.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you come to be here?

speaker: Hermit
en: Fate. I was given a death sentence. Unfairly I felt, but a man was killed. Hemming Jarl desired for me to live. The villagers ... did not. My sight and exile. That was our compromise.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you for this.

speaker: Hermit
en: His son will take his place?

speaker: Eivor
en: That is for Vili to decide.

speaker: Hermit
en: Vili has no say. Fate has already decided.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hemming would be pleased with our gift. I wonder if Vili has found his spear.

speaker: Thrall 1
en: They've been feasting for days in that hall. None for us lowly thralls, though.

speaker: Thrall 2
en: The brewery's almost dry, and still they call for more in Aegir's hall.

speaker: Thrall 3
en: Aegir's daughters haven's stopped reveling since he left.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 1
en: A newcomer! Wet your throat with us, and be merry!

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: Come drink with us, stranger!

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 3
en: Over here! Pay respect to the mistresses of the feast.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: Be welcome, Æsir. Our father's hall is a haven to all.

speaker: Havi
en: I remember there was a cauldron here once, brought by Thor from Hymir's hall.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 1
en: A cauldron a mile deep. A mile of mead. I miss that cauldron.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 3
en: Father bet the cauldron on a foolish wager with Suttungr and lost. But we still have the ale from our brewery!

speaker: Havi
en: Where is Aegir now?

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: Gone to Utgard. He sent the cauldron to Suttungr, but it never got there. So he's gone to find out what's what. But enough of that. You are visitor to our great land, and we know its secrets. Ask of us your questions.

speaker: Havi
en: I want to know the unknown. Where should I look?

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: There is a broken tower near Utgard that was once a place of great magic. Perhaps there is still some to be found there.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 1
en: To magic! May we never be without it!

speaker: Havi
en: Skal!

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: Let us tell you more about our homeland!

speaker: Havi
en: What animals will I find in the wild?

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 1
en: I have heard tell of a great bear of stone and ice that lives by a frozen lake.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: Enough talk! Time for a drink!

speaker: Havi
en: Skal!

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: Let us tell you more about our homeland!

speaker: Havi
en: Spin me a tale of tragedy.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: Once, Thor dashed the great serpent Jörmungandr against our shores. Many ships wrecked, many Jotnar drowned.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 1
en: Seek a lonely tree on the shore and walk beneath it. You will see. Now let us drink to the fallen.

speaker: Havi
en: Skal!

speaker: Havi
en: My thanks for your hospitality. I must go.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: You don't look well. Is our ale taking a toll on you?

speaker: Havi
en: Urgh! Tastes like a boar shat in my mouth. Where am I? I should... I should find out what I did while ale-addled. My mind is blank.

speaker: Havi
en: Ripe with wine and vomit. These are thrall's clothes. Where did they come from?

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 2
en: King Snortington demands tribute! Don't make us lock you up like we did your Aesir friend!

speaker: Havi
en: King Snortington the boar... once a prisoner, now free... I think we even made up a song about it.

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 3
en: Well, hello there. You turned out to have quite a head for heights.

speaker: Havi
en: I think I remember... being up high? How did we get the cart up there?

speaker: Daughter of Aegir 1
en: To the mighty reavers of the Ale Sea! The mice in the brewery still tell tales of last night's voyage.

speaker: Havi
en: Were we trying to sail somewhere? Across the Ale Sea to the land of... of... I can't recall it.

speaker: Havi
en: We made wild revels, it seems. But no harm done, except to my head. Aegir's daughters are hospitable indeed.

speaker: Cedric
en: If you don't give me Aelfred's jewel, I'll... I'll... widdle in your duck pond! This is your last warning! Give me Aelfred's trinket, or I'll piddle in your pond! Is this what you want, you filthy swindler? A pond full of piss? I'm happy to oblige. By God's hairy balls, you are a thief and a swindler! Give me the jewel Aelfred commissioned. I'll wear your guts as a hat. Give me Aelfred's jewel, you damn scoundrel. We have already paid for it.

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem agitated.

speaker: Cedric
en: What gave it away? The fact that I had to debase myself pissing in this swindler's pond? Or the angry shouting?

speaker: Eivor
en: This man has something of yours?

speaker: Cedric
en: And here's another God sent to shit in my stewpot. Sod off unless you are going to magic Aelfred's jewel out your arse.

speaker: Eivor
en: If the jewel belongs to Aelfred, it might be worth a pretty penny.

speaker: Jeweller
en: Oi, get out of it, you!

speaker: Jeweller
en: You! What are you doing here?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not your enemy... yet. But that man outside certainly wants Aelfred's jewel.

speaker: Jeweller
en: Jesus wept upon the Holy Cross. Fuck off the both of you. Aelfred will get the jewel when I get what I'm owed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Peace, or you'll feel my blade in your guts.

speaker: Jeweller
en: Sorry, my beef is not with you. I only ask for what coin is fair. It cost me double to make over what was agreed. I have a wife to feed.

speaker: Eivor
en: The jewel is for the king? Here's your money. Now, give me the trinket.

speaker: Jeweller
en: Gladly. And I don't care whether you give it to Cedric or not. He has all the finesse of a mad cow in bloomers.

speaker: Eivor
en: If the jewel belongs to Aelfred, then on your life, you'd be wise to deliver it for the agreed price.

speaker: Jeweller
en: Mary on a donkey! You deserve the bloody thing. It's not worth my hide. Much as my wife would love to be a widow.

speaker: Eivor
en: If the trinket is for Aelfred, I think I'll just take it.

speaker: Jeweller
en: Lord have mercy on me.

speaker: Jeweller
en: Enough of this, the guards will deal with you!

speaker: Cedric
en: You should have given me the jewel as agreed!

speaker: Jeweller
en: I'll break into your house and piss on your wife! I'm not taking this lying down. I can tell you that for the price of a warm beer.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have your jewel.

speaker: Cedric
en: Well, I didn't ask for your help, but I am glad of it. Aelfred commissioned this rare thing.

speaker: Eivor
en: How rare?

speaker: Cedric
en: Filigreed gold, centered with a rock crystal and enamel plaque. A miniature of our most beatific Lord, Jesus Christ... and... And you're going to just keep it, aren't you?

speaker: Cedric
en: And I have to tell the king I let a Dane steal his gift to his wife?

speaker: Eivor
en: You do. And also this. Every treasure he has, I'll take. Every poet who writes him into song will sing threefold of me. Because we are Vikingr, and this green and pleasant land will be ours.

speaker: Cedric
en: Bollocks.

speaker: Cedric
en: Return the treasure and we will forget we met.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop following me, or the jewel will not be the only thing you will lose today.

speaker: Cedric
en: Holy splinters from the cross. Alright, take it.

speaker: Eivor
en: You may have it. But tell your king it will all be mine soon enough. His jewels. His treasures. His city. His throne.

speaker: Cedric
en: What? No, I... God's pearly tooth! Here's payment for you and we will both forget this meeting.

speaker: Griseld
en: This madness has gone on long enough, Father. Untie me! Now!

speaker: Bad Father
en: To be honest, Griseld, the more you nag, the more I think we would all be better off if Aflanc just claimed you.

speaker: Griseld
en: Any time a woman dares to question you, that's your solution. Drown them in the river.

speaker: Bad Father
en: Your mother ran off to Swanage with your Uncle Acwel.

speaker: Griseld
en: I do not have an Uncle Acwel!

speaker: Griseld
en: You, stranger. Help me talk some sense into him, will you?

speaker: Eivor
en: This is your daughter? Why have you tied her up?

speaker: Bad Father
en: Because if I don't, she just runs off. Foreigns and their stupid questions.

speaker: Griseld
en: My father thinks a satanic sea beast, Aflanc the Terrible, sent floods to our farms. My sacrifice is to appease him.

speaker: Bad Father
en: We don't think. We know. Godfrey saw Aflanc with his own eyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: So you are going to throw your daughter in the lake and hope the beast accepts your offering? She'll more likely drown.

speaker: Bad Father
en: You're making it sound stupid when you say it like that. Look, there he is! He breaches the water, do you not see his demonic flippers?

speaker: Eivor
en: I would run if I were you. Your father is mad.

speaker: Griseld
en: Thank you. But until this demon is proven nothing but driftwood, I still might find myself a watery tart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sea beasts and demons. There is something fishy afoot.

speaker: Eivor
en: So this is their devil? I will find something to prove it is just a shipwreck.

speaker: Eivor
en: This should convince them not to sacrifice the girl to Aflanc.

speaker: Griseld
en: Well? Was it nothing but driftwood?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your sea beast was just a sunken ship.

speaker: Griseld
en: What? But this is something that any swimming fool could have discovered. No offence.

speaker: Godfrey
en: I told him. I told him it was nothing. But he wouldn't listen.

speaker: Bad Father
en: Shut up, you fool.

speaker: Godfrey
en: Said you plague him day and night. Complaining about his drinking, calling him a layabout.

speaker: Griseld
en: Father, you knew? That there was nothing there? So... this was your solution to be rid of me?

speaker: Bad Father
en: You're as bad as your mother. Nothing is ever good enough. I'm sick of listening to it!

speaker: Eivor
en: An elaborate ruse for so simple a problem.

speaker: Griseld
en: This cannot be forgiven. Murder was on your mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: You deserve reparation. Speak your justice and I will enforce it.

speaker: Griseld
en: Thank you, stranger. Leave, Father, leave my home and my life. Your actions have made me an orphan.

speaker: Godfrey
en: And know this. If you ever return, you'll be punished for your crimes. Come, Griseld, I shall be your rock now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Live well, Griseld, free from your father's mischief.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Can anybody hear me? Help! That didn't work out at all as you planned, did it? O, Alisa. You silly, silly girl.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that a child I hear?

speaker: Eivor
en: The cries are coming from inside that cave.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay there, girl! I will help you out.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: O, thank you, thank you! I thought I was going to die in here! I give myself very good advice, but I very seldom follow it.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're hurt. Hold on, I'll carry you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: That's the last time I go chasing rabbits. Especially white ones. Now, just a little rest, and I'll be ready for more adventures!

speaker: Eivor
en: You hurt yourself hunting a rabbit?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Hunting? No! He just seemed, well, in a hurry. I wanted to see where he was going.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take care with that curiosity, girl. You never know where it might lead. Farewell.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Tis done?

speaker: Eivor
en: Here are your blood-soaked bits of amber.

speaker: Deirdre
en: I felt them die, each by each.

speaker: Eivor
en: Boil these shards, make your potion.

speaker: Deirdre
en: I shall, I shall. I've been preparing for this since we met.

speaker: Eivor
en: You spoke of great power.

speaker: Deirdre
en: The spear. You'll have it in your hands soon enough. Once you defeat Balor.

speaker: Eivor
en: You said nothing of this.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Surely you remember Balor. He is heat, draught, the scorching sun come to earth.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know of no such creature.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Many heroes fell to him, but Wodin would not. The lance called Gae Bolg pierces his flesh. This is where he is weak.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Are you ready to fight him?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me drink.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Drink deeply. You'll remember. Balor is ancient. He is chaos itself.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Defeat him, and the spear is yours.

speaker: Balor
en: I have waited for you these many centuries, Fjölnir.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have come to take your power.

speaker: Balor
en: Come, take it, then.

speaker: Balor
en: You are twice-blind to believe you can defeat me. Which eye do you lack? Now! Come forward! Watch out! Cú Chulainn fell before me. You will be next.

speaker: Balor
en: I am the wrath of the sun. I will scorch you to cinders!

speaker: Balor
en: You best be careful. Don't fall asleep! No one can harm me! I'll suck the marrow from your bones! Fear my eye of fire! I will enjoy this! Show me your strength. You are puny. You amuse me. Return to ash! COME ON! FACE ME! Fool! Burn to oblivion!

speaker: Balor
en: I am Balor!

speaker: Eivor
en: What have I defeated? I must speak to Deirdre.

speaker: Deirdre
en: I felt you would prevail.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was an unusual contest.

speaker: Deirdre
en: The spear Gae Bolg is yours for crushing the Children of Danu and defeating Balor.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Despite all that's happened, Ciara will find solace that the Danu have been extinguished.

speaker: Eivor
en: Small comfort, I suspect.

speaker: Deirdre
en: I thank you for sparing her. Someday she may return to us here in the forest. Her spirit will be welcome.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Ciara would have been joyful that the Danu have been extinguished.

speaker: Eivor
en: She was once one of them. It swayed her reason.

speaker: Deirdre
en: I am sorry your path was fated to cross hers. But if it hadn't a sorry state would be on us all.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Ciara will be pleased the Danu have been quenched.

speaker: Eivor
en: She fights for those she calls "true druids."

speaker: Deirdre
en: Keep the spear close, Eivor. I sense a great battle ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Goodbye, Deirdre.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Slán (Goodbye), Eivor. Slán.

speaker: Norse Girl
en: The seats have spoken! Frode, write this down! Let it be known that candied pears emerge the victor this day!

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Aw, no!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: We hereby decree that only candied pears shall be served at feasts! Now everyone back to your starting positions!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Onto the next ruling! Shall we play in the woods or down by the river tomorrow?

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Stools on the hay-side are for the woods, and the side with the sacks of beans for the river. Pick your seats! No pushing, Bjornsson! I'm watching you!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Well, this is not good. It's a draw! This has never happened!

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Hm... what about the Tall One? Can we ask her to help break this tie!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Good idea, Frode! Tall One, sit by the hay-side if you vote for the woods! For the river... the side with the sacks of beans!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Come on, Tall One!

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Hay-side stools for the woods, side with the sacks of beans for the river!

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Hey! Hey, where are you going!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: The Tall One does not want to play, because the Tall One is a big baby.

speaker: Norse Girl
en: The answer is clear! We shall play in the woods tomorrow!

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Now, on to the next great matter...

speaker: Norse Girl
en: The answer is clear! We shall play in the river tomorrow!

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Now, the next matter for our Althing...

speaker: Norse Girl
en: We need a name for our merry band. The choices are Raiders of the Cake or the Shadow Dragons!

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Stools on the hay-side are for Raiders of the Cake, and side with the sacks of beans for Shadow Dragons! Pick your seats!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Tall One, you too! Just in case we end up in a tie again!

speaker: Norse Boy
en: It looks like we are tied... for now.

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Tall One, we need your help once more!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Come on, Tall One!

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Hay-side stools for Raiders of the Cake, side with the sack of beans for The Shadow Dragons!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: It is final! We shall henceforth be called Raiders of the Cake!

speaker: Norse Boy 2
en: I like cake!

speaker: Eivor
en: They are delicious.

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Now, on to the next vote...

speaker: Norse Girl
en: It is final! From now on, we are the Shadow Dragons!

speaker: Eivor
en: A fitting name for future warriors.

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Roar! Now, to our next vote...

speaker: Norse Girl
en: What should we do if we manage to capture a Pict soldier? Stools on the hay-side are for beating him up! Side with the sacks of beans for taking him prisoner! Vote!

speaker: Norse Boy
en: It looks like we are tied... for now.

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Tall One, we need your help once more!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Hurry, Tall One! We don't have much time left to play!

speaker: Norse Boy
en: Hay-side stools for beating up the enemy! Side with the sacks of beans for taking him prisoner to be questioned!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: The seats have spoken! We shall show no mercy! The Badge of Courage will be given to those who voted as such! You too, Tall One!

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, children. Remember, never go easy on your enemies!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Frode! Write that down! The Tall One's words will be remembered!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: The seats have spoken! We will take the prisoner for questioning! The Badge of Wisdom shall be awarded to those who voted for this! You too, Tall One!

speaker: Eivor
en: Remember, the more you know of your enemy the better. Do not let any opportunity to learn more of them escape you.

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Frode! You had better be writing these words of wisdom down!

speaker: Norse Girl
en: Thanks for the help, Tall One.

speaker: Eivor
en: The next generation inspires confidence. Snotinghamscire is in good hands.

speaker: Norse Man
en: This is taking too long. I need more fire, more oil! They must burn, they must burn... Please! My family, they've died injustly. They need to be burned! But this fire won't do. I must burn them before they turn into vengeful draugrs. There must be something around here that burns...

speaker: Eivor
en: Oil jars for the fire. This should be enough.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Thank you! Thank you. Now may they rest in peace...

speaker: Eivor
en: Will they truly rest? You said the draugrs, your family no less, would return vengeful.

speaker: Norse Man
en: It's my fault. I killed them. My greed robbed me of my senses and now my family. My brother was to inherit my father's wealth. But it was my right! They callled me a lout, a disgrace. They were right. Now our family fortune sits in the house. Worthless when there is nobody left to enjoy it with. A favor, I beg of you. Slay me so I may join them in Helheim and beg their forgiveness.

speaker: Eivor
en: Men like you deserve something worse than death. I hope your family condemns you, even in Helheim.

speaker: Azar
en: Good day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar, is everything all right?

speaker: Azar
en: Yes. No. It will be once that bastard is dead and hanging from my rafters as sausages.

speaker: Eivor
en: I believe I know who this is about.

speaker: Azar
en: Konstantinos has come to Ireland. Yesternight, his ship pulled into the bay.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will deliver you his head.

speaker: Azar
en: Your offer is appreciated, Eivor, but not necessary

speaker: Eivor
en: He threatens our trade, does he not? I protect my greater interest and provide my partner a service.

speaker: Azar
en: Very well. But do not deprive me of my revenge. Bring him back to me alive.

speaker: Eivor
en: Konstantinos's ship pulled into Dublin's bay. I should look for him there.

speaker: Eivor
en: The white-haired one must be Konstantinos. Azar awaits him.

speaker: Irish Woman 1
en: Set up camp here?

speaker: Konstantinos
en: As good as spot as any. We won't be on this dog shit island long. Just until we collect Azar's head.

speaker: Konstantinos
en: I can't walk.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's the idea. Your one-time partner is eager to see you.

speaker: Konstantinos
en: That thrice-cursed harpy should have been long dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Save your insults for your reunion.

speaker: Konstantinos
en: I'd hoped to finish you this time.

speaker: Azar
en: You were always careless.

speaker: Konstantinos
en: At least I took your eye. And your brother, the sniveling sop! Along with your loud bitch of a screaming mother. Come on, have at it. Let's end this quickly.

speaker: Azar
en: Quickly? O, no. No, no, my dear Konstantinos. This will last a very long time, indeed. Why else have I sharpened so many implements? I will unmake you tenfold for what you've done.

speaker: Konstantinos
en: You make a sorry cyclops.

speaker: Konstantinos
en: Damn you to hell. (Screams)

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar. What of Konstantinos?

speaker: Azar
en: Hogs feed on his bits.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you at peace?

speaker: Azar
en: At peace? No. But the world is a better place.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: That traitor is lost in Hel by now.

speaker: Soma
en: They will have the lost souls of the dead to answer to.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma.

speaker: Soma
en: Eivor. You're still with me through all this. Do not think I'll forget.

speaker: Eivor
en: We all need someone in dark times. Now let's collect Wigmund's head.

speaker: Soma
en: Good. At the first sign of trouble, my crew will jump in.

speaker: Soma
en: He's hiding. At the summit of the hill. I can smell him.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope he likes the view. It's the last he'll ever see.

speaker: Soma
en: Lightning tingles my blood, Eivor! I hear the voices of my slaughtered people on the air, calling Wigmund's name.

speaker: Eivor
en: He doesn't leave this monastery alive.

speaker: Soma
en: My palms itch. Where is that rat? I'm going to skin him alive. On sight. I will tear his throat from his neck with my teeth.

speaker: Soma
en: Wigmund! I want to see the light leave your eyes! Old dogs die slow, Wigmund! You can't delay your fate! My blade bays for your life, Wigmund!

speaker: Wigmund
en: We were led by the hand! Into the bowels of Grantebridge, and still we could not hold the city? That raving pagan handed me Grantebridge on a plate! And you dirty ' lost it for me!

speaker: Soma
en: You'll die in agony, bacraut (asshole)!

speaker: Wigmund
en: You can't kill me, Soma! Not truly. For what I am is unkillable!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop flapping your mouth and DIE!

speaker: Wigmund
en: Stop the heathen! Raider! Vikingr! Stop her!

speaker: Wigmund
en: She means to erase me! To banish me from your minds! Fight in my name! Die for me! Die for me!

speaker: Odin
en: That is no way to call for sacrifices.

speaker: Eivor
en: Their lives for yours. Is that how it works?

speaker: Wigmund
en: Their lives meant nothing. No land, no riches, no titles! But my name will live on.

speaker: Eivor
en: The reputation of a good man never dies. But your name will soon be a curse.

speaker: Wigmund
en: So be it. The riches I had in life gave me power.

speaker: Wigmund
en: To curse me from beyond the grave gives me still more.

speaker: Wigmund
en: Though I die, my order lives on elsewhere, everywhere.

speaker: Wigmund
en: Yield to us! Give us what we are owed! The trade, the riches, the legacy. All of it! Yield! Yield! Yield!

speaker: Eivor
en: If your Hell is real, I'm glad you'll get to see it.

speaker: Soma
en: We should return to camp. Before I let go, and burn this heap to the ground. Going forward, I must take care. Houses can be built anew, crops will return with time, but trust... that will take longer to repair.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you have a new friend and ally in me and my clan, Soma. The end of the storm is well in sight.

speaker: Soma
en: You're right, I know you're right. It's just... it's difficult to see that end when you're still in the storm's eye.

speaker: Letter to Order of the Ancients
en: Members of the Order, There has been a resurgence. The Danes of Grantebridge have banded together with the help of an outsider. They've retaken the city and destroyed my operations. I am cut off. I have gathered what men I have left and taken to a monastery on the Isle of Ely. I will remain here until you (the letter ends abruptly)

speaker: Soma
en: Eivor, you've been a guiding light. Calling out Galinn like that, exposing his treachery, made me sick with a quiet terror.

speaker: Eivor
en: A betrayal like that is already a kind of death. Galinn killed himself.

speaker: Soma
en: Of course. And now I feel somewhat lifted. The weight is almost gone... even if my heart needs mending. Ah, while I have you, Eivor, I'm reminded...

speaker: Eivor
en: I'd have done the same in your position.

speaker: Soma
en: That is calming to hear. Which reminds me...'

speaker: Eivor
en: A betrayal like that is already a kind of death. Galinn killed himself.

speaker: Soma
en: Of course. And now I feel somewhat lifted. The weight is almost gone... even if my heart needs mending. Ah, while I have you, Eivor, I'm reminded...

speaker: Soma
en: I have this for you. Keep it, knowing you have my highest respect, regard, and trust. My army is yours should you need it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma Jarlskona... my deepest thanks.

speaker: Soma
en: And... there's something else. As we prepared our assault, Birna had a word with me. We came to a sort of... understanding. It may be best if she tells you herself. Until next time, Eivor of the Raven Clan. I hope we will see you in Grantebridge soon.

speaker: Birna
en: Eivor...

speaker: Eivor
en: Birna, you struck quite a victory today.

speaker: Birna
en: Don't undercut your own ferocity, drengr. It was your blade leading the charge! You are indeed something to behold.

speaker: Eivor
en: We all fought hard. And now Grantebridge is yours. You have your home once again.

speaker: Birna
en: Bah. Soon merchants and priests and reeves (sheriffs) will run loose in its streets. All of its muddy charms will dwindle. Besides, with no room for me in Soma's heart, my home burned away in a quiet little house fire.

speaker: Birna
en: Her priority is Grantebridge and the people in it. That is noble, and beyond what I will ever understand. So I've decided I'm of better use elsewhere. With you, in your crew!

speaker: Eivor
en: You want to live with the Raven Clan?

speaker: Birna
en: And sail and raid with you. If you'll have me.

speaker: Birna
en: And look at this... who wouldn't?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll be happy to have you, drengr.

speaker: Birna
en: A relief to these ears... I've already packed my bags.

speaker: Eivor
en: Galinn? What are you doing?

speaker: Galinn
en: We are at the mountain's peak, Soma. With room for one alone. So I claim this summit, jarlskona. I claim Grantebridge.

speaker: Soma
en: You fucking rodent, Galinn. It was you. You let those Saxon insects into our home. You betrayed us!

speaker: Galinn
en: It was preordained, Soma. Like the sunset, like the birds' flight.

speaker: Eivor
en: You coward. You let an innocent die in your place.

speaker: Soma
en: You have your sibling in the bloodspring at your mercy. How could you waste your family so easily?

speaker: Galinn
en: There is no river of blood deep enough to keep my from my destiny.

speaker: Galinn
en: Only one verse of this song remains. It is my destiny to rule, it is your destiny to die. All of you!

speaker: Galinn
en: We all have our One Day.

speaker: Galinn
en: You cannot thwart the gods! You cannot change destiny!

speaker: Eivor
en: Destiny? If you kick a hornet's nest, it's not "destiny" when you get stung!

speaker: Soma
en: You were mad and naked on the moors and I folded you into my family! I trusted you!

speaker: Galinn
en: As it was foretold... as it was seen! Fling yourself from the mountaintop! Cling not to a place that isn't yours!

speaker: Soma
en: Fuck your prophecy, your lies!

speaker: Galinn
en: My vision has come to pass! I stand at the mountain's peak!

speaker: Eivor
en: You stand on the bodies of your brethren!

speaker: Galinn
en: H-how...?

speaker: Soma
en: Such a heavy price to pay for one so vile.

speaker: Galinn
en: I climbed to the peak of the mountain... to my... my destiny.

speaker: Soma
en: Your vision took you as far as the mountain's peak. But there was only room for one to stand.

speaker: Soma
en: I am the one standing.

speaker: Galinn
en: Please, Soma... my life in the lap of the gods. Please...

speaker: Soma
en: Lif? Lif, you're alive!

speaker: Eivor
en: These wounds are deep. You're lucky to be breathing.

speaker: Lif
en: Not luck. Tactics. Evil men like to talk.

speaker: Soma
en: Let's get him back to the longboats. We're going home.

speaker: Eivor
en: His wounds are deep, but he'll recover.

speaker: Soma
en: I should have guessed it was Galinn.

speaker: Soma
en: If I'd trusted my instincts, if I had dealt with all this alone, or discovered him sooner...

speaker: Eivor
en: Galinn deceived us all. He was a practiced liar.

speaker: Eivor
en: Galinn deceived us all. He was a practiced liar.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma, forgive me. I followed my judgment as best I could, but I was wrong. I'm responsible.

speaker: Soma
en: We killed the wrong warrior, Eivor. A terrible truth that tastes of soot and ashes.

speaker: Soma
en: Do not think I blame you. I held the blade. The decision was my own. Now I must explain myself to my people.

speaker: Eivor
en: The cost of war is always high, and victory can be sour. But you have your city back. And Wigmund is dead.

speaker: Soma
en: As may be all trust in me. After all, why should any trust me if I cannot trust my closest friends?

speaker: Eivor
en: Trusting people by their words, their deeds is as much as anyone can expect.

speaker: Eivor
en: But for you, it bit back like a rabid dog.

speaker: Soma
en: That's how I feel. Exactly.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is easy to think so little of other, to harden against the world. It's more difficult to trust those around you.

speaker: Soma
en: And does its difficulty make it more valuable?

speaker: Eivor
en: I think so. You are burdened with so much already. Do not let a serrated heart burden you too.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a lonely life, to live without trust.

speaker: Soma
en: It is the life of anyone with sense.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you are sustained by your people, Soma. To deem no person worthy of trust is to starve yourself.

speaker: Soma
en: Thank you for standing at my side in this. You have my oath and my arm in the battle to come, Eivor of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. One day I may need them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Galinn? What are you doing?

en: We are at the mountain's peak, Soma. With room for one alone. So I claim this summit, jarlskona. I claim Grantebridge.

en: As it was foretold... as it was seen! Fling yourself from the mountaintop! Cling not to a place that isn't yours!

en: Fuck your prophecy, your lies!

en: Your vision took you as far as the mountain's peak. But there was only room for one to stand.

en: I am the one standing.

speaker: Galinn
en: Please, Soma... my life in the lap of the gods. Please...

speaker: Soma
en: You live! Sweet gods among us, Birna, you're alive.

speaker: Birna
en: Galinn couldn't kill me. It's not my destiny.

speaker: Soma
en: Get this drengr back to the longboats. We're going home.

speaker: Eivor
en: Her wounds are severe, but not seeping. She will heal.

speaker: Soma
en: I should have guessed it was Galinn.

speaker: Soma
en: If I'd trusted my instincts, if I had dealt with all this alone, or discovered him sooner...

en: Galinn deceived us all. He was a practiced liar.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. One day I may need them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, it seems the wind calls me back to Randvi. Best tell her the good news.

speaker: Eivor
en: What of Essexe?

speaker: Randvi
en: We received a summons from the ealdorman and his Lady of Colcestre, requesting you specifically, for "a matter of great secrecy."

speaker: Eivor
en: Foreboding. And who is this ealdorman? One of King Aelfred's lackeys?

speaker: Randvi
en: According to my scouts, he is a man who cares more of his own indulgences than the safety of his people. Approach with care.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will leave at once.

speaker: Randvi
en: An alliance in Essex would be invaluable. But go with caution.

speaker: Eivor
en: The people here look poor and hungry.

speaker: Eivor
en: It seems Ealdorman Birstan has made this ruin his longhouse.

speaker: Wyatt
en: Why is my cup empty?

speaker: Aldrich
en: Perhaps because you have drunk the barrel dry?

speaker: Wyatt
en: Damn Birstan! His household is as poorly run as his lands!

speaker: Eadred
en: Estrid is a good wife, far better than he deserves.

speaker: Wyatt
en: You would say that, Eadred. Your wife acts like a sow in a skirt.

speaker: Eadred
en: My Sweterun is a worthy woman, you coxcomb! She's an excellent cook

speaker: Wyatt
en: With a fine nose for truffles!

speaker: Eadred
en: If Birstan does not return soon, wine will not be the only thing spilled upon his floors.

speaker: Aldrich
en: Now, gentlemen, everyone is fractious with this waiting. Let us be civil at least.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lord.

speaker: Wyatt
en: Ah! A heroic-looking Dane in our midst.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for Birstan, ealdorman of this shire.

speaker: Wyatt
en: Our lord is not at home. But his wife is receiving visitors upstairs, in her usual fashion. If you speak with her, pass on that we have run out of ale.

speaker: Gisele
en: Birstan's thegns disrespect you, lady. Sour ale in the air, muddy boot steps all over the floors! Ces Anglais sont des cochons. (These English are pigs.)

speaker: Estrid
en: Les anglais sont des hommes. (These English are men.)

speaker: Gisele
en: And they've eaten us out of hearth and home! We have but one cask of ale and two roasted pheasants left.

speaker: Estrid
en: Let us hope Birstan has at least killed a boar or two, or his thegns will add inhospitality to their list of complaints.

speaker: Gisele
en: Cochons! (Pigs!) Filthy swine!

speaker: Estrid
en: Chut, ma chere (Shh, my love). There is no use fretting.

speaker: Estrid
en: You! Guards will come at one cry from me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sheathe your blade, lady. I am Eivor of the Raven Clan, here at your husband's request.

speaker: Gisele
en: Another Dane.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Estrid, wife of the Lord of Essexe. As you may have heard, my lord is not at home.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am weary rounding up Saxons. Is your husband stolen, drunk, or wayward?

speaker: Eivor
en: If he's away, I'll speak to you.

speaker: Estrid
en: O, that you could, Eivor. For I am sure this hall would shake with our merry wit. But your accord must reached with him.

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't strike me as a meek Saxon wife.

speaker: Estrid
en: Do you yet see an ember of my Frankish fire, Raven-walker? Perhaps it dances in my eyes?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am weary rounding up Saxons. Is your husband stolen, drunk, or wayward?

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't speak as one from here. Where is your home?

speaker: Estrid
en: These rain-sodden bogs and fog-washed hill are not my home, thank Christ. I come from Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: My grandfather walked on Frankish sod. He spoke of an appetite for conquest that rivaled our own.

speaker: Estrid
en: Sadly, my conquests are reduced to pettish thegns and graceless men. All Frankish fire extinguished.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am weary rounding up Saxons. Is your husband stolen, drunk, or wayward?

speaker: Estrid
en: He'll be stalking the woodlands today, hunting games and ignoring the vital affairs of Essexe. One such affair is why we called for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I can find him, I'll remind him of his duties.

speaker: Estrid
en: Such would be a miracle. His favorite haunt is southwest of here. The lavender fields there attract the prey, God help him.

speaker: Eivor
en: With luck, he hasn't been eaten. But I'll return either way.

speaker: Estrid
en: Patience is a godly virtue, Eadred.

speaker: Eadred
en: Even the saints would tire of waiting for Birstan to hang up his bow. Dear Estrid, we must discuss the affairs of this land, with or without him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunting is a fine sport, but I hope the ealdorman has not become the prey. No good comes from a camp this bloody.

speaker: Eivor
en: The remains of the hunting party. This one was savaged by a large animal.

speaker: Eivor
en: They were caught off guard as they supped.

speaker: Eivor
en: They were attacked by a beast. Something strong enough to kill a horse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Some large prey left these tracks in the grass.

speaker: Eivor
en: The hunters were prey to a large beast or two. I can only hope that Birstan still lives.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birstan?

speaker: Birstan
en: Ready your weapon! Or accept your fate as a feast for bears!

speaker: Birstan
en: Do not let them charge you! Ha! We'll fight to the death, worthy one. Ha! Your weapon strikes true! This is one Saxon you won't kill today! Gets the blood coursing! You have savaged enough men today, beast!

speaker: Birstan
en: Well fought, friend. I would not have survived this ambush without you.

speaker: Birstan
en: You have my gratitude. To stumble upon me in my moment of greatest peril, perhaps you were God-sent?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Estrid-sent. Your wife and the thegns of Essexe both want your balls on a blacksmith's anvil.

speaker: Birstan
en: When do they not? You could return and report that the savage claw took me. "Poor Birstan, his exit, pursued by a bear!"

speaker: Eivor
en: And make the beast Lord of Essexe in your stead.

speaker: Birstan
en: No doubt Estrid would prefer his velvet paws to my calloused hands. So who are you? A sellsword?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm Eivor of the Raven Clan. You hinted at an alliance for the loan of my unique talents.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm Norse, and no coin-groveler.

speaker: Birstan
en: Intriguing! We Saxons hear only that Danes and Norse are ferocious barbarians, all teeth and claws, with little subtlety or wit. But ho! Are you the Norse I sent word to?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm Eivor of the Raven Clan. You hinted at an alliance for the loan of my unique talents.

speaker: Eivor
en: You speak ill of your wife. Has your love faded or were you ill-matched?

speaker: Birstan
en: As family, we are close as Cain and Abel. She is a willful woman, and I am a bad husband. You know me, it seems?

speaker: Eivor
en: Only by reputation.

speaker: Birstan
en: A deliciously teasing sentiment.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm Eivor of the Raven Clan. You hinted at an alliance for the loan of my unique talents.

speaker: Birstan
en: Sblood, yes! Let us return to Colcestre at once and we'll speak more of the delicate matter on my mind.

speaker: Birstan
en: I am glad you answered my summons. I did not expect such a skilled fighter!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's good I came when I did. You lost many men on this hunt.

speaker: Birstan
en: Good men, all. They will have the proper rites, and their families will be cared for.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your people sacrificed much for your sport.

speaker: Birstan
en: They did. There is no balm for my tortured heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why did you ask me here?

speaker: Birstan
en: Do you believe in true love, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have loved.

speaker: Birstan
en: But have you truly? Has a longing burned in your breast, a sweet, lingering pain? Paralyzing you with its sting?

speaker: Eivor
en: There is pain enough in battle, I do not seek it out in love.

speaker: Birstan
en: I long for it. The thrill of a fight softly won. My wife Estrid lacks fire. She is a fish out of water. Cold and dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: She showed great passion when I met her, keeping your thegns in check.

speaker: Birstan
en: O, they love her, it is true. Some with too much devotion. And I have not been a good and attentive husband. I have always been a plucked goose in matters of love. And a piss-poor ruler to boot.

speaker: Eivor
en: Strong must be the hand that steers the ship, Birstan.

speaker: Birstan
en: My hand would rather tug the catgut of well-crafted bow, my eyes narrowing at the sight of prey.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye. A crown sits heavy on the head.

speaker: Birstan
en: Then let us run wild and free in the woods as the wolves do! Live on our wits. Prowl and stalk and feast.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a romantic way about you, Birstan.

speaker: Birstan
en: Do not fret. My guards will not worry you when we are together.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mismark me if you think I'm capable of worry. Have you built your city in the ruins of another?

speaker: Birstan
en: No. These builders are lost to the annals of time. Far advanced of the Saxon hovels of wattle and daub. I have ambition to build a great palace, myself. With mosaics and balmy courtyards.

speaker: Eivor
en: What stops you?

speaker: Birstan
en: That which stops all but the most creative minds. Coin, imagination, talent.

speaker: Eivor
en: And your people? Is Essexe happy?

speaker: Birstan
en: That is a question I never really ponder. I suppose they are. I hope they are. Aelfred believes I rule like a chick-less hen. Flapping and squawking over nothing but the farmer's dinner.

speaker: Eivor
en: He interferes?

speaker: Birstan
en: No, he disapproves. Is that not infinitely worse? But look, we are nearing the hall.

speaker: Birstan
en: I must face the wolves at my door before we discuss your favor to Essexe, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be I can speed your business along?

speaker: Birstan
en: Ready to help me fend off the spears of their displeasure?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let them speak their woes. I'll advise you if you can.

speaker: Wyatt
en: Who is this owl, Birstan, that twitters in your ear?

speaker: Birstan
en: An advisor, nothing more, here to help Essexe navigate her brewing storms. Now, my dear brethren. Eadred, perhaps you will start us off. What troubles you?

speaker: Eadred
en: You're a disgrace, Birstan! Couldn't get a sow pissed in an alehouse. Aelfred's men are crawling all over Essexe.

speaker: Birstan
en: King Aelfred, yes... though it is within his right, the constant presence of his men is certainly an issue.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are they men or babes? If Aelfred meddles in the affairs of Essexe, send his men home in shrouds.

speaker: Birstan
en: Ah... we should challenge his right to rule? Was not Essexe once a thriving kingdom of its own? We should fight! Yes, fight!

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfred will get bored soon enough. He has bigger pikes to bake than are to be found in this stolid backwater.

speaker: Birstan
en: Aelfred's forces are only here because of Estrid's failed kidnap. Now that she is safe, they will soon be gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: When the months are coldest, the mistletoe is full grown, cloaked in her winter strength.

speaker: Birstan
en: Meaning... that... we should weather this, stay strong? Yes, that's it. Not bend in the wind likes stalks of wheat!

speaker: Birstan
en: An issue that must be dealt with. Indeed.

speaker: Birstan
en: And you, Wyatt? What do you say?

speaker: Wyatt
en: Your preparations for the Lammas festival. How can you think of spending so much coin, when your people are starving?

speaker: Eivor
en: Drink, be merry, eat your fill. Sing of great battles, for tomorrow we may die. There's no problem that mead and song can't solve.

speaker: Birstan
en: Do we not deserve such mirth? A great feast of happiness? The dark days of winter approach, let us drink them away!

speaker: Eivor
en: He should put his own ham fist in his purse and contribute to the festival.

speaker: Birstan
en: Yes, you worry about the cost of such a festival, one that thanks God for our great harvest? Contribute your own coin, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: Often should one make an early meal, nor fasting come to the feast.

speaker: Birstan
en: The feast, yes. The festival! This is not for full bellies, but to bless the loaf. Does that not bring us all good fortune?

speaker: Birstan
en: Starving, yes, that is not... good. I'll see to it.

speaker: Birstan
en: And Aldrich? Do you yap like a she-hound as Eadred does?

speaker: Aldrich
en: You know my thoughts, Birstan. The . How can we give men to Aelfred for his wars when our harvest suffers day by day?

speaker: Eivor
en: Refuse to send your men. Let's Aelfred people die for his hopeless cause against the Norse.

speaker: Birstan
en: Then... we... refuse?

speaker: Aldrich
en: Refuse our king? Has madness taken your wits, Birstan?

speaker: Eivor
en: Do they not defend your land? You'll need all the men you can muster to fight the coming wars.

speaker: Birstan
en: The Danes are a great threat when provoked. Those we cannot ally with, we must fight or lose our lands.

speaker: Eivor
en: Beware of sleep on a witch's bosom, nor let her limbs ensnare you. For she will not bring an early harvest.

speaker: Birstan
en: I... ah... bosoms that?... ah, no. I'm afraid I don't know what that means, Eivor.

speaker: Birstan
en: Suffers, dear me.

speaker: Birstan
en: There, have I not answered all your questions?

speaker: Wyatt
en: I thank you for your candor, Birstan. You have put my mind somewhat at ease.

speaker: Aldrich
en: Aye.

speaker: Eadred
en: Indeed.

speaker: Birstan
en: Good. With that, we are concluded, my lords. Now if you'll pardon me, I have much to discuss with my wife.

speaker: Wyatt
en: You are a stain on this shire, Birstan! Useless!

speaker: Aldrich
en: Useless...

speaker: Eadred
en: That's right.

speaker: Birstan
en: Yet, still you haunt my hall? Begone, I haven't time for your squabbling!

speaker: Birstan
en: I sense you had some fun there, Eivor. And your playful wickedness backfooted my squabbling thegns.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't know what you speak of, lord.

speaker: Birstan
en: That ceased their prattling! A fine outcome, Eivor. The very soul of balance.

speaker: Eivor
en: A firm hand is all you need, Birstan, whether on your hunting bow, or on your helm.

speaker: Birstan
en: You're certainly a better hunter than you are a diplomat, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I spend my effort where it matters most.

speaker: Birstan
en: If speech is silver and silence is golden, then you are rich indeed, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm a better hunter than talker.

speaker: Birstan
en: All this talk of hunting makes long for the woods.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your wife awaits, Birstan. Are you not worried some other man will drench your sheets with his sweats?

speaker: Birstan
en: Ha! She does as she must. As do I. But you will discover this soon enough.

speaker: Estrid
en: You have done the impossible, Dane. Returned my errant gander to his coop.

speaker: Birstan
en: My pettish love, such a stormy countenance clouds the sun of my return.

speaker: Estrid
en: Your thegns drank the ale the gifted us. All of it.

speaker: Birstan
en: Now that is a tragedy my heart will not easily overcome.

speaker: Estrid
en: If he looked at me for the same affection he shows for hunting deer, our marriage might have survived.

speaker: Eivor
en: I noticed your love has gone sour. Was it fresher than this?

speaker: Estrid
en: There is so little difference between love and hate, it's difficult to say where the sourness comes from.

speaker: Eivor
en: So what do you need of me?

speaker: Eivor
en: So what do you need of me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Essexe seems at odds with itself. Have you called me here to fix the many problems I've already seen today?

speaker: Birstan
en: No, no. I would not inflict the fighting of my thegns upon you, Eivor. Our matters are more delicate.

speaker: Estrid
en: And of a more personal bent. Requiring a finesse and discretion that these Saxons often lack.

speaker: Eivor
en: So what do you need of me?

speaker: Estrid
en: Our affairs are more of heart than of state, Eivor. What little passion there was between us faded into bickering long ago.

speaker: Birstan
en: We would have our freedom, Eivor. I from my wife, and my wife from Essexe.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am too sharp a weapon for so soft a task. Why not part and be done with it?

speaker: Estrid
en: O, were I a Dane! And divorce as simple as a slit throat. But it's not as easy as that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Does your god not allow husbands and wives to part?

speaker: Birstan
en: Our God, our king. There is much standing in the way of a joyous uncoupling. Ours was an arranged marriage, a political need, and not easily broken.

speaker: Eivor
en: Explain yourselves, clear and plain, and I will do it. The poetry here is mind mud.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then what is stopping you? Your King Aelfred?

speaker: Birstan
en: Ours was not a union of love, but necessity. Decreed by Aelfred's father to strengthen ties with Francia. Not easily broken.

speaker: Eivor
en: Explain yourselves, clear and plain, and I will do it. The poetry here is mind mud.

speaker: Eivor
en: Explain yourselves, clear and plain, and I will do it. The poetry here is mind mud.

speaker: Birstan
en: We had a plan, a simple plan. A woman lost and a woman found.

speaker: Estrid
en: Some time ago, we paid a Dane to kidnap me and ferry me safely to Francia. As you can see, he did not deliver.

speaker: Birstan
en: He was certainly thorough in other regards.

speaker: Eivor
en: Some Norse can be quick to take coin and slow to earn it. If I give my word, it is not broken.

speaker: Estrid
en: Could we try the kidnap again? Much of the planning is done. It would only take a more trustworthy overseer.

speaker: Eivor
en: It should be a bold venture if we do. Loud and brash and seen by all.

speaker: Estrid
en: During our Lammas festival? Merry peasants and guards with wandering eyes?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your return to Francia would need a swift ship. With a captain ready to leave England.

speaker: Estrid
en: We could ask him.

speaker: Birstan
en: I would have thought his steed and seamen spent.

speaker: Estrid
en: Come find me in the market, Eivor. Our unwelcome guests require food and ale to soften their anger.

speaker: Birstan
en: My wife is a gracious and attentive host, Eivor. The only thing that keeps my braying thegns at bay.

speaker: Eivor
en: And the woman found?

speaker: Birstan
en: A darling May-bud. Alfida, my childhood sweetheart. I left her twenty years ago in Maeldun to marry my prickled pear.

speaker: Eivor
en: Twenty years? Can an ember so cold be reignited?

speaker: Birstan
en: We can hope! You must fan the flame. Find her, bring her to my lakeside cottage, and light a bonfire there. I will know to come. I believe she lived in the last house of Maeldun. A small, sweet place where fond memories were made.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will do as you both ask, and ask Freyja for success in this love game.

speaker: Birstan
en: Good luck in your endeavors, Eivor. I pray you find my Alfida, with a fair face and a yearning heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, should I look for Alfida first or meet with Estrid at the marketplace?

speaker: Stowe
en: Isn't it pleasant, getting out of the city and into the wild?

speaker: Erke
en: It's too empty out here. No sound but the birds and the wind in the grass.

speaker: Stowe
en: Never fear, Erke. We'll soon be home, back to the racket and stink of the tanner's yard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Erke, Stowe. Ready to attack?

speaker: Stowe
en: I have reservations.

speaker: Erke
en: Sparrow-heart has reservations.

speaker: Stowe
en: Though Mercia wars often with Wessex, these people are Christians. Perhaps I can talk to them, to avert more bloodshed?

speaker: Eivor
en: You know the people of this isle better than I, Stowe. I trust you.

speaker: Stowe
en: Thank you, Eivor. I will do what I can.

speaker: Stowe
en: Brave soldiers! My name is Stowe, Reeve of Lunden, and this Dane at my side is Reeve Erke. He is my partner in Lunden. Together we see that justice is done. But more, he is my friend. In Lunden, we live in harmony with the Danes. So could you. But your king does not share our philosophy. Aelfred bleeds his land dry, works you all to the bone for a needless war. Now he wants you to die for it. So I beg you, in God's name, walk away from this camp. I will find you new and worthy employment in Lunden. You are good men and true. I would not want this day to be your last.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: This one's right. The Danes are here to stay, like it or not. What's good dying now?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Don't be a lackwit! Soon as you drop your swords, they'll murder us!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: That's no heathen talking. He's a Saxon. I, for one, believe him.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Come on, lads. It's a new life in Lunden for us. Better that than dying here in the mud.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: We'll deal with you traitors later. The rest of you, attack!

speaker: Eivor
en: Brave try, friend. But now we do things my way.

speaker: Eivor
en: When words fail, iron speaks loudest.

speaker: Eivor
en: The camp is ours!

speaker: Erke
en: That wasn't so hard, was it, Stowe?

speaker: Stowe
en: Even one's man death is too many.

speaker: Eivor
en: More lives than these are at stake, Stowe. You would warn them of our intention.

speaker: Stowe
en: I understand. I promised my aid, and I will keep my word.

speaker: Erke
en: Enough wringing of souls. Time to act.

speaker: Eivor
en: Onward! Take the Saxons' camp!

speaker: Eivor
en: The camp is ours!

speaker: Erke
en: That wasn't so hard, was it, Stowe?

speaker: Stowe
en: Even one's man death is too many.

speaker: Eivor
en: No sense raising the alarm. I will take care of them quietly. Be ready to come to my aid.

speaker: Erke
en: We have your back, Eivor.

speaker: Erke
en: Need some help, Wolf-Kissed?

speaker: Stowe
en: Could we not have talked with them first?

speaker: Eivor
en: This way is quicker. The dead don't argue.

speaker: Eivor
en: The camp is ours!

speaker: Erke
en: That wasn't so hard, was it, Stowe?

speaker: Stowe
en: Even one's man death is too many.

speaker: Eivor
en: The camp is ours. My warriors will arrive soon.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Passing through my lands, Hjorr met my father. The two got on like tinder and flame. And soon we were married.

speaker: Erke
en: You see, Stowe? Befriend a king and one is set for life. What could be simpler?

speaker: Stowe
en: And how do you like England, Ljufvina?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: A gloomy land, full of puzzling people. But when it shows itself in glory, it is magnificent.

speaker: Eivor
en: How does it look?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Crawling with Saxon soldiers like lice on a swine. The very sight sours my blood.

speaker: Erke
en: Would the sight of their bodies in the mud please you better?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: One way to find out.

speaker: Stowe
en: Eivor, I beg you, Aelfred's men or not, they are Saxons and Christians. If I could speak to them, we might avoid bloodshed.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: And lose the element of surprise. These people make their living by the blade. We should attack headlong.

speaker: Eivor
en: You know the people of this isle better than I, Stowe. I trust you.

speaker: Stowe
en: Thank you, Eivor. I will do what I can.

en: Even one's man death is too many.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ljufvina speaks true. In trying to save their lives, you would endanger ours. We fight.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: At last, a chance to test the mettle of these Wessex folk. I wonder how they measure against those of the North?

speaker: Erke
en: One way to find out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Onward! Take the Saxons' camp!

speaker: Eivor
en: The camp is ours!

speaker: Erke
en: That wasn't so hard, was it, Stowe?

speaker: Stowe
en: Even one's man death is too many.

speaker: Eivor
en: No sense raising the alarm. I will take care of them quietly. Be ready to come to my aid.

speaker: Erke
en: We have your back, Eivor.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Hogging all the fun, Eivor?

speaker: Stowe
en: We could have handled this in a more civil manner!

speaker: Erke
en: Too late for that.

speaker: Eivor
en: The camp is ours!

speaker: Erke
en: That wasn't so hard, was it, Stowe?

speaker: Stowe
en: Even one's man death is too many.

speaker: Eivor
en: The camp is ours. My warriors will arrive soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Just me against all of you? I like those odds.

speaker: Eivor
en: The camp is ours. My warriors will arrive soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now I must see about destroying Fulke's supplies.

speaker: Stowe
en: So many dead. Erke, did we do the right thing here?

speaker: Erke
en: At least at home, we've the law to guide us. Out here, the only rule is the sword.

speaker: Stowe
en: How will we ever share this land if we kill one another so readily?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The weak fall beneath the strong. It has always been so.

speaker: Stowe
en: No. There is more to this world than that. There has to be.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: Heroes aplenty, warriors so many, but most walk about with heads that are empty. Would a soul in these lands, pay heed to a man, who wanders this world without a clan? Hey! You! My eyes and soul do not deceive me! You are the Wolf-Kissed, are you not? Come, come!

speaker: Eivor
en: Greetings, bard.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: That face, that scowl... yes, indeed, you must be the Wolf-Kissed! Your fame and generosity are well-known to me!

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a flatterer's tongue, bard. But how do you know me?

speaker: Berk the Bard
