en: The deeds of the great are a bard's stock in trade. The brave are wealthy, the wealthy are brave. So it goes. How about it, Eivor the Wanderer? Part with a queen's ransom and live on in immortal song?

speaker: Eivor
en: Silver comes and silver goes, but the fame of the great endures.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: Both wise and generous! Truly you are history's mightiest champion. Now, hold tight while my muse inspires me.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: From beyond the whale-roads, from history unknown, did the Norse take a stand, and now all must atone. Now comes Eivor of the Ravens, with the sun for eyes, trailing a river of blood, enough to paint the skies! Succumb to your fate with a kiss, a blade to your throat, the wolf's fangs to your shins. For the one blessing and the one curse, is to meet the Wolf-Kissed!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your s are weak. However, you make up for it with your clever tongue.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: Tis the tale of a bard such as I! We give and give and get nothing back. So it goes. Farewell, generous champion!

speaker: Eivor
en: I heard you sing, bard. Your songs aren't worth a copper bit.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: Frugal and rude! You're even less fun than you look.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: There was a cheap little Norse. Stinking of ale, with a face like a horse, and a pony for a tail. What was the name of this hideous boar? To speak it brings shame, but it's Eivor! Eivor! Always second, never the first. Made to do a master's bidding, a servant cursed! Alas ends the tale of Eivor the Boar, the Cheap, the Second! Ei-ei-ei-vor! Oink!

speaker: Eivor
en: I could kill you with a single swing, but I'd rather not stain my weapon.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: I merely sung the truth! Your brutish threats hold no power over a bard like me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me find a fuller purse someday, and perhaps I shall return.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: The world weeps at its loss! Go forth and plunder, so that all may hear your praises properly sung."

speaker: Eivor
en: Greetings, bard.

speaker: Berk the Bard
en: Ah, Eivor of the Ravens! Have you changed your mind about living forever in song? Bit of coin for a soulful tune?

speaker: Asser
en: Send me a sign, O Lord. Illuminate my true path. For you are the shepherd and I am the lamb who follows your lamp. Your meaning is unclear, God of Gods. Please, there must be some other purpose for my life! You are the light of the world. So do these rays mean something?

speaker: Priest
en: You have not left the church in days. The stench offends even God's nose.

speaker: Asser
en: I have been looking at his scripture for hours. God is giving me a sign. If only I could see it... see his light.

speaker: Priest
en: A sign? God in Heaven. Give him a sign. Set him on his true path. Far away from me.

speaker: Asser
en: Yes! Illuminate me, O Lord. Illuminate me!

speaker: Eivor
en: What troubles you?

speaker: Asser
en: God will speak to me, I know it. He will show me my true path.

speaker: Eivor
en: God's light will show him his path? Maybe I can illuminate the lecterns somehow to cease his prattling.

speaker: Asser
en: Lord, your light falters! Please do not forsake me. Is the tenebrous pall of darkness my fate?

speaker: Asser
en: Another ray! Is that the sign? An empty lectern? Do you mock the hollow rattle of my soul, Lord?

speaker: Asser
en: Leave me be, I am deep in contemplation. I must follow His beacon.

speaker: Asser
en: Wait! This is it. It must be.

speaker: Eivor
en: That should do it. His God has spoken to him at last, with my divine intervention.

speaker: Asser
en: Psalm 119? Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path.

speaker: Asser
en: His words? Does He mean... that I should become... a writer?

speaker: Asser
en: And then? Of course... the unfolding of your words gives light and understanding to the simple.

speaker: Asser
en: My path is clear. I must throw off the shackles of brotherhood. I will dedicate my life to glorifying God, through another. My account must be one of the utmost grace, exhaustive, immortalizing the great acts of the prodigal Aelfred. Thank you, Lord, I will write a blessed praising Aelfred and his great works.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, I have set him on a path to glorify Aelfred? That pompous Saxon? I hope his writing reeks as much as he does.

speaker: Eivor
en: Asser, is it? How is your writing faring?

speaker: Asser
en: Who are you? An admirer? Can it be true, that so soon upon my path, God has sent me adulation? I have only just begun to walk in Aelfred's footsteps. But please read my scribbles. Enlighten yourself about our great king.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, I am sure it will be... informative.

speaker: Eivor
en: Asser should have stayed a monk. Not a patch on our sagas. Where is the drama? The heroic brushes with death? Let us hope Aelfred's life becomes more interesting than this.

speaker: Ivarr
en: This is not going to end well.

speaker: Ubba
en: Just keep you wits about you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Calm, Ivarr. Me and Eivor will take care of this.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I know.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, is there a problem?

speaker: Sigurd
en: We'll go see Tonna, just the two of us. Ivarr and Ubba will wait here. Better if Tonna thinks we've come alone. The truth is, I don't think any of us can stop Ivarr from cleaving her head open. It's all he was spewing the whole way over here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Right. Shall we?

speaker: Sigurd
en: We'll return shortly.

speaker: Ivarr
en: A small fortune for whoever sends Tonna to Hel.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll hold you to that.

speaker: Eivor
en: From what I overheard in Repton, the brothers had an arrangement with Tonna. What happened?

speaker: Sigurd
en: She's a mercenary. Ubba used her for men and information. But that relationship soured now that Burgred is all but defeated. From what I've heard, Tonna has a hunger for two things, soft silver and a stern hump. Neither of which earns you true loyalty.

speaker: Eivor
en: If she can't be trusted, what use is she?

speaker: Sigurd
en: That is for us to find out. We may be able to satisfy her...

speaker: Eivor
en: And if we can't?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ivarr did tell you to bring your axe.

speaker: Tonna
en: And here they are. As expected.

speaker: Sigurd
en: If she takes a liking to you, keep talking.

speaker: Eivor
en: She's more your type, I think.

speaker: Sigurd
en: No, no. This is your challenge.

speaker: Tonna
en: Come now, don't drag your feet.

speaker: Tonna
en: Sigurd. What brings you strolling into my camp this brisk day?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I suspect you already know.

speaker: Tonna
en: Yes.

speaker: Tonna
en: The embers on the air betray you. And yet, if you are here talking to me, King Burgred remains at large.

speaker: Tonna
en: And you are you, lovely dove? Want to perch your ass on my lap?

speaker: Eivor
en: Call me Eivor. Or Wolf-Kissed. "Lovely dove" will get your throat cut.

speaker: Tonna
en: Come now. You are too clever to run with those Ragnarsson dogs. Plenty of room on this side, if you want to earn some coin.

speaker: Eivor
en: We came for your help, not your flattery.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not interested.

speaker: Tonna
en: And why not? I've been told I have a rather expert tongue.

speaker: Eivor
en: Only good for yawping, I see.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Enough blabbering. You know why we're here.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's not why I'm here.

speaker: Tonna
en: "Where is King Burgred?" That is what you want. And what makes you think I have the slightest idea?

speaker: Eivor
en: We found letters, records of trade. The two of you have a history.

speaker: Tonna
en: What can I say? The king pays well for my services. If only I could say the same for those two Ragnarsson clods.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're dealing with me now. And I want to know what you know. Name your price.

speaker: Tonna
en: Very well. I could use another cow. And you can cover the cost.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here's your silver.

speaker: Tonna
en: Mmm, ripe as a plum, aren't you? So eager...

speaker: Sigurd
en: Out with it.

speaker: Tonna
en: Burgred paid me to steer the Ragnarssons clear of two areas. Ledecestre and Templebrough Fort. It was a hefty amount. If I were you, that's where I'd look. And that is all I know. Not more, not less. We are done here.

speaker: Eivor
en: When Ceolwulf is on the throne, do you think he will be pleased to hear you stood in his way? That you doubted him at all?

speaker: Eivor
en: Settle for half that amount and maybe Ceolwulf's first command won't be for your head on a platter.

speaker: Tonna
en: You've got stones.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Out with it.

speaker: Tonna
en: Burgred paid me to steer the Ragnarssons clear of two areas. Ledecestre and Templebrough Fort. It was a hefty amount. If I were you, that's where I'd look. And that is all I know. Not more, not less. We are done here.

speaker: Eivor
en: You take me for a fool?

speaker: Tonna
en: I take you for desperate beggars. I can smell it on you, like dung heap. Now that's my price. What say you?

speaker: Tonna
en: Mmm, ripe as a plum, aren't you. So eager...

speaker: Sigurd
en: Out with it.

speaker: Tonna
en: Burgred paid me to steer the Ragnarssons clear of two areas. Ledecestre and Templebrough Fort. It was a hefty amount. If I were you, that's where I'd look. And that is all I know. Not more, not less. We are done here.

speaker: Eivor
en: You heard me the first time. But I'll get what I need, one way or another.

speaker: Tonna
en: No, no. You have shot your chance. And if you show your faces around here once more, I will tear you limb from limb.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ledecestre and Templebrough Fort. Do you know these places?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I don't, but the brothers will. I'll bring this news to them. Don't stay around here long. We've got a king to catch.

speaker: Tonna
en: Watch yourself, lovely dove. There's nothing left for you here. Why are you still here?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Well, that is not the result I was hoping for. I hope you have another idea.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tonna keeps a close eye on whoever she deals with. If Burgred is keeping records, so is she. Somewhere behind those walls.

speaker: Sigurd
en: See what you can find. I'll go back to the brothers.

speaker: Tonna
en: Keep those gates locked. If they come within a foot of here, kill them.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: What happened out there?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: The Ragnarssons came through, just like Tonna said they would.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: I suppose they didn't reach an agreement.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Ha. What gave it away?

speaker: Eivor
en: Tonna's longhouse. I should have a look around.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tonna's house. I might find something useful there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Clever. Let's see what secrets you keep, Tonna.

speaker: Eivor
en: This might be something. Looks like Burgred once paid Tonna to steer the Ragnarssons away from two areas. Burgred's private haunts perhaps? He could be at either one. Shouldn't have been so greedy, Tonna. Right. Back to the brothers.

speaker: Tonna
en: Bad idea, lovely dove. Now I'm going to make you regret it. I am taking your head back to the Ragnarssons. That'll teach them to cross me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Straight to Hel with you.

speaker: Ubba
en: Sigurd's told us the news. Well done.

speaker: Ubba
en: Eivor. Tell us you learned something.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ledecestre and Templebrough Fort. What do you know about them?

speaker: Ubba
en: Hm. Ledecestre is a large village. And Templebrough... it's an old military fort, not much else.

speaker: Eivor
en: Burgred could be an either one. We should check both. As soon as possible.

speaker: Ivarr
en: And what do we do with Tonna? I would bet the sweat off my sack she's writing to Burgred now, offering silver for a warning about us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me worry about that.

speaker: Eivor
en: You won't be seeing her again. Not unless you are bound to Helheim. I'll collect now, if you don't mind.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ah. This one takes after me, brother.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We should get moving, drengr (courageous warrior). I can take the fortress at Templebrough.

speaker: Ubba
en: I will join you, Sigurd.

speaker: Ivarr
en: That leaves me Ledecestre, then. All by my fucking lonesome.

speaker: Ubba
en: Bring a friend, brother. Maybe Eivor dares to be called that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go on ahead. I'll catch up with all of you soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is all this? Who bangs the drums of war?

speaker: Kaija
en: Look at you. A battle-hardened vikingr! Just what we need.

speaker: Eivor
en: O, and what do you need this battle-hardened warrior for?

speaker: Kaija
en: One day we will be the greatest warriors beneath our banner. Skalds will write songs of the Wolf Pack. But, we must practice our raiding.

speaker: Eivor
en: Going on a raid? Then we shall raid. Three wolves, and I will be the fourth to your lead.

speaker: Kaija
en: Wolf Pack! Onwards!

speaker: Eivor
en: Wolf Pack!

speaker: Kaija
en: They ran, four warriors, like four limbs of one clawing body. Each limb built to kill! Destroy!

speaker: Kaija
en: They arrived at the village, torches, axes, and blades at the ready. Ready for the slaughter.

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: To war!

speaker: Kaija
en: Loot! Beauteous loot! Hacksilver is stuffed into the Big Wolf's purse.

speaker: Kaija
en: Full of lust for blood and battle, the Big Wolf smashes pots and bodies alike.

speaker: Kaija
en: His insides are all outsides now!

speaker: Kaija
en: Together, the Wolf Pack stands in the wreckage of the enemy village. Nothing remains but thralls to be taken, and flaming carnage! Come and kneel before your raid leader, Big Wolf!

speaker: Eivor
en: A successful raid.

speaker: Kaija
en: Yes! With your help, we slaughtered the Raven Clan for good!

speaker: Eivor
en: The Raven Clan, you say?

speaker: Kaija
en: Yes! Just like Kjotve jarls stories! One day, I'll be just like him! Death to Styrbjorn, death to the Raven Clan!

speaker: Eivor
en: Kjotve's young raiders. I'll see you wolves on another battlefield one day.

speaker: Trapped Boy
en: I'm trapped! Help. I've been trapped by a witch! Don't go! She'll come back and boil me in a pot! I'll be served with turnips for supper! I'll never get out! What if the witch comes back!

speaker: Trapped Boy
en: I hear you out there. Thw witch locked me in and left the key somewhere. Find that key!

speaker: Trapped Boy
en: Hello? This is the slowest rescue I've ever seen! Could you find the stupid key and get me out?

speaker: Trapped Boy
en: About time. I've been so bored in here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is this witch that locked you in?

speaker: Trapped Boy
en: A horrible old hag who wants to make me into rabbit stew! Thanks for helping me get out of here!

speaker: My Tale
en: The world is worried by witches. They fly from every tree. The ground hides nothing but goblins, crawling up your knee. The skies shake with shrieks of harpies, water fills wells with woe. But me, I'm locked up and luckless. I've got nowhere to go.

speaker: Mother
en: You naughty boy! Just look at this mess. The house has been upended! Who is this?

speaker: Trapped Boy
en: I fooled her! I told her you were a witch and you were going to eat me for supper!

speaker: Mother
en: Well, that's a fine how-do-you-do. It will take me weeks to put this place back in order.

speaker: Trapped Boy
en: We had a grand time!

speaker: Mother
en: I am no witch. I am the kindest, sweetest mum to ever lock her lad in a house. How else teach you not to pick your nose?

speaker: Trapped Boy
en: Thanks, stranger!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is the spot. Now I need only wait for Valka to arrive.

speaker: Valka
en: I will tie your hands now.

speaker: Eivor
en: What purpose will that serve?

speaker: Valka
en: You are too much the warrior, Eivor. You will not recognize your fear until you are helpless before it. Drink.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you say this will bring the vision back?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that all? You mean to leave me here?

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka, this is... W-why must I be tied?

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka?

speaker: Eivor
en: Untie me! The wolf is coming and I... I cannot reach my weapon! Valka! Valka!

speaker: Eivor
en: So many! Where did they come from? I have to break these bonds!

speaker: Eivor
en: The more I struggle, the tighter the bonds become!

speaker: Eivor
en: There must be a trick to this. What did Valka say? Give in to it. Be still.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's working! The bonds are loosening!

speaker: Eivor
en: Free! Now for the reckoning!

speaker: Eivor
en: They fade like a nightmare upon waking. What illusion is this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Accursed phantoms! Come, then! You'll not find me lacking!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gah! It's like fighting a river!

speaker: Eivor
en: I know you, wolf. I saw you on the ice, the day my father died. But I am not a child any more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Curse you! Die!

speaker: Eivor
en: No more will you stalk me!

speaker: Eivor
en: The wolf is gone... for now.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am ready, Valka. It is time.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: The Nornir told me you'd be here. The cord is forged. Gleipnir, I call it.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: I'll wager there's a good story behind that wound.

speaker: Havi
en: A tale for another time. Thank you for this.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: When you bind the beast, spare no loose ends. The cord will stretch or shrink to fit your needs.

speaker: Havi
en: How tightly will it hold? The beast may resist.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: The more you tighten the cord, the stronger it will hold and the greater it will hurt, 'til the beast is rooted to the ground.

speaker: Havi
en: Thank you, Ivaldi. You may go.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: You mean from Asgard, do you not? My debt to you is paid in full?

speaker: Havi
en: Yes, as promised.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Thank you, Havi. I... I did not expect you to remember.

speaker: Havi
en: Where will you go next?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Under the mountains of Svartálfaheimr. Our mountains. To free the earth's riches, for this is what I know best.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Back to my forge?

speaker: Havi
en: Yes, until your debt to me is paid in full. It was the dwarves who made the world a trading port.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: At least we trade in goods, not people, Slave Master. I'll be glad to be back underground, away from these angry skies.

speaker: Havi
en: Even thunder's fury won't weaken my will.

speaker: Havi
en: Týr! Are you near?

speaker: Týr
en: Havi! You are a balm to my eyes... what happened to yours?

speaker: Havi
en: A sacrifice for something greater. Is the wolf nearby?

speaker: Týr
en: Yes, but he's grown. I have kept him company, but he is consumed by a sadness I cannot understand.

speaker: Havi
en: Regrettable, but necessary. I knew from the start this wolf brought ill tidings.

speaker: Týr
en: From the start, it was a kind creature. But our mistrust and cruelty have robbed the poor wolf of its sweetness and life.

speaker: Havi
en: Would it be a kindness to kill it then?

speaker: Týr
en: We are past the time for such mercy. This wolf has power now that would test our strengths combined. I fear he is possessed of a power that renders him... ever-living.

speaker: Havi
en: Then we will offer him a different fate. This cord is unbreakable. You must convince him to wear it. It will act as a leash whose magic will signal that he is safely secured. An assurance to the Æsir who fear him. A beacon, that is all. No harm will befall the poor Fenrir.

speaker: Týr
en: Fenrir, yes. You know the creature's name. Did Loki tell you?

speaker: Havi
en: He did. It is a fine name.

speaker: Týr
en: Yes, Dweller of the Fens. An apt name for his current fate.

speaker: Týr
en: Fenrir! A good word has come!

speaker: Fenrir
en: Leave me.

speaker: Týr
en: I wish you well, Great Wolf. But a fear still hangs over Asgard. The Æsir worry about your growing size and strength!

speaker: Fenrir
en: Do they now...?

speaker: Fenrir
en: And what have they to be afraid of, old friend?

speaker: Týr
en: Havi brings a collar fashioned by the dwarves. A beacon that we may track from a distance, to know where you roam. Wear this and you may live and thrive in Asgard without worry.

speaker: Fenrir
en: I smell something... sour.

speaker: Havi
en: Wear the collar or return to Jotunheimr. There's no third way.

speaker: Týr
en: Son of Loki, have I not treated you with kindness? We are bonded, you and I. And as I trust my king, so you may trust me.

speaker: Týr
en: Open your mouth. As a pledge of faith, you may take my hand if I am untrue.

speaker: Fenrir
en: Fair.

speaker: Týr
en: Be swift, Havi.

speaker: Fenrir
en: It burns!

speaker: Týr
en: Havi?

speaker: Fenrir
en: Lies!

speaker: Týr
en: Unbind him!

speaker: Týr
en: Havi!

speaker: Havi
en: Here you stay, Fen-Dweller.

speaker: Fenrir
en: Here you die, Deceiver!

speaker: Fenrir
en: Brothers will fight one another... kill one another...

speaker: Havi
en: You speak in riddles?

speaker: Fenrir
en: The home of the gods turns red... red with gore...

speaker: Fenrir
en: It will be an age of storms... an age of wolves...

speaker: Havi
en: Where did you hear these words of prophecy?

speaker: Fenrir
en: Then comes the second great sorrow... when the Havi goes to fight the wolf...

speaker: Havi
en: How do you know these things?

speaker: Fenrir
en: This is the tale I tell myself each night in the cold and dark, before I sleep and dream of tasting your flesh.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you ever seen so many ships docked at once?

speaker: Bragi
en: Never. Nor has there been a gathering of kings so large as this.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Your clan is a foul stench!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: But we are strong, ' (weakling)!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Yes! Strong with stink!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Step closer, seal-face. And say that again!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: I said your stench is strong. That's your only strength. Your stench.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: I will feed your teeth, wrapped in your tongue, bacraut (asshole)!

speaker: Sigurd
en: You have just won your heart's desire, Eivor. Yet by the look on your face, you have lost your will to live.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gorm is here with the last of his men. Why does that troll dare show his face?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Leave it for another day. We are here under Harald's truce. And Gorm is too weak to try anything bold.

speaker: Eivor
en: He is a seed-stain on his father's trousers. I should wipe him from this world.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not tonight, Eivor. Leave it.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Basim, watch over this one and see that she warms herself with drink. I will find my father and escort him to the longhouse.

speaker: Basim
en: As you wish.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is Hytham well?

speaker: Basim
en: He will heal, but never fully recover. It is fortunate that you were able to succeed where he failed.

speaker: Eivor
en: My resolve was strong.

speaker: Basim
en: When you slew Kjotve, did you see a sigil on him? Silver, the size of my palm, bearing the symbol of an ash-tree.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take it. Trade it for what you can.

speaker: Basim
en: I know where Gorm is camped. If you wish to see him without anyone the wiser, there is a trick I can teach you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Already looking for another apprentice? All right, I'll bite. What do I do?

speaker: Basim
en: Use your cloak to obscure your face. Blend in to the crowd, divert attention, hide in plain sight.

speaker: Eivor
en: A gift of knowledge from a man I hardly know. Is this your way of asking me to join your brotherhood?

speaker: Basim
en: Not at all. So long as men and women fight to secure honor and freedom, their allegiance hardly matters to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this how your brotherhood operates? You sneak around in the daylight, stabbing your victims where they stand?

speaker: Basim
en: Said like that, you make me blush. We are seekers of justice, shepherds of man's will. We work in the dark to serve the light.

speaker: Eivor
en: I suppose there's no shame in using deception when honor is at stake. And Gorm is a stain on that honor.

speaker: Basim
en: Then let's see what can be done to cleanse that stain. Give it a try.

speaker: Basim
en: A few things you should know before you step into his camp. Walking unseen through hostile territory is an exercise in subtlety. A hood makes you forgettable, dismissed at a distance. Remain far from watchful eyes and you will be invisible to them. Do not draw blade or hammer, for these and other sudden movements can break your disguise. And in case I wasn't clear, you will need to put up your hood for the trick to work.

speaker: Basim
en: Gorm is there. In the camp ahead.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: What were you thinking? Drinking mead on an empty stomach.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: You have to eat something before drinking that much.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: How does that go... "Feed before mead"?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: I have some roasted lamb on the spit. Are you coming?

speaker: Gorm
en: Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: You ' (cowardly) shit! Take up your weapon and follow me beyond these walls. Let Odin's favor land where it may.

speaker: Gorm
en: You dare not break the king's peace here, so fuck you and your god talk. What say you to that?

speaker: Gorm
en: You can beat me, but you will kill me. Not under Harald's truce.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: You are all subject to King Harald's truce. Break his peace and you will be cast out of Alrekstad.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will give you no trouble.

speaker: Eivor
en: You were shat into this world without honor, Gorm. And you will leave as turd dumped into Hel's deepest ditch.

speaker: Gorm
en: Keep crowing, Eivor. You only make yourself an easier target.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Althing will have started. I should find Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Tell me Gorm still lives, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: It pains me to say... he does.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Thank you. His day will come.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ugh... gods, I hate long speeches.

speaker: Eivor
en: Only when you're not giving them.

speaker: King Harald
en: Many of you knew my father, Halfdan the Black. A great man who achieved great things.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: They buried Halfdan's leg near our temple! The crops have never grown taller!

speaker: Norse Man
en: They buried his arse near ours and we get nothing but a muddy river!

speaker: King Harald
en: I dream of something greater. A vast kingdom of warriors, in numbers the world has never seen. United under one king. One rule! Too much blood has been spilt fighting one another. Today we unify and turn our blades outward to conquer new lands! And who better to lead us to glory than me? I was blooded before the age of ten and I led the greatest army Norway has ever seen. But they saw a wise king seeks honest counsel. So I ask, who among you rejects this new arrangement?

speaker: Hjorr
en: I am not your enemy, King Harald, but I will not be your subject. Tomorrow we sail for greener shores, and so, my kingdom is yours.

speaker: King Harald
en: This saddens me, noble Hjorr. And does your wife agree? Is she not tired of limping ever westward?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: My husband and I are as one in this, lord. We do not limp together, we fly.

speaker: King Harald
en: I am sad to lose a woman of your spirit, Ljufvina. But I hold no grudge. May the fates grant you good luck.

speaker: Gorm
en: My king! I offer you my axe and my oath, ironclad!

speaker: King Harald
en: Gorm Kjotvesson. You dare show your face in this hall? Did not king Styrbjorn and his son Sigurd rid our lands of your foulness?

speaker: Gorm
en: The Raven Clan dishonored me, great king! They poisoned my father, Kjotve! They made a mockery of his honorable death.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bacraut! (Asshole!) You lie!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Hold, Eivor. Let it play out.

speaker: King Harald
en: This is a serious charge, Gorm. And a false one at that. My uncle saw your father die. Eivor Wolf-Kissed. You are Kjotve's slayer. This man has slandered your clan. What shall I do with him?

speaker: Eivor
en: I would send him to Hel, as I did his father.

speaker: King Harald
en: Understandable, but a quick death is too good for a draugr (ghoul) like him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Exile, lord. Banish him to the wilds where even a slave could kill him with impunity.

speaker: King Harald
en: A wise choice. Death would be too easy a way out.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are king of these lands, Harald. The decision must be yours.

speaker: King Harald
en: A modest and honorable answer.

speaker: King Harald
en: Gorm, I name you Worm and call you exiled. Leave these lands by the next full moon or I will feed you to the crows myself.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: King Harald, may I speak?

speaker: King Harald
en: The floor is yours, King Styrbjorn.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: My people have held our land since the days when Odin himself walked among us. My kingdom is humble, but we have paid for it in blood. Our victory over Kjotve is proof that we will not lay down without a fight. All here have buried friends, brothers, and sisters... sons and daughters. And I for one have had my fill of death. Let those who seek war look beyond our shores. If King Harald brings peace, then I am happy to bend my knee to him.

speaker: Sigurd
en: What?

speaker: Sigurd
en: What in Hel's name are you doing, Father?

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Securing a lasting peace, Sigurd. Our days of fighting are finished.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You said nothing of this to me, not a word! And I will not yield a title that should be mine by right!

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Then war will continue. Men will die, villages will burn, you foolish boy! This is our only way towards true peace!

speaker: Sigurd
en: You will die a thrall, you drink-addled cow! Alone and toothless in a bed of straw!

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Forgive my son. He is ruled by his emotions.

speaker: King Harald
en: I take no offense, Styrbjorn Jarl. And I thank you for your fealty. It is natural to fear change. To resist it. But all things change and all things end. The lessons of Ragnarök are clear. We will speak again soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: That was an ambush, lord. Did you know of Styrbjorn's plans?

speaker: King Harald
en: For some days, yes, I did. But it was not at my urging. This was his decision alone. Do you dream of a glorious future, Eivor? A warrior like you would be a boon to .

speaker: Eivor
en: I dream of a glorious death, but not at the cost of betraying my family.

speaker: Eivor
en: My fate is tied to my brother's. Where Sigurd goes, I follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: All I know of Fate is that its pattern is unknowable. I do not worry beyond that fact.

speaker: King Harald
en: You intrigue me, Wolf-Kissed. Orphan and sibling, warrior and poet. You are many in one, it seems.

speaker: Eivor
en: You know much about me.

speaker: King Harald
en: I have eyes and ears everywhere, as any effective king must. Would you not be one of my ravens?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am bound to Sigurd. And he to me. But if fate should cross our threads again...

speaker: King Harald
en: I understand. Yet should your fortunes change, you are welcome in my hall.

speaker: King Harald
en: I wish I understood you better. For those I do not understand, I do not trust. And I cannot stomach a lack of trust.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have nothing to fear from me, King Harald. My loyalty lies with my brother, Sigurd, and I bear you no ill will.

speaker: King Harald
en: Then know, that if you stay in Norway, both you and your brother must serve under me. Take tomorrow to think on this.

speaker: King Harald
en: It would be best for us both if you left Norway. To avoid the heat that comes with such friction.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no ambition to rule. Only to live and die with glory.

speaker: King Harald
en: That may be. But however firmly we make our choices, it is fate that decides our outcome.

speaker: King Harald
en: But let us leave these matters for another time. Tonight, we will eat and drink like gods and wake in a kingdom made new.

speaker: Holger
en: It was rubbish! You had discarded it!

speaker: Gudrun
en: It was not rubbish! I intended to use it!

speaker: Randvi
en: Please, calm down.

speaker: Gudrun
en: I found the evidence! He hasn't a leg to stand on!

speaker: Holger
en: That is not evidence! That is art!

speaker: Holger
en: You were never going to use that sailcloth! Admit it!

speaker: Gudrun
en: How could you know that?

speaker: Holger
en: Where is Sigurd? I have no doubt he will take my side.

speaker: Gudrun
en: If you think Sigurd will take the side of a thief, you are a brazen fool!

speaker: Holger
en: How dare you!

speaker: Randvi
en: Please. Quiet, stop yelling.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi, what is this?

speaker: Randvi
en: Another dispute, I'm afraid... with Holger stirring the pot once again. Will you sit in judgment?

speaker: Eivor
en: Judgment is the burden of a jarl. This is Sigurd's duty now.

speaker: Randvi
en: He refuses to leave his quarters. Right now, you are the only noble fit for this.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't know. It's not my place...

speaker: Randvi
en: Please. Only until Sigurd recovers his strength.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. Once more...

speaker: Eivor
en: Gudrun. Holger. Come forward. You will state your cases, and I will hear you out and be as swift in my judgment as I am able.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gudrun, you may speak.

speaker: Gudrun
en: I have been robbed, Eivor. My property defaced. Three days ago, I discovered some of my sailcloth missing. I scoured the settlement in search for it. Passing Holger's home, there I see it! Boldly displaced and worse ... defaced! With scrawls and silly stories upon it.

speaker: Holger
en: Lies and slander!

speaker: Eivor
en: Holger, quiet. You are well acquianted with the rules of this trial. Now... Gudrun, what did you do upon discovering your sailcloth?

speaker: Gudrun
en: I confronted him, demanding silver. For a sail with Holger's inky scratchings cannot be sold or bartered, can it? I ask only that I be paid for the property that was taken from me. Yet he refuses.

speaker: Eivor
en: So Holger took something that belonged to you and defaced it. Now you wish to be paid for the item. Do I understand?

speaker: Gudrun
en: That is right.

speaker: Eivor
en: Holger, what say you in your defense?

speaker: Holger
en: Short days ago, I found a pile of mildew-stained detritus beneath the docks and salvaged what I could. I wished to use it as a canvas, you see? As a conveyance for my latest works. The sailcloth was in such a state, and so obscured from view, I assumed it was refuse! Abandoned goods!

speaker: Eivor
en: I see...

speaker: Holger
en: My motives were honest, Eivor. Would a thief be so brazen as to display the fruits of his crimes? Hardly. Yet here she claims I have robbed and defaced her property, when all I took was rubbish left by to rot.

speaker: Gudrun
en: Nonsense.

speaker: Holger
en: My only crime here is that I gave something ugly and decrepit a bold new life.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see... so you feel Gudrun disposed of something and now unreasonably seeks its return.

speaker: Holger
en: Exactly, yes.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. I have heard enough.

speaker: Gudrun
en: I might have profited from that cloth. Holger has all but robbed me of a future boon!

speaker: Holger
en: It was garbage! Yet now it is part of something greater. If anything, I have increased its value. You ought to thank me.

speaker: Gudrun
en: O, I will thank you with the back of my

speaker: Eivor
en: Quiet. Let me speak...

speaker: Eivor
en: After careful thought, it is clear that

speaker: Eivor
en: After careful thought, it is clear that

speaker: Sigurd
en: What is this? What are you doing?

speaker: Eivor
en: Holger and Gudrun are at odds. I hoped to find a resolution.

speaker: Sigurd
en: That duty is mine alone, Eivor. You know this! Stand aside!

speaker: Eivor
en: You were not here, Brother. Nor did I wish to bother you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: A sallow excuse for a bold defiance. I hope you enjoyed it.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Are you finished singing, my dear skald?

speaker: Holger
en: My jarl, as I was saying I was

speaker: Sigurd
en: Stop! Enough! I have heard more than enough to render my judgment. For as long as I known you, Holger, you have spun words into lies. You weaken the minds of children, and delude the minds of men. I've shown you too many years of tolerance. And rather than exist in grateful meekness, as Holger the Liar, you sink lower.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You become Holger the Thief, robbing a woman of her livelihood, all in the name of your stupid stories!

speaker: Holger
en: Sigurd Jarl, no. Th-that is not the

speaker: Sigurd
en: This is the consequence of your actions. You will pay Gudrun the value of thirty sailcloths...

speaker: Holger
en: Thirty times? Surely you jest! That would ruin me, Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Do I look like one to play pranks, Holger? Pay the fee or be exiled!

speaker: Gudrun
en: Great jarl, if I may... I seek only compensation for a single sailcloth, the rest is

speaker: Sigurd
en: Thirty times! In silver! That is my judgment.

speaker: Holger
en: Eivor, please... does this not seem unfair?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd is our jarl. His word is law, whether or not you agree.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You see?

speaker: Holger
en: Of course, my jarl. As it must be. Forgive my defiance.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, the punishment must fit the crime. Your judgment is cruel and unfair.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Cruel and unfair? O, no. No, you have it backwards. I am the definition what is fair and what is not. I am your jarl, the source of all right and all wrong. The lord of justice in this place. Without rank, without order, without a chain of command, life cannot endure! Chaos will reign. Do you understand?

speaker: Eivor
en: As my brother and my jarl, I back you, Sigurd. But in the face of injustice, I cannot help but speak.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Have you never in your life known when to hold your tongue, Eivor? Nor defer to those wiser than yourself? My judgment stands. Thirty times the sailcloth's value. That is final.

speaker: Gudrun
en: Thank you, lord, for hearing us out.

speaker: Sigurd
en: See to it that judgment is carried out exactly as I have said. Should the need arise again, do not fail to rouse me.

speaker: Gudrun
en: Thank you, Holger. And please, do not let this blunt our friendship. I did not mean for this to escalate.

speaker: Holger
en: No, I understand. You were well within your rights.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd...?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Leave me be.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you wish it.

speaker: Randvi
en: I want to thank you for your judgment, Eivor. For stepping in, when Sigurd would not. In spite of what happened.

speaker: Eivor
en: Poor man. I have never known him to be so angry and reckless. Is that a side you have seen?

speaker: Randvi
en: Rarely. There have been moments when he was distressed, worried, afraid. But nothing like this. Never, ever, like this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let us do our best for him, as we take care of our own. We are his best hope for healing.

speaker: Randvi
en: If it isn't too late. In the meantime, we press on.

speaker: Basim
en: Thank you for treating Hytham with respect and kindness, Eivor. He has found a family among your clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: He is more than welcome here. As are you.

speaker: Havi
en: These fools dared stand in her path...

speaker: Havi
en: Several wounds. This one put up a fight. Briefly, I suspect.

speaker: Havi
en: How hard was he knocked into his rock? Most likely dead upon impact.

speaker: Havi
en: No other bodies on the war path. He was the last to die.

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa caught up to Calder. His warriors moved in while he pushed on... but Eysa tore through them like a whirlwind. The trail of the dead reveals her direction. Calder's too. And most importantly, the Salakar's... They're headed west.

speaker: Havi
en: Looks like these two brought all the fires of Muspelheim with them. And |Freya]] wonders why I have always refused to take her on a tour of that scorched dunghill.

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa and Calder fought here. Blood was spilt.

speaker: Havi
en: Two sets of footprints. One is stretched, like someone fled. The other, closer together, uneven, and lined with blood. They were hobbling, perhaps.

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa and Calder fought here. He gained the advantage... Foolish girl. Eysa, your rage makes you vulnerable. She's hurt, but not enough to stop her. Looks like she followed Calder up that hill.

speaker: Havi
en: No sight of Eysa or Calder. Only these curious Jotun buffoons who stand in my way. They should run. But they won't.

speaker: Jotun Warrior 1
en: Keep alert until we know what happened here.

speaker: Jotun Warrior 2
en: Something must have caused the Muspels to leave so abruptly.

speaker: Jotun Warrior 3
en: This looks to be the source of all that noise, Mogr.

speaker: Havi
en: There was a cart here. And drag marks leading to it.

speaker: Havi
en: These, or similar, were used to restrain someone.

speaker: Havi
en: The dead stack up. For these Muspels, Ragnarök came early.

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa's spear. Abandoned... Did Calder and his minions finally best her?

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa chased Calder into this camp. Leaking her lifeblood, blinded by rage, and utterly reckless. Looks to have cost her too. She came crashing in, mauling whatever halfwit stood between her and Calder. But those halfwits fought back in numbers. Injured and disarmed, she was overpowered and restrained. Calder then had her tossed onto a cart like a sack of turnips... Looks like they fled up that path. What is it Calder plans to do with the little princess now that she is his prisoner? Surely not...

speaker: Havi
en: These tracks lead west. I must find Calder. And the Salakar. For Baldr's sake.

speaker: Havi
en: Is this blood Eysa's? Or is she still proving too much to handle?

speaker: Havi
en: They paused here for a moment before continuing... most likely to re-secure Eysa's bonds. Even in her sorry state, I imagine her to be quite the handful... She even bested me. Temporarily.

speaker: Havi
en: Perhaps Baldr would not approve of my methods. Of the cruelty I must perform on his behalf. He and Eysa, they are young. Pure of heart, but lacking in logic... One day, they will grow up and see life as I see it. In the meantime, they must rely on me to ensure they live long enough to achieve that wisdom. And so, I do not have the luxury of being... faultless.

speaker: Havi
en: I hope I'm not too late. They made a turn, towards the river.

speaker: Havi
en: Prey lies ahead. But where is the hunter?

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa.

speaker: Calder
en: Is that you again, Mad One?

speaker: Calder
en: Come to tempt fate, I see.

speaker: Havi
en: I do not die this day. Can you say the same?

speaker: Calder
en: Ah, yes. You've proven once already how you like to strut around, unencumbered by fear.

speaker: Calder
en: Perhaps the Salakar did not give you an adequate taste of it?

speaker: Havi
en: Enough of this blithering. Hand over what is now mine, or shall I just take it?

speaker: Calder
en: To know fear, we must be subjected to it. When I am through with you, I will take Eysa's willful hugr. Soon after, the Salakar will be complete. Then, believe me, you will know fear... and pain. Just like your son.

speaker: Calder
en: Weak. Old. Frail. What happened, All-Father? Too much of that pretentious Asgardian air? I enjoyed poking my blades into Baldr's flesh. Seeing what was underneath. What purity. Full and true. The apple fell far in his case. Is that your best? Come now, Havi. Even your boy put up more of a fight. Such a desperate, feeble man. I wish all the Aesir could see you now. Surtr will be surprised when I present him with his own daughter's corpse, but I will make sure he knows the truth.

speaker: Havi
en: Why is Surtr collecting hugrs? What does he mean to do with the Salakar?

speaker: Havi
en: Tell me.

speaker: Calder
en: Why? Do you aim to finish my work?

speaker: Havi
en: Ask yourself how much you care to suffer in these final moments.

speaker: Calder
en: Do your worst.

speaker: Eysa
en: You are wasting your breath. He will not tell you.

speaker: Eysa
en: And he won't have to. His secrets are known to me. You want them? Move aside.

speaker: Eysa
en: Move aside or I will destroy it.

speaker: Calder
en: Traitor!

speaker: Eysa
en: Traitor? It is you who are slaughtering your own kind.

speaker: Calder
en: What I do, I do for Surtr!

speaker: Havi
en: Such devotion requires a strong hugr. All these Muspel sacrifices... you needed only look inward.

speaker: Eysa
en: Was he right? About you wanting to complete the Salakar?

speaker: Havi
en: Surtr will not trade my son for something he cannot use.

speaker: Eysa
en: So you will see it through. To what end? How many lives would you take?

speaker: Havi
en: For Baldr, I would drain all nine realms. Even Asgard.

speaker: Eysa
en: The words of a dreadful king... and a selfless father. It is the one thing that separate you from my own. You wish to reunite with your son. I wish to see my father's plans lie in ruin. No matter the price. Can you see both through?

speaker: Havi
en: I can, but I will need your help. The Salakar still requires the hugr of a suitable Jotun. Calder never found one... I must get hunting.

speaker: Eysa
en: Do as you will. In the meantime, I'll join my stepmother, wherever she may be.

speaker: Eysa
en: I will try to learn how the Salakar fits into my father's plans. Under the guise of a contrite stepdaughter, of course.

speaker: Eysa
en: Keep it. I will need a way to find you when it is time to confront my father.

speaker: Havi
en: You and this bauble share a bond?

speaker: Havi
en: I set out to use you to my advantage. It ends with me in your debt.

speaker: Eysa
en: If it were not for you, I would have never known what my father was capable of. He used our people. Turned them on each other. For his gain. I cannot forgive him. And to that end, I am your ally.

speaker: Havi
en: In Asgard, an ally is a friend.

speaker: Eysa
en: Let us not get carried away.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this The Leech's work?

speaker: Erke
en: Ja, new corpses, every day.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you're the only target for your people's fear, then they will turn on you.

speaker: Erke
en: They're scared. If I am to be redeemed, I owe them The Leech.

speaker: Eivor
en: How many bodies is that now?

speaker: Erke
en: A score has been uncovered. Definitely The Leech's work.

speaker: Eivor
en: How can you be sure?

speaker: Eivor
en: How many bodies is that now?

speaker: Erke
en: A score has been uncovered. Definitely The Leech's work.

speaker: Eivor
en: How can you be sure?

speaker: Eivor
en: How can you be sure?

speaker: Erke
en: Their eyes are scooped out, black empty caverns. Same as Tryggr's guards.

speaker: Eivor
en: There must be hundreds of people passing by here each day. Anyone see them dumped?

speaker: Erke
en: It's the riverbank, vinr (friend). Every crooked dealing in this city goes through here.

speaker: Erke
en: Heard from Stowe yet? About The Arrow?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Leech is my focus just now. Does something worry you?

speaker: Erke
en: Ah, no. Just checking up on the old sparrow-heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: You two are close. Like brothers.

speaker: Erke
en: Ja, ja. Close like brothers you could say.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stowe has seen the same. It's not only the docks.

speaker: Erke
en: How is that sparrow-heart? I worry for him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soft but unsullied. He helped me find Avgos, and that's enough.

speaker: Erke
en: Avgos. I had a hunch or two about the arse-blister. Should have acted.

speaker: Eivor
en: Any hunches about The Leech you want to share?

speaker: Gyda
en: Erke! Tell me it wasn't her!

speaker: Erke
en: It wasn't your daughter, dear Gyda. Take a breath.

speaker: Gyda
en: O, thank Freyja! I have such a fear I will find her down here. She works errands for a smith who sends her to these docks, most times at night. I can't stand it.

speaker: Eivor
en: She works for a blacksmith? Do you know where?

speaker: Gyda
en: Never told me his name nor where he hammers. Tight-lipped about everything, the stubborn girl.

speaker: Eivor
en: When did she go missing?

speaker: Gyda
en: A few days back, left after sundown. Never came home, my Regna. Gods, if I could see her again.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's your daughter's name, Gyda?

speaker: Gyda
en: She's Regna, named for my grandmother, born with the same eyes. One green, one blue.

speaker: Eivor
en: A beautiful name.

speaker: Gyda
en: I haven't seen her in two days, and fear the worst. In Lunden, you must always fear the worst.

speaker: Eivor
en: What sort of job did she have?

speaker: Gyda
en: Ran errands and the like. She would make a delivery, trade it for hacksilver, and scurry back to her smithy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you know the name of the man?

speaker: Gyda
en: Neinn, but I wish I did. I would box his ears and harvest his nuts.

speaker: Eivor
en: Anything else you remember?

speaker: Gyda
en: I had a neighbor once tell me she saw Regna lingering for a time under the Lunden Bridge. Worried me sick hearing that.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's a good place to start. Thank you, Gyda.

speaker: Erke
en: A shady smith, a missing child. It's a lead with some weight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lunden bridge after sundown. It's worth a look.

speaker: Erke
en: Good. I'll hang about here and keep things calm. And Eivor... don't drop your guard around these docks.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do I look like one who could?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: What's that song? I know it from somewhere.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: That's the healer's song, innit? She's always singing it when she comes by.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Another one's washed up!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Out of the way. Let the man work.

speaker: Gyda
en: I trust you'll find my Regna. There's nothing for me without her.

speaker: Eivor
en: Best wait until nightfall.

speaker: Eivor
en: Best follow him. See where this leads.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can't this clod walk any faster?

speaker: Eivor
en: Careful now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this the place? Or... No. Just meandering.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Have a good amble, Alff?

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: I feel like a man renewed. You have yourself a good night.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Who's there? Fuck off! There's someone after me! Help! They be sticking out of the shadows!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Easy there, Alff, another stray dog spook you?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Hold! I'll give you anything! The purse at my belt!

speaker: Eivor
en: How does a rat like you come across so much silver?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: I... I found it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Like I might find a knife at your neck?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: The silver's for a blacksmith at Bodilsburg Garrison! Oija. I only run errands for the man. I don't know nothing else. Put his head on the block. Not mine! Please!

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Flinched! At a torch, like she's some sort of witch.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Haven't you seen the burn scars? Lost her whole clan to the flame.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Thor's thunder! Keep it down out there!

speaker: Oija
en: You got the purse I'm owed? Eh, who the fuck are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm the one asking questions, soot-finger. Did you craft a set of surgeon's tools for someone called The Leech?

speaker: Oija
en: You thick shit! Nor Hel or Valhall will want you once I'm done.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm a friend, Oija. Your money's with your lad.

speaker: Oija
en: What have you to do with him?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm keeping him safe. Had a fear he was being followed.

speaker: Oija
en: Ah, I knew he was soft. Not like my other girl. She was hard as hog's breath, that one.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened to her?

speaker: Oija
en: Fell ill a few days back. So I sent her to the Good Sister Frideswid. Healer in town.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sister Frideswid...

speaker: Oija
en: Got broken bones, a boil on your bum, or too much birth blood? She'll mend you quick.

speaker: Eivor
en: She would need a broad set of tools for such work.

speaker: Oija
en: She would, and she has it. Comes to me for all her wants, and I craft for her what she needs.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not any more, you don't.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am with The Order. The Leech bade me give you a message.

speaker: Oija
en: The Order, eh? I'd need more testament than your word alone.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have this.

speaker: Oija
en: If it's silver, I'll accept it as payment.

speaker: Eivor
en: You know this is no ealdorman's coin.

speaker: Oija
en: Right, so... so what's The Order miffed about? I'm doing my duty.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here about The Leech. The tools you made were unsound.

speaker: Oija
en: That's not my doing! Sister Frideswid is breaking them faster than I can smith!

speaker: Eivor
en: Breaking them on the bodies of the poor and unwell? We warned her against such evil.

speaker: Oija
en: Now, that's not a fair read on her work. She never kills without reason.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is for us to decide. Where is she now?

speaker: Oija
en: Where she always is. The old forum in the shade of the Giant's Wall.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, brother. And keep this to yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not your place to demand things of The Order.

speaker: Oija
en: Maybe not, but I'm not saying shit until I hear something that makes me believe you are who you claim.

speaker: Eivor
en: Never compromise The Order.

speaker: Oija
en: You know piss-all, you cheat.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Order is Eternal.

speaker: Oija
en: You know piss-all, you cheat.

speaker: Eivor
en: May the Father of Understanding guide you.

speaker: Oija
en: Right, so... so what's The Order miffed about? I'm doing my duty.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here about The Leech. The tools you made were unsound.

speaker: Oija
en: That's not my doing! Sister Frideswid is breaking them faster than I can smith!

speaker: Eivor
en: Breaking them on the bodies of the poor and unwell? We warned her against such evil.

speaker: Oija
en: Now, that's not a fair read on her work. She never kills without reason.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is for us to decide. Where is she now?

speaker: Oija
en: Where she always is. The old forum in the shade of the Giant's Wall.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, brother. And keep this to yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is where The Leech dissects her prey.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Please, please. My aunt came here for her cough. She never returned. It's been days, I must see her.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: Get out. And don't come around here again.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: It's only a cough! On the braids of Freyja, I swear I'm fit to go home.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Easy, dear. You're delirious. Let the Good Sister fix you right up.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: I don't want to die in here! I'm bound for better things!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: You're not going to die, my dear. Have patience. We'll patch you up.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 4
en: She's confined herself to her studies for so many days and nights. Up to some strange alchemy there.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 5
en: You do not imply the Devil's work, I pray? The Good Sister speaks to God alone. We should all follow her example in our devotion to Him.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Gotta get out! Let me out!

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: Easy! Come on, let's get back to your cot.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Good Sister, Frideswid.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Mummy, my stomach hurts.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 6
en: Bear up, love. The Good Sister will see that you feel better.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Is that? No, all clear.

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: You won't catch me going past Frideswid's office. Heard screaming last time.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 7
en: God go with you, Sister Frideswid.

speaker: Sister Frideswid
en: And with you, child.

speaker: Sister Frideswid
en: For the gift of your eyes, I thank you, Regna. One blue, one green. Sign of the One Reborn. So fascinating. So beautiful. Bless you. You have advanced the cause of our kind.

speaker: Sister Frideswid
en: One more, that's all. I'm nearly finished.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's enough.

speaker: Sister Frideswid
en: Ah. It's you...

speaker: Odin
en: For all the dead we collect, dear sister, you and I are equals.

speaker: Sister Frideswid
en: Quite a charnel house. I lost count of how many. I suppose I've been greedy in my research. But not for lack of care. The Ancient Ones, the arbiters. They built us out of simple pieces. So easy to break. So difficult to mend.

speaker: Sister Frideswid
en: There must be an improvement. We should be stronger, faster, smarter. I could have fixed us. I could have made us better.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are blood and bone and spirit, Frideswid. Perfect as we are.

speaker: Sister Frideswid
en: You've such beautiful eyes. Finish it... would you?

speaker: Eivor
en: A young girl. Her eyes have been removed. I have a feeling this is the missing Regna.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is done.

speaker: Erke
en: Ah, The Leech is bled out. And did you catch a name?

speaker: Eivor
en: A nun, name of Frideswid.

speaker: Erke
en: What? The Good Sister? That can't be right. She was a saint. A healer and a... Gods. That brick fits this week's wall of shit.

speaker: Eivor
en: You knew her?

speaker: Erke
en: She saved me. Mended a broken leg. Thought I'd lose it. But not with Frideswid. You wouldn't know it was ever broken. The sands will run backwards now. Without her, we'll return to balancing humors.

speaker: Eivor
en: All of that for this. Secrets of the human form. How she saved lives.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brick of shit sounds about right. She was making dog meat out of Regna when I found her.

speaker: Erke
en: Fuck.

speaker: Eivor
en: You knew her?

speaker: Erke
en: She saved me. Mended a broken leg. Thought I'd lose it. But not with Frideswid. You wouldn't know it was ever broken. The sands will run backwards now. Without her, we'll return to balancing humors.

speaker: Eivor
en: All of that for this. Secrets of the human form. How she saved lives.

speaker: Eivor
en: All of that for this. Secrets of the human form. How she saved lives.

speaker: Erke
en: And how she ended them. It might be the ravings of a madwoman.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not every problem has a clean solution.

speaker: Erke
en: True, very true. I've built my name selling the hard fix. I'll live with it.

speaker: Eivor
en: This was her fix. All her ideas and discoveries written here. Ill-gotten gains.

speaker: Erke
en: I have a mind to burn that bloody tome. Is that the right call?

speaker: Eivor
en: Too many died for this book. It isn't worth its weight in blood.

speaker: Erke
en: You're right, it would be like plucking straw from shit. Too much bad with the good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin and Freyja weigh the worth of our lives, not some c*nt in a wimple.

speaker: Erke
en: Aye, get rid of it then. And tell no one of this.

speaker: Eivor
en: It has cures for everything. From boils to broken bones. It's worth keeping. We fight wars to save those we love, and pay in blood for what we win. This book ... This is your Good Sister's battlefield. Her kingdom.

speaker: Erke
en: You may be right. We can't return the dead to life, but their sacrifice can mean something.

speaker: Erke
en: If you need me, I'll be at Saint Paul's, searching for something on The Compass. Thanks for all this, Broga.

speaker: Azar
en: Your crew can find lodging here. Come. Let us find Bárid.

speaker: Bárid
en: Eivor! Blood of my blood. Look at you! You have Aunt Rosta's cheekbones.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you! The seven-year old lives in you still.

speaker: Bárid
en: It has been a long stretch since we pelted old Ganfrid with apple cores.

speaker: Eivor
en: He never forgave us for that.

speaker: Bárid
en: And Sigurd and the clan? How goes it all?

speaker: Eivor
en: There's much to tell you, Bárid, but let me breathe your Irish air.

speaker: Azar
en: Thank you for keeping my ports from being set ablaze in my abscene.

speaker: Bárid
en: "My ports?" Yes, Old Man, I can rule my city even without you here. Eivor, you arrive in good time. I'm hosting a feast in honor of my son, Sichfrith. He is seventeen today.

speaker: Eivor
en: A seventeen-year-old son.

speaker: Bárid
en: And rather a difficult boy at that. Come, there's much to show on the way to my castle.

speaker: Eivor
en: A kingship, a son, and a castle! Truly, you have a fine life, Bárid.

speaker: Azar
en: Castle? It is a wooden house. Finely crafted to be sure, but in Shiraz, it would be home to a middling rug merchant.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lead me to your rug merchant's wooden hovel, Bárid.

speaker: Bárid
en: Just look at her docks! Wee babe of a city, but the biggest port in all Ireland.

speaker: Azar
en: You cannot appreciate Irish air without enduring the stench of our docks.

speaker: Bárid
en: It's upon the strength of this port I plan to secure my kingship.

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar told me that your throne may not be entirely steady.

speaker: Bárid
en: King Flann needs some persuading is all. Dublin's vast trade web will bring wealth to all Ireland. If Flann can be made to see that, my kingship and that of my children's children will be safe.

speaker: Azar
en: I cannot guarantee your throne but a vast trading web is within my power.

speaker: Bárid
en: No one else I'd trust my commerce to, Old Man.

speaker: Eivor
en: You let him call you that?

speaker: Azar
en: I call him worse things.

speaker: Azar
en: This is where I leave you.

speaker: Bárid
en: Don't miss the banquet!

speaker: Azar
en: I'll be there shortly.

speaker: Aoife
en: Bárid! My mighty king!

speaker: Bárid
en: Aoife! This is my cousin Eivor. Show her the bow I had you make for her.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is for me? The craftsmanship is beautiful.

speaker: Aoife
en: Me best work. Give 'er a try. Hit the targets before the sand runs out. Think you can get them all?

speaker: Eivor
en: I just want to get a feel for how the bow handles.

speaker: Aoife
en: That's sure.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course I will. Stand ready to be astonished.

speaker: Aoife
en: Aren't you the confident one? Sure, I'll be embarrassed for you if you shat on the eggs.

speaker: Eivor
en: Watch my arrows fly.

speaker: Aoife
en: I certainly will. Go!

speaker: Bárid
en: Damn good shot!

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a very nice bow. Thank you, Bárid.

speaker: Bárid
en: Steps off a boat after a long sea voyage and shoots like a master!

speaker: Eivor
en: The bow needs tuning. But it is a very thoughtful gift.

speaker: Bárid
en: You had a long sea voyage. Haven't got your land legs yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well done, cousin. Wait, is that a house of God?

speaker: Bárid
en: Aye, Christ's own church. Ireland mostly Christian now and so is Dublin. Many Norse chew the wafer.

speaker: Eivor
en: You make a place for them.

speaker: Bárid
en: Them? I, myself, have a place in Christ's house as I do in the house of Thor. So long as a god has my back, he has my altar.

speaker: Bárid
en: I've built this city up from rubble. Twenty years ago, us Vikings were beaten. The Irish took revenge and sacked Dublin.

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar told me it is a Viking city.

speaker: Bárid
en: Norse founded it and I nursed it back to health. When I became king, I was king of a mud pit.

speaker: Bárid
en: There, up ahead. My home. My only regret is that my mother and my wife aren't here to greet you. They've gone to pilgrimage to the mountains just now. The waters there improve Mother's health. I am left to discipline my wayward son.

speaker: Eivor
en: And to host a banquet!

speaker: Bárid
en: Which should be already underway.

speaker: Irish Woman 1
en: Upp Bárid! Fo dia! (Greetings!)

speaker: Bárid
en: Here we are! Please, go enjoy yourself. I must have a word with my son. Come meet him before the night's out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar, I was not sure if I would see you here.

speaker: Azar
en: Why is that?

speaker: Eivor
en: I thought you'd rather take stock of your wares than placidly observe caterwauling Vikings.

speaker: Bárid
en: And you? You would rather spend time with this gossiping auntie?

speaker: Eivor
en: I like to greet everyone at parties.

speaker: Azar
en: There is no shortage of amusements. Enjoy yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know few people here, and of them, I know you are the one who is always ready with a sweet anecdote.

speaker: Azar
en: I do have some information you may find interesting. Sichfrith's stomach doesn't agree with cheese. Had an accident about it last week. The embarrassing, bed-changing kind.

speaker: Eivor
en: He shat himself?

speaker: Azar
en: Mortifying for a lad of that age. The kind of thing that would devastate him in front of his comrades. If one needed ammunition.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Azar. Your company is always enlightening.

speaker: Irish Man 2
en: Aye, you Bárid's cousin? It's a grand do, isn't it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hej. Enjoying yourself?

speaker: Irish Man 2
en: It's great (fun)! 'Tis a fine thing to celebrate Future King Sichfrith.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm curious, how do you feel Bárid has done as king?

speaker: Irish Man 2
en: Oh, he's done a lovely job, he has. Likes to throw feasts, invites us common folk! More host than king perhaps, but he's a fine man, and the city has never been busier!

speaker: Eivor
en: Can I ask, what is your life like in this city?

speaker: Irish Man 2
en: Well, there's a fair amount of work, isn't there? Hauling crates, shoveling muck. I'm a tanner, meself. Long days stripping hides and dousing 'em in cow piss. You can probably smell the stench!

speaker: Eivor
en: I can!

speaker: Eivor
en: Enjoy the feast, friend.

speaker: Irish Man 2
en: You as well.

speaker: Bárid
en: Enough with your willfulness. It is past time to put away childish things.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: What do you expect, Father? That I follow your example? The example of a pack mule?

speaker: Bárid
en: Sichfrith! I expect my son to act like a future king! Not roll in the muck!

speaker: Sichfrith
en: So Flann can take you on as his farting court jester?

speaker: Bárid
en: Think with your head and not your arse! Flann can assure my throne, which will one day be yours.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: That makes you the arse!

speaker: Bárid
en: Enough!

speaker: Bárid
en: Eivor. My son, Sichfrith. I'm sorry, I... I must clear my head. Could you speak to the boy?

speaker: Eivor
en: I was looking forward to meeting my cousin's son.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: So, you're the cousin who Da speaks so fondly of. Is this old fool reduced to importing Vikings now?

speaker: Eivor
en: In Norway, you'd be knocked to the ground by now.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Come on then, if you've any guts worth respecting!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine, whelp.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: You won't land a single punch!

speaker: Eivor
en: Only shitbirds mock their father under his own roof.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Right, because the cousin who just arrived has the authority over how I speak in my own home.

speaker: Eivor
en: In Norway, you'd be knocked to the ground by now.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Come on then, if you've any guts worth respecting!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine, whelp.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: You won't land a single punch!

speaker: Bárid
en: A lot of shit coming from that mouth. Word is you have trouble controlling it out the other end too.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: I guess I owe you thanks for not beating me bloody.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not here to quarrel with you, Sichfrith.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: That's an empty victory. You clearly lost on purpose.

speaker: Eivor
en: You made a rash challenge. No point embarrassing you in front of your father's people.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Da speaks so highly of you, I wanted to see if you lived up to the stories.

speaker: Eivor
en: Does anyone?

speaker: Eivor
en: You're unhappy with how your father rules?

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Da has the makings of a fine king, but ... he chooses to play the unctuous merchant instead.

speaker: Eivor
en: A visit to Norway might do a young Vikingr like you some good.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: I'd love to go with Da. Maybe the homeland would rekindle his warrior spirit. Give Dublin a fair and fearsome king.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've lost track of your father. Any idea where he might be?

speaker: Sichfrith
en: He wanted to clear his head. That means he's visiting grandfather's grave. Da has a chat with him almost every day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid can commune with the dead?

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Ha! No. His conversations are all one-sided. The grave sits at the top of the hill.

speaker: Bárid
en: I will find him. Thank you, Sichfrith.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Eivor! Teach me how to hit like that sometime?

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why so uneasy?

speaker: Bárid
en: Ah... A king must forever be on guard. When I'm upset or uncertain, I come here to seek my father's spirit.

speaker: Eivor
en: I didn't even ask after him. Somehow I knew he'd...

speaker: Bárid
en: Some years ago. He was destined to die in battle, and he did.

speaker: Eivor
en: He sits with Odin now. My family owes yours a solemn debt.

speaker: Bárid
en: That winter your family came to stay with us... I remember your birth, screaming like a warrior.

speaker: Eivor
en: The plague year, no one would take us in. No one but your mother and father. I owe your family my life.

speaker: Bárid
en: And what a life we had! I've fond memories of you and I slipping out to hunt

speaker: Eivor
en: in dead of night! Stars in the sky, moonlight on snow...

speaker: Eivor
en: ...and that's how I got that scar.

speaker: Bárid
en: I do feel bad about that. What about the one on your cheek?

speaker: Eivor
en: This? A caution from the gods about my vanity.

speaker: Bárid
en: Come, if we tell all our stories, we'll be here a week.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you see something?

speaker: Bárid
en: My imagination run amok. But, let us away.

speaker: Bárid
en: Funny how the slightest noise sets a fellow on edge.

speaker: Eivor
en: By Thor's hammer, Bárid. I could sleep a week.

speaker: Bárid
en: Not as spry as the old days, eh? When we'd search the night in hopes of catching a will o' the wisp.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did we catch one? I have a memory of catching one.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Bárid mac Ímair! Give yourself up!

speaker: Bárid
en: What? Back!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Grab him! Bind his hands!

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are these men?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Damn you bastards!

speaker: Eivor
en: Who were they?

speaker: Bárid
en: My ascension to the throne has not been without contest. The previous king's son, Thorstein is resentful.

speaker: Eivor
en: You told me nothing of this.

speaker: Bárid
en: You are my guest. I am not going to burden you with petty concerns.

speaker: Eivor
en: Petty concerns? I now know why you've been anxious all evening.

speaker: Bárid
en: Aye, 'tis worrying. He's never been so bold before.

speaker: Eivor
en: He sees you as a usurper to his throne?

speaker: Bárid
en: Perhaps. But he doesn't seem he wants to take it. He content himself by stealing and smuggling with his band of ruffians. It's petty Viking raiding, but it puts me in a bad light with Flann, that's certain.

speaker: Bárid
en: Keep a sharp watch. Brigands rove the streets tonight.

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: You can be sure of me, my king.

speaker: Azar
en: What? You know I am always the last to leave a party. What is wrong?

speaker: Eivor
en: We were ambushed by Thorstein's men. Rivals I was not made aware of.

speaker: Azar
en: Small wonder why King Flann does not embrace you, Bárid. You cannot keep control of Vikings in your own city.

speaker: Bárid
en: Thorstein makes me look like more of an arse than I do on my own.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see. It is the High King's disfavor that makes this shameful. My cousin, I will take care of Thorstein.

speaker: Bárid
en: No, I do not want to drag you into this sorry mess. Perhaps he'll accept silver to lie low.

speaker: Eivor
en: For a week or two. But then he'll be back and back again. I can remove this blot once and for all.

speaker: Bárid
en: Eivor, this is not your fight.

speaker: Azar
en: For any and all of your gods' sakes, Bárid, let Eivor help you.

speaker: Eivor
en: As of this moment, Bárid, my arm is yours. Whatever is needed to bring Flann's smile upon you, I will do.

speaker: Bárid
en: Eivor, I've never been so happy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your family saved mine those years ago. A fitting reply would be to secure your throne. I will start with Thorstein.

speaker: Azar
en: It happens that Sichfrith may know something. He once ran with Thorstein's gang.

speaker: Bárid
en: Sadly true. Seek him tomorrow in the marketplace. After a night of carousing, he likes to recuperate there.

speaker: Eivor
en: We will begin to forge a bond with High King Flann on rise of sun.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid said Sichfrith would be at the marketplace. I need to learn more about Thorstein.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it about this stone that captivates you, Fulke?

speaker: Fulke
en: The Saga Stone comes from an ancient race of beings, a generation of lesser gods. As do all the artifacts I collect for my church.

speaker: Eivor
en: You prayed to the Christ Jesus in your cell. Is your church not the Church of Rome, like these Saxons?

speaker: Fulke
en: These Saxons believe in Christ the Redeemer. But I know his true purpose. Christ the Educator, the keeper of secret knowledge.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this why Eadwyn loathes you? For preaching such an idea?

speaker: Fulke
en: Yes. Christians like her, like Aelfred, they believe Christ's purpose on earth was to wash us free of Sin. The Roman Church has been deluded by the lies of Saklas, or Ialdabaoth, the demiurge of many names. A lesser god. Saklas and his kind were wise in their time, but they lost sight of the true God, the Self-Begotten One, Lord of the Treasury of Light. This is why Eadwyn had me punished and imprisoned. What she calls heresy is, in fact, the true nature of the universe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yours is a strange saga, Fulke.

speaker: Fulke
en: And I have not yet reached its end.

speaker: Basim
en: Be on your guard, someone is watching us.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Take care, everyone.

speaker: Eivor
en: The villagers aren't happy we're here.

speaker: Basim
en: Eadwyn's eyes and ears, no doubt.

speaker: Fulke
en: This is the place, up ahead.

speaker: Sigurd
en: What is this tower?

speaker: Fulke
en: A ruin from England's Roman past.

speaker: Fulke
en: My acolyte found it abandoned and derelict. He took refuge here after his bishop expelled him for teaching the same truths that got me imprisoned.

speaker: Basim
en: He was a priest?

speaker: Fulke
en: He was and he is. The Bishops of England are simply too craven and deluded to understand the secret wisdom we possess.

speaker: Fulke
en: Brother Paul! Are you here?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ransacked, from floor to roof. Basim, stand guard outside.

speaker: Fulke
en: This was Eadwyn's doing, I have no doubt.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The stone is within?

speaker: Fulke
en: I asked Paul to hide it well. But I do not know where.

speaker: Notice of Excommunication
en: Be it known, he of the name Paul, consecrated priest of Oxeneforda, is henceforth abjured and severed from his Church and fellows for the spreading of pernicious heresies and blasphemies. May he be denied forgiveness unto the final days.

speaker: Fulke
en: Brother Paul is very clever. It could be hidden anywhere.

speaker: Fulke
en: This moves.

speaker: Sigurd
en: It must be there!

speaker: Journal Entry
en: Fulke has entrusted me with a most curious relic, a stone carved with strange and unearthly script. I have fasted and prayed in an attempt to unlock its meaning, but alas!

speaker: Fulke
en: Dear God!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this him, your acolyte Paul?

speaker: Fulke
en: My dearest friend.

speaker: Fulke
en: May you live as one with the true God, in the Treasury of Light.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Your friend paid the price for his loyalty. I imagine he was guarding the stone.

speaker: Fulke
en: Eadwyn's men did this. They killed Brother Paul and took my stone.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You. Always questioning, second guessing my wishes. You slowed us down and I missed my chance!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a stone, Sigurd! You're chasing shadows, like a madman howling at the moon.

speaker: Eivor
en: What matters is victory! Against Eadwyn and her allies.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This was my victory. To know my true self. My destiny! My

speaker: Eivor
en: Patience, Brother. We will find this stone, wherever it is. Right or wrong, you will have your answer.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I know the answer already, Eivor. I have seen it in my dreams. I know exactly

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim fills your head with twisted prophecies. He leads you like a chained dog.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Basim has shown me so much! He knows my mind, he

speaker: Fulke
en: Hold, both of you! You hear that?

speaker: Basim
en: Soldiers! Eadwyn's here.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: How dare you Danes befoul my lands?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Hold off, Eivor. First we talk.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Lady Eadwyn, a stone was taken from this tower. Inscribed with runes and the image of a tree. Do you know it?

speaker: Eadwyn
en: Yes. One of this heretic's blasphemous baubles. Is that why you've come?

speaker: Basim
en: We are here to trade. That stone for an assurance of peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you saying? We gave Geadric our word!

speaker: Sigurd
en: For the stone, we will leave your lands and not return.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: O, for this, you must bring me Geadric's head.

speaker: Basim
en: The stone is within our grasp.

speaker: Eivor
en: We made a promise, Brother. Brother.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: We have a deal then?

speaker: Sigurd
en: We accept.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: Done.

speaker: Eivor
en: We do not!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor! No!

speaker: Eadwyn
en: Cut them down! Leave none alive!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor! Are you mad?

speaker: Fulke
en: Eadwyn flees!

speaker: Eivor
en: We had our chance!

speaker: Sigurd
en: We will speak of this, Eivor! I will not forget!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Get ready. More of them!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor... you muck-minded fool!

speaker: Basim
en: That was our chance to recover the stone without letting of blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not betray Geadric!

speaker: Sigurd
en: That is not for you to decide!

speaker: Eivor
en: My promises are my own, and they are ironclad.

speaker: Basim
en: Your first oath is to your jarl. Sigurd Jarl, your brother and master.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that now your stance? In spite of promises made?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I am your jarl, and I have sight and wisdom well beyond what you know.

speaker: Eivor
en: A coward's answer!

speaker: Basim
en: Remember your place, Eivor. Or nothing good will come of all this.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's one view, Basim. I believe there will be other chances. We can keep our oaths and find this stone together.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay out of this.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Enough!

speaker: Basim
