en: If it wasn't clear why Sigurd is in command, it is now. Your temper runs too hot, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You want to settle things with Basim, you call a holmgang. Else you follow me. You listen to me. You do as I ask.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eadwyn will flee to her castle. You want your stone, it will be there.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Geadric's pathetic army will never breach the walls. We could have first taken the stone, then laid siege. That was always our plan, Eivor. I had no intention of betraying Geadric.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was your plan all along, yet you saw fit to keep me guessing through your fits of madness.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You are not always to be trusted. Your passions overcome you. I know that. My father knew that. Your father knew it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sit here and bemoan your fate, Brother. I have a promise to keep. And I mean to.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You think too much of yourself, Eivor. You do not have the wisdom of Odin. Come, Basim.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You move with the wrath of Odin, but you do not have his wisdom.

speaker: Sigurd
en: That will lead you astray, Eivor.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Come friend. We have a battle to prepare for.

speaker: Fulke
en: This quarrel with your brother is something to behold. Has it always been so heated?

speaker: Eivor
en: All my life, we moved as one, as family, as kin. I have always known his mind, and he mine... until this day.

speaker: Fulke
en: Time makes idiots of us all.

speaker: Eivor
en: You fought well today, Fulke. Would you fight beside me now?

speaker: Fulke
en: To wrest control of the shire from Eadwyn? I will.

speaker: Eivor
en: Geadric asked me to cripple her line of support. Would you know where she gets her rations and supplies?

speaker: Fulke
en: East of Oxeneforda, south of the Leah Villa, there's a place called Eatun Barn where eager merchants sell to soldiers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Meet me there. I'll come soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, Brother. You are lost in a sea-storm of your own making.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eadwyn's defenses have been weakened. But I could do more before joining Fulke.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I wish somebody'd chase these Britons out of here.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: This war is endless. Who cares who's our lord? The sheep must be shorn either way.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Smell that, Ceolbert?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I... I think so. A faint, grassy odor?

speaker: Ivarr
en: No, no, the air smells of distant thunder. Thor walks with us.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's Ivarr. Ceolbert, too.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr. Ceolbert.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Hej, Eivor. I was telling the ' here that Thor is with us this day. Our victory is assured.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, what is your plan?

speaker: Ivarr
en: That bastard Ynyr commands this hamlet. So let us show these folks what happens when a village bows to the Britons. Smash it to kindling, burn it to ashes, and cut Ynyr's tender throat. Right, my boy?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I hope to fight well, not cruelly. The cutting of throats, I leave to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ynyr is the Britons' best warrior. If he dies a brutal death, Rhodri will think twice about fighting back.

speaker: Eivor
en: Flames and smoke will warm Rhodri's desire for peace. Ynyr is a lesser concern.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Peace is for suckling babes, but as you like.

speaker: Eivor
en: If we prevail here, Ceolbert becomes ealdorman.

speaker: Ivarr
en: First an ætheling, soon an ealdorman. One day, the king! O, you are jumping rank, boy.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I hope to begin my tenure in peace, Ivarr. Let us finish this here, once and for all.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Even talks like an ealdorman now.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ugh... my blood runs hot. Let us rush in now and leave a trail of bloody kindling.

speaker: Eivor
en: A stealthy approach might earn us more time.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Bah! I prefer sound and fury. But do as you must.

speaker: Eivor
en: I want to go in quietly. No point bringing in every armed Briton down on your heads.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Am I to stand here drooling like the village idiot, waiting for your success?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert, listen to this old man's stories and wipe his drool for him.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I am not a patient man, Eivor. Put these dogs down quietly or I may just join you the way I did in Ledecestre.

speaker: Ivarr
en: We will stay behind and draw runes in the dirt. But do not take long, my blood is up.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor! Are you not done? Have you stopped to nap? Enough! I will have blood! Ivar...!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods, Ivarr. You're a rabid hound.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bloody kindling it is! We will smash this place to splinters!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Come, Ceolbert. The fight is on!

speaker: Eivor
en: Let the Saxon villagers flee, Ivarr. Only the Britons deserve our wrath.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Thor thunders beside us!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Aaah!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Light it up and burn it down! Burn it all down!

speaker: Eivor
en: Should rid this place of soldiers. Less support for Rhodri.

speaker: Briton Warrior 1
en: You think those Danes will ever stop coming for us?

speaker: Briton Warrior 2
en: You'd think killing Rhodri's brother shoulda been enough for 'em.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor, here comes Ynyr! He's roiling in like a winter sea!

speaker: Ynyr ap Cadfarch
en: Smoke! Someone set that fire. Find them.

speaker: Ynyr ap Cadfarch
en: Cowards! Quit your hiding spots and fight me, Ynyr! Son of Cadfarch! Killer of Danes.

speaker: Ynyr ap Cadfarch
en: Keep careful watch. Danes would gut your children for amusement.

speaker: Ynyr ap Cadfarch
en: Danes! They're in the camp.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I'll broil you alive and feed your balls to chickens, Ynyr!

speaker: Ynyr Ap Cadfarch
en: Ivarr! You lost on the beach at , and you will lose here.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Your army is weak! We will gut you like tired swine!

speaker: Ynyr ap Cadfarch
en: I'll pull your tongue through the back of your throat just to shut you up.

speaker: Ivarr
en: So much for Ynyr. Fearsome Briton, my bunghole.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ah! That's the last of them! Let us get a good view of our handiwork, Ceolbert! Join us, Eivor! Look here! Look upon this masterpiece!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor! Did you see Ceolbert fight? He is all balls now.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I give thanks for victory and ask penance for taking lives.

speaker: Ivarr
en: O Ceolbert, your god bores me to death. Have a laugh, we won!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: And I took no pleasure in it, Ivarr.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor and I were made for this, my boy. The song of swords, the blood-mist, the bone-crunching and baring of teeth.

speaker: Eivor
en: To survive a battle is to be born anew, in blood and screams.

speaker: Ivarr
en: My father died in a snake pit. Left nothing but moldy bones and putrid flesh. But by the gods, he had earned a place at Odin's table!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your father left a strong .

speaker: Eivor
en: There was once a village here. Of innocent folk. Working, hustling, cheating, laughing, whoring. Life. We turned it to kindling, men died, refugees fled. A village is turned to ashes.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Come now! We are Norsemen! That is our calling.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this enough blood paid, Ivarr? We've spilt enough to slake the thirst of Fenrir.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Why stop there?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert, I would know your mind on all this. Are you satisfied with our victory?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I... I believe I am. I'll still need word from Rhodri as soon as possible. What does he intend?

speaker: Eivor
en: He will see the flames. He'll know Wesberie has been destroyed.

speaker: Ivarr
en: The bleeding pus pit claims only a dragon can defeat him. We'll soon put that to the test.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is peace we want, Ivarr. Not revenge. If you cannon accept that, return to Repton now.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You do not know Rhodri as I do, Eivor. You do not know what a slippery, lying shit he can be."

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Enough talk of killing! I need a moment of calm.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You need mead.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: No, Ivarr. True calm. A walk in the woods to clear the air. Or... fishing. Would you go fishing with me?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Fishing, huh? Looking for a warm puddle to dangle your worm in?'

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I saw a small pond nearby. Will you come?

speaker: Eivor
en: We can all take a moment to allow our blood to cool.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: It's just up here.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I have no fondness for fishing. Where is the sport in it? There is no chance the fish will kill me.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Here will be good. Let's fish for eel. Deorlaf relishes nettle soup cooked with eels fresh from the water.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I will not fish. You go ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: All I have are my weapons.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Is that how Danes fish?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Hooked! Bring it to shore! Well done, Eivor. An eel!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Another eel! Almost enough for a hearty soup.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: That's enough for now. Bishop Deorlaf will be pleased. Let's go tell Ivarr about our catch.

speaker: Ivarr
en: That took longer than clearing this village.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: We caught some eel for a feast. The bishop should be pleased.

speaker: Ivar
en: The simple fellow comes now.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Ah! A strange way to celebrate victory. But then again, our Christ was a , was he not?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Bishop, greetings. We've the makings for a delicious soup!

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: I'm grateful, Ceolbert. But my heart is heavy. So many homes burnt. We'll be years rebuilding.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You should have seen Ceolbert fight. He will be an ealdorman with sack and guts. Fearsome and raw!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I should rather be fair and just. But I take the compliment.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: I have sent word to the Britons. I pray King Rhodri will again be open to peace. In spite of his brother's murder.

speaker: Ivarr
en: It worked in our favor! Look where we landed... Britons begging for mercy like whiny pups.

speaker: Eivor
en: I had my doubts about this plan Ivarr, but I believe it may work. The blow we dealt Rhodri is a painful one.

speaker: Eivor
en: We set the village ablaze, yes. But peace is not guaranteed. And it will take another sort of skill to win it. Restraint.

speaker: Eivor
en: The fighting is done, but the talking has not yet begun. We'll need to be careful about who attends our negotiations.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Our next steps are critical, my lords. And after what happened in Quatford, it is clear to me that Ivarr should lay low.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Lay low? After all I have done here, you tell me to dunk my head?

speaker: Eivor
en: The good bishop is right, Ivarr. You have a warrior's heart, not a peacemaker's.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Fuck you, Wolf-Kissed. I know Rhodri, and I know the kind of tricks he will pull. This is me warning you.

speaker: Ivarr
en: If you hear me farting, that is my welcome to the bastard!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: You bruised his pride, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you have some balm for it, by all means, share it.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: His pride makes him difficult. And his anger makes him hasty. But he is not without honest feeling.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I will hunt him a great boar, I think. And together we'll roast it over a fire and tell tales of war. That should please him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bishop, we must prepare for Rhodri's arrival. Rally our men and set up a camp just here.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Peace or war will be decided, but not yet, not now. We must wait.

speaker: Eivor
en: I loathe waiting.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: It is all in God's hands. We can but pray and give thanks for this moment of rest.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: The Britons have come!

speaker: Eivor
en: The moment has ended.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: This way, by the great oak.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Where is Ceolbert? He ought to be present for these talks, as our future ealdorman.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: He went hunting. For wild boar, he said.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: That was quite some time ago, no?

speaker: Eivor
en: We cannot wait. We should settle the peace now.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Lady Angharad, greetings!

speaker: Angharad
en: We come to speak of peace.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: We are gladdened to hear it. But where is your great king?

speaker: Angharad
en: He stays at the castle at my behest. I feared his presence would inflame the cutthroat, Ivarr.

speaker: Eivor
en: We have confined our cutthroat to his tent.

speaker: Angharad
en: Both of us fretting over our war-hungry companions, it seems we are of the same mind.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: A surplus of caution never did any harm. I count this as a blessing.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are wise to leave him behind. Your husband breathes the fire of war in a land of kindlings. Here we must have peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rhodri is the King of the Britons. All promises of peace must come from his mouth.

speaker: Angharad
en: In all things, the king and I act as one. As Lady of the Britons, I have full voice to speak for my husband and our people.

speaker: Bishiop Deorlaf
en: Then we accept, honored lady, your full authority.

speaker: Angharad
en: Perhaps, then, at long last we can end this war. Our peoples have suffered enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: And your proposal?

speaker: Angharad
en: We shall withdraw all our soldiers to the time-honored border of our lands. We ask only that you give us some days to collect our furnishings and leave Caustow Castle. In return, you pledge to end all hostilities as of this moment.

speaker: Eivor
en: These terms are generous. We have a truce.

speaker: Angharad
en: Truly.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Praise be, this is well and quickly done! God go with you and your king, Lady Angharad.

speaker: Angharad
en: I salute you all. You waged a good war. Let us now wage a lasting peace.

speaker: Angharad
en: Eivor, at the outset of our conflict, you gave me a boon of silver to ease our way to peace. As we have come to peace by another path, I return your silver in form of a small gift. Please accept this.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is fine craftsmanship, my lady. Thank you. I wish you well.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: I stand bewildered, Eivor. In the blink of an eye, years of blood and sweat are out to an end.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have walked a difficult road, bishop.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Ceolbert must learn the good news. Will you tell him when you see him?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll find him now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where in Helheim has Ceolbert gone to? Someone here must know.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you seen Ceolbert?

speaker: Norse Soldier 1
en: I don't keep track of the comings and goings of the ætheling. Ask another.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for Ceolbert, have you seen him?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Last I saw, he was sharpening arrow heads.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr. It's done.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Peace, eh? And now everyone is shitting themselves with happiness.

speaker: Eivor
en: If not happiness, then relief. Have you seen Ceolbert? I want to pass on the good news.

speaker: Ivarr
en: He asked me to go hunting earlier. But I'm in no such mood.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Hej, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you seen Ceolbert?

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: My brother saw him last.

speaker: Eivor
en: Drunk as a mackerel, isn't he?

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Celebrating the peace. Got started early.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wake up.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Huh?

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is Ceolbert?

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Ceol... bert?

speaker: Eivor
en: Did none of you see Ceolbert?

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Only him, drengr. You will have to wait until he sleeps it off.

speaker: Eivor
en: Does he often get this soaked?

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: By all the gods, he does. Twice a week. Once for three days, another for four. And twice on Sundays.

speaker: Eivor
en: And when you need him to sober up, what do you do?

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Keep this to yourself, but once or twice when I needed a quick word... I dumped him in a lake.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's worth a try.

speaker: Eivor
en: How long before he's fit to speak, would you say?

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: A few hours should do it. Unless you find another way to rouse him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Must be some way I can wake this drunk.

speaker: Eivor
en: That drunken lout should be awake by now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have a nice nap?

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Hmmm? What country is this?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for Ceolbert. Have you seen him?

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: If you must know, the little brat went off hunting boar some time ago.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I know, but where was he hunting?

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: He went south. That's all I know. Probably followed the stream here south to the forest.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Ah! Ah! By Odin and Thor, it's freezing!

speaker: Eivor
en: A nice nap?

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: That's a low thing to do to a man! Ach!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for Ceolbert.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: The soft Saxon boy?

speaker: Eivor
en: The next ealdorman, yes.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Said he was going hunting to bring back a feast for Ivarr and the rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know he went hunting, but where?

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Round the mouth of a cave nearby. Follow the stream up the mountain, south of here.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's enough to go on. Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened here? This doesn't look good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Blood. Ceolbert's? Or an animal he felled?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert's bow. Dropped.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fucking wolves.

speaker: Eivor
en: Paw prints and blood. Not from a boar. A wolf, dragging something through the dirt.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert?

speaker: Eivor
en: Tears of Freyja...

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Ahhhhh...

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert! You live!"

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I, oohhhh...

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay quiet. You are badly hurt.

speaker: Eivor
en: A dragon on the hilt. Gods. The Briton crest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep breathing, boy. You haven't got long. I will take you back to say your goodbyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can get you to the others. I'll go easy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shhh. Save your strength.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Ei... Eivor... I...

speaker: Eivor
en: Hush, Ceolbert. We'll soon be among friends.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here. Faster this way. Just breathe, Ceolbert. We'll soon be there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Some help, here! Ivarr! Deorlaf!

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: By the hand of Thor.

speaker: Norse Warrior (female)
en: Is that the ætheling?

speaker: Norse Warrior (male)
en: What has happened?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor! What happened...? No... No! You foolish boy, what did you do!

speaker: Eivor
en: I found him deep in a cave, beset by wolves.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Ivarr...

speaker: Ivarr
en: Easy boy, easy!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I-Ivarr...

speaker: Ivarr
en: Get me an axe, right fucking now!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr. He's gone.

speaker: Ivarr
en: An axe!

speaker: Eivor
en: His god will take him as he is, axe or not.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Go to your god, boy. And I will sing for you in Valhalla.

speaker: Ivarr
en: This was no wolf. Tell me what happened.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Britons did this. I found this blade in his chest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your war is back on.

speaker: Ivarr
en: What?

speaker: Eivor
en: He was killed with this.

speaker: Eivor
en: We were fools. An ætheling was entrusted to us in time of war. We did not protect him.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I taught him to protect himself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not well enough, this was stuck in his chest.

speaker: Ivarr
en: A Briton's dagger. Rhodri! But why?

speaker: Eivor
en: You murdered his brother. Did you think he would let that lie so easily?

speaker: Ivarr
en: I told you he was a trickster! Peace was never his goal. He takes blood for blood!

speaker: Eivor
en: Bishop Deorlaf! Over here!

speaker: Ivarr
en: The walls of his fortress will not protect him. I will sheath this dagger into his lungs.

speaker: Eivor
en: We must move fast, then. Attack before Rhodri can revel in his trick.

speaker: Ivarr
en: No mercy this time, Wolf-Kissed. You spared that wet turd, Leofrith. We will not spare Rhodri.

speaker: Eivor
en: I swear.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Lord above, what's happened? Ceolbert!

speaker: Eivor
en: Murdered.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: " who frees you from sin save you and raise you up."

speaker: Eivor
en: Send the boy's body to his father. He'll want a Christian burial.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lady Angharad said Rhodri is holed up in Caustow Castle. That may have been a lie or a tiny slip. Either way, we should find out.

speaker: Ivarr
en: There is a spot near the fortress to set up camp. We will scout it together.

speaker: Eivor
en: A good plan. We go now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait here 'til I return.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Fine. And remember...leave Rhodri to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: How are you holding up, bishop?

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: I am...gutted by this loss. Ceolbert would've made a good ealdorman. And one day, a fine king. A king forged by Viking battle-wisdom and a Christian compassion. A formidable man, he would have been.

speaker: Valka
en: Eivor, you have awakened. With more to share I hope.

speaker: Eivor
en: I returned to Asgard.

speaker: Valka
en: And what did you see?

speaker: Eivor
en: I bound the wolf Fenrir, Loki's son, with an unbreakable cord. The beast was enraged by my actions. We fought and I prevailed, but I could not kill the beast.

speaker: Valka
en: You visit lore and legend. Things I would never have imagined to be real. Parables, yet here you live them as memories.

speaker: Eivor
en: Every moment there was as tactile and as vital as you and I seated in this hut.

speaker: Valka
en: This is wonderful. Was there more?

speaker: Eivor
en: There was a... a betrayal.

speaker: Eivor
en: I betrayed my friend Týr. I stood by as the great wolf mauled him, tearing his arm off at the joint. I could have said something to prevent it. Given him a warning. But I did nothing.

speaker: Valka
en: How did it feel?

speaker: Eivor
en: I was unmoved by his pain. Not hateful, but I did not regret my indifference. A swig of poison that drinks like wine.

speaker: Valka
en: Selfishness unmeasured often feels this way. What else did you see?

speaker: Eivor
en: I witnessed a final vision from the Nornir. The coming of Ragnarök. All was fire and ash, a chaos like a foul wind from the depths of Ginnungagap. But we were ready for the coming storm. Eight of us, we drank the mead, then stood and marched to our doom. That was the end of the Nornir's prophecy.

speaker: Valka
en: How curious... Was there more?

speaker: Eivor
en: I can make sense of no more.

speaker: Valka
en: I see. The thrust of these visions seem clear to me. As in your first reverie, a fear of betrayal hangs upon you. Odin has seen fit to gift you with his infinite knowledge, and the treasure of his experience. Perhaps his tale is a warning. The indifference he felt is a great pity. See that you do not follow this same road. To do so would risk a loneliness, a personal exile, worse than death.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. Or... I hope I do. Thank you, Valka.

speaker: Eivor
en: This looks worth trying.

speaker: Braun
en: A drinking game always is! The rules are: One, you drink until you're the last one standing. Two, end of rules. Want to play?

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ha! Drool-monger! So slow.

speaker: Braun
en: You are quite the guzzler! Try again any time.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: O'er the waves we sail, cutting the ocean's skin... and when the dawn arrives, the time for hunt begins...

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: They are making me wait quite a while.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite a number you've taken.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: It was not me alone. My friends and I won them. We call ourselves the Toothbreakers. Sadly, we were separated. By a beast, of a kind we've never seen. In one fell swoop, it tore our group apart. We are supposed to meet here, to hunt that creature before returning home. And so, I wait.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait in safety, then.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Safe travels, and watch the woods.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: ...four! No, FIVE of those brown beasts!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: You never did like bears, did you?

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: I'd rather face a thousand wolves, really. Their teeth, their fur... I thought I was going to the halls.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: I cannot believe your trick worked.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: I had good help, too.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Arne, you are going to do just fine. Your skills will help us in the battle ahead! He will, right?

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Yes. Sure.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: ...Arne really flew, I swear it! He just needed that little push...

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: You do know this bird is not meant to fly?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Hogwash! Arne is a highly trained fowl. The rules of body and nature do not bind him! He will aid us in the hunt!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: I hope for his sake he flies fast.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Have you been drinking pig piss? It is clear that your Arne cannot fly or fight!

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Stop being an arse!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: By Odin! You lot have gone mad since I've been away!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: So, what is the plan?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: To charge in headfirst, attack by surprise!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: That worked out well for us the last time.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: No, we should be more careful this time. We track it, then we corner it.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Good stranger! Thank you for your help. I heard what happened! We are just about to set off on our grand hunt for the fearsome beast. If the thirst of the hunt itches your throat, will you join us?

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Into the unknown we go! Join us, kinsman!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: This beast bested us last time. We should be on our guard.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Tracks. There is no mistaking it, it came from the same creature that attacked us.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Grr!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Ack! Hey! Please, can we get along? Your horseplay will be our death.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: So, what brings you here, kinsman? Was it the pull of the wilderness? The thrill of the hunt?

speaker: Eivor
en: You could say that.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Then you will not be disappointed! However, be warned. This beast is quick to bite, and fearless.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Tracks. There is no mistaking it, it came from the same creature that attacked us.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Can you hear it? It's close. I feel it.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: There it is! Gods, it's even more ferocious than before!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: That glorious pelt... O, what a price it would fetch! Best us once, not twice! Your teeth will look nice on a string around my neck! Cull the storming beast, and skin him from his teeth!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Good fighting! What a beast we felled! You showed true grit out there. Thank you for joining our hunt.

speaker: Eivor
en: Predator or prey... you are what you choose to do.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: We are done here. If we ever meet again back on familiar ground, you are welcome to join us.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Th-that creature was even worse than a bear, truly. This wilderness is too much for me... I cannot wait to be back home.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Arne did so well! You too, of course! Now, we can return home with our head high.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Arne... o well. He lasted the longest, amongst the rest. Now, we can finally return home with our head high!

speaker: Hunta
en: My battle kennings have worn thin... I am no longer the reed among shields. The glimmer-blood, the hallowed skull-crack.

speaker: Eivor
en: The scourge of swan-roads...

speaker: Hunta
en: The iron-throng, the lender of silvergelds... I only wished to be a freebooter. Someone who writes their own destiny.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be glad you head to Valhalla with a poem on your lips.

speaker: Leofgifu
en: You found me out. I bow to this. But you will not unearth us all, you will not dig deeply enough. We are both a clot and cancer. We sit heavy in water, and yet we spread like a river's current.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you well?

speaker: Leofgifu
en: Why would you ask such a question at such a time as this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Beneath your words is something of a size unknown. A mystery. It lurks behind every frail word from your mouth.

speaker: Avgos
en: Arrows nocked! It's a hard thing to raise the rats of a city into warriors. Hook, set!

speaker: Eivor
en: You raised no one. You only trapped them in their cowering fear.

speaker: Avgos
en: Draw strings! First wave, fire!

speaker: Avgos
en: No! I gave these men order! I gave them purpose! I showed them their common enemy! Anchor strings! Second wave, fire!

speaker: Avgos
en: I was arrow for their rage. Without a foe to consume, we devour ourselves.

speaker: Odin
en: He speaks true. A man without an enemy defeats himself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Justify all you want, you're just a king-killer and a coward.

speaker: Avgos
en: Mighty high horse, you'd do the same if you were me. Aim! And fire!

speaker: Frideswid
en: One more, that's all. I'm nearly finished.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's enough.

speaker: Frideswid
en: Ah. It's you...

speaker: Odin
en: For all the dead we collect, dear sister, you and I are equals.

speaker: Frideswid
en: Quite a charnel house. I lost count of how many. I suppose I've been greedy in my research. But not for lack of care. The Ancient Ones, the arbiters. They built us out of simple pieces. So easy to break. So difficult to mend. There must be an improvement. We should be stronger, faster, smarter. I could have fixed us. I could have made us better.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are blood and bone and spirit, Frideswid. Perfect as we are.

speaker: Frideswid
en: You've such beautiful eyes. Finish it... would you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Burning to ash what you cannot possess. That's a child's way out.

speaker: Vicelin
en: To Hell with Lunden. Boudicca was right to burn it to the ground. It's a brick and mortar shithouse. So bright and beautiful set aflame. Will you rule over these cinders now? Yoke its people to your whims and needs?

speaker: Odin
en: You do have power here. Power you have earned.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have finished my work in Lunden. That's enough.

speaker: Vicelin
en: Lunden is only a beginning.

speaker: Vicelin
en: My order reaches further than your tiny boats can take you.

speaker: Vicelin
en: Never forget, Tryggr, my old friend. A man at sea may have gold and glory.

speaker: Vicelin
en: But he is always a slave to the churning tides. We are that tide.

speaker: Gorm
en: Wait. Wait. This is not the hall of five hundred doors.

speaker: Gorm
en: This is not the rock of the fallen. Where are the women on the winged horses?

speaker: Gorm
en: Where are the Choosers of the Slain?

speaker: Gorm
en: You. My blood enemy.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is Niflheim, the hell of mist and cold. This is where faithless dead come to die again. This is where ghosts fade to mist, to be forgotten.

speaker: Gorm
en: Your meddling has doomed us all, crow of battle.

speaker: Eivor
en: More lies from a liar born. Now speak the truth. What brought the Order to this place?

speaker: Gorm
en: To free a goddess, a creature of power and light... buried by the Jötnar in ages past.

speaker: Eivor
en: A pity, Gorm. You will not meet her now.

speaker: Eanbhert
en: If an evil man brings you biscuits, do you gift them to your children?

speaker: Eivor
en: I would not let good food to go to waste.

speaker: Eanbhert
en: I would let my children starve. A serpent's gift will always end in malice.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sweet from evil remains sweet. Even if it crumbles quickly in their hands.

speaker: Tata
en: Offa told everyone he was Christian. He was not, he was one of us. He only wanted the silver and the swords for his men of Mercia.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you have kept this tradition going?

speaker: Tata
en: Without flinching. Without hesitating. Offa would be proud of me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must have seen one hundred summers, old man."

speaker: Tata
en: It feels thus.

speaker: Gunilla
en: We must all turn to the Order. It keeps people well-placed. It is not truth, but true power.

speaker: Eivor
en: You desecrate the very purpose of life

speaker: Gunilla
en: No, no, no...I place power on power. The great becomes greater. You will see.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: This fire that burns inside... I've always had it. A longing to do something grand and important. But that door was always shut to me. My methods deemed too severe. I was cast out, shunned, scorned... But the Order, they took notice of me. Saw that it was courage that drove me. Courage to change the world for the better. They reopened that door.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you used your chance to destroy a way of life, you did not support.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: We have seen time and time again what happens when people are left to interpret for themselves. Knowledge must be controlled. Only then can the message be widely understood. The day where there is but one truth draws nearer. One truth, that is what the Order offers.

speaker: Odin
en: This ones sought to spark a new flame, but did so with a heavy hand, not a teacher's tongue.

speaker: Eivor
en: This cleansing of yours ends here.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: My work is incomplete, but not inconsequential. There are others who carry on, for one of the four is us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why did you say that? What does it mean?

speaker: Ingeborg
en: Now I go, a flame that grows bright, and burns evermore, ever light.

speaker: Eivor
en: To Helheim, where colder and crueler fires await.

speaker: Grigorii
en: It's funny, as a child I thought of snow as the tears of God, frozen by our sins. Weak with hunger, I stared into the sky, hoping it was me He wept for. Me He sought to save.

speaker: Grigorii
en: But God did not save me. The Vault did. He took me to a fine house. Gave me hearty meals. A warm bed.

speaker: Grigorii
en: For the first time, someone extended a hand, showed me kindness. Compassion.

speaker: Grigorii
en: And it was then that I made a vow. I vowed to never turn my back on he who was there for me when God was not.

speaker: Eivor
en: So you served The Vault, knowing full well what he was a part of.

speaker: Grigorii
en: The Order made our paths intersect. I owed them a debt, and I repaid it by saving this city from its own destruction.

speaker: Odin
en: A life debt is a strong motivator. It took hold of this one's hugr, drove it, and never let go.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yet not with the same compassion you were shown. Too many have suffered by your hand in pursuit of this cause.

speaker: Grigorii
en: You're right. Perhaps I deserve this death. But I am but one cog in a large wheel. One that still turns unhindered.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not for long.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where you have gone, there will be no tears waiting for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: What did you hope to gain with all this? What riches are worth so much misery, and the deaths of honorable men and women?

speaker: Audun
en: Only a feeble mind would call them honorable. They are privileged. Sedentary. Complacent. They wasted their resources. I secured our power through wealth. I contributed to the future of a glorious order!

speaker: Eivor
en: On the backs of honest people! Merchants and priests and nobles alike."

speaker: Audun
en: Eivor... you are wrong. Held back by your primitive cosmology. Nine worlds in the tree? No! Nine times nine thousand worlds. And as many suns!

speaker: Odin
en: I hung , sacrificing myself to myself. So does the Wise One seek wisdom.

speaker: Audun
en: Countless spheres, awaiting our gift, our enlightenment!

speaker: Eivor
en: I live in one world only.

speaker: Eivor
en: You live in none.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rest easy, reeve (sheriff). Your time has come.

speaker: Derby
en: Yes. Now I will be judged at the of the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: To Helheim with you.

speaker: Derby
en: Aye. Even Helheim needs a reeve.

speaker: Wigmund
en: Stop the heathen! Raider! Vikingr! Stop her!

speaker: Wigmund
en: She means to erase me! To banish me from your minds! Fight in my name! Die for me! Die for me!

speaker: Odin
en: That is no way to call for sacrifices.

speaker: Eivor
en: Their lives for yours. Is that how it works?

speaker: Wigmund
en: Their lives meant nothing. No land, no riches, no titles! But my name will live on.

speaker: Eivor
en: The reputation of a good man never dies. But your name will soon be a curse.

speaker: Wigmund
en: So be it. The riches I had in life gave me power.

speaker: Wigmund
en: To curse me from beyond the grave gives me still more.

speaker: Wigmund
en: Though I die, my order lives on elsewhere, everywhere.

speaker: Wigmund
en: Yield to us! Give us what we are owed! The trade, the riches, the legacy. All of it! Yield! Yield! Yield!

speaker: Eivor
en: If your Hell is real, I'm glad you'll get to see it.

speaker: Patrick
en: I was building a boat... to carry my family to safety one day.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what of the orphans you left behind? Do they get a boat?

speaker: Patrick
en: A brigade of bastards? They are the only ones left ruling England. My people were of the Kingdom. Now we are ruled by Christ-beaten bastards.

speaker: Havelok
en: The first man I killed for my Order, I cried and wept after trying to hold back the tears. But I told myself I am merely acting upon a foretold destiny, navigating the whim of greater Gods. My actions are simply pebbles.

speaker: Eivor
en: Pebbles that wash away in the surf, as harmless as dust.

speaker: Havelok
en: Pebbles were once bedrock. As were you.

speaker: Mucel
en: I served the young Æthelred. He will rise one day.

speaker: Eivor
en: He is no Aelfred, from what I hear.

speaker: Mucel
en: I lied to everyone. And they'll never know. They will tell stories of me as a good man who served his lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your hugr (mind) walks with a new beast.

speaker: Gifle
en: I wish my life was a carnival of drinking ale and pissing.

speaker: Eivor
en: It could have been, I am sure.

speaker: Gifle
en: No, we have not reached such a point. I used The Order to live a life of ale-drinking, but the price of my ale was murder. Sad really.

speaker: Herefrith
en: I died the day I hid behind these robes, this cross. To bring the light of my order to a wider view, I debased myself. Clawed my way to the top of this common religion, full of common men. I should have lived as the ancients did.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's the folly of mankind, Herefrith. We wallow in our failures like happy pigs in a sty of shit. You should have learned to enjoy it.

speaker: Tatfrid
en: You won. I concede. When s mention me, they will sing of my conquests.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cowards do not get s.

speaker: Tatfrid
en: I am no coward. In a long lost battle for Wessex, I was the victor. The scop could speak of that time. Focus on my lost honor.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, I'll leave your reputation as it is... here in the blood-blackened mud.

speaker: Beneseck
en: I sought pleasure with the silver I received from the Order. I shared it too, with many in need.

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't be blinded by the gleam of your bloodlust. Shared silver always comes at a cost.

speaker: Beneseck
en: What of it? I forged good from what you call evil. Lives were improved, lives worth more than the silver that paid for them. I do not regret the lives lost for the charity gained.

speaker: Yohanes
en: I cared about my family. Just my family. I loved them more than anything.

speaker: Eivor
en: And the families who fell by the Order's command. Were they not worthy of love?

speaker: Yohanes
en: You are a Dane! How can you speak of the value of a life? All are ranked as less-than-the-axe to you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Not true. I see honor in many people, many places.

speaker: Yohanes
en: You have proved here that your compassion has a hard and brutal limit.

speaker: Heika
en: These Hidden Ones, is that who you slave for?

speaker: Eivor
en: I slave for none. I'm scrubbing England clean of its filth for the safety of my people.

speaker: Heika
en: Ah, listen! Do you hear? The excuses of a mind enslaved.

speaker: Selwyn
en: Perverter of justice! Who dares execute the King's noose?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not in Aelfred's name that you carry out your work. You are the Order's executioner.

speaker: Selwyn
en: Ah. You peer through the veil, but you do not see clearly. Aelfred's laws are a slave's fever-dream. He offers shit-soaked beggars a seat at his table. Where the meek devour the strong. Who best to judge the fate of the wretched many, if not the strong and worthy few?

speaker: Odin
en: To protect your people, you must sheathe your hand in an iron glove.

speaker: Eivor
en: You grind your heels into the backs of freedmen, not those who deserve it.

speaker: Selwyn
en: The Order condemns all men to pain, for all men are but a shadow of the perfection we should know. The perfection of the Ancient Ones.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are only a man, reeve. One dead branch on a fast dying tree.

speaker: Hilda
en: Come child. Whisper what you've learned, and Mother will give you a treat.

speaker: Eivor
en: Coward. Using children to spy and steal for your Order.

speaker: Hilda
en: To educate them! Give me a child until he is seven, and I will give you the man... or woman.

speaker: Hilda
en: But what use are letters when a child can only write his name in pig shit? Or wisdom in a woman when she cannot wield it beyond her hearth?

speaker: Hilda
en: I taught little Aelwyn so much more, saved her from a life less worthy. She will find enlightenment in The Order, just as I did.

speaker: Hilda
en: If I could save them all, I would.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you can't. You've corrupted too many to save too few.

speaker: Hilda
en: My Order is the only way forward. It can quench our thirst for knowledge, if only Aelfred's slave-faith is defeated.

speaker: Hilda
en: And what would you sacrifice for infinite knowledge?

speaker: Odin
en: An immeasurable gift. Why refuse it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not their innocence.

speaker: Hilda
en: A pity.

speaker: Hilda
en: Non requiescat in pace. (They shall not rest in peace.)

speaker: Ealhferth
en: How sweet is the Shepherd's pipe when he calls his lambs to slaughter. I was born to Christians in the northern wilds. My mother would cradle me beneath the stars and whisper dovelike, "God watches over you."

speaker: Ealhferth
en: Then your people came. And God fixed his stout eye as they slit her throat for a copper ring. No stars threw down their spears as barbarians smeared her blood through fields of broken wheat. God watched all... and I hated him.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be Aelfred's God was testing you. A trial you failed.

speaker: Ealhferth
en: Aelfred's God is weak. Yet he would chain us all in His service. From our first breath to our death rattle. My Order wishes to break these mind-forged manacles. I am the wolf in lamb's wool.

speaker: Odin
en: He takes on the role of a god himself. A worthy path to walk.

speaker: Eivor
en: A wolf is but a walking feast for ravens.

speaker: Ealhferth
en: One more gift to you, Dane. A deadly truth, if you can find it.

speaker: Ealhferth
en: With my death, The Order will not die. It will only transform... into something far worse for all of us.

speaker: Blaeswith
en: The archbishop never suspected my heresy. I kept secrets as I gathered believers. I appeared so pious, my eyes bled for him. But I've never felt as much love for his god. Not like I do the old Gods. The true gods. Our ancient creators.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your life was a lie, you mean? You threw your honor into the ocean.

speaker: Blaeswith
en: When I told the archbishop my true belief, he was horrified. So I silenced him.

speaker: Eivor
en: That silence comes for you now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Burn in your Hell!

speaker: Odin
en: Stop! You misunderstand, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll eat your heart!

speaker: Odin
en: She has saved your brother!

speaker: Fulke
en: Animals, we are. Spit and vomit, shit and soil. But Sigurd is so much more. I gave him that understanding, that gift.

speaker: Eivor
en: You gave him pain!

speaker: Fulke
en: Yes! To awaken him! All that power! All that potential, locked away!

speaker: Fulke
en: A god trapped within a prison of bones. The pain was necessary to free him! Behold his terrible beauty!

speaker: Fulke
en: The beauty of the divine!

speaker: Odin
en: Hers was the great work, the highest achievement of humankind. Now you, Eivor—you must carry it forward.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd...

speaker: Redwalda
en: I once served and prayed under Saint Chad of Mercia at Tamworth. I was a monk. I should stayed there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did Saint Chad die with his axe at his hand?

speaker: Redwalda
en: Saint Chad will be revered for avoiding the axe. I wish I had done so myself, and not taken a path full of violent honor. The Old Gods will fade from our sight, in time. God forgive me, for I have sinned.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this a prayer? An offering? Or a final vestige of your oath?

speaker: Eorforwine
en: Only a charm I never finished.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now the trolls take you.

speaker: Kendall
en: I have seen a crown on a cleaning basin. There it was. I stole it. Ran with it. Hid it. Now maggots feast on it, I am certain. Let them rule Old Albion.

speaker: Cola
en: This is a mere moment. No one will remember it. No one. Not your name, nor mine. It all ends up the same.

speaker: Eivor
en: Regret torments you?

speaker: Cola
en: My only regret is losing to whatever you are. You reek of fading glory.

speaker: Cudberct
en: All of these men of God, festooned in gold and silver.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is enough to make one blind.

speaker: Cudberct
en: We ARE blind of now. Lennius was our only king. He saw straight and fought alongside Arturious. We have been blind ever since.

speaker: Eivor
en: No sunlight reaches where you are going. May you bathe in serpent skins. Your name, Frown-Hoard, Quick the Dead... whatever it may be, is stained forever.

speaker: Horsa
en: My name is Horsa. I left silver in the mouth of my home. Please see that it is spent well and frivolously.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vilijalauss (Will-less), now you die.

speaker: Wuffa
en: My... my sword is lost. Floating down a creek. I shall follow. Till I dance again, or drown.

speaker: Wealdmaer
en: Why, why, why? Lost are everyone.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mostly, Argr.

speaker: Wealdmaer
en: For , Eostre, and Saetere. I served the true gods. The old ones. To be killed by you holds honor! Killing holds all glory!

speaker: Eivor
en: No more winters for you.

speaker: Woden
en: Better to die than face my lords. I hope my Maegester Magnus forgives me. For so long I looked to him for guidance, for order.

speaker: Eivor
en: If your honor is slow, a true lord cannot forgive you. They cannot.

speaker: Woden
en: Bah! Now I will my gaze to Woden, Tiw, and Funor. I will continue to turn until I find some forgiveness.

speaker: Eivor
en: You will spin and drill yourself to a endless bottom.

speaker: Osgar
en: Offa betrayed us all in Deira. Now we crawl about for the scraps. Whatever crumbs you leave behind after your raids.

speaker: Eivor
en: You wish you were a raider. A drengr.

speaker: Osgar
en: Yes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Farvell (goodbye), Sword-Cloven.

speaker: Heike
en: In the Kingdom of Frisia, we honor your type, pagan. We strive as you strive to achieve the perfection of the Ancient Ones.

speaker: Eivor
en: Pagan?

speaker: Osgar
en: To be pagan is perfect.

speaker: Hrothgar
en: I once knew a man who cleaned all the rats in Lunden. He took his time. They loved him, and he loved them. They lived freely but came to see him for a scrub. Rats have a certain freedom, but they feed on shit. It's a coward's freedom. A Valholl for the vanquished.

speaker: Callin
en: I often awake in my vagrancy, shaking and sweating. I hope this stops now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Farvell (goodbye). The trolls await.

speaker: Beorhtsige
en: In these old wolds, I used to lie down and pray that the leaves would cover me. That I could drag them over me like a blanket... And join ... in a bed of leaves. Tuck me in, stranger. With a song.

speaker: Eivor
en: The sound of Odin stomping on your bones is the only song you'll hear.

speaker: Eivor
en: We sweat and toil to reach this moment.

speaker: Bercthun
en: The Ancient Ones lap at my sweat now. That war-sweat the hates so much, we long for.

speaker: Eivor
en: This god or that. A good feast with fresh battle milk on our brows is not something you will ever taste again.

speaker: Bercthun
en: Choke on my bones.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here. This marks fewer members of the Order. Keep this. It serves your cause better than it does my pocket.

speaker: Hytham
en: Ah good. I hope this one did not give you too much trouble. One more gone. The world is brighter for it. Another one? You are certainly proficient. It gives me joy to take these from you.

speaker: Hytham
en: As a token of my deep gratitude, I want you to have this.

speaker: Hytham
en: Keep this up and the land will be free of these monsters! There's more to be done, Eivor. There are more medallions to collect. You have done well but there are more still. Thank you. I expect there are more yet to claim.

speaker: Hytham
en: Eivor. Did Basim contact you in Norway? He said he would be joining you. Yet here you are, and I have no word from him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham, this will be hard to hear, but Basim attacked us in Norway. Vengeance for some transgression of ours, imagined or real.

speaker: Hytham
en: You mean... you mean you slew him yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd and I, together. I know this comes as a

speaker: Hytham
en: I do not understand. Why would he do such a thing? He loved Sigurd. He loved you!

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not understand it myself. Perhaps one day we can speak about this with more clarity. But for now, I am deeply sorry. Gorm is dead. Nameless and alone across the open sea.

speaker: Hytham
en: A Master of The Order, hewn from the trunk of their dying tree. You are getting closer to the roots.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here you are, Hytham... the last of The Order's sigils. You will find King Ælfred's among them.

speaker: Hytham
en: King Ælfred? Did our Poor Fellow-Soldier lead you to his hiding place?

speaker: Eivor
en: He did, for they were one and the same. Our Poor Fellow-Soldier of Christ was the Grand Maegester of the Order of the Ancients.

speaker: Hytham
en: He turned on his own Order? Fascinating.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not turned so much as trampled. His devotion to Christ and what he calls a Universal Order set him against them from the start. With all sincerity, he loathed the title and the duty he had inherited, and wished them destroyed.

speaker: Hytham
en: Wonderful. With his abdication, the last stronghold of The Order has been dismantled. All that remains are scraps, here and there. And you, Eivor. Now that you have seen our enemy and you understand our cause, I wonder if you would join us? Become a Hidden One.

speaker: Eivor
en: Was this your ultimate goal, Hytham? A trial by fire? It is a kind offer, but I do not believe we fight for quite the same cause. Your creed demands that you keep your triumphs hidden. I prefer my glory to be in plain view, for all to see.

speaker: Hytham
en: If I taught you our creed, if you spent time with it... it could open your mind to another view.

speaker: Eivor
en: Another view is always welcome, but to live without celebrating one's glory and honor and achievements is not a life for me. But know this... I would give my life in a moment for those I love, and who love me in return. All here, including you, my friend.

speaker: Hytham
en: I understand you well, Eivor. Very well indeed.

speaker: Eivor
en: What of Oxenefordscire? Sigurd told me he had business there.

speaker: Randvi
en: Ah, yes... Sigurd is there now, in fact. He bids you go meet him as soon as you can. He has partnered with a rebellious thegn called Geadric, and hopes to install Geadric as ealdorman in exchange for an oath. There's an alehouse in the center of Buckingham. Sigurd will meet you there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should join my brother, then. Where is Buckingham?

speaker: Randvi
en: Along the Great Ouse river that divides Oxenefordscire. Sigurd will be pleased to see you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soldiers on alert. What's happened here?

speaker: Eivor
en: These soldiers are tightly wound.

speaker: Eivor
en: An alehouse. This must be it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd's not here. I'll ask around.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for two men. Not locals, a Norse and an Arab.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: The fellas the soldiers came after? If I were you, friend, I'd keep mum about them.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for my brother, a large outspoken Norseman.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Norse? Ha! Was he part of the fight here? Prob'ly killed by Eadwyn's soldiers. Get gone while you can!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: These soldiers, always leave a bleedin' mess.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you the alewife here?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: You are not welcome here. I've had enough trouble with Danes today.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not here to cause trouble. I'm looking for my brother, a large Norseman.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: It was him what caused the ruckus! Him and that other one were here, talking to Thegn Geadric. Then Lady Eadwyn's soldiers swept in. A fight broke out. Your brother and the tanned fella got away. The soldiers nabbed Geadric, though. I was sorry to see that. He's well-liked in these parts.

speaker: Eivor
en: Which way did my brother go?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Hm. What's it worth to ye to find out?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm asking a simple question.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Look, Dane, you start a scene or a scuffle and I'll scream for soldiers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thieving cotter. Here's your silver.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Thank you kindly. Your brother and his friend jumped through that window and ran for the river. I'd wager they hid in one of the fish houses there.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are risking your life, and I'm the one who'll take it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O, my. All I know's they jumped through the window!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Guards! Help! Help!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Help!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: It's you! You threatened our Mae!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Come on lads, it's a fight!

speaker: Eivor
en: These soldiers are tightly wound.

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem to respect this man Geadric. If he was talking to my brother, it's because he wants what's best for this shire. Maybe you're a woman who also wants Oxenefordscire to be free and to decide its own fate. A woman who'll stand up for her village, who won't be crushed under the boot of oppression.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: I hope I am.

speaker: Eivor
en: Such a woman would help me find Geadric's friends.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: You're right, you are. Your brother and his friend jumped through that window there, and scampered off towards the river. It's a good bet they hid in one of them fish houses.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd and Basim headed south. They wouldn't go far. I'll check along the river.

speaker: Eivor
en: Smells like a fish-house. Good spot to hide.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Wait! Stop!

speaker: Basim
en: Ahlan wa sahlan, (Hello) Eivor.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We could have cut you to bloody giblets, Wolf-Kissed!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why so unnerved, brother? It's not like you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Half the soldiers in the shire are hunting us. You must have noticed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that why you haven't come home? You're playing hide-and-fetch with Mercian soldiers?

speaker: Basim
en: Your brother is a busy man, Eivor. Weighed down by pressing duties.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's good to see you again, Basim. Even if you haven't kept my brother trained on the task at hand.

speaker: Basim
en: It's not my place to lead your brother about like a bridled mare.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now there's an idea...

speaker: Eivor
en: I wasn't speaking to you, Basim. I'll hear Sigurd's answers from Sigurd.

speaker: Eivor
en: Haven't you some murderous errands of your own, Basim? Why are you here at all?

speaker: Basim
en: My path crossed with Sigurd's long ago. We work together now, toward a single purpose.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother... we should be forging alliances. Send this man back to his warren before he leads you astray.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, gods above! I'm grateful you've joined us. We have made strides towards an alliance, in fact. A local thegn called Geadric has pledged an oath to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've heard of him. The alewife also mentioned a Lady Eadwyn who commands the soldiers. Why not ally with her?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Lady Eadwyn's husband was the shire ealdorman, until Guthrum's army ended his life. Now she's taken up her husband's fight, with the promise of aid from King Aelfred of Wessex.

speaker: Basim
en: Eadwyn vows revenge on the Danes who stole her husband and her livelihood.

speaker: Sigurd
en: From what we know, Aelfred is a fearsome king. If Eadwyn can win his full support, this shire is lost to Wessex.

speaker: Eivor
en: So to fight her, you've pledged your sword to a minor thegn who likely commands a gang of farmers and fisherman.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Have faith, Eivor. A few hundred Saxons armed with hayforks and billhooks can be terrifying.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods.

speaker: Basim
en: All men and women, noble or peasant, have within them the seeds of something greater.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This is true. Sometimes greater than the average mind can fathom.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, Eadwyn has Geadric in shackles now. All your plotting has turned to ash.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not if we act soon. She dragged her prisoners to the longhouse. With you here, we can mount a surprise attack.

speaker: Eivor
en: If Geadric is our best chance for an alliance, let's see it done.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd. Has Basim talked you into something of little reward?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, have you lost hope in my warcraft? I heed Basim's wisdom, but he follows my lead. Always.

speaker: Eivor
en: He has the look of one who trusts none but himself.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Basim is secretive by nature. But he is wise and forthright. And he has opened my eyes to a magnificent truth. He has promised me a reward so unusual, so incredible, it will shatter your mind to shards.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother, our bond has the iron heft of a war axe. Do not let Basim and his prophecies of good fortune sway you from our simple goal.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Never. Our goal is fixed. We shall soon be the lords of Mercia, then all of England. But Basim has a deep insight. He's read wisdom in the lines of my face and heard the litany of my forefathers, and... Well, there will be time enough for my saga later.

speaker: Geadric
en: Untie me, cowards!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eadwyn. She's in there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Come. We'll batter the door.

speaker: Geadric
en: Sigurd! Kill this sweaty fishwife!

speaker: Eadwyn
en: Stay your blades! This traitor, Geadric, will face trial. As will all the treasonous thegns of this shire.

speaker: Geadric
en: You're the traitor, Eadwyn! Calling on Aelfred of Wessex, begging for his army!

speaker: Eadwyn
en: Clap your meadhole, Geadric. Lapdog of the Danes.

speaker: Geadric
en: You'll sell us out to Wessex! And that poxy-assed bastard Aelfred! We won't 'ave it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Lady, there is no need for slaughter. We all want peace for Oxenefordscire. Can we find some agreement?

speaker: Eivor
en: You're not the ealdorman here, Lady Eadwyn. Turn around and walk away, and we'll leave you be.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eadwyn. You're nothing now but a churlish widow. What power you had lies rotting in your husband's grave.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: You heathenish, fork-tongued Dane. Foul-smelling heap, I shit on you all!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Lady, choose your next words with care. For you see before you the future master of all England. Sigurd of the hungry Raven Clan. Lay down your arms, free my friend here, and kiss my lordly feet. You will not get a second chance.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, are you cracked?

speaker: Eadwyn
en: And you can kiss my rosy red arse, whey-face!

speaker: Eadwyn
en: I've done with this offal. I leave them to you! Flay them alive and tan their flesh for saddles.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Geadric, what have they done to you?

speaker: Basim
en: What kind of mess did you get yourself into?

speaker: Geadric
en: Untie me! I can still fight these bastards!

speaker: Geadric
en: Damn Eadwyn. Blood for Oxenefordscire!

speaker: Geadric
en: Damn her to Hell, the harpy escaped!

speaker: Geadric
en: Good Lord, you fight well. Thank you for that.

speaker: Geadric
en: Damn her to Hell, the harpy escaped!

speaker: Geadric
en: I was desperate to fight. You should have freed me!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Geadric, this is Eivor. My stone-armed sibling.

speaker: Geadric
en: Well met.

speaker: Eivor
en: That was your plan, Sigurd? To charm the lady with your vague hope of kingship?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Prophecy, Eivor. Not hope.

speaker: Geadric
en: No time to squabble. Eadwyn's taken most of the shire's thegns. She has her way, they'll be dead by supper!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Tend your wounds, Geadric. We'll free your friends.

speaker: Basim
en: And what of the holy woman, Fulke? You promised us a meeting with her.

speaker: Geadric
en: I did, aye. But it's a fair mystery why you'd want to talk with

speaker: Basim
en: Where is she?

speaker: Geadric
en: Thegn Holt will know. Fulke lives on his lands. But he'll be dead with the rest, if you don't stop the trial.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Tell us where and we'll go now. Their lives depend on the speed of your tongue.

speaker: Geadric
en: Southwest of here, halfway to Oxeneforda, at the Leah Villa Garrison.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Basim, Eivor. To horse!

speaker: Letter from a Captain
en: Lady Eadwyn, We have successfully captured the rebel thegns. We caught them as they were fleeing to Oxeneforda. We will proceed with their trial and execution as you ordered. For Oxenefordscire!

speaker: Letter from Aelfred of Wessex
en: Lady Eadwyn, You have my blessing in your efforts to secure control of Oxenefordscire. Should you need men at arms, do not hesitate to call on Wessex. -Aelfred.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Off again, Eivor. You and I, with blades drawn and hearts ablaze!

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is this Fulke that Basim spoke of?

speaker: Sigurd
en: An ally, Eivor. A most important ally. A holy woman who trades in prophecies and secret knowledge.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is not the sort of alliance we're looking for, Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: No, it's even better! You cannot imagine what discoveries await.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are speaking strangely, Brother.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Because I am alive, Eivor. My heart's alight with the fuel of battle-fire. Like old time, hey?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, Sigurd. Like old times.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Remember our hunts beyond the northern way? Our first big kill was a ten-point deer. We brought it down together. The arrows from our bows, like darts of ice.

speaker: Eivor
en: With sharpened shin-bones for skinning the beast.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You on the right, me on the left, we leapt and struck!

speaker: Eivor
en: We crashed to the ground like a felled tree. Then the bloody struggle.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Damn animal bit my hand! Never knew a buck could bite so hard!

speaker: Eivor
en: But I pierced its throat, spilling its life-wine into the drifts. That put an end to him.

speaker: Basim
en: Such tales you siblings tell.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Just one of a thousand, Basim. It was the glorious dawn of our lives.

speaker: Eivor
en: You haven't yet explained who this Fulke woman is.

speaker: Sigurd
en: When the time is right, I will.

speaker: Basim
en: She is the fulcrum of a larger plan.

speaker: Eivor
en: Above conquering England? What larger plan could we need?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Patience, Eivor. Patience.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine. Keep your dread secrets, Brother. But if this alliance fails, you may take them to your grave.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This fever will break once you know the whole truth. I promise.

speaker: Basim
en: There! We have time yet. They're holding the trials just ahead.

speaker: Sigurd
en: My blade is thirsty, friends. Shall we roll in like three barrels afire?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, we must be careful. Do not let the executioner swing his axe.

speaker: Eivor
en: They're about to execute the prisoners.

speaker: Judge
en: These subjects of the Lady Eadwyn have betrayed their oaths to the shire...

speaker: Thegn Sherwin
en: Not true!

speaker: Judge
en: Silence! They stand accused and are guilty of spreading calumny against our sainted Lady Eadwyn and engaging in sedition and general disreputable acts!

speaker: Thegn Brant
en: Pig shite!

speaker: Judge
en: Each shall be called to confess his perfidy. Confession grants atoned death. Failure to confess earns a disgraceful death.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: These are stalwart thegns. What have they done wrong?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Lady Eadwyn is behind this sham trial.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Who will Eadwyn come after next?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: Damned if I believe these men are guilty of anything.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: Get me out of here. Eadwyn will have me flayed alive.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay close. I'll help the others.

speaker: Thegn Brant
en: Rescue us! We can help!

speaker: Judge
en: Thegn Brant!

speaker: Thegn Brant
en: I stand innocent!

speaker: Judge
en: Do you confess to cravenly plotting to betray Lady Eadwyn?

speaker: Thegn Brant
en: My father, his father, and his father's father all fought for Mercia! I have fought for Mercia! Now you would shackle us to the whoremonger of Wessex? This trial is a sham, and you are an ass.

speaker: Judge
en: Disgraceful death!

speaker: Judge
en: Thegn Octe!

speaker: Thegn Octe
en: O, dear Lord.

speaker: Judge
en: Do you confess to abetting the disgraced Thegn Brant in his betrayal of Lady Eadwyn?

speaker: Thegn Octe
en: Have mercy! I am but a poor farmer. My crops have seen this shire through bad times. You, yourself, judge, borrowed three bales

speaker: Judge
en: Enough! A disgraceful death awaits!

speaker: Judge
en: Thegn Sherwin!

speaker: Thegn Sherwin
en: Aye.

speaker: Judge
en: Confess the many ways in which you betrayed Lady Eadwyn of Oxenefordscire.

speaker: Thegn Sherwin
en: I confess that you have oat mash for brains and that you couple with sheep!

speaker: Judge
en: Most disgraceful death!

speaker: Judge
en: Enough justice for now. We will break for the midday meal!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: A rebel!

speaker: Judge
en: Execute the prisoners at once!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: The executioner's been killed! Get the murderer!

speaker: Thegn Brant
en: We must bring down Eadwyn once and for all.

speaker: Thegn Octe
en: I stand with Geadric.

speaker: Thegn Sherwin
en: I owe you my life, friend.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: Friend, get me out of here before they have my head. Break this bleedin' cage open, would ya?

speaker: Thegn Brant
en: That's thegn justice for you! You'll regret this!

speaker: Thegn Octe
en: Fight for Geadric! For Oxenefordscire! Down with Eadwyn!

speaker: Thegn Sherwin
en: Is that your best shot? I'm taking you down! Thegns united!

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: For the shire! For God and Mercia! Down with Lady Eadwyn.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sorry about the others.

speaker: Eivor
en: Geadric sent me to find you. Let's go, now!

speaker: Eivor
en: Geadric sent me. Let's get away from this place.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: We can talk safely over there. We fought with our weaselly ealdorman for years. Now his widow wants to lop off our heads.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: Bless you all. Thanks to you, I live to pay Lady Eadwyn back in blood. I am Thegn Holt. Does Geadric live?

speaker: Eivor
en: He's safe in Buckingham.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Good thegn, we are at your side in this fight. To keep this land in the hands of those who love Mercia, be they Saxon or Dane.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: God in Heaven knows, I'd sooner see a Dane married to my daughter than sell a man of Wessex one of my pigs.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: If Geadric is behind you, then I am too.

speaker: Basim
en: We're told you know of a holy woman, Fulke. Where is she now?

speaker: Eivor
en: Can we not fixate on this cipher, Fulke? Eadwyn is our focus.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Fulke holds a secret that may turn the tide of this fight. Without her, I cannot achieve my full purpose here.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: The madwoman, Fulke?

speaker: Eivor
en: You see, Brother? Your mysterious Fulke has a mind in disarray.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Mad or no, I want to speak with her.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you want my backing, Brother, you'll explain yourself. How is a madwoman central to your plans?

speaker: Sigurd
en: When we find her, I will tell you all you wish to know. Until then, nothing.

speaker: Eivor
en: However deranged she may be, my brother wishes to meet her. The sooner you make this happen, the swifter this war will end.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: Understand this. Fulke is a heretic. A sower of poisoned knowledge and an enemy of the Church. She claims to have seen or spoken with God himself, and for this Lady Eadwyn had her imprisoned, I know not where.

speaker: Basim
en: At a monastery, I suppose. We should make inquiries.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, do we not owe Geadric some word of what has happened here?

speaker: Sigurd
en: You can speak with him in my stead. But we must hurry. Fulke's life may be in danger.

speaker: Eivor
en: We risk losing all the gains we've made here for the sake of this woman.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Trust me, Eivor. Fulke is of great importance. You'll soon understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope I will.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We have a camp to the east at Linforda. An old harbor on the Great Ouse. Meet us there.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: We thegns will raise a fyrd and join with you to take down Eadwyn. Whatever it takes.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: The thegns that died here were honorable and just. By my faith, I'll raise a fyrd of able men and take revenge on Eadwyn.

speaker: Thegn Holt
en: Bring this news to Geadric. And tell him we'll be ready when he calls.

speaker: Eivor
en: Every man will be needed.

speaker: Letter to the Judge
en: It has fallen to you to render judgment on those several thegns who have flouted Lady Eadwyn's rule. There is no question of innocence, but should they confess, let them die more easily.

speaker: Letter from Lady Eadwyn
en: Note well, although I cannot fathom his reasoning, our friend Aelfred of Wessex has requested that the heretic Fulke be kept alive. Therefore, be it so that this Fulke be taken to Saint Albanes Abbey and there imprisoned for the rest of her days. By commandment, your Lady of the Shire, Eadwyn

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. No soldiers here now. Geadric's cleared them all out.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Did you find your brother, then?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm touched that you would ask.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: I shouldn't'a made you pay. But the silver's been well spent. I've used actual barley for the ale, this batch.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: You had no real cause to frighten me. I'd'a told you where they'd gone, if you'd done me some sweet talk.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: I'm well ashamed I almost made you pay. But it all worked out right, didn't it?

speaker: Geadric
en: She's well supplied, that's for certain. Well done capturing these, lads.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: It was bloody business.

speaker: Geadric
en: Oil jars, springald arrows, fodder and the like. Take what's useful and burn the rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Geadric.

speaker: Geadric
en: Eivor! Do the thegns live?

speaker: Eivor
en: Every single one. They've set out to raise a fyrd of fighting men. They all stand with you, Geadric.

speaker: Geadric
en: We'll need every pike and poker we have to take down Eadwyn.

speaker: Eivor
en: In spite of our efforts, some were killed.

speaker: Geadric
en: Damn good men, all of 'em. I swear, I'll gut Eadwyn to honor those we lost.

speaker: Geadric
en: And you, and your brother, are you still with me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I like your bluntness, Geadric. My axe is yours. My brother's too.

speaker: Geadric
en: Eadwyn's plopped her haunches down in her castle now. She has men and supplies comin', curse her eyes.

speaker: Geadric
en: Where is your brother and the odd fellow?

speaker: Eivor
en: They continue their search for the woman, Fulke. He seems to think she will help us chase Eadwyn to an early grave. But I do not understand how.

speaker: Geadric
en: You do what you must, Eivor. I'll ready what men I've got for the coming fight. I'll move toward Cyne Belle Castle and bring up the fyrd for an assault. Eadwyn's fortress is strong and sure.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is there anything I can do to weaken her grip on the shire? Or make her anxious?

speaker: Geadric
en: Ah, there's a notion. You could chip away at her flag-bearers if you see them, and defend my fyrd if any are in strife.

speaker: Geadric
en: We stole some of her supplies here. If you see any other stores like this, destroy them.

speaker: Eivor
en: That I can do.

speaker: Geadric
en: When you're ready for war, you'll find me at a camp near Cyne Belle Castle.

speaker: Chad
en: It cannot end like this.

speaker: Chad
en: Is... is someone there? Hello? Please, anyone?

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened to you, stranger?

speaker: Chad
en: Burk, the man I work for. He did this to me, that evil man! I was simply doing a round of checks on our last shipment when he accused me of theft! Me! Theft! Please, bring me up to the bridge. I need some treatment, some medicine...

speaker: Burk
en: There you are, Chad. About time you showed your face... or what's left of it!

speaker: Chad
en: Burk? No! No! Get away from me!

speaker: Burk
en: Come along, Chad. We still have work to do.

speaker: Chad
en: Work? You still want me to work? I can't even see my own hands, you heartless bastard!

speaker: Eivor
en: He says you blinded him.

speaker: Burk
en: Aye, that I did. What is a leader to do when his men can't take their eyes off of his treasure, even after several warnings?

speaker: Chad
en: I ... I was not looking! You stabbed my eyes out!

speaker: Burk
en: Quiet now, Chad. Come, hand him over to me.

speaker: Burk
en: Do your best to follow me, Chad.

speaker: Chad
en: Just kill me instead.

speaker: Chad
en: Thank you, stranger. I thought my fate was sealed.

speaker: Chad
en: No-no... just let me die... I'd rather die...

speaker: Eivor
en: He might have been better off stuck below the bridge. Too late now.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Archives. This must be where Audun shuffles the council papers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wreaths, timber, food, wine... an expensive list of items to procure for a feast.

speaker: Eivor
en: Weapons and supplies, but not enough to arm and feed even the smallest army.

speaker: Eivor
en: A pile of official scrolls, stamped with a seal.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: Thank you, Audun. I will leave with these at once.

speaker: Audun
en: Of course.

speaker: Audun
en: Eivor, isn't it? What brings you to our archives?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have come to ask about these Christian texts. Ljufvina tells me the Red Hand is stealing them.

speaker: Audun
en: Hmm... And destroying them. I fear they will attack these archives next. The abbess here has offered to bring the texts somewhere safe. She's been working diligently on this matter.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: You flatter me, lord. I only wish to help.

speaker: Audun
en: Abbess Ingeborg, this is Eivor, our honored guests from the south. Eivor has offered to help rid Jorvik of the Red Hand.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: How can I help?

speaker: Eivor
en: An abbess does not strike me as a suitable choice against a gang of ruthless bandits.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: It is my duty to protect the role of Christianity in our lives. Texts like this were created for more than just perusing. They are a gift. They spread the word of God, and it is that which must be preserved, whatsoever the cost.

speaker: Eivor
en: I admire your resolve, but unless the Red Hand is dismantled, they will continue to harm those in possession of these texts. The Red Hand seems to know where to look for these texts. It may be someone is guiding them. What can you tell me? You know something else. That much is clear.

speaker: Eivor
en: You say you are keeping the texts safe. Where?

speaker: Ingeborg
en: Forgive me, Eivor, but as an outsider, I do not understand your stake in this. For that, I am reluctant to trust you. The texts are safest with me. I will do what I must to guard them from the Red Hand.

speaker: Eivor
en: I admire your resolve, but unless the Red Hand is dismantled, they will continue to harm those in possession of these texts. The Red Hand seems to know where to look for these texts. It may be someone is guiding them. What can you tell me? You know something else. That much is clear.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Red Hand seems to know where to look for these texts. It may be someone is guiding them. What can you tell me?

speaker: Eivor
en: You know something else. That much is clear.

speaker: Audun
en: The abbess has her suspicions.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: As much as it pains me to say, I suspect something foul at the rectory. I have heard whispering, collusion. And the bishop... he has been sneaking around the rectory, often visiting the priests in the cover of night.

speaker: Eivor
en: Time I pay these men of faith a visit.

speaker: Eivor
en: The rectory is on the road to the minster. I should look for the bishop there.

speaker: Audun
en: I have the Yuletide feast to prepare for as well. Do drop by for the festivities, Eivor. Have a drink or two.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here is the rectory. The abbess said she suspected secrecy among the priests and bishops. Seems quiet. Where is everyone?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Uh! Get away!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop!

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Ahh! Leave me be! Please.

speaker: Eivor
en: What has you doused in sweat and trembling so?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Th-the Red Hand! They're everywhere. Please, I don't want any trouble.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks as though everyone else has fled this place, so why are you still here?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Waiting for the bishop. One of our brothers said he would return soon. That's all I know, I swear it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is this other priest?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: He's locked himself in. That house, just there.

speaker: Eivor
