en: Someone is hiding in there. Doubt he will come out. I will have to find a way in.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: No! Stay away from me! Stay back! Agh!

speaker: Eivor
en: Musky. Been here long, priest?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Just who do you think you are, trespassing like this! This is my property you've destroyed!

speaker: Eivor
en: I hear you priests have been hiding ever since some Christian texts went missing. What are you hiding from?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: The Red Hand, who else? They muscle their way to and fro. No one has a done a thing about it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am looking for the bishop. Where is he?

speaker: Eivor
en: First your property, next your arm, and if you think I will stop there, you are mistaken.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Wh-What do you want from me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am looking for the bishop. Where is he?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am looking for the bishop. Where is he?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Gone to his quarters. Said he would return once he finished tending to a private matter. But that was some time ago.

speaker: Eivor
en: Show me there.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Wh-what do you mean to do with him?

speaker: Eivor
en: Now.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Lord forgive me...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Ahhh... I knew I should have left with the others.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: The bishop's quarters. What is that burning smell?

speaker: Eivor
en: It's blocked.

speaker: Eivor
en: Several Christian texts. The abbess was right to cast suspicions the bishop's way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Blood... there was a struggle here.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Lord above! Th-The bishop! N-no, I can't look. O, dear Lord...

speaker: Eivor
en: Oof... the stench. He looks like Surtr's shit.

speaker: Eivor
en: A charred letter beneath the body. He must have tried to hide it before he died.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone knew the bishop was conflicted and killed him before he could say a word.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a confession. The bishop played his part in destroying these texts against his own will. The rest of the letter is burnt, but makes mention of the minster and the abbess. Is that where she has been keeping these texts?

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Look around! Search every room! They are around here somewhere.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: It's them! It's the Red Hand. O Lord have mercy!

speaker: Eivor
en: Quiet.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Red Hand. I need to leave.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Find that pagan! We will burn that sinner, just like the others.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Stay out of the way, heathen! We will complete our work! You cannot stop us!

speaker: Eivor
en: The target sent the Red Hand after me. I must be closing in. It's time I head to the minster. The abbess knows more than she is letting on.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: The Firebrand's plan is coming to fruition.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: At long last. We've waited in the shadows for too long.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: Keep your eyes sharp and watch out for uninvited guests. She does not like interruptions.

speaker: Eivor
en: Red Hand all around. They must have secured the minster.

speaker: Eivor
en: Locked. There must be another way in.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: What... just what do you think you're doing!

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: This is no place for you, priest. Go. Now.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Blasphemy! Stop this at once!

speaker: Ingeborg
en: Something troubling you, Father?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Abbess! Look! They are burning all of these passages. Why are you not stopping this?

speaker: Ingeborg
en: Because I ordered them to.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: What...?

speaker: Ingeborg
en: The vellum that burn before you are covered in lies. So long as they exist, you cannot hope to see the world the way it truly is.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Lies? Abbess, what has happened to you? We are God's children, all! Do not renounce Him like this, please, I beg of you. You can still repent. God will forgive you. You know He will.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: Your mind has been poisoned, but worry not, we have the antidote. We will set a new example to which all may aspire.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Y-you... you're mad! You won't get away with this. I won't let you!

speaker: Ingeborg
en: There is no one to tell. No one who will hear your cries. If you cannot bear to watch them burn, then you should burn with them.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: I want it all destroyed. Every text, every passage, every scribbled piece of paper. Everything. It is time to end this.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier (Decoy)
en: Yes, Firebrand.

speaker: Eivor
en: The abbess is The Firebrand. She'll kill whoever stands in her way. Time I get between her and her next victim.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: But why must we burn them?

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier (Decoy 1)
en: The fire cleanses impurities, and it is our duty to purify the future of Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not The Firebrand.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier (Decoy 2)
en: When every text is destroyed, it will mark the beginning of a new chapter, just as The Firebrand says.

speaker: Eivor
en: Still not The Firebrand, but I have you now.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: Go, tell them the Abbess sent you, and bring the texts here at once.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 6
en: Yes, Firebrand.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: This fire that burns inside... I've always had it. A longing to do something grand and important. But that door was always shut to me. My methods deemed too severe. I was cast out, shunned, scorned... But the Order, they took notice of me. Saw that it was courage that drove me. Courage to change the world for the better. They reopened that door.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you used your chance to destroy a way of life, you did not support.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: We have seen time and time again what happens when people are left to interpret for themselves. Knowledge must be controlled. Only then can the message be widely understood. The day where there is but one truth draws nearer. One truth, that is what the Order offers.

speaker: Odin
en: This ones sought to spark a new flame, but did so with a heavy hand, not a teacher's tongue.

speaker: Eivor
en: This cleansing of yours ends here.

speaker: Ingeborg
en: My work is incomplete, but not inconsequential. There are others who carry on, for one of the four is us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why did you say that? What does it mean?

speaker: Ingeborg
en: Now I go, a flame that grows bright, and burns evermore, ever light.

speaker: Eivor
en: To Helheim, where colder and crueler fires await.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should return to Ljufvina. She will want to know about Abbess Ingeborg's involvement.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: What news do you bring?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Firebrand's name burns no longer. It was Jorvik's abbess, Ingeborg.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Gods, I would never have suspected. Does The Order's reach know no bounds?

speaker: Eivor
en: None. And it is often those we least expect who carry out their ambitions. The abbess, she sought to destroy all Christian texts in the city. Rid Jorvik of their ideals. She did utter a phrase that perked my ears—"One of the four is ours."

speaker: Lfujvina
en: Four? But there are only three targets in Jorvik. Could there be something we're missing?

speaker: Faravid
en: Damn Picts! Not only do they hold the North, but those lawless shits have free-roam in our lands as well!

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Hjorr said our spies are on the ground

speaker: Faravid
en: Under the ground! Only one of them has returned, bone-beaten and bloodied! The howling mother take them.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Ljufvina, a moment of your time? And Hjorr if he is about.

speaker: Lfujvina
en: I will be with you shortly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Two more left to hunt.

speaker: Lfujvina
en: The disputes coming out of the docks lately have been deafening. Head there and dig around. Something is bound to turn up.

speaker: Liv
en: We'll never get to watch another sunrise together. (weeping) Curse this damn roof and its loose tiles! My poor, sweet Bo! (weeping) Oh Bo! My beloved Bo! You had your whole life ahead of you!

speaker: Havi
en: Hey! What is it? Why the wailing?

speaker: Liv
en: It's, it's... (weeping)

speaker: Havi
en: Speak freely.

speaker: Liv
en: My beloved Bo. I never got to say goodbye! He was fixing the roof, when he slipped and fell, and now he's... he's...

speaker: Havi
en: I... I see. Perhaps it's not too late to help him.

speaker: Havi
en: There's nothing I can do for him now. But... these new abilities... Perhaps a way to help will reveal itself, and I can return.

speaker: Havi
en: If all she wants is to say a final goodbye... I think I can help.

speaker: Bo
en: What in the blazes... I'm... alive?! I am alive! Oh thank you, thank you, stranger! Haha! What luck to have this second chance! Never again shall I take even a moment of my time for granted!

speaker: Liv
en: Darling, I

speaker: Bo
en: And never again shall I step out onto that perilous roof of mine! Repairs?! Bah, there's more to life than maintaining tiles! Look out world, here I come!

speaker: Liv
en: Waaah!

speaker: Havi
en: Um... there-there.

speaker: Liv
en: But... I... never... got... to say... goodbye! Waaaah!

speaker: Havi
en: Yes, well, I'll... I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Havi
en: You're alive, yes. Now shut up. She has something to tell you.

speaker: Bo
en: Oh. Right... and uh, who would you be, miss?

speaker: Liv
en: Don't you recognize me, Bo? It's Liv, your love!

speaker: Bo
en: I've, err, never laid eyes upon you miss, lovely as you are.

speaker: Liv
en: You must have hit your head when you died! Have you forgotten our passion!? The life we built in this house? Look, Bo, where did you hide the treasure? Uh, our treasure.

speaker: Bo
en: Treasure...? What treasure?

speaker: Liv
en: Waaah!

speaker: Havi
en: Would you give it a rest!

speaker: Bo
en: Why do you keep bringing me back?!

speaker: Havi
en: To satisfy my curiosity. You. Do you know her?

speaker: Bo
en: Never met her before today.

speaker: Havi
en: You. What is the meaning of all this?

speaker: Liv
en: Uh...

speaker: Bo
en: Where is my house key? You robbed me when I was dead!

speaker: Liv
en: Fine! Yes! When I saw you fall, I thought, finally, I can take the valuables I know you've got stashed in your house! Maybe the house too! But with all the Muspels around, you can keep your stupid key! Good day!

speaker: Havi
en: Ugh. Leave me in peace, the pair of you.

speaker: Havi
en: Not so fast. Hand over the key.

speaker: Liv
en: Fine!

speaker: Havi
en: You're clearly resourceful. Do you know of the Crystal Caves overlooking Uldar? There's shelter there. Other dwarves. You'll be safe.

speaker: Liv
en: Then I'll be on my way. Here's your bloody key. And... thanks, I suppose.

speaker: Bo
en: What? What is so important that you can't just leave me alone? I already told you, my house and anything inside is yours. Now kindly sod off. For good! Oh for pity's sake, what now? Do you know how it feels to keep getting a new lease on life, but only for a fleeting moment! Look, anything in that house, help yourself. It's not like I've got any use for it. Now, if you don't mind, I'd like to rest. In peace! Either you've got a sickness or you are painfully lonely. Which is it? Actually, y'know what... I don't care. Mortal concerns are no longer mine. Go on, piss off with ya.

speaker: Randvi
en: One more thing... I do not know if you heard, but Svend passed away a short time ago. The poor man slipped away in his bed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I had not heard, no. And how is Tove? She must be gutted.

speaker: Randvi
en: It has been rough on her. She spends quite a lot of time at his burial mound. Speak with her if you have the time.

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem sad, Gunnar.

speaker: Gunnar
en: I am... Svend was a good friend to me, over the years.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am sorry I was not here to send him on his way. He was loved.

speaker: Gunnar
en: That he was. But suppose we honor him best by keeping the clan going. Anyhow, you probably need something, eh?

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem sad, Gunnar.

speaker: Gunnar
en: I am... Svend was a good friend to me, over the years.

speaker: Eivor
en: "Was?" What do you mean?

speaker: Gunnar
en: O, no, Eivor... You've been away. Sorry to say that Svend passed away not two nights ago. In his sleep.

speaker: Eivor
en: No... How is Tove?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Taking it hard. Very hard. You ought to go have a word with her. As far as I know, she's barely left his grave. Anyhow, you probably need something, eh?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm off. Be well, friend.

speaker: Randvi
en: One more thing... I do not know if you heard, but Svend passed away a short time ago. The poor man slipped away in his bed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes... I had heard, the poor man. I wish I could have spent more time with him before the end.

speaker: Randvi
en: I think we all wish that. Tove most of all.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tove? What is she doing here?

speaker: Tove
en: You are the only father I've ever had... I don't know how to draw without your hand to guide me. There was so much we were meant to do.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tove...

speaker: Tove
en: Eivor, it's Svend, he ... he passed, while I was away.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tove, I'm sorry I wasn't there.

speaker: Tove
en: No one was. We had planned to brand Tekla's barrel that morning, and we talked about what we might have for supper. When I went to collect him he was ... in his bed. Sleeping, I thought. But he was already gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sure he went in peace.

speaker: Tove
en: But he went with plans! Things he wanted to do. Things he meant to do. His death was so ... empty. Not like in our stories.

speaker: Eivor
en: What stories do you mean?

speaker: Tove
en: When we tell stories, the old and wise, they have this calm about them. They know when their end has come, and they are ready. Svend wasn't ready. And I wasn't ready either. He was supposed to teach me things. I'm still learning. Everyone looks at me like I will simply carry on his work. As if nothing happened. Because they don't know... They don't know I'm not ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: Life may ask more of us than we are prepared to give, but all we can do is our best. I was not prepared to lose my parents. But in a flash, they were taken from me. I pressed on, determined to live.

speaker: Tove
en: That must have been ... punishing. But you are so strong, so determined.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone else might have done better than me. Or worse. But this was the fate woven for me. So I live it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know Svend believed in you, in your craft. So do you believe in him? Do you trust him?

speaker: Tove
en: He was the most skilled artist I have ever known.

speaker: Eivor
en: And he chose you. You may step up or step down, whatever you decide. But know that he had faith in you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Life is not a story, Tove. It is a fractured shout, unguided by verse. Most of us meet untidy ends. If we knew the shape of our stories before we lived them, we would hardly attempt to live them.

speaker: Tove
en: I would have given anything for another day with Svend, even a wordless one. He was not ready to go.

speaker: Tove
en: When we tell stories, the old and wise, they have this calm about them. They know when their end has come, and they are ready. Svend wasn't ready. And I wasn't ready either. He was supposed to teach me things. I'm still learning. Everyone looks at me like I will simply carry on his work. As if nothing happened. Because they don't know... They don't know I'm not ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: Life may ask more of us than we are prepared to give, but all we can do is our best. I was not prepared to lose my parents. But in a flash, they were taken from me. I pressed on, determined to live.

speaker: Tove
en: That must have been ... punishing. But you are so strong, so determined.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone else might have done better than me. Or worse. But this was the fate woven for me. So I live it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know Svend believed in you, in your craft. So do you believe in him? Do you trust him?

speaker: Tove
en: He was the most skilled artist I have ever known.

speaker: Eivor
en: And he chose you. You may step up or step down, whatever you decide. But know that he had faith in you.

speaker: Tove
en: Thank you, Eivor. I need to get home.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be strong, Tove. And know that you are valued.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am sorry I was not here to see you off, old friend. When I close my eyes, Svend, I see your designs on the arms of gods. You have taught Tove well. Through her, you live on.

speaker: Tove
en: Eivor. Good to see you.

speaker: Eivor
en: How are you, Tove? Holding up?

speaker: Tove
en: Much better now, I think. I miss Svend every day, and yet he is here with me. His hugr (mind) infused in every design. Believing that, it helps.

speaker: Eivor
en: Glad to hear it. And happy to offer myself as your first canvas.

speaker: Tove
en: Good. Let's get started.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vagn.

speaker: Vagn
en: It seems as though all your raids have pushed certain sacred sites to seek out protectors. They have hired mercenaries to act as their champions of the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does this mean for me?

speaker: Vagn
en: Each river will have their defenses raised to their highest level.

speaker: Eivor
en: So I should avoid them?

speaker: Vagn
en: No! You should draw them out, slay them and claim their fancy weapons as your own.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vagn! I defeated all the champions and claimed their arms.

speaker: Vagn
en: Haha! You would have made a fearsome Jomsviking, Eivor.

speaker: Havi
en: I could not strike the killing blow. All my oaths remain unbroken.

speaker: Týr
en: Anyone lesser would have succumbed to his hatred.

speaker: Havi
en: If I could have done this any other way

speaker: Týr
en: There was no other way, Havi. Our fates are fixed.

speaker: Havi
en: Fate or no, you've made a great sacrifice on my behalf.

speaker: Týr
en: It was not for you.

speaker: Fenrir
en: Do not think your kindness has made you a new friend, Lord of Imbeciles. I will kill you. All of you, gorging on Æsir flesh.

speaker: Havi
en: You may strike the final blow, Son of Loki. But I will savor my years of freedom before we meet again.

speaker: Havi
en: Come, old friend. The healing hands of Freyja can help you.

speaker: Havi
en: Have you come to say what I fear?

speaker: Urðr
en: Not to say...

speaker: Verðandi
en: ...but to show...

speaker: Skulð
en: ...a vision of the times to come.

speaker: Urðr
en: None living or dead now equal our Havi in arrogance. To believe that you could remake your fate thus...

speaker: Verðandi
en: For all your efforts, for all your struggles, the threads of Fate still bind you as tightly as ever.

speaker: Skulð
en: And yet... from this pattern, a single strand escapes the fray... and stubbornly clings to weave. Æsir. Vanir. Your doom will come.

speaker: Skulð
en: The earth will shake. The sun will die. Jötnar will stalk your streets, as fire rains upon your heads.

speaker: Skulð
en: And the great wolf Fenrir will feast upon your blood.

speaker: Skulð
en: But you have found a way to live beyond this terror.

speaker: Havi
en: Let it flow.

speaker: Skulð
en: To cheat your death.

speaker: Havi
en: From the life-tree we go, to the life-tree we shall one day return.

speaker: Skulð
en: Mind and spirit will surge to a time far beyond your own. To a time in which you shall be reborn.

speaker: Havi
en: None may follow. Loki least of all.

speaker: Havi
en: It is done. Time to face our end.

speaker: Havi
en: This was not my day to die.

speaker: Havi
en: You fight well with your off hand, as if born to it.

speaker: Týr
en: Easier than expected. And how does the world look through a single eye?

speaker: Havi
en: It keeps me alert, focused. You are strong as ever, Týr. I'm glad for your swift recovery, body and hugr (mind).

speaker: Týr
en: What's done was bound to be. I bare no ill will to any here, not you, not Fenrir, not even Loki.

speaker: Havi
en: I'm not ready to forgive the trickster.

speaker: Týr
en: Will you punish him?

speaker: Havi
en: Not in this life. But he will not join us in immortality. The world we wake into will be free of his malice.

speaker: Týr
en: If it must be so...

speaker: Freyja
en: Your journey has borne fruit.

speaker: Havi
en: Of the sweetest kind. Life. Which I intend to share, of course.

speaker: Freyja
en: We are fortunate that luck follows you like a dark feline. Against all odds, your success is what redeems you. Endears you.

speaker: Havi
en: And how charming do you find me now?

speaker: Freyja
en: Just enough to keep me awake.

speaker: Havi
en: I've barely seen Frigg since we

speaker: Havi
en: I will not give up. I never do.

speaker: Freyja
en: Good.

speaker: Thor
en: All-Father! Giant-slayer! Doom-bringer! (laugh) Do you remember your fight with the Builder? The jötunn who disguised himself as a craftsman? It wasn't long ago.

speaker: Havi
en: I remember.

speaker: Thor
en: I must admit, it was a glorious kill! I should have told you then, but my envy consumed me.

speaker: Havi
en: It was a good fight.

speaker: Thor
en: We should go hunting soon! Remember the days we used to hunt? With our wolves, ?

speaker: Havi
en: A good idea. We will hunt Jötnar soon... without the wolves. Just the pair of us, Skull-smasher. Bone-Breaker.

speaker: Thor
en: Let old times be new times! (laugh) I will be seeing you, Old One. Sleep with one eye open!

speaker: Havi
en: Farewell, Son.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will Alfida remember a lover from so long ago? Would I?

speaker: Eivor
en: The last house in Maeldun. Alfida should be here.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: We've got the woman we came for. Leave that lackbeard to lick his wounds.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone was interrupted preparing their supper. Taken? Or fled?

speaker: Eivor
en: A second bed. Alfida doesn't live alone.

speaker: Angry Plea
en: Enough, Malden. No one enjoys high jinx more than me, but due to the number of oil-based fires, I cannot in good conscience allow unlimited access to such incendiary material. Therefore, all oil jars in the village have been collected and placed under lock and key. If you behave like children, you will be treated as such. Yours in exasperation, Brother Thomas

speaker: Eivor
en: A spilled pail of water. Someone was in a hurry.

speaker: Eluric
en: Leave me be, warmonger! You have my sister, is that not enough?

speaker: Eivor
en: Peace, boy. I'm not with these men. I came to speak with your sister, that's all.

speaker: Eluric
en: A Dane in Essexe? Now here's a day riddled with strange portents and happenings.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is your name?

speaker: Eluric
en: I'm Eluric, the man of this house. Who are you, and why have you come?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for your sister, at the behest of another.

speaker: Eluric
en: Behest? We got no money to speak of, and my sister is well past the marrying age.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you know where they're holding Alfida?

speaker: Eivor
en: Why did they take your sister?

speaker: Eluric
en: Some of Aelfred's men beat a child of the village for stealing bread. My sister would not stand by and see injustice done.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you know where they're holding Alfida?

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you know where they're holding Alfida?

speaker: Eluric
en: Yet another stay at the king's pleasure. The prison camp at Brentwood. Far to the west.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll bring her to the lake house north of there. Meet us there if you wish.

speaker: Eluric
en: If you promise you will find her, I will.

speaker: Alfida
en: You would cage me like an animal? Cock-tossers, all of you!

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be Birstan's love, Alfida. They haven't broken her spirit.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will need to find a key.

speaker: Alfida
en: Someone, please! These bollock-beards left me to rot!

speaker: Alfida
en: What... what is this? You're not one of them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay quiet. I'm here to free you.

speaker: Alfida
en: I cannot walk. My ankle... They were not gentle with me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I will carry you.

speaker: Alfida
en: Who are you, who risked so much to save me?

speaker: Eivor
en: A friend.

speaker: Alfida
en: Of Eluric's? Is he alright, the poor boy!

speaker: Eivor
en: Not your brother. Someone else who wishes to rekindle a... a friendship.

speaker: Alfida
en: Gentler please!

speaker: Eivor
en: You'll soon be safe, rest easy.

speaker: Alfida
en: They beat me! My bones ache! My ankle! The pain!

speaker: Eluric
en: Bless the saints! Here you are, Sister, safe and well!

speaker: Alfida
en: O, my leg... it pains.

speaker: Eivor
en: We're almost there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rest now. Soon you will be up and about again.

speaker: Eluric
en: Alfida! Did they hurt you?

speaker: Alfida
en: Takes more than some cockshy milksops to break my will. Beating a boy half to death for stealing bread? I'll not see it done.

speaker: Eluric
en: Growling bellies mean nothing to those pay-swords.

speaker: Alfida
en: Eluric, pay more mind to the world. It is cruel and dark for those who cannot stand up for themselves.

speaker: Eivor
en: Alfida, can we speak in private?

speaker: Alfida
en: He is a good boy. But without a father to guide him, he's grown softer than I'd hoped.

speaker: Eivor
en: You raised him alone? Where were your parents when he was a child?

speaker: Alfida
en: Dead of the plague that came when he was three months born. Suiters shun your door when you have a babe on your teat. Now it's your turn. Why did you come for me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here at the request of Ealdorman Birstan. He wonders if you could love him again.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found him cowering like a frightened pup near your house. He may need a firmer hand.

speaker: Alfida
en: You would judge us? My parents died and left me alone with a babe when I was little more than a girl myself. Now speak plain. Why have you come for me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here at the request of Ealdorman Birstan. He wonders if you could love him again.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here at the request of Ealdorman Birstan. He wonders if you could love him again.

speaker: Alfida
en: Love him? Dear old Birstan, he remembers!

speaker: Eivor
en: He does.

speaker: Alfida
en: I've thought of him sometimes myself. But with my brother to fend for, I could not waste a life mooning.

speaker: Eivor
en: He has thought of nothing but you, Alfida. And with his wife Estrid returning to Francia, he sent me to find you.

speaker: Alfida
en: How it would work between me and him? I'm a poor woman, have been always. But the ealdorman... O God, help me!

speaker: Alfida
en: I'll give him a go. How could I not, O bless!

speaker: Eivor
en: He'll come if you call. At the lighting of the bonfire, he'll ride here to meet you.

speaker: Alfida
en: Eluric, come you and sit with us. I have something to say...

speaker: Birstan
en: My... my apple-blossom girl! Is it really you?

speaker: Alfida
en: It is. Though crows have left their footfalls round my eyes.

speaker: Birstan
en: They still shine brightly, as when we were children. Has Eivor told you all?

speaker: Alfida
en: Aye, she has.

speaker: Birstan
en: And do you accept me, love? My heart feels like it will burst.

speaker: Eivor
en: Give her time, Birstan. A passion rekindled in haste will soon fall to embers.

speaker: Birstan
en: Of course! You are absolutely right. And we have a lifetime to recapture what was mislaid.

speaker: Alfida
en: I hope it will not take that.

speaker: Eivor
en: And this young lad is Eluric, Alfida's brother.

speaker: Eivor
en: And this young lad is Eluric, Alfida's brother.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now that you are reunited, what will you do?

speaker: Birstan
en: Are we reunited? I must hear it from your lips, Alfida. It has been many summers, and I have aged ungracefully.

speaker: Alfida
en: I will hear your wooing, Birstan. God help me, I have nothing to keep me in Maeldun.

speaker: Eivor
en: And this young lad is Eluric, Alfida's brother.

speaker: Eluric
en: Hello, Your... Your worshipfulness.

speaker: Birstan
en: I am Birstan, nothing more or less. And you are a fine, strong lad of... how old?

speaker: Eluric
en: Nineteen summers.

speaker: Alfida
en: He's all the family I have, Birstan. If I'm to stay, you must welcome us both into your heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: We have one half of our bargain done, Birstan. I will return with news of the other.

speaker: Eluric
en: Does this mean we're leaving Maeldun?

speaker: Birstan
en: You are, my boy. To live with me in Colcestre. Perhaps I can teach you the joy of the hunt!

speaker: Eivor
en: Before you go, Eluric... I'd suggest a long, slow walk around the lake.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should leave them to their reunion. The next piece of this drama is the kidnap in Colcestre.

speaker: Alfida
en: Dear Birstan... I cannot believe you would come for me after all these years.

speaker: Birstan
en: I never stopped thinking of you, Alfida.

speaker: Alfida
en: I had forgotten his charm, still so boyish and eager to make me happy. The silly arse.

speaker: Birstan
en: She has not changed at all. Her soft features, her earthy strength. She will make a good wife.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Spread out around to the side of 'em, lads! Stay on your toes, or we'll be on the gibbet!

speaker: Eivor
en: You there. Why are you crawling about?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: A patrol of Eadwyn's men is coming this way. We're going to jump 'em.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Steady, boys. Lambs to the slaughter.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Caught 'em by the balls, we did! Well done, wayfarer, couldn't've done it without you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Dear God, we're in trouble. Watch out over there, men! O, Christ in holy Heaven.

speaker: Eivor
en: Geadric asked me to help you whenever I could.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Eadwyn's soldiers've got us in a tough spot. We're grateful for any help you can give.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: That was a near-run thing. Thanks for helping us out.

speaker: Journal Entry
en: A few of us came looking to join a fyrd hoping for a quick victory and plenty of spoils. But now we're lost and hungry. Some soldiers marched by while we hid in the underbrush. Eadwyn's men. We'll see some fighting soon. God help us.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Eadwyn's men! They're after us.

speaker: Eivor
en: You there. What's wrong?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Here they come! Quick, men, or they'll wipe us out!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: You pulled our asses out of the fire, friend. We're grateful to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have weakened Eadwyn's defenses enough. Ambushing her soldiers should be my final strike before the battle begins.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: The Lord works in mysterious ways, taking his servant in so terrible a fire.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Bishop Ealhferth was no man of God.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Hush! Selwyn has hanged men for better thoughts.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Why does Aelfred not do something? Selwyn's bloodlust will doom us all.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 4
en: Selywn punishes criminals, as it should be.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: He's the worst criminal of them all!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: Those who do wrong must be punished.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 5
en: Jesus would preach forgiveness!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: Jesus did not live in the cesspool that is Wincestre.

speaker: Selwyn
en: Good people of Wincestre. Open your eyes. See how Aelfred's lofty ideals are weighed down in the mire of human effluence.

speaker: Selwyn
en: These prisoners before you do not live by Aelfred's laws. They live above them. They wallow in shit, only guided by their own perversity. Hubert here, his wits addled by ale, spoke false of Bishop Ealhferth, our pious servant of Wincestre, who even now lies cold in his grave-shroud.

speaker: Leona
en: Ealhferth was no man of God! He'll burn for his sins!

speaker: Selwyn
en: Your wife is a baying shrew, Hubert! Is there a man here who has not supped rancid mead from her cup?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 6
en: When will your work be done, Selwyn? When all of Wincestre falls to your justice?

speaker: Selwyn
en: Wincestre has passed judgment, Hubert. May God have mercy on your cankerous soul.

speaker: Selwyn
en: There are rats in the grain store, and Aelfred has set the traps. You cannot steal and be welcomed at our hearths. You cannot slander and keep your tongue. You cannot walk freely through our streets, mocking our laws, our king's edict. And so I ask, who has the right to determine the fate of the perverse, if not the goodly people of Wincestre. I am but your humble servant. Leona, you have been found guilty of harlotry and defamation. May God have mercy on your pockmarked soul.

speaker: Selwyn
en: I will kill you for this. Protect your servant, Wincestre. You will not pervert justice! Who dares to defy Aelfred's laws? The degenerates must be punished. You are the enemy of Wincestre.

speaker: Selwyn
en: Perverter of justice! Who dares execute the King's noose?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not in Aelfred's name that you carry out your work. You are The Order's executioner.

speaker: Selwyn
en: Ah. You peer through the veil, but you do not see clearly. Aelfred's laws are a slave's fever-dream. He offers shit-soaked beggars a seat at his table. Where the meek devour the strong. Who best to judge the fate of the wretched many, if not the strong and worthy few?

speaker: Odin
en: To protect your people, you must sheathe your hand in an iron glove.

speaker: Eivor
en: You grind your heels into the backs of freedmen, not those who deserve it.

speaker: Selwyn
en: The Order condemns all men to pain, for all men are but a shadow of the perfection we should know.

speaker: Selwyn
en: The perfection of the Ancient Ones.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are only a man, reeve. One dead branch on a fast dying tree.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should meet with Goodwin, see what he has found on The Quill.

speaker: Leona
en: Selwyn is dead? His lies poisoned everyone against us, and for what?

speaker: Eivor
en: Some only care for their own power and position. I am sorry I could not save your husband.

speaker: Leona
en: My son is not an orphan today. You did more than enough.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: What news do you bring?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Needle will never sting again.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Well done, Eivor. Who was hiding behind the name

speaker: Hjorr
en: My love. There has been an attack at the markets. The dockmaster, Grigorii, is dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Needle. Sold off the wares he seized to collect silver for The Vault.

speaker: Hjorr
en: He had no such authority, why would anyone believe him?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The council seal. That rat!

speaker: Hjorr
en: This is getting out of hand. How he was able to obtain this is... concerning. I must return and prepare for the Yuletide feast, but I will do so with a bent ear and a keen eye. Be safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Firebrand's flame burns no longer. It was Jorvik's abbess, Ingeborg.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Gods, I would have never suspected. Does The Order's reach know no bounds?

speaker: Eivor
en: None. And it is often those we least expect who carry out their ambitions. The abbess, she sought to destroy all Christian texts in the city. Rid Jorvik of their ideals. She did utter a phrase that perked my ears—"One of the four is ours."

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Four? But there are only three targets in Jorvik. Could there be something we're missing?

speaker: Faravid
en: Damned Picts! Not only do they hold the North, but those lawless shits have free-roam in our lands as well!

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Hjorr said our spies are on the ground

speaker: Faravid
en: Under the ground! Only one of them has returned, bone-beaten and bloodied! The howling mother take them!

speaker: Ricsige
en: Ljufvina, a moment of your time? And Hjorr if he is about.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: I will be with you shortly.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have knocked two names off the list. The Firebrand and The Needle.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Well done. Who were they?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Firebrand was Jorvik's abbess. She sought to destroy all Christian texts in the city. Rid Jorvik of their ideals.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Gods... does The Order's reach know no bounds?

speaker: Eivor
en: None. And it is often those we least expect who carry out their ambitions.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I heard what happened at the minster and the markets. The dockmaster, the abbess, both killed. Was that you?

speaker: Eivor
en: They were two of the names in the letter. Only one remains, The Vault.

speaker: Hjorr
en: This is getting out of hand! I hope you have the final name.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm working on that. I found this on The Needle.

speaker: Hjorr
en: The council's seal.

speaker: Eivor
en: And the abbess uttered something that perked my ear as well: "One of the four is ours."

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Four? But there are only three targets in Jorvik.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I must return and prepare for the Yuletide feast, but I will do so with a bent ear and a keen eye. Be safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: A valuable seal... and a riddle, "One of the four is ours."

speaker: Eivor
en: "One of the four"... Ricsige, Faravid, Audun, and

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Hjorr. The four members of the council.

speaker: Eivor
en: We should search their offices now. While they are occupied with the Yuletide feast.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Yes... yes. Come. To the Archives.

speaker: Eivor
en: Could I have missed something?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: We will find out soon enough.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The room to the left that is where the councilmen confer.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have seen these. Weapons, and supplies. Enough for a small group of fighters.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Hardly enough for Halfdan's army.

speaker: Eivor
en: Could be why Faravid is pressing the council for more silver.

speaker: Eivor
en: A list... what Jorvik needs for the Yuletide feast.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: That is Audun's handwriting.

speaker: Eivor
en: Items have been struck out. Where did he find the funds to make this large a purchase?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Audun is a well-connected man.

speaker: Eivor
en: A wax seal, similar to the one I found in the sewers.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The seal you took from The Needle's hand. You don't think someone could have stolen it...?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's keep searching.

speaker: Note to Silversmith
en: To be delivered to: Coppergate Market I will need this smelted down, and I will procure more if necessary. Breathe not a word of this to my wife. -Hjorr

speaker: Eivor
en: This desk... it looks as though it has been moved here.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: That's Hjorr's desk.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is loaded with silver.

speaker: Eivor
en: Scratch marks on the floor.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Hjorr's desk used to be against the other wall.

speaker: Eivor
en: So why the change?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: A hidden entrance... where does this lead?

speaker: Eivor
en: Guard the door.

speaker: Eivor
en: There was wine here. Whoever moved it did so in a hurry.

speaker: Eivor
en: A load of wine was removed from here, and the room smells of almonds. It may be the wine was poisoned.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: It it likely the wine for the Yuletide feast. Do you think one of the council means to kill someone?

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks that way.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: It is not him. Not my Hjorr. He would never do this, he...

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Keep your focus. Once we have all the facts, then we can worry about Hjorr. Right now, we need to get to Yuletide feast. The people are in danger.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: You're right. The Roman Amphitheater. Let us go.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you see the wine?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: No.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then there is still time.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The entire council is here. Any one of them could be The Vault.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need you to keep an eye out for the wine. I will speak to each of the council members. See if I can trap them in a lie.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Even Hjorr?

speaker: Eivor
en: Even Hjorr. If he is The Vault, I will not allow him to kill all these people. Ljufvina...

speaker: Ljufvina
en: I heard you. Just... grant me one thing. Confer with me before you make your move.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, to speak with the council members. I will speak of the wine and watch for their reactions. That may lead me to The Vault.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ricsige.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Ah. Come to join in the feast, have you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have some bad news. The wine for the feast has spoiled.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Of course it has. Why would I expect differently? I'll have my men dump it. There may be more wine in my private stores, I'll send a man to retrieve it. Is there anything else?

speaker: Eivor
en: That is all. Enjoy the feast.

speaker: Ricsige
en: I shall try.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I will have the silver ready in the coming days. Thank you, Boe.

speaker: Boe
en: Of course.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hjorr. Who was that?

speaker: Hjorr
en: There you are. I was beginning to worry.

speaker: Eivor
en: Worry not. We have tracked The Vault here. He is someone on the council.

speaker: Hjorr
en: You are certain?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am. Once I discover who, I will dig my blade into his heart and end this for good. Until then, it is important that I investigate without raising suspicion. I need your help.

speaker: Hjorr
en: Of course. What do you need me to do?

speaker: Eivor
en: Drink yourself into a drunken fit.

speaker: Hjorr
en: What? Why?

speaker: Eivor
en: I need a distraction. Keep their eyes off of me. The wine should arrive soon. Drink three full cups, then make a scene.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I can't be seen doing that. You'll have to find another way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Just do it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: What a delightful feast.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Audun has outdone himself.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: He has indeed. The High Reeve of Jorvik has a bright future ahead if he keeps this up.

speaker: Eivor
en: Audun, it seems you have found the funds to go ahead with the feast after all. You must be elated.

speaker: Audun
en: That is putting it lightly! Look at it. I could have not asked for a better turnout. Soon the feast will begin, and these people will be given everything they deserve.

speaker: Eivor
en: We should honor you. I will fetch us some wine.

speaker: Audun
en: N-no I mustn't indulge. The wine is for the people of Jorvik. But when it arrives, do help yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid, a word if I may?

speaker: Faravid
en: Ah, drengr! If it's to join arms with me, the answer is yes. We can use someone like you against the Picts.

speaker: Eivor
en: I may be courted. But I am selective with whom I join. Are you a drinker?

speaker: Faravid
en: Hah. If that is a challenge, I am up for it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very well. I will return with some wine.

speaker: Faravid
en: Wine? Come now, we will do this over ale. That will give us a good measure of who can better fight its lure.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Eivor. Have you uncovered who The Vault is?

speaker: Eivor
en: I believe I have. Each of the council members has given me reason to suspect them. Some more than others.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Who is it you suspect?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hjorr refused to drink the wine when I proposed he help flush out The Vault. What's more, The Needle was collecting silver for The Vault. I think Hjorr was taking this money and funding The Order.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hjorr has been managing Jorvik's money shortage, yet we find silver aplenty on his desk. The same desk concealing the wine.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Gods, no...

speaker: Eivor
en: The town's funds in decline. A treasurer's hand in the coffers. It is all connected. For these reasons, I think Hjorr is The Vault.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: How could I have been such a fool...

speaker: Eivor
en: I need you to focus now, Ljufvina. These people are in danger. I need your help.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think Faravid aligned himself with The Order, and plans to use The Needle's silver to fund his war against the Picts. When I pressed him about a drinking contest, he opposed drinking the wine and insisted on ale.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid's fixation on his war makes him seem innocent, but it is exactly why I suspect him. The Needle was collecting silver for The Vault. A lot of it. Faravid needs silver to feed his men in his war against the Picts. It must be him.

speaker: Eivor
en: For these reasons, I think Faravid is The Vault.

speaker: Eivor
en: As the king, Ricsige has access to all. The coffers. The archives. A bounty of wine. He felt us closing in, knew we would search the archives and tried to implicate Hjorr to throw us off his scent.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ricsige groans about how wrong things are going. The money shortage. The war with the Picts. But Ricsige's problems are his own doing. He funds The Order using Jorvik's coffers and sits back while Hjorr takes the heat. It is the perfect ruse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Audun was the one pushing for the feast from the start. He planned it, which means he would have had access to the wine. And he was helping Abbess Ingeborg collect Christian texts. She turned out to be The Firebrand.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Yes... yes you're right. And the wine?

speaker: Eivor
en: Of all the councilmen, he knew the wine had not yet arrived. When I offered some, he flat out refused, insisting it be saved for the guests.

speaker: Eivor
en: This Yuletide feast was Audun's idea. He planned it, which means he would have had access to the wine. What's more, he was close with Abbess Ingeborg, The Firebrand. I think he was helping her dispose of the Christian texts.

speaker: Eivor
en: For these reasons, I think Audun is The Vault.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not yet. I will return shortly with my decision.

speaker: Audun
en: Brothers, sisters. Dear friends. Welcome all. Before we begin, I would like to introduce our honored guests. Here with me are some of Jorvik's most revered lords. Men and women who have kept Jorvik trudging through these harsh times.

speaker: Audun
en: I am pleased to say that today, on the day we honor Yule, we honor as well the nobles to whom we are all so indebted.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The wine! Audun is The Vault!

speaker: Eivor
en: Too late for them. We must not miss our chance.

speaker: Audun
en: Join me now in celebrating their successes, and yours. To everything you deserve and more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shit.

speaker: Audun
en: And now, deafened and blinded by your lust for indulgence, your foolish pride, I will tell you just what nobility is. A death sentence! A new world of order is upon us! A pity none of you will live to see it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Get the councilmen to safety. I will handle Audun. Go!

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Protect the king!

speaker: Audun
en: There is no escape. No future for people like you. The hierarchy will be reformed. Kill anyone who tries to escape!

speaker: Eivor
en: Audun! Save these breaths. They will be your last.

speaker: Eivor
en: What did you hope to gain with all this? What riches are worth so much misery, and the deaths of honorable men and women?

speaker: Audun
en: Only a feeble mind would call them honorable. They are privileged. Sedentary. Complacent. They wasted their resources. I secured our power through wealth. I contributed to the future of a glorious order!

speaker: Eivor
en: On the backs of honest people! Merchants and priests and nobles alike.

speaker: Audun
en: Eivor... you are wrong. Held back by your primitive cosmology. Nine worlds in the tree? No! Nine times nine thousand worlds. And as many suns!

speaker: Odin
en: I hung , sacrificing myself to myself. So does the Wise One seek wisdom.

speaker: Audun
en: Countless spheres, awaiting our gift, our enlightenment!

speaker: Eivor
en: I live in one world only.

speaker: Eivor
en: You live in none.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hjorr, Ljufvina. Where did they go?

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you alright?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: We're fine. Faravid and his karls escorted King Ricsige back to the Royal Hall. Everyone is safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's regroup there.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Audun. That sniveling little shit!

speaker: Faravid
en: Conspiring right under our noses.

speaker: Ricsige
en: I don't care! I want answers!

speaker: Eivor
en: Calm, Lord Ricsige. Audun is dead.

speaker: Ricsige
en: That doesn't calm me. I wanted to rip out the bastard's spine out myself. You want to calm me? Start talking.

speaker: Eivor
en: Audun aligned himself to a secret group that was plotting to overtake Jorvik.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: He had help from two others. Grigorii, the dockmaster, and Ingeborg, the abbess.

speaker: Ricsige
en: And you, Eivor. You were after these conspirators from the moment you arrived?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, though I could not let it be known. This group can reach any person, permeate the walls of any city. Much like the worms of a spoiled apple, they would eaten Jorvik from the inside out if we let them.

speaker: Faravid
en: But you stopped that from happening. We owe you a debt of gratitude. You can be sure Halfdan Jarl will hear of this.

speaker: Ricsige
en: If the threat is gone, then you have my gratitude as well. I'm alive today, and so are many others because of you. I would like to name you an Honorary High Reeve of Jorvik, Eivor. Would you accept?

speaker: Eivor
en: It has a nice sound to it. You honor me, lord.

speaker: Ricsige
en: You have earned it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then, if I may, a hoard of silver is left unaccounted for in the grottos beneath these streets.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: That's right. Silver the dockmaster was collecting.

speaker: Ricsige
en: What do you propose we do with it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hardworking merchants were robbed of their wares. Honor Yuletide by giving the silver back to the honest citizens of Jorvik.

speaker: Hjorr
en: A wise suggestion. I agree.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Fine. I will see to it that Hjorr distributes the silver evenly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Without resources, Halfdan's army will perish against the Picts. I say we fund the war. Give Halfdan's men what they need to turn the tide. Future Danes and Saxons will thank us for it.

speaker: Faravid
en: You will hear no argument from me.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Then it will be done. Hjorr will see that your army gets what they need.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Come, Faravid, help me secure this hoard. I could use a bloody walk.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: We have a saying in Bjarmia. "Only the dead get to complain."

speaker: Eivor
en: And we're still living.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I could muster a few complaints about the king and the treasury, but I shall forbear. You did it, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: We did. It may be we were the recipe to keep Norway from Harald all along.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: We still can be.

speaker: Eivor
en: No. Norway is behind me now, and the rest of England ahead. That said, I must be going.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Wait!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this a bitter farewell?

speaker: Hjorr
en: Let it be said that I do wish you had more trust in me. But no. There are no ill feelings here. You did what you had to do. If it were me, I do not know that I could have been as level-headed. You remain a friend, Eivor. Let that be clear.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Should you ever need us, we will come.

speaker: Eivor
en: One last thing. The silver on your desk, Hjorr. It planted a seed of doubt in my mind, so I must know. What is it for?

speaker: Hjorr
en: I suppose I can forego the element of surprise. I hired a silversmith to craft a love token for Ljufvina. A Yuletide gift.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: You sneak.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will take my leave before you shame the throne.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Until our paths cross again, old friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: In this world or the next.

speaker: Hjorr
en: If you drop by Jorvik again, please join us for an ale. I know of a place down the street.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now it seems the wind calls me back to Randvi. Best tell her the good news.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tewdwr's bodyguard. Killed by knife.

speaker: Eivor
en: This pot has been broken, and it's covered in blood. A weapon, maybe?

speaker: Eivor
en: Blood. Could be Tewdwr's if he was the heavy thing being dragged.

speaker: Eivor
en: Muddy footprints. Someone was hiding back here.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: This guard's throat has been cut!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Open up! Tewdwr?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: What's happened here? Open this door!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Come out of there!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gwilim's pouch. I wonder if it still has his little "something stronger." But why is it here? Better hold onto it.

speaker: Eivor
en: So. What does this lead to? The murderers hid here, lying in wait while we approached outside. They jumped from the shadows to kill the bodyguards. And to disable Tewdwr. Then they dragged him away. That accounts for everything... ...except Gwilim's pouch of herbs.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm still unbalanced by Gwilim's special something. Maybe Mother Modron will know the contents?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: There she is!

speaker: Cynon
en: What is the meaning of this? Blood soaking our soil, and your weapon coated in the same?

speaker: Eivor
en: Cynon, please, more has happened here than you can see. Give me a right to parley my innocence.

speaker: Cynon
en: I should have heeded Tewdwr's misgivings about the heathen party guests. And now he has paid with his life. With Tewdwr gone, Glowecestre will be without an ealdorman. Eye for an eye, your Raven Clan will lose their chieftain.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Get the murderer!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hands tacky with old blood from the new king. It would be best to lie low.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Terrible business. Poor lad.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I came as soon as I heard. Tewdwr is missing?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Murdered! By those visiting Danes no less. It's true what they say, soulless killers the lot of them!

speaker: Eivor
en: There is Modron, up ahead.

speaker: Modron
en: Hello again.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Mother, it's the friend of the mangled-leg man!

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor. You remember.

speaker: Modron
en: Indeed. It's a surprise to see you. Is everything quite all right?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, it is not. I awoke in Tewdwr's wrecked home. Blood, but no body. Cynon's men are after me for the lad's murder.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Oh-oh! Did you stab him? Mother, can I see?

speaker: Modron
en: Blood, but no body? We must see what has happened to him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Last night, I made merry in a most foolish way.

speaker: Modron
en: O? The gossip mill has not ground its wheat this way yet. What you do need?

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you recognize the contents of this pouch?

speaker: Modron
en: A very unusual blend. There is a druid who uses this mix to aid sleep.

speaker: Eivor
en: A monk called Gwilim poured some of it into my drink last night. The effects were intense.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: Search the houses! Can't have gotten far!

speaker: Modron
en: They're coming for you. If they know I've aided you, it'll be my head next.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you

speaker: Modron
en: I've seen nothing, and no one.

speaker: Modron
en: Damn Christ-sons, what is it they want now? They make this place unlivable for pagans.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Mother, if the stranger wants more of the herbs, they can talk to the Druid Halewyn?

speaker: Modron
en: Yes! Halewyn's cabin is on a lake near where the Cearrwell and Great Ouse rivers meet. But he's a strange fish. Rarely does he speak to mortals, preferring the company of spirits. Now, I've business at Rollendritch. Find me there later.

speaker: Eivor
en: That must be the home of the druid.

speaker: Eivor
en: The fellow's land is peopled by men of straw.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Mortals be gone. I'm summoning a spirit of the woods. I'll speak to no one else!

speaker: Eivor
en: Just as Modron said. Maybe I should disguise myself?

speaker: Halewyn
en: If you be mortal, I will not speak to you. I am waiting for the spirit, they come, they come.

speaker: Eivor
en: He may not speak to Eivor, but perhaps he will speak to the spirit of the Mari Lwyd.

speaker: Halewyn
en: O spirit, you have finally come! Days ago, a passing cloud foretold your arrival with drops of sun-scented rain. But what form of being are you beneath this guise of horse and bone? From the realm of the fae? I know you cannot say. I press no more.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Whatever you be, now you are here the ritual may begin! But the men of straw must announce you with sparks! Ignite the sky to begin anew, here at the death of the season. Until then, I await you, giving thanks in the glen.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halewyn said that the wicker men must announce me with fire... Perhaps I should set them ablaze.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Ah! A wicker man speaks! Now let them speak in chorus!

speaker: Halewyn
en: Yes, another joins the throng.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Another!

speaker: Halewyn
en: Let there be cacophony! One more, one more.

speaker: Halewyn
en: They roar! Do you hear them? A chorus of fire!

speaker: Eivor
en: That should be the last one! Back to the druid.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Whatever you are, the spirits of straw have burst into flames as herald of your arrival. Come... come this way.

speaker: Eivor
en: This symbol is one I have seen carved into shields and headstones.

speaker: Eivor
en: This dagger is upside-down.

speaker: Eivor
en: A hangman's noose. A knife. And the vials smells of poison. Three ways to kill someone?

speaker: Eivor
en: Their mouths are open, like they've been screaming secrets.

speaker: Eivor
en: Two ladles carved from a single branch. The grooves match.

speaker: Eivor
en: The statue of a woman, Sabrina, watches me from the water below.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Speak to me, O wind!

speaker: Eivor
en: I have come to ask you a single question.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Something about your demeanor and your physical manifestation now gives me pause. Are you truly a spirit of light?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am a spirit as any other.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Then prove it. You must know the depths of the world's mysteries before I will help you. Tell me the proper use of charms.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very well. Ask your riddles.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Which charms protects from evil spirits?

speaker: Eivor
en: The symbol of the Celtic Knot wards off harm.

speaker: Halewyn
en: A secure knot indeed. Only one of light need not fear it.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Tell me, O being of air and light. Which is the charm you would use to leave the past behind?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Athame Dagger cuts our ties with the past.

speaker: Halewyn
en: The upturned blade! Things can be reversed! You know this charm.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Which charm is it that gives speech to the dead?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Skull Souls charm summons voices from death's realm.

speaker: Halewyn
en: In such fashion, I speak to druids long dead. But of course you, a spirit, would know that.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Which charm summons aids for maidens?

speaker: Eivor
en: Maidens in peril are protected by Sabrina of the Severn.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Sabrina the water nymph! Yes.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Which is the charm that weds souls?

speaker: Eivor
en: The charm of the Double Spoon.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Yes! Such that a wedded pair can sup broth together.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Man and woman are made of earth, of water and wind. Which charm clods the earth, dries the water, and stills the wind?

speaker: Eivor
en: Threefold Death stops life's wind, returns a body to earth, and renders water into poison.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Threefold Death is the charm!

speaker: Eivor
en: Give me a measure of time.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Are you a spirit of darkness? If it be not so, come back and try anew.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are these things he's asking me? There must be trinkets around his house that will help.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Speak to me, O wind!

speaker: Halewyn
en: Have you found yourself? If you are a spirit of light, answer me this...

speaker: Halewyn
en: You are a spirit of light! Mabon be praised. Would you like some bread and cream?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, just the answer to a question. This herb-pouch made its way to Glowecestre in the hands of a strange man. Do you know it?

speaker: Halewyn
en: Aye. A mix to help him sleep. I filled this very pouch. And over a dandelion wine, he spoke fondly of his home, Cudd Lladron.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cudd Lladron? Very well. I thank you, Halewyn, but this spirit has others to visit this harvest moon.

speaker: Halewyn
en: Go with the wind and leaves, good friend of the hills!

speaker: Eivor
en: Cudd Lladron. Strange name. Meanwhile, Modron awaits me at the stones nearby.

speaker: Havi
en: This must be the place.

speaker: Havi
en: Muspels were here. I can still smell their stench in the air.

speaker: Havi
en: Now, where shall I point this one?

speaker: Inscription
en: One door opens when Sol blazes her path across the sky, the other when her pale brother peeks out from the darkness that follows.

speaker: Havi
en: This may have to match one of the doors.

speaker: Havi
en: That did something.

speaker: Havi
en: Strange place. Reeks of death... I wonder what secrets I will uncover here.

speaker: Havi
en: Drag marks... and blood was shed. But only a small amount... Were the victims still alive?

speaker: Havi
en: Only Muspels leave ashen footprints like these. One set larger than the rest.

speaker: Havi
en: Sigrun and Halstein... Whoever did this... I will see that there is a price to pay. The wounds in their chest... identical, and cauterized. I've seen nothing like it. It's... unnatural.

speaker: Havi
en: Whoever was here made it a point to occupy this space.

speaker: Havi
en: More elven symbols. Whatever was in this wall sat undisturbed for many ages. Until now. Eysa sought to enter this vault and unlock its secrets. But before she could do so, someone beat her to it.

speaker: Havi
en: That being led a group of Muspels here. Sigrun and Halstein were likely prisoners among them. Injured but very much alive. The dwarves were taken to the center of this chamber where it appears that some sort of ritual was prepared. The orchestrator came for the ancient elven object built into the wall. Possibly even used it in the ritual... Is that what led to the dwarves' deaths? The Muspels then left, taking the object with them. But the purpose of this ritual of their remains a mystery to me.

speaker: Havi
en: That sigil... I think I glimpsed it before in Eitri while I searched for Baldr. Perhaps I will find some answers there.

speaker: Havi
en: I have seen the sigil from the vault around here before. Find it, and I may find the culprit. Amid all this... excitement, I have had little time to dwell on Ragnarök. When will the storm break? Tomorrow? Or far in the future... I think the latter more likely. I have Loki imprisoned for whatever role he has played in Baldr's predicament... His son too is bound by my chains. And what of Surtr? The prophecies say he must play a part in Ragnarök... But for now, he is merely the abductor of my child, not the bringer of the twilight. Still... once Baldr is safe, I will return to Asgard and raise an army. Muspelheim must be conquered. Without mercy.

speaker: Havi
en: A key maybe? Or a part of one.

speaker: Havi
en: Another key? Are there more?

speaker: Havi
en: A third key. Looks as though it may be complete.

speaker: Havi
en: Well, well... Whoever helmed the ritual at the vault was once here.

speaker: Havi
en: Writings on the ritual... They are performed at night. There is emphasis on something called a "Salakar." My elven is rusty... "Vessel of souls," I think. Is this the object from the vault?

speaker: Havi
en: The culprit was deciphering elven runes... Something about the binding of only the most powerful hugrs...

speaker: Havi
en: The culprit searches for a Jotun and a Muspel subject to complete their work. Muspels killing Muspels...

speaker: Havi
en: A letter from Sinmara... There's much secrecy about the culprit's affairs. Only she and Surtr are aware.

speaker: Havi
en: The vault is marked here, along with a second location. Another ritual site, perhaps?

speaker: Havi
en: You're light on your feet, Eysa. Following me now?

speaker: Eysa
en: You've become quite useful, Aesir. My gratitude, for opening the vault. Now, tell me, what happened there?

speaker: Havi
en: I'm following the stink as it rises. As are you. Care to tell me why that is?

speaker: Eysa
en: Days ago, Sinmara ordered my best warriors to the vault without bothering to inform me. I've not heard from them since.

speaker: Havi
en: Well, you're casting your suspicions at the right people. Whose quarters are these?

speaker: Eysa
en: His name is Calder. An adept in magic. Or "seidr," as you Asgardians sometimes call it. This place is where practices it.

speaker: Havi
en: Whatever he's doing it, it is not seidr. At least not as I know it. He is using something called a Salakar. It is part of a deadly ritual. And from what this room tells me, the dead will continue to pile up. Dwarves. Jotnar. Muspels.

speaker: Eysa
en: I don't know what you're talking about.

speaker: Havi
en: You wouldn't. Your stepmother despises and distrust you. Your father only the latter of those. For now. But in time, thanks to her venomous whispers, he may come to hate you as much as she does.

speaker: Eysa
en: This is a lie. All of it. Your twisted attempt to pit me against them.

speaker: Havi
en: Sift through the mess yourself. No other truth lies within.

speaker: Eysa
en: Where are you going?

speaker: Havi
en: After the Salakar. Whatever it is, your father needs it. It may be the only leverage I have to get my son back.

speaker: Havi
en: Calder marked a place on a map surrounded by waters just northeast. If he's planning another ritual there, I may be able to understand what this Salakar holds.

speaker: Havi
en: Calder may be nearby. This roof should give me a clear view.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: Lord Calder, with your permission we will now return to Eysa.

speaker: Calder
en: Soon. I have need for you still.

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa's warriors. Where do they fit into all this?

speaker: Calder
en: You are one of her captains, yes?

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: A duty I share with two others here.

speaker: Calder
en: I thought I saw something in you. Stout. Resolute. Step over here.

speaker: Havi
en: Sigrun and Halstein were two of the most revered Sons of Ivaldi. If such prestige is a requirement for these rituals, then Calder is surely luring that Muspel to his death. I wonder if there's a way I can observe the ritual up close.

speaker: Havi
en: I need to approach Calder without him taking notice. Perhaps the best way is with deception...

speaker: Calder
en: Come! Join me, chosen ones! Together, we will enact Surtr's will! Who among you will hold that distinct honor? Let us see...

speaker: Calder
en: Steady. In service to Surtr we have nothing to fear.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 2
en: What are you going to do with that?

speaker: Calder
en: I will just have to try another.

speaker: Calder
en: Hold your head high, warrior, and the Salakar will welcome you in.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 3
en: Let it bring me the greatest honor.

speaker: Calder
en: Weak.

speaker: Calder
en: A fierce hugr burns within. Will you offer it to Surtr?

speaker: Muspel Warrior 4
en: If this is what I must give...

speaker: Calder
en: What a waste.

speaker: Calder
en: Your Lord thanks you... for all that you will give.

speaker: Calder
en: Worthless.

speaker: Calder
en: An unparalleled honor.

speaker: Calder
en: Unsuitable. Each and every one... I will return at nightfall with new subjects.

speaker: Havi
en: Calder has left, but without successfully claiming a hugr. He may try his hand another night. As will I.

speaker: Calder
en: Kill the intruder!

speaker: Havi
en: Damn.

speaker: Calder
en: You!

speaker: Havi
en: No! Mind the Salakar!

speaker: Eysa
en: Let me kill him!

speaker: Calder
en: Kill them!

speaker: Havi
en: Calder fled north-west, with Eysa snapping at his heels. They can't have made it far.

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa chased after Calder like a rabid hound. Though he is no helpless rabbit... What signs might I find of this pursuit?

speaker: First Suitor
en: I'll be the one to find it. Just you wait and see.

speaker: Bil
en: It must be around here somewhere.

speaker: Bil
en: I think there are some spots you missed!

speaker: Eivor
en: What are these men hunting for?

speaker: Bil
en: My comb. Whoever finds it wins an evening of my company. Care to join them?

speaker: Second Suitor
en: I think I found the comb! Wait... this is a jawbone.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think this is yours.

speaker: Bil
en: Halt in your search! A winner, and my comb has been found. Now, the prize for finding my comb is some of my time. A walk in nature, maybe more if that is where our conversation takes us.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see. Lead on.

speaker: Bil
en: You are different than the kind my flights of fancy attract. Burdened, decorated, and... delicate.

speaker: Eivor
en: Delicate?

speaker: Bil
en: The others, they are like clubs. Blunt and ungainly, you are nimble, like a knife.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you so in need of suitors that any passing woodsman or vikingr will do?

speaker: Bil
en: I was married once. My Alfi died five winters back. Ours was a perfect marriage. I do not need another. But, am I to go the rest of my days without love or attention? I think not.

speaker: Eivor
en: And the comb?

speaker: Bil
en: Could be a comb, could be a brooch, or an arm ring. So long as it's lost and to be found by a helping hand

speaker: Eivor
en: Any good tales come of this?

speaker: Bil
en: Once I thought the same man had stumbled across me three times... gave me a fright. Turned out to be triplets.

speaker: Eivor
en: If this comb is worth nothing to you, what shall I do with it?

speaker: Bil
en: You could keep it. Comb your hair. Or, I could comb it if you like.

speaker: Eivor
en: Comb my hair? Is that why those men scrambled over each other?

speaker: Bil
en: I could do more than comb your hair, find all your knots and snags and tame them... if you'd like.

speaker: Eivor
en: My shoulders are tense, and my hair is a tangle. I could use a softer touch for these kinks.

speaker: Bil
en: Then let me.

speaker: Bil
en: Hm-hm. Delicate touch, indelicate voice. This was fun, Eivor. Hold on to the comb, as a keepsake.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Bil. You tamed some knots I haven't been able to reach myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you for the offer, but I cannot. Here, your comb.

speaker: Bil
en: You keep it. It was a reward for my champion. Farewell.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to find all of the shards and place them before I can open that door.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be one of the shards I need to place on the pedestal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's impossible, Aletheia. I know you want me to work with her but I know, I know. But what more can I do? She won't trust me...

speaker: Eivor
en: Is Kassandra... talking to herself? She is truly mad. Good riddance.

speaker: Old Woman
en: You there! Could you kindly step into this pool so I might complete my ritual for the fairies?

speaker: Old Woman
en: Oh, yes. Could you please be a dear and wade into the Fairy Pool so I can sacrifice you to the fairies?

speaker: Eivor
en: You're asking if you can kill me?

speaker: Old Woman
en: Since the nightmares started, the fairies have whispered in my ear, promising power if I find sacrifices for them. They've even led me to one of their treasures for my hard work. The prettiest shard. So please, into the pool now.

speaker: Eivor
en: What if I stay out of the pool and buy that pretty shard from you instead?

speaker: Old Woman
en: Oh... The fairies won't be pleased. But my daughter is getting married soon and I'd love to get her a wedding gift. All right. The shard is yours. Run along now.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you want me to go swimming, you're going to have to make me.

speaker: Old Woman
en: That's no trouble at all, dear. I'll help you right in.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fairies are tricky creatures. Are you sure that shard isn't muddling your mind?

speaker: Old Woman
en: I haven't quite felt like myself lately... You could be on to something. Take this shard far away from me, please!

speaker: Eivor
en: One step closer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Footprints. Walking at a hastening pace.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's all the shards. Time to unlock the temple and end the nightmares. And Kassandra thought I needed her help.

speaker: Flann
en: God has heard my prayers.

speaker: Eivor
en: You flatter me, lord, but what's wrong? Where's Bárid?

speaker: Ciara
en: He's not returned, nor the two messengers sent after him.

speaker: Flann
en: This cannot be simple misfortune. It hints at some dark design.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me go after him, lord. If he lives, I will find him.

speaker: Flann
en: Even with your cunning and guile, you would not go unchallenged. Not without a Kings' Pass, and few Vikings have those.

speaker: Ciara
en: I'd wager a few from Donegal do.

speaker: Eivor
en: Donegal? A Norse settlement?

speaker: Ciara
en: A port, on the western shore. A fair bit of their trade finds it way to Aileach, so someone there is bound to have a pass.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this port well-guarded?

speaker: Ciara
en: It's crawling with Norsemen grown lazy on success. They'd not expect someone to go Viking on them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. I'll go to Donegal now and get one of these passes... with your leave, lord.

speaker: Flann
en: If it means fewer lives lost, you have my blessing.

speaker: Eivor
en: If there are any Kings' Passes to be had, I may well find one here.

speaker: Eivor
en: This should get me through Aileach's gates.

speaker: Eivor
en: An impressive fortress. One cannot help but wonder what's within. Now to see how they treat someone with a Kings' Pass.

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: What business have you here?

speaker: Eivor
en: The business of kings. Here is my pass.

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: Go on, then.

speaker: King Niall
en: Who are you to come before the Kings of Aileach unannounced?

speaker: Bárid
en: Fergal?

speaker: Bárid
en: You're not Fergal. I don't know you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am... Sturm of Donegal. Who is Fergal?

speaker: King Domnall
en: The King of Dublin speaks of a cousin who advised us for a time.

speaker: King Niall
en: A glorified goat herder who should have taken our advice. So, Sturm, what brings a Viking from Donegal here?

speaker: Eivor
en: You tell me. I came at your invitation.

speaker: King Domnall
en: There is some mistake. I sent no such message.

speaker: King Niall
en: It wasn't me. It could've been you-know-who. But he hates Vikings.

speaker: King Domnall
en: Forgive my brother's bluntness. We will get to the root of this, I assure you. Can I offer you a drink?

speaker: Bárid
en: Yes! More drink! I haven't seen the bottom of my cup since I got here. If I wasn't a trusting man, I'd say they're trying to keep me drunk.

speaker: Eivor
en: No drink for me. I'll return when you have finished your... kings' business.

speaker: Bárid
en: If it's not drink you're wanting, you should take a tour of the ringfort. It's... it's renowned throughout all the land.

speaker: King Domnall
en: As we've told you several times, King Bárid, the Ringfort of Aileach is not open to guests.

speaker: King Niall
en: In fact, you could even say that it's closed for a select few.

speaker: Bárid
en: Ah... so, you're keeping prisoners there?

speaker: King Domnall
en: O have a drink, you two! Do ya think I haven't taken a few hostages myself?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll seek out a place to rest until you remember why I was summoned here.

speaker: King Domnall
en: Of course, of course, your pass will grant you free run of this place.

speaker: Bárid
en: If you see Fergal, say hello for me!

speaker: King Niall
en: For the last time, Bárid, the ringfort is off limits!

speaker: Eivor
en: If I read Bárid right, freeing Fergal could be the key to liberating Aileach. And to do that, I need to get inside that fort.

speaker: Eivor
en: My pass won't get me into that ringfort. I'll need to find another way.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll need a key for this.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope this is the right key.

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: Hey! You're Eivor, right? You serve King Bárid. We were meant to check on the king and report back, but soldiers grabbed us and threw us in here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll let you out. Return to King Flann, if you can.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is there someone here named Fergal?

speaker: Fergal
en: I am he. Who wants to know, Viking?

speaker: Bárid
en: I serve Bárid mac Ímair and King Flann Sinna. They offer you freedom.

speaker: Bárid
en: Join us, cousin! We've been having a grand old time, the kings and I.

speaker: King Domnall
en: It's the who've turned this place into a prison. He's taking hostages from all the families. To control all of Ireland!

speaker: King Niall
en: Shut your gab, Domnall! Eogan will kill you if you talk too much.

speaker: King Domnall
en: And Flann will kill us if we don't.

speaker: King Niall
en: It's like Domnall said, it was Eogan! He told us to delay whoever came until...

speaker: Bárid
en: Until what?

speaker: King Domnall
en: Until the abbot can move his forces in.

speaker: Eivor
en: How many men? How many?

speaker: King Domnall
en: We don't know, no one does. He has some companies at Armagh, more men than he lets on. That's all I know!

speaker: Bárid
en: Left to my cousin, you'd both be puddles of blood and gut, but King Flann might spare your heads.

speaker: Bárid
en: You'll be treated as hostages, not prisoners, until your king decides what to do with you. Now, think on your sins.

speaker: Bárid
en: It'll be easier in the end to let them keep their crowns, but they don't need to know that yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Flann must learn of this trap.

speaker: Bárid
en: I've already sent messengers to pull his army back. I wasn't going to sit on my arse, waiting for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm impressed.

speaker: Bárid
en: Don't be. It took days of drinking that swill before Niall finally grew bored and careless.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've outdone yourself. I'll be sure to let the king know who the real hero was today.

speaker: Bárid
en: Thanks to you, cousin. Make sure that message reached Flann and I'll join you all later. May Sol and Mani guide ye!

speaker: Winfrith
en: I said to take care! Did I not say to take care?

speaker: Eivor
en: Winfrith, Bertham. You look dour for festival-goers.

speaker: Winfrith
en: I'm not dour, I'm furious! My fool of a son released the cattle we were raising for the feast! Just let them go!

speaker: Eivor
