en: You let them go? Why?

speaker: Bertham
en: Would you believe it's because I am a lone wolf who says "damn the rules"?

speaker: Bertham
en: Would you believe I took them to the river for one last graze but one of the cows looked at me strangely and I got scared?

speaker: Eivor
en: That I believe. Do you want me to get them back for you?

speaker: Winfrith
en: Take Bertham with you. Perhaps you can protect him from the terrifying cattle. Go on, love. Go with Eivor.

speaker: Bertham
en: Very well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where were you when the cow frightened you?

speaker: Bertham
en: Across the river. That-a-way. I'm not generally afraid of cattle, but the look in this one's eyes! I thought it might hurt me! They're big cows!

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps this is an opportunity to overcome that fear you claim not to possess.

speaker: Bertham
en: This is where it happened. They shouldn't be too far.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Let's begin tracking.

speaker: Eivor
en: Look there, Bertham. Another cow, and your first lesson.

speaker: Bertham
en: All right. Show me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, learn to wield the bow. Arrow rests on the string, pull it back, breathe ... aim ... and release.

speaker: Bertham
en: You make a challenging thing sound simple.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand this is daunting. Even domesticated creatures possess a worthy strength. And so, even in slaughtering and eating them, we must show the respect. I do not begrudge you your fear.

speaker: Bertham
en: Thank you. I begrudge myself quite a bit. I feel quite foolish.

speaker: Bertham
en: I hope you aren't too annoyed that you need to look after me today. And clean up my mess.

speaker: Eivor
en: If anything, this is more relaxing a day than I have enjoyed in recent memory.

speaker: Bertham
en: O! O! There! I see the last one!

speaker: Eivor
en: Well done. You are now a tracker. Perhaps that can be your role. You track, Mayda shoots.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bertham!

speaker: Bertham
en: O my goodness. Did you see that, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: It took me a moment to believe it! Fine work, Cow-Fearer. You have overcome your enemy.

speaker: Bertham
en: Please don't make that my new nickname.

speaker: Bertham
en: Thank you, Eivor. This part is tougher than I thought! Mayda won't believe I've done this. Nor will my mother.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bertham, were you really scared by a cow? That seems unlikely for a farmer's boy.

speaker: Bertham
en: Well ... if I tell you what really happened, will you tell anyone?

speaker: Eivor
en: Never.

speaker: Bertham
en: It's ... it's to do with Mayda. She's always saying I'm so soft and sweet and kind and lovely.

speaker: Eivor
en: All good things.

speaker: Bertham
en: It's terrible. Who wants sweetness? I want to be brave and manly. I thought if I let the animals go, I could hunt them myself and show her I was a good provider, and strong. Then I took out my bow, and the cow did look at me ... and I did get frightened. So that part isn't entirely false

speaker: Eivor
en: There is nothing wrong with having a good heart. I'm sure Mayda is fond of you because you're a kind young man, not in spite of it.

speaker: Bertham
en: Thank you, Eivor. I hope you're right... But all the same, I do intend to brag, just a little.

speaker: Bertham
en: I feared asking this of Mayda, but ... do you ever feel sorry for the creatures? That you must hurt them so?

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not seek yo cause them suffering. I aim for the heart, that it might be a quick death.

speaker: Bertham
en: Can't imagine being so skilled. Mayda is much the same way. One shot, rabbit dead. Clean.

speaker: Winfrith
en: Bertham. Did you manage not to hurt yourself?

speaker: Eivor
en: Winfrith. I give you your son, Bertham the Beast-Slayer.

speaker: Winfrith
en: The Beast-Slayer!

speaker: Bertham
en: You should have seen me out there, Mother. I was a terror with an arrow! But I should go!

speaker: Winfrith
en: Go? Where?

speaker: Bertham
en: I want to show Mayda while the blood is still fresh! See you at the feast!

speaker: Winfrith
en: Well, Eivor. Thank you. Whatever you did out there, I'm pleased for it.

speaker: Hilda
en: A fishmonger can't sell week-old fish. Where's that husband of yours? Off fishing again?

speaker: Vera
en: So he says, but the only thing he ever catches is more gambling debts. I fear I cannot keep him around.

speaker: Hilda
en: Bah! You're better off without that wastrel.

speaker: Vera
en: My husband should be back by now. The poor lug worries me so.

speaker: Hilda
en: He fishes along Scarborough shore, beneath the tower ruins, does he not? That's foolish, the cliffs are too steep.

speaker: Eivor
en: One who has need of their wits wanders wide... I might find good fishing below the Scarborough cliffs.

speaker: Eivor
en: Crushed to death. An unlucky way to die. Doubt he felt much.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Did you hear that sound after I pushed the rock?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: That fisherman was asking for it. He should have paid his dues when we asked for them.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Yeah, to Hell with his sad Pickering love story and his homely fish-stall wife.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: That reminds me, remember to go down and get that ring, eh?

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you the wife of the man who fishes below the cliff?

speaker: Vera
en: My husband fishes there, yes, and I run the stall. Do you fancy some fine, fresh fish?

speaker: Eivor
en: I found your husband.

speaker: Vera
en: And where is that fool? Drunk in some bed? Working off a debt?

speaker: Eivor
en: Dead, I fear. Some bandits crushed him with a rock, hoping to fleece him.

speaker: Vera
en: No! Wh-why... that sweet fool, leaving me penniless...

speaker: Eivor
en: Here, take this ring. I found it on his body. It is rightfully yours.

speaker: Vera
en: His mother's ring! That fool, that damned, soft, loving fool. Thank you stranger. At least I have this.

speaker: Eivor
en: The bandits made off with all that he had.

speaker: Vera
en: That worthless man! Even in death, he leaves me penniless! The useless pig!

speaker: Vera
en: Marry, they said. Marriage has left me naught but a poor widow with nary a fish to sell. That lovesick fool... I warned him to stay away from the cliffs.

speaker: Gunborg
en: Who goes there?

speaker: Havi
en: I am Havi. Lord of Asgard.

speaker: Gunborg
en: You...? You're a long way from home. Or are the Aesir now invading us as well, jailer of Ivaldi?

speaker: Havi
en: Ivaldi owes me his freedom. Where is he? I would speak with him.

speaker: Gunborg
en: Be my guest. I assume you know the way to Helheim?

speaker: Havi
en: He's... he's dead? How?

speaker: Gunborg
en: How else? Or do you need both eyes to see the Muspels everywhere?

speaker: Gunborg
en: That was uncalled for, I... Walk with me.

speaker: Gunborg
en: I am Gunborg. Leader of this shelter. Or, what remains of it, now Ivaldi is gone. He was trying to make contact with the other shelters. There was an ambush. Glod's soldiers. And ... something else. Something worse. A creature of fire and fury. It ... it devoured Ivaldi whole.

speaker: Havi
en: No doubt bred in Surtr's dungeons. Perhaps with Loki's aid, before I could make him my captive.

speaker: Gunborg
en: You and your captives. Regardless, Uldar fell soon after Ivaldi did. Our mines, and miners ... any survivors now serve Glod.

speaker: Havi
en: Is that name meant to mean anything to me?

speaker: Gunborg
en: Glod is Surtr's bastard sson. Half-Muspel, half-Jotun. A nightmarish being, capable of tearing a dwarf in two.

speaker: Havi
en: An unthinkable end for anyone, whether warrior or otherwise.

speaker: Gunborg
en: I saw it with my own eyes. I still see it when I try to sleep.

speaker: Havi
en: Your people will have vengeance.

speaker: Gunborg
en: No. The people of Uldar are finished.

speaker: Havi
en: It takes little effort to do so.

speaker: Gunborg
en: You mock my kind? I saw it with my own eyes. I still see it when I try to sleep.

speaker: Havi
en: I ... spoke out of turn.

speaker: Havi
en: And yet ... Glod has not simply slaughtered your people. He needs your miners. To what end?

speaker: Gunborg
en: The invaders hunger for secrets buried deep in the ground. Ancient relics. The Muspels place great importance in them.

speaker: Havi
en: And how do you know this?

speaker: Gunborg
en: Enough, Havi. We have suffered enough. Now I must endure all these questions?

speaker: Havi
en: Aid me with your knowledge, and I shall strike a blow against Glod, and all Muspels.

speaker: Gunborg
en: In Uldar, we had someone gathering information for us. The miner, Fritjof. He's been silent for days now, which is unlike him. Probably dead, for all I know.

speaker: Havi
en: Anything sought by the Muspels must be mine. Where was Fritjof last seen? Perhaps I can find him.

speaker: Gunborg
en: There is a house in Uldar, its owners killed by Muspels long ago. There, we would exchange messages with him.

speaker: Havi
en: This house ... how do I find it?

speaker: Gunborg
en: It's the tallest house in the Jeweler's District, by the city's south gate. Just ... look for the gold in the streets. You'll see.

speaker: Havi
en: Fritjof may be the key to obtaining these relics Surtr seeks. I must find him.

speaker: Gunborg
en: Do as you must, Lord of Asgard. I have too many burdens of my own to worry about yours as well.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: We fight for the warrior besides us, nothing else. Not gold, not glory.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: True. Battle pours out its strong red wine, and we are drunkards.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Bloodlust and battle-drunk. It is the only time I am alive.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Hush, do not fret, my faithful friend. It is a great honor to be sacrificed as Odin's steed. Today you die, but tomorrow you run free in the green fields of Asgard.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: They say Halfdan Ragnarsson is the strongest of Ragnar's sons.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Strong he is. Once, he took an arrow in the shoulder. He tore it out and shot it right back. He hit that Saxon through the eye of his helm at three hundred paces. A true tale.

speaker: Eivor
en: You. Where are Sigfred and Toka?

speaker: Goll
en: Ah. Battle must be near. The crow has come for the feast.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a clever tongue, friend, but tomorrow we all speak in a language older than words.

speaker: Goll
en: Fate already knows who lives and who dies.

speaker: Eivor
en: Again I ask. Where are the others?

speaker: Goll
en: Fetching more catapults for tomorrow's attack. You can wait.

speaker: Eivor
en: I shall wait. Somewhere else.

speaker: Eivor
en: Far from home, before another city of strangers. When did our lives become a , Sýnin? Yes. I know the day. The very day when Mother and Father died. Count Odo will not hear reason, Charles plays games. I cannot trust the lives of my people with such men. The queen now, she I could trust, but she lacks power. My place is here. With Sigfred and Toka, come what may.

speaker: Toka
en: Eivor, you return. That means all is ready and we cannot turn back now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why do you worry? You'll collect more swords.

speaker: Toka
en: I know how to fight other warriors on the field of battle. This is a city. There will be flames.

speaker: Eivor
en: It matters not. Tomorrow we will fight as warriors, not ruthless killers. This I swear, upon my honor.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Ah, Eivor the Talker. And to whom have you so freely given your word about how my battle goes?

speaker: Eivor
en: I said it, the gods heard it. That is enough.

speaker: Sigfred
en: And if I say we burn this city to ashes and feed the crows with children, what say you?

speaker: Eivor
en: If you truly would say such a thing, who am I to heed your words? But I thought you a better man than this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I would say, mind who is first to feed the ravens, lest it be yourself.

speaker: Toka
en: Eivor does not mean these words.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Quiet, Toka. Let the Talker speak. Come, Eivor. Tell me again how I shall feed the crows.

speaker: Eivor
en: My steel will speak for me tomorrow, to my foes. I have no quarrel with you. Yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Say what you like, Sigfred, but we are free thegns, all of us. You are not our jarl nor our king.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Good. Good! Keep that fire burning through the night. It shall kindle our vengeance at the break of dawn.

speaker: Toka
en: Time to go lie on my furs. How do you do that, Eivor? Sleep before a battle, I mean?

speaker: Eivor
en: Easy. I remember my mother's murder, each moment. Second, I recall every word the All-Father ever said to me. And finally, I think upon this war-filled world, and of the next, the hall of endless wonder. Only then do I rest.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Today, warriors, we shall take that city, and sack it, and burn it to the ground. And tonight, friends, we shall feast in Odo's palace... or in Odin's hall, with the choosers of the slain! Now is the time of honor. The hour of our glory.

speaker: Sigfred
en: The day of vengeance!

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Shields!

speaker: Gozlin
en: Who is the King of Glory? The Lord is strong and mighty in battle.

speaker: Gozlin
en: He trains my hands for war, so that my arms may hold this cross of gold. I shall not yield.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Brave Sif, bring the gift of victory. Odin, lend me your helm of awe. Vidar, feed my need for vengeance. O Vanir, O Aesir, crush these walls!

speaker: Ebels
en: I am the gates of Paris!

speaker: Ebels
en: Die for me, heathen coward!

speaker: Ebels
en: No, coward! Fight fair!

speaker: Sigfred
en: The gates! The gates have fallen! The city is ours! Spare no one!

speaker: Toka
en: By Sif and Týr, the day is ours!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fate favors the brave. Now what, Sigfred?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Rush the palace gates! We will bring the whole place crashing down on Odo's skull.

speaker: Dani
en: Welcome, Wanderer, to the home of Dani the Dead One. To my shame, I can't offer better hospitality. My enemy got here first.

speaker: Havi
en: I am not that wanderer. I am but a simple traveler–

speaker: Dani
en: Ha! Save it, Havi. I get around. At least, I used to before Durf took over my foundry, locked up my men and cut down my ropes.

speaker: Havi
en: Ropes?

speaker: Dani
en: When I ran the foundry, I had rope-lines strung all over Døkkerland. That's how I moved parts so quickly, see? Ropes!

speaker: Havi
en: Sounds like quite an operation, like you were building an army.

speaker: Dani
en: I could supply a hundred armies! But what does that matter now that Durf and his paid Muspels have taken everything?

speaker: Havi
en: Are any of those rope-lines of yours still usable?

speaker: Dani
en: Not many... but if someone were to free my men, we could string them back up. Get you across Døkkerland in no time.

speaker: Havi
en: Seems like a reasonable bargain. Where are your men imprisoned?

speaker: Dani
en: Locked inside the foundry. There are two sets of keys, each carried by a Muspel.

speaker: Havi
en: So, if I retrieve the keys from the Muspels and free your men, you will repair the rope-lines?

speaker: Dani
en: If you free my crew, I'll take back the foundry, and, by , we'll tie more knots than the Nornir.

speaker: Havi
en: The Muspels here hold the keys to Dani's dwarves.

speaker: Havi
en: Those must be Dani's dwarves in the cages.

speaker: Havi
en: Something tells me that's the last of them. We'll see if Dani the Dead One makes good on his bargain.

speaker: Havi
en: Dani has wasted no time building himself back up. I should remind him of our bargain.

speaker: Havi
en: Congratulations on your prosperity, Dead One. I take it Durf is no longer a problem.

speaker: Dani
en: Ha, I had him tossed in the lava. It won't kill him for long, but it'll be a slow, painful road back.

speaker: Havi
en: Speaking of roads, you promised to ease my passage once your position was restored.

speaker: Dani
en: Ah, did I? That sounds like the old me. A weak pathetic creature alone in a crumbling home... Dani the Dead One, Foreman of Hel's Foundry, Rigger of Rope-lines, will not be bound by promises!

speaker: Dani
en: I could use a warrior like you!

speaker: Havi
en: You have used me from the start!

speaker: Havi
en: Give me a reason not to toss you in the lava.

speaker: Dani
en: I needed to make sure it was you and not some imposter riding your reputation. Some people have no honor down there!

speaker: Havi
en: I have no time to dirty my hands further. You will make good on your bargain or, by Durinn's beard–

speaker: Dani
en: Of course, of course! And so there's no hard feelings. I'll have my workers do double-shifts at half pay.

speaker: Havi
en: You do not need to do that.

speaker: Dani
en: I know, but I can't let them think I've gone soft.

speaker: Dani
en: The rope-lines are yours to enjoy. Swing by anytime!

speaker: Gill
en: O Starlight, my Starlight. A swift death by a sharp sting separates up, both by lip and by heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Whether by land or by sea, we never shall part.

speaker: Gill
en: A fellow romantic soul. Perhaps you might be able to aid my plight.

speaker: Eivor
en: What ails you?

speaker: Gill
en: A witch told me that one sting from the fuzzy little demon would steal my breath! But! My love keeps bees!

speaker: Eivor
en: You cannot deliver your love letter because there are bees in the way? I could carry it for you.

speaker: Gill
en: If you would do this kindness for Gill, then you must be a kindred spirit. Do you also enjoy the stamen AND the petal?

speaker: Eivor
en: I enjoy much of many things.

speaker: Gill
en: I had a feeling you would understand! I've painted my love in words in this letter. Let your romantic heart guide you.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I find this love of yours, I will deliver your feelings. I am sure your words will lead me to your heart's desire.

speaker: Gill
en: Thank you! O, thank you, stranger! I shall call you Sunshine, for you broke through the clouds of my loneliness.

speaker: Eivor
en: The sweetness of honey on the tongue, with the danger of being stung. It is like love. Always a chance of losing.

speaker: Gill
en: O Starlight, my Starlight. A swift death by a sharp sting separates up, both by lip and by heart. Have you given my letter to my beekeeping love? The hive is not far!

speaker: Eivor
en: Starlight, Starlight. Which of these keepers of the bees fits Gill's poems?

speaker: Eivor
en: Would you say that your hair could be described as "bracken colored tresses"?

speaker: Serle
en: I beg your pardon?

speaker: Eivor
en: It matters not, return to your work.

speaker: Eivor
en: Would you say that you are cow-eyed and willow-limbed?

speaker: Mille
en: O-o! I suppose! I'm not sure what that means, but it is pretty. Are you composing a poem in my likeness?

speaker: Eivor
en: My mistake. Apologies.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you consider yourself a man who had features so delicate that God himself must have painted them on with a fine brush?

speaker: Warin
en: Yes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Forgive my intrusion.

speaker: Serle
en: You've returned. Did you forget something?

speaker: Eivor
en: An admirer of yours asked me to deliver a letter.

speaker: Serle
en: I know these words. I've kept the brothers of this letter beneath my pillow. To finally meet my Secret Bard... I must go.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have delivered the letter. Now to see if Gill has met his match.

speaker: Serle
en: I've kept your letters under my pillow to give me dreams as sweet as your words. Now I know, my love is sweet as apples.

speaker: Gill
en: My Starlight, it's as if my heart is to burst with this happiness. My love requited.

speaker: Serle
en: Now tell me more of my lashes and how they are like the...

speaker: Gill
en: Your lashes! Why they're beautiful, but they are a candle in the brilliance of your hands. So warm and strong in mine...

speaker: Eivor
en: Good for you, Gill. Best of luck to you both.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hello again.

speaker: Mille
en: The wandering poet! Hullo again!

speaker: Eivor
en: Not me, but an admirer who prefers to remain secret until you two can meet. I have a letter with more details.

speaker: Mille
en: O, goodness! Many thanks. I cannot wait to meet my admirer!

speaker: Eivor
en: I have delivered the letter. Now to see if Gill has met his match.

speaker: Mille
en: Ew! Gill! This had better be in jest! Because if you are writing me love letters, that is vile, and I am telling Mother!

speaker: Gill
en: Millie! Stop! The letter wasn't for you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sorry, Gill, looks like you will have to face your love yourself. Best of luck.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hello again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I have a letter for you.

speaker: Warin
en: Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have delivered the letter. Now to see if Gill has met his match.

speaker: Gill
en: W-Well, hello. This is quite the surprise.

speaker: Warin
en: You've got a beautiful heart and a mastery of verse. But, I do not return your feelings, Gill. But, Serle fancies you. I understand if you do not want his company. He isn't very handsome.

speaker: Gill
en: He does? The lad with the hair of bracken and smoldering gaze? Serle, you say? I must compose another letter!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sorry, Gill, looks like you will have to face your love yourself. Best of luck.

speaker: Havi
en: Builder!

speaker: The Builder
en: Ah! Your timing is perfect!

speaker: The Builder
en: We found the perfect spot! Did you bring the water?

speaker: Havi
en: As promised.

speaker: The Builder
en: Wonderful. As it blends with my paint, its magic will power the runes of protection that I here inscribe.

speaker: Havi
en: No rune will protect you from my wrath if I catch you playing games.

speaker: The Builder
en: A perfect mix!

speaker: Havi
en: Wait! What are you doing?

speaker: The Builder
en: Harnessing hugr (mind) magic to bind my spirit to these enchantments. It amplifies the strength.

speaker: Havi
en: Hugr magic? You learned this from the Jotnar?

speaker: The Builder
en: They practice a form of hugr magic, but this is my own technique. And it's just... about... done. Could you lend a hand and bring me a few jars of paint? As many as you can.

speaker: The Builder
en: Be careful with that jar, it's fragile. Easy... Remember, just place it, don't break it.

speaker: The Builder
en: Do take care. We can replace the paint, but the time to prepare it is lost.

speaker: The Builder
en: That's well enough. Exactly the right spot.

speaker: Havi
en: What now, Builder?

speaker: The Builder
en: Perhaps you should move out of the way, atop that rock? The view will be much better.

speaker: The Builder
en: Well done. You've smashed all my jars. Now, take a break and climb up on that rock.

speaker: Havi
en: There. Will that do?

speaker: The Builder
en: It will indeed! Hold... hold...

speaker: The Builder
en: ...And there it is! A thing of beauty!

speaker: Havi
en: The runes you painted conjured this shield?

speaker: The Builder
en: They did. And if all goes well, it will protect your allies and roast your enemies.

speaker: Havi
en: Show me.

speaker: The Builder
en: With pleasure. Draw some invaders out from the woods and into the shield. Alive, of course. They must be alive.

speaker: Havi
en: The barrier will not harm me as I cross?

speaker: The Builder
en: You have my word, Havi.

speaker: Havi
en: Over here, you stinking shits! Skulking about like cowards!

speaker: Havi
en: Am I so fearsome that you hide like mice in a farmer's field?

speaker: The Builder
en: That's good! Draw them closer!

speaker: The Builder
en: Yes, yes! It works!

speaker: Havi
en: Look at that! Like moths to a flame!

speaker: Havi
en: Come, you fatherless curs! I am one, and you are many. What have you got to lose?

speaker: Havi
en: The fools. They run towards their doom.

speaker: Havi
en: Builder! Is your shield supposed to flicker like that?

speaker: The Builder
en: The shield is unstable!

speaker: Havi
en: Your shield is failing, Builder! They're passing through!

speaker: The Builder
en: I don't understand! They should be dead! Hold them off while I try to restore it!

speaker: Havi
en: Ah! It burns!

speaker: The Builder
en: Come back inside while you still can!

speaker: Havi
en: What now, Builder? Your shield has failed.

speaker: The Builder
en: No! Not at all! I just need to make some adjustments.

speaker: Havi
en: Builder, your shield summons an army, but it is as weak as your word.

speaker: Havi
en: This is not what you promised!

speaker: The Builder
en: Never mind that now! They're coming from all sides!

speaker: Havi
en: I should have let Loki have his way with you.

speaker: Havi
en: You need to fix this now!

speaker: The Builder
en: I'm painting as fast as I can!

speaker: The Builder
en: I almost have it!

speaker: The Builder
en: Well, that was not as smooth as I had hoped, but the means can be forgiven when the end bears fruit.

speaker: Havi
en: A sour fruit, not as sweet as you promised.

speaker: The Builder
en: It held! The shield worked wonders.

speaker: Havi
en: It worked well enough. Impressive but unstable.

speaker: The Builder
en: Don't fear, my friend. The problem is no more. I have mixed the proper solution. With enough materials and the right incentive, I pledge to build a tower so tall, it would shield all of Asgard.

speaker: Havi
en: Materials we can find, that's no issue. What incentive do you mean?

speaker: Havi
en: Your coming here was no accident, was it? You desired Freyja well before you arrived.

speaker: The Builder
en: If I had announced my desire from the start, you would have hurled me back through that portal. But my offer is honest, and my magic is real. For a wife and a queen, I will give you the means to protect your kind.

speaker: Havi
en: You name an impossible price, Builder. Is that your trick? Aim high to land somewhere in the center?

speaker: The Builder
en: I don't haggle like a common fishmonger, Havi. I desire Freyja, with all my heart. So ask yourself... is one marriage a fair exchange for the salvation of Asgard and its people?

speaker: Havi
en: Why the Queen of Asgard? Is it you intent to rule at her side?

speaker: The Builder
en: Nothing so bold! I would be happy to simply bask in her beauty. She can govern the realm however she sees fit.

speaker: Havi
en: Freyja is not mine to barter like a bale of wheat. I will ask her what she desires.

speaker: The Builder
en: Do what you must, but my price stands firm. No Freyja, no shield. I have no other needs.

speaker: Havi
en: And you have no other friends. So tread lightly here.

speaker: Proppa
en: I am sorry, Son, for our wretched, stank-infested house!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hej, child. Your home is cursed with shit?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: I wish I could laugh but... I cannot. Yes! That rank odor is from the Devil! The Devil who produced me with his prick! O, that smell! He dips his arrows in cow dung and never washes... says it brings him luck. We're doomed to choke in Father's shit-house! The cow dung he keeps is in those crates. It has mutated into the most unholy of pungent monsters. O! O! Yes! Once free of those disgusting dung-crates, the house will be clean again.

speaker: Proppa
en: Be careful in there, stranger! The smell could kill you!

speaker: Proppa
en: These berries are the only thing keeping me alive in the face of such a vile smell.

speaker: Proppa
en: Wonderful, the house is habitable again!

speaker: Eivor
en: The stink from those crates is gone, but in my experience, if you do not cure the source, shit returns.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: My father. Degolas. He's a famous archer, but he never washes. Never. I'm going to confront him. That pox. Mother, I'm going to get Father back. I've had enough, change is in the air. Literally!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Father! The war is over! Our home is clean! You can stop stinking up the earth! Take a bath!

speaker: Degolas
en: I will, one day, get down, but my heroic odor will persist! It is what gives me my special powers! God told me.

speaker: Degolas
en: O! My mud-coat... Ah! I am soaked! Ugh! Water! I hate water! My coating is gone. My layer of sacred warrior shit has run off.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Mother, you won't believe it! Father has been cleansed. We can live without the toxic clouds he once produced.

speaker: Proppa
en: Thank the good Lord! Baptized again, my beautiful Degolas! My love, you are finally clean, our home also. Come here my love, I can see your skin again!

speaker: Eivor
en: How does it feel to be clean again, Degolas?

speaker: Degolas
en: This clean feeling is strange to me. I was happy as a degenerate mud-ball. I never worried about these vain ventures.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your desires are not always those of your gods, your family, and your... well, those you lie with.

speaker: Degolas
en: I feel I've sold my warrior self. The grim inspired my bow. My shit-arrows would strike fear into my foe's... nose.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well I'm certain your arrows will still fly true, you did not lose your archer's skill.

speaker: Degolas
en: Only time will tell. Be well, stranger.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Loki Rabbit! I call on you, nay, demand of you: Send me a ' champion to test my might!

speaker: Norse Man
en: I am waiting to fight your champion, Loki Rabbit! Send them forth to meet me in the square!

speaker: Norse Man
en: Is this the champion you've conjured for the holmgang, Loki Rabbit? Looks like a fine fighter to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: A warrior I am, but I have nothing to do with a rabbit.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Your champion comes crawling back, Loki Rabbit! Good! I am ready.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Aye, I've been ready. I am ready! Fists up!

speaker: Eivor
en: Yield.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Aye! And what did Loki Rabbit promise you, champion? Wealth? Fame? Honor?

speaker: Eivor
en: The rabbit said nothing. A lesson you should learn.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are you off to, "Loki?"

speaker: Norse Man
en: We will crown a new champion today! Me! Loki! Your champion has fallen! Reward me! Where is Loki Rabbit? He's... he's gone!

speaker: Eivor
en: Guise is a trickster's trade. That man will forever play the fool.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why are you praying here?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: We pray for strength to face the one within that cave. A devil in man's form who commands the beasts themselves. Many times we have seen him feeding the wild beasts and speaking with them. Even the wolves do not savage him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sure? You Christians are quick to name "Devil" that which you do not understand.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: The birds in this wood are restless and swift to attack. Only yesterday a fox snatched a baby from its crib. Have no doubt, He Who Walks Backwards is among us. Either he will come out of there, or we will go in.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Have a care, stranger! Do not speak to him! Your immortal soul is in peril!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this the lair of a man or a beast?

speaker: Eivor
en: You keep company with a bear. Are you as the monk says?

speaker: Beastmaster
en: The animals be my friends. I hear 'em, and they hear me. They hurt this one. Now they want to hurt me.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you have set your beasts on people before?

speaker: Beastmaster
en: Thems that hurt my friends get hurt. But I never hurt no baby.

speaker: Eivor
en: In Cent, I came across a man besieged by the animals of the forest. He was killed by rats in the end.

speaker: Beastmaster
en: Then he got his due. He snared a she-wolf for her pelt. She were pregnant.

speaker: Eivor
en: How do you know that?

speaker: Beastmaster
en: Just know, that's all.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have only been defending those you love. Stay here and tend to your friend. I will see to the monks outside.

speaker: Beastmaster
en: Don't kill them. Don't want that. Scare 'em off. It's the animals they fear, remember?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Have you slain him? Or has the Devil's tongue swayed you?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Another who commands the beasts! The Devil's spawn is among us! Flee!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll put the fear of nature's claws into these superstitious fools.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not know if you are what they say you are, but I have seen to your tormentors. As you said, it is the animals they fear. Now they think there are two devils in the woods.

speaker: Beastmaster
en: Ha! That'll keep 'em away. You are beast-friend. Eawynn likes you. Bye-bye.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not know if you are what they say you are, but I have seen to your tormentors. I laid about them with my blade.

speaker: Beastmaster
en: Blood brings blood. More will come. Things worse now. Eawynn and I better go somewhere else.

speaker: Eivor
en: I did what I could. Farewell, then, and good fortune.

speaker: Eivor
en: A beast's life is not worth a person. You are a murderer. The monk is right to call you Devil.

speaker: Beastmaster
en: You're the same as all the others! Get 'im, Eawynn!

speaker: Eivor
en: No more will fall prey to the beasts you command.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your devil is slain.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: God be praised! Then we can go home at last. Take this as a sign of our gratitude.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Are you going to enter the water or not?

speaker: Norse Man
en: No! The waters are too cold! But... the quicker I am baptized, the bigger business will be.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: One does not receive the Holy Spirit under the watchful eye of God simply to improve trade!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: That man needs a push. Or a good scare.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: A moment in frozen water is a minor bit of suffering for a lifetime serving the Great Father! Do! It!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: One cannot become one of God's children without going through the proper ritual!

speaker: Norse Man
en: No! I have avoided the water for weeks, and I do not intend to freeze this Yule!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: No wonder the people avoid your market stall. You positively reek.

speaker: Norse Man
en: I have a delicate body! The cold will take the life out of me!

speaker: Norse Man
en: Ah!

speaker: Eivor
en: There you go.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Cold, cold! The ice waves are taking me, save... Hey, this is not so bad.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Good God, at last! I hearby baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit within us all! You are now... a child of God!

speaker: Norse Man
en: So, is this it?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: It is. Go forth and walk His holy steps, new child!

speaker: Norse Man
en: If his steps go to the market, then so be it. But first... I could go for a nice swim.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Thank you for getting that man into the water. We had been waiting for too long! But we are patient. Anyone keen on the teachings of our Lord is welcome. Perhaps...?

speaker: Eivor
en: No.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have done enough.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Come one, come all! Norse and Saxons alike! Newly blessed food, made and touched with our Lord's holy grace!

speaker: Havi
en: Hearken you to the tale of my deadly duel with two of the most feared warriors of Muspelheim. And so victory was mine, as it ever shall be.

speaker: Azar
en: Ah, Eivor, a welcome vision for my eye. Ah, my business partner. Why hello, Eivor. Ah! A visit from my good friend.

speaker: Azar
en: I always enjoy the dance of trade. Care to indulge in profitable commerce? New contracts, new riches. Many kingdoms desire to trade for our goods.

speaker: Azar
en: Perhaps that's enough. Enough for today? We'll close the books on that. Very well.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it you do here again? Can you remind me what you do here? Tell me about what you do here.

speaker: Azar
en: I trade our trade post resources. Foreign lands can provide us with rare exotic goods.

speaker: Azar
en: Always a pleasure. Farewell, Eivor. Another time. I look forward to your return.

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar. I'm curious to know how you came to Ireland.

speaker: Azar
en: It is not an altogether happy story. I was once the most powerful trader in Shiraz. Then I was betrayed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. That is hard fortune.

speaker: Azar
en: By my partner.

speaker: Eivor
en: Worse still. A knife to the back is a wound that never heals.

speaker: Azar
en: Konstantinos was a friend of my father's. One whose greed devoured my family and empire. But now I am here, where I am surrounded by new friends.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are pleased you found us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar, we are good friends now.

speaker: Azar
en: Ah! Let me guess. You wonder how I lost my eye.

speaker: Eivor
en: Such a loss is a badge of honor among the Norse.

speaker: Azar
en: Not for me. I told you of my partner, Konstantinos. Betrayal was not enough for him. In his fury to take all I had, his men beat me, left me for dead. They slew my family. I survived, but not in one piece.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sorry. I did not mean to bring up a painful past.

speaker: Azar
en: You are my friend. It is best you know.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Hmm, such exquisite fletchings. Fitting feathers for a king-slaying. These arrows are very lovely, very lovely indeed...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Touch not that throne. It was blessed by a priest, as were the arrows.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: How dare you touch those sacred arrows! You've desecrated a martyr's place! Halt, stranger! Show me those arrows.

speaker: Eivor
en: These are just arrows, plain and simple.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why are you so passionate about these arrows?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: When Father James blessed the late King Edmund, he blessed that holy throne and all upon it.

speaker: Eivor
en: The blessing did not take.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: That depends on your opinion of King Edmund. I wonder... I have studied those arrows, but never dared touch them. But since you plucked them anyway, would you sell them to me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm willing to sell, but the King Edmund arrows might be mixed up with my own.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: I've the eye of an archivist, able to sort new from old. The kingdom's history shall be restored. Just sell them all to me.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: These arrows are the very same that pierced good Saint Edmund. I must study these holy relics! Thank you!

speaker: Eivor
en: If you are as they say, then I will keep them. They may prove of use later.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: I would pay heavy coin for them. I'm a sage, a chronicler of histories. Return to me if you desire riches.

speaker: Eivor
en: Still looking to buy arrows?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: More so now than ever.

speaker: Eivor
en: Alwin. You mentioned something about an egg hunt?

speaker: Alwin
en: I did indeed! But it will be much more than a simple search for eggs. This will require a sound mind and a keen eye.

speaker: Eivor
en: This seems like an activity for children.

speaker: Alwin
en: It is! That's why I made it extra challenging. I had Alvis write the clues as riddles and made sure to hide the eggs in difficult-to-find areas. Here is your first clue to start the hunt.

speaker: Eivor
en: This should be the last one.

speaker: Alwin
en: And how goes the hunt?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have found many, but only you will know if I've found them all.

speaker: Alwin
en: Fair enough. Show me your eggs.

speaker: Alwin
en: You have indeed found them all! You see, Eivor? Sometimes it's as important to test your logic and perception, just as much as your skill with a blade.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Fenton! Fenton! Jesus Christ! Fenton! There are wolves in that forest! Come here, your cursed sheep! You'll make yourself a wolves' dinner. I'm calling you! Fenton! Here boy!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Fenton! I'm not following you into that forest, you woolly sack of mange! Fenton? Fenton...! Jesus Christ! Fenton...! Will anyone help? I think he went off to the north somewhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: That sounds like a sheep, and not a happy one.

speaker: Eivor
en: That sheep will be torn apart if I do not do something.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you Fenton? Your master is calling you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe it will come if I whistle?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this sheep lost? I wonder if it belongs to someone nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will it follow if I whistle?

speaker: Eivor
en: It works! The sheep follows my whistle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep up, will you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Come on, let's get you home. You do want to be home, don't you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Lucky I came along when I did. I don't much like wolves, either.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: There you are, Fenton! You've escaped for the last time, you walking mutton chop!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Hold still, you woolly git!

speaker: Eivor
en: I went through all that just so you could kill that poor beast?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: A man like me can ill afford to slaughter a sheep for vittles, but the ealdorman demanded it, and I must obey.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Between you and me, I've been dying to murder this bastard for ages. Fenton was a royal pain in my arse. Still, you did me a good turn, stranger. Take some meat for your help. The ealdorman won't miss it.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's mutton stew for me tonight. Farewell.

speaker: Severn Champion
en: We'll cut you down where you stand, filthy heathens!

speaker: Eivor
en: Grendel must have tracked this mold here, but from where? The trail leads southwest.

speaker: Eivor
en: More mold. I am on the right path.

speaker: Eivor
en: The source of the mold must be near.

speaker: Eivor
en: The mold trail leads into this pit.

speaker: Eivor
en: The reek. Ugh.

speaker: Eivor
en: This woman speaks of her child, Grendel. A cruel fate the gods have woven.

speaker: Eivor
en: My head swims with fever dreams. What. Just. Happened.

speaker: Mother
en: Grendel? Grendel! Is that you? Answer me!

speaker: Eivor
en: A key! So fitting, yet what use is a key with no lock?

speaker: Eivor
en: Mold, just mold. Sending visions, like a seer's brew.

speaker: Mother
en: You! You smell like my son. My son's blood! Where is he? Where is my boy?

speaker: Mother
en: His blood is on your hands, you monster! You killed my child, my only child! My sweet precious boy!

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't make me do this!

speaker: Eivor
en: What wickedness is this?

speaker: Eivor
en: You. The woman from the farm. You lied about the Danes.

speaker: Mother
en: To protect my boy. He never meant to hurt anyone. But the others, they could not see. He kept growing in body, but not in mind. He was my boy. My sweet little Grendel.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wulfhilda must know the truth of this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Abbess.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Eivor, you live yet! Pray, tell all.

speaker: Eivor
en: I slew a monster that was but a man. Then I tracked his mother and killed her too.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: His mother!

speaker: Eivor
en: She struck at me in the dark, and I defended myself. But it was no hero's deed.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Those poor souls. I shall pray for them tonight at Barking Abbey.

speaker: Eivor
en: Leaving already?

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: I must. The bishop is eager for a full accounting of the Beast of East Anglia.

speaker: Eivor
en: Leave my name out of your tale. It is nothing to be remembered for.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Understood. Perhaps it would work better as a song. I dabbled in verse as a youth. It may be time to lift the pen again. But what story shall I write? The full truth of this thing may be hard to fathom.

speaker: Eivor
en: Give them a comforting one... about heroes and monsters. For the truth, the bone-cold truth of everything, is often hard to take. It cuts like a cruel north wind on the neck.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: God saves us all, Eivor. I take my leave now, but will write you once my poem is complete. Farewell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, and farewell to you, too, Wulfhilda. Make it a good tale.

speaker: Eivor
en: An inspiring tale, far more fitting than that terrible day. At least she changed my name. And she got a dragon in. Always with the dragons.

speaker: Havi
en: Where is everyone?

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: A wolf should be peeled not pampered. It would make a fine coat.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: I'll wager Týr is raising that wolf so he can fight it!

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: He took the wolf as a trophy. That's the story I heard.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Go see Týr's new pet. You'll soil your britches!

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: Where did he find that beast?

speaker: Havi
en: Is that the same wolf as before? How did it grow so fast?

speaker: Týr
en: Witness the Wolf from the Well!

speaker: Týr
en: Look at the size of this beautiful creature! Impressive, isn't it?

speaker: Loki
en: Clear eyes, strong haunches. It must come from powerful stock.

speaker: Havi
en: You fools, it could swallow the moon next month if it continues to grow like this.

speaker: Týr
en: I know your mind, Havi, but this wolf is not your enemy. The signs of Ragnarök, when it comes, will be clear for all to see.

speaker: Havi
en: Týr, you roll bones in a game you do not understand.

speaker: Týr
en: That may be, but I'll assume the risk. If there's a price to be paid, I'll pay it.

speaker: Loki
en: It's the Jötnar that trouble us now. Have you spoken with the Builder?

speaker: Havi
en: The Builder, yes... Is Freyja nearby?

speaker: Týr
en: She's teaching Thor about organizing armies. A battle they're both losing.

speaker: Havi
en: Come along then. You must all hear what I have to say.

speaker: Týr
en: You spoke with the Builder? You saw his work?

speaker: Havi
en: I did.

speaker: Loki
en: And the sacred water, was it put to use?

speaker: Havi
en: It was.

speaker: Loki
en: Your tongue is shorter than your temper today, Havi.

speaker: Havi
en: Indeed.

speaker: Freyja
en: These markings are your warriors. Now, here we have the four corners of the sky held up by Austri, Vestri, Nordri, Sudri...

speaker: Thor
en: Enough of this sorcery, woman! Just point me towards the enemy, and I will handle them!

speaker: Freyja
en: Havi, you look troubled.

speaker: Havi
en: The Builder gave me a demonstration of his magic. He conjured a shield that killed invaders on contact.

speaker: Týr
en: That would do well for us!

speaker: Freyja
en: But your expression says otherwise.

speaker: Havi
en: I fear the price is too high.

speaker: Freyja
en: What does he want?

speaker: Havi
en: You.

speaker: Freyja
en: Me?

speaker: Thor
en: Does he take us for slavers? I will smash his skull 'til he shits out brains!

speaker: Týr
en: Now, hold on. Everyone. Let's weigh the

speaker: Freyja
en: Do not finish that thought.

speaker: Freyja
en: What was your reply?

speaker: Havi
en: I told him it was your choice alone.

speaker: Freyja
en: You didn't refuse him outright?

speaker: Havi
en: I evaded his question to gain us time. Time to devise a better idea.

speaker: Freyja
en: One that does not involve selling off your queen, I trust.

speaker: Havi
en: The safety of Asgard is more important than any one of us.

speaker: Freyja
en: Is that why you've been off alone, hunting wolves and fretting about your future?

speaker: Havi
en: For good reason. If the Builder believes he has a chance, he will continue his labors.

speaker: Freyja
en: A dog will not keep working for the mere promise of a bone.

speaker: Thor
en: How about I beat on his liver 'til he builds us a wall for free!

speaker: Týr
en: Might we consider

speaker: Freyja
en: I will not barter with my body!

speaker: Loki
en: That would be a first.

speaker: Thor
en: Hold on, I've got it... the blunt end of my hammer on his family stones!

speaker: Loki
en: You are overthinking this, all of you. Give this Builder an impossible task... a deadline of, say, . When he forfeits, as he no doubt will, Freyja remains free, and we may finish his work as intended.

speaker: Thor
en: He would be mad or stupid to agree!

speaker: Loki
en: You underestimate men of intellect, Lord of Storms. The Builder is a proud man. He won't back down from a challenge.

speaker: Freyja
en: I do not like this.

speaker: Havi
en: Nor do I, but we must act. Loki, bring this offer to the Builder.

speaker: Loki
en: Your will is my deed, Rune-Writer.

speaker: Freyja
en: You grapple with forces outside your control.

speaker: Havi
en: You were eager to see the deal done.

speaker: Týr
en: We're Æsir. She's Vanir.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Watch out! Keep your distance!

speaker: Havi
en: The wolf!

speaker: Havi
en: Shit! Týr! Stand back! I'll get it!

speaker: Norse Man 4
en: Wolf! Wolf...!

speaker: Havi
en: Out of the way! The wolf is mine!

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: The Havi leads the hunt!

speaker: Havi
en: Stand clear! I will catch it!

speaker: Norse Man 5
en: I'll sharpen my axe with your teeth, beast!

speaker: Havi
en: Do not fight the beast! Leave it to me!

speaker: Thor
en: The size of that beast! A worthy hunt!

speaker: Havi
en: The final blow is mine.

speaker: Havi
en: Halt, you well-weaned wolf!

speaker: Havi
en: Are you the wolf foretold? Are you my doom? Are you destined to destroy me?

speaker: Havi
en: I am the Dead Walker! I am the Living Ghost! I cannot die! We will see which is stronger, your fate or my will!

speaker: Havi
en: If I spare your life, will you do the same?

speaker: Havi
en: I warned you well, and look where it has led.

speaker: Loki
en: Havi, stop!

speaker: Loki
en: Stay your axe!

speaker: Havi
en: Out of my way, Loki.

speaker: Loki
en: You swore an oath to never spill my blood!

speaker: Havi
en: Step aside, and I won't have to!

speaker: Loki
en: This is my blood!

speaker: Havi
en: What?

speaker: Loki
en: He is my son!

speaker: Havi
en: Bastard!

speaker: Havi
en: Týr, you've cared for this wolf. You will be its jailor. Take it to Lyngvi, bind it there. Make sure it never leaves the island.

speaker: Havi
en: I can speak with the dwarf, Ivaldi. May he find a more permanent solution.

speaker: Týr
en: Come, boy. You're safe with me.

speaker: Loki
en: Be kind, Justice-Bringer.

speaker: Havi
en: Loki... there will be a reckoning.

speaker: Loki
en: Of this, I have no doubt.

speaker: Havi
en: The skies darken like an ill omen. My impossible task grows more urgent.

speaker: Journal
en: It's terrible! It's the worst event to happen in the days of mankind! The Gleemen have broken their bonds of friendship and composition. I heard that it was all the fault of that wicked Ostrydd! She made her way qmong their numbers and turned Cynewulf and Ysane upon each other like wild dogs. I can only drown myself in woe and hope for more blessed music-filled days.

speaker: Tattle Rag
en: Ja, Word is that Cynewulf ran afoul of the guards and now croons from his cell. Someone thought they saw Kitt, but it was just some nun taking alms for the church. Ysane's still playing venues near Lundenwic. Critics have been saying her new stuff is mushy rubbish.

speaker: Cynewulf
en: Truth! Truth and love have been shackled by these dogs of the regime! Justice will be served and my tale will be told! Ysane? Kitt? Anyone?

speaker: Eivor
en: You disagree with the terms of your captivity?

speaker: Cynewulf
en: If love be a crime, then yes I do! For I am only guilty of sych a boon! Me, Cynewulf of the Gleemen!

speaker: Eivor
en: I see. And whose wife did you bed?

speaker: Cynewulf
en: O, the guard captain's. And the alewife, Lugg. And Ysane's muse. But, who am I to deny women my company?

speaker: Eivor
en: A scoundrel and a poor friend.

speaker: Cynewulf
en: That may be so! But, this scoundrel will play naught but the sweetest music for his freedom. You understand? I, Cynewulf, have been freed from my bondage and am eternally in your debt.

speaker: Eivor
en: Make good use of your freedom then. Apologize to your friends, and stay out of trouble.

speaker: Kitt
en: God is good! God's love lingers. God has saved me from broken fingers!

speaker: Eivor
en: I have never seen a nun play such an instrument.

speaker: Kitt
en: I learned the tagelharpa from church. I used it for coin, turned away from God to a life of sin. The Gleemen we were called, the finest bards in all of Lunden. Our music moved statues to tears. But no more. The Lord demanded I return to the fold. I begged Ysane to join me, but she still toils with devil and drink. Music and dice have led her astray, she and that ... Cynewulf. All my financial woes stem from their greedy shenanigans.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have debts, you mean. Large enough to send you into hiding.

speaker: Kitt
en: How dare you imply that I hide behind my cloth from men who would break my instruments for a mere fifty silver!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fifty silver, I can cover. But for that sum I want to hear The Gleemen perform together, one last time.

speaker: Kitt
en: O, you are temptation-wrapped redemption, stranger. I have missed the dice dearly. Perhaps God has other plans...

speaker: Ysane
en: O, Ostrydd, my Ostrydd.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is not the first time I've heard a skald sing through tears.

speaker: Ysane
en: It's my beloved Ostrydd! She loves me no more. Thus my quill stays dry, no poetry falling from its once proud beak.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you only write verse when you are in love?

speaker: Ysane
en: Surely! I've not written a ballad about God since I was a girl. Only love moves my heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Some of the best verses I have ever heard were thrown in battles of wit and rhyme, not lovesick crowing.

speaker: Ysane
en: O? I have never seen such a battle, please enlighten me.

speaker: Eivor
en: In our battles, for glory and blood we do sing, and give praise to the high one, for Odin is king. And we beg that the High One will give us his nod, that we someday might dine alongside our War God.

speaker: Ysane
en: Yes, yes, I see the bricks of this verse. Fight... night... brawl... Valhall... No, Odin's hall. Get me my quill!

speaker: Eivor
en: My breakfast was nothing but curds and some whey. 'Tis a bit bland but keeps hunger away.

speaker: Ysane
en: Poetry about food! I quite like that, yes! Gooseberries... make merry? No, no... hm.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should like to hear what music you write. Will you perform it somewhere?

speaker: Ysane
en: If I can get Cynewulf's bastardly face to help me with this meter. But you will have my thanks in this performance regardless.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ysane, Kitt, and Cynewulf. That is all The Gleemen. Now we will see if they play the square.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: I love you, Cynewulf!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Ysane!

speaker: Norse Man
en: This new material doesn't hold a flame to the intensity of Ysane's older work.

speaker: Cynewulf
en: Come one, come all! Friends! Fans! Lovers! You demanded our reunion, and thus, God has gifted our merry trio with just an assembly!

speaker: Ysane
en: With fresh poems bestowed on me by a new muse. One with the heart of a warrior and eyes of frost.

speaker: Kitt
en: An, tu, thrio. (One, two, three.)

speaker: Ysane
en: Hear me, friends and fighters, come one and come all. May we meet up once more inside Odin's Great Hall!

speaker: Ysane
en: For my breakfast there's bread, eggs and lox on my plate! See this bounty I've got? Life in Lunden is great.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tove... trading a needle for an arrow, I see.

speaker: Tove
en: Eivor, can you teach me the art of archery?

speaker: Eivor
en: I would be happy to.

speaker: Eivor
en: See how I'm standing? Plant your feet in the ground, no wider than your shoulders. Breathe in as you draw the arrow back. Look at the point you want to hit. Now imagine the arrow passing straight through it, and far beyond. Breathe out, then release.

speaker: Tove
en: Thank you, Eivor. Now I have something for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: See? All in the eye.

speaker: Tove
en: Thank you, Eivor. As a gift, I could design a new tattoo for you. Something to decorate your scar.

speaker: Eivor
en: A kind offer, but I want this scar visible.

speaker: Tove
en: O, I did not mean to offend. In any case, I do have a tattoo for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gudmund, it appears your ship is like one of Holger's stories. Never quite finished.

speaker: Gudmund
en: Get me some decent wood and I can finish it in a week. But Styrbjorn won't gift me any.

speaker: Eivor
en: There was little plunder from Avaldsnes, but if I come across any, it will be yours.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your Eira is growing fast.

speaker: Gudrun
en: Fast but not big. A little rabbit, that one.

speaker: Eivor
en: Small and quick beats big and slow. I'll start taking her on raids soon.

speaker: Gudrun
en: Would you, please? It would give me a break.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hej Tekla, what is brewing?

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't hurl into the barrel, ok?

speaker: Tekla
en: Think you can match horns with me, hm?

speaker: Eivor
en: Staggering already?

speaker: Eivor
en: Like Odin, mead is my lifeblood.

speaker: Tekla
en: That was well drunk... well done... well... drunk... done.

speaker: Alvis
en: Well, look who it is!

speaker: Eivor
en: Practicing your wordplay, Alvis?

speaker: Alvis
en: Ah, Eivor... the only mouth in Midgard from which I fear mockery.

speaker: Eivor
en: You taught me the art of writing poetry, old friend. It is only natural that I surpass soon.

speaker: Alvis
en: How about another lesson, then? A quick flyt (word battle), right here, right now. What do you say?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's try flyting.

speaker: Alvis
en: I always put a few coins down as a wager. Most of those who enjoy flyting have an equal fondness for betting. But today, we'll abstain. Let me begin.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm ready.

speaker: Alvis
en: In flyting, it's key to match cadence and rhyme! It's as much about sound as it is time. So be careful in choosing the words you say...

speaker: Eivor
en: With your teachings, I'm sure my next challenger I will slay.

speaker: Alvis
en: Hmm, no. The rhyme is good! But too many words upsets the rhythm.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a very fine teacher, I'm sure I'll excel.

speaker: Alvis
en: Interesting... you have the cadence correct. But you failed the rhyme.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll recall what you've taught ere I enter the fray.

speaker: Alvis
en: A fine answer! Perfect rhyme and a lovely cadence to match my line.

speaker: Alvis
en: Now let us examine meaning! Ahem. In flyting, you'll need to be cutting and keen. It's about wielding wit more than venting your spleen. If I tell you you're foolish, and stupid, and dull...

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I'll tell you you've nothing inside of your skull.

speaker: Alvis
en: Ehh! A good response! I called you stupid and you turned it around. Flyting about wit, you matched my meaning. When you think of too many perfect retorts, use the one that best matches the meaning.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I will spit in your face, and I will bash in your skull.

speaker: Alvis
en: Not bad. Not bad. The rhyme is there, the sound is good, but... consider that I said you were silly, and you told me you would kill me. At times, it might be best to... remain on-theme. Something to consider.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I will make a fine goblet from out of your skull.

speaker: Alvis
en: Not bad. Not bad. The rhyme is there, the sound is good, but... consider that I said you were silly, and you told me you would kill me. At times, it might be best to... remain on-theme. Something to consider.

speaker: Alvis
en: Last one... So go then, and conquer the world with your wit! Go be clever, be quick, show your spirit and grit! I look eagerly forward to seeing how you fare...

speaker: Eivor
en: I look forward to becoming far more than you can bear!

speaker: Alvis
en: A good rhyme, but a bad structure. Close. You're close.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will flyt you with flourish and best you with flair!

speaker: Alvis
en: Perfect, yes! You could destroy me with such a line!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will make you regret what you've taught me today!

speaker: Alvis
en: I haven't taught you enough if you think that line works! Where's the rhyme?

speaker: Alvis
en: Your flyting's astounding, you're worthy of praise! You swing a fine axe, and you turn a good phrase!

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Alvis. I'll take the lesson to heart.

speaker: Alvis
en: There's still much for you to learn about flyting, but I'm confident you'll pick it up. Happy to help you learn if you'd like to come back again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps I will. Thank you, Alvis.

speaker: Eivor
en: Svend. Have you designed any new tattoos?

speaker: Svend
en: A few worth looking at.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tove says she is trying out some new tattoos.

speaker: Svend
en: She is. And she is getting better at it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me have a look.

speaker: Svend
en: Go ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hej! Can you point me to some good hunting grounds?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: I could, but I don't want every iron-foot with a bow scaring away the game. Bring me three deer antlers to prove your skills and I might just have a story for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: A worthy challenge. I will see you soon.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Eivor, come to keep your blades sharp? Wolf-Kissed! Welcome back!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar. I have something here you might like to see.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Thunderclap of Thor! Is that your father's axe? I have not seen this beauty since... Well, for some time.

speaker: Gunnar
en: I forged this weapon long ago. Still looks good. One of the finest, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: It has a blunted blade, but it swings well. Can you sharpen it?

speaker: Gunnar
en: I can give it a better edge and reinforce the handle. And as luck would have it, I have one ingot left for the job.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sure?

speaker: Gunnar
en: The Fates have willed it so! But in future, bring your own metal ingots. I cannot forge them from empty air.

speaker: Gunnar
en: That should do it. Anything else?

speaker: Eivor
en: And how are you, Gunnar? Holding up?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Ja, work is good and my spirits are strong, but my nights are newly cold. My lady left me, if you had not heard.

speaker: Eivor
en: I had. Sorry to hear it. You were together... how long?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Ahh... Five weeks it was. Five beautiful, passionate weeks. But all that is done. Will I never find my Brunhilde?

speaker: Eivor
en: Valkyries do not walk the world as they once did, Gunnar. Maybe set your sights a bit lower.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Lower? My friend, look at my wares, my weapons. I'm not a man to settle for less than the finest of anything!

speaker: Eivor
en: That is all for now.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Return anytime!

speaker: Eivor
en: They must be finished now.

speaker: Randvi
en: The king has called for his best mead, so the talks are concluded. It should be safe to enter.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm ready to face the thunder. I will speak with the king now.

speaker: Guthorm the Wise
en: Excellent, King Styrbjorn. I will take this proposal to my nephew. I believe he will see the wisdom in it.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Good. It is all I can hope for. May the

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: May the winds favor your voyage, Guthorm.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Eivor, come forward. And explain in plain words why you willfully disobeyed my commands. Do you mock me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not mock you, king. I mean to embolden you... against your enemies. And your own poor judgment.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: You know nothing of my judgement. You know nothing of my plans and strategies.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd would agree with me.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: My son might agree with you, but he would obey me. He knows his place.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not as well as he knows his father.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Imagine you are harassed by an enemy with warriors that vastly outnumber your own. What profit does open war bring? Would it not be better to work quietly, through diplomacy, gaining alliances? Waiting until the day our numbers outweigh our enemies' and our victory is guaranteed?

speaker: Eivor
en: Do we have any allies to speak of? Or is that your excuse to do nothing?

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Your confidence blinds you to so much in plain sight, Eivor. Day and night I toil to forge ties with clans to the north. Very soon you will see the fruits of my efforts. Only then you will understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kjotve and his clan will never negotiate with us. They speak the language of war, so we must answer back. I have waited a lifetime to take back the honor that Kjotve took from my family. Now is the time to act. My time to act.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Are you so blinded by vengeance that you cannot see beyond your nose?

speaker: Eivor
en: All your talk of diplomacy is cowardice, not strategy. If you do not have the will to finish this fight, only say it.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I will finish it when we are certain to win, Eivor. And that day is fast approaching.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that all?

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I'm at a loss with you Eivor. When I took you in as my own, never did I imagine such disrespect from the child of Varin. Your father was a fine man. Just and loyal to me. He died bravely so that we might live.

speaker: Eivor
en: He died a coward, lord. A fate I will not mirror.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Why do you carry such a useless burden? Let it go. Think only of the days to come. Of your future, and the victories at hand.

speaker: Eivor
en: My honor has been stained. Until it's wiped clean, I want nothing else.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I refuse to pick at that wound again. But if there is something that can chase these shadows from your thoughts

speaker: Randvi
en: Sigurd has come! Down at the docks, his ship is here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Lord King.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Ah. Eivor, you are welcome here.

speaker: Eivor
en: How does it feel to be home?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Not as free of care as you might imagine. It has been many years since I reclaimed my throne, but I have never taken it for granted. Not since my time in the marshes. Since then, I have been busy. Guthrum and I are inching towards common ground. A is forthcoming.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that why you have summoned me? To find common ground?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I hope to. You are one of the great Lords of Mercia. Calling you a friend would be a benefit to all England. What say you to a treaty, Eivor? Naming you Lord of all lands northeast of your settlement.

speaker: Eivor
en: In exchange for what?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Your allegiance. Not to me, but to Christ. And to the Order I have convened in his name.

speaker: Eivor
en: I honor your offer, Lord. And the trust you place in me. So here is my answer.

speaker: Eivor
en: You gave me this years ago. A beautiful piece. But it sits heavier in my pocket than on my heart.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: You refuse, then?

speaker: Eivor
en: Have no fear. This is not a new chapter in our conflict. I am leaving these lands for distant shores. You'll have no more trouble from me.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: In search of new wars? Fresh lands to conquer?

speaker: Eivor
en: In search of myself.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Ah. The most difficult destination on Earth. I wish you well then. God be with you on your journey.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am bit full up with gods at the moment. Yours may have to take another boat...

speaker: Guthrum
en: He faces the rising sun. Good.

speaker: Eivor
en: So the rumors are true. The Great Conqueror has been conquered himself.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Eivor! How many summers has it been?

speaker: Eivor
en: Far too many, friend.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Something amuses you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I hardly recognize you. Is this the Guthrum I left behind, or some other gentler man?

speaker: Guthrum
en: The Guthrum you knew is indeed no more. Aethelstan, I am now called. My Christian name.

speaker: Eivor
en: Christian name?

speaker: Guthrum
en: A new name for a new life.

speaker: Eivor
en: At the expense of all you gained.

speaker: Guthrum
en: I have not lost as much as you might think. King Aelfred and I have a lasting peace, in fact.

speaker: Guthrum
en: He has taken western Mercia. East Anglia is mine. We are now discussing the fates of East Mercia and the North. The Danes, Eivor, are here to stay.

speaker: Eivor
en: With Christ as their jarl.

speaker: Guthrum
en: He is a powerful God. Within his sacrifice hides the greatest boons. Forgiveness, hope, love. Would you not consider hearing his message for yourself?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no time to meet new gods. I am leaving England. And have only come here to say my goodbyes.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Will you return to your father's land?

speaker: Eivor
en: Elsewhere. To unmapped places, in search of the unknown.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Ah, an adventure worthy of Odin. You and he share a love for knowledge and discovery, I have noticed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Share is not strong enough a word.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Come, then. We must drink and tell stories before you go. If they are to be our last, they must be our best.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Young Harald has made quite a name for himself in our time away.

speaker: Eivor
en: Twelve or thirteen years, I think.

speaker: King Harald
en: Sigurd! Eivor! You are welcome here! Come.

speaker: King Harald
en: I got word that you would visit, but I... did not expect you so soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stout men huddled around a map, with eyes as hungry as their bellies. Little has changed here.

speaker: King Harald
en: Yes. I have spent half my life worrying over hastily drawn maps. But this is not a land we mean to conquer. It is a land in need of aid.

speaker: Eivor
en: Iceland?

speaker: King Harald
en: Yes. Our friend Ingolfr sends word that his new is in peril. Cold winters and simmering blood feud. I have agreed to send supplies and men, enough to bring peace and ride out the winter. Eivor, it may be your coming here, at this time, to this place, is a blessing from Thor himself. Would you and your brother lead this expedition for me? I cannot think of a better pairing to see this through.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, this is fated. I long for such an adventure. Tell me your mind. Does your heart-fire burn for another expedition?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am grateful for the offer. But I have not come here to walk down well-worn roads. I am here to say farewell. For once and all.

speaker: King Harald
en: For once and all? Are you leaving England as well?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am. Sailing west. Accompanied only by myself. To a land on no map.

speaker: King Harald
en: For what need?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll discover that only when I arrive. But that is tomorrow. Today I would like to spend time in the company of those I love. And tell stories from long ago.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Beginning when?

speaker: Eivor
en: Long, long ago. You understand?

speaker: King Harald
en: Uncle, clear the room. And bring mead and roasted (minke whale) for three.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now. Where to begin?

speaker: Valka
en: Will you not wait for morning?

speaker: Eivor
en: I must get to Lunden by the week's end. A crew awaits me there.

speaker: Valka
en: Not even a goodbye?

speaker: Eivor
en: Everyone knows I am leaving.

speaker: Valka
en: But not when. Does Randvi know tonight is the night?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. We said our goodbyes.

speaker: Valka
en: I wish I understood all this, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you remember my first visions? Before we came to England... Odin and Sigurd, the wolf, the Nornir?

speaker: Valka
en: Yes. They prophesized so much that came to pass.

speaker: Eivor
en: They were not prophecies, Valka. They were memories. My own. Or, not my own. But lent to me by another. One who lives within me. My second hugr. Do you understand?

speaker: Valka
en: I... I wish I did.

speaker: Eivor
en: For so long, I considered only two possible futures for me. Surrender to these malicious memories, or reject them utterly. But now I see a third way. And as I grow older, it draws my interest. I want to learn from them. But I do not know where this path will lead me. Nor what it might unleash. This is why, for now, I wish to be alone.

speaker: Valka
en: I see. Thank you for your trust, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Embrace me, friend.

speaker: Valka
en: Farewell, Eivor Wolf-Kissed. May Odin guide your way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not this time, Valka. This time, I will be guiding him.

speaker: Hytham
en: Eivor. Have you given my offer some greater thought?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, Hytham. I have not.

speaker: Hytham
en: Then I will ask again tomorrow.

speaker: Eivor
en: How does a heart so large hide in such a modest man?

speaker: Hytham
en: I don't follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: To work so tirelessly for strangers...fighting not for yourself, not for your people, but for all the world. That takes compassion of a size I have never known or seen in others.

speaker: Hytham
en: Ah. I thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you not worry about your own family? Or your clan back home? How did you come to be so rootless?

speaker: Hytham
en: I do have a clan, as you call it. But no family. I was orphaned quite young. It may be this lack that drove me to join the Hidden Ones. They have certainly treated me as a son.

speaker: Eivor
en: I too lost my family. But I gained another, this Raven Clan. I owe them my life, and I would give them mine.

speaker: Hytham
en: I feel the same gratitude, but on a larger scale. You see, anyone can join the Hidden Ones, and therefore everyone is worthy of our love.

speaker: Eivor
en: I admire your cause, Hytham. But I do not have the focus needed to carry forth your Creed. My mind is often... divided. Between the present and the distant past. And it will take some time to understand why.

speaker: Hytham
en: Ah, is it time?

speaker: Hytham
en: Forgive me, Eivor. We keep our training to a strict schedule.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course, carry on. And good luck with this lot. They're a wild crew...

speaker: Eivor
en: So many Danes, so many Norse. This will be the send-off Hemming deserves. All the funeral preparations are in order. Be patient, Hemming Jarl, we are about to send you on your final journey.

speaker: Eivor
en: No longer besieged by chickens, I see.

speaker: Norse Warrior (male)
en: Throw the dragons on the fire with the great jarl! We shall devour them together!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me, what funeral gift did you manage to offer your jarl?

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Some voda survived the fire. It will keep Hemming warm in Odin's hall.

speaker: Eivor
en: If he is not careful, that voda will burn all of Valhalla down.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will your god-water survive these flames?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: It will. And should Hemming Jarl so desire, our God will be ready to accept him into the Kingdom of Heaven.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've not seen your face among the Hemming Clan. From where do you hail?

speaker: Norse Warrior (female)
en: I come on behalf of the mighty Halfdan Ragnarsson of Northumbria. To deliver a gift to the departed Hemming Jarl. These people are good drinkers, and good warriors. Halfdan will be pleased.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hjorr, old friend. It is good to see you here. Is Ljufvina here as well?

speaker: Hjorr
en: One of us has to stay in Jorvik. She wishes she could be here, but alas, our duties never rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye. Never. Only Hemming Jarl has that privilege now.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Eivor, we meet again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan, it is good to see you.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Aye, if only our meeting were to take place during a more joyous occasion.

speaker: Eivor
en: To come all this way... you must have known him well.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Not as well as I would have liked. But he was a fine warrior, and an honest man. One I could trust. And I trust very few. To Hemming Jarl, Skal.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye, Skal.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brothers, sisters, kin and clan. It is time.

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor. My father sets forth on his final voyage.

speaker: Eivor
en: May the winds favor him.

speaker: Vili
en: The nobles have offered up their funeral gifts. All but you. Present what you have and the celebration may begin.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have it here...

speaker: Eivor
en: In just a moment, Vili. I will return.

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor. My father sets forth on his final voyage.

speaker: Eivor
en: As he must.

speaker: Vili
en: The great Halfdan Ragnarsson sent a beautiful gift with his men. As have all those who loved Hemming. Only your gift remains. Present what you have and the celebration may begin. (returns to choices)

speaker: Eivor
en: A shield bearing the rune of Gungnir, exalted spear of Odin. May it guide this great's man aim. Eternal be your war-strength, Hemming. Drenched in battle-dew, may you fight until the sky-wolf swallows the sun.

speaker: Eivor
en: A shield bearing the sign of the Web of Wyrd, woven into this shield as you wove your spirit into our lives. May the skalds sing of you as the gods embrace you. Feast, my friend, in the halls of the free and brave.

speaker: Eivor
en: In council, you were the wisest. At the hearth, the kindest. In battle the bravest. May the sign of , the Rune of the Way, guide you to the hall to many doors.

speaker: Vili
en: Stand at my side.

speaker: Eivor
en: Speak from my heart, Hemmingson.

speaker: Vili
en: Today we mourn the passing of Hemming Jarl of Snotinghamscire. My father. Our father. He was a towering force. A strength to fear and admire, now gone. Yet together we are the example of his greatness. I see him in each of you. His love for battle, but also peace. For wisdom, sorrow, and joy. His generosity. His spirit. In you, I see his life. And ... His love of drink. Gods, did he love drink! We are these things because he was these things.

speaker: Vili
en: Father. We shall be to our children what you were to us. And when they are ready, we will meet you again.

speaker: Trygve
en: You have made this old man proud. Each of you.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you us.

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: Nine days One-Eye hung from the tree. Nine worlds he saw. Nine runes he found. Nine nights he bled.

speaker: Vili
en: Father, receive your loyal servant.

speaker: Vili
en: Give him a fine farewell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sunniva, ride to Hemthorpe and prepare the longhouse for the Althing. The next jarl will soon take his seat.

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: You have seen what was needed?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have. More than enough.

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: Hemming Jarl was the greatest man I have ever known.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Drink as the great jarl would!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Who will take the great jarl's place? Will we decide at the next Althing?

speaker: Sunniva
en: Have they given their jarl a fine farewell?

speaker: Eivor
en: They have. None drink so well and so deeply as Clan Hemmingson.

speaker: Sunniva
en: The declaration of succession must happen soon, before we are too drunk and exhausted to remember our names.

speaker: Eivor
en: I agree. Call on those who must attend. The Althing will begin shortly.

speaker: Eivor
en: While rides through the sky, there is more celebrating to be done.

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: You look... uneasy.

speaker: Vili
en: I am not so drunk I cannot stand but... hang on to me a moment.

speaker: Eivor
