en: You do your father proud by this celebration. And by taking his seat. He wanted this, Vili.

speaker: Vili
en: I mourn for myself, Eivor. For us. You know my heart. It beats for the passion of battle-heat. Not... not this.

speaker: Eivor
en: As long as I have known you, Vili, you have possessed strength you rarely saw in yourself. A wildness. A joy of life. You are your father's son. But you have never let yourself be the fullness of that man. Not until now.

speaker: Vili
en: A warrior rises with the dawn to follow fresh tracks in the new fallen powder. For that is where adventure lies. I will follow these new tracks, Eivor. Wherever they may lead.

speaker: Eivor
en: As did your father's heart when he was our age. But he grew up. And so shall we. Now go on, man. Show them you are a Hemmingson.

speaker: Eivor
en: I felt the same. But in time, we all rise to the needs of the people. Who says you won't come to enjoy it?

speaker: Vili
en: Yes, yes. You're right. And certainly if you can lead, a Hemmingson can.

speaker: Vili
en: People of Hemthorpe. Of Ulkerthorpe. Of Snotinghamscire. We honor neither Trygve nor my father by continuing to mourn. These men dedicated their lives to bettering all of Snotingham. They died in that service. Now, I humbly pledge my life to following in their path. And I ask each of you to rise. And be to me what Trygve was to my father. Together, we shall build the world they wished to build.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have already learned that people prefer shorter speeches to long ones, Vili Jarl.

speaker: Vili
en: Hm. It will take time to wear that title with comfort.

speaker: Vili
en: My father never swore a formal oath with your clan. There was no need, for you are family. Let it be known that Hemmings and Clan Raven are true-sworn friends from this day forward. Do you accept?

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye.

speaker: Vili
en: Well...

speaker: Eivor
en: Be fair. Be just. And call upon us often, Arse-Stick.

speaker: Vili
en: I am sure I will.

speaker: Vili
en: Burdened by grief... drowning in mead. And paralyzed by a thought... I stand between that man and jarldom.

speaker: Eivor
en: You stand side by side, Vili. And one of you must step forward.

speaker: Vili
en: My father placed us side by side, because he trusted your vision. So what do you see?

speaker: Eivor
en: Drunk as you are, I see before me a man full of passion, vigor, and love for his people. I see a jarl. Your burden will get easier to bear. Take your father's seat. And make it your own.

speaker: Vili
en: I will.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Now let them know, Arse-Stick.

speaker: Vili
en: People of Hemthorpe, of Ulkerthorpe, of Snotingham. Today, I pledge myself. As my father was, I shall be your jarl. Hemming was a hero, not for who he was, but for the people he led. With Trygve by my side, with all of you, we will have glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have already learned that people prefer shorter speeches to long ones, Vili Jarl.

speaker: Vili
en: Hm. It will take time to wear that title with comfort.

speaker: Vili
en: My father never swore a formal oath with your clan. There was no need, for you are family. Let it be known that Hemmings and Clan Raven are true-sworn friends from this day forward. Do you accept?

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye.

speaker: Vili
en: Well...

speaker: Eivor
en: Be fair. Be just. And call upon us often, Arse-Stick.

speaker: Vili
en: I am sure I will.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see a drengr before me. A man who yearns for the glory of battle. Trygve should be jarl. And you ... you should follow your own path. Wherever it may lead...

speaker: Eivor
en: ...off a cliff and into the ocean, if that is what you need.

speaker: Vili
en: You know how to ruin a good moment, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Some time ago you asked about living with us. As one of our war-band. Is that something you still want?

speaker: Vili
en: To raid with you and Bragi? Gods, yes. Imagine the blood and mead we would spill.

speaker: Eivor
en: For old times, then. And new alike.

speaker: Eivor
en: Watch the look on the old man's face when he hears what we have planned.

speaker: Vili
en: I stand before you as Vili Hemmingson, but not as a jarl. There is only one man with the needed honor and wisdom. Only one man my father deemed worthy of following him. Trygve, jarl of Snotingham. May you walk proudly in Hemming's path.

speaker: Trygve
en: What is this?

speaker: Vili
en: Old friend, you deserve this. And so much more. Be proud.

speaker: Vili
en: My future is elsewhere, Trygve. I will go with Eivor, to live and fight beside the Raven Clan.

speaker: Trygve
en: I... I do not know what to say.

speaker: Vili
en: Say yes.

speaker: Trygve
en: Yes. Thank you, Vili. Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well done, Arse-Stick.

speaker: Vili
en: Until my path leads me home, I serve under your banner, Eivor.

speaker: Trygve
en: Eivor, let my first decree be Hemming's wish. An alliance between our people. When you call, we will rise.

speaker: Eivor
en: As we shall for you, Trygve Jarl.

speaker: Trygve
en: No one can live up to Hemming Jarl, but I will do my best to serve in his stead. Thank you, Eivor. I entrust Vili to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi will want to know about this. It is time I returned to the settlement.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thyra, you've outdone yourself with this bonfire.

speaker: Thyra
en: It is my design but many hands helped to gather the wood.

speaker: Eivor
en: The gods will favor us when they see the smoke and all the offerings we've collected for them.

speaker: Thyra
en: Speaking of offerings, everyone has gathered their sacrifices and left them for collection at the shrines near the waterfall.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you about to ask me to act as collector?

speaker: Thyra
en: Eivor. You are our leader. Everyone looks to you to set the example in both war and in celebration. Also you are very strong and have a knack for carrying things.

speaker: Eivor
en: So my true value is as a pack horse.

speaker: Thyra
en: Would a pack horse be entrusted with choosing which god receives our offerings? Go and see what the people have left at the shrines. Choose only the offering that you think is best and return here.

speaker: Eivor
en: It looks as though people left messages to the gods. I wonder who wrote what?

speaker: Eivor
en: The offering has been made.

speaker: Thyra
en: Lift your torch and commit our offerings to the god of your choice.

speaker: Eivor
en: We offer this to you, Lady Freyja. May you grant us many riches on our raids.

speaker: Eivor
en: May we find fortune and return safely.

speaker: Thyra
en: You've done well, Eivor. You've represented our clan with humility and grace. I know that everyone appreciates all you do for us. You should check in front of people's homes. There might be tokens of thanks waiting for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Each festival seems to bring with it more revelers.

speaker: Thyra
en: It would appear that Ravensthorpe is gaining a reputation for our celebrations.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I ain't in the business of helping you.

speaker: Fulke
en: Dear man, would you live under Eadwyn's boot? For that is where you will be if these supplies reach her castle.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I'd give them over to any man for enough silver. I've a livelihood to keep.

speaker: Fulke
en: I had silver, before I was caged, and I will again. You need only give me time. I'm as good as my word.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: It's a crying shame, your story. But a few supplies ain't going to rewrite the history of the world, woman.

speaker: Fulke
en: Good friend, your wares will bring death to the farmers and merchants of this land. Could you live with such a burden?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: None of my concern.

speaker: Fulke
en: Not until there's a sword at your neck.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's Fulke.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Stop that! That's my livelihood!

speaker: Fulke
en: You have a brusque way of ending an argument.

speaker: Eivor
en: We don't have time for philosophical discussion.

speaker: Fulke
en: It's for the good of your shire.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You've lost your senses.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's the noise about?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: She's trying to rob me. I warn you, soldiers are coming to escort me any minute.

speaker: Fulke
en: This merchant is taking supplies to the castle. Oil for boiling, arrows, shields, rations. I offered to buy them, but he refuses.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I don't sell on a future promise of profit! Eadwyn's a valuable customer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I'll make you a new offer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here's more than enough coin, friend.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: By Jesus, you're a better customer than your needling partner.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's wartime. I'm in no mood to barter. Walk away now or die in a ditch.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You stinking Dane.

speaker: Fulke
en: He should've taken the silver I offered him.

speaker: Eivor
en: How about a story? I'll spin you a tale in exchange for your wares.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: That's an odd bargain, Dane, but I'll bite. Sing me one of your sagas.

speaker: Eivor
en: The wild winds wandered, The seas spit salt. The night fell into slumber. Wise Odin rose and bade farewell, He pulled on boots of leather.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Bit of a slow start. Pick it up.

speaker: Eivor
en: Long before, before the beginning, Before you and I and the others. Wise Odin looked with his one wane eye, And stared and blinked and thundered.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: This Odin fellow, he's one of your gods, innit?

speaker: Eivor
en: The moon burns red, The sea foams gold, Wise Odin utters the words.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Right, this is not what I wanted. Stop it, will ye?

speaker: Eivor
en: The snake coils, Loki yowls, Poison drips from the mouth

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Enough! Enough! Is this some sort of Nordic curse? Run! Go!

speaker: Fulke
en: How does it end?

speaker: Eivor
en: They all die.

speaker: Eivor
en: He said soldiers are coming. We can use these oil jars to surprise them. Fewer reinforcements for Eadwyn.*

speaker: Fulke
en: I see visions of burning men. The screams of soldiers aflame. If we place the oil and supplies near the hay along the road, it will burn like hellfire when the soldiers arrive.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take position on that bluff and watch for the soldiers, would you?

speaker: Fulke
en: You'll hear me howl as the men approach.

speaker: Fulke
en: The wounds on these bodies weep like little eyes. Should we hide them? Fresh kills will arouse suspicion.

speaker: Eivor
en: What was that?

speaker: Fulke
en: My howl! Eadwyn's men approach.

speaker: Fulke
en: Prepare yourself. The soldiers are close.

speaker: Fulke
en: That overhanging branch is a good vantage for a first strike.

speaker: Fulke
en: They're here!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Where's this oil merchant? Said he'd be here all day.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: He'll show. We'll set up here for now.

speaker: Fulke
en: Spring the trap now!

speaker: Fulke
en: I'm with you! Attack! Soldiers of Saklas, may you die in ignorance! Cut them down, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's the last of them. Eadwyn will be waiting for aid that never comes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Something wrong?

speaker: Fulke
en: No, no. Quite the opposite. At Sante Albanes, your brother claimed kinship with the gods. Is it true? Is he descended from the Archons' children? The Isu?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not to be blunt, Fulke, but only half of what you say ever makes any sense to me.

speaker: Fulke
en: Forgive me. I often presume too much of my audience. Men who fear damnation, when ignorance is the greatest of all evils.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ignorance of what?

speaker: Fulke
en: What a perfect sentence.

speaker: Fulke
en: I'll ask more simply. Could your brother be descended of the gods? Or could he be a god himself?

speaker: Eivor
en: How is that possible? You don't believe such a thing yourself, do you?

speaker: Fulke
en: Not elusive Self-Begotten Light who reigns over all. But a lesser god, imperfect and given to temptation.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't know. I want to deny it, but I've... I've seen things in my life. Visions. Prophecies. It's difficult to explain.

speaker: Fulke
en: Heed your visions, always. You may have been touched by true knowledge.

speaker: Eivor
en: You spent too much time locked in that fetid cell, Fulke.

speaker: Fulke
en: Weeks of fasting and prayer and abstinence can clarify that which we otherwise fail to see.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd is only a man, the son of a king, and my brother. He may think highly of himself, but he's no god.

speaker: Fulke
en: Yet it's possible his line of kings was fathered by a god? In ages past?

speaker: Eivor
en: We haven't time for these fantasies, Fulke. It's time I regroup with Geadric. To see how his assault preparations are coming along.

speaker: Fulke
en: Godspeed, Eivor. I will stay here. To pray for the souls of the dead before I join you.

speaker: Letter from Lady Eadwyn
en: Be it known that her Ladyship is well pleased with the quantity and quality of the supplies delivered at Eatun Barn. Heretofore, the Trade Tax shall be reduced for your goods.

speaker: Ake
en: I am surrounded by fools and brigands!

speaker: Eivor
en: The long days have made you restless, Ake. You've become quick to solve problems with your fists.

speaker: Ake
en: What are you implying? Are you saying that I can't hold my own in a battle of wits?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, that's not at all

speaker: Ake
en: I'll have you know Alvis isn't the only flyting master here! We'll have a contest and I'll show you who has the winningest wit! Let's make it even more interesting and place a wager!

speaker: Eivor
en: O, Ake. You will regret this.

speaker: Ake
en: How many tokens are you willing to part with?

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not wish to take too much from you, Ake.

speaker: Ake
en: Are you scared of a fight now, O Wolf-Kissed the Brave. It's high time someone stood up and made you behave. I'm the roughest, the toughest, the biggest, the best! If you think my ale's good, put my fists to the test!

speaker: Eivor
en: I traverse land and oceans, I fight and I bleed. You just sit on your arse turning honey to mead.

speaker: Ake
en: Hmph! I suppose that was rather good.

speaker: Ake
en: So because I don't grandstand or boast just like you! You think being an apprentice is all I can do?

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, a quieter life seems a smart one to choose. While I'm out drawing blood, you're home nursing your brews!

speaker: Ake
en: You have quicker wit than I expected.

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't know who I am, don't go doubting my skills! This is more than just wits, it's a battle of wills!

speaker: Eivor
en: If you think you can best me, you're drunk or insane. I'm the cure for what ales you've got rotting your brain.

speaker: Ake
en: O! You cut me to the quick!

speaker: Ake
en: Now you're trying my patience, so I'll end it here: You are as thick and as weak as a bad English beer.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've got talent at flyting, in time you'll be skilled. But for now, tame your tongue, for it might get you killed.

speaker: Ake
en: I have no choice but to admire that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now stop going 'round picking fights in my town. You may brew a good drink, friend, but I'll put you down.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Eivor. It is good you are here. We are ready to make our offering.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is it ready?

speaker: Sunniva
en: Everything you gathered is in the boat. They are preparing it now to be sent to the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: Which god will be receiving our bounty?

speaker: Sunniva
en: I leave that choice to you. You can send the offering to Thor, god of strength and thunder. Or our Lady Freyja the Beautiful.

speaker: Eivor
en: A difficult choice.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Perhaps you should make the offering to the god who speaks most to you.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Freyja. A fine choice. May she watch over us in foreign lands.

speaker: Sunniva
en: The honor and glory is yours, Eivor. Take your place at the springald and light the flame that calls to the gods! Here is something to add to your enjoyment of Sigrblot. A gift from your clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: The offering is made. May the gods smile upon us!

speaker: Havi
en: The dwarves, they are dear to me... I remember when they first wriggled free from Ymir's flesh, even as I forced the dying breath out of his throat. I took pity on them. Gifted them with reason... For this, they will always be in my heart. And in my debt.

speaker: Havi
en: So... Ivaldi is dead. A pity... but Uldar may yet reveal something of value that I can trade for Baldr, or use against Surtr.

speaker: Havi
en: Loki and I, we brought Baldr here once, to Uldar, when he was just a boy. Now both are captives. Loki, deservingly, by my hand, and Baldr by Surtr's.

speaker: Havi
en: Baldr will be saved, and his mother avenged.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: Bad enough to be stuck in this pathetic city, but to serve under Glod as well...

speaker: Muspel Warrior 2
en: Do not speak ill of Glod if you value your life. You've seen what he can do.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 3
en: There's no glory to be had here, watching over these dwarves.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 4
en: Better than searching every last nook and cranny of the palace, eh?

speaker: Havi
en: Uldar's people are weak. Always have been. Too busy squabbling over their mines. I'd wager they put up no real fight against the invaders.

speaker: Havi
en: Gold in the streets. The house I seek should be close. This is where Gunborg told me to look.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 5
en: I once saw Glod crush an orge's skull like it was a raw egg.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 6
en: How can we trust Glod? He's half-jotun.

speaker: Havi
en: What happened here?

speaker: Havi
en: The artisans who once worked here... Their life's work... How trivial these trinkets must seem now, given all that has happened.

speaker: Havi
en: Jewelry for every occasion. This building surely played host to important moments in the lives of many. And look at it now.

speaker: Havi
en: Someone was beaten, tortured perhaps, then dragged along the ground here.

speaker: Havi
en: Fritjof writes of holding cells within Uldar. Therefore, dwarves who disobey may yet live, like this 'Tyra' he mentions.

speaker: Havi
en: What do we have here?

speaker: Havi
en: The Sons of Ivaldi tried to warn Fritjof of increased Muspel activity in Uldar. I wonder, did he get to see the message?

speaker: Havi
en: This place was used to exchange messages, but Fritjof was careless. The Muspels found out, ambushed him, and took him from here. To the holding cells, then... I need to get into the smelting foundry.

speaker: Havi
en: These relics Surtr seeks... I will seize them for myself, and use them to barter for Baldr's life. Or to end Surtr's.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 5
en: Everywhere in Uldar feels cold, except the foundry.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 6
en: The dwarves struggle with the foundry's heat. Filthy little maggots don't know how good they got it.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 7
en: Say one thing for this infested shithole, at least the foundry isn't all bad.

speaker: Havi
en: Here. I can feel the smelting foundry's heat... I see why the Muspels keep prisoners here. Roast the hope out of them, the poor bastards.

speaker: Havi
en: I pity the dwarves here. If this is their future, then for them Ragnarök cannot come soon enough. I, however, forge my own destiny.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 8
en: Shut your mouth, wretch! Or do you want to bake in the cells? Stop whining! Get back to work! You work or you die!

speaker: Dwarven Captive 1
en: We are saved! Th-thank you! Do you have water?

speaker: Havi
en: No. Now which one of you is Fritjof?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 1
en: Fritjof? No. I am

speaker: Havi
en: Then I do not care.

speaker: Havi
en: You. Are you Fritjof?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 2
en: I don't know any Fritjof.

speaker: Havi
en: I'm looking for Fritjof.

speaker: Dwarven Captive 3
en: They... they took him below.

speaker: Dwarven Captive 1
en: Why didn't you just say you were Fritjof? That might have gotten us out of here.

speaker: Dwarven Captive 3
en: What do we do now? If we escape, they'll just capture us again, or worse.

speaker: Havi
en: Fritjof?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 4
en: I don't know him. D-don't kill me, please.

speaker: Havi
en: Fritjof?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 5
en: Piss off! Before the guards think I called you here.

speaker: Tyra
en: Hey! (I know where he is!) Fritjof, yah! Fritjof! Hey. Hey! Fritjof? Hey! Fritjof! (I know him! Come here!) Fritjof? Fritjof! (I know where he is! Get me out! I'll show you!)

speaker: Havi
en: Fritjof? Are you there...? Nothing.

speaker: Havi
en: Fritjof? Is that you?

speaker: Havi
en: No, you cannot be Fritjof. But you know of him? Then... are you Tyra?

speaker: Tyra
en: Tyra! Yah! Dere! (Come! Get me out and we'll go to him.) Dere! Fritjof!

speaker: Havi
en: Do you even know where he is?

speaker: Tyra
en: Fritjof! Yah! Fritjof! Dere! (Come!)

speaker: Havi
en: Wait, wait. Do you understand me?

speaker: Tyra
en: Ehh... (I understand that we'll die if we stay here.)

speaker: Havi
en: Just... stay behind me. And keep quiet.

speaker: Tyra
en: Yah, yah... Fritjof!

speaker: Havi
en: Shh. Hold your tongue!

speaker: Tyra
en: Oh! Shh. Yah. (Try it, see what happens.)

speaker: Havi
en: Can you climb? No? Then we'll have to find another way out.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 9
en: You're telling me an Æsir defeated Surtr singlehandedly? Not in this lifetime.

speaker: Havi
en: Now... with this power... I can hide in plain sight, exit quietly. Stay close.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 10
en: She's off to become someone else's headache, eh? Gobby little shit.

speaker: Havi
en: I'd be surprised that ruse worked, if Muspels weren't so stupid.

speaker: Havi
en: The Lord of Asgard hides from no one. You. Don't die.

speaker: Havi
en: Now, to find Fritjof. Which way?

speaker: Tyra
en: Yah, uh, Fritjof... uh... hey!

speaker: Havi
en: Where do you lead me? Tyra...?

speaker: Havi
en: Tyra. Hm. A good name. Like Týr, of Asgard.

speaker: Havi
en: Never mind. We should hurry. Where now, to Fritjof?

speaker: Tyra
en: Dere, dere. (Come, come.) Fritjof!

speaker: Havi
en: I swear, if you leave me astray, there will be trouble.

speaker: Havi
en: Frankly, I'm surprised you could even see this... 'mighty galleon' from up there.

speaker: Tyra
en: Ac rwy'n synnu bod gennych chi ddigon o ddeallusrwydd i wisgo'ch hun. Ac eto dyma ni. (And I'm surprised you have enough intellect to dress yourself. Yet here we are.)

speaker: Havi
en: In any case... I don't suppose we can simply sail all the way to Fritjof?

speaker: Tyra
en: Nah. Ymddiried ynof, dw i'n eisiau hefyd cael gwared a ti cyntaf ag y gellwyf. (Believe me, I want to get shot of you as soon as I can, too.)

speaker: Havi
en: Then, the saga of Havi and Tyra begins. Don't say anything too noteworthy, there's a good lass. Let us find this relic.

speaker: Tyra
en: Rydyn ni'n arbed Fritjof. (We're saving) Fritjof.

speaker: Havi
en: Yes, yes, him too. Lead on...

speaker: Tyra
en: Agh!

speaker: Havi
en: I see them. Keep out of the way.

speaker: Tyra
en: Yah, yah...

speaker: Muspel Warrior 11
en: I'm telling you, I was there. Glod grabbed the poor fool's head and crushed it, in front of us all.

speaker: Havi
en: Come. We must not delay further. Take me to Fritjof.

speaker: Tyra
en: Fritjof, yah. Dere. Dere! (Come. Come!)

speaker: Havi
en: The language you speak... You're not from here, are you?

speaker: Tyra
en: Beth roddodd e i ffwrdd? (You're a clever one. What gave it away?)

speaker: Havi
en: Well... you picked a Hel of a time to visit Svartalfheim, that's for sure. Where do you lead me, Tyra?

speaker: Tyra
en: Ble ydw i'n eich arwain chi? Ydych chi wedi bod yn talu unrhyw sylw? (Where do I lead you? Have you been paying any attention?) Fritjof. Rydyn ni'n mynd i achub (We're going to save) Fritjof.

speaker: Havi
en: That isn't... Very well.

speaker: Havi
en: The Sons of Ivaldi were active here. But no longer, I suppose.

speaker: Tyra
en: Pfft. (Fuck all of them, especially) Ivaldi.

speaker: Havi
en: No, they were not of much use to you. Or Fritjof. Or Ivaldi, for that matter. Let's go. Truly, I regret letting Svartalfheim fall to Surtr. Had I been more vigilant, perhaps Baldr would have never fallen into his clutches.

speaker: Tyra
en: Baldr? Mae e'n Æsir gorau, ynte? (He's the only good Æsir, right?)

speaker: Havi
en: My son. As kind as he is naïve. Let us hurry.

speaker: Havi
en: Which way is it?

speaker: Havi
en: Tyra.

speaker: Havi
en: That's what I get for trusting a dwarf. There must be a clue here.

speaker: Havi
en: The road heads west, and has fresh tracks from a cart. Clearly in regular use.

speaker: Tyra
en: Yah... Rwy'n credu mai dyma ydyw. Ai dyma'r ffordd i (I think this is it. Is this the way to) Fritjof...?

speaker: Havi
en: This main road continues north, away from Uldar. A road like this surely leads to another city...

speaker: Tyra
en: Uh... Nid wyf yn credu mai dyna'r ffordd i'r safle cloddio. Ond gallwn i fod yn anghywir. (I don't think that's the road to the dig site. But I could be wrong.)

speaker: Havi
en: There must be another way to be sure. Look around, Tyra.

speaker: Havi
en: What is this? Lettering, intentionally damaged, and written in a script I cannot read. Tyra? Can you make sense of that?

speaker: Tyra
en: Yah, yah! Fritjof, Fritjof! Dere! (Come!)

speaker: Havi
en: I find you impressive, Tyra.

speaker: Tyra
en: Eh?

speaker: Havi
en: A lesser dwarf would only be interested in saving their own skin. Yet here you are, on this journey, determined to save Fritjof.

speaker: Tyra
en: Wel, go brin y gall yr amheus hwnnw achub ei hun nawr, a all? (Well, that numpty can hardly save himself now, can he?)

speaker: Havi
en: I only wish I understood you as you seem to understand me. When we get to our destination, be sure to stay out of harm's way, yes?

speaker: Tyra
en: Cawn weld. (We'll see.)

speaker: Tyra
en: Agh!

speaker: Havi
en: Wolves. Why did it have to be wolves?

speaker: Tyra
en: Hey. Hey!

speaker: Havi
en: Foolish beasts. Come, Tyra, we must not delay.

speaker: Havi
en: I will do what must be done. But the relic is what I seek. For now, Fritjof is no more than a stepping stone.

speaker: Tyra
en: Hey! Hey! Ble yr uffern wyt ti'n mynd? Dabre'n ôl! (Where the bloody hell do you think you're going? Get back here!)

speaker: Havi
en: Tyra? Have we arrived?

speaker: Havi
en: What is this place? Is this where they dig for relics?

speaker: Tyra
en: Shh!

speaker: Havi
en: Mmnh.

speaker: Tyra
en: Fritjof. Yah?

speaker: Havi
en: You think Fritjof is here? Time to find out. Wait here.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 12
en: Glod's in a good mood, now he's got the relic. Well... as good a mood as he gets...

speaker: Muspel Warrior 13
en: And what did Glod say when you gave him the relic?

speaker: Muspel Warrior 14
en: Nothing. But I've still got my head on my shoulders, at least.

speaker: Fritjof
en: You haven't heard the last of Fritjof! Muspels will fear the name! I'm not afraid of Glod! Bring him here! I'll show him! I found your damn relic, and this is the thanks I get? That's right! You all keep your distance! Bloody cowards! I'll kill you all! For what you've done to me, Uldar, to Ivaldi!

speaker: Havi
en: Fritjof?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Who's asking?

speaker: Muspel Warrior 15
en: You know we don't have a spare for that key, right? You think Glod'll be happy to hear you dropped it down there?

speaker: Muspel Warrior 16
en: Then help me fish it out! Anyway, that blind dwarf can rot in his cell for all I care.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 17
en: Eysa? Pfft. Forget her. Wanton little tart. Sinmara, now that's beauty.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 18
en: She'd sooner rip out your ball-sack and slit your throat than look at you, you soft-cock.

speaker: Havi
en: This must be the key for Fritjof's cell.

speaker: Havi
en: Gunborg sent me. Your people and mine share a common cause. The relics.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Well, I know of only one, cursed thing. It blinded me!

speaker: Havi
en: Where is it now?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Get me out of here and I'll tell you where to find it.

speaker: Havi
en: Can you walk?

speaker: Fritjof
en: I'm blind, not crippled. But... one wrong step, and I'll be taking a lava bath.

speaker: Havi
en: Then I shall carry you.

speaker: Havi
en: Stay quiet, Fritjof.

speaker: Fritjof
en: And you watch your bloody step.

speaker: Havi
en: Are there other relics here?

speaker: Fritjof
en: No idea.

speaker: Havi
en: Wait here.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Like I have a choice.

speaker: Havi
en: The path is clear, Fritjof. Time to move.

speaker: Fritjof
en: I'll just have to take your word for it. Move, indeed.

speaker: Tyra
en: Ydy e'n iawn? Dywedwch ei fod yn iawn. (Is he alright? Please say he's alright.) Fritjof? Oh Fritjof. Fritjof! Wyt ti'n iawn? Dywed rhywbeth! (Are you alright? Say something!)

speaker: Tyra
en: Fritjof! (What the bloody Hel happened to you?)

speaker: Fritjof
en: Tyra? Thank the stars you're safe. I'm alright, I'm alright. Y'know all things considered. This one got you out too?

speaker: Havi
en: Enough prattle. Where is the relic?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Not one for small-talk, are you?

speaker: Havi
en: Isn't that everything a dwarf says?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Ha! Not bad. Just... keep your breeches on, yeah? That relic I found, the Muspels have it. Took it to the palace, I'd wager.

speaker: Havi
en: And what is it?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Damned if I know. Moment I yanked it free from the ground, there was a blast of bright white light and that was the last thing I saw.

speaker: Havi
en: That's not what I asked. What does it do?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Other than blind unsuspecting dwarves? Dunno. Muspels didn't seem sure either. Hence taking it to that bastard scholar, up in the palace.

speaker: Havi
en: This palace, a Muspel stronghold, I take it?

speaker: Fritjof
en: You're a sharp one. Ivaldi was commissioned there, long ago. Einar's there now. Piece of shit. He's the one who'll have your relic.

speaker: Tyra
en: Einar? (What are you saying about) Einar?

speaker: Fritjof
en: He's... he's a traitor. A dwarf, working for the Muspels. So don't you believe a word he tells you. You get a chance... you kill him.

speaker: Havi
en: I shall judge who lives or dies. Where is this palace?

speaker: Fritjof
en: If we're still by the dig site, you can probably see it, to the south. Modest little place, sitting atop a great bloody rock.

speaker: Havi
en: Modest little place, indeed. Very well. I shall take this relic for myself. What will you do now?

speaker: Fritjof
en: What's it to you, whatever-your-name-is.

speaker: Havi
en: If I find you have lied to the Lord of Asgard, I will want words with you.

speaker: Fritjof
en: You? You're...? Oh my days. Well, look, I got nothing to hide. We'll make for the shelter, go see Gunborg.

speaker: Havi
en: Very well. If you're true to your word, then we shan't need cross paths again.

speaker: Havi
en: Now you're free, what's next for you both?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Reckon me and Tyra will head over to the shelter, check on Gunborg. Just... once I'm ready. These last days have been challenging.

speaker: Tyra
en: Einar? (unintelligible) Einar?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Don't speak the traitor's name. Not to me.

speaker: Odo
en: Eivor of England.

speaker: Eivor
en: You sent for me, said the queen was in peril.

speaker: Odo
en: I did. Come with me.

speaker: Odo
en: Look at these workers. Working happily. Working with pride. The beauty of my family vineyard depends on them. The quality of the wine is their doing. They're not beasts of burden. They take as much pride in these grapes as I do.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not here to admire your vineyard.

speaker: Odo
en: No. But this is more than a vineyard. It is a vision for Francia. A vision that cannot exist under Charles.

speaker: Odo
en: Ah! Plucked the grapes right on time, Roland. Très bien. (Very good.) Dependable as always.

speaker: French Man 1
en: Merci, monsieur. (Thank you, sir.)

speaker: Odo
en: These grapes produce the wine that my vineyard is famous for.

speaker: Eivor
en: I admit, there is an uncommon beauty to these lands.

speaker: Odo
en: Indeed. Come. I am slower than I once was. My physician says the wounds you have delivered should have taken me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You chose to have that fight.

speaker: Odo
en: And you fought for your people and for your honor. I do not hold it against you. Any true leader would have done the same. We are more alike than we first appear, Eivor. And I will carry the scars to remind me.

speaker: Odo
en: I feared my message would not get past Sigfred's many axes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigfred has left these lands. Those axes belong to Toka Sinricsdottir now.

speaker: Odo
en: That should be cause for celebration. But I fear Toka is yet another devil in a mail-shirt.

speaker: Eivor
en: Toka has learned much from Sigfred. Some of what she has learned is how not to be.

speaker: Odo
en: I hope you are right.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigfred is dead. They are Toka's axes now.

speaker: Odo
en: By whose hand?

speaker: Eivor
en: Mine.

speaker: Odo
en: I knew you were not like him. He was a careless butcher with no concern for what meat he chopped.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your message said Richardis was in peril. Is that really why you sent for me?

speaker: Odo
en: These men represent the growing rebellion against Charles the Fat. I now accept the bitter truth that I find more honor and courage in you, Eivor, a Northerner invader, than my own king.

speaker: Eivor
en: Honor is not bound by country or creed.

speaker: Odo
en: Indeed. And it seems Richardis also knows this. She and that bastard Bernard are more than mere pawns in Francia's future.

speaker: Eivor
en: I gave Bernard to Charles as a bridge to an alliance.

speaker: Odo
en: Yes, well, the boy barely lasted a day with that betrayer before running back to Richardis.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bernard... a part of me wanted to hand him over to Charles.

speaker: Odo
en: What grace you possess prevented you from condemning the boy to a hell in this world. He is better off with Richardis.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is the queen?

speaker: Odo
en: She's hiding in a tavern in Amiens, guarded by my men. But those men have not reported back in... too long.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find Richardis. I am duty bound to return the aid she once gave to me. And... she is my friend.

speaker: Odo
en: There is one more thing. This rebellion will succeed. And when it does, my path to the throne will be well charted.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your true ambitions.

speaker: Odo
en: I was a loyal servant to Francia, to Charles and to God. But Charles has been exposed. You want a Frankish king who will never march on England. I am that king.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I kill Charles for you.

speaker: Odo
en: If you killed Charles for Francia, we would not forget.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are an honorable man, Count Odo. If I have a chance to kill Charles, I will.

speaker: Odo
en: And in so doing, you will have sealed an alliance between the people of your clan and all the peoples of Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: First I must seek out Richardis in Amiens.

speaker: Odo
en: Then go, Eivor the Wise. My prayers will ask the Lord to guide that blade of yours. We will overcome this evil, as we always have.

speaker: Eivor
en: No. Murdering Charles on the hope it will bring security to my clan is not the kind of deal I want to make.

speaker: Odo
en: I misjudged you, Eivor. You stand before your people's best hope...

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough. You offer a promise you cannot keep, Odo. I'll go to the tavern in Amiens and find Richardis.

speaker: Odo
en: Fine. Bonne chance (good luck), Eivor. I will pray for you to succeed where my men have not.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: It was a massacre. Mon dieu (My God), bodies scattered like children's toys.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: They say it was a demon. Some say the queen, she... My, what vile witchery has befallen us?

speaker: French Woman 1
en: There's another diable (devil) now. We should go.

speaker: Eivor
en: These men must have been the queen's guard. Tavernkeep, what happened here?

speaker: French Man 2
en: Hide. I am not sure it is gone... the monster... so much blood... just hide!

speaker: Eivor
en: Better to look around myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Was this how the queen escaped, or the way her enemies got to her?

speaker: Eivor
en: More of Odo's men. They failed to safeguard the queen.

speaker: Eivor
en: A monk. What was he doing here?

speaker: Eivor
en: A red poppy. Yes, these are Odo's men.

speaker: Eivor
en: A scroll. It has an odd marking. Could have been a part of Bernard's studies.

speaker: Eivor
en: The tavernkeep may know something about this scroll and its marking.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is a dead monk upstairs. And a scroll in a tongue I do not understand.

speaker: French Man 2
en: It's... probably scripture... written in .

speaker: Eivor
en: The boy-prince reads Latin...

speaker: French Man 2
en: Bernard? Yes! They were here. That monk was his teacher. He's from the church here in Amiens. I heard the queen tell Bernard to go to the priests and nuns there when he's in trouble.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I will look in on this church and hope to find the queen there.

speaker: French Child 1
en: Hear ye, hear ye! Amiens to celebrate King Charles' great victory over the heathen chieftain they call Sigfred. Show your faith and loyalty to the crown by dressing in Amiens blue. Garments at a discount!

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: I saw the boy, I know it! The bastard princeling is around here somewhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bernard is here.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: You hear what Charles means to do to the queen?

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: I don't care if she's a witch or diable (devil). Nobody should be burned alive.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bernard.

speaker: Bernard
en: No! I won't go back to my father. Something is wrong with him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quiet, boy. I'm not going to take you to Charles. Not again.

speaker: Bernard
en: But last time

speaker: Eivor
en: This is different. How did you escape?

speaker: Bernard
en: I snuck through the villa wall where there's construction. I climbed! Then I found Richardis at the tavern. I did it all on my own.

speaker: Bernard
en: Eivor! Thank goodness it's you.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened?

speaker: Bernard
en: The monster took us to Father's villa. But Richardis distracted him and I snuck through the construction along the wall. There is a tower there, and if you climb and climb, you can go right over.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is Richardis? Where is the queen?

speaker: Bernard
en: The monster... she left with him.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mean the one who slaughtered so many at the tavern?

speaker: Bernard
en: He said we'd be brought to Father for something. A test. I was

speaker: Eivor
en: What kind of test?

speaker: Bernard
en: I... he called it a trial... yes, that is what he said. A . At Father's villa here in Amiens.

speaker: Eivor
en: He means to burn her alive. Go Bernard. Go to your house in Lisieux. I will see to Richardis.

speaker: Bernard
en: I can help. I know... things. You do not have to hurt my father. He is just... he gets confused sometimes.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must keep yourself safe, Bernard. The fate of Francia depends on your survival. It will be a grand task for you to sneak all the way down the Seine alone. This is a hero's burden. Are you up to it?

speaker: Bernard
en: I can do it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Now go.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep going and do not look back. I will see to Richardis.

speaker: Bernard
en: Au revoir (Goodbye), Eivor.

speaker: French Soldier 4
en: Back away, heathen. Church business. Christians only.

speaker: Eivor
en: Locked. Maybe there is a way over the damaged section.

speaker: French Soldier 5
en: Gate duty again, merde. Why can't I just give the key to the workers and be done with it...

speaker: French Soldier 6
en: My feet ache! The renovations better be worth all these double shifts.

speaker: French Soldier 7
en: They won't be.

speaker: Eivor
en: The wall is being repaired. Bernard mentioned escaping through here.

speaker: French Soldier 8
en: Is the queen really going to be put on trial? By her own husband?

speaker: French Soldier 9
en: The king, you mean. I heard it will be a trial by fire.

speaker: French Soldier 8
en: It cannot be! Surely God would stop this.

speaker: Charles
en: It appears that God himself is here to bear witness to this trial. May He show infinite mercy on the innocent. And if one is guilty of lying... scheming... committing adultery... may His holy wrath punish your wicked soul.

speaker: Richardis
en: I have nothing to fear from Him. It is you, Charles, who must seek His forgiveness.

speaker: Charles
en: We will soon know who God has blessed with His favor.

speaker: Richardis
en: My guardian angel approaches.

speaker: Gozlin
en: That is no angel. Before my king and before God, it's time I sent this diable (devil) back to Hell where it belongs.

speaker: Eivor
en: Alive? Stand aside, bishop. Your God does not bring men back more than once.

speaker: Gozlin
en: For Engelwin. For Little Mother. For my brother, Ebels. I will purge you from this place.

speaker: Eivor
en: Out of my way, bishop, or I will kill you again.

speaker: Gozlin
en: The Lord spared me. I am His wrath!

speaker: Richardis
en: "Thou hast delivered my soul from death, mine eyes from tears, and my feet from falling."

speaker: Charles
en: Why is the fire moving so slowly?

speaker: Eivor
en: I think you want the pain. You like it.

speaker: Gozlin
en: I want only to send you to Hell!

speaker: Richardis
en: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me."

speaker: Charles
en: She should be burning!

speaker: Gozlin
en: Your wickedness is inhuman!

speaker: Richardis
en: Lord, heaven and earth obey your command. Deliver me as you deliver those who love you, and know your name!

speaker: Charles
en: My beloved wife... it was not you, it was me. All along it was me. I am damned. I've been damned from the very beginning...

speaker: Gozlin
en: Why do you hunt us?

speaker: Gozlin
en: The Bellatores will...

speaker: Richardis
en: I must find Bernard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bernard is safe. I sent him back to the house in Lisieux.

speaker: Richardis
en: Once again, he uses you. You radiate God's grace.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mistake grace for the flush of victory.

speaker: Richardis
en: Poor Bishop Gozlin, I will pray for his soul. He served the Lord the best way he knew how.

speaker: Eivor
en: Charles and I need to talk. It may be the last time he talks to anyone.

speaker: Richardis
en: No! He is a wounded man who was tortured as a child. Burned and burned again. His whole life is fear. Fear of fire. Fear of God. Fear of disloyalty. He deserves mercy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not a moment ago, he was to have you burned alive! What would you have me do?

speaker: Richardis
en: Spare him. Subdue him somehow. I can take him to our remote cottage in the east where he will receive priestly guidance. There, we can live out quietly while I continue to prepare Bernard to succeed Charles. I assure you, he will grow up to be a ruler without ambitions for England. Spare Charles and your people will be safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine. If I can, I will spare him. But I need to be sure he can abide these terms.

speaker: Richardis
en: I know you will do what's right. The Lord works through you, and he is merciful.

speaker: Eivor
en: Charles has dishonored all of his allies and his people. I will not swear an oath to spare him.

speaker: Richardis
en: This is folly, Eivor. Killing Charles will not assure the safety of your people.

speaker: Eivor
en: If not, let it avenge all the Norse he has felled here in Francia.

speaker: Richardis
en: Father, bless these men who stand humbly in your judgement...

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: A tough fight, but Sigfred Skull-breaker led us to victory again.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Yes. And now these wooden beasts will bring the gods' wrath down upon this city.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: These wooden warriors are ready. Thanks to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Glad to lend a hand, friends.

speaker: French Child 1
en: Hear ye, hear ye! The heathens are marching on the gates of Paris! By order of Count Odo, bring your stock and wares behind city walls. Or travel south to Troyes! Count Odo says, "We will overcome this evil, as we always have."

speaker: Eivor
en: I should join Sigfred at the bell tower. We need to scout some ground for his catapults.

speaker: Eivor
en: A trail of blood. Sigfred passed this way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigfred cut a bloody path through this tower.

speaker: Sigfred
en: There. That workshop. The perfect place for our catapults.

speaker: Eivor
en: An army of wooden giants to bring down the walls.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those Franks. What are they doing?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Ah. They slay another of their own today.

speaker: Eivor
en: For what?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Who can say? If a man prays to the wrong god, sleeps with the wrong woman, follows the wrong king... by Frankish law, that man dies.

speaker: Eivor
en: Among the Saxons, it is much the same.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Aye, but the Saxons are fewer, they are divided, and they fight both us and the Celts. These Franks though, united under a great king...

speaker: Eivor
en: It would be like unleashing Fenrir the wolf upon the world.

speaker: Gozlin
en: We are God's priests, and we are good. But if thou do that which is evil, fear! For we beareth not the sword in vain.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are those two? I have seen the warrior priest with Count Odo before.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Gozlin and Ebels, warriors and brothers. One leads the priests of Paris, the other the Frankish armies.

speaker: Gozlin
en: For we are God's priests, avengers to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must

speaker: Ebels
en: Brother! You talk too much!

speaker: Sigfred
en: Come on, let us go take that workshop now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite a show they put on. We'll have to fight those Franks soon.

speaker: Sigfred
en: True, but today is not that day. My men are ready. Come, let us take some ground for the catapults.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would never give my warriors a shameful death like that.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Nor would I, but I have met rotten rulers in many lands.

speaker: Eivor
en: You speak true, Sigfred. The Franks have no monopoly on wickedness.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Almost there. Now, let us travel light and stick to the rooftops.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Sigfred Skull-breaker is here!

speaker: Sigfred
en: Come, men! We shall take this workshop and make it our own.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: We scouted the place. They keep watch, but not well.

speaker: Sigfred
en: And the sight lines?

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: A perfect place for our catapults to hurl stones upon that cursed town.

speaker: Eivor
en: I never took you for a rooftop runner, Sigfred.

speaker: Sigfred
en: I am no goat-footed climber like you, but I hold my own on cliffs and walls.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Attack! Vengeance or death!

speaker: Eivor
en: Our new catapults are eager for battle.

speaker: Sigfred
en: The crack of wood and stone is the sound of victory... and vengeance.

speaker: Eivor
en: This place has a good line of sight on the city walls for our catapults. Well done, Sigfred.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Push on! Seize the workshop!

speaker: Eivor
en: A great victory. The gods smiled upon this day.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Indeed. This gives us another place where our catapults can smash down their walls. Eivor. Know you the fate of Vidar Odinsson?

speaker: Eivor
en: The god of vengeance, who fights besides his father in the battle at the end of days.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Yes. Vidar avenges him. Vidar twists the great wolf's neck with his bare hands, then stabs the beast through the belly.

speaker: Eivor
en: So say the Nornir.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Days like today, I walk in the shoes of Vidar, avenging my brother. Other days, there is nothing.

speaker: Sigfred
en: We will bring those walls down on Odo's head. And I will avenge my brother.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is good. We shall meet back in camp when all is ready, Sigfred.

speaker: Stowe
en: Eivor, welcome to the West Market.

speaker: Eivor
en: A lawman like you could set folks on edge in a square like this. Why not wear a cloak?

speaker: Stowe
en: Hide my face? Not a chance. It does people good to see a lawman on the hunt.

speaker: Stowe
en: And once we've found The Arrow, this order needs to know we'll be after The Leech and The Compass as well.

speaker: Stowe
en: You and Erke found the identity of The Leech?

speaker: Eivor
en: Some holy healer, she was called Frideswid. Had an appetite for eyes.

speaker: Stowe
en: If this order can corrupt Lunden's favored saint, what hope do we have?

speaker: Eivor
en: Any noise yet about The Arrow and recruits?

speaker: Stowe
en: I've heard whispers. Somewhere here, a man gives you a coin. And this coin grants you entry to a contest run by The Arrow's men.

speaker: Eivor
en: Which man? I see too many here.

speaker: Stowe
en: He's good at blending in, I haven't spotted him yet today.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll sniff around. You stay back.

speaker: Stowe
en: Eivor... what was your impression of Erke?

speaker: Eivor
en: You suspect him of something?

speaker: Stowe
en: I don't know. Whoever killed Tryggr was a close friend. And it was Erke who found the body. I know Erke so well. And I can't bear to think he'd do something so vile, but...

speaker: Eivor
en: Then don't. Wait for proof before you condemn your friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: Erke has been a great help. Why doubt him now?

speaker: Eivor
en: You know him better than me. If you suspect him, only say the word.

speaker: Stowe
en: No, no. I believe in Erke. It's me I don't trust. I feel unfit for my post somedays.

speaker: Eivor
en: Erke was torn up by the Good Sister's dark dealings. I don't know him well, but a guilty man doesn't have a clean conscience like his.

speaker: Stowe
en: Forgive me. My latest thoughts have been restless. I've been a reeve (sheriff) for so long, fighting for God's justice. I shed my earthly attachments for His great plans. But...

speaker: Eivor
en: But you couldn't shed Erke and his friendship?

speaker: Stowe
en: No. No, I'm not sure I could.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's good to talk. Unburden your soul. Clears the mind and lifts a weight off the chest.

speaker: Stowe
en: Yes, indeed. And thank you for listening.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should find one of these coins soon. Will you be around?

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not good to attach yourself to any one person. Be your own man, forge your own path.

speaker: Stowe
en: I should, I know...

speaker: Eivor
en: I should find one of these coins soon. Will you be around?

speaker: Eivor
en: I should find one of these coins soon. Will you be around?

speaker: Stowe
en: I'll return to Saint Paul's just down the road. Godspeed, Eivor.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: He goes by "The Arrow", I'm told. A fit name for a keen archer. Can't wait to meet the man himself.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: About time someone did something about those filthy outlanders ruining our city.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Aye, fucking pond scum coming here with their hands out. Lunden for Lundeners, vermin stay on the other side of the wall.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: You got a coin? Show me? Is that a coin? For the archery contest?

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Keep off, boy-o. This is my coin. You want one, you talk to my mate Hussa, and he'll point you true.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: I heard the take for this job is three stubs of silver a month. Is that true?

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Ja. And they pay you more if you drag your brothers into it. Hussa's earned a fortune skimming the docks of Lundenwic.

speaker: Propaganda Poster
en: Are you tired of feeling like a minority in your own city? Do you long for purpose and comradery? Join our ranks, and we will provide an arrow of direction and strength.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Begone, you reek of someplace else.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've a bow and a body ready to serve The Arrow. So why turn away the sharpest eye in Britain?

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: I haven't come this far trusting any old sellsword on the street. How do I know you aren't some rat looking to sink our ship?

speaker: Eivor
en: I would never. A common friend sent me.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Did he now? And what's our common friend's name?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hussa sent me. Your men in Lundenwic.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Hussa did? Well, he's a keen one, all right. Has a good eye for soldiers. But do you align with our values? What think you of outlanders?

speaker: Eivor
en: Outlanders bring exotic riches. Spices, silks, and gems. They are the wealth of port cities.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: I've no quarrel with them dumping their trade. But, they should leave after. Lunden for Lundeners.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wrong answer. I need to find another way to get the coin.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not fond of too many Outlanders in one place. I never want to be in the minority.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Exactly! They must not replace us. Heh, ja. You know exactly what we're about. Take this coin. It will give you entry at the coliseum. Welcome to The Arrow's kinship. With luck, you will gain rank.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what right does a Norse-born have to challenge the right of an Outlander to Lunden's soil.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Get fucked!

speaker: Eivor
en: I need a moment.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Verily, I believe you.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was Egbert of East Anglia.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Yeah, right. Begone, 'afore I kick your teeth in.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wrong answer. I need to find another way to get the coin.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stowe of Lunden. He gave me leave to knock you about until you squealed.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Stowe? Stomp this one into the dirt!

speaker: Eivor
en: I need a moment.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Verily, I believe you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Some of these men have pocketed their coin already. But which? Ignore your purses lads.

speaker: Eivor
en: There we go. Hm, this coin is engraved with an image of the Lunden Coliseum.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: I keep seeing 'em round my mum's house. Outlanders, thinking they can stink up the place.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Come on! Take it, you fucking coward!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Hit him! Go on!

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: You like her?

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Well, yes.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: So, make her yours. Women don't need reason, they need to be told what to do. Better you than some Outlander pig breeding her.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: What's your business, shooting or watching?

speaker: Eivor
en: You're looking for skilled archers. And now you've found one.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: This contest is private. Invitation only.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your men are handing out these coins like they were on fire. Is this enough?

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: It's enough to keep us talking. But I'll want to see how well you handle that bow before you go any further. Want a trial round to test your eye?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll shoot a practice round, just to be sure.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Go ahead, then. They're all set up.

speaker: Eivor
en: How was that?

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: How unfortunate. A stirring of wind stole your chance.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: You've got quite an eagle's eye on you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've had enough practice. Let's begin.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: A real fanatic, you are. Get ready...

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: It's a simple contest here. Hit all targets true before the sand runs down! Here's a new competitor. A Norse from the northern wilds of Mercia. And, our current reigning champion, Saer! Alright take your mark! Hooks set! Arrows knocked! Fire!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: We're halfway down the sand! Odin's beard! Did you see that! Incredible! A perfect strike!

speaker: Saer
en: A cheat! A cheat!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: It was a fair shot, carry on!

speaker: Saer
en: You can always forfeit if you're not having fun!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Time! Bows down! Saer leads to victory!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: A poor showing. Such a pity.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait, I can do better.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: I often say the same. And it always costs me a little fortune.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've got a racket here. Cutting my purse strings for a few more arrows.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Let's loosen those arrows! Targets up! Bows ready!

speaker: Eivor
en: With The Arrow looking for the best archer in Lunden, you would best be sure.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Well the conditions on your matches weren't exactly the same.

speaker: Saer
en: What? Right from the bull's arse this is!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Let's loosen those arrows! Targets up! Bows ready!

speaker: Eivor
en: I lost in a fair contest. It is not worth grousing over.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: If that's the case, then Saer will meet The Arrow, uncontested.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Eivor leads to victory!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: That's deadly aim you have. Best I've seen for some time. Well shot. You have earned your place at The Arrow's side today. He'll be eager to meet you. Haul yourself to the Imperial Arch and speak with our man, Hussa. Recite the phrase, "May the Father of Understanding Guide Us," and he'll know it's you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can shoot a mid-flight seagull through the eye.

speaker: Saer
en: And you're still only good enough to beat me once.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Well shot. You have earned your place at The Arrow's side today. He'll be eager to meet you. Haul yourself to the Imperial Arch and speak with our man, Hussa. Recite the phrase, "May the Father of Understanding Guide Us," and he'll know it's you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't have time for this. Maybe later.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Why bother me at all then?

speaker: Eivor
en: I see you've still got your targets set up.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Do you have a coin now?

speaker: Eivor
en: You mean this coin?

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: The Arrow is making his speech at the Imperial Arch. On your way now!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you Hussa?

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: Ja, and who's asking?

speaker: Eivor
en: May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: And May the Mother of Wisdom Give us Strength. You're to stand just there. Look your best when The Arrow comes forth. And keep still.

speaker: Eivor
en: Loki's wind cast my arrows aside.

speaker: Saer
en: You're a poor shot, that's the end of it.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: After two attempts, Saer remains the winner. The Arrow awaits his new champion at the Imperial Arch. Don't delay.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Go lick your wounds elsewhere. Everyone's heading to the rally.

speaker: Avgos
en: Friends, brethren, good people of Lunden! We've had a hard week. Cowardly invaders stole into our Governor's home and robbed him of his life!

speaker: Avgos
en: Tryggr, my friend, my leader. Slaughtered like a dog! By outsiders, by the enemy! Do we expect these Reeves to guide us? Thumb-arsed halfwits let Tryggr die! They think we're safe! But, our Governor knew. He confided in me his real plans to protect Lunden. The drunken Danes of Northumbria polluting the north. Aelfred and his men of Wessex rallying to the south. Of all this, Tryggr said, "Avgos, what we need now are strong borders and strong soldiers. Today, I honor that wish. I present to you, good people of Lunden, our new elite archery force. These elite archers will be stationed at our springalds! Ready to attack invaders by land or by water. And further, until these storms of accusations clear, I will take Tryggr's place at the head of our fair city. Not that I could replace him, for Tryggr was a pillar of steel. But I can try. Let me be your arrow, let me point a true way forward. Some will be naysayers. Those who wish to discredit me. And those who wish to keep Lunden weak. Listen not to them, friends. I serve only Lunden. I serve you. Lunden is a place of prosperity. Prosperity we must export to all of Britain's kingdoms. No more false kings with their lies. Heed the ancient ways, the true strength of Lunden. Rule Lunden. Rule Britain. Rule the world! Into order and truth!

speaker: Avgos
en: Guards! At arms! Cover my retreat! Don't just stand there, you bloody clots! Kill that one there!

speaker: Avgos 1
en: Arrows nocked!

speaker: Avgos 2
en: It's a hard thing to raise the rats of a city into warriors.

speaker: Avgos 1
en: Hook, set!

speaker: Eivor
en: You raised no one. You only trapped them in their cowering fear.

speaker: Avgos 1
en: Draw strings! First wave, fire!

speaker: Avgos 2
en: No! I gave these men order! I gave them purpose! I showed them their common enemy!

speaker: Avgos 1
en: Anchor strings! Second wave, fire!

speaker: Avgos 2
en: I was arrow for their rage. Without a foe to consume, we devour ourselves.

speaker: Odin
en: He speaks true. A man without an enemy defeats himself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Justify all you want, you're just a king-killer and a coward.

speaker: Avgos 2
en: Mighty high horse, you'd do the same if you were me.

speaker: Avgos 1
en: Aim! And fire!

speaker: Stowe
en: You're unharmed. Praise be to God!

speaker: Eivor
en: It'll take more than a few lads with newly polished bows to fell me.

speaker: Stowe
en: The Arrow was a boy?

speaker: Eivor
en: A man with a boy's brain. Called Avgos.

speaker: Stowe
en: Avgos? That can't be right.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could return with his head on a spear if you'd like to see.

speaker: Stowe
en: No, you've no reason to lie. Yet Avgos, my old friend, had no cause to murder. He saw Lunden as a kiln of rage. To harden the softness of its younger men. Perhaps I ignored in him what I hoped to see. Ambition, greed, anger.

speaker: Eivor
en: From one man, such hatred is easy to spot. But from many, it's a fog that fills the room.

speaker: Stowe
en: Power. Men will claw for it and cling to it at the cost of everything.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very true. And it's cold comfort... when glory has the taste of your family's blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: With Avgos gone, I'll turn my attention to The Leech.

speaker: Stowe
en: Erke should be down by the quays. He'll be waiting for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: If The Compass should emerge, we'll let you know.

speaker: Stowe
en: Then I'll be at Saint Paul's Church, waiting for the good word. Take care, Broga.

speaker: Eivor
en: Two targets down, only The Compass remains. If it were my men killed, I would be on my way to Lunden now.

speaker: Stowe
en: The Compass will come, and we must be ready. Expecting the worst.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't want anyone catching me off guard. Could we take the fight to him?

speaker: Stowe
en: There may be a way. Let's regroup in the church when you've had time to rest, Broga.

speaker: Nel
en: I see you! Mother is going to be so angry. Come out, Walter! You can't hide from me! Walter! This isn't funny anymore!

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are you yelling at? I see no one.

speaker: Nel
en: My brother! He's right in there! A goblin turned him into a fish.

speaker: Eivor
en: A goblin turned him into a fish?

speaker: Nel
en: He won't come out of the water to do his chores. Mum's going to be so angry. O, whatever will I do?

speaker: Nel
en: I've got to get him out of that pond. It won't be easy, he's mean and slippery. Walter! You're gonna be in so much trouble when mum hears about this. She told you not to talk to goblins!

speaker: Nel
en: That's not the right fish. My brother has brown eyes.

speaker: Nel
en: You're no help. My brother is swimming around this pond!

speaker: Nel
en: That one smells like my brother, but it's not him.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not convinced at all that your brother is under a goblin's spell.

speaker: Nel
en: Keep fishing! I've got treats for you, Walter. Worms and such.

speaker: Walter
en: Another one! That's enough.

speaker: Nel
en: Walter! Stay in the bushes!

speaker: Walter
en: We've got all we need.

speaker: Nel
en: We don't have them yet, you pudding head!

speaker: Walter
en: Don't call me names.

speaker: Nel
en: Pudding head! Pudding head!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your brother looks pretty healthy... for a fish.

speaker: Nel
en: We thought it would be fun to get someone else to do the fishing for us.

speaker: Eivor
en: So you "fooled" me.

speaker: Nel
en: And it worked! If you like, you could leave us the fish anyway. We'll swap 'em for brittle at the market.

speaker: Nel
en: Walter, we got the fish! Thank you, stranger!

speaker: Nel
en: What? No fish?

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid. Flann's gift is on its way to Meath.

speaker: Bárid
en: Very good. I was just preparing to leave for the coronation, though I now have a problem on my hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it?

speaker: Bárid
en: Flann's , Ciara. She was here delivering a formal invitation and now I do not know where she's gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you think she's in trouble?

speaker: Bárid
en: No, I think she is amusing herself somewhere. Likely perusing Dublin's markets. We need her. The high poetess is an important member of the king's court. There cannot be a coronation without one.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find her. Where should we meet?

speaker: Bárid
en: By Dublin's gates. I will ready the horses.

speaker: Ciara
en: O, Flann Sinna, great lord of Meath... King of Kings, soon to be... Pure of blood, whole of heart. A leader of all men lost in the dark. For a greater tomorrow he shall bring, the Southern Uí Néill King of Kings.

speaker: Eivor
en: If that is the voice of the poetess, the standard is low in these lands.

speaker: Ciara
en: O, Flann, O, Flann, isn't he grand? He who... something here that rhymes!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Enough of your yawping. For the sake of our ears, shut your mouth.

speaker: Ciara
en: Sure, and you're an idiot.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: You are all the same.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Grab the bitch!

speaker: Ciara
en: Fé! (Damn!) Won't you let a caged bird sing?

speaker: Eivor
en: Shit.

speaker: Ciara
en: I'd hoped an audience of tone-deaf Danes might permit!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you Ciara?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Hold her down!

speaker: Ciara
en: Wonders of wonders, how much trouble can I be in at once?

speaker: Eivor
en: Can't help you. This one comes with me.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: No, no, no. She will answer for this insult.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can't change your mind?

speaker: Eivor
en: You owe me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like our poetess has made friends with the ground.

speaker: Eivor
en: On your feet, poetess.

speaker: Ciara
en: Mo lén! (Poor me!) Everything is spinning...

speaker: Eivor
en: A cold bath will remedy this quickly.

speaker: Ciara
en: Agh! Mo léir-chrech! (Alas!) What was that for?

speaker: Eivor
en: To flush the ale from you. If you think I'm going to lug you to Tara, you're mistaken.

speaker: Ciara
en: Tara? Wait, who are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid sent me to collect you. He's waiting at the stables.

speaker: Ciara
en: Ah, an envoy. Tell me, how much coin would an envoy be wanting to speak nothing of this brawl to Bárid? He'll tie a guard to my hip the next time I'm in Dublin. That man can be so sensitive sometimes, do you know what I mean?

speaker: Eivor
en: I do. Bárid is my family.

speaker: Ciara
en: Well then, I think my mouth has gotten me in enough trouble today.

speaker: Eivor
en: Try opening it less. Works for me. Shall we?

speaker: Ciara
en: Bárid has never spoken of you. What name do you bear?

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor. I hail from Norway, now settled in England with the rest of my clan.

speaker: Ciara
en: A clan, eh? Are they all fist-thumpers like you?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is because of these fists you live to sing another day, poetess.

speaker: Ciara
en: So true.

speaker: Ciara
en: Bárid!

speaker: Bárid
en: I was beginning to worry. What took?

speaker: Eivor
en: There was ... trouble.

speaker: Ciara
en: Ara (Ah), no need to be so tense. Shall we ride for Tara? We don't want to be late for the coronation.

speaker: Bárid
en: After you.

speaker: Ciara
en: I was surprised to meet a member of your family, Bárid. Eivor tells me she's come from England.

speaker: Bárid
en: Yes. Eivor is helping to establish trade in Dublin. Secure valuable resources with far away lands. In time, Dublin will become the heart of Ireland's trade, one that each and every kingdom can benefit from.

speaker: Ciara
en: That will no doubt please the future High King.

speaker: Bárid
en: Yes, well, above trade, I am hoping Flann can see Dublin as a friend and ally.

speaker: Ciara
en: You and many others.

speaker: Eivor
en: A relationship with Bárid would be one worth fostering. It would be foolish of your king to ignore it.

speaker: Ciara
en: It appears Eivor is not abreast with our kingly history, Bárid.

speaker: Bárid
en: We were hoping to have a meeting with Flann. My wish is to strengthen our ties. Can you see it done?

speaker: Ciara
en: Perhaps. We will see how the evening goes.

speaker: Ciara
en: Quite the event, hm?

speaker: Bárid
en: Spared no expense, that much is clear.

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: Ara (Ah), my lady, one of the priests has gone missing. A violent mess is left of his tent. I fear something terrible has happened.

speaker: Ciara
en: Missing? Are you sure?

speaker: Eivor
en: Could be nothing. Could mean danger. Where is Flann?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: He's not yet arrived.

speaker: Eivor
en: That gives us some time. Ciara, act as if nothing were amiss. Bárid and I will look into it. Where is this tent?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: Up the hill to the left.

speaker: Ciara
en: Be careful.

speaker: Eivor
en: There was a fight here.

speaker: Bárid
en: It is the eve of the coronation and already trouble brews.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep your wits and stay close. We do not know anything yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Something dark happened here. We must follow the blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: Animal carcasses. We'll go back and follow another trail.

speaker: Eivor
en: A succulent roast. Let us go back and follow another trail.

speaker: Bárid
en: The blood leads off away from the main camp. Perhaps towards those tents.

speaker: Eivor
en: The blood stops here. Where do these cart tracks lead?

speaker: Bárid
en: This story is like to have a poor ending.

speaker: Eivor
en: I fear so, cousin.

speaker: Bárid
en: On such a momentous day as well. Flann's coronation may not be as hoped.

speaker: Eivor
en: There. A cart up ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like they hit a snag. Recognize him?

speaker: Bárid
en: That is Senan. The priests. Bastards stripped him of his clothes.

speaker: Eivor
en: That camp up there. What is it?

speaker: Bárid
en: Annagh Doo is no camp. Though it appears someone has made it into one.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's go.

speaker: Bárid
en: What do you think?

speaker: Eivor
en: The priest was kidnapped. They took his clothes. I believe whoever did this means to wear them.

speaker: Bárid
en: A disguise?

speaker: Eivor
en: We will soon find out.

speaker: Eivor
en: There. And that one is dressed as the priest. Follow my lead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sent to kill Flann. The letter is unsigned. An unknown enemy. Come. We must bring news of this to Ciara.

speaker: Bárid
en: I'm with you. You handled yourself well, Eivor, I have to say. You really are no stranger to these sorts of encounters.

speaker: Eivor
en: You did not do so bad yourself.

speaker: Bárid
en: Aye. We stopped the death of a king this day. If only we knew who was behind it.

speaker: Eivor
en: No idea who would go to such lengths.

speaker: Bárid
en: You can take your picks of the Northern Uí Néill kings. Though it is the kings of Ulster who particularly dislike Flann.

speaker: Eivor
en: Different king, same story.

speaker: Ciara
en: You're back.

speaker: Ciara
en: Any story?

speaker: Eivor
en: The priest is dead, and so too are his killers. Bandits. I found this.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's an order to kill Flann. One of them was to disguise himself as a priest, cut Flann's throat during the coronation.

speaker: Bárid
en: Right under our noses.

speaker: Ciara
en: Why take the risk? Why not poison? Or striking at him in his sleep?

speaker: Eivor
en: Poison can fail, and to kill him in his sleep lacks spectacle. But your point is sound. The killer would have not made it out alive. He was ready to die. Whoever plotted this is intent on seeing Flann fall. We need to warn him.

speaker: Ciara
en: After the coronation. I will not have this gnawing at him. Flann earned this. He will enjoy it. Meet him afterwards at his quarters in Durrow. He will make time for you there.

speaker: Ciara
en: Now if you take my excuses, I need to tidy up.

speaker: Bárid
en: Come along, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: The water was not that murky, was it?

speaker: Ciara
en: You don't know much about the role of the poetess, do you, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Enlighten me.

speaker: Ciara
en: I will.

speaker: Ciara
en: Well, what are you waiting for? I asked to be excused, that meant you as well.

speaker: Bárid
en: I see other kings here. News of Flann's inauguration has reached far and wide. Come, we should join them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that him? Flann?

speaker: Bárid
en: Yes.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are they doing?

speaker: Bárid
en: Blessing him. Abbot Eogan is the highest ranking official among the Christians. His blessing asserts that Flann is ready to fill the boots of his predecessor.

speaker: Bárid
en: It is all done before the Lia Fáil, a sacred stone that is said to endow the rightful kings with long reigns.

speaker: Eivor
en: Does it work?

speaker: Bárid
en: Depends on what you consider long.

speaker: Eivor
en: Coronations are long. Where is the food?

speaker: Bárid
en: You have not changed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here. I may as well enjoy myself.

speaker: Ciara
en: Flann for Éirinn i tig thocaid , do nach - forcraid forba niäd náir co nertgail. Rop slán, rop suthain a ríge, réim co abra, noco-géba brí na rí bas amra. (Flann over Ireland from the blessed house of Túathal Techtmar, where the heredity of a noble warrior with mighty bravery is not exaggerated. May his kingship be healthy, may it last for long, a course as broad as the borders; no greater king shall ever seize the hill-top or Brega.)

speaker: Ciara
en: Filleam glúine, tócbam láma – lúad cen chréidim, corop suthain slicht no-d-bágaimm: Flann for Éirinn. Flann for Éirinn. (Let us bend our knees, let us raise our hands – give praise with no decrease, so that the family line I here boast, may last forever: Flann over Ireland. Flann over Ireland.)

speaker: Bárid
en: And with that, Flann's enemies multiply.

speaker: Eivor
en: This warring of dynasties runs deep. If he's a smart king, he'll be eager for allies.

speaker: Bárid
en: Smart he is, but also impassioned. His plan to subdue the North is not driven by power so much as it is bloodlust.

speaker: Eivor
en: Back there on our ride from Dublin, Ciara made it seem there was more to you and Flann. What am I missing?

speaker: Bárid
en: A detail. A large detail. You see, the northern king who crowned me, Áed Findliath... he murdered Flann's father and took his place as High King. Then, as is custom, he married Flann's mother.

speaker: Eivor
en: Safe to say there is no lost love between you.

speaker: Bárid
en: None. To Flann, Áed was a venomous snake and so too are the ones he favored. Winning his trust will be no simple task.

speaker: Eivor
en: We just thwarted an attempt on his life. That should at least perk his ears up.

speaker: Bárid
en: Let us hope. I will leave immediately for Durrow. Meet me there, soon as you can.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Arne! Fly up, Arne! You can do it, pet! Come on! Come on, we did not train all that time for nothing! Arne! Fly! Fly to me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Dropped something?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Good ol' Arne, my beloved pet, fell down... well, flew his way down below. Now, the poor thing is stuck. I cannot seem to encourage my Arne to fly back up. Looks like we still have a long way to go.

speaker: Eivor
en: It cannot fly. I will have to lead it back up.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Watch out for his... affections. Arne is the fiery sort, loves to give... kisses. Please don't kill him if he pecks you a bit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop that.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Stop pecking, Arne!

speaker: Eivor
en: By Odin, this bird is as foul as they come.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Your voice is beautiful, Arne!

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Thank you for bringing Arne back into my arms! I would like to repay your kindness. I have what is left of Arne's family. Unfortunately, they didn't survive their training quite as well. Try it, they're quite delicious!

speaker: Norse Woman
en: I guess I will go back to my friends, the Toothbreakers. I hope they still wait for me at the port! Come on, Arne. Let us take flight.

speaker: Eivor
en: A winged companion is a boon.

speaker: Eivor
en: You can fly to Helheim.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Arne! Bah, Loki's arse.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: I suppose it was his fate. He was one of the slower ones. I guess I will go back to my friends, the Toothbreakers. I hope they still wait for me at the port!

speaker: Andhrimnir
en: Who will join us on this wild hunt? Which among you hunger for a challenge. Who here has an appetite for adventure?

speaker: Havi
en: Hail, Andhrimnir! Off again to hunt the Immortal Boar?

speaker: Andhrimnir
en: Yes. Yet again, Saehrimnir has risen from his bones and escaped my kitchen. It should prove to be a vigorous chase.

speaker: Havi
en: You never tire of tracking this beast.

speaker: Andhrimnir
en: No hunt is more thrilling, and his meat has no equal. Come!

speaker: Andhrimnir
en: Run! Run, you sluggards! Have you no appetite? This meat is not to be missed! Take care! He is cunning! Saehrimnir is as deadly as he is delicious! It is worth risking death for the meal of your life!

speaker: Boar Hunter
en: Ha, Ha! What a beast! What a monster! O, I have never felt more alive!

speaker: Boar Huntress
en: I can almost taste its flesh! I hunger for a haunch!

speaker: Andhrimnir
en: Skillfully done, Lore-Keeper! I will save you the juiciest cut! Come, you brave butchers! Let us prepare a true heroes' feast!

speaker: Bárid
en: Ah! Eivor! Look at me, part of Flann's war council! Not bad for a vikingr, eh?

speaker: Eivor
en: You have gained his trust?

speaker: Bárid
en: I wouldn't say that, no. He's a bit suspicious of me, in fact. But he needs my army, so he holds his nose.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course he does. Vikings smell.

speaker: Bárid
en: My king.

speaker: Flann
en: We are ready to deliver Aileach a weighty blow. But our enemies are now alerted and will rally in greater numbers.

speaker: Bárid
en: Cashelore castle divides Ulster and Connacht. Taking it would isolate each from each.

speaker: Flann
