en: Cashelore is the stepping stone to all the North. It is an imposing fortress atop a steep cliff. It must be ours.

speaker: Bárid
en: But for that very reason, lord, it will cost us dearly to storm it.

speaker: Flann
en: Loss of men is a price well paid. Victory will bring many more flocking to our cause.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take care, king. Your ambition may overleap your reason.

speaker: Bárid
en: What is your counsel, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Cunning over courage. A single spy slips in and breaks the gate locks. Then our soldier floods in.

speaker: Flann
en: It is worth the attempt. You have seem to have a feel for this, Eivor. I select you as this "single spy."

speaker: Bárid
en: Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a good challenge.

speaker: Flann
en: We have a scout near the castle. She may be able to help you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those defenses could stop the gods!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hej! Are you Flann's scout?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: You are a bold adventurer to ask in these parts. Yes, I am.

speaker: Eivor
en: How might I enter the castle?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Alone? You can try to climb its walls, a foolhardy move for such a small force.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is there a way to enter unseen?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: There must be a path below. Builders down there have reinforced the walls. A wily vikingr could use their equipment to find a way in.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am that vikingr!

speaker: Flann
en: Bravely done, Eivor. Cashelore will be ours!

speaker: Bárid
en: Eivor! I have your back!

speaker: Eivor
en: I count on you, cousin.

speaker: Eivor
en: Flann! Watch our flank!

speaker: Flann
en: Press on, Eivor! Press on!

speaker: Flann
en: Upp! Eivor! Help me open this!

speaker: Eivor
en: Yours for the taking!

speaker: Bárid
en: Sack the castle!'

speaker: Flann
en: Co búaid! (To victory!)

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: Stay back, you puny Dane.

speaker: Flann
en: Sláinte! (Cheers!) To a battle well fought, and blood well spilt!

speaker: Bárid
en: To Ireland!

speaker: Eivor
en: Skal!

speaker: Flann
en: Ah!

speaker: Moenach
en: Another cup, my king?

speaker: Flann
en: Where is our court poet? This deserves a song. Eivor, it is essential that you speak with her.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ciara? Is she here?

speaker: Flann
en: I greeted her arrival. She will build my glory throughout Ireland. Her song will be repeated in every village and hamlet. And you, Eivor, with your keen eye, can give details of my bravery, the bravery of all my soldiers, for her to craft a ballad.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll give her your message, O brave king. Bárid, you deserve another drink.

speaker: Bárid
en: And you as well! Come back for another before the night is out.

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: Then he come at me, eyes blazin' like hellfire itself.

speaker: Irish Soldier 3
en: Sure, sure he did. I saw it happen.

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: I'd nothin' but a stick! Well, I held it crosswise and I hoped for the best.

speaker: Irish Soldier 3
en: I tried to help. I was too far, I was.

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: He swung and sent the stick to splinters. He grabs me collar, he's about to land the mortal blow!

speaker: Irish Soldier 3
en: O, I thought your tune was played.

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: I look him in the eye and he says, "Is it yourself, Ronan?" He knew me! It's me cousin, Conall!

speaker: Irish Soldier 3
en: It was marvelous to see! Ol' Connall. Always the good lad.

speaker: Eivor
en: You sing with conviction.

speaker: Ciara
en: It is the mournful song of the Lia Fáil, the ancient stone you saw at the coronation.

speaker: Eivor
en: That stone, it seemed to... It...

speaker: Ciara
en: The legend is that the stone will bring woe. But the song claims that if Ireland came to peril, the stone would rain a storm of wonders.

speaker: Eivor
en: From where would the song draw this wisdom?

speaker: Ciara
en: I do not know, but my mother sang it. My mother's mother sang it as well, and her mother, and hers. Back to the very first women of the isle. The mere sound of the words connects me to my ancestors and this fertile soil.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are lucky, I've left my land far behind.

speaker: Ciara
en: You need not leave to feel the land change beneath you. That's why I'm stuck in this court like some sort of dancing goat.

speaker: Eivor
en: Surely you can leave any time you wish.

speaker: Ciara
en: I can, and I will. But not until Flann rules all Ireland.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is he such a great man as that?

speaker: Ciara
en: He understand that to be king is to be king of all. Though I'm pagan, he made me court poet. He respects the old ways.

speaker: Eivor
en: I admire your passion.

speaker: Ciara
en: Thank you for that. Not everyone is so appreciative.

speaker: Eivor
en: I appreciate you for all your qualities, Ciara.

speaker: Ciara
en: I've got more than a fine voice for singing, if that's what you're asking. Is that what you're asking?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm asking if you'd like to take advantage of a Norse who finds herself alone with a bewitching Irish woman.

speaker: Ciara
en: Ara, don't you have a way with words, Eivor? And I'm not saying never...

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem to have set your course and steer it true.

speaker: Ciara
en: I come from the back country. We follow the old ways. Christians worry about the world to come. We live in the one we have.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take care you do not place all your hopes in a single person.

speaker: Ciara
en: Ach, he's not without flaws, that one. But he can unite the island and protect my people.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ja, I all but forgot. Flann sent me to remind you to begin his ballad.

speaker: Ciara
en: He needn't worry. I know my purpose here.

speaker: Eivor
en: If it is as glorious as that song was lovely, Flann is certain to gain many followers.

speaker: Ciara
en: Good night, Eivor. I'll see you in the morning. Slán. (Be safe.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Good night, Ciara.

speaker: Eivor
en: A beautiful morning... Ah! Bárid asked me to return to him last night. I should apologize.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Havi! Tell this rump-cloud that he can't just wander about Asgard, poking his pecker in every cavern he pleases!

speaker: The Builder
en: I was only curious, dwarf. I meant no offense. I am merely a seeker of knowledge.

speaker: Havi
en: The dwarves give nothing away for free.

speaker: The Builder
en: Apologies for the distraction, master blacksmith. I'll leave you to your work.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Well, what shall I craft for you today, High One? Bottomless breeches for soiling yourself on the battlefield?

speaker: Havi
en: What were you and the Builder discussing?

speaker: Havi
en: Have you ever heard of hugr (mind) magic?

speaker: Havi
en: Do your people believe they will survive the final battle?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Havi, my gentle jailor. You know we dwarves give nothing away for free. If you want your question answered, I'll need something in return.

speaker: Havi
en: Such as?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: A hidden fact known only to you, Far-Seer, that I may share in your secret knowledge of the world.

speaker: Havi
en: The sun and moon are pulled by two horses across the and skies. are their names. And each morning's dew is the fallen slobber from Hrimfaxi's foaming mouth.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Curious. Thank you, Havi.

speaker: Havi
en: The winds that blow over the sea are stirred by the wings of a great eagle named , who sits at the edge of the sky.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Interesting indeed. I have often wondered at its source.

speaker: Havi
en: The humans will survive Ragnarök in force, in , eating morning dew until their race is renewed.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: The humans are a hearty people indeed, much stronger than we give them credit for.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: So, you asked what that sack of sheep guts was after? He wanted to know how magic affected your hugr (mind).

speaker: Havi
en: Why would he want to know the effect of magic on my spirit?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Not just you, Havi. The lot of you! Æsir and Vanir alike. I told him to shovel his shit somewhere else.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: So, you asked about hugr (mind) magic. That is Jötnar business. They can move a man's mind from one place to another. But they only dabble from what I know. Like wee boys playing with fire... don't know a wick from their dick.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: As for your answer, many dwarves will die in the final battle. Ground into earth and reclaimed by the mountains.

speaker: Havi
en: You talk of blood and bone, but I speak of your hugr. (mind) Can your spirit survive when life leaves the body?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Some say their hugr (mind) enters the items they craft, others believe they live on in song. Personally, I don't give a rat's ass for philosophy.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Now if that's all you came to know, you can piss off and let me work.

speaker: Havi
en: I have one more need. Can you forge me an unbreakable chain?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Chains are overrated. One weak link and it's worthless. Let me craft a cord that Thor himself could not break.

speaker: Havi
en: It must be strong enough to bind a powerful beast.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: I will sluice my sweat into this cord, Havi. All knowledge I have and skill I own will define it. And what will I get in return?

speaker: Havi
en: Make good on your claim and your contract is fulfilled.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: I smell bait, what's the trap?

speaker: Havi
en: No trap, no trickery. Forge me this cord, and you shall be free of my service.

speaker: Havi
en: My thanks and my hospitality. What more could you need?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Bah. You cannot barter with a man who's squeezing your balls.

speaker: Havi
en: You may always return to the Land of Fire, Ivaldi. And die as your brothers did. Roasted on a spit.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Hm... to craft such a cord, I'll need a few impossible ingredients.

speaker: Havi
en: Name them.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Eye the list there. I have a bear's tendon, a fish's breath, and...

speaker: Havi
en: "A cat's footsteps" and "the root of a mountain". How do I find these?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: How the fuck would I know? The riddles will guide you.

speaker: Havi
en: I have no patience for riddles, dwarf.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Those riddles are as ancient as the world. With lore passed down from Nyi and Nithi to Northri and Suthri, Austri and Vestri, Althjof...

speaker: Havi
en: I understand. I will return shortly.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: ...Dvalin, Bivor, Bavor, Bombur, Nori, An and Anar, Ai, Mjothvitnir, Veig and Gandalf, Vindalf, Thrain, Thekk and Thorin, Thror, Vit, and Lit, Nar and Nyrath, Regin and Rathsvith...

speaker: Havi
en: He's made the base already? The Builder works fast. A bit too fast.

speaker: Havi
en: How is he building that tower so quickly? There's more to this stranger than meets the eye.

speaker: Havi
en: Let's see what you can make of these, Ivaldi.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Aha! I know a cat's footfall when I hear one. Bring it here.

speaker: Havi
en: I found everything you asked for.

speaker: Havi
en: How soon can you finish this unbreakable cord?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: As soon as it wants to be made. You cannot rush this kind of magic. It flows with a speed all its own.

speaker: Havi
en: Find me as soon as it's ready.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: By the way, after we spoke of the hugr, a cousin came by with his own spirit tale. I don't trust coincidence, so this one's free.

speaker: Havi
en: What did he say?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: He told me his sister's husband Borìn drank a mead brewed in Jotunheim... and it sent his hugr into a goat!

speaker: Havi
en: The spirit of a dwarf in the body of a goat?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Stranger still, his sister didn't even notice!

speaker: Freyja
en: Havi!

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Don't drag me into this!

speaker: Freyja
en: The tower is nearly finished!

speaker: Havi
en: Do not fret. The final hours are ticking down.

speaker: Freyja
en: Not fast enough. I feel the jaws of a trap closing upon me.

speaker: Havi
en: Knowing you are in a trap is the first step to avoiding it.

speaker: Freyja
en: You don't care if I'm married off to this Builder, do you?

speaker: Havi
en: You are the Queen of Asgard, the Host of Fólkvangr, the shepherd-of-the-slain. Of course I care.

speaker: Freyja
en: Yet you act as if I'm some treasure to be traded about.

speaker: Havi
en: It does not worry me. He would not live beyond his wedding night. You would see to that.

speaker: Freyja
en: Mad Deceiver, I should neuter you and make you his bride!

speaker: Havi
en: Have no fear, Freyja. Whatever things transpire today, you marrying the Builder will not be among them.

speaker: Freyja
en: At least have the sense to admit you betrayed my trust!

speaker: Havi
en: I was wrong to use you like that. I will confront the Builder and pry the truth out of him.

speaker: Freyja
en: A limp apology, but it will suffice for now.

speaker: Freyja
en: Once the Builder is dealt with, turn your spear on Loki. Every chance he had, he dug us deeper into this mess.

speaker: Havi
en: If Loki is up to something, I will see to it that he is punished, blood-oath be damned.

speaker: Havi
en: I must speak with Brokkr.

speaker: Havi
en: The dwarves have come up with a crafty way to cross the lake.

speaker: Vesall
en: Sindri, you son of a rock, where did you hide your tools? How can I tell Brokkr we're missing the tools? I'll cut down that oak tree now Sindri is gone. Can't stand the sight of it without him here.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive
en: I hear Vesall can't find the master's tools. It's too horrible to even think about. Now Brokkr is all alone. How will he manage without his big brother to guide him? Last time I saw the master, he was sitting under his oak tree, roasting his acorns, oiling his favorite hammer.

speaker: Havi
en: I must find a way to ease Brokkr's sorrow. And make him amenable to my wishes.

speaker: Brokkr
en: You lied to me. You said you would save him.

speaker: Havi
en: I said I would find him.

speaker: Brokkr
en: That ain't my brother. Not any more.

speaker: Brokkr
en: What happened? Tell me. Everything.

speaker: Havi
en: As I neared the village, I... I heard a great roar. Like that of a wounded bear. Soon after, I witnessed the final act of a mighty battle. Sindri beset by giants on all sides. It was he who made the god-like roars.

speaker: Brokkr
en: He... he always did have a deep voice.

speaker: Havi
en: He wielded his hammer and chisel with uncommon skill.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Yes... yes! I have seen him do it many times in the workshop.

speaker: Havi
en: Giants lay strewn about. Slain by Sindri's hand. But then... One, of cowardly aspect, struck your brother treacherously in the back. Yet even as Sindri succumbed to the blow, he lobbed his chisel and struck the coward dead. Right between the eyes.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Sindri did all that?

speaker: Havi
en: So it will be written.

speaker: Vesall
en: Where could they be?

speaker: Havi
en: Is something wrong, Vesall?

speaker: Vesall
en: Everything is wrong! We're burying the greatest smith who ever lived and we don't have his tools to put with him.

speaker: Havi
en: I came across some at Alethorp. If you want I can fetch―

speaker: Vesall
en: Those were just the spares. He never took his best ones from the shelter.

speaker: Havi
en: I see. How is it that such valuable instruments have been misplaced?

speaker: Vesall
en: Misplaced? Don't be daft. Hidden, more like.

speaker: Havi
en: By Sindri?

speaker: Vesall
en: To make sure no one else ever touched him. Particularly Brokkr. Except now we can't find them!

speaker: Havi
en: You have no idea where they might be?

speaker: Vesall
en: Well, they ain't inside the shelter, I can tell you that. But they can't be too far. Wouldn't be surprised if they're somewhere up high.

speaker: Havi
en: I thought dwarves were afraid of heights.

speaker: Vesall
en: Not our Sindri. He was quite the climber. Now me, well, I prefer to keep my feet on the ground. Right where they should be.

speaker: Brokkr
en: How can I talk with you when my heart is torn asunder?

speaker: Havi
en: I am very fond of the dwarves. Yet their constant needs... It is exhausting. Oh Loki, friend, betrayer... What I'd give for a moment of your gilded conversation. Even the lies.

speaker: Havi
en: If I was Sindri, where would I hide my beloved tools? Somewhere high up perhaps?

speaker: Havi
en: A majestic oak... Surely this is Sindri's beloved acorn tree?

speaker: Havi
en: That nest looks like a promising hidey-hole. If I had wings, I could reach it easily enough.

speaker: Havi
en: Finally. The tools of Sindri's trade.

speaker: Havi
en: I must reunite these tools with Sindri's remains before the ceremony begins.

speaker: Havi
en: The disaster has been averted.

speaker: Vesall
en: Now I see why some call you "god."

speaker: Havi
en: You're making me blush. Still, I have my moments.

speaker: Havi
en: Heroes die. But not their legacy. Such was Sindri's courage that tonight he feasts in Valhalla, the first of his kind to ever do so.

speaker: Havi
en: Ivaldi has come. Perhaps he can be of use.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: I'm here for the mead, not the company.

speaker: Havi
en: You dwarves and your love of mead. It's caused me enough trouble already.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: It wasn't a dwarf who ransacked half of Jötunheim in search of some mysterious mead.

speaker: Havi
en: I wouldn't know anything about that.

speaker: Havi
en: You know, old friend, now would be a good time for some grand gesture.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Like what?

speaker: Havi
en: A respectful speech from you, Sindri's greatest rival, would surely―

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Fuck off.

speaker: Havi
en: We must all make compromises. I can even give you the honeyed words...

speaker: Havi
en: Time soothes the well of suffering. Brings hope that sees beyond chill death. Recasts the whirlpool of sorrow into the placid waters of the philosophic mind.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Are those words for Sindri or Baldr?

speaker: Havi
en: Baldr lives! Why would he need such words?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Of course, of course. I didn't mean to... well, you know.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Fine, I'll do the speech. But it will be one of my making, not yours. We dwarves don't care much for poetry. Still, we can't set about making speeches until the torches are all lit up.

speaker: Havi
en: Who knows how long it will take before the dwarves get around to lighting the torches. It will be faster if I do it.

speaker: Havi
en: The dwarves have saved a place for me. This is a great honor that they bestow.

speaker: Brokkr
en: My brother... A true master... He was...

speaker: Ivaldi
en: I did not like Sindri and he did not like me. Still, he was good with a hammer. And a chisel. And a saw. And he knew how to work the bellows... some said better than anyone. Even me. Brokkr, your brother was a fine smithy. I... I admired him greatly.

speaker: Havi
en: Master Brokkr, you've given Sindri an excellent send-off.

speaker: Brokkr
en: It's the least he deserves... But is it really true he feasts in Valhalla?

speaker: Havi
en: It is. I saw it in a vision. Come, let's take a stroll.

speaker: Havi
en: Now, tell me, are you prepared to continue Sindri's good work?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Helping Ivaldi was not my brother's work.

speaker: Havi
en: But defying Surtr was. It's what got him killed.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Greed for mead is what got him killed.

speaker: Havi
en: It took courage to go after that mead. A direct challenge to Surtr's authority.

speaker: Brokkr
en: This is crooked thinking.

speaker: Havi
en: Seems straight enough for me.

speaker: Brokkr
en: ...You know, I don't reckon I owe you a bloody thing.

speaker: Havi
en: I risked my life to retrieve your brother's body. Now I prepare to risk it again. For you and all of Svartalfheim.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Bollocks. You ain't doing anything out of the goodness of your heart. I know what you're after. I know all about your lad Baldr. I have ears, you know. Even in my grief. So, don't pretend you're here for us because I―

speaker: Havi
en: Would you have me abandon my own son and strive only for your salvation?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Okay, when you say it like that... I... I need time... I'm still grieving, you know. Let me think on it. Alright? A little old think.

speaker: Havi
en: I should check on Brokkr. See if he has come to his senses. If he hasn't, I must... encourage him further.

speaker: Rhine Champion
en: You will die on these swords, invader!

speaker: Eivor
en: What a handsome cat. Hello, friend of Freyja. What's wrong?

speaker: Norse Child
en: Hey, Nali! Come back, you sneak!

speaker: Norse Child
en: No, stop! Aw, pig poop! He ran off again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cats are free spirits, aloof and haughty, like the goddess Freyja.

speaker: Norse Child
en: I know. But ever since old Kottr, that old sea-cat has run wild, scaring the chickens and scratching me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. Ship's cats are good luck. Do you need help catching him?

speaker: Norse Child
en: O, yes, please.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hey!

speaker: Norse Child
en: Aww, pig poop! He got past me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Here, little one!

speaker: Eivor
en: Got you, little mouse-biter.

speaker: Norse Child
en: Wow! Nali hasn't let anyone touch him since old Kottr died. But he sure loves you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you want to join my crew, Nali? You would make a fine raider, I think. Every longship needs a brave cat for luck, and for the rats.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like I have another raider.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hello, Nali. You're settling in well. Now earn your keep.

speaker: Flann
en: At the ready. We march soon.

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: Where do you hail from?

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: Southern Uí Néill.

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: Ah, I know it. Many's the winter I spent there as a boy. O, those honeyed oat cakes!

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: Fill you up morning 'til night, that's sure. And yourself?

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: Brega.

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: Ah. Small wonder you came down for the winters. Cold as the hangman's heart up there.

speaker: Flann
en: The missing piece has arrived.

speaker: Flann
en: Welcome, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lord. This has the looks of a Norse war camp. Plenty of stout-looking men.

speaker: Flann
en: The fruits of your labor, Eivor. The kings you've helped have sent men and more as tribute. You have my thanks.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank me later. A battle looms.

speaker: Flann
en: True enough. Your cousin awaits inside the tent of command. I'll soon follow to plan our next move.

speaker: Havi
en: Baldr, do you think I fear fate? No, you and I, we forge our own paths... we are fate.

speaker: Halstein
en: Havi? Are you well? Havi's not well.

speaker: Havi
en: A passing weakness. It's nothing. We should continue.

speaker: Halstein
en: Are you sure? We could rest a while.

speaker: Havi
en: They kidnapped my son! Murdered his mother! I will not rest till I repay these wrongs!

speaker: Havi
en: Forgive me. You lifted me from that flyblown Hel, set me on my feet again. You do not deserve my rage.

speaker: Sigrun
en: And you do not belong among the dead. Not yet. Now, come on. Your gift awaits.

speaker: Havi
en: You still have not told me the nature of this gift, nor why you offer it.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Its nature you will know soon enough. As to why... well, you have seen the suffering the Muspels brought to Svartalfheim.

speaker: Halstein
en: Fire and ruin and slaughter. They made wasteland of our green meadows, and enslaved those they didn't kill.

speaker: Havi
en: They keep your people as slaves?

speaker: Halstein
en: Aye. Surtr works them for some dark purpose of his own. What that is, we don't yet know.

speaker: Sigrun
en: We can't fight them, Havi. Our people are broken, forced into hiding. But now the tides of fate have washed the Lord of Asgard to our shores.

speaker: Havi
en: I'm not your savior. I mean only to find my son and return him.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Rid us of Surtr, and you might save us nonetheless. That is why we offer you our gift.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Look upon the splendor of our halls, Havi.

speaker: Havi
en: A sight to stir a careworn heart. In all the Nine Worlds, the crafters of Svartalfheim have no equal.

speaker: Halstein
en: A Muspel! Oh, hammer and tongs, they're here!

speaker: Sigrun
en: They're looking for the gift!

speaker: Havi
en: This dolt dares to steal a gift intended for me?

speaker: Sigrun
en: Havi, you have to stop them!

speaker: Havi
en: With pleasure. Keep back. I will deal with this.

speaker: Halstein
en: Well done, Havi!

speaker: Sigrun
en: We should search around here. Hopefully with better luck than that Muspel.

speaker: Sigrun
en: It must be around here somewhere!

speaker: Havi
en: What are we looking for? I see nothing but stone.

speaker: Sigrun
en: There should be a hidden catch... It's somewhere... right about... here!

speaker: Sigrun
en: Take it, Lord of Asgard. Put it on. From the dwarves of Svartalfheim to you.

speaker: Havi
en: This is a mighty gift, indeed.

speaker: Halstein
en: Told you they'd like it.

speaker: Havi
en: With this bracer, you can draw out the essence of fallen foes. Steal their powers and make them your own. Try it now, with that Muspel you killed.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Havi, you must absorb the power of the Muspel.

speaker: Havi
en: I feel it! Fire charges my blood!

speaker: Sigrun
en: Aye, but you'll need more of it before you can take on their powers. Let's keep moving.

speaker: Halstein
en: Best keep moving!

speaker: Muspel Warrior
en: It's the Æsir! Sound the alarm!

speaker: Halstein
en: Here they come! Protect us, Havi!

speaker: Muspel Warrior
en: Spawn of Asgard! Flame and ash take you!

speaker: Sigrun
en: Yes, Havi! Absorb the essence of those you slay to charge the bracer.

speaker: Havi
en: A powerful incentive to kill the enemies of the dwarves.

speaker: Halstein
en: Aye, it's almost as if we planned it or something.

speaker: Halstein
en: The door's blocked! Barred from the other side!

speaker: Sigrun
en: Calm yourself, sparrow-heart! Havi will find us a way around.

speaker: Halstein
en: Let's be about our business quick! Where there's one Muspel, there'll be others.

speaker: Havi
en: Let them come. I have death enough for all.

speaker: Havi
en: I drew upon the Muspel's power, and the lava did not harm me. What other gifts might this bracer grant me?

speaker: Sigrun
en: Havi? Are you there? Open the door!

speaker: Halstein
en: They're taking too long! Oh, what if the Muspels got them? We're doomed!

speaker: Sigrun
en: Stop your fretting. They'll be here.

speaker: Halstein
en: I knew you could do it! Didn't I tell you, Sigrun?

speaker: Sigrun
en: Aye, sure. You never doubted for an instant. Havi, your bracer's magic will run dry if you do not replenish it. Look around. See if there's something here that will help you to do so.

speaker: Havi
en: The bracer feels weak. Drained of power... Perhaps remnants of hugr abide in that shrine. I should check.

speaker: Havi
en: The bracer grows weak. I must find a way to revitalize it.

speaker: Havi
en: I can sense the bracer... speaking to the shrine. As if they are alive to one another. The bracer grows strong once more.

speaker: Halstein
en: No, Havi, not the shrine! It is sacred!

speaker: Havi
en: Nothing is sacred anymore.

speaker: Sigrun
en: We must hurry. If the enemy found these hidden halls, they can find the shelter.

speaker: Havi
en: Shelter?

speaker: Halstein
en: A sanctuary. A secret hideaway only the dwarves know. When the invasion began, our people took refuge in such places.

speaker: Havi
en: But the threat of discovery means we're always on the move. Halstein and I left our own shelter in search of resources. When we returned...

speaker: Halstein
en: Everyone was gone! Leaving nothing but a secret sign to show us how to follow.

speaker: Havi
en: That shelter is somewhere nearby. We'd better find our companions before the Muspels do.

speaker: Halstein
en: Another door? By Ymir's bones! What we've done to deserve this?

speaker: Havi
en: Those flowers.... Like the shrine, they call out to the bracer... though their voices are but faint.

speaker: Sigrun
en: The High One always finds a way, no matter the obstacle.

speaker: Havi
en: Obstacle? It was just a door, Sigrun.

speaker: Havi
en: These flowers are useful when it comes to revitalizing my powers.

speaker: Halstein
en: The floor... it's gone.

speaker: Sigrun
en: If that block of stone was closer, we could make the jump. The Muspels and their fire-sludge. It's everywhere.

speaker: Havi
en: I will move that block nearer so we can make it across.

speaker: Halstein
en: Thanks, Havi! I knew you wouldn't let us down!

speaker: Havi
en: And I never will. You saved my life not so long ago... I will forever be in your debt.

speaker: Halstein
en: Havi, the bracer... It allowed you to take on the guise of a Muspel.

speaker: Havi
en: Then I shall use this new trick to my advantage. I will walk among them, yet not be one of them.

speaker: Halstein
en: Havi, do you see those guards ahead? Why don't you approach as if one of them, and then give them a big nasty surprise?

speaker: Sigrun
en: Well done, Havi. Now, let's be on our way.

speaker: Havi
en: Sinmara.

speaker: Sinmara
en: I thought I heard the mewing of an Aesir kitten. My husband should have stamped on you when he had the chance. But mercy is no flaw of mine.

speaker: Havi
en: I will see red vengeance on all of you for what you have done.

speaker: Sinmara
en: And I will enjoy watching you fail.

speaker: Sinmara
en: You should have stayed in Asgard!

speaker: Sinmara
en: You fight well. Better than your woman, at least.

speaker: Havi
en: Come at me, then! Let's finish this!

speaker: Sinmara
en: Oh, I'll be back. I will hunt you to the far corners of the Nine Worlds. Treasure every moment, Havi, for death is at your heels, and you know not the hour it will find you.

speaker: Havi
en: Sinmara! Damn you to Hel!

speaker: Halstein
en: You beat Sinmara! I'd never dreamed I'd see it! Fate has truly sent us a hero!

speaker: Havi
en: Fate bends to my will. Now, show me to this shelter of yours.

speaker: Sigrun
en: The sign they left us spoke of a hidden path. Look around in the woods. That will set us on our way.

speaker: Sigrun
en: That symbol! A dwarf-mark. It points the way to the shelter.

speaker: Halstein
en: Let's examine the map for any clues.

speaker: Sigrun
en: See here, Havi. This is a map of Svartalfheim. You can see the shelter should be nearby. There are other shelters too. We only have a rough idea of their locations, but when you get close, you'll see the signs.

speaker: Halstein
en: I can't wait to see their faces when we arrive! Fimbar, Hroth, old Grott and his dirty beard!

speaker: Sigrun
en: Fimbar still owes me twenty silver from losing at cards. Bet he thought he'd got away with it, too.

speaker: Halstein
en: Remind me never to play you at cards.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Ha! The day you part with a coin is the day the sky falls down.

speaker: Halstein
en: Another! We must be getting close!

speaker: Havi
en: It is a hard path we walk, and well-hidden.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Has to be, or else the Muspels will find it. But day by day, they're learning to read the signs.

speaker: Halstein
en: And once that happens, no dwarf will ever be safe again.

speaker: Halstein
en: Where is the next sign? It should be here!

speaker: Sigrun
en: Hidden, perhaps? Let's look around.

speaker: Halstein
en: You found it, Havi!

speaker: Sigrun
en: Good work. Let's be on our way, then.

speaker: Sigrun
en: It can't be far now! Follow me!

speaker: Halstein
en: Wait, are you sure it's that way?

speaker: Sigrun
en: Have a little faith, Halstein. I know what I'm doing.

speaker: Sigrun
en: We are getting closer.

speaker: Halstein
en: You sure about that?

speaker: Sigrun
en: Yes. We should go left after the next sign.

speaker: Halstein
en: No, no. I'm certain it's to the right.

speaker: Sigrun
en: You are mistaken as usual. Follow my lead.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Hmm. Might be I took a wrong turn.

speaker: Halstein
en: I told you, didn't I? Less haste, more care. Let's retrace our steps.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Yes, yes, this is the right path. The Sons of Ivaldi have steered us true, I see it now.

speaker: Halstein
en: "Have a little faith, Halstein! I know what I'm doing, Halstein!"

speaker: Sigrun
en: Oh, shut your face.

speaker: Havi
en: Who are these Sons of Ivaldi you mentioned? Ivaldi is a name well known to me, but he never spoke of children.

speaker: Halstein
en: Yes, he was your slave once, wasn't he?

speaker: Sigrun
en: Halstein.

speaker: Halstein
en: Oh. Sorry. Perhaps slave wasn't the right word. Your freedom-deficient associate.

speaker: Sigrun
en: The Sons of Ivaldi are those who follow Ivaldi's teachings. We're not all male, either, though you can be sure whoever came up with the name was.

speaker: Halstein
en: Ivaldi learned much from the Aesir during his time in Asgard. Not least the value of being prepared for unexpected attack.

speaker: Sigrun
en: After his return, we set up a network of shelters. Boltholes, in case of disaster.

speaker: Halstein
en: It's thanks to us there are any dwarves left free at all. If freedom's what you can call it.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Speaking of which, first order of business is to find the chief and warn him about those Muspels. Else there'll be no one left for us to protect.

speaker: Brudd
en: Sigrun and Halstein! Well, slap my bollocks and call me an elf! You found us! And with all those Muspels on our doorstep!

speaker: Sigrun
en: You know about the Muspels?

speaker: Brudd
en: Wouldn't be much of a chief if I didn't! Hope you didn't wear yourself out coming to warn us!

speaker: Halstein
en: Actually, we kind of did...

speaker: Brudd
en: And who's this you've got with you?

speaker: Havi
en: I am Havi, called Wolf's-Bane, Raven-God, the High One of Asgard.

speaker: Brudd
en: That right? They call me Brudd. Arse-Scratcher, Snot-Snorter, He of the Crusty Toe.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Havi is here because we have an enemy in common. Surtr has taken his son captive.

speaker: Halstein
en: He fought Sinmara to a standstill. I saw it!

speaker: Brudd
en: Surtr, eh? Any enemy of that overstacked stack of hearth-sweepings is a friend of mine. Come inside. You two, get some rest.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Wait, Havi. Before you go, I have another gift. We would not have made it here without you.

speaker: Havi
en: Nor I without you, my friends. I'd say we're even.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Take this all the same. It's silica. Bring it to a blacksmith, and they will put it to good use on your behalf.

speaker: Havi
en: Thank you, Sigrun. And you, Halstein. May our paths cross again soon.

speaker: Brudd
en: Silica! You must have done something right! That stuff's rarer than hen's teeth these days.

speaker: Havi
en: The Muspels?

speaker: Brudd
en: Aye. They seized the mines, and now they guard 'em carefully, bunch of overly flammable bastards. Still, if you ever need more, you're welcome to slaughter your way to one of their stockpiles.

speaker: Havi
en: My son is in Surtr's clutches. I have no time for diversions.

speaker: Brudd
en: Might be you change your mind once you see it put to use. Let me show you our blacksmith.

speaker: Grungir
en: Salutations, Chief! Who's your friend here?

speaker: Brudd
en: They've got too many names to remember. All you need to know is, they've got silica.

speaker: Grungir
en: And a bracer of such craftsmanship as makes my hammer-arm weak with envy! That's a fine thing indeed. But maybe not so fine that it can't be enhanced somewhat. Any half decent blacksmith should be able to help you improve it. Assuming you have the right materials, of course.

speaker: Brudd
en: Others here will be glad of a stranger's silver. Look around awhile, if you like.

speaker: Havi
en: You know my purpose. I have no time to tarry here.

speaker: Brudd
en: "He asks for death who goes to battle unprepared." I'll see you at the entrance when you're ready.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 1
en: I ain't one to complain, but there is far too much work.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 2
en: The toil never ends.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 3
en: You're here to save us, High One?

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 4
en: I'd kill for a bowl of dry roasted acorns.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 5
en: I already have.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 6
en: Where did you put that scroll I was writing?

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 7
en: Ah... Up there in the middle... no, the left... I mean the right... Yes, definitely the right. Sort of.

speaker: Sigrun
en: We should get back to work... Svaladal awaits.

speaker: Halstein
en: Svaladal?

speaker: Sigrun
en: We may have friends stranded up there. We cannot just leave them to die.

speaker: Halstein
en: We're not heroes, Sigrun. The road to Svaladal is long and treacherous.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Have you forgotten already? We've run with the High One.

speaker: Halstein
en: We won't be running with the High One when we go to Svaladal.

speaker: Sigrun
en: Fine. Have a rest, eat something. And after, I will bend you to my will.

speaker: Brudd
en: You know, you ain't the first stranger to come around here. A while back, our scouts saw a Jotun creeping about, name of Hyrrokin.

speaker: Havi
en: Hyrrokin? No doubt she flees the wrath of Suttungr and Gunlodr. Hers was not a name I expected to hear in this place. Her presence may be an ill omen, or it might mean nothing at all.

speaker: Brudd
en: You Asgardians like to be vague, don't you? Walk with me now. Let's have some straight talk.

speaker: Havi
en: One thing puzzles me. You cower in these holes like rabbits. Why not fight back?

speaker: Brudd
en: We fought at first. Fought hard. But they hit our leaders, scattered us. Once they divided us, we were done.

speaker: Havi
en: Then join together! Raise your axes and throw them off!

speaker: Brudd
en: That simple, eh? Look, we don't even know where the others are. The shelters were planned so that if one of us was caught, we couldn't give them all away. But you could find 'em, I'd wager.

speaker: Havi
en: My business is with Surtr. And rescuing my son.

speaker: Brudd
en: You might have noticed that Surtr can't be killed. Could be a problem.

speaker: Havi
en: I will find a way. Or else, I will seize what he values most, and trade it for Baldr's freedom.

speaker: Brudd
en: Either way you'll need our aid. You don't know an inch of this land. Listen, Havi. I understand. This isn't your war. You just want your son back. But those Muspels on our doorstep, they ain't no joke. If they find us, we're dead meat. Thing about Muspels, though, is they love to fight amongst themselves. All that's stopping them is fear of Surtr. Take out their leader, they'll tear themselves apart. Flee back to Muspelheim, most likely.

speaker: Havi
en: And Svartalfheim will once again belong to the dwarves.

speaker: Brudd
en: Dwarves who'll be very, very grateful to the one who delivered them. There's more gifts where that bracer came from.

speaker: Havi
en: I make you no promise. But I will seek out your shelters. Perhaps there I will find the means to save Baldr.

speaker: Brudd
en: Good enough for now.

speaker: Brudd
en: Welcome to Svartalfheim, Havi. From here, you're on your own.

speaker: Havi
en: Hearken to the of how I slew some ice bears. I approached a group of beasts from downwind, and caught them by surprise. In short order, a great beast was upon me! A glorious battle indeed, I think you'll agree.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like more of Soma's forces followed the beacon back to camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: Galinn, is that right?

speaker: Galinn
en: That's right. And you are Eivor, the infinite fighter. Or, forever warrior. It's a glorious name.

speaker: Eivor
en: Many thanks. You were in a tight spot when we found you.

speaker: Galinn
en: Indeed. The Saxons pursued me, ran me bloody through the swamps and into the lap of bandits... then the wolves came. We all have our One Day, the day we die. How you greet that day is all that matters. I'm proud to say that I was ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, it's good to see you breathing still.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lif, Soma says you're the man who built her longships.

speaker: Lif
en: That's right. Each has a sharp keel, a stout mast, and a poem etched into the hull to sing the praises of the drengr (courageous warrior) who commands her. A longship is heavy with fate. Just a few lengths of wood between you and a watery grave. What better place to put a line of poetry, hm?

speaker: Eivor
en: Agreed. It's good to fight beside you, Lif.

speaker: Lif
en: Likewise, Eivor. Thanks again for plucking me and my warriors from the mire.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're Birna.

speaker: Birna
en: And you are Eivor, Sunbeam. You cut through the fog like the sun burns through ice.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're in high spirits, all things considered. The ambush, losing your home...

speaker: Birna
en: In this moment, yes. But, ah, you feel that? The moment has passed. We are free to pursue the next. What a gift!

speaker: Eivor
en: It is good to have you in this fight, Birna.

speaker: Birna
en: I like you, Eivor. You may help me here or step on me, and by the look of you, I'd welcome either.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: I'm burning with the wrath of Odin. We'll retake Grantebridge. Then the shire.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Wigmund's rat-soldiers killed my man in his bed. He'll be in Hel now, forever. Wigmund dies for that.

speaker: Soma
en: The day is new, and the air is bracing. Are you ready for the fight ahead?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's take your city back.

speaker: Soma
en: That's what I like to hear. Meet me at the western gate of Grantebridge. We've assembled there.

speaker: Dag
en: Have care you do not enjoy taking orders from anyone but your jarl back home. I fight for Sigurd, none else.

speaker: Eivor
en: While you're on this ship, Dag, you fight for me. And for Soma's loyalty, we fight for her.

speaker: Soma
en: Two teams, hidden. One on each side of the door. Move when you get the signal, and not a moment before.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Wigmund must know we're here.

speaker: Soma
en: As he should. I will reason with him, he will reject my offer of peace, and our conversation will have a surprise ending.

speaker: Soma
en: Wigmund! Honor-thief! I know you're up there!

speaker: Soma
en: Return Grantebridge to me, Wigmund. No more of our people need die. We may talk this out, lord to lord.

speaker: Wigmund
en: What have we to talk about? You have nothing I need. Worth by birth, heathen. I was born a noble. You were plucked from a giant's armpit!

speaker: Soma
en: I built this town! From a mud hut to a thriving port. And we both know you'll bleed those riches dry without my guiding hand.

speaker: Wigmund
en: Leave! Go die in the muck where you belong, heathens!

speaker: Soma
en: Wigmund, Wigmund. Let's try one final time... quit Grantebridge. And when she is mine once more, I may spare your life.

speaker: Wigmund
en: Pah! I command Grantebridge! I am master here! And I will scour you rats from this land like rot from a festering wound!

speaker: Soma
en: Let me give you some advice, old bear. The surest way to stop a wound from festering isn't with a blade. It's with fire.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now! Danes of Grantebridgescire! Retake what's yours!

speaker: Soma
en: Augh! Look at Grantebridge! What has Wigmund done to her?

speaker: Eivor
en: No time for that! We must free her first!

speaker: Soma
en: I haven't seen Wigmund since we breached the wall. Regroup at the longhouse. We'll surely find him there.

speaker: Soma
en: Death for any Saxon breathing!

speaker: Eivor
en: No prisoners! No mercy!

speaker: Galinn
en: These dogs will destroy the city's food supply! Protect the fields with me, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm a your side, Soma.

speaker: Soma
en: Haha! Raise your blade to me! Fucking try it!

speaker: Lif
en: The waters have calmed here! Go on, I'll weather the last of these whelps.

speaker: Soma
en: Wigmund! You cannot hide from me forever! Come face your death!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: Heathen eels! Wigmund has gone! He's gone!

speaker: Soma
en: Any man who fights for Wigmund dies!

speaker: Soma
en: Let your plague-ridden body feed my fields. Eivor, to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: No sign of Wigmund here. He may be hiding within the city walls. Shall we search?

speaker: Soma
en: No. He'll be gone, count on it. Argr (weak) coward. But we've struck a bold claim today. Walk with me. I want you to sound our battle horn to announce our victory. Let all the shire know that Grantebridge is retaken! The sound of the horn means prosperity, long life, bounty.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why me?

speaker: Soma
en: Why not? You were the keystone to this attack. You turned the tide. Let the wind from your lungs breathe life back into my city.

speaker: Soma
en: Look at you all! Warriors! Handsome! Beautiful! Blood-soaked!

speaker: Soma
en: Grantebridge is ours once again! Tomorrow you will stamp out the last of Wigmund's fading fires! But tonight... tonight, we feast as gods! Hey!

speaker: Soma
en: My clan throws the best feasts, I think you'll find. You enjoy yourself?

speaker: Eivor
en: I did. But were you celebrating or mourning? You looked unsure.

speaker: Soma
en: The night of the attack, I heard sounds of bloodshed coming from the longhouse. In moments, the city was overrun with Saxons. So I called a retreat. We all have our One Day, but not like that. Not that day.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have heard this before. That the Saxons appeared as if from the shadows.

speaker: Soma
en: In all my time in Grantebridge, this tunnel was my most careful project. The best kept secret in the city.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now a hundred or more Saxons know the smell of it.

speaker: Soma
en: The only people who knew about this tunnel were me and the three in my inner circle.

speaker: Eivor
en: You believe you were betrayed?

speaker: Soma
en: I know I was.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wigmund could have escaped in the chaos of the fight.

speaker: Soma
en: The city was teeming with my men, posted at all gates. Wigmund was shown this tunnel and used it both to enter and escape.

speaker: Eivor
en: By whom?

speaker: Soma
en: That is where I hesitate. Between Lif, Galinn, and Birna, I cannot say. But they are the three who helped me dig this in secret. I hoped you might lend me your wits. You are a fresh ally. I could use your eyes and ears.

speaker: Eivor
en: I promised you I'd help secure your city. That task isn't yet done, it seems.

speaker: Soma
en: Good. I sent Galinn, Lif, and Birna to destroy what remains of Wigmund's power throughout the shire. Meet with them, raid with them, get to know them as best as you can. Find out which of them betrayed me.

speaker: Eivor
en: A betrayal so wicked, I cannot imagine. Yet someone willing to break an oath like that must bear some sign or defect.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll do what I can. But you know your warriors far better than I do.

speaker: Soma
en: Between you and me, my heart is clouded. I love these three as if we shared a womb.

speaker: Eivor
en: You could plan your attack and see if it flushes out the traitor.

speaker: Soma
en: Too great a risk. This snake could compromise us at any time.

speaker: Soma
en: I need clear, sound judgement. I need you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have me.

speaker: Soma
en: Thank you. Feel free to take a look around as you wish. Search the city, the tunnel. And here, a gift, for retaking Grantebridge with us. One of the few things I have left from my blood family.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma. To understand your people well, I should better know you.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you rise to the rank of Jarlskona?

speaker: Soma
en: My king, Guthrum, led the Summer Army through this land. When he marched into Wessex, I volunteered to defend the city. To encourage trade so that our forces would be rich and strong if called upon. Guthrum agreed. So I grew the city up from very little and fell in love with her. It was a dagger in the heart to lose it, and a balm to have it back.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I can find your traitor, what will you do with them?

speaker: Soma
en: They will die by my hand. No pain, no public humiliation. A traitor or no, the bastard is also one of my closest people, my friend. My family. Only I will bear the burden of causing their death. It will not muddy the minds of any other. That is enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why do you love Grantebridge so deeply?

speaker: Soma
en: I was orphaned young, but old enough to remember it. I feel I've been reaching for a family all my life. Grantebridge is more than some silver boon. She's a place for me to build that family, for anyone who needs one. Wanderers, smugglers, and craftsmen alike.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have the plants you asked for. It took some effort.

speaker: Valka
en: Good, good. Thank you, Eivor.

speaker: Valka
en: Here you are. And be careful. This brew will feel as cold as ice on your lips, yet will burn like a fire in your belly.

speaker: Valka
en: Eivor. What has happened? What have you seen?

speaker: Eivor
en: Stranger things yet. But... something took me out of it, pulled me away.

speaker: Valka
en: Hm, yes, that can happen. Return when you are rested and we will try again.

speaker: Havi
en: I have things to do yet before I can leave.

speaker: Valka
en: Come, settle your mind and tell me what you have seen.

speaker: Eivor
en: Strange things, Valka. I am learning much and seeing more than my mind can understand.

speaker: Valka
en: Go on.

speaker: Eivor
en: In Jotunheim, I sought and found a mead of incredible power. It promised a strange effect. To drink it would deliver me from death. Shield me from the destruction of Ragnarök. By this mead, I hoped to live beyond my own death, well into the future.

speaker: Valka
en: Fascinating. Was that your final vision?

speaker: Eivor
en: They have not ended, not yet. Something compels me to return to Asgard.

speaker: Valka
en: The elixir is ready when you are.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Shhh!

speaker: Eivor
en: Some coins have been taken from me. Green footprints... Could be a child. What's this? There's something odd going on in these woods.

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: We've been found!

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Aw! Retreat!

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: Play with us! Come, to the land of St. Martin's! It is shrouded within an eternal twilight!

speaker: Eivor
en: You live here? Where are your parents?

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Questions, questions! Those can wait. Let's go up first.

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: Welcome to St. Martin's Land, weary traveler.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: I thought we got away, Sis!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your hands and feet are swift, children, but your stealth needs work.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Aw! We were close!

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: We will give you what we took, traveler, but first... you must listen to our story! Once, a long, long, time ago, in a faraway land, there was a sister

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: And a brother!

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: I was getting there! But yes, and a brother. They lived happily in the Land of Saint Martin all by themselves with delicious beans.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Lots and lots of beans! And cake!

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: But now, life is harder... There are no more beans, or cake, and we have to take what is not ours.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: We're not bad children, just hungry.

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: Sorry, large walker.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is no shame in surviving. And there is nothing you should not do for family.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: You're wise, large walker.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here, take this. It is not delicious beans, but it will fill your bellies. For a time, anyway.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Really?

speaker: Eivor
en: This is what "large walkers" should do. Provide for "small walkers."

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Here, large walker!

speaker: Eivor
en: A necklace?

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Yes, it's a St. Martin's seal! You're welcome here anytime, large walker. You're one of us now. Visit us, okay?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will. Take care now, small green walkers.

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: Thanks for playing with us, large walker!

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Would be nice to have some cake, Sister.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here, take my silver. You were going to anyway. Buy what you need. Only steal if you cannot afford it.

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: Thank you... but I do not think we deserve this.

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't deserve to live like this either. Spend the silver wisely.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Here, large walker!

speaker: Eivor
en: A necklace?

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Yes, it's a St. Martin's seal! You're welcome here anytime, large walker. You're one of us now. Visit us, okay?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will. Take care now, small green walkers.

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: Thanks for playing with us, large walker!

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Would be nice to have some cake, Sister.

speaker: Eivor
en: These are unforgiving lands for Danes and Saxons alike, let alone children. Take care now.

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: You're back, large walker!

speaker: Eivor
en: Back in St. Martin's Land.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Yay!

speaker: Otherworldly Voice
en: Oooooh, this is no place for children! Stay awaaaaay!

speaker: Otherworldly Voice
en: Heed my warning, child! This will be the last place you visit if you don't. Ooooooh!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hello there.

speaker: Old Man
en: Oh. You're not a child.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you're not a spirit.

speaker: Old Man
en: No. Just an old man whose son drowned playing near these ruins many years ago.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sorry. That's terrible.

speaker: Old Man
en: It was. Now I spend my days warding away children from this place so no other parent must suffer as I did.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will leave you to it.

speaker: Old Man
en: Thank you. Be careful on the way down.

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor. Have you seen Wallace?

speaker: Eivor
en: Petra, what is wrong?

speaker: Petra
en: It's my brother. Wallace was meant to return hours ago, but I've seen neither hide nor hair of him. He's usually punctual. I'd like to search the woods for him, but alone I fear I'd have little luck. Would you join me? Two could cover much more ground.

speaker: Eivor
en: We should go now. Do you know where to start?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am busy just now, but I will return soon.

speaker: Petra
en: When you can. Thank you.

speaker: Petra
en: Still no sign of Wallace. Do you have time to look for him?

speaker: Petra
en: Near . It's where he buys his tanning liquids. I know he sometimes makes camp at a crossroads between here and there.

speaker: Petra
en: We can retrace his steps. With luck, he hasn't done anything foolish.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is he prone to that sort of thing?

speaker: Petra
en: Never. That's why his absence worries me. I told you how we found him, didn't I?

speaker: Eivor
en: You did. Led by a white elk to a lost babe in the woods. A fated encounter.

speaker: Petra
en: Fated, yes. As if gifted from one guardian to another, he was bestowed on us like a... like a babe among the reeds.

speaker: Eivor
en: Over there. He may have stayed somewhere nearby.

speaker: Petra
en: If he did, he left traces.

speaker: Petra
en: O, no. Eivor, over here.

speaker: Eivor
en: A set of tools. If they belonged to Wallace, why would he take them from his satchel here?

speaker: Petra
en: That leads below ground to who knows where. Let's keep our wits about us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Careful, Petra. Look at its eyes. There's something wrong with this one.

speaker: Petra
en: A strong scent down here. Strange and heady. I don't recognize it.

speaker: Eivor
en: It has a familiar sourness, but I can't place it. Not the smell of death. It is almost... pleasant.

speaker: Petra
en: Hm. Wallace stayed here. Seems he made something to eat.

speaker: Petra
en: Why would he leave his campsite? Where could he have been going?

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone was wounded. A knife attack, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: Must be Wallace's clothes. The trousers are wet... probably pissed himself.

speaker: Petra
en: O my God, Eivor! Eivor! Come this way!

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor! Here! What are you waiting for?

speaker: Eivor
en: What have you found?

speaker: Petra
en: I saw it, Eivor. I saw him nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wallace?

speaker: Petra
en: The white elk! The white elk that brought me to Wallace years ago! It was there, I saw it there!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you certain?

speaker: Petra
en: As sure as I see you now! He's back! Our guardian is back, leading us to my brother!

speaker: Petra
en: Hurry! There's no time!

speaker: Petra
en: Here! Here, Eivor, inside!

speaker: Eivor
en: Petra? Where are you?

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor! I'm here!

speaker: Petra
en: Come!

speaker: Eivor
en: Petra? Hello? Mímir guide me. Have I lost her too?

speaker: Eivor
en: Petra! Show yourself! It's getting dark!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah! The elk. He will know where she has gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am... I am sorry to trouble you, lord.

speaker: The White Elk
en: Eivor. Nice to see you here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you the white elk Petra told me about?

speaker: The White Elk
en: Ha! Of course I am. Look at me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe you can help me. Petra has disappeared. I need to find her before the sun slips away.

speaker: The White Elk
en: No, no. Petra hasn't disappeared. She's close, very close. And waiting for you. Follow me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are the guardian of this place. Do you live a comforting life... out here among the hills and dales of Mercia?

speaker: The White Elk
en: O, I get on, you know. I eat, I sleep, I frolic. I want for nothing and enjoy every moment. It is a decent life. And what are you and Petra doing out here, lurking about the woods. Hunting maybe?

speaker: Eivor
en: In a way, yes. We are looking for her brother, Wallace. She's been waiting for him all day.

speaker: The White Elk
en: O my dear, yes! Where could Wallace be? O where, O where indeed? Ha!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is Petra near? I fear we've lost her.

speaker: The White Elk
en: She was here a moment ago.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wh-what is happening?"

speaker: The White Elk
en: I cannot stay! Not here. Not now!

speaker: Eivor
en: Jotnar! Here in Midgard?

speaker: Eivor
en: Take your evil back to Suttungr's hall! Return to Jotunheim! Go now or die here! What have you done with Petra!

speaker: Eivor
en: What have you done to Petra! Answer me!

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor. Stop! I'm here!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will make them talk, Petra! I must know the truth. I must know where you are!

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor. I am right here. There is no need to question this carrion further.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, yes. Sorry...

speaker: Petra
en: Now come! I believe I know where we will find Wallace.

speaker: Petra
en: Up there! His trail leads this way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Petra! I met your old friend, the white elk. But he vanished before my eyes, before I found you.

speaker: Petra
en: You were visited!

speaker: Eivor
en: For a time. We talked until he vanished into the empty air. A shame, really. I enjoyed his presence.

speaker: Petra
en: Ah! Look there!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is strange seidr (magic), Petra! Where are you?

speaker: Petra
en: Over here!

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor, come on! I'm up here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Petra! How are you doing this?

speaker: Petra
en: There's no trick to it. I think about it, and it works. Easy as walking. Try it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Again? Petra, how?

speaker: Petra
en: Just come to me. I'll show you.

speaker: Eivor
en: How can I do that, Petra?

speaker: Petra
en: Yes, just try it! Move! Run in a straight line!

speaker: Eivor
en: No no no! Too far! Too far!

speaker: Eivor
en: Amazing...

speaker: Petra
en: You did it, just like your Sýnin! And not a scratch on you. Now let's go! Wallace should be over there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sure Wallace is here? I see no one.

speaker: Petra
en: I believe so. We should ask the rabbits. They will know something.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course! The rabbits!

speaker: Petra
en: We've been here before...

speaker: Eivor
en: This is where the wolves attacked us.

speaker: Petra
en: Right. Let us hope their spirits are not restless and that they do not wake to maul us!

speaker: Eivor
en: O no! The wolf spirits have wakened!

speaker: Petra
en: Good day, squirrel. I hope I am not intruding, but have you seen my brother Wallace?

speaker: Petra
en: Damn! This one doesn't speak rabbit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Petra! Hurry!

speaker: Petra
en: Tell me, little rabbit, have you seen a man named Wallace around here? Mm. I see, I see. Thank you for your help.

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor! Look! The elk has returned!

speaker: Petra
en: There. Do you see it? The white elk! Leading us to Wallace! Just as before!

speaker: Eivor
en: I see him! I do!

speaker: Petra
en: Come on, Eivor! Chase the elk!

speaker: Petra
en: No no, please! Don't disappear! Not now! Not until we have Wallace!

speaker: Eivor
en: No, no! Don't go!

speaker: Petra
en: Wait... we... we're home. Full circle with nothing to show for it.

speaker: Wallace
en: Ah... so what are we looking at?

speaker: Petra
en: Wallace? You stone-brained stoat! We've been looking for you!

speaker: Wallace
en: And here I am! Freshly rested and ready to work.

speaker: Petra
en: You're days late!

speaker: Wallace
en: I was carrying quite a burden coming home. Slowed me down some. So I made a camp and picked some mushrooms for a nice soup. Turns out, I picked some funny mushrooms. Sent me into a tizzy. Tore off my clothes, woke up naked and bruised in the woods.

speaker: Wallace
en: So I snuck home, naked as the day God made me, and grabbed some clothes. Now I'm off to get my tools.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mushrooms.

speaker: Petra
en: So the elk. Just another dream.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe so. But don't scoff at dreams. They are often worth more than our waking hours.

speaker: Eivor
en: I may still be buzzing from these mushrooms, but... this is nice.

speaker: Petra
en: I had fun today. Maybe we could do it again. Without the mushrooms?

speaker: Eivor
en: We could. But I will have to ask the rabbits for permission.

speaker: Wallace
en: You and Petra, chasing a white elk in the woods, high as wispy clouds, my God! I could barely breathe for laughing!

speaker: Eivor
en: Where to?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Nowhere in particular. I only want to celebrate.

speaker: Eivor
en: Didn't think you were the type.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You have drawn a dark conclusion of me, haven't you? That is all well and good. I have drawn some about you as well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you leading a lamb to slaughter?

speaker: Ivarr
en: See what I mean? Dark. Too dark.

speaker: Ivar
en: You there... Get lost.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Sit down.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I know I have been a cock. But you are a good fighter, I respect that. Let it be said that Ivarr the Boneless considers Eivor a friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who calls you "boneless"?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Some bacraut (asshole) I killed in Hibernia. Used his guts to shine my spear. Called me boneless because I move like a reed in the wind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not because you're always too drunk to plow?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Valhalla. That is where I am bound. I can smell the blood and taste the mead. I will sit beside the high one with my axe in hand.

speaker: Eivor
en: A fitting end for a Ragnarsson.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You would think, eh! Me, Halfdan, we'll be there. But Ubba... no... I think we are chasing the same victory. Not anymore.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does Ubba want?

speaker: Ivarr
en: To grow old and fat on a farm somewhere, with little Ubbas to chase about.

speaker: Eivor
en: He wants an heir. It's a common dream.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Not for a warrior! Not for drengir like us! He was different before. But this place, England... it softened him.

speaker: Eivor
en: What was he like before?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Like me. Ferocious. Wild.

speaker: Eivor
en: With respect, I don't think anyone is like you.

speaker: Ivarr
en: If that is a compliment, I missed it. All I mean to say is, things were easier some time ago.

speaker: Eivor
en: If it bothers you so much, why not strike out on your own?

speaker: Eivor
en: People change. And it may be that you change with them, or you go your separate ways. If it bothers you so much, why not strike out on your own?

speaker: Eivor
en: If it bothers you so much, why not strike out on your own?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Because he is my brother. I love him. And I will do what it takes to drag him back around to my way of thinking. We are warriors, all. And that is to the death.

speaker: Eivor
en: Outdid myself again. Ugh. Did I miss the crowning?

speaker: Eivor
en: He's worse off than I am.

speaker: Eivor
en: How much did we drink? I don't remember this at all.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Where is my son?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: We sent word to Repton, but we've had no word, lord. I suggest we carry on.

speaker: King Burgred
en: You sought me out, old friend. And here I am, standing before the throne from which I reigned not long ago.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You stand before us to accept this 's unanimous decision. That you are unfit to rule and are hereby deposed. We demand the abdication of your kingdom and your crown to Thegn Ceolwulf.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Mercia has spoken, lord. The crown...

speaker: King Burgred
en: Is that you, old friend? Ah, yes, I see it now. Forgive me. The robes of righteousness sit so loosely upon your shoulders.

speaker: King Burgred
en: If the heavens mismark me as king, forgive its obscuring light! Amen! Now... where is my crown?

speaker: King Burgred
en: Forgive my nerves. Here I am, an upright man who never once learned how to bend the knee. And yet... I shall try.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Ah, how simple it is. How easy to kneel without fear... and feeling.

speaker: Ivarr
en: He's mocking you, man! I'd kill the fucker.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Worry not, Dane.

speaker: King Burgred
en: I shall resign this crown, and this pagan-infested kingdom, and the favors of these two-faced men... but I will do so on my own terms. My demands are simple. Firstly, you must

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: You fool, look around you. You have no leverage here. Plead for your life, for it is the only thing these men will grant you.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Yes... yes. Forgive me, I... Do not harm me, I beg of you. Please. I'll go anywhere. Here! I resign it! Here!

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Take this lord and his wife to Rome. He is hereby exiled, never to return.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: The witan recognizes King Ceolwulf of Mercia, second of his name. A just king. A merciful king. God save the king!

speaker: Sigurd
en: He better be worth all this trouble.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Mercian soldiers! Marching on Repton.

speaker: Ubba
en: Leofrith...

speaker: Ivarr
en: Loyal to the ugly end, the bastard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gather what men you have and split them between the north and south gates. That should divide his forces.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Ceolbert is there. Eivor, you must save my son.

speaker: Eivor
en: He'll come through this, I promise.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I will stay here with Ceolwulf. Go.

speaker: Eivor
en: They've breached the walls. I must find Ceolbert.

speaker: Eivor
en: Any sign of Ceolbert?

speaker: Ivarr
en: No. Boy is likely cowering in a haystack somewhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep an eye out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you seen Ceolbert?

speaker: Ubba
en: No, but we caught sight of Leofrith fleeing across the river. He was chasing someone.

speaker: Eivor
en: It has to be Ceolbert. He's the only prize worth taking in this mud sink.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert! He's in trouble.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I won't back down, Leofrith! I will not!

speaker: Leofrith
en: Don't make this harder than it has to be, boy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Leofrith! Let him walk. You answer to me.

speaker: Leofrith
en: I answer to my king. I silence Danes... with this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lay it by, Leofrith. There's nothing left to fight for. We've stormed Repton. Only a matter of time.

speaker: Leofrith
en: I cannot do that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then you will die.

speaker: Leofrith
en: Someone will.

speaker: Eivor
en: You can't win this, Leofrith. Even if you defeat me, the Ragnarssons have won the day.

speaker: Leofrith
en: I have fought many a Dane in my time. I'm still standing.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're slowing.

speaker: Leofrith
en: Bah!

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a strong-willed thegn. Burgred was lucky.

speaker: Leofrith
en: To stand in the way of you and Mercia is my duty. I will die before I yield.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're finished.

speaker: Leofrith
en: Not yet. Fight me, heathen!

speaker: Leofrith
en: Go on, then. End it.

speaker: Eivor
en: No appeal to your god? Or your king?

speaker: Leofrith
en: I swore an oath to serve Burgred to the death. I fought. I lost. We both know how this goes.

speaker: Odin
en: An honorable thegn fighting a dishonorable war.

speaker: Eivor
en: Burgred abandoned him, betrayed his trust. If I were Leofrith, I'd want to know.

speaker: Odin
en: Why rob him of this last glory? A warrior ready to meet his god and bask in his praise. To live will only lead him to shame.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not an oath he would keep if he knew the truth.

speaker: Odin
en: Then choose. Truth... or glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand, Leofrith. Live to fight another day.

speaker: Leofrith
en: What?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your loyalty to Burgred is not a loyalty returned. He resigned the crown and fled to Rome. He's gone.

speaker: Leofrith
en: You lie...

speaker: Eivor
en: Lie to a man seconds from death? What would I gain?

speaker: Eivor
en: He saved himself and left you to die. All this fighting, it's for nothing. For no one.

speaker: Eivor
en: To betray one so trusted, so close... it's a dishonor worth a thousand deaths.

speaker: Leofrith
en: Eivor... you have shown me a great kindness. It... it is only fitting that I do the same. At Venonis, there is a statue with a scroll laid in a small bowl. You must burn it.

speaker: Eivor
en: A scroll?

speaker: Leofrith
en: Your name is on this scroll. At Burgred's request, I put it there. When it is found, the Zealots who read it will hunt you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are they?

speaker: Leofrith
en: It doesn't matter now, you haven't much time. Burn the scroll. Or they will never stop hunting you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where will you go now?

speaker: Leofrith
en: Rome.

speaker: Eivor
en: Come on. Let's take you back.

speaker: Eivor
en: You fought well, Leofrith. With honor. You will go to your god as you are now.

speaker: Leofrith
en: I am ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: We Norse have a name for men and women with courage like yours. Drengr. I name you one now.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: He didn't deserve this.

speaker: Eivor
en: He chose this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Come. We should get back.

speaker: Eivor
en: Careful, you're injured.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I'm all right. Really. A few nicks and cuts from the battle, that's all.

speaker: Eivor
en: These wounds will heal quickly. You're lucky.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I threw myself at him, Eivor. But he only toyed with me. He knew I couldn't touch him.

speaker: Eivor
en: You should have stayed hidden, Ceolbert. This wasn't your fight.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: It was. It was our fight. Yours, mine, my father's. I had to help.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you did. You showed courage today. Bravery. You're a boy no longer.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Back there, with Leofrith... I didn't think you'd spare him.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is no honor in killing a man misled. He believed his king would die fighting for Mercia.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: He knows the truth now.

speaker: Eivor
en: And with that truth, he forged a new path. You were right about him, Ceolbert. And right to believe the line that divides us can be thinner than it seems.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Back there, with Leofrith... why did you see it fit to kill him?

speaker: Eivor
en: Leofrith was a fighter who knew the cost of war. He died defending an idea he believed in, true or not. There is some honor in that.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I... I think I understand.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ceolbert!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Look at you, bloody and battle-worn! Could be chieftain of your own clan with courage like that!

speaker: Ubba
en: No less than the King of Mercia, Brother. One of these days...

speaker: Ceolbert
en: And how is my father taking to his new role?

speaker: Ubba
en: See for yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're an odlingr now. Or , I think you'd say. Next in line for the throne. It's an honorable title. One that demands good judgement. Be careful who you trust.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: My son, are you well?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Yes, Father. Well enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: He honored you today. Fought bravely, against many stalwart foes.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: You have my thanks, all of you. And my blessing.

speaker: Eivor
en: We knew what this alliance might cost us. But it's over now, and everyone has gained something. Silver, honor, allies.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Agreed. Today we turn a new page. All of England must know... the Kingdom of Mercia has a new king.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ubba and Ivarr lost countless men in this fight. You want to show your thanks? Hold to your end of the bargain.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Of course. All of England will soon know that the Kingdom of Mercia has a new and powerful king.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happens now?

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Word of Burgred's deposition will spread quickly. The other kingdoms of England will soon enough know that Mercia has a new king.

speaker: Eivor
en: The remaining kingdoms of England won't respect your path to power.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Nor will many in my kingdom. Burgred's soldiers will stand tall in the face of this turmoil, all across Mercia, against us.

speaker: Sigurd
en: That we shall remedy soon enough. I am riding for Oxenefordscire directly, to forge an alliance with some thegns there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shall I go with you?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not 'til I know more. Linger here a while if you can. Strengthen our friendships. I will send for you soon enough.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Sigurd, I would feel better if Ceolbert was away from here, until Mercia is more stable.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Would you welcome him among your clan?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Hm. Do you have a horse, young aetheling?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I do. A young steed called Theobald.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Good. I can ride with you as far as the River Nene. You may find your way from there.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Thank you, Sigurd. This puts my mind at ease.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Be ready for my call, Eivor. It will come!

speaker: Ubba
en: You and Sigurd make a good pair. The future of England will be pagan from top to bottom.

speaker: Ubba
en: Take this, Wolf-Kissed. As a sign of friendship. And should you call, the Brothers Ragnarsson will come.

speaker: Eivor
en: You honor me, Ubba.

speaker: Ivarr
en: See that? Sly bastard, trying to win your heart. Well, two can play that game.

speaker: Eivor
en: How kind of you Ivarr.

speaker: Ivarr
en: My pleasure. Our friendship is the best thing to come from this mess. Maybe Ceolbert too, the brave little twig.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's good to hear...

speaker: Eivor
en: Now then... Leofrith said there are hunters after me. Zealots. If I don't clear my name, I'll be marked for death. I should head to Venonis.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, it seems the wind calls me back to Randvi. Best tell her the good news.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Take care of yourself, Eivor. The world is a dangerous place.

speaker: Motull
en: Havi! You coward! Come fight me! Face me! Havi...!

speaker: Havi
en: What is it?

speaker: Motull
en: Havi! You must let me through!

speaker: Havi
en: Why? What do you want with the Well of Helheim?

speaker: Motull
en: To return to my wife, Ronnow. Our village was destroyed. I died with my axe. She did not.

speaker: Havi
en: Good warrior, Helheim is no place you want to be. I have given you the honor of of joining my warriors. Do not be fickle.

speaker: Motull
en: If it was your love, you would move the Nine Realms to reunite with her. You care not for us warriors! I challenge you to a duel. If I win, fulfill my wish. If you win, send me to Hel because I am an unfit warrior.

speaker: Havi
en: That is an unfair fight. I cannot win, and you cannot survive.

speaker: Motull
en: Who am I to trick a trickster? Come, Havi, are you a prick and a coward? Grant my wish, you soft-cock!

speaker: Havi
en: I raised armies while you were shitting your rags. Come, lose and take your place in Hel!

speaker: Motull
en: Yes, my lord.

speaker: Havi
en: Friend, even if rejoined, it will not be as you were. Helheim makes shadows of us all. Your beloved would be ash in your arms.

speaker: Motull
en: I miss her, Havi. I miss how she'd weave flowers in my hair. I miss her crooked front teeth.

speaker: Havi
en: Then take that memory with you. Hold it as an ember against your chest until Ragnarök. At the end of all things, you will see her.

speaker: Motull
en: Thank you. You have earned your title as wise. I will fight in your honor, and keep your name clean in my mouth.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone did not want them to get inside these ruins. The letter on the body mentioned three keys.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Frankish flag. What are they doing there?

speaker: Eivor
en: A symbol of the Hidden Ones on this wall. There's a small slit at the bottom...

speaker: Eivor
en: Unlocked. Time to see what lies ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: One key down, two to go. I should find the other ruins.

speaker: Eivor
en: Two keys. Just one more to go.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Did the others find anything? Why did they not send word?

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Could be they are on their way ... I just want to go back to the city. I can't stand another night here.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: If we see that shadow again tonight, I am riding back in the dark.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have all three keys. Now to use them.

speaker: Eivor
en: It opened. What have the Hidden Ones locked away inside?

speaker: Eivor
en: This has been lying here for centuries, since the Hidden Ones left Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soft footfall. Someone is hiding.

speaker: Eivor
en: A letter? It was not here when I entered.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not all the Hidden Ones left Francia. I will not find them if they do not want to be found, but I will honor their gift.

speaker: French Soldier
en: Stand down! This is not your silver!

speaker: French Man
en: Not a chance! It's our silver, you took it from us!

speaker: French Soldier
en: What? They have a heathen on their side?

speaker: French Man
en: Are you friend or foe? No matter. Help us, stranger! I promise you a reward!

speaker: French Soldier
en: Stand down, I say! Stand down!

speaker: French Man
en: Only if you leave this cart behind!

speaker: Eivor
en: That is the last of them. I could speak to the men and find out what happened here.

speaker: French Man
