en: Thank you, stranger. We underestimated their strength, and without you, we would have perished.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not often I find civilians robbing armed soldiers.

speaker: French Man
en: This is our silver they were trying to take. They raise our taxes and keep the coins for their own indulgence. True, you helped win it back, but we are not inclined to share. I trust that you will let us pass? In return, we will give you a map we stole from the governor's men.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where does it lead?

speaker: French Man
en: The governor has a place up north. The map shows a secret entrance. Imagine what you might find there! We plan to raid it ourselves, but I did promise you a reward.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take the silver and leave the map.

speaker: French Man
en: Thank you, stranger.

speaker: Eivor
en: Map to a secret entrance... I wonder where it leads.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be the place the peasants mentioned. A mint, interesting.

speaker: Eivor
en: As you said, without me you would be dead. Walk away with your lives, and leave the silver.

speaker: French Man
en: You're as bad as them. Fine, take the silver, and may you burn in Hell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Silver can buy happiness.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will take both. Leave, and be grateful to leave with your lives.

speaker: French Man
en: You will regret this. Get the fucker!

speaker: Eivor
en: Map to a secret entrance... I wonder where it leads.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be the place the peasants mentioned. A mint, interesting.

speaker: Eivor
en: To the north? I have been there already and have found this treasure.

speaker: French Man
en: Is that so? Well, then as someone with so much, surely you can be merciful and let us leave in peace?

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine. Keep your silver, you fought and earned it.

speaker: French Man
en: By God! Merci, and bless you on your path.

speaker: Eivor
en: As you said, without me you would be dead. Walk away with your lives, and leave the silver.

speaker: French Man
en: You're as bad as them. Fine, take the silver, and may you burn in Hell.

speaker: Sigg
en: Get ready for hide-and-hunt, everyone!

speaker: Pebble
en: Look at that! It's a giant!

speaker: Braggi
en: Play hide and seek with us, giant! I bet you hide real good!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hide-and-hunt is a true warrior's game. It is good that you play it.

speaker: Sigg
en: Then play with us! This lot's easy, but you'd be hard to find. Go hide with the others! And after the count, I'll seek you out like the mighty wolf, Fenrir!

speaker: Sigg
en: Everyone hides while I count down! After the count, I will seek you out! Everyone go hide, but stay in the village! Outside the village is out of bounds! Twelve, 'leven, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four... three-two-one! Ready or not, here I come!

speaker: Pebble
en: This is my spot! But we can share.

speaker: Sigg
en: The mighty Fenrir stalks the land in search of its prey!

speaker: Sigg
en: I found you, Braggi! I mean, the wolf did!

speaker: Braggi
en: No fair! You're too good!

speaker: Sigg
en: No, you're just bad 'cause you always hide in the same spot.

speaker: Sigg
en: I am getting closer... My keen wolf-nose is picking up a scent... Awooo! Fenrir is getting hungry!

speaker: Sigg
en: Found you, Pebble!

speaker: Pebble
en: Aw! You peeked, didn't you!

speaker: Sigg
en: Ha! Nothing escapes the mighty nose of Fenrir!

speaker: Sigg
en: Come out, giant! You won the game!

speaker: Sigg
en: I lie not! You won! I surrender, giant!

speaker: Braggi
en: The giant is the champion!

speaker: Pebble
en: The Hider in Shadows, the one who lurks unseen!

speaker: Sigg
en: Not too bad, but I can do it better.

speaker: Eivor
en: Farewell, children. Play well and stay warm.

speaker: Sigg
en: Get ready for hide-and-hunt, everyone!

speaker: Eivor
en: A warrior's game. In these times, even children must hide from two-legged wolves.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Aldwyn! My love beams bright, my heart...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Go away, Bertha!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Aldwyn, my sweet! I'm here, I'm here! I even wrote you a poem, the kind you adore. Will you not listen? "Your starry eyes are like plates. With stars upon them, instead of food..."

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Bertha, please, you simply do not understand me! Just leave me be!

speaker: Eivor
en: Barrels of fresh ale. Whoever lives here has a taste for strong drink.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bags of malted barley and hops. Fine ones at that. This ale-maker knows his craft well.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Are you here to steal Aldwyn from me? But of course, his handsome face is a sight to behold!

speaker: Eivor
en: Troubles of the heart?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: I am merely a worm next to a flower such as he. My words have not captured his fancy, he is immovable.

speaker: Eivor
en: You chose the wrong words.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Listen to you! If you are such a poet, help me open the door to his heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: You say he's a brewer. Praise his skills at the craft.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Aren't you a wise devil? Why didn't I think of that!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Here comes a tale, about legendary ale, so famous and delicious, it's the greatest in sales! It's drunk by kings and lords, devils and sinners. So good is its taste, it makes Aldwyn the winner!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: These words about my ale, sung by a honey-voiced angel! Tell me, which of you sang such sweet words to me?

speaker: Eivor
en: She crafted these words and sang them out for you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I never knew you crafted such wonderful word-songs, Bertha. Come in, I want to hear more...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Thank you, friend. Take these trinkets I crafted for Aldwyn! Seems I don't need them anymore.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those were my words. I told her what to say. She merely sang them.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, my. What a disappointment. I thought they were your words, Bertha... I wish to repay you, beautiful stranger... let's warm up at my hearth. Or better yet, let's do more than that.

speaker: Eivor
en: That sounds good. Let us go inside.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Nooooo! Aldwyn!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You wield more than honeyed words, don't you? Take as a gift anything you like from my house, but please, leave my heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will pass.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Suit yourself. It would have been a good time.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Here, stranger. Good art should not be without reward. Take this silver as my patronage for your craft.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: You will never find another one like me, Aldwyn!

speaker: Eivor
en: Men are vain creatures. Sing of his strength and beauty, compare him to a powerful mountain.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: I shall try it your way, wordsmith.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Aldwyn, your shoulders stand tall and hulking like the King of the Hills. My lips long to be caressed by your forested beard!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Ugh.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: I will wait forever, Aldwyn! Make me your ale-muse, and together we'll froth with passion, ferment with love!

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem... an ill match for Aldwyn. You could find love elsewhere.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: I refuse! Aldwyn's scent, the fermented hops on his breath... He's unmatched by any other stallion at the alehouse!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sure. Good luck then, whoever you pursue. I've done all I can.

speaker: Eivor
en: Give me a moment, I will come up with something.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think I know what to say.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Let's hear it then.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am nearing the Afon river at Uffentune. This was where Aelfred said the battle with Ubba took place.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ubba. So Aelfred spoke true. May you join your brother, old friend. Wherever he found his final resting place. Rest well, my friend.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: We owe Eivor a lot, my love.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I know. I know. And with this last affray, I hope the debt will be cleared. I long to return home, to our warm hearth.

speaker: Eivor
en: Geadric. After Rouecistre, I was not sure you would come again.

speaker: Geadric
en: I have chosen my side. I would sooner bed a hog than allow Aelfred to pillage the land I love.

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum will trample Aelfred's ambitions like weeds in the dirt. Mercia might rise further yet.

speaker: Geadric
en: Perhaps I shall one day sit upon the throne of all England. King Geadric the drunken ass!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll raise a cup to that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Deorlaf. You have come again at my call.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: I have, but this does not sit well with me, Eivor. This is a Christian feast, and the people here are not soldiers.

speaker: Eivor
en: I come only for Aelfred.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Innocents will die for your ambitions. I am your ally now, but after this, I must turn back to Mercia. I have much to repent.

speaker: Eivor
en: So long as I do not lose your friendship, your oath will be fulfilled.

speaker: Erke
en: Eivor! It is good to see you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Erke and Stowe. I released you from your debt and yet... you came.

speaker: Erke
en: Lunden is quiet enough, and Stowe here felt the sharp stab of conscience.

speaker: Stowe
en: I could not let you down, Eivor. That's not what an honorable man does. So here I am, despite the reservations.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you, Broder. I did not think you would be here either.

speaker: Broder
en: I have seen to my brother, sent him to Valhalla with grave-goods. I am done with sorrow, Eivor. Now I am bloody angry.

speaker: Eivor
en: Erke. Stowe. Good to see you again.

speaker: Erke
en: I have been saying we ought to get away from the city for a while. Get good, honest cow shit in our nostrils.

speaker: Stowe
en: It does not sit easy with me, warring on Saxons. But a debt is a debt, and Aelfred is no king of mine.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you, Broder. I was not sure you would come.

speaker: Broder
en: Should I sit at home, eyes red and nose dripping? Brothir feasts in Odin's hall. He has gone where I hope to join him one day.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: There you are, Raven!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ljufvina, Hjorr! It warms my heart to see you well.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Well as ever. Better since we skinned those Order rats.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hunted down more in Wincestre on Aelfred's behalf. Now we come to take his kingdom.

speaker: Hjorr
en: How quickly a coin can flip when tossed from hand to hand. Only a fool is a betting man.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye, Hjorr. Aelfred thought to use me, but he will find differently at Cippenhamm.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: There you are, Raven!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ljufvina, my old friend! And I see you have convinced your husband to stumble southwards.

speaker: Hjorr
en: Couldn't let her carve all the glory for herself. Ljufvina was just boasting of her heroics in Suthsexe.

speaker: Eivor
en: She took the fort single-handed while the rest of us sat back and sipped mead. You should have seen her.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I have come to make sure my warrior-wife's enthusiasm for battle does not get her slaughtered.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Have you ever met a woman less in need of a guardian than me, Eivor?

speaker: Hjorr
en: You will have one, nonetheless.

speaker: Eivor
en: Finnr, stand tall. A light heart lifts all those around them.

speaker: Finnr
en: Ah, Eivor. Who would not be joyous, reaving at your side?

speaker: Eivor
en: And how you feel bringing sorrow to the Saxons on their holy day?

speaker: Finnr
en: It darkens my mood. I have learned some of the Christ-Lord's teachings. He preaches peace where our gods delight in battle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let their delights be ours then. We have many battles to wage before the end.

speaker: Finnr
en: And I will be beside you for them all, my axe ready and my heart stout!

speaker: Eivor
en: Finnr! You have come far at my call, old friend.

speaker: Finnr
en: I have done all I can to help King Oswald find his feet. I leave East Anglia in good hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: You do not plan to return, then?

speaker: Finnr
en: No. When I heard of a mighty warrior in the west, who brings terror to the Saxons... I came to join you. If you'll have me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Once we have seen to Aelfred, we will raise a horn... not as allies, but as companions.

speaker: Finnr
en: If drinking and feasting be in my future, I will follow you to Hel.

speaker: Vili
en: You soft-cheeked Anglo boys, have you brought your mothers with you?

speaker: Eluric
en: My mother is worth ten of your men.

speaker: Vili
en: I do not doubt it. I have seen those strong Saxon hens, clucking round the hearth as you farmers play with your cocks.

speaker: Eluric
en: Ha! And she'd welcome you in Colcestre, Vili. Better than those sour-lipped thegns who haunt our hall.

speaker: Vili
en: Look, you Saxon bed-wetters! Here is a real warrior.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili, what tales are you weaving for these soft-downed Saxons? Don't make me regret supporting your jarldom.

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor, you know I will take your childhood scrapes and secrets to the pyre.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good... I would hate for something to happen to you in the coming fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili, leave these poor boys alone. Their ears are too delicate for the filth you pour in.

speaker: Vili
en: Boys is right. This streak of cat-piss is barely of his mother's tit. And the Essexe boy has hands like a milkmaid.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ha, such fiendish ribaldry between you two. You laugh in the face of fear, tweak Old Man Death's beard.

speaker: Eluric
en: I will do my mother and my Lord proud today, Eivor. The Lord knows I have not been the best of sons.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good to see your spirits high. Fight well, my friends, and we will feast together in victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tewdwr. It is good to see you.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I gave you my word. Besides... Aelfred's faith is strict, and he has no love for pagans.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have changed much from that God-whipped boy. That is good to see.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: And you taught me a lot, Eivor. Our time together was... well, it taught me much.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am glad, Tewdwr.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: In fact, I composed a poem for the occasion. Would you like to hear it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Later, Tewdwr. I have many allies to greet before the battle. Stay safe and well, until then.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I was always him, but my faith was like a veil. I am glad you helped me lift it.

speaker: Eivor
en: And now another education. You'll see how we Norse bands fight.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I am all aquiver with anticipation.

speaker: Soma
en: Do you believe the Saxon lord? Is Ubba really dead?

speaker: Guthrum
en: Aye, a few survivors found their way to us. The great man is gone, the last vestiges of Ragnar's legacy begin to fade.

speaker: Soma
en: We have lost many fire-bloods. This land has sapped our strength. There will be too few of us to settle when we are done.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Eivor! You made it unscathed.

speaker: Eivor
en: They came... from all over England.

speaker: Soma
en: I never thought it possible, Eivor. That you would rally Saxons and Norse under your black-feathered banner.

speaker: Guthrum
en: They see the tyranny of this elf-king. He would crush them all under heel, and plug their hearts with his god.

speaker: Soma
en: So, what is the plan, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: When is their feast day?

speaker: Guthrum
en: A few nights from now. But their revelry has already begun. We should attack now.

speaker: Soma
en: That is unwise. Soldiers pace the paths of the village.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then the night of the feast, under cover of darkness. That is when we will strike.

speaker: Soma
en: Ubba will not have died in vain.

speaker: Guthrum
en: We await your instructions, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let us plan our approach. But whatever happens, Aelfred is mine.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will greet my allies first.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Good, come find us again when you are ready.

speaker: Guthrum
en: All is ready, and your allies have arrived. Speak to them if you like. I'll be here when you're done.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Eivor! You made it unscathed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let us speak of our plan to take Cippanhamm.

speaker: Soma
en: They are not expecting us. We should not meet much resistance on the way.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Then quietly, through the fields? It will be already too late once they see us.

speaker: Soma
en: Your young Saxons can be our eyes to the west. Better to keep their soft hands away from the conflict.

speaker: Guthrum
en: My scouts reported that a few nobles have arrived for the festivities already.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. If we capture the thegns, they will be no danger when I confront Aelfred.

speaker: Guthrum
en: And we could persuade them to support a new king of Wessex. I will subdue the lords.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take Deorlaf and Tewdwr with you. They could prove useful in convincing the thegns. Broder, take Erke and Stowe and capture the garrison. Make quick work of any Saxons that dare cross into the village.

speaker: Broder
en: Gladly, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: We each know our parts. May they blunt their swords against our might.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tonight, Wessex's last resistance will crumble.

speaker: Guthrum
en: I follow you, Eivor.

speaker: Soma
en: And I.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be ravening wolves and croaking ravens. Stand firm, your axe-arm strong, and together we will win this final battle. And remember... Aelfred is mine. Soma with me. Everybody else go quickly to the village.

speaker: Eivor
en: Advance. Be on the lookout for any stray guards.

speaker: Eivor
en: Get to the village and wait for my signal.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's smoke the rat out of his god's house!

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfred! Face me and I will spare the last of Wessex from my torch.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Did you think my king would turn his back on you, Eivor? When your knife is smeared with the blood of Werham?

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand aside, Goodwin. I come for Aelfred.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Aelfred is long gone. And this good Christian feast, a cup of honey-wine to trap some wasps.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is he?

speaker: Goodwin
en: Calling his allies to his side. All those who wish to see Wessex under one God. You cannot win England with your sorry crew of deluded farmers and godless fools.

speaker: Eivor
en: At least I would not leave them to die as I scurried through the cornhusks like a rat.

speaker: Goodwin
en: You have no understanding of duty, the loyalty I freely give. His plan for England, for the world, is worth the cost of my life.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then sing your tuneless hymns.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Come, Raven-Feeder, do your worst.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Such empty fury. It does not matter if I die as long as Aelfred is safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your life means so little?

speaker: Goodwin
en: I have no fear of death, for this battle is only the beginning.

speaker: Eivor
en: Only darkness will come to claim you.

speaker: Goodwin
en: For all your boasts, warrior, I scratch at you like a cat.

speaker: Eivor
en: You yap like a dog.

speaker: Goodwin
en: We could have been allies, but now you'll fall by my sword.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will never bow to Aelfred.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are beaten, Goodwin.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Beaten? No, not so. By my death, my lord may live.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfred used you, fool. He threw you in my path. For what? He only delays what is inevitable.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Kill me then. It makes no odds. For here you stand. Bloody and breathless, no closer to my king, no closer to the throne. This island will never be your home, Eivor. You will not subdue her with vicious force, or win her with cocksure words. We Saxons will always stand firm. Shoulder-by-shoulder against thieves and tyrants, whose envious eyes fall upon England.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I must strike down all of England to subdue her, let it begin with you.

speaker: Goodwin
en: O Lord, into your hands I commit my spirit.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, I will use you, as you used me. A few hours in the company of my men and you will lead us to your sparrow-king.

speaker: Goodwin
en: That I cannot allow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma!

speaker: Soma
en: The men of Wessex! They came from every house and hovel!

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma! Fall back!

speaker: Soma
en: For life!

speaker: Soma
en: For death!

speaker: Soma
en: For glory...

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma!

speaker: Soma
en: For Valhal

speaker: Eivor
en: No!

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you see Aelfred?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: No. But your Saxon boys were ambushed. One lays wounded.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hold these men back, I'll find them.

speaker: Hjorr
en: Go, Eivor. They will not better us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald... come, get up. This is no time for weep-wailing.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I... I cannot. And there is a blackness closing in around my eyes. It frightens me.

speaker: Eluric
en: Forgive me, Hunwald. I should have been quicker.

speaker: Hunwald
en: No, no... you were my staunch protector, Eluric.

speaker: Eluric
en: Eivor, have you seen graver wounds?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will carry him from the fray. To that farmhouse there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will get you to safety, Hunwald. Stay calm.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I... I may be all right. There is so little pain just now...

speaker: Eluric
en: Please, Eivor. We must get him to the farmhouse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald, listen to me. You survived the battle of Botolphston. Do not let this scratch best you now.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I'm so cold. Has winter come so soon?

speaker: Eivor
en: You will warm yourself with mead and dancing yet, my friend.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Perhaps not, Eivor. It may be I will sit besides my father soon. Will he be proud of me?

speaker: Eivor
en: He will pull you to his breast, sob bright words of welcome... and tell you no man ever had a worthier son.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I am glad to have known you, Eivor. My truest...

speaker: Eivor
en: I should check on Guthrum at the feast hall.

speaker: Eluric
en: I will not leave his side, Eivor. I owe him that much at least.

speaker: Eivor
en: There was nothing more you could have done. Friendship has a hollow ring if there is no threat of losing it.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Do not waste your efforts here. Go help the others!

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to see if Broder has taken the garrison.

speaker: Eluric
en: I will not leave his side, Eivor. I owe him that much at least.

speaker: Eivor
en: There was nothing more you could have done. Friendship has a hollow ring if there is no threat of losing it.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Do not waste your efforts here. Go help the others!

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum! I need you fighting with the rest.

speaker: Guthrum
en: These men will not surrender! And one little cock-flogger barricaded himself behind that door there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find a way in.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: You will regret this unholy interruption!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: You attack us on our holy feast day?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Protect the thegns at all costs!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Cippenhamm will not fall to you scum.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Leave me be! I am no threat to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to see if Broder has taken the garrison.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good work, Guthrum. I hope the rest have fared as well.

speaker: Eivor
en: If Aelfred has fled Cippanhamm, it may be Ljufvina tracked him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good work, Guthrum. I hope the rest have fared as well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Broder! What can I do?

speaker: Broder
en: Eivor! The garrison has more defenders than we hoped. My men are being slaughtered.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find a way to open the gates from the inside.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hurry! These waves of reinforcements are Hel-sent.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is most of them. Make sure the garrison stays under our control. I need to help the others.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should check on Guthrum at the feast hall.

speaker: Eivor
en: If Aelfred has fled Cippanhamm, it may be Ljufvina tracked him.

speaker: Vili
en: I am Vili, if you would know who cleaves your skull!

speaker: Eivor
en: They are weakened. Let us finish this!

speaker: Geadric
en: You fucking Wesexians will not move on Mercia.

speaker: Vili
en: For Eivor and the Raven Clan!

speaker: Geadric
en: This feast will end in blood.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: You will not rout us, interlopers. Not on this Christ mass.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: Stand true, God protects us on his day of feasts!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: These Danes defy our God and king!

speaker: Eivor
en: That's it, they are fleeing! The last of the Saxons are fleeing. The battle is won!

speaker: Guthrum
en: Cippenhamm is ours! Tend to the wounded and gather in the square!

speaker: Guthrum
en: They are routed! The city is ours. Wessex will follow!

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum Jarl, we are not without losses. Some of them grave.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Their king is fled, his patsy struck down. Defeat rings loud in their ears, and I will be their lord before the spring is here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum, hear me... Soma is... she is gone.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Soma?... Dead? She has gone to the endless feast. And is the better for it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Many fought for us and died. They deserve peace.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Are you ready to honor them?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, there is nothing more to say.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must speak to those still living.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must speak to those still living.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is done, Broder. You fought well.

speaker: Broder
en: I saw him, Eivor. In my darkest moment, Brothir stood beside me, and all was as it used to be. Then the battle ended. I feel him no longer.

speaker: Eivor
en: There will be other battles.

speaker: Broder
en: Aye. And there you'll find me, Eivor. In amongst the blood and death, Brothir at my shoulder. Until the Valkyries claim me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have given me more than I would ever have asked for. How will I repay it?

speaker: Broder
en: Keep him in your thoughts. For when man is mourned, his deeds cheered and his songs sung, he cannot die.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you think there will come a day when winning will not be enough?

speaker: Vili
en: You can always fight with me if you want to taste crushing and loin-soiling defeat.

speaker: Eivor
en: My very presence would make that impossible.

speaker: Vili
en: Enjoy this victory, Eivor, whatever it brings you. Only a coward thinks he'll live forever.

speaker: Eivor
en: Erke. You wear a furrowed brow.

speaker: Erke
en: Stowe is taking matters hard. You know how sensitive he is.

speaker: Eivor
en: A man of faith and stout morals. Small wonder he is tormented.

speaker: Erke
en: His support for you has taxed him hard. I'll take him back to Lunden. Maybe he will find some comfort there.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are his comfort, Erke, not the city you watch. He is in good hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: My thanks, Stowe. You came to my aid, when you were free to turn away.

speaker: Stowe
en: And still it breaks my heart to look upon what we have done today. Was it the right choice? I do not know. But it is done now.

speaker: Eivor
en: If Aelfred had his way, there would never be friendship between Norse and Saxon. You fought for peace. Be proud of that.

speaker: Stowe
en: I wish I could be. And in time perhaps I will.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your first battle, Eluric. You fought well and with honor.

speaker: Eluric
en: Is the glory you Danes seek? You can keep it. I saw Hunwald die, the light dim in his eyes. That could have been me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You will never be the same. But you will be stronger for it.

speaker: Eluric
en: I have wasted so much time in pouting like a child. No more, Eivor, no more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ljufvina... Gods, I did not know. Is he

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Hush. What good can words do, Eivor? Keep to silence. He is gone. For what days I was given to spend with you. For each breath that carried your sweet whispers, I give thanks. No more, your fingers in my hair. No more your arms around my waist. The days will be cold hereafter, all color dimmed. Goodbye, my only. My heart ends with you. What is left... will go on.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are not injured, Tewdwr?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Bruises, that is all. I have taken the Lord into my heart and He watched over my sorry bones. Those who fell sit beside him now.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what of my heathen friends?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I used to believe in damnation for all who turned from his light. But there is a wondrous communion in friendship honored.

speaker: Eivor
en: Even though your god-son preaches peace?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: And we shall do that, Christians and pagans, side-by-side. Never persecuted.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your Christ would smile at that, I think.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Your Freyja would, too.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: He shall come to judge the living and the dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Deorlaf. Geadric. There is a solemn air about you.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: To disturb such holy revels with blood and murder... I fear God may never forgive me for this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Had your God taken Aelfred's side, we would have not won. So it may be that you did his work after all.

speaker: Geadric
en: Aelfred still lives. And now I am twice his enemy. Give me one more fight and I will gladly make it a third.

speaker: Eivor
en: He is defanged and little of threat to us now.

speaker: Geadric
en: That slippery eel may yet surprise you.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Atonement is a long and lonely path, and I must soon leave to take my first steps upon it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your debts to me are paid. I wish you well on your journeys.

speaker: Guthrum
en: My heart is heavy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Many fought for us and died. They deserve peace.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Are you ready to honor them?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, there is nothing more to say.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must speak to those still living.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Time to send our friends to their great reward. Will you do the honors?

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing awaits them. They lived, they died. Now their bodies will burn to cinders. Their ends here.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Well, do not share that with them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Victory is ours. But it came at great cost. Soma Jarlskona, who stood at Guthrum's right hand... She will live on in our memories. From now 'til the end of days. And to Hjorr... warrior, husband, and friend. He made the ultimate sacrifice. I here repay it. And to Hunwald whose kind heart has now led him to his father's side. May his god welcome him with open arms. Let us send them on their way, all our beloved dead, our fallen warriors. And speed them... to their end.

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum?

speaker: Guthrum
en: When the reeve died, did he take comfort in knowing he would soon see his god?

speaker: Eivor
en: He was strangely peaceful in the end. As if death meant nothing.

speaker: Guthrum
en: We stumble through our years, ravenous, grasping. Spilling blood, stealing gold, and it is never enough. This life is never enough. Would it not soothe you to know there is something beyond all this? Not war and valor, but quiet and peace?

speaker: Eivor
en: I think... I think the afterlife men hope for is only a reflection of their regret in this life. All I wish for now, is to live among the friends I have made. That is what counts.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Aelfred made me swear fealty upon the cross of their god's son. He held such faith in it... a plain, unadorned thing. It burned between my fingers, as if I had pulled it from the fire. A feeling strange and powerful, but gone in an instant. I have not felt its like before.

speaker: Eivor
en: What will you do now?

speaker: Guthrum
en: Whatever, I must do. England is my final home, Eivor. And I will do what it takes to remain.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should return to Swanburrow, and tell her of Hunwald's fate. Better the news come from me than a stranger.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor!

speaker: Randvi
en: Are we safe?

speaker: Eivor
en: It will be many winters before Frankish troops land on the English shore.

speaker: Randvi
en: My spies say Paris fell.

speaker: Eivor
en: It did. But the situation is thornier than that.

speaker: Randvi
en: In what way?

speaker: Eivor
en: The queen, Richardis, believes she can subdue the mad king in isolation. They have withdrawn to a faraway place.

speaker: Randvi
en: But Charles has such a stormy reputation. Can this queen tame such a man?

speaker: Eivor
en: Richardis has a deep well of courage to draw from. And she holds sway over Charles like no other.

speaker: Randvi
en: That is comforting.

speaker: Eivor
en: I killed the mad king, Charles the Fat. Odo, the Count of Paris, means to take the throne.

speaker: Randvi
en: Is that good for us?

speaker: Eivor
en: Time will tell. But Odo is an honorable man and he has a kingdom to rebuild.

speaker: Randvi
en: That is comforting.

speaker: Eivor
en: We also have a hardy ally in Toka Sinricsdottir.

speaker: Randvi
en: She is young.

speaker: Eivor
en: And a quick study. She'll do right by us.

speaker: Randvi
en: Perhaps they need not know the danger we faced.

speaker: Eivor
en: We came home with bounty, glory and some Frankish foods. I can ask the raiders to keep their tales to that.

speaker: Randvi
en: They will say everything and then some.

speaker: Eivor
en: Afraid so.

speaker: Eivor
en: New strength comes to weathered halls. Now, I can rest.

speaker: Hunwald
en: What horrible souls are hunting me? Me, the son of a beloved ealdorman! Was it naive of me to believe my status as a nobleman held some sway over the ceorls and serfs of this shire? What cause have any to dishonor me?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: We need stronger leadership in Lincolnscire. We can't go on like this, waiting for our ealdorman to heal, or suffering the idea of Hunwald taking his place.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Look, boats there. We could sail the waters to Lincoln. Sink the ships of any enemies in our way!

speaker: Eivor
en: What were you told when the guards exiled you?

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, scraps of nonsense. I woke to screaming. A man grabbed me, said I was an immediate danger to my father. Ha. Horsepucky! Mercian soldiers then shackled me, rode me blindfolded to the river and told me plainly: start anew elsewhere or face death in Lincolnscire.

speaker: Eivor
en: What did they mean?

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, some nonsense about me praying for his death, hungry for his inheritance.

speaker: Eivor
en: Speak plainly, Hunwald. I can't help you if I don't know the full story. You hold no grudge against your father?

speaker: Hunwald
en: No, never! No, I suspect the order for my exile came from on high. Perhaps one of Burgred's final orders once he was deposed.

speaker: Eivor
en: That would surprise me. Burgred was battling Danes until the end. He had bigger things to worry over.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Perhaps you're right, he's too contained. It must have been King Aelfred, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: King Aelfred of Wessex? That's another kingdom entirely.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes, but Aelfred has a fearful hatred of the Danes! He must have heard that I am courting one! A beauty who knows no equal!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your Dane ladylove. Right.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Here's Lincoln. The city of my birth, the cauldron of my present sorrows.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mercian guards everywhere. Follow me.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Right behind you, shadow-walker. My heart beats like the drums of your dragon-boat.

speaker: Hunwald
en: O how can a place I once called home look so alien to me now! So harsh and un-wanting. Fear not Lincoln, I shall make you mine again.

speaker: Eivor
en: This town is your home?

speaker: Hunwald
en: It was, and should still be! O, to see it now fills my eyes with tears.

speaker: Eivor
en: Save weeping for prayers. We're not inside yet.

speaker: Hunwald
en: One day, I won't have to skulk around this town with my face hidden. I will walk proudly among the people I love.

speaker: Eivor
en: How was your father the last time you saw him?

speaker: Hunwald
en: He was... quite poorly. But he has the heart of a lion and the holy spirit itself within him! A bout of illness would never bring him low.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did he think highly of you?

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, yes, yes indeed! The thegns and clergy of Lincolnscire are not fond of me, but they do not yet know me well enough. Not truly.

speaker: Eivor
en: The people of Lincoln are not welcoming to Danes.

speaker: Hunwald
en: It's troubling, I know. Your folk are strong, hardy, noble! Creatures straight out of stories and tales.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are also a living people, Hunwald. More than a story. We are real and flawed.

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, yes, I am well aware. Blunt and stalwart, honest and true. I have a Dane ladylove with all those qualities, you know.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a Dane lover... and she's a Valkyrie as well, I suppose?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: There's damp on the air. I fear gray clouds will gather soon.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Aye. And foul deeds are brewing. The horses can feel it too, neighing and rolling their eyes.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: That's them being horses, mate.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: No one has heard from the ealdorman in weeks? What's happened?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Lord Hundbeorht is surely fighting the Danes to the north.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: No, no. He's made a pact with them. There's peace now. Ain't you heard?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Naw, that can't be true.

speaker: Hunwald
en: My home is just there. We've made it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Careful. The house is being watched.

speaker: Hunwald
en: What? Where?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: I have barely enough silver to buy peat from those bandit smugglers. They hoard everything.

speaker: Raeganhere
en: Hunwald! Praise God, you live!

speaker: Hunwald
en: I do, my dear Raeganhere. Body and soul! Tell my father, his son has returned, and in fighting form! It is urgent I speak with him.

speaker: Raeganhere
en: I'm sorry, lord, but your father has been taken.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Taken? When?

speaker: Eivor
en: Weeks ago, lord. And well ill he was when they carried him off. I wish I could say more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you looked for him?

speaker: Raeganhere
en: O, I dare not go asking after him, for fear of stepping above my caste.

speaker: Raeganhere
en: But he'll be in good hands, don't you worry. Up there with the abbess and her sisters and all.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who took the ealdorman? Was it soldiers or men of God?

speaker: Raeganhere
en: There were men with swords and those of the cloth. And a healer, too, one who had often been a guest in this house.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Galwyna. One of the sisters my father put great faith in.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did he walk out the door himself, or was there a struggle?

speaker: Raeganhere
en: He wasn't took, nor did he walk. He sort of limped his way on.

speaker: Eivor
en: On his own, or was he forced?

speaker: Raeganhere
en: On his own. It was the Abbess Acha who suggested he be moved. She feared his illness was fast coming.

speaker: Hunwald
en: He still has friends in Lincoln, that's a good sign.

speaker: Raeganhere
en: Bishop Herefrith among them. He's kept a vigil at the town hall, looking after things in your father's absence, until he returns.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will we find trouble there, at the town hall?

speaker: Raeganhere
en: You mean soldiers and the like? Aye, there have been many, many more about since your father took his leave.

speaker: Eivor
en: Right. We'll find a quiet way in if we can.

speaker: Raeganhere
en: I wish you the best of luck in your endeavours, Dane.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who was that fellow?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Raeganhere? He's an old fixture of my family's household. Loyal to the end. He helps run the place, and he's known me since I was a little lordling. A simple fellow, but worth every pinch of his salt!

speaker: Eivor
en: Lincoln seems a good place to trade.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Does it?

speaker: Eivor
en: The market is flush with goods.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes, it must be. Growing up, we never wanted for anything in my father's home. Bread and poultry and field fruits of all manner. I suppose this is where our servants purchased them. Lincoln's boon was ours as well.

speaker: Eivor
en: How often did you leave your house, Hunwald?

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, from time to time. Yes.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Acha! Herefrith! Tell Lord Hundbeorht his son has returned!

speaker: Acha
en: My lord! You're well.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Lord Hunwald...

speaker: Herefrith
en: We had no news of your return. You might have sent a messenger and spared us the suspense.

speaker: Herefrith
en: You should have sent forewarning of your return to avoid the violence that dogs you. Lives might have been spared.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Why so surprised to see my return, bishop? Was I rumored dead?

speaker: Herefrith
en: O, worse than dead. It is my reluctant duty to report the rumor that you were lost in the North, bedding a Dane of some squalid farm.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not the Dane he's been plowing. And I don't own a farm.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I know you mean well, bishop. But there's no cause to insult Swanburrow's honor. You leave my ladylove out of this.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Ah, your mystery Dane has a name. Sadly, the people of this shire will hardly be comforted, now that you have swelled your father's tolerance for pagans into a sin.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no patience for insults and rumor. We've come to speak with Lord Hundbeorht, that is all.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald came to me for aid, and I agreed to help. Whatever rumors you've heard have nothing to do with me.

speaker: Herefrith
en: I am simply worried that Lord Hundbeorht's wayward son is in danger of besmirching his reputation beyond repair. That is all.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no patience for insults and rumor. We've come to speak with Lord Hundbeorht, that is all.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no patience for insults and rumor. We've come to speak with Lord Hundbeorht, that is all.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Lord Hundbeorht has gone, I'm afraid. He would not say where to, but I'm sure he will return shortly. Once the storm has passed.

speaker: Hunwald
en: What on earth do you mean by that? What storm?

speaker: Herefrith
en: Your father feared for his life, Hunwald. In his weakened state, he could not defend himself. Not against a Dane, certainly.

speaker: Hunwald
en: How dare you! Eivor is above reproach!

speaker: Herefrith
en: See this from my view, Hunwald! You arrive after a strange absence with a hired Viking in tow, demanding to see your father. This does not, in my estimation, imply benign intentions.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald's seen the point of a dagger more than once this week. I'm only here to protect him.

speaker: Acha
en: Your father was at my hospice for some days, and very well treated. But he left in secret, that is all we know.

speaker: Hunwald
en: In secret? That's odd. He's not one to scurry about in the dark.

speaker: Herefrith
en: I'm sorry, Hunwald. We have searched high and low for him but to no avail.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I meant to murder you, these stones would be slick with your gore already.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Such violence, good heavens. God must have purpose for you pagans in His holy plan, but I confess to utter bafflement.

speaker: Acha
en: Hunwald, your father was at my hospice for a time, but he left of his own accord, without saying a word. That's all we know.

speaker: Eivor
en: Our coming here has nothing to do with you. This is a matter between the boy and his father.

speaker: Acha
en: I disagree. Everything this boy does concerns us. He's the son of our ealdorman.

speaker: Acha
en: I all but raised you, lad. Bounced you on my knee and taught you scripture. So when I tell you we don't know where your father is, nor why he left our hospice in his ailing state... it's because we don't know.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Come, abbess. We should leave this young lord to his scurrying thoughts. There is nothing more of use we can say to him.

speaker: Acha
en: Take care, my boy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay within these walls where you're safest. I'll have a look around, see what I can learn about your father.

speaker: Hunwald
en: If my father spent time at the hospice here, the healers who work there may know something. Talk to them if you can. Find out what they know.

speaker: Homeward
en: was a virtual representation of one of Eivor Varinsdottir's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan in 2020 through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: I will take three Paris mansions.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: We know you are greedy, but why three?

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: One for me, one for my horse, and, uh, one for my axe!

speaker: Goll
en: You are late for the feast, crow.

speaker: Toka
en: Longships on the shore. As beautiful as swans.

speaker: Eivor
en: More like wolves, circling for the kill.

speaker: Toka
en: True, this is no raid. When we get inside those walls, what happens, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: You have fought before. Bled. Killed.

speaker: Toka
en: Yes, but... there are children in that city. They cannot flee. When the wind is right, I can hear them yelling, playing games.

speaker: Eivor
en: There need not be a slaughter. We may still persuade the Franks to yield... though I am unsure of the best way...

speaker: Toka
en: Tell this to Sigfred.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Tell me what?

speaker: Eivor
en: We are here, they see our strength. Let them give up their silver, sign the treaties, and we sail home.

speaker: Toka
en: To gain fame and wealth this way is good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Count Odo leads the Franks in Paris, yes?

speaker: Toka
en: Aye. He defends the city and draws other nobles to cause.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can talk to this Odo.

speaker: Sigfred
en: No more talk.

speaker: Eivor
en: The High One says 'tis better to live than to die, that the dead till no fields.

speaker: Sigfred
en: You quote the All-Father at me? I shall burn Paris, with or without you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have lost thegns enough. Would you rule a wasteland?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Go, then. Talk Count Odo out of his silver, if you can.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will at that. Toka, where is this Odo?

speaker: Toka
en: You might pick up his trail at Pontem Esera. But go with stealth, that is enemy ground.

speaker: Sigfred
en: And Eivor, this Odo is no willow reed. He does not bend in the wind.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: How can we spy on the heathens through all these leaves?

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Keep your voice down! Do you want to be captured and eaten by the heathens?

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: If it means getting out of this miserable tree...

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Merde! A twig, it has snapped.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be the fort Toka mentioned. I need clues to Odo's whereabouts.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Take heart, comrades. Count Odo shall lead us to victory. The Northmen have not won yet!

speaker: French Soldier 4
en: Another message for Odo, left to rot on his desk. Why bother, nobody knows when he's coming back.

speaker: French Soldier 5
en: Have faith in the count. He's kept us fed, so if anyone can hold Paris, he can.

speaker: French Soldier 4
en: Sigfred and his lot will be eating in the Palais before month's end, mark my words.

speaker: French Soldier 5
en: Have you so little faith in God and Odo? I hate standing watch with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odo should be at his manor. The one with red flowers.

speaker: Eivor
en: This way is well-guarded. Best to find another way in.

speaker: French Man 1
en: How dare you bar me from going this way? Who says I cannot enter?

speaker: French Soldier 6
en: Lord Odo says so. It is because of the coming siege, no? We cannot fill the castle with hungry mouths.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now to find Odo's red flower manor.

speaker: French Child 1
en: Who will defend our Frankish land? Brave Lord Odo, we know he will. Who will save us from the Northman? Who will defend our Frankish land? Lord Odo stands at the king's right hand. Every Northman he will kill. Who will defend our Frankish land? Brave Lord Odo, we know he will!

speaker: French Man 2
en: The Northmen burnt my house and killed my son. Now the plague takes my wife! Why does God torment me? Why?

speaker: French Woman 1
en: Easy, milord. You drank too much wine and your tongue runs free in its grief.

speaker: French Man 2
en: No, I must hide! Northmen drink the blood of saints. Revealed to Prophet John. Everyone, in the wine cellar!

speaker: Theodrate
en: Hold, stranger. Who goes there?

speaker: Eivor
en: Pardon me, my lady, but I seek an audience with Count Odo.

speaker: Theodrate
en: I see, but my husband is busy recruiting nobles to aid in the coming war.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good lady, I too wish to pledge my blade to defend Paris from the heathen hordes.

speaker: Theodrate
en: I see. Are you one of our allies from the barbaric fringes of the kingdom?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I have journeyed a great many days along the coast and down the river.

speaker: Theodrate
en: And do you have a signed and seal writ of audience? Without a proper writ, I simply cannot allow you inside. We must be wary of assassins, you know.

speaker: Eivor
en: O, the scrolls. I left it in my saddlebags. I shall fetch it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need one of those noble writs to meet with Odo. One of the guests might have one.

speaker: French Man 3
en: Our newest guest has gone mad. He's hiding in the wine cellar!

speaker: French Woman 2
en: I won't believe it! One of our nobles, cowering like a stablehand?

speaker: Theodrate
en: Good ally, I cannot grant you an audience with Lord Odo without your writ.

speaker: Eivor
en: Greeting, friends. What is the trouble?

speaker: French Woman 2
en: One of Odo's guests has got filthy drunk and locked himself in the wine cellar. Shameful.

speaker: Eivor
en: Was he invited here to help defend Paris?

speaker: French Woman 2
en: Perhaps, but what sort of help can such a lout provide? I am dubious, I tell you.

speaker: Eivor
en: That drunken noble might have one of those writs I need to meet with Odo.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: Someone, help me bash down this door. One of our guests has locked himself in the wine cellar.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: O, Lord Clovis! You have drunk yourself to sleep after making a frightful scene. Please, show me a kindness and help Lord Clovis outside while I clean up this mess.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing to fear. I will carry Lord Clovis outside for some fresh air.

speaker: Eivor
en: This drunk has a paper in his pocket. Looks like the writ I need to meet with Count Odo.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have returned with the writ permitting me to speak with Count Odo.

speaker: Theodrate
en: Excellent, you may enter. And we do appreciate your efforts on our behalf.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to find Count Odo.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not getting in this way.

speaker: Lord Corvus
en: You see, dear Lothar, Odo has trusted me and me alone with the key to his study.

speaker: Lord Lothar
en: How did such an outrage come to be?

speaker: Lord Corvus
en: Because, dear Lothar, I gift him with rare vintages, whole casks from as far away as Greece.

speaker: Lord Lothar
en: Bah. Servant, bring more wine!

speaker: Lord Corvus
en: I shall see to our wine, dear Lothar. Farewell.

speaker: Lord Corvus
en: Merde! My precious key to Odo's study... stolen!

speaker: Gozlin
en: −and with Count Odo leading us, we shall drive these heathen devils back into the abyssal sea!

speaker: French Man 4
en: As you say, my lord, but these Northmen are mortal, not demons. They want land and plunder.

speaker: Odo
en: True, the Northmen are fierce and the king is... slow to defend us. Yet every one of you swore an oath before God to defend this realm. We will overcome this evil, as we always have. I cannot compel you to do your duty. Your hearts must guide you. Gozlin, kindly show our guests out.

speaker: Odo
en: Come out and say what you wish to say, Eivor of England.

speaker: Eivor
en: You saw me enter, fair enough. But how do you know me?

speaker: Odo
en: My scouts speak of a famed warrior with a raven. Do you think us fools?

speaker: Eivor
en: I did not expect such courtesy.

speaker: Odo
en: Mulled wine, what we call in vin chaud. Properly spiced, heated, and served with fruit. My one vice.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wine grapes do not grow in the North. We drink mead.

speaker: Odo
en: Mead. Eivor, you risked much to see me, I respect that. But why? You have land in England, no?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no wish to settle my people in Francia.

speaker: Odo
en: Then how much coin will satisfy your lust? A hundred ? A thousand? And after you, who's next? Ragnar and his sons came here years ago. We bought them off with silver and they burned Paris anyway.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not want silver. I want England free of Frankish meddling. We're not a part of your kingdom.

speaker: Odo
en: And I would like our kingdom free of Norse "meddling" as you call it. But for argument's sake, what are your terms?

speaker: Eivor
en: As I said, Charles leave England alone. Second, he embraces Sigfred as an ally. And finally, he lets Sigfred's thegns keep their land in the north.

speaker: Odo
en: Rouen and Amiens were my father's lands! You shall never claim my birthright.

speaker: Odo
en: Your army will never take Paris. And you will never have peace. Not here, and not in England.

speaker: Odo
en: My men will escort you out. When we next meet, it shall be on the field of battle. Farewell.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must return to camp and tell the others what Odo said.

speaker: Eivor
en: No point in going back there.

speaker: Sigfred
en: You arrive in time to drink. What will you take?

speaker: Eivor
en: Wine, much wine. It was a long journey.

speaker: Sigfred
en: The Hero of Ravensthorpe, the skalds called this one. Gifted at war and at words, they say. But I see no treasure.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Where is Odo's silver? Have you kept it all for yourself?

speaker: Eivor
en: It went as you said. The man is no reed. He would not bend, would not yield.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Franks love to talk, but their words are as empty as the wind.

speaker: Eivor
en: True, but a wise sailor still listens to the wind. It may foretell a coming storm.

speaker: Eivor
en: Much talk is idle, but hard words lead to hard choices. Have a care.

speaker: Eivor
en: A fierce wind can snap a tree, even one as strong as Odo. Is Charles the wind... or will he break like a reed?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Now. Two things we must do to carry this siege. First, we shall take some ground for our catapults.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will help with this. Somewhere near Paris, I guess, but is it guarded?

speaker: Sigfred
en: The Franks lack the men to hold the whole city, only the walled island, the Île de la Cité. Still, go with care.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. And the second thing?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Find a flaw in their defenses. A place where our warriors can breach their walls. Or a way for our ships to encircle the island. Some weakness we can exploit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Agreed, but how?

speaker: Toka
en: Might be that I know a way, but... it carries risk.

speaker: Eivor
en: Speak, Toka.

speaker: Toka
en: In the slums south of the walls, there is a smuggler, a woman.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Her Breton lover.

speaker: Goll
en: Heh, heh.

speaker: Toka
en: She's not my lover, just a campfire fling. But if anyone knows the city's weak points, she does. I would go myself, but... we... Nolwenn, she...

speaker: Sigfred
en: They quarreled. The smuggler stole Toka's necklace before she stole her heart. Now, Toka misses her necklace.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will talk to this smuggler and find a weakness in the Franks' defenses. You have my word.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Good. All is settled then.

speaker: Toka
en: No, uncle. There is another thing. Odo will not see reason, but Charles might. We should speak to him again.

speaker: Sigfred
en: You wish for more talking.

speaker: Toka
en: We should speak to the fat king, gain a truce.

speaker: Eivor
en: What! He tried to kill me. Why talk to him again?

speaker: Toka
en: Those stone walls will not yield, not without a bloody fight. He may give us silver without half our clan dying on those walls.

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps Toka is right. Charles may still yield.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Go, niece. Talk to every king and bishop in the land, just like Eivor the Talker. It matters not. But soon comes the end of talk. Soon, the spears will clash and the city will burn. Be ready to fight that day.

speaker: Eivor
en: My word, once given, is never broken. I will fight at your side, Sigfred. Never doubt.

speaker: Toka
en: Enough! Friends, uncle. We are of one heart here.

speaker: Toka
en: I will seek the king at the Clever Fox, a tavern on the northern bank. Pierre says he carouses there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Toka is a good thegn. Someday she may stand in front of an army, like you, Sigfred.

speaker: Sigfred
en: I hope so, but for now she stands with me. Meet me at the bell tower, Eivor, when you are ready to fight some Franks. Instead of talk to them.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you laugh at, thegn?

speaker: Goll
en: They say you stink of crow-shit, hero. But you smell like Frankish piss-wine to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to lay the groundwork for the siege, but what to do first?

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: How long have you been chasing me, Wolf-Kissed? Seventeen winters? Eighteen? Do I now haunt your dreams? Do I warm your loins? (laugh)

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: You remember this...? Your father's axe. The weapon of a coward, a scorn-snake. Ah, few things would please me more than to kill with this blade. But I know you would defy me to the death, fighting for a glorious end. That I will not allow.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: You will live your final days as a slave, humiliated. Your death will be a lonely one. Haha... Kill the rest of her crew. Make them suffer. Eivor Wolf-Kissed is no more! That name is dead to this world!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: You will be worth your weight in silver. To the ship.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: You move and I take your eyes. You hear me?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Winds blowing from the south.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: We can tack north, then cut west.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Now, what did I just tell you, you...

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Kjotve will skin you alive! You will never... never leave this

speaker: Eivor
en: No feast for you, Sýnin. My crew is in danger. You must be my eyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: My crew is in danger. I need to reach them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mm. Better.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, I feel better. Stronger.

speaker: Eivor
en: Save that for later.

speaker: Eivor
en: Avaldsnes. Where that oath-breaker is holding my crew.

speaker: Eivor
en: One of Kjotve's men. I need to be careful.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kjotve's warriors. I should stay out of sight.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Once this land is under Kjotve's lash, we will live like jarls.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: It will not happen while Raven Clan lives. They fight like berserkers. Eivor Wolf-Kissed killed a score or more single-handed.

speaker: Eivor
en: A clash of iron. There is fighting nearby.

speaker: Dag
en: Grah!

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag, you old hound! You live!

speaker: Dag
en: I do! Slipped away in the sword-clash. And what of you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Kjotve tried to sell me off, a mistake he'll regret.

speaker: Dag
en: Not today he won't. I saw him board a ship at Avaldsnes not long ago. Sailed east, leaving our crew behind.

speaker: Eivor
en: There must still be time to save our men. I will find them. You ready the longship.

speaker: Dag
en: You glory hound! You would take the rescue for yourself, so the victory song is written about you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I could storm the beach then. Slay two dozen men, seize our dragon-boat, and hoist the sail in triumph. Up to you.

speaker: Dag
en: No, no. I will take the beach. A far more dangerous path. You search the longhouse for our crew.

speaker: Dag
en: O, and here... this corpse will not have need of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go. I'll meet you by the ship.

speaker: Eivor
en: The longhouse. My crew should be inside.

speaker: Rikiwulf
en: You squirm like that and my axe will miss your neck! Unpleasant for both of us.

speaker: Bragi
en: If I am to die, I want to make a mess of it, bacraut (asshole)!

speaker: Bragi
en: You coward! Unbind me and stick an axe in my hand!

speaker: Rikiwulf
en: I owe you nothing, raven-shit. Yours is a clan of thralls and peasants.

speaker: Eivor
en: You! Lay that axe aside or die by mine.

speaker: Rikiwulf
en: You should be on a slaves-ship to Ireland, Wolf-Kissed! But if you wish to be my first sacrifice, Odin will be more than happy to receive you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You just killed yourself, ergi (coward).

speaker: Rikiwulf
en: I will sell you to Hel herself! Kneel, Wolf-Kissed, and I will spare your life!

speaker: Eivor
en: Shut your hole and fight.

speaker: Rikiwulf
en: Die, you sack of shit!

speaker: Eivor
en: Father. You should have held onto this until the bitter end.

speaker: Varin
en: If I give my life, will you spare my clan?

speaker: Rosta
en: Varin! No! Pick up your axe.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: Kill them all!

speaker: Young Eivor
en: No!

speaker: Bragi
en: Eivor... Eivor!

speaker: Bragi
en: Eivor! Are you bewitched? Unbind us!

speaker: Eivor
en: What? O... yes, of course.

speaker: Bragi
en: Well fought, Wolf-Kissed! Even if your wits were somewhat rattled.

speaker: Eivor
en: Listen here! If you can breathe, you can fight. Now come, we take back our ship.

speaker: Bragi
en: You do not need to tell us twice!

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag, Bragi... grab your oars. The whale-road leads us home.

speaker: Dag
en: Gods, it is about time!

speaker: Bragi
en: Stop yawping and start rowing!

speaker: Dag
en: Rather silent, Eivor. Anything to say for the mess you led us to?

speaker: Eivor
en: We suffered no losses in this fight, and the men who humiliated us are dead. What is there to say?

speaker: Dag
en: O, something like, "I was stupid, selfish, reckless, blind, boneheaded, and I smell like blood and shit."

speaker: Eivor
en: I like my version better.

speaker: Dag
en: Eivor, look. Someone is setting up an outpost on that island.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kjotve's men. Gnawing at any piece of open land like dogs worrying a bone.

speaker: Dag
en: Even with you half in the grave, we could easily take them.

speaker: Dag
en: Kjotve will come for us, now. Harder and stronger than before.

speaker: Eivor
en: No surprise there. This war has spun on for three generations. I hardly expect him to relent.

speaker: Dag
en: Your hatred for that man burns bright, Wolf-Kissed! I could warm my balls on it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Would you not prefer a pair of sealskin britches?

speaker: Dag
en: Just take care, Eivor. Such hatred can make you careless. What he did to your father, he did to all of us. You are not in this fight alone. King Styrbjorn will scold you for setting out against his wishes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course he will.

speaker: Dag
en: Is that not something you worry over?

speaker: Eivor
en: I worry only that our king will not see that I'm right until it's too late.

speaker: Dag
en: What about Sigurd? What would he say?

speaker: Eivor
en: If Sigurd were here, he would be sitting beside you, wiping the blood from his axe and smiling into the breeze.

speaker: Dag
en: And what will you tell our king about this misadventure?

speaker: Eivor
en: Only the truth. That we attacked Kjotve's fortress, killed his men, and weakened his control of this land.

speaker: Dag
en: Will you mention the part where you lost your crew and were nearly sold as a thrall? Will that be part of your ?

speaker: Eivor
en: If there is a skald (poet) who dares sing that verse, it will be his last song.

speaker: Randvi
en: Well, well! The feeder-of-ravens returns. And not half dead. We though we had lost you, Eivor. For good this time.

speaker: Eivor
en: A warm welcome as always, Randvi.

speaker: Randvi
en: You look like reddened shit. What happened?

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing to crow about, except to say the men who delayed us are dead. And how are you?

speaker: Randvi
en: Well enough. Though I have spent many tiresome days calming the rages of our king. He is not happy with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I expected as much. And what of Sigurd? Has he returned from his raids?

speaker: Randvi
en: My husband should be home today. The last we heard, he was approaching Stavanger.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good to hear. We have need of his courage.

speaker: Dag
en: Sigurd will not save you from his father's wrath, Eivor. You should know that by now.

speaker: Randvi
en: Did your raid not go as planned?

speaker: Eivor
en: They rarely go as planned, but we killed many of Kjotve's warriors. And there was this... my father's axe among the dead.

speaker: Randvi
en: Ah! After so many years. You should take it to Gunnar. He will give it back its edge.

speaker: Eivor
en: A good idea. After I see our king.

speaker: Randvi
en: That I do not advise, not yet. He is meeting with a messenger from the North.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can wait...

speaker: Randvi
en: A cloud hangs over you. Is something wrong?

speaker: Eivor
en: Seeing my father's axe after seventeen winters... it stirred something in me. A feeling I have not had since... the day he was killed. Since I got this.

speaker: Randvi
en: Memories of past agonies. Of sadness and pain.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should speak with Valka. She could help me make sense of my... feelings.

speaker: Randvi
en: Take your time getting settled. I will see you at the longhouse.

speaker: Dag
en: I think you have lost your edge, Eivor, just like that axe. Maybe Gunnar can help with both.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will let you know.

speaker: Eivor
en: That must be Faravid's camp ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cold and dirty, must be the place.

speaker: Ulf
en: Throw yourself in Ginnungagap, you bastard. I am not a dog.

speaker: Faravid
en: Yet here you are, barking again.

speaker: Ulf
en: Because we beg for scraps at Halfdan's table. Like dogs.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid.

speaker: Faravid
en: Ah, Eivor my friend. Is Donecaestre hospitality to your liking?

speaker: Ulf
en: I'd be careful calling this one friend, Faravid. The crow who comes flapping when Halfdan gives a whistle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan and I spoke, and what of it?

speaker: Ulf
en: This is our fight, our chance for glory. Fly on home, crow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lend me a knife, Faravid. This whelp needs gelding.

speaker: Faravid
en: Ulf, piss off.

speaker: Faravid
en: Small men always talk big. So, was Halfdan generous? Did you get what you came for?

speaker: Eivor
en: If I help with your fight against the Picts, Halfdan will consider me a friend. So point the way, Faravid.

speaker: Faravid
en: The Picts raided that monastery, plundered its silver and gold.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Saxons build more churches than barns and fill them with herds of monks.

speaker: Faravid
en: Yes, monasteries make tempting targets, and not just for us. We tracked Pictish raiders heading north.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gold is fine, but victory is our treasure. What's your plan?

speaker: Faravid
en: To open their bellies with my knife.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know the place. My raiders sacked Elmet not long ago.

speaker: Faravid
en: Ah. And then they picked the bones left over from your feast.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm ready to fight. Let's put them in the ground.

speaker: Faravid
en: Halfdan didn't send you north to fight a skirmish we could win with half our numbers. Why are you here, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: In truth, he doubts your loyalty. Fears your heart is not in this fight.

speaker: Faravid
en: Doubts my loyalty? I have fought for Halfdan, killed for Halfdan, bled for Halfdan, and he doubts me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing I have seen gives me reason to doubt you. But Halfdan, he seems a cautious man.

speaker: Faravid
en: Cautious? He was always leery, but now fear's gnawed him down to the bone.

speaker: Eivor
en: To help you battle the Picts, nothing more. He knows my reputation and he knows what advantage I bring.

speaker: Eivor
en: You question my word?

speaker: Faravid
en: You never gave it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I give you my word, Faravid. I'm here to fight Picts.

speaker: Eivor
en: You question my word?

speaker: Faravid
en: You never gave it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I give you my word, Faravid. I'm here to fight Picts.

speaker: Faravid
en: To arms, dogs. Let's roast some Picts!

speaker: Faravid
en: Watch for ambushes.

speaker: Ulf
en: Shoulda stayed in Donecaestre. More mead, fewer Picts.

speaker: Faravid
en: There's no glory in guard duty. Move out!

speaker: Faravid
en: The Picts are just ahead. Lead the way and we'll watch your back.

speaker: Faravid
en: Keep it down or we're all dead.

speaker: Faravid
en: These Picts are a sneaky lot, masters of guile and ambush. Have a care.

speaker: Faravid
en: They spotted us! Run forward, faster, faster!

speaker: Faravid
en: Thank Thor, we made it. That was good war-work, all.

speaker: Eivor
en: This cave is a passage. The Picts are using it to cross the mountain.

speaker: Faravid
en: A gift for us. You track them through the cave, we'll circle around back and snare any who try to slip away.

speaker: Pict Warrior 1
en: I'm done in with raiding good and godly places. I should be home filling my belly, not mucking about on the wrong side of the wall.

speaker: Pict Warrior 2
en: Ah, boil your head. We'll gang forth with our friends soon, and then we'll all eat like kings. Heed my words. Wrong side of the wall.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Picts march this winter with help from an unknown quarter. Hmm.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Picts spoke of Stenwege. Their camp.

speaker: Faravid
en: That's to the north. Their chief may be there.

speaker: Pict Warrior 3
en: Danes! Run!

speaker: Faravid
en: Stop them! Before they reach Stenwege!

speaker: Faravid
en: They spotted us! Run forward, faster, faster!

speaker: Pict Warrior 3
en: Run! The heathens have found us!

speaker: Ulf
en: Ulf! Ulf! Glory for Ulf!

speaker: Pict Warrior 4
en: Go home! Go home!

speaker: Eivor
en: They'll tell the chief!

speaker: Pict Warrior 4
en: To Stenwege! The chief must know!

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't let them get inside! Stop them!

speaker: Faravid
en: That's the last one!

speaker: Faravid
en: They got away.

speaker: Faravid
en: Pict raiders, south of the wall. Don't like it.

speaker: Faravid
en: Let us regroup at Stenwege. We need to plan our next move.

speaker: Faravid
en: The Picts don't raid often during winter.

speaker: Eivor
en: Their scouts are dead. The Picts won't know we're here.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Picts will be on guard. Have a care.

speaker: Faravid
en: The hornets have led us to their nest. More than a chief up there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like the forward camp of an army. But would the Picts dare attack in winter?

speaker: Faravid
en: Halfdan thinks not. And the Picts may use that to their advantage.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's find out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why would the Picts make war in winter? They must have a reason, something to gain.

speaker: Pict Warrior 5
en: Nothing I can see out there.

speaker: Pict Warrior 5
en: Give me a swing at those Danes!

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, to hunt down the Pict chief.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's the chief. Now to strike him down.

speaker: Pict Warrior 6
en: Have you come to join your fallen? Hah!

speaker: Pict Warrior 6
en: You Norse are simple. Simple fight. Simple death.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're on the wrong side of the giants' wall, friend. Have you come to make war in wint

speaker: Eivor
en: Fool! He might have talked!

speaker: Faravid
en: We got what we came for.

speaker: Ulf
en: Is that more Frankish wine? I'll take a few casks, and that silver there.

speaker: Faravid
en: Ulf... that's Halfdan's share.

speaker: Faravid
en: Eivor, just in time to divide the spoils. Take some mead, if you like.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Picts are at Magnis. This map spells it out.

speaker: Ulf
en: Ah, the Wolf-Kissed is a reader. That's dark seidr (magic) I'll never mess with.

speaker: Faravid
en: Worry about the Picts later. Now's the time for treasure and spoils. You earned it.

speaker: Ulf
en: It should be ours, we did the work! All of it. And nothing for Halfdan, warming his cock in a Saxon castle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Open that cask and we'll have a taste. We'll celebrate, together.

speaker: Faravid
en: Sorry, friend, but that's Halfdan's take. You understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fair enough. Halfdan gets what he is owed.

speaker: Ulf
en: Fuck Halfdan. If the Raven wants wine, the Raven gets wine. Open it, Faravid.

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't make me say it twice. Crack the wine and drink with me.

speaker: Eivor
en: He won't notice one missing cask, so unless there's something wrong with it, let's have a taste.

speaker: Faravid
en: There's nothing wrong with it, friend.

speaker: Faravid
en: If you insist, we'll all drink some stinking wine.

speaker: Faravid
en: A little sour but not bad. I've always preferred ale myself. Or spiced mead. What I won't drink is one of Moira's herbal brews. She claims they're a tonic. But there's no telling what she hides in those drinks.

speaker: Eivor
en: Moira. I met her at the feast.

speaker: Eivor
en: Moira? Who is she?

speaker: Faravid
en: She's an herbalist from the north. Always skulking in the shadow of Halfdan's throne.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a big throne. Don't you all skulk around it from time to time?

speaker: Faravid
en: I see. Because Halfdan thinks I'm disloyal, now you don't trust me. Has our battle-bond earned me no favors with you, Eivor?

speaker: Faravid
en: Why all these doubts, Eivor? You're a warrior, not a rumormonger.

speaker: Eivor
en: Doubt is too strong a word. But there is a feeling of mistrust among you. I want this alliance to be ironclad.

speaker: Faravid
en: Then let me change your mind. I've got a plan to win this war for good. Before the winter sets in. Magnis is a strong fort, but we'd be attacking from the south. With speed, we'll catch them off guard.

speaker: Eivor
en: With Halfdan's blessing, I'd fight beside you anywhere. Name the time and place.

speaker: Faravid
en: No. Halfdan is done fighting for the winter. He thinks it too great a risk. But I say we can win this war before the next snows. If we tell him of this plan, he'll refuse. But if we succeed, you and I together, he'll sing our praises all the louder.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right, we fight. And I swear by Sif's blade, I'll say nothing to Halfdan.

speaker: Faravid
en: Good, good. Victory is ours.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll fight with you, Faravid, but I will not lie to Halfdan if he asks.

speaker: Faravid
en: If you tell him, he'll demand we forswear our attack. Are you willing to risk a victory like that? Our glory?

speaker: Eivor
en: If I tell him, he'll know what we intend, but we'll fight nonetheless, in spite of his anger.

speaker: Faravid
en: Fair is fair.

speaker: Eivor
en: There are no secrets in this world or the next. The All-Father sees everything.

speaker: Faravid
en: We need not fear Odin's eye, only Halfdan's wrath.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must return for Donecaestre for a time, but I will join you for this battle.

speaker: Faravid
en: Deliver this goblet to my jarl. He has a fondness for them. And tell him his share of the spoils is coming.

speaker: Faravid
en: When you're ready, find me near Jorvik at a place called The Wolds.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: We have it! Stenwege is ours!

speaker: Ulf
en: Halfdan's share shrinks after each victory. Like his cock, eh?

speaker: Faravid
en: Halfdan will be waiting for his gift in Donecaestre. Don't keep him waiting.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid should be waiting at Stenwege.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Where's Halfdan Jarl? Will he be here?

speaker: Faravid
en: Eivor! Good to see you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are the Saxons? We need them to take that fortress.

speaker: Faravid
en: Patience. Ricsige promised an army.

speaker: Eivor
en: What about Hjorr and Ljufvina?

speaker: Faravid
en: Ljufvina is ahead with a dozen of Jorvik's swords. Come. Our Saxon allies have reached Magnis. We should march.

speaker: Faravid
en: Meet us on the field near the fortress. We'll make our plans there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will Halfdan join us? Or stay home, out of spite.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan doesn't know our plan. But he'll hear the aftermath soon enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: This plan... I feel uneasy.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: It'll be a good fight, I've faith in it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid's plan had better be sound.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let us hope this goes well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid's army.

speaker: Faravid
en: Eivor, over here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Today you may regain your glory. Think on that.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: We did wrong to follow Ulf and would make things right by following you this day.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Are the shields ready? The battle is near.

speaker: Halfdan
en: On the battlefield once more, old friend.

speaker: Faravid
en: Yes, my jarl. As in days of old.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Who are you to speak of the old days? The days where my word was bond. The days where the light of my glory lit the world. How dare you speak of those days! As if they meant anything to a traitor like you!

speaker: Faravid
en: Who told you of this?

speaker: Halfdan
en: My new ally is more loyal than my old friend.

speaker: Faravid
en: Eivor Two-Faced. That's your name.

speaker: Eivor
en: I came for Halfdan. To prove my worth and loyalty to him. You brought this down upon yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gently, friend. I told Halfdan because it was my duty.

speaker: Halfdan
en: My Saxon vassal is more loyal than any man in my army!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ricsige. That silk-tongued devil!

speaker: Halfdan
en: Silk-tongued and loyal to the end, you backstabbing curs! Both of you! Traitorous schemers!

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a sick man, Halfdan. You see traitors under every cobble, behind every tree.

speaker: Halfdan
en: A sick man? You deny you went behind my back?

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough, Halfdan. Name your traitors when the fighting's done.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Easy for you. Nobody's poisoning your damn wine.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Enough bickering, all of you! We are at the edge of war. Preserve your rage for the enemy!

speaker: Halfdan
en: Ljufvina talks sense. We fight this battle and we end this war. At this moment, nothing else matters.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Look there. The Picts send a message.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Raven-Tamer, with me. You'll talk them into a surrender with your sword-sharp tongue.

speaker: Halfdan
