en: Stay back, men.

speaker: Eivor
en: These Picts came in great numbers. They came to fight.

speaker: Halfdan
en: If this is a trick, do what you must. Draw steel and cut them down like harvest corn.

speaker: Eivor
en: Turn tail and run, back beyond the wall.

speaker: Pict Warrior 1
en: The Romans built that wall to keep us out. But they are gone and we remain. Someday you too will disappear.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Wall or no wall, we have more gods than you.

speaker: Pict Warrior 1
en: We may have but one God, heathen, but we have many more friends.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Who now is the rightful king of Northumbria?

speaker: Ricsige
en: The kingdom has spoken!

speaker: Halfdan
en: Glory for Halfdan! I'll have your head, Ricsige!

speaker: Faravid
en: Die you bastard dogs!

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Careful. They mean to burn us!

speaker: Eivor
en: Extend the ladders!

speaker: Faravid
en: Charge! And may the skalds remember us!

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to get that drawbridge down.

speaker: Faravid
en: Press on! Let the Picts remember this in their Hell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eyes open for the coward, King Ricsige.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Attack! Attack for Halfdan! This is the last of them!

speaker: Halfdan
en: For Thor! For Ragnar! For Halfdan! The sweet taste of victory. And Ricsige defeated. Was he the thorn at my back? The traitor I suspected all this time?

speaker: Eivor
en: Save your praise, Halfdan. Ricsige may yet live.

speaker: Halfdan
en: That coward will be dead in a snowdrift somewhere. It matters not.

speaker: Eivor
en: This day is not done until we've seen his corpse. Do not relent, not yet.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Eivor. Rise like an eagle, or caw like a crow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hold the wall!

speaker: Eivor
en: Block that gate!

speaker: Halfdan
en: Thor sends more Pict skulls to my hammer.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Ricsige! There!

speaker: Faravid
en: He's fleeing to the north!

speaker: Ricsige
en: Leave me be, you devil!

speaker: Eivor
en: You meet the spirits this day, traitor.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Faithful counselor. Please, help me back to Jorvik. Let my heart expire at home.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no favors left to offer you, Ricsige. Soon you will walk beside your god.

speaker: Ricsige
en: But I... I see no light. I feel no warmth. Only... an icy darkness, a cave.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hel's frozen door, welcoming you.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Wh-what waits for me there, Eivor? What waits for me?

speaker: Halfdan
en: A traitor's death for a treasonous fool.

speaker: Eivor
en: He was a hero in tales he told himself. A Saxon who loved his homeland. You cannot begrudge him that.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Hmph. There is something in that. No more Saxon kings, Eivor. I am through playing the puppeteer. The fate of this shire rests on my shoulders alone.

speaker: Eivor
en: You'll take the crown yourself? And the extra burden it brings?

speaker: Halfdan
en: I will. But I won't rule alone. My friends... and my allies... will keep me standing upright.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Let's talk of our alliance in Jorvik. Leave this king to his winter kingdom.

speaker: Eivor
en: There, that's the statue the Zealots use.

speaker: The Mark
en: Eivor of the Raven Clan - Ledecestre

speaker: Eivor
en: Done. Nothing but smoke and ashes now. That should get those Zealots off my back.

speaker: Havi
en: I've gathered enough of these fragments. I wonder what a decent blacksmith can do with them.

speaker: Havi
en: I've gathered enough silica. Time to seek out a blacksmith and see what they can do for me.

speaker: Grungir
en: Seems like you've got enough materials to enhance your bracer. Give it here and let me see what I can do.

speaker: Elga
en: Seems like you've got enough materials to enhance your bracer. Give it here and let me see what I can do.

speaker: Skavi
en: Seems like you've got enough materials to enhance your bracer. Give it here and let me see what I can do.

speaker: Haf
en: You have plenty stuff. Make bracer better. Give. I fix it.

speaker: Eivor
en: He seems eager to trade goods and wares.

speaker: Eivor
en: Olav, tell me about your falling out with Gorm.

speaker: Olav
en: He caught me stealing from his locked chests. I wished to trade with the villagers here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then he gave you a good thrashing, did he?

speaker: Olav
en: Yes, yes. Now I stay in my safe place.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can hike into the woods, straight for Gorm... or gather raw materials and trade for better weapons.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gorm is in these woods somewhere. I will find you, Gorm. No matter how long it takes. Where are you hiding, Gorm?

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods, hurting all over... thought I was dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: You want me to... to eat these?

speaker: Eivor
en: Our friends healed me with their berries. I am grateful.

speaker: Olav
en: Yes, yes. And elderberries have a good taste, too. And good for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I feel much better. Do these elderberries grow wild around here?

speaker: Olav
en: Yes, yes. All through the land, here and there.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you come here, Olav? Are you a prisoner here?

speaker: Olav
en: No, no! The cave is my safe place. Safe from Gorm and his anger. Safe from the talking crystal.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see.

speaker: Olav
en: Watching, always watching Olav! The talking crystal!

speaker: Eivor
en: A camp near the village. Gorm could be there.

speaker: Eivor
en: One of Gorm's camps. I might learn where he's hiding. Or find some resources at the least.

speaker: Eivor
en: One step closer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gorm must be near. His doom has come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why is this place so heavily guarded? What are you hiding, Gorm?

speaker: Eivor
en: The leader of this bridge cliff camp may know Gorm's whereabouts.

speaker: Gorm
en: Keep digging, you beardless dogs!

speaker: Thegn 1
en: You heard the man! Move those shovels!

speaker: Gorm
en: Power beyond measure awaits us, men! A mountain of silver to the first digger to open the way!

speaker: Thegn 2
en: Gorm, we have found nothing but a gate we cannot open.

speaker: Gorm
en: I shall call upon our ally. Heed me, Gorm of the Order. Ancient Ones, I summon you! Speak to me, you stone-dwelling god-woman!

speaker: Juno
en: In time, what once was, shall be again.

speaker: Gorm
en: What does that gibberish mean? Gods burn it all. Keep digging, mules. Power beyond measure awaits. Power beyond measure.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gorm Kjotvesson.

speaker: Thegn 2
en: Gorm, did you find Olav the Unlucky?

speaker: Gorm
en: I did. I locked him away for thieving. And when I return, I will see that the beasts of the woods pick at his flesh 'til his bones are clean. Nobody steals from me and walks away breathing. What news from our camps?

speaker: Thegn 2
en: In truth, they have grown quiet. Little to no word at all.

speaker: Gorm
en: Hm. No matter. Focus our efforts on the dig.

speaker: Thegn 2
en: Sir, I hate to ask, but...

speaker: Gorm
en: What? Spit it out.

speaker: Thegn 2
en: It may be your talking crystal is a Dwarvish trick. As in the sagas when

speaker: Gorm
en: Silence! Speak no treason against my Order. We are all-wise, all-knowing, and all-powerful. Better to cut out your own tongue than speak against the crystal goddess.

speaker: Gorm
en: Eivor Wolf-Kissed!

speaker: Eivor
en: I crossed the broad sea for you, Gorm. Are you not flattered?

speaker: Gorm
en: For one reason only, I see. You snake.

speaker: Eivor
en: One reason only!

speaker: Gorm
en: Wait. Wait. This is not the hall of five hundred doors. This is not the rock of the fallen. Where are the women on the winged horses?

speaker: Gorm
en: Where are the Choosers of the Slain?

speaker: Gorm
en: You. My blood enemy.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is Niflheim, the hell of mist and cold. This is where faithless dead come to die again. This is where ghosts fade to mist, to be forgotten.

speaker: Gorm
en: Your meddling has doomed us all, crow of battle.

speaker: Eivor
en: More lies from a liar born. Now speak the truth. What brought the Order to this place?

speaker: Gorm
en: To free a goddess, a creature of power and light... buried by the Jötnar in ages past.

speaker: Eivor
en: A pity, Gorm. You will not meet her now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gorm's crystal-eye. It hums with a strange feeling. Unearthly. What was Gorm digging for? Something deep inside this cave?

speaker: Eivor
en: Olav should know his tormentor is dead. I owe him that much.

speaker: Unknown Voice
en: The probabilities lead us here. The calculations give us hope.

speaker: Eivor
en: This... this is not for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should return to Olav. He deserves to know what happened here.

speaker: Eivor
en: No need to hide now, Olav. Gorm is dead.

speaker: Olav
en: Gorm... dead? B-by your hand?

speaker: Eivor
en: He paid a bloody price for broken honor. I will not say more. Return to your sister.

speaker: Olav
en: O, I will! Yet I would first join the villagers at their fire. They tell stories and I like to listen, though I do not hear.

speaker: Eivor
en: Storytime? Telling s of their own?

speaker: Olav
en: Yes, yes. They tell stories, yes. Come, listen!

speaker: Konwahawíhshon
en: Sok ki' Rarón:tote' wahshakohró:ri' ne Iottsi'tsíson, wahèn:ron' "Háo' tho iétene tsi nón:we rotihsken'rakéhte' tionkkwirotakwén:ni." Tehnitsá:ron ki' tho thní:tahkwe', ia'tehnikà:nere' tsi iohsón:waien tánon' akwé:kon kahsonwahòn:tsi. Iottsi'tsíson iakotatenekwen'tawà:kon, tànon' Rarón:tote' iehsòn:ne ì:rate'. (Then Rarón:tote' told Iottsi'tíson, he said "Okay, we'll both go where the men are unearthing the tree for me." They were both standing there, they saw a hole and the hole was all black. Iottsi'tsíson is holding her belly and Rarón:tote' is standing next to the hole.)

speaker: Konwahawíhshon
en: Sok ki' ohsón:wakon ia'ontke'tó:ten', á:ienhrek tóká' tkahné:kare'. Thontaiawénhstsi', Rarón:tote' iahshakò:reke'. Ohsón:wakon ia'eià:ten'ne' ne Iottsi'tsíson. Tsi wa'akoia'ten'hátie' wa'eienahá:ton' tsi nahò:ten' wa'ekwé:ni'. Ohtehra'shòn:'a, kahtehrowá:nen's tánon' ken' nikahtehrà:sa's ia'éhawe' tsi ia'eià:ten'ne' tsi tetiotshonwà:karas. (Then she looked in the hole, and it seemed as though there was water in it. All of a sudden, Rarón:tote' pushed her. Iottsi'tsíson fell in the hole. While falling, she grabbed on to whatever she could. She then grabbed and brought all sorts of roots, big and small, down with her into that dark hole.)

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. You want me to tell a story. All right. Let me think...

speaker: Eivor
en: A story of betrayal. Of selfish malice. And of gods who act as spoiled children. Of all our many gods, it is Odin who is the most revered. He is the All-Father, the High One, the wise king. But for all his glories, he can also be the most elusive of his kind. Selfish, solitary, stubborn... even cruel. In days long gone, it came to pass that Odin's son Baldr died suddenly, felled by his only weakness. Mistletoe. Believing his son's death an accident, Odin sent a message to the Jotun, Hel, asking her to return his beautiful boy to life. Hel agreed, but on one condition. Only if every living creature in the nine worlds shed a loving tear for Baldr. At once, Odin sent word to every corner of the world, asking all to weep for his beloved boy. And all did... but one. A Jotun named Thokk refused to cry for Baldr. "Let Hel keep what she has received," Thokk said with malice. And that was that. Baldr was gone forever, sent on a funeral-ship across the sea, buried in Midgard amid trees and rocks. What Odin did not know, is that Thokk was none other than the trickster Loki in disguise, a god he knew as a friend. Worse still, it was Loki who led Baldr to his death by a sprig of mistletoe. All these tricks and feints, Loki had conceived. Some say it was in Loki's nature to be so cruel. Others argue it was revenge for deeds done by Odin to Loki and his children. There is a third view. That all these acts, kind and cruel, were sewn long ago in the pattern of their lives. That we are not the authors of our own destiny, but only its readers. And that we... O...

speaker: Eivor
en: ...that we should fight against this view. For it is deeply unwelcome.

speaker: Karonhiaktátie
en: Enkwakaratón:hahse' ne A'nó:wara raoká:ra, né: ne oh ní:ioht tsi wa'thate'nówiia'ke'... (I'll tell you a story about a turtle, about how its shell was broken...)

speaker: Eivor
en: Gorm brought this stone across the whale-road for a strange purpose. I do not know why, but it seems to belong to this land.

speaker: Konwahawíhshon
en: Ióhskats. Kwah rahsnonhsà:ke wenhni'táhere'. (Beautiful. The moon is at your fingertips.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Take it. And guard it. It may be that one day you will know its purpose.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, each of you. For all you have done.

speaker: Konwahawíhshon
en: Aiá:wen's ki' iethihsothokon'kénha aiesahaharáhten', Kenhnarà:ken. (White woman, I hope your ancestors will guide you on your path.)

speaker: Helgi
en: No word from Gorm. And he has taken all the ale. So much work for so little reward!

speaker: Worker Man
en: Thanks for wrecking the voyage. Now I've got no work. What a hero.

speaker: Fortune Seeker
en: What a waste. No gold, no glory, nothing but rain, trees, and Gorm's lies.

speaker: Wet Blanket
en: I told you so.

speaker: Hilde
en: Jora of Jorvik! You shirked your work for quite some time!

speaker: Eivor
en: Jora is no more. My name is Eivor, a drengr of the Raven Clan. And my purpose is fulfilled.

speaker: Hilde
en: Purpose? What purpose?

speaker: Olav
en: Gorm is dead! The troll is dead!

speaker: Hilde
en: Olav?

speaker: Olav
en: Sister, let us celebrate! Gorm Kjotvesson is no more! Slain by Eivor Raven-friend. Eivor Forest-strider. Eivor Olav-saver!

speaker: Hilde
en: What is this?

speaker: Eivor
en: I had a long-standing blood feud with Gorm and his clan. It is now laid to rest.

speaker: Olav
en: O, the skalds will sing of this day! How Eivor traveled far and wide, hunting Gorm along the world's rim!

speaker: Eivor
en: Songs or not, Gorm is dead. Now I suggest you leave this place. There is no purpose for us here.

speaker: Hilde
en: I... I do not disagree. Gorm was a madman and a troll, indeed. But he paid us in silver, and that was enough. Brother, are you well? I feared the worst for you.

speaker: Olav
en: I am well, yes. O so well. And I may stay! To linger, one season or two, with the friends I have made.

speaker: Hilde
en: As you wish, Brother. And you... Eivor. Where will you go? Across the sea with us? Or back into the woods?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will sail with you. Let's go.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take care of yourself, Olav, in this life and the next.

speaker: Olav
en: Goodbye. Goodbye!

speaker: Eivor
en: Far wends the whale-road before me. Dark are the deeds that brought me here. Fate may bind my bones to this land, but for now, I walk the sea.

speaker: Eivor
en: A few tasks remain. But I will ready myself and return.

speaker: Hilde
en: I can linger a few days in port. Speak to me when you're ready to sail.

speaker: Hilde
en: Eivor, you return to us.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do.

speaker: Hilde
en: Ready to lift an oar on our long voyage back to England?

speaker: Eivor
en: The tracks have disappeared. We need to split up and sweep for signs.

speaker: Viking 3
en: Yes, lord, but... what is it we are chasing? A stack of paper? What need has our king of this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Trouble yourself over the spears of the foe. Kjotve's life itself is worthy enough cause.

speaker: Viking 3
en: Of course, lord.

speaker: Warrior
en: You will go no further, Raven's get! The Valkyries call your names!

speaker: Eivor
en: The trail has been largely trampled, but I have picked up our quarry. Here!

speaker: Viking 3
en: These tracks are fresh. We're closing on them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Prepare yourselves. Kjotve will not just hand over what he has taken, and his very best will be with him.

speaker: Frodri
en: Hey you! Pssst! Help me! This bear is trying to kill me! Please help!

speaker: Frodri
en: Ha! No dwarf dinner for you, you greedy beast!

speaker: Havi
en: There, you're safe. What enraged the beast?

speaker: Frodri
en: Haven't the faintest idea! One minute I was frying some bacon, and the next, that brute was trying to steal it!

speaker: Havi
en: You... were cooking? Here?

speaker: Frodri
en: Of course! Damn well lost my appetite now though, haven't I? Stupid bear.

speaker: Havi
en: I'm not so sure it's the bear who was stupid.

speaker: Frodri
en: Of course, this is yet another tale within the cursed saga that is my life! That's right... I am cursed! This damn ring. Nothing but bad luck ever since I got it!

speaker: Havi
en: Are you sure you know the difference between bad luck and a bad choice?

speaker: Frodri
en: So! I have taken upon myself to rid the world of the ring and its cursed seidr. I shall destroy it! And I'd jolly well appreciate it if you accompanied me.

speaker: Havi
en: You seek my protection for... disposing of a ring?

speaker: Frodri
en: Not just any ring! A cursed ring! Cursed by a Jotun witch!

speaker: Havi
en: A Jotun witch? Now you have peaked my interest. Tell me your tale as we walk, and you will have my aid.

speaker: Havi
en: This ring−

speaker: Frodri
en: Cursed ring!

speaker: Havi
en: This cursed ring. How did you acquire it?

speaker: Frodri
en: Focus on the destination! Not the journey! Ours shall end soon, atop this very mountain! Finally, my unlucky saga will end! (stomach grumbling) Ugh... that damned bear. Its claws couldn't claim me, but hunger still might!

speaker: Havi
en: Didn't you say you lost your appetite?

speaker: Frodri
en: Pish-posh! My heroic voyage requires sustenance!

speaker: Frodri
en: Ah! I am saved! Mushrooms! And so colorful!

speaker: Havi
en: Stop. Do not eat those mushrooms. They're−

speaker: Havi
en: You truly are an idiot, aren't you.

speaker: Frodri
en: Curse that ring! It somehow poisoned the mushrooms!

speaker: Havi
en: Just... stay there. And don't eat anything else off the ground. I'll get something you can eat.

speaker: Frodri
en: Oh you are... (retches) you are kind. Do hurry though... (burps)

speaker: Frodri
en: Ooh, my stomach.

speaker: Havi
en: Some actual food will settle it. Possibly.

speaker: Frodri
en: Good thinking! You, uh, happen to have any? That bear got all of mine.

speaker: Havi
en: Here, eat this.

speaker: Frodri
en: Oh... well, I guess it will have to do.

speaker: Frodri
en: Well, let's not dally any further. Come along.

speaker: Havi
en: You mentioned a Jotun witch? Did she give you the ring? Or was she the one who cursed it?

speaker: Frodri
en: I cannot say for sure. I saw her travelling, like she was in a hurry. I wanted to question her, y'see. A Jotun, alone, obviously up to no good.

speaker: Havi
en: Did you happen to catch her name?

speaker: Frodri
en: Of course! Hear-oh-kin, I think?

speaker: Havi
en: Hyrrokin? You saw her in Svartalfheim?

speaker: Frodri
en: Pretty sure it was Hear-oh-kin. Either way, she gave me the ring. Just gave it to me. Told me it would bring me good luck, but that it must be kept far away from her for the magic to work.

speaker: Havi
en: I have used the exact same tactic with my children, more than once.

speaker: Frodri
en: No, you misunderstand... she gave me the wrong ring! This one is cursed! Nothing but bad luck happening to me all the time. It's so draining, But the end of my suffering is nigh... We're almost there! Come on, this looks like a shortcut!

speaker: Frodri
en: Agh! What's that! Get away! Get away! Jormungundr himself!

speaker: Frodri
en: Come along! This ring won't destroy itself.

speaker: Havi
en: The path is surely clear enough for you now.

speaker: Frodri
en: Well, the land could be flatter, but I suppose this will do... Now, let me tell you more of my perilous plight. Why, my bad fortune would make even Gæfuleysi look like the luckiest dwarf alive.

speaker: Havi
en: I suggest silence. Less, uh, chance of being overheard by further dangerous animals.

speaker: Frodri
en: Yes, yes, good thinking. My words cannot be unlucky if they are unspoken. You are wise!

speaker: Frodri
en: Here! We are here! My salvation is finally at hand!

speaker: Havi
en: Then do not delay. Rid yourself of the ring−

speaker: Frodri
en: Cursed ring! How many times...! Have you even been listening?!

speaker: Havi
en: More than I would like. Cursed ring, yes. Go on, get it done.

speaker: Frodri
en: Yes! I shall finally be free of this torment! This burden!

speaker: Havi
en: I know the feeling...

speaker: Frodri
en: Be gone, foul−

speaker: Frodri
en: Aa-aaaaaaagh!

speaker: Havi
en: Very unfortunate.

speaker: Havi
en: Interesting. The ring survived, just down there, I see.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this where justice hides when she's tired?

speaker: Goodwin
en: Hides? S'plood, no! This is a wake, my friend. A celebration to ease The Quill on her way to eternal damnation.

speaker: Eivor
en: You heard.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Hilda's were not only eyes in Wincestre. My spies tell me stories of an avenging angel striking down the unworthy.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have been called worse.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Be thou hale, Ealdorbana! That's life-destroyer in our dialect.

speaker: Eivor
en: I sat easy with my kins-bane, old honey-waves alive in my horn, and my eyes on the door, expecting my death, yet unafraid.

speaker: Goodwin
en: You're quite safe with me, Dane. For now. If the mead is fresh and the air is cool, you may often find a friend, even amongst your enemies.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could use someone like you in my settlement. With ink on his fingers and a sense of honor.

speaker: Goodwin
en: I would love to devote myself to the study and practice of the law. There is a weariness in war I wish I could shake off.

speaker: Eivor
en: Impossible. Even in death, our battles will rage on. It's the way of things.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does a reeve do, exactly? Besides sniff around the king's coattails for the scent of praise?

speaker: Goodwin
en: I enforce and interpret the laws here. Not man's, but God's law, the natural laws that move the world and hold it together.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, if it keeps you busy...

speaker: Eivor
en: Your English mead, Goodwin... it tastes like cat piss.

speaker: Eivor
en: In Mercia we would drink ten times this. And feast till our names were forgotten and our britches were lost to the forest.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Does that happen?

speaker: Eivor
en: As often as possible.

speaker: Goodwin
en: I must thank you before the ale dulls me. By cutting The Order down to size, you have given England a hope of unity. It must be a sour apple to swallow, knowing that you are the last of Wincestre's enemies.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sure The Seax is dead?

speaker: Eivor
en: A reward will ease my hurt. As much silver as a longship can carry.

speaker: Goodwin
en: All in good time. A witan has been called to deal with our dead bishop. When this business is done, Aelfred will shower you with silver.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sure The Seax is dead?

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is your king now?

speaker: Goodwin
en: Aelfred is busy with the Ealdormen of Wessex. A witan was lately called to discuss the little matter of a bishop's timely death.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sure The Seax is dead?

speaker: Goodwin
en: The bishop is dead, that's certain. And if the bishop was The Seax, The Seax is dead. A transitive property of mortality, you see?

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't believe it. Too much theater in Wincestre. Overwrought prayers and wailing women.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Well, you could pay your respects and see for yourself. The funeral is today.

speaker: Eivor
en: If he rots, I will leave with my silver. But if he lives, there's work to be done.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Watch your step, Eivor. He'll be a hefty corpse in death. Alive he'd be much bigger.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Whether you find or make a corpse, meet me at the witan with your report.

speaker: Eivor
en: If the bishop is worm meal, then here should be the proof.

speaker: Harriet
en: Lord, grant my brother Ealhferth eternal bliss, where joy endures for all those beloved of God.

speaker: Eivor
en: A sad day for Wincestre.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Maybe now, God will reward us with a man who truly believes in him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you know Bishop Ealfherth?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: No, but I plan to write an epic poem of his grisly demise. O, poor Ealhferth, scorched of face. All your woeful companions, bold ' (armored), weeping, weeping as you are... er...

speaker: Eivor
en: Sleeping?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Perfect! Yes!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you the bishop's family?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: God no. Just here to make sure that impious bastard is actually dead. He bedded my wife, the randy bastard!

speaker: Eivor
en: Such a grisly fate. Did you know Ealhferth?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: By reputation, I did. He was no friend of Aelfred's. I once heard them quarreling at a witan.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am sorry for your loss.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Makes no odds to me. But I am sorry for Harriet. She cared so much for him, more than a sister should.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you know Bishop Ealhferth?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Barely. But can you still smell the burned flesh? It's rife across the whole graveyard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Only his face was burned. That seems like a strange accident.

speaker: Eivor
en: Only his head and neck are burned. Is this what Wemba meant? That they stole his friend's face?

speaker: Eivor
en: These clothes do not seem to fit this frail body.

speaker: Eivor
en: The face is burned, and his clothes don't seem to fit his frail body. It could be Wemba's friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: And this corpse's build is slight, frail. Goodwin said Ealhferth was a brute.

speaker: Eivor
en: A peasant's clothes? Strange discovery in a churchyard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Threadbare clothes. Did they belong to Wemba's friend?

speaker: Wemba
en: A stranger comes to Wemba.

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't mourn like they do.

speaker: Wemba
en: Wemba's always here. Helping the sleeping. Singing to them, so they are not frightened before they meet God.

speaker: Eivor
en: The sleeping? You mean the dead?

speaker: Wemba
en: Wemba helps the monks. Dig, dig, dig.

speaker: Eivor
en: You dig the graves. Did you bury Ealhferth?

speaker: Wemba
en: Have you seen Leof? My poor friend. Poor, poor Leof.

speaker: Eivor
en: Leof? What happened to him?

speaker: Wemba
en: Sleeping, sleeping like my dog when I hugged him too hard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone hurt Leof?

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw a pile of dirty clothes just here. Is your friend Leof a beggar?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not interested in your friend, you moon-calf. I want to know what you've seen.

speaker: Wemba
en: Leof spoke with the bishop's friend. They showed him their gleaming blade.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone hurt him? Is that what you mean? Speak up!

speaker: Eivor
en: What about the bishop, Ealhferth? Did you dig his grave?

speaker: Wemba
en: No, no. I don't bury a lord in a pauper's husk. Poor Leof, they showed him their gleaming blade.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone hurt your friend, Leof?

speaker: Wemba
en: Yes, yes. And while he sleeped, they stole his face.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not just stolen, but burned.

speaker: Wemba
en: It's you. Did you find dear Leof? It is lonely without him.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sorry, Wemba. I think someone killed your friend.

speaker: Wemba
en: Hm. Then I will sing a sad song, for he was the only one who ever cared for me. May angels welcome him. (humming)

speaker: Wemba
en: Are we friends now?

speaker: Wemba
en: You hurt Wemba with your stinging words. Bad, bad, bad.

speaker: Eivor
en: This funeral is a shadow-play. The Order killed an innocent, burned his face so no one could tell, and interred him in Ealhferth's place. His sister knows more than she lets on.

speaker: Harriet
en: Leave me to my grief.

speaker: Harriet
en: What now?

speaker: Eivor
en: A pretty show you've laid on here. But I know the truth.

speaker: Harriet
en: You would dare speak to me? When my poor brother Ealhferth lies cold in his shroud?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your brother is The Seax. And no more dead than I am.

speaker: Harriet
en: Heresy. My brother was the bishop of Wincestre!

speaker: Eivor
en: How better to hide than behind a bishop's robes? He is no man of God. He serves The Order. And you buried him when Goodwin got too close to the truth. Or rather, you buried another in his place, the poor gravedigger's friend.

speaker: Harriet
en: I, no, you cannot just...

speaker: Eivor
en: When Goodwin got too close to the truth about your brother's place in The Order, you buried him. Or rather, you buried another in his place. The poor gravedigger's friend, burning his face so no one would know.

speaker: Harriet
en: How did you... no... I

speaker: Eivor
en: Your brother's not in that crypt. Tell me where he is before more lives are lost.

speaker: Harriet
en: I will not tell you anymore. Guards!

speaker: Harriet
en: Alright, alright. Have your way. It won't do you any good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Talk now or you will join the poor unfortunate you murdered in his grave.

speaker: Harriet
en: You bastard Dane! You're as bad as them. I only ever wanted to serve God. Guards!

speaker: Harriet
en: Alright, alright. Have your way. It won't do you any good.

speaker: Harriet
en: Do you not see I am in prayer?

speaker: Eivor
en: May we speak of your brother's death?

speaker: Harriet
en: Have you no shame? Leave me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know the burden you bear. Such a weight of sin you have taken on, and all for your brother's sake. I know he lives.

speaker: Harriet
en: No, he's... he said it was for the good of all, he... I am his loyal sister, and I tell you he is dead. You hear me? Dead!

speaker: Harriet
en: Leave me alone, I cannot betray my brother.

speaker: Eivor
en: We both know your brother's faith was a cloak of lies. He used your God's words for his own ends.

speaker: Harriet
en: Who are you to judge a man of faith? You, a Dane who believes in giants and wolves that eat the sun! Begone!

speaker: Harriet
en: Get away from me, demon.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will leave you in peace, then.

speaker: Harriet
en: Guards, protect me!

speaker: Harriet
en: Why are you doing this?

speaker: Harriet
en: Why won't you leave me alone!

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough of this cat and mouse. Where is your brother, the one they call The Seax?

speaker: Harriet
en: He's a ghost now. But he will make himself flesh once more at the witan. And Aelfred will be king no more!

speaker: Eivor
en: He means to kill Aelfred?

speaker: Harriet
en: Regicide? No! The king will step aside, and Ealhferth will lead us all, risen and resplendent as the Lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are a damned fool.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Seax must be hiding in the crowd, biding his time to strike at Aelfred.

speaker: Alfred
en: In the past, Anglo Saxons prospered in both warfare and wisdom. But the decay of English prose has been creeping. Not priest, clerk, or abbot can turn the letter of their sermons from Latin to English. And how can we understand God's words if they are not spoken in our tongue? Ealhferth is dead. And we mourn him. But the foul deeds of the unrighteous are sown among our holy deeds like cockles and tare in a field of wheat. Education, wisdom, enlightened thought, this will raise us above the sins of our fathers. These I will demand of the next bishop of Wincestre. And so we meet to discuss all worthy candidates. And choose the man who will shepherd our flock.

speaker: Ealhferth
en: The king is mine!

speaker: Goodwin
en: By God, it is true, the bishop lives!

speaker: Ealhferth
en: Stand down, Goodwin.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: They'll kill us all!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 5
en: God save us!

speaker: Ealhferth
en: Why do you defend this tarnished crown?

speaker: Goodwin
en: Enough, you scheming cur!

speaker: Alfred
en: Greater men than you have died on my sword.

speaker: Ealhferth
en: How sweet is the Shepherd's pipe when he calls his lambs to slaughter. I was born to Christians in the northern wilds. My mother would cradle me beneath the stars and whisper dovelike, "God watches over you."

speaker: Ealhferth
en: Then your people came. And God fixed his stout eye as they slit her throat for a copper ring. No stars threw down their spears as barbarians smeared her blood through fields of broken wheat. God watched all... and I hated him.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be Aelfred's God was testing you. A trial you failed.

speaker: Ealhferth
en: Aelfred's God is weak. Yet he would chain us all in His service. From our first breath to our death rattle. My Order wishes to break these mind-forged manacles. I am the wolf in lamb's wool.

speaker: Odin
en: He takes on the role of a god himself. A worthy path to walk.

speaker: Eivor
en: A wolf is but a walking feast for ravens.

speaker: Ealhferth
en: One more gift to you, Dane. A deadly truth, if you can find it.

speaker: Ealhferth
en: With my death, The Order will not die. It will only transform... into something far worse for all of us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ealhferth will not cheat Loki's dread daughter twice.

speaker: Alfred
en: I owe you my life.

speaker: Eivor
en: An irony not lost on me, Aelfred.

speaker: Goodwin
en: My king, we'll go by back streets to the Old Minster. Eivor may find us there when all has settled.

speaker: Harriet
en: Ealhferth, my love! No!

speaker: Eivor
en: Curse you, Dane. My brother served God!

speaker: Eivor
en: He was not a Christian, he abhorred your god.

speaker: Harriet
en: But why strike him down? Have you no compassion for good men!

speaker: Eivor
en: He wrapped himself in a death cloak to murder your king.

speaker: Harriet
en: Shouldn't you rejoice at the death of a king? You are a heathen and a devil!

speaker: Eivor
en: We both have more questions than answers. But if you know this key, perhaps we can help one another.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is its home?

speaker: Harriet
en: You treated me with kindness, but this damned order. Their machinations killed my brother, so the rest may rot. Take this key to the ruins beneath the bishop's house. You may find answers there.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be it. The door to Ealhferth's secrets.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll send this to Hytham. He may make some sense of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Everything they did was to undermine Aelfred.

speaker: Eivor
en: She lied to me. There is nothing here of The Order. I should see Aelfred for my reward.

speaker: Alfred
en: Come forth, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here is far enough.

speaker: Alfred
en: When wrongdoers came to devour my flesh, these enemies stumbled and fell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have the laws of hospitality been thrown out, Aelfred? I did exactly as we agreed.

speaker: Alfred
en: That you did. But do not mistake necessity for friendship.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are a man of your word. A man of God.

speaker: Alfred
en: Indeed. By His example, I live my life. Goodwin...

speaker: Goodwin
en: Here's the only silver fit for one of your dragon-boats. A reminder of Christ's sacrifice and our charity.

speaker: Alfred
en: This too, I offer you. Live here among us in peace as a Christian, or die a pagan in a blood soaked field. All you have to lose is life everlasting.

speaker: Eivor
en: And if I choose neither?

speaker: Goodwin
en: He offers you hope, Eivor. A life of purpose above and beyond this one. You'd be a fool to refuse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your reign will end, King of the West Saxons. Raven wings will beat until your throne crumbles to dust.

speaker: Alfred
en: You were wrong, Goodwin. This one is beyond saving.

speaker: Goodwin
en: You had your chance, damn you!

speaker: Eivor
en: I did not want it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Damn you, Aelfred.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll return to Hytham and Randvi. They'll want to know what happened here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should talk to Hytham about my next targets. I should speak with Hytham. I should talk to Hytham.

speaker: Hytham
en: I have something here for you. Tidings that may displease you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me.

speaker: Hytham
en: You remember Kjotve's son, Gorm? He has since taken his father's place in The Order.

speaker: Eivor
en: Interesting. Is Gorm here in England? Is he another blotch on our list?

speaker: Hytham
en: He is one of our targets, yes. But he is not in England. He is further west, in fact. A land called Vinland, discovered centuries ago by an Irish sailor called Brendan. The Order of the Ancients has some recent fascination with Vinland, but I cannot say what it might be.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me find out for you, after I silence Gorm.

speaker: Hytham
en: Vinland is far away, according to my source. It may take weeks to find him, after a long and perilous journey.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is no danger that would cow me, Hytham. I will speak with Randvi and arrange passage.

speaker: Randvi
en: Have you spoke with Hytham about Vinland?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. I have marked it on the map, with a bit of guess work as to its location. Let me know when you wish to leave.

speaker: Eivor
en: What can you tell me of Vinland? Is it a real place or a merely a rumor?

speaker: Randvi
en: Rumor or not, I found someone willing to sail you there. She claims to have seen it once before.

speaker: Eivor
en: If she's willing to risk her life besides me and make the long journey, I'll take her at her word.

speaker: Randvi
en: Nessa is her name. Meet her at the docks when you are ready to leave.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will go now. And end the life of Gorm Kjotvesson where the Valkyries cannot find him.

speaker: Randvi
en: It is a long voyage, Eivor. Be careful.

speaker: Nessa
en: Good day to you, stranger.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nessa, is it? I am Eivor. Randvi said you would be my guide.

speaker: Nessa
en: That is right. Passage to across the seas to Saint Brendan's land, is that right?

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi called it Vinland.

speaker: Nessa
en: One and the same. It is a three week trip by longship. Arduous, dull, possibly fatal.

speaker: Eivor
en: Should we survive, you will be compensated.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor. Before you go... You must be dressed as a when you arrive. To be seen as you are would raise suspicions. Gorm runs this new camp. And it is a good bet all but a few will be loyal to him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good thinking.

speaker: Randvi
en: Only taking care of our prized drengr.

speaker: Nessa
en: First things first, Eivor. My ship, my rules. Second, you follow the rules. Third, if you listen to my rules, you live.

speaker: Eivor
en: Understood.

speaker: Nessa
en: Good. Let me know when you're ready and we'll get going.

speaker: Nessa
en: Say the word and we are off.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will leave my gear behind and dress the part. To Vinland we go.

speaker: Nessa
en: Hop in, we'll leave now.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will be back.

speaker: Nessa
en: And I will be here.

speaker: Nessa
en: Ready to set sail? Say the words and we are off.

speaker: Eivor
en: Three cold weeks on the whale-road. Past mountains of ice and kingdoms of stone. lands. All this way to kill a man. Gorm Kjotvesson, the son of my father's old foe. What dark work does The Order have so far across the open sea?

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone in charge. I had better step with care. No friends here.

speaker: Hilde
en: You! You look stronger than most of the others. What's your name?

speaker: Eivor
en: Jora. Of Jorvik.

speaker: Hilde
en: Jora as in "Horse"?

speaker: Eivor
en: My father never wanted children.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this place?

speaker: Hilde
en: Nyhofn, a wild place found on no map.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are we settling here?

speaker: Hilde
en: That is not our plan. Too many in the woods.

speaker: Eivor
en: They threaten us?

speaker: Hilde
en: You ask too many questions, Horse. Your task is to keep your mouth shut and do as I tell you. Now unload that ship and then I'll have you carry those

speaker: Dockhand
en: Hilde! Hilde!

speaker: Dockhand
en: Hilde, we can't find Olav.

speaker: Hilde
en: Loki's arse. Not again.

speaker: Dockhand
en: We cannot send supplies to Gorm without his guidance.

speaker: Hilde
en: Haul what supplies to the nearest camps, then. Gorm's men will do the rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me go. I can carry whatever supplies Gorm needs.

speaker: Hilde
en: That's Olav's job, Horse. Not yours. You stick to this port and keep your head down!

speaker: Hilde
en: Ask around about Olav. Someone must know where he has run off to.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I can find this Olav, he may know where Gorm is.

speaker: Valka
en: Hm. This will do. Thank you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Anything to help you feel at home.

speaker: Valka
en: I am most at home helping others. May we return to the subject of your visions?

speaker: Eivor
en: We could. If you think it worth something.

speaker: Valka
en: I need one more ingredient to finish an elixir for you. Look around the pond there. You will find what I require. Once brewed, this elixir will help you dive deeper into your visions, to see them more clearly.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have the plants you need.

speaker: Valka
en: Good, good. Once added to the elixir, it will be ready to drink. In taking this, you will have access to the All-Father's wisdom. You will walk the path of Odin, and live as he lived so long ago. Prepare yourself for a journey, into another time, another plane.

speaker: Valka
en: The elixir is ready. It will taste like misery itself, but it will open your mind to the sights and sounds of the nine worlds.

speaker: Valka
en: Eivor. Awake so soon...?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. The fog cleared suddenly. I can speak of what I have seen, but... I felt pulled away.

speaker: Valka
en: Say nothing of it now. Return to this another time.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will. When I am ready.

speaker: Valka
en: Welcome back. Your face is bright and your eyes seem clearer. Tell me of everything you have seen.

speaker: Eivor
en: I... I have been to Asgard. The seat of the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw through Odin's eyes, just as you said. In every vision, I inhabited his form. Lived as he once lived. In his body, I was myself. But I was carried by his whims. His thoughts were as known to me as my own. We... were two, but we existed as one.

speaker: Valka
en: And what have you learned?

speaker: Eivor
en: More than learned, I felt... I felt everything. His fears and doubts, his loves and passions.

speaker: Valka
en: Incredible. What else?

speaker: Eivor
en: I consorted with Loki, the trickster. We quarreled often, as siblings. But soon our fights grew dark. When he revealed he had sired a wolf cub, my rage was unbound.

speaker: Valka
en: Because he had hid the truth from you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. Because he knew that wolves were not allowed in Asgard. He flaunted my command.

speaker: Valka
en: Perhaps this was the purpose of your vision. To overcome an inner fear and find forgiveness in your heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe. But before my vision ended, I was seized by great purpose. I devised a plan, a voyage to Jötunheim. And then I awoke.

speaker: Valka
en: Interesting. Was there anything else?

speaker: Eivor
en: I heard a prophecy warning of Ragnarök, the destruction of the world, the end of all time. And the Nornir. They warned me of the great wolf Fenrir, and how he hungered for my blood. But there was something else. Hope. I was undaunted by the coming cataclysm.

speaker: Valka
en: Perhaps this aspect of your vision inspires bravery. Truly you are touched by the gods. Was there more?

speaker: Eivor
en: There was nothing more, nothing of great significance... the dream has faded.

speaker: Valka
en: Eivor, your visions are unlike any I have encountered. Leave me now. I must think on what you have shared.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Something on your mind?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Hunwald
en: Eivor, I realize the strides you've taken to aid me. My oath to you will last an eternity.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: You'll owe me a blood oath when all our work is done.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Hunwald
en: Blood? Dear Lord...

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Wait here 'til I return.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Can your god speak through you, Herefrith? Can he tell me where the ealdorman is?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: Our Lord is not a trained dog who speaks on command. My goodness.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: When did you last see the ealdorman?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Acha
en: Leave us be. It is not your place to be asking such questions.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald's father was recuperating here not long ago. Someone may have seen him depart.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Do you know where your ealdorman is?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: I can tell you a few things. But not here in the open. Follow me.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: This is far enough. Tell me what you know.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O, I know loads of things about our ealdorman. I know his favorite foods, I know when his bedclothes get changed, and I know he hates being bled with leeches. That sort of thing.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: But where has he gone?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Ah, where? I have no bloody idea. Is that what you asked me?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Forget it.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: You there. Do you know where your ealdorman has gone?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I don't. And if you like your hide where it's at, you won't ask that 'round here again!

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Where is the ealdorman? Did you see where he went?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: I... I... I don't know. Ealdorman who? Sorry, I'm busy!

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Are you the head sister here?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Aye. And I'm not comforted by the sight of you wielding weapons like a war chief. We're a hospice, not a barracks. It's bad enough I've got these armored codpieces watching me work. Now you...

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Please don't hurt me. These poor souls need me.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Calm, sister. Lord Hunwald sent me. He asked me to speak with the people here.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: H-Hunwald? That's not a name I expected to hear again.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: No harm will come to you or those you care for. I'm only looking for your ealdorman.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: I'd be risking my neck telling you anything. And if my head rolls, these sick and ailing folk will follow me to the grave.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Your ealdorman would agree. So the sooner I find him, the more quickly these prowling guards will leave your hospice.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: That's a pleasant thought. Our lord was in a bad way here, and getting worse, in spite of our efforts. Then, quite against my instructions, some guards moved him out. I overheard them talking about a bathhouse. There's no working bathhouse in Lincoln. So I gather they meant the old ruins just south of here, by the eastern walls.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Ruins just south of here. I will look there, thank you.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: I pray you find him. He's in desperate need of care.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: It wern't wise to let those Mercians nobles use our tunnels, if you ask me.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: What choice did we have? 'Least this way, they'll leave us be.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: They killed one of their own! What's to stop 'em from splitting our skulls as well?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Cause they fear us, see? No one takes us for fools, you got it?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Remember... God punishes those who wish ill upon... upon...

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Go on... ill upon who?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Eh? Sorry, I was miles away. What?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Christ Jesus. You haven't got enough brains in your head to blink, have you?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: These tunnels run deep. Was the ealdorman fleeing to a hideaway beneath Lincoln?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 5
en: Ow! Ah! Dammit...

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Ach. As if baptized by a mud priest.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 6
en: More Mercians traipsing across our routes. Can't piss from here to Bolingbroc without someone demanding some ungodly deal.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 7
en: All this traffic has made smuggling a difficult job.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 6
en: Smuggling will always be difficult. But I prefer it to paying tribute. Never again will we bend to the Mercian crown.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: There was fighting here. About what?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: A violent struggle between nobles and bandits. The bandits did not fare so well.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: A noble's cloak with the image of a swan. Looks like the ealdorman passed this way.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Someone took a nasty fall.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I know a lonely door that would love to meet this key.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: A key. Useful if I had a door to match it."

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: A Saxon nobleman paid some bandits for permission to sneak through these tunnels on their way to Bolingbroc castle.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Mercian nobles made a deal with some bandits. Paid them hush money to let them sneak through these caves. When the time came, the bandits ambushed the nobles. But it did not end well for the bandits. In the struggle, the ealdorman's cloak was torn off. But he got away and headed east for Bolingbroc castle. That's my best lead.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. Fresh air.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Why can we not enter the keep now? Is it all gold and silver up there?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Pipe down, lad. And keep your nose out of that business. It's not a topic you need knowing about.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I'm on the right track. That keep is well protected.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: At times, I wonder what in God's name we are here for. Hundbeorht is his own prisoner.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: He's an ill man, leave him be. Besides, we ain't got it too rough. We can hunt in the wolds of Lindsey and whore in Botolphston.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Too right, too right. I've gone dumb with idle time. Grab some ale, and let us skin some animals later.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: My lord, you carried yourself as a true-born king, born in a time of wolves. You have earned a long rest.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: "Hundbeorht"
en: Thank you, beautiful Galwyna. So firm is your loyalty. None know me as well as you do.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: Thank you, lord. It is now time for your bath. May I wash you?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: "Hundbeorht"
en: Yes, good, good. Time for the washing. The very last washing. Very good indeed.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: There now, my lord. All is prepared. Shall we begin the washing?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: Eh? Who comes?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Welcome, stranger. Are you here to pay tribute to our Lord Ealdorman?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I heard voices as I entered. Were you speaking with him? Does his hugr (mind) speak through you?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: I am not sure what to call it, precisely. Words form in my mind, and I give them voice. Often, they sound like my dear lord.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Can I ask a favor of him? On behalf of his son, Hunwald?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: You could try, but he never speaks when others are present.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Your ealdorman is long past the days of good conversation.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: Yet still he makes good company. I've been instructed to wash and prepare his earthly vessel.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Instructed by whom?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: Soldiers. They brought him here as he protested, feebly. I did my best to make him comfortable... until he slipped away.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: This biscuit has been dry for some time, sister. How long has the ealdorman been dead?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: "Dead" is such a drastic word. I like to think of my lord as... transformed.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: That's not untrue.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: Have you need of anything?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald deserves to know the truth about his father's fate. He is owed an inheritance and deserves a chance to become ealdorman himself.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: All in good time, I imagine.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: No. Now.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: When the guards put him in my care, I was told to keep all this a secret... until the appointed time. When I asked who gave these orders, they struck me. I wish I could say more.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I've seen all I need to. But Hunwald will need proof.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Why has your ealdorman's death been obscured? The people of Lincolnscire deserve to know his fate. Hunwald above all.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: When the guards put him in my care, I was told to keep all this a secret... until the appointed time. When I asked who gave these orders, they struck me. I wish I could say more.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I've seen all I need to. But Hunwald will need proof.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I've seen all I need to. But Hunwald will need proof.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: Of course. You're welcome to search through his effects, though I'm not sure what trinket would best serve your purpose.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I'll find something.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Dried herbs and berries, crushed into powder.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: The time between my lord's departure and his burial is ... longer than usual. My lord must keep up appearancce for his upcoming rites.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I don't know what this is. And I'd rather not ask.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: Yes, I thought the same. Troubling.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Foul. Rat droppings everywhere.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: Even in death, my lord is a friend to all of God's creatures.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: A box of musty clothing. And a brooch with a crest... the house of the ferocious swan. This will do. I'll return this brooch to Hunwald in Lincoln. I hope this poor boy can withstand such ill news.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Take care.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: And you.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: I shall take you to your family crypt at within Lincoln. There you may lay beside your forebearers, the great and glorious kings of old Lindsey.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Galwyna
en: Please. Do not desecrate our Lord.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I am Dane, not a cruel grief-monger.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Hunwald
en: Eivor! What news?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Your father is dead.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Hunwald
en: Wait. What?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: The sigil of Hundbeorht's house. I found it near his body.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Hunwald
en: No. No, this cannot be! He was strong. A pillar of Lincolnscire. He cannot be gone. He ... He...

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Acha
en: O, you poor boy. I'm so, so sorry.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Hunwald
en: I am a man, Acha! Do you hear me? I am a man, and I am my father's son. Do not forget it!

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Keep steady, Hunwald. You're now the head of your house.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Hunwald
en: Another swan takes flight. Only I remain, last in line of... dwindling nobles.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: He's been dead for some time. That was obvious by the state of his corpse.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: One of you knows more than you're letting on.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: That a son has lost his father is always a cause for sadness. But your shire has also lost its ealdorman. That is a cause for worry... and often war.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Acha
en: I'm sorry, Hunwald. I had already asked a priest to administer last rites when your father disappeared.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Hunwald
en: What?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Acha
en: I didn't tell you sooner because I... I thought by some miracle he had survived.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Hunwald
en: You lied to me!

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Acha
en: You silly sobbing moon-calf. Will you never grow up?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: Lord have mercy on that woman. She should have said something. It was her duty to say something.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald was the son of an ealdorman. Will he take his father's seat?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: The title's not hereditary, but he can plead his case before a shiremoot. King Ceolwulf must then ratify the decision.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: It may be your best option is to leave Lincolnscire to Danes in the north. They don't suffer fools and traitors.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: The Danes of Grimsby are welcome to put a man forward, but a shiremoot must decide who takes the seat.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: You need a new ealdorman here. And it falls to King Ceolwulf to make that choice.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: For once, we find agreement, Eivor. The nobles here will convene a shiremoot to select a new candidate. The winner will stand before the king for approval.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Explain how this works, your shiremoot.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Aelfgar
en: A moot is a meeting of lords. We convene from time to time to steer the course of our shire.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: It was always my intention to convene a moot. But between our troubles in Lincoln and the bandits' raids, we slipped into a pattern of convenience.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: We have a similar custom, what we call an althing. An assembly of good folk.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: With so many like habits, there should be peace between our people and yours. Perhaps that begins now.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald is an obvious candidate. But I don't any of you beyond the tip of a spear. I'll see to it that he is protected until your shiremoot gathers.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: None here wishes the boy ill, but do what you think necessary.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Someone in the shire wants Hunwald dead. If I have to assemble an army to make sure this meeting is not an ambush, I will.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: The shiremoot is a lawful, Godly assembly. Hunwald will be safe, as will you be.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Apart from Hunwald, who else will stand for the ealdorman's seat?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: If I may be so bold, I should like to put my name forward. Under my care, the shire has found some peace this past month.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Aelfgar
en: I will offer my name as well. My family has ancient ties to this land. And I am proud to say, I have forged quite a friendship with the Danes to the north.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: Good. My priests will spread word of the moot across the shire. We'll convene in a few days' time.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Aelfgar
en: Do visit my estate, Eivor. I have something for you. Something I think you'll enjoy.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: I'll find the time.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: Eivor, a word if you don't mind.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Is the word "Christ" or "pagan"?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: I deeply regret my churlish ways when we first met. I did not treat you as my God commands ... with kindness and love.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Love is a difficult feeling to command.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: Yes, quite. In any case, thank you for putting this mystery to rest. I do hope we'll see you at the moot.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: With Hundbeorht's death an open secret, Hunwald's enemies may strike again. I should find him before they do. Acha went to console him. I should follow her.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: Best of luck at the coming shiremoot, bishop.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: I would tell you my fate is in the hands of our Lord. But somehow I believe that won't be the whole story.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Eivor
en: You fear something?

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: I fear everything these days... in small doses.

scene: In the Absence of an Ealdorman
speaker: Herefrith
en: Give my best to Aelfgar and Hunwald, should you see them.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is Tuam. One of these cottages is where The Cursed hides.

speaker: Eivor
en: Locked. Someone around here must have a key.

speaker: Eivor
en: Beneath the village? That's odd.

speaker: Eivor
en: Loki's balls!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is the meaning of all this?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: Please! Get me out of here!

speaker: Eivor
en: What tragedy has befallen you?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: Thanks be, you're not one of them.

speaker: Eivor
en: One of who?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: The Danu! Not like any druids I've ever seen before. They grabbed me and me mates. We got lost in the fog, and... Me mates!

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep your wits about you.

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: The High Druid, calls herself The Cursed, she sacrificed 'em bit by bit, you understand? First a hand, then a leg...

speaker: Eivor
en: You should run while you're intact. But first, what is The Cursed planning to do?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: She dragged ol' Fintan to some ritual. Poor man! I daren't think what's become of him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Save yourself.

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: I will. I'm done with this place!

speaker: Eivor
en: The luck of Thor be with him.

speaker: Eivor
en: A shoddy sacrifice. They will learn of no portents from this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Púca? What would that be?

speaker: Eivor
en: A sacrificial ritual and something about a púca. It is not much, but Ciara may know what it means.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ciara said to meet outside the village to the south.

speaker: Ciara
en: Eivor! I delivered the cure.

speaker: Eivor
en: Has Bárid escaped Flann's wrath?

speaker: Ciara
en: He has and is much relieved. The soldiers are coming back to themselves. What have you learned?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Cursed will perform a sacrificial ritual.

speaker: Ciara
en: Sacrifice? Fé (Alas), The Cursed is then a High Druid.

speaker: Eivor
en: I learned that she is. But what does that mean?

speaker: Ciara
en: She wields great power. She will be protected by her acolytes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not only her acolytes. I also learned the ceremony will be protected by a... What was it? A pook?

speaker: Ciara
en: A púca? That will be dangerous. But we've no choice. The ritual will likely be held at Carnagan. We must look there.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is a púca? A kind of animal?

speaker: Ciara
en: "A kind of animal?" I will explain on the way. Come.

speaker: Eivor
en: You promised to explain about the púca.

speaker: Ciara
en: Sure, they were once marvelous creatures. Able to take the forms of any animal. Now... they're dangerous.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this a jest?

speaker: Ciara
en: Have you no such creatures in Norway?

speaker: Eivor
en: There is Fenrir, wolf to the gods, but he is unusual.

speaker: Ciara
en: Well, púcas are common in Ireland.

speaker: Eivor
en: Púcas, sacrificial rituals, is this your world?

speaker: Ciara
en: The Children of Danu are an aberration. True pagans oppose them. Flann knows our traditions will disappear without his support. He has pledged not to let that happen.

speaker: Ciara
en: Careful now. Púcas are quick. Search for tracks showing long claws. And stay on your guard.

speaker: Eivor
en: There. Tracks.

speaker: Ciara
en: The púca! Follow it!

speaker: Eivor
en: It looks like a wolf.

speaker: Ciara
en: Because the púca is in the shape of a wolf just now.

speaker: Eivor
en: This fog enters into my head.

speaker: Ciara
en: Mine as well.

speaker: Púca
en: Stay away!

speaker: Eivor
en: Did the wolf speak?

speaker: Púca
en: I warned you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah!

speaker: Eivor
en: What in the nine realms was that beast?

speaker: Ciara
en: Whist! The ritual has begun. This way.

speaker: Ciara
en: That's the High Druid. The Cursed.

speaker: Eivor
en: She will not live to see the rising of the sun.

speaker: The Cursed
en: Who dares defile this sacred spot?

speaker: The Cursed
en: Traitress!

speaker: Druid 1
en: The priestess of the stone!

speaker: Druid 2
en: Blood for the earth spirits!

speaker: Druid 3
en: The ritual is profaned! It is the priestess!

speaker: The Cursed
en: You!

speaker: The Cursed
en: You betrayed us. I curse you with all the powers of the moon.

speaker: Ciara
en: Your curses mean nothing.

speaker: The Cursed
en: You drew back when we most needed your awful might. And now...

speaker: Ciara
en: The Cursed is dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: She accused you of betraying the Children of Danu.

speaker: Ciara
en: I was once one of them.

speaker: Eivor
en: How can this be?

speaker: Ciara
en: Deirdre warned me against them, but back then it seemed the only hope.

speaker: Eivor
en: You knew these people. Why did you not direct me to The Wren?

speaker: Ciara
en: They only wanted to use me. Distrustful and secretive. I never knew their true names or anything about them. A glen of great beauty lies on our road. Find me when you're ready and I'll confess my errors there.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's beautiful.

speaker: Ciara
en: I used to wash my cares and pain in this pond. Would it be all right if I...?

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course.

speaker: Ciara
en: As a young girl, when the Christians cleared the forests of druids, I fled and stumbled on this spot.

speaker: Ciara
en: How would I survive? My friends? The world I knew? Soon, I turned to the Children of Danu. At first they pledged simply to keep the old ways alive. Then, one by one, druids turned to dark rituals.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then they turned to worse.

speaker: Ciara
en: Yes, even murder. I disavowed the Children and now pray for their destruction.

speaker: Eivor
en: The High Druid spoke of some sort of "awful might."

speaker: Ciara
en: Fantasies. An ancient fable of a people long lost. The druids are now dispersed without a champion.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have King Flann.

speaker: Ciara
en: My hopes are placed in him, but am I a fool? He has no deep love of the past. He hopes to build a new Ireland. He pledges that my people will be part of it, but once he's king, storms will come. I cannot know where he will take refuge.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are no fool.

speaker: Ciara
en: You and I have been through much together. We came near death. I would like to celebrate life.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this why you brought me to this place?

speaker: Ciara
en: Tis a lovely glen. Perhaps we could pass some time here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would like very much to pass some time with you.

speaker: Ciara
en: Aye. Lovely. Lovely, indeed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ciara. I admire you a great deal. But it's best not to form entanglements in time of war.

speaker: Ciara
en: Mo lén (Too bad), Eivor. You drive a woman mad, you do.

speaker: Berbha Champion Brother
en: Looks like Odin has sent us one of his dogs, Sister.

speaker: Berbha Champion Sister
en: No matter, Brother. We'll bring this dog to heel.

speaker: Azar
en: Eivor. Are you prepared to go to Ireland?

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar! You did not tell me the king was my cousin!

speaker: Azar
en: It was most amusing this way, was it not? A little mystery?

speaker: Eivor
en: I prefer to know what is what, but it was a pleasant surprise.

speaker: Azar
en: He's eager to see you. Shall we set sail?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ja, I would like to see this land, and my cousin Bárid!

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not yet prepared for this voyage.

speaker: Azar
en: I will wait.

speaker: Azar
en: Eivor. Are you prepared to go to Ireland?

speaker: Azar
en: Ireland. A patchwork of petty kings jostling for hills and pastures and green, green glens. My adopted isle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar, how is it that Bárid, as Norse as ice, is King of Dublin?

speaker: Azar
en: Dublin is a Viking city, Eivor. But, in fact, merchants and beggars come from all parts to parade in its muddy streets.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odd to think of Bárid as king of the city.

speaker: Azar
en: It perhaps sound grander than it is. Ireland has many, many kings. They litter the countryside. And Bárid's throne is not secure. Flann Sinna calls the tune.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is he?

speaker: Azar
en: Soon to be crowned High King of all Ireland! Flann distrusts Vikings, though he needs them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid will find a way. As a boy he wasn't much of a fighter, but somehow always came out all right.

speaker: Azar
en: I'm sure what you say is true. Certainly, he is loved by his people.

speaker: Azar
en: Hytham? Things have not gone as planned. Hytham!

speaker: Azar
en: Perhaps you can aid me to locating Hytham.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is your purpose with him?

speaker: Azar
en: I have brought a sampling of goods from Ireland. That is if I can bring my ships to dock.

speaker: Hytham
en: Azar. I see you've met Eivor Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Azar
en: Ah, so you are Eivor. In fact, I bring you a message from Ireland.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know no one in Ireland.

speaker: Azar
en: The letter is from Dublin's king. Sadly, I seem to have misplaced it.

speaker: Eivor
en: The King of Dublin? Why would such a one write to me?

speaker: Azar
en: He wishes to expand trade to England. The purpose of my bringing goods here.

speaker: Hytham
en: Azar is from the East, but lives in Ireland now. But in matters of trade, Azar, your king should petition Randvi.

speaker: Azar
en: He claims to know Eivor. He asked me to accompany you on the trip there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know no king and am certainly not about to journey to Ireland.

speaker: Hytham
en: But first, Azar, you must build a trading post. In fact, where is your trading ship?

speaker: Azar
en: Ah, yes. An unfortunate incident, most concerning. Trading rivals have blocked the river and thus my goods.

speaker: Eivor
en: A blocked river hurts all Ravensthorpe. Stay. I'll put things right.

speaker: Hytham
en: As you see, Eivor is a person of action. Find me later, when the river is safely clear.

speaker: Azar
en: Of course, my friend! I thank you, Eivor. I will find the king's letter in the meantime.

speaker: Eivor
en: You keep insisting I know an Irish king. It is a fantasy.

speaker: Eivor
en: What manner of king is it that sends me letters from Ireland?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. Here is the blockade to be cleared.

speaker: Eivor
en: They won't like that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar's trading rivals are defeated. The river is clear. Now we'll see about this so-called "King of Dublin."

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar! The river is clear, save for a few bodies and sticks. Your goods will get through.

speaker: Azar
en: Your reputation comes honestly, then, though I am not sure about the name Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Eivor
en: The scar on my neck.

speaker: Azar
en: Ah. My Viking name would then be Azar One-Eye.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Azar One-Eye. My men will help construct your trade post.

speaker: Azar
en: Then I am twice-debted to you. If ever you change your mind about Ireland, I will be found in the trade post, once built. O, and I found your letter. Here.

speaker: Eivor
en: My cousin Bárid is alive! And King of Dublin! The nornir never fail to delight.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You men, mount up and follow me! There's work to be done!

speaker: Ivarr
en: I should have seen this coming. I should have known he would come for the weakest of us.

speaker: Eivor
en: You opened a bloody wound when you killed Rhodri's brother.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Anything worth doing must be paid for in blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: In Quatford, you told me Rhodri gave you that scar on your face. Is it a story worth telling?

speaker: Ivarr
en: If not worth telling, it is worth remembering. Years ago, I was headed back from the Western Isle. Ah, they have got fighters there! I had taken a bit of a beating, putting me in a surly mood. I wanted blood and silver, nothing more. So me and my drengr, sailing across the coast of Cymru, see a for landing, covered in mist. We drag our ships ashore, and just then a cry came from atop a hillock. The troll-cursed Britons. The fog clears a bit, and there they are, all lined up. The biggest one calls out, "I am Rhodri, king of this land." "That means shit to me," I scream back. I give my boys a nod, and we raise up our axes and charge before they take a breath. We have the numbers. But the Britons are clever. It's marshland. The bog catches our boots, sucks us to a standstill. One by one, Rhodri cuts us to bits. He gets to me, lays his blade at my cheek and gives me this nick. "Leave this land, and give your people fair warning," he says. "Tell them King Rhodri gave you that cut." "Hen shit," I say. Rhodri laughs and lets me go.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite a story, Ivarr. Son of Ragnar, killer of kings, conqueror of England and the Western Isle. You have lived a saga worth ten.

speaker: Ivarr
en: That I have.

speaker: Ivarr
en: That sweat-sopped slug is just beyond those walls. "May only be defeated by a dragon," my itching ass. He'll meet one, alright.

speaker: Eivor
en: Send a message to your men. We can build a camp here and lay plans for a surprise attack.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr's men waste no time. They're eager to pay out our revenge.

speaker: Baeldaeg
en: I been waiting to get back at these Britons ever since you broke me from that cage, Dane. The time is nigh.

speaker: Eadric
en: There's my liberator! I'll do you proud, I will.

speaker: Orlaf
en: Eivor! I'm ready to get back at them Britons. You'll not see me lagging behind, doin' nothing but looting corpses. Not this time!

speaker: Ivarr
en: I am ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: What in the name of Loki have you done?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Called in a dragon to help me slay Rhodri. Now what say you, Wolf-Kissed? Are you ready for war?

speaker: Eivor
en: Rally the men, Ivarr. Let's have at it.

speaker: Ivarr
en: It is a good day to die.

speaker: Eivor
en: The gate looks to be well defended.

speaker: Ivarr
en: My men are loading a cart with cauldrons of oil. We will blast right through that fucking gate.

speaker: Eivor
en: We're not ready yet. Patience, my friend.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Bah!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ready to take this miserable castle? The dragon is hungry for Briton blood.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Rhodri! Show yourself!

speaker: King Rhodri
en: I am here, Boneless Ragnarsson. How is it you come in force when our peace has been concluded?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Do not mock us, whoreson. You splattered blood on our peace with the butchery of young Ceolbert!

speaker: King Rhodri
en: Speak what nonsense you please, Dane. If you mean war, our defences are sure.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Gaze upon my face, King of Crow-food, and meet the dragon that will devour you!

speaker: King Rhodri
en: I see a spent old man playing at serpents.

speaker: Eivor
