en: Enough talking, Ivarr.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Bring the oil cart and set the fires! When I am done with Rhodri, I will tear the fat from his shanks and use it to fry our bread.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Get the cart, boys. We will light it up in front of the gate!

speaker: Eivor
en: Get the wagon to the gate!"

speaker: Ivarr
en: They've sent soldiers to stop our cart! I will wash the castle walls with Rhodri's blood.

speaker: Eadric
en: Come on, lads! Roll it to the gate.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Knock! Knock! Send 'em to the everlasting bonfire!

speaker: Baeldaeg
en: Closer! Closer to the bloody gate!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Now, Eivor! Set it ablaze!

speaker: Eivor
en: Get back! I'll light it up.

speaker: Orlaf
en: Great John the Baptist, it worked!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Storm the castle. Give no quarter.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Springalds! Keep your head down. Find cover. Push the mangy dogs back!

speaker: Eivor
en: That was clever.

speaker: Eadric
en: Eivor opened the bleedin' gate!

speaker: Briton Warrior
en: Holy ! Danes!

speaker: Eadric
en: Over the drawbridge, boys!

speaker: Orlaf
en: Drawbridge be damned!

speaker: Eivor
en: The keep! It's through there.

speaker: Briton Warrior
en: Protect the king!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Rhodri! Your dragon has arrived! He is hiding behind that door. Remember, he is mine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bash it down.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: Ivarr the Boneless. You make a pitiful dragon.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ahhh... Bastard kicked me in the liver. I need some fresh air.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ya.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I've felled the rotting old oak.

speaker: Eivor
en: He's not dead.

speaker: Ivarr
en: No. I have something else planned. Spectacle, remember?

speaker: Eivor
en: You have won, Ivarr. and if you will not kill him now, then let him go. Humiliation will chase him to the end of his days.'

speaker: Eivor
en: The man is dying. Come away, let the Norns spin his fate.

speaker: Eivor
en: He is nothing now but a sad sack of flesh. Kill him and be done with it.

speaker: Ivarr
en: O, no, this will be good. I have some specifics in mind. A place and a method. Come!

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. Let's get this over with.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not just now. I will return when I'm ready.

speaker: Ivarr
en: So be it. We will be waiting, right Rhodri, old friend?

speaker: Ivarr
en: There you are. Let us take King Rhodri to a spot he will fine... breathtaking?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Load this lump of lard onto your horse and we will go. Take care he stays alive.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor! Do not forget that load of rotten flesh called Rhodri.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are we going?

speaker: Ivarr
en: An overlook I found while scouting. A view, one fit for a dying king.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's no need for spectacle, Ivarr. Let the man die.

speaker: Ivarr
en: No, no, no. He must die with style.

speaker: Ivarr
en: How are you doing, dear king? Stay with us. You must not miss what is coming.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I killed King Ælla, King Osberht, King Edmund. And now King Rhodri. Who else can claim such a string of victories?

speaker: King Rhodri
en: Just... finish me.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not my place to interfere in this feud.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Valhalla must look such a sight.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Does he breathe still?

speaker: Eivor
en: Barely.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Rhodri! Are you listening? For years I wore this scar with shame. Nicked by a Briton, and left alive! I tried to cover it with a beard, a cloak. But as your fame grew, I began to beam with pride. A king gave me this mark! What say you to this, Rhodri? Huh? Speak up, you old bag of sweat and grease.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Here we are. Bring him close.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Haul him up there. To the top. And keep him breathing.

speaker: Eivor
en: Finish this quicky, Ivarr.

speaker: Ivarr
en: See here? A hungry blade!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Now comes the dragon, to feed on his favorite meal... the blood eagle!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr, is this

speaker: Ivarr
en: The birth of a blood eagle is a sight to behold, my friend. First, I slice the length of your spine.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: Aaaah!

speaker: Odin
en: That is a Norseman. The true essence of old heroes.

speaker: Eivor
en: The blood eagle has no true meaning for Ivarr. He is doing it simply to take pleasure in suffering.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Now to pull back the flesh.

speaker: Odin
en: The method will always outlive the meaning. Few in time will care why this man died. But the how, that is a song for the ages.

speaker: Odin
en: The fog between good and evil grows thick over time. But glory never fades.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is nothing glorious here.

speaker: Odin
en: Life is not pretty. It is a bloody fight.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Out come the lungs. And we spread them like wings...!

speaker: Ivarr
en: All of Mercia can see him now.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've seen enough.

speaker: Ivarr
en: We are not finished, Eivor. This sage we have written together, it needs an ending. Here and now.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is ended, Ivarr. I am done with this place.

speaker: Ivarr
en: A fight to the death, you and me! If I win, I am the greatest vikingr who ever lived. If I lose, what a tale you have to tell.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are battle-drunk, Ivarr. Goodbye.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Poor Ceolbert. He barely said a word.

speaker: Eivor
en: When?

speaker: Ivarr
en: I pushed that dragon dagger into his heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: No.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Just a soft little squeal. Then nothing.

speaker: Eivor
en: You sick fucking bacraut (asshole)!

speaker: Ivarr
en: The things a man must do. The trials one must face, the friends you must betray. To achieve one's destiny. And become King Killer forever more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Traitor! Ceolbert was

speaker: Ivarr
en: Like a son to me! Yes, yes! So fight me, Wolf-Kissed! To a glorious death!

speaker: Ivarr
en: This is a life, Eivor! To fight high above the world. Valhalla awaits!

speaker: Eivor
en: You were too reckless, Ivarr. A storm of mindless chaos.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Mindless? Have you no sense of menace! When I stabbed Gwriad, you winced. You cower in the face of sudden drama.

speaker: Ivarr
en: We are only warming up! How good will it feel when all is afire!

speaker: Ivarr
en: O, if Ubba could see me now, he would rage with disappointment!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Watch out!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Bleed! Like Ceolbert.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You're not so smart.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Come down, Eivor! I have only begun to enjoy this!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Do you remember your first kill? Mine was a boyhood friend. He squealed like a piglet. Like Ceolbert. Like the old days, yes? When iron bit into flesh like teeth into bread.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Come on, Eivor.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Do not shame me, Eivor! Finish me well.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Hold a moment, Eivor... let me ask you something...

speaker: Eivor
en: Speak, then. Or I take your tongue.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Will you see your father in Valhalla, Wolf-Kissed? Or is the coward in Helheim, weeping tears of ice?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Gulled again! Ha!

speaker: Ivarr
en: So close to death. So cold is my heart! Where are the winged maidens?

speaker: Ivarr
en: My long road ends. The Valkyries approach. My axe, Eivor. Hand me my weapon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin may have use for you. But this is more than you deserve.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ah...

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not shame him.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I hear... I hear their wings...

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor! Give it here...!

speaker: Eivor
en: To Helheim with you.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor...

speaker: Eivor
en: Carry the body to Quatford. We will say our goodbyes there. And send a message to Ubba. Tell him...his brother is dead.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Eivor, hello. Another dark day clouds our victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bishop, Ubba.

speaker: Ubba
en: Dead at the hands of a Briton. I cannon imagine the shame my brother felt in his final hour. Were it not for this peace...

speaker: Eivor
en: I killed him.

speaker: Ubba
en: You?

speaker: Eivor
en: After peace was made, Ivarr murdered Ceolbert and pinned the crime on Rhodri. To get another swing at him.

speaker: Ubba
en: How do you come to know this?

speaker: Eivor
en: He told me himself.

speaker: Ubba
en: I am always one who desires the truth, Eivor, but this... this is a hard thing to hear. Did he die well?

speaker: Eivor
en: He died a fighter. In all his glory.

speaker: Ubba
en: As he wanted, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: He died defending a grievous lie. I cannot say that is dying well.

speaker: Ubba
en: Ivarr... I spent my whole life repairing the damage he inflicted. Still, he was my brother.

speaker: Eivor
en: Death at my hand was his final aim. He wanted the glory of a bloody end.

speaker: Ubba
en: An end you did not deny him.

speaker: Ubba
en: With Ivarr gone, peace and quiet are now possible. That is something. I will console myself with the thought that we will meet again in Valhalla, axe in hand.

speaker: Eivor
en: You will.

speaker: Ubba
en: For good or ill, he lived life by his own rules. What man can say better?

speaker: Eivor
en: He lived his life at cross-purposes. I often found him strange and his actions puzzling. But not all men are meant to be understood.

speaker: Ubba
en: He needs a proper farewell. I will prepare a ship. For his funeral pyre.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bishop, send word to Lady Angharad. Say that her husband died by treachery. And that Ivarr has paid the price for it.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: As soon as I am able.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you heard from King Ceowulf? I cannot imagine his grief.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: He is felled by it. Still, he makes plans for this shire. I am to be ealdorman here. Therefore, Sciropescire declares herself your friend and ally, and will remain so for the length of my days.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am grateful, bishop.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: God go with you, Eivor. Wherever you may lead.

speaker: Ubba
en: To you, my brother. May your time in Valhalla be bright and glorious.

speaker: Eivor
en: Raw bringer of battle-song, the boneless one sails into a singing-glory on a flaming water-steed.

speaker: Ubba
en: Wind across the water, the battle maidens beat their wings to carry a king to Odin's hall of corpses.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr gone. Sciropscire an ally. I should confer with Randvi.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sounds coming from that old church.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is someone there?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hmm. Scraps and rags... left for the rats.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eh. Hard as stone. And the stench is ripe.

speaker: Unknown Voice
en: You! How dare you! Crowland's throne belongs only to the one true King of Briars!"

speaker: Eivor
en: This throne of muck and manure? I suppose that makes you... the Lord of Shitsby?

speaker: Unknown Voice
en: How dare you insult the brave and valorous soldiers of

speaker: Eivor
en: ...Of Shitsby, yes. I know your type.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you have a problem with me, show yourself!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 0
en: We await the Lord of Crowland, trespasser. Leave or die!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not going anywhere until you cowards show your poxy faces!

speaker: Eivor
en: Strange. I am not the one true King of Briars, yet here I sit.

speaker: Unknown Voice
en: Insolent ferret! Kill this usurper!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: We will fight for this muddy kingdom tooth and nail!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Crowland is ours, cur!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Don't let this one escape!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: No one defiles this sacred throne and goes unpunished!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fools in the thrall of an absent king. Pitiful.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: How dare you look at me like that! Show respect to your liege! Bow! Why won't you bow to your kind? You! Serf! Bring me ale!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: You dare to steal the royal treasure! Guards! Guards! Get him, men! Nobody touches the king's gold! Come on, all of you! Kill the traitor!

speaker: Eivor
en: A king of straw men. Well, there's an end to his madness, poor soul.

speaker: King of the Hill
en: No one can knock me off this hill. No one, I say! Just try it. You'll see. My blood runs hot, my hands twitch with anticipation of yet another grisly kill! Quake and shit yourselves, all who would unseat me! This is my hill. Every patch of it from the scrabble grass down there to the airy heights here!

speaker: King of the Hill
en: Not one step closer!

speaker: King of the Hill
en: I warn you, stop!

speaker: Eivor
en: What did you say to me?

speaker: King of the Hill
en: No one has ever dared to come all the way up before. What happens now?

speaker: Eivor
en: We fight!

speaker: King of the Hill
en: Hold! I give in! No more shall I challenge everyone.

speaker: Eivor
en: See that you don't.

speaker: King of the Hill
en: No one can knock me off this hill. No one, I say! Just try it. You'll see. My blood runs hot, my hands twitch with anticipation of yet another grisly kill! Quake and shit yourselves, all who would unseat me! This is my hill. Every patch of it from the scrabble grass down there to the airy heights here!

speaker: Eivor
en: At it again? I thought I shut you up last time.

speaker: King of the Hill
en: Huh... You again!

speaker: Eivor
en: Quit stalling.

speaker: King of the Hill
en: Enough! I can't take anymore! I won't bother anybody any longer.

speaker: King of the Hill
en: No one can knock me off this hill. No one, I say! Just try it. You'll see. My blood runs hot, my hands twitch with anticipation of yet another grisly kill! Quake and shit yourselves, all who would unseat me! This is my hill. Every patch of it from the scrabble grass down there to the airy heights here!

speaker: Eivor
en: This madman will not stop!

speaker: Eivor
en: You little shit. How many times must I beat you to mush?

speaker: King of the Hill
en: O! Just you try.

speaker: King of the Hill
en: O I give up. I give up! You are the better fighter.

speaker: Eivor
en: Never forget that.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm tired of defeating you.

speaker: King of the Hill
en: O. It's no pleasure being defeated. The hill is yours. You're the true champion.

speaker: King of the Hill Declaration
en: No one wil doubt me, For King of the Hill am I. No one will gainsay me, For King of the Hill am I. No one will spit upon me or call me a fool or humbug, For King of the Hill am I. No one, I say!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hamtunscire, the last Saxon stronghold.

speaker: Randvi
en: And very heavily guarded. King Aelfred is preparing for war. You will meet tremendous resistance.

speaker: Eivor
en: As will Aelfred. Is Guthrum Jarl there with his army?

speaker: Randvi
en: He is. He and Ubba have gathered a sizable force and intend on launching an attack on Aelfred soon. If we support their assault, England will fall to us. A pagan land where a multitude of gods may freely roam.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will go to Hamtunscire and speak with Guthrum. Send word to our allies to gather on the Thames, just outside the shire.

speaker: Randvi
en: I will. May the gods share in this, our final victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it?

speaker: Valka
en: Eivor, you must not go. You must not! The signs, the portents, they shout and wail! Your leaving will be our doom!

speaker: Eivor
en: Speak clearly, Valka. What have you seen?

speaker: Valka
en: I have thrown the bones, I have stirred the offals of beasts, and in the rising steam, I saw the end of all. Though this battle you may win, this war you will not. Your foe will be your master, your hope will be your grief. This is fate. Our fate.

speaker: Eivor
en: I thank you for this, Valka. But the yarns of fate are too frayed for me to follow now. I owe this fight to my friends and allies, and I will see it through.

speaker: Valka
en: Go then. With great care. But know that the home you leave will not be the home to which you return.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am nearing Werham, deep into Aelfred's heartland. I hope Guthrum has a sound plan.

speaker: Eivor
en: Strange to see Norse and Saxon banners flying side-to-side. I should find Guthrum.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma!

speaker: Soma
en: Eivor. You came at Guthrum's call. It is good to see you.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you, Soma. There is an uneasy peace here, both armies with their hackles up. Was blood spilt?

speaker: Soma
en: No. We took Werham without resistance. These Saxons accompany their lord, as we stand beside Guthrum.

speaker: Eivor
en: So this fort is not the sum of his ambitions. Guthrum's plan is to bring the Saxons to the table?

speaker: Soma
en: If he can win the peace without a fight, he will do so.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how likely is that?

speaker: Soma
en: Just now, they sit on their thumbs in the church. Talking in circles. Come, I will take you to him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is Guthrum meeting here? Is it Aelfred?

speaker: Soma
en: That's right. The King of the West Saxons agreed to negotiate. Seems we have him on the back foot.

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum should be careful. Aelfred speaks with Loki's tongue.

speaker: Soma
en: Guthrum is not a babe-at-teat, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nor is Aelfred. If he has come, it is for his own advantage.

speaker: Soma
en: Then give us counsel. Stand by Guthrum, show our strength. The king of hayseeds will soon be humbled, trust me.

speaker: Guthrum
en: We took this town as if it were a straw-hall. Do not challenge me, Elf-King.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Your show of swagger and strength has my attention, Guthrum. But we agreed on terms. What more do you want?

speaker: Guthrum
en: The crown of Wessex.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Wessex has a king. And that king has the backing of the Almighty. Yours is a fever-dream, Dane.

speaker: Eivor
en: We need not ask for it, Goodwin. We will take it. As we have taken all the kingdoms of England.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have learned nothing since the Danes came here. Guthrum will not bend his knee, oath-breaker. Just as I would not.

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum does not negotiate with oath-breakers. Men whose words are only shadows of their thoughts.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Ah, Eivor. Our blunted tool returns, lord.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I have given you all I care to, a to leave Werham. You swore an oath upon the cross and that pagan hammer.

speaker: Goodwin
en: And when you scurry back to whatever shit-soaked hovel you crawled from, we will release your men.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Speak again, handmaid, and I will feed your tongue to Eivor's raven.

speaker: Goodwin
en: A fair trade. We already have your cock.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are we done with this pissing contest? If Guthrum has given you his word, then he will honor it. We will leave this town.

speaker: Goodwin
en: You have one day. Do not test the king's patience further, or our men will return to Werham with force.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: And if you doubt my convictions, know that the Afon River near Uffentune runs red with the blood of your countrymen.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Their commander... what did his men cry as he fell? Ulla? Ubba? Yes, that was it.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Remember, you have taken my silver. In return, I expect your honor. I will await news of your retreat in Cippanhamm.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Ubba dead! It cannot be! Gods, I will tear that Saxon's skin from his bones if this is true!

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfred hisses with a snake tongue, but he gains nothing from this lie.

speaker: Soma
en: When news of this spreads through the camp, no Saxon will survive the day.

speaker: Eivor
en: You swore upon the cross?

speaker: Guthrum
en: O, I have no intention of cowing to that milk-sack. Now, more than ever, I will take his throne. And his head.

speaker: Eivor
en: In Wincestre, Aelfred used me as a tool and cast me aside. So let the betrayer be betrayed. We will burn this village to the ground. After that, we take care of Aelfred.

speaker: Eivor
en: Burn Werham to the ground, make it a Saxon pyre!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: You oath-breakers! We had a truce.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: And now it is ended. And you'll feel my axe in your gut, piglet.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: For Ubba! Every great Norse you've sent to Valhalla, I'll send ten to your Hell.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: You won't burn Werham, scum!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Lord Jesus Christ, help me stand against the filthy heathen threat.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Your God-son has forsaken you, Saxon.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: You have no honor, Dane! You will not steal our land.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: It is too late, little man. Our gods have spoken with war and wit. This is our England now.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: My blood needs fire, after cooling in this sodden field.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: You'll burn in Hell, traitorous scum!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: I will feast on your marrow in Valhalla!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fire and flame! Burn it all! Leave nothing standing! Let vengeance steer your swords!

speaker: Guthrum
en: Set Werham ablaze. Destroy everything. Their roofs to splinters, their bones to dust. Payment for those warriors they have sent to Valhalla.

speaker: Eivor
en: Their prayers go unanswered this day. We should find Soma.

speaker: Soma
en: Stand firm all. Do not lose your nerve.

speaker: Eivor
en: This place is routed, Soma!

speaker: Eivor
en: Good work, we leave now. There are forest ruins just east of here, along the road. Come on, men, move!

speaker: Eivor
en: Saxons ahead!

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is your king now, Saxons? Cowering like a mouse.

speaker: Guthrum
en: For Ubba! His blood soaks your soil!

speaker: Eivor
en: Every soul we meet, sent to their god. Let us keep moving!

speaker: Eivor
en: More Saxons. Draw your weapons.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Cut down the stragglers.

speaker: Soma
en: The ruins are close, keep moving!

speaker: Guthrum
en: Every Saxon is eager to meet his maker.

speaker: Guthrum
en: We can rest here a moment. Now, tell me what you know of that breaker of rings. Weak and wretched troll.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfred is a wily fox. He appears frail but draws upon an inner strength. He will not be easy to oust.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Fury will fuel my army and my claim.

speaker: Eivor
en: It will not be enough. You must find a weakness.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Yes, that is why I called you here. Do you balk at the opportunity to bury the Saxon king?

speaker: Eivor
en: I must first hear a plan to balk at.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Aelfred spoke of Cippenhamm, a squat hovel of sheep and peasants.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, why does he go there and not to Wincestre? Your scouts must know, they are the best in England.

speaker: Guthrum
en: A holiday feast, their Saxon Christ mass. Aelfred will warm his heels by the fire while Ubba lies cold in an English field.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have called upon my allies to join us in this fight. But I must know where to send them. Is Cippenhamm our final prize?

speaker: Guthrum
en: It is. But uh I will need my men for the coming fight as well. The hostages Aelfred took. If there is a chance to save them...

speaker: Eivor
en: We will not lose more friends today. Where are they held?

speaker: Guthrum
en: A place further ahead through this forest. They call it Hamtun Blockade.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma, ride north to the Thames and lead my allies south. They should be gathered by now.

speaker: Soma
en: I will.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Gather on the river passing Cippenhamm. The rest of you, set up camp there.

speaker: Guthrum
en: I called you Raven-Feeder once. At Portcestre, you were hotheaded as Thor. You have become a true leader, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is much to come, Guthrum, before we can rest with mead in our hands and songs in our ears.

speaker: Guthrum
en: I will crush Aelfred's skull with my bare hands if Ubba is dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: We cannot dwell on this, even if it is true. If you want the throne, only strategy will deliver it.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Or bloody wrath will steal it. I will follow this Aelfred, hound his heels. Revenge burns within me.

speaker: Eivor
en: A wise man once told me we do not dash ourselves against hopeless causes. We arrive unexpected, strike swift.

speaker: Guthrum
en: You turn my words against me now, Wolf-Kissed?

speaker: Eivor
en: I took them to heart in my darkest times, my friend.

speaker: Guthrum
en: And Sigurd? He is back with you?

speaker: Eivor
en: My brother's story is a long one, and for another time.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ridding the land of a strong ruler will make Wessex harder to tame.

speaker: Guthrum
en: You almost sound like you respect him, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have come to understand the trials of leadership, Guthrum. It is hard not to when you cradle something as fragile as life within your hands.

speaker: Guthrum
en: There, this is the blockade. The hostages must be in these buildings. What is your plan?

speaker: Eivor
en: We can tread quietly so as not to alert the guards. But I can raid this place in moments with my crew.

speaker: Guthrum
en: I will follow your lead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you see your men?

speaker: Guthrum
en: No, but we must keep looking.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Do you think he kept his word? He swore he would not kill them.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot say for certain, just hope we find them soon.

speaker: Guthrum
en: I had to hand them over. Aelfred demanded it.

speaker: Eivor
en: We will save them, Guthrum. Stay calm.

speaker: Guthrum
en: There! These are my men!

speaker: Norse Soldier 1
en: I told you Guthrum wouldn't leave us here to rot.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough skulking!

speaker: Guthrum
en: These Saxons do not deserve compassion. I will wash my blade in their blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go to the camp near Cippenhamm. Find your countrymen there.

speaker: Norse Soldier 2
en: Good! We will pay back the Saxons for the insults they heaped on us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum! Some of your men!

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: We will not be feasting in Odin's hall tonight, boys!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you Guthrum's men?

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: Aye! Free us and we will fight by your side.

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: Every Saxon who spat at me will die.

speaker: Eivor
en: You will have your chance, but don't be foolhardy. Let your steps take you far from here to our camp near Cippanhamm.

speaker: Guthrum
en: There is a camp set up north by Cippenhamm. Go there!

speaker: Norse Warrior 8
en: As long as I can cut some Saxons down, I don't care where we face them.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Thank you, Eivor. You did a great deed here. Their families will raise a cup to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need no thanks, Guthrum. Let us speak more when we are safely away.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are safe here. Let us speak, Guthrum.

speaker: Eivor
en: You should join your people at the camp. Even a surprise takes preparation.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Your bravery, your leadership, Eivor... you wear it well. You have grown much since last we spoke.

speaker: Eivor
en: You judged me fairly, Guthrum, harsh though your words were. But I do not make the same mistake twice.

speaker: Guthrum
en: How is your brother Sigurd?

speaker: Eivor
en: He lives, a changed man. But he is free of Fulke's torment. That at least was a deed well done.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Will this all be worth it in the end? Everything we have done, everything we have sacrificed to win this land? Sometimes I dream of soot-black furrowed earth. And blood seeping from seedlings, poisoning our future.

speaker: Eivor
en: We must believe our way of life will survive. Our fates are woven, but our deeds forge our destiny.

speaker: Guthrum
en: And so to our final battle. We will wait for you at the camp.

speaker: Norse Warrior 10
en: Guthrum! My jarl! We must speak!

speaker: Guthrum
en: Another matter that needs my attention. I will meet you at the camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those Dane invaders, they came from East Anglia, is that right?

speaker: Randvi
en: Yes. Dane invaders who serve a man called Rued. He seems to be sowing discord among Saxons and friendly Danes alike. Years ago, the Sons of Ragnar hoped to pacify the land. They appointed a steward named Finnr to find a suitable Saxon king. But the kingdom has fallen into ruin since, with no king and violent raiders ravaging what little peace remains. I suggest you make for East Anglia and find out what their steward is doing wrong.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will make the trip east, then. Speak to this Finnr myself.

speaker: Randvi
en: A good plan.

speaker: Eivor
en: Northwic. Suffering hard times, I see.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Dark times, dark times! You tend to your sheep, to your cattle, and look away from the knaves that creep ever closer! East Anglia still stands without a king but for how long? Who will defend us in the battles to come? Raise your voices and your mugs tonight at the Spanking Pig. For those mugs may be your last.

speaker: Finnr
en: Wha... what? What's happening?

speaker: Eivor
en: Finnr?

speaker: Finnr
en: No, not unless Halfdan sent you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I sent myself. I want to speak with Finnr, the steward who should be working to put a king on that throne.

speaker: Finnr
en: Ah, you're in luck then, for I have found the man already. I'm only waiting on him to get married.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's pretend Halfdan did send me. Then we pretend you're Finnr, his steward of East Anglia.

speaker: Finnr
en: Right...

speaker: Eivor
en: How do you expect to find a king for this kingdom when this is the speed you work at?

speaker: Finnr
en: I found him already! And as soon as he's married, we'll plunk his arse down on that throne.

speaker: Eivor
en: Whoever you are, I want to know why there's no king on East Anglia's throne?

speaker: Finnr
en: Because the man in question ain't been married yet. Once he is, East Anglia will have its king... and little else.

speaker: Eivor
en: Which man?

speaker: Finnr
en: You know, stranger, you interrupted a beautiful dream. I was sailing through Helheim, drifting on a boat of fire.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dreams of death often run ahead of the real thing.

speaker: Finnr
en: O, wouldn't that be a burden off my shoulders. What business have you with a backwater king, anyway?

speaker: Eivor
en: Danes from here attacked my clan. I want to know why, and how to make sure it never happens again.

speaker: Finnr
en: Ah, that'd be Rued's clan. They killed the last man I put here, Aethelstan. I suspect they'll do the same to our next monarch.

speaker: Eivor
en: A Dane who cannot keep the Danes in line? Not much of a steward, are you?

speaker: Finnr
en: If I knew how, I'd have rid our lands of them long ago! Rued's clan plagues us all, Dane and Saxon alike.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are the sorriest soldier I've met in this country. Kick your king in the arse and fight back.

speaker: Finnr
en: He needs more than a kicking! He's got nothing he should have to win this fight. No courage, no army, no charisma! If he wants to live longer than a season, he'll need the backing of his bride's family. Which he hasn't! They loathe maggot.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is he, your king maggot?

speaker: Finnr
en: Oswald of Elmenham. He was King Edmund's counsel before the invasions. And like it or not, he's the last Saxon noble with any sway.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why not crown a Dane instead?

speaker: Finnr
en: Halfdan Jarl made it clear. He wants a Saxon king married to a Dane. For a greater show of unity. But Oswald's not the sort of man you'd chase into battle with a grin. He's soft. And the settled Danes don't trust him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is he now? I'll get the measure of him, see what I can do.

speaker: Finnr
en: You just missed him. He's headed for Elmenham just now, pleading once again for peace. If you go by the north gates and along the road, you may catch him.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: ... they rushed in like wolves, killing and burning as they went!

speaker: Norse Man
en: It wasn't us!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Your folk destroyed this country once before! Now you're doing it again!

speaker: Norse Man
en: We live here, you blistering fool! We were attacked as well!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: You live here because you took our land!

speaker: Norse
en: I built myself a home here! Rued's clan attacked us as well!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O how nice to have a home to speak of, man! Mine was burned to the ground years ago! And by whom, I wonder?

speaker: Oswald
en: Please, all of you! Be we Dane or Saxon, we all want the same peace... with land to till and a home to keep, without fear of Rued's violence.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Til they break the peace with another bleedin' raid!

speaker: Oswald
en: Nonsense. Their homes are here now, same as ours. Our futures run together, not apart.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: So what of these Danes attacking us, eh? What will you do about them?

speaker: Oswald
en: When I am king

speaker: Oswald
en: When I am your king, I'll set things right.

speaker: Norse Man
en: You will be king when I am a flying troll.

speaker: Eivor
en: You handled that well. Disputes between Saxon and Dane don't always end so cleanly.

speaker: Oswald
en: That was a clean result?

speaker: Eivor
en: A dispute ending without bloodshed is as clean as they come.

speaker: Oswald
en: Quite a brutal outlook...

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor of the Raven Clan. Are you Oswald?

speaker: Eivor
en: A king should be harsher in tone with those who disrupt his kingdom.

speaker: Oswald
en: I'm not yet king. So I'll listen to my people before deciding what tone to take.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor of the Raven Clan. Are you Oswald?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor of the Raven Clan. Are you Oswald?

speaker: Oswald
en: I am... You're not here to kill me, are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not in the habit of killing kings. But I do like meeting them.

speaker: Oswald
en: I am Oswald, yes. For as long as I can hold out.

speaker: Eivor
en: So what happened here, Oswald?

speaker: Oswald
en: A clan led by a Dane called Rued attacked this morning. They've been sacking farms and hamlets across East Anglia for some time now, growing more brazen by the day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do they know this is Halfdan's land?

speaker: Oswald
en: They must. They just don't care.

speaker: Eivor
en: Their chaos has touched my home as well. And I'm here to see that it doesn't happen again. Lately I've come to learn you are the hook that all hopes hang upon. As king, you could unite all Saxons and friendly Danes.

speaker: Oswald
en: A minor weight to bear, isn't it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Who else if not a king should bear it?

speaker: Oswald
en: Travel with me, Eivor. We can discuss my tenuous future on the road home.

speaker: Eivor
en: What begs your attention in Elmenham?

speaker: Oswald
en: Wedding preparations. Elmenham is on guard as we ready my marriage to the Dane woman Valdis. She's a cousin of Halfdan's.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. A well-matched marriage can forge a strong alliance. So what's the hold up?

speaker: Oswald
en: The hold up? I don't yet have permission to marry Valdis. Her brothers don't approve of me.

speaker: Oswald
en: Slow down. Something is... not quite right here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hold. There is smoke ahead.

speaker: Oswald
en: That's Beteleah. It could be the same men who attacked the walls of Northwic.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay here. I'll have a look.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Do you see how they tremble as we thunder by? It makes my guts all wobbly with glee.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: I never knew you as a man given to verse!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Ah, their little worries. Their little lives. They mean nothing to me. They're flies on shit.

speaker: Eivor
en: That should be the last of these pig-faced cowards. Oswald will be relieved to know of this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rued's clan. They left none alive.

speaker: Oswald
en: God rest their souls. I'm needed at home to make yet another fruitless attempt to impress my betrothed's family.

speaker: Eivor
en: Show more grit than you're showing me now and they may start to like you.

speaker: Oswald
en: Yes, sorry. I'm just... shaken. If you joined us at dinner, that might ease their minds a touch. Think about it. My doors are open to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll be happy to join you. Tell me when and where.

speaker: Eivor
en: My presence alone won't sway the family of your intended bride. That's work you must do yourself.

speaker: Oswald
en: Yes, yes, you're absolutely right. I'm merely hoping you might provide me with... perspective.

speaker: Eivor
en: That I can do.

speaker: Eivor
en: It takes more than a feast to impress a Dane. If you want to marry into this family, you must become one as well.

speaker: Oswald
en: I'd be a troll's groom if it helped the people of this kingdom. Only tell me how.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Oswald
en: Wonderful. Visit us in Elmenham, whenever you have time.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's worse here than I feared.

speaker: Eivor
en: A healthy-seeming town. This Oswald has done well for himself.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Look there, a lone Dane. Can't trust that.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Shh. Be kind, yeah? As Christ would command.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald, where is this dinner you promised me?

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor! You came. Dinner will still be served, but I am afraid you are too early. My intended and her family are not ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: This intended of yours, Oswald. Who is she? One of love? Or politics?

speaker: Oswald
en: Her name is Valdis. And people don't marry for love these days, Eivor. This is an arrangement for East Anglia's benefit. She's from a Dane family whose military might is not to be trifled with. But her brothers... their motives are selfish. Why don't you have a look around and come back later? Dinner will not disappoint.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does one do to pass time in a place like this?

speaker: Oswald
en: Have a walk by the countryside to work up an appetite. Travelers sometimes leave offerings at Cedd's Stone, a beautiful altar in the woods just east of here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll have a look around. Thank you, Oswald.

speaker: Oswald
en: Lords, Ladies. This is a day of peace and fraternity. I asked you here to Elmenham to offer my thanks and extend my generosity. Finnr, our steward. To our guests of honor, Brothir and Broder, and to my lovely bride-to-be, Valdis.

speaker: Broder
en: You get to plow our sister because Halfdan commands it. But you won't drag us into bed with you, you hear?

speaker: Oswald
en: Broder, that is

speaker: Brothir
en: The last Saxon king we backed wasn't half as mushy as you. And we lost a hundred and fifty men protecting his maggoty arse!

speaker: Valdis
en: Brothir!

speaker: Oswald
en: If you're going to be rude, then I must ask you to leave. This is my home, and I won't be insulted here.

speaker: Broder
en: Is that why you've come? To back this thegn (nobleman) who smells of goat shit and sheep pebbles?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sorry, did you say something?

speaker: Broder
en: Do I bore you, Wolf-Kissed?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm here to protect my clan. If that means helping your king secure his throne, well, so be it.

speaker: Brothir
en: You'd be safer crowning the throne. It's made of less wood than this one!

speaker: Eivor
en: We'd all be safer if you had the stones to stand up to Rued's clan. But between the pair of you, I can't see a single nugget.

speaker: Broder
en: You watch your tongue, Wolf-Kissed. Or you'll find it freed of your face!

speaker: Eivor
en: So easily wounded by words. Imagine the ruin my axe would inflict on your flaccid ego.

speaker: Broder
en: My flaccid what?

speaker: Oswald
en: O! Please, stop this.

speaker: Eivor
en: You heard me.

speaker: Brothir
en: That's it!

speaker: Brothir
en: She called us flaccid!

speaker: Eivor
en: Limp, weak, soft...

speaker: Oswald
en: Ridiculous! Absurd!

speaker: Valdis
en: This is no way to ensure I'll be queen!

speaker: Finnr
en: Ha! Reminds of home, those bygone days. Ah! To be so full of vigor again!

speaker: Oswald
en: This is not how we settle disputes in East Anglia!

speaker: Valdis
en: Brothers! Stop this! Or I'll have both your arses!

speaker: Oswald
en: Calm yourselves!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: That was expensive! Watch out!

speaker: Finnr
en: Not worth much now!

speaker: Finnr
en: Stop, all of you! That's enough fun for tonight!

speaker: Eivor
en: If that's all you've got, it's little wonder East Anglia's in the state it is.

speaker: Brothir
en: About the challenge I'd expect from a friend of Oswald.

speaker: Broder
en: You're weak, sheep-herder. Your Norse friend here can't change that. We're better off without a king.

speaker: Oswald
en: Well, that's me done.

speaker: Finnr
en: I think I prefer dream nonsense to these ale house brawls.

speaker: Oswald
en: What a waste of time and good mead. These brothers will never back me and my claim.

speaker: Eivor
en: This dance is just beginning, Oswald. Get some rest, you'll need your energy.

speaker: Oswald
en: And will I see you in the morning? We have much to discuss, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll find a place to lay my head.

speaker: Oswald
en: And Eivor, if you can help me right this situation, you'll have a strong alliance with East Anglia. That much I promise.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is an army of the dead down here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Strange, her voice is like a lullaby. I wonder where it leads.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it you want? Who are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Poison! I need to get out of here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll kill you for that. Have you anything to say?

speaker: Merec
en: One of you swallowed it! Who was it? There is nothing tasty about a brooch. My brooch! My brooch! Dear Heaven, I'll never get it back!

speaker: Eivor
en: Lose something?

speaker: Merec
en: Polished the family brooch up for my niece, put it down for two seconds, and it's gone! One of the sheep must've swallowed it.

speaker: Eivor
en: That would be one hungry sheep.

speaker: Merec
en: It was my grandmother's, given to her by a very wealthy, uh, admirer. How will I get it back without hurting any of my lovely sheep?

speaker: Letter from Niece
en: Uncle Merec, Mother tells me that you wish to give me grandmother's brooch. Oh, dear uncle! I shall treasure such a keepsake! -Your loving niece

speaker: Merec
en: Ah, yes! Feed the sheep and see what... comes out...

speaker: Merec
en: See what's there!

speaker: Eivor
en: By the gods, how do I find myself doing this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Wh-what has this sheep eaten? Nothing in there. Nothing. I must continue my search.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have had no luck finding your brooch.

speaker: Merec
en: Alackaday!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm...Ah! A brooch. Not in very fine condition.

speaker: Merec
en: You'll frighten the sheep!

speaker: Merec
en: See what's there!

speaker: Eivor
en: By the gods, how do I find myself doing this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Wh-what has this sheep eaten? Nothing in there. Nothing. I must continue my search.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have had no luck finding your brooch.

speaker: Merec
en: Alackaday!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm...Ah! A brooch. Not in very fine condition.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here's your brooch.

speaker: Merec
en: Whew! That smell'd knock over a horse!

speaker: Eivor
en: Just take it.

speaker: Merec
en: It'll need a washing, but my niece will be grateful! Many thanks, stranger.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not help in this way again.

speaker: Merec
en: What have you done?

speaker: Merec
en: Not Dewdrop!!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm...Ah! A brooch. Not in very fine condition.

speaker: Merec
en: Stop! Have you lost your mind? All my lovelies! You monster!

speaker: Eivor
en: Here's your brooch.

speaker: Merec
en: Whew! That smell'd knock over a horse!

speaker: Eivor
en: Just take it.

speaker: Merec
en: It'll need a washing, but my niece will be so grateful! Many thanks, stranger.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not help in this way again.

speaker: Merec
en: Did you have to kill Dewdrop? She had such soulful brown eyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: You wanted the brooch. You have it. Your niece will be grateful.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Norse Woman
en: I heard the Gyldan Sparrow was carrying more 'n candies and spice from Aksum. He had a hefty necklace in there too.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Makes sense as to why The Compass would send the whole boat into the drink then. Bloody shame. Worth a pretty penny.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: This harbor houses sunken treasure?

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Norse Woman
en: Ja, the current's too strong to pull the wreck out, so we're left to lament the loss. You interested?

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: I am a strong swimmer. I fear no cold, current, or drengr of the deep.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Norse Woman
en: Then by all means, we can scrape together a reward fit for the cargo's rescue.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: That must be the corpse of the Gyldan Sparrow that merchant mentioned.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: One chest with treasure, another with this bottled message. I wonder if it has preserved its message.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: I found a message in a bottle. It looks like the treasure was eaten by fish.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: One chest with treasure, another with this bottled message. I wonder if it has preserved its message.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Norse Woman
en: A message in a bottle? Ah, wise. Hid a necklace in a cow's stomach. Guess you'll have to go fishing for the rest of the treasure.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: Come now, you little scaled cowards. Pull on my line.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: Slippery bastards. Must be the necklace. That is a lot of silver. Why shouldn't I keep it?

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: I have the treasure you seek.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Norse Woman
en: Do you? Please, give it here, then.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: Found this necklace in the guts of a fish. I could not get rid of the smell.

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Norse Woman
en: Even reeking of fish, this is priceless. Many thanks!

scene: Last Flight of the Gyldan Sparrow
speaker: Eivor
en: I risked my neck swimming into the drink, so the spoils are mine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin... I feel you close... an uproar of memories, stretching far into the past. I have silenced you and your influence. But I know you have so much to say.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are with me always. Deep within my hugr. I could trap you in this darkness until my end, resisting forever this second side of myself. Or I could learn from you. To better understand the world that once was. Long, long ago. But not here. Not in sight of those who would not understand what I am. Who we are. I have done all I can for my people. It is time to say goodbye. And set forth for distant shores. And new adventures.

speaker: Odin
en: Eivor... I am still with you, drifting at the edge of your memory.

speaker: Odin
en: You have tamed the Odin within you, but I have not disappeared. I am with you always, embedded deep within your hugr. Will you keep me in the darkness until your end, resisting forever this side of yourself? Or could you learn from me? To better understand the world that was. The world I left behind. But not here. Not in sight of those who would not understand who you are. Who we are. Have you not done all you can for your people? Say your goodbyes. And set forth for distant shores. And new adventures.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: What's this? What do I have to do? Have I lost my touch? Am I cursed? I... I just can't get it right. Stupid. You're stupid. A fool. That's what it is! You think you know what you're doing, but you don't.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mmm... Smells good.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, please! I'm irritated enough already. The last thing I need is someone lying to my face.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a compliment, Saxon. Take it. What are you brewing anyway?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I call it Ledecestrescire sauce.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is a mouthful. What is wrong with it?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: It doesn't come close to meriting such a sizable name, that's what's wrong with it. And I've tried. Lord, have I tried. But I cannot for the life of me strike the perfect balance. I should just give up.

speaker: Eivor
en: As I look around, that is hard to argue.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You wouldn't happen to be carrying an eel would you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not the first thing I grab when I set off for the day, no.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I've fished everything in Ledecestre but the eel.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you think this elusive river-snake could be the answer to your sauce woes.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: There's only one way to know for sure.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. If I wrangle one, I shall bring it to you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Yes, please. I must try, if only to rule it out. Thank you!

speaker: Eivor
en: I have your eel.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, good! Please, add it to the pot.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Ahh. Here it is. Would you be so kind?

speaker: Eivor
en: You want me to taste this?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Of course, for your palate is far less tainted than mine. Take a generous amount, too.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: And? Verdict?

speaker: Eivor
en: No... not quite there.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, Lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: Uh... If it helps, I've had worse.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I suppose that's it then, it's over. Time for me to pack up my things and see what the fruits of another kingdom might offer me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where will you go?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Worcester, I think. Though I'll be buggered if I'm going to name my sauce after that paltry place. Thank you... for all your help. I don't know many Danes, and don't care to, but you've helped bring closure to this journey. If I could ask one more favor of you, it would be to take this failure to the grottos below my home. I can't stand the sight of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Farewell. Luck be with you. You will need it.

speaker: Eivor
en: These new visions of Odin trouble me. Am I alone in seeing them? Or do the tales of Svartalfheim hold some other meaning? Perhaps I should warm my bones by the fire, gather my thoughts for a moment.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tove? How've you been?

speaker: Tove
en: The fire made me think of the myths and legends Svend loved.

speaker: Eivor
en: Would you indulge me with a tale? I would be glad to hear of Svartalfheim.

speaker: Tove
en: I... would not tell it half as well... But... his favorite was a fable, to remind us to find meaning in our deeds, and not in how others think of us. Svartalfheim was not short of legendary dwarven blacksmiths. Everyone has heard of Ivaldi, of Brokkr and Sindri. But this tale is of a stone mason. He lived as far south as he could, where Gullnámar meets Vangrinn. His workshop sat upon the shoreline. Obsessed with glory, his love of masonry had all but died. He scoured the shore, seeking precious stones washed up from other realms. Then he saw it. Something beautiful, glittering, shimmering across the water, upon an island he had never dared travel to. He hastily built a boat, working long into the night. He set sail, and found many rocks that sparkled and dazzled upon the island. He cried out in joy! To craft anything from such stones, he would be remembered for all time. Then he felt a sudden sting on his foot. Then another. And another. His eyes adjusted to the dark... So consumed was he by his desire for renown, he failed to realize he had walked into a nest of snakes, until it was already too late. And so, clutching the stone that sealed his fate, there he died. Remembered, yes, but only for his folly.

speaker: Eivor
en: A fine tale, Tove, and well told. Svend would be proud.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you and Brigid well?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Of course. I just... The flames soothe my mind. As do the tales told here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you have one to share, Gunnar? A legend of Svartalfheim?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Aye. A story of a king... who could not see the wood for the trees. Hreidmar. Greatest of dwarven kings. Within his palace in Gullnámar, he wanted for nothing except an heir. Hreidmar and his wife had grown old. Perhaps... too old. Late one night, consumed with worry, Hreidmar walked in the shadow of his vast mountaintop palace, tears in his eyes. "Great King, what ails you?" a voice said. Afraid, Hreidmar saw no one. "Who goes there?" he replied. Then he saw who addressed him. A vast and ancient tree, perhaps almost as old as Ymir himself. Hreidmar sat upon its roots, and told the tree he feared he was too old to give his subjects the legacy they deserved. The tree was so moved, it wept and offered its tears to Hreidmar. "Drink, Great King," it said, "and your woes shall be washed away." Hreidmar observed the grass, the meadows, the leaves of the tree. His subjects' happiness could be seen in how they cared for the land. His legacy was all around him. Hreidmar felt at ease, realising he had everything he needed, and asked that the land receive the tree's gift instead. The tree's happy tears flowed evermore, enriching the land. Nine moons passed, and a baby's cry rang through Hreidmar's palace. Long would dwarves place gifts in the weeping tree's roots, in memory of Hreidmar and his kindness that shaped all he touched.

speaker: Eivor
en: All things happen when they should, old friend.

speaker: Gunnar
en: ...I hope so.

speaker: Alvis
en: Eivor! Whatever is the matter? Have you been spending too much time drinking Valka's special sauces again?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am... troubled by visions of Odin... and of Svartalfheim. They... flood my mind without warning, without invitation.

speaker: Alvis
en: Aha! Which is how Thor flooded Svartalfheim... Thor, fast to act but not so fast to think, would stomp and thump and fight and bump everywhere he and Mjölnir should go. One day, he found a giant in Jotunheim with such ferocity that Thor's killing blow was felt through all Nine Realms! The ground shook! Mountains rose up! Hills tore apart, creating canyons! And north of Svaladal... ...the massive lake that housed the springs of Yggdrasil split open, flooding all of Svartalfheim! The dwarf king, Hreidmar, acted swiftly. He built three mighty dams, preventing further damage to his realm, working alongside his beloved subjects. So surprised was one builder to see the great king working as an equal that he slipped, tumbling into the raging waters below. Without hesitation, Hreidmar leapt! Once from his horse! And again, from the center of the dam's lip, diving into the frightful torrent! Before the builder could even cry for help, Hreidmar was pulling him onto dry land. And so two statues were built to honor the king, one for each leap of unthinking bravery, and stood until the end of days.

speaker: Eivor
en: Until Ragnarök...

speaker: Alvis
en: Aye! So you see, actions ripple outward like a stone falling into a lake. Or like Thor crushing a Jotun skull with Mjolnir!

speaker: Eivor
en: Affecting everything, whether foretold or unknown...

speaker: Alvis
en: I... fear my tale has only worsened your concerns.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm? No, a good story is... a log that feeds a mind's flame. Thank you, friend.

speaker: Randvi
en: I hear you seek tales of Svartalfheim. You are not alone in your glimpses of the Aesir.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have seen them too?

speaker: Randvi
en: No. Only the power the visions hold, and their effect on those once held dear...

speaker: Eivor
en: You... you speak of Sigurd...?

speaker: Randvi
en: Do you want my tale or not?

speaker: Randvi
en: There was a dwarven miner who cared only for his work. Mining was all he knew, all he wanted to know, and all he would ever know. One day he heard a strange noise. All his long life, working in the northern mines of Vangrinn, he had never known a boulder... to squeak. He ignored it, at first. But as the hours passed, the squeaking continued, relentlessly. When the miner could take no more, he split the boulder apart with his pick. And then he saw... A squirrel. Until now, pinned by the boulder. Afraid and tired, the freed squirrel climbed into the miner's long beard and slept for three days. When the dwarf awoke the next day, he found fruit and nuts waiting for him. A gift from the squirrel. The first the miner had ever received. Finally, the miner had a friend. The squirrel led the dwarf to a stone hill within a lake. There, the dwarf would fish for supper, while the squirrel played in the trees. One night, watching his fishing line, the dwarf drifted off to sleep, smiling, enjoying the happy squeaks of his friend above. When the sun rose, its light did not find the dwarf, for he had turned to stone, his short-lived bliss captured evermore.

speaker: Eivor
en: And the squirrel?

speaker: Randvi
en: It never left his side. Hoping his friend would awaken, just as the miner had waited for the squirrel to do the same.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd... he is not lost to us.

speaker: Eivor
en: In every great story, there is truth to be found. I wonder what could be found in Svartalfheim, in the place they spoke of...

speaker: Eivor
en: Guildford is a town of farmers and grain silos. Ubba will be nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: All is ready?

speaker: Ubba
en: For a town of farmers and shepherds, this place bristles with swords. One of them is a thegn by his dress. Serious men with him too. Went into the longhouse.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've already put some of this town to the torch, but there is more to do here.

speaker: Ubba
en: Not like you to leave a job unfinished.

speaker: Eivor
en: If we take care, we might avoid drawing the thegn's attention while we burn the grain silos.

speaker: Ubba
en: Ah! Was that a jest? Bring them on! Been too long since I met a Saxon worth half a shit.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Danes are crawling all over Suthsexe! We must bolster the s. Recruit more soldiers!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: The king's already pulled every able man into his service. Scanty pickings out there.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: They ain't proper soldiers, either. Farmers and tradesmen. The last showed up with hayforks and shovels!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: I don't want excuses. I need more men!

speaker: Eivor
en: Little do they dream how close we have come already.

speaker: Ubba
en: Farmers and tradesmen! This land is ours for the taking.

speaker: Ubba
en: All this sneaking about is giving me a cramp in my arse.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is hard to be quiet with you complaining.

speaker: Ubba
en: Hiding like field mice. It is not our way.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are not hiding like field mice. We are stalking like lynxes.

speaker: Ubba
en: Can we not just kill the lot of them?

speaker: Eivor
en: Do it my way first.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Danes! The Danes have come! Call the thegn!

speaker: Eivor
en: They spotted us!

speaker: Ubba
en: Thank Odin for that! I am sick of skulking around. Now where's the big man?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Rats in the wheat fields? Not on my watch.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Danes! The Danes have come! Call the thegn!

speaker: Eivor
en: They spotted us!

speaker: Ubba
en: Thank Odin for that! I am sick of skulking around. Now where's the big man?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Rats in the wheat fields? Not on my watch.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've burned the silos already. Just had to be sure the job was done.

speaker: Ubba
en: Seems so. Maybe we can have some fun with those Saxons, though?

speaker: Eivor
en: Or we could return to the camp without risking our lives?

speaker: Ubba
en: This is Wessex, Eivor. Wouldn't hurt to thin the herd a little.

speaker: Ubba
en: Is it over? I was just working up a sweat.

speaker: Eivor
en: There will be Saxons enough to test you in Portcestre.

speaker: Ubba
en: I will hold you to that. See you at the camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: Norvid. I'm told you need my help.

speaker: Norvid
en: Eivor! Yes! I've spent so much time filling my shop with new Ostara items that I haven't had time to finish decorating the settlement.

speaker: Eivor
en: You want me to decorate?

speaker: Norvid
en: Of course! A new banner here, a pile of bones there. You can even change the big tree if you'd like.

speaker: Eivor
en: I worry that my taste may not be the same as everyone else's.

speaker: Norvid
en: Enough! You'll do fine. O, don't forget to play some of the games. You'll want to collect as many festival tokens as possible. I've got some really good items for you! Here, have some tokens on me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Norvid. I'll do my best to decorate the settlement. But if it's a disaster, I'll be blaming you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Norvid. I decorated the settlement as best I can. I must say, I think I did a good job of it.

speaker: Norvid
en: Splendid! It looks very ... festive. Here, take some tokens. And don't forget, you can change the decorations whenever you wish.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm off, be well friend.

speaker: Rada
en: Seer, please. We'll die without blood-mead. Your magic will save my farm, my family.

speaker: Eivor
en: What troubles you, my friend? Why won't the seer answer your call?

speaker: Rada
en: I know not! But without her draughts, my family is doomed.

speaker: Eivor
en: The door is locked, and nobody is stirring within. Better look around.

speaker: Eivor
en: Blood, leading away from the house. Something's amiss.

speaker: Eivor
en: Butterflies. Someone has lost a lot of blood.

speaker: Seer
en: I bear this pain with grace, Freyja, but please, show me a sign...

speaker: Seer
en: You have my thanks, kind one.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your wounds are grave. Should you not rest in bed? I'll carry you home.

speaker: Seer
en: It is no wound, but the blood is mine. I made the potion, Freyja's Blessing, to help the crops grow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Blood-mead.

speaker: Seer
en: Good, you know of it. From my pain, life springs. Please, help me to the clearing. The field needs the blood-mead.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is a farmer at your house who needs it as well. She waits desperately for your return.

speaker: Seer
en: O no, but my fields... If I fail in my task, the harvest is doomed. Please, bring me to the next bloodstone.

speaker: Seer
en: Ngh!

speaker: Eivor
en: Seer!

speaker: Seer
en: The pain surges, but I must finish the ritual.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could take her to the next bloodstone. She could finish the rite. Or I could bring her back the house, where the farmer waits.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here is the place. Are you strong enough to finish the ritual?

speaker: Seer
en: I am, though I must rest. Then I will chant and sow the blood-mead, a task I must perform alone.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. What else can I do?

speaker: Seer
en: You've done enough, and for that, I thank you. But return in a few days and see the ripening fields.

speaker: Eivor
en: I shall. Farewell, seer.

speaker: Seer
en: May the gods watch over you, kind one. Farewell.

speaker: Seer
en: I call upon you, Freyr, blessed brother to Frejya! I plead with you, O Vanir! Leave a bounty where my blood-mead falls!

speaker: Rada
en: The seer! Is she well?

speaker: Seer
en: Rada, my blood and pain are the will of Freyja and Freyr. Speak now. What do you need of me?

speaker: Rada
en: Seer, my crops wither, and my family starves. Harvest comes soon, yet our fields remain barren.

speaker: Seer
en: I know your land suffers, Rada. Take the rest of my blood-mead, and water your soil. All will be well in a few days.

speaker: Rada
en: Thank you, blessed seer! I will see to my fields at once. Thank you. You are both welcome to any good crops my farm will produce. Look for me at my farm in a few days!

speaker: Skegi
en: Look... look what they have done to it.

speaker: Stikla
en: We should stop coming here, Skegi. It only saddens you and angers me.

speaker: Skegi
en: Yes... yes, you are right.

speaker: Stikla
en: Then let's go. And never come back.

speaker: Skegi
en: Just a moment longer...

speaker: Eivor
en: You're looking to set foot in there? I would not advise it.

speaker: Stikla
en: In my youth, I could. Both of us could. We would not think twice about taking back what is ours.

speaker: Eivor
en: You lived here?

speaker: Skegi
en: It was a fishing village once. Built it with our bare hands, all of it. But bandits drove us out the moment they saw how plentiful the waters were. The fish here are not shy, and they are difficult to sate.

speaker: Eivor
en: You make it hard to resist. I may have to see for myself.

speaker: Skegi
en: It will not be easy. Why not take my wife with you? Stikla would love to raise Hel against these dogs.

speaker: Eivor
en: What would it serve? Only a matter of time before more roving bandits catch a whiff of this place.

speaker: Skegi
en: We know. Such is the case in all of Lincolnscire. But it would be a small victory. A chance to dip our feet for a while.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. I'll take her. Always good to rekindle a flame.

speaker: Eivor
en: On me, Stikla. We will whet your blade with their bones.

speaker: Stikla
en: It is long overdue.

speaker: Stikla
en: They fight like children!

speaker: Eivor
en: You are difficult to sate! I like it.

speaker: Stikla
en: All this blood! The waters will run red!

speaker: Eivor
en: You fight with great passion, Stikla.

speaker: Stikla
en: I have longed for this!

speaker: Eivor
en: That is all of them.

speaker: Stikla
en: Skegi will be thrilled. Let us go to him.

speaker: Skegi
en: You made it look effortless.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stikla is a stout fighter. Worthy enough to raid with the best drengir. It may be what she is destined for.

speaker: Skegi
en: You honor her. And believe me, I have tried. But she is stubborn. Insists on looking after this old and frail hound.

speaker: Eivor
en: When you die, have her seek me out.

speaker: Skegi
en: Ha! You jest, but I shall take you up on it. Until then!

speaker: Eivor
en: Not a good idea. If anyone is to take care of these bandits, it'll be me and me alone.

speaker: Eivor
en: Still gazing, eh?

speaker: Skegi
en: Just a little longer. Have you changed your mind? Will you take Stikla and send those bandits to Hel?

speaker: Eivor
en: This fishing spot is safe for now. Have a walk, dip your feet if you like, but do not stay long.

speaker: Skegi
en: We won't. Thank you, stranger. Farewell!

speaker: Skegi
en: You! That was flawless. You fought with fervor! The likes of which I have not seen since Stikla here was a young raider herself. Thank you, young warrior. We built this village with our own hands before it was taken from us.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is not the day you take it back. Only a matter of time before more roving bandits catch a whiff.

speaker: Skegi
en: We know. Such is the case in all of Lincolnscire. But you have given us a small victory to celebrate.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have a walk. Dip your feet if you like, but do not stay long.

speaker: Skegi
en: We won't. Farewell.

speaker: Eivor
en: I wonder how Halfdan fares, now that he sits on the throne.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hmm. Moira may know where Halfdan has gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: Moira, is something wrong?

speaker: Moira
en: Weep for Northumbria.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is it Halfdan? Has he gotten worse?

speaker: Moira
en: His heart is broken. He is a mere shadow of himself. With Faravid lost and his brothers away, he wallows in paranoia and sadness.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could speak with him. Where is he now?

speaker: Moira
en: Wandering the fields of Picheringa with his beloved Beonton.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll find him. Thank you, Moira.

speaker: Moira
en: Picheringa is in the east. Just follow the road to Scarborough.

speaker: Halfdan
en: No glory, no hope. Nothing but snow, silent as a corpse in its grave.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand up, Halfdan. I'm taking you back to Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: Up, my lord. You're a king, you're not allowed to sulk. Men bled and died to sit you on that throne. So go, sit.

speaker: Halfdan
en: My brother, Ivarr... did he die well?

speaker: Eivor
en: He died fighting.

speaker: Halfdan
en: You slew my brother and never said a word. You kept this from me!

speaker: Eivor
en: It was no secret. Ubba knew, did he not

speaker: Halfdan
en: Leave me!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not. I've come to see you safely home. Now get up.

speaker: Halfdan
en: I... I mislaid my hammer. I think Beonton ran off with it, but I'm not... I'm not... I'm not well, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll find your hammer. And then you'll come with me.

speaker: Halfdan
en: I was on my way to Scarborough. If you find my hammer, bring it to me there.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's Beonton, guarding the hammer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdrunk needs his hammer.

speaker: Eivor
en: The lighthouse. Halfdan awaits.

speaker: Eivor
en: This hammer is not meant to be thrown, Halfdan. Remember that next time.

speaker: Halfdan
en: My father, Ragnar, he gifted this to me. Took it off a Finnish chief. Still warm with blood when he handed it to me. I had fourteen winters.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ragnar Lothbrok was a great king.

speaker: Halfdan
en: A Finnish arrow killed my mother. A shield-maiden she was, as fierce as a wolf swallowing the sun. My father swore to kill the men who took her from us. And he did, fourteen against one. But that was years ago, in the east. And this is the west, where my father lies dead, a pile of bones in a pit of snakes.

speaker: Eivor
en: And here we are, still telling stories of his life and deeds.

speaker: Halfdan
en: How did my brother die?

speaker: Eivor
en: With his hand on his axe, awaiting the maidens of the battle-slain.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Hm. Now he drinks at our father's side, awaiting the war at the end of days.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr murdered an innocent man, a good man. He earned the death I gave him.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Hm. If the codes of honor demanded his death, you did what had to be done.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Beonton, my boy! Come here boy!

speaker: Eivor
en: A dog always forgives. But he needs you home. All of Northumbria does.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Hmph. Do a last thing for me. Light the beacon for all to see. And let it burn.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Thank you, friend. You're always welcome at my hall.

speaker: Havi
en: This looks like a bird's nest.

speaker: Vaskr
en: It... it can't end like this. I don't care what anyone says... If only I could talk to you, Svass...

speaker: Havi
en: Is everything alright?

speaker: Vaskr
en: I wish I knew, High One.

speaker: Havi
en: You recognise me?

speaker: Vaskr
en: Of course, but I have no quarrel with you. And even if I did, I have more pressing matters. I... I must get into the dwarves' shelter.

speaker: Havi
en: You have a death wish?

speaker: Vaskr
en: No, but if that's what it takes to be reunited with my love, it is a risk I must bear.

speaker: Havi
en: They hold a Jotun captive?

speaker: Vaskr
en: No. The one I love is... a dwarf, Svass. And, as strange as it might sound, I think he loves me. With everything happening in this crazed world, I know how important it is to hold on to things that are precious. Do you think you could help me? All I want is to speak to him, to know I'm not alone in feeling what I feel.

speaker: Havi
en: Very well. But I cannot take you inside looking like this. Can you shapeshift?

speaker: Vaskr
en: How's this?

speaker: Havi
en: Had to be a wolf, didn't it?

speaker: Vaskr
en: Come again?

speaker: Havi
en: Just... stay by my side, and... don't eat anybody.

speaker: Vaskr
en: I'm not an animal, you know.

speaker: Vaskr
en: So... what's your plan?

speaker: Havi
en: I don't know. And stop talking or you'll give us both away. Do you know the way to the dwarf you seek?

speaker: Vaskr
en: I have his scent.

speaker: Havi
en: Then lead the way, but stay by my side. Ah, there's a good girl.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 1
en: Whoa! Havi! Hold it there. You cannot bring that, that thing in here! It'll eat us whole!

speaker: Havi
en: Be calm, friend. This is my pet. She won't harm a soul.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 2
en: Your pet? We have heard tales of you hunting every last wolf out of Asgard.

speaker: Havi
en: Well, don't believe everything you hear. Now, let us pass.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 1
en: Where is your 'pet' going now?

speaker: Havi
en: I'll go see.

speaker: Svass
en: Vaskr? Have you lost your mind? You know what they'll do if they see you in here!

speaker: Vaskr
en: I couldn't wait another moment. And I had some help.

speaker: Svass
en: I can see. Thank you, High One.

speaker: Havi
en: It was no bother. And I have done far more for love, believe me.

speaker: Vaskr
en: So, am I mad? Or are you feeling this too?

speaker: Svass
en: You're not mad. You're... amazing. I can't believe you'd risk your life for me.

speaker: Vaskr
en: In a heartbeat.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 3
en: Wolves! Help!

speaker: Vaskr
en: We must help them! Come, High One!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 3
en: A Jotun! A Jotun got inside! Kill it!

speaker: Havi
en: No! She fights the wolves! She is your ally!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 4
en: Find a happy place, find a happy place, find a happy place... Go find some other place, will you!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 1
en: Get back! Get back!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 5
en: What the Hel is going on?!

speaker: Havi
en: Just some wolves seeking death. Move aside!

speaker: Havi
en: You could have hidden, kept your identity secret... Twice you have now risked your life for love.

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 6
en: The Jotun! She led the wolves to our door!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 7
en: The Jotnar are our enemy!

speaker: Havi
en: Silence! Are you simpletons, with minds locked by what you believe and blind to what you see?

speaker: Svass
en: You all saw. Vaskr didn't hesitate to help. She was there... in a heartbeat. Accept her. Or she and I both leave.

speaker: Vaskr
en: You mean it?

speaker: Svass
en: Yes, I do. I would be a fool to let you slip through my fingers.

speaker: Havi
en: Then my work here is done. Good luck, the pair of you. And to all of you.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is madness.

speaker: Eivor
en: What have you done, Charles? He slaughters his own servants. Madness.

speaker: Eivor
en: Two keyholes. I should look around.

speaker: Charles
en: I always knew it. She was pure. I am the monster.

speaker: Charles (demon)
en: When they schemed and lied. When they cheated and attacked. Who was there for you? It was me.

speaker: Charles
en: I know, demon. I see clearly now. I should never have doubted you.

speaker: Charles (demon)
en: And now we smash the little ones. All the little ones.

speaker: Charles
en: Against the stones... against the stones... I know...

speaker: French Woman 1
en: Save me, O mother of mine! Spare my life, please!

speaker: Eivor
en: A key. Could work on the door in the main hall.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need a second key.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: I-it is madness! The servants did nothing wrong but serve the king faithfully! He is truly

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Do not say it! We just do what he asks or we will end up like... if we don't kill them, he'll kill us.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Merde. This is a nightmare.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe I should search the upper level.

speaker: French Man 1
en: I hear you coming, my king. Please, stay back! I will burn you! I know your fear! I have fire!

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not him. I am not the king.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods...

speaker: Eivor
en: Strange...

speaker: Eivor
en: A Christian holy book. No key inside.

speaker: Eivor
en: Another key. I should try these on the main hall door.

speaker: Eivor
en: This kingdom has riches beyond my wildest mushroom cap dreams. The bedroom of the king and queen... like it has never been touched.

speaker: Eivor
en: Could be Charles' wedding ring. Why is he not wearing it?

speaker: Eivor
en: I should try these keys on the main hall door.

speaker: Eivor
en: This better work.

speaker: Charles
en: She's the angel. The saint. The one who shimmers with the Lord's light. And so, they were right about me. All of them were right.

speaker: Charles (demon)
en: I know.

speaker: Charles
en: We are what they say. It has always been us. Even as they seared me, I feigned to be purged of all demons. But I knew. No amount of burning would rid me of you. And burn me they did. Below the scarred flesh, you were still there. You were still here. You have always been here. (crying) I embrace you, demon.

speaker: Charles (demon)
en: Louder.

speaker: Charles
en: We are the demon! We are

speaker: Charles
en: I am not the only demon who lurks in these chambers.

speaker: Charles
en: No one is allowed in here! Least of all a Northern heathen!

speaker: Eivor
en: He seems to resist my attacks.

speaker: Eivor
en: He fears the fire for a reason.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now is my chance.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stunned him. But too far from the braziers. I need him closer to the fire.

speaker: Charles
en: It burns! Not the fire!

speaker: Charles
en: You killed the bishop Gozlin, you diable!

speaker: Eivor
en: I killed him before. Maybe he will rise from the dead again.

speaker: Charles
en: No! Charred again!

speaker: Eivor
en: Quit your wailing and fight me.

speaker: Charles
en: Fool! I am not mortal, but you are. Die! I will crush you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could lock him in this room.

speaker: Charles
en: You stay out of there!

speaker: Eivor
en: Or what, Charles?

speaker: Eivor
en: This is where it ends, Charles.

speaker: Charles
en: Get away from her!

speaker: Eivor
en: I could trap him in here to spare his life.

speaker: Charles
en: Ha! I am too fast for such tricks. Nice try, heathen.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to weaken him further.

speaker: Eivor
en: Behind bars or kill you. I have a lot to think about.

speaker: Charles
en: It will be you that I crush against the stones.

speaker: Charles
en: All you had to do was give me my son. You have doomed your people. I will never forget it.

speaker: Charles
en: Let me out of here, you swine!

speaker: Eivor
en: Not before you swear that you and your troops will never come to England.

speaker: Charles
en: You had every chance to secure a treaty between our peoples. All you had to do was deliver me my son.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is larger than the fate of one boy!

speaker: Charles
en: Maybe for you.

speaker: Charles
en: You did deliver my son... but how can I make such an arrangement when as we speak Sigfred is preparing his next raid?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigfred is gone. He has no more armies and no power to work against you.

speaker: Charles
en: Fine. On my honor and the life of Bernard, you have your treaty. My armies will not march on England. Not while I still breathe.

speaker: Eivor
