en: Good. Soon I will sail back to Ravensthorpe. But if a week or a month or a year goes by and I see one Frankish shield−

speaker: Charles
en: Do not worry, diable. You will not.

speaker: Charles
en: No, look away my Queen.

speaker: Richardis
en: Worry not, husband. I am here for you.

speaker: Richardis
en: Leave us. All will be as I promised.

speaker: Eivor
en: And if not, I will come back for him.

speaker: Richardis
en: I know.

speaker: Richardis
en: You have done enough here. Just go.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will you take him east, as you said?

speaker: Richardis
en: Leave us, Eivor.

speaker: Richardis
en: You are alright. Do not worry. I will protect you. God is with us.

speaker: Richardis
en: No! O Charles! What have they done to you? What have I done to you? It did not have to be this way.

speaker: Eivor
en: His death is payment for the many he has killed. And a mercy for those he has yet to.

speaker: Richardis
en: Speak not of mercy while his blood is still warm. What have you done was driven by selfishness and anger. Not mercy.

speaker: Eivor
en: He left me no choice.

speaker: Richardis
en: No, you made a choice. You are not who I thought you were, Eivor. You are not an agent of the Lord. You are a murderer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Charles was a threat to my clan. He was mad beyond reason.

speaker: Richardis
en: And should your clan be threat to one of your neighbors, I hope God grants them the wisdom you lack. Now leave us.

speaker: Madman
en: You mock old Cuthbert, stone soldiers. Hopping in and out, in and out. Like robins on a woodpile. It's impossible. Twenty-five, then twenty-six? They come and go and take my wits with them. They doff their caps and steal my sense. I cannot leave until I know the true number. I cannot! Lords and ladies, lords and ladies, dancing in a dell. Jigging in their shirts and socks to dance me off to Hell.

speaker: Eivor
en: What troubles you, old man?

speaker: Madman
en: Please, I beg you. How many are there? I must know.

speaker: Eivor
en: How many what?

speaker: Madman
en: The stones! Everytime I count them the answer is different. First twenty, then twenty-one! The fairy-folk make a madman out of me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rocks cannot appear and disappear. I shall count them.

speaker: Madman
en: Run round and around, pick up your skirts, don't drag your robes through the dirt.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your stone sentries, I have counted them.

speaker: Madman
en: And? How many lords and ladies come to dance a jig?

speaker: Eivor
en: There are thirty-one. I think that was the count.

speaker: Eivor
en: There are twenty-one, I am as sure as I can be.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am certain there are twenty-seven now! How can this be?

speaker: Madman
en: See! Never the same, never the same. Please. Count them again, you must, to save my wits!

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot get the same number twice!

speaker: Madman
en: Never the same. Never the same. Cobweb cloaks and magpie hats!

speaker: Eivor
en: Now there are 26. How can this be?

speaker: Eivor
en: There are thirty, I think?

speaker: Eivor
en: Are there twenty-one? I cannot see.

speaker: Madman
en: See! Never the same, never the same. Please. Count them again, you must, to save my wits!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is madness, they change each time.

speaker: Madman
en: Don't close your eyes. Or they'll steal the glinting flint, scrobble it away.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot understand it, but now there are twenty-seven.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think there are nineteen.

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps there are twenty-three?

speaker: Madman
en: Ha! They have bewitched you too. Twirl and spin, dance and grin. Pyewhacket comes to bite your shin. Who came crawling from the maw like a fat black rabbit without any legs? I see you. Glisten, little imp. Twenty-seven. Twenty-one. Twenty-three. Twenty-four. Twenty-two. Twenty-two. Twenty-two.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't know how to help you. It seems as if the stones appear and disappear at will.

speaker: Madman
en: You should not stay here. Leave, leave before they claim you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Does Skrýmir toy with me? Casting his magics in England?

speaker: Eivor
en: That stone, was it here before? And where is my mad friend? Damn this cursed place.

speaker: Eivor
en: That bishop's mind was afflicted by a strangeness I do not understand. He held a crest, and a key. I should look around for what it unlocks.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: It's been too long. We should check.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to be quick. The guards will find the body soon.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Merde! (Shit!) The bishop is slain! Find the intruder! Don't let them escape!

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to go!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is a lot of wealth. Engelwin would make a good raider.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now this is new.

speaker: Eivor
en: Journals. He seemed at war with his own thoughts.

speaker: Eivor
en: This letter is addressed to Charles, and tells on the attack of Melun. It was to be sent this night to a brothel in the tavern. The king must be there now!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is a strange symbol. It must have some meaning.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tavernkeep! I'm looking for some... company.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: Northerner! A strapping youth like you has appetites of equal measure I'm sure, and any other time I'd be happy to help.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why not now?

speaker: French Woman 1
en: It's locked off. A special visitor, you understand. You'll have to try your luck with the amateurs here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is any visitor really so important that you would refuse honest custom?

speaker: French Woman 1
en: That's a reasonable question, one which I can't answer for the sake of my head. Which is an answer of sorts, if you think on it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would really like to change your mind.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: If your... need is that great, you can try talking to the door guard. He's at the bottom of the stairs.

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps silver will help?

speaker: French Woman 1
en: You know, it just might. You're not going to get in the front door, but as with most things in Paris, there's another way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go on.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: That big tree outside the front door might be worth your attention. You didn't hear anything from me, though.

speaker: Eivor
en: My thanks.

speaker: Eivor
en: That door is reinforced.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Who are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Bishop Engelwin sent me with word for the king.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Did he now? And did he happen to send you with the watchword?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have an urgent message for the king. If he does not receive it, I will be sure to tell the bishop why, and who.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: You are one of his Northern spies, I suppose. I heard there was trouble. Alright, stand back.

speaker: Eivor
en: I only want to visit your establishment, and see if Frankish women are as beguiling as I have been told.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Keep your pants on, Northerner. I told you, no one gets in tonight without the watchword.

speaker: Eivor
en: The bishop gave no watchword, there was no time.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: You think I'm stupid as a pig's ass, don't you? Get lost. Next time, I'll break your head for you!

speaker: Eivor
en: There must be another way inside.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: I told you to leave!

speaker: Eivor
en: A hidden entrance. Where does it lead?

speaker: Eivor
en: Now to find the king.

speaker: Charles
en: Yes, my holy queen. You are sinner and saint. My confessor and my lover. How I admire and desire you.

speaker: Charles
en: Are you real? What are you, another diable (devil)?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not an enemy, not yet. I am Eivor, of the Raven Clan in England.

speaker: Charles
en: Flesh and blood. A Northerner by the look of you. Why do you disturb me? Where are my guards?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your guards are not coming. Your bishop will not be joining us either.

speaker: Charles
en: Engelwin? You've done me a favor, Northerner, though you don't know it. That bishop was an unholy annoyance. What is it you want?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your soldiers strike at Norse villages. Their attacks grow more common by the day. You make war against us, without cause.

speaker: Charles
en: Without cause! This is my land, a kingdom established by God! You are invaders and devils, a scourge I am called to cleanse. My cause is God himself!

speaker: Eivor
en: Francia may be your land, but England is not.

speaker: Charles
en: Ah, the real reason for your intrusion, diable (devil). You are not concerned with war or justice. You want me to spare your people.

speaker: Eivor
en: I want to prevent your armies marching on my land.

speaker: Eivor
en: You claim your cause in the name of your god. We claim it by our own strength. Either way, those claims end in this land.

speaker: Charles
en: I begin to understand you, diable (devil). You don't care for Francia. You want clemency for England and for yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: I want you to stay in your own land.

speaker: Eivor
en: War is uncertain, and dangerous. Often it begins in one place, only to end unfavorably in another.

speaker: Charles
en: War is war. But you mean England. O yes, I understand you, diable (devil). You came to plead for your own neck.

speaker: Eivor
en: I came to make an agreement to save many necks, perhaps even your own.

speaker: Charles
en: You murder your way into another land, and you think to stop me driving you back out with negotiation? I am a king. You are a godless invader. Who are you to parley with me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am one who might have killed you already, yet you live.

speaker: Charles
en: Perhaps this is opportune. What do you think? Could it work? It might work. There is something I require. If you accomplish it, I will be more open to consider your... proposal.

speaker: Eivor
en: A deal within a deal. How like a king. What is the task?

speaker: Charles
en: My queen, Richardis, has been taken. I want her returned to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I assume I must first find her.

speaker: Charles
en: My spies tell me she was taken by those belonging to a zealous faction within the Church. I know nothing more.

speaker: Eivor
en: You do not seem overly troubled by her absence.

speaker: Charles
en: Marriage for kings is more often a matter of politics than of the heart. In any case, I doubt she is in danger. And you can be certain I want her safe return.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I do this, you will agree to leave England in peace.

speaker: Charles
en: Peace! That is a strange word in the mouth of an invader. But again you presume too much. Do this and you will have earned a place at the negotiation table, nothing more.

speaker: Eivor
en: When we next meet, it will be with your queen to discuss your ambitions for England.

speaker: Charles
en: As you say, diable (devil). God will make it so. Now, you must excuse me...

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: It is not right. They dishonored our brothers.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Sigfred will make sure the Franks answer for it.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Wolf-Kissed. You were gone overlong. We'd had trouble.

speaker: Eivor
en: Engelwin is dead, though there is a sickness in these Franks I do not understand.

speaker: Sigfred
en: That is very good. It is as I told you. You see now why it is pointless to try to deal with them?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yet I must. Information with him led me to their king. Charles and I have reached the beginnings of an agreement.

speaker: Sigfred
en: You met with their king! Do you make yourself my enemy now? Toka failed to bring me any but you, and now you defy me!

speaker: Eivor
en: I had to act or miss the opportunity. I did not mean to defy you.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Yet you have, and while you did we were attacked and took losses you might have helped prevent.

speaker: Eivor
en: I told you what I came here to do. You're not my jarl, Sigfred. I do not need your permission to act.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Be careful how you speak, Wolf-Kissed. This is my clan. While you were away making agreements, we were attacked.

speaker: Eivor
en: You said there was trouble.

speaker: Sigfred
en: There was another attack, and we found our missing watch. Curse those raven-starvers. I will gut every one of them! You might have helped prevent this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why? What has happened?

speaker: Sigfred
en: You will see what it is you are eager to make peace with. Toka will show you. I have our revenge to plan.

speaker: Toka
en: Come with me, Wolf-Kissed. You remember our missing watch? While you and Sigfred went after Engelwin, I searched for them. But they were gone. After this second attack, we found them.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you mean? Where were they?

speaker: Toka
en: Come and see.

speaker: Eivor
en: These wounds were not made by sword, or by animals.

speaker: Toka
en: It is the Franks. You said yourself, there is a sickness in them. There is no honor in what they do. These were my friends!

speaker: Pierre
en: I have seen this before. People disappear sometimes. When they return, they are like this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Toka, I need your help. Charles asked me to find his queen. If I can, I might stop this sickness reaching England.

speaker: Pierre
en: The queen was at Evreux yesterday, in the company of priests. You will find her there.

speaker: Pierre
en: You think all I do is drink wine and bed handsome men and beautiful women? Merde! (Shit!) I have eyes all over Francia, and they see many things. Some of those things I must attend to, now.

speaker: Pierre
en: When you have the time, Eivor, come and see me. I have more work for you.

speaker: Pierre
en: When you have the time, Eivor, come and see me. I have a proposal for you.

speaker: Toka
en: Sigfred is right, Wolf-Kissed. Even with this proof of the Franks' cowardice before you, you still want to bargain with them. I will not go against my uncle. I am sorry. I cannot help you in this.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're right. Your duty is to your own clan, Toka. My duty is to mine. It is why I came to Francia. I will go to Evreux alone.

speaker: Toka
en: When you are done in Evreux, meet us at our forward camp, west of Paris. We have a siege to prepare.

speaker: Eivor
en: To keep Charles' armies from England, I must find his queen. She was seen with priests at Evreux. That is where I must go.

speaker: Havi
en: I should return to the shelter. Perhaps the dwarves there can aid me in finding a Jotun worthy of the Salakar.

speaker: Havi
en: I wonder which of these dwarves can help me find a suitable Jotun? Perhaps if I listen to their chatter, some font of wisdom will reveal itself.

speaker: Brammer
en: Come to humiliate us some more?

speaker: Havi
en: Help me, and I'll compose you a saga so exalted it will endure Ragnarök itself.

speaker: Havi
en: But first... I need a name and a place.

speaker: Brammer
en: For what?

speaker: Havi
en: For whom. The mightiest Jotun in all of Svartalfheim.

speaker: Brammer
en: We know the one. Right hand of Suttungr... Malvigr.

speaker: Lom
en: Here because of us.

speaker: Havi
en: She is... worthwhile.

speaker: Lom
en: Gave your son Vidar quite the beating once, didn't she?

speaker: Havi
en: One day, Vidar will make me proud. But why would Malvigr care about you two?

speaker: Brammer
en: Brammer' and 'Lom' aren't our real names. Allow me to introduce... Fjalar and Galar.

speaker: Brammer
en: The ones who 'killed' Suttungr's father?

speaker: Havi
en: I heard something about him trying to out-drink a couple of dwarves? And after, befuddled, tripping and breaking his neck?

speaker: Brammer
en: Suttungr wasn't happy. Held us responsible. But luckily we'd acquired some mead, some special mead, and well, Suttungr is partial to a bit of mead. We bartered it in exchange for our lives. Except afterwards, some thieving twat went and stole it!

speaker: Havi
en: Loki, most likely. It's always Loki.

speaker: Brammer
en: Whoever it was, Suttungr didn't catch them. So he decided to take it out on us instead. Sent Malvigr to hunt us down. Been incognito ever since. Can't trust this lot not to sell us out.

speaker: Lom
en: Still, she hasn't found us yet.

speaker: Brammer
en: She will. Malvigr's dangerous prey. Even for you... But we can help balance the scales. Our old house north of here. Sunk in a lake. Inside, upstairs on a table, you'll find a cup of great potency.

speaker: Lom
en: Cup?

speaker: Brammer
en: You know. The cup?

speaker: Lom
en: Oh yes. The cup.

speaker: Brammer
en: Has the power to do wonderful stuff. For instance

speaker: Havi
en: So, I bring you the cup. And then?

speaker: Brammer
en: We show you how to use it against Malvigr.

speaker: Havi
en: It's a deal.

speaker: Brammer
en: Face it, Lom, no one wants to hear our saga.

speaker: Lom
en: What? But we're Giant-killers!

speaker: Brammer
en: Shh, keep it down. You know we can't sing of that. Not even here.

speaker: Lom
en: Why not?

speaker: Brammer
en: We've got a price on our heads, remember?

speaker: Lom
en: Well, I'm getting tired of all this pretending.

speaker: Brammer
en: You won't be so brave if you-know-who finds us. She'll rip our lungs out through our arses. No, no... best let our die if it means we get to live a little bit longer.

speaker: Brammer
en: Remember, the house is in a lake. It's not all sunk, mind, but you're gonna have to swim to enter through the front door.

speaker: Havi
en: This is the place. The old home of Brammer and Lom. Or whatever they're called. I should find a way inside. Looks like I'll be getting my toes wet.

speaker: Havi
en: This wondrous cup of theirs, it should be on the table over there.

speaker: Havi
en: Nothing... Perhaps someone has already been here and stolen it. Assuming there was a cup in the first place...

speaker: Jotun Warrior 1
en: High One'? More like 'Feeble One'! Malvigr has trained us well! You have no hope! Might as well give up, you one-eyed fart!

speaker: Jotun Warrior 2
en: It was the dwarves! They sent us a fast raven telling us you'd be here! They say you are the most merciful of all the Æsir.

speaker: Jotun Warrior 2
en: It's best to leave one of your enemies alive, so they can tell of your greatness!

speaker: Havi
en: Everyone knows of my greatness.

speaker: Jotun Warrior 2
en: Perhaps there are one or two who have not yet heard?

speaker: Havi
en: Just tell me where Malvigr is.

speaker: Jotun Warrior 2
en: What... what's in it for me?

speaker: Havi
en: I do not know. But I will tell you this. The longer you make me wait, the worse it will be.

speaker: Jotun Warrior 2
en: Malvigr is at the dam to the west. And now? Will you spare me?

speaker: Havi
en: Until next we meet.

speaker: Jotun Warrior 2
en: There will be no 'next'. You can be sure of that.

speaker: Havi
en: Look me in the eye, and meet your fate as a warrior should.

speaker: Jotun Warrior 2
en: Please... just make it quick.

speaker: Havi
en: I will find Malvigr at the dam west of here. She is a worthy foe... Loki told me how she and Angrboda once came to blows... It did not go well for Angrboda. If the Salakar rejects Malvigr, then it is a false tool and Surtr pins his hopes on a worthless toy.

speaker: Havi
en: These rugged views... they remind me of when I once roved the land with Frigg. The cool night spent together beneath the stars. She enjoyed the solitude as much as I. And the trouble and danger even more. And then came the war with the Vanir. Taking Freya as my bride, it helped end that strife. But it ended many other things too.

speaker: Havi
en: What trickery is this?

speaker: Havi
en: There is the dam. But this tempest... it is... unnatural.

speaker: Havi
en: So, the traitors have been betrayed...

speaker: Malvigr
en: They had hope by serving you up, I would show them mercy. Clearly a misapprehension on their part.

speaker: Havi
en: Yet here I am... served up.

speaker: Malvigr
en: If I were here for you, High One, I would have brought an army. No, Suttungr will have his vengeance. But not here.

speaker: Malvigr
en: I know why you have come.

speaker: Havi
en: ...I have a bone to pick with you. After what you did to my son, Vidar, I must

speaker: Malvigr
en: Vidar put up an honorable fight.

speaker: Havi
en: That is not what I heard.

speaker: Malvigr
en: Do not believe the stories.

speaker: Havi
en: Upon his return, too weak to stand, he squirmed like a worm caught in the sun.

speaker: Malvigr
en: You should have seen me. My acolytes had to carry me home on their backs... No, your boy fought well.

speaker: Havi
en: Is that why you spared his life?

speaker: Malvigr
en: It is... But you aren't here to avenge Vidar's honor. You have come to steal my hugr... and I intend to stop you.

speaker: Havi
en: How do you know this?

speaker: Malvigr
en: Æsir, Jotun... You and Loki are both mad. And Hyrrokin is just as bad. And Thor is so stupid he might as well be mad. You spread chaos wherever you go... yet you are all known quantities to us. Surtr is not. He rarely emerges from Muspelheim, and when he does, he shares little with us. Thus, while here, I have sent my spies to learn what he plans. Beyond wiping out the dwarves like he did the elves of Alfheim.

speaker: Havi
en: What do you know of his plans?

speaker: Malvigr
en: I know that he found a powerful elven relic. And that his minion, Calder, was tasked with finding the hugrs necessary to sustain it. That Calder is now trapped within said relic. And that you would have me join him.

speaker: Havi
en: I must trade the Salakar for my son.

speaker: Malvigr
en: You, the one who almost killed Suttungr for his mead, will hand over a legendary relic, take your son, and leave? Just like that?

speaker: Malvigr
en: Put your mania aside, Havi. Work with me. Together we will foil Surtr's ambitions.

speaker: Havi
en: I cannot take the risk... With each breath, Baldr is a step closer to death.

speaker: Malvigr
en: I was a parent once... but we must look beyond ourselves. For the good of all.

speaker: Havi
en: We have spoken long enough.

speaker: Malvigr
en: So be it.

speaker: Malvigr
en: Come! Inflict a fate worse than death on me. Or die trying.

speaker: Malvigr
en: Vidar tried something similar when he and I fought. I assume he learned it from you.

speaker: Malvigr
en: Nicely done! Impressive footwork. Should I prevail, I must adapt some of these maneuvers for my own use. That was sloppy, Havi! Keep focused! This is a fight to the death, not a lovers' tiff!

speaker: Malvigr
en: You are the greater warrior... but this is not the right result. Do what you came here to do! Get on with it, Blind One! End my misery!

speaker: Malvigr
en: Oh Ymir, true All-Father, my body comes to you, sent by the same imposter who claimed your own. As for my hugr ... do not weep for me.

speaker: Malvigr
en: I do not deserve this.

speaker: Havi
en: No... you do not.

speaker: Havi
en: Malvigr was right... I must find out more about the Salakar. Perhaps Hyrrokin...? But I've seen nothing of her since my arrival in Svartalfheim.

speaker: Havi
en: That leaves Ivaldi... I must seek him out. Where was it? The old workshop ruins in Vangrinn? Yes, that is the place.

speaker: Havi
en: And Ivaldi? Maybe he still lives. In one of the other shelters... I must seek him out.

speaker: Havi
en: Can't get through... What could be on the other side? And what must I find to get me through?

speaker: Havi
en: Baldr will be saved, and his mother avenged.

speaker: Tekla
en: Who could Guthban be? One of us? Eivor! A moment?

speaker: Eivor
en: Tekla, you look like you wrestled a bear. Is something wrong?

speaker: Tekla
en: Gods, Eivor. I was robbed! On the road between here and Lincoln.

speaker: Eivor
en: By who? Did you get a good look at them?

speaker: Tekla
en: They were Saxons, I know that much. A pack of them! Lifted four barrels of my ale and all the coin I had on me! The biggest one pulled me off my horse and stuck his mouth in my ear. Said "Tell Guthban we expected him home soon."

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthban? That's "Battle Bone" in the . Are you sure?

speaker: Tekla
en: That's what he said. It's not someone here, is it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not that I know of.

speaker: Tekla
en: I do not begrudge us taking in orphans, Eivor. But some of these Saxons, we hardly know them. You ought to ask around.

speaker: Eivor
en: A good idea. You take care of yourself, let me see to this.

speaker: Tekla
en: Thank you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rowan.

speaker: Rowan
en: Ah! Eivor. How's the day, my friend?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am well, Rowan. I had only a small question. Do you know anyone named Guthban?

speaker: Rowan
en: Guthban? Hm. Nothing comes to mind. Should I?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not a question of should.

speaker: Rowan
en: Ah. Is it a horse?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, it's

speaker: Rowan
en: A lover?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, Rowan. It's... it's no one.

speaker: Rowan
en: You came here to ask me about no one?

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you for your time.

speaker: Eivor
en: Octavian.

speaker: Octavian
en: Ah! Salve, Eivor. How are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, thank you. A question. Does the name Guthban mean anything to you?

speaker: Octavian
en: Guthban. Hmm. It's not Latin, is it?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a name, I think. But no face comes to mind. I fear it may be a moniker. A false name.

speaker: Octavian
en: So you came to me? Why would you come to me about a false name? Do you think my name is false?

speaker: Eivor
en: No. Is it?

speaker: Octavian
en: I am Octavian, I have always been Octavian. Now please, Eivor, this is not a good time for me. I am terribly busy. Good day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tarben. Do you have a second? I was wondering if

speaker: Tarben
en: I am Guthban, Eivor. It means Battle-Bone. Not the name of a cheery baker, is it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not one who bakes bread, no. So how did you earn this name?

speaker: Tarben
en: Before I came here, I lived another life. A brutal, bloody life. I served with a gang of mercernaries. I was their weapon, roaming the wilds of England. Did whatever they asked of me. And all they asked was violence. When I left, I laid this sword on the grass and made a vow. I swore never to spill another drop of blood. To abandon acts of violence. To never kill again.

speaker: Eivor
en: A hard promise for a hard man.

speaker: Tarben
en: It wasn't. Not for me. This life here is all I've ever wanted. I've never been more at peace. This is my doing. I brought all this upon you. It is down to me to fix it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tarben. By threatening you, they threaten my clan. I cannot allow that.

speaker: Tarben
en: These men are foul, Eivor. You should not have to fight my battles for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you not hear me, Tarben? If they threaten you, they threaten me. So let us face them. Together.

speaker: Tarben
en: Very well. Meet me outside when you're ready. I believe I know where they will be.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you wish to face your old friends, I am ready when you are.

speaker: Tarben
en: Good. I'll lead the way.

speaker: Tarben
en: I want you to know... should it comes to blows with my old crew, I can handle it myself. Forgiving me is all the work you need to do.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is nothing to forgive. You walked away. They pursued. By axe or by fist, I will do what must be done to protect my clan.

speaker: Tarben
en: You are living the life you want, aren't you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Before we're spotted, tell me what I should expect here. Will they attack us on sight?

speaker: Tarben
en: I shouldn't think so, no. Nothing like that. It's not how Wilf operates. Yes, he's a clever one, and rather kind when you meet him. Makes you feel like you're a friend. Family, even. I met him a decade ago and he was the first person to truly welcome me. To see some value in me. He told me I had a gift. For intimidation, persuasion... violence. Just by the size and strength of me, he knew how to use me.

speaker: Eivor
en: So what do they want from you now?

speaker: Tarben
en: They'll want me back. They'll want me to be the man they think I am. Monstrous and massive. Wilf and them were the only family I had then. But their love was... conditional. Wilf only loves what he owns.

speaker: Eivor
en: So what do you intend?

speaker: Tarben
en: I know I won't go back. I don't want more blood on my hands. But apart from that, it's hard to say. Who knows what they have in mind?

speaker: Eivor
en: We're stopping...

speaker: Tarben
en: That house there. They're likely within. It won't look like much, Eivor. But don't be fooled. And don't take Wilf lightly, charming as he seems. The man is a serpent.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've met plenty of charmers who turned out to be snakes.

speaker: Tarben
en: I know, I know. Only a warning. Let's go inside.

speaker: Wilf
en: Guthban, my boy! As I live and breathe, you got my message! And you've brought a friend. Who might you be, Dane? His new leash?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor. And the woman you robbed was one of my clan. That will not stand.

speaker: Wilf
en: I know, I know. I'm busted up about it. But tell... Tekla, was it? Tell her that her ale is some of the finest we've tasted.

speaker: Tarben
en: I am done with you, Wilf.

speaker: Wilf
en: But we are not done with you, boy. We gave you food, shelter, ale to drink, riches galore. We made you who you are.

speaker: Eivor
en: For all you did for him, he repaid you with blood and sweat, did he not?

speaker: Wilf
en: You're a fiery one, I like that. But the ink was dried on this deal well before your number arrived in England. If you wish to clear Tarben's name, I'm happy to help with that. It's only a small matter of cost... Some weeks back, soldiers confiscated my personal wares, shall we say. Tried to confiscate me as well, but I gave them the slip. If you're keen, you could recover my belongings and return them to me. Do that, and your name is clear.

speaker: Tarben
en: I... I can't. I promised myself I would leave all this behind, but...

speaker: Eivor
en: If it will clear Tarben's name, we will recover what is yours. Where are these soldiers?

speaker: Wilf
en: Camped not far to the west. A battalion of bloated, brainwashed military men. You can't miss it for the smell.

speaker: Tarben
en: Wait here then. We will return before you sprout another pair of horns.

speaker: Wilf
en: God go with you, Eivor.

speaker: Tarben
en: Eivor, this isn't your fight. You don't need to do this.

speaker: Eivor
en: But I am. Now listen. When we reach the camp, leave everything to me. I will find Wilf's goods and bring them to you. If I am spotted, it won't be pretty. Many may die, and I do not want you involved. You must not break your vow.

speaker: Tarben
en: No vow stands above my duty to my friends, Eivor. I could not leave you alone with them should they attack.

speaker: Eivor
en: If it comes to that. Stand aside until then.

speaker: Tarben
en: I will. You have my word.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. Wait here... and stay out of sight.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is everything. I'll return to Tarben.

speaker: Tarben
en: You found it!

speaker: Eivor
en: I did. Let's bring this back to Wilf.

speaker: Tarben
en: You handled that better than I would have.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this the sort of work you often did with Wilf and your family of marauders?

speaker: Tarben
en: A quick robbery like this? That was the least of our work. We stole from the poor, killed the helpless, cheated the dimwitted. We were lower than slugs. I shudder to remember our best days, and I weep for our worst.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let it go then. Remember only what makes you a better man.

speaker: Wilf
en: O ho! They have returned!

speaker: Eivor
en: We have your goods.

speaker: Wilf
en: Beautiful! Beautiful, put them there.

speaker: Tarben
en: The ledger...

speaker: Wilf
en: Of course. Happy to honor it, my goodness! Such a lack of trust these days. It's a dark age, no mistake.

speaker: Tarben
en: That's it then. We're done?

speaker: Wilf
en: Aye. You are free to walk from this place and live as Tarben the Boring Bread Maker for the rest of your days.

speaker: Wilf
en: But you, Eivor. If you ever get tired of the settled life... we could always use a thief with your skills. Think about it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tarben... are you satisfied?

speaker: Tarben
en: Yes, I cannot thank you enough, Eivor. I feared the worst when I heard my old moniker, Guthban. Hadn't heard it in years. Dredges up fearful memories.

speaker: Eivor
en: I imagine. How did you fall in with that bunch?

speaker: Tarben
en: After my mother died, I sought family. Wilf offered it. He looked at me, took me in, and told me who I was. Who I could be. I don't crave that belonging anymore. Among you lot, people accept me as I am. The greatest gift I ever got. Peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: Many men are calm because they have never known a storm. You weathered the storm and worked through it. That is a rare thing.

speaker: Tarben
en: That means a lot. Thank you.

speaker: Tarben
en: You think Tekla will be upset with me when learns why she was robbed?

speaker: Eivor
en: She's a kind enough woman. And she has faced greater danger than a few thieves.

speaker: Tarben
en: I suppose you don't build a clan of warriors without seeing your share of danger.

speaker: Tarben
en: You caught my attention, you know. The moment I first saw you, I knew there was something special about you. You have an empathy. I see it in your eyes, having witnessed its absence in so many. You see a problem and you solve it. For you know it is better to see it done than to let it fester.

speaker: Eivor
en: The curse of leadership, I suppose.

speaker: Tarben
en: A calling can feel like a curse, but you wear yours well.

speaker: Tarben
en: Ah, it's good to be home again... that is, if I haven't robbed myself of the pleasure of calling it home.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tarben, in spite of all, you are welcome here. And you owe us nothing but the work you love.

speaker: Tarben
en: Right. Payment in fresh loaves of bread. I can manage that.

speaker: Eivor
en: But first, one scrap of your past remains.

speaker: Tarben
en: Right. The ledger.

speaker: Eivor
en: Toss it. And purge the past.

speaker: Tarben
en: With pleasure.

speaker: Rowan
en: Push me any further, Holger, and I will make you eat that wretched hat of yours!

speaker: Holger
en: Do you not know fine millinery when you see it, Rowan? I could trade that hat for two of your horses.

speaker: Randvi
en: Silence, both of you!

speaker: Rowan
en: Randvi, I demand that this matter be settled here and now.

speaker: Randvi
en: Have patience, Rowan. There is a time and place for such disputes.

speaker: Holger
en: Rowan, please. This is pointless and absurd. If you were able to see what I have done with the perfect

speaker: Rowan
en: Randvi, I beg you. Silence this fool.

speaker: Randvi
en: Please, just wait. Until Eivor comes, we cannot settle this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rowan, Holger. Why all this shouting?

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor, thank Tyr.

speaker: Eivor
en: I heard shouting. Is something wrong?

speaker: Rowan
en: Holger robbed me! And I demand he be punished!

speaker: Holger
en: Ah! Robbed is a pointed word. Does the deer rob the stream when she takes a drink? Does a cow rob a field as it crops on sweet grass.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor , this matter require sensitive judgement. Will you...?

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course. From the beginning, please

speaker: Dag
en: Well, now! There is no excuse too small, I see ... nothing to keep you from coveting that seat, is there?

speaker: Eivor
en: In Sigurd's absence, who has better claim to oversee these disputes?

speaker: Dag
en: You might leave them to work it out for themselves. But that would mean ... letting go, would it not?

speaker: Eivor
en: Please start again. Tell me all that has happened.

speaker: Holger
en: I will start. I have been falsely accused by this Saxon philistine!

speaker: Rowan
en: A filly what? Are you mocking me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Silence, please. I will hear both of your complaints and render a decision, awarding compensation if needed. Understood?

speaker: Eivor
en: Rowan, tell me your version of these events.

speaker: Rowan
en: Huh. As you are aware, Holger and I are neighbors. Near enough that I often catch him at my stables, stealing my tools.

speaker: Holger
en: Borrowing!

speaker: Eivor
en: Holger, let him speak.

speaker: Rowan
en: Stealing, borrowing ... my point being, I have always allowed him to use whatever he pleased. I greatly admire your Norse generosity and had hoped to match it. But this morning, Holger stretched the limits of my grace. Entering my stables for their feed, I found my most beautiful, gentle mare stripped of her tail! Bereft! Not a strand in sight! I am ashamed to say my natural suspicion drew me to Holger. And how right I was! For when I peered across the lane, there he was, gripping a horsetail brush slathered with indigo, dragging it across a sheet of

speaker: Holger
en: Painting, Rowan! I was painting! You make it sound so crude.

speaker: Rowan
en: You see? Such willful arrogance! It will take ages for Aelfgifu's tail to reach its former length. I demand compensation!

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. Thank you, Rowan.

speaker: Eivor
en: Holger. Let me hear your side.

speaker: Holger
en: Eivor, you have known me as a skald for years. You have seen how my poems bring life and joy and wisdom to our people. And you know that my work requires a certain, let us say, freedom ... to make use of rare resources to compose my verses. Often, when lacking the proper tools, I have made use of novel items. Alvis's walking stick. Tove's inks. All were given gladly.

speaker: Rowan
en: You cut off my horse's tail to make a brush, you bleedin'

speaker: Eivor
en: Rowan.

speaker: Holger
en: As I was saying, this morning, in the throes of a poetic reverie, I realized that my latest piece required delicate brushwork. I could have used a frayed stick, some cloth, my hands, but no ... I needed something gentler, softer. To make a perfect brush, I needed the fine hairs of a well-raised horse. And so I availed myself of a local resource..

speaker: Rowan
en: You clipped Aelfgifu's tail to the rump! Without asking!

speaker: Holger
en: It was early, I did not wish to wake you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Holger. I believe I understand your position.

speaker: Eivor
en: I believe I have heard enough. If you will

speaker: Rowan
en: My horse looks like a fool, Eivor! No handsomer than a donkey now. You must do something.

speaker: Holger
en: Do not conflate hair with beauty, Rowan. She remains radiant. Aelfgifu's hair will grow back in no time.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quiet, both of you. Now listen...

speaker: Eivor
en: Rowan. However daft his approach, Holger meant you no harm and lost you no coin. The horse's hair will grow back.

speaker: Rowan
en: But

speaker: Eivor
en: And you, Holger ... your habit of borrowing without asking ends today. Apologize to Rowan and greet as friends.

speaker: Rowan
en: This had best be a very good apology.

speaker: Holger
en: It will be! Ahem— To you, O man of horses, I do offer my utmost apologies. And to Aelfgifu, most elegant of mares, I dedicate my finished work. You are, respectively, a king of men and a queen of horses, and I exalt you. I... am... sorry.

speaker: Rowan
en: Hmff.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rowan, does this satisfy you?

speaker: Rowan
en: As much as it can. I accept the apology.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Then by Tyr's blessing, let this matter rest. We are done here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Return to your homes in peace.

speaker: Holger
en: I will return your tools and offer you one of my paintings as a sign of good will.

speaker: Rowan
en: Hmph. Unless your paintings can regrow horse tails, I have no use for them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Holger. Rowan is clearly in the right. You sheared the tail from his horse without gaining permission.

speaker: Holger
en: I borrowed the tail! Borrowed! Does the reality of regrowth not make this a victimless crime?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a two-victim crime, Holger. Though they are unharmed, you took without asking and that will not do. As the horse's value has diminished significantly, you will pay Rowan its market price.

speaker: Holger
en: But the horse was not for sale! Rowan, admit it!

speaker: Eivor
en: My decision is final, Holger. Pay what you owe and meet tomorrow as friends.

speaker: Holger
en: And if I do, may I keep the horse?

speaker: Eivor
en: Pay the man and be done with it. Rowan, does this satisfy you?

speaker: Rowan
en: It does. Thank you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Then by Tyr's blessing, let this matter rest. We are done here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Return to your homes in peace.

speaker: Holger
en: Would you allow me to pay you with a vibrant painting? After all, in some ways, you helped in its creation.

speaker: Rowan
en: Absolutely not. Silver is the only color I wish to see from you.

speaker: Randvi
en: That Holger, he is quite a character.

speaker: Eivor
en: I almost envy him. To see the world through such a muddy glass and live with such petty concerns. He hasn't a care in the world.

speaker: Randvi
en: Let's not walk too far with that idea. I need you right where you are.

speaker: Mildberg
en: They call me Mildberg the Miracle Legs! Come on! Someone must be brave enough to challenge me? Many have tried, none have beaten me. For God kissed my feet when I was a babe and made me swifter than a swallow. Who dares to challenge the great Mildberg, given fleety-feet by God himself?

speaker: Eivor
en: You are pretty cocksure for a child.

speaker: Mildberg
en: You would be, too, if you had miracle legs.

speaker: Eivor
en: Miracle legs? They seem pretty normal to me, girl.

speaker: Mildberg
en: Looks can be deceiving. Have you heard of the great Pheidippides? The mighty hero of old? Ran all the way from Marathon to tell the king they won the battle. Then guess what happened? He only fell down dead!

speaker: Eivor
en: Dead? From running?

speaker: Mildberg
en: It was very far. Girls can't fight, it's the rules. But like Pheidippides, I am going to be the fastest messenger who ever lived.

speaker: Eivor
en: So when the Norse defeat the Saxon armies, you'll quickly bear the bad news to your king?

speaker: Mildberg
en: Them sissy-britches? Fat chance. So, do you want to race or not? I've beaten everyone else in the whole world.

speaker: Eivor
en: In that case... let's run!

speaker: Mildberg
en: Ah! Great Pheidippides, give me speed!

speaker: Eivor
en: You are fast, I grant you. But you will not outrun me! Let's see these miracle legs of yours!

speaker: Mildberg
en: Hey! God gives cheaters boils on their bums.

speaker: Eivor
en: No other Saxon has been able to keep me on my toes like you, little one.

speaker: Mildberg
en: I never thought I would be beaten. But you run like the wind! I am glad I had a real challenge.

speaker: Eivor
en: And I am glad to have given you one.

speaker: Mildberg
en: Do you like interesting places? I've run all over Wessex. Found some scary, spooky, magic spots!

speaker: Eivor
en: Exploring such is what I live for.

speaker: Mildberg
en: I'll give you my diary. I call it, The Many Wondrous Runnings of the Galloping Miracle Legs. Bye-bye!

speaker: Audumbla
en: Moo. (I am sad.) Moo. (I am hungry.) Moo. (It has been so long.)

speaker: Havi
en: Audumbla, who shut you up in here? You should be free.

speaker: Audumbla
en: Moo. (O, how nice.) Moo. (What a relief.)

speaker: Havi
en: Nothing less than a god could confine this ancient creature against her will. Was it the Trickster? Some other menace? Or do I imagine ill omens where none exist?

speaker: Audumbla
en: Moo. (I feel you.) Moo. (You are near.) Moo. (I will find you.)

speaker: Audumbla
en: Moo. (I have found you.) Moo. (Thank you and good luck, godling.)

speaker: Havi
en: It was simple thirst that drove this primeval creature. Even the gods are subject to common needs.

speaker: Havi
en: Slake your thirst, Man-Maker. May you bring forth new things to amaze us all.

speaker: Blind Man
en: O, gods. Where is that fucking spring? This is impossible! Which way? Curse it! Curse it! Curse it! Curse the day I was born!

speaker: Eivor
en: Something wrong?

speaker: Blind Man
en: I'm blind, you idiot!

speaker: Eivor
en: I simply had not noticed your blindness.

speaker: Blind Man
en: Open your eyes! How can you miss it?

speaker: Eivor
en: I caution you not to insult me, stranger.

speaker: Blind Man
en: O, right. You're the victim.

speaker: Eivor
en: I spoke to you out of friendly concern.

speaker: Blind Man
en: My life is shit. I'll never find my way to Clee Hill Spring.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why do you seek that spring?

speaker: Blind Man
en: Do you know nothing? The enchanted waters heal people! You just have to show up. But I'll never make it. Unless ... Unless you lead me there. Dear Lord, yes! Walk loudly, friend. I'll follow wherever you go.

speaker: Blind Man
en: Lead me to Clee Hill Spring! My sight will return! I'll see birds and trees! Flowers and clouds!

speaker: Eivor
en: War and squalor as well.

speaker: Blind Man
en: O, thank you so much for pissing on my dreams. Do me a kindness, would you? Shove something in your gruel hole.

speaker: Blind Man
en: Is that the spring I hear? It's nearby! Hurry!

speaker: Eivor
en: We are here. Clee Hill Spring.

speaker: Blind Man
en: What? You expect gratitude? I have stumbled after you over rocks and troughs. Did you slow down? No.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've done what I can.

speaker: Lame Man
en: Dear Lord in Heaven. Give me strength! Ahh... I give up! It is just too far. O, I'll never make it. O, dear Heaven, why have I been afflicted with these legs?

speaker: Eivor
en: Why do you cry out so much?

speaker: Lame Man
en: Ah! Sorry, friend. I questioned the Lord in a moment of weakness. I crawled this far, but it seems I will never get to Clee Hill.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why go there?

speaker: Lame Man
en: Long ago, Saint Milburga's prayers brought forth a miraculous spring bursting forth from the top of that hill. A simple visit cures all ailments! In fact, the spring is the source of this small fall of water right here.

speaker: Lame Man
en: What? Are you going to take me to Clee Hill Spring? O, thank you, stranger! It is a joyous day!

speaker: Lame Man
en: I fervently hope I'm not too heavy. Huh... You seem to be of sturdy build. On to Clee Hill and Saint Milburga's miraculous spring!

speaker: Lame Man
en: Make haste, O stranger! For I am eager to walk again! Once more know the joy of striding across a grassy knoll on a summer's day!

speaker: Lame Man
en: Who are you, stranger? Someone doing penance? A Samaritan? An angel sent from on high?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Norse.

speaker: Lame Man
en: O.

speaker: Lame Man
en: The holy spring! At last. Merely breathing the fresh air blown across its burbling waters will cure me. Thank you, good soul.

speaker: Lame Man
en: Who is that man?

speaker: Blind Man
en: What? Who said that?

speaker: Lame Man
en: I'm right here before you.

speaker: Blind Man
en: Do you mock me? I'm blind!

speaker: Lame Man
en: Ah. Sincere apologies. I did not realize.

speaker: Blind Man
en: I meet nothing but village idiots. Why do you speak from the ground? Stand up and greet me proper.

speaker: Lame Man
en: Alas, my legs are afflicted. I cannot stand.

speaker: Blind Man
en: What good are you? A heap on the ground!

speaker: Eivor
en: I can see that I have done little good. I'll leave you two here to argue.

speaker: Blind Man
en: Good riddance, too!

speaker: Eivor
en: I see a way you can help one another.

speaker: Blind Man
en: Would you please stick a cork in it for two minutes!

speaker: Eivor
en: I've brought you both here. It's your decision what happens next.

speaker: Blind Man
en: Huh! A lot of good bringing us here did!

speaker: Blind Man
en: It's obvious this piddling stream is useless. I'm stuck, blind as a dead dog, with no one to guide me on my way.

speaker: Lame Man
en: I have no one to help me get around. Woe, O woe. Sometimes I almost lose faith.

speaker: Blind Man
en: Wait.

speaker: Lame Man
en: What?

speaker: Blind Man
en: I need someone to lead, and you can see!

speaker: Lame Man
en: And I need someone to carry me!

speaker: Blind Man
en: Together we are as one full man!

speaker: Lame Man
en: Ah! Heaven-sent joy! O! All because of this Dane! Thank you, stranger.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Nornir work a tangled weave.

speaker: Note of Gratitude
en: Whatever spirit or god or sprite that inhabits this spring, I give you thanks. For years, years! I suffered rashes and pustules, pox and outbreaks, bleeding scabs, cracked fingers, and pus flowing from my eyes. But lo! This spring has cured them all. If only the lame fellow I saw crawling this way, or even the unpleasant blind man would come here. Surely a miracle would befall them, too!

speaker: The Blessed Spring
en: Here I fervently give my thanks to the healing stream blessed by our good , she of the miraculous veil. I came in great distress and drank deeply of the muddy waters while praying to the blessed saint. I was overcome by a great trembling, as if my limbs had taken on a separate life! Much to my embarrassment, a violent purgation of my entrails ensued. A miraculous strench arose-- the stench of my sins! I prayed for forgiveness and, lo! The trembling ceased. I have never felt better!

speaker: Havi
en: Jotunheim... I have not set foot in this realm in some time. I must find the witch Angrboda. She knows all that happens here.

speaker: Havi
en: These woods whisper with Jotnar magic. Not everything is as it seems.

speaker: Havi
en: Angrboda's home was right here when last I visited. It may still be.

speaker: Havi
en: Illusions. But any obstacle can be overcome, if looked at the right way. The witch's house. There you are.

speaker: Angrboda
en: You are reckless Hyrrokin. Midgard is no crucible for your experiments.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: No, indeed. It is as a great barn, swollen with vermin, bulging at the gables.

speaker: Angrboda
en: You underestimate the humans. You always did. When the end comes, they will outlive us.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: They are mindless ravagers, who will destroy us and inherit the Nine Realms. I cannot allow that.

speaker: Angrboda
en: They are capable of more than you know, and I will not help you bring about their ruin.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Then you are a fool!

speaker: Angrboda
en: Please, enter. Do not trouble to knock or announce yourself.

speaker: Havi
en: Angrboda. I have traveled far to find you.

speaker: Angrboda
en: And you are brave to darken my door alone. Where is my lover, the dark fox that slinks between my sheets?

speaker: Havi
en: Loki has stayed in Asgard, to help rebuild the damage from a recent attack.

speaker: Angrboda
en: How generous... and entirely unlike him. You used to be much better at lying.

speaker: Havi
en: I am not Loki's keeper. I have come to understand Jotnar magic, your method for moving hugr (mind) from one body to another.

speaker: Havi
en: Our parting was bitter. He has made many enemies among the gods.

speaker: Angrboda
en: My Loki. He's an acquired taste. One that can soon turn sour.

speaker: Havi
en: I am not Loki's keeper. I have come to understand Jotnar magic, your method for moving hugr (mind) from one body to another.

speaker: Havi
en: I am not Loki's keeper. I have come to understand Jotnar magic, your method for moving hugr (mind) from one body to another.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: The Mead. You seek the Mead.

speaker: Angrboda
en: Hyrrokin! You have long outstayed your welcome.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Then I will take my leave. But remember what I said, Angrboda. You will see things my way in time.

speaker: Havi
en: Who was your visitor?

speaker: Angrboda
en: She's powerful, and cruel, and none of your concern.

speaker: Havi
en: The Mead she spoke of. Where can I find it?

speaker: Havi
en: You were discussing the humans in Midgard.

speaker: Angrboda
en: Were we? Why would Jotnar concern ourselves with such lower beings?

speaker: Havi
en: Because you think them hardy and ambitious.

speaker: Angrboda
en: You know much, Far-Seer. But not enough to save you.

speaker: Havi
en: The Mead she spoke of. Where can I find it?

speaker: Havi
en: The Mead she spoke of. Where can I find it?

speaker: Angrboda
en: A slip of the tongue. Forget what you heard.

speaker: Havi
en: Do not play games with me, witch. You would sell any truth for the right price.

speaker: Angrboda
en: If one had the means to pay it. There is a root called hag's claw. It grows at the bottom of a waterfall to the south, at the forest's edge. Bring me three roots from the place where the red moss thrives. Then we will speak of the Mead.

speaker: Havi
en: I will hold you to it.

speaker: Havi
en: The waterfall should be nearby, but I see no sign of it. If I look about, I may yet find a way to see the unseen.

speaker: Havi
en: This land hides its secrets well, but no secret is safe from me.

speaker: Havi
en: Angrboda said to look where the red moss grows. A cavern beneath the lake. This land is savage, but full of marvels.

speaker: Havi
en: Thor's beard! Look at this place! Yggdrasil's great tendrils reach everywhere in this realm.

speaker: Havi
en: That must be the hag's claw Angrboda spoke of.

speaker: Havi
en: A pungent root. There should be more around.

speaker: Havi
en: One more root should do it.

speaker: Havi
en: The air smells strange down here.

speaker: Havi
en: Dank and drear. They say Hel is the same.

speaker: Havi
en: Where are those cursed roots?

speaker: Havi
en: That will be enough for Angrboda. I should find my way out.

speaker: Havi
en: The reek from this root turns my stomach.

speaker: Havi
en: I have done as you asked. Now where is my wisdom?

speaker: Angrboda
en: Give it a moment to brew.

speaker: Angrboda
en: There. An elixir to ready your spirit.

speaker: Havi
en: How will this bring me the Mead?

speaker: Angrboda
en: It will open your mind to the secrets of the world.

speaker: Angrboda
en: While we wait, let us speak of Asgard. How fared your defenses after the last attack?

speaker: Havi
en: We, uh... we have been weakened... by treachery. Without time to rebuild, we... we may not withstand another attack.

speaker: Havi
en: Wait, I... I did not mean to say that. I feel... strange.

speaker: Angrboda
en: Hag's claw has a way of untying the tongue. Now, you have said you want the Mead, but how badly? How much would you sacrifice to be freed of fate's shackles? Would you give your tongue, your hand, your sight?

speaker: Havi
en: I would... I would give all that... and more.

speaker: Loki
en: I would like to see that.

speaker: Havi
en: Loki! What trickery is this?

speaker: Angrboda
en: I have sapped your strength, Havi. And I will take your life if your answers displease me.

speaker: Loki
en: Did you think I would not come for you, after what you did to my son?

speaker: Angrboda
en: Our son. Fenrir. A name I think you have heard before.

speaker: Havi
en: Y-yes. In the final reckoning, the wolf Fenrir will be my doom.

speaker: Loki
en: Now you know, now you can no longer deceive, tell me... what will you do with him?

speaker: Havi
en: I want to kill him! But I cannot. I swore an oath to you, Loki, and I will not break it. I will not take his life.

speaker: Havi
en: Fenrir will be imprisoned until the day of the prophecy, when we will meet upon the . As we are fated to.

speaker: Loki
en: Then we will bind you until that day. As you mean to bind our son.

speaker: Angrboda
en: An eye for an eye.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: I see she let you live. You must have done something right.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Let me help you down from there.

speaker: Havi
en: No! Wait!

speaker: Havi
en: You could have let me down gently.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: That would presume I cared for your comfort.

speaker: Havi
en: Then why release me at all?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: For the same reason you are in Jotunheim. You seek the Mead, and I can help you get it.

speaker: Havi
en: I assume there is a price?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: I want a small sample for myself. The rest is yours. Fair?

speaker: Havi
en: Do I have a choice?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Of course you do not. The Mead is kept by Suttungr and his daughter Gunlodr in the vault at their home in Utgard. The vault is opened only on occasion of a great feast when Suttungr shares the bounty of his cellar.

speaker: Havi
en: And it would be a poor host who did not throw a feast for a distinguished visitor... say, the High One of Asgard.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: You are not as ox-witted as I feared.

speaker: Havi
en: Why do you want the Mead?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: My motives are not your business, as yours are not mine. All you need to do is get it.

speaker: Havi
en: I must bring a mighty gift to Suttungr if I am to earn my welcome.

speaker: Havi
en: I know where the Mead is now. Why should I honor our bargain?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Because you know nothing of how it works. Now stop wasting time.

speaker: Havi
en: I must bring a mighty gift to Suttungr if I am to earn my welcome.

speaker: Havi
en: I must bring a mighty gift to Suttungr if I am to earn my welcome.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: That idiot drunkard Aegir recently lost his cauldron to Suttungr in a wager, but it disappeared on the way to Utgard.

speaker: Havi
en: Suttungr would be grateful indeed if I returned that cauldron to him.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Seek the tree that wears the scars of the world-serpent's scales. The cauldron would have passed by there.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: You might also bring a gift for Gunlodr. There are treasures that would flatter her in Thrym's house by the lake near Utgard.

speaker: Havi
en: I will bear that in mind.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: When you have the Mead, join me at the well of Mimir. There I will show you how to escape your doom at Ragnarok.

speaker: Havi
en: Should I search for the cauldron now or head for Thrym's hall?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, a new letter. Looks like I have a new letter. A message has come.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should talk to Hytham about my next targets. I should talk to Hytham.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should talk to Hytham. I should talk to Hytham about my next targets."

speaker: Eivor
en: Jorvik is now free of The Order's influence.

speaker: Hytham
en: Brilliant as ever, my friend. Thank you. For all you have done.

speaker: Hytham
en: Ah, there is something for you. An odd letter arrived a few days ago. Signed by one calling himself

speaker: Eivor
en: A Poor Fellow-Soldier of Christ?

speaker: Hytham
en: That's right. Someone you know?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not by sight. But this soldier has intimate knowledge of The Order. He is the reason I have found them so easily in the cities.

speaker: Hytham
en: The letter says you must travel to Wincestre, visit God's house, and look for a man in white. Then recite this passage... "When pride cometh, then cometh shame. But with the lowly cometh wisdom."

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. I will speak with Randvi, get a fuller picture of all this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham received a message from Wincestre. From someone calling himself a Poor Fellow-Soldier of Christ.

speaker: Randvi
en: Your hidden ally. Very interesting. More targets I assume.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. So what do you think? Could it be a trap?

speaker: Randvi
en: As a West Saxon stronghold, Wincestre will be a rather unwelcome place for you. But that is nothing you cannot handle. If you go, do not go boldly.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will make my way to Wincestre. The letter asked me to meet a man in white at a house of God. And then recite this phrase. "When pride cometh, then cometh shame. But with the lowly cometh wisdom."

speaker: Randvi
en: A passage from their holy book, I believe. Interesting. Go with care.

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps some pretty flowers will get her to open the door.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, you have lured me in. Explain yourself.

speaker: Lonely Man
en: It's just been a while since anyone passed this way, and I wanted to be sure you would stay and visit.

speaker: Eivor
en: By pretending to be a pretty young maid?

speaker: Lonely Man
en: My mother used to tell me stories, legends of a forgotten king. Of magic swords rising from misty lake waters. There was often a fair maiden. Lonely and locked away. I fell in love with that sweet fantasy. So much more romantic than a pathetic man whiling away the hours until death.

speaker: Eivor
en: A sad shadow-play. So, where is your mother now?

speaker: Lonely Man
en: Dead these last three years and buried under the flowers she loved. I wanted to move on, but I cannot bear to leave her.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your mother would not want you to be so love-starved. Leave this house of grief.

speaker: Lonely Man
en: You are right. She was always so happy, laughing and singing. It would break her heart to see me so forlorn. I will not let sentimentality be the shackles of my soul. I will find work in the village. Even meet a girl and start my own family.

speaker: Eivor
en: And tell them stories of magic, heroes, and fair maidens.

speaker: Lonely Man
en: Thank you, stranger, you have given me a glimpse of a sweeter life. This was hers, take it, for it saddens me to look on.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope you find what you are looking for. Farewell.

speaker: Lonely Man
en: I am glad you stopped by. It brought me some comfort.

speaker: Eivor
en: Many lose loved ones. And they do not bind themselves with grief-shackles. Your mother is at peace.

speaker: Lonely Man
en: And what of my peace? My life here is pallid and dank as a grave-shroud.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your life is your own to live.

speaker: Lonely Man
en: You are right. But now I beg you, leave me to my sorrow.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope you find what you are looking for. Farewell.

speaker: Havi
en: Here is the story of how I bested all three of Sinmara's champions. Next, fate steered me into the path of a mighty Muspel, and battle was joined! As I travelled on, I met a towering giant of flame and stone! Once again, I had shown my prowess, and proved that none can defeat me!

speaker: Havi
en: Let me tell you of a glorious battle I had with the fire giants. As I made my way onward, I saw Muspels lurking ahead of me. I attacked in a battle-fury! As I wiped the blood from my weapon, a group of Muspels took me by surprise! Did my tale please you, Valkyrie? I have more where that came from.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kassandra is certainly... odd. I wonder if I can truly trust her.

speaker: Cursed Skye Civilian 1
en: In my dream, an eagle flew over the island before a plague killed us all.

speaker: Cursed Skye Civilian 2
en: I saw an eagle flying over the island too! But instead of a plague, a flood overtook us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Took you long enough. I was beginning to think all this talk of gods and nightmares might have scared you off.

speaker: Eivor
en: I said I would come. So, great artifact hunter, did you track it down as easily as you said you would?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not quite but after studying this island, I've found our next step. I'll lead you to it, if you're ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: On to this "next step". This shared expedition is starting to feel tedious.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Spoken as if finding an ancient artifact long hidden away was supposed to be simple.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not ready yet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hurry back when you are. I'm not exactly on the Isle of Skye for pleasure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Finally ready to head to our next step? These nightmares aren't going to stop unless we find the artifact.

speaker: Eivor
en: I take it you've been hunting these artifacts for a long time now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. Quite some time.

speaker: Eivor
en: What led you to this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Strangely enough, a vacation gone horribly wrong. Now, it has become a destiny of sorts.

speaker: Eivor
en: What exactly are we going to do with this artifact once we find it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will take far away from this land for safe keeping. To a place where no one can maliciously wield its power.

speaker: Eivor
en: Power? So it's a weapon of some kind?

speaker: Kassandra
en: In the wrong hands, it is. The kind of weapon that should never be used.

speaker: Eivor
en: A weapon that shouldn't be used? That sounds like a sentiment spoken by someone too weak to wield its power.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It might sound strange to you. But trust me—its power is not to be taken lightly. The survival of your world depends on that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is it. Somehow, this stone formation will bring us closer to the artifact. I think it's a riddle of some kind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, of course it is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Since you're clearly an expert at playing with rocks, get to solving it then.

speaker: Eivor
en: I feel something... light and heat.

speaker: Eivor
en: The great, artifact hunter is stumped by a pile of rocks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I—it's not that simple. There's a trick of some kind. Maybe it's a riddle...

speaker: Eivor
en: It is. And I already solved it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's it? There's nothing.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, of course you don't see it. You don't have my... gifted sight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That gift wouldn't run in the family, would it? Who might your parents be?

speaker: Eivor
en: Mind yourself and focus.

speaker: Eivor
en: It looks like the Isle of Skye, but there are several markings on it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Could it? No, it couldn't be... a map?

speaker: Eivor
en: I didn't feel the need to state the obvious.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So? What are the markings?

speaker: Eivor
en: There are several triangles. And one "X" not too far from here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are we waiting for? "X" marks the spot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So do you just spend your days attacking strange women in graveyards or do you have other duties?

speaker: Eivor
en: I take care of my people. We have a settlement, Ravensthorpe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be nice. I've travelled alone for what feels like a lifetime now.

speaker: Eivor
en: You speak as if... How old are you, exactly?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Older than you'd think. But everyone tells me I have a young face.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a very pretty bird flying above you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Her name is Sýnin.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I had a bird once. A long time ago. An eagle named Ikaros.

speaker: Eivor
en: I prefer ravens. Eagles are too...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Godly?

speaker: Eivor
en: Gaudy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're quiet. Not thinking of throwing another axe at my head, are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: No. I'm just not compelled to fill silence like you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good! That fight took a lot of me. Not sure I'm ready for a second.

speaker: Eivor
en: You kept me on my toes as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Was that a compliment?

speaker: Eivor
en: There's nothing here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stand right here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can't you trust me? Or at least pretend to so this goes faster?

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you know—?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lots of practice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Another ambush! They must be drawn to the temple!

speaker: Eivor
en: They're very persistent.

speaker: Cursed Skye Civilian 3
en: (The blood of the god in your veins is not meant to walk these lands, mercenary!)

speaker: Eivor
en: Are they... speaking your language?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Little less talking, more fighting!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen this before. We'll need shards—keys—to place on this pedestal. That should open

speaker: Eivor
en: No. We need to talk. Those people that attacked us—were they speaking your language?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I already told you, the artifact has made them go mad.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eivor, when are you going to see that I'm here to help?

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine. We've come this far together. I trust you have good intentions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: And if you say you're not hiding anything, I believe you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You might not be hiding anything...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not!

speaker: Eivor
en: But people here speaking your language is not a coincidence.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, you're lying. I'm sure of it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have I been anything but helpful to you since I got here?

speaker: Eivor
en: In the first ambush, those men seemed to know you. Now, they're speaking your language. You can't take me for such a fool.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a chance that my arrival on the Isle of Skye might... be what activated the artifact's powers. But it's not certain. And even if it's true, that's all the more reason for me to remove it.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, that's all the more reason for you to leave so I can remove it myself. You've done enough. I can't trust you, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have no idea what you'd be dealing with. You need my help.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know what I must do from here. And if those men are after you, it'll be even easier for me to continue by myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eivor, please! The powers of the artifact are unlike anything you've seen!

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing is too powerful for me! Besides, I'm sure I'll make better use of this "weapon" than you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine! I've had enough of you anyway. You're impossible!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're too brash, Eivor. And it will undo you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I still need to find all the shards before I can open the door. Better get going.

speaker: Njord
en: Skadi... O Skadi... Why are you so cold? O, Skadi! I curse the day... you were seized with lust... for my perfect legs... Go back to your f-frigid mountains! The sea is my mistress!

speaker: Havi
en: Njord, your drunken laments ripple through Asgard. What has brought you to this state?

speaker: Njord
en: I have... a beautiful... beach home... in Noatun! The most... perfect place in all Asgard! But is it enough to make Skadi happy? No! She wants us to freeze up in the... f-fucking mountains!

speaker: Havi
en: She is Jotun. You should have known this before you married her.

speaker: Njord
en: She chose me! Can I help it that I have such beautiful feet?

speaker: Havi
en: You cannot keep this up. Your wailing will summon a sea storm.

speaker: Njord
en: I care not. I have mead enough to keep me warm till... till... till Skadi and her clan return to their f-frigid homeland.

speaker: Havi
en: Maybe they will, but not before plundering the vast riches from your beautiful home.

speaker: Njord
en: I had not thought of that! By Ymir's balls, I must return to shore! Bring me a boat! I still have my pride.

speaker: Njord
en: I refuse to swim like a... fish... fisher... fisherman! Bring me a boat!

speaker: Njord
en: Skadi... Skadi... her heart is as cold as her... mountain peaks.

speaker: Havi
en: Having a Jotun for a wife cannot be easy.

speaker: Njord
en: The only time she ever really smiled... was when that... goat... nearly ripped Loki's balls off! I remember thinking ... that one is cruel... and magnificent! But the pleasure was not worth the pain. And now... I have her... whole ... whole cursed clan to deal with.

speaker: Havi
en: I know a rune that will dull the edges of their weapons.

speaker: Njord
en: Only if it will... blunt her tongue.

speaker: Havi
en: I hope you find peace, noble Njord. A bad match can be troublesome, but not worse than having nothing to love.

speaker: Njord
en: My home at Noatun will bring me pleasure enough. But what about you, Wily One? What do you love?

speaker: Havi
en: Knowledge, Sea King, and the pursuit of it. Untangling mysteries, uncovering lore... that is what feeds me.

speaker: Njord
en: Then from what I kn-know of the world and all the... realms... you will never go hungry. Good luck to you.

speaker: Havi
en: Dain, the Lifeless One. Why has this noble stag wandered so far from the tree, Yggdrasil? The sight of this majestic creature gives my own heart wings! I will follow in the same spirit.

speaker: Havi
en: Here is Duneyr the Unknowing! Have you eaten your fill of Yggdrasil's green leaves?

speaker: Havi
en: Durathor as well! Has some disaster befallen the Tree of Life, or is this simply a gathering of the hallowed herd?

speaker: Havi
en: Even Dvalin has roused from his Thriving Slumber! Does this wild run come from a place of joy, or fear?

speaker: Havi
en: And finally, Eikthyrnir. From whose horns flow the rivers, Sid and Vid.

speaker: Havi
en: So this was the purpose behind their prancing. An offering to their caretaker.

speaker: Havi
en: Thank you, noble harts. I will put this gift to good use and remain your steadfast protector.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: I'm too old. Much too heavy! How will I ever get this done? If only Rose was here. She would help me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Having trouble, farmer?

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Rose? Is that you? It is! My daughter, my child! I can scarcely believe it.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are a little confused.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: I've been longing to speak to you again.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have never spoken to you before.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Rose, Rose, do not jest with your father and his failing eyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very well. It is good to see you... again.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Such a pleasure to have you at my side, Rose. But I'm so tired, so very tired. I cannot move those crates to shelter.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Yes, Rose. Right there. You were always very clever, child. Put the others there, as well.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Rose! You've grown up to be quite strong!

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: That's the last of them. Come join me, Rose. It's been ages since we had a chat.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: White roses. Once we named you, they became your mother's favorite flower.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: You and your mother made all our clothes. You were always a danger with a needle.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Remember Fidelis? He would never leave your side.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Rose, you're such a help. Let us reminisce, shall we? The tale of how I courted your mother?

speaker: Eivor
en: Why not?

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: You never tire of that one. Well. As a young man, I was sent to a great lord to help with his livestock. That first day, I brought the cows in from the field and there was this milkmaid, her smile like sunshine in a storm. I fancied her, she fancied me. We found our way to a storeroom to make better acquaintance.

speaker: Eivor
en: And then?

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: What? O, yes. What was I saying? Ah, your mother and I in the storeroom. Yes. Well. The lord wandered in and caught us making merry. He fell into a dark rage and raised his axe, and me wearing nothing but a smile! Your mother had a quick wit, "Why master," she said, "This boy can fetch you more milk than you'd ever have use for." Well, the lord liked his milk, so says he, "Bring me this milk and perhaps I'll show mercy." We threw on our smocks and ran for the cow pen. We milked the cows in a frenzy and carried back two buckets. The lord spooned off some cream to taste. Satisfied, he had his servant set the milk in the shade and declared, "More!" "In a thrice, master," your mother said, and we ran outside. "How will we get more?" I asked. "The cows are spent!"

speaker: Eivor
en: I must know what happened.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Yes? O, "The cows are spent!" Your mother bade me not to be a ninny. She led me in a circle back to the buckets in the shade. "We'll bring him these again and call them new!" So we brought the master the same milk again. Again he was pleased, again he asked for more. And again we circled around! Soon the master had ten buckets... by his count. So he gave us his blessing. We ran for the stables, stole a horse, and never looked back. Not long after, you were born. The pinkest little babe a father could hope for! We named you Rose, after the cow. That reminds me—your mother's ring! She wanted you to have it. Here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you... Father. It will remind me of Mother always.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rose. Your mother wanted you to have this.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Rose! You've returned. Sit with me, I'll tell you a tale from my youth.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: There's the time I caught your mother with the blacksmith. O, my, yes. That's quite a story.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: ... and he never sat down again!

speaker: Eivor
en: I must go... Father. Take care.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Such a delight to see you, Rose. Come back soon!

speaker: Eivor
en: I... I do not know what to say. You should keep it to remember... mother.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Such a sweet girl. I'll bequeath it to you when the time comes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must go... Father. Take care.

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: Such a delight to see you, Rose. Come back soon!

speaker: Elderly Farmer
en: The rosebush we planted by your mother's grave has grown all the way up the old oak tree. You remember, it's just outside there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sleep well, old friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sleep well, old friend.

speaker: French Woman
en: O Newfather, O great one... we look to your guidance from now on, O strongest one.

speaker: French Man
en: No more with the weak god. We are now with the fearsome warrior god!

speaker: French Man
en: Who disturbs our worship?

speaker: French Woman
en: Merde! (Shit!) It's a Northern one! "In the darkest hour when demons come, call on me brother and we will fight!"

speaker: Eivor
en: Pure madness. Maybe they left something to explain their behavior.

speaker: Eivor
en: They lost faith in their God and found fickle solace in a new one.

speaker: Banski
en: "Travel to Svartalfheim," she says. "Paint all the signs to the shelters," she says. Risking my neck every bloody day, more like it... Might've painted a few too many of these, come to think of it...

speaker: Banski
en: Agh! Tried to sneak up on me, ya frosty bastard! Not today, Jotun!

speaker: Banski
en: Haha, Jotun! You can't fool me with your current shapeshifting! Even in your current ugly form!

speaker: Havi
en: Stand your ground! You address no Jotun, you sniveling sack of

speaker: Havi
en: Where did he go...? And how do I get out of here?

speaker: Banksi
en: "Vermin," you Jotnar called us! And so, vermin shall feast upon you! Good riddance, scum!

speaker: Havi
en: I have bested your traps, coward! Now show yourself, or you will make an enemy of Havi, Lord of Asgard!

speaker: Banski
en: Lord of Asgard? Yeah right! And I'm Hreidmar, king of dwarves, freshly resurrected! Try harder, Jotun!

speaker: Banski
en: Hey Jotun! You should lighten up!

speaker: Havi
en: You sneaky little...

speaker: Havi
en: We meet at last.

speaker: Banski
en: What in the... How did... No Jotun has ever outsmarted my trap! Oh. Oh crap. You're really not a Jotun, are you? Which means you're

speaker: Havi
en: The Lord of Asgard, yes. And in no mood for such trickery. Even though I must admit... I admire your cunning. You managed to fool me, if only for a brief moment. Many have tried. Few have succeeded. Even fewer lived to tell the tale. Who are you, dwarf?

speaker: Banski
