en: Banski, they call me. Before the invasion, I was an artist. Some clever clogs reckoned I should paint all the signs to all the dwarf shelters. And that's how I found this empty shelter here. Thought I would use it to get a little payback, y'know, teach some Jotuns a lesson. Admittedly, it's not the most efficient means of revenge. But every journey begins with a single step, eh! Still, never thought I'd catch an Aesir in my trap. Uh, unintentionally, I should point out!

speaker: Havi
en: All you caught was my attention. And perhaps a tiny sliver of my respect.

speaker: Banski
en: Then, if you'll indulge me, what went wrong? What was the failure in the trap?

speaker: Havi
en: You're far from the first trickster I've tangled with. And you have much to learn, to be worthy of the title.

speaker: Banski
en: Everyone's a critic.

speaker: Havi
en: There was no failing, other than your prey was the wisest and most cunning of all beings in the Nine Realms.

speaker: Banski
en: And modest too!

speaker: Havi
en: Another of my attributes.

speaker: Havi
en: You underestimate your enemy. You're telling me Jotnar actually fall for this child-like ruse of yours?

speaker: Banski
en: Literally, yes! You saw the bodies. Can't help themselves. They see a dwarf dive down, and, boop, in they go. Same as you, if you recall.

speaker: Havi
en: Yes, my curiosity got the better of me this day.

speaker: Havi
en: The rats... I'll be happy to never see them again. But you had too few. A pack of wolves would be better. They'd make short work of your prey.

speaker: Banski
en: Ah, yes, a pack of wolves. Very easy for a dwarf to catch and handle. Why didn't I think of that, eh?

speaker: Havi
en: Get one to chase you down here. Every journey begins with a single step.

speaker: Havi
en: I have nothing more to say. But... you should look your prey in the eye. Let them know who has bested them.

speaker: Banski
en: Ah, yes, get within reach of someone, a far bigger someone, with an increasing desire to kill me. What a terrific idea. In any case... I am no warrior. And this shelter here is all I have with which to fight back. All I have are my wits, my anger, and my shelter.

speaker: Havi
en: Then what more do you need? Good hunting, Banski.

speaker: Banski
en: And to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: So quiet here. Is everyone at the longhouse?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd Jarl. Back where you belong. O, I missed you, my brother.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yes, you missed me. Once or twice, I hear.

speaker: Eivor
en: What?

speaker: Sigurd
en: You took your time to find me. Was it for this, to enjoy your time on my throne?

speaker: Eivor
en: I did only what you asked of me.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And you slew all those who questioned you?

speaker: Eivor
en: That is not what happened. Randvi... Randvi will tell you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: O yeah, will she? My dear wife, brought to me as a gift by her clan to pacify my ambition. Yes, I'm sure she will be the one to tell me the truth!

speaker: Eivor
en: What did that witch Fulke do to you?

speaker: Sigurd
en: You cannot begin to imagine the things I have seen. What I've learned.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Born of gods, is who I am. A Lord of War! A Roman Mars! I know who I am, I know my destiny! And you will not hinder me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Forgive me, I am faint. Tired of the day and all that has passed. I need air.

speaker: Randvi
en: He's been this way since his return. Could you speak with him? Settle his mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can try.

speaker: Holger
en: Stand with cheer, one and all. Today is a day of celebration! Our jarl is with us! Tonight, let us drink and eat in honor of his return! And now, I will delight you with a poem in praise of the man, a new composition of my own.

speaker: Gudmund
en: Do you miss your home, Yanli? Are you happy here?

speaker: Gudrun
en: Don't ask her that! Not while Holger is singing.

speaker: Yanli
en: Have I not heard this song before? Or do all Norse songs sound alike?

speaker: Gudrun
en: Please, whatever you learn from us, do not judge our people by the sound of Holger's warbling.

speaker: Yanli
en: He is doing us a service with his singing.

speaker: Gudmund
en: Making us deaf?

speaker: Yanli
en: No, don't you see? As soon as he begins to sound good, that is the moment you know you have had too much to drink!

speaker: Rowan
en: Reda, you are like no child I have ever met.

speaker: Tekla
en: I had the same thought. You speak with such wisdom for a young man. An old soul in a new body.

speaker: Reda
en: Not so new as you might think. I could be your grandfather.

speaker: Petra
en: I've never been much for ale, nor anything that unsteadies my hands, but this is delicious! You are a wonder, Tekla.

speaker: Tarben
en: Hints of honey and flowers. Wonderful.

speaker: Tekla
en: You are too kind, all of you. But I could not have brewed this batch without Tarben's help.

speaker: Tarben
en: O, no. It was nothing, really.

speaker: Petra
en: Look at you! Can't accept a word of praise. Slapping it away like a playful cat.

speaker: Octavian
en: Eck, this fish is off. Has a ripeness I can hardly stomach.

speaker: Merton
en: All right, quit your whining then. Leave it for the rest of us.

speaker: Octavian
en: Ah, I mean no offense! I am simply more accustomed to a Mediterranean diet. Grapes, olives, shellfish and the like.

speaker: Rodolf
en: Right. How is that working out for you in England? Getting your fill of olives?

speaker: Merton
en: Eh. From time to time, yes. My lover Julia sends me some as often as she can.

speaker: Rodolf
en: Right. Your lover from afar.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi. Sigurd has been through so much. Be patient with him.

speaker: Randvi
en: Of course. I cannot imagine. The savagery of that woman, Fulke.

speaker: Eivor
en: For all her wretchedness, she seemed to... to like him. I know that sounds strange.

speaker: Randvi
en: How do you mean?

speaker: Eivor
en: She claimed to know him, to admire him. Said he was a greater man than we could ever know. Yet for all her praise, she tortured him to the brink of madness and death. I do not understand why.

speaker: Randvi
en: In time Sigurd may come around. And if he does, he may be willing to speak.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi...

speaker: Randvi
en: Have you spoken with Sigurd yet?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not yet. Soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim. Will you not join us?

speaker: Basim
en: In time I may celebrate. But tonight has a melancholy mood. I would rather sit here quietly, alone with my thoughts.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand.

speaker: Basim
en: Do not let Sigurd's present mood upset you. He spoke warmly of you as we sailed him. I believe he still trusts you more deeply than he can express.

speaker: Eivor
en: We trust each other.

speaker: Basim
en: That is clear. Enjoy the feast, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where's Sigurd gone?

speaker: Eivor
en: In the cemetery. His mood is dark.

speaker: Eivor
en: There you are, Brother.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you doing here? I was looking for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd...?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Dag died defending my honor?

speaker: Eivor
en: So he claimed.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Then he was a fool. My honor needs no defense. It is stone-solid. Unblemished.

speaker: Eivor
en: I offered him a way out, but

speaker: Sigurd
en: Shhh... Say nothing more of the past. It is gone. There is a rift as deep as death between then... and now.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I was tested, Eivor. In a crucible of blood and fire. And in my agony, I was reborn. You may think me less than I was, but this is not so. I am greater than before. My mind is a wellspring of prophecies. Visions that tell me who I truly am. And for all that, I am grateful for my suffering.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, I want to understand. But all this...all you say makes little sense.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Basim saw these things in me. Fulke too. Despite her cruelty, she spoke the truth. I am more than the man I was, more than this hobbling stick that stands before you. You must look harder, Eivor. Deeper. See for yourself what they found in me. Do you see it? My greater self?

speaker: Eivor
en: I... I don't know what that means.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Look! This is the face of a god!

speaker: Eivor
en: I see only my brother and my truest friend, returned to where he is loved and cherished. Where he is meant to be.'

speaker: Sigurd
en: You are kind, but your eyes are clouded by the past, a place I can no longer see. I fear our paths diverged long ago. Go. I wish to be alone. Return to my feast and drink for me. Celebrate the days to come in my name.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, it seems the wind calls me back to Randvi. Best tell her the good news.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan is not here. Where is he?

speaker: Eivor
en: Moira. Is Halfdan about?

speaker: Moira
en: Eivor, welcome. Halfdan has stepped outside with Faravid. They shouldn't be far.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Go on, steady your balls! And ask her to shake arses with ya!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: B-but I've n-never d-danced with anyone before...

speaker: Faravid
en: Ricsige. I struggle to be surprised.

speaker: Halfdan
en: I was caught off guard, but I shouldn't have been. A fog set in, and I couldn't see the forest before me. Old friend. Long ago, we stormed this sea-of-wagons under winter's blanket... you've stood at my side for many long years.

speaker: Faravid
en: Proudly, brother. Come. Let's share the balm of all torment, the soothing liquid of chaos.

speaker: Eivor
en: The ceremony hastens to start, let's not to keep the crowd waiting.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Eivor. Yes, let us go. To inscribe our names in history.

speaker: Halfan
en: No more pulling strings. This throne and its burdens are mine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Moira. How are things in Wyke?

speaker: Moira
en: I get by. There will always be those who dislike me. But how I handle their ire is up to me... so yes, things are mostly well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enjoying the festivities?

speaker: Hjorr
en: Wolf-Kissed, yes. Happy to be here.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The crowning of a new king, it's not something I've seen this close!

speaker: Eivor
en: Save some mead for the rest of us, Faravid.

speaker: Faravid
en: Ah! I have to thank you, Eivor! For your counsel, for your blade. All this would not be possible but for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mean more to your king than you know. Take this goblet.

speaker: Faravid
en: No, you keep it. Gifting him a goblet from the spoils of war was a ritual between Halfdan and I. This one should be yours.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have a new brother, much like Halfdan. Not by blood, but through the battles we've fought, hand in hand. Through him I have learned that battle bonds run deeper than blades can cut. I will never forget that lesson.

speaker: Faravid
en: The words of a poet. Now let us drown ourselves in mead. For friendship.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Have you had enough fun? My crowning must come soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll save some for later. Let's make a king of you.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's early, Halfdan. We have more barrels to drain and merriment to make.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Of course, of course. Return when you've had your fill.

speaker: Halfdan
en: To Eivor and the Raven Clan of Mercia, our newest ally, in blood and glory!

speaker: Eivor
en: To Halfdan King, I lift my horn and raise my brow to speak this praise... Crown spire, stout oak of Valkyries, spinner of battle wisdom... long may you live and rule. !

speaker: Eivor
en: Moira. What is this metal? It's soft, like Roman pipes.

speaker: Moira
en: Ah! That's lead. A toxic metal.

speaker: Eivor
en: Was it lead that drove the Romans mad? Can metal do this to a man?

speaker: Moira
en: O, God in heaven, yes. The Romans knew this well. And my poor mother, she... she drank from cups like these for so long, she

speaker: Halfdan
en: You! All these years, you gifted me poison! You gifted me madness!

speaker: Faravid
en: Old friend, please. Your sickness has clouded your judgment.

speaker: Halfdan
en: This sickness was no accident. I trusted you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sheath your weapon, Faravid.

speaker: Faravid
en: Eivor, make this man see sense. He is old, sick, and his mind is unclear

speaker: Halfdan
en: Horseshit! You want me dead, you lying shit hog! I was a fool to not see it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan, stop! This is a man of honor.

speaker: Halfdan
en: You stand beside this... this traitor?

speaker: Eivor
en: I do. Let truth guide us here, not madness.

speaker: Halfdan
en: I am Halfdan Ragnarsson, Wolf of War, Lord of Jorvik, ruler of men. I am king!

speaker: Faravid
en: Not my king. I will not bow to a man who accuses me of treason.

speaker: Halfdan
en: In days yet to come, men will sing the praises of Halfdan. And scorn the life of Faravid the betrayer!

speaker: Faravid
en: You are the hero of a coward's tale. A man who hid behind his best men and claimed their victories for his own!

speaker: Halfdan
en: You are banished! Out! Never again set foot in my lands!

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, king. I

speaker: Halfdan
en: No more. Leave me.

speaker: Faravid
en: You are fearfully quiet, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: One should never break a silence without reason.

speaker: Faravid
en: I fear for Northumbria now that Halfdan is king. Many may suffer if his madness goes unchecked.

speaker: Eivor
en: And who is to blame for his madness, Faravid?

speaker: Faravid
en: I should demand an apology for that. But there is no need. Soon I shall be long gone. Far away across the whale-road, where the fates guide me.

speaker: Faravid
en: End of the road. Goodbye, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you know? About the goblets, the lead? Now's the time for truth.

speaker: Faravid
en: I hope one day we may raise our spears together, old friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: We hope for many things in this life, yet we earn so few of them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Treason must never go unpunished.

speaker: Faravid
en: After all we did together, after all we won.

speaker: Eivor
en: If any of my clan committed such a betrayal, I would rip his flesh from his bones.

speaker: Faravid
en: You're not the warrior you used to be, old friend.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Traitor! Kill him! Feed him to the wolves!

speaker: Faravid
en: Look at him, Eivor. Is this how a leader should behave? Halfdan! Come to your senses!

speaker: Faravid
en: The end of our road.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Stand, you treasonous bastard. Stand and fight me!

speaker: Faravid
en: Old friend, do you remember the days we raced our horses across the length of this land? You were always faster, you always won. Because I let you win, my "jarl." So I will let you win one last time. We will meet once more. In the corpse hall.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Argh!

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan. It's time I go.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Hm?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm leaving for Mercia. Going home.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Then go with this. A sign of friendship. A bond between our clans and a symbol of the pain and suffering it took to win the peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope we were right about him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, it seems the wind calls me back to Randvi. Best tell her the good news.

speaker: Norse Man
en: With Hemming Jarl gone, can Vili hold the reins? Will he guide us true?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: You are the Wolf-Kissed one, the Raven of Battle whose fame grows with each waxing of the moon.

speaker: Eivor
en: I struggle with the choice Hemming left for me. I would have your council on the matter.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: A slaughter must be made. Many sheep at the bottom of the Sleeping Jotun, before the pyre is lit. Follow.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Come creatures. You are to serve the gods and bid them welcome our beloved Hemming Jarl with ale and open arms.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you have the gift of foresight, seer? Can you augur what is to come?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: I see what need be seen, when it need be.

speaker: Eivor
en: A great gift.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: A great burden.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did Hemming Jarl consult you often? Did he unburden his woes?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: We spoke often. Yet too often he left with more burdens than he brought.

speaker: Eivor
en: He worried about the future of his clan. About who would be jarl.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Speak less. Lest our words draw foul spirits to dog us.

speaker: Eivor
en: As you wish.

speaker: Eivor
en: Volva, I

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Your heart is restless. Your mind is clouded. You seek more than a guarantee of good omens.

speaker: Eivor
en: I seek the gods' wisdom.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: You wish to know who would best serve this clan as jarl.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do. Between Vili and Trygve there is no clear choice.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: We stand in the shadow of the giant, the great keeper of secrets. Here you'll find a drink of the resounding sea. Ascend the Sleeping Jotun. Consume the waters. And meditate at its peak. Do not seek answers to your questions. They will find you.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is the summit. To seek an answer I should clear my mind and still my heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hemming Jarl? Is it truly you?

speaker: Hemming
en: Of spirit. Not of flesh.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why have you not reached Odin's hall?

speaker: Hemming
en: I will in time. As the flames of my pyre burn, I will ride the path of wood-smoke to the All-Father's hall of champions.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am grateful to see you once more, jarl. I struggle with the task you set before me. To choose your heir is not an easy thing. One man is beloved, but does not want the task. The other man is fit for the task, but is not favored.

speaker: Hemming
en: I could not give you any more counsel in life, Eivor. So too in death am I rendered silent.

speaker: Eivor
en: Forget wise counsel and rational arguments. What does your heart tell you?

speaker: Hemming
en: My heart is stopped. It says nothing.

speaker: Eivor
en: This should not be my decision, Hemming. The choice was always yours to make! You were their chief.

speaker: Hemming
en: As Sigurd is your chief! But that does not quench your appetite for glory, as you covet his place upon the high seat of your clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not seek to replace Sigurd! Fate weaved our futures long ago. We are only following its pattern!

speaker: Hemming
en: Yet you see it coming. You welcome it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shall I renounce my fate, then? Abandon the path to glory I walk?

speaker: Hemming
en: No. I want you to die in defense of it.

speaker: Hemming
en: This is not how I remember you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aaah!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is how I remember you.

speaker: Hemming
en: This is why I fight so well.

speaker: Eivor
en: You left me too soon, Hemming Jarl. Your shire's fate is uncertain.

speaker: Hemming
en: I trusted you to make the right decision. I still do.

speaker: Hemming
en: Your edge is blunted by indecision. You lead warriors now, never waver.

speaker: Eivor
en: You did, Hemming Jarl. You did.

speaker: Hemming
en: And that is why my words should land true. Trust your judgment.

speaker: Eivor
en: You pushed me, Hemming. I never intended this.

speaker: Hemming
en: Have no regrets, Eivor. You have given me the great battle-death I sought in life.

speaker: Eivor
en: You old fox. Was that the point of riling me up?

speaker: Hemming
en: Ah. The All-Father... he comes to welcome me to his wall. And I must follow. The choice you make will be the right one.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Althing (clan gathering) is tomorrow, and a jarl must be chosen. I should speak with Sunniva about this.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: You have seen what was needed?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have. More than enough.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Hold right there, you speedy hare. No entry to you past this point without a password to annoint.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this place?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: A den for those who answer the call of a slick and slippery midnight brawl! To compete, a phrase that must be spoken, but it seems you don't yet have this token. Worry not, young pup, and look around, if memory serves, there's a clue to be found.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand aside and let me in, or I'll have no qualms wiping clean that grin. You'll be less pale, more black and blue, and none shall care for the likes of you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: O God, a poet, just like me. Yes! Yes! Your entry will be free. Now ball your fists and step right in, there's fun to be had and bone broken!

speaker: Eivor
en: Naked fists and walleyed lisps.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Ah! A keen eye and a clever nose, you'll need them both to keep on your toes. Enter, enter, take your shot. But, careful! Don't get beat to snot.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Are you ready?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ready.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Splendid! And now for your opponent... Let's see if you don't take a fall against the one they call The Wall, Edward of Lincoln

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Watching you rub bodies was an absolute treat. You move just like a noodle, my favorite thing to eat. I would please me to no end to watch you fight again. So whenever, now, or then, return promptly to my den.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Ah, back again, hm? Ready for more?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ready.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Splendid! And now for your opponent... There may be shared blood in your veins against this rapid-firing Dane, Bolla of Cent.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Ah, back again, hm? Ready for more?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ready.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Splendid! And now for your opponent... I think it's time your head got stung, for none remain but the silver tongue. One on one, you'll fight with me, champion of the BBB.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I've never been in such a fight, you walloped me with all your might. It seems to me you've proven to be champion of the BBB.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am honored, I think.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Go on now, carry our name, with only pride and never shame! Remember how it was you came to be blessed with so much fame! Farewell!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Not a brawler remains who dares suffer these pains. You are the winner, the victor, you see, champion of the BBB.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: You there! I know you! You're one of us, BBB! Gave us quite the throttling. Fancy bumpin' into you out here.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Ha! If my eyes don't deceive. The BBB misses you dearly, brawler! Keep our spirit alive!

speaker: Randvi
en: I have received a unique summons from Snotinghamscire in the north. From your old friend, Vili.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili! A name I have not heard in ten winters or more. How is he?

speaker: Randvi
en: Well, it seems. Vili asks that you join him in feast and celebration, in honor of his father, Hemming Jarl.

speaker: Eivor
en: A welcome invitation. It'll be good to see him again.

speaker: Randvi
en: It is worth recalling that his father, Hemming Jarl, would be a formidable ally. Will you go?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will leave for Snotinghamscire today.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. They will be pleased.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be Snotingeham. Saxon and Dane live in peace. I expected nothing less for land under Hemming Jarl's rule.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Trygve spoke true. You have come to England.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have. And I mean to stay.

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: You're a long way from Norway, Wolf-Kissed! Vili will be pleased to know it.

speaker: Eivor
en: We have all come a long way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Snotingham... it'll be good to see Vili again.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Pour the mead! Eivor's come to Snotingham!

speaker: Eivor
en: Skal!

speaker: Trygve
en: Make sure the supplies are secured. We may set off at any moment.

speaker: Trygve
en: Do I trust my own eyes? Is that truly who I see?

speaker: Eivor
en: Trygve, you old hound. How are you?

speaker: Trygve
en: Eivor, a friend of old is a good omen.

speaker: Eivor
en: Look at this. Your chin-grass might be mistaken for hedges now.

speaker: Trygve
en: But a healthy jarl-beard it is not.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what of Vili? I was happy to get his message.

speaker: Trygve
en: I stand in Vili's place today. He and his father have gone to Ulkerthorpe to stave off an invasion of Picts. We've laid a long siege, and Hemming Jarl looks to finish the job.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have not fought besides Vili and his father since we were young. They have my blade if they need it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would have come with warriors at my back if I knew Vili was at war.

speaker: Eivor
en: Off looking for a fight. I should have known.

speaker: Trygve
en: Yes, Vili's sword always finds its way into trouble, sooner or later.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not a bad way to live.

speaker: Trygve
en: In spite of these war-cries, you should know that Vili's father is more frail than you last saw him.

speaker: Eivor
en: How could that be? Hemming Jarl is an ox.

speaker: Trygve
en: So he is. And he'll be pleased as Skoll with the moon in his jaws at the sight of you. Come. The swiftest path is by river, but these waters are hostile to Norsemen. You bring good luck with you. We could guide the sail-steeds downstream.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm ready for whatever danger awaits. Prepare your convoy and we'll be off.

speaker: Trygve
en: Our jarl has waited long enough. We follow the Wolf-Kissed to the encampment.

speaker: Trygve
en: Eivor, the Raven Clan's Wolf-Kissed... you'll soon have more names than the All-Father himself.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've traveled far, spilling the dew of slaughter. A reputation is the price of victory.

speaker: Trygve
en: Indeed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ready the sea-beasts. Eivor Wolf-Kissed is here to escort us up river.

speaker: Eivor
en: I remember when Vili and I were small children, you spun many epic yarns for us over the hearth-fire. But I do not remember you telling us how you came to serve Hemming Jarl. Is it a tale worth telling?

speaker: Trygve
en: It is, but a sad one... I suppose I was the age you are now. Skadi had sent us a harsh winter and much of our clan was starving. To feed us, my family incurred a large-work debt. But my youth rendered me too proud to pay it off. I wanted to raid, not toil. For my failure, Hemming Jarl could've taken what he wanted from my family. Including our lives. But his heart is kind. He spared us, and I pledged myself to him. Gladly so. So it has even been.

speaker: Eivor
en: A story of quiet honor. If we had more tales of that kind, the world might be a more forgiving place.

speaker: Eivor
en: Picts ashore! Protect the convoy!

speaker: Eivor
en: That's all of them. But stay on guard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Picts on the ridge! Guard the convoy!

speaker: Trygve
en: Careful, Eivor! These supplies bring fire to the Ulkerthorpe siege.

speaker: Trygve
en: The convoy remains, Wolf-Kissed!

speaker: Eivor
en: Oars, back us around. The convoy is laid bare.

speaker: Trygve
en: The convoy is unscathed. Hemming Jarl will be pleased.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot leave Hemming's convoy unprotected.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have orders to go to Stoneburgh, but our camp is just ahead, so hurry on without me. Vili and Hemming Jarl will be pleased to see you.

speaker: Norse Soldier 1
en: Shred my sheepskin. That there is Eivor the Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Norse Soldier 2
en: Eivor, hail! We have not laid eyes on you for some ten winters now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hail, friend.

speaker: Hemming
en: The Picts cower. Muster the men for battle.

speaker: Hemming
en: Freyja's kiss, you came. Welcome.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your son sent for me, Hemming Jarl. One of the happier messages I have had in England.

speaker: Hemming
en: I wish I could expand on this happiness with good news. But we are in the center of a storm. And yet my old heart sings great songs at the sight of you. You look good, Eivor. Strong. Healthy.

speaker: Eivor
en: My heart sings as well. It is good to see you again.

speaker: Hemming
en: Yours is a poet's heart, I am told. What a mix of spirits you have.

speaker: Eivor
en: I was told you were ill, Hemming. I hope these stories are bigger than the truth.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course, of course. You know how rumors grow. A fish the size of a hand at catching is the size of a man the next morning.

speaker: Eivor
en: It warmed me to hear Vili's name again. In coming to England, I thought I had left the best of Norway behind.

speaker: Hemming
en: He often thinks on the old country as well. Seems to think his life was simpler then. It may be he is right.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Movement on the walls!

speaker: Hemming
en: We must end this soon. Before the weather changes.

speaker: Eivor
en: The whole of my clan would be here if you called them.

speaker: Hemming
en: No need. These men are flies for swatting. Even now, Trygve rides for Stoneburgh, should any Picts escape. It will all be ended by this time tomorrow.

speaker: Hemming
en: You have known me as your jarl for an age. And I have known and loved you all since you were babes. An easy burden to bear.

speaker: Vili
en: Let's hope you fight better than you age, old friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're not slurring, Vili. Have you mislaid your ale?

speaker: Hemming
en: Today, you do not fight for me. Not for each other. Today, you fight for your children. Fight so that they may grow, so they may be good and just, as you are. For them, today, we take back Ulkerthorpe!

speaker: Vili
en: Trygve and Eivor have brought us arrows and oil to bring fire-light to the Picts, to feed their traps! The first to signal from the top of the tower, their war chief's weapon in hand, drinks my mead for the month!

speaker: Eivor
en: Thor's beard, it's good to see you, Vili.

speaker: Vili
en: O, is it? Or have you come to snatch glory from my calloused hands?

speaker: Eivor
en: We can snatch glory together. Unles you're too frightened to fight beside me.

speaker: Vili
en: O, no! This is a contest now. To the top of that tower, and the Pict chief is the prize.

speaker: Eivor
en: You can have your glory, Vili. I am here to support you and your father.

speaker: Vili
en: Such humility. Where is the Eivor I once knew?

speaker: Eivor
en: It has been too long, Vili Hemmingson.

speaker: Vili
en: Yet here you are, back with the old clan. That is what matters most.

speaker: Eivor
en: For old times, then.

speaker: Vili
en: And new alike.

speaker: Hemming
en: Fight, Hemmingsons! Bring victory today, for tommorow we feast!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Light the arrows! May they burn with flame unbridled!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Glory to the Hemmingsons!

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: The Pict chief will fall by my hand!

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Avenge our fallen! Show no mercy!

speaker: Vili
en: The Pict chief hides behind men like a coward. I have no doubt he will be well fortified. Look for him on high ground.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will have his head for Hemming Jarl.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Vili and the Wolf-Kissed fight by our sides again!

speaker: Eivor
en: The chief will make his stand in the tower.

speaker: Eivor
en: There, the chief.

speaker: Pict Warrior 1
en: They come for the chief! Stop them!

speaker: Pict Warrior 2
en: The chief is dead! Run! Flee to the hills!

speaker: Eivor
en: You're injured.

speaker: Hemming
en: No no, stop stop. I am fine. There is more blood here than injury.

speaker: Eivor
en: Pride cannot heal you Hemming. Only care and bandages.

speaker: Hemming
en: My clan fought well, did they not? You saw it, the heart in these people. How they rallied behind their jarl.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have that effect on men. They trust you.

speaker: Hemming
en: And they love my son all the more. But he lacks the trust of our thegns. And I am running out of time to persuade them.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're sick.

speaker: Hemming
en: And you accept it. Unlike my son. He thinks me immortal... because he must. He does not want what I have to give him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Was it Vili who summoned me? Or you, Hemming?

speaker: Hemming
en: I thought you would come faster if it was Vili's name you heard first. I need your wisdom, Eivor. Your discretion.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have it, of course.

speaker: Hemming
en: There will be an Althing soon, in which the nobles must name a new jarl. And I am torn. I would have my son follow in my steps, but he is reluctant. He follows his warrior's heart. Others will name Trygve. A fine man with a mind for leadership, but his lineage is tattered, and he is less bold.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have known Vili since we were small. He is bold and courageous, and your warriors love the man. The nobles should choose him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Trygve is wise, and has a keen mind to lead. At the Althing, no one would doubt his succession if he was named.

speaker: Eivor
en: Both men are honorable, but they do not hold a bearded axe to Hemming Jarl. Let us not burden ourselves with the Althing-choice yet.

speaker: Hemming
en: Your sight is clear and your mind is sharp. Let that guide your thinking in the days to come. Vili departs for Kinder Downfall soon. Ride with him. And talk, like old friends made new.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I see any Valkyries lurking nearby, I will send them away.

speaker: Hemming
en: I can fight them off a while longer.

speaker: Hemming
en: Vili waits for you below, Eivor.

speaker: Old Harek
en: Gods, grant me power to offer this sacrifice! Give me the strength to give to you!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is happening up on that cliff?

speaker: Eivor
en: What is all this?

speaker: Old Harek
en: My life. The fruit of my work, all gathered here, and now I lack the strength to throw it off this cliff.

speaker: Eivor
en: You carried everything up here only to throw it all down?

speaker: Old Harek
en: The horse did most of it. It is the only way I can send my belongings into the next world. My children will not bury it with me. They say they do not want it, but I know they will sell it once my light burns out. Will you lend me your strength? Throw everything over the cliff. The farther you throw, the better their chance of reaching the next world.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that how it works?

speaker: Eivor
en: Why is everything packed in straw?

speaker: Old Harek
en: I did not want anything to break.

speaker: Old Harek
en: That contains a bow given to me by Halfdan the Black after I put an arrow under King Sigtyg's left arm.

speaker: Eivor
en: That sounds like quite the shot.

speaker: Old Harek
en: That contains a silver harpoon head I received from King Harald, for pulling Halfdan's frozen body out of ice.

speaker: Eivor
en: They are a generous family.

speaker: Old Harek
en: May the gods grant you luck for your efforts.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope it is good luck.

speaker: Old Harek
en: You missed a few things.

speaker: Eivor
en: The gods will get the idea.

speaker: Old Harek
en: Thank you for your help. You did not have to do this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kind and courageous people live the best lives, but it can be a difficult path to keep.

speaker: Old Harek
en: I have tried to live well. It is enough that the gods know that, even if the name Harek Gand is forgotten in Midgard.

speaker: Eivor
en: So what will you do, now that this task is done?

speaker: Old Harek
en: Done? That was to announce my arrival. Now, I leave this world. Enjoy your life.

speaker: Old Harek
en: To Asgard!

speaker: Eivor
en: What! Wait!

speaker: Old Harek
en: Thank you...!

speaker: Eivor
en: Thor's Hammer... that was a shock.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Did you hear? The Danes tried to kidnap Lady Estrid.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I was there! I saw it! Not much of a raiding party. Just a ragtag band, chased off by Aelfred's men. Laughing as they went.

speaker: Estrid
en: There you are, Eivor! Over here!

speaker: Eivor
en: I came first to help you. Your need seemed more... pressing.

speaker: Eivor
en: They are, though time will tell if the fire is rekindled.

speaker: Estrid
en: And now my marriage awaits your executioner's sword.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will it not be strange to leave this place? You've lived here half your life.

speaker: Estrid
en: Yes, but what is to keep me here? A loveless union and the dirt mounds of two babes who never took a breath.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you always missed Francia?

speaker: Estrid
en: I have. Or rather I miss the woman I was when I lived there. Somewhat freer and more hopeful.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what of our plan, the great Lammas kidnap? Is this a Christian feast?

speaker: Eivor
en: You speak with some sadness. Has your time here always been tragic?

speaker: Estrid
en: There have been tears, but also great passions. Love, foolishness, regret. Yet is that not all lives? The best lived of them?

speaker: Eivor
en: And what of our plan, the great Lammas kidnap? Is this a Christian feast?

speaker: Eivor
en: And what of our plan, the great Lammas kidnap? Is this a Christian feast?

speaker: Estrid
en: Yes! It's a wonderful evening, a blessing of the harvest. Full of fruits and fires, drinking and dancing.

speaker: Eivor
en: Revelers with muddy minds and glazed eyes. That's good for us. And what of the ship that will sail you home?

speaker: Estrid
en: I know just the one! And her captain is full of fire. Come, I will take you to him.

speaker: Eivor
en: This captain, who is he?

speaker: Estrid
en: Not much more than a boy in his seventeenth year. Full of youthful bravado.

speaker: Eivor
en: A Saxon?

speaker: Estrid
en: A Dane. Though Eadred calls you raiders. He says that you are here to steal England.

speaker: Eivor
en: Some may be. But I've come to settle a stretch of land. I'm not so keen to return to the winters of my birth in Norway.

speaker: Estrid
en: Norway, ah! It must be beautiful. Rugged and fearsome. And cold as anything, the frozen North.

speaker: Eivor
en: So cold that the light hangs in the sky. A road for the Valkyries, who carry our dead warriors to the eternal feast.

speaker: Estrid
en: An eternal feast would be a merry end.

speaker: Estrid
en: We are here.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is a brothel.

speaker: Estrid
en: The captain's name is Hrolfr, called Rollo in my tongue. Tell him of our new plan and agree to whatever reward he demands. He may take some convincing, for we did not part on the best of terms.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll bring him round by force or persuasion. Just be ready for my signal at the Lammas festival.

speaker: Rollo
en: Ah!

speaker: Eivor
en: Rollo?

speaker: Rollo
en: Please, I'm just a poor Christian brother with nothing left to give!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Someone's at the door, Rollo.

speaker: Rollo
en: O! Is it that I asked for?

speaker: Eivor
en: Estrid sent me.

speaker: Rollo
en: Did she now? As a parting gift for the man who rattled her bones, huh?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, I'm here to collect you.

speaker: Rollo
en: Can it wait?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Oi! Bring out the one they call Rollo! The king's men want to ask him a few questions.

speaker: Rollo
en: No, no, no, no, no, no!

speaker: Eivor
en: Just a second!

speaker: Eivor
en: Good day, sir, come in.

speaker: Eivor
en: Move, move!

speaker: Rollo
en: Some help here!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Bloody fucking Danes! Open this door.

speaker: Eivor
en: Out! Now!

speaker: Rollo
en: Follow me!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: We found your camp, Dane! Your friends are trussed up. No one can help you now!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: I'll rip your heart out Dane!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: Your warriors found better lodgings under our lock and key!

speaker: Rollo
en: I may be drunk, but you are as ugly as a hog! Even ale-addled, I'm worth ten of you! Surrender to Rollo Longshanks! Where are my men, you lap-dogs?

speaker: Eivor
en: Estrid did not lie. You have fire!

speaker: Rollo
en: And who are you to Estrid?

speaker: Eivor
en: Only a friend. I'm Eivor, of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Rollo
en: Norse, by the music of your speech. Then you must forgive me. Those Saxons knew about my camp. I was mind-drunk to leave my warriors behind!

speaker: Eivor
en: Go to your men if you must. Only tell me where to find you. We have much to talk about.

speaker: Rollo
en: Northeast of here, by the river's mouth. Follow me, or come when you can.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Run a brothel they said, spend most of the day lying on your back. Job would be a good 'un without the lusty swains of Essexe.

speaker: Special Services
en: Brother Musevus: delights in oil. The hotter the better. Brother Alexander: seeks the company of the sweetest of beards. Brother Martin: Two ladies (one blonde, the other excessively hairy) Brother Asen: he likes to drink. And watch. Brother Michael: goats (make sure Phillipa has her horns filed) Friar David: candles (we must order more from the priory) Brother Tepavus: rough

speaker: Rollo
en: Saxon bastards! Rollo the Imprudent? I'll show them! I'll be Rollo the Gelder soon enough!

speaker: Eivor
en: Or Rollo the Screamer if you don't keep it down.

speaker: Rollo
en: Was it you who gave Ivarr the Boneless his name? I hear talk of his deeds around the campfire but the name I never understood.

speaker: Eivor
en: He was Boneless before I met him. Now he's bones on a pyre, that's all I know for sure.

speaker: Rollo
en: And King Aelfred? Can you imagine their king in the sky-blanket Týr sends our land? He'd be bluer than my father on nights the mead is strong. He'd fall asleep in the snow with a dog keeping him warm. Ah, this talk makes me long for the old times. The good old times!

speaker: Rollo
en: No! What is this? Why are my people bound?

speaker: Rollo
en: It's worse than I feared! So many of my people gone...

speaker: Eivor
en: ...and the rest at each other's throats. They believe one of your number is a traitor?

speaker: Rollo
en: Lork and Gerhild have been at my side all season. I don't like to doubt them, but my people are taken, and my ship is gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: If the traitor lives, all of you are at risk. Let me talk to them. The innocent have nothing to hide.

speaker: Rollo
en: Very well. But do not let Loki whisper lies in your ear.

speaker: Ake
en: While you were drinking and whoring, Rollo, the Saxons attacked us. And these two were nowhere to be found.

speaker: Rollo
en: Neither betrayed us, Ake! Gerhild is my sworn shield-sister and Lork served my father well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Seems like the Saxons didn't get all of Rollo's clan. I should speak to both, and see if I can find some evidence around the camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gerhild, is it?

speaker: Gerhild
en: Aye, Rollo's sworn sword-sister. I've served him proud and true. You cannot think I betrayed him?

speaker: Eivor
en: You weren't here when the Saxons attacked.

speaker: Gerhild
en: I was hunting! There's fine game in the trees outside the camp, and our people need meat.

speaker: Eivor
en: What was your prey?

speaker: Gerhild
en: Rabbits for stew. Rollo's favorite.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are you to Rollo?

speaker: Gerhild
en: I am shield-sworn, so long as England and that Frankish witch do not sway him from the true path. Our people deserve better.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hear envy, but of Estrid or Rollo I cannot tell.

speaker: Gerhild
en: You know nothing, Raven-beak. My concern is for my fellow Danes. You'll find no treachery here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lork accused you of treachery. He saw you with a Saxon.

speaker: Gerhild
en: Lork? You believe that old crow? His bones crumble, and his mind wanders with age. Or he wallows in jealously, take your pick.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're lying. I found racks and racks of game.

speaker: Gerhild
en: You're more wit than your face suggests. I went to meet a lad from a nearby village. Rollo's not the only one who dallies with the locals.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's all for now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lork, yes? What is your story?

speaker: Lork
en: You want to hear my story? Then bring me a mug of ale, and we'll sit and talk as equals. Elsewise you can hang.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where were you when the Saxons came?

speaker: Lork
en: Hunting rabbits, wasn't I? Sick to death of carrots and turnips. Then I heard Gerhild shouting and all Hel broke loose.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you see anything at all?

speaker: Lork
en: Gerhild, talking with a Saxon. Couldn't hear them, but wasn't nothing good. Sure of that much.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why should I believe you? You could be lying to save your own skin.

speaker: Lork
en: Ask her. Says she's loyal to Rollo, but I've known her since she was a babe. Full of spite and ambition, always was.

speaker: Eivor
en: How long has your sword served Rollo?

speaker: Lork
en: I owe his father a blood oath. If that means wiping Rollo's arse until I die, so be it.

speaker: Eivor
en: And if Rollo was dead, that oath will be fulfilled. You must tire of battle.

speaker: Lork
en: I'll feast in Odin's hall one day. But not with the stain of dishonor on my hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're lying. I found a rack full of game nearby. Enough to feed the camp for days.

speaker: Lork
en: Told you, I was hunting.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stick to that story, and I'll tell Rollo to take your treacherous head.

speaker: Lork
en: I was sleeping in the forest, wasn't I? Heard Saxons tramping through the trees, so I hid. Not fool enough to face 'em on my own.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have what I need for now.

speaker: Eivor
en: I might find some evidence to test their stories.

speaker: Eivor
en: No need to hunt when the camp is full of fresh kills.

speaker: Eivor
en: The camp is well stocked with fresh rabbits and game.

speaker: Eivor
en: This looks to be a good spot to hide. Somewhere to wait out a Saxon attack?

speaker: Rollo
en: Have you made your decision?

speaker: Eivor
en: Gerhild claimed to be hunting, as Lork did. Rabbit.

speaker: Rollo
en: She rarely hunts. She's been a terrible shot since we were children.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your shield-sister is jealous. She thinks you neglect your people by sleeping with the enemy.

speaker: Rollo
en: She always had ambition, but she accepted my leadership, swore on her shield.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lork saw her with a Saxon. She claimed he was her lover.

speaker: Rollo
en: Yet she has berated me many times for taking Estrid to my bed. I did not think her a hypocrite.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lork said he was hunting, but your racks are full of fresh rabbits.

speaker: Rollo
en: Why would he lie unless he had something to hide?

speaker: Eivor
en: He tires of his blood oath, and with your death, he would be free.

speaker: Rollo
en: He has become old and frail, but he served my father well. I would have freed him without bloodshed.

speaker: Eivor
en: This man knew the Saxons were coming and hid. He was either in league with them or a coward.

speaker: Rollo
en: A sad fall for a great warrior no longer in his prime.

speaker: Rollo
en: Have you come to a firm conclusion?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have.

speaker: Rollo
en: Let me hear it. Both choices will pain me, but let it be the truth.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gerhild betrayed you.

speaker: Gerhild
en: No, that's not true! Rollo, I beg you...

speaker: Eivor
en: A shameful death on bloody Saxon soil.

speaker: Odin
en: Both had reason to betray their jarl. But only one had the ice-heart to do so. I hoped you chose well, for you denied them a seat in my hall.

speaker: Eivor
en: There can be no feast in Valhalla for a break-faith.

speaker: Rollo
en: She was always a jealous crow, beak-pricking over every decision I made.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lork betrayed you.

speaker: Lork
en: Lies! And curse you, boy, for letting this outsider sway your heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: A shameful death on bloody Saxon soil.

speaker: Odin
en: Both had reason to betray their jarl. But only one had the ice heart to do so. I hope you chose well, for you denied them a seat in my hall.

speaker: Eivor
en: There can be no feast in Valhalla for a break-faith.

speaker: Rollo
en: He served my father, but he always thought me a callow lackbeard.

speaker: Eivor
en: TBA

speaker: Eivor
en: On second thought, perhaps there is more to be learned.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing more can be done here, but your warriors might still be alive. And I will need your help, after they are free.

speaker: Rollo
en: There's a Saxon camp with a dock at Port Walton. It might be they were taken there.

speaker: Lork
en: Always knew there was something wrong with her.

speaker: Rollo
en: Spare me your sullen words! My heart is torn. Go, find something useful to do.

speaker: Gerhild
en: I told you I was loyal. How dare you doubt me?

speaker: Rollo
en: Forgive me, Gerhild. But even now, there are some who will. You should make yourself scarce for a while.

speaker: Ake
en: I've heard of a safer place than this, south of Colcestre. Let's you and I go take a look, shall we?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sorry that your people suffer, Rollo.

speaker: Rollo
en: Thank you, Eivor. I have much to think on as we journey.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll leave you to those thoughts.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rollo's men, caged like plump hens.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Let's give the ravens a feast of Saxon blood!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: May Fenrir gnaw your bones!

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Valhalla awaits us!

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: My sword will bring you sleep!

speaker: Eivor
en: Rollo's men are free. Now we discuss the terms of the kidnap.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: To the dock! Make the ship ready to sail!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your axe-arm is strong, Rollo.

speaker: Rollo
en: Never doubt me, Raven-Feeder. These Saxon king slaves did.

speaker: Eivor
en: You showed great loyalty to your kinfolk. Stay true to that, and your name and deeds shall spread far.

speaker: Rollo
en: Good advice. Such is my fiercest desire.

speaker: Eivor
en: If it's renown you want, then aid me now. I have a task that will set your name ringing through the longhalls.

speaker: Rollo
en: O! Tell me!

speaker: Eivor
en: I need someone with a swift wave-steed in good repair to bring the Lady Estrid across the sea to Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: These warriors want a leader, not a lovesick boy who spurns them for whores and mead.

speaker: Rollo
en: You shame me, and rightly so. Love cuts deeper than an axe, but I'll dwell on the pain no longer. My people need me.

speaker: Eivor
en: As do I. You owe me a debt. I call on it now.

speaker: Rollo
en: My axe is yours. Speak.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need someone with a swift wave-steed in good repair to bring the Lady Estrid across the sea to Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need someone with a swift wave-steed in good repair to bring the Lady Estrid across the sea to Francia.

speaker: Rollo
en: Another kidnap scheme! Estrid is unshakeable. All right, then. Let we two triumph where one failed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need you stout-hearted in this, whatever your passions for Estrid.

speaker: Rollo
en: We had our time together. Now that's done. I will not fail you here, nor her.

speaker: Eivor
en: We will meet with your men inside Colcestre, on the night of the Lammas festival.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili!

speaker: Vili
en: There you are, come! Ride with me to the falls. They are Freyja's gift to these unforgiving lands.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. But if I don't faint at the sight of them, you have oversold the view.

speaker: Vili
en: You fight with impressive skill, I should say. I taught you well, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: You taught me how to fight empty air, Vili. And trees and snowdrifts and the like.

speaker: Vili
en: No, I am certain I saved you from a snowdrift once. And a murderous tree. That's how I remember it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Any man who would call a tree murderous is a man who has had one too many blows on the head.

speaker: Vili
en: That tower there... it recalls the broken wall in Norway, on the road to my uncle's, remember?

speaker: Eivor
en: I do. I remember the bite of that winter's chill as we sheltered from the wind for hours. It was you who got us stuck there.

speaker: Vili
en: Searching for the chickens you let loose before the Yule feast, I'll have you remember.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's good to ride with you again, Arse-Stick.

speaker: Vili
en: I told you, that was meant to be a dragon's tail

speaker: Eivor
en: It was a woody little twig in my eyes. No dragon's tail.

speaker: Vili
en: Must I remind you of your own disrobed adventures in the predawn streets of Stavenger? Eivor the Pant-less, a head soaked with mead, and many pockets full of vomit.

speaker: Eivor
en: A dragon's tail it was then.

speaker: Vili
en: Are you sure you want my father's mead? Not afraid you might wake up tomorrow, naked, face down in a hog's pen?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that what you call your house?

speaker: Vili
en: Stoneburgh! Was Trygve not sent there by Father to help? We must go!

speaker: Eivor
en: Trygve!

speaker: Trygve
en: We will get you back to Hemthorpe and the seer will see to your wounds. For now, bear the pain. You will live.

speaker: Trygve
en: Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened?

speaker: Trygve
en: I came too late to stop this. The Picts set fires and ran. They mean to spite us! There are more people trapped within. Free them, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tend the wounded. We'll get them out.

speaker: Trygve
en: I will tend to the injured, but there are many more in danger. Bring them here if you can!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Help! Someone, please!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Move quickly, please!

speaker: Eivor
en: Leave your things! Get to Trygve, you will be safe with him.

speaker: Eivor
en: No survivors here. But there may be others that still draw breath.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Quickly, everyone! Get the wounded to Trygve. He is by the gates! Come, quick! Help anyone you can!

speaker: Vili
en: There are more people to save! We are running out of time!

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: Please, my parents are trapped! Help me and help them!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Please! Anyone! Save my family! We're in here! Save my wife, please. Leave me be!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Not me! My wife. Save her first!

speaker: Eivor
en: I have to move fast.

speaker: Eivor
en: Forgive me. There is nothing you can do now. Get to safety.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: O, my dear Hilda... why! I cannot live without you! I cannot bear to go on.

speaker: Eivor
en: She has drawn her last breath...

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Is anyone, anyone out there?

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Thank you, thank you. There are others, please help them too.

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: Please hurry, he cannot breathe!

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: Stay with me! We'll get you out.

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: Thank you, drengr. Thank you!

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: No! No, no, ah!

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: Thank you, stranger, I thought this was my last day on Midgard.

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor! Eivor, where are you? Get over here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Move! Move! Get to safety!

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor! Over here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili? Where are you? Answer me!

speaker: Vili
en: We need to clear a path!

speaker: Vili
en: I will get the man, Eivor. You carry the woman!

speaker: Vili
en: Niflheim will have to wait. You are staying here today.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: O, thank the All-Father...

speaker: Eivor
en: Hold on to me. I can get you out.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: O, thank you, Vili, thank you. I draw breath because of you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I thought I might have to rescue you, Vili.

speaker: Vili
en: Had I died, it would have been my time. My fate is already spun.

speaker: Trygve
en: I'm sorry, but you cannot endanger yourselves like this, lords. You have people to lead, a future to consider.

speaker: Eivor
en: The old man has wisdom, Vili. You have the full weight of this clan on your back.

speaker: Vili
en: My father carries that weight. I do the fighting and feasting and I am expert at both. It is good to have you watching my back again, Eivor.

speaker: Trygve
en: You see what I deal with, Eivor? The mind of a troll in the body of an Æsir.

speaker: Eivor
en: Still the same Arse-Stick as when we were children.

speaker: Vili
en: Pff... I'll never change.

speaker: Trygve
en: This is hardly the time for lightness, you two. We have many injured to comfort.

speaker: Vili
en: That is your domain, Trygve. I don't wish to be seen as a savior and healer all in one afternoon. The waters at Kinder Downfall will soothe my wounds. If my father needs me, I'll be there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili, stop...

speaker: Trygve
en: Eivor... wait a moment. Hemming Jarl has confided in you? About his health?

speaker: Eivor
en: He has. He said Vili wasn't taking it well.

speaker: Trygve
en: Vili lives in another world entirely, right now. He is cracked inside, and will not face the full truth laid before him.

speaker: Eivor
en: How are you? Have you braced yourself for what is to come?

speaker: Trygve
en: I... I have made my peace with the future, yes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Worry yourself with the wounded here. I will talk to Vili myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili was right. The Kinder Downfall is beautiful. Now where is he?

speaker: Vili
en: It's a cold, dark day, Hel's door is ajar. Little cubs of mine, don't stray too far. It's a cold, dark day, come sit by the hearth! Come hear of the tales, from before your birth. O'er the mountains, o'er the seas, the flame of Surtr grows...

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor, you found my secret haunt.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would be deaf to have not heard you singing. Your crow's cackle could awaken the dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: These skirmishes with the Picts, they've worn you down.

speaker: Vili
en: Not at all. The more scars, the better the boast. Look at my father, a battle-worn veteran, carved up like a goat on a spit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not a metaphor I'd use just now. Not in his state.

speaker: Vili
en: These waters are magnificent, no? They comfort and heal. They are Freyja's gift to man.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili. You need to face it. Your father is dying. When he departs for the corpse hall, you will take his place. As expected.

speaker: Vili
en: The novelty of this soggy North has worn on me, Eivor. Too warm for winter living, too cold for summer. I have heard Mercia is more temperate. Dense forests, bright colors, thriving streams. Is that how it is in your settlement?

speaker: Eivor
en: You would always be welcome to live and prosper with us. But that is a matter between you and your father.

speaker: Vili
en: I could make the old man understand. For I have no desire to be jarl, and he must accept that.

speaker: Eivor
en: You defy a long tradition, Vili. The son takes after his father, that is the way of things.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are to be jarl, Vili. Your father expects it, the people of Snotinghamscire expect it.

speaker: Vili
en: I only want sun on my skin and an axe on my hand. Ale and adventure! Not the staid life of a jarl.

speaker: Eivor
en: You defy a long tradition, Vili. The son takes after his father, that is the way of things.

speaker: Eivor
en: You defy a long tradition, Vili. The son takes after his father, that is the way of things.

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor...

speaker: Eivor
en: I have my own reasons to see you made jarl. The Raven Clan wants friends in England. And you are among my very best.

speaker: Vili
en: You do not need me in that seat to secure an alliance. You and Sigurd are beloved here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your father is dying, Vili. Now is the time to get your house in order.

speaker: Vili
en: It is not my house. It is the clan's house, and the clan will decide what happens next.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a chance to end on good terms with your father. I wasn't afforded the same luxury. Don't squander it.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Vili! Vili, come fast!

speaker: Vili
en: Another attack?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: It's your father! He hasn't got long. Come to the longhouse!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hemming Jarl is at the edge of death. I must see him before he goes.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: This must be Loki's doing.

speaker: Norse Solider 1
en: No, no. This is life, my friend.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Will Hemming Jarl go to Heaven, mother?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: I... I hope he will. If he has accepted Christ into his heart, the Lord will most certainly receive him.

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: O, dear Hemming! Our jarl!

speaker: Norse Man 4
en: He'll soon join our forefathers.

speaker: Norse Soldier 2
en: Eivor. Hemming Jarl still clings to life.

speaker: Hemming
en: To see you both together again, like this. It recalls days long past. Makes me feel... young again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hold on to that feeling. And take it with you to the hall of the slain.

speaker: Hemming
en: You've become a great warrior, Eivor. A warrior and a leader, worth song and verse.

speaker: Eivor
en: I had many good teachers, Hemming Jarl. You chief among them.

speaker: Hemming
en: I beg of you now... do not let my lessons die. Pass them on.

speaker: Vili
en: The seer is on her way, Father. She has remedies for you. Cure and charms.

speaker: Hemming
en: I held you here, Vili... in one proud hand when you were fresh from your mother's womb. I watched you grow, a dirty-haired boy, swinging sticks and running through the mud, dreaming of glory. I... I am proud of what you have become, Son. And I am proud... proud of what you will become. No matter... I... I...

speaker: Vili
en: Father...

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili...

speaker: Trygve
en: We must prepare for the funeral.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll send for my clan. You call on the nobles of this shire.

speaker: Eivor
en: The nobles have begun to arrive. Trygve needs our help to see this through.

speaker: Eivor
en: We will be at the funeral pyre, overlooking the village.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Should a new threat to Hemthorpe emerge, who will step up to meet it? Vili? I am not sure...

speaker: Eivor
en: A worthy pyre for Hemming Jarl. His journey to the Halls will be heralded by roaring flames.

speaker: Trygve
en: Eivor.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Drengr.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sunniva, thank you for coming.

speaker: Trygve
en: Ah, the sight of old friends lets my heart rest easy.

speaker: Sunniva
en: We came as soon as we heard. Bearing gifts for Hemming Jarl.

speaker: Eivor
en: The celebration will last many days. How soon 'til we begin?

speaker: Trygve
en: The pyre's construction is underway, and all of our guests are lodged and welcomed. We could begin shortly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. You handled this well, Trygve.

speaker: Trygve
en: I pledged my life's oath to Hemming Jarl. There is nothing I would not do for him. The Althing must be held when the week is out and the funeral is done. The nobles of this shire will name Vili the jarl of our clan. This assumes they will be sober after a week of drinking and weeping.

speaker: Vili
en: It will be a grand funeral. Father will have a clear view of his lands from here. The flames will burn bright and tall for all the shire to see. You've done well, Trygve.

speaker: Trygve
en: This was his favorite spot in the shire. I suppose we should get started. Our guests need looking after.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will look for you later, to save you from them once the mead has really soaked in.

speaker: Trygve
en: You are a true gift, Eivor. Thank you.

speaker: Vili
en: Trygve is Hemthorpe's rock. With him around, the city can keep its peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: He's a good man.

speaker: Vili
en: I must be away for a short time, Eivor. I want to retrieve something for my father. A gift.

speaker: Eivor
en: When did you have time to make a funeral gift?

speaker: Vili
en: It was something I had hoped to give him in life. You must see it to believe it.

speaker: Sunniva
en: I brought a gift from the Raven Clan. I stored it at the watchtower on the far side of Hemthorpe.

speaker: Vili
en: Very kind, thank you. I should like to see it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should look over the gift first. It must be worthy of Hemming Jarl.

speaker: Sunniva
en: There is a heaviness to your look, Eivor. What troubles you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hemming desired my counsel before he died. Wanted my opinion on the future of this clan's leadership.

speaker: Sunniva
en: That would be Vili, would it not?

speaker: Eivor
en: If tradition held, yes.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Trygve has tasked me to help the volva with the sacrifices. Could we speak with her to ease your thoughts?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a good idea. But let me go alone.

speaker: Eivor
en: Set scouts around the village. The people here must mourn in safety.

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: What will happen now that our beloved jarl is lost? Who will take his place?

speaker: Eivor
en: Edyt.

speaker: Edyt
en: Eivor. Are you looking to return to your settlement?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, let's depart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Actually, I will stay here for now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There you are! Ready for that drink?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's head inside.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not quite yet. There are some things I need to take care of first.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't keep me waiting for long.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're back. Shall we go into the longhouse?

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are... a lot of people. I haven't been to a party in some time. I guess I'm nervous.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not as though you're going in there alone. I'll be with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You just saved an island from descending into total madness. You can handle one drink.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you've been to one party, you've been to them all. It's not as though you've forgotten how to be around people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'd be surprised.

speaker: Eivor
en: Come on.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I guess you're right. Let's go inside.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Okay.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, I'm ready for a drink. What about you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm, I've always wanted to try mead. Can't be any worse than Markos's wine. Eivor, what do you say we find out who the real Norseman is with a little drinking contest?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'd say you don't know what you're getting yourself into.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can really hold your mead. Now if we had been drinking wine, I would have won.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wine! That's child's play!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not if it's from Markos's vineyard. That swill could peel paint from a vase.

speaker: Eivor
en: Markos? Who's Markos?

speaker: Kassandra
en: An old friend that made truly terrible wine. Maláka.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ha! I guess you're good for (hic) something after all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ah! I drank all the mead! That makes the better Norseman!

speaker: Eivor
en: Better indeed. Congratulations.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I haven't been this drunk in a thousand years.

speaker: Eivor
en: Huh? A thousand years? What are you talking about?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Never mind. Should not have said that. Maláka!

speaker: Eivor
en: Mel-kah'? You really are drunk! Now you're just spouting nonsense.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, it's a Greek swear word. It's ma-lá-ka!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ma-lá-ka. Ma-láka Maláka!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka! That's it! You got it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now let me teach you

speaker: Wedding Guest
en: The bride and groom are here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are we... are we crashing a wedding?

speaker: Eivor
en: It was arrogant to assume these people were here to celebrate us saving their asses. Come. Let's join in their revelry.

speaker: Old Woman
en: Oh, it's you! Thanks for bringing me to my senses at the Fairy Pools. I would have missed my daughter's wedding if you hadn't.

speaker: Ex-Lover
en: But I still love you!

speaker: Bride
en: Please, our courtship is long over and I've married another man. You need to leave.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you say we make that bride's day and get rid of that asshole?

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't you mean that maláka?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Indeed!

speaker: Bride
en: Oh, thank you! You saved my wedding!

speaker: Kassandra
en: We actually saved it twice.

speaker: Eivor
en: All in a day's work.

speaker: Bride
en: Well, you did your best. He's going to stay but at least you tired him out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sorry we couldn't do more.

speaker: Groom
en: Aren't you the heroes who saved the island? And our wedding!

speaker: Eivor
en: I did a little more than she did. But yes.

speaker: Bride
en: We would love it if you both gave a toast at our wedding.

speaker: Eivor
en: We hardly know you. What would we say?

speaker: Groom
en: But your exploits have made our wedding a day to remember! Please, regale us with your tale!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could be up for that. What about you, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: All right.

speaker: Eivor
en: But if we're going to do this together, Kassandra, let's make it interesting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you suggest?

speaker: Eivor
en: A flyting competition, of course.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not now. Heroics are tiring work. I need a moment to relax before telling the story.

speaker: Bride
en: If you change your mind...

speaker: Groom
en: So? Will you give us a toast?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ah, never tried it myself. I should warn you, though, I've battled wits with great philosophers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop boasting and prove yourself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My day began the strangest way... An axe thrown at my head, intending to slay. There stood Eivor, hot-headed and brash.

speaker: Eivor
en: To see us now, you're not believe our clash.

speaker: Eivor
en: And there stood Kassandra, looking like an ass.

speaker: Bride
en: Not too quick on her feet, is she?

speaker: Eivor
en: You wish you had the skill to swing first.

speaker: Bride
en: Not too quick on her feet, is she?

speaker: Eivor
en: Er... Um...

speaker: Bride
en: Not too quick on her feet, is she?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It took an ambush or two and one dusty old temple... For Eivor to see that I could be helpful. But somehow I've melted her cold, Norse heart...

speaker: Eivor
en: As if. I haven't forgotten she caused the nightmares.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eivor!

speaker: Groom
en: Is that true?

speaker: Bride
en: I really thought this would be better.

speaker: Eivor
en: It'll sadden me to see my new friend part.

speaker: Eivor
en: And despite her transgressions, I'll give her a fresh start.

speaker: Bride
en: I really thought this would be better.

speaker: Bride
en: I really thought this would be better.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eivor did the heavy lifting, left the tracking job to I... In the end, we triumphed, chasing the nightmares far from Skye. And to the bride and groom on this historic day...

speaker: Eivor
en: Hopefully tonight, you'll finally sleep okay?

speaker: Groom
en: Bit of a lackluster note to end on...

speaker: Eivor
en: Expert tracking? You're foolish.

speaker: Groom
en: Bit of a lackluster note to end on...

speaker: Eivor
en: If your love survives this, nothing stands in your way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Um... Well... Uh...

speaker: Groom
en: Bit of a lackluster note to end on...

speaker: Bride
en: That was wonderful! You're really made this a night to remember.

speaker: Bride
en: That was certainly something.

speaker: Groom
en: Maybe you two should stick to saving the day. And leave the storytelling to the skalds.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's been a while since I've been the center of attention.

speaker: Eivor
en: How does it feel?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Strangely familiar. I'm glad you invited me here tonight.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was nothing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, really. Thank you. I needed this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: More than I knew.

speaker: Eivor
en: Edyt! Did you come for the wedding?

speaker: Edyt
en: Couldn't miss it! My cousin is the bride. And of course, I should thank you. Clearly you were able to help my people, otherwise, we wouldn't be here celebrating.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can't take all the credit. I had some help.

speaker: Edyt
en: True! Valka put you on this path, after all. Was she right, by the way? Did you part ways with that girl, Randvi, as she foresaw?

speaker: Eivor
en: No. Randvi was never on the Isle of Skye.

speaker: Edyt
en: Ah, well, even Valka makes mistakes. Still, it's good you didn't need to say goodbye to a friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: What an unforgettable night.

speaker: Letter to You
en: I do not have long now, a few hours at the most. This place is as good as any. A beautiful view of the setting sun or the bright stars should I last into the night. I have met people so afraid to die alone, but as I lie here writing this, I see there see nothing to fear. After all, it is a journey we must all take alone, with no one and nothing in tow. And so to whoever should find me, I leave you this key to my home, in hopes that that which I leave behind can find new meaning.

speaker: Eivor
en: Burn long and hot, bright wolf of the branch. And guide Soma's gilded warriors home.

speaker: Soma
en: I know what you must think.

speaker: Eivor
en: What must I think?

speaker: Soma
en: That it's foolish to search the for so few people.

speaker: Eivor
en: You told me the soldiers you lost were your best. Vital to retaking the city. Do you think it's foolish?

speaker: Soma
en: Not at all.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then why would I?

speaker: Soma
en: You have the look of one who does well with solitude. You're alone, a wanderer. It may be you think of soldiers as war fodder, and little else. But these warriors are more than a blade and shield. They are my family. Nothing short. I've lost a city this week. I will not lose them too.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. And if your people yet live, we will find them.

speaker: Soma
en: There. Lif's longboat. I recognize the hull.

speaker: Longship Inscription
en: A builder of ships, a lover of art, He carries his honor like a shield on his heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: This poem is about Lif. Did he write this about himself?

speaker: Eivor
en: A group of Danes, held captive.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Can't wait to see what Ealdorman Wigmund does to these prisoners. Should be good for a laugh.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Lord Wigwund'll see you hanged from the tree in the city square.

speaker: Lif
en: Free me! I'm no use here, not with the wind gone from my sails.

speaker: Lif
en: If you would be so kind, I've had quite the day...

speaker: Soma
en: Look through the fog, Lif. Follow the beacon. Our camp is at its base. We'll return when we've found the others.

speaker: Lif
en: We'll head straight to the camp. And see that everyone's shipshape when you return.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lif is a prim and proper man, isn't he?

speaker: Soma
en: He lives by a strict code of honor, more than most. And builds the best longships I've ever sailed. They're the reason we escaped Grantebridge alive. He's not the strongest man, but he's wise and canny and hard to pin down. Like a fish wriggling free of a net.

speaker: Soma
en: This longboat is Birna's, I think. All scraped and bashed, it's hard to tell.

speaker: Longship Inscription
en: A ship as staunch and veiled as this, Fit for a smuggler who could kill with a kiss.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here's a poem about Birna.

speaker: Eivor
en: Saxons surrounding that old hut. There may be Danes trapped inside.

speaker: Birna
en: That's right! Tire yourself out! Weak little kittens, can't even open one barricaded door!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: You'll rot in Hell when we're done with you!

speaker: Birna
en: You'll suck my toes when I'm standing on your head!

speaker: Soma
en: That's Birna, for sure. If my head was in a bucket of water, I'd still know.

speaker: Birna
en: Ha! Soma! I knew I heard someone sweeping the hearth outside. We handled it just fine. Thinking of starting a new town, in fact. This house being our first.

speaker: Soma
en: Birna... I pitched a camp nearby, under a burning beacon. We'll meet you there when I've found the others.

speaker: Birna
en: Thank you, Soma. And you as well, Sunbeam. We'll head to the camp now. I'll have everyone singing songs and dancing jigs by the time you get back.

speaker: Old Roman Letter
en: Dearest Gratian, Your performance at the was unfortunate, however the army is loyal to you here. We would like to march on Gaul and defend it, as many of our men ar native to it. The soldiers long for your inspiring speeches and the young fire you imbibe them with in battle. Please meet me in at your behest. We will make plans to take Thrace once more. Magnus Maximus

speaker: Eivor
en: Birna's like a grapevine, curly and hard to predict. While Lif's like a wood beam, sturdy, straightforward.

speaker: Soma
en: Birna has a genius for tactics, sees well ahead of things. Lif deals with what's just there before him. Practical in all ways. Both have helped me find my footing in desperate times. It's important to keep those who disagree with you close as family.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wolves. They've surrounded someone. Must be careful.

speaker: Galinn
en: Loki's laughing behind his shackles, wretched carrion beasts! I don't deserve this! Leave me! Run!

speaker: Soma
en: Galinn, you look terrible.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened here?

speaker: Galinn
en: Saxons chased me into the fog, ran me smack into a nest of bandits. But Freyr was on my side, and I saw them before they saw me.

speaker: Soma
en: Are you the only one of your crew left standing?

speaker: Galinn
en: I am. And hardly standing myself. But with the blessings of Odin and Freyja, they'll be feasting well with the gods.

speaker: Soma
en: We have a camp nearby, Galinn. I'll take you there myself. Eivor, join us when you're ready.

speaker: Soma
en: The beacon has drawn the last of my soldiers. By tomorrow, our strength will have returned, and we can retake our city. I have not yet spoken to Lif, Birna, and Galinn about this. After my missteps, I worry what they must think of me.

speaker: Eivor
en: They'll be grateful you risked your life to find them. I would be.

speaker: Eivor
en: It doesn't matter. What matters is how you lead them forward, from this point on.

speaker: Eivor
en: That won't be on their minds. They'll be dreaming of all the ways they want to kill the Saxons who took their homes.

speaker: Soma
en: By Thor's hammer, I am glad we're together. In spite of our setback. Galinn, you look... well worn. Do not grieve the men you lost. They will be singing your praises in the corpse hall, waiting for us

speaker: Galinn
en: Thank you, jarlskona.

speaker: Soma
en: Lif. You'd outlast any tempest.

speaker: Lif
en: It's good to be back, Soma. All as one. And know this, that I would follow you through the eye of the storm if you called.

speaker: Soma
en: Birna...

speaker: Birna
en: I'm delighted you're alive.

speaker: Soma
en: I'm delighted to be living. I lost so many after all this, but I still have you three. That makes me the most blessed warrior in Midgard. And Eivor. You have more than proven your worth. Help us reclaim our city, and you will have an ally in me.

speaker: Eivor
en: My blade is yours. For Grantebridge.

speaker: Soma
en: We'll rest for the night. Gather our strength and our wits. And at the break of dawn's light, we retake Grantebridge! Pass the night in our camp, Eivor. Take anything you need.

speaker: Braun
en: It's Woden, I tell you!

speaker: Sunniva
