en: Don't be thick, Braun. Everyone knows Odin leads the Wild Hunt.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Eivor! Who leads the Wild Hunt?

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin. Why?

speaker: Sunniva
en: I was explaining to him the way of Oskoreia. This one wants to turn it into a pageant.

speaker: Braun
en: Not a pageant, a parade! I was thinking some of us could dress up like gods, from both lands. Maybe you could lead it, Eivor!

speaker: Sunniva
en: Oskoreia isn't a celebration! It's when the Veil between the worlds grows thin, and the dead will haunt us if we don't honor them.

speaker: Eivor
en: True. And they say the gods come to Midgard to hunt. Not just beasts, but men also. It wouldn't be wise to draw their attention.

speaker: Mad Monk
en: You are wise to be wary of the gods' wrath, Dane, but it's not by hiding that you'll evade the Wild Hunt!

speaker: Braun
en: I told you not to pester the locals, Uncle. Have you been in the herbs again?

speaker: Mad Monk
en: Don't patronize me, you little shit! And you will call me Brother Maxwell like everyone else!

speaker: Braun
en: No one calls you that!

speaker: Sunniva
en: I've seen you around, planting your smoking pots everywhere. The whole village smells like a seer's hut.

speaker: Mad Monk
en: Those pots are placed where the fabric of the Veil is weakest, letting us perceive unseen threats before they are upon us!

speaker: Braun
en: I'm sorry, Eivor. He shows up like this without warning. I told him he could stay with me while he's here.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're right to offer hospitality. And we should mark the Wild Hunt in some way. It's a source of fear for people of both faiths.

speaker: Sunniva
en: And how do you think we should mark Oskoreia, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: With tests of skill and strength. Like Thyra's archery range. Show the Hunt they'll find no easy prey here.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Swinda is setting up another event, since her last tournament was so successful.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good! Tell her we'll use it, not to celebrate, but to prepare for the Wild Hunt.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Tell her yourself. You're the one leading this ... preparation.

speaker: Eivor
en: Me? I didn't

speaker: Sunniva
en: And be sure to visit Gudmund's homage to the dead, or didn't you notice the ship in the middle of the settlement?

speaker: Eivor
en: I noticed the ship.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Good. May Odin's wisdom guide you.

speaker: Braun
en: So no parade?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have a better job for you, Braun. You'll be the judge of whose actions will impress the gods. You'll be the Keeper of the Tokens.

speaker: Braun
en: I will be the best judge you have ever seen, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Go see Norvid about the tokens. Tell him I sent you and I'll come find you later.

speaker: Mad Monk
en: My herbs let us see the invisible, but it's you, as leader, who must cross the Veil and discover the mysteries of the nether realm.

speaker: Eivor
en: I never said I was leading

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe I should've let Braun have his parade.

speaker: Alvis
en: Ah, good. Eivor's here. Now we can settle this.

speaker: Eivor
en: What seems to be troubling you?

speaker: Alwin
en: This stick-in-the-mud doesn't want to celebrate Ostara!

speaker: Alvis
en: It's the equinox! The veil between our worlds will be dangerously thin. We need to prepare!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why not both? Prepare for the equinox and celebrate Ostara. I see you've already started on the decorations.

speaker: Alwin
en: Of course we have! It's what we do! We've also organized some new events and brought back some favorites from Yule.

speaker: Alvis
en: All this noise and merriment will attract the spirits!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will aid you in protecting the settlement, Alvis.

speaker: Alvis
en: Good. Find me after dark. And before he explains the egg hunt to you, just know that I was coerced.

speaker: Alwin
en: Now then, there is much to do. Norvid will need your help decorating and Mayda might need some words of encouragement. She didn't take being crowned the May Queen very well.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is a lot. And this egg hunt?

speaker: Alwin
en: O, it's already started! Speak with me when you are ready to start the hunt!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: I love you, Otta! Smack those rocks!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: O, you are lucky to be here, warrior! You'll see a sight rarely seen by mortals!

speaker: Eivor
en: Have I walked into another realm?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Otta hits rocks as far as the eye can see!

speaker: Otta
en: The name's Otta Sluggasson. I usually try to dodge Danes like youself, but you seem friendly.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: I saw an angel swallow the last rock you hit, I swear I did, Otta!

speaker: Otta
en: Mm, nothing more sweet than the crack of a good clean rock-hit. Like a warrior's axe cutting through a shield wall.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would like to see this "rock-hit" you speak of.

speaker: Otta
en: All right. Here's a taste of my fire. Get ready, kids.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm impressed, Otta Sluggasson.

speaker: Otta
en: If you want, some try and do the same with their bow. But my best time is hard to beat.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would not want these kids to lose a hero by besting you.

speaker: Otta
en: I like this Viking. Kids, gather round! Are you sure you want to challenge me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine, Otta. I will show these children what a true legend is.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Otta, will you sign this stone I kept?

speaker: Otta
en: Sure thing, kid.

speaker: Otta
en: Well struck, Dane! Nice one! Well, I'll be... You knocked the straw right out of that dummy's belly! Well, well. Twang! Twang! Twang! You've got some firepower in you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: The Dane's got a fine shot! Two legends here together! Tell the poets!

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Otta Sluggasson. This game is joyful. If you add a cup of mead and some popped oats, could be a fine manner of passing time.

speaker: Otta
en: You're right, Eivor of Raven Clan! Hey, come on back if you ever want to dance again.

speaker: Jason
en: Paola, my love! Come look! It is just how you imagined it! Paola?

speaker: Jason
en: Hello, stranger.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this place?

speaker: Jason
en: Do you like it? My wife and I constructed it from ancient stones. It is a house of dreams and memories, fashioned from gossamer and summer breezes.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is beautiful.

speaker: Jason
en: Paola and I have traveled near and far. The things we've seen! And done! When I say "far" I mean to distant lands beyond your imagination. Each brick of this castle is a memory from our adventures.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have gathered wisdom from your travels.

speaker: Jason
en: I have, and it is this. It's all very well to prepare for tomorrow, but do not forget today. Today, this hour, this moment, is a precious gift. Paola and I will look out from our window over the green of England and recall the hours of our travels. From our window we can relive our adventures. There she is, now. I must go to her.

speaker: Eivor
en: I thank you for your words, friend.

speaker: Note from Housebuilder
en: Paola and Jason, Thanks to you for your drawing, it was a great help. I have built many a house in my days, but as I worked on this one, I thought of your travels and travails. I did my level best to put them in every stone.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Welcome to Aelfheim! If I had my eyes, I would show you its splendor myself! A land of Endless Mist! Please join me in my daily jaunt through this magical land. I am seeking the . The Dark Elves pushed me out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfheim, you say? Have you drunk a seer's concoction?

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: No, I am as blind as they come. However the Light Elves guide me through this realm, and I sense it. The path is fraught with delight. Energies the Light Elves dropped. And at the end, the third paradise, Wind-Blue.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Wind-Blue, higher than all the realms?

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Higher than Valhalla itself. I use the magic bowls of Muspel lit by the Light Elves to guide me. We will see the Wind-Blue together. Please illuminate the path into Aelfheim!

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Ah. I sense the Light Elves. The luxury of their strong souls! Here they are.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you from here?

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: I hail from . Joined Guthrum on his march through the swamps. But losing my eyes, they left me behind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your family? Friends?

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: They are back in Zealand. But no need! I have the Light Elves who love and care for me now.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: We are close, so close! From here, a final leg to this journey. Yes, here, this is the path. The Wind-Blue is across the swan-road. I can see it! A river-steed will be needed to cross!

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Careful now... we don't want to attract any unwanted attention from the Dark Elves. O, how they haunt me.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: There. That is Freyr's castle. He keeps court in there. Or did. Until the Dark Elves came.

speaker: Eivor
en: You were right about those Dark Elves. For Odin!

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: The Dark Elves have returned! Spare them no mercy, burst their skulls into small crumbs! Cut their large ears off! Please let me find the Wind-Blue! You foul Dark Elves are ruining it!

speaker: Eivor
en: You can have your Wind-Blue now, in peace, old drengr.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Ah, yes. The realm is safe... for now. Hej, drengr.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yanli. This list... are these debts?

speaker: Yanli
en: No, those are the names of deliveries I have yet to make. Still waiting on payment.

speaker: Eivor
en: These are quite far away, and in all directions. It may be they don't have time to travel here.

speaker: Yanli
en: That could be. If you had a mind to deliver them yourself, I could cut you in. Surely they wouldn't refuse you payment.

speaker: Eivor
en: An interesting idea. Maybe when I have the time.

speaker: Yanli
en: Keep the note, just in case.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: My lovely stone. My dear and lovely stone. I was waiting on that for ages. Thank you!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: A cask of rosewater mead! I never thought that would get here. You're an angel sent from Heaven.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: My bowls and cutlery. At last, they came. Thank you, stranger.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Is that... is that my new anvil? Lord, I thought it had been pilfered by bandits. I cannot thank you enough.

speaker: Yanli
en: Do my eyes deceive me, or did you deliver all of my remaining orders?

speaker: Eivor
en: I think I did, unless I miscounted.

speaker: Yanli
en: I had no idea. Here one day, gone the next. Thank you for that. You deserve some compensation.

speaker: Sten
en: I cannot even weep!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why the cursing, vikingr?

speaker: Sten
en: These are the funeral embers of the last of my raiding crew. One by one, they have fallen.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a heavy loss.

speaker: Sten
en: There is more. Just days ago, news from Norway tells me my family has been taken by the plague. All of them, all!

speaker: Eivor
en: Vikingr...

speaker: Sten
en: My wife, my children. All my pretty ones. It is too much.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must grieve for your loss, friend.

speaker: Sten
en: I cannot weep! As a raider, I taught myself not to. Could you... could you give me leave to weep?

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Sten
en: You are a vikingr, as am I. Perhaps if you gave me leave, I would water the earth with a storm of tears to soften the pain.

speaker: Eivor
en: Consider me your chieftain. Consider that I command you. Weep, vikingr! Weep!

speaker: Sten
en: It is no good. I cannot... I-I cannot, uh, uh. O, god!

speaker: Eivor
en: Weep, my friend. I'll leave you in peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: We must distract your mind from this sadness. Let us fight a to first blood.

speaker: Sten
en: It is a good idea. I cannot weep, but I can still fight.

speaker: Sten
en: Take this! Ah, this feels good!

speaker: Sten
en: Huh. It is always good to fight. But friend, it did not take away my grief.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: What? What are you saying? The red sparrow will settle in the cuckoo's nest? One leg? Who will lose it, her or me? In water, iron then shall float. As easy as a wooden boat? Iron? What madness do you spout, devil?

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is that man talking to?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Matilda. Pig sees the future.

speaker: Eivor
en: Loki's twisted threads. What trick is this?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: None. You drink. Pig speaks.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hello, pig!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I must drink more, to get clearness on your words, pig. Clearness... That is such a strange word? Is that a word?

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't feel anything. Are you a talking pig?

speaker: Pig of Prophecy
en: I, Matilda the Seer, lift the veil. Shall I show you what is to come, Raven?

speaker: Pig of Prophecy
en: River's swan. The does hold the clever boy. He , the . Beneath the Sacred City, where panthers prowl. He will find what stole the Maiden's Blush and begin the final journey. Gods will rise and kings will fall, but never will the blackbirds sprawl. . 13.0.0.0.0. Betrayal burns your blood, Raven-Feeder. Brother against brother, till wolves devour the sky. The rooster taunts the hen. "Nock, nock," says he, all a-quiver, "I'll steal your chicks and sling a feather in your eye." Trapped in the , bound for glory. What will you give for its tarnished hue? Who will die? Chop the wood. Grind the corn. They'll lie in ashes before the morn. The cat is in the well. Let us ring now for her knell. Ding-dong, ding-dong bell. and . Thirty years, the of the licentious lion tear at the earth and sod. Shame on him who thinks ill of it. , dance and prowl. Weave through the baa-lambs, as they howl. He is bound in sleep-thorn. Free him! Free him! Green horses! Riding from the dragon-land. He who has the mercy of God. Lords will bind him in scarlet ribbons, sap his strength. But they give his people voice. Who are you? A seeker. A wanderer. A killer. Woman or man, you wear a magician's cloak and speak to ravens. He cuts down the stalks, waving-wild under a gibbous moon. But Christ's army will follow poor soldier to the sands and back. Swarthy he comes. Eternal yonder sea. Strike his sword in the land. Smack your lips, for you shall be the king's suckling sauce. Men of the Church Father. Serpent's tongue sets torches alight in the winter night. Seeking to end the first of the line.

speaker: Eivor
en: Whatever was in that brew ... it was powerful and mind-twisting.

speaker: Eivor
en: That pig. Where did you get such a surprising creature?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Market.

speaker: Eivor
en: And... is that all you have to say?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Pig speaks enough for both of us.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: These are strange things you tell me, Matilda the Seer! Strange things indeed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Near an old harbor. This is the camp.

speaker: Sigurd
en: How do we charm her when she's in our care? Do we say what we're after? Or do we dance around the idea?

speaker: Basim
en: From what I've learned about Fulke, she's not shy about sharing her esoterica. If we ask her one question, she'll answer ten.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Good. But we mustn't seem eager. She could use it against us.

speaker: Basim
en: And here's Eivor.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ah! You've timed things well. The holy woman Fulke is close by.

speaker: Basim
en: Imprisoned at the Saint Albanes monastery, just around the bend.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This is our moment, Eivor. After this, everything changes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I might be pleased for you, if I knew who this woman was or why we needed her.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I have explained enough. Now is the time for action.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've done nothing of the sort. Nothing but give me your blind word!

speaker: Sigurd
en: I wish to speak to her! Me, your jarl! That alone is reason enough!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why? So she might cast a spell and turn Eadwyn into an eel?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Fulke is not the only advantage we seek here, Eivor. There will be treasures in Saint Albanes, more than we can count.

speaker: Eivor
en: You can steal all the silver and gold you want. But if there are no more farmers in the field to hire, it's useless metal.

speaker: Basim
en: Men from all across Mercia would heed the call to fight a woman pledged to Wessex.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have already plundered Saint Albanes Abbey and lifted its treasures from nave to crypt. I saw no prisoners of note.

speaker: Sigurd
en: She is there. I know it. And she is the most valuable treasure of them all.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor. There was a time when you would follow me without question, because we trusted one another. Because you knew I would never lead you into folly. Never wager our lives before I knew the cost.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Is there something that holds you back from embracing me as you once did? As your brother? Your family?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, you know I would never betray your... your trust in me. I'll fight with you. But there must be limits to this chase. Geadric is counting on us.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Of course he is. And soon we will deliver. Come.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Saint Albanes will not disappoint. It is famous for its treasures.

speaker: Eivor
en: We'll see about that.

speaker: Sigurd
en: When you raided Saint Albanes, are you sure you saw nothing? No crypt? No prisoners?

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing I can recall for certain.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do we know of this woman?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Very little. She appears to be an adventurer of sorts.

speaker: Eivor
en: The thegn called her a heretic.

speaker: Sigurd
en: All the better for us! She is clearly someone who knows her own mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: I admire your optimism, Brother.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Where is this woman?

speaker: Basim
en: There will be a crypt or dungeon. Near the central church, I believe.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Here's the monastery. Saint Albanes.

speaker: Basim
en: Fulke is held inside. Somewhere well protected.

speaker: Proclamation Concerning Fulke
en: Brothers, I caution each of you to resist engaging in ecclesiastical debate with the prisoner called Fulke. She has 's ability to turn one's words—and even holy scripture—back upon one, making the speaker appear foolish and unlearned. We must not let her indulge in these dark arts. Restrict conversations to the subjects of food, weather, and praise of Lady Eadwyn. Dalberre, Abbot

speaker: Eivor
en: Through here.

speaker: Sigurd
en: At long last.

speaker: Fulke
en: ...for like holy Judas, I thank you, beloved Jesus, for the wisdom to pierce 's cloud... to see beyond and above the lies of Ialdabaoth, to know the that is the last mystery that is the twenty-fourth mystery. Amen.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Who dares enter this sanctuary?

speaker: Eivor
en: This stony cave reeks of piss and salty tears.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: How dare you!

speaker: Sigurd
en: We've come for the woman, Fulke. She need not bedevil you any longer.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: The mad heretic?

speaker: Fulke
en: Ah! The Self-Begotten Spirit has sent an angel to deliver me!

speaker: Basim
en: Open the door.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Her heresies must be punished. Not by Danes, or Mahometans, but by true Christians.

speaker: Eivor
en: Choose, friar... stand aside, or fight.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: If we must come to blows, my Lord will protect me... and my reward shall be assured.

speaker: Eivor
en: Permit me, friar, to make an offering to your church.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: A Dane who gives alms to the righteous. I... I bless you, and pray for your wayward soul. Take this key.

speaker: Eivor
en: Friar. Our hands are bloody with the gore of your guardians. Is your God so starved of martyrs that you wish to die as well?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You make a fine point. Let me pray on this.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: The Lord bids me welcome all strangers. Here, friend. Take the key. And depart with your strange friend.

speaker: Fulke
en: Praise thee, Lord of the Treasury of Light, for this chance of deliverance.

speaker: Fulke
en: Are you sent by the angels of Saklas? Or the Self-Begotten One above?

speaker: Eivor
en: That I cannot answer.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You are the woman called Fulke?

speaker: Fulke
en: I am Fulke in this realm. A humble seeker of the Self-Begotten One's true nature.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And you are a collector of artifacts?

speaker: Fulke
en: The instruments of the children of Saklas the Fool, yes I am. I have many such curiosities.

speaker: Basim
en: And you possess an object, a polished stone with unusual markings?

speaker: Fulke
en: Now, you're a curious one. A cowl and robes hiding tawny skin. And that devilish blade.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why do we linger here? Soldiers will be coming!

speaker: Fulke
en: There are stables behind the monastery where we can speak in peace.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Lead the way.

speaker: Fulke
en: Come.

speaker: Basim
en: How long were you imprisoned?

speaker: Fulke
en: Some weeks, perhaps a month.

speaker: Basim
en: For your so-called heresies?

speaker: Fulke
en: Heresies, yes. I have been blessed to discover many profane objects in my lifetime. Objects which attest to the works of the demiurge, the false god worshiped by these robed imbeciles. Across and Francia, I found these relics and carvings. And here in England too. Lady Eadwyn claims they are blasphemous. But her mind is clouded. The true worth of these objects is immense.

speaker: Sigurd
en: May we see these objects?

speaker: Fulke
en: If you wish to know the truth of our origins, I will show you today.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I would indeed. Where you go, I will follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough of these mysteries, Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Fulke is a curator of objects of great worth. One of which may reveal my true nature.

speaker: Eivor
en: True nature? You said this was about victory. About defeating Eadwyn!

speaker: Sigurd
en: To know that I am descended from the ancient gods is a victory. It would give me dominion over this land.

speaker: Eivor
en: Descended of the gods? Brother, what by Odin's eye are you saying?

speaker: Basim
en: Fulke, we have heard that you possess a profane stone with strange markings and the image of a tree.

speaker: Fulke
en: That I do. A monolith I call the Saga Stone, for it came to this land with the Dane, Ragnar Lothbrok.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Do you have it?

speaker: Fulke
en: It is the sun and moon of all my sacred objects.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will you buy and trade this stone for an alliance? Or more fighting men? Is it useful for anything other than flattering yourself?

speaker: Eivor
en: While you waste precious hours dreaming of your true nature, our hope for a swift victory is fading.

speaker: Eivor
en: All this secrecy for a carved stone, Sigurd? To what lengths will you go when you have a real mystery to conceal?

speaker: Fulke
en: Perhaps I should leave you three alone, to hammer through your differences.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We are unified. We only wish to see the stone, to read the runes inscribed upon it.

speaker: Fulke
en: No one on earth can read those runes. The language is unknown and probably long dead.

speaker: Sigurd
en: There is no risk in letting us look.

speaker: Fulke
en: No risk at all.

speaker: Fulke
en: Praise thee, O Self-Begotten one, for sending these three to deliver me from my punishment.

speaker: Eivor
en: No whispering gods led me here, Fulke. I brought myself.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You came because I called you, Eivor. They spoke through me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother you have my head spinning.

speaker: Fulke
en: And you fascinate me more with each passing moment. The Saga Stone is hidden away in the care of my acolyte. Are you ready to go see it?

speaker: Eivor
en: The sooner we see this slab of rock, the better. Let's go.

speaker: Fulke
en: Approach the stone with an open mind, Eivor. You may find it more interesting than you expect.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to explore and get my bearings. I'll return when I can.

speaker: Fulke
en: You are my deliverer. I will await your return.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke...

speaker: Fulke
en: Are you now prepared to see the stone?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. Let us go see the slab of rock.

speaker: Fulke
en: You may find the stone more interesting than you expect.

speaker: Jotun
en: Lonely? Miserable? Nothing impresses the ladies like smashing your opponents' face in! Utgard's fighting pit... the place where legends are made! You're not a warrior till you've knocked someone's teeth down their throat!

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Follow me to the pit, and we will destroy our opponents together! Who will fight beside Dugr the Bold? Join me, and I promise you victory!

speaker: Havi
en: I heard you calling for a fighting partner.

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Two fight with two, that is the rule. But have no fear! You'll have little to do but watch as Dugr the Bold destroys his foes!

speaker: Havi
en: I had expected fearsome opposition in the Jotnar fighting pits.

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Fearsome, yes! Too fierce for you. But you can stand behind me. I'll deal with them single-handed.

speaker: Havi
en: You seem to be having trouble finding someone to join you.

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Proud fools! They are afraid I will show them up with my fighting prowess. You're not afraid, are you?

speaker: Havi
en: What is my reward if I help you?

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Besides the glory of victory? Well, I have traveled far in this realm. I would be willing to share the location of some rare treasures.

speaker: Havi
en: I like your confidence, at least. I'll take this challenge.

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: And you won't regret it! For Dugr the Bold is not only a great warrior but a shapeshifter of peerless skill! Pick an animal. Any animal! I will take on that form in the combat to come.

speaker: Havi
en: I don't like the sound of this. Another time.

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: You won't get a fight without me! I'm the only game in town!

speaker: Havi
en: I am no friend to wolves, but it would be good to have one on my side for once.

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Cunning and savage! I like it. Let's go!

speaker: Havi
en: I have always found the lynx a swift opponent.

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Ah, you favor speed and agility over strength? A good choice. Now for combat!

speaker: Havi
en: Of all the beasts of this land, the bear is the most fearsome.

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Brute strength and savagery! Very well. Now let's fight!

speaker: Havi
en: A rabbit? What good is a rabbit?

speaker: Havi
en: What in Hel's name was that? A rabbit? Did you hope to nibble your opponents to death?

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Ah... well, by making myself seem feeble, I made them lower their guard! All in a day's work for Dugr the Bold!

speaker: Havi
en: Are you even able to transform into a real beast?

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: Of course I can! Anything I want! Er... I just don't want to right now.

speaker: Havi
en: I'd better get some reward for carrying you in that fight, or I'll stick your bobtailed arse in a stew.

speaker: Dugr the Bold
en: I found a note on a dead traveler. It will lead you to treasures and secrets. At least I hope it will.

speaker: Havi
en: Another tower, where there was none before.

speaker: Havi
en: A hideaway. And still in use by the looks of it.

speaker: Havi
en: Dead ships, their skeletons washed to shore. There was great ruin here.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Heaven will swallow the smoke of Ealhferth's pyre.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Very poetic. But he's going to be buried in the grounds of the Minister.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Ah, now we can always pay our respects!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: If you say so.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Do you believe in souls? A part of us that lives on with God after we die? Bishop Ealhferth's passing has made me wonder.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones. Does Magister Bata not teach you the scriptures?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Girl 1
en: Magister Bata is a horse's dangles.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: And here is the axe I used to swat a fly.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have ventured from your burrow.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: And you have plunged my city into chaos. I had hoped you would use the lessons of your subtler gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: We have no subtle gods.

speaker: Goodwin
en: If The Gallows is truly dead, perhaps we can allow cautious revelry?

speaker: Eivor
en: I did only what I agreed to, Aelfred. If your crown now weighs heavy, I would gladly take it from you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sweep your own hearth, Aelfred, if you do not like my broom.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be I should take my now. Leave you to the snakes that remain?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Forgive my outburst. God sowed in me a passion, but English prose is an instrument long out of tune.

speaker: Goodwin
en: We all want better for our people, don't we, Eivor? Yours and ours?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Quill remains. What do we know?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: The decay of learning has been gentle in Wessex. We enjoy the office of wise men, but we have neglected the study of wisdom.

speaker: Goodwin
en: The Quill preys on this lapse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you discover more from the writings I found?

speaker: Goodwin
en: I did. The Quill is calling the children of Wincestre to arms.

speaker: Eivor
en: Read this. The Quill wields cutting words that call all the children of Wincestre to arms.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone disagrees with your reforms, Aelfred. And he's calling the children to arms.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Now we know why so many children scurry through the streets. Feral and untutored.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can talk to some, see where they lead me.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Good. Find me at the ale-house when you're done. And try not to scare the piss from any of them.

speaker: Eivor
en: We Norse are the monsters of your 's bedtime tales. I promise nothing.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see you, child. Come.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Girl 1
en: The bad reeve, Selwyn. I saw you punish him in the square.

speaker: Eivor
en: He hurt many people.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Girl 1
en: Yes. He hurt my mother to death, then took her good luck charm. Perhaps you found it? A little carved tree? It is all I have to remember her by.

speaker: Eivor
en: Such a sad story. Take this. Perhaps it will keep you off the streets and out of trouble.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found no charm, lucky or otherwise.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Girl 1
en: A bit of silver then? For my troubles.

speaker: Eivor
en: It wouldn't have the same value, would it?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Girl 1
en: You ugly Dane! May God curse you with boils on your face!

speaker: Eivor
en: Spry little mouse. Will you lead me to your Quill?

speaker: Eivor
en: You there, little cutpurse.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 1
en: Keep your beak out, nosey. I'm starving!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 2
en: Get off me, you oaf.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Stop struggling and give back the apple.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 2
en: Apple? I didn't scrobble nothing. Get your fat hands off me, cow-breath!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stealing apples, eh?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 2
en: Fruit don't feed a growing boy. Do you have any chicken?

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't. But maybe you can tell me what you know of The Quill?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 2
en: The Quill? God blind me, you're brave! Find Aelwyn and Wigbert. They see everything.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: God's beard! You'll set Wincestre ablaze!

speaker: Aelwyn
en: Roly-poly mutton man, you can't catch me!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: God help me, I'd rather be shoveling dung in again.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: You again. You should mind your own beeswax.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelwyn, is it? You wield fire like a flaming Jotnar.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: It was burning when I found it. Hot days like this, things just go whoosh!

speaker: Aelwyn
en: Well?

speaker: Aelwyn
en: Oi! Wigbert, you great moon-calf!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Hand it over, Aelwyn! We saw your little shadow take it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: What you looking at?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not sure, looks like an old lady's been rolling in shit with all the other ugly sows. A hog in a dress maybe?

speaker: Eivor
en: How about I pay you to scuttle off to the tavern and drink yourself senseless?

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Deal. Better than running around after you grubby urchins.

speaker: Eivor
en: Turn around, walk away, and you keep your insides, inside.

speaker: Female Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Alright, alright. No harm meant. Stay out of trouble you grubmite.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: Ha! That showed them!

speaker: Eivor
en: Trouble seems to follow you.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: And I wriggle out of it like a slippery eel. Why are you following me?

speaker: Eivor
en: What is so important that you risk his little neck for it?

speaker: Aelwyn
en: Keep your sticky beak out of our business.

speaker: Eivor
en: Whose business? The Quill's?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for The Quill. So I am asking you, his little worker bees.

speaker: Eivor
en: Setting fires, stealing things is a fearful day's work. Aren't you supposed to be in lessons?

speaker: Aelwyn
en: You don't need book learning when you're street shrewd. That gets you real places.

speaker: Eivor
en: Or gets you noticed, by The Quill for example. Does he pay you well to do his dirty work?

speaker: Aelwyn
en: Us? Working for The Quill? Shows what you know.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that so?

speaker: Aelwyn
en: I am innocent as a lamb. They were The Quill's thugs, and you killed them. Wouldn't want to be in your boots.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: They were The Quill's ninnypops. Smart stuff to throw coin at them, they will be too squiffed to bother you now.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: Those were The Quill's meatmops, and you sent them scurrying off with their tails between their legs.

speaker: Eivor
en: It sounds like you owe me your life.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: This one's brave and strong. Might be able to help us.

speaker: Eivor
en: So you're not working for The Quill?

speaker: Aelwyn
en: We steal to stay alive and out of The Quill's clutches.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you know where I can find him.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: They come up from the sewers like rats.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: Go on, give her what you took. Maybe she can save us?

speaker: Aelwyn
en: Good luck, Dane. Try not to get maimed and all that.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should watch out for a mousetrap.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Girl 3
en: I like the pretty things, but Magister Bata says stealing is wrong.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Girl 4
en: I'm going to marry King Aelfred, and he's going to whisk me away from this toil.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Girl 5
en: Everyone died and left me alone on the streets.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 4
en: I didn't get nothin' today.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 5
en: There's never enough food. I'm always starving.

speaker: Aelwyn
en: That's her! Dimwit Dane! Dimwit Dane! Didn't guess The Quill's a she!

speaker: Hilda
en: Now, now, Aelwyn. Few have the wit that you and I possess. Most see the world in simpler terms, where we are the weaker sex.

speaker: Eivor
en: A brood mare who preys on innocents, and you brag about strength.

speaker: Hilda
en: How little you know. Defend your mistress!

speaker: Hilda
en: Ealhferth, may your roof shield me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ealhferth's roof? Does she flee to the bishop's house?

speaker: Hilda
en: 'Keep your wits. The Dane wants my blood. Do not leave my side! Guards, protect me!

speaker: Hilda
en: Show yourself, murderer! Show yourself, shadow-walker. This heathen will kill us all. Come then, you rabid hound.

speaker: Hilda
en: Come child. Whisper what you've learned, and Mother will give you a treat.

speaker: Eivor
en: Coward. Using children to spy and steal for your Order.

speaker: Hilda
en: To educate them! Give me a child until he is seven, and I will give you the man... or woman.

speaker: Hilda
en: But what use are letters when a child can only write his name in pig shit? Or wisdom in a woman when she cannot wield it beyond her hearth?

speaker: Hilda
en: I taught little Aelwyn so much more, saved her from a life less worthy. She will find enlightenment in The Order, just as I did.

speaker: Hilda
en: If I could save them all, I would.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you can't. You've corrupted too many to save too few.

speaker: Hilda
en: My Order is the only way forward. It can quench our thirst for knowledge, if only Aelfred's slave-faith is defeated.

speaker: Hilda
en: And what would you sacrifice for infinite knowledge?

speaker: Odin
en: An immeasurable gift. Why refuse it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not their innocence.

speaker: Hilda
en: A pity.

speaker: Hilda
en: Non requiescet in pace. (They shall not rest in peace.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Goodwin said to meet him at an ale-house nearby.

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: Oh, dear Lord, let me die.

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: Not again...

speaker: Irish Soldier 3
en: Mo lén. (Oh no.) I've shat me-self!

speaker: Bárid
en: Eivor! Please, we need your councel.

speaker: Bárid
en: Come, the army has been poisoned.

speaker: Eivor
en: Curse of Loki.

speaker: Flann
en: Speak, whoreson! Who?

speaker: Moenach
en: That's the man, my king!

speaker: Flann
en: You accuse Bárid?

speaker: Moenach
en: It's him what gave me the poison. Seven silver he paid!

speaker: Flann
en: The King of Dublin.

speaker: Bárid
en: My king. I...I

speaker: Flann
en: Only the Irish were poisoned. Your Danes are hale and hearty.

speaker: Ciara
en: My lord

speaker: Bárid
en: Flattering words and servile gifts, all to mask treachery.

speaker: Ciara
en: My lord, you know this cannot be true. Danes don't use poison and Bárid is no man of guile.

speaker: Moenach
en: My king, it was him! He says to me, "Poison the feckin' Irish," he says. He threatened me life!

speaker: Flann
en: Silence!

speaker: Bárid
en: Take this man away!

speaker: Moenach
en: No ... No! I done nothin'.

speaker: Flann
en: Ciara, I chose to place you at my right hand because you see clear. Still, I cannot trust this Dublin Dane.

speaker: Bárid
en: My king, I have faithfully served you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Trust him better, lord.

speaker: Flann
en: I said silence! Danes often fight for either side.

speaker: Flann
en: Bárid, stay within these castle walls while I consider your position. I must first find care for my soldiers.

speaker: Ciara
en: You well know, my king, I have a friend who can heal most any malady.

speaker: Flann
en: One of your scattered coven of forest-dwelling pagans?

speaker: Ciara
en: Let me speak with her. She'll find a cure.

speaker: Flann
en: Ara (Ah), go. Take a soldier with you for protection.

speaker: Ciara
en: I choose you as my soldier. Meet me at the stables near the front gate.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid, you should be grateful your head is still upon your shoulders.

speaker: Bárid
en: I am. By the gods, I am.

speaker: Ciara
en: Come, let us find my friend, Deirdre.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is this healer?

speaker: Ciara
en: She's a druid, wise despite her youth. Are you ready?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am curious to meet her.

speaker: Eivor
en: A few moments, please.

speaker: Ciara
en: Shall we go see Deirdre now?

speaker: Eivor
en: Poor Bárid. I'm disappointed that Flann even considered the accusation true.

speaker: Ciara
en: The poisoning had two goals. Disable our army and put the blame on Bárid.

speaker: Eivor
en: But who's behind it?

speaker: Ciara
en: The soldiers cough blood. It must be the poison used by a druid cult, The Children of Danu.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are they?

speaker: Ciara
en: When the Christians came with sword and fire, some few druids banded together. Eventually they vowed to destroy the Christians. They turned to mayhem and murder. Many disguise themselves and live among the villagers.

speaker: Eivor
en: What of Deirdre and druids like her?

speaker: Ciara
en: True druids oppose the Danu. But they are scattered and disorganized. That is why I am so determined to help Flann to the throne as of Ireland. He will stamp out the Children of Danu, leaving true druids to carry on.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me more about your friend.

speaker: Ciara
en: Deirdre is a druid I have known for years. We learned together.

speaker: Eivor
en: You were once a druid?

speaker: Ciara
en: I was. There are many pagans and druids isolated in forests all around Ireland.

speaker: Ciara
en: This way, across the river.

speaker: Eivor
en: This land is unsettling.

speaker: Ciara
en: I am unsure of the way. Follow the stone path as best as you can.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ciara!

speaker: Ciara
en: Wolves!

speaker: Ciara
en: You see what's Connacht's like. A wild place. It's where I'm from.

speaker: Ciara
en: Deirdre's hut. Eivor, she is a druid, so a bit...

speaker: Eivor
en: Eccentric?

speaker: Ciara
en: Yes. That's it. Eccentric.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Ciara! Are you ready at last to return to the joys of the forest?

speaker: Ciara
en: Deirdre, this is my friend, Eivor. I'm sorry to say we've come for help.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Fé amae (Alas), I'd hoped the auguries were mistaken. Children of Danu?

speaker: Ciara
en: Yes. Flann's army is spitting blood.

speaker: Deirdre
en: You know what is needed.

speaker: Ciara
en: I'd hoped you'd find another way.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this about?

speaker: Ciara
en: The Children of Danu make the poison, but they also hold the key to its cure.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Amber made from the sap of an ancient tree sacred to them. Each Child of Danu carries a shard of this amber.

speaker: Ciara
en: Once steeped in its owner's blood, the power that is held deep within the amber is set free.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is a somber request. How will I find one of these dark druids?

speaker: Ciara
en: A friend of ours tried to discover the identities the Danu have taken. He hoped to find one called "The Wren."

speaker: Deirdre
en: Then that friend was killed. The Danu are truly dangerous.

speaker: Ciara
en: You may find something in his abandoned house, up north near Port Auley trading post at the mouth of the Ballysadare.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find this Wren, steep the amber in his blood, and return once I have done.

speaker: Ciara
en: I pray the spirits guide you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah! "The Cursed" hiding in Tuam planned the poisoning. I will tell Deirdre and Ciara and give them the amber stained in blood.

speaker: Ciara
en: Eivor! I worried you'd come to harm.

speaker: Eivor
en: I did not, but The Wren did.

speaker: Deirdre
en: May The Wren's blood ooze into the loamy earth and feed the forest with red milk. Give me the shard for the cure.

speaker: Deirdre
en: The humors of the ancient tree live on in the amber, now sparked by blood. Look, it turns deep crimson. The cure will be painful. The soldiers will writhe and plead to be killed as a mercy. But in a few hours, they will be well.

speaker: Ciara
en: Thank the spirits of the earth.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Wren carried a note.

speaker: Ciara
en: A note?

speaker: Eivor
en: The poisoning and the plan to accuse Bárid was the doing of someone called The Cursed. There is a cottage in Tuam where The Cursed hides. Perhaps we can find who made the poison there.

speaker: Ciara
en: It is a small hope, but hope still. It is nearby. We must go.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Not yet, the cure is prepared. You must deliver it as quickly as you can.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will look for this mysterious Cursed. You take the cure to Cashelore.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Three or four drops on each soldier. No more.

speaker: Ciara
en: Thank you, good friend. Goodbye. Eivor, I'll meet you under the tree outside Tuam heading south.

speaker: Deirdre
en: The Cursed will be your second Child of Danu, Eivor. There are others. Were you to bring me all their shards, I could mix you a potion that would give the force of the blazing sun.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will fell this one, then I will think on the others and your mysterious sun.

speaker: Deirdre
en: Before you go... there is a darkness rolling towards Ciara. Please watch over her.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Should be up there in the trees ahead. Can you smell it? It stinks of death and evil.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know that scent well. Carrion and death. Loki's reek.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Saints save me!

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: The maulings have drawn in a starving wolf pack.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did the wolves get a bite of you?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: No, I am unhurt. Thank you, Dane. I... misjudged you.

speaker: Eivor
en: No need. But tell me what happened.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: These beasts came scavenging for fresh meat.

speaker: Eivor
en: I meant, why are you out here with the dead cattle again?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: I'm searching for my best milch-cow. She's missing.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you found her?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: No, but I found a Danish axe. It belongs to Hrothgar, leader of their war-band.

speaker: Eivor
en: You know for a fact this axe is his?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Yes! He brandishes it about the village, demanding ale.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will speak to this Hrothgar and his war-band.

speaker: Eivor
en: That woman is certain a nearby band of warriors caused these maulings. We have no other clues.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: I know the men she means. They're staying at the church near Brisleah Farm. Come, meet them. Their leader, Hrothgar, is a great man ... for a heathen. He is no cattle killer.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have curious opinions, Wulfhilda. And an uncommonly opened mind.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: I should say the same of you. Most heathens would point to witchcraft or monsters, but you seek an earthly cause.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have seen many strange things, but the answers are usually close at hand, if only hidden.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: True, yet in this case, the Church has tasked me to explain the unexplainable. That at time introduces... unholy ideas.

speaker: Eivor
en: And your Church accepts your... unholy ideas?

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: They tolerate it. Lucifer is a deceiver and God Himself works in mysterious ways. So, I too must remain open to all possibilities, mundane and otherworldly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Which is why you tolerate a heathen like me.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Perhaps. Or perhaps all of us, heathen and Christian, stand within the folds of a greater mystery.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Something's off, Eivor. Hrothgar's men are rowdy sorts, but the air is far too still.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand back, priestess. This is war-work.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Hrothgar and his men, they... they were good to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have a care, Wulfhilda. The killer may yet linger here.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Their leader, Hrothgar. I do not see him among the dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: I shall find him.

speaker: Eivor
en: See, more fresh mold. Same as in the fields, on the cows.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: The villagers say it is the Devil's Mark. What do you say, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: I say find the mold and we find our killer.

speaker: Eivor
en: The same marks as before. Bite marks, a mauling. These are not weapon wounds.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: What manner of demon can fell so many well-armed warriors?

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Eivor, look up. More blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone crawled into the loft. Or dragged a body up there.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Hrothgar sometimes slept in the loft. Have you looked up there?

speaker: Hrothgar
en: Back, you! Back, I say. I can still draw blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are Hrothgar, leader of this war-band?

speaker: Hrothgar
en: I am. A raider, and proud of it. For the little time I have left.

speaker: Eivor
en: I bear ill news. Your warriors have fallen. Who or what did this awful thing?

speaker: Hrothgar
en: The monster did this thing. It killed us while laughing. Laughing. It broke my axe and gouged me. I... I crawled up here to die.

speaker: Eivor
en: What was it? Did you see?

speaker: Hrothgar
en: A foul Jotun... a night-goer from the world's rim... it spoke, named itself Grendel... said it would return.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. We shall wait for it to come back, you and I.

speaker: Hrothgar
en: Not I, my wounds are too great and my spirit takes ship. Send them to Helheim ... for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ride with the winged women, friend. I will handle this Grendel, whatever manner of monster it may be.

speaker: Hrothgar
en: Wait, warrior. There were... two...

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Best hide to not scare the demon off when it returns.

speaker: Eivor
en: We'll wait up here for it to show itself again.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Get your rest, warrior. I'll stand vigil with prayer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wulfhilda, be still. Something stirs.

speaker: Grendel
en: Wake. Play. Wake. Play.

speaker: Eivor
en: Beast! Today you die!

speaker: Grendel
en: No kill! Play! I play!

speaker: Grendel
en: Mother! It hurts! Mother, help! It hurts me, Mother!

speaker: Grendel
en: Play. Grendel only want to play. You make Grendel hurt. Mama. I want to go home.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: By all that is holy and bright. What manner of monster is that thing?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not a monster, but a man. Strange to behold, but this Grendel is... was... a man.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: But where did it come from?

speaker: Eivor
en: All men have mothers. This one called out for his, in the end.

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: And all of us, even the most hideous, have souls. O Lord, forgive this... man... his sins and grant unto him your grace and everlasting love.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mold, everywhere. Stay here, Wulfhilda. I'll follow this trail...

speaker: Wulfhilda
en: Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May all these souls rest in peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: Jorvik's trade depot. This must be where the merchants' wares are being kept.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Dockmaster, I do not see him. Is he here?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Keep walking. You have no business here.

speaker: Eivor
en: He has a loud mouth, usually stands right around here yawping. Hard to miss.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Fuck off.

speaker: Eivor
en: There must be another way in.

speaker: Eivor
en: The depot is well guarded by the Red Hand. The Order has a stake in these docks.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: What are you doing? You're supposed to be in the market!

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: I know, I... I forgot which merchants to collect from.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: I cannot believe this. Black cloth. On their stalls. Gods, never you mind. Someone else will take care of it. You are playing with fire, boy. The Needle is known to sting for far less than this.

speaker: Eivor
en: It seems like the complaints by the merchants never reached the council.

speaker: Eivor
en: Seized exotic wares. These are worth plenty, something that could be on the Red Hands' agenda. Accumulating wealth.

speaker: Eivor
en: "The sting of a Needle..." I'm on his trail...

speaker: Eivor
en: So the Dockmaster seizes cargo and resells it through merchants in the marketplace. The ones involved bear black cloths. I may be able to get their attention by showing some silver around the marketplace.

speaker: Eivor
en: Coppergate market. I'll flash some silver to the merchants. That should get their attention.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Have you any wine for sale? There's nary a drop in town.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Sorry. All the wine's been bought up for the Yuletide feast.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Shame. I could do with a cup. But alas, this feast is the talk of the town. I am eager for it! Good man, that Audun.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hear me, friend. I have a haul of silver that will sink my ship. Can you help me spend it?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Keep it down, would you? You'll get yourself killed, flaunting like that, especially around here!

speaker: Eivor
en: What good is a market if I cannot sniff around the stalls, eager to spend my gains?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: You want to let go of your silver? Try the narrow alleys. Now begone.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Keep your focus. There was trouble at the depot earlier.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: What do you mean, trouble?

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: I don't know for sure, but The Needle is calling for more protection. Meet me here at nightfall. We will go see him together.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those guards will return after dark. I might be able to follow them to The Needle.

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: We will go one by one, and if any of these peddlers gives you a hard time, remind them just who it is they work for.

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: O', with pleasure.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hey, friend. I have a hoard of silver I am aching to spend. Can you help me? What have you got?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I have nothing left to trade, but Coppergate market is the right place. Ask around, you'll find someone who will bend an ear.

speaker: Eivor
en: My thanks.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hear this marketplace sees its fair share of silver pass through. I have something that may interest you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: You will want to speak to Grigorii.

speaker: Eivor
en: The dockmaster?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Sorry, who are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone who wants to do business. With Grigorii.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: I don't know your face, and I've said too much already. Please go.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 1
en: Psst. Psst! Hey!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 1
en: Did I hear you talking about silver?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am looking to spend a large sum, not fork it over to some street beggar.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 1
en: Oi! I'm no beggar, you dolt. I'm with the big dogs.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mean The Needle?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 1
en: You have something he wants. If you truly want to make a trade, head to the statue near the east gate.

speaker: Eivor
en: I shall. Watch yourself around here, young one.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 1
en: Who me? Ah! Please, I've a bigger sword than the lot of 'em.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is the statue the child talked about. Now, to find the hidden key.

speaker: Eivor
en: Found the key. Now, to locate the hideout.

speaker: Eivor
en: Empty carts... and a black cloth marking the house. This is the place.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hmm... locked.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Sorry I was late. The lady. You know how it is.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Just hurry, will you? We have rounds to make.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I follow them, they should lead me to The Needle.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: I will eat your eyes and make soup of your bones!

speaker: Eivor
en: A key. Where to?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hiding among the rats, Needle? Fitting.

speaker: Eivor
en: There must be another way in.

speaker: Eivor
en: The sound of metal... A workshop, in the sewers. What is The Needle's operation?

speaker: Eivor
en: All this silverware... some still in their crates. Has this all been seized as well?

speaker: Eivor
en: They are melting the silver into bars and coins. What do they plan on doing with it?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: No, please! Don't do this! I promise... I promise you your silver next week!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Please! Don't do this. It's a misunderstanding. That's all. I'll pay.

speaker: Norse Warrior 8
en: You had your chance.

speaker: Norse Warrior 8
en: Faster! Or would you prefer another thrashing?

speaker: Eivor
en: All this silver... it is being minted into coins.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not surprised to find you creeping down here.

speaker: Grigorii
en: You! You don't belong down here.

speaker: Eivor
en: "We run a clean dock in Jorvik." I believe those were your words. And yet here I find you, swimming in silver from all the wares you seized. Are you the Needle, or just another of his pawns?

speaker: Grigorii
en: You have it all wrong. The fabric of this world has been used up, torn, shredded, you see. Someone must be there to stitch it back together. Someone with a firm yet steady hand. Who can thread a needle. Someone like me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a shit poet, but at least my question is answered.

speaker: Grigorii
en: Yes, well, we all have our weaknesses. Yours appears to be the iron between us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Think your men are going to stop me?

speaker: Grigorii
en: I would not undermine them so. The Red Hand are loyal to our cause. Which is more than I can say for the merchants. Make it quick. Meet me in the marketplace when you are done.

speaker: Norse Warrior 9
en: Block the exits. Don't let this one escape!

speaker: Eivor
en: That damned bacraut (asshole)... slipped through my fingers. I'll finish this in Coppergate market.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: P-please, no! I-I can explain! Mercy!

speaker: Grigorii
en: No need. I am well versed in the spouting excuses of bottom-feeders like you. Come come... walk with me. It is good to walk.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Grigorii...

speaker: Grigorii
en: Good to take in the air. The sights. The sounds. The smells.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: P-please, Grigorii. I-I-I didn't think you would mind. It was just a few coins!

speaker: Grigorii
en: Shh shh... I understand. It's not your fault, it was mine, for thinking you had anything but empty air between your ears.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: With all the silver I've given you, I have nothing left to feed my children, let alone myself. Please, understand.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: O, dear God...

speaker: Grigorii
en: Merchants of Jorvik. I promised you a future rife with opportunity. And what was the one thing I asked in return? Do you remember?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Loyalty.

speaker: Grigorii
en: Loyalty!

speaker: Grigorii
en: Let this serve as a lesson, should any of you think it a good idea to threaten my operation.

speaker: Grigorii
en: I run this operation. I do the thinking. You do as you're told.

speaker: Grigorii
en: It is a simple demand. I bring you the wares. You get rid of them. You give the coin to my men and you don't. Ask. Questions.

speaker: Grigorii
en: You. I expect your payment by next nightfall. Do not fail me.

speaker: Grigorii
en: It's funny, as a child I thought of snow as the tears of God, frozen by our sins. Weak with hunger, I stared into the sky, hoping it was me He wept for. Me He sought to save.

speaker: Grigorii
en: But God did not save me. The Vault did. He took me to a fine house. Gave me hearty meals. A warm bed.

speaker: Grigorii
en: For the first time, someone extended a hand, showed me kindness. Compassion.

speaker: Grigorii
en: And it was then that I made a vow. I vowed to never turn my back on he who was there for me when God was not.

speaker: Eivor
en: So you served The Vault, knowing full well what he was a part of.

speaker: Grigorii
en: The Order made our paths intersect. I owed them a debt, and I repaid it by saving this city from its own destruction.

speaker: Odin
en: A life debt is a strong motivator. It took hold of this one's hugr, drove it, and never let go.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yet not with the same compassion you were shown. Too many have suffered by your hand in pursuit of this cause.

speaker: Grigorii
en: You're right. Perhaps I deserve this death. But I am but one cog in a large wheel. One that still turns unhindered.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not for long.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where you have gone, there will be no tears waiting for you.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: What news do you bring?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Needle will never sting again.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Well done, Eivor. Who was hiding behind the name

speaker: Hjorr
en: My love. There has been an attack at the markets. The dockmaster, Grigorii, is dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Needle. Sold off the wares he seized to collect silver for The Vault.

speaker: Hjorr
en: He had no such authority, why would anyone believe him?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The council seal. That rat!

speaker: Hjorr
en: This is getting out of hand. How he was able to obtain this is... concerning. I must return and prepare for the Yuletide feast, but I will do so with a bent ear and a keen eye. Be safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: One down, two left.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The Christian texts will lead to another, I'm sure of it. Search the archives.

speaker: Havi
en: Hopefully the dwarves have gained an understanding of the Salakar's true use. My future may depend on it... Ragnarök is inevitable. To avoid it, impossible. But if there is one thing I know... impossible is impossible.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Oh, you're back.

speaker: Havi
en: Sinmara's plans lie in ruins.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: I just hope you know what you're doing.

speaker: Havi
en: Surely I should be asking that of you? Now tell me, what does it do?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Ain't got a clue. These Light Elves and their sneaky―

speaker: Havi
en: You've learned nothing?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Whatever its use, the power it contains... it holds more than what you said.

speaker: Havi
en: Such as?

speaker: Brokkri
en: Well, for a start, there's a bloody dwarf in there.

speaker: Havi
en: ...Anyone we know?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Nah, and it's not important. Dwarf hugrs don't carry much weight. Not even mine.

speaker: Havi
en: So, what does it contain?

speaker: Brokkr
en: All I know is that it's more than Malvigr, Calder, and some dwarf no one cares about.

speaker: Havi
en: Fine. In the stories, what was the actual point of the Salakars?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Hugrs were what vitalized them, but it was the magic that gave them their purpose. And that magic was different to each one.

speaker: Havi
en: "Magic?" You mean seidr?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Nah, some elf shit no one knows anymore.

speaker: Havi
en: Except Surtr.

speaker: Brokkr
en: That fire nymph? She sent word.

speaker: Havi
en: And?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Your plan worked. Sinmara's ready to barter if it means getting you out of the way.

speaker: Havi
en: Where?

speaker: Brokkr
en: At the bridge leading to Feigardr. Light the beacon and she'll come out with your lad.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: The power that the Salakar holds... it must not fall into Surtr's grasp.

speaker: Havi
en: I'll reclaim it. Once Baldr is safe.

speaker: Brokkr
en: I've got a bad feeling about this.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: For once, we're in agreement.

speaker: Havi
en: Retaking the Salakar won't be easy. I may have to release Loki, and ask for his aid. His talent for theft is unmatched. What I have done to him, and him to me... Once I have rescued Baldr, we will be even. Loki will see that.

speaker: Havi
en: I must announce my arrival.

speaker: Sinmara
en: Do you bring that which is Surtr's?

speaker: Havi
en: Give me what is mine! And I will hand over what is his!

speaker: Sinmara
en: Come midway!

speaker: Havi
en: ...Baldr, I got you. I got you.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: Kill the Æsir! Quick!

speaker: Muspel Warrior 2
en: No mercy!

speaker: Havi
en: Baldr! Baldr!

speaker: Havi
en: I must get inside!

speaker: Havi
en: Baldr must be close for the illusion to have worked.

speaker: Havi
en: Baldr is behind one of these doors. Locked cells... I must find the proper keys.

speaker: Havi
en: It's written in Baldr's hand! No light but only darkness visible... revealing sights of woe, realms of endless agony. This hopelessness... It is not the Baldr I know, no matter his pain and turmoil.

speaker: Havi
en: One of the many prison keys... Not all of them are here, it seems.

speaker: Havi
en: I think there's something hidden in the back. The prisoners weren't just lying around.

speaker: Havi
en: So much death. The Muspels don't take no for an answer.

speaker: Havi
en: There is something on the other side. Maybe the dwarves hid something here?

speaker: Havi
en: A hidden room behind this wall? It seems nothing can contain these tricky inventors.

speaker: Havi
en: Ugh! I guess I shouldn't touch every piece of paper I find lying around.

speaker: Havi
en: Truly, Calder!? Truly!? You dare to torture my own flesh and blood!? If only I could bring you back from the dead and kill you all over again!

speaker: Havi
en: This blood trail... Whoever was dragged here was badly wounded... Yet he was strong. It took at least four jailers to hold him.

speaker: Havi
en: There! Beyond that door lies the dark heart of the prison... and my son.

speaker: Havi
en: No... No!

speaker: Sinmara
en: The High One. Brought low. Mistletoe...

speaker: Sinmara
en: ...symbol of hope. Renewal... but not for Baldr. We forced so many drafts down his gullet. His torment was... quite beautiful. Blind fool! You never saw what was in front of you.

speaker: Sinmara
en: Here is your child. His light gone before you even set foot here! And the rest of him? It now skulks in Helheim. Allow me to reunite you with your boy.

speaker: Eysa
en: No!

speaker: Sinmara
en: Traitor!

speaker: Sinmara
en: You were never worth my effort.

speaker: Sinmara
en: I've seen dwarves with better stature.

speaker: Sinmara
en: Take care of it.

speaker: Sinmara
en: Damn you, Eysa!

speaker: Sinmara
en: Thank you, Mad One! For giving me cause to stamp out my traitorous stepdaughter! I remember how Frigg's soft flesh parted beneath my blade!

speaker: Sinmara
en: Finally. The hero of Asgard. But you are an imposter! Heart as black as tar. Savage. Monstrous. You've locked that truth away. Built a code to act as its jailer. But the darkness cannot be kept hidden. It oozes out, like pus from a wound, poisoning everything it touches. That is what it means to be Odin the Deceiver.

speaker: Sinmara
en: You never fail to disappoint! You cluck and scratch like an old hen! If you're going to fight, fight!

speaker: Seer
en: Silence, you children of gods... And heed my tale of time's beginning. All was dark. There was no sand, there was no sea. No earth nor sky, no grass nor wind. 'Til fire met ice in the gasping void. And from this scream came the giant Ymir, first of all beings... Proud Ymir, cruelly killed. Yet from whose bones and blood and brains the world was made... The world you walk and war upon...

speaker: Young Eivor
en: There you are.

speaker: Skald
en: Eivor, here's a tune for you! One to liven your step.

speaker: Varin
en: Ah, there you are, my little drengr.

speaker: Varin
en: Go!

speaker: Varin
en: So, did you see our king?

speaker: Varin
en: Yes, good. Come, Eivor. Did you find the... the ring?

speaker: Varin
en: Yes. Now... now for our little plan. When you see us talking, be quiet as a wood mouse and then surprise him with our gift. And you hold it out like this and look him in the eyes and you say, "Styrbjorn King, may our clans be forever bonded in friendship and in love." You think you can do that for me?

speaker: Young Eivor
en: Mm-hmm.

speaker: Varin
en: Good. Tonight, you will be the cord that unites our people. And I'm so proud of you, Eivor.

speaker: Varin
en: Get up, Olaf! Stay lucid, friend!

speaker: Olaf
en: My sword is gore-greedy. I am ready to fight!

speaker: Holger
en: I hewed the heads of joyless hel-dogs! I imbibed Odin's brew and I snipped the scraggly beards of troll-kings! I danced naked upon the bleaching beaches...

speaker: Tove
en: Drink, Holger. And save your poems for your king.

speaker: Holger
en: He is your king as well.

speaker: Tove
en: He is, but I don't have to sing his praises for my meals.

speaker: Holger
en: Hello, little one! Ready to celebrate this great day?

speaker: Young Eivor
en: I have a gift for the king. Then I will dance.

speaker: Holger
en: Good! Kings love those arm-fetters. Raise your horn with me, Tove. Tonight we sleep in the heat of clan-fire. Made happy by mead.

speaker: Tove
en: Skal, you old skald!

speaker: Sigurd
en: O! No drink in your fist? Come on. I'll find you something.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can't. I have a tribute for your father.

speaker: Sigurd
en: O, what a piece! That must be worth two sturdy longships! Give it here. I'll pass it on.

speaker: Young Eivor
en: My father asked me, Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Suit yourself. But you're not getting any mead!

speaker: Norse Man
en: Valka's seiðr works through my hammer! (laugh)

speaker: Gunnar
en: When you speak with the king, hold it up to the light, show him the fine details. See there? I etched his name in runes, on the outer bend. You'll show him?

speaker: Eivor
en: Mm-hm.

speaker: Gunnar
en: You are just like your father, little berserker! Skal to you!

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Skal! (Cheers!)

speaker: Gunnar
en: You see? She agrees!

speaker: Rosta
en: So, you have the ring? Good. This was worn by your grandfather in a battle on the Northern Way.

speaker: Young Eivor
en: Mother?

speaker: Rosta
en: Yes?

speaker: Young Eivor
en: Can we show Sigurd the cairn stones we stacked yesterday?

speaker: Rosta
en: That's a good idea. We'll do that in the morning, at first light.

speaker: Rosta
en: Now go. You have a gift to deliver.

speaker: Varin
en: Eivor, wait.

speaker: Varin
en: Skal to Styrbjorn, the true King of Rygjafylke! Tonight we are all made anew! Skal!

speaker: Varin
en: Eivor. Eivor, come.

speaker: Young Eivor
en: King... May our clans be forever bonded in friendship and love.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Thank you, Eivor. Now and forever, I am pledged to you. (laugh)

speaker: Varin
en: Harken well in hall of kings...

speaker: Norse Soldiers
en: Hoo! Haa! Hoo! Ha!

speaker: Varin
en: On ocean-steed, my words gain wings. Odin's mead, I forth will bring. For noble deeds, thine honor sing!

speaker: Norse Soldiers
en: For noble deeds, thine honor sing!

speaker: Varin
en: The brave men slain, Valkyrjur wakes...

speaker: Norse Soldiers
en: The brave men slain, Valkyrjur wakes!

speaker: Varin
en: Reward for strain to Valholl takes!

speaker: Norse Soldiers
en: Reward for strain to Valholl takes!

speaker: Varin
en: Then horns resounds the mighty hall!

speaker: Norse Soldiers
en: Then horns resounds the mighty hall!

speaker: Varin & Norse Soldiers
en: For those who fight, for those who fall

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: We're under attack!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Kjotve's clan!

speaker: Varin
en: Ready yourselves, men! Ah!

speaker: Varin
en: Good Rosta, go. Not you, Eivor. Not just yet.

speaker: Svala
en: It is foretold. The curtains are raised. Nothing is true until it is severed from the branches of Yggdrasil.

speaker: Rosta
en: Down!

speaker: Rosta
en: Come. Eivor...

speaker: Rosta
en: Go! Now!

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Stop! Please!

speaker: Rosta
en: Ride! Go!

speaker: Varin
en: Kjotve! Show yourself!

speaker: Young Eivor
en: Momma!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Grah!

speaker: Young Eivor
en: Sigurd!

speaker: Varin
en: Kjotve! Let's end this bloodshed.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: O, I will!

speaker: Rosta
en: Speed to Valhalla.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Fire!

speaker: Rosta
en: Sigurd, take the horse.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Alright, wait here.

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: Now it's my turn to offer you a deal, slave-whore. Accept your fate and die a coward, here before your people... and I will spare the rest.

speaker: Rosta
en: Fight, my love! Do not listen!

speaker: Varin
en: If I give my life, will you spare my clan?

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: You have my word.

speaker: Rosta
en: No, no, Varin! No Varin! Pick up your axe.

speaker: Young Eivor
en: No!

speaker: Kjotve the Cruel
en: Kill them all!

speaker: Cynebert
en: O, you must try my ale sometime! You must! My abbey brews the best in Cent.

speaker: Basim
en: It certainly sounds worth the risk of my immortal soul.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Ah, your God is rather a hard taskmaster?

speaker: Basim
en: And your God forbids the . It sounds to me like he's never heard of England.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Not all that is written in the scriptures is God's honest truth.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I do a roaring trade at Reculver and Tunbridge. They pay well for my catch.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: The monks? Do those parchment-skinned Christians ever eat meat?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Don't you believe in Jesus? They refrain because he died for our sins.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: No one will stop me sucking the marrow of a nice leg of lamb. Not even God's seed.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Well, I hope eternal damnation is worth it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: It's rare to see Abbot Cynebert down this way.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Abbot who?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: You know, the rich one, the monastery that brews ale. He keeps half the menfolk in the county from their wives.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Ending up with an ale-soused wastrel is another reason I've not taken a husband.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: If you're waiting for a sober one, you'll die an old maid.

speaker: Basim
en: Eivor? You have news?

speaker: Eivor
en: Cent's new ealdorman will be Thegn Tedmund.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Tedmund! O, the Lord is testing me. He is made mouse by you Danes! Barely leaves his fortress at Rouecistre. How might I gain his influence if he will not speak to me? Or to anyone! 'Tis a puzzle.

speaker: Eivor
en: To inspire loyalty, Tedmund must owe you something. Such as... his life?

speaker: Cynebert
en: Go on...

speaker: Eivor
en: A fortress stormed, a man kidnapped. If you beat back his enemy, saved him from sure death, his gratitude would be...

speaker: Cynebert
en: Swell? It would know no bounds. But that fortress will be harder to pry open than a nun's knees.

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps, perhaps not.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you hiding something, Basim?

speaker: Eivor
en: Has he any family we could hold for ransom? You could swoop in, rescue them, play the hero.

speaker: Cynebert
en: There's nobody in this world that Tedmund cares more for than Tedmund. I could think on it, but we haven't much time.

speaker: Basim
en: There's another way. Much easier...

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you hiding something, Basim?

speaker: Eivor
en: We can take him from Rouecistre Fortress. We'll need a small, experienced force of men.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Rouecistre is not a house of straw and sticks! It is a garrison, crawling with soldiers. I don't see how it's possible.

speaker: Basim
en: I don't believe it's necessary...

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you hiding something, Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: There is a lumber mill nearby, correct?

speaker: Cynebert
en: Beamasfield. Aelfred invests much in fortifying Wessex, and uses our forest to do so. The mill provides his wood.

speaker: Basim
en: Tedmund is there.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Impossible! How do you know?

speaker: Basim
en: I heard rumors that Tedmund had been lured out of self-exile. To manage work on the fortifications on Canterbury.

speaker: Eivor
en: Taking him from a lumberyard is less dangerous than assaulting a fortress. But your rescue attempt will not have the same flair. Is it worth it?

speaker: Cynebert
en: It may still work. Yes, yes, bring him to the Megaliths.

speaker: Eivor
en: And Fulke?

speaker: Cynebert
en: When I have Tedmund's fealty, you shall have Fulke. Now go, I will rustle up a small rescue party.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm wary of this abbot, Basim. He is self-serving and evasive. Can he really deliver Fulke?

speaker: Basim
en: The abbot is a friend of Fulke's, that is clear.

speaker: Eivor
en: So long as he doesn't suspect our motive, we may have a chance.

speaker: Basim
en: Indeed. This brings to mind , perhaps you've heard of it? The scorpion and the frog.

speaker: Eivor
en: A children's story?

speaker: Basim
en: A cautionary tale. The scorpion wants to cross the river, but he cannot swim. So he enlists the help of the frog. The frog agrees to carry him on his back, extracting a promise that the scorpion will not sting him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me guess, the scorpion reneges, blaming his nature, and both drown?

speaker: Basim
en: The scorpion crosses the river and stings an innocent man, killing him. So, what does this tale tell us?

speaker: Eivor
en: That your stories are clouded and their meaning doubly so?

speaker: Basim
en: It shows that every tale has a thousand possible outcomes, many of which are surprising. If the abbot does not deliver Fulke, he will die at my hand, and we will continue our search.

speaker: Eivor
en: A sobering approach.

speaker: Basim
en: Beamasfield is just ahead. Lead, I will follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope this chase will catch us a plump hen.

speaker: Basim
en: Once the abbot has Tedmund's gratitude, he will deliver Fulke. It will cost us nothing more than this.

speaker: Eivor
en: If that leaden-wit keeps his word.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, you prefer to work in the shadows.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: One more time, I'm telling you. If he says my boots are dirty or my hair needs combing. I will split him open.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: You're full of swamp gas. You'll do what you always do, bow and scrape to our good Thegn Tedmund.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: I'm not even sure it's him we're working for.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: Don't be daft. Who else would it be? A changeling spirited there by fairy-folk? Get back to patrol.

speaker: Tedmund
en: Get back to work. Time is coin, and you're spending mine! Do you dare question the orders of the great Thegn Tedmund? I will have you flogged! I could throw a stone and hit a dozen men who'd do a better job than this! We have a quota to fill, we must keep the Danes from Cent!

speaker: Eivor
en: Danes? No, no! Protect me.

speaker: Tedmund
en: I'm not who you think I am! Let me go!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop caterwauling and you will live!

speaker: Tedmund
en: Live? O Saints protect me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Silence will save you, Tedmund! Silence, not your saints.

speaker: Basim
en: Flee, my friend. We have the man we came for. Does this venture not set your blood ablaze?

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't prefer working in the shadows?

speaker: Basim
en: And so we have. To steal a man, take him with swiftness, and escape without anyone on our heels. We hide in plain sight, such is our way. But only until the moment of success. The final strike.

speaker: Eivor
en: I prefer to act and speak plainly. Kings and lords who do not are often misunderstood.

speaker: Basim
en: Yet, as a leader yourself, you cannot deny that subtlety and intrigue are a cloak you must wear. How many of your clan know the true circumstances of Sigurd's absence?

speaker: Eivor
en: Mmm.

speaker: Basim
en: You see my point. A leader must know when to speak and when to stay silent, for silence is not always a lie.

speaker: Eivor
en: It can feel like one. You truly embrace the concept of hiding in plain sight, eh? To its very fullest.

speaker: Basim
en: As I do in everything.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Halt Danes! In the name of Aelfred, King of Wessex, I demand you release his royal subject into my care!

speaker: Basim
en: Come no closer, Christian! Else your man dies by my blade!

speaker: Tedmund
en: Please! I'm not the man you want.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep your eye on this one. He'll be worth a hefty bounty.

speaker: Basim
en: Any false moves and I will snip your heels.

speaker: Eivor
