en: We have your man. Now let's finish this shadow play and be gone.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Are you sure that's Tedmund? He's dressed as a lord, but that man is shorter and fatter than I recall.

speaker: Tedmund
en: I'm not Tedmund! I'm not! I swear upon the holy rood, I am not Thegn Tedmund!

speaker: Cynebert
en: What in Heaven's name is happening here?

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are you? Speak quickly, or I will slit your throat and leave you for the crows.

speaker: Shergar
en: Shergar! I am called Shergar! Lord Tedmund pays me a measly coin to serve as his double!

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother Shergar? You are far from Augustine's priory!

speaker: Cynebert
en: I left the cloisters many moons ago, Your Holiness. The monastic life was not my calling.

speaker: Eivor
en: We can use you yet, Shergar. Summon Tedmund to a meeting. Get him out in the open.

speaker: Shergar
en: Tedmund has no care for me or what I have to say. My orders come from letter, never by mouth. I hardly know the man.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're of no use to us then. Perhaps I should just kill you, here and now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rouecistre is our only path forward, whether by stealth or force. Shergar, has the fortress any weaknesses? Any breaches or water wells we might use?

speaker: Shergar
en: I ... I couldn't say. I've only been there once. But Tedmund has holed himself in its keep, and that's all but impregnable.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're of no use to us then. Perhaps I should just kill you, here and now.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're of no use to us then. Perhaps I should just kill you, here and now.

speaker: Shergar
en: No! Wait, wait. Let me think. Let me think! Ah! Danes! To storm the walls, you need Danes! There's a raiding camp west of here I was told to be wary of. Acting as Tedmund, I ordered a band of soldiers to capture them. If you hurry, you may be able to stop this.

speaker: Eivor
en: If another band of Danes wants to join our assault, we'll have the distraction we need to get inside Rouecistre.

speaker: Basim
en: If the Saxons don't slaughter them first.

speaker: Shergar
en: I am still Tedmund to the men in the field. I could speak with their captain, send his men away.

speaker: Basim
en: It's a fearless plan.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Nornir knit winding paths that cannot be unknotted. It seems Rouecistre was always in our path. Abbot, stay alert. We will send word when we are ready to capture Tedmund.

speaker: Cynebert
en: And this fool? He knows much of our plan.

speaker: Eivor
en: He'll come with us. And if he betrays me, I will roast his balls over a roaring fire.

speaker: Shergar
en: You will not regret this! My wily ways and quick wit will cease the need for bloodshed.

speaker: Basim
en: I still might kill you yet, man, if your prattling doesn't cease.

speaker: Shergar
en: The rewards for being Tedmund are rapidly diminishing.

speaker: Basim
en: And how does one become a double? Are there vigorous challenges and tests to overcome?

speaker: Shergar
en: I was born with the misfortune of looking like someone else. I should have stayed on God's chosen path.

speaker: Eivor
en: What took you from it?

speaker: Shergar
en: I am the seventh son of a poor farmer. And not wanting another mouth to feed, my father gave me to the monks.

speaker: Basim
en: The cloistered life did not suit you?

speaker: Shergar
en: I thought there would be great comfort in repetition. But instead, I found nothing but prayer and backbreaking toil.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Norns weave strange destinies. Now your life depends on the story you weave for yourself.

speaker: Shergar
en: I am not a good forgery. Stilted, leaden, my hands sweat, and I have a stutter when I am nervous. But I will try.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, the cornerstone of all great art.

speaker: Shergar
en: The captain does not know Tedmund well. If we keep our heads, he will not question my orders. I hope.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do what you want with him. I won't risk our plan on the shambling of this fool.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Come, Brother Shergar, and perhaps today would be the time to consider a vow of silence?

speaker: Eivor
en: An army of Danes are all we need to take the fortress.

speaker: Basim
en: Let us hope.

speaker: Basim
en: It is best to snare a wasp with honey. Have you ever considered more subtlety?

speaker: Eivor
en: I leave manipulation to you, Basim. You appear to see it as an art.

speaker: Basim
en: It is both art and science to bend a man to your will. And harder still to convince them that they are firmly in control.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shergar was quick to betray his lord. Do you not think he would sell us out as swiftly?

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps. Perhaps not. I do not presume to know a man's heart in so brief a meeting.

speaker: Eivor
en: His prattle was sad and ugly. Like a weeping babe.

speaker: Basim
en: You have little patience for chittering squirrels.

speaker: Eivor
en: And yet I allow you to squeak in my ear. Along all the roads and byways of Cent.

speaker: Basim
en: Because you are wise, and you see the same qualities in me.

speaker: Eivor
en: That must be it.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are nearing the camp. Let us hope there are Danes enough to storm a fortress. Otherwise, this abbot's game is a long one.

speaker: Basim
en: It must be played if we are to reclaim Sigurd.

speaker: Basim
en: We are too late. There is great horror here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those who remain must be saved. Whatever the cost.

speaker: Shergar
en: Let us approach the captain with caution. He drinks too much and does not need a reason to kill us.

speaker: Shergar
en: Yes, it is I, Thegn Tedmund. Coming to discuss the orders I gave you not one day ago.

speaker: Basim
en: This ham hock will get us all killed.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Oi, let us free, you festering canker on a sow's arse! You murdered our people! Men, women, children! Your sister rides your piss-soaked rod.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 5
en: Pipe down you dogs. You're slaves of Cent now.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Thegn Tedmund? What are you doing here?

speaker: Shergar
en: How dare you address me in such a defiant manner! Don't you know who I am?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: You are Tedmund, as I said. And I mean no disrespect, lord... but I was told you were back in Rouecistre.

speaker: Shergar
en: O yes? And do I, um... do I look like I'm in Rouecistre?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: You... do not, sir.

speaker: Basim
en: A wise man is always unexpected.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: You travel in strange company, lord. An Arab and... a Dane?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm here to advise your thegn in the ways of my people.

speaker: Shergar
en: That is correct! A cultural exchange of sorts... perhaps one day I will visit... your... um... Dane... Dane-land.

speaker: Eivor
en: Norway.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mistake me for a foreigner, but are we not all just the measure of the places we have seen?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Right, well... that aside, have you any further orders, lord?

speaker: Shergar
en: Yes, yes, I order... I order you... to stop loitering and return to your barracks, you scab-wit.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: And what of the captured Danes?

speaker: Shergar
en: You must kill them all! Every last− Sorry, no. Leave them here. Tied up. As a... a feast for wolves and crows. That is all. You may depart. Shoo.

speaker: Eivor
en: A convincing ruse that has earned you your freedom. Go. And make your life anew, not in another man's boots.

speaker: Shergar
en: I will. This small sup of power has got me thinking, perhaps I can be a leader of men?

speaker: Shergar
en: Yes, yes. Hurry along, men. Warm thighs and ale awaits!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Come on, you laggards! You have Tedmund's orders.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mistake me for a foreigner, but are we not all just the measure of the places we have seen?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Right, well... that aside, have you any further orders, lord?

speaker: Shergar
en: Yes, yes, I order... I order you... to stop loitering and return to your barracks, you scab-wit.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: And what of the captured Danes?

speaker: Shergar
en: You must kill them all! Every last− Sorry, no. Leave them here. Tied up. As a... a feast for wolves and crows. That is all. You may depart. Shoo.

speaker: Eivor
en: A convincing ruse that has earned you your freedom. Go. And make your life anew, not in another man's boots.

speaker: Shergar
en: I will. This small sup of power has got me thinking, perhaps I can be a leader of men?

speaker: Shergar
en: Yes, yes. Hurry along, men. Warm thighs and ale awaits!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Come on, you laggards! You have Tedmund's orders.

speaker: Eivor
en: To Hel with this talk. Let Saxon blood soak this land!

speaker: Eivor
en: God speed, Danes. This is too rich for my blood.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Oi, let us free, you festering canker on a sow's arse! You murdered our people! Men, women, children! Your sister rides your piss-soaked rod.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 5
en: Pipe down you dogs. You're slaves of Cent now.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: You will not see another sunrise, swine balls!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tied up like animals. I need to free them.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: We owe you our lives, friend. These Saxon whoresons would have killed us all.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, they would have. And now's your chance to hit back. March with us on Rouecistre and drain it of riches.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: I would gladly, friend. But we few will not break those iron-thick walls.

speaker: Basim
en: And we have no allies in Wessex, none who could be called upon to attack their countrymen.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mercia will heed the call. Geadric will provide our vikingr hoard. We'll send a message to Oxenefordscire. The men of Mercia would gladly take a swipe at Wessex. What is your name, warrior?

speaker: Runa
en: Runa Egilsdottir.

speaker: Eivor
en: We need ships, Runa.

speaker: Runa
en: We have a small fleet moored upriver. But a naval chain blocks passage to Rouecistre's walls.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will remove it, and your people will bring their ships. Now, gather these fallen weapons and armor. Geadric and the men of Oxenefordscire will need them to hide their Mercian origins.

speaker: Runa
en: My warriors were denied Valhalla today. I cannot bear the idea of gifting their weapons to more Saxons.

speaker: Basim
en: Their sacrifice was great... their gift will be all the greater.

speaker: Eivor
en: And they will know justice with our victory. It will calm their restless shades. I promise. Will your men bring the armor to the battle?

speaker: Basim
en: And what is our plan?

speaker: Eivor
en: In the morning, you will go to Buckingham, remind Geadric of his promise. When you have his bond, meet me on the shore near Rouecistre, with his ships.

speaker: Basim
en: Abbot Cynebert must be warned in advance. He'll need time to muster his rescue party.

speaker: Eivor
en: Runa, that is your task. I'll tell you where to meet him before you leave.

speaker: Basim
en: All seems in order. At first new light, I will leave.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. That gives us time to drink.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've traveled so far to carry out your duty. Is this the life of a Hidden One? Always on the move?

speaker: Basim
en: Mine is not the usual path. The creed does travel. Our ideals are universal, we believe that.

speaker: Eivor
en: So there's nowhere you call home?

speaker: Basim
en: No place I call home. No.

speaker: Eivor
en: Weird.

speaker: Basim
en: For me, home is family. But I have no family.

speaker: Eivor
en: No one? Not even Hytham?

speaker: Basim
en: Parents, brothers, all dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: I lost my parents when I was nine winters along. Without Sigurd, I would've... I would've.

speaker: Basim
en: There is always one unbreakable bond.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes.

speaker: Basim
en: Children, they bewilder you. They can cause you so much worry, fill you with joy. Even stop your heart. And if you're lucky, they replace you.

speaker: Basim
en: I was not so lucky. I had a son. I miss him terribly. Even now.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sorry, Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: He was taken from me. By someone I trusted. A friend, a mentor. A man who I would trust with anything. But a man you trust with anything... can take everything.

speaker: Basim
en: He took all I had.

speaker: Basim
en: All I had.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rouecistre will not be an easy nut to crack. Time to prepare.

speaker: Rolf the Raider
en: You there! You look like you could handle yourself in a fight. Eivor Wolf-Kissed, is that you? Make way for Eivor, the Terror of the Western Shores!

speaker: Eivor
en: It is Rolf, ja? We raided with you that one time, up on the northern coast.

speaker: Rolf
en: I am flattered you remember.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was the first time Styrbjorn let us raid so far from home. And Sigurd was sure you took more than your fair share. You are still raiding at your age?

speaker: Rolf
en: We need to grab what we can before Harald has his say across Norway. But I only plan them now. I let others do the heavy work. In fact, I am looking for someone to lead my crew.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would like to help you out, but I have my own crew now.

speaker: Rolf
en: I did not mean you, but I could use your help choosing a leader. I have picked out a few to be tested.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tested how?

speaker: Rolf
en: If you want to see someone's true character, test it in battle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Show me your picks.

speaker: Rolf
en: My crew is gathered down by the docks. Locals mostly. Even a couple farmers hungry for excitement.

speaker: Eivor
en: How do they compare to me and Sigurd?

speaker: Rolf
en: There is no comparing. You are building some reputation, Eivor. They talk about you up and down the coast.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good talk or bad?

speaker: Rolf
en: Depends on who you talk to. Mostly good. Do not worry about the bad.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, they should worry about me.

speaker: Rolf
en: This is my raiding crew, Eivor. What they lack in experience, they make up for in... other areas.

speaker: Rolf
en: Together, we will hammer these lumps of meat into men and women of iron. Into raiders.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, which from this unlucky lot would lead your crew?

speaker: Rolf
en: See, that big brute? Audbjorn. He does not speak much, but he could power a ship by himself.

speaker: Rolf
en: That shield-maiden is Ashild the Keen. Her blade is as quick as her wits. And then, there is Thorgils...

speaker: Thorgils of the Thick Head
en: Rolf! Who is your friend?

speaker: Rolf
en: Keep your head on the fight or someone will crack it!

speaker: Thorgils
en: All right!

speaker: Rolf
en: That one is so thick, he could shatter your shield, but the other men like him. And those are the best of the bunch.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, those three, ja? I have handled more.

speaker: Rolf
en: You want to fight them all at once?

speaker: Eivor
en: Why not? Raids are the stuff of chaos itself. They need a test with no rules.

speaker: Rolf
en: Challenge them, but do not damage them. It was hard enough finding this many.

speaker: Rolf
en: Listen up, you sea slugs. This is Eivor Wolf-Kissed, who has killed more men than you will ever meet.

speaker: Thorgils
en: Eivor Wolf-Kissed! I've heard of you! This will be great!

speaker: Rolf
en: You want to lead my crew, you must fight Eivor. Best fighter wins. No killing, no maiming. Other than that, no rules. Understand?

speaker: Thorgils
en: I am rea

speaker: Rolf
en: Fight!

speaker: Eivor
en: A raider needs to be ruthless.

speaker: Ashild
en: I am better than any man here.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have much to learn.

speaker: Thorgils
en: Have I won?

speaker: Eivor
en: You will have to fight me first. Maybe you want to sit back down.

speaker: Thorgils
en: No, no, I will be fine. And do not worry about me, worry about yourself!

speaker: Rolf
en: That's enough!

speaker: Thorgils
en: Did I win?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, but you fought well. You have a good chance.

speaker: Thorgils
en: I would rather have some mead...

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you see what you were looking for?

speaker: Rolf
en: Yes. I did not think Thorgils could do it, but he is thick-headed, like his old man.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait - That is your boy? Tiny Thor? He used to barely reach my belly.

speaker: Rolf
en: He has grown, and now he will want to take everything from me. But such is the way of children. Take some silver for your trouble, and a little extra. For cheating you and Sigurd on that raid. Good luck!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Oswald is dead! Oswald is dead! We mourn the loss of our future king and hope for East Anglia! We will remember his brave fight in Dunwic. We will remember his sword against Rued's. And above all we shall remember the man's devotion to God and his mission. Raise your mugs to Oswald tonight at the Spanking Pig! That is what the man would have wanted!

speaker: Finnr
en: Another king lost, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop washing your face with mead.

speaker: Finnr
en: How can I face Halfdan Jarl now? I've failed him again.

speaker: Eivor
en: We can take the battle to what remains of Rued's clan, before they hit back.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have not failed him. Rued's clan is badly weakened. We can still cure what ails this land.

speaker: Finnr
en: What thegns (nobles) would risk their arses now? Oswald was the last with even a scrap of courage.

speaker: Eivor
en: We can take the battle to what remains of Rued's clan, before they hit back.

speaker: Eivor
en: These storm clouds of despair will not solve anything, Finnr. We need action.

speaker: Finnr
en: What action?

speaker: Eivor
en: We can take the battle to what remains of Rued's clan, before they hit back.

speaker: Finnr
en: Easier said than done. His men are holed up at Burgh Castle, a fortress on the sea.

speaker: Eivor
en: On the sea? Then it must have a harbor.

speaker: Finnr
en: It does. Guarded by a gate of hefty iron, held in place by timber spikes. Difficult to force open.

speaker: Eivor
en: Timber burns.

speaker: Finnr
en: It does. But how do we reach it?

speaker: Eivor
en: We rig your ship with oil at her front and sail it ablaze at the gate.

speaker: Finnr
en: They would see us coming. Long before we reached the walls.

speaker: Eivor
en: We raise a ', an army of East Anglia's farmers. Throw them at the front gate as a distraction.

speaker: Finnr
en: Saxons willing to die for a bunch of Danes? It's a stretch.

speaker: Valdis
en: It can work, Finnr. If they fight in Oswald's name, that is all the courage they will need.

speaker: Finnr
en: Hmph.

speaker: Valdis
en: You there. Did you hear of Thegn Oswald's fate?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Aye, we did. He dragged Rued to the bowels of Hell, the Dane devil.

speaker: Valdis
en: Rued may be gone, but his clan still plagues East Anglia. Would you join us to rid your kingdom of his dogs?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: For Oswald? Aye! Anything!

speaker: Finnr
en: Two eager Saxons is not yet a fyrd (peasant army). But you may be right. We may have a chance.

speaker: Valdis
en: I can ride to Elmenham and muster what remains of Oswald's men there. But who else would join us?

speaker: Finnr
en: The Reeve (Sheriff) of Theotford, Wynnstan. He is a bitter old barnacle, but he would fight to the death for this land.

speaker: Valdis
en: We can assemble a forward camp at the ruins north of Burgh Castle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ride with me, Finnr. Let's pay this reeve a visit.

speaker: Finnr
en: With any hope, Theotford remains untouched by Rued's violence.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hope is a scarce word in this kingdom.

speaker: Finnr
en: Maybe so, but I would rather hold on to something, anything, than ride with empty hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: If Rued's clan continues to roam this kingdom unchecked, the people of East Anglia will be as ravaged as these lands.

speaker: Finnr
en: And where do we find ourselves? Riding into the fens to beg a horde of frightened farmers for aid.

speaker: Eivor
en: To fight for a king that you gave them, Finnr. Remember that.

speaker: Finnr
en: It was my task to find them a king, not protect that king against every danger that might befall him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald wasn't crowned yet. Nor was he married. I say you have some work yet to do.

speaker: Finnr
en: Right, right. No need to remind me how far I fell short.

speaker: Eivor
en: Watch your back. Rued's clan may still be nearby.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: These fucking farmers must have more than this.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: What did you expect, brother? Sword and silver? We had a bit of fun! That's what matters.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: The Wolf-Kissed one! This day keeps getting better.

speaker: Finnr
en: East Anglia has suffered enough under you!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: And we're not done yet, old man!

speaker: Eivor
en: Rued's men are a blight on this land.

speaker: Finnr
en: Blight is too kind a word. A seer's curse!

speaker: Finnr
en: Theotford. Just ahead...

speaker: Eivor
en: Woodsmoke and ash. Rued's men have been here.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Eat, my child. These are no times to waste what the lord has given us.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: What about you, Papa? There's so little. There will be none left.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Eat so you'll have strength.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Everything is gone, Reeve (Sheriff)! Everything!

speaker: Wynnstan
en: Calm, my friend. We will rebuild. I promise you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: I en't got the strength no more.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: Stand tall.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: You have a will of iron coming here, knowing your kind did all this!

speaker: Eivor
en: Rued's clan is your enemy, not me. I come on behalf of the late Oswald of Elmenham.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: You're still a Dane from top to toe. And it's your meddling that led to Oswald's death, leaving our kingdom for the worse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald was a friend and ally, reeve. He fought beside me, and I by him.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: And look where that got him.

speaker: Eivor
en: East Anglia will fall if Rued's clan is not defeated. Fight with me to drive them off, for Oswald and your kinsmen.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald died defending East Anglia, defending you. Will you not do the same?

speaker: Wynnstan
en: What? Die in defense of a lost cause? I have problems of my own.

speaker: Eivor
en: East Anglia will fall if Rued's clan is not defeated. Fight with me to drive them off, for Oswald and your kinsmen.

speaker: Eivor
en: East Anglia will fall if Rued's clan is not defeated. Fight with me to drive them off, for Oswald and your kinsmen.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: Pretty words, Dane. But the men of Theotford have their own battles to fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you need an axe, I am standing right here.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: There's a village to the east, King's Bury. It was taken by Rued's men a fortnight ago. And I'll not rest until it's back in our hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me and my raiders take the village. Save your strength and join us for the fight to come.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: A bold offer... If you do as you promise, the pikes of Theotford will be yours.

speaker: Finnr
en: I will take this news to our forward camp, Eivor. Follow when you can.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will see you there.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: King's Bury's church has a great horn atop its steeple. If you manage the task, blow it and I'll know you kept your word.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: You there, Dane. A word, if you will.

speaker: Eivor
en: You called to me?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: We heard you talking with the reeve (sheriff). And we wish to fight beside you. We owe Oswald for his good deeds and fair rule.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm glad to hear it. Go to the ruins north of Burgh Castle. The army gathers there.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Have you seen Mother?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: O, blessed. Your mother? When was last you saw her?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Before the bad men came. Said she'd be right back. But she ain't.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: She will be, little one, I'm sure of it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: If you say so.

speaker: Eivor
en: King's Bury. Infested with Rued's men.

speaker: Eivor
en: Time to sound the horn and signal victory.

speaker: Elegy for the Royal Martyr
en: Here lies Edmund, father of East Anglia, a good and godly man. May he lie here in peace, surrounded by the children of God, until Doomsday whent he dust shall return to the earth, and the spirit shall return unto Heaven. Lord have mercy on his soul.

speaker: Eivor
en: The reeve (sheriff) has come to join me. Let's hope his promise holds.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: The horn! It's been so long since I've heard that sweet sound.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: Praise be.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: Hail, Dane! Over here!

speaker: Eivor
en: I held to my oath, reeve. I hope you will honor yours.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: My promise holds, aye. Theotford will join you in the fight against Rued's clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: With your aid, we may yet save East Anglia.

speaker: Wynnstan
en: In past times, that horn was used to muster fyrds all across our land. You may find others who have warmed to its call.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Whatever willing men you find, rally them soon at the ruins north of Burgh Castle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wenlocan Outpost. If I take the cargo here, the Britons will be weakened and want peace.

speaker: Briton Warrior 1
en: We were fools! "Peace," they said. "There'll be peace!" And what? Of course there's no peace!

speaker: Briton Warrior 2
en: I've fought in this miserable country for two years gone. Lost half me foot and most of me mind.

speaker: Briton Warrior 1
en: We kill them, they kill us. They kill us, we kill them. Simple as that.

speaker: Briton Warrior 2
en: All part o' God's grand plan.

speaker: Note of a Giving Soul
en: A dead man spoke to me! Poor fellow, he look like he died rough. Said a few coins would help him on his way to the afterlife. He frightened me worse than a lightning storm. I gave him all I had. I must ask a priest if I'm cursed.

speaker: Baeldaeg
en: You! Dane! Get me out of this cursed chicken coop!

speaker: Eivor
en: Men for Deorlaf's . More valuable than cargo.

speaker: Eivor
en: I give you freedom. Now you give your shire your pike.

speaker: Baeldaeg
en: I will.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's done. Now to track down their supply line. We'll drag Rhodri back to the peace table soon enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quarry and cargo done. Now to meet Ivarr and Ceolbert in Wesberie, before Ivarr stirs up more trouble.

speaker: Orders Concerning Prisoners
en: Should you capture any Saxons, keep them alive. We'll make use of them to build earthen works or to work the quarry. Ynyr ap Cadfarch.

speaker: Azar
en: Eivor. Welcome to my shop.

speaker: Eivor
en: I came to ask a favor.

speaker: Azar
en: It is pleasant to strengthen friendships. What do you seek?

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid wishes to show Flann the value of Dublin's trade. Could we obtain a gift from a distant land?

speaker: Azar
en: This is the very problem vexing me. You see, I have acquired land in Rathdown. Previously owned by Thorstein, in fact. But the land has gone to thorn and dog. Smugglers as well! Once cleared, its trading route will serve our hearts' desire.

speaker: Eivor
en: In this case, my heart desires an exotic gift. Which would be...?

speaker: Azar
en: A spice merchant I know covets pelts of fine fur. Rathdown has an abundance. It is a perfect match.

speaker: Eivor
en: Spice is a gift fit for a king. Thank you, Azar.

speaker: Azar
en: It is north of here. You go clear of it smugglers, while I sit on my ass. No need for thanks.

speaker: Eivor
en: Smugglers. Azar needs them cleared away.

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: Are you Eivor? Over here.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are one of Azar's men?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: I am. Azar tells me you two are interested in furs to trade for a gift.

speaker: Eivor
en: It will show King Flann the reach of Bárid's trade.

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: We'll get the furs you need.

speaker: Eivor
en: How can I help?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: With trade post supplies, we'll build up the post for better and faster trade.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where would I get these supplies?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: Monasteries are a good place. They'll have what you'll need.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm curious how you and Azar work together.

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: I gather pelts, treat 'em and send the fur to Dublin. Azar trades them across the seas. We want to build up the post. Both to send bundles of furs to Azar more often, and to store more to send.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ireland must have many trading posts.

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: It does. Each post trades specific goods. Here, we gather furs, but elsewhere, all manner of things.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, friend.

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: Goodbye, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: The supplies the overseer spoke of.

speaker: Eivor
en: This should be enough supplies to build something.

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: I see by your smile that the expedition was fruitful. Should we build something?

speaker: Irish Man 1
en: Well done. We'll send the furs to Dublin. Azar will help you find more posts to capture.

speaker: Eivor
en: Goodbye, friend.

speaker: Azar
en: Eivor, the furs have arrived from Rathdown. We can now trade for Flann's gift. Come, check the storage.

speaker: Eivor
en: Azar, you have your trade post.

speaker: Azar
en: In fact, I have heard from the trader himself. We have furs enough for Flann's gift. Here, my friend. Make the trade.

speaker: Azar
en: Fine spices that cannot be obtained anywhere else. I will see them delivered for the coronation. Flann will certainly grasp the strength of Dublin's trade. Speaking of, Eivor, there are abandoned trade posts across Ireland.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're suggesting I claim them to increase Dublin's reach.

speaker: Azar
en: We will gain access to goods we could not otherwise obtain. There is great bounty to be had.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will look for opportunities. Meanwhile, I'll find Bárid. He'll be pleased to hear of Flann's gift.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: After all that has happened... what if Soma is just cursed with bad luck?

speaker: Galinn
en: Soma has only ever pleased the gods. Deserting her now, breaking your oath, that is what will bring us ill luck. Eivor. I'm honored you have joined us.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's your plan here?

speaker: Galinn
en: All the shire supports Soma ruling the city. These hamlets do not. They're feeding and outfitting Wigmund's army. So we will burn their homes, quick and devastating, like the thunderclaps of Thor.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you come to be in Soma's clan?

speaker: Galinn
en: A vision from a set me on this path. It pricked my mind like a splinter, then faded. But I wanted more. For months, years, I ate only , mushrooms, sacred plants, hoping to see something new. But my body dwindled. I lived addled, maddened, a wanderer. Taken in by Saxons and spat out... again and again. Until Soma found me, naked and alone in the fens. She clothed and cared for me, humbled as I was. I owe her my life.

speaker: Eivor
en: Visions can be strange and powerful. What did you see?

speaker: Galinn
en: I was climbing a mountain, a lion and a snake upon my back, weighing me down. I struggled. Then Soma appeared, and she eased my burden. When we reached the peak, there was hardly enough room to stand. On a point like the tip of a blade, we teetered there, gripping one another. Tightly. I know I can seem distant, obsessed. But the gods are with us always. I see it as my duty to shelter Soma from their ire.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you think of the others, Lif and Birna?

speaker: Galinn
en: Lif, he's a talented sailor. If a little... enthusiastic. And Birna, well... Birna thinks of life as a grand joke. She was a smuggler when Soma pulled her from the muck, making a living on lies. Birna is part of my clan, and I will fight beside her, irreverent as she is. But she has no care for her destiny.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am eager to start throwing torches.

speaker: Galinn
en: Now let's rid these hamlets of Wigmund's rats. Light your torches and set arrow tips ablaze, Eivor. The red enemy of the branch will make quick work of this place.

speaker: Galinn
en: We are a curse, visited upon them all!

speaker: Eivor
en: Leave no house unburnt.

speaker: Galinn
en: This is what they get for helping rend Grantebridge from Soma!

speaker: Eivor
en: For licking Ealdorman Wigmund's boots!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: Bring their heads to Ealdorman Wigmund!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. The smell of burning roof thatch and heady turf fire.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now that was something. Wigmund is sure to take notice.

speaker: Galinn
en: You stamped and roared like fiery Surtr himself, marching through the flames of Muspelheim. I'll see you back home, drengr (courageous warrior).

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ubba Ragnarsson has come. He claims to have some business with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ubba Ragnarsson. You are a long way from your king's side.

speaker: Ubba
en: Eivor, yes. A long stroll through the hils and fields of Mercia. All so I could thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank me?

speaker: Ubba
en: For sending my brother to his just rewards, in spite of the harm he caused you and everyone around you. I could not keep him in line in this life. But I have no doubt the All-Father will put him to good use in the next.

speaker: Eivor
en: A darkness followed your brother, one I am not sure he understood. But as you say, he is now where he belongs.

speaker: Ubba
en: He is. And as a show of thanks, I came to offer you a gift. A token of my respect.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you.

speaker: Ubba
en: Put it to good use Wolf-Kissed. And may we meet again soon. On a battlefield, if the fates are kind.

speaker: Eivor
en: My mind is fixed on Suthsexe. Basim and I have a chance to save Sigurd. But we will need an army.

speaker: Randvi
en: That is for you to decide. The more alliances you have, the better your chances at victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will go now. And I will bring Sigurd back with me. That is a promise.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. I will send word to our allies at once. Meet with Basim when you can. He should be in Croindene by now.

speaker: Eivor
en: The breadbasket of Wessex. Land of plenty.

speaker: Broder
en: Is Lunden as dark and grubby as they say?

speaker: Erke
en: Not since it almost burned to the ground. All those charred roof timbers really let in the light.

speaker: Brothir
en: I heard about that. The whole waterfront, up in flames.

speaker: Stowe
en: With that aside, we are making great strides to improve the lives of its people.

speaker: Broder
en: If Eivor does not show soon, I am packing and riding home.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Shut your blowhole, Broder. You want me to tell Halfdan how easily you break an oath?

speaker: Brothir
en: Ah, Brother! Did you forget she has Halfdan Jarl's ear? Stop talking if you know what's good for you.

speaker: Broder
en: With mighty Eivor at our head, we cannot fail!

speaker: Guthrum
en: You can always fail. Believing you cannot is the first step.

speaker: Brothir
en: There's a cheery thought.

speaker: Brothir
en: Eivor, you giant steaming bowl of elk piss! King Oswald sends his regards.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brothir, Broder. Or is it the other way around?

speaker: Broder
en: Gods, you're a sight to stir a weary heart.

speaker: Brothir
en: It is not his heart that's stirring...

speaker: Broder
en: It's, ah... good to see you Eivor.

speaker: Brothir
en: O, stop mewing like a heartstruck kitten! He's been moping since the wedding.

speaker: Eivor
en: There will be time later to reminisce. Are you madmen ready to spill some blood?

speaker: Brothir
en: After that bastard Rued, some nice soft Saxons will make easy meat for my blade.

speaker: Stowe
en: Eivor! My second favorite Norse!

speaker: Eivor
en: Must we always drift together on such violent tides?

speaker: Stowe
en: That is the way of things. Yet the meeting of friends is a glimmer of light in these dark days.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ever the optimist, Stowe. It's good to see you both.

speaker: Erke
en: I brought no pleasant words, only my blade. Let's see which proves more useful.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ljufvina! Once again we will battle side-by-side!

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Greeting from the North, old friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how is Hjorr?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Still griping about the mess we made of Jorvik's council. But grateful for the help. To be honest, I think he's upset he didn't see the problem sooner. His pride is slow to heal.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you for heeding my call, friend. Sigurd will be grateful when he hears you have come.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: For your brother, I would upturn every rock in England.

speaker: Guthrum
en: You wouldn't be the first man to fall asleep on watch. But you would be the loudest.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: I did not mean to fail you, Guthrum Jarl. It was only for a moment. I was so tired.

speaker: Guthrum
en: As are we all boy. We marched hard to get here.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Still, let's not disappoint me again. You hear?

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: My jarl! I'm...sorry...

speaker: Guthrum
en: You must be Eivor. I've heard much of you, young one. They say you're something. We'll see.

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum Jarl, Saxon-bane and reaver of the south. I'm honored to meet you at last.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Respect where it is due. I like that. Here's hoping you fight as smoothly as you talk.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor of the Raven Clan. I have carved a furrow through this teeming land, and the skalds sing loud of my deeds.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Those who boast have something to prove. The great have no need for it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay around a while and judge for yourself.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Oh I will. have no fear of that.

speaker: Basim
en: Eivor hopes to rescue Sigurd from the madwoman Fulke, now ensconced in Portcestre fortress. If you wish to crown yourself King of Wessex, Portcestre must fall. An alliance here serves us both.

speaker: Guthrum
en: You promised a great army, but you couldn't breach a crone's garden with what you have assembled here.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is not the sum of my forces. Where are the rest?

speaker: Basim
en: Your allies are on their way. We must be patient.

speaker: Eivor
en: We cannot wait for them. We march as soon as we are able.

speaker: Guthrum
en: With these numbers? Are you keen to see Valhalla today?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not sit on my heels while Sigurd rots in that she-dog's care!

speaker: Basim
en: We might muster for an attack in the woods east of Portcestre, but there are scouts between there and here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Scouts I can manage. Point me at them and I will blind Fulke's eyes.

speaker: Basim
en: One walks the road between Briggworth and Cicestre, another on the river bank north of Crawleah. A third keeps watch on the hills south of Croindene. But I warn you, these are all we know of. There may be more.

speaker: Eivor
en: A risk we must take. I will find the scouts. You move the men into position near Portcestre.

speaker: Guthrum
en: That is a rash gamble, Raven-Feeder. If we are spotted, we will be vulnerable.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you want victory, come now or not at all. Every hour we waste could be Sigurd's last.

speaker: Guthrum
en: You had better be all they promised.

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim, good to find you here. What news do you have?

speaker: Basim
en: Fulke remains at Portcestre, just as we suspected. And as of three days ago, Sigurd was with her, alive.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is the best news we could hope for. And how are you?

speaker: Basim
en: I am well. And keen to see my old friend again.

speaker: Eivor
en: He will be glad to see you, I am sure.

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum Jarl. Your second, Soma, talked often of you and your conquests.

speaker: Guthrum
en: They are all of one in my memory. A single great battle that stretches from my first breath to the end of this sentence.

speaker: Eivor
en: That sounds glorious. A living Valhalla.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Perhaps it does. But what happens when all the dead wear the same face and their pleas become a senseless blare? Where did Torsten die? On a field or in a marsh? We were close as brothers once, yet I don't recall where or when.

speaker: Eivor
en: You wear the scars of battle, and not only on your skin.

speaker: Guthrum
en: The needle of loss becomes blunt when you have been pierced enough. But enough of that.

speaker: Eivor
en: You speak with great feeling. In the tales, you are merciless in battle.

speaker: Guthrum
en: I am merciless in battle, yes. And melancholy in my bed. A balance of humors, I suppose.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why did you come to my banner if you mistrust my judgement?

speaker: Guthrum
en: I want Portcestre. You want what is held within her. And I will not become king by passing up chances like this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have faith, then. Together we will triumph.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Ah, faith. The most mysterious of words. They use it a lot here in Wessex. I'm not even sure what it means.

speaker: Erke
en: Eivor has brought many allies together from all over the land.

speaker: Stowe
en: Like these two fine fellows! Brothir and Broder, was it?

speaker: Broder
en: Careful, Saxon. We're here for the killing, not to make friends.

speaker: Broder
en: That snake Fulke hides behind walls of stone. But Eivor will drag her out.

speaker: Brothir
en: Still got a soft spot for her, don't you, Brother?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Him and Eivor? Ha! Lower your aim, friend, you'll have better luck.

speaker: Eivor
en: They said there would be a scout on this hill.

speaker: Eivor
en: I smell blood on the air.

speaker: Eivor
en: Death is close. Did someone find the scout before me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Slain by wolves. My work has been done for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: There, a scout.

speaker: Eivor
en: You will tell no tales to Fulke now.

speaker: Eivor
en: A scout patrols the riverbank north of Crawleah.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke's scout. Right where Basim said he would be.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: No sign of the Danes. Not sure what Fulke's worried about.

speaker: Eivor
en: Interesting. This scout was carrying orders from Fulke. Basim would like to see this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Orders from Fulke. I should show this to Basim, once I've dealt with the others.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have seen to the scouts. Basim and Guthrum will be waiting in the woods east of Portcestre.

speaker: Basim
en: Your fellow Norse look forward to Valhalla but not you. Why is that?

speaker: Guthrum
en: When you have stared into as many dead eyes as I have, it is hard to see anything but emptiness. In the end, we are meat for the butcher's blade, sure as hogs. That is all there is. Nothing more.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Ah, here's the Raven-Feeder now.

speaker: Eivor
en: The scouts are dead and you are safely encamped. I told you this would work.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Time will tell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Any eye that saw you has been dimmed by death.

speaker: Guthrum
en: You are not short on confidence. That much is clear.

speaker: Eivor
en: A leader should not second-guess themselves. Nobody respects a tremble-heart.

speaker: Guthrum
en: I have known plenty as brash as you. Not many are left in this world.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have a method, Guthrum. And though you may not see it, it has served me well.

speaker: Guthrum
en: If your method is to risk hundreds for the sake of one, then you are right. I don't.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found something of interest on one of the scouts. Fulke has news of Croindene's fall. She is gathering men and supplies. Perhaps to weather a siege?

speaker: Basim
en: If she is allowed to dig in at Portcestre, it might be months before we can get Sigurd out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you still say I am reckless in my haste, Guthrum?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Saxons! Saxons from the west!

speaker: Guthrum
en: I say your haste has put us squarely in the shit.

speaker: Basim
en: Fulke was forewarned! There must have been more scouts than we knew of.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's done is done. Save your breath for the fight.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Eivor, this mess is of your making!

speaker: Eivor
en: We kill them here, or behind the walls of Portcestre. Either way they die.

speaker: Brothir
en: That's the way, Eivor! For glory, and for Odin!

speaker: Eivor
en: They are giving ground! Push them back!

speaker: Basim
en: The tide turns for us!

speaker: Eivor
en: The Saxons falter!

speaker: Broder
en: Run them down! Trample them into the mud!

speaker: Eivor
en: They flee like rabbits!

speaker: Broder
en: Then we chase them like hounds!

speaker: Brothir
en: That ugly bastard's head is mine!

speaker: Broder
en: Not if I get there first, slow-arse!

speaker: Eivor
en: Leave him! The day is already won!

speaker: Eivor
en: No!

speaker: Eivor
en: Death has found you, Saxon.

speaker: Eivor
en: If Sigurd dies today, I will find your corpse and piss on it!

speaker: Eivor
en: I decide your fate today, Saxon.

speaker: Eivor
en: When you see your god, tell him I sent you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not. Go and tell Fulke what you saw today. Tell her Eivor is coming to tear her heart from her chest.

speaker: Broder
en: He is dead. No breath within him. Gods, I've never seen the raucous bastard so quiet.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are wounded, Broder. Let me bear your brother to the camp.

speaker: Broder
en: He was always quicker than me. Beat me out of the womb by mere moments. Now he has beat me to Valhalla. Even in death, he had to be first.

speaker: Eivor
en: This crow-feast is my doing.

speaker: Broder
en: No blame stains you, Eivor. He cut his own path. Always did. For him there is no more strife and pain. Only glorious battle, and the forever-feast.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Reckless stripling! I warned you the risk was too great!

speaker: Basim
en: Peace, Guthrum. It is Fulke who merits your wrath, not Eivor.

speaker: Guthrum
en: You have not seen the half of my wrath! How many of my men now lie dead on account of this glory-hoarder?

speaker: Eivor
en: Many have died, my friend here among them. The fault is mine. Knowing that is shame enough.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Small comfort that is to the dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: You knew the danger as well as I did, Guthrum. You saw opportunity, and you took it.

speaker: Guthrum
en: Indeed. The fault is none but mine for putting my trust in you.

speaker: Eivor
en: In spite of our losses, we claimed victory here. Arguing over blame will not bring the dead back.

speaker: Guthrum
en: If this is what a Raven Clan victory looks like, I cannot wait to see what happens when you lose.

speaker: Ubba
en: What happened here?

speaker: Broder
en: Ubba, Soma. You come at a black hour.

speaker: Soma
en: And too late to bloody our blades, more's the pity.

speaker: Guthrum
en: I hoped to take Portcestre with this one, but Fulke is forewarned now. I have no more appetite for this. I will go west.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go, then. But know you leave me in a time of need.

speaker: Guthrum
en: What you need is to swallow your pride, Raven-Feeder. Listen to wiser heads than yours.

speaker: Basim
en: Eivor...

speaker: Eivor
en: I will hear you, Guthrum Saxon-bane, if you wish to speak your piece.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am no errant child to be talked down to by my elders!

speaker: Guthrum
en: No. You are supposed to be a leader. So listen now.

speaker: Guthrum
en: You want your jarl back, you must be cold as frost. Bravery is your enemy as often as your friend. We do not dash ourselves against hopeless causes. We arrive unexpected, strike swift. Gather your allies. Pick your moment. Then, and only then... you crush them. You can triumph yet. Go with the wisdom of Odin, the power of Thor, the wit of Freyja. Go and find your brother.

speaker: Basim
en: Guthrum spoke in anger, but there is wisdom in what he says.

speaker: Eivor
en: I heard, and heeded. I am not too proud to admit my mistake.

speaker: Basim
en: Then there is wisdom in you as well.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not need him to tell me when I have made a mistake. Brothir les dead on my account.

speaker: Basim
en: I am glad to hear it. The unexamined life is not worth living.

speaker: Eivor
en: We will wait for our allies before the final attack. Until then, we have work to do.

speaker: Eivor
en: First, we need a new camp. The Saxons think we have retreated. But we will draw even closer... here.

speaker: Ubba
en: Arrive unexpected.

speaker: Eivor
en: Erke, Stowe, ride there ahead of me. Together we will bring them down.

speaker: Stowe
en: It brings me no pleasure to fight my own people, but a debt is a debt. We will leave immediately.

speaker: Erke
en: Besides, they're men of Wessex, Aelfred's folk. No brothers of yours.

speaker: Eivor
en: Erke, Stowe, Ljufvina, ride there ahead of me. Together we will bring them down.

speaker: Stowe
en: It brings me no pleasure to fight my own people, but a debt is a debt.

speaker: Erke
en: Besides, they're men of Wessex, Aelfred's folk. No brothers of yours.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: We will set off immediately. Together we will fall upon them as Thor's hammer.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will take care of the camp myself. Once I have cleared it out, we will move our warriors in. I'll risk no more losses.

speaker: Soma
en: After that, we should strike at Fulke's supplies all across Suthsexe.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes. If she is allowed to dig in at Portcestre, we will lose our chance to rescue Sigurd.

speaker: Eivor
en: The letter I found on the scout mentioned Briggworth, Gildefort, and Crawleah.

speaker: Basim
en: They produce weapons in Crawleah, food in Gildefort. Briggworth is a stronghold. Many Saxon swords there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ubba, I need your axe-arm at Gildefort. Soma, you and your men will aid me in Crawleah.

speaker: Soma
en: Count on us.

speaker: Basim
en: I will go to Briggworth and take the measure of things there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. I will join you after I've dealt with the Saxon camp.

speaker: Ubba
en: A lion's heart and a crow's cunning. Guthrum judged you too swiftly.

speaker: Eivor
en: We have work to do. Let's be about it.

speaker: Basim
en: Soma and Ubba, I apologize. I would have liked to offer better welcome after your long journey.

speaker: Soma
en: I am only sorry we could not be here sooner.

speaker: Ubba
en: We'll need a short while to organize the men, then we'll set off as soon as we're able.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ubba Ragnarsson, it puts me to ease to see you here. Welcome.

speaker: Ubba
en: Eivor Wolf-Kissed tempts me with a swipe at Wessex... who am I to resist?

speaker: Eivor
en: Here we might finish the work your father began, a decade back. Are you ready?

speaker: Ubba
en: More than ready. I am hungry.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now here is a welcome face. Soma, how fares Grantebridge?

speaker: Soma
en: We thrive, just as we did our first year. And I have you to thank for that.

speaker: Eivor
en: The risk I took was far less than you are taking now. I thank you for heeding my call.

speaker: Soma
en: An oath is an oath, Eivor. Silver-gilded and ironclad.

speaker: Broder
en: What I would give to be there when he appears in Odin's hall. Old One-Eye will have his hands full tonight. But I cannot let my brother lie forgotten in unknown soil. I must take him home, bury him with what finery I can muster.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. May Freyja watch your way, Broder. Until we meet again.

speaker: Broder
en: Aye. Until then.

speaker: Cursed Man
en: Away, curse-tusks. Return to the beastmaster and tell him I will not fall to the drum of your deviled hooves. You drive me mad with snorting! I did not mean to snare the she-wolf. Tell him. Tell your master her blood is not on my hands. Beg him, please. He must remove the curse! The forest and fields have risen up against me, red in tooth and claw.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dead? From fear or something else?

speaker: Eivor
en: These are the ramblings of a madman, but the animals, I cannot deny they tormented him.

speaker: Eivor
en: If this is connected to the beastmaster I met in Essexe, his reach is long indeed.

speaker: Eivor
en: He was terrified. Believed himself cursed after killing a she-wolf and her cub.

speaker: Eivor
en: And that stench! Rubbish and rotting food. In his fear, he barricaded himself inside, little wonder the rats came.

speaker: Eivor
en: He fulfilled his own prophecy, and nature took its revenge.

speaker: Bolri
en: Now where... where is it...? Is that it? No... Think... think! If not here...

speaker: Havi
en: Are you alright? It is not safe to be out here.

speaker: Bolri
en: Not safe? Why this town is the jewel of Svartalfheim. There is nowhere safer, I assure you. No, I merely seek a toy my son dropped. But no matter, he has more than enough at home. And I must get back, my wife will be wondering where I got to. Come, walk with me a moment. I shall introduce you to my boy. He's always wanted to meet an Æsir.

speaker: Bolri
en: Now, I understand your concern. We too have heard the Muspels are coming. But, I fail to see what they could want in Svartalfheim.

speaker: Havi
en: But they are already here. Close by, even. This is why I urge you to find shelter.

speaker: Bolri
en: You Æsir. I have heard how you are famed for your sense of humor. Tell me, have you met Thor?

speaker: Havi
en: We are very close, yes.

speaker: Bolri
en: My son, he loves nothing more than hearing of Thor's adventures. Perhaps you could spare us a tale, if you have time.

speaker: Havi
en: Let's keep moving.

speaker: Bolri
en: Oh, yes, of course.

speaker: Havi
en: Where are your people?

speaker: Bolri
en: My people? Why, all around us. Probably looking at us from their window, but pay them no heed. It's not every day an Æsir

speaker: Havi
en: What is it?

speaker: Bolri
en: Forgive me, I... I must have forgotten your name. Keep calling you 'Æsir,' which feels quite rude of me.

speaker: Havi
en: I have many names. My friends call me Havi. You may, too.

speaker: Bolri
en: Oh. Thank you. Havi. A fine name.

speaker: Havi
en: Let's get you home.

speaker: Bolri
en: Hm? Oh. Yes, yes.

speaker: Bolri
en: Here, my home is this next one. I must ask, mind your step, my wife only just potted the lovely plants this morning. And, and... Do you... Do you see that?

speaker: Havi
en: See what?

speaker: Bolri
en: M-Muspels. Going into my... home. No!

speaker: Havi
en: What now...?

speaker: Havi
en: This toy hammer. Is this...?

speaker: Bolri
en: Mjolnir, yes! My son's pride and joy. Tell me, have you met Thor?

speaker: Havi
en: Uh, as I said. We are... very close, yes.

speaker: Bolri
en: My son, he loves nothing more than hearing of Thor's adventures. Perhaps, uh, perhaps you could spare us a tale, if you have time. He should... he should be here. Any moment now, he should... be here.

speaker: Havi
en: My friend, you must leave this place. It is not safe. And I think you may know that, yes?

speaker: Bolri
en: Not safe? Why, this town... this town... this town is the jewel of

speaker: Havi
en: You must listen to me. Your wife and child, they are not coming back here. No dwarf is coming back to this town. They're almost certainly dead. Everyone except you. The Muspels must have killed them all. There's no other explanation.

speaker: Bolri
en: You are... mistaken. Confused. Or cruel. I cannot tell which. I do not care which. Get out. Get out of my home.

speaker: Havi
en: Look around you! This is no home! This is a grave!

speaker: Bolri
en: I said get out! Get out of here! I invite you in, tell you of my... my son... my son... Where, where is he? Where is my son? What have they... Where are they?

speaker: Havi
en: You must leave this place, before the Muspels find you too.

speaker: Bolri
en: Get out. Go.

speaker: Havi
en: Very well... I'm sorry, for what it's worth.

speaker: Havi
en: Forgive me, my friend, I will not be able to stay any longer. Please, pass on my regards to your wife and son.

speaker: Bolri
en: You're... leaving? Oh. But I'm sure they'll be only a moment.

speaker: Havi
en: I must... get back to my own son. I'm sorry.

speaker: Bolri
en: I understand. Of course.

speaker: Havi
en: I hope you find that which you need.

speaker: Bolri
en: Find...? Oh! Yes. I was looking for something. I'm sure it'll turn up.

speaker: Havi
en: ...Good luck to you.

speaker: Dag
en: Where is he? Where is Sigurd?

speaker: Eivor
en: He ... He is alive.

speaker: Dag
en: But not with you? Where is he?

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag, not now. I need to speak with Randvi

speaker: Dag
en: You never found him, did you? Tell us, Eivor! We deserve the truth!

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to speak with Randvi. Step aside. Now.

speaker: Dag
en: You never found him ... because you didn't look.

speaker: Dag
en: I see you, Eivor. I know what you are.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor ... you come alone. I fear what that means for Sigurd.

speaker: Eivor
en: I ... I could not find him. That madwoman Fulke she ... she slipped away. Took him to Suthesex. We need an army. Call on our alliances. Remind them of their oaths to me. We must act before

speaker: Randvi
en: Before?

speaker: Randvi
en: Before what, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: She tortured him, Randvi. Did unspeakable things. Severed his arm and left it as a gift. I fear she means to kill him. Slowly.

speaker: Randvi
en: Gods...

speaker: Eivor
en: East Anglia is with us. Their King Oswald has pledged his loyalty to us.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor King-Maker we shall call you soon.

speaker: Randvi
en: Some interesting news. King Ceolwulf has sent Ceolbert to Sciropescire. He hopes to install him as ealdorman there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good for Ceolbert. He should do well, considering all he has learned from you.

speaker: Randvi
en: I gave him only a taste of my knowledge. The rest he will need to figure out for himself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Finnr, welcome to our home. May you find a second wind here, one to fill your sails and send you across the world and back.

speaker: Finnr
en: That is an image I will fix in my mind, Wolf-Kissed. Happy to be aboard.

speaker: Eivor
en: In Essexe, I played matchmaker and a heartbreaker. An easy way to forge an alliance, but let us stick to war and diplomacy.

speaker: Randvi
en: Understood. Thank you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I entered Eurvicscire to meet Halfdan Jarl, and I left a friend of Halfdan the King. We have an oath at last.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Very good.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can hardly begin to describe what happened in Glowecestrescire. I think you will learn soon enough.

speaker: Randvi
en: But we are allied with them?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. For all our pains.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Nice to see Sigurd back where he belongs.

speaker: Randvi
en: Word of our growing settlement has reached outside ears. So have a look around... you may see a few new faces.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are allied with the Danes of Grantebridgescire. Their jarlskona, Soma, has pledged an oath.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are allied with the Danes of Grantebridgescire. Their jarlskona, Soma, has pledged an oath.

speaker: Randvi
en: Well done, Eivor. These early victories will pay off well.

speaker: Eivor
en: They will. In more than one way. One of Soma's finest fighters, Birna, has pledged her blade to us. She's a powerful fighter, and a charming spirit. I think she'll fit in nicely.

speaker: Randvi
en: Glad to have her. Good work.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birna. Welcome to the Raven Clan's nest.

speaker: Birna
en: Good to be here, Sunbeam! The people here seem to be a mixed bag of nuts and seeds. I feel right at home.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are at home. Settle in and get a feel for the place. We will be heading out soon enough.

speaker: Birna
en: Of course. A quick drink and a friendly brawl, and I will be ready for the raids ahead.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Swanburrow, I...

speaker: Swanburrow
en: No... Gods, no, don't say it. Please, Eivor, don't say it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am sorry.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: O, my Hunwald! No. My poor swan, O gods!

speaker: Eivor
en: He fought bravely, and turned the tide to secure a victory. Your dear Hunwald died a hero, and will be so remembered.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: O gods, I know he would have fainted to hear such praise from your lips. Thank you, Eivor. Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: He walks among warriors now.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Yes. The lucky man, I imagine he does.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know words are a poor salve for a wounded heart. I will leave you to mourn.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know words are a poor salve for a wounded heart. I will leave you to mourn.

speaker: Eivor
en: And know that we are here for you, always, should you need us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hamtunscire has fallen, and with it the Kingdom of Wessex. But the cost was great. Maybe too great for all we gained.

speaker: Randvi
en: Rest, then. You have earned it.

speaker: Eivor
en: On the backs of so many. Time will tell if it was worth it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Jorvik is now free of The Order's influence.

speaker: Hytham
en: Brilliant as ever, my friend. Thank you. For all you have done.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have purged The Order of the Ancients from Jorvik with Ljufvina and Hjorr's aid. And should we ever need theirs, they will come.

speaker: Randvi
en: You do this work, well, Eivor. Is it a prelude to you joining the Hidden Ones?

speaker: Eivor
en: I doubt it. Not enough glory in these back-alley brawls.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: So this is where you devise your plans. A cozy room, well fit and fortified.

speaker: Randvi
en: I advise. Sigurd and Eivor devise. But yes, it happens right here.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: My father told me once, that all a good army needs is bread, water, and an accurate map.

speaker: Randvi
en: Axes and shields are useful as well. But I think your father is onto something.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Yes, he was simplifying of course. You'd need clothes and rest as well... and good company, of course.

speaker: Randvi
en: Not as pithy when you say it like that.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: No.

speaker: Randvi
en: How long you'll be expect staying here?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I don't yet know, long enough to absorb your wisdom I hope.

speaker: Randvi
en: You will have a long grey beard by then '.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: This map does look a bit old, You could probably find better .

speaker: Randvi
en: O, Yea? How so?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: You see Northrumbia? It's ruled by Danes now. Halfdan Ragnarsson, Ubba and Ivar's older brother.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good to know, I will make a note of it. You said Eivor would be joining us?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Soon yes, she was on her way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. Glad to see you made it, Ceolbert.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Thanks to Sigurd. He was a good guide and even better company. He told me some incredible stories. The best ones were about you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hopefully nothing too embarrassing.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: There were a few gems.

speaker: Randvi
en: Not to interrupt, Eivor, but what of Ledecestrescire?

speaker: Eivor
en: The alliance is won. The Sons of Ragnar are friends to our clan.

speaker: Randvi
en: Glad to hear it. Well done to you both.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lincolnscire is a friend to us.

speaker: Randvi
en: Wonderful news. And who is our ally there?

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfgar is now Ealdorman of Lincolnscire. I believe he will be a good friend to our clan.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. I hope he is a man we can trust.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lincolnscire is a friend to us.

speaker: Randvi
en: Wonderful news. And who is our ally there?

speaker: Eivor
en: The boy Hunwald is the new Ealdorman of Lincolnscire, and he has sworn allegiance to us.

speaker: Randvi
en: The loud one, an ealdorman? Well, should he ever wish to call for aid, he need only shout.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lincolnscire is with us, under a new leader called Herefrith. A bishop.

speaker: Randvi
en: Let us hope he keeps his flock in line, and ready for the coming fights.

speaker: Eivor
en: The fires are out in Lincolnscire. They stand with us again, with Aelfgar as their ealdorman.

speaker: Randvi
en: Let us hope he proves a more reliable friend.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Hunwald, dear. Look, it's Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald, Swanburrow. Good to see the both of you.

speaker: Hunwald
en: And you, Eivor! Ah, it is good to see this place again after so much time away. I find such an easy joy here. And to think we will be living here, I am overjoyed.

speaker: Eivor
en: That joy will last right up until your first blood-sacrifice.

speaker: Hunwald
en: M-my first what?

speaker: Eivor
en: Later, my friend. Come. And enjoy your stay.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Eivor! It's Swanburrow. Hello.

speaker: Eivor
en: Swanburrow. You made it.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: I did. I should send a letter to Hunwald to give him the news. You know how he frets over me.

speaker: Eivor
en: He misses you, that is certain. But as ealdorman, he cannot afford to let his grief overpower him.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: I pray he fares well. I adore the lad, but I worry the burden will be too great.

speaker: Eivor
en: He should be fine. He has the heart of a leader. Now come, settle in. And enjoy your new home.

speaker: Eivor
en: Grim.

speaker: Grim
en: I do not envy you the position you were in with Lincolnscire. I lead Grimsby simply enough, but to choose the fate and bruise the ego of not one but three men? It's not how we Danes should be spending our precious days.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not above unpleasant work. I do what's needed for my settlement and its people.

speaker: Grim
en: Better than most, my friend. I wish you good fortune in the times ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lord Aelfgar. How does it feel to be ealdorman?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Much the same. My duties are more manifold, as are the people in my care. But the feeling is remarkably similar. I think I shall be quite comfortable in my role here, Eivor. Thanks to your impeccable judgement.

speaker: Acha
en: Aelfgar cares as much for his people as a goat cares for politics. Rest easy, knowing that you have broken no wheel.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald. Ealdorman of Lincolnscire.

speaker: Hunwald
en: It does have a lordly ring, does it not? Like the name itself was a holy notch waiting for the right peg to fill the space.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how do you find your responsibilities?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Well... answering complaints and levying taxes are a bore to be honest. But the spirit of an ealdorman flows in my veins. I shall find a foothold soon enough.

speaker: Raeganhere
en: I wish you the best of luck in your endeavours, Dane.

speaker: Acha
en: So you elected a man-child to lead us. To be a vacuum of leadership where a solid pillar is needed. God preserve us all.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lord Aelfgar.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Eivor. Things certainly are interesting with Hunwald as ealdorman. He's making most of his father's mistakes, but with a passion and honesty I quite admire.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hardly surprising. I hope you'll be there for him if he needs help.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: I will. Rest assured.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lunden is with us, and cleansed of The Order.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. Hytham will be pleased.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Order has been purged from Lunden. For now, they hold no power there.

speaker: Hytham
en: That is good news. And I would celebrate, but for the fact that Jorvik now suffers from the same infestation.

speaker: Eivor
en: Jorvik is a city under Norse control. I should have less problem finding allies here.

speaker: Hytham
en: That is a hopeful way of seeing it. Speak to Randvi when you wish to travel there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi. Our work is done in Oxenefordscire, but the cost has been high.

speaker: Randvi
en: I feared as much when this letter arrived. From one called Fulke, addressed to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: From Fulke? Gods, that witch.

speaker: Randvi
en: It is there on the table...

speaker: Letter from Fulke
en: To the Wolf-Kissed One, Blessings of the Self-Begotten One upon you, Eivor. I write only to ease your mind and let you know that Sigurd is in good hands and fine company. I will treat him with all the care he deserves. The order to which I belong has use for such a man. He is, in many ways, the pinnacle to which we aspire--a god in man's fleshy accoutrements. I only hope he comes to know and understand this as well as I do before his suffering breaks him. Fulke The Instrument

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke is with The Order of the Ancients. The same Order Kjotve followed. The Order that Basim and Hytham have pledged to destroy.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor, what has happened?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd has been taken hostage. Captured by King Aelfred and given to a woman named Fulke. A very dangerous woman.

speaker: Randvi
en: What does she want with him?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will spare you Fulke's ramblings, but know this... Sigurd did his part to secure an alliance with a thegn called Geadric. Geadric is an honest man and will come when I call. Until that time, Basim will locate Fulke. Look for his message when it comes.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are allied with Sciropescire, but at a... grievous cost. Young Ceolbert was killed.

speaker: Randvi
en: Yes, my scouts told me. Such a tragic death for so dubious a gain. I hope you paid his killers back in kind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Justice was done.

speaker: Randvi
en: Ceolbert will be remembered. He was good company, in the short time he was with us.

speaker: Eivor
en: He was.

speaker: Eivor
en: I bring fair tidings, Randvi. Hemming Jarl in Snotinghamscire has passed, but his clan remains allied to us.

speaker: Randvi
en: Sad news, but you made the best of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw my old friend Vili on my visit. He has now joined our clan, and will serve as a raider on my ship.

speaker: Randvi
en: I remember the young man. He will make a fine addition to your crew.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw my old friend Vili on my visit. He is their jarl, now. And he is pledged to aid us in times of need.

speaker: Randvi
en: What happened yesterday? You and Sigurd disappeared during the feast. And when he returned, he went straight to our room, without a word.

speaker: Eivor
en: We talked for a time. I asked many questions but got few answers. I wish I could say more. Sigurd wants to blame me for every mishap that has befallen him, but gives me no credit for his rescue. I don't understand.

speaker: Randvi
en: Yet he does speak with you. With me, he has gone totally silent. So... what now?

speaker: Eivor
en: This is for Suthsexe. We burned it to the ground to save one man. Yet he is barely the man we were searching for.

speaker: Randvi
en: Quite so.

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim. Have you spoken with Sigurd lately?

speaker: Basim
en: We talk from time to time. Why?

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you noticed any change in him? Any loss of... of happiness? Or feeling?

speaker: Basim
en: He appears to me... more thoughtful. Introspective.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thoughtful? That seems an understatement. He speaks as if he hears the voices of the gods whispering in his ear.

speaker: Basim
en: We live in a strange time, Eivor. Among stranger people. Sigurd may be among the blessed. But who can say for certain?

speaker: Eivor
en: Indeed.

speaker: Hytham
en: I'm grateful to see Basim returned. There's so much more I wish to learn from him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, it seems the wind calls me back to Randvi. Best tell her the good news.

speaker: Randvi
en: You've been away for so long!

speaker: Eivor
en: Were you worried?

speaker: Randvi
en: Of course I was. Such a long voyage, Did you do what had to be done?

speaker: Eivor
en: I did. And I am eager to focus on problems closer to home.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is done. Gorm is dead. The Kjotvesson clan is wiped from this world.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. I would like to hear everything about your journey to Vinland when you have time.

speaker: Eivor
en: One day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gorm is dead. Nameless and alone across the open sea.

speaker: Hytham
en: A Master of the Order, hewn from the trunk of their dying tree. You are getting closer to the roots.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cleared Wincestre of The Order, yet to do so meant working with King Aelfred.

speaker: Hytham
en: Your Poor Fellow-Soldier led you to the King of Wessex? How very strange. He... or she... is toying with you, it seems.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Order in Wincestre has been wiped out. But we are no longer welcome there. My contact was none other than King Aelfred himself. The Order wanted him dead, so he fought back.

speaker: Randvi
en: Aelfred? The line between friend and enemy is a porous one.

speaker: Eivor
en: That glimpse of flame and terror was gone in a moment... yet my thoughts remain darkened by it. I should return to Ravensthorpe and reflect on what I saw.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ravensthorpe. An island of calm in this turbulent land. But my vision of fire still troubles me. It would be good to rest beneath my dear old tree. I've always found peace there in the past.

speaker: Eivor
en: The tree is overrun with mistletoe. When did that happen?

speaker: Eivor
en: Now let the sighing of the branches soothe me, and may all thoughts of chaos fade.

speaker: Eivor
en: Disturbing thoughts invade my rest. Merely a dream, or something more?

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps I can reclaim my dream of Svartalfheim.

speaker: Eivor
en: The smell of death lingers in my nostrils. That was no mere dream. I must seek Valka's wisdom.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mistletoe...

speaker: Valka
en: The air hangs heavy around you, Eivor. You are troubled.

speaker: Eivor
en: I had another dream. A vision, like the last. This one full of fire.

speaker: Valka
en: Tell me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw the god Baldr, broken and beaten, held captive by Surtr. I-I tried to save him, but I was defeated, left to die in a pit of corpses. When I awoke, I found this in the fold of my clothing.

speaker: Valka
en: Baldr also dreamt of his own death.

speaker: Eivor
en: This tale I know. Afterwards, his mother Frigg visited every thing, living or dead, and had them swear not to harm him.

speaker: Valka
en: But she overlooked the mistletoe bush.

speaker: Eivor
en: And so fate had its way.

speaker: Valka
en: Not all visions are premonitions, Eivor. But all hide wisdom, if we have the wit to see it.

speaker: Valka
en: Drink this, if you would know more. Then go to the sacred circle behind my hut. There is more mistletoe there.

speaker: Valka
en: Lay the mistletoe around the circle, light it, and stand within. We shall see what your dream has to teach you.

speaker: Eivor
en: The mistletoe is in place, ready for burning.

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka! What is the meaning of this? Is this some part of your ritual? The flames draw ever closer!

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka! Would you burn me alive?

speaker: Valka
en: If you would reach your dreams, Eivor, you must not run from the fire. You must become it!

speaker: Eivor
en: These dark visions oppress me. The warm light of wakefulness is sweet relief. And yet... and yet, I must see more, wherever the darkness leads me.

speaker: Eivor
en: A message from Valka. If I drink the potion, I can return to my vision.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can reclaim my vision of Svartalfheim.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aaah!

speaker: Valka
en: What is it? What did you see?

speaker: Eivor
en: All my struggles mattered nothing in the end. My son was lost before I began, his premonition come to pass.

speaker: Valka
en: Your son?

speaker: Eivor
en: Baldr! Havi's son. You know what I mean!

speaker: Valka
en: So Baldr met his fate, as was foretold. Ever you have sought to elude the looms of the Nornir, but we are all caught in their weave.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, I will not believe it. There is more to see yet. Why was I thrown from my dream?

speaker: Valka
en: Perhaps it was not the vision that rejected you, but you who rejected the vision. Perhaps you are afraid of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I fear nothing!

speaker: Valka
en: I think you do. And until you recognize that fear, give in to it, embrace it... the vision will not return. Some walls cannot be overcome by potions alone.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me what I must do. This saga does not end here. It cannot!

speaker: Valka
en: Meet me in the forest when darkness lays upon the land. There we shall see how fearless you truly are.

speaker: Eivor
en: The wolf is coming, brothers and sisters. It finds us all in the end, no matter how we hide. In its jaws is an end or a beginning, and we will never know which till that last black bite. Should we lay down for it, then? Bare our throats to its teeth? Or fight with every sinew in our bodies to hold it away, knowing always that our strength must fail, and the wolf will take us? I know only this. Each day is a gift from the dead to the living. Each smile brought by another's tears. And when the wolf runs free, all we will have are those we fought to keep. So I will keep you, my people. I will fight the wolf for every inch of this land, till the hour he claims me. I will buy you your days of love and laughter. Use them well.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Look lads, there's Eivor!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: We're with you, Eivor!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Those castle walls won't be thick enough to stop us!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: Long live Geadric!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: None will stop us!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 6
en: Eivor, Geadric and victory!

speaker: Note to Eldest Son
en: We're right proud of you soldiering and all, Ned, but we need you back home. Your father can't half harvest the crops with that wrist of his, and your brother's perilous drunk most of the day. Please leave the war to itself and come home.

speaker: To Be Given to My Mother Should I Die
en: Mum. They've a strong fort, and I'm told we must take it. When the boiling oil pours down, I'll hear me mates' screams just afore it reaches me. Me last thought will be of you, Mum. Ned

speaker: Geadric
en: We ain't ready to attack yet, Eivor. Eadwyn's still too strong. Too well supplied, and got more men coming.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll return soon.

speaker: Geadric
en: See that our fletchers have arrows enough for everyone. Twenty to a man.

speaker: Geadric
en: Bring those men here. In formation.

speaker: Geadric
en: God above. Will we never be ready?

speaker: Eivor
en: Geadric.

speaker: Geadric
en: Eivor. Have you dealt Eadwyn a few bruising blows?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have. She'll feel the pain soon enough.

speaker: Geadric
en: Excellent. My men are itching to attack the fortress, but we'd be fools to force it now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why is that?

speaker: Geadric
en: On account of Eadwyn's got too many traps and defenses. Her springalds'd cut us to bloody stumps, before they poured boiling oil upon us like a summer tempest!

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep the men at the ready. I'll slip in alone and see what I can do about these defenses.

speaker: Geadric
