en: By my joints and ankles, you're a tough one.

speaker: Eivor
en: The castle keep looks impregnable. That will be Eadwyn's last stand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Alright. I'm in.

speaker: Eivor
en: The springalds are large bolt-casters. I must disable them.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could rig these cauldrons.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's more to be done, but this should be enough to launch the assault. Now it's down to Geadric to lead his men.

speaker: Geadric
en: I say we wait. There's too much riding on this.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I am Sigurd Jarl, Lord of East Mercia. And I say we fight. Now.

speaker: Geadric
en: You're a good man, Sigurd. And I'm thankful for all you've done. But without Eivor, I make no moves. We wait.

speaker: Moira
en: Slow sips, Halfdan. It helps the brew stay down.

speaker: Moira
en: Drink the rest.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Yes, yes. Thank you, Moira. That is all for now.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Her soothing herbs lift the fog from my mind, for a time.

speaker: Eivor
en: How long has she been mixing these for you?

speaker: Halfdan
en: You're stalling, Eivor. Tell me what you've learned. What news from the North?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Picts were beaten back. We took their lives and their treasures. Faravid asked me to deliver this.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Is he taunting me!? Faravid poisons the wine he gifts me. These goblets are a cruel joke. He's mocking me!

speaker: Eivor
en: We did capture some barrels of Frankish black. He said they were for you. But I made him open a cask. We drank together, there was no poison.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Speak without guise, Eivor. Does he plot against me or no? Does he keep secrets? Give me something I can use.

speaker: Odin
en: Now you must choose between treason and madness. Between the serpent's fang and the bite of a rabid wolf.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid asked for my silence, but Halfdan expects the truth. If I am not careful, these lies will pile up, one upon the next.

speaker: Halfdan
en: You've grown awfully silent, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid has planned an attack on the Picts at Magnis. Without you.

speaker: Halfdan
en: That twin-faced, back-stabbing, glory-eater!

speaker: Halfdan
en: When? Tell me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I won't know until we meet again. At a place called the Wolds.

speaker: Eivor
en: I fought some hard battles at Faravid's side and found him to be an honorable man.

speaker: Halfdan
en: No, no, he's a wily one, that man. He's got you fooled as well. You must keep digging. Where is he now, what's he doing?

speaker: Eivor
en: We're to meet at a place called the Wolds.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Good, go to him. Watch. Listen. Unearth his lies. You'll find them.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you fear poison, lord, you must consider everything. Even Moira's brew.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Impossible. Moira has been with me for an age. She's no witch, she's kind and... Hm. Perhaps you could speak with her, find out for yourself. She stays within Donecaestre, not far from here. If you learn something, find me north of Donecaestre. One of my scouts there has troubling news.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Heel, Beonton! We're going for a walk, down to the temple.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should see Moira about this brew she's been feeding Halfdan.

speaker: Eivor
en: No sense wasting a fine goblet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Moira's not here.

speaker: Eivor
en: This letter came from Wyke. She must have gone there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should go to Wyke. Find Moira.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a small village. Moira's house must be near.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: C'mon outta there, you heathen lover!

speaker: Moira
en: Away from my house, you ruffians!

speaker: Eivor
en: What's this ruckus?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Stand back, Dane. There's a witch within that house. We've come to burn it down.

speaker: Eivor
en: She's no witch, she's Halfdan's healer.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: That proves it! Dark magic, that is!

speaker: Eivor
en: Clear out, all of you! Before I beat you senseless.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: You can't hide forever!

speaker: Moira
en: O, goodness! You're not... not one of them. You must help me slip free.

speaker: Eivor
en: Moira, we must go. Before they burn your cottage to cinders.

speaker: Moira
en: I can't go out there! They'll steal me away and burn me at the stake.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. I see two ways out of this but neither is without risk.

speaker: Moira
en: Do what you must, only hurry. I leave myself in your hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm as good with words as I am with weapons. It will take some convincing, but I can talk my way out of this.

speaker: Moira
en: Lead on, then. I shall follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go home, all of you. This woman is in my care now.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Who died and made you sovereign of Northumbria now?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am the Wolf-Kissed. Killer of Men, Feeder of Ravens. Stand back or I will wear your bones as ornaments.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Jesus. Ease up now. We was only protecting our hamlet here. Tell Halfdan he can have 'er.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, leave this woman alone. Even look her way again and it will be the last thing you see. Moira, it is safe to go.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand back, ceorls. This woman serves Halfdan Ragnarsson.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Pfft. We're not moving, heathen. We're watching you!

speaker: Eivor
en: You will talk to my fists!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Up your arse, Odin-fucker.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: This'll be fun. You can't take us all on.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, leave this woman alone. Even look her way again and it will be the last thing you see. Moira, it is safe to go.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Hey! That foul witch escaped! Bah, let's go. We'll come again tomorrow. And again and again until she leaves for good!

speaker: Moira
en: Are they gone? Thank the light!

speaker: Eivor
en: You give a good scream and fall. Then I'll carry you through the mob as if I've done you serious harm.

speaker: Moira
en: O Lord above have mercy. Yes, fine. I'll do it. Whatever it takes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Time to be convincing.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Yes, that's right! Sinners deserve to die!

speaker: Moira
en: Are they gone? Thank the light!

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, leave this woman alone. Even look her way again and it will be the last thing you see. Moira, it is safe to go.

speaker: Eivor
en: We'll be safe here.

speaker: Moira
en: Thank you, Eivor. A thousand times, I thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: And if I asked you to drink your own brew?

speaker: Moira
en: I would, gladly. And often do, from time to time. To ensure it is not overly bitter before serving to Halfdan.

speaker: Eivor
en: When you said there's no cure for what ails Halfdan ... you mean he's touched in the head?

speaker: Moira
en: I fear so. The same malady bedeviled my mother. The body breaks down and the mind falls apart over time. It's a terrible thing.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need your help, Moira. The brews you mix for Halfdan. What goes into them?

speaker: Moira
en: O, quite a diverse mixture, let me see... lavender, rosemary, meadowsweet, yarrow, soothing herbs, nothing uncommon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you cure his illness with such a brew?

speaker: Moira
en: My medicine is meant to alleviate his pain, not cure it. I fear there is no cure at all for what ails Halfdan.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should return to Halfdan. He said he would be at the Temple of Flora.

speaker: Moira
en: Tread lightly this topic with him. If you would tread it at all.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Who's out there?

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan, good to find you here.

speaker: Halfdan
en: The Raven-Feeder returns! Now keep quiet. I'm hunting a band of traitors lurking about this swamp.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who told you there were traitors here?

speaker: Halfdan
en: My scout. He asked me to join him here, but he's nowhere to be found. Have a look around, tell me if you see something.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Eivor, search the perches and lookouts here. He could be spying from above. Olav! Speak to us! Where are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: He's clinging to life. I should carry him down.

speaker: Olav
en: Ugh... h-help... ngh...

speaker: Halfdan
en: Olav!

speaker: Eivor
en: I found your scout, but his wounds are grave.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Olav. Poor Olav... he'll be buried with honors, I'll see to that.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Walk the bridge, old friend. I will see you on the other side. Beonton may track his attackers. Get 'em, boy.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Good boy! Follow their trail!

speaker: Halfdan
en: Sniff 'em out, boy! We'll paint the ground with their blood!

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are these men you suspect of treason?

speaker: Halfdan
en: Thieves who stole my war spoils.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks abandoned. Are you sure someone is here?

speaker: Halfdan
en: The trail ends, but nobody's here. Hmph.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here, a hidden entrance. They might be lurking below.

speaker: Eivor
en: These pipes burst and flooded the tunnel.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Even this old Roman work cannot withstand the icy kiss of winter's goddess.

speaker: Eivor
en: Look there! The pipes cut through that wall. Could there be more rooms beyond?

speaker: Halfdan
en: Eivor! Something's there!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hold on. We'll find a way through.

speaker: Halfdan
en: I can't get through!

speaker: Eivor
en: The way is blocked!

speaker: Eivor
en: There must be a way to let Halfdan through. An opening of great size.

speaker: Halfdan
en: You've done it! We must hurry.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Romans were fine craftsman. These chambers are vast and decorated, and laced with piping.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Yet, they went mad and vanished, just like their gods. Moira's books tell us so. Ah! Here you see! Spoils of war. Mine. Stolen from me! (scream)

speaker: Halfdan
en: I am beset on all sides, Eivor. By plotters and schemers.

speaker: Eivor
en: What kings and jarls are not? Your territory is vast and wealthy.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Every day, decisions I make change the lives of thousands. It is a burden few could bear. Yet, I do. I do.

speaker: Halfdan
en: You spoke with Moira. What did you learn?

speaker: Eivor
en: She means well. I don't believe she would poison you, not willingly.

speaker: Eivor
en: She also said she's seen your illness before. In her own family. Said it came on slow but was... incurable.

speaker: Halfdan
en: No... No no no. This is not an illness. This is poison. Somehow, someone is poisoning me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Shhh! Listen...

speaker: Halfdan
en: These will be thieves who stole my tribute.

speaker: Ulf
en: Wolf-Kissed and Halfdan, well met! Come, fill your bellies with mead.

speaker: Halfdan
en: You stole this tribute! By rights this is mine! It was meant for me!

speaker: Ulf
en: We stole nothing! Faravid gifted this to us! For a hard day's battle!

speaker: Halfdan
en: And did you take my scout's, Olav, in that battle? Your brother in arms? Did he, too, have to die for this tribute?

speaker: Ulf
en: That was... that was Olav? Damned fool, we thought he was a thief!

speaker: Halfdan
en: The only thieves here are the ones drinking my mead and spit-shining my silver. You! Cowards and traitors!

speaker: Ulf
en: We are owed this bounty, jarl! For battles won and blood let! Eivor, you tell him!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is treason. And treason is punishable by death.

speaker: Ulf
en: Faravid treated us better than you ever did.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Faravid is nothing, and you are less.

speaker: Ulf
en: Glory! Glory for Ulf!

speaker: Eivor
en: They only took their rightful share.

speaker: Halfdan
en: You are traitorous worms, but Eivor seems to think you deserve pity. So I will give it this once. Return my spoils to Donecaestre, and I'll wipe this day from my memory.

speaker: Ulf
en: I can't do that. It is our share. We fought for it, killed for it, bled for it. If we don't get the glory, we deserve our share

speaker: Halfdan
en: The barking will stop!

speaker: Halfdan
en: They forced my hand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take hold of your fear, Halfdan. It can poison your mind.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Faravid killed this man, not me! He forced my hand with slights and trickery! He

speaker: Halfdan
en: Forgive me, I... I find it hot in these furs. The day must be warming. You have a meeting with Faravid. Isn't that right?

speaker: Eivor
en: I do. At the Wolds.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Yes, I know the place well. It's on the road between Jorvik and Picheringa.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Press him, Eivor. As hard as you can! Never let up! And bring me proof of his treachery... or otherwise.

speaker: Eivor
en: His forces are gathering at Stenwege. It's from there he plans to attack the Picts at Magnis.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Hmph. I see. Say nothing of what you told me. He must not know that I am aware of his plan.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll take my leave, lord.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Press him, Eivor. As hard as you can! Never let up! And bring me proof of his treachery... or otherwise.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Traitors... thieves... no right! They had no right to... it's rightfully mine, yes, yes... Faravid the rat! Words are poison...

speaker: Pious Wife
en: How am I supposed to be happy with only your stupid face to look at for the rest of my life?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You said you loved my face!

speaker: Pious Wife
en: I do. Which is why I wanted a smaller, sweeter version of it. Ostara will bless me with a child.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: That pagan rock holds no magic. Besides... there are wolves. Big ones. With teeth.

speaker: Pious Wife
en: I am going to that stone, and you cannot stop me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why do you quarrel?

speaker: Pious Wife
en: Because my husband has the courage of a quivering dormouse. All I ask for is a child.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not sure how I can help with that.

speaker: Pious Wife
en: There is a rock, a place of great power. They say that all woman who spend the night there come away pregnant.

speaker: Eivor
en: From a rock?

speaker: Pious Wife
en: From the fertile power and energy it holds. I must see it for myself. Will you protect me on the road?

speaker: Pious Wife
en: Every woman I know who has gone to the rock has left with child. It's a miracle.

speaker: Eivor
en: And this is not a Christian belief?

speaker: Pious Wife
en: The legend says that Ostara, the goddess of spring, transformed a bird into a hare at this very spot. The hare then laid colored eggs for her festival! The place has great magic.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birds becoming hares? Hares laying eggs? We Norse have stranger stories.

speaker: Pious Wife
en: Here we are.

speaker: Pious Wife
en: Wolves!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay out of harm's way, I will deal with them.

speaker: Pious Wife
en: Perhaps that silly bugger was right, the wolves are fearsome. Thank you, you saved my skin.

speaker: Pious Wife
en: This is the sacred place.

speaker: Pious Wife
en: Great Ostara, bestow your blessing upon me. Give me that which I so desperately desire. A child.

speaker: The Rock
en: Ostara shall grant you wish, through the power of a sacred ritual. Do you both seek the goddess's... succor?

speaker: Eivor
en: This woman has come to take in the power of the rock of fertility.

speaker: The Rock
en: And she will. All leave satisfied.

speaker: Pious Wife
en: However long it takes and whatever is needed of me. I will give it.

speaker: The Rock
en: Yes, my dear! Feel the power of the goddess! Take it all in.

speaker: Pious Wife
en: But it is so... big...

speaker: Eivor
en: Many women come here. How many children has this rock brought forth? A lot of women have had their greatest desire granted. Are there cuckoos in the nest?

speaker: Eivor
en: The essence of the gods is certainly spreading itself all over Suthsexe.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should leave them to their, er... ritual.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is that boy doing all the way up there?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Boy 1)
en: Jump, little flea! Jump, flea! Jump!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Girl 1)
en: Stop it, you grubkin. If he falls, God will punish you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Boy 2)
en: Go on, Esobert! It's yours for the taking!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Girl 2)
en: He's so brave! Like a young King Aelfred!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Girl 1)
en: He's going to fall. O, my days, I can't look.

speaker: Esobert
en: I'm going to do it! You see if I don't. I'm just screwing my courage to the sticky place. O, it is high. Why is it so high? If I die, tell her I think only of her. I will show her I love her! Or die trying!

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you doing all the way up here?

speaker: Esobert
en: Don't try and stop me. I will get that flower... and then she'll see how much I love her.

speaker: Eivor
en: A brave choice, little fellow.

speaker: Esobert
en: Even if I get smashed on the ground like an... an... overripe plum... I am just getting my breath back. The climb was hard. I'm girding my erm... loins...

speaker: Eivor
en: Loins, eh? Or I could get it for you? I would hate to see such a ferocious flame snuffed out.

speaker: Esobert
en: I mean, if you insist. But I could get it if I wanted to. Just so you know.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Boy 2)
en: Saints alive! Did you see that? God sent Esobert an angel!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Girl 1)
en: Is it over? Did he fall? God's buttered crumpets, I never told him I loved him.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Boy 2)
en: That stranger got it for him. Oi, that's cheating!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Boy 1)
en: She missed, the stranger missed! That could've been Esobert's mangled noggin.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Boy 2)
en: What a terrible show, boo, boo...!

speaker: Esobert
en: If I'd known it was that easy...

speaker: Eivor
en: You'd have done it yourself. Risked life and limb. But great men know the value of a champion.

speaker: Eivor
en: What will you do with such a treasure?

speaker: Esobert
en: It is for her. It is all for her, so she will finally notice me.

speaker: Ealhswith
en: Æthelflæd? What do you say to the sweet boy?

speaker: Æthelflæd
en: Thank you for the flower. It is very beautiful.

speaker: Esobert
en: Now we are bethrothed, and I will grow up to be a great king and you will be my fair lady.

speaker: Ealhswith
en: What say you, daughter? Do you think him a worthy suitor? He risked so much to declare his love. I will tell my husband, the king, you claim our daughter's hand. When you are a bit older of course. Come dearest.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Boy 2)
en: s holy cattle! You actually gave a flower to the princess!

speaker: Esobert
en: And now we are bethrothed.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Girl 2)
en: Takes more than that. There's holding hands and grunting. And then sometimes praying... "O, God! O, God!"

speaker: Esobert
en: King Esobert the first. The Flea of Wincestre!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child (Boy 2)
en: All hail the Lord of the Saxons. Esobert the Flea!

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: This is an outrage!

speaker: Trygve
en: Our strong feelings for Hemming come with much grief.

speaker: Eivor
en: Festive.

speaker: Trygve
en: Too festive! And too soon. Fires, fights, and every man soaked in mead. Ugh! This has gone too far.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hemthorpe could burn before the pyre is lit.

speaker: Trygve
en: Gods, have I failed my dear jarl?

speaker: Eivor
en: Peace, Trygve. I'll do what I can to calm things.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: That Saxon did what? How dare he insult our culture! He is a dead man if I ever get my hands on him.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Did you see that sobbing sack of meat with the roosters?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: What an arse-hole...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: That man is being attacked by chickens!

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Someone get that drunk away from the chickens!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: I didn't see them coming! I never looked down! I never saw them coming!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Stay back, foul beasts! Help me! Someone help me!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Flee, warrior, flee! Loki's horde lays waste here!

speaker: Eivor
en: You mean Hemming's famous fighting roosters?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Dragons with mighty claws! Save me from their wrath!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Thank you, mighty Thor! You've saved my life.

speaker: Eivor
en: When you sober up, steer clear of roosters.

speaker: Norse Man 4
en: Did you see what happened to the house where they kept the voda? It has gone up in flames!

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: Fire! Fire!

speaker: Norse Man 5
en: Not the voda... I love the voda...

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: Help! Fire! Save my voda! It burns!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this voda you speak of?

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: A gift without price, fit for a jarl's lips! But hurry! It catches flame!

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: Please, retrieve my voda, I beg of you! 'Tis my funeral gift! The honor of my family at stake!

speaker: Eivor
en: If this is your voda, I managed to save it from the licking flames.

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: You dared Surtr's Heat! Yes! A most potent drink, distilled from grain by the . Dip your horn and have a drink.

speaker: Eivor
en: A bit of drink in the belly never hurt...

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: Watch yourself... the voda sneaks up on you quick.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was too late for your... your voda, as you say.

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: Ah, balls! I dragged it all the way from Rus! It is back to water ale for me, I suppose.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you drink enough, ale is a fine fix to any problem.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Very true, very true. Join me if you desire.

speaker: Eivor
en: A bit of drink in the belly never hurt...

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: Come out, you dung-eating rat!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: No! You'll hurt me!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: They're going to kill him! I told him not to do it. Now he's locked up in that house with no way out.

speaker: Eivor
en: What madness is this?

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: You dare wash our beloved Hemming with your filth!

speaker: Eivor
en: I asked you a question, friend.

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: There's a Saxon within. One stupid enough to try sending Hemming to Heaven over Valhalla.

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: Now he cowers behind a locked door!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I only did right by his immortal soul!

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: You will get what is right for you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Calm yourselves, all of you. I will speak with him. Unmask his true intentions.

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: Get that stain out here now!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: O my God!

speaker: Eivor
en: The people are quite upset.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Leave me be! I did nothing wrong!

speaker: Eivor
en: You should walk out of here on your own, before you cannot walk at all.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Yes, yes! I'll walk, I'll walk! Don't hurt me, please! There's a key there. If you open the door I... I will follow you out.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: You got the key... use it.

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: You'll pay for your wrongs, desecrator!

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough. Let him speak to explain himself.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I loved Hemming, I swear! I only want him to fly free in the Kingdom of God!

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: So you drench his body with your filth-waters?

speaker: Eivor
en: Was it your Christian holy-water?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Of course! I anointed him in the name of the Lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: Never inflict your Christian mysteries on a dead Norseman.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: But I only

speaker: Eivor
en: These are your neighbors. Respect them. Learn their ways. And you will draw breath long into old age.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: O, no...

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: There you are, baptized as one of us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hemming was never one to weep over a bit of rain. Neither should you.

speaker: Norse Woman 4
en: He insulted our noble dead!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hemming would laugh at the very idea.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shut your mouths, both of you. Your antics have outlasted their welcome. Now go.

speaker: Eivor
en: Some order seems to have been restored. Now to Trygve to let him know.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've calmed the guests as much as they can be in their grief.

speaker: Trygve
en: They mourn. It is to be expected. Still, thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how do you feel, old friend?

speaker: Trygve
en: I mourn more deeply than most, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hemming would be proud of what you have accomplished here. All you have done for him.

speaker: Trygve
en: I hope so.

speaker: Eivor
en: This ache will pass, Trygve. With time.

speaker: Trygve
en: Yes. It will.

speaker: Eivor
en: Toka said King Charles carouses at this tavern. Strange, to drink and make merry on the eve of war.

speaker: French Man 1
en: The river brims with trash and rotting corpses. How wicked a world, where evil runs amok.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: Take heart, beloved. God's light shines upon us like the rays of the sun.

speaker: French Man 1
en: The sun? We buried our son. It is not right for a parent to outlive a child.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: Dear husband, we will all be together again in Heaven's golden city.

speaker: French Man 1
en: Bah! Priests go to Heaven, farmers go to work.

speaker: Harlequin 1
en: Come one, come all, enter our humble hall! Drink, dance, and sing to the madness of the king!

speaker: Toka
en: The Fat King! What other king could I mean? They say he sleeps here.

speaker: Taverner
en: He slept here, he ate here, he drank here, and he left here. Where he went after that, who am I to say?

speaker: Eivor
en: No luck finding the king?

speaker: Toka
en: Eivor! No, no luck. Finding such a large, famous man should be easy, but not for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Come, let us drink.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are these strange folk?

speaker: Toka
en: Fools with no shame or no honor, players who perform for the king.

speaker: Eivor
en: One of these fools may lead us to that greater fool, the king.

speaker: Toka
en: Don't bother, it's like talking to drunks or . Or drunken Geats. Eivor. I should thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: For what?

speaker: Toka
en: For backing me against Sigfred. He will not talk to the Franks, but... we should still try, yes?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. And you can do this thing, with or without him.

speaker: Toka
en: But I failed. Nobody here will tell me where to find the king. What should I do?

speaker: Eivor
en: A wise shield-warrior must know both sword and words. Watch and learn.

speaker: French Man 2
en: Today marks the end of an age. So drink, friends. Let us toast to the end of the world!

speaker: French Woman 2
en: I will drink to that! Life is too short for abstinence.

speaker: French Man 3
en: Ah, but the wine is a mocker, drink is the devil's sacrament, and like its master, it only deceives.

speaker: French Man 2
en: I'll drink to that. A toast, to wine, madness, and to... O, why not? To the king!

speaker: Toka
en: "Watch and learn," you said. See? Not so easy to find a king, is it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Greetings, good sir. I would offer my sword to your king. Where may I find him?

speaker: Harlequin 2
en: When the great bear was sleeping, the jesters went creeping, into the great bear's room! The jesters were all drinking, dancing, and singing, even if waking the bear spells doom!

speaker: Eivor
en: The bear might be the king. So, the king had a room?

speaker: Harlequin 2
en: Pantomime is a naughty boy, and a naughty pantomime be he. He drank down wine, he crept upstairs, and he stole the fat bear's key!

speaker: Eivor
en: You there, acting strange. Where is your king?

speaker: Eivor
en: As mute as the dead. No matter.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah hah, Charles, I have found your hiding spot.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found what I need. Charles enjoys the theater in Amiens.

speaker: Toka
en: Good. Let us go.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, he may lash out if he meets one of Sigfred's clan. Best I go alone.

speaker: Toka
en: As you wish. But meet me here when you are done and tell me what he said.

speaker: French Child 1
en: Hear ye, hear ye! Sigfred the Slayer and his heathen horde march on the gates of Paris. Count Odo calls for all loyal warriors to gather at Île de la Cité!

speaker: Pantomime
en: How should we mere mortals measure the greatness of a king?

speaker: Harlequin 3
en: By his height? By his weight? By the length of his... sock?

speaker: Pantomime
en: No, do not measure a royal majesty by the size of his... anything! Instead gauge his words. Test if they be honest... or a... crock!

speaker: Harlequin 3
en: Friend Pantomime, again you err. Words are like water, everflowing. Estimate our royal ruler's regal deeds, rather than his talk!

speaker: Pantomime
en: Good Harlequin, you have made everything suddenly and abundantly clear. O mighty Charles lies low in the back of a darkened theater.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like the backstage. Maybe Charles lurks within.

speaker: Unknown Voice
en: O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed; happy shall he be, that takes the little ones...

speaker: Charles
en: Yes, demon, what? What does it do to the little ones?

speaker: Unknown Voice
en: It dashes them against the stones!

speaker: Charles
en: No, no, no...

speaker: Charles
en: Ah, it is only the heathen. Led astray by Lucifer, but mortal all the same.

speaker: Eivor
en: Charles. I heard two voices. Who else is back here?

speaker: Charles
en: No one but me and this weak creature of flesh.

speaker: Charles
en: Forgive me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Talking to that which does not exist opens the door for something that does. This I know.

speaker: Charles
en: Let me assure you, my demon exists. As does my God.

speaker: Charles
en: Kill me. Make me a martyr king.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should slay you where you stand, for that trick you played on me and the queen.

speaker: Charles
en: That will not get you what you want. Peace, and a free hand in England, correct?

speaker: Eivor
en: Odo won't see reason. Sigfred wishes to burn the city down. But you, you can save Paris.

speaker: Eivor
en: Put aside what you and I want. Think of your kingdom. Your people.

speaker: Eivor
en: Only you can save your people from Sigfred's wrath.

speaker: Charles
en: If the world were so simple, bread would grow on trees. Odo is a great man... with greater ambitions. All of my nobles make demands of me. So does the . And the Greeks, the Slavs, the Saxons, the Saracens. And you, you Northmen. You demand land, hostages, tribute. Sometimes the best move is not to move at all.

speaker: Eivor
en: You would let your enemies slaughter one another.

speaker: Charles
en: I will let my enemies paint God's green earth red with infidel blood... while pious Charles prays only for peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is there nothing you want?

speaker: Charles
en: Yes... By now you know, I care not a whit for my barren wasteland of a wife.

speaker: Eivor
en: But your son, Bernard.

speaker: Charles
en: My only heir. Bring me the prince, unharmed, and I will consider the merits of your offer. Else, begone.

speaker: Eivor
en: You want him brought to a dingy theater, where you talk to yourself in the dark?

speaker: Charles
en: No. Present my son to me on the field of battle, before all my men and vassals.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why then? Why wait?

speaker: Charles
en: My nobles need to see me getting something from you Northerners. Now, until that day dawns, there is the door.

speaker: Eivor
en: You look none the worse for ale. How much did you drink?

speaker: Toka
en: Not enough to make me enjoy those awful Frankish skalds. But tell me, will Charles sign a truce?

speaker: Eivor
en: He will not even speak to us until we hand over his son, Bernard?

speaker: Toka
en: But we do not have the bastard boy.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, but I know where the queen took him. The plague ward, south of the city.

speaker: Toka
en: I will gather my thegns and take them hostage.

speaker: Eivor
en: To seize the prince lacks honor. But we should keep an eye on the boy all the same.

speaker: Toka
en: Hmm. I know a man with keen eye and light step. Pierre.

speaker: Eivor
en: A wise choice.

speaker: Toka
en: So. One step closer to breaching the walls and burning a city.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes... and I do not want this thing, but what else can we do? See you back at the camp, Toka.

speaker: Valka
en: The Nornir have spoken...You will betray Sigurd.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, this is wrong. That cannot be right!

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin fought against his fate. It can be done.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shit...Kjotve's warriors.

speaker: Eivor
en: This one would not have come alone. I should find the others.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: I have a feeling...just the three of us...we should return to Nottfall with our report. While we can.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: We can bring Kjotve news of the longships, or we can wake him with Sigurd Styrbjornsson's head. Which is better?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: All right! When Ljot returns, we weigh our next move. But I am not one for sticking around, hear me?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Quit bawling, you babe. They may be drunk, but they're not deaf.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd must know about this.

speaker: Sigurd
en: With each day we wait, Kjotve grows stronger.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I speak as your king, Sigurd. Not your father. Heed my warnings or be off!

speaker: Sigurd
en: You will be king of nothing if you do not act soon.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: We do not have the men to storm Kjotve's fortress. The losses would ruin us!

speaker: Sigurd
en: The losses have ruined us, Father! Until we cut off this serpent's head, it will poison us, day by day, drop by drop!

speaker: Eivor
en: The poison has already polluted our waters.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Gods, Eivor, what happened?

speaker: Eivor
en: Spies in our camp. Three men, sent by Kjotve to kill us as we slept.

speaker: Eivor
en: I returned the favor.

speaker: Sigurd
en: There, you see? This is what waiting brings. We must answer this insult!

speaker: Eivor
en: They came from Nottfall, that whaling village under Kjotve's control.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We hit him there. Burn it down, before Kjotve learns his spies are dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: He may have sent more. I can search the village while you round up the crew.

speaker: Basim
en: No need. I will send Hytham to search the area.

speaker: Basim
en: You can rely on him while we are away.

speaker: Eivor
en: We? Do you mean to you join us?

speaker: Basim
en: I have not been bred for Valhalla like you, but this will be far from my first battle.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I do not like this, but I will not stop you.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Do not lead my son into the same storm that follows you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Warriors! Drengir! When I was away, far from these frozen shores, wondering if I should ever see home again, I grew afraid. Afraid I would not return in time to see Kjotve's end! Afraid I would not see him bleed out like a stuck pig in a drift of snow! But here I am, home in time to join those I have missed, those I love, in this glorious fight! Today we seize Nottfall from Kjotve! Tonight his heart will pulse with worry, tomorrow it will burst from fear! He will beseech the gods for aid, but they will be deaf to his cries. And soon the Raven Clan will feast on his dead! You know these isles best, Wolf-Kissed. Lead us to victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will show the way, but you must lead us there.

speaker: Sigurd
en: O, Eivor, I missed having you at my side. How I wished I could have taken you along on my travels.

speaker: Eivor
en: Styrbjorn did not trust fate with both of our lives.

speaker: Sigurd
en: He had no reason to fear. Together we are unstoppable.

speaker: Eivor
en: Get ready!

speaker: Sigurd
en: The Ravens claim Nottfall for Odin!

speaker: Eivor
en: Raze this place! Burn and pillage! And let all who pledge to Kjotve feel the frost of our steel!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Let the flames have them! Supply Wagons. We should destroy them.

speaker: Basim
en: Watch your backs!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, destroy those wagons.

speaker: Basim
en: Notfall lies in ruin! Let the blood and ash be a warning

speaker: Bragi
en: Ships are coming!

speaker: Guthorm the Wise
en: Hail, Raven Clan! You reap a bloody harvest!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Who are you, gestr (stranger). Name yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know his face. He met with you father not long ago.

speaker: Guthorm the Wise
en: I did indeed. I am Guthorm, uncle to King Harald of the North. I speak for my nephew when there is need.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This is not King Harald's land. Why does he send warriors so far south?

speaker: Guthorm the Wise
en: You may ask him yourself. My lord?

speaker: King Harald
en: Thank you, Uncle. You are Sigurd of the Raven Clan, is that right? Son of the wise King Styrbjorn?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I am. And you are standing on his land, King Harald. Land we have reclaimed with blood and steel.

speaker: King Harald
en: That I see, and I honor it. For I have not come to war against you, but for you. At the request of your father.

speaker: Eivor
en: The canny wolf. Was this the plan he spoke of?

speaker: King Harald
en: I offer my support. With my warriors, your Raven Clan can take Kjotve's fortress and settle this rivalry for good.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This is good news, Eivor. The wandering king will tip our fortunes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Any man who wishes to see the end of Kjotve is a friend of mine. We thank you, King Harald.

speaker: King Harald
en: Your trust in me will be repaid.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a shame, great king, that you came all this way to offer aid that we do not need.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I must strongly disagree, Eivor. This is a gift from the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: That may come with a price.

speaker: King Harald
en: Worry not . The balance has been paid. This victory shall be yours to savor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why risk your men to help us, king? Have you a stake in this fight?

speaker: King Harald
en: This war between Kjotve's clan and your own has long simmered on my southern border. I wish to see it put to rest. There will be no peace while Kjotve lives. But there is much agreement between your father and me.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This blood feud runs deep, King Harald. We welcome your help, but I must lead the charge.

speaker: King Harald
en: I see. Is this a question of honor?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is. Many winters ago, Kjotve broke an oath to our fathers. He betrayed a friendly peace and slaughtered many...

speaker: King Harald
en: I understand. Sigurd Jarl will lead the assault against Kjotve and his clan. Give him full command of my ships and my warriors. When your victory is in hand, Sigurd, find me in Alrekstad and we will celebrate together.

speaker: Guthorm the Wise
en: Our men will gather at Florli, near the mouth of the fjord northeast of here. Will you join us?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Hold a moment. You captain our longship, Eivor. Meet us there and we will claim Kjotve's head for the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother, I have waited too many years for this day. When Kjotve stands before us, give me the final blow.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You will have it Eivor. You deserve it.

speaker: Dag
en: Eivor, give us a hand! Harald is generous with his troops. More than I would be

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot fathom his game. He is either a young fool... or deceptively wise.

speaker: Dag
en: Whatever his reason, I have a good feeling this war is near its end.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Good timing. We would have stormed the place without you.

speaker: Eivor
en: What have you seen?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Soldiers aplenty. Wagons going in and out. That weasel Burgred is here, I'm sure of it.

speaker: Ivarr
en: The bathhouse there, and that church, see? I sent a scout to check them both. Should be back any moment now. Did you see Ubba and Sigurd in Templebrough?

speaker: Eivor
en: No. And if Burgred is hiding here, I won't have to.

speaker: Ivarr
en: There are a lot of things we would not have to do if we stuck to killing kings. Thanks to my brother, now we are into making them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Burgred's wife was hiding there. Ubba's taken her back to Tamworth.

speaker: Eivor
en: Something wrong?

speaker: Ivarr
en: My brother, that's what.

speaker: Eivor
en: No small tension between you two. Thought you'd be more like-minded.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You and Sigurd always see eye to eye?

speaker: Eivor
en: More often than not.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You are still young. You live to my age, and you will see. The closer you get, the greater the stink that rises.

speaker: Eivor
en: He's doing the best he can to see this through. So am I. It would go over easier if you were of the same mind.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I'm here aren't I?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ubba has his way and you have yours, that much is clear. I'm not here to play favorites.

speaker: Ivarr
en: No, you are here to make your mark. I know what it means to be a young drengr (courageous warrior). You think of glory and destiny.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've got me all figured out.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I know your type, Wolf-Kissed. But me, I am not looking as far into the future as you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Time's up for your scout, I'd say. He's either dead or run off.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Give him a chance.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can't risk them seeing us, and Burgred slipping away again. You stay here and wait for your scout. I'm going in.

speaker: Eivor
en: The church is well-guarded. Might find a way around.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Keep it up, lads. Every little bit helps.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: The farmers are starting to push back.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Then kindly remind them of their duty to Mercia, and to their king. You heard Leofrith. Secure whatever food you can. The Danes won't hesitate to burn our fields. And if we can't eat, we can't fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite a haul of goods they've hidden away.

speaker: Eivor
en: Crates full of food and supplies. Burgred's not giving up without a fight

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be the bathhouse. Need to find a way inside.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: This is bollocks! We should be out there, fighting to take Tamworth back from the Danes!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: We're to secure our food-stored first. Leofrith's orders.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Leofrith's orders... pah! The king's grown tired of him, you know. That's what all the men are saying.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: Tired? How do you mean?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Are you blind? He questions Burgred's orders every chance he gets. Has done ever since the Danes showed up.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you lost your mind?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I feared you were one of them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep quiet. What are you doing here?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I'm... I was looking for Burgred.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are Ivarr's scout...

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I hoped I might find Burgred myself, and talk him into surrendering. But he's not in Ledecestre.

speaker: Eivor
en: How can you be sure?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Leofrith passed this way with some men. I eavesdropped. It seems they're only stockpiling food here. But he did say something of interest... gave orders to send more men to Burgred's wife, the Lady Æthelswith. She's in Templebrough.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: She would know where Burgred's hiding.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not anymore. We stormed the fortress and took the lady back to Tamworth.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: She would know where Burgred's hiding.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Do you hear that? The sounds of battle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr... let's get you out of here, now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are you going?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I know my way around. We'll go through the market. This way!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Find the king! Put him on his knees before me.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: They're everywhere!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay close to me!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Wh-what do I do?

speaker: Eivor
en: Fight, man! Fight!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Burgred! Where are you, you little shit! Burgred! Face me, lord!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you hurt? Speak up.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I... I don't think so... My God... I didn't want it to come to this.

speaker: Eivor
en: They would have killed you, Ceolbert. You had no choice. Now don't move.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Where is your king, Saxon? Where is he?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: Lord our Father, grant me salvation

speaker: Ivarr
en: When does their God find the time to answer so much mumbling and whimpering?

speaker: Eivor
en: You're reckless, Ivarr! Ceolbert could have been killed.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Who am I to stand in the light of a boy searching for his balls?

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't excuse yourself. You enjoy this too much.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Stop. It wasn't Ivarr who sent me. I sent myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have caution, boy. Until your father is crowned, you're Mercia's enemy, not its champion. You understand?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Now return to Repton and remain there until we call.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Will you not stay, Wolf-Kissed? There is no king, but we have corpses to loot!

speaker: Eivor
en: Burgred's Lady Aethelswith is in Templebrough. I'm going to find out what she knows.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm off to Tamworth. The Lady Aethelswith may be singing a sweeter song.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Take everything! Pile the soldiers here! Let these people bear witness to the carnage that awaits their kingdom. Whoever trains these Mercian soldiers should be relieved of their duty, I think!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Abase yourself, worms! Faith is all that stands between you and damnation! Repent now and be forgiven, or burn in Hell for eternity! And eternity, I assure you, is a very long time! You might think going down to the market and back takes a while, but that's nothing to eternity! So watch out!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: I am heavy with sin! I need guidance!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Pater noster, qui es in caelis, sanctificetur nomen tuum.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: How can I believe when the Danes are knocking at our doors?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Faith is our salvation! Faith will bring us to the Lord!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: I want to join, but my wife won't have it! Should I leave her?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Faith will show you the way! Make the right choice!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You there! Dane! Come and be saved!

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't you get tired of all that yelling?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Welcome, heathen. Praise God, who has brought you here to join us.

speaker: Eivor
en: My ship is not steered by your god.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Cease your blasphemy! You have been summoned by God to be baptized! Submit or pay the price!

speaker: Eivor
en: And how do you plan to make me?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Faith is our weapon, and the only one we need.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your threats aren't worth the breath of my arse.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: We'll see about that. Faith! Cleanse this pagan scum!

speaker: Faith
en: Sinner! Die at the hands of Faith!

speaker: Eivor
en: Think twice, nun. I won't be dying today.

speaker: Faith
en: Smite the unbelievers! Smite them till they're smoten!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you so keen to meet your god?

speaker: Faith
en: The only good heretic is a very dead heretic!

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin's spear! Did your father mate with an ox?

speaker: Faith
en: Salvation through pain! Come get some!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that the best your god can give? People will worship anyone these days.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Faith! Faith...! You monster, how could you? She was so sweet, gentle, and delicate!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Great! Now I have to find someone else to tell me what to do.

speaker: Eivor
en: Acha. Where is Hunwald?

speaker: Acha
en: I tried to console him, but he pushed me away. I love the boy, I do. But I fear what would happen if he took his father's title. He's fragile and scattered. I saw him ride north, following the paved Roman road. To the old tall tree where he often passed time with his father, I imagine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald loved you like family. And you lied to his face.

speaker: Acha
en: In my way I was trying to protect him. O Saint Cuthbert, give me strength.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oaths and ale work better than your prayers and saints.

speaker: Eivor
en: What devil put you up to all this deception?

speaker: Acha
en: I wasn't put up, Eivor. I felt compelled to carry on for the good of the shire. Until I knew the truth.

speaker: Eivor
en: A pretty answer for an ugly lie.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have better people to speak to. Wallow in your self-made grief, abbess.

speaker: Acha
en: Go then. Why linger here?

speaker: Acha
en: I must beg forgiveness from my God. The Lord lifts up the meek... we must praise Him.

speaker: Eivor
en: That must be the tree Acha mentioned. Hunwald may be nearby.

speaker: Hunwald
en: These woods, Father. O, these woods... I remember the days we spent here together. Here upon this spot. Ducking and hiding through the rushes. With bow and arrow. Chasing rabbits and squirrels. A thousand arrows I fired, and a hundred trees I bled, but not a single animal could I catch. All of them, fled.

speaker: Hunwald
en: H-hello! Eivor? Is that you?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Eivor, what a pleasant surprise! Would you drink with me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald...

speaker: Hunwald
en: Come! Sit, sit. Stay with me a while and comcemplate... conmemtate... contemplate the view.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be easy with your grief, Hunwald. If you're not careful, it's a poison you'll bear in your blood for the rest of your life.

speaker: Hunwald
en: No need to worry! For I have found the antidote for it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Collect yourself, Hunwald. There's many a man in Lincolnscire who'd pay to see your head on a pike.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Well they can wait a moment!

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's have a drink. To the memory of your father.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Here we go a wassailing, among the leaves so green!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not gorge on grief, nor give in to sadness, but let your aching love light the mead of your eyes and lead you to triumph.

speaker: Hunwald
en: That is... quite lovely. My father would have liked you. He liked all those who could swing a sword and speak a verse with ease.

speaker: Eivor
en: He had a large heart and a love for his people. I think I would have liked him, too.

speaker: Eivor
en: An outsider whose people ravaged his shire? I think he would have hated me.

speaker: Hunwald
en: He and I used to wander up this way all the time. He would take me hunting. And I would catch the most wretched little things, if I caught anything at all. I was a rubbish hunter. But he always said he was proud. Each and every time.

speaker: Eivor
en: A toast...

speaker: Eivor
en: ...to your father, Lord Hundbeorth of Lincolnscire. He may have dwindled from this world in death, but in life, he was as stalwart as this tree.

speaker: Hunwald
en: A wise old oak, yes!

speaker: Eivor
en: Skal.

speaker: Eivor
en: To you, Hunwald. You have love in your heart and hope in your eyes. That's more than many can say.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Eivor, I... can't begin to...

speaker: Eivor
en: All right, lord. You're all right. Skal.

speaker: Eivor
en: To this great land that bore you. It was here long before your father, and it'll be here long after he's gone. Skal.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Skal!

speaker: Hunwald
en: And then ... and then my father says, "It's the right goat, but it's the wrong end!"

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ah, my Swanburrow loves that one. She has a great sense of humor, my ladylove. Father would have liked her.

speaker: Eivor
en: Right, your Dane ladylove. She sounds lovely. Too lovely to be real.

speaker: Hunwald
en: You know what? We should visit her! We should go to Brimsgy! Er, Grimsby! Yes, yes, there's no time to lose!

speaker: Eivor
en: After you.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Nothing like drinking and riding to jostle your troubles away.

speaker: Eivor
en: And the contents of your gut.

speaker: Eivor
en: Before I let it pass, Hunwald. I spoke with Aelfgar before this. He gifted me a weapon of your father's. Should I find that odd?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Hmm. I'm not sure. They often went hunting together, so it's not strange that he should have something of my father's.

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't want it yourself? As a memento mori?

speaker: Hunwald
en: No, no. You're better suited to such gifts. I'm a talker, not a fighter.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Now come... and enjoy the splendor of my shire.

speaker: Eivor
en: You Saxons and your tiny splendor. You have never seen mountains, have you? Or deep fjords like a giant's axe wound. Or towering falls that steam in the dead of winter. Snow sparkling like a blanket of jewels. That is splendor.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Well if your homeland is so splendor-ful, why come to England at all?

speaker: Eivor
en: You cannot grow crops on a blankets of jewels.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ha! Very true.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll admit, your countryside does take the breath away.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Quite so, quite so. I love this land. And should I follow my father's footsteps, I shall do my solemn duty to protect her. I know many think me foolish, inexperienced... but I would ask that they judge me by my future hopes, not my past reputation. If I am given sway over this land and show myself to be a poor leader, shame me, punish me, of course. But give me that chance. By God, I just want to have that chance.

speaker: Eivor
en: What was that?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Birds, Eivor! Has no one told them today is a day of grief

speaker: Eivor
en: Hsst! Quiet...

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop here. Something isn't right. I'll find the trouble before it finds us.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Eivor! I am sweating from pit to toe! Do not leave me here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hush! Stay calm.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Oi! Stay down! They're close!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Wait for my signal. You'll get yours, bloody heathen.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hide or fight, Hunwald! Now!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Father, give me strength to survive this!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ah! Eivor! Help!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Devils! Who sent you? Speak or be damned!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Well struck, Eivor!

speaker: Hunwald
en: I'm over here.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's twice they tried to kill you, Hunwald.

speaker: Hunwald
en: And twice failed!

speaker: Eivor
en: We had luck. But if you're not more careful, they will succeed. Someone in Mercia wants you dead. And they'll kill anyone in the way to see it done.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes! Including my dear Swanburrow. My ladylove! Come, let us hurry away!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm serious Hunwald. Are you hearing me?

speaker: Hunwald
en: Plain and clear! Follow me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald, are you sure this place is safe!

speaker: Hunwald
en: The safest spot in the shire, yes! Here I am, with a chance to be ealdorman, but I have yet to prove myself worthy. To you. To the shire. To her! I can do nothing without my darling lady. You've made me realize how much I neglected her through this fatal stupor of mine!

speaker: Eivor
en: This I must see for myself.

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, thank the heavens, there she is!

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Hunwald! I thought for sure you'd be dead. Why didn't you send word?

speaker: Hunwald
en: It has been far too long, my little jewel. I'm so very sorry for that.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: I am fine, my love. I wilted without you, but still I grow. And who is this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, yes, I am proud to present, Eivor of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Hello, Eivor. A pleasure to meet you.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you, Swanburrow. I wasn't sure what to make of Hunwald's stories, yet here you are.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Surprised to find a Dane by his side?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not quite. I'm surprised to find a Saxon at yours. Hunwald seems to endear himself to all sorts.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Eivor agreed to help me find my father. But I'm afraid it hasn't gone well as I'd hoped.

speaker: Eivor
en: Getting to know one another will have to wait. Hunwald's in danger and so are you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You really have been courting a Dane. It's a side of you I didn't expect.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: People say we're an odd couple. I do not care much what people say.

speaker: Hunwald
en: As every boat needs an anchor, every man needs his Swanburrow. The light of my life. Eivor has been my champion as I stake my claim in Lincolnscire. But I'm afraid it hasn't gone well as I'd hoped.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: What's happened?

speaker: Hunwald
en: My father is dead. Died of a cruel disease, apparently. Then shunted off to a cellar for burial.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: O, my love, I'm sorry.

speaker: Eivor
en: And someone in your shire wants to make sure Hunwald follows his father to the grave.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Let them try. I'll cut their throats.

speaker: Eivor
en: A Shiremoot will soon be held. Hunwald should stay here, out of sight, until he can attend.

speaker: Hunwald
en: What if I left it all behind, my love? Forget my father's seat. What if I stayed here with you? Just the two of us.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Hunwald, no. This shire must be led with courage and heart. Follow in your father's footsteps and lead this shire as he did.

speaker: Eivor
en: Whatever strength you lack, you have in Swanburrow. Heed her advice.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes... If anyone can lift my spirits in time for the Shiremoot, it's you, my dear.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Come inside and rest your bumbling bones, love. Be well, Eivor. And thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: We had a deal, Hunwald, my aid for an oath. If you won't stake your claim here, then I have no reason to lend you my sword.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I'm sorry. My will falters from time to time. After some rest, my senses will return.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Lie down, love. You'll be fine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rest, Hunwald. By sunrise, you'll have shed all your tears and pissed out the last of the ale.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Eivor is right, Hunwald. Tomorrow is a new day.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes... yes, resting next to my angel will heal all that is broken within me.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: Be well, Eivor. And thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep watch over that one. Men have come for him, more than once.

speaker: Swanburrow
en: My blade will keep him safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not doubt it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke's men get their weapons from Crawleah. I will see what I can do about that. Soma should be somewhere nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma. What is happening here?

speaker: Soma
en: Bandits, taking advantage of the disorder in Suthsexe to fill their pockets. Odin smiles on us today.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let us make sure this place is burned to the ground. Fulke will get no more weapons from here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have burned part of the town already. Finish the job with me. Fulke will get no more weapons from here.

speaker: Soma
en: We could charge in while they are distracted, but it would be safer to use fire arrows.

speaker: Eivor
en: We strike hard. No better time than now.

speaker: Soma
en: Lead and I will follow.

speaker: Soma
en: Move in! We take the fight to the enemy!

speaker: Soma
en: Fulke's plans will be smoke and ash.

speaker: Eivor
en: She will not hide from me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Burn this town to the ground!

speaker: Soma
en: Fulke's men will have to fight with twigs.

speaker: Soma
en: Good work, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soon there will be nothing left.

speaker: Eivor
en: We burn them from afar. Watch them scatter like cats.

speaker: Soma
en: A sound decision. I agree.

speaker: Soma
en: Archers, take your position! Stand ready, Eivor. When they see us, they will charge. We must defend the men.

speaker: Soma
en: Here they come! Stand fast, Eivor! Protect the archers!

speaker: Eivor
en: They will not get past me!

speaker: Soma
en: More Saxons Hold them back!

speaker: Eivor
en: Come at me, Saxons! I will cut you down like wheat!

speaker: Soma
en: Save your energy, Eivor. There may be more yet!

speaker: Soma
en: Again they come! How many more can there be?

speaker: Soma
en: Their numbers dwindle. We are winning!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not falter now, Soma!

speaker: Soma
en: Never.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough! Crawleah dances with hearth-tongues. Soon it will be ashes.

speaker: Soma
en: Archers! Lower your bows and return to camp!

speaker: Soma
en: We cannot leave the archers undefended!

speaker: Eivor
en: The best defense is to attack! Go! Get in their teeth!

speaker: Soma
en: Move in, men! Storm the town!

speaker: Eivor
en: I left Fulke's supply carts in cinders. Good to see they have not been replaced. She will get no more weapons from here.

speaker: Soma
en: Victory without risk? I'll take that.

speaker: Eivor
en: The forges have been destroyed. No more weapons will be made here.

speaker: Soma
en: Well fought, Eivor. My archers and I will return to camp and await your further orders.

speaker: Havi
en: The shelter must be nearby. A clue! One of their shelters must be nearby. I should look around for any signs leading to the shelter.

speaker: Havi
en: This way will take me to the dwarves. This points the way to a dwarven shelter. A dwarf-mark. They must be in hiding nearby. I must be close to a shelter. A dwarven rune. I must be on the right track. Dwarves have left their mark here. The dwarves hide their paths in plain sight. There is a shelter not far from here. Dwarven markings. If I follow, they will lead me to a shelter. A runic symbol. A shelter must be close.

speaker: Havi
en: What are they looking at? There must be something...

speaker: Havi
en: I wonder what this nonsense means. A poem or a riddle?

speaker: Havi
en: A dead end... in every sense.

speaker: Havi
en: If Baldr were here, he would surely find wonder in these crystals. He has a child's innocence, my boy. I pray he has it still, after... all of this. These dwarves... I need them, though it chafes me to admit it. Be gracious, Havi. Humble and patient.

speaker: Havi
en: Glorious dwarf-kind... reduced to this?

speaker: Havi
en: A hugr shrine? Just a dead-end.

speaker: Havi
en: How did the dwarves get all the way up here?

speaker: Havi
en: So this is where they hide.

speaker: Havi
en: So much gold, so little worth.

speaker: Havi
en: The most disrespectful dwarves I have ever met.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Fine work. A long house to rival any I have seen. Now come. Randvi has found something I would like you to see.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor. Sigurd. I give you England... and its four kingdoms. Mercia, East Anglia, Northumbria, and Wessex. From the few plans and maps I discovered here, I believe the Sons of Ragnar have pushed further into Mercia, here...

speaker: Randvi
en: My scouts will soon tell me if I am correct.

speaker: Eivor
en: And where are we?

speaker: Randvi
en: Here. In this unnamed copse of trees.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Unnamed? We cannot let that stand. What will we call this place?

speaker: Eivor
en: I might have an idea. Ravensthorpe. The village of ravens.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Hm. I like it. The poet in you sings once again. One day, this name will be known throughout all of England.

speaker: Randvi
en: A name is only a beginning. If we want renown, we must build. Expand.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Agreed. We should begin with a forge. Can you help Gunnar get working again?

speaker: Eivor
en: We will need cargo, supplies.

speaker: Sigurd
en: For that, our neighbors will provide, whether they wish to or not.

speaker: Randvi
en: Scarcely arrived and now we must raid?

speaker: Sigurd
en: We cannot master this land merely by asking.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll go and speak with Gunnar now.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Good work, my dear. And what else have you found?

speaker: Randvi
en: Short notes, mostly. Scraps of plans, old letters. A few rune-stone messages. It took some time to decipher the mess and piece it all back together.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Not a bad place, Eivor. Not at all! Can I help you with anything?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd wants your forge up and running as soon as possible. For that we need supplies and riches.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Ah! You mean to go a-viking, then! Good, good. How I miss those days! Ransacking and pillaging, blades singing and shields splintering.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would ask you to join us, but you are the only blacksmith we have. We cannot afford your loss.

speaker: Gunnar
en: O, it's no bother. Better I forge axes than swing them. My place is here, not pulling on the oar of a river-horse. Though you do remind me... I found a map among the bandits' rubbish. Marked up with the locations of Saxon monk-huts.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. Bandits know as well as we do, monasteries are full of riches and loot.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Take the map with you. And put it to better use than they did.

speaker: Eivor
en: We lack the needed supplies to build Gunnar's forge. I should gather the crew and go raiding.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bend your ears and listen all! For the good of our clan, it is time we go a-viking! Today we raid, that tomorrow we may build!

speaker: Dag Nithisson
en: At last! We will crack these Christian monasteries like a row of hens' eggs!

speaker: Bragi
en: The Saxons know we are here, Dag. Their monasteries will be well guarded.

speaker: Dag
en: Nah! By nothing more than priests and prayers, I'd wager!

speaker: Bragi
en: Eivor. Look there. A monastery.

speaker: Dag
en: I stand ready... only say the word!

speaker: Eivor
en: That is all we need for Gunnar... but if there is more, we should claim it.

speaker: Eivor
en: This was a good day and some fine work from all of you. We should return home and unload everything.

speaker: Dag
en: Are you certain there aren't a few more gold nuggets squirreled away somewhere?

speaker: Eivor
en: My gut tells me no.

speaker: Dag
en: So, Eivor? What's your count?

speaker: Eivor
en: My count? Dag, I have no need to count my kills. They number too many.

speaker: Dag
en: Likely story, Wolf-Kissed. Me, I killed... twenty-six I think.

speaker: Bragi
en: Nah... There were barely a dozen when we arrived, Dag.

speaker: Dag
en: No, no. You missed them. They attacked from the forest.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Back so soon? And with good news, I hope.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think we have all we need.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Ah! This is wonderful, Eivor! A forge bigger and hotter than my old forge back in Fornburg. Come visit me anytime. For weapons and gear, there is no man better than me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will, Gunnar. Have no doubt.

speaker: Norvid
en: The Saxons break their kingdoms into smaller territories called shires. This one is called Ledecestrescire... it isn't spelled how you think.

speaker: Sunniva
en: And as you suspected, the Sons of Ragnar moved there some months ago. We know for sure that Ivarr and Ubba are alive and well in Repton.

speaker: Randvi
en: Excellent work, both of you. Now have a rest and a horn of ale. You have more than earned it.

speaker: Norvid
en: Thank you, Randvi. We'll be here if you need us.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, in here.

speaker: Eivor
en: What will you keep in this room?

speaker: Sigurd
en: My finest weapon. For this room is yours... here you may lay your head, hang your axe, or be alone with your thoughts. Do you like it?

speaker: Eivor
en: It suits me well. But I would be just as happy lodging with the raiders on the wharf. I need no special treatment.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This is not special treatment. I want you here in the longhouse, close at hand. I may be the jarl of this clan, but you and I lead together. As ever. So get acquainted with your room. And when you are ready, meet me at the stables.

speaker: Eivor
en: A letter box, for messages and requests.

speaker: Eivor
en: A bed better than many I have slept in. And a good place to recover. Hm. Not much, but it is mine.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes. Be ready to ride at a moment's notice.

speaker: Hytham
en: Count on it, my friend. The path ahead is bright.

speaker: Basim
en: With glory at its end.

speaker: Dag
en: But why now?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Dag, please. This must be done.

speaker: Dag
en: Yes, and I can help! Look at me, look at these arms! I am a beast!

speaker: Eivor
en: What was that about? Is Basim leaving us already?

speaker: Dag
en: Sigurd means to leave as well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that true?

speaker: Sigurd
en: We know the Sons of Ragnar have camped in the North. It would do us well to pay them a visit, to strengthen our ties to this land.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that where Basim has gone?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Basim's motives are his own, leave it at that. We have more pressing plans. I am riding to Ledecestrescire, to a town called Repton. Eivor, I expect you to join me when you have finished here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can come now. I only need a horse.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not yet. First speak with Randvi. She has more than one task for you here. Apart from growing this settlement, you must seek out alliances as well. We cannot pacify England with so few friends.

speaker: Dag
en: Then I must join you, Sigurd. For I am a fitter companion on long roads.

speaker: Sigurd
en: No, Dag, you belong here with the raiders. And you will act as Eivor commands.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ride in safety, brother. I will follow as soon as I can.

speaker: Dag
en: Yes! And I will keep our raiders sharp.

speaker: Dag
en: Do as Eivor commands? Is he testing me?

speaker: Eivor
en: He may be. Sigurd is a wise man.

speaker: Dag
en: I would sooner take orders from a louse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Briggworth. A forest of Saxon swords awaits within those walls of stone. I should consult with Basim. He will be nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: What have you discovered?

speaker: Basim
en: Briggworth swarms with guards, reinforced from the river. Word is that two of Fulke's finest oversee such matters.

speaker: Eivor
en: We should kill these leaders and burn their ships. Crippled and put to panic, their men will be in no place to join Fulke at Portcestre.

speaker: Basim
en: Frightened men look to their own interests. A good plan.

speaker: Basim
en: One down, one to go. The other should be somewhere in the keep.

speaker: Basim
en: One down, one to go. The other should be near the boats.

speaker: Eivor
en: On my way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now the boats. We burn them to the waterline.

speaker: Basim
en: I am with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: No more sailing for these Saxons.

speaker: Basim
en: Indeed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have seen to one of Fulke's lackeys already. I will see to the other just as well. That and the ships in the river.

speaker: Basim
en: Good. Without leaders or transport, they will be no help to Portcestre.

speaker: Basim
en: One down, one to go. The other should be somewhere in the keep.

speaker: Basim
en: One down, one to go. The other should be near the boats.

speaker: Eivor
en: On my way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now the boats. We burn them to the waterline.

speaker: Basim
en: I am with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: No more sailing for these Saxons.

speaker: Basim
en: Indeed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke's lackeys are already feeding the worms. But we can burn their ships all the same.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes. Deny them a way to travel, and they will not trouble us at Portcestre.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now the boats. We burn them to the waterline.

speaker: Basim
en: I am with you.

speaker: Basim
en: Our work is done. Fulke will have no help from Briggworth now. See you back at camp.

speaker: Brodir
en: You can cross now! The bridge should hold!

speaker: Brodir
en: Why repair these bridges when they just fall apart!

speaker: Havi
en: I mean no offense, but it does seem a pointless task.

speaker: Brodir
en: Such is life among the dead. The corruption what eats at these bridges is fed by the same Hands who demand their maintenance.

speaker: Havi
en: And whose hands are those?

speaker: Brodir
en: The Hands of Nidhogg. A twisted collection of druids, mystics and priests who serve the ruler of these pestilent lands.

speaker: Havi
en: Nidhogg? I know that name. A creature whose depravity is legendary. He reigns here?

speaker: Brodir
en: Aye. Drinking the sap of Yggdrasil's roots, while his Hands gather the living and dead for him to feast upon.

speaker: Havi
en: And the ones responsible for the rot that eats at these bridges? If I eliminate them, it would ease my passage through here?

speaker: Brodir
en: Nidhogg is the true root of the rot, but cutting away his Hands would slow its spread. You could start with my owner. He's a dark druid who patrols this area, dressed to inspire terror and loathing.

speaker: Brodir
en: The dark druid may be hard to spot in the mist, but his attire is unmistakable.

speaker: Havi
en: That must be the druid the thrall spoke of.

speaker: Havi
en: With luck, the druid won't detect my approach.

speaker: Havi
en: Some of the druid's belongings might be useful among these degenerates.

speaker: Brodir
en: My liberator!

speaker: Brodir
en: I shouldn't be surprised that you were sent from above.

speaker: Havi
en: Not sent. I serve my own purpose. Enjoy your found freedom, I'm off to face my fate.

speaker: Brodir
en: Would you stay a moment to cut your travel time by half?

speaker: Havi
en: You promised me swiftness once before if I helped you, and I am no further along now.

speaker: Brodir
en: These things take time. You've slain one of Nidhogg's serpents, not cleaned out the nest.

speaker: Havi
en: I do not have time to hunt down a whole cult.

speaker: Brodir
en: I do not expect you to destroy all the Hands of Nidhogg. I just need an item ... from the hands of a merchant.

speaker: Havi
en: A merchant? And I suppose a thrall wouldn't have coin to purchase this thing.

speaker: Brodir
en: I've saved up for my freedom and it's all yours. I just need three little stones which you'll likely get for free.

speaker: Havi
en: Then why do you even need me? Why not get it yourself?

speaker: Brodir
en: She doesn't serve ... thralls, even former ones. But I've seen my old owner go into the shop. Somewhere around the tower.

speaker: Brodir
en: The entrance is somewhere around the tower. I believe it requires a singular sight.

speaker: Havi
en: That I have.

speaker: Havi
en: Another thief...another opportunity.

speaker: Havi
en: I must move carefully.

speaker: Havi
en: My patience has been rewarded.

speaker: Havi
en: Greetings, trader. I seek three stones

speaker: Wolfsbane
en: So, you're the one! Why didn't you say so sooner? I hate when fated items linger here unclaimed.

speaker: Havi
en: You knew I would come for the stones? Are you a seer?

speaker: Wolfsbane
en: No, but down here, one needs to traffic in prophecy from time to time. I supply what's required, no questions asked.

speaker: Havi
en: A most discreet agent of fate.

speaker: Wolfsbane
en: There are the stones. Come talk to me when you're in the mood to spend. Money is always welcome.

speaker: Brodir
en: The moonstones!

speaker: Havi
en: They're yours. And now, if there's nothing more required of me

speaker: Brodir
en: You may go. I have what I need. I hope the payment provided was equal to the effort.

speaker: Brodir
en: Too close together and the trap may be avoided ... too far apart and their power grows too weak...

speaker: Havi
en: Wake up!

speaker: Havi
en: The placement of the stones has activated their power. Is that what struck the thrall down?

speaker: Left Hand of Nidhogg
en: Go, beast! Show me what you've learned!

speaker: Havi
en: This wolf seems almost human! And so white!

speaker: Havi
en: A power protects this creature. I need something to counter it.

speaker: Havi
en: Found your weakness, wolf.

speaker: Brodir
en: No! Leave her alone!

speaker: Brodir
en: Stay your amazement, traveler, and help me kill some cultists!

speaker: Brodir
en: You don't own us!

speaker: Brodir
en: I won't let them hurt you, Systir! Not anymore!

speaker: Brodir
en: Systir will recover once I move her away from the moonstones' influence.

speaker: Havi
en: Away? I thought the moonstones helped her resist the spell.

speaker: Brodir
en: No, they weaken us. Our true forms are wolves, so ... I'll wait until you're gone. She may be ... confused.

speaker: Havi
en: Hah, I understand. I'm heartened that family bonds could survive such a place, but I will be glad to quit this land of rot.

speaker: Brodir
en: Not everything in this place is as corrupt as the wyrm who gnaws at it. Some keep hope alive for the Rebirth that will be Ragnarök. You have my thanks and my pledge. When you find yourself sorely hurt, we'll catch your scent and come.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Eivor! You have arrived just in time!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is it Sigrblot already?

speaker: Sunniva
en: The days are long and the nights are warm and lit with fires.

speaker: Eivor
en: And it marks the beginning of raiding season!

speaker: Sunniva
en: We still need to finish gathering offerings for the gods so we can earn their favor. With their blessings we will have calm waters, good winds and much bounty!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar must be busy forging weapons and army.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Yes, he aske to bring in an extra set of hands. Swinda has already set up her forge by the training ground.

speaker: Sunniva
en: But weapons are not the only tools of war, Eivor. You must train your mind as you train your body.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eager to see what this mind training would look like.

speaker: Sunniva
en: I would show you around but I need to get my offering ready for the bonfire. Check around the settlement to see what's needed. Perhaps you can make yourself useful!

speaker: Eivor
en: Am I not already useful?

speaker: Sunniva
en: O! Be sure to say hello to Norvid. But first, take this torch and mark the beginning of the festival!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I will not stand for it! Rob me of my coin, rob me of my house... to Hell with it, rob me of my wife! But may God strike you where you stand if you rob me of my pie!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this about god and pies?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Someone stole my pie, and I, a skilled sniffer, am going to weed that pie thief out!

speaker: Eivor
en: All for a piece of pie?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: It is no ordinary pie! My pies top any other pies, and the blasted pie thief knows it! The smell... O, the smell! The thief went down this road!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Come out, thief! I know you are here, I can smell my pie! The thief should not be far. I will find that scoundrel!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Mmm, the fragrance of melted butter... comforting, warm.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: A-ha! The thief came by! I am on the trail! My pie is near, my nose does not lie! Come out, thief!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: The coy sweetness of berries... I smell it!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O-ho, the thief must be near now. I recognize my pie's allure to any nose! Come out, come out! Mmm, the aroma of a pastry baked just right... the thief is near!

speaker: Norse Child
en: Hmm... I think this is just the right amount...
