speaker: Norse Child
en: Ah!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Caught, scoundrel. Now, give me my delicious pie back.

speaker: Norse Child
en: Delicious? Your pie was blander than my late father's face.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: What did you put in my pie? This smell, this... aroma. It's never produced such an effect before!

speaker: Norse Child
en: I added some honey. It'll enhance the berries by a bit...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Good God... it does enhance the sweet smell. That is... remarkable. Unheard of. A miracle!

speaker: Eivor
en: It seems like this child would make an extraordinary baker, and Jorvik could use one less thief.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Well... it does smell spectacular. You have a keen sense for the culinary arts, child. You want a job?

speaker: Norse Child
en: God's piss of luck! Thank you so much. You won't regret it, I have so many ideas.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Just stop stealing the pies.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Ah, thank you for your help. Come by my stall should you have a craving for pie.

speaker: Norse Child
en: Pies! Pies! Get your sweet, warm pies here!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Our crust is unprecedented, a delight to any mouth! Blueberries, raspberry... and honey! A heavenly combination!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You, have a pie for the trouble.

speaker: Eivor
en: They have a tavern. I should see if anyone there knows where to find Little Mother.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: It's painful enough dealing with these zealots, but it's even worse since that nun got her fancy prisoner.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Shh! We are not supposed to talk about it. Do you not fear God?

speaker: Eivor
en: Tavernkeep! I'm new here. Can you tell me about Little Mother?

speaker: French Man 1
en: Her deliverance rituals are all these drunkards talk about. Isn't that right, Bastien, you loudmouth sot!

speaker: French Man 1
en: Take a seat, Northerner! Bastien's buying, and he'll tell you all about it! Right, Bastien?

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: That's me alright! Bastien the Loudmouth. Bastien the Drunk. And let's not forget, Bastien the Drink-buyer, eh barkeep. Sit down, Northerner! I'll buy you a drink too.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: You have us at an advantage, Northerner. Where do you hail from?

speaker: Eivor
en: I just got in from Melun.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Melun! You're not one of Sigfred's, are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm just passing through, friend.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Do not go through Aquila! That's where they take the poor fools for deliverance. They might take you too! (laughs)

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me about Little Mother and her deliverance rituals.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: I can tell you it's a lot of extra work for us! Since she got her special prisoner, it's worse.

speaker: French Soldier 5
en: Shh! Bastien! We can't speak of God's business!

speaker: Eivor
en: A special prisoner?

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Someone close to the king, they say. A woman, no less.

speaker: French Soldier 5
en: Mon Dieu! (My God!) Bastien!

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Ah, but we cannot speak of that lest God hears us. Drink up, my friends! Bastien is buying!

speaker: French Soldier 6
en: Little Mother just won't let us rest! We are working day and night. I'm barely getting any sleep!

speaker: Eivor
en: I overheard you mention Little Mother.

speaker: French Soldier 7
en: What are you doing listening to people's conversation? Damned Northerner!

speaker: Eivor
en: Easy friend, I am just curious.

speaker: French Soldier 7
en: If you're so interested in Little Mother, you can walk out the back, up the path, and knock on her door!

speaker: Eivor
en: Little Mother's house. I should look around.

speaker: French Soldier 8
en: People say Little Mother is a fanatical, but the truth is she helped me turn my life around.

speaker: French Soldier 9
en: Me too, brother. She was the only one who ever told me the hard truth. I could not deny it.

speaker: French Soldier 8
en: Amen. I wouldn't listen to anyone, but I listened to her. I'm a better man today because of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Little Mother has the queen. The seal on this note is the same symbol I found in Engelwin's room.

speaker: French Man 2
en: Submit yourself to God, resist the devil and he will flee. He will flee. He will flee.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will get you out of there.

speaker: French Man 2
en: No! Leave me alone! I have to pray so my deliverance will come. Go away!

speaker: Eivor
en: Says here Little Mother plans to put the queen through a deliverance ritual. Mentions an underground chamber beneath the crypt in Aquila. I need to find that crypt.

speaker: French Soldier 10
en: You're either here for a deliverance ritual or you're on your way to somewhere else. Understand?

speaker: Eivor
en: It would be wise to cover up. The less attention I draw, the easier it will be to find the queen.

speaker: French Man 3
en: Aquila is no place for your kind. Leave.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: There's another poor soul here for that dreadful ritual. Terrible, terrible. God save them.

speaker: French Child 1
en: There was a man who went to bed, the devil got inside his head, deli-vry-ance for him they said, then Little Mother killed him dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hey there! Who taught you that song?

speaker: French Child 1
en: I made it up myself! It's about the deli-vry-ance they do at the creep. I think they must have delivery-ed this deer too.

speaker: Eivor
en: The creep... you mean the crypt?

speaker: French Child 1
en: Yeah. I see people go there all the time, but I'm not allowed. Mother says the guard will beat me if I go too close.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will have a talk with those crypt guards.

speaker: French Child 1
en: Be careful! Don't talk to Little Mother! She'll give you a de-liv-er-y-ance and you'll end up like the deer!

speaker: French Soldier 11
en: I've lost my family, my future, and now the key to the crypt as well. The only thing I have left is wine so... santé (cheers)!

speaker: French Soldier 12
en: Keep your voice down! You've made enough trouble tonight. If the captain finds you drinking, you're done. And if he finds that we've lost the key, we're both done. Keep quiet and help me look for it.

speaker: Eivor
en: The guard's key. It must unlock something nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is a smell of blood amongst the dust, and a taste of iron on my tongue.

speaker: Eivor
en: A Christian sarcophagus. Most are ancient, but this one is new.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: This is the queen, no matter what the Bellatores say! Surely Little Mother won't hurt her. It isn't right.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: O! You startled me. You are one of the new assistants? Good, that is good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I have been sent to help.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: You've picked a bad time. They have the queen in there. It doesn't seem right. I ... I don't think I can do it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will. Tell me what to do.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: Really? Okay, Little Mother needs her knife dipped in sacrificial blood. It is on the table. Then you must take it to her.

speaker: Eivor
en: Alright. I'll prepare the knife and take it to Little Mother. You stay here.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: I am only helping, it is not like I'm involved in the ritual. I just prepare the knife, and take it to Little Mother. That is all.

speaker: Eivor
en: The ritual could get me close to Little Mother without putting the queen at risk.

speaker: Eivor
en: The knife is well made, but the edge is dull. It would not cut easily. I need to dip it in the blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: The knife is covered in blood. I can use it to get close to Little Mother while keeping the queen safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Deliverance seems to come at a high price.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I attack openly, they could kill the queen. I need to find a way to get close to her without raising suspicion.

speaker: Euphrasia
en: We have the queen herself! Who would have thought we could reach her so soon? Where is my assistant? I cannot begin without my knife.

speaker: Richardis
en: This is not the work of God. You know the scriptures, Euphrasia. Where do they instruct you to do such things?

speaker: Euphrasia
en: My instruction comes from God, as you will soon see.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is the queen, and she's being held by Little Mother. Those are her elite guards. Best not to try to take them head on. Maybe I can find a way to distract them.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I open the cage in the other room, the guards might leave to investigate.

speaker: Eivor
en: Please, get me out of here! They will kill me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Those guards have the key to the cage. Opening it would create a distraction.

speaker: Eivor
en: Get out quickly, before we're discovered.

speaker: French Man 3
en: Thank God, I could not take any more! I was going to leave my wife, now she is the only person I want to see!

speaker: Euphrasia
en: What was that? Guards, check the cage.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should not be seen.

speaker: French Soldier 13
en: What was all that noise? The cage is open!

speaker: French Soldier 14
en: Merde! The key is gone from my pocket!

speaker: French Soldier 15
en: Check the cage!

speaker: French Soldier 13
en: Find the prisoner!

speaker: Euphrasia
en: When my assistant returns with my knife your deliverance will begin. You should know, your Majesty, I am only God's instrument.

speaker: Richardis
en: Is your knife God's instrument too?

speaker: Euphrasia
en: I can tell you the devils fear it. How they scream at its touch! Is that the devil's fear I see in your eyes now?

speaker: Richardis
en: You mistake faith for fear. You are lost, Euphrasia!

speaker: Euphrasia
en: Ah, here is my assistant with my knife. We can begin. I am Little Mother, touched by Saint Taurinus, chosen by God.

speaker: Euphrasia
en: You are just another royal broodmare mated to a king she doesn't love. In your bitterness, you turn him against God. You see, Your Majesty, you can hide nothing from a true servant of God.

speaker: Richardis
en: God himself knows I do not try.

speaker: Euphrasia
en: That is a lie. You speak for the devil now, do you know that? But we will cut him right out of you. Then we will get to the truth, you and God and I. Put your faith in that. Assistant, my knife.

speaker: Euphrasia
en: God! Saint Taurinus! Save me!

speaker: Euphrasia
en: Who are you! Guards! To me!

speaker: Richardis
en: "I will surely deliver thee... because thou hast put thy trust in me." I am sorry she had to die. She was not always like this, and too young for such bitterness. Your methods are uncompromising, but your coming was God's doing. You are a Northerner, aren't you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor of the Raven Clan, and I'm not here because of any god. I am here because your husband, the king, sent me.

speaker: Richardis
en: Charles sent you for me?

speaker: Eivor
en: There is no time. We have to find a way out before we are discovered.

speaker: Richardis
en: I know a way. Follow me.

speaker: Richardis
en: I did not thank you for rescuing me. It was a brave thing to do.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was not bravery. I am only here because I have an agreement with Charles to return you to him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rats!

speaker: Richardis
en: The plague brought them. The vermin have no shortage of food here.

speaker: Richardis
en: We are blocked in.

speaker: Eivor
en: The wall is weak.

speaker: Richardis
en: You have been used by God today, do not doubt it. But I have to go now. There is somewhere I must be.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was not your God who freed you, it was me. And I did it only to return you to your husband. That is where we're going.

speaker: Richardis
en: You think because you did something, it was not God? God used a donkey once. He can use anyone. Even you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nevertheless, I am taking you to Charles.

speaker: Richardis
en: It is not me Charles wants. I can trust you. I know it. I perceive God working something strange through you. I will show you what Charles seeks.

speaker: Eivor
en: You could be trying to deceive me.

speaker: Richardis
en: Yes, I suppose I could. But I am not. Do you really not see the strangeness in all this, that it must be God?

speaker: Eivor
en: I see only that your God makes it so you can never be wrong.

speaker: Richardis
en: I like you, Eivor. I can see why God chose you, and why we should be friends. We will go together.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: We will leave under the cover of night. I will enter the camp alone.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: We will not leave you, Editha, no matter the danger. No matter the risks. We do this together or not at all.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Quiet! I thought I heard something.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 4
en: What do we do?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Do absolutely nothing, I will do the talking.

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't you know it's forbidden to consort like this under God's roof?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Take what you want, heathen. Just leave us be.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must be the abbess here. Why do you hide in a musky old church?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: We are not hiding. We sought to flee the shire in the midst of this ungodly war. But in our haste to leave, I lost my crosier. Fell into the hands of some guards in a camp just below, and I am not leaving without it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dangerous endeavor for three sisters of the cloth. What is your plan? You're gonna bore them with Bible passages until they give it back?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: "Do not be afraid or discouraged. For the Lord your God is with you wherever you go."

speaker: Eivor
en: It just may work. Or better yet, I can get your crosier back.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: You would help us?

speaker: Eivor
en: Mercian soldiers make good practice, and now I am invested in your plight. Lead the way.

speaker: Eivor
en: How long since you fled the ministry?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Must be weeks now. We had no plan and no help. We just knew we had to get out of Ledecestre. Whether it is Burgred on the throne or one of yours, makes no difference. Their reign would be less than godly. No offense.

speaker: Eivor
en: None taken.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: This is the camp. One of them has my crosier.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Abbess's crosier should be somewhere in this camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: The crosier. I have it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Let's go, down to the river!

speaker: Eivor
en: You're unlike any sisters I have seen, bare-fisting armed men like that.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: "I can do all things through Him who strengthens me." We Christians take matters into our own hands well enough. We are nearly there! Lincolnscire is on the other side.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Wolves! Not today, devils. Not today.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Let's cross, sisters.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now I've seen everything.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: That is far enough. Sisters, gather round. Let us pray to the Lord our God, and thank him for watching over us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your crosier.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: The Lord sent me a shepherd to help lead my flock today. Thank you. You did not have to do what you did.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is truth to that. You would have done fine on your own. I will never look upon sisters of the cloth the same way after today.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: And I will never look upon heathens the same way. Farewell.

speaker: Sigfred
en: We should talk later, Eivor.

speaker: Toka
en: Eivor! Come here! Have you ever seen something like this?

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this? Racing against pigs?

speaker: Toka
en: Yes! What is more amusing than watching drunken men race against pigs?

speaker: Eivor
en: We have done worse things to entertain ourselves.

speaker: Toka
en: Would you like to try, Eivor? There is a small prize for the winner. Or... are you not fast enough?

speaker: Eivor
en: Explain the race to me.

speaker: Toka
en: Run along the lit pathway as fast as that old swine Hermod. The first to do two laps win.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where do I start?

speaker: Eivor
en: Good sport, Eivor! You will start here. Run when the pig starts running. To raise the stakes and fun, I will join you too. Ready?

speaker: Eivor
en: Almost convinced me. I will return later.

speaker: Toka
en: Shameful, Eivor! One does not shy away from a challenge like this!

speaker: Eivor
en: Pig races haven't finished?

speaker: Eivor
en: You can still run one.

speaker: Toka
en: You are fast, Eivor! But I will catch up soon enough!

speaker: Eivor
en: Try!

speaker: Toka
en: Are you tired, Eivor? Age catches up with all of us, I guess.

speaker: Eivor
en: Just warming up.

speaker: Toka
en: Shit! Look at us, losing to a pig! The gods surely sent Gullinbursti!

speaker: Eivor
en: How they mock us.

speaker: Eivor
en: They don't make pigs that fast in England. O, and you're pretty quick as well.

speaker: Toka
en: I won the race, but Hermod is the big winner tonight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Another victory for my saga.

speaker: Toka
en: Seems your legs were blessed.

speaker: Eivor
en: No matter the winner, the joy was in the doing.

speaker: Toka
en: Indeed! And we sure sliced open Francia's belly this time, eh? Now to feast on her entrails!

speaker: Eivor
en: The winnings are worthy of a serpent's lair.

speaker: Toka
en: And the roads glistened from the dew of slaughter!

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. Though, one wonders if such butchery was needed.

speaker: Eivor
en: No lessons today, Eivor. I doubt I will remember them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Truly, Toka. Tonight we drink.

speaker: Toka
en: And tomorrow... we vomit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Listen to my words, Toka. Long after the bodies are buried and the houses rebuilt, the Franks will remember this day. All we have is an uneasy truce with Charles.

speaker: Eivor
en: And glory worthy of our ancestors.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe you should put down that ale-prow for a time.

speaker: Toka
en: Without doubt. But that time has not yet come!

speaker: Eivor
en: You are hopeless.

speaker: Toka
en: That is clear. I took a handsome sword amid the fighting. Have it. A keepsake to remember this day by.

speaker: Eivor
en: You honor me. I will cherish the blade.

speaker: Toka
en: By the way, I was glad you did not turn over Bernard. I miss Sinric, but a father like Charles is worse than no father at all.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could not doom the boy. It is not a price I think my clan would have me pay for their safety.

speaker: Toka
en: By the way, I was surprised you gave the boy to Charles. It is an ill fate to be prince to such a lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're right, Toka. But what I did was not for Bernard. It was for us. And for my clan.

speaker: Pierre
en: Ah, Eivor. Here is something even you have never done. Tossing food for sport.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cheese throwing?

speaker: Pierre
en: The most pungent game of them all. Nastier than Charles himself.

speaker: Eivor
en: You... enjoy this?

speaker: Pierre
en: I prefer to eat the cheese, but who am I to question the games of the people. So, want to toss some cheese?

speaker: Eivor
en: How do I win this game?

speaker: Pierre
en: You need to throw at least two blocks of cheese past the green banner. Quite simple. O, and you have three tries to get it done.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will not hurt to try. Should be easy.

speaker: Pierre
en: Just try not to hit anyone.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe later. I will leave you to the cheese.

speaker: Pierre
en: Take too long and there will only be crumbs left to toss.

speaker: Eivor
en: Still throwing cheese?

speaker: Pierre
en: Yes. So, feeling sharp, Eivor?

speaker: Pierre
en: Bravo, Eivor.

speaker: Pierre
en: O, need to throw harder than that!

speaker: Pierre
en: Good throw, Eivor! Never underestimate the cheese!

speaker: Eivor
en: Did I underestimate the

speaker: Pierre
en: You definitely earned a prize so, here, some stray silver from the spoils of Paris.

speaker: Pierre
en: Shame. I guess if you can't beat them, you eat them.

speaker: Eivor
en: You expected a different outcome?

speaker: Pierre
en: I thought you best for rallying a siege and swinging a sharp stick. Was not sure how you would toss some cheese.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is much about me you don't know, Pierre.

speaker: Pierre
en: O? Pray tell, what else should I know?

speaker: Eivor
en: I could tell you... or I could show you...

speaker: Pierre
en: In return, I could also show you a few tricks, of the Frankish persuasion.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will have to repay the favor then, with my own set of skills.

speaker: Pierre
en: Shall we find someplace quiet, then? Away from this rabble.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lead the way.

speaker: Pierre
en: That was... nice.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was.

speaker: Pierre
en: I hope you know... well, Eivor. You know how I am. I indulge in the finer things in life. Various fine things, in fact, and

speaker: Eivor
en: Pierre, we both know what this was.

speaker: Pierre
en: Then good.

speaker: Pierre
en: Is this something they do often where you're from? I think I might like it there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Worry not about what I might teach.

speaker: Pierre
en: Right. Plenty to celebrate about this night, don't let me spoil your fun. Go on.

speaker: Eivor
en: Worry not about what I might teach.

speaker: Pierre
en: Right. Plenty to celebrate about this night, don't let me spoil your fun. Go on.

speaker: Eivor
en: Something was amiss with Sigfred earlier. A little ale may have lifted his spirits by now.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Eivor the Talker.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite a trove of riches, Sigfred.

speaker: Sigfred
en: What were you doing with Count Odo as Charles' army marched on me and my men?

speaker: Eivor
en: I was trying to gain his surrender. What of it?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Is it not strange that you met with Odo, Richardis, even Charles himself, and yet all three still walk around with their heads?

speaker: Eivor
en: Everything I have done has been for my clan.

speaker: Sigfred
en: It is curious that we must drench our blades in battle-sweat to enjoy a night like this.

speaker: Eivor
en: We fight because we must, born in blood, doomed in die, our threads woven by unseen hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: There need not be blood for us to celebrate. We find countless reasons to feast.

speaker: Eivor
en: This celebration is not about us and those we killed. It is for our dead. So that we may honor them.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Hmph. The Frankish blood... the feasting... I still feel nothing. I find no peace in any of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: You avenged your murdered people. You gained glory in their names.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Is that why I did what I did? Vengeance and glory? I wonder anymore why any of us do the things we do. Is it Valhalla? Is it clan? Or maybe we grant ourselves reasons to go from one mead cup to the next. Maybe there are no reasons, and we are no different than wolves, driven by some inner hunger we can never understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: That may be, but for the sake of our peoples we must continue to act otherwise.

speaker: Sigfred
en: No. I do not believe there is a hall waiting for us. This world is our hall. We get but one. I shall not pretend. Francia's cup overflows with lush farmland, fat farmers, and fatter purses. All the more for us to drink. Tomorrow, we quit this place and head south for greater bounties than even a king can grant.

speaker: Eivor
en: We gave Charles our word.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Our word? You are the one who failed to return his son Bernard. Have you forgotten?

speaker: Eivor
en: That was different. Charles would have

speaker: Sigfred
en: Fuck Charles! We spared Paris today, but tomorrow we march for Burgundy. And after that, all of Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot let you do it, Sigfred.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Then stop me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to go after him.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Will it be a holmgang then, Wolf-Kissed?

speaker: Eivor
en: I only ask that you honor your agreement.

speaker: Sigfred
en: What does a crow-starver like Charles know about honor? I owe him nothing.

speaker: Sigfred
en: And he owes me everything.

speaker: Eivor
en: No amount of Frankish blood will bring Sinric or the others back. Some wrongs can never be made right.

speaker: Sigfred
en: All this talk of right and wrong. Honor. As if we can judge. It has no meaning. Can we explain all the blood on our hands, Eivor? Or are we two jesters on this Frankish stage, awaiting our final performance? Draw your weapon.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you want to find peace, this is not the way. We must build fresh bonds, look forward to something new.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Look forward. Look back. It is death in both directions. We are but a morning fog that will inevitably lift. Now answer my challenge or dishonor yourself!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your sorrow will linger if you do not face it directly. My blood, the blood of more Franks, will be no salve for your grief.

speaker: Sigfred
en: It is as if you speak with Sinric's voice. I have been at sea with no stars to guide by since he died.

speaker: Eivor
en: And if your brother were here, what would be his counsel?

speaker: Sigfred
en: To move forward. To live.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have killed yourself, Sigfred.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Ha! If that is so, I will embrace the quiet that awaits.

speaker: Eivor
en: If it is death you want, fine, I will give it to you. But this is your doing, Sigfred.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Finally, the fabled Eivor of the Raven Clan has come.

speaker: Sigfred
en: My time here is over. My kin are dead. The ones who remain must decide what is right for themselves. Let it be Toka's time.

speaker: Eivor
en: What will you do?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Leave this place. Ask different questions. Forget everything I know and... and find a new way.

speaker: Toka
en: Sigfred!

speaker: Toka
en: Where is he going?

speaker: Eivor
en: Away.

speaker: Toka
en: Then I am going with him.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, Toka. Your clan needs you.

speaker: Toka
en: A solitary man, but never more so than when he stood alone, tasked with rousing our desperate clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: He led well, but all leaders must one day step aside. That, or see others die because they held onto power for too long.

speaker: Sigfred
en: I knew it would come to this, the moment I saw you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I did not come here to kill you. But I will!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is madness.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Madness? No, Talker. It is who we are.

speaker: Sigfred
en: You are close, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is your doing. You forced my hand.

speaker: Sigfred
en: And I welcome the long dark.

speaker: Eivor
en: Toka, I

speaker: Toka
en: I know. He chose this.

speaker: Toka
en: May you find peace in the great hall. And when you drink with Father again, tell him of the glory I won for us.

speaker: Toka
en: I thought him a saga hero, never to fall.

speaker: Eivor
en: He was formidable. But stubborn.

speaker: Toka
en: When his strong voice echoed in this place, we knew what to do. We had courage... daring...

speaker: Eivor
en: And his fire still burns in your folk. Skal!

speaker: Toka
en: Skal.

speaker: Toka
en: I lack a taste for mulled wine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sometimes a leader must drink the thing they wish not to.

speaker: Pierre
en: I have word from Count Odo.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does he want?

speaker: Pierre
en: An audience with Eivor, it is urgent. He says the queen may be in peril. My spies confirmed this. Charles has been hunting again for her and the boy.

speaker: Toka
en: What do you think?

speaker: Eivor
en: Odo would not lie. If he says it's urgent, I must go. I owe the queen a debt and I am honor bound to see this through.

speaker: Toka
en: Then go. You have fortune's favor, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: The Good Sister was murdered, and where were your guards! You hear me Erke? Her blood's on you! It's a ruse, I tell you! It's them that killed Tryggr and shifted the blame!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Avgos was a hero, and you let him die! A hero for all Lunden! They'll hand Lunden to the unwashed tides, mark these words!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Death to the usurpers!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Stollid Reeves! (Stupid sheriffs!)

speaker: Eivor
en: Some surly guests outside.

speaker: Erke
en: Eivor... we were... we didn't see you enter.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's about time you found each other. Stopped tiptoeing around it.

speaker: Erke
en: Yes, I've found Stowe, and he's found me, and... here we are... together.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you stepped out today? There's a strange feeling brewing in the streets.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be cautious with that. Anyone could've walked in.

speaker: Stowe
en: They might have. And I'll serve penance before God, but I will not feel shame. Not ever.

speaker: Erke
en: Times being what they are, Elska, I'd rather not join Tryggr among the headless.

speaker: Eivor
en: You make a well-timed point. Have you stepped out today? There's a strange feeling brewing in the streets.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you stepped out today? There's a strange feeling brewing in the streets.

speaker: Erke
en: I've heard the shouts. The deaths of Avgos and Frideswid have angered many.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's hope The Compass numbers among the offended.

speaker: Stowe
en: I don't doubt it. But are we ready for him?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's go over all that's happened up 'til now.

speaker: Stowe
en: Tryggr was killed and dismembered by men who worked for him, men he trusted. Avgos, The Arrow. Our brother in arms. He wanted Lunden for The Order.

speaker: Erke
en: And the Good Sister. That's another knife to the back. Lunden's Saint, Sister Frideswid. She was The Leech and the city was her meat market. Your bishop has already issued an apology on behalf of the Church.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's time we focused on The Compass. Gather all we know and lay it out, plain as day.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's time we focused on The Compass. Gather all we know and lay it out, plain as day.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have more to do first. I'll be back.

speaker: Stowe
en: We'll be waiting.

speaker: Stowe
en: Are you ready?

speaker: Stowe
en: Aye.

speaker: Eivor
en: We let fly the feather-dart, squeezed raven-ink from a loathsome leech. Now we wait, wolf-tensed, for the master of the river-rib to return and revenge his shaken warriors.

speaker: Erke
en: Well, well... this one's got the gift of Odin's mead.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's on your mind, Stowe?

speaker: Stowe
en: We know The Compass is a sailor, a captain from Francia.

speaker: Erke
en: And he won't like hearing he's got a leak in his hull, so to speak. With the deaths of The Leech and The Arrow, he'll want to hit back. But we can't know how or when.

speaker: Eivor
en: Apart from this, the man's invisible. A coward if you ask me.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Burn in your Hell, you bloody reeves!

speaker: Erke
en: We're penned in!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is there another way out?

speaker: Stowe
en: The tower! There's an open window they can't have reached.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll go up. You find a way out!

speaker: Stowe
en: Eivor, make for the steeple!

speaker: Erke
en: The Nornir still spun for us, my Stowe. We've many years yet. Come on!

speaker: Erke
en: Thor's hammer, what was that?

speaker: Stowe
en: Eivor! We're at the door! Erke! Help me with this!

speaker: Erke
en: I'm trying! It's blocked!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: They're blocked inside!

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Let them burn!

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Kill them all!

speaker: Stowe
en: Cowards! Open this door and face us!

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: That's only a taste of the hellfire you'll see!

speaker: Stowe
en: Let's go!

speaker: Erke
en: Fresh air!

speaker: Stowe
en: You'll pay with your lives.

speaker: Erke
en: Come at me!

speaker: Stowe
en: Eivor, we're still inside!

speaker: Erke
en: Do take your time though, we may throw a picnic!

speaker: Stowe
en: Let's go!

speaker: Erke
en: Fresh air!

speaker: Stowe
en: That's the lot of them.

speaker: Erke
en: Let's get clear of this inferno!

speaker: Eivor
en: I had a view of the city from the roof. There's a new flotilla in the harbor.

speaker: Erke
en: The Compass.

speaker: Stowe
en: Bastard. If we commandeered the springalds that Avgos built, we could rain a cloud of arrows on the invaders.

speaker: Erke
en: I'd sooner take the flank and go around this army to the boats. If we cut the head of this beast, The Order's men will be easy to rout.

speaker: Eivor
en: I want those springalds on our side. I'll follow you Stowe.

speaker: Stowe
en: Up on the ramparts. We'll redirect their fire.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's focus on The Compass. Kill him, and the battle's won.

speaker: Erke
en: I can lead you straight to him. Through the reeds, like Stowe's Moses.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll go my own way. Less danger to you both.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll go my own way. Less danger to you both.

speaker: Erke
en: Whatever happens, this ends tonight.

speaker: Stowe
en: May God guide our swords and cover our backs.

speaker: Erke
en: Don't be reckless, Little Voice.

speaker: Stowe
en: I'll see you when it's done, Erke. Count on it.

speaker: Stowe
en: Follow me to the ramparts, Eivor! They'll have no chance!

speaker: Stowe
en: The springalds are close!

speaker: Stowe
en: You are no match for us!

speaker: Stowe
en: Regroup with me, Fyrds!

speaker: Norse Warrior 8
en: No one left to save you! Where's your silver? Where?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Let me go! My children? Where are you?

speaker: Norse Warrior 8
en: It's that damned Norse!

speaker: Stowe
en: Let's turn these springalds back on The Compass.

speaker: Erke
en: Follow me. I know a path straight to the docks. We'll be able to flank them.

speaker: Erke
en: Let's go!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: I can't breathe! I can't— Please help! Someone, I can't get free! Help! Anyone! The door's blocked!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Ah! My arm! Get me out of here! Please!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: My home! Ruined. I am deep in your debt, stranger.

speaker: Erke
en: This way! The docks are burning! Take this path. You'll avoid most attention. I'll give you cover when I can.

speaker: Stowe
en: Godspeed, my friends.

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Burn it to the ground!

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: Forward, forward! Kill them all!

speaker: Vicelin
en: Avgos and Frideswid were too confident. I don't suffer from the same disease. I'll drown and burn every last man, woman, and child in this shithole city.

speaker: Eivor
en: So this is The Compass. Large enough to ford an ocean.

speaker: Vicelin
en: Look here, Stowe and Erke's lapdog! You've stolen me from Francia!

speaker: Vicelin
en: Will none of you lift a finger to aid your master?

speaker: Vicelin
en: Persistent bastard! Defiant to the end! You die here, Dane!

speaker: Eivor
en: Burning to ash what you cannot possess. That's a child's way out.

speaker: Vicelin
en: To Hell with Lunden. Boudicca was right to to the . It's a brick and mortar shithouse.

speaker: Vicelin
en: So bright and beautiful set aflame. Will you rule over these cinders now? Yoke its people to your whims and needs?

speaker: Odin
en: You do have power here. Power you have earned.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have finished my work in Lunden. That's enough.

speaker: Vicelin
en: Lunden is only a beginning.

speaker: Vicelin
en: My order reaches further than your tiny boats can take you.

speaker: Vicelin
en: Never forget, Tryggr, my old friend. A man at sea may have gold and glory.

speaker: Vicelin
en: But he is always a slave to the churning tides. We are that tide.

speaker: Norse Warrior 9
en: We surrender! Please! No more. No more!

speaker: Norse Warrior 10
en: Vicelin's dead! Relent! Relent!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: They're fleeing!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Lunden stands!

speaker: Erke
en: There you are. The drengr we must thank for our good fortune.

speaker: Eivor
en: How do I look? Half-drowned and half-burnt?

speaker: Stowe
en: Not half of either. And far better for the blood on your blade.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Compass is dead. Lunden is yours... to wreck or rebuild.

speaker: Erke
en: We will rebuild. We'll strengthen the walls, reunite families... and likely use less wood, more stone.

speaker: Stowe
en: Ill-timed, Erke. I'd like a quiet moment to pray.

speaker: Erke
en: We'll take it together.

speaker: Eivor
en: Until our next meeting, I trust you'll heed my call if I should send for you.

speaker: Stowe
en: You came to Lunden in search of a friend, Eivor. You found two.

speaker: Erke
en: Aye, Broga. And you deserve this.

speaker: Erke
en: A silver ring for your raven perch. It was Tryggr's before he gifted it to me. I say you've earned the right to wear it now.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm touched, Erke. I'll carry it with pride.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, it seems the wind calls me back to Randvi. Best tell her the good news.'

speaker: Sichfrith
en: I'll never learn.

speaker: Eivor
en: Morning, Sichfrith.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Eivor. It was a rough night. I drank too much and I'm desperate to calm my belly.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot help your belly. But could you tell me what you know of this man Thorstein?

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Ah, Da told you I tried to join his gang, eh? Thorstein's a real Vikingr. Like you but louder.

speaker: Eivor
en: You weren't allowed to join?

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Too young and gangly. Ama wouldn't even show me where his hideout is.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me a bit about this Ama.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Likes her ale the way kittens like milk. Spends her time getting tiddly on the docks, chatting up passer-bys.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will speak to her. Perhaps Thorstein will regret not letting you in his gang.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Listen to me. If you're smart, you won't cross Ama. She's a vicious fighter.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enjoying her ale. Likely to be Ama.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you drinking, friend?

speaker: Ama
en: The finest ale in town. I like fine things, so you have my attention. What are you doing here, darling?

speaker: Eivor
en: Looking for a good drink and good company.

speaker: Ama
en: You've stumbled in the right alehouse. Excellent ale and better conversation.

speaker: Eivor
en: The ale leads to chatting leads to ... well, who knows?

speaker: Ama
en: Let's find out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that all you can do?

speaker: Ama
en: O, you are wicked!

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep going, I'm still thristy.

speaker: Ama
en: Come now, darling, stop before you make a sick mess.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are a compelling woman. What is it you do?

speaker: Ama
en: You may have heard of Thorstein? I'm one of his most trusted friends.

speaker: Eivor
en: I had heard of him. Very impressive that he trusts you.

speaker: Ama
en: He's like a brother to me. A not-very-bright brother. He entrusted me with a key to his secret lair.

speaker: Eivor
en: He has a lair? I would very much to see that.

speaker: Ama
en: Over in Dubgaill Landing? Sorry, Thorstein would get all pouty. But perhaps you'd like to join me for a meal?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'd rather join you for something else.

speaker: Ama
en: Ooo! I can't wait to find out what that is! But hold that thought, I don't feel well. I best move about a bit.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to get that key from her.

speaker: Ama
en: Hey! What are you up to?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ama, you're a too-trusting fool. Your key is mine. Now to find Thorstein's hideout.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this the lair Ama spoke of?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here for you, Thorstein.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, I've got you, Thorstein my friend.

speaker: Thorstein
en: Beautiful haul as usual, lads. I love the smell of wealth. Now, where in the name of Freyja's fat minge is Ama?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: I dunno, Thorstein. You know how she is.

speaker: Thorstein
en: Swilling ale? Now? She's gotten worse than ever.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: You want us to look for 'er, Thorstein?

speaker: Thorstein
en: She yanks my scabbard, that one. No, go about your duties. She'll show up.

speaker: Thorstein
en: Agh! Who are you? How did you get in here?

speaker: Eivor
en: You made a mistake when you came for Bárid mac Ímair.

speaker: Thorstein
en: Oh gods. You plan to kill me? Give my head to whatever Irish master you and Bárid serve?

speaker: Eivor
en: I serve no Irish master.

speaker: Thorstein
en: Bull's-scat! If you had any Norse loyalty you'd be like me. Running the filthy god-eaters from the island. The King of Dublin should look out for Vikings, not try to make nice with those cunts who killed our forebears. Join me. I could use someone with real balls, and the silver is good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be silent and I may show you mercy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Common refuse, delivered to your judgment, King Bárid.

speaker: Bárid
en: Thorstein, author of the plot to waylay me and my cousin.

speaker: Thorstein
en: You know how it is, Bárid. A fellow needs some silver. A king could fetch Dublin's treasury in ransom! Although, I'm not certain you'd bring in quite so much.

speaker: Eivor
en: Say so, Bárid, and I will cut out his insolent tongue.

speaker: Bárid
en: On your feet, Thorstein, you bloody my floors. It is a weighty decision. I would have my closest friend advise me. Eivor. How shall I deal with this ruffian?

speaker: Eivor
en: All must see that you are a just, resolute king. A stately and dignified execution is called for.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must show all Dublin that your justice is swift and harsh. A miserable, drawn-out death will make it clear.

speaker: Eivor
en: People delight in public spectacle. Torture the man until he cannot walk and no one will dare cross you again.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Well said, Eivor.

speaker: Bárid
en: I want no blood feud lasting generations, Thorstein. You are not worth the bother. Dublin confiscates your land and silver. I banish you forevermore. Begone by sundown.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bend the knee and show your thanks.

speaker: Thorstein
en: Best to you, king. I've better places to be than Dublin.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Father! Why choose weakness?

speaker: Eivor
en: Give every enemy a length of rope, soon they will carry your noose.

speaker: Bárid
en: Peace! Flann Sinna will soon rule all Ireland. Flann Sinna has the power to make or undo my kingship and that of my son. He is the center of all. But Flann distrusts me. He does not believe I'm truly Christian. By showing Christian mercy, I begin to change his mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are more shrewd than I took you for, cousin. Maybe Thorstein's release is a worth a kingdom. But will mercy be enough?

speaker: Bárid
en: That is why I must build trade. Flann will see that the strength of Dublin's ports is the strength of Ireland.

speaker: Eivor
en: Show him the power of that trade, cousin. Obtain some rare item from afar, some spice, or gem, or weapon

speaker: Bárid
en: and gift to him at the coronation! It will represent Dublin's reach. And help secure my crown!

speaker: Eivor
en: Flann will hear of your Christian mercy. Meantime, I will speak to Azar about a gift.

speaker: Bárid
en: Meet me before the coronation. We will go together.

speaker: Ake
en: Ah! Good, you're here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where's Alvis?

speaker: Ake
en: Yes, well, you see, Alvis and I got into a little argument. I may have made some disparaging remarks about his paranoid fears.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm. I don't imagine he took that well.

speaker: Ake
en: No, he did not. He told me that if I was so sure his fears were baseless, then I should perform the ritual in his stead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you ever done anything like this?

speaker: Ake
en: Goodness no. But he left a list. Anyway, how hard can it be?

speaker: Eivor
en: What does the list say?

speaker: Ake
en: It says to start by lighting fires 'round the settlement to create a "protective barrier against spirits." Utter nonsense and a waste of time.

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps, but I would feel better honoring Alvis' wishes.

speaker: Ake
en: Of course. Of course. Go light the fires and then return to me. There are more steps on this list.

speaker: Eivor
en: This looks to be the spot. That's one fire pit down. I see a fire pit over there. There. The fire should last until morning. I think I've found one of the fire pits. May this fire protect us. That looks like a fire pit. This should burn brightly. All the fires have been lit. I should return to Ake.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ake. All the fires have been lit around Ravensthorpe.

speaker: Ake
en: Good. Now follow me. The next step takes place in the forest.

speaker: Ake
en: You warriors are so worried about your spirits. Like today is any different than any other day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be careful, Ake. That kind of thinking can leave you defenseless in the face of the unknown.

speaker: Ake
en: Perhaps. Or perhaps it leaves me more time to work on my craft and not spend so much time worrying.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does Alvis ask for this next step?

speaker: Ake
en: We're to draw out any spirits that have crossed into our world and would do us harm, and destroy them.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how will we find them?

speaker: Ake
en: There will be a rune or ward that has let them into our world. I assume we'll know it when we see it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Seems easy enough. And how do we banish the spirits?

speaker: Ake
en: Hmm. It doesn't say. Maybe we can talk to them? Otherwise I've found a punch to be a reliable deterrent.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm here, Ake.

speaker: Ake
en: Come, Eivor. Let's finish this foolish errand.

speaker: Ake
en: Odin's beard!

speaker: Eivor
en: Still think the spirits are a foolish myth?

speaker: Ake
en: Now is not the time for admonishments, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: It is done.

speaker: Ake
en: I can barely believe it! We both saw that, didn't we?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, Ake. It would seem you owe Alvis an apology.

speaker: Ake
en: I do. But I would never give him the satisfaction. It's back to the brewery for me.

speaker: Gerhild
en: Stop eating my garden, you filthy little things! Hey! I saw you, get back here! Where are you hiding now?

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem distressed.

speaker: Gerhild
en: So would you be if your every crop of turnips was demolished by a horde of mangy horrors!

speaker: Eivor
en: I assume you mean the rabbits in that field?

speaker: Gerhild
en: Aye, them! They're nowt but rats with ears stuck on! I'd slay 'em if I could, but they're too damned fast.

speaker: Gerhild
en: When I catch you, I'll impale you! Maim you! Send you to bunny Hell!

speaker: Gerhild
en: That's right! Get in there! Mash their little bunny heads in! Go on! Nail those bobtailed little shits! Three less pesky vermin bastards in the world! Yes! That's what you get for eating my turnips, you bucktoothed fuckanapes!

speaker: Gerhild
en: You got them! Every last one! Exterminated like the hairballs of Satan that they are!

speaker: Ahlstan
en: Flopsy? Lord Snuffles! What have they done to you?

speaker: Gerhild
en: Just taking care of business, Ahlstan. I warned you what would happen if you let them in my turnip patch again.

speaker: Ahlstan
en: My babies! They're not to blame! How could you? You've gone too far this time, wife!

speaker: Eivor
en: You gave names to those rabbits?

speaker: Ahlstan
en: They were my best friends. My only friends. They just... they loved turnips so much! I couldn't deny them!

speaker: Eivor
en: And the chance to torment your wife was not at all in your thoughts, I suppose?

speaker: Ahlstan
en: What other amusement do I have in this grim and cheerless life? I am wed to a sour-faced shrew, her misery my only joy. Look at her scowling now! Face like a bulldog licking piss off a nettle. See what I must wake up to each morn?

speaker: Eivor
en: My apologies. I did not know they were yours.

speaker: Ahlstan
en: Apologies will be cold comfort to Flopsy in his barrow tonight. But it is not you I blame. Gerhild is the villain here, as always. Leave me now. Let the hag delight in my tears. I don't care anymore.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, at least Lord Snuffles will make you a fine stew tonight.

speaker: Ahlstan
en: I can't eat him! You monster!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will if you won't.

speaker: Ahlstan
en: By God, you're as vile as she is!

speaker: Eivor
en: There is little of love in your dealings. Is there no way you could leave her?

speaker: Ahlstan
en: Leave her? And have her think she has won? Never!

speaker: Eivor
en: Those were your husband's rabbits?

speaker: Gerhild
en: Aye, and he loved them nearly as much as I love my turnips. Look at him cry now. The sharpest pain is the sweetest ache.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is cruelty the only coin in your marriage?

speaker: Gerhild
en: O, no. There's also spite and malice.

speaker: Eivor
en: These two are a match in misery. I should leave them be. They deserve each other.

speaker: Eivor
en: These wares belonged to a smuggler. I wonder if there is silver in returning these.

speaker: Norse Child
en: Why won't you just stay still! Ugh! This one first... then this one... ugh! No! Stay still, stones! Or else the bad Pict-people will come for me...

speaker: Norse Child
en: Can you tell the stones to stand still, please? I need to build a stone man so it will protect me from the Pict-people! I keep trying but... I just can't do it right.

speaker: Norse Child
en: Whoa! You're really good at this!

speaker: Eivor
en: Think of this as a test, of mind and wit. Stack the cairn stones high and wide.

speaker: Norse Child
en: But they keep falling...

speaker: Eivor
en: You have to let the air and nature's beauty guide you. Shape, balance, expression are key.

speaker: Norse Child
en: O, wow! Thank you for showing me how.

speaker: Eivor
en: Steady your hands and your heart, tiny-giant. Goodbye.

speaker: Norse Child
en: I'll be okay on my own, Mama and Papa. Don't worry about me, I'll have an army of stone men to protect me!

speaker: Instructions
en: How to make a Stoneman Find stones, there are some by the river. Stack stones to make Stoneman. Stoneman will protect me. Protect us.

speaker: Birna
en: The hair gets longer, the nails grow, even when the corpse is cold. I've seen it myself.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: That's not true.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: You think, what, there's a bit of life left in someone long dead?

speaker: Birna
en: No, it's the fumes in a body. Odors grow after a killing, so they have to escape by any means they can.

speaker: Birna
en: Eivor, my muscle-banded friend! There's a nest of Wigmund's men just here. We're going to pick it clean.

speaker: Eivor
en: Every last one?

speaker: Birna
en: The fewer lice in the bush, the less itchy the pussycat. That's how I see it.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you come to join Soma's army?

speaker: Birna
en: I'd been in England for ages, before Guthrum, Ivarr, Ubba... smuggling under the eyes of Saxons and Danes alike. I lied, stole, had my nose broken. Life wasn't easy, but it taught me how to bear the pain. I just laughed it away. When Soma took me in, she saw more than a smuggler in me. I was useful to something greater than myself. Useful to her vision.

speaker: Eivor
en: In a world where few saw you as worthy of trust, she's one who did.

speaker: Birna
en: Right. And I love that about her. I love... everything about her.

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem to bring life and spirit to this clan. Does Soma feel the same?

speaker: Birna
en: If I knew what was going on in another person's head, I'd find life dreadful and dull. But Soma seems to enjoy my company.

speaker: Eivor
en: In what way?

speaker: Birna
en: Her own way. Just not in the way I'd like. Painful truths are easy to bear when you can laugh, you see? Delight in the face of suffering is an act of rebellion.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you think of Soma's other warriors, Galinn and Lif?

speaker: Birna
en: O, Lif's got that raw animal pull. Every time I see him, I want him to climb me like a tree and nest in my armpits. He brays about being honorable, but I've never met a man of honor who starts a fire just to be praised for putting it out. And Galinn, he broods like it's an art form. He's got this... self-importance that is just so charming.

speaker: Eivor
en: We could talk all day. But these Saxons may fly from their nest.

speaker: Birna
en: You and I should take a closer look. My men will hang back and come running if things go sideways.

speaker: Birna
en: Fighting beside you should bring a thrill. Happy I can see it up close.

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't get too close. I might black your eye or bruise your head.

speaker: Birna
en: You'd lose your elbow before the bruises showed.

speaker: Birna
en: You're light on your feet and quick through the grass.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sound carries over snowdrifts. I learned young.

speaker: Birna
en: I practiced by sneaking in and out of bedroom windows, every chance I had.

speaker: Birna
en: You've made more noise than Ragnarök's end, and these Saxons still don't see you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not everyone is so fox-eared as you.

speaker: Birna
en: More's the pity.

speaker: Birna
en: Fighters, to me! Give these Saxons something to play with besides their cocks!

speaker: Eivor
en: You know their god forbids that form of pleasure.

speaker: Birna
en: Is that right? It explains much!

speaker: Birna
en: Come, boy! I'll wear your jaw like a crown!

speaker: Eivor
en: That's all of them.

speaker: Birna
en: Ah, the solitude of after-slaughter. Shame about the smell, though. Men shitting themselves.

speaker: Letter from Wigmund
en: Thegn Randwald, Enclosed is a small gift to show my gratitude for all you've done. The men are well trained and are eager for war. I have never seen a group of soldiers more ready to reclaim what is rightfully theirs, nor more ready to defend it once they do. Your loyalty is unmatched and I know your continued support is something I can rely on. Victory will be ours. Wigmund

speaker: Eivor
en: You fought very well, Birna.

speaker: Birna
en: Is that how you flirt, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that how I what?

speaker: Birna
en: Easy now, drengr (courageous warrior). I'll see you back in Grantebridge.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should return to our camp.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Eivor has returned! Hail, Wolf-Kissed!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald. This is quite a surprise. Welcome.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes, I surprised myself, for what it's worth. If I cannot be ealdorman, I can at least honor my father by acting as one. My lord has sent you the best archers in Lincolnscire, and I am here to lead them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. We will rain death upon our enemies today. Good work, Hunwald. Be ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ealdorman Hunwald, you honor your father by answering my call. Swanburrow sends her regards.

speaker: Hunwald
en: My ladylove! Let her name be my flame of hope, for I confess the thought of this battle turns my guts to water.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fighting is easy. Just look your opponents in the eyes, then put an axe between them.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes, I remember. Well, I have brought the best archers in Lincolnscire to lend their bows to your cause.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. We will rain death upon our enemies today. Good work, Hunwald. Be ready.

speaker: Stowe
en: I appreciate your efforts to spare the innocent, Eivor. At least we saved some lives here.

speaker: Eivor
en: One day, Saxon and Dane, Norse and Briton, will live as brothers and sisters, as they do in Lunden.

speaker: Stowe
en: I only wish the path to peace were not paved with so many skulls.

speaker: Eivor
en: We cannot choose the way the world is. Our only choice is how to face it.

speaker: Stowe
en: And so violence begets violence. "An eye for an eye" as the Good Book says. But soon, we will all be blind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not quite. Whoever makes the last strike should still have one eye left.

speaker: Stowe
en: "In the street of the blind, the one-eyed man is called the Guiding Light."

speaker: Erke
en: Does that holy tome of yours have a quote for everything?

speaker: Stowe
en: Eivor, forgive me. I have slain too many of my own people already. I cannot kill more. I must return to Lunden.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you, Erke? Do you feel the same?

speaker: Erke
en: Someone has to keep an eye on him in the big city. He would only get himself killed otherwise.

speaker: Eivor
en: We took this camp together, so I will ask no more of you. Return home, and let your friendship be a beacon to our peoples.

speaker: Stowe
en: Godspeed, Eivor. I pray you come back safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ever my staunch ally, Ljufvina. Are your men ready?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: They are. Bows strung and arrows fletched. We will harry the enemy from the flanks to keep them off your back. They will not have a moment's peace from us.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know I can count on you, Ljufvina.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: What are friends for?

speaker: Eivor
en: Birstan. I'm glad to see you again. How is your family?

speaker: Birstan
en: Alfida keeps my house and heart in order. She has even charmed that old shrew Eadred.

speaker: Eivor
en: And Eluric? He has not returned?

speaker: Birstan
en: I hear stories of a man full of tempests, picking fights in taverns. We must hope, when hope is all we have.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am sorry for your troubles but glad for your help.

speaker: Birstan
en: I have brought for you a ram of unsurpassed craftsmanship. Their gates will not hold long against it.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is a fine gift indeed. I will make good use of it.

speaker: Birstan
en: Fight hard, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: When have I done otherwise?

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma Jarlskona. You seem grave.

speaker: Soma
en: I am thinking on the battle to come. Every conflict has a cost. I wonder who will pay this time?

speaker: Eivor
en: We are no strangers to loss, you and I.

speaker: Soma
en: The ache of absent souls is a wound that never heals. But we may return your brother to your side. There is that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke and her men will bear the cost today, not us.

speaker: Eivor
en: I wish I were as sure of it as you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili, you stiff old arse-stick! How are you?

speaker: Vili
en: That's Vili Jarl to you, peasant. Now take a knee and kiss my ring.

speaker: Eivor
en: The power of jarldom has gone to your head, I see. Has Snotinghamscire fallen to ruin yet?

speaker: Vili
en: The land thrives under my guidance, I believe. But gods, I am itching to kill something, and so are my berserkers.

speaker: Vili
en: Careful, Eivor. Don't make me thrash your hide as I did when we were children.

speaker: Eivor
en: As I recall, it was you who always finished snot-faced and teary-eyed.

speaker: Vili
en: Well, it will be Saxons weeping today, after me and my berserkers get hold of them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do that, and you and I will raise a horn together.

speaker: Vili
en: I look forward to it. Now let us find your brother.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ubba. Any advice before we begin?

speaker: Ubba
en: Advise? You need none of that now. You stand in no one's shadow, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lofty praise from the son of Ragnar Lothbrok.

speaker: Ubba
en: It may be that one day our paths lead us to doom, Eivor. But at least we can say the footprints we left were our own.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bishop Deorlaf. Strange to see a man of God on the battle lines.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: It may surprise you, but I was no stranger to horse and hunt in my younger days.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is Saxons we fight this day, Deorlaf. Not Britons, and not in Mercia.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: It is Fulke I fight. A false Christian, preaching a corruption of God's word. If I can assist in her downfall, I will.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then you are welcome here, friend.

speaker: Basim
en: You are quite the agent of chaos. Fulke's men are chasing their tails, not knowing where you will strike next.

speaker: Ubba
en: Portcestre has neither the supplies nor the forces to keep us out now.

speaker: Basim
en: And you have bought time for your allies to arrive. Many have come, not least the bishop here.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: As I promised. As a keeper of God's word, it would be poor form if I did not keep my own.

speaker: Ubba
en: Now, if the talking is done, there's blood to be spilled!

speaker: Soma
en: Eivor. Dark news. We have found a letter on one of the dead. Fulke has called for aid.

speaker: Eivor
en: Reinforcements?

speaker: Soma
en: A Saxon army marches from Wincestre.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Then my men and I will ride to meet them. We will harry them every step of the way, to buy you time.

speaker: Basim
en: We may begin the assault at once. Or you might wish to speak with your allies if you have not done so already?

speaker: Ubba
en: Warm words do that the chill of battle-fear.

speaker: Eivor
en: We march. When the sun sets on this day, Sigurd will be returned to us and Fulke's head will be on a spike.

speaker: Basim
en: Let us begin.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not be long.

speaker: Basim
en: Return when you are ready.

speaker: Basim
en: Your warriors are eager for battle. Are you?

speaker: Fulke
en: Eivor! Did you enjoy the gift I left you in Canterbury?

speaker: Eivor
en: You will die today, Fulke. But your men may live if you come here, to me, and settle this alone.

speaker: Fulke
en: We have nothing to settle. Die on these walls if you will. It is your choice.

speaker: Eivor
en: No wall is high enough to keep me from you.

speaker: Fulke
en: Then come. Claim your brother, if you can. I shall wait with him. If you would find us, you need only follow his screams.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke!

speaker: Eivor
en: What will the skalds say when they speak of this day? They will say we unleashed such rampant slaughter that Odin himself stirred on his throne to watch! They will say that ravens blacked the sky to feast on Saxon dead! So raise your sword with me now, brothers and sisters. For today is the day we carve our names into legend!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm coming for you, Brother.

speaker: Ubba
en: So many battles and so few scars, Basim! What's your secret?

speaker: Basim
en: I don't get hit.

speaker: Ubba
en: Aha! The simplest strategies are the best!

speaker: Eivor
en: Clear the way! Let's take down that palisade!

speaker: Vili
en: Ravens will tear your flesh.

speaker: Eivor
en: Another palisade! We have to knock it down!

speaker: Soma
en: Do not let your swords fall, onward, onward!

speaker: Vili
en: Rip their spines out, spill their guts!

speaker: Eivor
en: Break open that gate! Watch out for the oil! Courage, men! Let the ravens gorge on Saxon meat!

speaker: Ubba
en: You all die here today!

speaker: Basim
en: Push forward, we have them on the run.

speaker: Basim
en: Watch your left!

speaker: Vili
en: You watch YOUR left!

speaker: Basim
en: I'm trying to help!

speaker: Vili
en: They can't keep us back!

speaker: Ubba
en: Soma! You fight like Vidarr, hungry for revenge!

speaker: Soma
en: I would say the same of you, Ubba Ragnarsson!

speaker: Vili
en: Ubba! Do you have sight of Eivor!

speaker: Ubba
en: Are you her nursemaid? Why do you ask?

speaker: Vili
en: Old habits. Pay me no mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: The men cannot get through! We need to get them away from these archers!

speaker: Ubba
en: We fight as brothers and sisters, we fight for blood!

speaker: Soma
en: No! Valhalla calls to me.

speaker: Ubba
en: You will not break me, Saxon shit-fly.

speaker: Basim
en: I will fall if I take more blows. Aid me!

speaker: Vili
en: Fight beside me! Lest I fall. I will die with an axe in my fist!

speaker: Soma
en: Do not fall, Eivor. We need your axe-arm!

speaker: Ubba
en: Do not fail now, Eivor, call on Thor's strength.

speaker: Basim
en: Guard yourself, Wolf-Kissed. You are Sigurd's last hope.

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor! Pull back, you cannot fall here!

speaker: Soma
en: Well done, Eivor. All fall in your wake.

speaker: Ubba
en: There, Eivor! You are our champion.

speaker: Basim
en: Your strength is unmatched, Eivor!

speaker: Vili
en: That ugly bastard didn't stand a chance!

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep fighting, men! I will take care of the gate.

speaker: Basim
en: For Sigurd!

speaker: Soma
en: What waits for you on the other side of death, Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: I thought I knew once. Now I think otherwise.

speaker: Soma
en: A bad day to be uncertain.

speaker: Eivor
en: Springalds! Damn these Saxons! I will make a path.'

speaker: Eivor
en: They cannot hold us back! Make your ancestors proud!

speaker: Vili
en: You Saxon sheep-fuckers die here.

speaker: Soma
en: Your blood will stain this place for eternity.

speaker: Eivor
en: Onward! Let nothing stand in your way!

speaker: Vili
en: I've killed twenty Saxons already!

speaker: Soma
en: I lost count around thirty.

speaker: Vili
en: Hmph... well... I wasn't counting the short ones!

speaker: Eivor
en: The keep is in sight! We must fight our way to it!

speaker: Ubba
en: Your Hell has come to claim you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fight hard! Odin's eyes are upon you this day!

speaker: Eivor
en: A mistake I will not make twice.

speaker: Eivor
en: These Saxon slack-bladders are no match for Norse steel!

speaker: Soma
en: For Eivor! For Sigurd!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd must be close. Up these stairs!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd was here once, but no longer. Where has Fulke taken him?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this Sigurd's blood?

speaker: Basim
en: Still fresh.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd. Every instant of your torment, Fulke will suffer tenfold.

speaker: Eivor
en: The church! Fulke must have taken him there. Come on, Basim!

speaker: Basim
en: Face us, Fulke! Your cowardice betrays you.

speaker: Eivor
en: This door will need the strength of two!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke!

speaker: Fulke
en: I have done all I could to help him, Eivor. The rest is up to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nooo! No!

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother! Brother! I'm here for you. I have you.

speaker: Basim
en: Let me stay with him. You deal with Fulke.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll come back for you, I promise.

speaker: Eivor
en: You cower from me, Fulke? Like a rat in the dark?

speaker: Fulke
en: We are all in the dark, Eivor. It is the search for the light that brings us closer to the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: Save your babble. Death is our language now.

speaker: Fulke
en: You fight beneath a banner of ignorance, Eivor. I could pull back the curtain for you. Give you a glimpse of what lies beyond.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need nothing from you.

speaker: Eivor
en: This ends here.

speaker: Fulke
en: A pity to kill one with such... potential.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are your fine words now, paladin?

speaker: Fulke
en: If you will not raise your eyes to the light, I'll bury you in the dark.

speaker: Eivor
en: So you can fight after all.

speaker: Fulke
en: You meddle in matters you do not understand!

speaker: Fulke
en: Blind of mind, blind of sight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you afraid, Fulke?

speaker: Fulke
en: My cause is greater than you can comprehend.

speaker: Fulke
en: The light of the Monad is all I need to guide me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why do you hide, coward?

speaker: Fulke
en: You have power, Eivor. Maybe more than you know.

speaker: Eivor
en: No more words, poison-tongue!

speaker: Fulke
en: Even when I offer the truth, you refuse it.

speaker: Fulke
en: You are more like Sigurd than you know.

speaker: Fulke
en: Do you not wonder, Eivor, at the things I have learned?

speaker: Eivor
en: Every word you say is madness.

speaker: Fulke
en: Sigurd is an Ancient One! An archon, Nephilim, Isu, call him what you will. He is reborn!

speaker: Eivor
en: He is my brother and my jarl. And you are mind-sick.

speaker: Fulke
en: He is everything we should hope to be!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke! Damn you to Hel!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke! you can't run from me forever!

speaker: Eivor
en: Nobody touch her. She's mine.

speaker: Fulke
en: You are too late, Eivor. I have opened your brother's mind to the truth. That is my victory.

speaker: Fulke
en: And you will go with me to the grave.

speaker: Fulke
en: You can wound my flesh, but my work will live on for all time! You are more like your brother than I realized, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Burn in your Hell!

speaker: Odin
en: Stop!

speaker: Odin
en: You misunderstand, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll eat your heart!

speaker: Odin
en: She has saved your brother!

speaker: Fulke
en: Animals, we are. Spit and vomit, shit and soil.

speaker: Fulke
en: But Sigurd is so much more. I gave him that understanding, that gift.

speaker: Eivor
en: You gave him pain!

speaker: Fulke
en: Yes! To awaken him!

speaker: Fulke
en: All that power! All that potential, locked away!

speaker: Fulke
en: A god trapped in a prison on bones! The pain was necessary to free him!

speaker: Fulke
en: Behold his terrible beauty!

speaker: Fulke
en: The beauty of the divine!

speaker: Odin
en: Hers was the great work, the highest achievement of humankind. Now you, Eivor—you must carry it forward.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd...

speaker: Sigurd
en: I can walk. Let me... let me walk.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor... I will... I will fight... as a thresher through a field of wheat, Mad One.

speaker: Eivor
en: What has she done to you?

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Eivor! We delayed them as long as we could.

speaker: Ubba
en: Reinforcements from Wincestre have come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Get Sigurd to a boat. I will hold them off until you are safely away.

speaker: Basim
en: Fight well, Eivor. Find us at the settlement when you can.

speaker: Soma
en: Archers! To the walls!

speaker: Ubba
en: Damn these Saxon dogs! Don't they give up?

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand with me, Ubba. We'll turn the tide.

speaker: Soma
en: Stay strong! Victory is close at hand!

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep your wits about you, Soma. Don't get careless now.

speaker: Soma
en: Never!

speaker: Eivor
en: One last effort! Drive them back!

speaker: Ubba
en: By Thor, we're not done yet!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not falter now, men! For Odin, and for glory!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that the last of them?

speaker: Soma
en: We have beaten them back for now, but without Guthrum's army, we do not have the numbers to hold this fort.

speaker: Eivor
en: We found Sigurd. That is what matters.

speaker: Ubba
en: Guthrum has hasty in his judgement, Eivor. You are fit to stand with the best of us. Go to your brother. The words of one beloved will heal him faster than herbs. I will see to matters here.

speaker: Eivor
en: May the gods guide you, Ubba. Until we meet again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma Jarlskona. It seems we have won.

speaker: Soma
en: A great victory. Not even these walls could stand against us.

speaker: Eivor
en: This land will be ours in time. What now for you?

speaker: Soma
en: Ubba and I will go west, driving the Saxons before us. Aelfred will not hold the crown much longer.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope one day to see you both there.

speaker: Soma
en: I would like that.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's one more thing...

speaker: Ubba
en: What are you doing still talking to me? Enough goodbyes. Go to Sigurd!

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. Be well, Ubba.

speaker: Eivor
en: Howe did you like the taste of battle?

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: That was... exhilarating! Reminds me of my younger days.

speaker: Eivor
en: Had you not delayed those reinforcements, we might never have succeeded. You are brave for a priest.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Do not underestimate the faithful. We give out lives to a God we cannot see or touch. There is no greater bravery than that.

speaker: Eivor
en: We could not have taken this fort without your archers, Hunwald. My thanks.

speaker: Hunwald
en: O, it was nothing, you know! All in a day's work.

speaker: Eivor
en: I may need call on them again one day.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ah. Was this not the only...? Right, because I was hoping... Well, never mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birstan. Your ram was invaluable in breaching this fortress.

speaker: Birstan
en: A trifle in comparison to the great service you have rendered me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You will have a good story to tell Alfida upon your return.

speaker: Birstan
en: There is that. But battle is not so thrilling and glamorous as the stories tell. I shall have to spruce it up a little.

speaker: Eivor
en: You look pleased with yourself.

speaker: Vili
en: Smell that air! Smells like victory!

speaker: Eivor
en: Smells like blood and brains and the soiled underclothes of dead men.

speaker: Vili
en: Aye, isn't that what victory smells like?

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps to you, arse-stick. I'll take roasting meat, warm mead, and a fire.

speaker: Vili
en: Ah, you always were soft. Get on with you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ljufvina. I am glad to see you made it through.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Be proud, Eivor. You found Sigurd, against the odds.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found his shadow. But I must hope that the scars Fulke has inflicted on his mind will heal.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Sigurd is strong. It will take more than pain to break him.

speaker: Eivor
en: You did not see him, Ljufvina. There was an emptiness in his eyes.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: I am sorry to hear that. Let us hope for the best.

speaker: Eivor
en: They bring a feast, and build their own guesthouse. These are very generous guests.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Did you see that one who came with the new arrivals? She looks young to be raiding.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Are they raiders? A strange company.

speaker: Toka
en: That is a good sword.

speaker: Toka
en: Is that everything? This feast has to be great.

speaker: Pierre
en: Yes. It is our last chance.

speaker: Toka
en: Wolf-Kissed!

speaker: Eivor
en: Welcome to Ravensthorpe. I am Eivor, though you seem to know me already.

speaker: Toka
en: You are well known to us. I am Toka Sinricdottir, and the Frankish bore with me is my advisor, Pierre. We are here on behalf of Sigfred of Francia, renowned warrior and leader of the Northmen there.

speaker: Eivor
en: You look to be at home here already.

speaker: Toka
en: How could we not be? What have you done in this place is amazing. The guesthouse is a fitting addition. We have also bought new tastes for your longtable from Francia. If it is drink you prefer, we have mulled wine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very generous. Some might say overly generous.

speaker: Toka
en: Consider it a token of good will from the hand of my uncle Sigfred. You know, clan to clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: There'll be blood if any here heard I refused a feast, so... consider it accepted.

speaker: Toka
en: Yes! You honor us. Ravensthorpe reminds me of how Francia used to be. Given the chance, I would visit often.

speaker: Eivor
en: You would be welcome. Yet you do not share your gifts for nothing. I await the boon you surely will ask of me.

speaker: Toka
en: Tales of your judgment prove true. You can teach some of that wisdom over ale this day. Shall we begin?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let us see if these Frankish treats hold up to scrutiny.

speaker: Toka
en: Let us eat!

speaker: Eivor
en: I have other concerns right now. We can feast later.

speaker: Toka
en: We will be ready for you.

speaker: Toka
en: Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this feast ready to begin?

speaker: Toka
en: Just say the word!

speaker: Pierre
en: How one can prefer ale to wine! Mon Dieu! (My God!) It astounds me still! You Norse may have us Franks on the battlefield, but when it comes to drink, we stand unbeaten.

speaker: Eivor
en: This wine is great, I admit.

speaker: Pierre
en: So Northerners do have a sense of taste!

speaker: Eivor
en: It will always be ale for my cup.

speaker: Pierre
en: It is not only the channel that separates us, there is an entire sea of bad taste!

speaker: Eivor
en: If it makes me drunk, I'm glad to drink it.

speaker: Pierre
en: Are there no standards anymore?

speaker: Toka
en: I want to show you something...

speaker: Toka
en: In our travels throughout England, I have taken swords in raids and battles. This I took in a against two oafish brothers in East Anglia. 'Tis but a wound-twig, but is still my favorite.

speaker: Eivor
en: So you have travelled to all corners of this land before arriving at Ravensthorpe. To what end?

speaker: Toka
en: I mean to entice you and others like you to join in the glorious raids along the river Seine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who have you talked with thus far?

speaker: Toka
en: Many... Jarl Hemming, Guthrum, even Halfdan...

speaker: Toka
en: Paris itself is set to be sieged, and after that we will have amassed more riches than anyone in England has dared imagine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me guess how many jarls will join you on your Frankish raids and sieges. None.

speaker: Toka
en: They just fail to see the scale of the bounty we stand to plunder.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you really want, Toka?

speaker: Toka
en: Every word I have said is true. But there is something else... a new power is rising in Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: What kind of power?

speaker: Toka
en: The Frankish Kingdoms have been united under one king, Charles the Fat.

speaker: Toka
en: And with this combined strength, Charles has begun a slow march against the Norse villages there. He killed my father and wiped out my village...

speaker: Eivor
en: I am sorry for your father and your village. But we have our own troubles here in this land.

speaker: Toka
en: With Charles the Fat in power, those troubles will worsen. After his campaign in Francia, he will come for England.

speaker: Toka
en: Charles will come for you and your clan. His armies multiply by the day. Real soldiers and cavalry, not like the Saxon farm hands and gillers in these parts.

speaker: Eivor
en: If the Raven Clan were to help you, what is it you would ask of us?

speaker: Toka
en: Our chieftain, Sigfred, prepares to siege Paris and make the Franks rethink their actions against we Norse. And our longships will grow heavy with treasure in the doing.

speaker: Randvi
en: My scouts attest to the claims of Toka and her people. But, before now, I saw no reason to involve our clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you see reason now?

speaker: Randvi
en: If the mad king Charles does have ambitions for England, we should act. This Sigfred she mentioned, he rallies the Norse there. Joining him could be our chance to push back against this new king.

speaker: Eivor
en: Or I can meet this Charles myself. And if he will not deal with me, I kill him.

speaker: Randvi
en: This problem is bigger than one king. If we kill one, another will rise. Were he murdered by a Norse from England, it could bring the Franks to our shores even sooner.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I will be mindful of who I kill and who I ally with in Francia. Could be a stable king is the way to keep Ravensthorpe safe.

speaker: Toka
en: Let me see the sword. I... wish to examine the ironwork.

speaker: Pierre
en: No! I stole this and it is mine.

speaker: Toka
en: Fine. If you will not show it to me, I will have to take it. Ready yourself, Pierre. I challenge you to a holmgang!

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough. Toka, you came here looking for help with this new Frankish threat. The Raven Clan will answer your call.

speaker: Toka
