en: You will? You will! I promise, you will not regret this. Find Pierre when you have prepared and we will make for Francia at once.

speaker: Pierre
en: Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ugh, my head. I should have kept to ale. Toka said to find Pierre when I'm ready to travel to Francia.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Bjarte! Bjarte! Come home! Follow my voice, Bjarte! Bjarte? Can you hear me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Looking for someone?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: My husband... he was not supposed to leave home on his own. I fear he has fallen asleep somewhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fallen asleep?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Yes. A curse he has carried his whole life. At any moment, his eyes roll back and his body simply collapses.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dangerous to be out there on his own. You think he would have gotten far?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: His bag is gone. I fear he may have taken it to go fruit picking down south near the old ruins. Bjarte, where are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will keep an eye out for him.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Thank you. He snores, if that helps.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Of course not. No, no, no, I-I'm just resting my eyes, I swear it. (snoring) Enough! You know not to touch me there. (snoring) No, you are the one with the big nose, not me. (snoring)

speaker: Eivor
en: A man who falls asleep at any moment. How did you last this long? It's not enough that you're deadweight, I have to listen to your babbling as well.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Bjarte! Bjarte! Come home! Follow my voice, Bjarte! Bjarte? Can you hear me?

speaker: Norse Woman
en: O gods, Bjarte! Bring him inside!

speaker: Eivor
en: Lucky it was me that found you. Me on a good day, I might add.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found him asleep beneath a tree. He's unharmed.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: My poor Bjarte. I am so glad he's all right. You saved his life.

speaker: Eivor
en: Luck was with him. No hungry wolves or roaming bandits. The note he carries is helpful, but he must have more caution. He may not be so lucky the next time.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: You are right. I will wait until he wakes, and when he does, I will belt him.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is a start. Farewell.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: I can breathe again. You're all right! I was filled with worry.

speaker: Rilda
en: I'm scared for Father. Can you see him down there?

speaker: Runa
en: No, I can't see anything! The lake's dark, and I'm cold.

speaker: Rilda
en: What can we do? Father is alone down there...

speaker: Rilda
en: Hey, you! Can you swim? Our father's down there, looking for treasure.

speaker: Runa
en: He dove way down deep, but I can't see him anymore.

speaker: Rilda
en: Do not worry, Runa. The warrior will find father.

speaker: Runa
en: What if you're wrong? He's been down there for hours.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here's their father, and the treasure that lured him to his doom.

speaker: Eivor
en: That lake goes deep.

speaker: Runa
en: Did you at least find the treasure?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. Take this bracelet your father sought. By rights, it's yours.

speaker: Runa
en: Thank you, brave traveler. We knew you would find it.

speaker: Rilda
en: And what about Father, did you find him?

speaker: Eivor
en: This lake must serve as your father's grave now, but with this last gift, his memory survives.

speaker: Rilda
en: You mean... he drowned?

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw no one. It might be that he went to find food.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where's the rest of your family?

speaker: Rilda
en: Mother got sick and never got better, and now she's under the ground. There's no one else.

speaker: Runa
en: Rilda, remember. Father's sister in Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sell that trinket for food, then travel to your aunt. Your father would wish that.

speaker: Eivor
en: You two best scurry off. There's nothing for you in the lake.

speaker: Eivor
en: This world is hard, and the gods care not.

speaker: Spinster
en: Every day my loins wither with waiting. When will he come to me?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: God doesn't give a rat's arse about your love life.

speaker: Spinster
en: Then do it for the money. I am willing to pay good coin to someone who believes in true love.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I will not be caught up in your womanly schemes, witch.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know a few things about love.

speaker: Spinster
en: Do you? Or did you hear the chime of my coin purse?

speaker: Eivor
en: Does it matter?

speaker: Spinster
en: No. Not when the village children pelt my door with vegetables, call me "old maid" and "witch."

speaker: Eivor
en: You need someone to protect you? From children?

speaker: Spinster
en: Leave your scorn. There is a man, we have been secretly betrothed for years. But his father refuses our union. So you will kidnap him and make it look good! His house is near here, surrounded by red flowers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait... I will kidnap him?

speaker: Spinster
en: You will know my love by his red hair. And try not to kill his father. That will put a damper on our happy day.

speaker: Spinster
en: I will roast him a fat hen. Or a stew. Would he like that?

speaker: Spinster
en: Shoo, fly, and bring me my love.

speaker: Eivor
en: Surrounded by red flowers. This must be her love's house.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here from your love.

speaker: Lover
en: Who are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: That's the spirit! Let us make your father believe the fiction.

speaker: Lover
en: Wait. What? What is this?

speaker: Eivor
en: I, the dread Vikingr Eivor, have come to steal your sons!

speaker: Lover
en: Saints preserve us! The heathens have come to slaughter us in our beds!

speaker: Eivor
en: You will fall to our Vikingr might!

speaker: Lover
en: What in God's name? You brute!

speaker: Lover
en: Please, please!

speaker: Eivor
en: That's it, keep up the act.

speaker: Lover
en: Ow, my head.

speaker: Eivor
en: You'll be with her soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, this is him. O my sweet pudding! Please, lay him gently down.

speaker: Lover
en: Who are you? What is this?

speaker: Spinster
en: Hush, my love. All will be well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait... so this boy is your lover? Or no?

speaker: Spinster
en: He will be. I have watched him for many turns of the Sun. And now he will know of my burning love. Thanks to you.

speaker: Lover
en: You watched me? That is... so...

speaker: Eivor
en: Strange and unnatural?

speaker: Lover
en: Romantic. That you would go to such lengths, to win my heart? It touches me in places I cannot speak of.

speaker: Spinster
en: You have my thanks, Dane. Take your reward and leave us. Plow me, soft one, scythe weeds from my field.

speaker: Jordri
en: Of course, of course! Just my luck. I knew I should have waited for the ground to dry out... Stupid, useless cart. That's what I get for buying second-hand.

speaker: Havi
en: What is the problem?

speaker: Jordri
en: It's this cart! Stuck in the mud, see. And so, my sacred duty will never be fulfilled!

speaker: Havi
en: Sacred duty...?

speaker: Jordri
en: That's right. In my family, when our days are nearly done, we hide our most beloved treasures behind waterfalls.

speaker: Havi
en: Why?

speaker: Jordri
en: Because, what is a waterfall with nothing behind it? A water-fail, that's what! Of course, with Muspels everywhere, I cannot wait until I'm nearly in the ground. Think you could help me out?

speaker: Havi
en: I'll pull the cart free.

speaker: Jordri
en: The cart? No. Lug this chest up those cliff there. Much quicker if you do it. I'll make it worth your while.

speaker: Havi
en: I'm actually very busy

speaker: Jordri
en: It'll take a mere moment. Found the perfect spot already, right behind one of the waterfalls. Walk along that log, follow the path up the cliff, go through a little cave, and you'll find the right waterfall. You'll know you're in the right spot when you find the white flowers. Bring me a few, would you, so I know you managed to find it.

speaker: Havi
en: White flowers. Very well.

speaker: Jordri
en: Oh, you are kind! I'll wait for you right here.

speaker: Havi
en: Overcoming a challenge increases its worth. You'll be fine. And I'm busy.

speaker: Jordri
en: Well... it's your loss.

speaker: Havi
en: Changed your mind, eh?

speaker: Havi
en: Sacred duty, indeed. (sigh) This is the first cave, but not my destination. The path must continue on to the correct waterfall.

speaker: Havi
en: Is that... ah, yes. White flowers.

speaker: Havi
en: There. Proof for the dwarf.

speaker: Jordri
en: Aha! My saviour. Well then, do you have the flowers?

speaker: Havi
en: I do. Here.

speaker: Jordri
en: Ah, excellent! And, uh, you did put the chest where I asked, yes?

speaker: Havi
en: Of course.

speaker: Jordri
en: Good good. Then you have my thanks. My sacred duty is fulfilled.

speaker: Havi
en: And my reward?

speaker: Jordri
en: Oh, the finest of all! Gratitude. And the satisfaction of a job well done.

speaker: Eivor
en: The festival is underway. I should speak to Rollo about our plan.

speaker: Eivor
en: How are your people, Rollo? Recovered and ready for what tonight holds?

speaker: Rollo
en: Lork's death hit hard. Many served long with him and relished his tales of warriors lost and battles won.

speaker: Rollo
en: Gerhild's treachery was a blow. Few were surprised it came to that, only that her dark ways took such a brutal turn.

speaker: Rollo
en: Put that aside. We're ready now. What would you have of us?

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait for my signal. When I approach Estrid, that is your time.

speaker: Rollo
en: I am your axe, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Unleash your war dogs. Set things afire. Bring panic. Act like the barbarians they think us to be.

speaker: Rollo
en: We'll stick their hearts with needles of fear!

speaker: Eivor
en: Night will fall soon. Then is our moment to strike.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: They used to sacrifice . So that his seed might fall on the fertile land and grow the grain anew!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I don't care for that pagan pomp. There is just one God now, and He gives us everything we need. In this life and the next.

speaker: Rollo
en: This is what we do to Saxon god-slaves! We pillage! Pillage and plunder!

speaker: Estrid
en: I am ready when the time comes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stand down, you Saxon dogs! The Lady of Essexe is ours!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: We'll eat your livers and drink your marrow! Saxon dregs! Odin owns you all! Cower before your masters!

speaker: Rollo
en: Take their ale and their women, we will feast like kings tonight!

speaker: Estrid
en: I'm being kidnapped! Kidnapped! Guards! Guards!

speaker: Eivor
en: You're coming with me!

speaker: Estrid
en: O! O! Desist, you foul Dane! Guards! O, woe unto me! Put me down!

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin's beard! You wouldn't fool a child with that howling.

speaker: Estrid
en: Unhand me, fiend! Unhand me, you filthy Dane! Birstan, my love! My love!

speaker: Estrid
en: We are safe enough to walk I think. Aren't we?

speaker: Eivor
en: Who assigned those guards to you?

speaker: Estrid
en: Yes, you noticed as well? That was Thegn Eadred, he insisted. He does worry for me so. O, what a thrill! My heart is racing!

speaker: Eivor
en: Be glad it still beats at all. Your screaming drew half the guards in Colcestre down upon us.

speaker: Estrid
en: I wanted to give a good performance. My father always said I was quite the actor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I won't deny your enthusiasm.

speaker: Estrid
en: Did you not have even a little fun?

speaker: Eivor
en: To steal away a princess, it did give a thrill.

speaker: Estrid
en: A woman fights bravely against her abductors. Yet what will they do with me now? Is my virtue safe with you?

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not in danger if that's what you mean.

speaker: Estrid
en: Come now, Eivor... you can stand against Aelfred's brutes, but you shudder at a maiden's gentle teasing?

speaker: Estrid
en: It is done. And all that stands between me and my home now is a foaming ribbon of surf and silt.

speaker: Eivor
en: You did well, Rollo. You and your people. Are you ready to sail?

speaker: Rollo
en: Loki's hissing son churns the waters between our coasts. We'll need time to rest as we wait for fairer weather.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have a care, then. Aelfred's soldiers will be looking for Estrid, even if Birstan's will not.

speaker: Rollo
en: Now's not the time for such worries, Eivor! Tonight we celebrate! Let's get you some mead!

speaker: Estrid
en: Birstan will meet you northeast of Colcestre tomorrow. You have earned all my husband promised, and more. Come find me, if you like. Away from these reveling Danes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should find Birstan. No doubt, he's hunting again.

speaker: Lork
en: Thor's thunderous hammer! That was like the great days, where I stood sword to sword with your father, Rollo!

speaker: Gerhild
en: Those Saxon milk breads. They never saw us coming!

speaker: Rollo
en: Yes! A ruse worthy of the trickster Loki. Their Idunn stolen by us mere mortals!

speaker: Rollo
en: I am proud of us. We did a good thing, for Estrid and her lord. Maybe now we can all be happy?

speaker: Lork
en: Made me feel young again! And I have you to thank. You believed me, though I was a coward. Won't make that mistake again.

speaker: Estrid
en: What lies ahead, I wonder?

speaker: Eivor
en: A new life... or an old life renewed.

speaker: Estrid
en: My old life... Francia. Mon Dieu (My God), I feel as if I have been sleepwalking these past years, waiting for something to shake me awake.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you awakened now?

speaker: Estrid
en: Yes, these past weeks have been stirring, breathtaking. Your passion and strength, Eivor, I've never met such a... burning soul.

speaker: Eivor
en: You make too much of it. All I have done, I did for my clan and the glory it brought me.

speaker: Estrid
en: Why does your honesty make you more alluring still? Le cœur a ses raisons que la raison ne connaît pas (The heart has reasons that reason does not know).

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you dream while you sleepwalked?

speaker: Estrid
en: I did. I dreamed that all my fleeting happiness was a prelude to something bigger. Glimpses of greater joy, greater love.

speaker: Estrid
en: Lie with me, Eivor. Under the stars of England. Give me a last bittersweet moment before I leave her shores.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll be with you tonight. But tomorrow your new life must begin. I hope you won't look back.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shhh. Still your lips... and come here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I shouldn't. You can't start a new life by repeating the habits of the old.

speaker: Estrid
en: My goodness. You're a philosopher too. I wish I had met you earlier. Years ago.

speaker: Estrid
en: Come, let us return to the others. The fire is calling, the men are merry, and the mead is sweet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Isn't Rollo the man to shake you awake? He adores you.

speaker: Estrid
en: Rollo's still a boy, with boyish dreams.

speaker: Eivor
en: But he is honest. He could love you if you gave him a chance. It would be quite a match.

speaker: Estrid
en: Do you not know me better, Eivor? Mon petit coeur est blessé (My little heart is hurt). Come, I am suddenly chilly. Let us join the others by the fire.

speaker: Randvi
en: O, hello, Eivor. Good day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi, are you well? You seem distant.

speaker: Randvi
en: I am fine. Only a little tired, but well enough. Shall we look at the map?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not until you tell what is wrong.

speaker: Randvi
en: O, I think I have... I feel somewhat trapped. In this room, in this settlement, in this life.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot help you with your life, just now. But I can get you out of this room. What do you say?

speaker: Randvi
en: I don't know. There is much work to be done.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop. Forget about alliances and responsibility for just a few hours. We could take a ride. To Grantebridge, or somewhere nearby. For a change of pace.

speaker: Randvi
en: That sounds lovely. And too far to consider just now. But thank you, Eivor. Maybe another time. Now, what was it you needed?

speaker: Eivor
en: Take a break, Randvi. Let's make for Grantebridgescire and get you out of this musty room.

speaker: Randvi
en: Do you mean now? Right now?

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course. You said you were tired of all this, so why not? Stretch your legs and fill your lungs.

speaker: Randvi
en: I did ask, didn't I? You're right. Lead the way, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Follow me.

speaker: Eivor
en: We won't take the longship today. This trip is for us, just you and me. Is that a problem?

speaker: Randvi
en: Not at all. So long as I get some air and sun, I will be fine. I spend too much of my day in the longhouse.

speaker: Eivor
en: We'll need to cross the river at some point if we want to enter Grantebridgescire. If you know a better way, I would love to hear it.

speaker: Randvi
en: Is swimming not an option?

speaker: Eivor
en: Swimming? I don't know... Are you joking?

speaker: Randvi
en: A boat or a horse would always do, but I am not opposed to the more traditional methods.

speaker: Randvi
en: Please, Eivor. Not the longship.

speaker: Eivor
en: Right.

speaker: Randvi
en: This water smells... off.

speaker: Eivor
en: You get used to it.

speaker: Randvi
en: I do not wish to.

speaker: Randvi
en: It really is lovely here. I have not been this far east of the settlement. Isn't that awful?

speaker: Eivor
en: You think safety "awful"?

speaker: Randvi
en: To live one's life in so small a pen. And hear stories from you and the scouts without ever venturing further. Gods, do you smell that? The earth and the air. It is good to be out here.

speaker: Randvi
en: That was thrilling!

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi the Ravager. I should clear a seat on my longship for you.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor, there. What is that?

speaker: Eivor
en: This is where the Summer Army retreated when Grantebridge was lost. They seem to have resettled the city in full now.

speaker: Randvi
en: Right, right. I know this land so well by its map. But to see it in person brings it to stunning life. A Roman marvel. I will not soon forget this site.

speaker: Eivor
en: And here we are. Welcome to Grantebridge. We should make our way to the longhouse.

speaker: Randvi
en: Ah, it's bigger than I imagined. Rustic, woody, beautiful. And everything seems quite new.

speaker: Eivor
en: Under Soma's guidance, the Summer Army built this town up from a small village. They wanted a hub for trade near Lunden, and a launching point for incursions into Wessex.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, it is impressive. Some interesting architectural ideas here too.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait here.

speaker: Eivor
en: We can go.

speaker: Magni
en: Well, well, well! Is that Eivor I see?

speaker: Magni
en: It's been quite a while since I've seen your face around here!

speaker: Eivor
en: I know you, I think. One of Soma's loyal men. Magni is it?

speaker: Magni
en: Ja, good memory.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good to see you, again. This is Randvi, a dear friend and sturdy fighter.

speaker: Magni
en: Well met, Randvi. Eivor seems to have a preference for befriending lovely women.

speaker: Randvi
en: You know, I noticed the same thing.

speaker: Eivor
en: I expected more people about, Magni... has something happened?

speaker: Magni
en: Soma rounded up some warriors and took them west. She's hoping to open a new trade route with Oxeneforda.

speaker: Magni
en: Things have been... different since Soma died.

speaker: Magni
en: Only now, in times of trouble, I have discovered I am not the surrogate leader I should hope to be.

speaker: Randvi
en: What sort of trouble?

speaker: Magni
en: O, a pack of surly bandits have encamped nearby. To the east, at the water's edge. They attack all merchants who travel here by river or road. And word is spreading quickly. It's keeping traders at bay.

speaker: Eivor
en: That could cripple your town if it carries on too long.

speaker: Magni
en: It has crippled me already. The bastards stole my horse yestermorning.

speaker: Eivor
en: So what will you−

speaker: Randvi
en: We can take care of them, Magni. And if we do not find your horse, we will steal you a new one.

speaker: Magni
en: O, that would ease my mind. I have nothing to offer you for this deed, but the bandits surely would. Take from them what you like.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. Consider the matter handled. Eivor, come. We have a camp to raid.

speaker: Randvi
en: The bandits are camped on the river, he said. East of the water's edge.

speaker: Eivor
en: You volunteered us for a fight, Randvi. Is that your idea of a pleasant ride through the country?

speaker: Randvi
en: It must be. I surprised even myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Away from the table for a day, and already you are lusting for blood.

speaker: Randvi
en: A feeling you must know well, no? I have always wanted to experience the world as you do, and now I will... unless you have a more interesting day planned for us.

speaker: Eivor
en: We will help Magni and clear these bandits. But do not be rash when we find them. The Raven Clan needs your steady hand.

speaker: Randvi
en: Yes, indeed, my lord. I shall follow your order to the letter.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I did not know any better, I would say you're teasing me...

speaker: Randvi
en: O certainly not, Eivor Wolf-Kissed, iron-fisted drengr. I would never tease one with such commanding authority.

speaker: Randvi
en: There. The bandit camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. Stay close. And do as I do.

speaker: Randvi
en: Brood and look sternly at the horizon?

speaker: Eivor
en: By all means.

speaker: Randvi
en: Nicely done!

speaker: Eivor
en: Shhh...

speaker: Randvi
en: I thought you wanted to do this in secret?

speaker: Eivor
en: You seemed hot for a battle, so here we go.

speaker: Randvi
en: There. That's done. Now to deliver Magni his horse.

speaker: Randvi
en: That was a thrill, Eivor. We are champions of Grantebridge! Do you know of any other towns that need liberating?

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't think we have had enough drama for one day? We should return to the settlement.

speaker: Randvi
en: Or we could have a drink. To celebrate our victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: At home. Tekla has all the mead and ale we could want.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor, our outing has hardly begun. Find us an ale house and let us make ourselves at home.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's us return the horse, and if your thirst remains, we'll look around.

speaker: Eivor
en: Magni. We solved your bandit problem.

speaker: Magni
en: Did you? Well done! And did you find my sweet mare?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your horse is outside, waiting for you.

speaker: Magni
en: Thank the gods she is safe. And thank you, Eivor... and your friend, Randvi, wherever she is.

speaker: Eivor
en: She's here somewhere...

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor! Over here! Look at this.

speaker: Magni
en: O ho! Someone is thirsty.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you determined to get drunk?

speaker: Randvi
en: I am determined to get you drunk. Come on! Scared I will outpace you?

speaker: Eivor
en: To be honest... a little.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you playing at?

speaker: Randvi
en: A drinking contest. You versus me. Wolf-Kissed versus Table-Maiden.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi, we can do better than Table-Maiden.

speaker: Randvi
en: Mead-Queen, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. Let us drink.

speaker: Randvi
en: Beautiful.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should keep my head clear.

speaker: Randvi
en: A shame, because we aren't leaving until you take me on.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are you?

speaker: Randvi
en: Come on, what do you say?

speaker: Magni
en: Randvi! Don't let her win. Randvi! Focus!

speaker: Magni
en: A good sup, Eivor, but Randvi's done you better.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah! There, you see. Should have not tried to outdrink me, Randvi! It cannot be done.

speaker: Randvi
en: Hm, strange. I see your lips moving so rapidly, yet all I hear is "Thank you, Randvi."

speaker: Eivor
en: Gah! Any more and I'll drown.

speaker: Randvi
en: Ha! I am the Mead-Queen! Slayer of Wolves and Barrels! I told you I would drink you under the table.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, are you satisfied? My head is ringing like a bell.

speaker: Randvi
en: More than satisfied. Now come, we'll ride this off and take in the air as we head home. After just one more step.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gah, Randvi...

speaker: Randvi
en: It's a sunken tower near a waterfall, close to home. We can stop for a look and then you are free of me. It's near the highest point of a hill just south of the settlement. Easy to spot, I'm sure.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. One last stop then.

speaker: Randvi
en: I know it might not show, Eivor, but I am terribly excited.

speaker: Eivor
en: O, it shows.

speaker: Magni
en: Leaving already? Well, I do hope to see you again... Randvi. Return any time.

speaker: Randvi
en: I might have to, Randvi. Thank you for everything.

speaker: Magni
en: No, no. Thank you. Safe travels.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think you may have punctured poor Magni's heart back there.

speaker: Randvi
en: What can I say? Not the first, and it will not be the last.

speaker: Eivor
en: I name you Randvi... Slayer of Bandits, Breaker of Hearts.

speaker: Randvi
en: I will sound it with pride. Sunniva described this tower for me. A desolate, yet peaceful place. I am eager to see it.

speaker: Eivor
en: After a full day of action, finally you wish to calm down.

speaker: Randvi
en: I have had my fill of adventure. Time for a little rest.

speaker: Randvi
en: I was wondering something. You and Soma... was there something more to your bond? You spoke of her with a particular shine in your eyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: We grew very close, very quickly. Is that what you mean?

speaker: Randvi
en: No, I mean... did something happen between you two?

speaker: Eivor
en: What sort of question is that?

speaker: Randvi
en: An innocent one. Innocent as a newborn babe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing happened between us. That is my answer.

speaker: Randvi
en: Hm. I find that... disappointing. If I were you, I might have tested the waters. Eivor, entangled by a hardy jarlskona as she leads her army to victory and prosperity. A rather appealing match.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm going to pretend your last words were taken by the wind, Randvi.

speaker: Randvi
en: If you must.

speaker: Randvi
en: Look there, that must be the tower! Take the bridge!

speaker: Randvi
en: Just as beautiful as Sunniva's stories tell. Can you imagine how it looked when it was first built, hundreds of winters ago? Sometimes when looking at a map, I imagine little people in their little armies, traversing the land. And now, staring at these ruins, I imagine people of old, how they lived, never knowing what would become of their monuments.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a fertile imagination.

speaker: Randvi
en: I want a view from the top. Shall we?

speaker: Eivor
en: Lead on.

speaker: Randvi
en: Keep up!

speaker: Eivor
en: Mind where you put your fingers. These stones are old and weathered.

speaker: Eivor
en: You climb well for one who folds maps.

speaker: Randvi
en: You jest, but I have raised the frames of longhouses and hammered the ribs of longships. My hands are calloused from hard work.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, well... look at this!

speaker: Randvi
en: A stunning view. It reminds me of my early years in Norway. How I used to climb the hills beyond the wood.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have an adventurer's heart. I hardly see it behind the table, but now I've watched you scale a tower in furs, soaking wet.

speaker: Randvi
en: I was rowdy in my youth. Hunting, sailing. I was a wildling of the open air, before I became this staunch and stoic woman. Married off in service of peace between two clans. A noble and worthy role, but not one I had ever imagined for myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: You would have made a fine, wandering warrior. A jomsviking, free to come and go as she pleased.

speaker: Randvi
en: I think so too. It may be we would have sailed together, over the open seas. Raiding or... traveling.

speaker: Eivor
en: Or faced each other on the field of battle. Without your marriage to Sigurd to secure peace, our clans might still be at war.

speaker: Randvi
en: True. Very true.

speaker: Randvi
en: Thank you for today. Every bit of it has been a dream and... and I am not keen to wake.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then don't. We can stay here, as long as you like.

speaker: Randvi
en: Yes...

speaker: Eivor
en: What was that...?

speaker: Randvi
en: O no, I am... I am sorry. I shouldn't have. I got away from myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: No need to apologize.

speaker: Randvi
en: Sigurd is your brother and I... I have put you in a very different position. The heart does not do politics like the head.

speaker: Randvi
en: Though I am newly separated from Sigurd, I should not have made such a frivolous advance. Forgive me.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be the mead, it may be the air. But there is no need to apologize.

speaker: Randvi
en: I am sober enough. But the truth of it is... I have felt this way for some time now. I care for you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is... comforting to hear. I have long felt the same way. But I banished the thought that this would ever happen.

speaker: Randvi
en: Many times I wished to tell you. Wished to say what was in my heart and what I desired, but duty kept me from it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Say all you like.

speaker: Randvi
en: Today has meant so much. We rode, we fought, we drank, we laughed. You showed me your world. Not in words but deeds.

speaker: Eivor
en: Deeds are more direct than words...

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi... I do wish I could indulge this feeling further. But that is not possible.

speaker: Randvi
en: Of course, yes. I was foolish to—Let this be a dream, then. A moment that never happened but in our minds. I would not wish you to see me so weak as that.

speaker: Eivor
en: You need feel no shame. This stays between us. And at worst, we have had a beautiful day. As friends and kindred spirits.

speaker: Randvi
en: More than enough for me. I would like to stay here, if it is all the same to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would like that.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am honored by your feelings, Randvi. But I value you as a friend. I hope that does not disappoint... it is my highest praise.

speaker: Randvi
en: Of course, thank you. I do apologize.

speaker: Eivor
en: You need feel no shame. This stays between us. And at worst, we have had a beautiful day. As friends and kindred spirits.

speaker: Randvi
en: More than enough for me. I would like to stay here, if it is all the same to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would like that.

speaker: Randvi
en: Today has meant so much. We rode, we fought, we drank, we laughed. You showed me your world. Not in words but deeds.

speaker: Eivor
en: Deeds are more direct than words...

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm. Must have returned back to the settlement.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi. You left so suddenly.

speaker: Randvi
en: There is work to be done. There always is.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see.

speaker: Randvi
en: But do not think for a moment that I have forgotten you and our wonderful day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nor would I wish you to.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. Then we see eye to eye.

speaker: Eivor
en: And heart to heart.

speaker: Randvi
en: Yes, indeed. Until our next moment alone, we should return to our great work. England will not pacify itself on our behalf.

speaker: Eivor
en: No indeed.

speaker: Randvi
en: Back to work then.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi, why did you leave? We could have returned together.

speaker: Randvi
en: We could have, but I was... restless. A quiet walk alone clears the head. And you do snore a little. Like a wounded bear.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's a lie.

speaker: Randvi
en: I had a wonderful time, Eivor. Thank you for your company. And your friendship.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you for yours.

speaker: Randvi
en: Now. Shall we get back to it?

speaker: Havi
en: This is the mountain I seek. There is no higher peak.

speaker: Havi
en: This looks like the right place. I swear, dwarves would choose riddling over rutting.

speaker: Havi
en: There is the seed, in the mountain's rocky grip. Some heat may free it from its shell.

speaker: Havi
en: The seed will not sprout root until I get it into some water.

speaker: Havi
en: I must retrieve the root for Ivaldi before it takes hold.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kjotve has set a rearguard while he sacks the village. We've spotted warrior in three watchtowers. I will attack the one to the north, you three can handle the other two.

speaker: Viking 1
en: You sure, Eivor? We would be stronger attacking as one.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, but not as swift. We need spare as much of the darkness as we can for the main attack.

speaker: Viking 1
en: Of course, Eivor. We will meet you on the other side of the line.

speaker: Viking 2
en: Swift as snakes now. Let's not keep Kjotve waiting.

speaker: Viking 2
en: No alarms raised. Eivor must have taken the second tower by now.

speaker: Viking 3
en: One more to go. Let us finish this.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's all three. The first blow well struck!

speaker: Viking 3
en: They were completely surprised. Was like killing sheep.

speaker: Viking 1
en: It is odd though... you would think Kjotve would prepare for a counter attack.

speaker: Viking 2
en: The gods favor the bold, friends. We have caught him unawares, that is all.

speaker: Eivor
en: We will return to the main host. You will sharpen the edge of the sword. Join the front line of attack.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thyra! We need an archery challenge to test our skills.

speaker: Thyra
en: This range tests a hunter's sense to know when to shoot and when not to shoot.

speaker: Eivor
en: When does a hunter not shoot?

speaker: Thyra
en: Imagine we're hunting together. You step on a branch and I shoot without thinking. What do you think happens.

speaker: Eivor
en: I take your point.

speaker: Thyra
en: In this contest, archers score points for hitting the right targets, and lose points for hitting the wrong ones.

speaker: Eivor
en: Seems straightforward.

speaker: Thyra
en: There's also a time limit to make it more challenging. You want to give it a shot?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hand me a bow.

speaker: Thyra
en: Start on my mark... Begin!

speaker: Thyra
en: Halfway mark.

speaker: Thyra
en: Lower your bow.

speaker: Thyra
en: I do not think I could do better. We have a champion.

speaker: Swinda
en: You must be Eivor. I am Swinda. Gunnar asked me to help forge and repair weapons.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well met! I'm happy to have the extra help. Why have you set up at the fist-fight grounds?

speaker: Swinda
en: Sunniva told me you would not mind if I used the fight ring to test my weapons. I have actually made a bit of a game of it. That way I can test my metal while your warriors practice for battle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Using real weapons? Do you wish to kill them before they set foot on the battlefield?.

speaker: Swinda
en: Ha! No. There are rules to my tournament! You must yield once you've had enough and take time to heal. Was Sunniva wrong to let me set up this tournament?

speaker: Eivor
en: No. No need to worry. We could all use some combat practice. Competition breed comradery.

speaker: Swinda
en: Yes, comradery! In fact, everyone in the tournament must choose a second, an ally to fight by your side.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have a Jomsviking in the barracks who would make a fine ally.

speaker: Swinda
en: Very good. I've prepared three different types of weapons for you to test. Are you ready to join the tournament?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm ready.

speaker: Swinda
en: Good! Choose your weapon.

speaker: Eivor
en: This has a good weight to it.

speaker: Swinda
en: There are three rounds with no breaks in between and stop fighting if an opponent yields. Are you ready?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ready and eager!

speaker: Swinda
en: A true warrior! Also, the likely be unfair depending on your opponents and the weapons you choose. And remember, it won't be one on one. May the gods grant you luck!

speaker: Swinda
en: Fighters ready? Begin!

speaker: Swinda
en: You two fight well together.

speaker: Swinda
en: Always more enjoyable with an ally!

speaker: Swinda
en: Let's see how you do on your own.

speaker: Swinda
en: I give you the last drengr standing. Eivor of the Raven Clan!

speaker: Swinda
en: You have certainly mastered that weapon. Here, some extra tokens, you deserve them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me more about Cent.

speaker: Randvi
en: Basim has written, claiming to have found the woman Fulke and asking for your aid. He has taken shelter at Saint Hadrian's Priory.

speaker: Eivor
en: Any news of Sigurd?

speaker: Randvi
en: Nothing he mentioned. But if he has found the Paladin Fulke, Sigurd cannot be far behind.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will go as soon as I can.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. Be safe, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag. Basim has brought word of Sigurd's location. We are leaving at once to find him.

speaker: Dag
en: Well done, Eivor. After so long, it finally occurs to you to search for our jarl. I applaud your half-hearted effort. I will not be joining you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag, this is no joke. On the ship. Now.

speaker: Dag
en: Someone needs to stay home and direct the affairs of the settlement. As you seem to shun this place as often as possible, it must fall to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd's life is at stake. We need you there.

speaker: Dag
en: No. I am needed here.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you wish to stay, so be it. But when Sigurd is back among us, we will see what status you have among the raiders.

speaker: Dag
en: Say whatever makes you feel superior, Eivor. I know Sigurd will understand my decision.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you doubt me so completely that you will not raise your axe to save your jarl?

speaker: Dag
en: A fine way of putting it, Wolf-Kissed. But go... find the jarl, bring him back. Only do not get lost along the way, as you seem to more and more these days.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is not done, Dag. We will speak when I return.

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim has news of Sigurd. I should find him soon.

speaker: Brother Hortbert
en: Did not Augustine make a distinction between faith and understanding? That is my point.

speaker: Basim
en: So you hold no stock in faith, only in rational proof? The science of the divine. You're bold to defy your teachings.

speaker: Brother Hortbert
en: No... no... that's not what I mean. Let me... let me explain if I might. How to put it...?

speaker: Brother Hortbert
en: What I mean to say is, faith is paramount. Yes. For without it, Christ's sacrifice means nothing.

speaker: Basim
en: He died to save us, did he not? From the original sin of Adam and Eve? Yet evil persists.

speaker: Brother Hortbert
en: Yes, evil persists. Because he gave us free will.

speaker: Basim
en: Does a newborn babe slain by a despot have free will?

speaker: Brother Hortbert
en: Yes... no, I mean... that is too simplistic.

speaker: Basim
en: Or the priest whose heart is torn from his chest by the wolf? Judas, who was predestined to betray the Nazarene?

speaker: Brother Hortbert
en: Some argue Judas was used...

speaker: Brother Cedric
en: Do my ears deceive me, Brother Hortbert? You question the scriptures? Declare Judas an innocent? A preposterous blasphemy!

speaker: Brother Hortbert
en: N-no, that is not what I said! Brother Cedric... am I not the most pious of His servants?

speaker: Brother Cedric
en: Out! Out!

speaker: Eivor
en: Making new friends?

speaker: Basim
en: A person's tongue gives you a taste of their heart, Eivor. And such information is often useful.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how do these sallow Christians taste?

speaker: Basim
en: It was only a figure of speech, Eivor. And I have tired of it already.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this how it must be between us?

speaker: Basim
en: Of course not. I'm grateful that you have come.

speaker: Eivor
en: So what of the joy-canker Fulke? In your message you say you tracked her to Cent.

speaker: Basim
en: She is here somewhere, and as of last month, Sigurd was with her. But there is no guarantee this will be the case tomorrow.

speaker: Eivor
en: we're wasting time, Basim. Fulke took Sigurd for some dark purpose. Let's find them before it blackens.

speaker: Basim
en: I agree. The time for talk is long past.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened in Mercia still puzzles me. Fulke saw something in Sigurd. A power, a legacy. What is it she wants?

speaker: Basim
en: Her motives are difficult to fathom. But that can come later. Let's find your brother first.

speaker: Eivor
en: Agreed. If we do this, you'll earn the right to call me friend ten-thousand fold.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, what is your plan?

speaker: Basim
en: We are deep in their god's heartland, a heathen and a heretic. To hunt Fulke, we'll need a Christian snare.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fulke is hardly a saint herself. These Christians abhor her strange ideas.

speaker: Basim
en: True. But unlike us, she can carry herself as one of them. She won't hide from everyone, not with a prisoner in tow.

speaker: Eivor
en: So where to begin?

speaker: Basim
en: I've made a friend. Abbot Cynebert. Full of pious fire, but with ambition that far outweighs his wit.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what does your friend Cynebert know?

speaker: Basim
en: Come, I will introduce you. And we'll hear the full tale together.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you found some peace in your time alone, Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: I am always at peace. And never alone. I move along the people of the world with great joy. I watch them, study them, learn from them at all times. This is our duty, the Hidden Ones' calling.

speaker: Eivor
en: You know, for the first time since we've met, you sound more like your apprentice than yourself.

speaker: Basim
en: Hm. Surely Hytham sounds like me ... if I have taught him well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your creed and your tenets, you mean?

speaker: Basim
en: That's right. And our sense of... how should I sa ... deep responsibility to the betterment of mankind.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's quite an ambition. But it doesn't explain what you see in Sigurd. My brother is not so generous.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, but your brother is... someone special. Important. And I want him to see that. I hope to show it to him.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Is this not a blessed plot? God's own country. And this Eden should be given to his servants to tend.

speaker: Basim
en: Abbot Cynebert. This is the Norse I spoke of.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Ah, yes, and quite a fearsome one at that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim says you know the paladin, Fulke.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Indeed. The Lady Fulke passed this way not more than a month ago. We talked, we drank. A very pleasant woman.

speaker: Eivor
en: And where is she−

speaker: Basim
en: Eivor will be your axe, abbot. Whether to fell a tree or hew the limbs from an enemy.

speaker: Eivor
en: What have you promised him?

speaker: Cynebert
en: O, just a trifle, Eivor. A little problem I believe you can help me with.

speaker: Eivor
en: Speak your terms plainly, abbot. I will decide if the bargain is worth my time.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Ah! Your wolf shows its teeth, Basim.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you know where Fulke is, do not rattle my bucket. Tell me now and we'll talk terms later.

speaker: Cynebert
en: The hot-tempered one stirs up strife, Basim! Will this rebellion-caked Dane do what I ask?

speaker: Basim
en: This Norse is one who knows the value of silence and secrecy. The perfect choice for our subtle business.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's cut to the point. What favor would you ask in exchange for Fulke?

speaker: Cynebert
en: Some weeks ago, our ealdorman in Cent was called to God. A terrible loss. King Aelfred has chosen his replacement, but has not yet announced the name. I must know it... now.

speaker: Eivor
en: All of Cent will see soon enough which thegn he has chosen. Why not wait?

speaker: Cynebert
en: I want... early access. To woo him, before his exalted position is made public and every fool is at his door.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who else knows the chosen man?

speaker: Cynebert
en: The king's emissary. Sent with a letter of congratulations to the new ealdorman. Intercept him and bring me the news. When I know the thegn's name, we'll discuss how I might win his favor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why not kill him in secret and petition Aelfred for the seat?

speaker: Cynebert
en: As a man of God, I cannot. Besides, he who stands behind the throne can better pull on the puppet's threads.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your king will not be happy, his Church meddling in his politics.

speaker: Basim
en: Does this not delight you, Eivor? A chance to defy Aelfred?

speaker: Cynebert
en: I am God's humble shepherd, sent to protect his lambs. If Cent's new ealdorman is a wolf, I would blunt his claws.

speaker: Eivor
en: If we do this, how will you find Fulke? I want some kind of assurance.

speaker: Cynebert
en: Do you have ears in every church, abbey, and cathedral in Cent? Because I do. And I will find her.

speaker: Basim
en: And we will do the deeds too staining for a Christian soul?

speaker: Eivor
en: This emissary. How will I find him?

speaker: Cynebert
en: Tonbridge Monastery sent word that the king's men always pass a few nights in their hospitality. Begin there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll get the ealdorman's name, you find Fulke.

speaker: Cynebert
en: All in good time. Now, if we are done, I have business up the south coast. Folcanstan has the best fish in Wessex.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I will find you there when the ealdorman's name is mine.

speaker: Basim
en: Cynebert is ambitious, but well-connected. We will not find Fulke without him.

speaker: Eivor
en: I suppose we'll see. What will you do?

speaker: Basim
en: I am not done playing with these Christians yet. I will see you in Folcanstan.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Augustine said "Seek not to understand that you may believe, but believe that you may understand"?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: In the four centuries since Augustine wrote, many advances have been made in our understanding of the scripture!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I... only meant that the scripture alone...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Enough! I will not hear another word. The scripture alone... this is bordering on blasphemy.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Blasphemy! No, no brother...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Never speak again until you have learned to obey God's will and not your own.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: You would force a vow of silence simply because God gave me an enquiring mind?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Ah! Blasphemy! Blasphemy!

speaker: Eivor
en: If Aelfred's emissary spent a few days here, someone may know where he went.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: You're not welcome here.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: I have no time for your twittering. We are not friends, be gone.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 5
en: Did she speak to you of the Betrayer's scriptures? I am troubled in my spirit.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 6
en: Shhh, it is heresy to even think of it. Forget her words, her blasphemies. Think only on Christ and his redemptive message.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 5
en: She spoke freely of a deceit of angels. That we are the defiled race, ones who can never find salvation!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 6
en: If you are Hell-bent on believing this, you are already lost to the Lord of Flies.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Stay away from me, stranger.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: I'm busy, leave me be.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 4
en: A bear? Of fur and tears? Why does he cry?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 5
en: My brother saw him in the old stone ring with his own eyes. Rubbed them twice to be sure.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 4
en: Someone should do something.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 5
en: What? Ask him to move on? Or perhaps he can live with us here and the children will ride his matted back?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 6
en: They sent my husband to work at the Beamasfield, the lumber mill. They mean to fortify us against the Danes.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 7
en: My sister said they're all tall and strong. Muscles rippling, hair braided and woven with spice.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 6
en: And what will you do if one carries you off?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 7
en: Dream of the pretty, straw-haired bairns (children)I'll have.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sober enough to answer me?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 7
en: You have fine hair. It shimmers like... woven silk.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't have time for flattery. I seek Aelfred's emissary.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 7
en: The only man of Aelfred's I know is Orvyn the legless.

speaker: Eivor
en: And he is...?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 7
en: Hm. Haven't seen him in years. Probably dead drunk, or just dead in a ditch. Why do you think they called him legless?

speaker: Eivor
en: Because he has no legs?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 7
en: Baw! It's a figure of speech, Lord in Heaven.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 8
en: God teaches obedience and humility, and yet our abbot would defy Aelfred?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 9
en: How so? He is simply being a good shepherd, keeping Cent and her rich lands in the hands of the Church.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 8
en: But the Danes? Do they not nestle at our borders? Like ash-scaled serpents?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 9
en: Danes in Cent? I don't believe it. Aelfred overspeaks their danger so he may take from us as he pleases.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 10
en: I heard he was captured by Danes, and they ate his heart.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 11
en: Ealdorman Deogol got blind drunk and likely staggered off the white cliffs.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 10
en: So who will take his place? Thegn Fairfax? Landry? Tedmund?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 11
en: None are worth the shit on a sheep's arse. I would not case my vote for one of them.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 10
en: A defiant stance for one who cannot cast a vote.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: He's gotten so paranoid now, he won't even leave the keep tower. Captain's calling him Mouse-Balls.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: What's made him so frightened?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: He said the Danes are coming. Coming for him. He saw it in a dream. Let's hope Mouse-Balls doesn't end up our next ealdorman.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for someone.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 12
en: Speak your piece, I have work to do.

speaker: Eivor
en: Seen anyone here on the king's authority?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 12
en: I've been wondering that myself! Did someone bring news of the ealdorman? Lord Landry's make a good one.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: You trying to catch flies, or would you ask something of me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for a man. He passed through here on the king's business.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Bugger off, eh? Or I'll call the guards. I'm sick of people. You need to heal your own ills.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe some coin will loose your lips?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: A wise move, mud-wit. It so happens I did see Aelfred's man. He's long gone though. Maybe Gowan the Bard knows where?

speaker: Eivor
en: Where will I find him?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: He was pissed as a newt. Last I saw, he was passed out in trees between the harbor and bridge. Now go find someone else to vex.

speaker: Eivor
en: And people are sick of you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Jesus wept! Guards, guards! A Dane, saints preserve me!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Help me! This Dane has murder in mind!

speaker: Eivor
en: How about you help me from the goodness of your heart? And then I leave you alone?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: A wise move, mud-wit. It so happens I did see Aelfred's man. He's long gone though. Maybe Gowan the Bard knows where?

speaker: Eivor
en: Where will I find him?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: He was pissed as a newt. Last I saw, he was passed out in trees between the harbor and bridge. Now go find someone else to vex.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 13
en: I'm in no mood for wind-belching. So choose your words well?

speaker: Eivor
en: I heard the king's men came through here, caused a stir. A man of your wit noticed them I bet?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 13
en: I am witty! Finally someone sees. I'm always telling my wife, but will she listen? Will she bollocks.

speaker: Eivor
en: You choose your words well. What do you know about Aelfred's emissary?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 13
en: Course I do! I'm apprentice to a famous flyter, the Silent Monk. Challenge me for it!

speaker: Eivor
en: You'll call me word crusher, your wits I will addle.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 13
en: Eh... alright, you bested me.

speaker: Eivor
en: The king's emissary... I need to know where he went, after he stayed here.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 13
en: And I need to know why I've started getting boils under my armpits. Time will tell, eh?

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfred's emissary. Where?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 13
en: Him and the bard ended up in the copse by the bridge doing the Lord knows what. Sounded like they were murdering a cat.

speaker: Eivor
en: Singing?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 13
en: If you say so.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 14
en: Who are you? Loitering and lollygagging?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for someone, an emissary from Aelfred. Have you seen such a man?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 14
en: O, la-di-da. Listen to you all high and mighty. Get away with you, yer valley-lily.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you would rather feel the edge of my blade, it can be arranged.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 14
en: Now that I respect! Forceful, to the point, as refreshing as a summer ale.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me what you know, or this will go badly.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 14
en: For you, maybe. I'll be dead, and you still won't know a thing.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm wasting my time with you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 14
en: Now that's just hurtful. No need to dig the blade in.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a strange fish. Did you see the man or not?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 14
en: I did. He was getting pie-eyed with that bard Gowan and causing quite a ruckus. They left together. See? That wasn't hard was it?

speaker: Eivor
en: Harder than it should have been.

speaker: Eivor
en: There was a bard drinking with the emissary. I should find him, see if he knows anything.

speaker: Eivor
en: That ale-swamped scop can't have gone far.

speaker: Drunken Bard
en: ... So cold... brrrr... Someone stole my trews?

speaker: Eivor
en: You there... you alive?

speaker: Drunken Bard
en: Patience is a tired horse, plodity, plod, plod.

speaker: Eivor
en: Another tottering teat-sucker who can't hold his drink. Let's clear your head.

speaker: Musical Musings
en: These bells! What incredible music they make. It is like the singing of angels. A waste to bury them away in churches! I would love to compose a great work to harness their beauty. The deep knell of the largest would provide the anchor of the piece. The harmonious tolling of the smaller bells would be the choir and the smallest would soar above the tune, a descant of chimes. Gowan the Bard

speaker: Drunken Bard
en: It's cold as a witch's tit in here!

speaker: Drunken Bard
en: Ow! Why do you smite me so?

speaker: Eivor
en: God's trews! Fie on you. What infernal wakes me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you the tale-weaver?

speaker: Gowan
en: Gowan the dandelion, for the seeds of my stories flit upon the winds of Wessex! But why, mule, do you kick my noggin?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm the one you sing of, bard. Stern of eye and scant of mercy. Have you not seen the ravens feasting in my wake?

speaker: Gowan
en: Enough! Your word-mangles are making my hair ache!

speaker: Eivor
en: Who I am is no concern of yours.

speaker: Gowan
en: And I do not care. Did you want something, or did you just wake me to torment me?

speaker: Eivor
en: You and Aelfred's emissary were drinking in the tavern. Tell me where he went.

speaker: Gowan
en: Were we? I was so ale-addled... perhaps a small and silver thing upon my palm might help me recall?

speaker: Eivor
en: How about something long and sharp in your gut?

speaker: Gowan
en: Alright! No need for that. You paint a vivid picture, Dane. He was headed to the white coast to the southeast. Dover Fortress. He said it is where they train those religious fanatics. Zealots! They pray all night instead of sleeping.

speaker: Eivor
en: No one would drown themselves in weeping with one less bard in the world. Tell me what you know.

speaker: Gowan
en: You Danes aren't ones for bargaining, are you? He was headed to the white coast to the southeast. Dover Fortress.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have some coin. And rent a proper bed for the night.

speaker: Gowan
en: Ah, bless you, for stories are my currency friend. How else am I to make my living?

speaker: Eivor
en: A more honest profession? Plowing fields, milking cows...

speaker: Gowan
en: Manual labor! God's blood! There's a fortress to the southeast where paladins pray by night and fight by day. Dover, on the white cliffs.

speaker: Eivor
en: My thanks, and in return, wisdom. Too much beer-bibbing will grow a fool in wit and words.

speaker: Gowan
en: My thanks, weaver of the obvious. Now leave me to my unholy punishment.

speaker: Eivor
en: The emissary made for Dover Fortress, on the southeast coast.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: Cent is in disarray.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: How so?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: No one to lead us, no hand upon the helm.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: Aelfred will choose a new ealdorman.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: He already has, and yet we know nothing. And now all trace of the edict is gone.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 5
en: Someone will step up, take the reins. And it will be as it ever is. They will lead, and we will follow.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: You have the curiosity of a day-dead flounder.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dover. The emissary is somewhere here. Perhaps I can find the letter without bloodshed? The bard said paladins trained at this fortress. This will not be an easy fight.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 15
en: I carry the king's word, but there's no hand to put it in.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I could steal the letter without killing the emissary, it would keep me out of trouble.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 15
en: Who interferes with the king's business? Guards! Guards!

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfred's chosen ealdorman is a thegn called Tedmund. The abbot Cynebert will want to know.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should meet Basim and the abbot in Folcanstan.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Ha! Eivor of the Raven Clan! The Eye of Odin will serve our purpose!

speaker: Hildiran
en: I have discovered the secret of the Eye.

speaker: Eivor
en: What can you mean?

speaker: Hildiran
en: It is one thing to look upon it, but quite another to listen. It will sing to you, Wolf-Kissed. It will sing of treasure.

speaker: Eivor
en: You speak in riddles.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Take it. Hold it close. Go to the coast of East Anglia. Once there, follow the song. You will see.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am to listen to an eye with my ears. I fear you mock me.

speaker: Hildiran
en: There is no mockery. Go. You will understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this? The Eye of Odin has found something.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is Hildiran's song. It gets louder as I approach its object.

speaker: Hildiran
en: I see you are unable to open a simple door.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your singing stone tells me something is within. But the door will not move.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Have you still the amulet of Freyja?

speaker: Eivor
en: You burden me with so much jewelry.

speaker: Hildiran
en: You may have fooled Freyja, but your strength is no match for Odin.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mean to say that I must continue to train.

speaker: Hildiran
en: New shrines of Hugrheim await you. If you like, come visit me. I have more treasures to bestow.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Meanwhile, keep this. There may be other hidden playthings of the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: The amulet should now be strong enough for me to enter Odin's Vault.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is likely that once through this gate, there will be no way back. Am I ready for this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not yet.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Ha! At long last!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this?

speaker: Hildiran
en: Vengeance.

speaker: Hildiran
en: I control Hugrheim now. If you die, your mind is forever lost.

speaker: Hildiran
en: You will not last long.

speaker: Eivor
en: There, Valkyrie!

speaker: Hildiran
en: I would like you to meet my guests!

speaker: Hildiran
en: You search for your very death!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why have you turned against me?

speaker: Hildiran
en: My mother, her mother, and back generations have sought you out.

speaker: Hildiran
en: You are resilient, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Hildiran
en: A pleasant surprise.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have done nothing to you or any of your grandmothers!

speaker: Hildiran
en: The blood of Valkyries flows in my veins. Blood once spilled by the One-Eyed!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is all this talk of Valkyries?

speaker: Hildiran
en: You well know, the Valkyrie Hildr was betrayed by Freyja and imprisoned by you!

speaker: Eivor
en: That's the spot!

speaker: Hildiran
en: You must defeat all of me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Perfect!

speaker: Eivor
en: Another one!

speaker: Eivor
en: Annoying pests!

speaker: Eivor
en: You speak madness!

speaker: Hildiran
en: You imprisoned Hildr in the cell of ice, where she died of starvation after Ragnarök.

speaker: Eivor
en: Too many! Stay away! I must thin them out! Still more! Will I never be done with you?

speaker: Hildiran
en: I attack as a swarm!

speaker: Eivor
en: O, yes! Surprised by death.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Strike a blow and I will vanish as the wind, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Hildiran
en: You are an ocean away. You will never get me at this rate.

speaker: Eivor
en: I feel you near.

speaker: Eivor
en: Crusher!

speaker: Eivor
en: Drink your own blood!

speaker: Hildiran
en: My mother told the tale since I was a child. How to use the amulet, how to defeat the One-Eyed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot make sense of your ravings.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was... not entirely a dream.

speaker: Hildiran
en: The fight was fought in two spheres. You have defeated me both here and in the Mind's Realm.

speaker: Eivor
en: But why have we fought?

speaker: Hildiran
en: I wished to take vengeance for my fore-mother of countless generations ago, Hildr.

speaker: Eivor
en: Revenge upon me?

speaker: Hildiran
en: Untold generations of my fore-mothers lead back to a powerful Valkyrie named Hildr. She was Freyja's lover.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Odin burned with jealous fury. He threw Hildr into prison where my long-ago grandmother languished for years.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your long-ago grandmother was Freyja's lover?

speaker: Hildiran
en: All she had left of Freyja's love was her amulet.

speaker: Hildiran
en: With each generation, my family vowed vengeance on Odin, whom we have watched for with vigilance!

speaker: Eivor
en: You take me for Odin?

speaker: Hildiran
en: I did. But I was mistaken. You are far wiser than he. In defeat, I offer my loyalty.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a tale fit for a drunken madwoman... but I accept your pledge.

speaker: Hildiran
en: I am grateful to assist you, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Hildiran
en: No need for this ancient beacon any longer.

speaker: Hildiran
en: If you wish, there is training yet to be done. Treasures to be had! Come see me to prepare or to learn more about Hildr.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would like that.

speaker: Eivor
en: "Untold generations." It is a long time to carry a grudge.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, I see. These objects are used as beacons.

speaker: Hildiran
en: I marvel at you, Eivor! Such armor.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is my honor to wear the shielding of a Valkyrie.

speaker: Hildiran
en: It suits you well.

speaker: Randvi
en: Ah, there you are.

speaker: Eivor
en: You wanted to see me?

speaker: Randvi
en: As Sigurd has so ordered, it falls to us to expand our presence in England.

speaker: Eivor
en: He wants to forge alliances. Ironclad, with every Norse, Dane, and Saxon here.

speaker: Randvi
en: Right. We are the outsiders here. Making friends will help.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where do we start?

speaker: Randvi
en: My scouts come and go daily with interesting news and tidings, and I am beginning to get my bearings in this fractured land. As I learn more, I can give you insight into each territory, before you commit to a journey there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course.

speaker: Randvi
en: Once you have gained an ally in a territory, return home and speak to me. We'll decide your next move then.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. So where do we start?

speaker: Randvi
en: You have two options just now. Join Sigurd in Ledecestrescire to the north, and meet with the Sons of Ragnar Lothbrok. Or head south to Grantebridgescire to meet an army of Danes led by one Guthrum Jarl and his second, Soma. I should add, our young friend Hytham has been conferring with his own contacts in the cities. His research could be useful in winning us alliances throughout the cities of England. Speak with him and see what he needs.

speaker: Note of Support
en: Bless you dearie. You're an inspiration to us all. Accept these few carrots, they've turned black and all, but the Good Lord made them and they give sustenance.
Here in solitude, forever enclosed, I foreswear all earthly pleasures. I pay my penance within these walls, never to see the light of sun again. A sinner am I, the joys of life I have forsaken.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you doing in this dungeon?

speaker: Anchoress
en: I devote myself to solitary prayer, to confession and fasting.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have broken the lock. You can leave.

speaker: Anchoress
en: But I choose to live this way. I am an anchoress. This is my entire life.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sealed up here? All day and night for life? It is an odd way to worship.

speaker: Anchoress
en: I am at complete peace with the world. Can you say as much?

speaker: Eivor
en: How can you be at peace with the world if you live beyond its reach?

speaker: Anchoress
en: I know the pain it can inflict.

speaker: Eivor
en: Come outside. Your god won't be angry for just a few moments. Come. Come.

speaker: Anchoress
en: I will follow you, if only to feel the grass beneath my feet. I will repent when I return. I came here after the dark times. Pestilence and hunger. The death of my father. It's been years. I wonder what it will be like to once again feel a cool breeze, the warm sun, the scent of lavender?

speaker: Anchoress
en: Ah! The world! It is so beautiful. The earth's beauty renews us. Thank you, stranger. My life begins anew.

speaker: Kenrick
en: This time I am going to do it. This time! O God! Why did you fashion me from such weak clay? Be brave, Kenrick. Do it for Ethelind.

speaker: Eivor
en: You pace about like a dog afraid of a beating. What troubles you?

speaker: Kenrick
en: O, stranger! Here's a tale. I love Ethelind, a hunter's daughter. But the hunter's a fearsome fellow. Set me a task, he did. There's an arrow, stuck in that tree above, that the hunter once fired there. Before any man can have Ethelind, they need to climb up and get it. Many suitors have tried. All failed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like child's play to me. Maybe I can help.

speaker: Kenrick
en: O, you do mean to help me! God bless you!

speaker: Eivor
en: A lynx. And he does not like visitors.

speaker: Kenrick
en: Hey! What's going on? Are you all right up there?

speaker: Eivor
en: This one has a letter. Perhaps it will shed some light on this strange affair.

speaker: Kenrick
en: You did, er, remember the arrow, right? You are still up there, aren't you? Um, have you got it yet?

speaker: Kenrick
en: You got the arrow! Praise be to you, stranger! Bring it back, won't you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have the arrow, proof of your boundless courage.

speaker: Kenrick
en: O, thank you, stranger! I'll name our firstborn in your honor, swear I will! Er... what is your name?

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor.

speaker: Kenrick
en: Eivor, eh? Er... well, maybe just something that rhymes with it, then? Would that do?

speaker: Eivor
en: I found the other suitors. A lynx had made its lair up there. A hunter like Ethelind's father would have know that.

speaker: Kenrick
en: Surely an innocent mistake? But I must bring him the arrow! He'll be so pleased someone's got it at last!

speaker: Eivor
en: I found a letter from Ethelind. Seems she didn't think much of you. You were far from her first choice.

speaker: Kenrick
en: O, I know. She's made no secret of that. But now they're dead, and I'm not, so... tra-la-la!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sure her father will be thrilled.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sure her father will be thrilled.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your bakery is done, Tarben. And our feasting table will be warmer for it.

speaker: Tarben
en: Eivor, that is... kind of you. I hope one day I can repay you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are among friends here. There is no need.

speaker: Tarben
en: No need, but a desire. An earnest one. I remember the good things people do for me. To warm my heart in times when... ...when kindnesses are few and far between. There was one more thing, though if you had a moment. A grain merchant has set up downriver. I want to bring a half dozen bags home, but I would need an extra pair of hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can lend a hand.

speaker: Tarben
en: That's a relief. I did not fancy asking Holger.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot help now. Maybe later?

speaker: Tarben
en: No rush. Just let me know.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tarben.

speaker: Tarben
en: Eivor. Shall we go?

speaker: Eivor
en: Tarben. What brought you to our clan?

speaker: Tarben
en: Your reputation. Heard folks say a band of hard-drinking, battle-scarred warriors had washed up on shore. Said you had settled in the center of Mercia, taking in whatever flotsam, jetsam, and jumble of misfits came to your docks.

speaker: Eivor
en: And this appealed to you?

speaker: Tarben
en: More than anything. Always been a bit of a drifter. The thought of settling in a rowdy camp felt like a good balance. And being a baker, I knew my services would not be sniffed at.

speaker: Eivor
en: I did not take you for a baker when we met. You have the look of someone who swings an axe.

speaker: Tarben
en: I do hear that a lot.

speaker: Eivor
en: But baking is your only craft. Is that right?

speaker: Tarben
en: I have always enjoyed it. And I have always been good at it. But when I am not able to find such work, I take odd jobs where I can. So long as I can work with my hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, we have that in common.

speaker: Tarben
en: A question, Eivor. You are a warrior, a fighter, that much I know. But if you could stop fighting, what would you do?

speaker: Eivor
en: You ask the wrong question. I can stop fighting. But to do so would be to deny the essence of who I am. I think you mean... "If I had to stop fighting, what would I become?

speaker: Tarben
en: No, you've given me the answer I wanted. It's good you have found what calls you. A rare and happy thing.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Yes, yes, I see you both. What can I

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: It's you. Wh-what are you doing in Mercia?

speaker: Tarben
en: Collecting grain. Thirty silvers' worth if you can spare it. I do have the coin.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Right. Well... take what you need and get going.

speaker: Tarben
en: That should cover it. Thank you kindly.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Of course. And you, ah, you take good care of yourself. Yeah?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that your usual vendor? He seemed... a little surprised to see you.

speaker: Tarben
en: Did he? Well... could be he knows somebody who looks like me. There's no shortage of big bearded men around here, yeah?

speaker: Eivor
en: I suppose not.

speaker: Eivor
en: About your question earlier, what would I do if I weren't a warrior? I would ask the same of you. Is baking bread your greatest wish?

speaker: Tarben
en: Is there something wrong with wanting to bake bread? The Romans baked bread. The Egyptians baked bread.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a fine trade. But is it your calling?

speaker: Tarben
en: It is my calling to feed people, I'd say. To be of service to those I care for, and who care for me. That brings me joy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Put that way, it is a noble pursuit.

speaker: Tarben
en: I don't know that it's noble. It's simply what gets me up in the morning. And gives me purpose for the rest of my day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Need help with your grain?

speaker: Tarben
en: No need, no need. I'll do the rest myself, bring it in and put it where I like.

speaker: Eivor
en: Alright. It was good to speak with you, Tarben. A welcome diversion.

speaker: Tarben
en: You too, Eivor. Thank you for your help.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: Kraka! Kraka! Where did you get to, you stupid bird? What's happened to you up there...? I knew you weren't ready. Probably got yourself hurt again. Maybe I can get up there myself, somehow...?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: What ails you? Have you lost someone out here?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: In a manner of speaking. I'm waiting for someone to return from an errand. You... probably wouldn't believe me if I told you.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: There is little I wouldn't believe. Speak, while you have my ear.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: I have a crow, Kraka. Found him, injured, back when the invasion started. I nursed him to health, and he chose to stay with me. We share a bond. I swear, it's like he scouts the land, and I can understand what he sees. Have you ever known a such a thing?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: It sounds most familiar. So your crow is lost. Out here?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: Not out here. Up there on that damn lump of rock in the sky. Reckon there's something good, something really valuable up there. So I sent Kraka to see what he could find. He's got a talent for finding treasure, y'see. So up he went. And that was the last I saw of him.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Then I shall keep an eye out for your Kraka.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: Unless you can sprout wings of your own, I don't see how.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: I am full of surprises, dwarf.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Kraka
en: Seems I'm not the only shapeshifter on this rock. Kill these bastards, so that we may both spread our wings again, eh?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Enjoying Muspel hospitality, I see.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Kraka
en: They caught me before I could steal what I came for, for my master. The dwarf below. 'Kraka', he calls me. Long ago, I invaded this land. The dwarves fought back. Wounded, I changed form, hid as a crow, before the dwarves could finish me. Believing me to be a mere bird, Skavi found me. Took me in. Saw that I was healed to full strength.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Never knowing your true nature?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Kraka
en: I doubt he'd welcome the news. No matter... The treasure on this rock, I must retrieve it for my master. I owe him my life. Would you aid me? I cannot offer anything in return, but Skavi, I'm sure he could.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: I promise nothing.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Kraka
en: Understood. But if you find it...

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Saved you the bother. I already have it.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Kraka
en: All I ask is you give it to Skavi. Please.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: You'll not give it to him yourself?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Kraka
en: I have burdened him enough. I'll not burden him with the knowledge that he helped his enemy. He deserves better than that.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Very well. Good luck to you, Kraka.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Kraka
en: And to you.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: This looks worthy of my attention...

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: Well...? Don't keep in suspense, Æsir.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Here. I have something for you.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: You... do? What is...? It cannot be. How did you−

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: As I said, I am full of surprises.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Indeed. And Kraka, my crow. Did you see him?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Aye, I found Kraka. He... has chosen his own path.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: You speak as though he told you himself... What? Out with it.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Kraka... is a Jotun. He sought to bring you this treasure, as thanks for saving his life.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: A Jotun? A... shapeshifter. He understood my every word. The things I confided...

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: He said he burdened you enough.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: Well that wasn't his choice to make! He... he should have... (sigh)

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: I found Kraka. He... he helped me find the treasure. But he has chosen his own path. Flew south, unharmed.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: I see. Well, safe travels, friend... (sigh)

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: No, I didn't see your crow. All I saw were Muspels and a Jotun they'd captured.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: I thought Muspels and Jotnar were allies. Well, they can all rot for all I care. Especially if they dared lay a hand on my Kraka. (sigh)

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: That bracer of yours. That's how you got up there?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: What of it?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: I can enhance it, should you wish, as thanks.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Enhance it how?

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Skavi
en: Meet me at my forge and I'll show you how. Of course, same could be said of any smith worth his or her salt. And these rocks in the sky? If you find any more treasures on them, bring 'em to me and I'll see what I can do.

scene: The Ballad of Kraka and Skavi
speaker: Havi
en: Very well. I'll meet you at the shelter.

speaker: Eivor
en: That sound? Almost human, but... Gods!

speaker: Grieving Man
en: Your skin was pale as midnight mist. Hair threaded with dew. Eyes glassy, limpid, accusing. Still so beautiful, so pure.

speaker: Grieving Man
en: Please, my love, you must forgive me. I cannot sleep, I cannot eat.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who do you speak to? There is no one here.
