speaker: Grieving Man
en: We are together now, wife. You will never leave my side. Whispering in my ear like a moth's wings.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is that wailing coming from? It is as if the walls are crying in anguish. This man is haunted by some terrible deed.

speaker: Grieving Man
en: You! You blew upon the threads and they severed. She is gone, dust and bones, dust and bones.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have done some mischief here. I can smell the guilt with the rotting flesh.

speaker: Grieving Man
en: No, no! What have you done? Her sobs, her screams. I can no longer hear her call to me!

speaker: Eivor
en: He murdered his love? Little wonder he is crazed with guilt.

speaker: Havi
en: He finished the tower. Have we been outplayed?

speaker: The Builder
en: Like what you see? Quite the tower, hm?

speaker: The Builder
en: Not my best work, but it has a certain glow. Now then, where's my queen?

speaker: Havi
en: You're finished? The tower is functional?

speaker: The Builder
en: One rune remains, which I shall inscribe after I am wed.

speaker: Havi
en: Who helped you complete the work, Builder? You could not have managed so quickly on your own.

speaker: The Builder
en: Our agreement said nothing about outside help. Now, where is Freyja? I tire of waiting.

speaker: Havi
en: Outside help? Interesting choice of words.

speaker: Týr
en: Hail, Havi! Hail, Builder!

speaker: Thor
en: We bring you your bride?

speaker: The Builder
en: Freyja! My beloved!

speaker: The Builder
en: Why does she leer so wickedly?

speaker: Havi
en: Freyja is so excited that she has refused food or drink until the marriage is consummated.

speaker: The Builder
en: I am pleased, but somewhat surprised since this unwilling union was thrust upon her sight unseen.

speaker: Havi
en: Once she saw this tower—a testament to your strength—she knew you to be a great man indeed!

speaker: Havi
en: She starved, Builder. Hungry for you. Eager to consume you like a moist and dainty morsel!

speaker: The Builder
en: Splendid! She'll be please to know, I have an appetite to match her own! Our union will be a feast of the senses!

speaker: Havi
en: She agreed to marry you for the sake of Asgard, but she is not warmed by the idea. In fact, you revolt her utterly.

speaker: The Builder
en: If she hopes to dissuade me from this union, she'll be quite disappointed. I am committed to seeing this through.

speaker: Týr
en: Enough chatter! We have upheld our end of the bargain. Will you finish your work?

speaker: The Builder
en: I'm sorry, but... I've never seen such wild eyes. Why does she look so feral?

speaker: Havi
en: Since hearing of your offer, she hasn't closed her eyes. She fears what she might miss in the abyss of comforting sleep.

speaker: The Builder
en: This is no dream, my love! It is all quite real! Speak and tell me you agree!

speaker: Havi
en: Asleep or awake, her eyes swim with naught but the image of you. She is blind to all else.

speaker: The Builder
en: Blinded by love or disgust? I do not grasp your meaning.

speaker: Havi
en: She was shocked into a waking sleep at the news of her betrothal. She prefers this dreamlike state to the ugly reality.

speaker: The Builder
en: It will be a rude awakening if she does not come around willingly! I will not use her gently.

speaker: Thor
en: Quit stalling and kiss her, dung-mead! Consummate your betrothal!

speaker: The Builder
en: Yes, a kiss! A brief taste to whet my appetite!

speaker: The Builder
en: Delicious! Your lips are two pillows on a bed of reinrose petals!

speaker: Loki-as-Freyja
en: And yours are cold and rough as unpolished stone.

speaker: The Builder
en: What trickery is this?

speaker: Havi
en: Is something wrong?

speaker: The Builder
en: Her voice! It's hideous.

speaker: Loki-as-Freyja
en: I've been told it has a seductive quality.

speaker: Thor
en: By a wolf.

speaker: The Builder
en: Treachery! Bring me the real Freyja or my offer is withdrawn!

speaker: Freyja
en: I'll bring myself if you don't mind.

speaker: Týr
en: Freyja, you don't need to

speaker: Freyja
en: You have next to nothing, Æsir! Only this useless monument to your ineptitude.

speaker: Thor
en: Ah

speaker: Freyja
en: You've been a good boy, Thor. Don't gamble your winnings.

speaker: Freyja
en: And you, Havi...

speaker: Freyja
en: You tried to avoid responsibility by not making a choice, but that was a choice in itself. And look where it has brought us!

speaker: Havi
en: We have taken you for granted, it's true. That ends now.

speaker: Havi
en: No one has done more for Asgard than me. Did I not carve this land from Ymir's steaming flesh and bones?

speaker: Havi
en: You are no one's prize just yet. If this scheme turns sour, I will fight for you 'til my sinews snap and my bones break.

speaker: The Builder
en: Has this sad spectacle been for my sake alone? I've seen better drama on the festering carcass of a dead pig.

speaker: Havi
en: Finish your work. Or suffer.

speaker: The Builder
en: No Freyja, no shield.

speaker: Loki-as-Freyja
en: To Helheim with him, Havi! I know where he keeps his enchanted paint.

speaker: Havi
en: Show me.

speaker: Havi
en: Thor, Týr, watch our guest closely. Freyja... I hope we will have words when this is done.

speaker: Havi
en: Why do you still wear Freyja's form?

speaker: Loki-as-Freyja
en: A reminder of who's at stake.

speaker: Havi
en: Change back, this is disturbing.

speaker: Havi
en: Where do we go now?

speaker: Loki
en: I don't know. I didn't say I was watching him every moment.

speaker: Havi
en: So, you do not know where he kept his supplies?

speaker: Loki
en: They must be nearby! He never left this area! Mostly never!

speaker: Havi
en: Footprints.

speaker: Loki
en: Large footprints.

speaker: Havi
en: We have found the worm's lair.

speaker: Loki
en: Are those the Builder's pets? He has strange tastes.

speaker: Havi
en: Ignore them. Find the paint.

speaker: Havi
en: Not what we need. Useless. Nothing here.

speaker: Havi
en: Those runes. I know them. The Builder's supplies must be hidden behind this door. Loki, give me a hand.

speaker: Loki
en: Coming.

speaker: Loki
en: Wait!

speaker: Loki
en: Shapeshifters!

speaker: Havi
en: More deception! The Builder will suffer for this.

speaker: Loki
en: Now, let's smash that door.

speaker: Loki
en: Shapeshifters!

speaker: Havi
en: More deception! The Builder will suffer for this.

speaker: Loki
en: Where there's guards, there's goods. There's a door further in. Help me smash it.

speaker: Havi
en: Hold, Loki. We need to talk.

speaker: Loki
en: What is it, Havi?

speaker: Havi
en: Loki... did you know this Builder before we met him at Heimdall's tower?

speaker: Loki
en: Did I... know him? As in friends? Or know of him?

speaker: Havi
en: Did you invite him here?

speaker: Loki
en: I... I did, yes. He rescued my son from Jotunheim, so I agreed to bring him here, and help him find work. That's all.

speaker: Havi
en: Make this right, Loki. Or the blood-oath that binds me is forfeit. For you and your son, is that clear?

speaker: Loki
en: As a cloudless sky, High One.

speaker: Havi
en: More deer.

speaker: Loki
en: Go ahead. I'll watch your back.

speaker: Havi
en: That's cold comfort.

speaker: Havi
en: A quiet crossing might be best.

speaker: Havi
en: Ymir's blood. Loki! Slay these shape-shifters!

speaker: Havi
en: Is that all of them?

speaker: Loki
en: I hope so. Let's get the paint and go.

speaker: Havi
en: I have the paint.

speaker: Loki
en: Then let us fade like shadows in the light.

speaker: Loki
en: We got lucky.

speaker: Havi
en: Let us take what we need and go! We've no time to tarry.

speaker: Loki
en: It appears we've underestimated him.

speaker: Havi
en: On your advice. Find some way to hinder his efforts or I'll offer you as his prize.

speaker: Loki
en: I live to serve, Raven-Feeder.

speaker: Týr
en: Our Havi returns.

speaker: Thor
en: Stay right there, Builder. We're not finished with you.

speaker: The Builder
en: You survived my trap. How disappointing.

speaker: Havi
en: Invaders from Jotunheim. We slaughtered them all.

speaker: Thor
en: Buri's ballsack! Can I kill him now?

speaker: Havi
en: We do not need this honor-cheat. We will complete the tower ourselves.

speaker: The Builder
en: My hugr makes it work. I am bound to it through the magic of your realm.

speaker: Havi
en: You perverted our sacred waters. We have every reason to kill you.

speaker: The Builder
en: Well reasoned. They should call you the God of Hindsight. All-knowing after the fact.

speaker: Havi
en: I will finish the inscription. Builder, you stay with me. You others, go.

speaker: Freyja
en: "Elhaz." For protection.

speaker: The Builder
en: You gutless worm. Slayer of my kin. Oath-breaker, spirit-taker! I didn't build this tower to keep your enemies out. I built it to keep you in!

speaker: The Builder
en: You thought you could slay my people without punishment or price! You and your slab-headed son!

speaker: Havi
en: Their lives were the price of their arrogance.

speaker: Havi
en: His head is exposed. How do I reach it?

speaker: Havi
en: I could get a better shot at his head from above.

speaker: Havi
en: Dammit. Missed!

speaker: The Builder
en: You shaped the nine worlds, but you do not control them.

speaker: Havi
en: Control them? I only wish to survive them.

speaker: The Builder
en: Your bones will form the cornerstone of a new world ruled by Jotnar!

speaker: Havi
en: Your time has passed. There is no turning back the seasons.

speaker: The Builder
en: If our doom is assured, I will ensure that you share it.

speaker: Havi
en: Almost...

speaker: Freyja
en: Is the Jotun dead?

speaker: Havi
en: And his magic dies with him. Does that worry you, Trickster?

speaker: Loki
en: What are you implying?

speaker: Freyja
en: Were you behind this, you dishonorable Truth-Tangler!

speaker: Loki
en: What do you know of honor, Freyja? You've bedded more men than all the halls in Midgard.

speaker: Týr
en: You're a fine one to talk of sexual appetites. You fathered a wolf cub!

speaker: Loki
en: I'll not hear a lecture from the Lord of Petty Rules, who stiffens at the thought of laying down the law! And before you threaten to brandish your hammer, Thor, remember... without it, you'd be no better than a troll, only twice as stupid.

speaker: Havi
en: You festering ballsack, swollen with the foulest drippings of Ymir's corpse. No oath is worth this abuse!

speaker: Loki
en: But you won't break it, Havi. You cannot. All your efforts to evade destiny will only fling you further along its course. If you're not careful, you may be the author of your own destruction.

speaker: Havi
en: Leave him. He will do little harm while his son remains captive.

speaker: Thor
en: A mouthful of iron would put a stop to his babbling.

speaker: Freyja
en: What now, Wise One? We have returned to the place from which we set out. Ragnarök is coming, and we are no safer.

speaker: Havi
en: There may be a solution in Jotunheim. Hugr magic, they call it. I will travel there to see it for myself.

speaker: Havi
en: Until I have the final binding, Loki's son must not leave that island. In time, it shall serve as a sanctuary for all wolves.

speaker: Týr
en: I will watch over him as one of my own kin.

speaker: Havi
en: Then I leave the realm in your capable hands, my queen. If my own are empty when I return, I will accept destiny with both.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: Who is the most gorgeous girl? You are, yes you are. Snuffling through the leaves, making daddy a fortune! Good girl, Lady Trotters, good girl.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: Nice pig.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: Pig? You ignoramus. Lady Trotters is a hog. And the most unique and singular beauty.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: Shall I leave you two alone?

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: Please do, and not for the reasons you are insinuating. You are confusing her delicate nose with your earthy stench.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: Some like my smell. So she's a mushroom hog? I have heard of such rare beasts.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: Mushrooms? She sniffs out treasure.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: Treasure?

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: Epping Forest is full of it. And Lady Trotters finds it. Ah, she has the scent! Come, I'll show you.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: There you go, my lovely. Find us riches and you shall have sweet red berries for supper!

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: More rancid socks. Bandits leave them lying around and Lady is drawn to their unholy stench! A lost cause. I'm going for a nap. If Lady runs off, follow her, would you? What she finds we'll share. The socks are all yours.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: Run, Lady. Find me something heavy and rich!

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: Yes! A fine hoard. Good Lady Trotters, you are the best of hogs! Go, Lady Trotters, run like Fenrir is on your heels!

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: You are a beast to rival Gullinbursti, Freyja's beloved golden boar! Did the dwarves make you, too? What I wouldn't do for a beast as clever as you!

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier (female)
en: Get that boar, its nose is golden!

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: You will not harm a bristle on the beautiful boar's back!

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier (female)
en: Give us that boar!

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: I'll protect you, Lady.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier (female)
en: I'm taking the beast over your dead body. No one kills the beast, it's worth more than all your lives put together!

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: There, good girl. The nasty, smelly thugs won't bother you anymore.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: Wake up, Lady Trotters found treasure!

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: Did she, now? Well, you must have the knack. She does not take to strangers kindly. Do you, girl?

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: Bandits attacked us, but I took care of them.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: Bandits? If you hadn't been there, I dread to think. Please, keep all the treasure. Your payment for my sweet girl's life.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: That is an incredible animal you have there.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: Isn't she? Bramble-sharp and gentle as a kitten. Earns her keep and more besides.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: I wish I had as good a companion as Lady Trotters. One of my gods, Freyja, had a boar. It is said that the gloom of the Murky Regions was lighted, such was the glow from its mane. But Lady outshines him.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Boarmaster
en: Aye, she does. I will never find another friend like her. Well, goodbye. Fare safe on your travels.

scene: The Boar with the Golden Nose
speaker: Eivor
en: And you. Happy hunting, Lady!

speaker: Ascila
en: Look! His tongue's been torn out. Haha.

speaker: Tristan
en: Stop it, Ascila! His ghost will haunt us!

speaker: Ascila
en: There is no ghost. Danes don't have souls!

speaker: Eivor
en: This man is a Norse warrior, and his body deserves respect! Where is his axe? He cannot go to Valhalla without it.

speaker: Ascila
en: Hurrey ran off with it. Don't hurt us! We didn't mean anything! Please.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not harm you. I just want to get this man's axe returned. Where has this boy gone?

speaker: Ascila
en: Over that way. He was playing with it. Slaying monsters.

speaker: Eivor
en: You there, boy. Give me the axe before you hurt yourself.

speaker: Hurrey
en: I am no mere boy. I am Hurrey, slayer of monsters. You'll have to win it from me in single combat.

speaker: Eivor
en: A monster slayer? Well, as a fellow warrior, I must trade for the axe in a warrior's charm. Thick arms of Aegir and thighs of Thor. Strength, honesty, and wit crave all wise warriors!

speaker: Hurrey
en: I can feel this Norse magic running from my fingers to my toes. I bet I can beat you in a race back to that body!

speaker: Eivor
en: With a warrior of your might, clearly it must be a battle to the death. If you fell me, tell my brother I love him.

speaker: Hurrey
en: Wait! No! I'll give it back, just... just no battle to the death!

speaker: Eivor
en: You show me mercy, Monster Slayer. Go, I'll race you back to the fallen warrior.

speaker: Ascila
en: Look, there's a spider crawling around his eye! I think it's eating it.

speaker: Tristan
en: Eew! Careful, that Dane's back with Hurrey.

speaker: Hurrey
en: We have returned to give this dead warrior his axe back because... because why?

speaker: Eivor
en: A vikingr must have his axe to gain entrance to Valhalla. Home of our gods and eternal glory. It is a warrior's final home.

speaker: Eivor
en: Though we know not your name or your clan, you are a warrior of good stock. Odin welcomes you to his table in Valhalla.

speaker: Hurrey
en: Amen. And one day, us warriors will join you, fighting monsters in eternal battle.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: I have returned.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar. It's good to see a face I trust, even your frightful mug. I thought this could be our shared saga, but it's time to leave, and we spent time naught but a drink together.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Gunnar
en: Worry not, Eivor. You and I have many tales to tell yet. And our names ring out clear and with honor.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: Ja, a tale. A tale of Glowecestre. Beautiful land, full of damned fools.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Gunnar
en: Ha! I will drink to that. You have my thanks.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: Anything for you, old friend.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Gunnar
en: Then let us say our farewells to this Wicker King, and then be on our way home.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, Randvi will be eager to meet Brigid.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: Brigid and Gunnar have already gone ahead. I should join them.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: You owe me your prophecy, witch.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Modron
en: And I shall give it. You are a great warrior, conqueror of this land, and that of your birth. But, at the end of all things, you will find yourself with nothing but your regrets.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: I... I see.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: Tell me please. What of Modron?

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: Dead and burned on a pyre much like this one.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: I didn't think... I hoped you would spare her at least.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: We first met at Simkin's wicker man ascension. I was besotted with you at a glance.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Modron
en: So long ago... Some poetic symmetry after twenty years of prosperity.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: Gwen.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Gwenydd
en: Please don't do it. We can burn something else. Someone else.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: Peace, dearheart, I will join the dirt that grows the trees and the barley. My body feeding the gods, worms, and even you. So, I will be here. And, a long, long time from now, when you're old and wrinkled like an apple... you will see me again.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Gwenydd
en: Father, I thought I could be ready.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: It is time.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: Then this is yours.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: This is your path, Tewdwr. No thorns and briars could keep you from it.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: And you, Eivor, friend of Glowecestrescire. You have lived up to your reputation.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: I know you owe me less than nothing, but please, take care of them.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: I take no pleasure in the suffering of others. You would know this if you had given me a chance.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: Twenty years I have been your ealdorman. Now these old bones are ready for my last duty. I have worked alongside you. Clearing fields, brewing drink, births, and deaths. All, growing and learning.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Halewyn
en: The wicker man is ready, O King. Your altar awaits.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: I am honored to be your Harvest King. With this flame set, may our crops be plentiful and our winters brief!

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: Despite it all, he has the ending he prayed for.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: Straight to the mouths of hungry gods.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: Eivor, the honor is yours.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Praise the Harvest King!

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Bloody pagans.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Why does Cynon have to go?

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: He's saving us all, love.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Dear God, preserve Cynon's soul.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Thank you for your life, O King.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Gods, please bless our fields with this sacrifice.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Cynon
en: Our Father, who art in Heaven. Our Mother, who art in Earth. Please—Please accept this offering. Take of me my flesh and bone and bless... bless... (screaming)

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: The burning of the Harvest King. It is a momentous occasion for many here. Like the Christ, he sacrifices himself for his people. So that they may prosper.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: But this is an empty platter for your gods. Hungry bellies are known to retaliate.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: None can take Cynon's place. And to put his corpse in the pyre would be an insult. Christ turns his eyes from this ritual.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: But you condone it?

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: I am to be Tewdwr of a united land. I can no longer turn my eye from anything.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: Tradition dictates the burning be overseen by the high priestess. Modron is missed here.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: My hand has hindered this blot (ceremony) twice then.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Gwenydd
en: Then I will oversee, as is my right, my blood.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: I took Modron from you. You have every right to feud with my line. Once you're old enough to hold a sword.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Gwenydd
en: Mother saw your fate. The future will punish you greater than I ever could.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: Punishment or not, you will go into the future as Glowecestrescire's ally.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Modron
en: Ealdorman Tewdwr.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: Mother Modron.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: So you two will form an accord? Heathens and Christ-kin in an uneasy truce?

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: The pagans of Glowecestre are my people, just as the children of Christ are.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: And our alliance?

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: Strong as iron.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: And someone I will never forget.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Halewyn
en: Let the flame be set. May the crop be abundant!

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Tewdwr
en: Eivor, the honor is yours.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Praise the Harvest King!

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Bloody pagans.

scene: The Burning of the Wicker Man
speaker: Eivor
en: Now, it seems the wind calls me back to Randvi. Best tell her the good news.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: By the gods of Asgard! What happened to this place?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: What's happened here?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Alwin
en: Eivor's here, thank the gods above! Though it seems they have forsaken us. I am sorry to tell you, Eivor ... Tekla is gone.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: What? Dead?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Alwin
en: No, no, no. She's on an errand and left her apprentice in charge. It was him who did all this.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: Who is this apprentice?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Alwin
en: A fellow called Ake. He'll know what happened here. You need to find him!

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: Me? Why not you?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Alwin
en: Somebody's got to clean up this mess! Besides, I'm startlingly drunk. You go on!

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Alwin
en: My cup has run dry! How is anyone meant to survive without something to drink? I need to drown my sorrows!

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: That must be Ake. It would seem drunks are not the best trackers.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: Those Saxon scum cannot get away with this. They will fear my very name. And Tekla will see that I am worthy of her faith. There they are! Down there. But where are the barrels?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: You. Are you Ake?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: Who's asking?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: Do you not know me? I am Teklas's friend, Eivor. I want to know why you left her brewery in shambles.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: Take that back! I'd never do such a thing. It was those Saxon bandits! And I'm gonna slay every last one of 'em.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: Bandits? In Ravensthorpe?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: It seemed nice enough. I invited 'em to try Tekla's new brew. We get drinking and the next thing I wake up and the barrels are gone! Now that you are here, we can solve this together. With our fists!

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: You got bandits drunk, they behaved as bandits do, and now you seek violence? Ake, you're not in a state to solve problems.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: O no? Well, how about I show you the kind of state I'm in? You'll see how a brewer fights!

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: Lower your fists. We can go back to the brewery until you sober up.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: Enough talk! Have at me!

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: I have no quarrel with you, Ake.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: Looks like you do!

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: Get out of my way! I've got to find the bandits!

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: No fair! I wasn't ready.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: Ake, go back to the brewery.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: I traveled across the sea to study under a master brewer. Tekla entrusted me with her finest ale ... and I lost it! If you knew what it was like, to fear losing the faith of the one you admire, you would not be so callous.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: I will make you a deal. We will go get the barrels back. But I will do it. You wait at the boat. No more fighting.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: Very well. It must be with the bandits. Call if you need help. Between you and me, your left jab could use a little work.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: All right. Where have they hidden the ale?

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: This is Tekla's ale. I would know those barrels anywhere. She truly is a master.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: Now to get this back to Ake's boat.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: Tekla's ale is safe.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: Thank you, Eivor. You are a hero among heroes. My final request would only be that we keep this matter between us.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Eivor
en: That I can do.

scene: The Case of the Missing Ale
speaker: Ake
en: I got a few of these Yule Tokens from Norvid. Happy to spare them, as payment for your kindness. Perhaps you can spend them on some fighting lessons.

speaker: Havi
en: Listen close, and I will tell you the of how I crushed Angrboda's champions. After that, I came face to face with a Jotun of extraordinary size! Barely had they fallen than I was seen by a Jotun patrol, and battle was joined once more! Forward I went, knowing great glory would be mine when I laid low my next opponent. My foes were mighty indeed, but of course... I prevailed!

speaker: Eivor
en: What has happened?

speaker: Sichfrith
en: They have summoned Flann. I hope he shows soon, if only to end this bickering.

speaker: Flann
en: Speak.

speaker: King Cerball
en: Lord, there has been much deliberation these last few days. News of Eogan spread like a mountain fire.

speaker: King Conchobar
en: The people are frightened. We are unsettled, to say the least. A trusted unveiled as a pagan conspirator.

speaker: King Cerball
en: The druids have permeated the Church at the highest level. There is no telling how far down it goes.

speaker: King Conchobar
en: Something must be done. We must rid them of this land. Begin an inquisition.

speaker: Ciara
en: How dare you speak like this? Eogan acted alone.

speaker: King Cerball
en: He belonged to a sect. There are others like him. Do you deny it?

speaker: Ciara
en: I do not deny it. But then you will speak only of the Children of Danu.

speaker: King Cerball
en: A weed that grew from druid roots. If we allow it to thrive, how can we ever be certain this will not happen again?

speaker: Ciara
en: Flann, I do not like what these men are implying. Do not entertain this.

speaker: King Conchobar
en: You would presume to tell your king what to do? You, who share those druid roots? You even know the sect by name. Perhaps, like Eogan, there is more to you than meets the eye.

speaker: Ciara
en: Bastard!

speaker: Flann
en: Enough! Speak to her like that again and rats will sup on you, alive.

speaker: King Conchobar
en: Apologies, my king. Poetess. I do not mean to cast suspicion, only to draw a very real comparison. We do not know where the next threat will come. And we cannot simply hope that it will not come. We must put aside our differences and come together as Christians if we wish to preserve an Ireland under God.

speaker: Ciara
en: Flann, if you do this

speaker: Flann
en: I know well where you stand, Ciara. Are there any others who wish to speak?

speaker: Sichfrith
en: I will. This gathering has shown something very clear, that there is solidarity in this cause. If we do nothing, the weeds will continue to sprout, leading to unrest across the kingdoms. But if we act, begin an inquistion, it will lead to unity this land has sorely lacked.

speaker: Ciara
en: These are my people, Sichfrith!

speaker: Sichfrith
en: And there are those within who threaten the very fabric of this land. Can you really stand there and defend them?

speaker: Flann
en: Anyone else?

speaker: Eivor
en: Such an inquisition will require many resources. It will be a burden on each and every kingdom. But in time, it is reasonable to think it will lead to the outcome you seek. Just know what you're doing to secure it.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is being proposed is a bold strategy. The consequence of which cannot be properly weighed just now.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must allow time to reflect, lord.

speaker: King Conchobar
en: Every moment we waste weakens our position.

speaker: King Conchobar
en: Lord, we kings are all in agreement. There is but one move to make.

speaker: Flann
en: We will launch an inquisition. Every druid will face a choice. Reform or exile. The future of Ireland is a wholly Christian one.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where did Ciara go?

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: Set off for her house, just down that road. Looked mighty upset.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ciara is not of sound mind. I need to settle her down.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ciara.

speaker: Ciara
en: Get out! Leave me be.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this? What are you doing?

speaker: Ciara
en: Flann, the spineless fool. What was he thinking?

speaker: Eivor
en: He saw an opportunity to unite the kingdoms. He seized it. It is what any king would do.

speaker: Ciara
en: Do not defend him!

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not, but consider what would happen if he ignored these allied kings. You are right to be upset. But you know Flann best. This was not a decision he made lightly. Let us go back and talk with him. If anyone can convince him to reconsider, it's you.

speaker: Ciara
en: O, I will. Whether he wants to or not.

speaker: Eivor
en: What?

speaker: Ciara
en: I am sorry, Eivor! I cannot let them erase us.

speaker: Flann
en: Eivor! Can you hear me? Eivor!

speaker: Flann
en: Are you all right?

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you see Ciara?

speaker: Flann
en: I expected her here. Eivor?

speaker: Flann
en: What is that? Do you think it is Ciara?

speaker: Eivor
en: It must be. I do not know what she's trying to do, but she's angry.

speaker: Flann
en: This is my fault. I must speak with her.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be too late for that. She said she would not let you erase the druids.

speaker: Flann
en: But what means will she use?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Lia Fáil. I think she'll try to use it to stop you.

speaker: Flann
en: A stone.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is an ancient part of her lineage. There may be more to it than myths and legends.

speaker: Flann
en: I knew my decision would upset her. But I was certain she could find a way to understanding.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was no simple decision. By choosing one, you betray the other. Choices that weigh heavily require ample time to reflect if you are to find the best outcome.

speaker: Flann
en: I acted rashly. I listened to frightened men, Eivor. Men whose loyalty I hungered for.

speaker: Eivor
en: Clear your head, lord. We are nearly there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ciara!

speaker: Ciara
en: Leave. Leave now.

speaker: Flann
en: Ciara.

speaker: Ciara
en: You want to rid the world of us? I'll rid it of you.

speaker: Flann
en: Where is she? Ar Día... (By God...)

speaker: Eivor
en: Your sword, Flann. Stay close to me.

speaker: Flann
en: Eivor! What do we do?

speaker: Eivor
en: Fight!

speaker: Flann
en: These are my men!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's them, or you. Now fight!

speaker: Flann
en: Back! Get back!

speaker: Eivor
en: They will not listen. Ciara has taken their reason somehow. Defend yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot let you walk this path.

speaker: Ciara
en: You would stand in my way? I thought you of all people would understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do. This is too far.

speaker: Flann
en: Listen to her, Ciara. There can be peace between us.

speaker: Ciara
en: Just another lie.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep your guard up.

speaker: Flann
en: Ciara! Where are you? Ciara!

speaker: Eivor
en: Flann

speaker: Ciara
en: I will raise the stakes. How about the king's blood on your hands?

speaker: Flann
en: Eivor! Agh!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is not a force you can control, Ciara. It will consume you.

speaker: Ciara
en: So be it!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's enough, Ciara. Surrender now.

speaker: Ciara
en: Nothing but a ruthless raider! Hollow inside. You speak of honor. Where is yours?

speaker: Eivor
en: You know.

speaker: Ciara
en: With Bárid? His son? Another pawn in this endless war.

speaker: Eivor
en: He is my blood.

speaker: Ciara
en: Ah yes, and you will throw away all reason to defend what you are sworn to. I am no different. My people will live to see tomorrow if it means I have to kill you today.

speaker: Ciara
en: You are unrelenting!

speaker: Eivor
en: Battle hardened over many victories. Do not make me add another.

speaker: Ciara
en: Do as you must. As will I.

speaker: Ciara
en: Have you not had enough?

speaker: Eivor
en: I bathe in battle lust. Now stop, Ciara. Before it's too late.

speaker: Ciara
en: I will die before I let them trample us!

speaker: Ciara
en: I told you I would never see the druids into darkness. Why pretend to be my ally?

speaker: Eivor
en: I pretended nothing. I thought... I hoped you could be better. Better than Eogan.

speaker: Ciara
en: Don't compare me to that demon!

speaker: Eivor
en: No? Look around you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You set in motion what the Children of Danu hoped you could. You became the vessel for their plot.

speaker: Ciara
en: I always have been...

speaker: Ciara
en: After Mother died, I became the last. The last who could awaken the Lia Fáil. Never did I think I would use this gift so foolishly.

speaker: Eivor
en: What now?

speaker: Ciara
en: It ends. Eogan, the Children of Danu, they only exist in pursuit of the stone's power. And I am the key to unleashing it. You must kill me. Kill me, Eivor. If I die, Tara's power dies with me and there will be nothing left to lead my people astray. The old ways will return. Let me do this. Let me save them. Please.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is a sacrifice that would honor your gods. I will make it swift.

speaker: Ciara
en: Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Prepare yourself.

speaker: Flann
en: No!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's what she wanted, Flann. The Lia Fáil can never again be used for harm. She did not die for nothing.

speaker: Flann
en: I will make damn sure of that.

speaker: Flann
en: Agh!

speaker: Flann
en: Ciara, I'm so sorry...

speaker: Eivor
en: You may be the key to this power, but the stone is the source. Destroy it.

speaker: Ciara
en: You know I cannot.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your ancestors are souls in another realm. They will not despair of this stone's loss. Sometimes we must sacrifice what we treasure most to protect the ones we love.

speaker: Ciara
en: Bury the past, build the future...

speaker: Ciara
en: Until we meet again. Slàn go fóill. (Farewell for now.)

speaker: Flann
en: Ciara.

speaker: Flann
en: I bow my head in contrition. I failed you. I failed you and the true druids of Ireland. For that I truly apologize. I will speak to the kings and undo my rash decision. The land you have wished for is secure.

speaker: Ciara
en: I hope it is so, Flann. Farewell. Farewell, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where will you go?

speaker: Eivor
en: How are you feeling?

speaker: Flann
en: Bruised. Battered. But I'll live. Though it'll take some time to reclaim my pride.

speaker: Eivor
en: Took a lot not to kill you.

speaker: Flann
en: If you wanted to, that was your chance. I suppose at the end of all this, it's safe to call you a friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: See to it that Sichfrith's reign is long, and you shall never know me as your enemy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you met with the other kings? I take it that is why you have come.

speaker: Flann
en: I have. The inquisition is buried. High King is a leader to all who share in his land. You helped me see that. My only regret is not having understood it sooner.

speaker: Eivor
en: You work to secure a future for all. Ciara would be pleased with this outcome.

speaker: Flann
en: I know there is much that awaits for you in England, Eivor, but you can set your boots in Ireland anytime you please.

speaker: Eivor
en: Farewell, Flann. Until we meet again.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: What do you think my father would think of all this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid wanted to ensure the Dublin he left you could stand upright on its own two legs. And while he could not see it through, he would be proud you did.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: I will never forget what you did for my family.

speaker: Eivor
en: Our family, Sichfrith.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep well. And may your father's hugr be with you always. It shall with me.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Psst, Eivor! Over here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Smuggler. I last saw you in the tunnels.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: That was before your army started the burning and pillaging.

speaker: Eivor
en: This slaughter is not my doing. I mean to end this.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: You have not won yet. Charles is marching towards Paris with his .

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods. His army comes?

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Word is that they are close and riding hard.

speaker: Eivor
en: All the more reason I must hurry and end this thing. I need a hidden way into Odo's palace.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: I know a way but there is a band of Frankish warriors milling about...

speaker: Eivor
en: Show me. Upon my honor, I give you my word that Toka and I... we do not want this.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Fine. I will lead the way.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Those guards are too close to the tunnel!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will chase them off.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: We will die if we don't get into Odo's palais somehow.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: There is a tunnel around here. Keep searching, men.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: Hurry now, Eivor. Down into the dark we go.

speaker: Eivor
en: A fine haul of Norse war gear and Frankish riches. Looks like Nolwenn smuggled for both sides.

speaker: Nolwenn
en: That tunnel takes you into the palais.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Nolwenn. And you?

speaker: Nolwenn
en: I will save what I can of my trade goods and leave through other tunnels. Godspeed, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: A safe journey for you, too.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Those are the largest gates I've ever seen. We will never batter them down.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Sigfred is moving his catapults up. It will take time, but these walls will fall.

speaker: Eivor
en: The guard's key. It must unlock something nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: This will take me right over the palace walls. Perfect.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now to sneak inside Odo's palace.

speaker: French Man 1
en: You're sneaking into the palais for a tryst? How can you think upon animal lusts, today of all days?

speaker: Albrada
en: We may die today. Should I spend my last moments scrubbing floors or making love?

speaker: French Man 1
en: May God have mercy on your soul, Albrada, sneaking through the back door like that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Following that lovestruck maid should lead me into the palace.

speaker: Albrada
en: O, where is my beloved? What could delay him now of all times?

speaker: Eivor
en: These tunnels should lead right under the palace.

speaker: Albrada
en: Who are you and what are you doing? Have you escaped from your cell? Whatever you are doing, stop. Mon cher is coming and... and he'll lock you up!

speaker: Eivor
en: The jailer must have taken the key with him after reading that note.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Those fool workers fled, leaving windows open and scaffolding everywhere.

speaker: French Soldier 4
en: Can't blame them. I should be home, minding my goats.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now that I'm inside the palace, I need to find someone to point me towards Odo.

speaker: Eivor
en: Pardon me, good sirs. Where may I find Count Odo?

speaker: French Man 2
en: Count Odo? Who cares about Count Odo? Where is our good friend, Walter du Sens?

speaker: Eivor
en: Why? Who is Walter du Sens, a great warrior?

speaker: French Man 2
en: Walter, a warrior? No, he is Count Odo's family priest. He's begging Odo to give us more wine. We plan to be passed out drunk by the time the Northmen bust into here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odo's priest might lead me to Odo, but I need to sneak past these guards to the servants' wing.

speaker: French Soldier 5
en: Listen, I am the chief jailer, so if I say hurry up and board those walls, you hurry up and board those walls.

speaker: Eivor
en: This key looks like it should open something important.

speaker: Eivor
en: Even more guards in the hallway, I must tread with care.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odo's bedroom. If his wife is inside, she might know where he is.

speaker: Henriette
en: O my lady, why the count will not attend to you, I will never know. The mother of his children. To think it. So stubborn, that Odo. And that pathetic Walter du Sens! Too drunk to give last rites. A travesty, that one is.

speaker: Eivor
en: Pardon me, but is that food for Count Odo?

speaker: Henriette
en: No, this is for Lady Theodrate, his wife. She lies at death's door. And who are you in such garb?

speaker: Eivor
en: A healer, from . What happened to the lady?

speaker: Henriette
en: While helping wounded soldiers off the walls, she took an arrow in the belly. Persuade that worthless priest Walter to give her the last rites, if you can. He's just upstairs.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will see what I can do. Thank you.

speaker: Walter Du Sens
en: To die a drunken priest, disgraced before God. Unfit even to say last rites for the countess. And Count Odo, he was disgusted with me. If I were only a man, not a drunken beast! He will not talk to me. Say he is keeping watch for King Charles. No time for wine-drunk priests.

speaker: Eivor
en: Special wine, maybe for a high feast. Could come in handy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Pardon me, Father, where is Count Odo?

speaker: Walter du Sens
en: O-odo? His foolish pride will kill us all.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, but where is he?

speaker: Walter du Sens
en: Who are you again? I can tell you nothing without more wine. My memory has gone all hazy.

speaker: Eivor
en: A bottle of wine for that drunken priest. As if he needs another.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here is your wine. Now do you remember where is Count Odo?

speaker: Walter du Sens
en: Wine? Ah, sweet, precious wine? The water of life, the blood of Christ, the fiery of phlegm of the world?

speaker: Eivor
en: Red wine, nothing more. You may have it.

speaker: Walter du Sens
en: O, Heaven hears my prayer. Now I can die.

speaker: Eivor
en: Before you do, where is Count Odo?

speaker: Walter du Sens
en: Odo... I do not know, but his wife lies wounded in their master bedroom. She may have answers. On the second story, along the main hall. Here, take the key, I locked the door.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thanks.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should head to Odo's bedroom.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hello, key. Which door will you unlock for me?

speaker: Theodrate
en: Is that you, Odo, my love? No, you are too tall. Are you the priest? The light has grown dim, I see nothing but shapes. Father, will you hear my confession?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not the priest, my Lady-ness. Just a friend seeking Count Odo, nothing more. Do you know where he is?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sorry, ahem, your great Lady-ness, but I must speak to Count Odo. Where is he?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, yes, I am the priest, Your Lady-ness.

speaker: Theodrate
en: Forgive me, Father, for I have sinned. In my own pride, I went to battle without armor, thinking God would be my shield. And now I'm dying, and I will never see my sweet children again. Where are they, Father? Are they safe?

speaker: Eivor
en: They, ah, are safe with that good man, Walter du Sens. Do not fear.

speaker: Theodrate
en: Thank you. But Father, please. Will you carry a message from a dying woman to her beloved husband?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will, my dear. What I should I tell Count Odo?

speaker: Theodrate
en: That he is a good man. That he must live, for our children's sake. For Paris. For Francia. He must not... die for a mad king.

speaker: Eivor
en: I promise I will do this, good lady. Where may I find your husband?

speaker: Theodrate
en: Odo remains locked in his sanctum.

speaker: Eivor
en: His sanctum?

speaker: Theodrate
en: Up the landing and across the hall. My husband still hopes Charles will ride forth and save the city.

speaker: Eivor
en: Locked in, you said?

speaker: Theodrate
en: There is a key in the bureau... take it... help my husband, any way you can. Death creeps upon me now, slow and quiet, like a shadow at day's end. Eyelids so heavy... Mother... where are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Farewell, good lady.

speaker: Eivor
en: No point in going back there.

speaker: Walter du Sens
en: My lord Odo. The day is lost. Give the order to strike the banners and lay down our arms. Please.

speaker: Walter du Sens
en: What good are our deaths, milord? Your lady-wife lays dying. Go to her. Your duty, as a husband

speaker: Odo
en: My duty is here. When Charles and his army arrive, we will join the attack. We will crush the heathens between the hammer of Charles and the anvil of Paris.

speaker: Odo
en: Leave, Walter. Go comfort my wife as best as you can. God, it seems, has chosen a different fate for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: The priest is right. Lay down your arms. Save your city.

speaker: Odo
en: Among the Northmen, is not death in battle the best way to die? Come, share a glass of wine with a doomed man.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have heard many a warrior cry out for their mothers as their life's blood feeds the ground. I no longer can say if this is the best way to die.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your wife's wound is severe, an arrow to the gut. I saw her. I fear she won't last the night.

speaker: Odo
en: And I won't last the next quarter of an hour.

speaker: Eivor
en: She said to be strong for your children. Do not throw away your life for a mad king.

speaker: Eivor
en: Many have died today. Many more will die if we do not end this thing.

speaker: Odo
en: Look at these works at stained glass. Delicate, priceless. Evreux's artisans spend years crafting each piece.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wondrous works, I grant you that.

speaker: Odo
en: We brought them here for safekeeping. In the hopes that your invading horde won't smash them to pieces.

speaker: Odo
en: You tell me to surrender my city, abandon my honor? You tell me to live out my days as Sigfred's prisoner? What would you do?

speaker: Eivor
en: I would fight. And someday, I will die with steel in my hand. This I know, it is my doom. But today is not that day.

speaker: Odo
en: And if I put you on your back, bleeding out and crying for your mother?

speaker: Eivor
en: My mother is already dead.

speaker: Odo
en: Come, Northerner. Bleed for Paris.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not make me slay you.

speaker: Odo
en: Honor demands one of us die.

speaker: Odo
en: God, lend me your might.

speaker: Eivor
en: A fine blade for a fine warrior. You fought well, Count Odo. But not well enough.

speaker: Odo
en: Give me a quick death. Do not make a spectacle of my defeat.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those are not Sigfred's horns.

speaker: Odo
en: Charles and his army! He arrives in time to save the city.

speaker: Odo
en: They do not fight. I see a flag of truce.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigfred and Charles will hold parley. I must be there, my voice must be heard.

speaker: Odo
en: As should I. But I am your prisoner.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I release you on your honor and trust you to keep our truce.

speaker: Odo
en: Thank you, Eivor. I shall.

speaker: Charles
en: Lord Sigfred. I offer a gift of silver as a token of the love and friendship between us. Let us have peace.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Silver for a truce?

speaker: Charles
en: Not a truce, but a lasting bond. I name you my Lord of Rouen, and you bend the knee to your king.

speaker: Sigfred
en: I do not kneel to wooden gods, let alone living men. But no matter. Let me take counsel.

speaker: Toka
en: Eivor! Thank the gods, you live.

speaker: Eivor
en: As do you, good. I made it inside the palace. Odo would have surrendered the city, but...

speaker: Toka
en: But Charles showed up with his mighty flag of truce.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye. And you?

speaker: Toka
en: After we split up, I took my thegns and secured the bastard prince. He's nearby, safe.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Eivor! The gods do favor the brave. The lucky and the brave.

speaker: Eivor
en: So it is said. And Charles, he offers us a hoard of silver?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Indeed. And all we have to do is sail away.

speaker: Toka
en: He brings enough treasure to make every war-thegn here wealthy beyond dreams!

speaker: Eivor
en: For those who lived.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Gambling our lives for silver, that is our way. Now, do we take his offer?

speaker: Toka
en: By Loki's bloody balls, yes. And call him king if it makes the old troll happy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Treasure is what we want. Treasure and a truce. Take his offer.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have dealt with Charles more than you. He may stab us in the back.

speaker: Sigfred
en: He can try. And if he tries, I will take his silver and his throne.

speaker: Toka
en: Uncle, we came for wealth and peace for our clan. We can't take all of Francia. We are too few.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your battle, Sigfred, your choice. I'm here to forge my own truce with Charles.

speaker: Sigfred
en: You earned your share of the wealth, all the same.

speaker: Toka
en: Never fear, Eivor. Charles must put his kingdom back together. He cannot attack England after today.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Charles. We take your gift and in return, we give you peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigfred.

speaker: Charles
en: This man, Sigfred, swears to be my loyal friend and protect our lands in Amiens and Rouen...

speaker: Odo
en: Gozlin, Ebels, and my wife died defending Paris from these river pirates. And now you offer them the very silver we paid you to defend us. Are you mad? Wait. We know you are. Let me ask instead, are you a coward or a fool?

speaker: Charles
en: Sigfred swears to protect our land in the north

speaker: Odo
en: If you surrender my birthright, you are no king of mine!

speaker: Eivor
en: Count Odo! I bested you in battle and spared your life. Honor the terms of our truce.

speaker: Odo
en: This heathen knows more about honor than my king.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Today has been a good day, but I tire of long speeches. We will take our silver and go. You Franks may stay and pursue your own quarrels.

speaker: Charles
en: Wait. A final matter. Eivor of England. Bring forth my son, Prince Bernard.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am as good as my word. Toka, bring out the boy.

speaker: Bernard
en: King Father! Take me home!

speaker: Charles
en: There, there. Stand straight like the future King of Francia. God watches you.

speaker: Toka
en: I want mead and music. Silver and song. Dancing, and someone warm in my sheets. Come friends, let us feast.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot hand over the boy to one such as you. He is free to go where he wills.

speaker: Charles
en: You dare defy me?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Do you want battle, king? I will take your silver and your balls.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not wreck your truce over one small boy.

speaker: Charles
en: Bernard is not any boy, he is my only son and heir!

speaker: Sigfred
en: What, have you forgot how to make another?

speaker: Charles
en: This is not over, Eivor of England.

speaker: Sigfred
en: We have won a great victory and a great treasure. Come, we feast.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Tomorrow the Franks will bury their dead, thanking their God that they yet live. And they should, for Paris was merely kissed this time. Should we breach those walls again, we will bare our teeth and bite. And should Charles judge it wise to draw swords against us again, let him remember the glint of our axeblades. Let him remember the red mist on the air. The taste of iron...

speaker: Toka
en: Enjoy the feast, all! A purse full of silver to any who can drink more ale than I! Skal!

speaker: Eivor
en: I should return to Hildiran.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hildiran, I return.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Yes. Very good. Your skills are improving.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is a reason I'm doing this, yes?

speaker: Hildiran
en: Of course! All will be revealed once we manage to open Freyja's Gate.

speaker: Eivor
en: What lies beyond? You seem to know much about it.

speaker: Hildiran
en: I know much about many things, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Eivor
en: You dodge my questions like they are arrows.

speaker: Hildiran
en: You ask questions like you have a right to the answers. Keep training, Eivor. There is a reason to all of this. Patience.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am finally finished. These answers had better be worth the effort.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Eivor. You return.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have completed my training.

speaker: Hildiran
en: So you have. Walk with me.

speaker: Hildiran
en: I have been busy while you have been running around. The last of the rock has been cleared. Now you will see the full entryway.

speaker: Eivor
en: This was here the whole time? We built our settlement so close to it and had no idea.

speaker: Hildiran
en: There are no coincidences when the gods are involved. Everything happens as needed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot see how to open it.

speaker: Hildiran
en: That is because Freyja built it so that only someone with the strength and will of the All-Father himself could open it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, so that is why you put me through so many trials.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Exactly! Now, take this and hold it aloft.

speaker: Hildiran
en: There. That is what we have come for. Reach out and take the orb, Eivor.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Good. Now hand it to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does it do?

speaker: Hildiran
en: This is Odin's Eye. It will act as a compass for us to find the next location.

speaker: Eivor
en: Next location? This wasn't the treasure you needed?

speaker: Hildiran
en: I do need it! It will lead us to Odin's vault.

speaker: Eivor
en: I feel like I've been used.

speaker: Hildiran
en: Maybe you have. But you are stronger and now have access to my weapons and armor. Seems like it was worth it. Continue to train. Hugrheim will always be open to you. Visit me should you wish to see my collection again.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O! Me apple cart hath fallen! These apples must be eaten. They are too juicy to be left to rot!

speaker: Eivor
en: You have lost your apples.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: But I have. A devilish wind took me over, and I worry for them. But I've saved the finest and juiciest. O! These apples explode in your mouth with the iridescent light of Jesus.

speaker: Eivor
en: What makes them special? An apple is an apple, no?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, I beg to differ, my friend! You see, every year we make the pilgrimage to the west, Hamme's farm.

speaker: Eivor
en: Farmer Hamme to the west?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Yes, we call him "The Hammer." And his apples are fine, have this sweet iron tinge in them. My friends have already made it back. They are surely feasting already, but... I fell on some misfortune. Me cart busted. O, if only me back wasn't knotted like a dying oak.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, eternal thanks for carrying the crate!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll be happy to share in the bounty of these apples with you once we meet up with your friend.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, surely. We will share the Lord's work with ye. The iron tinge, you will taste it. We all have earned it after fasting.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fasting? Is that when you lack food for your god?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Yes. We show our devotion. Remove distraction. But now, we give in to the fruits of our Creator's Work. Sharing an apple with a friend is the most sublime experience... O!

speaker: Eivor
en: It is nice to sometimes sit back and simply enjoy an apple.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: With our fortune always changing in life, it is important to enjoy simple pleasures...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O I am so excited for you see my friend and eat apples with us. The act of walking, the pilgrimage we are going on!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: We will prostrate ourselves for Guthlac at the end of this glorious pilgrimage. Drown in his reward.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Here we are! Our tiny sanctuary. Join in prayer for the apples if you like. We .

speaker: Eivor
en: Bob?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: It is the only way to piously reap the reward of our Holy Father. Praise be to Him.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: O, Brother Holthwulf, and you've made a friend as well. Good to have you back!

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Norse Man
en: Anyone? I'm stuck!

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Eivor
en: I hear you. What is wrong?

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Norse Man
en: Thank the gods! I wanted to get the new shipment done early and accidently boxed myself in.

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Eivor
en: If that is all, I can get you out.

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Norse Man
en: Not so fast! Avoid breaking the jars. The sauce is delicious, but smells like a sun-soaked fish barge.

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Norse Man
en: Please! Make a path through the jars so I can get out. And-and, don't break any. The smell is awful!

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Eivor
en: Burri's balls... that's foul.

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Norse Man
en: O, thank the gods, you've unblocked me.

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Norse Man
en: You must have the grace of a cat! Not a drop spilled, thank the gods. I owe you my freedom.

scene: The Demon Odor at the Tithe
speaker: Norse Man
en: O... Just a few broken... but the smell will be here for weeks. Huh... Still, you have my thanks.

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Norse Warrior
en: A merry tune! Play it again, Saxon!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Bard
en: The Lord made me and the Lord made thee, and the Lord made and . So if you would close to Heaven be, have another ale or three! Drink some mead and drink some rum, for ye know not when the Lord will come. So drink thy ale and drink it fast, who knows if it may be your last!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Bard
en: You there, Dane! Come join your fellows! Music is my gift to you all!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Eivor
en: Here is a merry gathering. A Saxon, playing for Norsemen?

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Bard
en: "What joy a man gives is given back threefold." So my love used to say. Dear Cearo. I sing now for her.

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Eivor
en: Used to?

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Bard
en: Used to. But now is no time for sadness! Join our revels! I was about to open a cask for my new friends! Come one, come all! Nothing heals the heart of woe like a mug of ale.

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Norse Warrior
en: You look like the sort who laps at their brew like a kitten.

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Eivor
en: Wrong. Thor himself pales when he sees me take up my drinking horn.

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Ha! Come and prove it, then! Saxon, give us a song!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Show me how the Raven Clan drink!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Eivor
en: You'll be under the table before I've even warmed up.

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Norse Warrior
en: O-ho! We'll see about this!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Eivor
en: I feel cold fingers spreading through me. This is poisoned ale!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Urgh. Feels like Jörmungandr is turning in my stomach.

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Norse Warrior
en: By Odin, this new ale is strong. I think I'm going blind.

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Bard
en: A hundred lives I promised my love as she lay dying, a Danish arrow in her breast. A hundred lives for hers. But there is one who has not been laid low. Let me see to that.

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Bard
en: You will die as my Cearo did!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Eivor
en: It won't be me that dies today!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Eivor
en: God, my head!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Bard
en: I'll grant you the long peace of the grave!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Bard
en: Murderer! Reaver! Death to all Danes!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Eivor
en: Even sickened, I am more than your equal!

scene: The Devil Has All The Best Tunes
speaker: Eivor
en: He lured his prey with music, then poisoned them like a spider. Grief sick or not, the world is better without him in it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: Heathen! This is a place for proud converts like myself.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: I seek those who wish to join the great and superior holy path I am on.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: I want you to know that you can be like me, no longer dumb and angry like heathens.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hej, Monk. No need to brag of your faith.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: Have you recently tested your faith? Considered your holy path? It is a better way, I swear to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am content with my gods.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: Not as content as I am with mine, I am sure. He allows me to avoid rage, I am never angry. Never.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good for you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: Without anger in my life, I am completely changed, no longer obsessed with riches, like you. They are meaningless because He loves me. Go ahead and burn my house, destroy my belongings, I will never get angry.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: Yes, go ahead, destroy my crates and take my belongings inside them. God provides me enough.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: You see? I am not angry. Make yourself at home, it does not bother me. You will soon change from your pagan ways.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: You seem lost and homeless. Make of mine what you will. You could burn it to the ground, and it will not change me.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: Go ahead and slaughter my livestock. It is not something I wish to do, but I would gladly allow you to do it.

speaker: Eivor
en: And all of this homestead, the livestock, this is all yours?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: They are not mine, but God's. I have converted to God, and now I share all things.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, you mentioned that.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: Go ahead, destroy more. My faith cannot be broken.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: Thank you, Lord. For sending this devil to test my faith.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: Yes, burn it down. Make a pyre of the past.

speaker: Eivor
en: Curious good man, what were you before you became so devout?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: I was just like you, a stupid heathen, lost and violent. Speaking of which, you should try praying before it is too late.

speaker: Eivor
en: Too late? For what? The eternal buggery you possess? And now you stand? I worry that stool is covered in shit.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: O, no, that's... I mean, that key... do what you like with it. Throw it in the river. My faith will not budge.

speaker: Eivor
en: This hut reeks. As if... a battlefield... corpses? Are these your other converts? Or your past crimes?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: You desecrate my integrity by insinuating such... But my faith cannot be desecrated. Praise be to my Lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: Praise be to nothing. What crimes lie beneath your veil of Christ?

speaker: Eivor
en: What crimes have you gotten away with? You are no convert, you are a filthy opportunist. The Church gave you riches?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: I am a strong, Christian, mild-mannered man of the cloth. My pagan past is gone. I am

speaker: Eivor
en: A hypocrite. With not a shred of honor. You should pay for your crimes. People die unjustly in your newfound faith.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon man
en: I gave you a chance, heathen! I am a better, richer man for what I did. I changed course, and... Fuck it! I am still the blood-hungry whore I once was! Fucking die you putrid shit-eater! Die a thousand ways and times like the others!

speaker: Eivor
en: You would have sworn an oath to a pile of shit, you liar! Full of false pride. You should be judged at an for your crimes!

speaker: Eivor
en: Those willing to give everything away are often those who have taken too much.

speaker: Proclamation for Those Who Love Cats
en: Their meow is the divining rod to Heaven. Their claws are angelic hooks meant to climb the walls of Eden. No serpent or dragon can take them from my home. Felinus Maximus. I feed with them, I meow with them, I have build them a shrine in honor of them. They must be revered as saints, one day God will see their holy plan, for they speak through him to us. Praise the Holy Meow

speaker: Letter to Mother
en: Dear Mother, Every night I pray and proclaim to the heavens: Dear God Why So Many Rats! I regret to inform you I cannot pay my food tax nor send you the oats and barley for your beer and porridge. The taste of your beer and porridge brings me so much joy, however the rats of our land have taken the counsel of the devil and own the fertile soils like serpents in heaven. I pray to God every day and night they will one day grant me freedom from their pestilence. Your faithful son, Cyneburt the Infested

speaker: Outpost Leader
en: That god-cursed bacraut has deserted again! Come back or be branded a deserter! Do you want to be an outlaw? This is your last chance!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why are you shouting?

speaker: Outpost Leader
en: Eyvind has wandered off again. Every time, he claims he got lost in the mountains. I have had enough. If I have to risk more men looking for him, he will be branded and outlawed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eyvind... He is Gunnar's sister's son, if I have it right. Do not fire your irons yet, I'll have a look around.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, Eyvind is asleep on his watch. That would explain some things.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eyvind! Wake up, or you will be cast into the wild.

speaker: Sleepwalker
en: ... Must stay awake... they could be anywhere...

speaker: Eivor
en: Is he walking in his sleep?

speaker: Sleepwalker
en: ...They are everywhere... if we die, everyone dies... ...Must not fall asleep... need to see them coming...

speaker: Eivor
en: Eyvind, wake up! You are headed for the edge! Is he going to ride the rope-slide?

speaker: Sleepwalker
en: ...Windy... storm coming... Wha...? Ahhhhhhh!

speaker: Eivor
en: Eyvind, Eyvind! Calm down. You were asleep.

speaker: Eyvind
en: No, I was flying through the air!

speaker: Eivor
en: In your sleep. A harsh awakening, true, but at least you live. Have you always taken these dream walks?

speaker: Eyvind
en: Since my posting here. When I am in bed, I worry about ways we could be attacked. When I am on watch, I cannot stay awake.

speaker: Eivor
en: Only a fool stays awake all night worrying. You're tired when you get up, and the problem is still not solved.

speaker: Eyvind
en: You speak with the wisdom of Odin, Eivor. I will think on these words when I am in bed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Consider them on your watch and sleep when in your bed. But now, report back before you are labeled a deserter. Go.

speaker: Brewer
en: How could my notes be missing? This was going to be better than mead! This was going to be the choice drink in the Land of the Picts.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you need−

speaker: Brewer
en: Please go away. I don't have time for you right now. My life's work is in crisis.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone might be looking for this list. I should gather the ingredients on here for them, too.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think these notes might belong to you.

speaker: Brewer
en: You're my savior. Say, you wouldn't mind gathering the ingredients on this list for me? I'm making a smoky drink that's stronger than mead. You can play a small part in making history, if you help.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here. I've gathered everything on your list.

speaker: Brewer
en: You're my hero. Mark my words. This drink will take the Land of the Picts by storm soon enough. Once I make it, of course!

speaker: Havi
en: Once I did battle with one who had betrayed me. Listen close, and I will tell you how it went. And so victory was mine, as it ever shall be.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You have the wrong man! I've never heard of a Hunwald. I can't even properly say the name! Is it Hunwald or Honwald?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Please! This is a mistake. I've told you, my name is not Hunwald. It's Roderick!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: And I've told you... to shut your flappers!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Someone help! They mean to hang me for something I did not do!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: They said a Dane would likely follow close by, and lo and behold.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: Begone! This prisoner comes with me!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: What concern is this to you, heathen?

speaker: Eivor
en: That is not Hunwald.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: Why don't you let us decide?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Help me down.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Get me off this thing!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Untie me, quickly!

speaker: Eivor
en: Seems there's a bounty out on Hunwald.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: He's ruffled some feathers, that much is clear. You know him?

speaker: Eivor
en: I do.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Then the Lord truly is watching over me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Right place, right time.

speaker: Eivor
en: The next time someone mistakes you for Hunwald, tell them Hunwald is dead. He died in the battle of Chippenham.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Poor man. He must have ruffled some feathers to warrant all this heat.

speaker: Eivor
en: He could be a real pest, but was gentle and well-meaning.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Sounds like you were fond of him. My sympathies.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Thanks for saving my neck, stranger. I pray I can return the favor someday.

speaker: Ealwyn
en: How do I get through another night without you? O, Sphinxy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those are the cries of a broken heart. Who died?

speaker: Ealwyn
en: My beloved cat, Sphinxy. And please, do not be so crass. Sphinxy has simply... passed on. She is in God's hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing hurts quite like a fresh wound. But in time, it will heal and life will return to normal.

speaker: Ealwyn
en: If only. Instead, I find myself missing her more and more with each passing winter.

speaker: Eivor
en: How long ago did Sphinxy pass on?

speaker: Ealwyn
en: Eleven years ago tomorrow. A long time, I know.

speaker: Eivor
en: A little. Have you thought about honoring Sphinxy with a shrine? It is no burial, but it may ease your grief.

speaker: Ealwyn
en: I am halfway there, but I cannot bring myself to sort through her things. I simply do not have the strength.

speaker: Eivor
en: You alone must find the strength, lest you spend the next decade as you are now.

speaker: Ealwyn
en: True words. I shall try.

speaker: Eivor
en: Still mourning, hmmm?

speaker: Ealwyn
en: What else can I do? I do not have it in me to fetch what remains of my poor Sphinxy. Her shrine will forever be incomplete.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will help you. We will build Sphinxy a shrine together. Where should I start?

speaker: Ealwyn
en: My home. It's where she... she...

speaker: Eivor
en: There must be something I can find in here for the cat's shrine... if I can sort through all the rubble.

speaker: Eivor
en: Just how many cats do you have?

speaker: Ealwyn
en: Those are Sphinxy's children. O, they must be so big now!

speaker: Eivor
en: Agh! Shit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here we are. This will do. I will add this to the shrine.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have found some of Sphinxy's belongings.

speaker: Ealwyn
en: You have? O, wonderful! Would you bring them to the shrine just over there, beneath the shrub?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is done. A shrine dedicated to Sphinxy, whenever you care to pay your respects. And a home you can return to again. It may take some getting used to without Sphinxy, but her children need you.

speaker: Ealwyn
en: And here I thought all Danes were ruthless plunderers. Murderers! You have a soul that would grace the heavens. Like my Sphinxy. Lord light your way.

speaker: Rima
en: Hello. Need something forged?

speaker: Eivor
en: Good day. Is Gunnar about or... did he leave and not mention it?

speaker: Rima
en: My name is Rima, and Gunnar is a good friend of mine. Asked me to run his shop while he's away.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is good to meet you, and strange to see Gunnar away from his forge.

speaker: Rima
en: Well, as far as I know, he's got a very compelling—and beautiful—reason for his absence. So here I am.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, if Gunnar has faith in you, I do too.

speaker: Rima
en: Then I'd say you have fine taste. Have a look at what I've got.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll see you later, friend. I must be on my way now, goodbye. I have to go, see you soon.

speaker: Rima
en: So long. Farewell, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: What transpires in Glowecestrescire?

speaker: Randvi
en: You may have noticed that Gunnar has disappeared from his forge. He has traveled to Glowecestrescire in search of a wife.

speaker: Eivor
en: A wife?

speaker: Randvi
en: He is in love.

speaker: Eivor
en: When did this happen?

speaker: Randvi
en: When doesn't this happen with our dear, lovelorn blacksmith? But there is a bright side. He has asked you to join him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Join his search for a wife?

speaker: Randvi
en: And see that he does not make a fool of himself. I believe he thinks that your presence would bolster his image.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. I'll be Gunnar's keeper. If only to bring him back in one piece.

speaker: Randvi
en: Very generous of you. Make for the town of Glowecestre. You will find him there.

speaker: Eivor
en: There you are, Gunnar. And with a smile like I haven't seen in some time.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Eivor, over here!

speaker: Gunnar
en: Eivor! Thought I smelt you on the wind!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar, with the speed you left home, I thought you've been carried off by Valkyries.

speaker: Gunnar
en: I have. This Valkyrie right here. Brigid, my heart's root, meet Eivor.
