speaker: Eivor
en: It takes a rare woman to nail down our Gunnar.

speaker: Brigid
en: (He's a good man. One who admires you greatly.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Uh, good to meet you as well.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you find a woman in these backwoods?

speaker: Gunnar
en: She came through the settlement selling runes. Outshone every stone in her satchel. She offered me a trade, a rune for the brooch I was making. I got the better deal, but she loves the ugly little thing.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you do around here, Brigid? Except keep Gunnar out of mischief.

speaker: Brigid
en: I specialize in runes, spells, and charms.

speaker: Eivor
en: And my Gunnar? What are you gonna do with him?

speaker: Eivor
en: So, is the wedding here? When you spoke of a wedding feast, Gunnar, I hoped it would be at home.

speaker: Gunnar
en: No, no, no, we're here for the festival and blessings. Brigid's hand must be given. You know me, Eivor, I'm forged in honor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Whose blessing? I see no pitchfork-shaking father or weeping mother.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Ha! Glowecestre's ealdorman, Cynon. He helped raise Brig since she was a pup.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you a family, Brigid?

speaker: Brigid
en: (My mother and father walk together in . Cynon helped raise me.)

speaker: Gunnar
en: Brig's Ma and Pa were the last high priestess and ealdorman. They've since passed on, but the current ealdorman looks out for her.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should like to meet this ealdorman of yours, if our kinfolk are to be joined.

speaker: Gunnar
en: A union forged in love! Come, we'll go find him. O, and don't blame me if he's heard a tale or two about you. What about it, Brig?

speaker: Brigid
en: (No thanks, you two are bags of hot air around each other. Let Eivor get the earful.)

speaker: Gunnar
en: Right. No daylight to waste then, eh?

speaker: Eivor
en: So, the ealdorman may have heard a tale or two about my exploits?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Not all from me! Your name will be on the lips of every skald for years to come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm. And the Mercians here are not unsettled by lurking vikingr?

speaker: Gunnar
en: They came from all over to celebrate Samhain. Most are too busy with the festivities to pay us mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Samhain? Is that what these carved roots are for, this tradition?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Aye! Faces cut into lanterns to ward off evil spirits and guide children home.

speaker: Eivor
en: They have a haunted look about them. Let's bring a few back.

speaker: Gunnar
en: There's the ealdorman. Cynon!

speaker: Eivor
en: A good leader, seeing to his people's needs. Let us join hands when his task is done.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Ja. Then let's introduce you to Tewdwr.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Hands as clammy as a dead haddock, but his heart is in the right place. And he'll be ealdorman after Cynon.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Tewdwr! This is Eivor, my chieftain.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Ah, yes. The way Gunnar speaks, I expected

speaker: Eivor
en: Me to ride in on a winged horse? Cure the sick and the blind? His compliments are as blunt as his hammer.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Ah, more pagans crowding our table. Just lovely. What brings you here?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here to hasten my friend's marriage and drink my weight in ale. If friendship comes afterwards, then all the better.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have I wronged you? I am here only for the wedding. Where I come from, we do not poison the well of friendship so swiftly.

speaker: Eivor
en: The way people hear talk, Cynon's boots are hard to fill, and your feet look small.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Ha! All good friendships start with wit-battles.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: And what has Dane friendship done for Christian Mercia? Unseated God-right kings for puppet rulers?

speaker: Eivor
en: So-called puppet kings keep your lands safe and your bellies full. I ask no thanks, only hospitality.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here as a friend to Gunnar. I do not like to make enemies when breaking bread. So tread careful, boy.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Apples! Eivor, wait until you try the cider. You like cider, eh, Tewdwr? Cider?

speaker: Cynon
en: Ahh! You must be Eivor? Tewdwr, I see you've welcomed our honored guest! Come just in time for my last Samhain!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: At your behest, we welcome all pagans set upon God's own Glowecestre.

speaker: Cynon
en: Tewdwr, as your Harvest King, I demand that you remove the turnip from your arse and be merry.

speaker: Cynon
en: So you've come to meet the family? Before you whisk my Brigid away to her life as a smithy's bride?

speaker: Eivor
en: We're honored to have her join the Raven Clan. But your lush landscape will be hard to match.

speaker: Cynon
en: I must give away girl and land in this misty season. But Gunnar is a good man, and he speaks tirelessly of you.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: If you will excuse me... I have matters to attend to.

speaker: Cynon
en: Ah, yes, the shrine! And with so many thieves and fangs on the path. A fellow may fall in God's service.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Cynon! I do not need a heathen escort!

speaker: Cynon
en: Youth cut down in its prime. Without even the memory of warm thighs and cider to sustain him in the afterlife.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then, by my honor, I shall not rest until I return him to you safely. Aye, Tewdwr?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I see I'm outmatched. Though a Dane joining in praise to Saint Kenhelm? God will weep.

speaker: Gunnar
en: My ladylove calls, Eivor. O, if you'd like to join us later, we're going hoodening this eve.

speaker: Cynon
en: Go. May you have a fire-forged friendship. Watch for fairies, fen-folk, and fiends. I have a hand-fastening to oversee, an apprenticeship to officiate, and a pig to slaughter.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Shall we, then?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Samhain! Cynon humors these Pagans too much. It is the first thing gone when I am ealdorman. Fires and magic, spirits in the air, Glowecestrescire has strayed from God's light.

speaker: Eivor
en: People need carousing. Especially before the winter frost. A festival brings warmth and cheer.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: God's light does not dim as the nights chill. But the winters are hard upon the children. Seeing them run around...

speaker: Eivor
en: It lightens the heart. Are there priests in your lands? I have met a few, liked even fewer.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: The profane has gone unchallenged here. I alone am the reformation. They are a flock in need of the shepherding.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how will you lead this great renewal?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: They will fill the church's pews, and we will thank Him for the gifts He brings. Not false idols of wood and clay.

speaker: Eivor
en: And yet are we going to pray at the idol of another? Is this Saint Kenhelm your god?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: No. And we do not call him such. He is simply closer to the Lord's ear. Low in a mead of kine under a thorn, lieth poor Kenhelm king-born. Is this land not beautiful, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Aye.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Look, the path is untouched by danger. So, your company is not needed.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a kinder man than the mask you wear. You won't be rid of me. I'll keep my word to Cynon for your safe return.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't understand this Christian praying. I thank Odin while standing. Why get your knees dirty?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: To humble ourselves before God. Besides, I've dirtied my knees doing worse.

speaker: Eivor
en: That sounds like a tale I'd like to lend my ear to.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Please Eivor, I must pray.

speaker: Eivor
en: Should I watch or... turn my back?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: O Lord, gift upon this lowly servant your greatest gift. Patience.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not have to interrupt your prayer to protect you, Tewdwr.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: And yet, you insist on doing so... What is it you're looking at? A hare?

speaker: Eivor
en: Tewdwr, get to safety!

speaker: Eivor
en: Find somewhere to hide!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Where did they come from?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Fell the swine!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Whew, that was close.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Eivor! Thank you... for saving my life.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is good I was here to protect you. Maybe Cynon has the eyes of prophecy.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: sblood. Cloven hoofed and sent by himself! This land must be returned to God's grace.

speaker: Eivor
en: More likely this shrine is in their territory.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Lord, we thank thee for Your protection

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not safe here.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Give me my moment's prayer, Eivor. I ask only this.

speaker: Eivor
en: We should return to Glowecestre. Unless you'd like to thank the little martyr here for tonight's feast?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I am not a babe in the woods in need of constant guard. Go on without me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I gave Cynon

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Yes, yes, your word. And when I see him, I will say you protected me from being skewered upon those devils' tusks.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: And Eivor? I owe you a drink at least, later, if you'd have one. Find me at the festivities.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Eivor! There you are.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here I am.

speaker: Gunnar
en: So! What adventures did you find in my absence?

speaker: Eivor
en: Escorted Tewdwr to the shrine of some Christian saint. Our path was not peaceful. Accosted by a singular of boars.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Odd. That path is usually safe. Are you injured?)

speaker: Gunnar
en: But you saved his hide? I bet it was quite the sight, two of you as a pair.

speaker: Eivor
en: I kept my word to Cynon, and that spatchcock Tewdwr lives.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Restraint, Eivor? I was half-expecting you to wallop the lad round the head and arse.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've bridged hands with most of England, Gunnar. And, I've held my temper around worse than Tewdwr.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did Tewdwr become Cynon's successor? He speaks with his God's fire, but I do not quite believe it.

speaker: Brigid
en: (I watched the church fathers harden Tewdwr's heart. He believes he is doing God's work.)

speaker: Gunnar
en: Hm. Tragic that is. I think the lad can still be molded, Eivor. You might be just the one to do that.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need a drink.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Try the cider. It's from last year's apple harvest.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Skal.

speaker: Eivor
en: Skal.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, you invited me to a hoodening. What mischief is this?

speaker: Brigid
en: (We dress up as spirits and creatures of the veil to beg for treats.)

speaker: Gunnar
en: Glowecestre gives their glut to otherworldly visitors. And, if you dress as one, you'll get that bounty yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Freely given? Hmph, I've only seen such a thing done at feasts.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Then we'll turn you into a beastie, and have you roam the hills braying for sweets and drinks.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's hardly a disguise. Just a cloak and some bones.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Nonsense! You are the very spirit of the Mari Lwyd. Now, let's hooden!

speaker: Gunnar
en: Become the Mari Lwyd, the spirit who sings for cake and ale! And you cannot have your cloak back until we leave.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll keep this covering, but even a knife to my throat could not make me sing on command.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Shame. I've heard your voice. Clear as a bell. Larks fall from the sky in envy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar, if no one else is dressed this way, I will fill your shop with sheep.

speaker: Gunnar
en: That house for sure.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Eivor, Eivor, put the hood on!

speaker: Eivor
en: Locked. No one home.

speaker: Eivor
en: Trick or treat.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: What business have you? O, the Mari Lwyd. Right, right, we're doing cakes instead of beer this year. Samhain night and the moon is high, Mari Lwyd haunts my door...

speaker: Eivor
en: Give me sweets, and candied treats, the kind I most adore.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Haha! Here, then. Sweets for the Mari Lwyd, you've earned it.

speaker: Eivor
en: The air is chilling, and ghosts are spilling all across the misty moor.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Ooh, ghosts and beasties. Here, spirit, take your reward.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Are you playing the role of trickster spirit?

speaker: Eivor
en: Can trickster spirits see? The eyeholes in this mask are terrible.

speaker: Gunnar
en: All it takes is a mask and some sweetcakes to turn you into a gentle skald.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not going to sing, Gunnar.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you ready to rhyme with me?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Down the road from my abode, there is an open veil...

speaker: Eivor
en: Hope to gods this Mari Lwyd doesn't fail.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Ah, have a cake for your troubles, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've been here knocking, and a-walking, now give me cake and ale.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Brilliant, that is!

speaker: Gunnar
en: Lads getting into their cups scaring the wee ones.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Eivor, mighty warrior, knocker of doors, victors of cakes. How does it feel to pillage what is freely given?

speaker: Eivor
en: A worthy haul. And a tradition worth keeping up!

speaker: Modron
en: Then... through the mist of the night, they saw a woman at the crossroads, dressed in all white. And the children knew they should not have been out in the late, and in the dark. So, they bent low to the ground.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: It's !

speaker: Modron
en: That's right, my love, Y Ladi Wen. The White Lady. Her dark eye fell upon the children and

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Haha!

speaker: Modron
en: Which is why none of you should run out alone to the woods tonight. You will stay in sight of the tree and the wicker man. Yes?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Yes, Mother Modron.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Yes, Mother Modron.

speaker: Modron
en: Now, the first of you to bring me back a candied chestnut shall have a treat!

speaker: Eivor
en: Good

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: O! Thank the gods! We've been waiting for children all night to empty our stores so we can go to the party. Have some extra.

speaker: Eivor
en: Look at these cakes! Sweet as honey, Gunnar. You should see this. Gunnar?

speaker: Eivor
en: ...My cakes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have come to rhyme with you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: In the gloaming, see her roaming, hidden 'neath a hood...

speaker: Eivor
en: To each dwelling, fate foretelling, it's the Mari Lwyd.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Well done.

speaker: Eivor
en: Never knowing who is knocking, wanting something good

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O, very nice.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar? Damn deserter.

speaker: Gunnar
en: You are either fearless or stupid, boy, to speak to someone of the Raven Clan this way.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: Fitting name for scavengers! Winged rats taking what isn't yours!

speaker: Gunnar
en: I'll peck out your eyes and feed them to your god.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar, we are guests here. Let him go, we can hooden more.

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem to want your nose broken, so let me oblige.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Christ, not again.)

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: It's you lot we should be burning alive!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sure you don't want to stay in Glowecestre?

speaker: Gunnar
en: They know how to have fun!

speaker: Gunnar
en: Thor's beard! My leg!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar!

speaker: Brigid
en: (Be careful, my love!)

speaker: Modron
en: Enough! Keep your brawls to the other side of the river! There's children about.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: I don't answer to you, witch.

speaker: Modron
en: Tamas Fletcher, I brought you into this world, wiped your mother's birth blood from your face. Mind your tongue.

speaker: Modron
en: Let's see that leg, then.

speaker: Gunnar
en: It's nothing.

speaker: Eivor
en: Careful with the old man, he's had many winters worth of wounds.

speaker: Brigid
en: (You're lucky Modron's around to patch this up.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Your aid is welcome.

speaker: Modron
en: Men drown themselves in ale on Samhain. But I fear for the fragile peace when Tewdwr becomes ealdorman.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Men will be foolish, regardless of who holds power.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Will he walk again?

speaker: Modron
en: The gash is deep. If I cannot save the leg, the pigs will eat well tonight.

speaker: Eivor
en: That man called you a witch.

speaker: Modron
en: I lead those who follow the Old Ways in Glowecestrescire. But I offer my healing services on both sides of the river.

speaker: Modron
en: Gwenydd, my love, go back to the house and bring me the garlic salve.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: And the worms? Are we cleaning or cutting, Mother?

speaker: Modron
en: Yes, grab the worms just to be safe. Now, go, child. I promise not to cut it off before your return.

speaker: Gunnar
en: , give me strength!

speaker: Brigid
en: (Mother Modron is known for her dark humor, Gunnar.)

speaker: Gunnar
en: I'm glad you're all finding my mortal injury so funny. Go, Eivor, make merry and try to loosen Tewdwr's shoulders.

speaker: Eivor
en: Modron, you do not have to save his leg. I will understand.

speaker: Modron
en: That limb will be fine. But no medicine in England will stop the dribble from his mouth. I do not work miracles.

speaker: Eivor
en: A child.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: I have—I have—Cakes. Mummy made. Here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Good evening.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: It's dead of night. You lie unaware. A terrible sight comes up from her lair.

speaker: Eivor
en: A wicked sprite has come to scare— (spooky noises)

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Alright, alright, you did cause a fright. Take a sweet reward.

speaker: Eivor
en: A horse's skull with terrible hair.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Not very scary, is it? Take half a nettle-cake and get gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: O, hello, little one.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: The croaking toad hopped down the road, followed by an owl...

speaker: Eivor
en: Just beyond their fetid lake, the ghosts are on the prowl.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: That was a little weird, but I like it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Through foxes' dens and murky fens, the frightful spirits howl.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've come to trade barbs for cake and ale!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: It's past the little 'un's bed times, and I want to retire. Take your cake and go.

speaker: Eivor
en: With bitter ale and sweet friends. That is a fine way to end a day.

speaker: Eivor
en: I though the Church condemned this celebration?

speaker: Gwilim
en: I ain't the church! Name's Gwilim, and I turned to God just three years back.

speaker: Eivor
en: You look like a man with a past. What were you before you took up the cloth?

speaker: Gwilim
en: Me? A grain farmer. Had to take up the sword a few times to protect me crops.

speaker: Eivor
en: What brought you to God?

speaker: Gwilim
en: Ye know ye need to change after the third night you wake up britchless in pig shite. With no idea how you got there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you like Glowecestre?

speaker: Gwilim
en: Aye, 'tis a beauteous place. Shame they're losing their ealdorman.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enjoy the festival, Gwilim.

speaker: Gwilim
en: Aye, perhaps a drink later.

speaker: Eivor
en: Alone with your thoughts at last?

speaker: Cynon
en: Eivor! Perhaps. Every moment is sweeter when you are the Harvest King. All this bounty... soon I will join it. But, eat, drink! Enjoy all that Glowecestre's lush woods offer.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Eivor! There you are.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tewdwr.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: You're well met. Gwilim here has challenged my honor in a contest of drinks.

speaker: Gwilim
en: Join us. The lad will be easy pickings.

speaker: Eivor
en: Give me a cup!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Some ale, then!

speaker: Gwilim
en: One fer me as well!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gwilim, the warrior-monk. Now we can match wills with a flagon in hand.

speaker: Gwilim
en: Ha! Ale is known to blunt even the sharpest of blades, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: For a shaveling for the Christ Lord, you have a lot of scars, Gwilim.

speaker: Gwilim
en: Not every tonsured man is a wet-eared abbey babe. I came to God after I had scarred my soul with sin.

speaker: Eivor
en: To holy hearths and humid eyes. It is the best drunkenness returns a man to royal reason! Skal!

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps later, Tewdwr. I will find you again and defend my honor in ale.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Ready for that drink, Eivor? But fair warning, my reputation will not suffer another blow.

speaker: Cynon
en: Keep on! The honor of Glowecestre is at stake. I will not leave these lands to one who laps at ale like a cat!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: That's foul!

speaker: Gwilim
en: Come, lad! The leader of Glowecestre should hold more mead than that!

speaker: Cynon
en: I have seen babes in arms drink a hogshead of ale faster. Drink, man, drink.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're sweating!

speaker: Gwilim
en: Come on lad, show the Dane yer mettle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Too strong for you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not as (hic) slow as you look.

speaker: Cynon
en: Good effort, Tewdwr. This merriment feeds my soul. Here, another drink on me. For allies new and old.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of all the ealdorman I've met, you are the most unburdened. What is your secret?

speaker: Cynon
en: None. It is well-known. The burdens I carry will soon leave this world with me. So drink, to my life and death!

speaker: Eivor
en: Death?

speaker: Cynon
en: I am to be sacrificed in the wicker man as King of the Harvest! Like Ealdorman Simkin before me, and all before him.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Horrible barbaric practice. A burnt offering after poor crops. They hope well-fed gods will smile upon them.

speaker: Eivor
en: A true father sacrifices himself for his people, give his all, his blood and flesh. A great honor, but a sad fate.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: When you speak these words, it reminds me of the Christ.

speaker: Cynon
en: Aye, lad. Now you can see how a man like myself sees the value in both.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your people are loyal to you, Cynon. Seems a waste to throw your life away.

speaker: Cynon
en: Their loyalty would falter if I shirked my duties. I will die glorious in flame, not live to further choke my homeland.

speaker: Eivor
en: A toast then, to Ealdorman Cynon! Joyous and generous! Let each man show him loyalty until he suffers death.

speaker: Cynon
en: My friends, you are kind to me. I'd like to toast my successor, Tewdwr! May he wear the horns, head high.

speaker: Eivor
en: Weak! What is this? Water? I feel like Thor chugging oceans, no effect to my head or step.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Haha! You heard the woman, give her something stronger!

speaker: Gwilim
en: This'll work faster than any tonic.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good! Give me visions of all creatures that roam these hills, and a sore head tomorrow to pay for it!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Ugh, that tastes awful. It feels good, though.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Eivor, speak true... my feelings be damned. I have been an arse, do not deny it. And I for that... I'm sorry.

speaker: Eivor
en: A colossal horse's arse, yes!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Soft words from a heartless heathen!

speaker: Eivor
en: Only fiercer than fire among ill friends. I can be very as nice as a spring gale.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: And how nice is that?

speaker: Eivor
en: Very, very nice.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I think I might like you even better when you're mean.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nice enough to tell you that you are wrong for the ealdorman's seat.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Maybe you are correct. I wanted to be a cardinal, but the men who raised me said I'd serve God better as an ealdorman.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are your own man. Not theirs. The only ones you should be serving are your people.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tewdwr, with Gunnar and Brigid's marriage, our clans will unite. But we could join by oath as well.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: O! Yes. My first ally as ealdorman. I accept! We shall make an oath! How do we start?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ja! The greatest... greatest oath and the greatest union. To the oath!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: The treaty! The greatest!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Shhh! People are sleeping! More ale to seal our friendship! This way, this way, look out for... the .

speaker: Eivor
en: Sow? Like pig?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Flaming pig. Chases you home at night. Silly words to scare silly children.

speaker: Eivor
en: Pfff... you see magic as the stuff of children's dreams?

speaker: Twedwr
en: Perhaps I judge too much... truths I half-believe. Foolishness sometimes take my tongue. I have to piss.

speaker: Eivor
en: A great blackness chases stars across the sky in great whorls of color and light. Whooosh!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Here we are. Right inside here. I feel warm. Do you feel warm?

speaker: Eivor
en: Always warm here. It's a wonder you don't walk around naked.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Yes... erm... well, come on in.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tewdwr? Tewdwr!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tewdwr! Where are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hel's breath. What happened last night?

speaker: Eivor
en: And the effects of that draught still cling.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tewdwr? Are you here?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Eivor. A moment of your time?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Eivor! Good to see you, I—erm. Did you want something or... I was wondering...

speaker: Eivor
en: What's wrong?

speaker: Gunnar
en: Brigid and I were thinking, with everything calming down the way it has... maybe you could find a spare moment and...

speaker: Eivor
en: You want to be married.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Yes. To each other.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes... I imagined. Gunnar, to see you so happy as been a pleasure. And to marry you would be an honor. Shall I put out a call to any friends abroad?

speaker: Gunnar
en: I'll be honest, Eivor. I came here with the lot of you because nothing and no one kept me back there. The Raven Clan is all the family I need. And Brigid too. From all she's said, she's better off here than with those she calls kin. Just a couple of foundlings, we are.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then let's not bother with tradition. If you've your bride and your blade, we will see you wed. As jarl, I do it gladly.

speaker: Eivor
en: About you and Brigid. When do you wish to be wed?

speaker: Gunnar
en: The sooner I can make her my wife, the happier I will be. But we are fine to wait until everything has settled here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough waiting! Cool your forge and cover your anvil. Let's get you married.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Wonderful! Shall we gather everyone?

speaker: Eivor
en: Gather your wife and your courage. I'll bring the people together.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have a few things to attend to, but we will see you married soon enough.

speaker: Gunnar
en: We will be ready when you are.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am honored to stand before you, Gunnar, Brigid, on this bountiful day. To celebrate the strength of your bond and see you wed. I am in witness of a love that inspires and empowers. I invite you, now, to speak your vows.

speaker: Gunnar
en: To you, my darling, Brigid, I offer this blade, forged in flames that burn as brightly as my heart does for you. A blade as sharp as your wit, as glinting as your beauty. May it sing through the air as sweetly as your voice meets my ears.

speaker: Brigid
en: (, how I adore you, Gunnar. I am ever so luck to have found you, my love.)

speaker: Gunnar
en: And I you. I give you my sword and my promise that I will stand at your side forever.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Long have I dreamed of my own future, and sought solace in hope and premonition. But no amount of scrying or foresight prepared me for the sweeping adventure of meeting you.)

speaker: Brigid
en: (You are a soul like none other. A man as strong as he is gentle and as kind as he is fierce. My hear soars alongside yours.)

speaker: Gunnar
en: Such poetry, O dear! You make me cry, my love.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Let us fly together, through this life and beyond.)

speaker: Gunnar
en: I offer you this ring, and take yours in kind. I will wear it with pride and honor, warmed by the love of so perfect a lady.

speaker: Brigid
en: (And I will wear it with love, adoration, and faith everlasting.)

speaker: Gunnar
en: This is the greatest day of my life! Embrace me, my love!

speaker: Eivor
en: With our couple now bonded in matrimony... now we drink!

speaker: Eivor
en: Alvis, I am surprised you did not serenade the bride and groom with a verse or two.

speaker: Alvis
en: O, I wished to, I did. But all that came to me were insults and jibes. Another time, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brigid. I gift you a formal welcome to our clan and our family. You are a fine addition to Gunnar's life and to ours.

speaker: Brigid
en: (Thank you, Eivor. I couldn't be happier to be here. I hope to know you better in the coming months and years.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes... of course, I... as I say, it is wonderful to have you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gunnar, you old trout... you're a married man. Never thought I would see the day.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Nor did I. And not for lack of trying.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a strange feeling, Brother. Weddings are the beginning of something, but this feels like something of an end.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The first happy union in our home. We have matured into something greater, so yes... a beginning and an end, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how are the marriage customs in your country, Hytham? Something like this?

speaker: Hytham
en: Like this in all the most important ways. There are smiles, cheers and warm embraces. All that is needed, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've been among us for quite some time, Reda. Are you ready to settle? Make a home here?

speaker: Reda
en: For a year or two, perhaps. But I am not the settling kind. I am a wanderer, always searching, never finding. Maybe one day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka. I want to thank you for all you have done for me. My visions have lessened of late, and I... well, I find it hard to explain how different I feel. Grounded. Unified. At peace.

speaker: Valka
en: That is good to hear, Eivor. Very good to hear.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi... Saw you looking a little lonely. Thought I might come and join you.

speaker: Randvi
en: How nice. Are you enjoying yourself?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am. I never thought I would see gruff old Gunnar so enraptured by a woman.

speaker: Randvi
en: Enraptured by anything, for that matter. He's a hard one to read. But I am pleased for him. And for this day of rest and respite. After everything, a few days of feasting will do the people some good. They need this.

speaker: Eivor
en: They do.

speaker: Randvi
en: Will you walk with me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Anywhere. Lead on.

speaker: Randvi
en: Something has been on my mind for some time. I am no seer, but I foresaw this day long ago. Not Gunnar's marriage, but our situation. Our success.

speaker: Eivor
en: How do you mean our success?

speaker: Randvi
en: I mean to say that I saw our settlement flourishing, through our victories in war and in diplomacy. And from the day we set out from Norway, I knew that you would make a fitter leader than Sigurd. It was never in his character to lead. It was always within yours.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see.

speaker: Randvi
en: Do you?

speaker: Eivor
en: You might have warned me.

speaker: Randvi
en: You would not have listened.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fair.

speaker: Randvi
en: I do hope you see it now, in all that you have done for us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi, you and the people here have done more for me than I could ever repay. I am honored by your faith in me. And your confidence.

speaker: Randvi
en: As I am honored by your love.

speaker: Randvi
en: As I am honored by your friendship.

speaker: Eivor
en: And I by yours.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor, I want you to know that Sigurd and I are... We are severing the bonds of our marriage.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sure?

speaker: Randvi
en: Sigurd's desires are bigger than any man or woman can offer. He longs for something more, something only he can find.

speaker: Eivor
en: All he wants is far, far away. All I need is right here.

speaker: Randvi
en: We share a love that is steadfast, and I have faith it will forever be so. But it is not the love of a wife and her husband. It was not an easy decision. But after we talked with honesty, we embraced more warmly than we have in a great while. I think we will be happy.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope so. And I am pleased for you.

speaker: Randvi
en: I am pleased for myself. Sigurd's desires are bigger than any man or woman can offer. He longs for something more.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what about you? What are you looking for?

speaker: Randvi
en: I have all I need right here. With you, with our people.

speaker: Eivor
en: I want to say, Randvi... I love you, and I have for some time. I did not pursue it, not wanting to betray my brother's trust.

speaker: Eivor
en: But that does not mean I did not desire it. Does that surprise you?

speaker: Randvi
en: Gods, I worried you saw me as a woman starved for the affection of her husband. That it was loneliness driving me.

speaker: Randvi
en: But it was you, Eivor. Only you. Everything you are, everything you will become.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi... without you I would have lost my way, a thousand times.

speaker: Randvi
en: I never told him outright, but I doubt he will be surprised. I think he may have suspected it even. Some time ago.

speaker: Eivor
en: If he suspected it, he never said anything.

speaker: Randvi
en: He is more observant than I often give him credit for. I believe he sees us as we are. And as we hope to be. We can wait to tell him. Give it a few days, when the feasting is over and everything is settled.

speaker: Eivor
en: Agreed. I have waited long enough for you, and you for me. What is another few days?

speaker: Randvi
en: The blink of an eye.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am grateful. So much of our prosperity we owe to you. I hardly know where to begin.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are my truest friend, Randvi. My right hand. My greatest ally.

speaker: Randvi
en: I give you my word it will always be so. I'm happiest by your side and in your company.

speaker: Randvi
en: Shall we find our way back to the wedding? Brigid might give another speech. We must not miss that.

speaker: Eivor
en: About that... I have not understood a single word of hers since Glowecestrescire!

speaker: Randvi
en: Really. I find she speaks beautifully. With poetry, even.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you kidding?

speaker: Randvi
en: Am I?

speaker: Randvi
en: Come, we should go.

speaker: Reda
en: What do you think of all this? A little dull, in my view.

speaker: Knud
en: I think it was nice!

speaker: Eira
en: I liked the part where they gave each other swords.

speaker: Sylvi
en: I'm never getting married. When I get a sword... I am keeping it!

speaker: Gunnar
en: Eivor! I wanted to thank you, on behalf of myself and Brigid. Our wedding was the greatest day of my life. And it could never have gone so well without you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Truly, Gunnar, it was my pleasure.

speaker: Havi
en: I will tell you now the tale of how I laid low the Lord of the Fire Giants and all his kin! As I travelled on, I met a towering giant of flame and stone! Soon enough, I chanced upon a fearsome Muspel, glowing with inner fire!

speaker: Viking 1
en: Seems Kjotve's roused an army to hurl against us.

speaker: Viking 3
en: Eivor will expect us at the hall. First, let us clear the streets of Kjtove's dogs.

speaker: Viking 2
en: Haha! Finally! A real fight!

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. You are still alive.

speaker: Viking 2
en: You think such as these could kill us? Ha!

speaker: Viking 2
en: This fight should have been harder.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is beginning to strike me odd as well. Still, stay alert. Kjotve's best fighters will be defending the hall. And they know are are coming now.

speaker: French Man
en: There! There! Do you see it? Mon Dieu! (My God!) On the roof of the chapel!

speaker: French Woman 1
en: Merde! (Shit!) I see it, I see it! The ghost of St. Germain... O! It's true! I will faint.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: Don't be dramatic! It's just a shadow. Wait... is it? Now I don't know.

speaker: Jotun 1
en: When will these damned snows end?

speaker: Jotun 2
en: When your damned complaining does.

speaker: Jotun 3
en: No blizzard has ever blown so long. This reeks of sorcery.

speaker: Havi
en: And here are the storm-bringers. Explain this mischief.

speaker: Kala
en: This tempest is our vengeance.

speaker: Vindr
en: Cold winds for a cold heart.

speaker: Kala
en: Three times we asked for Gunlodr's hand! Three times we demanded she choose between us!

speaker: Vindr
en: Three times my brother's hideous face drove her away.

speaker: Kala
en: It's YOUR face, shit-wit! We're twins!

speaker: Havi
en: You conjured this storm because your feelings were hurt?

speaker: Kala
en: This storm is the storm that rages within us! The noble pain of those wronged in love!

speaker: Havi
en: The lady said no. Move on.

speaker: Kala
en: I don't like your tone, Aesir. You think you're better than us, just like she did. Maybe it's time to shut your mouth.

speaker: Havi
en: Why don't you come and try?

speaker: Kala
en: Utgard will be buried beneath the snows of our fury!

speaker: Vindr
en: Your bones will be swallowed by ice!

speaker: Kala
en: We will not stop till Utgard is no more!

speaker: Havi
en: The skies have cleared. The blizzard is over at last.

speaker: Jotun 4
en: Did you hear? That blizzard was all on account of some angry suitors Gunlodr rejected.

speaker: Jotun 5
en: Men! Do they ever really grow up, or do they just increase their ability to do damage?

speaker: Jotun 6
en: O, It was so much easier to sneak around behind Grognir's back when you couldn't see your hand in front of your face.

speaker: Skald
en: Two mighty Jotnar dwelt close to the sky. Their faces the same, they bewildered the eye. They came down to Utgard, fair Gunlodr to try. "Marry us, Gunlodr." But Gunlodr said "Why?" "My books are my husbands, I've no need of more. Your breath is appalling, your manners are poor." "You boast of your might, but it's minds I adore. So thank you for coming, now there is the door."

speaker: Aswig
en: Come back here and untie me! There are wolves, bears! You will be sorry when I am eaten! Who will sing of your deeds then? You ungrateful peasants. If poetry be the cake of... food... then I am its baker!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why were you tied up?

speaker: Aswig
en: A wee misunderstanding between myself and the good folk of the hamlets hereabouts. Your name, good-kin?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor of the Raven Clan. And now I have freed you, so go about your business.

speaker: Aswig
en: Wait, may I enquire? The dulcet timbre of your voice. The godlike strength of your gait. You are a warrior, yes? A lone skiff bobbing on the sea of opportunity. Wait, what is that on the horizon? Adventure!

speaker: Aswig
en: The stars prophesied our meeting! I am the gleewoman Aswig the Mellifluous. You have heard of me? No matter. Destiny has made you my muse! I shall follow you, record your great deeds with poetry.

speaker: Aswig
en: This will not make great poetry, Eivor. Do something. Anything.

speaker: Aswig
en: Fleet of foot and long of gait, O Eivor, do I prate your fate.

speaker: Aswig
en: Eivor charges up her bow! Watch that arrow go and go! O'er hill dear arrow fly. Rain down death from up on high.

speaker: Aswig
en: Eivor climbing like a spider! O, I'm honored to be beside her. Eivor like a mountain goat! Toss your hero half a groat. Eivor climbs on top of the world!

speaker: Aswig
en: Eivor leaps into some straw. Stares sure death right in the maw. Nary a scratch or broken bone. Children, do not try this at home.

speaker: Aswig
en: Eivor running from the past, with mighty speed to flabbergast. Eivor ran away, away. Bravely ran away, away.

speaker: Aswig
en: Regard our hero. So skilled with a rod!

speaker: Aswig
en: Eivor, like a golden eel, breaks the river's watery seal.

speaker: Aswig
en: Eivor's face now obscure, I've never seen one so demure. Eivor, skulking in the shadow, meek and quiet as a sparrow.

speaker: Aswig
en: Eivor is walking like a duck! It's like she doesn't give a... fa-la-la-la and nonny nonny noo.

speaker: Aswig
en: When danger rears its ugly head, Eivor balks and just stops dead.

speaker: Aswig
en: Eivor ran into the fray. None of you will survive the day. Eivor gives the Saxons grief. Hack and slash them, break their teeth!

speaker: Aswig
en: Just a tiny scratch is all. Eivor will but walk it off! Eivor, forgetting how to dance, takes an arrow in the arse.

speaker: Aswig
en: Parting is a sorrow that fills my cup to over flowing.

speaker: Aswig
en: My muse returns! At last I can continue my epic tale of your exploits. It was just getting good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough. Stop following me.

speaker: Aswig
en: I cannot, for walking in your footsteps has let me sup at the cup of inspiration. You are my life's great purpose.

speaker: Eivor
en: I won't give you any money, if that is what you seek.

speaker: Aswig
en: Money? You offend me. I am an artist, grubby coin does not sustain me. Poetry is my bread and mead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I trust this does not have to get bloody?

speaker: Aswig
en: Bloody? Pitiful Judas, no. I will take my leave.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough with you.

speaker: Aswig
en: A piffling sum. But I will take it. Aswig, you will have bread and milk for sup tonight. It is surely a day amongst days.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now I thank you, but please, take your leave.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough! I won't listen to your blabber anymore.

speaker: Aswig
en: First there was a famine and now, look here, a feast! Fare thee well, Eivor of the Raven Clan. Your exploits will live on in me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now I thank you, but please, take your leave.

speaker: Aswig
en: Fare thee well, brave hero! Perhaps we will meet again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods, I hope not.

speaker: Ermina
en: Ugh! The baby is coming! Hoo, Mother was right. Always keep the legs closed. Fucking shit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your baby is coming. Where is the nearest healer? I can take you.

speaker: Ermina
en: No need for a healer, love. Just to get to the top of that hill. I can do the rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: What? All the way to the top? And, you intend to go alone in your state?

speaker: Ermina
en: Yes! I'll roll my fat corpse up this hill if need be.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is too far to carry you like this without hurting your babe. I shall have to take you by horse.

speaker: Ermina
en: You need not help me, but who am I to look a gift Dane in the mouth.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is dishonorable to leave a pregnant woman to the elements. Why does the baby's father not come to you?

speaker: Ermina
en: The baby's father is a god. of the Wood saw me on Solstice and wooed me with his song.

speaker: Eivor
en: You laid down with a god?

speaker: Ermina
en: Aye, is that so shocking? Mary grew Christ from the touch of God. I heard of a Dane god who laid down with .

speaker: Eivor
en: Loki. And, he was also a horse at the time. You didn't get mounted by a horse god, did you?

speaker: Ermina
en: No! It was very much a man. A godly man, definitely not a mortal. But, I didn't see him by light of day so who knows.

speaker: Eivor
en: Picked up our trail. Hold on!

speaker: Ermina
en: Child out of wedlock. I should raise the babe out here. Safe from town gossip. Raising it as a bastard. How they'll talk. Ha. Lying with woodland gods and living out in the wilderness, I should become a witch. What do you think, love?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that all it takes to become a witch?

speaker: Ermina
en: We're not far now, love. You can leave me on the steps of the temple if you want. The rest should come naturally.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not leaving you to bleed out or be taken by wolves. If your god-lover cannot join you in birth, then I will guide your child out.

speaker: Ermina
en: I doubt he will. I ran after our little encounter. Thank you, love, you have been kinder to me than my own kin.

speaker: Eivor
en: We've made it to the shrine. Do you think the otherworldly father will be able to find us?

speaker: Ermina
en: I wasn't impregnated by a god, just an ordinary man as bored as me! Doubt he'll want anything to do with this child.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see. Then we shall focus on the child instead. Breathe deeply and try to relax. This will take time. I will build a tent.

speaker: Eivor
en: You did a great job. A healthy baby girl. Just hear that cry. Warrior's lungs.

speaker: Ermina
en: A girl. I've no knowledge of warriors or what to name them. How about your name, then? Little Eivor.

speaker: Moccus
en: Ermina! I've been looking everywhere. Bran told me you'd run off and I worried the worst. Is that? Is

speaker: Eivor
en: This is your god-lover? I expected more.

speaker: Moccus
en: God-lover? Should I take that as a compliment of my prowess or an insult to my name?

speaker: Ermina
en: Go, Moccus. Our families would never approve the union, and if you're to have any reputation, you will forget me.

speaker: Moccus
en: I think I get a say in that! I care not about status, and if all we have together is some hut in the woods, then so be it!

speaker: Eivor
en: A hut in the woods does sound fit for a witch and her babe.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Ready. Aim. Fire! How difficult could this possibly be? You nock your arrow into the bowstring, pull it back, aim, and fire! Try again! Lord save us all if we ever have to rely on you lot to defend us with bows. Remember, faint aim never won fair battle. Again!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Unbelievable. Which one of you did that?

speaker: Eivor
en: I did.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: What marvelous aim. For a moment, I thought my training was getting into these thick skulls.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: See if you can hit one of the targets above.

speaker: Little John
en: Hey, stop messin' around!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: That was sound aim! Amazing!

speaker: Tuck
en: That was a fluke, I bet.

speaker: Little John
en: Yeh! I bet you can't hit that... uhhh... that chicken, right o'er there! The one hanging from the pole!

speaker: Little John
en: Go on then, hit that hanging chicken from here. No cheatin'!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Huh, to hit that chicken would require some kind of special technique.

speaker: Little John
en: Hey, stop messin' around!

speaker: Little John
en: Wha... thas mad!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Extraordinary. That was true skill and aim. On the mark! Well, friend, you can count on us to lend a hand against King Constantin and his well paid Picts. And thank you for showing these turnips some skilled marksmanship. Visit us again. As for the rest of you, keep practicing!

speaker: Hastily Scribbled Note
en: More goods! More silver! The poor grow more desperate everyday while the Pict camps overflow with their stolen silver and supplies. Any amount you can give might save a starving child.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me about Grantebridgescire.

speaker: Randvi
en: A force of Danes, called the Summer Army by the Saxons, is camped north of Grantebridge, at some ruins across the river. We should curry favor with their leaders, Guthrum and Soma, if we hope to win their trust and allegiance. My scouts did not meet them in person, so I can say little for the state of their army. Consider this a starting point.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will leave right away.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. And may the blessings of Freyja follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi mentioned this place. The last known location of the Summer Army.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Hold. Who goes there?

speaker: Eivor
en: A friend and ally. I'm looking for the Summer Army.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Camp leader is up top. You can't miss him.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Those Saxons caught us without weapons. It's no way to die. That's true Christian behavior. Slaughtered us in our sleep.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hail! What has happened here?

speaker: Magni
en: Who is asking?

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Magni
en: I have heard the name! You helped the Sons of Ragnar overthrow the Mercian King! Well met.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you and your men fail to take the village?

speaker: Magni
en: No, no, we had it for a time. Was nothing but a cluster of wattle-and-daub huts when we came. We made it lively. Grantebridge was a thriving hub of trade and song under the care of Soma, our jarlskona. But the Saxons took it back. They appeared within the city, as if rising from the shadows, and drove us out.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's terrible. How were you ambushed?

speaker: Eivor
en: They just appeared in the city?

speaker: Eivor
en: What about the city walls? And your guards?

speaker: Magni
en: The walls were unbreached, the guards unaware.

speaker: Magni
en: It was like they burst out of the center of the city itself! Setting aflame everything in their path, shouting some nonsense about an ancient order of warriors. By the time I saw the fires, too many of us were killed or captured. Our jarlskona, Soma, she bellowed a retreat and we took refuse in the ruins. But in the chaos, we were separated. She and the bulk of our forces fled north-east into the swamps. I'd follow if we were fit to. We need her iron fist.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can find Soma. Be ready when we return.

speaker: Magni
en: She'll be deep in the fog of by now. Find her longship. That's your best bet.

speaker: Dag
en: Looks like Ragnarök itself came for Grantebridge.

speaker: Eivor
en: A great battle raged nearby... hold course. We'll see what else lies within the fog.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma cannot be far. I should have a look around. There, a beached longship. Dane markings.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Cut us loose. Hurry!

speaker: Longship Inscription
en: Jarlskona keeps family clutched firmly in fist, Loves deeply her city of summer and mist.

speaker: Eivor
en: This was a fine longship. Fit for a chief. It must belong to Soma.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is your jarlskona nearby?

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Not here. Soma dragged the Saxons east from her longship to tire them out and lose them in the fog.

speaker: Soma
en: You're still in fighting shape. Take a walk about the camp, your strength will return. We will recover the longboat tomorrow. I will not leave it to the muck.

speaker: Soma
en: Take him to the shelter for warmth.

speaker: Soma
en: Slap some moss on that gash and wrap it well.

speaker: Soma
en: Egil? Egil, look at me. Remember the boars you felled our first day in England? Hold his arms. Nine, large and fat. Fed us for a week. Yeah?

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Yeah

speaker: Soma
en: Yeah.

speaker: Soma
en: You'll be chasing more in a month, my friend.

speaker: Soma
en: You come like a Valkyrie out of the fog. But we have no dead to give you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must be Soma.

speaker: Soma
en: Let's talk elsewhere. Give them a chance to rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite a hit you took. How many were lost?

speaker: Soma
en: It's kind of you to ask, but with so much blood in the water and death on the air, I'd know your name and purpose first.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor of the Raven Clan. I came for you, looking for a friend and ally.

speaker: Soma
en: I see. I'm Soma, Lord of Grantebridge. Though it seems an order of lunatics wishes to strip me of that title.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Order of the Ancients?

speaker: Soma
en: Sounds right. The Saxon called Wigmund is one of them. He robbed me of my city, forced us into these swamps. I've rallied some of my soldiers, but my three advisors are missing. If we hope to retake Grantebridge, I'll need them at my side.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me about them.

speaker: Soma
en: They are my best, my inner circle: Birna, Galinn, Lif. We may as well be of the same blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I can reunite them, and we retake your city, can I call you a friend and ally?

speaker: Soma
en: If you can do all that, you can call me whatever you want.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is this Wigmund? And what does he want?

speaker: Soma
en: He's a flailing Ealdorman under the old king. A bitter man digging his fingernails into Grantebridge, just to say he can. He's made many attempts to unseat me before. This time, he managed the trick.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened to Grantebridge?

speaker: Soma
en: The ealdorman, Wigmund, seized it from us. I'm not sure how he managed, but he will not keep it. Not for long. He has supporters outside the city, but this attack seemed to come from inside the walls. From the heart of Grantebridge.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's find your advisors.

speaker: Soma
en: Agreed. We'll look for signs of their longboats along the river. And if we are swift, we will find them before the wolves do. The fog is more hindrance than hiding place now. Let's light the way back.

speaker: Havi
en: This is the tale of how I sent three evil swamp witches back to the mud of Albion. Ahead of me I saw what I knew to be my prey... and I struck! Once again, I had shown my prowess, and proved that none can defeat me!

speaker: Eivor
en: The chanting. It's faint, but I recognize Modron's voice.

speaker: Briton Warrior 1
en: The mother is communing with the gods on this most holiest of times, and we're stuck guarding the door.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: I'd rather be out here in case the ritual goes sour and we end up as a meal for the gods.

speaker: Modron
en: Blood and sweat, death and birth. Turn this man from beast to earth. Forest Father. Take this body. Eat of him and feed the land. Cernunnos, hear my plea and guide my hand. Cut down our foes. And fill our fields with grain to sow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have I stepped into Alfheim, or is this a new realm entirely?

speaker: Modron
en: Sweat and blood, death and birth. Turn this man from beast to earth.

speaker: Eivor
en: Modron! Stay your blade, or die at my hand.

speaker: Modron
en: I should have known Cynon wouldn't have it in him to quarter you for the dogs.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a cold bitch who throws her lover to the wolves for her own crimes.

speaker: Modron
en: You understand so little. No matter. Let me enlighten you with the fury of the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take this!

speaker: Eivor
en: Die Modron!

speaker: Modron
en: Do it, then. Leave Glowecestrescire in the hands of that Christian, and for what? Your name and some trade routes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you doubt the power of your gods to sway the mind of a man? Tewdwr is no longer the zealot you believe him to be.

speaker: Modron
en: A man will lie to save his skin. When you are gone, he'll gut me and burn my people. The gods showed me this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cynon spoke of your vision. The Nornir spin their fatal threads, but without your plan, his heart would remain unchanged.

speaker: Modron
en: Then I've no regrets. But I had a vision of you as well, one of a path that twists like the River Ouse.

speaker: Odin
en: A seer's spinnings twist limb and word alike. Prophecy is a river, and we are powerless to fight its clutches.

speaker: Modron
en: She was fighting to protect her people.

speaker: Odin
en: But she ground your name to dust! Sullied the honor of herself, and her people.

speaker: Eivor
en: I cut my own path.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Mama!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Lord in his mercy. What sorcery happened here?

speaker: Eivor
en: The high priestess, Modron, tried to kill you.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Why? In God's name. I've done nothing to her.

speaker: Eivor
en: She feared the church would use you as god's hammer. So she convinced Cynon to have you killed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cynon and Modron conspired to bring about your end. Now, both lie dead by my hand.

speaker: Eivor
en: I killed Modron, but Cynon lives to burn in the wicker man.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Such a waste of life. The devil whispers into the ear of man. But we must ignore his voice.

speaker: Eivor
en: Modron had a vision of you wiping out the pagans. And Gwenydd is Cynon's bastard, so he simply did it to protect his kin.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Love's for one's child is a virtue, but wrath is a sin. How can one entangle with the other.

speaker: Eivor
en: We all lose our heads when our legacy is threatened, be that name, kingdom, or child.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, what of the witchling?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I'll see that she's cared for. She has no guilt in this.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: I will not join your Church of Christ.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: You won't have to.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cynon is dead for your lies. Your wicker man will burn empty.

speaker: Eivor
en: I spared Cynon. Say your goodbyes and keep out of my sight, witch.

speaker: Gwenydd
en: Mother?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: What is this? Is this... are we in Hell?

speaker: Eivor
en: No. We are in England. How are you feeling?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I feel well... but it's a little fragrant in here, is it not?

speaker: Eivor
en: You will live to be ealdorman yet, Tewdwr. Despite the many attempts on your life.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Attempts? Untimely death? God's blood!

speaker: Eivor
en: Cynon was behind the attempt on your life. Modron brought you here.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're safe, and the ceremony will proceed in Glowecestre.

speaker: Modron
en: Your wounds should heal by the next moon, if you get some rest.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Then you have my thanks, Mother Modron!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Lovely woman, utterly terrifying though. Let's return with haste. This cave is a place of nightmares.

speaker: Eivor
en: We cannot allow Kjotve an exit. I will circle wide and try to get behind them. You keep pressing on. Odin guide you.

speaker: Viking 1
en: And you, Eivor!

speaker: Viking 2
en: Kjotve must be hiding in one of these houses.

speaker: Viking 2
en: Kjotve! You have run out of mountain. The gods demand justice for your cruelty!

speaker: Gorm
en: Speak you so to my father? Squawking birds fall to earth in the shadow of a king!

speaker: Viking 2
en: I see no king!

speaker: Kjotve
en: Enough, enough. Welcome to my temporary meadhall, Raven. Now, go back to the baubles left to you. These are beyond your ken.

speaker: Eivor
en: It won't be so easy as that!

speaker: Kjotve
en: Ah! Styrbjorn's little housecat! Come to claim a name, have you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor. Leave the scrolls and be gone. Or I could split your withered heart.

speaker: Kjotve
en: I will have to kill you then. Gorm!

speaker: Gorm
en: I have the other, father.

speaker: Kjotve
en: You're fast and strong, young Eivor, but you've much to learn.

speaker: Kjotve
en: Get the scrolls, son. We need to regroup and return North. Styrbjorn will be close behind these little birds.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hel's breath! Curse you, Kjotve! I will collect ' for this one day!

speaker: Viking 2
en: Come lord, we can still catch them...

speaker: Eivor
en: Pigs rushing the butcher's knife. No. We are beaten here. Savor the taste of defeat, then spit it out. In knowing we may never need eat of it again.

speaker: Viking 2
en: Ahh, Kjotve struck hard. Something's broken.

speaker: Eivor
en: Has he slain you?

speaker: Viking 2
en: Ha! No, lord. I'm afraid I'll have more rings of you yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rest easy then. We come by failure honestly. Styrbjorn will see. And, when Sigurd returns, we will carve our debt from Kjotve's poisoned hide.

speaker: Bron
en: Friend, I've lost my key. Good fellow! I've locked myself out! I haven't the strength to break open my door.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is your house?

speaker: Bron
en: I set my key down, only to watch it fall into the river. My name is Bron.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hej, Bron.

speaker: Bron
en: Ah, a Dane! I have an object inside that you'd be interested in—the legendary horn of Ragnar Lothbrok.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have Ragnar's horn? How can you know it was his?

speaker: Bron
en: You have me there, friend. I cannot be certain. It's a very old Dane horn. Help me into my house. You can judge for yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am curious to see this horn.

speaker: Bron
en: I hid it somewhere long ago. Forgive me, I can't recall just where. Help me search.

speaker: Bron
en: Ah, yes! Now I remember. It must be behind there.

speaker: Bron
en: Well done, friend!

speaker: Bron
en: Ah! Look at that!

speaker: Eivor
en: That's no horn.

speaker: Bron
en: Let me have a look.

speaker: Home Owner
en: Hold!

speaker: Home Owner
en: Thieves! You filthy Dane, get out of my house!

speaker: Eivor
en: This man told me this house was his.

speaker: Home Owner
en: Have you any idea how important I am? I shall have you both flayed and hung from the city gates.

speaker: Bron
en: Friend, it's all a simple misunderstanding.

speaker: Home Owner
en: If you were indeed deceived, Dane, you'll return my bibelot and help me kill this villain.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bron is my friend. I will defend him to your death.

speaker: Bron
en: Bless you, Dane!

speaker: Home Owner
en: Prepare to die, piles of horse droppings!

speaker: Eivor
en: So what was this all about?

speaker: Bron
en: He bragged about that object all over the village. Keep it, friend. You deserve it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here is your item. Bron here is a liar and a thief. He deserves what he gets.

speaker: Bron
en: No!

speaker: Eivor
en: So much for him.

speaker: Home Owner
en: You've helped me, Dane. I will not send you before the magistrate for robbery. I trust you are grateful.

speaker: Eivor
en: I regret only that I did not hear the battle-song of Ragnar's horn.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will join the main body of the war-band and lead the assault. I want you to scale the rear face of the hill and draw fighters away from the front. Allow none to escape.

speaker: Viking 3
en: I can hear the Valkyrie singing! Come, shield friends, it is the dawn of our immortality!

speaker: Hrolfr
en: You're too late, Raven. My father has what he came for.

speaker: Viking 2
en: You must be the younger son.

speaker: Hrolfr
en: I am Hrolfr. Learn it well before I kill you.

speaker: Viking 2
en: You and your father will wander in Niflheim before this night is done.

speaker: Hrolfr
en: We die in glory or not at all, little bird! Now come, face Hrolfr and fall!

speaker: Hrolfr
en: Well fought, bird. But it avails you nothing. Baubles you shall have, but the real treasure is gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've claimed the hall! Well done. What have you there?

speaker: Viking 2
en: A trunk, brimming with treasure, lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: The same drops of wrought sunlight which drew Sigurd's eyes south, down the Volga. What of the scrolls?

speaker: Viking 2
en: Scrolls? There are none here, Eivor.

speaker: Jora
en: Eivor! We have found a secret path out of the hall!

speaker: Viking 2
en: What is this about, Eivor? We've won, have we not?

speaker: Eivor
en: Kjotve, that worm in Fenris' ass. He must have made off with the scrolls. Come, we must away. We cannot let Kjotve escape.

speaker: Erlend
en: This quest will put me in the ground. I am lost and honor-bound. Where is honor to be found?

speaker: Erlend
en: You arrived without a sound!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you a skald? I have never heard poetry shouted in this way.

speaker: Erlend
en: A skald? O, no, not at all. I am truly looking for honor, and have become lost as a result.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are looking for honor here? It is a bit remote.

speaker: Erlend
en: I am the seventh son of a seventh son. I am expected to bring great honor to my family, but everything has been done!

speaker: Erlend
en: My uncles and brothers have all had great victories or even greater deaths! There is nothing left for me to do! The gods have been deaf to my pleas, but you are here.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, you want a great victory from me... or a great death?

speaker: Erlend
en: No! I want to live! And I could not possibly hope to win against you.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is true.

speaker: Erlend
en: But maybe you could lead me to a victory?

speaker: Eivor
en: I can tell by looking at you, you are not a great warrior. You know it too, there is no reason to deny this. I could bring you a chance at honor... an animal of some kind. Something you could handle.

speaker: Erlend
en: Yes, yes! That could work! I could add a few details, nothing too exaggerated. Skalds do it all the time.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, now you are a skald? Do not go anywhere. I will only do this once.

speaker: Erlend
en: I will be here. On my honor. Make sure to bring me a beast!

speaker: Eivor
en: Now, win your honor!

speaker: Erlend
en: They are much bigger up close! I do not think I can do this! I DO NOT THINK I CAN DO THIS!

speaker: Eivor
en: Come, Erlend! Honor calls!"'

speaker: Erlend
en: Waaaa!

speaker: Erlend
en: I did it! What an incredible fight!

speaker: Eivor
en: You got a few stabs in. How was your... first kill?

speaker: Erlend
en: Gods! I have never felt so alive! My hugr (mind) soars on ravens' wings!

speaker: Eivor
en: With this rebirth comes a new name. From this day, you will be called... Erlend Wolf-Whip, Killer of Curs.

speaker: Erlend
en: It suits me! You know, now that I think about it, I think my story should be told in verse. Farewell, Beast-Baiter!

speaker: Eivor
en: Not great, as far as deaths go, but neither was he.

speaker: Olga
en: Elspeth, I was wondering... have you seen Hilde's brother about?

speaker: Elspeth
en: Olav the Unlucky? Why, are you sweet on the fellow? Is that it?

speaker: Olga
en: No, no, just worried about him, that's all.

speaker: Elspeth
en: Ah, well. I have some bad news for you, lass. Gorm comes roaring up shouting "Wot's all this? Who's been in my gear?" An' he stares right at Olav.

speaker: Olga
en: O, sweet Olav! The poor man. What then? Was he all right?

speaker: Elspeth
en: Olav, he tries to run, but says, "I weren't stealin', I was tradin'!" But Gorm would have none of that.

speaker: Olga
en: I can't bear to hear another word! Good Olav, to think he may have been hurt. Or worse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Trading? Who could this Olav trade with here?

speaker: Worker Woman
en: Grab a shovel from Gorm's storehouse.

speaker: Worker Man
en: No. It is a rotten place, that storehouse. Have you seen it? A bloody mess.

speaker: Worker Woman
en: If it's a mess, then clean it, dung-brain.

speaker: Worker Man
en: He beat Olav bad. Thrashed him and locked him away in the storehouse.

speaker: Worker Woman
en: You know why? Because Olav stole from Gorm and got caught. You're not stealing, are you?

speaker: Worker Man
en: N-no.

speaker: Worker Woman
en: Good. Now less whining, more working.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gorm's storehouse. A good place to start.

speaker: Aud
en: Helgi, that fine honey mead you have. Pour me a horn, would you?

speaker: Helgi
en: I have ale for you, Aud. But no mead.

speaker: Aud
en: What? We had a whole cask.

speaker: Helgi
en: Gorm smashed it over Olav's head, right there in the storehouse.

speaker: Aud
en: Thor's hammer, I am done with this place. Send me home, Helgi. I heard Gorm took a strap to Olav?

speaker: Helgi
en: Yes. The fool stole goods to trade with the jar (natives).

speaker: Aud
en: So Gorm dragged him off to the storehouse for a beating? That explains the mess.

speaker: Eivor
en: This Olav was trading with locals. Good to know there are other folk around.

speaker: Guard 1
en: No, you tell Gorm he got out of the storehouse.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Gorm is not here. So until he is, I won't worry on it.

speaker: Guard 1
en: You should. You are the one who lost him.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Maybe so, but I am sailing back to England at first light. May Loki eat this place.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Where is Gorm at anyway? We have supplies waiting for him.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Only Olav would know. But he had a kind of accident.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Olav the Unlucky. The fool earned his nickname.

speaker: Guard 2
en: This whole cursed venture is unlucky if you ask me.

speaker: Eivor
en: This Olav cannot bear any loyalty to Gorm. Could be he will aid me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Smashed crates. Somebody crawled off, left a trail of blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: Finding Olav may be the key to finding Gorm. Or at least, a helpful ally.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone picked the lock and got away. Or was hauled off. Could be a trail.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone broke through here, made quite a mess. Could be Olav went this way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Footprints. Might be Olav's.

speaker: Eivor
en: This trail leads to high ground. Good, I can get my bearings.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods. Never have I seen such a place. Quiet. And not a stone building in sight.

speaker: Iroquois Man
en: Iah nowén:ton tékken kí:ken ión:kwe. (I have never seen this woman.)

speaker: Iroquois Woman
en: Oh kwah niiawen'hátie'? Ó:ia ión:kwe iah kèn:'en tekanákere' onkwaná:takon ísewe's. (What's happening? Another stranger in our village.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Those two carry themselves like leaders. It's worth a try.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hail friends. Do you... do we understand one another?

speaker: Konwahawíhshon
en: Ó:ia Kaniatara'kehró:non. Tiok nahò:ten thikà:te' kí:ken ión:kwe. (Another woman coming from the sea. There's something different about her.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Do any of you speak ? Or ?

speaker: Konwahawíhshon
en: Kí:ken otsi'tèn:'a wa'onátshi'ne kí:ken ión:kwe. Thikà:te' nen' nè:'e. (This woman became friends with a bird. That's a rare blessing.)

speaker: Eivor
en: This is Sýnin. Her name means Insight.

speaker: Konwahawíhshon
en: Ientia'ténhawe' kí:ken tsi nón:we ó:ia Kaniatara'kehró:non íthre's tánon' enhináhskon'. Enhoia'takéhnha' tóka' enhonatenróhake' kí:ken. (I'll bring her to the other man coming from the sea that lives in the village, and we'll give her to him. He'll help her if they become friends.)

speaker: Eivor
en: Sýnin, you made us some friends.

speaker: Eivor
en: These huts and clothes. Am I in Midgard still?

speaker: Eivor
en: Waterfalls are places of power in the old s.

speaker: Konwahawíhshon
en: Kí:ken ó:ia Kaniatara'kehró:non rotáhska. (The other man coming from the sea will be happy.)

speaker: Olav
en: I hung in the tree! , you hear me!

speaker: Eivor
en: There is a language I know well. But the words are mind-sick.

speaker: Konwahawíhshon
en: Sathón:te' ken thí:ken? Rotia'tátkon. Satshétsen't tóka' enhskwé:ni'. Thó:ner é:ren enhtshia'tenhá:wihte' ne kèn:'en. (Did you hear that? He is a witch. Get rid of him if you can before he brings it here.)

speaker: Olav
en: Then I threw my eye in the well! This is wisdom!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sounds like the ranting of a seer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are you?

speaker: Olav
en: Olav, I am. Olav. Called the Unlucky, but don't you believe it.

speaker: Eivor
en: And where is

speaker: Olav
en: Promise you will do it quick!

speaker: Eivor
en: What?

speaker: Olav
en: Do not stab me from behind, drengr. Like Sigurd and the dragon. Please!

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not here to kill you. I have come for Gorm.

speaker: Olav
en: N-not here to kill me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not today.

speaker: Olav
en: O, stay clear of Gorm, then. He is not a good man, not a good man at all. Why would you need to see such a terrible man?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a matter of honor, and Gorm owes me a great debt. Let us leave it at that.

speaker: Olav
en: O, good. Yes, yes. Honor is good. Olav will help. Olav will help you so much. Honor is the only thing, yes. The only thing.

speaker: Eivor
en: My reasons matter not. Will you help me find him or no?

speaker: Olav
en: O yes, yes! Olav is helpful. Olav helps in your nameless feud. Olav obeys! I will tell you everything, even the secrets of earth and sky!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you always pry into the affairs of others?

speaker: Olav
en: No, no! Olav makes talk only. Olav has no one to talk to. I have hidden myself away, to wait for now, and think of riddles no one will hear. But I will help with your mysterious errand. I will, I will.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw signs of a struggle at your camp. Did something happen between you and Gorm?

speaker: Olav
en: Nothing to speak of. He, uh, did not care for me trading with the villagers here. Beat me and put me in chains. I slipped away, free! Not so unlucky, am I? Still alive. Yes, still alive.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Point me toward Gorm.

speaker: Olav
en: Not possible. He is away. Far away at the camps in these woods. All well-guarded. Might be at any one.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why camps? Is he settling here? Or searching for something?

speaker: Olav
en: Searching. Yes. Always searching. And never finding, the mean, mean bacraut (asshole).

speaker: Eivor
en: And how do I find these camps?

speaker: Olav
en: I can show you. Follow, follow, follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Olav, would you tell me something?

speaker: Olav
en: Anything Olav can tell, Olav will tell, my new and big friend!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why would Gorm cross the sea to this nameless wilderness? It seems a great risk for so little.

speaker: Olav
en: Gorm carries with him a crystal that talks. It tells him where to go and what to do!

speaker: Eivor
en: A talking crystal?

speaker: Olav
en: It is truth! The elf-stone tells him to seek, and so he seeks. And when it says dig, he digs. Such a mystery!

speaker: Eivor
en: What is he digging for?

speaker: Olav
en: That is a mystery he will not tell. But my guess is the best guess. He seeks the door to Jotunheim.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm.

speaker: Olav
en: Look! Out across the river. One of Gorm's camps. All look like that. All of them.

speaker: Eivor
en: They are well-guarded, you say?

speaker: Olav
en: O yes. By fierce men. Warriors who attack any stranger on sight. Any one! And they are all well-armed. Not like you! As well-equipped as a stable hand.

speaker: Eivor
en: It does not take much to kill a man.

speaker: Olav
en: But sharp steel helps, o yes.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are not wrong. I could use better weapons.

speaker: Olav
en: Olav will help. Gather ore and hides to barter for war gear.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ore and hides, I can find out there?

speaker: Olav
en: Yes yes! Some in the woods. Much more at Gorm's camps. Then trade it all with the people here. Easy as a smile, yes, yes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not understand their language. Can you translate for me?

speaker: Olav
en: No need, no. We talk with signs. Just walk up to a trader and start trading. Take this. Some goods to get you started.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you for this, Olav. And until I say otherwise, speak nothing of this to anyone.

speaker: Eivor
en: Might be a good idea to trade, now that I am here.

speaker: Wallace
en: Thank you for this. Whether fur, meat, or bone, we will provide only the finest.

speaker: Petra
en: And if you intend to go hunting... consider bringing us your kills. We will prepare the hides and heads.

speaker: Wallace
en: Aye. I've been mounting Petra's trophies for years. And she's a discerning woman.

speaker: Petra
en: In all things.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll keep that in mind. Enjoy your new home.

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor. You seem to be someone with a penchant for... trophies.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do like victories, but I rarely keep a record of them.

speaker: Petra
en: Your weapons show the marks of great battles. And you walk with a pride that speaks to your triumphs. Am I wrong?

speaker: Eivor
en: You are not. Why do you ask?

speaker: Petra
en: To bolster our trade, of course. Wallace is the finest tanner and taxidermist in all of England. If you wish the tales of your hunts to outlast you, there is no better way than making trophies of your kills. If you defeat a rare and worthy creature, bring it to us. We will display it for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: A good idea. Keepsakes to adorn the longhouse. Thank you, Petra.

speaker: Petra
en: O, and before you go, could you spare a moment? For a small favor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not have the time right now. But I will return."

speaker: Eivor
en: Petra. Good day.

speaker: Petra
en: Ah, you're back.

speaker: Petra
en: For the past few evenings, I have heard the howling of a pack of wolves just beyond the border of our woods. Unchecked, they will ravage the wild game in this area. And once the deer are dead, they may turn to us.

speaker: Eivor
en: You feel we should drive them off?

speaker: Petra
en: I would eliminate them entirely. With your permission, of course. And your help, if possible.

speaker: Eivor
en: A good idea. I will join you now.

speaker: Petra
en: Good. A pack of wolves is a foolish thing to underestimate. Let's go.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not have the time right now. But I will return."

speaker: Eivor
en: Petra. Good day.

speaker: Petra
en: Ah, you're back.

speaker: Petra
en: This way. I last saw them prowling around just up the hill.

speaker: Eivor
en: You lead, I'll follow.

speaker: Petra
en: Our settlement is in quite a nice spot. Beautiful terrain. And the animals here are healthy and populous. But wolves are a worry. It may be why the Ragnarssons moved on. Humans upset the balance of nature, and nature pushed back.

speaker: Eivor
en: By attacking us?

speaker: Petra
en: A wolf will do whatever it takes. They were displaced, now they come to our door.

speaker: Petra
en: Come this way.

speaker: Petra
en: Look here. Bread crumbs and crusts. They must have stolen something from Tarben's store. Or off a table somewhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: You saw breadcrumbs from where you stood?

speaker: Petra
en: They stand out clearly from the soil and grass. See there?

speaker: Petra
en: Come this way. Ah. Smell that? That's a male wolf, marking his territory, warding off the competition.

speaker: Eivor
en: How do you know it's a male?

speaker: Petra
en: Different odor. You pick it up.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you come to be such a skilled tracker?

speaker: Petra
en: My family were hunters and trackers. From further east than you have ever seen, I imagine. But I've lived in England for most of my life. This is where we found Wallace.

speaker: Eivor
en: You two are siblings as Sigurd and I are siblings. Bound by honor, not blood.

speaker: Petra
en: Yes. To hear my mother tell it, we came upon Wallace abandoned... a babe in the woods. We took him in.

speaker: Petra
en: Look. The wolves made a kill here. They're in the area.

speaker: Petra
en: Those trails... they must have dragged the poor beast away. We're getting closer.

speaker: Petra
en: Ah! See those teeth marks on the carcass? They're different.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is the pack's doing. Not just one.

speaker: Petra
en: That's right. Let's go on.

speaker: Eivor
en: So your family found Wallace in the woods?

speaker: Petra
en: We were traveling through the forest when I spotted a white elk ahead of us. I chased it, hoping to take it down. I lost it as I came to a clearing, and there on the ground... was a wee babe. Our little Wallace. Swaddled and alone.

speaker: Petra
en: Ah! Look at that. The pattern on the grass. They slept here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am impressed, Petra. You have a raw skill.

speaker: Petra
en: You have seen nothing just yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: So you saw a white elk... and that led you to Wallace?

speaker: Petra
en: That's right. It felt fated. We took him in and nursed him back to health. I was scarcely more than a toddler myself, then. And from that day forward, we were raised as brother and sister.

speaker: Petra
en: Hmm... these kills are fresh. They're likely near enough to hear us. Probably fled the scene not long ago.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Ah! Help!

speaker: Eivor
