en: I think we've found our wolves!

speaker: Petra
en: You there! Get to cover! Eivor, with me. Let's end this.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am at your side.

speaker: Petra
en: Careful, they're aggressive!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Keep back! Keep back!

speaker: Eivor
en: There. That should be all of them.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, thank you! Thank you so much! Both of you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you all right? Were those your sheep?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: They were, God take 'em. They were all I had in the world. Poor blighters never stood a chance. I lost my cows some months back. Now the sheep are gone. Frowning Jesus, what sort of farmer am I?

speaker: Petra
en: I'm sorry for you loss. With the wolves gone, you can recover in peace.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Not without the blessings of God, I won't. But I shall try.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have your life, farmer. With that alone you can always rebuild.

speaker: Petra
en: Eivor, hold... I hear something.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: What? I don't hear anything.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O! Goodness gracious me! Felix! Rosemary! My beauties! You are alive! Come here, my precious angels!

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, that worked out.

speaker: Petra
en: This was grand, Eivor. You hunt almost as well as you fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Give me a few weeks, I'll learn to track as well as you. Or better.

speaker: Petra
en: I would be happy to be so humbled.

speaker: Eivor
en: This was a joy, Petra. Do not hesitate to call on me the next time you spot any errant beasts.

speaker: Petra
en: You are the first on my list, Eivor. See you soon.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: It's searing my flesh! O God! The pain is unbearable! I cannot move! Help me! Help! Please!

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened? Were you bit?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, yes. Snakebit. Just like you!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Attack!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You and your foul brothers and sisters have churned the very soil of this sacred land. No more! You're going back north where you belong! We will rid England of your kind for good!

speaker: Eivor
en: Feeble.

speaker: Eivor
en: My thanks, for your contribution.

speaker: The Infinite Noise of Men
en: was a virtual representation of one of Eivor Varinsdottir's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Come on, Bertin's been gone for too long. That fool is dead! Me and you, we can get that damned King of Rats.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: I have a bad feeling there will be a trap waiting for us. You can't take the Rat King lightly...

speaker: Mae
en: Hold tight. Just hold on tight. O, please don't fall. The wind is strong, but you are stronger. Just hold on.

speaker: Mae
en: Careful, please! This leaf cannot fall.

speaker: Mae
en: Stay back. Do not touch this tree!

speaker: Eivor
en: All right. What is your name?

speaker: Mae
en: Mae...

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor. Something about this tree important to you?

speaker: Mae
en: It's the leaves. My father said he would return home before they'd all fallen to the ground. And now only one remains.

speaker: Eivor
en: And still no return.

speaker: Mae
en: It's been six weeks... Six weeks since he's gone to Lincoln in search of work. I wish he stayed. Just one more season. He was so sure the fields wouldn't yield, but we could have tried!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your father sounds like an honest man. Went looking for work to take care of you. He would make every effort to return home, and that is reason enough to hope. But this... it serves no purpose to fret like you are.

speaker: Mae
en: Then what should I do?

speaker: Eivor
en: Carry on as if he were to return tomorrow, no matter what happens to this leaf.

speaker: Mae
en: Yes... yes, I shall do as you say. My father would want the same. Thank you, Eivor.

speaker: Mae
en: Maybe... maybe I'll wait just a little bit longer. 'Til the goats begin to bray, or... yes, a little longer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Six weeks is much too long for a father to leave a child. If he was going to return, he would have done so by now.

speaker: Mae
en: O, no...

speaker: Eivor
en: You can talk to this leaf, pray to your god, shout at the stars, but your father's fate was forged long ago. Like mine. Like yours.

speaker: Mae
en: Stop talking like that! He'll come back! He said so! Just... just leave me be.

speaker: Mae
en: He'll be back, you'll see! Before the leaves fall, just like he said!

speaker: Eivor
en: All I can say for certain is that this leaf will fall. You should hope for the best, but prepare for the worst. That way, if your father never returns, your heart will not break. But if he does, you will weep with joy.

speaker: Mae
en: I haven't thought of it that way, but it is a simple idea to live by. You're right. I must carry on, with or without him. Thank you, Eivor. May the Lord be with you.

speaker: Mae
en: Maybe... maybe I'll wait just a little bit longer. 'Til the goats begin to bray, or... yes, a little longer.

speaker: Mae
en: Ah! What! No! no no no! You... I suppose that's it, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: Carry on with your life, Mae. Everything will be all right.

speaker: Mae
en: No! You wicked devil! I told you not to do that!

speaker: Eivor
en: It is for your own good, Mae. Your father would want you to carry on with your life, not waste it away like this.

speaker: Mae
en: Leave me alone! And never come back! I don't ever want to see you again!

speaker: Sif
en: Alvar is an old fool, trying to live his dream. But when do we bring in the harvest?

speaker: Alvar
en: Listen up, crew! Sharpen your blades and your wits. We will go a-pillaging we will! Blow, winds! Fill my sails! Carry us across seas and fjords! We'll soak the beach in blood, we will. No gold hoard is safe from us!

speaker: Eivor
en: You are a long way from home, Norseman.

speaker: Alvar
en: Ah! I may be, but my sixty winters have not slaked my taste for raiding. Ans I have the finest crew on the sea.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have no crew.

speaker: Alvar
en: Do you not see them? Stout fellows all. And you! Make yourself useful and help prepare the ship, friend.

speaker: Alvar
en: Yes! Bring ore. We'll need to repair weapons and shields.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you have no blacksmith.

speaker: Alvar
en: Ah! Nonsense. Black Bjorn is about somewhere. He's our man.

speaker: Alvar
en: Bring planks! We'll face teeth-jarring storms. The ship will cry for repairs.

speaker: Alvar
en: Thor in Heaven, we'll need hay! We'll use it to set fortress walls afire!

speaker: Alvar
en: We're ready to launch out on the roiling sea! Summon Skarde, Knut, and the rest of the crew! Blow your horn!

speaker: Alvar
en: O, by the gods! Will you blow that damn horn?

speaker: Alvar
en: The battle-horn is sounded! Men! Make the blood-rain fall in a thunderstorm!

speaker: Eivor
en: Wolves!

speaker: Alvar
en: Enemies! Battle is upon us, men! Let none survive our bloodlust! Die, you miserable Saxons! Gah! These Saxons fight with their teeth!

speaker: Alvar
en: Huh! That was a battle for the ages, that was!

speaker: Eivor
en: You're lucky to still be alive.

speaker: Alvar
en: The crew fought like heroes. No Saxon survived, just like the old days!

speaker: Eivor
en: Friend, there was no crew. Only you and me. Your Saxons were but mangy wolves.

speaker: Alvar
en: No! Bjorn, Skarde, they were all here, fighting at my side. Heh! Just as they did in the raids of yore.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gone now. Today you led their shades on a ghost ship. Your raiding days are done. Your crew feasts in Valhalla.

speaker: Alvar
en: Can it—can it—can it be? Huh... If so, it was worth it. One last raid. Thank you, my friend.

speaker: Sif
en: Has my fond husband calmed down yet? It's soon time to bring in the harvest.

speaker: Vagn
en: Eivor, those clues you've found... they speak of a river on the Northern border of . I've marked it on the map for you. But caution! My scouts tell me the area is well-guarded. If you are ready for the challenge, I say let's go! You are strong enough to take on whatever comes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ready.

speaker: Vagn
en: Good luck! May you succeed where many have failed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vagn! Have you cooked up any new legends for me to go chasing?

speaker: Vagn
en: Eivor, you make it sound like I'm telling tales! But now that you mention it...

speaker: Eivor
en: And is this Lugh real or will I be chasing after another myth?

speaker: Vagn
en: Will that matter when you are wearing a new set of armor?

speaker: Eivor
en: No.

speaker: Vagn
en: Before you go, I've added more stock to my list of wares. Take a look when you have a free moment. O, and my scouts tell me that the rivers have been replenished and are ripe for raiding!

speaker: Eivor
en: Vagn! I found more clues for you to decipher.

speaker: Vagn
en: I am eager to see where these will lead us!

speaker: Vagn
en: Ah ha! The rest of the armor set is hidden across the River Erriff. A quick word of warning, Eivor. There is a Champion who resides at the end of the river. If past encounters are to be trusted, he might be holding on to Lugh's legendary spear.

speaker: Eivor
en: If past encounters are to be trusted, he will not be in possession of that spear for long.

speaker: Vagn
en: Ah, Eivor. I have been meaning to mention to you... the Legacy of Saint George.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this some sort of ridiculous legend?

speaker: Vagn
en: It is! The story is that the revered saint's legacy, lost for hundreds of years, is divided and hidden across England.

speaker: Eivor
en: Such a great treasure and yet no one has any idea where even a single piece could be?

speaker: Vagn
en: Until now. For months I have heard whispers that match the stories. And now my scouts have returned with a map! The Rivers Severn and Exe both play a part in George's legend.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very well. That is where we will search.

speaker: Vagn
en: But keep an eye out for hints of other hiding places. Nothing is know for certain. Whether any of it actually exists, I cannot say... Care to go find out?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sounds tempting. I'll go.

speaker: Vagn
en: Good luck!

speaker: Hytham
en: Eivor, there you are. I have something for you. A message... quite strange.

speaker: Eivor
en: Something for me? What is it?

speaker: Hytham
en: A letter, requesting your presence in the southwest. A village called Athelnay.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing strange about a summons for me, is there?

speaker: Hytham
en: It is not the recipient I find strange. It is the sender. The letter is signed, A Poor Fellow-Soldier of Christ.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. Our mysterious partner.

speaker: Hytham
en: For a short time, I hoped it might be Basim feeding us the names of these targets. He seemed the most likely man for a time.

speaker: Eivor
en: Only one way to discover the truth. Thank you, Hytham. I will take care of this.

speaker: Arne
en: Hog's golden bristles, Frode, how did I let you talk me into this?

speaker: Frode
en: Stop clucking like a laying hen, I'm the one with the broken leg. At least grab Old Hisser's tale while you're up there!

speaker: Arne
en: Something is hissing. Jörmungandr's fangs, are there snakes up here too?

speaker: Frode
en: Alright, alright. Well, you'll have to get down somehow. Can you see a haystack or something?

speaker: Arne
en: A haystack? Are you mad! From this height? That's certain death. No, my fate is sealed. I will just wait up here to die.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone is stuck?

speaker: Frode
en: My brother. Chasing some foolish legend that if you see Old Hisser from above and catch his tail, he will grant you a wish.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what of your leg?

speaker: Frode
en: Likely sprained trying to climb up to rescue him. We are a sorry pair.

speaker: Arne
en: You made it up! You truly are a brave one!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll help you down, but how is a big, strong Norse like yourself afraid of heights!

speaker: Arne
en: And snakes! I don't know how I let my brother talk me into these schemes. I think I just give in to his endless goading. But I'm sick to the back teeth of him, "Climb up, Arne! Go in that cave of wolves, Arne! Eat that red mushroom!"

speaker: Eivor
en: Siblings are a source of great joy, and equal misery. I too have a brother.

speaker: Arne
en: Does yours put you in the maw of death every opportunity he gets?

speaker: Eivor
en: Come, let's get you down. And perhaps you can tell him how you feel.

speaker: Arne
en: Talk of my feelings? To my brother? I would rather let the snakes gnaw on my tender parts.

speaker: Eivor
en: This way.

speaker: Arne
en: It's too high to get down from here!

speaker: Eivor
en: There, the ladder. Watch your step.

speaker: Arne
en: Which way now?

speaker: Eivor
en: This way.

speaker: Arne
en: There! Another slithering devil waiting to get me!

speaker: Arne
en: Yes! I'm alive! Brother!

speaker: Frode
en: Thank you, stranger. For bringing this waste of breath back to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are welcome... but what is the story you spoke of? Old Hisser?

speaker: Arne
en: A pretty legend. He who catches Old Hisser's tail will find their heart's wish granted.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found such a story in a manuscript. Up in the tower.

speaker: Arne
en: Then may it bring you more luck than it did us. Maybe you will even solve the serpent's mystery.

speaker: Arne
en: We have followed England's legends and found little but peril. It is time to hang up our well-worn boots.

speaker: Frode
en: Farewell! May Odin litter your path with riches.

speaker: Eivor
en: Goodbye. Keep each other safe, for a good brother is the truest treasure from the gods.

speaker: Frode
en: Now see, you big lump? All that wailing, and it was as easy as a hop and a jump.

speaker: Arne
en: Keep that up and I'll leave you here for the wolves. Ah no, look at your leg. Is it truly broken?

speaker: Frode
en: No, sprained is all. But I'd like to see you get by without me. Couldn't even climb down a ladder without mewing like a newborn.

speaker: Egwald
en: Please... I seek a strong union to establish my kingdom. This is the island kingdom of Norsexe! I am King Egwald himself, lord and protector of this verdant land.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is your kingdom, you say?

speaker: Egwald
en: Indeed it is. Norsexe, and I am its first and reigning king, Egwald. And as soverign, I seek a keen ally to secure my strength.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kingdom? This island here?

speaker: Egwald
en: Yes, from shore to shore. My brothers and I came upon this unclaimed land some months ago and found it suited to our ambitions. Sadly, my brothers were drowned in a terrible squall soon after, along with our riches. There was an arm ring among them. To you I offer this arm ring, in exchange for my loyalty. Find the ring among the wreck and you may call a king your friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: A good arm ring can be as important as blood to the heart. If I find it, I will let you know.

speaker: Eivor
en: A fine golden oath-hoop. One worthy of a king.

speaker: Tattered Letter with Raven Blood on It
en: Dear Ubba, King of the Danes, Our brother Egwald of Nothing has gone mad and locked us in his longship. I write this letter with a quill in my teeth plucked from a loyal falcon. This letter is sealed with our blood, we will fight alongside you if you please send men to kill our mad brother who claims an island is his own yet cannot claim loyalty from his own kin who fought and brought him across the North Sea to the land of the Angles. Egfried and Sigwald of Norway

speaker: Chronicles of Norsexian Kings
en: First of my kind, I have come from the ancient fold in order to secure my legacy. This land of the Angles is not fit for my brothers, usurpers to the Ancient Kingdom of Norsexe. They must be treated with the same dishonor they have treated me with when they state, "He is no king." I rule. No other. Egwald Rex of Norsexe.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found your arm ring. Amidst the wreckage of your ship.

speaker: Egwald
en: By all that is great, I cannot believe my eyes and ears! Now, you are pledged to the Kingdom of Norsexe! That will show him.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am honored to forge an alliance with your stock, King Egwald of Norsexe. Long may you reign.

speaker: Egwald
en: Thank you. As you are pledged to me, I am pledged to you. If ever I have an army to lend, you may make use of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your past is dubious. I cannot trust a man who lost his brothers so easily. And so suspiciously. What really happened?

speaker: Egwald
en: Nothing! The arm-ring is mine. Mine! This kingdom was to be one of the greatest in England. The ring-shine has blinded you! Now, I blind you with blood, usurper!

speaker: Egwald
en: You have broken a sacred alliance with the greatest of kingdoms!

speaker: Havi
en: Here is the tree Hyrrokin mentioned, its bark cut deep by Jörmungandr's sharp scales. I should look around for the missing cauldron.

speaker: Havi
en: Steel and flesh met here, but jötnar leave no corpses.

speaker: Havi
en: They turn to earth when they die. Back to the tilth they came from.

speaker: Havi
en: A ditch was dug so the cart would break a wheel. This was an ambush.

speaker: Havi
en: This cart bears the sign of Ægir.

speaker: Havi
en: Something huge was dragged this way.

speaker: Havi
en: If it was Ægir's cauldron they dragged through here, it must be large indeed.

speaker: Havi
en: The trail of destruction leads toward that giant root.

speaker: Havi
en: They slaughtered that animal for it's innards and used them in their ritual. Likely the thieves employed this magic to hide their loot.

speaker: Havi
en: The mitten of the great jötun Skrýmir, dropped here long ago. Maybe the thieves took their burden inside.

speaker: Havi
en: Soft moss, all around. Hard to imagine this place once fitted a hand.

speaker: Havi
en: The missing cauldron. But how did they get it into this cave?

speaker: Havi
en: That was not there before. Hard to know what is real in this realm of illusion.

speaker: Havi
en: There must be a way to reach it.

speaker: Jotnar
en: To arms! Ægir sends allies to claim back his cauldron!

speaker: Havi
en: This cave is home to these jötnar. They must have fallen far to live in such cheerless squalor. It seems his sons have been hiding here, awaiting their chance to take it back.

speaker: Havi
en: Too big to carry. But things are not always as they seem in Jotunheim.

speaker: Havi
en: The cauldron has grown smaller. I'm getting the measure of these illusions.

speaker: Havi
en: This cauldron should be enough to win Suttungr's favor.

speaker: Havi
en: I could go to Utgard now, but a gift for Gunlodr would improve my chances at getting the Mead.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Erik Loyalskull
en: If you come looking for bears, there are none living here. Not now. But I have a better proposition than a rousing hunt. If you are a true drengr, a warrior with honor running like sunlight in your veins, then you may help me fulfill my destiny.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: You're a long way from any warm hearth, warrior. Is this where you call home?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Erik Loyalskull
en: My name is Erik Loyalskull. The great King Ragnar Lothbrok named me such, when we fought, tearing up the fields of England. We built families, overthrew kingdoms, sailed mountains, fought for whole seasons, and now... now he is gone.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: All of Norway laments the passing of King Ragnar. I cannot imagine this sorrow his warriors now feel.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Erik Loyalskull
en: We are but six who remain, his most loyal drengir. Yet without his guiding light, his strength and video, we are lost. It was in this cavern that I knew my life was tied to Ragnar's. We were young, hunting a bear, when we chanced upon this spot. He killed it with nothing but a knife. Leapt on its back, held tight, writhing like a fly on a dragon, he stayed put and it was done. Together we celebrated the kill, as if we had felled the beast together. That is when I knew I would live and die for this man. I did not die beside my lord in Ælla's pit of snakes. But I can make amends. Fight me, warrior. Send me to meet him in Odin's hall.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: I must wait for the ideal time to fight such a warrior of your class, drengr. Have patience.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Erik Loyalskull
en: I will wait.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: It is with great honor I will fight a true drengr. When you're ready.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Erik Loyalskull
en: Very well. For Ragnar Lothbrok, the true King of Norway.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Erik Loyalskull
en: For Ragnar, for glory, for the wandering drengir do I raise my blade. You honor me with your skill and ferocity. That is all that matters. You are a true drengr. Ragnar would have liked you!

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Erik Loyalskull
en: A fitting end to honorable warring. Now I go to see my brother, he who laughed at death, scourge of all England, Ragnar Lothbrok.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Farewell, drengr. Listen for hoof-beats, and follow the Valkyries home.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: The nets are well set, you have stocks for a hundred moons. You will live a long and hearty life.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor Thorsson
en: But father, you are not too ill to stay!

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: But I am. The weavers have sent me many portents. I only await a proper death, 'til the family axe of honor passes to you.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: The air is filled with the smell of fish guts. Your catch appears generous. Your nets overflow with silver stock. You are lucky.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: Good warrior, you carry yourself with the spirit of a drengr I am a drengr too.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: In fish monger's slacks? Is this your way of hiding? Or protecting those around you?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: My life has had many chapters. Ragnar Lothbrok himself started as a farmer, you know. He often envied my choice.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: You rode with the Great Army of Ragnar?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: I did. And it was here in England that I saw a land so fertile you could spit and food would grow. Waters teeming with fish. I met a Saxon lady, Æthelswig, and we have made a fine life for ourselves. The best clams in all of East Anglia. But now I must show my son the way of the drengr. How to die with honor.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: I respect your desire for an honorable death.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: I want my son to watch. He should have the final word when I pass. He will not see me die on a bed coughing like a crow.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: I accept your fight. We will show your boy how drengr do their bedding.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: Do you hear this son? Today you will see the color of the blood that made you! The color of courage and honor above all. Any weapon will do!

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: Now you see son, we are drengr.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: Ah yes, the boil of battle! Its heat returns to me! Watch me son! A true drengr can win a battle with a twig or stone! Son... do not look away! My end is near!

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor the Fish Monger
en: I have reached the glory-gate. Think of me, my boy. My dear love. Now you know.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor Thorsson
en: Father, I... I understand. I see the glory you spoke of. Go now to Valhalla, and join Ragnar in the war-eternal.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Your father is a fine warrior. A drengr to the end.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Thor Thorsson
en: One day I will honor him. And make myself a drengr.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Nokkfylla Shine-Eye
en: I am not normal. I am beyond anything that any man has ever witnessed. I am a wound that festers. A shit that stinks in the sun. Trolls fear me. I am mind-fucked. Once a drengr, now a draugr. A walking dead. Rotten within and without. Fuck.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Greetings. Is this battlefield yours?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Nokkfylla Shine-Eye
en: This is the gutter of an unchained drengr. A lost drengr. That is what I am I am vile. I should not be allowed to suck on clean air.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: A drengr kills honorably, with glory and pride. Were these men not innocent?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Nokkfylla Shine-Eye
en: Many of them were. Many were not. Their blood is now mingled and it stinks of the iron of my blade. What an end. Beloved Ragnar Lothbrok, he always kept me in check. He steadied the ship of my hugr (mind). Without him, I have lost my bearings. I scare myself. Not a thread of decency remains. The drengr I was, I have lost him. Would you end this suffering? For me?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: You live with a great pain. One that cannot be eased by a ' (penance), nor a reckoning.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Nokkfylla Shine-Eye
en: Yes. You know my pain. And you look as through you could end it. Do this, then, a final kindness for an unworthy wretch.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Lost drengr, I will fight you. And help you find what Ragnar gave you.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Nokkfylla Shine-Eye
en: Loki's children, take me one and all.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Nokkfylla Shine-Eye
en: This one arm has learned the tricks of both! Beware! Odin owes you! Death to us both! Go meet your god! Gar! Odin! Trolls! Bra! Take your last breath!

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Nokkfylla Shine-Eye
en: You have lanced me, Nokkfylla, the fetid boil. Let this death be the only good I have done since my master's death.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Odin welcomes all kinds, so long as they war louder and drink faster than the last man.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Gotafrid Fairrobes
en: My weapons are polished and prepared, if you wish to dance.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Hail, warrior. You keep this estate?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Gotafrid Fairrobes
en: I do. I am Gotafrid Fairrobes, celebrated drengr of the Great Heathen Army. Trusted golden helm of Ragnar Lothbrok. I intend a clean and honorable battle as my days grow old and rotten. I wish to keep myself dignified in my death-rattle.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Your upkeep is impressive.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Gotafrid Fairrobes
en: My war garments are unblemished. Well-groomed and pristine. Ragnar taught me self-respect when we summered here.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: A clean conscience, unblemished oaths, and immaculate loyalty are of higher value than any well-dusted piece of armor.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Gotafrid Fairrobes
en: A resonant thought. Now will you oblige me? An honorable and clean battle is all I ask for now.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: May Odin visit us in this dance. Let us fight.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Gotafrid Fairrobes
en: Prepare your garb for a last drenching of raven-wine.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Gotafrid Fairrobes
en: My battle-irons are in prime condition. Immaculate strike. Such precision. My weapons are dulled and impure. I shall only use the sharp and aseptic. Only the purest.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Gotafrid Fairrobes
en: Ah, my wounds bleed clean. Thank you for this last song of well-wrought iron and immaculate blows.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Go to your shining, flawless victory... farewell, honorable drengr.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Skegjold Frenzy-Seeker
en: For Odin, for Thor, for Freya and the Valkyries, and the Saggy-Britches. Come to me, Ragnar. Find me in the Frenzy. Hommm....

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Hail, warrior. Are these wetlands your longhouse? Your meadhall?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Skegjold Frenzy-Seeker
en: This is a drengrs ritual chamber. I am Skegjold, pledged to Ragnar Lothbrok in hugr (mind) and body. Iron and soul. I seek one willing to take the ritual and engage me in combat to the death.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. For an opponent you could do worse than me.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Skegjold Frenzy-Seeker
en: Join me then, in Drengr-. Ragnar taught it to me at Uppsala for nine moons and I never stopped. I will only fight one who enters my frenzy, for if we are not in the same state, I will have an unfair advantage.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: What is the potion then? Mead and rotten bread?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Skegjold Frenzy-Seeker
en: A sacred ale of high volatile spirits. And Thor's fungus, the Amanita Muscaria. Ragnar and I would quaff this great elixir before each new raid. I often saw him transcend the laws of battle. Drink of the brew that bubbles here in my pot. Then we will enter the frenzy together, and only one of us will leave.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: May you walk the Bifröst with heavy steps, drengr.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Skegjold Frenzy-Seeker
en: This is for the lady of many names! Now the All-Father sees me. He opens his arms, ready to receive!

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: You fought well, and our journey was fair. Now yours continues.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Skegjold Frenzy-Seeker
en: Now I transcend. Farewell. It is my turn to see the god of poetry.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: This is drengr territory. One of Ragnar Lothbrok's wandering warriors lurks here.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: You carry no blade, only shields?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Orwig Neverdeath
en: I am impervious to all but the iron of a true drengr. Ragnar Lothbrok knew this, and bade me carry only boards. As a challenge. Now he is gone, and I remain. I wish to die, but I cannot. For he made me too strong. Now I spend my time longing for his company.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: You must have a weak point.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Orwig Neverdeath
en: None that I am aware of. I was always at the center of Ragnar's shield wall. He trusted me with the defenses of his great army. My flesh, scarred and trained by Ragnar, is now like an iron weave. It pains me. How can I join him if none can kill me in battle? I see no way in which this can occur. Unless, you prove me wrong, fair challenger.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Let me do the honor of breaking Ragnar's shield wall.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Orwig Neverdeath
en: I hope you will. Let me now prepare the shield wall. Lord Ragnar, will this be the day?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Orwig Neverdeath
en: Stand fast, warrior. And if Loki rules the day, you may have a chance. I am a fortress impenetrable. This is my skill. This is my curse. I am Orwig Neverdeath. I wish to die. Yes! Break me, drengr! I... I never thought I would feel this! Vulnerable. Death, lurking near!

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Orwig Neverdeath
en: I... I have been breached. Victory is yours. Victory is mine...

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Stand fast and tall, he who cannot die. The gates open for you.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: A scroll recounting Ragnar Lothbrok's death.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: This pit. It fits the description in the letter about Ragnar Lothbrok.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: There is the cage that held him. The site abandoned, as if used once for a ritual, and never again. Here. This is the place where Ragnar Lothbrok met his end. He must have been naked and bloodied, every drop draining into the pit. This supreme drengr of all men, now King Aella's prize.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Ragnar Lothbrok
en: "I have seen this day a thousand times! Baldr keeps a cup of mead for me. I welcome my entry into the land of champions!"

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Mocked, ridiculed, humiliated, his honor did not budge. Dragged by cowards, thrown to snakes. They were more afraid than him.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Ragnar Lothbrok
en: "I face death with a thirst on my lips. My reputation cannot be unwritten, inscribed on the hearts of those who fought beside me!"

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Set upon by venomous snakes, he stood and spoke with honor and spine, for all those who live their lives for glory alone.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Ragnar Lothbrok
en: "O, how the young pigs would grunt if they knew how this old boar suffered! You will meet them, Aella! One day, they will come!"

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: His men came too late to save him. Those who fought for him, they loved him dearly. Their oaths, unbreakable. I have sent your drengr to meet you, great king. You will be with them once again.

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: There, where he fell. Something glints in the soil. There is something in a pit. Something left behind?

scene: The Lost Drengir of Ragnar Lothbrok
speaker: Eivor
en: Ragnar's dagger. A fine seax of Damascus steel.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to clear this fort and break this chain to get our ships safely upriver. The mechanism should be inside.

speaker: Eivor
en: With the chain down, Geadric and the ships can get through.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Eivor, we await your orders.

speaker: Eivor
en: You brought your weapons and armor?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Aye, Raven-Tamer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. Now we dig in, and wait for our friends.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well met, old friend.

speaker: Geadric
en: When the chance arrived to lodge an axe in the sod of Wessex, you thought of me! Such an honor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is everything else in place, Eivor? Are we ready to take Rouecistre?

speaker: Eivor
en: Rally our army. We will drag this mouse from his hole.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not yet. I need more time to prepare.

speaker: Eivor
en: Basim...

speaker: Basim
en: Are you ready, Eivor? Your allies stand firm. We await your final order.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let us take Rouecistre.

speaker: Eivor
en: I still need more time.

speaker: Geadric
en: We are through, Eivor! Good work, Eivor!

speaker: Geadric
en: Ha! He was no match for you!

speaker: Geadric
en: The ram can't pass through the flames, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Then we'll put them out!

speaker: Eivor
en: Defend the ram!

speaker: Basim
en: Keep those Saxons back!

speaker: Basim
en: We must find a way to lower that drawbridge.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will see to it.

speaker: Geadric
en: The way is clear! Onwards!

speaker: Geadric
en: Another gate! It will not hold against us!

speaker: Eivor
en: Beware that burning oil!

speaker: Geadric
en: Break down that gate!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tedmund is holed up in the tower keep, press forward.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep going! Inside!

speaker: Basim
en: They have the keep sealed tight down here, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then we must look higher up for a way inside.

speaker: Basim
en: A good strike, Eivor! Another Saxon goes to his grave!

speaker: Tedmund
en: I'll kill you before I let you take this fortress.

speaker: Tedmund
en: I'll cut you down, Dane. Rouecistre will not fall to you rabid pack of mongrels. Kill me, and all of Wessex will rise against you!

speaker: Tedmund
en: You dare take this fortress, Dane? Aelfred's army will smear your innards across the battlements.

speaker: Eivor
en: We are not here for stone and sand, Thegn Tedmund.

speaker: Tedmund
en: I shit on you! You and your toy gods! I will not bow to you like some puppet lord. I would rather die.

speaker: Eivor
en: How much will your king pay us to keep your sniveling head upon your neck?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: An army marches upon us from the south! A holy man from Saint Hadrian's Priory, backed by a fyrd!

speaker: Tedmund
en: Ah! Then Cynebert? God be praised! If riches are all you care about, the Church has it in abundance.

speaker: Eivor
en: If the terms are fair, you'll have your freedom. A chest or two of silver for a shit-stained sewer rat.

speaker: Basim
en: Stay quiet or I'll not be able to stop my friend from slitting your throat.

speaker: Tedmund
en: Ah! Watch yourself, heathen! You handle me too roughly!

speaker: Tedmund
en: You will die for the indignities you have showered upon me, Dane!

speaker: Eivor
en: I mean no offense, thegn. You are only a hefty ransom to me, nothing more.

speaker: Tedmund
en: This is why you batter down my gate, kill my men, for a purse of grubby coin? You have no honor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough, or I'll return you to the Saxons with ten fewer fingers.

speaker: Cynebert
en: You there! Heathens! Let this good man go, or suffer an iron sickness!

speaker: Basim
en: And what do you offer us in return?

speaker: Cynebert
en: Your lives!

speaker: Eivor
en: We lost many good men storming this keep. It will not be in vain, Christ-slave. Twenty chests of silver.

speaker: Tedmund
en: Give them what they ask, Cynebert.

speaker: Cynebert
en: A hefty sum, that will leave God's coffers hollow. I cannot give it up without some assurance... Tedmund?

speaker: Tedmund
en: You extort me in return for my life? You were swiftly met, abbot. Not long after these... these scallious worms took my fort.

speaker: Cynebert
en: On the Lord's bidding, Tedmund! At prayer, a terrible vision befell me. A host of heathens, your life in danger...

speaker: Tedmund
en: A coincidence I find rather... rather omnious, abbot. Do you−

speaker: Cynebert
en: God help you man, are you well?

speaker: Tedmund
en: Air... I need... I need air!

speaker: Eivor
en: He's dead.

speaker: Basim
en: The work of a poison, no doubt.

speaker: Cynebert
en: No no no no, rouse the man! He cannot be dead! He must not be dead!

speaker: Eivor
en: Poison? How does the man die of poison in our arms!

speaker: Basim
en: Many great kings and paranoids have carried poison in times of war. As an alternative to capture. And ransom.

speaker: Cynebert
en: A catastrophe! Aelfred will choose another and... by the saints, Aelfred! How will I explain this to the king?

speaker: Eivor
en: We followed this road to its end, Cynebert. You may not like where it led, but you owe us our half of the bargain.

speaker: Cynebert
en: You shall have your paladin. I... I need a day. Return to my abbey tomorrow and you shall... O dear, O, dear.

speaker: Eivor
en: These delays are grinding at my bones. We should abandon Cynebert, find Fulke ourselves.

speaker: Basim
en: Peace, Eivor. Speak with Geadric and relieve him of his oath. I'll meet you at Cynebert's abbey

speaker: Eivor
en: You fought like beasts escaped from your hell today, Geadric. Your oath to me is fulfilled.

speaker: Geadric
en: It was good to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with you against the pox-dogs of Wessex. May our friendship endure.

speaker: Eivor
en: This tangle-briar of Christians and lords means nothing to me. I'm here for Sigurd.

speaker: Geadric
en: I understand. When you find him again, come see me. We'll feast and sing with mead and friendship to warm us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Agreed.

speaker: Flann
en: Eivor, you did well at Aileach. We march in the morning. I'd think it no small thing for you to lead my honour guard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you not get Bárid's message, lord? You must pull back, not move forward. This ruse is part of a larger trap not yet sprung.

speaker: Flann
en: Bárid believes to know the minds of these kings, but the Church has taken root and flourished since my uncle's day.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Church is behind the plot against you. Did the message say nothing of Eogan?

speaker: Flann
en: King Niall and King Domnall were doubtless seeking to cast blame elsewhere. The Church is a convenient scapegoat.

speaker: Ciara
en: What if there's some truth to Bárid's suspicions?

speaker: Flann
en: Eogan is the Abbot of Armagh, God's Appointed in Ireland. I cannot doubt him on the word of a... friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mean a pagan.

speaker: Bárid
en: Why are you all still here? Did my message not get through?

speaker: Eivor
en: It did, but King Flann is not convinced.

speaker: Bárid
en: You must pull out of Clogher now, my king. Before we are surrounded by Eogan's army.

speaker: Flann
en: You do not command me, Bárid mac Ímair. If there was an army, my scouts

speaker: Bárid
en: Your scouts are dead! Baldur's blood, Flann! How many must die before you learn to trust?

speaker: Flann
en: You forget yourself, Bárid! Do not invoke your false gods in my presence!

speaker: Bárid
en: Listen! What's that?

speaker: Bárid
en: Eogan's wolves have arrived. I didn't come this far to die in a tent, my king.

speaker: Irish Soldier 1
en: We're under attack!

speaker: Eivor
en: Come on!

speaker: Bárid
en: Drive them from the heart of the village! I'll take more heads than you, cousin!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not wager on it!

speaker: Flann
en: If we hold off this assault, we will save the day!

speaker: Eivor
en: They are all around us!

speaker: Bárid
en: The archers have fire!

speaker: Eivor
en: They come from the fields!

speaker: Bárid
en: Blunt those archers' barbs! Leave none alive!

speaker: Eivor
en: The ravens will have your eyes! You come like wolves, now die like dogs!

speaker: Bárid
en: Seek out Flann and Ciara at the barricades. I'll gather the men and meet you back here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Until then, cousin.

speaker: Ciara
en: We could use your help, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Come with me! I will be your shield.

speaker: Eivor
en: They're on the ropes.

speaker: Ciara
en: They have no honor. Show them no mercy!

speaker: Flann
en: That's the last of them!

speaker: Eivor
en: They retreat.

speaker: Ciara
en: You've saved us.

speaker: Flann
en: We held them off. At a great cost.

speaker: Ciara
en: Eivor? Where is Bárid?

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid, can you hear me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid mac Ímair!

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you seen King Bárid?

speaker: Irish Soldier 2
en: Aye, he was headed towards the farm on the edge of the village.

speaker: Eivor
en: A cold hand that grips my heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid!

speaker: Eivor
en: Bárid?

speaker: Bárid
en: Eivor...?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm here.

speaker: Bárid
en: A glorious end, don't you think? Worthy of a , maybe... And you thought I'd gone soft...

speaker: Eivor
en: No one knew your true measure.

speaker: Bárid
en: Except you, cousin... You never doubted me.

speaker: Bárid
en: Not even you, cousin... You had your doubts... Good thing I was too stupid to give up...

speaker: Eivor
en: Your bravery will be remembered, Bárid. I'll see to it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hold your weapon well, cousin. I will see you in Valhalla.

speaker: Bárid
en: Sichfrith is my Valhalla, Eivor. Valhalla need not be a place... It can be... a legacy... Flann must back him. Have him swear by his God. There's nothing the Christians fear more than their Almighty's wrath.

speaker: Eivor
en: It will be done.

speaker: Flann
en: A hero's funeral. Bárid has become a greater man in death than he was in life.

speaker: Eivor
en: Or maybe we were too small to see his full size.

speaker: Flann
en: A harsh truth, but fair. He saw more clearly than I, and I ignored his council. Eogan will pay for his death.

speaker: Eivor
en: What then? When the abbot is gone and you've tamed the North, what of Sichfrith? Will you give him your royal support?

speaker: Flann
en: When he has proven himself. It would not be good politics at this time

speaker: Eivor
en: Trolls take your politics! Bárid gave his life in your service. If this is how you repay loyalty, you'll be in short supply.

speaker: Flann
en: Twice you've stung me with truth. I'll return the favor. Sichfrith isn't ready... but he could be with proper teaching.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. He'll benefit with your wisdom.

speaker: Flann
en: And my support. But neither throne will be secure while Eogan lives.

speaker: Flann
en: We'll throttle that snake. And afterward, the fate of this land will be in your hands. Yours and Sichfrith's.

speaker: Ciara
en: The horses are being made ready, my king. Sure you don't want to rest your bones and leave by dawn's light?

speaker: Flann
en: My thoughts ride too rough for sleep. I've an army and reputation to reclaim. The second may prove harder than the first.

speaker: Ciara
en: My mother used to tell me that The Morrígan used to feed on the death of heroes, then fill men's heads with thoughts of war. I imagined using the Tara stone to drown out their song, the way Bishop Patrick drove the snakes from Ireland.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's no power strong enough to do what you say. Not even the gods can change fate. The world is destined to end in war.

speaker: Ciara
en: ′Twas naught but the fantasy of a young girl, so.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell Flann I'll come to him after I've arranged things with Sichfrith.

speaker: Ciara
en: Tell him yourself, I'm not leaving yet.

speaker: Havi
en: This is the old workshop that Ivaldi spoke of. I should check if he's already here.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Shoddy. Very shoddy. Utterly useless. Where's a decent saw when you need one?

speaker: Havi
en: Found anything worthy of your talents?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: These will have to do.

speaker: Havi
en: Soon you can put them to good use.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: By Ymir. Is that a... a Salakar? I never knew they actually existed.

speaker: Havi
en: I know all the s of your people, yet I've never heard of

speaker: Ivaldi
en: I never said my people...

speaker: Havi
en: You mean the Light Elves?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: There aren't many who remember the children of light, or their stories. I do.

speaker: Havi
en: When Surtr invaded their lands... they begged me for aid. But the with the Vanir had only just ended, and I was... weary.

speaker: Havi
en: Long after, I learnt how Surtr devoured the elves' immortal light. Hugr by hugr. Maybe it's the same light that now allows him to renew himself after death?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: During the conquest, he must have uncovered knowledge of the Salakars.

speaker: Havi
en: But to what end?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: What hugrs does it hold?

speaker: Havi
en: Those of two warlords, one a Muspel, the other a Jotun.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Nothing more?

speaker: Havi
en: Nothing more. At least not of value.

speaker: Eysa
en: He speaks the truth.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: You deal with a fire nymph?

speaker: Eysa
en: A fire nymph? I am the finest fire nymph in all of Svartalfheim.

speaker: Havi
en: Allow me to introduce Eysa, treasonous daughter of Surtr, and... my friend.

speaker: Eysa
en: You grow dewy-eyed in your dotage.

speaker: Havi
en: What have you unearthed?

speaker: Eysa
en: Only rumors. My father is rebuilding something large and powerful, though its exact nature I cannot fathom.

speaker: Havi
en: And the Salakar is intended to be part of this... this something?

speaker: Eysa
en: Most likely. Either way, its value to my father is so great he may indeed trade your son for its return.

speaker: Havi
en: Return to your stepmother. Arrange a trade. And one more thing...

speaker: Havi
en: I would feel better knowing you're protected.

speaker: Eysa
en: Sinmara travels far and wide, but I will rejoin her as you wish.

speaker: Havi
en: Whatever the Salakar is, I must steal it back once Baldr is safe.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Why?

speaker: Havi
en: Ragnarök comes. I've made plans, but they are not ideal. Perhaps the Salakar offers another way? One that will allow me to truly save those I care about... Even you.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: To unlock its secrets, I will need help. There are rumors of a shelter nearby. Its dwellers may be able to assist me.

speaker: Havi
en: I know the place. Home to the most ill-tempered shits imaginable.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Try looking near the largest karst south of here.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Tell them I sent you. No dwarf would give up the chance to work with Ivaldi.

speaker: Havi
en: Vangrinn was once home to your rivals Sindri and Brokkr. Your name may not carry much weight here.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Don't make me laugh. No one cares about those two. I'll follow you once I have finished taking what I need.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Do not linger. Go find me some helpers. Perhaps I should take another peek at the Salakar? Ah, dammit, better not. I will need help if I am to study the Salakar.

speaker: Oglehr
en: Can't you see I'm busy? Do I look like I got time for small talk?

speaker: Havi
en: Hello there. I bring word from Ivaldi.

speaker: Reihi
en: What do I care? Go talk to the ganger.

speaker: Havi
en: Ganger?

speaker: Reihi
en: Yeah. The chief. Name's Oglehr.

speaker: Havi
en: Let's see, which one is Oglehr...

speaker: Havi
en: Strange. I just spoke to that fellow.

speaker: Havi
en: A word, my friend? Ivaldi requests your aid.

speaker: Vesall
en: Ain't my concern. Go talk to Oglehr.

speaker: Havi
en: He's the master of this workshop?

speaker: Vesall
en: Master? Nah, but he's the chief when the masters ain't here.

speaker: Havi
en: Those two aren't him. I will keep looking.

speaker: Havi
en: I should go speak with Oglehr again.

speaker: Oglehr
en: What do you want?

speaker: Havi
en: Ivaldi sends me. He requires the help of a skilled artisan.

speaker: Oglehr
en: A meeting of minds, huh? Well, it ain't up to me. You'd best talk to Brokkr and Sindri.

speaker: Havi
en: They still breathe? Where are they?

speaker: Oglehr
en: No idea. Sindri went off adventuring. He does that. Mind you, it's been a while since he left...

speaker: Havi
en: How much of a while?

speaker: Oglehr
en: Couple of weeks.

speaker: Havi
en: And his absence doesn't worry you?

speaker: Oglehr
en: Not my business where he goes.

speaker: Havi
en: And Brokkr?

speaker: Oglehr
en: Went to look for Sindri. Bit of a worryguts, that one. Ever since he mucked up the forging of Mjölnir. Anyway, look, leave your name and I'll pass it to Brokkr when he shows up.

speaker: Havi
en: Tell him Havi of Asgard was here.

speaker: Oglehr
en: Havi of...? By Ymir. Really it is you?

speaker: Havi
en: I'll return tonight. In the meantime, fetch Ivaldi. He's at the old workshop ruins.

speaker: Havi
en: Of all our enemies, Sinmara is the most vicious. I remember when she and Surtr were bitter rivals. She led the coup against him. Almost claimed his crown. And then... announced their marriage! I know not what deal was struck. But we must remain forever alert to her plots.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Three times it stung me! Three! On the hand! Then the neck! Then on me eyeball!

speaker: Ivaldi
en: A true master would ignore such trifles.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Trifles!? That gadfly was the size of a squirrel! A big one.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: An ogre could tear me limb from limb, and still my severed hands would finish the job. That is focus. That is passion. That is

speaker: Havi
en: ...horseshit. Master Brokkr, I'm glad you have made it home. And your brother? Did you find him?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Yeah, you never did say where he was...

speaker: Havi
en: I believe Sindri went adventuring.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Adventuring? No, no, that's not it. He went to find the special mead. Had a hankering, he said.

speaker: Havi
en: Special mead?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Yeah. The special mead.

speaker: Havi
en: Suttungr's special mead?

speaker: Brokkr
en: What's that frosty arse got to do with it? We ain't in Jotunheim, in case you hadn't noticed. There's this mead they make down at the brewery. So sweet it can... it can... Well, it's bloody sweet, alright? Anyway, Sindri had an itch for it. Just a horn or two he said. So, off he goes. That was half a moon ago. I told him not to do it. Too many giants out there. But he wouldn't listen. Him and his cravings.

speaker: Havi
en: Where can I find this brewery?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Alethorp. Southeast of here. Other side of the marsh. Can't miss it... You're going to rescue him?

speaker: Havi
en: I will find him, yes. And afterwards, you and he will repay me by helping Ivaldi with a job I need done.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Now hold on, we didn't

speaker: Havi
en: Good, good, we have a deal.

speaker: Havi
en: That gadfly? It was Loki. Thor himself could have not withstood the sting.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Remind me, whe do I find myself in your company?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Be grateful, child. You might learn something.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Child? Fuck off. I'm the same age as you.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: And in all that time, consider what I have learned. And what you haven't.

speaker: Brokkr
en: So why was the 'great' Ivaldi snooping around our old workshop?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Hoping to find something useful. More fool me... Seems this dump is no better.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Is it too much to ask for some decent tools around here?

speaker: Brokkr
en: You wouldn't know "decent" if it sprouted wings, flew up your arse sideways, and laid a golden egg.

speaker: Havi
en: I must hand it to Sindri. Even after all that has happened, he still has the defiance to seek out a horn of Svartalfheim's finest.

speaker: Havi
en: Ah, the sweet scent of mead. Fouled by the scent of Muspels. Jotnar too.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: I'm out of mead! Bring me another barrel!

speaker: Havi
en: The smell of mead grows strong. This must be where everything is stored. Sindri's nose would have guided him here.

speaker: Havi
en: I don't believe in locked doors.

speaker: Havi
en: Thank you. Much obliged. The Muspels aren't making any use of this place. They let it rot.

speaker: Havi
en: Now to find the door this key unlocks.

speaker: Havi
en: I sense that Sindri has been here.

speaker: Havi
en: Surely there is some sign of Sindri here?

speaker: Havi
en: This blood is many days old. One trail leads in, the other out.

speaker: Havi
en: This hammer bears the mark of Sindri. And here, a bag of roasted acorns.

speaker: Havi
en: A chain was placed here. From the scarring, something heavy was suspended from it. I've carried enough dwarves recently to know they are not as light as they look.

speaker: Havi
en: Is this Sindri's special mead? Given the puddles on the floor, he must have taken a bath in it.

speaker: Havi
en: What do we have here?

speaker: Havi
en: The Muspels have a prison not far from here. Jarnshus, they call it.

speaker: Havi
en: Some days ago, Sindri was captured while sneaking outside. He was dragged in here for interrogation. His belongings were seized. Even his roasted acorns, one of the many dwarven delicacies I will never fathom. They tried to loosen his tongue using the same sweet mead he himself sought. Almost drowned him in it. But the shelter has not been raided... So, Sindri must have remained strong and refused to give them its location. Instead, he was dragged away. Bloodied. Drunk as a fish... but alive. Most likely to face further tortures. At a makeshift prison named Jarnshus... That is where I should go next.

speaker: Havi
en: This place reeks of misery. More than I would even wish upon Loki, no matter his crimes. It's likely Sindri was brought here many days ago. I hope I'm not too late.

speaker: Havi
en: The giants have no mercy. When I face them, I will show them none.

speaker: Havi
en: Most of the dead have been roasted upon the flames. But that body over there... I hope it's not who I think it is.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 2
en: The shortlings smell sweet when they burn. Must be all that mead in their fat little bellies.

speaker: Havi
en: I know this mark. Whoever he was, he had his hugr cruelly stolen... I can sense that the Salakar was satisfied on this occasion. Was this Calder's first victim!? And that amulet... the sigil... Sindri! Reckless fool! All this for some mead!? Oh well. It is done. I must return the body to Brokkr.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 3
en: This place, it is too much. Not even the dwarves deserve to suffer like this.

speaker: Havi
en: Chance led to Sindri's capture. But the nature of his death... that was not chance. When the enemy realized they had such a prize in their clutches.

speaker: Havi
en: Dwarven hugrs, even one such as Sindri's, are of lesser value. Still, it can't be coincidence that Calder sated the Salaker with the hugrs of so many races... Muspel, Jotun, dwarf. Who knows what else.

speaker: Oglehr
en: It cannot be! Is this Sindri? Noblest of dwarves?

speaker: Vesall
en: Please, let this not be our missing master!

speaker: Brokkr
en: Who is this you bring!? No! It can't be!

speaker: Havi
en: Master Brokkr, I share in your grief. Truly I do... Your brother was the worthiest of dwarves. More so than you will ever know.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Oh Sindri... no, no... my dear Sindri...

speaker: Havi
en: The funeral arrangements are being made outside. I must use this chance to bend Brokkr to my will.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mayda. I hear that you have been chosen as the May Queen.

speaker: Mayda
en: Ugh. I hate it. I told them I didn't want to but everyone seemed so excited. And now I have to wear this horrible flower crown. It's unbefitting of a warrior.

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps you would feel pride if you had a crown that matched your spirit.

speaker: Mayda
en: Well, this may sound silly, but I want a crown made from a beast, not a garden. Bertham overheard Sunniva talking about an animal that is killing much of the wildlife in the forest. She hasn't had the chance to track it yet, but I would be honored to wear a crown made from such a predator.

speaker: Eivor
en: A request that I can easily grant. I will return with a crown befitting of our May Queen

speaker: Mayda
en: Thank you, Eivor. I will be in your debt.

speaker: Eivor
en: The creature should be close by. I should begin tracking.

speaker: Eivor
en: A sight of true carnage. This must be the work of the beast. This creature has been gutted in a way I've never seen before. The beast must have talons or claws.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is a trail of blood. It should lead me to the beast.

speaker: Eivor
en: This looks like it would belong to a farmer, but there are no farms in the forest.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Help! Anyone! Save me from that monster!

speaker: Eivor
en: Easy, friend. I am here to slay the beast of the woods.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Thank the gods! I was certain this would be my end!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me. Where has the beast gone?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: It's there! Do you not see it?

speaker: Eivor
en: I see only a chicken.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: It wears a clever disguise, but don't be fooled. It is a monster! Please, you must kill it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Very well. Stay here while I deal with the beast.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is safe. Where did you find that chicken, Hel?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: All my thanks! I still can't believe Romi attacked me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Romi?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: The chicken you just killed. I was bringing her to market when a bear appeared. I thought I was done for but Romi defended me. She took down the bear like it was nothing. I tried to calm her down but once she had a taste of blood, she was beyond reasoning.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's ... a very special chicken.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: And to think she was about to be dinner. I'll never harm another chicken again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me. May I use Romi to craft a crown for a friend?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Yes, of course. It would be an honor to have something of Romi live on. I'll even help you with it.

speaker: Eivor
en: May Queen. I give you your crown.

speaker: Mayda
en: Eivor! It's wonderful. What horrible beast gave its life to make such a powerful object?

speaker: Eivor
en: It was a winged creature the likes of which I've never encountered before. Its beak dripped of blood and its talons were sharper than any blade.

speaker: Mayda
en: I can tell that it was a powerful foe. I wish I had been there with you to see it in action.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was truly something to behold. Are you more confident in your role now?

speaker: Mayda
en: Yes, Eivor. I will wear this crown with pride. Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Seems Oswald has set out for the day. I should have a word with him.

speaker: Valdis
en: Clear the mess in the longhouse. And wake my brothers with the coldest water you can find. Eivor, good to see you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are Oswald's powerful bride-to-be, Valdis.

speaker: Valdis
en: I'm not his. This marriage is to be an alliance. Nothing more. Besides, the man can barely carry a sword or speak with conviction.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald is many things, but a gifted leader he is not. Still, of everyone I have met here, he is the only one willing to be responsible for the place.

speaker: Valdis
en: I will leave you to your day. You can find Oswald by the docks. Watching the river calms him, apparently.

speaker: Oswald
en: Ah! Good morning. Up bright and early.

speaker: Eivor
en: You can labor like a ' (slave), but you're no good with feasts. Not a good start for a king.

speaker: Oswald
en: No, indeed. I find a solitary comfort in my menial labors. Not something a king should admit to, I suppose.

speaker: Eivor
en: The brothers shamed you at dinner. It's your duty to answer their insults. Don't let the matter lay unresolved.

speaker: Oswald
en: O, it was a petty row with hen-house wolves. I'd sooner answer the moo of a cow than worry about their insults.

speaker: Oswald
en: I have a wedding to plan and a Kingdom to save. I haven't time to suffer fools.

speaker: Eivor
en: They betrayed your hospitality, Oswald. Where I'm from, that's a grave insult.

speaker: Finnr
en: Well well, here's the mud-soaked Saxon who's been taxing my patience.

speaker: Oswald
en: Steward Finnr... I know I failed to impress at dinner yestereve, but fear not. The Danes will come around in time.

speaker: Finnr
en: You stake claim to the throne, you dazed dog with no bone. If Lord Halfdan were here, he'd squeeze ale from a stone...

speaker: Finnr
en: ...yelling "Finnr, my drengr, stick this cur in the ground!"

speaker: Eivor
en: All mewling and spitting, here's Finnr, the hound. He has bark but no bite, just a puppy, I've found.

speaker: Oswald
en: What just happened?

speaker: Eivor
en: That's flyting, Oswald. Using rhythm and rhyme to lay a man flat. Try it, match his verse.

speaker: Finnr
en: There's no man you can lead, you dunce of the s...

speaker: Oswald
en: Uh... em... a glutton you are, just stop eating your words!

speaker: Finnr
en: Not bad, not bad...

speaker: Eivor
en: He's an ugly puss, so when he brags, hit him back with something about his looks.

speaker: Finnr
en: I hail from the North where the winter's our season...

speaker: Oswald
en: But you're foul, you're a blister, you're a... a...

speaker: Eivor
en: ... plague-ridden lesion.

speaker: Oswald
en: O, yes! That's very good. Plague ridden lesion.

speaker: Eivor
en: He's got the wit of a boar, so when he insults you, make him feel stupid.

speaker: Finnr
en: When I'm done with you, cur, you'll be raven-flock food...

speaker: Oswald
en: But your brain's soaked in mead and your...

speaker: Eivor
en: ...head's made of wood!

speaker: Oswald
en: Wood! Head's made of wood.

speaker: Eivor
en: Under all that posturing is a sniveling boy, so dig deep. When he brags, take a jab at his manhood.

speaker: Finnr
en: I've sailed squalls and north winds. You? Not even a breeze.

speaker: Oswald
en: But the winds that you sail...

speaker: Eivor
en: ...blow between both your knees.

speaker: Oswald
en: Blow between both your... O! You mean farting! Ha!

speaker: Finnr
en: Oswald, my boy. You're useless without your raven. This one's wrong for the throne! He's too soft and too tame...

speaker: Eivor
en: Hit him back and make it personal. Attack his mother.

speaker: Oswald
en: When you crawled from the womb, you were ugly and lame! Your poor mother, she fainted away from the shame.

speaker: Eivor
en: He'd take two seats on a longship! He'd do well to remember that, Oswald.

speaker: Oswald
en: A walrus? A whale? A behemoth by name? No, it's Finnr the Fool, drunk and reeking with shame!

speaker: Eivor
en: Go on. Give some back. About his height this time.

speaker: Oswald
en: You claim you're a Dane, but your bloodline is stained. A wee dwarf must have ravished your mum in the rain.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well spoken. Before sword clash and blood flow, we destroy our enemies with well-timed words.

speaker: Finnr
en: You have a talent for verse, I'll give you that. But how long will that silver tongue hold up against an iron axe?

speaker: Oswald
en: Let's find out, Finnr. I challenge you to a '!

speaker: Finnr
en: You don't mean that, Oswald.

speaker: Oswald
en: That's a fight to settle disputes, no? A holmgang?

speaker: Eivor
en: A fight to the death, yes.

speaker: Oswald
en: Let's talk it out, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: Too late, the challenge has been made. But a fight against Finnr wouldn't be anything to boast about. You'll fight me.

speaker: Oswald
en: Hold on, this is

speaker: Eivor
en: That said, I shouldn't be seen killing a Saxon in the streets of Elmenham.

speaker: Finnr
en: There's a nice islet downriver, near Seahenge. The water will wash the blood clean away.

speaker: Eivor
en: Prepare the square and we'll meet you there. I hope you're ready.

speaker: Oswald
en: I have to be. Just give me a moment to mentally prepare.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not make us wait long, it would not be kingly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you ready for the holmgang?

speaker: Oswald
en: I hope so. I just need to prepare. I'll meet you at the islet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you ready for the holmgang?

speaker: Oswald
en: I hope so. I just need to prepare. I'll meet you at the islet.

speaker: Finnr
en: You made it. Now tussle with care, and go easy on our future king. He is the only man left who can claim the crown.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kings are made, not born, Finnr. So let us see what we can make of Oswald.

speaker: Finnr
en: Done.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've still got the touch for drawing a square.

speaker: Finnr
en: I've been in East Anglia many summers now, but I'll always be a Dane.

speaker: Oswald
en: Must we do this, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Strength and courage are always a boon, Oswald. You'll need both if you want the Danes to accept you as a king.

speaker: Oswald
en: True strength comes from resolve, Eivor. It speaks to us, a stern voice from within.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have never heard of talking guts. But a swift axe would silence that inner voice in seconds. You must be prepared.

speaker: Oswald
en: Wait. You're unarmed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Just do your best. I'll be fine.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you should thank your god that I am.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where's your resolve, lord? Stop whining and attack me.

speaker: Oswald
en: Aaaah!

speaker: Eivor
en: We will forge a king out of you yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't hold back.

speaker: Eivor
en: You felt that one.

speaker: Oswald
en: I'm still here.

speaker: Finnr
en: Hard to believe this one will marry Valdis, don't you think?

speaker: Finnr
en: Ha! You expect the Danes to follow this pork belly?

speaker: Oswald
en: I'm... I'm still breathing, aren't I?

speaker: Eivor
en: Show me what you can do, Saxon.

speaker: Finnr
en: Come now! Inspire us, king!

speaker: Finnr
en: You'll never be king at this rate. Is this the best East Anglia has to offer?

speaker: Oswald
en: Yes, and I'll... I'll prove it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Come on! Fight!

speaker: Finnr
en: Finish this, Eivor. It pains me to watch!

speaker: Finnr
en: Eivor is the victor. But you've shown us something, Oswald.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay down, Oswald. That's enough.

speaker: Oswald
en: I will... I will not stay down.

speaker: Oswald
en: Ah! Was that too hard?

speaker: Eivor
en: It was a good strike. Keep going.

speaker: Finnr
en: Oswald of Elmenham. You may be a king to us Danes yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: What you lack in strength, you make up for in grit.

speaker: Oswald
en: Yes. I'm nothing if not... gritty.

speaker: Eivor
en: You fought bravely. Not with great skill, but with spirit. And courage. Always push back with everything you have, even if you have to get dirty, even if you must break the rules. Because there are no rules, not if you answer a challenge head-on. That's where honor lies.

speaker: Oswald
en: Not winning the fight, but living through it.

speaker: Finnr
en: A seaside brawl won't change the brothers' minds. Oswald must show results. Redress old wrongs. Fight back against Rued and his men.

speaker: Oswald
en: The raiders who attacked Beteleah have a camp down the coast. The sooner we remove them, the better.

speaker: Finnr
en: That would go a long way to building you up. And if you brought gifts for the brothers, spoils from the raid, they'd be in your debt.

speaker: Eivor
en: Time to wet your blade, Oswald.

speaker: Finnr
en: Eivor, I expect your longship crew could help with this attack.

speaker: Oswald
en: No one has been willing to take a stand against Rued's clan before. We're a kingdom of farmers and merchants.

speaker: Eivor
en: Even farmers and merchants can fight when led by the right person.

speaker: Finnr
en: I hope your faith in pig farmers is not misplaced, Eivor.

speaker: Oswald
en: There is work to do, yes. But we will rise to meet Rued's clan. God will make certain of it.

speaker: Finnr
en: They've left none alive!

speaker: Eivor
en: Neither will we.

speaker: Oswald
en: There may be prisoners here. Keep an eye out for them.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I see any, I'll let you know.

speaker: Eivor
en: You fight well, Oswald! Does the threat of death drive your blade further? Whatever compels you, hang onto it.

speaker: Finnr
en: I have not tasted battle in years! There is still vigor in these bones. Come on you filthy whoresons, there is iron to be kissed!

speaker: Eivor
en: Now to kill any stragglers.

speaker: Finnr
en: Over here!

speaker: Finnr
en: Ah, that'll do nicely.

speaker: Eivor
en: Find something?

speaker: Finnr
en: There's a crate of here. More than enough to make everyone happy.

speaker: Eivor
en: We'll take it to the ship.

speaker: Oswald
en: A hard won fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: The first of many, Oswald. Have you the will to keep it up?

speaker: Oswald
en: This is my gift to the brothers. I have more than enough wealth in Elmenham to widen their eyes. But this will be a symbol of my commitment to our fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a good start.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take what riches you find to Northwic. Then send for the brothers. I'll meet you there.

speaker: Mead-Stained Letter
en: We have taken Serpent's Landing. The road to victory is clear for Rued Jarl. We have broken this kingdom, their warriors are like headless fowl with no king to lead them in battle. East Anglia is ours this day.

speaker: Havi
en: Let me tell you of the day I fought three warriors. I made my way onward, but a terrible enemy loomed in my path! A glorious battle indeed, I think you'll agree.

speaker: Havi
en: Here is how I laid low a group of legendary warriors. I sensed the coming battle would not be easy, but I knew my strength would be equal to the task. Next was a battle to set a skalds tongue to stirring song! Thus my tale concludes, in glory and honor!

speaker: French Woman 1
en: Husband! What are you doing? We're going to miss Little Mother if you don't hurry yourself!

speaker: Eivor
en: They're gathering for something.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: Is that the time? The service with Little Mother is about to begin. I have to hurry!

speaker: French Man 1
en: We are all sinners. Not one of us is pure. We all will answer to God, and so we all must seek deliverance! By the grace of God, Little Mother is here to aid us. She is almost ready to begin! Make your way to the church!

speaker: Eivor
en: They're gathering somewhere. They might know something about the queen.

speaker: French Woman 3
en: Find a seat where you can. Little Mother will soon begin.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should find a seat.

speaker: Euphrasia
en: The dark waters covered me. Then his holy light came and O! The glory of his brightness.

speaker: Euphrasia
en: You will recall the miracle of Saint Taurinus, how he raised a burned girl back to life. As a child, I was too burned and near to death. At his altar, the saint appeared, touched me, and I was healed. Time could not corrupt the saint's holy body. He touched me so that now... I might touch you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Loki himself could not tell a better story.

speaker: Euphrasia
en: God is light. But what have you done in his light? All are turned to their own way, and gone astray into darkness. The devil has hold of your thoughts, your hearts, and your very bodies! No one is safe, whether you are pauper, king, ... or queen.

speaker: Euphrasia
en: Choose this day whom you will serve, for judgment is coming. And with it comes either deliverance, or damnation!

speaker: Euphrasia
en: Let us pray.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gone! This Little Mother knows something about the queen. I need to find her.

speaker: French Woman 4
en: Have you seen my husband? He should have been back from the ritual by now, shouldn't he?

speaker: Eivor
en: The saint defeats three Jotun by holding a cross before them. Lucky for him, Fenrir was not among them.

speaker: French Woman 5
en: My child is always daydreaming. Surely it's not natural. Could it be the devil? Would deliverance help?

speaker: French Man 2
en: It very well might. It can be wise to deal with problems early. We must train up children in the way they should go.

speaker: French Woman 5
en: We are poor, and cannot afford to pay anything.

speaker: French Man 2
en: Remember the widow's mite. There is always something we can give, no matter how little.

speaker: Eivor
en: These writings encourage people to seek freedom from the devil through "deliverance."

speaker: French Woman 4
en: Why is it taking so long? Does deliverance always take this long? It's been days.

speaker: French Woman 3
en: Have faith. Your husband is with Little Mother who works only God's will.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should talk to that woman.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are troubled.

speaker: French Woman 4
en: It's my husband. He went for deliverance and hasn't come back. It's been days. O, it's all my fault!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me about deliverance.

speaker: French Woman 4
en: My husband was going to leave me, but he loves me! The devil got into him somehow. We sent him to Aquila for a deliverance ritual. Little Mother said it would rid him of the devil.

speaker: Eivor
en: The ritual happens at Aquila?

speaker: French Woman 4
en: Yes, Little Mother has a sanctum. O, my poor husband. Do you think he's okay?

speaker: Eivor
en: I think you should prepare for the worst, and pray to your God for the best.

speaker: French Woman 4
en: O! Yes, I must pray. I must pray...

speaker: Eivor
en: I should go to Aquila, where rituals are being done.

speaker: Eivor
en: A message has come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bjorn Bloodtooth. Berserkers make fierce foes, but powerful allies. His strength would bolster our settlement. I should seek him out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bjorn Bloodtooth's cave should be close by.

speaker: Eivor
en: That must be Bjorn the Berserker.

speaker: Bjorn
en: My eyes cannot forget the sight, Njal. Her hair so long and falling down. How are you called, you bear-skins, you wolf-shirts, you tasters of blood? They call us the shield-biters, the wall-breakers, born in battle's flood. Soon, Alfhild, soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: A man who fights beside a great white bear. You are Bjorn Bloodtooth.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Ask the dead. What do they tell you?

speaker: Eivor
en: They say "we do not want shape-shifters in these lands."

speaker: Bjorn
en: They wished me dead. They are not the first. And you. Come to make your name in battle? Another corpse at my door won't matter.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not here to fight you, Bjorn. I am Eivor of the Raven Clan, and I offer you a seat in our hall.

speaker: Bjorn
en: I have no clan and no need of another.

speaker: Eivor
en: You prefer to live alone here with your bear?

speaker: Bjorn
en: I prefer vengeance. Against the man who hung my wife and left her for the crows.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who is this man?

speaker: Bjorn
en: A Mercian lord, whose name shall not sour my lips. He has scores of men, an army perhaps. But that will not stop me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then let me help. If you truly wish to avenge your wife, you must not fall in battle.

speaker: Bjorn
en: I shall think it over. Njal! Go with my bear, fill her belly. And if Njal trusts you, who knows? Maybe we do as you say.

speaker: Eivor
en: A mixing bowl for making berserker brew. Smells of piss and nightshade.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are tame for so wild a beast.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that so? Tell me, what does a bear like you eat? Whatever you want, hmm? Best you show me, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: The skalds say Bjorn carried you into battle when you were but a bear cub; Raised you as one would raise a child.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your favorite flowers? They are not food, Njal. Reminds me of summer in Norway. We had fields like these near Hemming's hall. I can see why Bjorn keeps you around.

speaker: Eivor
en: The lake. It's fish you want. I can help with that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fishing arrows! Now to catch something for Njal.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you want some fish, Njal? Here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nothing better than fresh fish! Eat your fill, friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: These men were looking for you, Njal. Bjorn may be in trouble as well.

speaker: Bjorn
