en: You have a strong war-arm, Raven-shirt.

speaker: Eivor
en: These men did not come for the fame of defeating a legendary berserker.

speaker: Bjorn
en: No. They were followers of the Mercian lord. My blood enemy. My wife's killer.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did your wife die?

speaker: Bjorn
en: Fame has two faces, Eivor of the Ravens. In Norway, many a young thane wanted the glory of killing me. They died. I grew tired of killing. Alfhild and I, we came here for a new start, a quiet life.

speaker: Eivor
en: But fame sailed ahead of you. This Mercian lord learned of your deeds, sought to boost his own name with your blood.

speaker: Bjorn
en: You have the right of it. Only he wanted me to drink the berserker brew first. When I refused, he demanded, offered gold, even taunted me. Then he... he hung her. Alfhild.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your blood feud is just. But if it is something you must do alone...

speaker: Bjorn
en: No, your words are wise. I do not want to die fighting. I want to die knowing my wife is avenged. I want to kill that man. Help me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me what you need.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Nightshade. It's the last bit of magic I need for my berserker brew.

speaker: Eivor
en: You shall have it. And when this is over, I trust the Raven Clan will have your axe.

speaker: Bjorn
en: When you find the nightshade, bring it to me beneath the gallows tree south of Beodoricsworth. Nightshade often grows near graveyards, and Saxons build their graveyards near churches.

speaker: Pict Warrior 1
en: Did you hear what happened to Archibald?

speaker: Pict Warrior 2
en: Aye, the drunken fool. I was there when he lit that thing on fire. We all told him not to, but he dared tempt fate.

speaker: Pict Warrior 1
en: You saw it all? Go on, tell us what happened.

speaker: Pict Warrior 2
en: The myths, Wilfred, they're true. A legendary Pict warrior who can rip a wolf apart with his bare hands!

speaker: Pict Warrior 1
en: You saw him?

speaker: Pict Warrior 2
en: I don't know what we saw, not exactly, but there's something up there. Archibald held his torch all brave like after lighting the fire. The next thing we know, his head dropped to his feet! We ran!

speaker: Pict Warrior 1
en: Should we at least fetch his body?

speaker: Pict Warrior 2
en: You can. I won't go back up that cursed mountain for all the silver in this land.

speaker: Eivor
en: Speak your name, warrior.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have it your way.

speaker: Pict Warrior 3
en: Your life's purpose was to die for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, he speaks.

speaker: Eivor
en: You fought well, warrior. But your legend ends, bound to no name.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your friend has been avenged.

speaker: Pict Warrior 1
en: Y-you killed the legendary warrior? Th-that is madness! Y-you're crazy!

speaker: Pict Warrior 2
en: Well. At least Old Arch can rest easy, now.

speaker: Flann
en: Eivor, I have you and Ciara to thank for curing my men, even if the source of this succor does not sit easily with me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not all druids are your enemies, lord. It is the Children of Danu who attacked you.

speaker: Flann
en: Ciara has told me of this druid cult. They are no great threat if they must strike from shadows.

speaker: Bárid
en: Perhaps they only sought to sow doubt among their enemies. And the friends of their enemies.

speaker: Flann
en: I regret my earlier distrust. But I've seen too much Irish blood spilt by Danes to give trust easily.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know what it is to be blood-bound, lord. It burns so bright it can blind to all else.

speaker: Bárid
en: So king, if Aileach is the prize, how do you mean to take it? The ringfort there is the strongest in all the lands.

speaker: Flann
en: Yet the kings of Aileach dwell outside its protection, foolishly leaving themselves vulnerable.

speaker: Bárid
en: Still, that's a long march over uncertain soil. Your army will be exposed to forces unknown.

speaker: Flann
en: Abbot Eogan has offered land at Clogher where our army will make camp. From there, we move onto Aileach.

speaker: Ciara
en: This just arrived. The Kings of Aileach want to talk peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: They surrender before you touch their soil? I know those who would die for such a reputation.

speaker: Flann
en: I don't like it. The wording is vague, asking much and promising little.

speaker: Bárid
en: What's the harm in hearing them out? If we start with the sword, we have nowhere else to go. They know me, they'll listen.

speaker: Flann
en: You would speak for me?

speaker: Bárid
en: If you would honor me with your trust.

speaker: Flann
en: Do you have an opinion, Eivor, or will you simply side with your cousin?

speaker: Eivor
en: My cousin gives wise counsel. You lose nothing but time. And if talking fails, answer with steel.

speaker: Flann
en: Time marches more quickly when you have an army to keep fit and fed. But I will consider your words.

speaker: Eivor
en: Diplomacy can't achieve what a single blade could. There's no shame in weakening your enemy from within.

speaker: Bárid
en: I could have used your support, cousin.

speaker: Flann
en: Even if I could consider what I think you're proposing, such a deed would cast the stain of dishonor on my reign.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not my decision to make, lord. Too much is balanced on the edge of Skuld's sharp blade.

speaker: Flann
en: So, you would leave it to your fate? Drift along like a leaf on the river?

speaker: Flann
en: My life has been one of warfare, plots, and intrigue. I have never known the trust of a brother and do not give mine over easily. Bárid mac Ímair, King of Dublin, I hereby authorize you to speak for me, Flann Sinna, High King of Ireland and all of her people.

speaker: Bárid
en: I will honor the faith you have placed in me, my king.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do I have your blessing to accompany Bárid, King Flann?

speaker: Flann
en: I'll not waste our time on formalities, Eivor, but you'll not be going with Bárid. I need you elsewhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me where.

speaker: Bárid
en: You must build up some good will among the Northern Uí Néill, as you've done for other kingdoms. Ciara will provide the details at the pigeon coops.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will earn you their favor, lord, for the trust you've shown my cousin.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfway there.

speaker: Eivor
en: That will have earned King Flann some support. I'd best go see him at Clogher.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Care to sing a song? Helps me pass the time. Come here, raider. Have a sit with me. Hear a story or two

speaker: Eivor
en: That song... you have spent some days on a longship.

speaker: Skari
en: O, many! See all this salt blasted hair? Took a pummeling over the years, all that sea water. Feels like hay now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Better keep away from the horses, then.

speaker: Skari
en: Ha! You are very quick. And sturdy by the looks of you. But you are not from that Ragnarsson camp there, in Repton. I would have recognized you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I belong to another clan. What are you doing away from yours?

speaker: Skari
en: I have been cast out. Too old, too frail. Deadweight, as they say. I will have to get used to watching the sights of war from afar now.

speaker: Eivor
en: No shame in that. Not many of us can say the lived long enough to simplt retire. You have earned it.

speaker: Skari
en: But have I? Or have I missed my chance? I though I knew what lay ahead, but now that is foreign to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Embrace it. Sail the seas. Write your songs and bellow out on the wind. Sounds nice to me.

speaker: Skari
en: You are far too young to speak so wise. There is a bright future for you and your clan. I would like to add to it. Take this key, and if you find yourself in Repton, seek out my quarters near the docks. There's a large oak tree out front. inside, you will find a few of my most prized items. Take them, I no longer have any need.

speaker: Eivor
en: You honor me.

speaker: Skari
en: Call it a gift, from the old guard to the new. Odin guide your way, young drengr (courageous warrior).

speaker: Eivor
en: I should keep an eye out for this old raider's home if I ever am in Repton.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be that old raider's place. He said he wanted me to have his things.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that everything?

speaker: Eivor
en: This crate is filled with songs. Must have taken a long time to write them all out. I should return it to the old raider.

speaker: Eivor
en: These are some trinkets you left behind, old man.

speaker: Skari
en: Ah! You've come back. Why are you wasting your time with me?

speaker: Eivor
en: This crate has all of your written songs. This is not a gift I can accept or repay. You'll want to revisit these someday. They should stay with you.

speaker: Skari
en: I had forgotten all about them. Something to work at on this new journey of mine.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have only the setting sun to tell you when to stop.

speaker: Skari
en: And maybe not even then! That is twice you have earned my admiration. Please, tell me your name.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor.

speaker: Skari
en: Eivor. If the gods will it, I will find my seat at Odin's table before you. And there I will speak of you, so that when the time comes to claim your seat, they will greet you by name. Farewell.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Hearken to me, if wisdom you seek.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am here, old man. Tell me your tale.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Three young men came to me not long ago. Braggarts, full of drink and sin. Death had claimed a friend of theirs, so they set out to find Death, and teach him a lesson.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is foolish. We Norse do not seek to control death. We embrace it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Aye. But rudely they demanded of me, "Tell us where to find Death! You are old, you must know him!" "Look no further," said I. "He is under the great oak in the forest behind me." And that is where they went.

speaker: Eivor
en: A strange tale, and one that lingers like a terrible dream.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this the great oak the old man spoke of?

speaker: Eivor
en: Death. So this is what the old man meant. But what happened here?

speaker: Eivor
en: By his pallor, I would say poison took this one's life. What was he reaching for, I wonder?

speaker: Eivor
en: Strangled. That is no bandit's work.

speaker: Eivor
en: Killed by poison. No sign of a struggle. He must have taken it unknowingly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Food and ale. But why make a camp here, if they were searching for Death as the old man said?

speaker: Eivor
en: Silver. No doubt this played some part in this sorry scene.

speaker: Eivor
en: The three men found hidden treasure beneath the tree. They made camp while they decided how to split the prize. Two of them turned on the third. But he was one step ahead of them, and had already poisoned their ale. So the glister of silver drove these greedy fools to murder. It seems they found Death after all. Or Death found them.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You alright there?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, hello. I do not mean to intrude but... I am looking for someone.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: And who would that be, then?

speaker: Eivor
en: I... do not know exactly.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Well, that'd be why you en't found him. But you're free to pass the time just here if you like.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: These are soul cakes, love. Do you know soul cakes?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I do. I enjoy them.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: They're small things, size of a lumpy fist, so they'll bake fast. Keep your eyes sharp!

speaker: King Aelfred
en: And the butter? Do I... baste them?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: No need, love. We'll leave the butter for mealtime.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I look forward to it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Right then, I'll leave you to this. If you need me, I'll be doing the washing up next door.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite a step down from your former work, lord.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: As their guest, I volunteered to help with the daily chores. They offer me a bed. I tend the cakes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do they not feel strange giving orders to their king? Or do they know?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: That knowledge would benefit no one.

speaker: Eivor
en: I read your message. You went through a great deal of trouble to obscure yourself as this Poor Soldier of Christ. As I remember, you even sent yourself one of these letters in Wincestre. A clever touch.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: The Order wanted me dead. I had to be careful.

speaker: Eivor
en: You said you knew nothing about The Order then. Plead ignorance. But you knew everything. Their names, their schemes.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Would you join me for a walk?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: You look well, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am. The wars have ended, and my settlement thrives.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: The wars have not ended. You have simply stopped fighting. But men are brewing plots in meadhalls and bedrooms. You will see.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how are you, Aelfred? Getting used to the idea of being unremarkable?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I am well. Better than I expected. In this exile, I have found a somewhat nourishing peace. Each morning, I am awakened by the sun and growing cormorants, I bathe in the chilly water of the marsh, I eat from shrubs and drink from buckets. It is a good life. Simple. Blessed.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I have never been so far west. I find it quite peaceful here. Calming.

speaker: Eivor
en: I traveled a long way to hear one name, Aelfred. Who is The Order's Grand Maegester?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Tell your shadowy friends that England is swept clean. Your work is done.

speaker: Eivor
en: You?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Grand Maegester was not a title I desired. It passed to me on the death of my brother, from my father before him. Defilers of God's majesty and grandeur. I was their master, and I loathed them. With Goodwin, I set a plan in motion to destroy The Order from within. But my troubles with the Danes delayed that plan.

speaker: Eivor
en: But your trouble with this Dane is what led to their demise.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: You are Norse, are you not?

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a good ear.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I owe you my thanks, Eivor. For that, I give you this, the key to my study. That you may better understand the good you have done.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: With The Order all but destroyed, you have made room for a greater idea, one to take its place. A universal, divine order. Inspired by God for the betterment of man.

speaker: Eivor
en: With a Poor-Fellow Soldier at its head.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: You have saved England, whether or not that was your intent. Now, let England save you.

speaker: Eivor
en: England is no more, lord. You are the last of her kings, and yet you have no kingdom.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Look around you. God's works are wondrous, they cannot be ignored, nor resisted. In time, all those who accept God will flourish. And all those who defy Him will fall away. Should you remain in England, you too will one day be her subject.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: O, bloody crumbs! The cakes are burnt! Where is that man! Young man? Where have you gone?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Damn. That may have earned me a night of washing linens. I do not know if we shall meet again, Eivor. God willing, we will... as one lord to another, perhaps.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I'm coming, my lady. I'm here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfred gave me a key to unlock his study. Somewhere in Wincestre.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: O dear, o dear. Look at them. Little balls of soot.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Good lady, forgive me. I was lost in thought.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: No matter. Just let them cool and we'll begin again.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Direct me and I will obey.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is it, Aelfred's study. What secrets has he kept hidden away?

speaker: Eivor
en: Rantings and ravings, not unlike Fulke's delusions. Is there more to all this that I understand?

speaker: Jotun
en: Havi, he called himself. Serpent-tongue, I say.

speaker: Havi
en: The roots of the world-tree Yggdrasil feed from the Well of Mimir. I am close.

speaker: Havi
en: I sorely underestimated the heft of your balls, oath-breaker. You dare show your face?

speaker: Loki
en: Oath-breaker? I did to you what you did to my son. This is only fair.

speaker: Havi
en: And Suttungr? What of him?

speaker: Loki
en: Don't blame me for your own lack of character. You stole the Mead!

speaker: Havi
en: For the safety of my people, Loki! For Æsir, for Vanir, for all Asgard!

speaker: Loki
en: But not for Jötnar. Not for me.

speaker: Havi
en: You let the Jotnar into Asgard! So many dead, all so you could smuggle in your son.

speaker: Loki
en: He was not safe here. They knew what he was and knew what he would become. Just as you do!

speaker: Havi
en: I swore to you I would not harm him. That is the truth!

speaker: Loki
en: That is the truth now. But how it will gnaw at you, knowing that to kill my son will undo your doom. Release him, Havi. Release Fenrir, or I swear I will kill you here and now.

speaker: Havi
en: You are out of favors, trickster. And you are welcome to try.

speaker: Loki
en: You might be strongest, but I was ever the quicker one!

speaker: Havi
en: Curse you, Loki. We were like brothers once!

speaker: Loki
en: I will feed your corpse to Fenrir!

speaker: Havi
en: You meant to have me killed! I will never forgive that.

speaker: Loki
en: Why wait till Ragnarök, when you can die now?

speaker: Havi
en: No quarter this time, Loki! You have gone too far!

speaker: Loki
en: When my son is loosed from his bondage, he will ravage all of Asgard!

speaker: Havi
en: Let's see if you fight as well as you lie!

speaker: Havi
en: Are you finished?

speaker: Loki
en: Curse you, Havi.

speaker: Havi
en: Your own distrust has undone you. Now go, and do not show your face again.

speaker: Loki
en: I cannot be other than who I am. All this was fated. All this will happen again.

speaker: Havi
en: But you will not be here to see it.

speaker: Loki
en: Do not be so sure of that. The game is not over. The game is never over.

speaker: Havi
en: Gone, to who knows what mischief. But I will not see him again soon.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Bring the Mead. As soon as you can.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: The probabilities lead us here. The calculations give us hope.

speaker: Havi
en: Speaking with someone?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Do you have the Mead?

speaker: Havi
en: I do. Must I drink it now?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Not yet. For once you drink, your hugr will take flight and be ever-fixed. Drink only when the hour of your death approaches.

speaker: Havi
en: Then why are we here?

speaker: Mimir
en: When Ragnarok has come and gone, this place will remain. Remain, and remember.

speaker: Havi
en: Wise Mimir, keeper of the well. Give me your counsel.

speaker: Mimir
en: You who seek immortality may find it within these waters. But there is a price.

speaker: Havi
en: As always.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: The Mead is not magic alone. It requires the sacred waters of Mimir's well to ferment into its final state.

speaker: Mimir
en: Before you take these waters, you must infuse them with the blood of the Aesir. To remember you, it must know you. Surrender a part of yourself to the waters that nourish the world-tree. Only then will you have that which you desire.

speaker: Havi
en: You yourself have lost much for wisdom, beheaded by those who did not value your learning.

speaker: Mimir
en: My hugr is here. That is all that matters. I have learned to live incomplete, as will you.

speaker: Havi
en: And if I make this sacrifice? What then?

speaker: Havi
en: Gunlodr warned of chaos and change. I would know the cost.

speaker: Mimir
en: Aesir blood will infuse this water, and the poor humans of Midgard will be forever altered. What happens then, none can say.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: This is what the others feared. But then they always cared overmuch for vermin.

speaker: Havi
en: And if I make this sacrifice? What then?

speaker: Havi
en: And if I make this sacrifice? What then?

speaker: Mimir
en: While death and ruin rage all around, the world-tree will keep you. Your body will die, but your hugr will live on here. In time, you will be born anew, into a new world birthed from the ashes of the old.

speaker: Havi
en: Do you vouch for this strangeness?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: I must believe it, for there is one I love dearly who depends upon it.

speaker: Havi
en: And there is no other way?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: None.

speaker: Havi
en: It seems I have no choice.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: You never did.

speaker: Angrboda
en: How much would you sacrifice to be freed of fate's shackles? Would you give your tongue, your hand, your sight?

speaker: Havi
en: I would give all that and more.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: It is done.

speaker: Mimir
en: The sacrifice has been made. Whosoever drinks of the Mead, the world-tree will remember them.

speaker: Havi
en: And you? What is your sacrifice?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: My liberty. Suttungr and Gunlodr will not forgive this trespass. They will hunt me now, to the edges of the nine worlds.

speaker: Havi
en: What are they to you?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: We ruled together for a time, a noble triad. As Father, Mother, and the Sacred Voice. Six times we tried to blunt the fangs of Ragnarok, and six times we failed. The Mead was our seventh. But they feared how it might change the humans for the worse, so they locked it away and banished me from Utgard. By your efforts, you have returned to me what is mine. The ashes of my husband. He made his own sacrifice for knowledge. With a few changes to this Mead, I may undo old sorrows.

speaker: Havi
en: Do as you will. I have had my fill of this cursed realm.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Bright-mind, heart's-ease, beloved. I will not fail you again.

speaker: Havi
en: My work here is done. Now to Asgard, to save my people.

speaker: Havi
en: Here is the true tale of how I defeated two of the Muspels' greatest fighters. As I wiped the blood from my weapon, a group of Muspels took me by surprise! Next, fate steered me into the path of a mighty Muspel, and battle was joined!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Hey, hey! Careful with that one.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd!

speaker: Sigurd
en: O, look at you, blood-soaked drengr. Have you been warring without me?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, and you, salt-cured vikingr. I smell the stink of a dozen kingdoms in your beard.

speaker: Sigurd
en: It's just the start.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Randvi, my dear wife. Your husband returns, bringing gifts and riches to share.

speaker: Randvi
en: And new friends, I see.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yes! Basim... and Hytham. We met in Miklagard, and they showed me her buried secrets.

speaker: Basim
en: We are grateful to Sigurd for his invitation, and eager to pay tribute to your king.

speaker: Eivor
en: My brother is always very careful with the company he keeps. If you are standing safely beside him, he must like you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, save the introductions until our bellies are full. I will see my father, tell him of my time away.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This morning we traded with a ship passing south. They told us Eivor the Wolf-Kissed was captured by Kjotve's men.

speaker: Eivor
en: They must have cut the tale short. I killed my captors and recovered my crew. And for that, your father scolded me. You know where I stand, Brother. Nothing short of war will dislodge Kjotve from our lands. But he disagrees.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I know, I know. Father thinks too much and acts too little. Today that changes. I promise you. By the winter's end, the name Kjotve the Cruel will be a curse on the lips of a drunken fool.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: My son. Welcome home.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ah, Father...

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Tonight we feast and celebrate your return, Sigurd. The tables are laid with barley and lamb, bread and mead

speaker: Sigurd
en: And no more, I beg you. I want nothing you would not serve a . Let me be the one to honor you. I bring gifts and tales from faraway lands. After two winters away, I am full up with both.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Very well, very well. Come inside.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And when we are fat and satisfied, Father, we will talk of Kjotve and his clan. And how we may end their terror, once and for all. He has dogged us too long. Shamed us for too many seasons. I know this. Eivor knows this... It ends now.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Yes, of course. When the time is right.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Through Rusland we barreled down the Volga river, raiding as we went, shadowy tribes hurling spears at our ship. At Miklagard, we saw men bedecked in riches as vibrant as the Bifröst itself. These we took for our troubles, of course! We sailed to Rome, then Africa. Past oceans of sand, warriors of all colors, and beauty the eyes must weep to behold. And now, I have returned! With riches and glory to share with my family, my friends, my ice-forged drengir! So take what you desire from my hoard. For this... this is only a taste of things to come. Tomorrow, the Raven Clan starts anew!

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Skal, Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Skal!

speaker: Eivor
en: And you, Eivor. Come! I have something special for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd has raised the reputation of this clan to new heights, lord. We could not have asked for a more joyous return.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: O, but we could have. Had Sigurd spent his last two winters here in Fornburg, defending our lands, we might have been rid of Kjotve by now.

speaker: Eivor
en: You always said we needed more warriors to fight Kjotve. And for warriors, we need wealth, which Sigurd has brought us.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: The wealth he brings will not buy us an army. It only buys us time before our end.

speaker: Eivor
en: You talk like a man with one foot in Helheim. Have you no plan of your own to rid this land of our enemy? Will it fall to Sigurd and me?

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I do. But it will fall to you and Sigurd to accept it. And I must have your word that you will.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you so order it, my king, it will be done. You have my axe until the end.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Hmm. We shall see.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor. Have you paid a visit to Valka?

speaker: Eivor
en: I did.

speaker: Randvi
en: And...?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not something I can speak on. Or wish to.

speaker: Randvi
en: I understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your bed will be warm tonight with your husband returned. That must be a good feeling.

speaker: Randvi
en: It is a different feeling. Warmer, but with less space to stretch my arms and legs.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you not happy to see your husband returned?

speaker: Randvi
en: Of course. But it has been so long, he seems a stranger to me. Three winters we are married and he has been away for two.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you not rekindle the flame that once burned hot?

speaker: Randvi
en: Hmph. When he crawls into bed to warm me, as you say, it will be with farts and honeyed breath.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. We should all be so lucky.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham is it?

speaker: Hytham
en: Yes, and you are Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am. I hope this ruckus does not overwhelm you. We tend to drink and talk at equal speed.

speaker: Hytham
en: Not at all. The woodsmoke from your firepit does sting the eyes. But the warmth is welcome.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of course. It must be rather warm where you live.

speaker: Hytham
en: Where I live changes from week to week. But always I am with my mentor, Basim.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your mentor? For what cause?

speaker: Hytham
en: A noble one, a cause as true as the world is old. But let us leave it at that for now.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. But if you hope to stay tight-lipped for the rest of the night, keep clear of Tekla's mead.

speaker: Hytham
en: Ah. Thank you for the warning. It will not be a problem.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: You have a good memory.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you have no mead. Can I fix that?

speaker: Basim
en: Sigurd spoke often of you on our journey. Called you his right arm, a celebrated warrior. I am honored to meet you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Likewise, Basim. And how did you come to meet my brother?

speaker: Basim
en: He set down in Constantinople some months ago, to rest and resupply he told me. But I knew otherwise. Men with eyes that gleam like his are always up to something more. I think he wished to raid the Hagia Sophia.

speaker: Eivor
en: That sounds right.

speaker: Basim
en: I will not bore you with the details of our meeting, but I liked your brother from the first. I saw something in him that captivated me. As if a forgotten memory of an old friendship had suddenly resurfaced.

speaker: Eivor
en: He has that effect on people. Enjoy your evening, Basim.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I thought long and hard on a gift worthy of you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have snared my curiosity, Brother. What is it?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not yet. Drinks first! To my first night in Fornburg in over two winters. It must end with me soaked and wall-eyed, shouting at the shadows of trolls!

speaker: Eivor
en: And you want me to sail with you on these honey-waves?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yes! You are stuck with me, drengr. Now drink!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Gah! You would put Thor to shame!

speaker: Eivor
en: Forgive me. On your first day back, I should have let you win.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Gods, you should have let me start!

speaker: Eivor
en: From drinking to breathing, you turn everything into a competition, Brother. I must always be prepared.

speaker: Sigurd
en: True enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have been away too long, Brother. You do not know the spiced kick of Tekla's mead.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Mm. It does have a new taste. I like it.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is good to have you back, Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yes, I have missed this terribly. When I first met Basim, I regaled him with tales of our homeland. And it was then I felt a hard longing to return at once.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Come. This brings us to your gift. These excellent men were my shepherds through much of their homeland, the Abbasid Caliphate. They are a clan not joined by blood, but by a common idea. A brotherhood of shadows executing their own form of justice. In my time with them, they shared many of their most hidden secrets. For which I am grateful. And now... I gift one of these secrets to you. A weapon, for the finest warrior I know.

speaker: Eivor
en: Beautiful craftsmanship. What kind of smith makes a weapon like this?

speaker: Basim
en: It is less a weapon than a tool. One we have used for centuries to fight injustice and evil.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not the most threatening weapon, is it? A bracer with a tiny blade.

speaker: Basim
en: It may not look like much, but those who underestimate its effectiveness are often the first to die by its sting.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham is not amused, it seems. Am I not worthy of this gift?

speaker: Hytham
en: It is not about worth, Eivor. It is a matter of devotion to our creed. And... and training

speaker: Basim
en: Hytham, please.

speaker: Hytham
en: Mentor, I must protest. This is deeply unorthodox. Our wrist-blade is a sacred tool

speaker: Basim
en: Do not make a fetish out of cold metal, Hytham. What matters is the mind of the one who wields it. Please. Try it on.

speaker: Basim
en: The blade should ride on the underside of your arm. To conceal it from your target.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no wish to hide this. And I would rather not make the same mistake you two have. I like it.

speaker: Hytham
en: This is no mistake. This is a voluntary sacrifice to prove our devotion to

speaker: Basim
en: A good start, Eivor. but you must learn how to use it effectively.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Outside. This is not something for all eyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lead on.

speaker: Eivor
en: This clan of yours. It has a name?

speaker: Basim
en: Indeed, but among the tenants of our creed is a vow to never reveal too much to outsiders. In time, you may learn more. But not here, where the walls and trees may have ears.

speaker: Eivor
en: I look forward to it.

speaker: Basim
en: Here, let me lead you through our most basic techniques. Wielded with skill and care, our blade delivers a singular killing blow. As you near your target, find your window to strike. Timing is essential.

speaker: Basim
en: Excellent.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have not seen a blade so sharp.

speaker: Basim
en: Some targets are trickier than others. Keep that in mind before you strike.

speaker: Hytham
en: A decent attempt.

speaker: Basim
en: Take that one down from the ledge.

speaker: Basim
en: That's it.

speaker: Sigurd
en: How about a challenge? Leap down upon that target from above.

speaker: Basim
en: A perfect strike. Use your surroundings when possible. Strike from that haystack, for instance.

speaker: Basim
en: Exactly. Just like that.

speaker: Hytham
en: Mentor, does Eivor intend to join us?

speaker: Basim
en: Not that I am aware.

speaker: Hytham
en: Then why offer her the blade? Surely we have more

speaker: Basim
en: Hytham. Hush. You wield the blade well. Let us leave Eivor to enjoy her gift in peace. Come.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor. Let us walk to the docks and take in the night air.

speaker: Sigurd
en: What do you make of my new friends?

speaker: Eivor
en: They seem generous and menacing in equal measure.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I know what you mean. And they have learning too. They wield numbers and writing as if it were magic. Basim has shown me so much about the world. All of which I will share with you... when the time is right.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ah! I missed the smell of this land.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you returned for good, or do you mean to join this shadow brotherhood?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Leave all that aside, Eivor. Tonight we are family again. The here and now is what matters. Our kinship, our clan... our glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: I missed you, Brother. Your clear head and your courage. We have not had enough of both in recent months.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You flatter me, Wolf-Kissed. Keep it up.

speaker: Eivor
en: From here to Valhalla, I will always be by your side, Sigurd. Always.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This fjord has grown too small to contain me, or I too large. There is so much more beyond these stony fangs that rise around us. England, Ireland, Francia... all greener pastures, ripe for the plucking. Tomorrow we make new war on Kjotve. And reclaim the lands he took from us. And from there, we build a kingdom. For us.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm with you. Only say the word.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Good. Get some rest and return here at first light.

speaker: Keith
en: All we want is to share our music with the world!

speaker: Bishop of the Ruins
en: Devote yourselves to Godlier activities.

speaker: Keith
en: You stomp our spirits with your talk of devils.

speaker: Bishop of the Ruins
en: God will strike you down for your malodorous melodies! Dancing! Music! Songs and poems, they are all Satan's dark dalliance!

speaker: Keith
en: Take a breath, all that vitriol can kill a man!

speaker: Bishop of the Ruins
en: Go back to the hellhole you crawled out of.

speaker: Keith
en: This is our home! We're not tourists.

speaker: Keith
en: Now you have broken my flow! How can a man compose with you spewing in his ear?

speaker: Eivor
en: Why the wailing?

speaker: Keith
en: We are a band of bards. Ahead of our time. Musical prodigies even. But that madman, the self-proclaimed Bishop of the Ruins is our biggest critic. He calls our playing "the Devil's bagpipes."

speaker: Eivor
en: That strange instrument, made of bladder and bone? It does wheeze like an old woman.

speaker: Keith
en: He drives away our audience with his doom-knelling. All we want is to bring a little joy to this jilted generation.

speaker: Eivor
en: A worthy aim. Maybe he needs convincing of your talents?

speaker: Keith
en: You would volunteer? Ah! Your are a lover of fine music, this is surely an omen!

speaker: Bishop of the Ruins
en: Renounce your perverted ways before the Lord of Flies claims you!

speaker: Keith
en: Music and dancing make me whole, worry not of my immortal soul.

speaker: Bishop of the Ruins
en: Ah! My ears are bleeding.

speaker: Keith
en: Play on, play on!

speaker: Bishop of the Ruins
en: This cacophony, it is as if a thousand devils grind their pointy teeth!

speaker: Keith
en: You do not appreciate great art!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why not let the boy play music? He brings pleasure to the people.

speaker: Bishop of the Ruins
en: Music is the Devil's wind-breaking! Foul and rancid. I, as the Bishop of the Ruins, will not stand for it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bishop of the Ruins? Is this title Aelfred-given?

speaker: Bishop of the Ruins
en: It is God-given! He spoke to me as I stood one night pissing against the stones. I am his instrument to stamp out the Devil's tune.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then you and I must disagree.

speaker: Keith
en: Punch the priest! Smack my bishop! Clout that cleric!

speaker: Keith
en: You have done us a great service! I will compose this day into a song! Farewell.

speaker: Eivor
en: May you continue to make merry harmonies.

speaker: Keith
en: Smack my bishop! Smack my bishop!

speaker: Dead Body
en: Heaven won't let me in! I'm stuck being dead. Wayfarer! I'm dead. I'm so dead! Help me, wayfarer, or you'll see me in your dreams! I'm warning you! In your dreams, I said!

speaker: Dead Body
en: Speak!

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you?

speaker: Dead Body
en: I died a terrible death, killed by wolves or something. Nobody read the last rites! I'm stuck in purgatory. Have a heart, wayfarer, give a little something to help free me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Give something?

speaker: Dead Body
en: A little... offering to help a fellow out on my journey to the land of the dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am not fooled by trickery.

speaker: Dead Body
en: Don't pester dead people! Fifty pieces of silver will be enough to bring me peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find you... and kill you.

speaker: Dead Body
en: Twelve pieces of silver?

speaker: Eivor
en: You'll soon be dead enough.

speaker: Dead Body
en: A head of cabbage?

speaker: Eivor
en: You're stuck in this realm? I'm very sorry for you, dead man.

speaker: Dead Body
en: It is an embarrassing situation. Just leave your offering on the ground, please.

speaker: Dead Body
en: What about it, wayfarer? Are you listening? I'm a dead man!

speaker: Eivor
en: It is rare that spirits return to the land of the living. How can I know what you say is true?

speaker: Dead Body
en: I am a talking dead man, is that not enough for you?

speaker: Dead Body
en: What about it, wayfarer? Are you listening? I'm a dead man! I don't have all day, wayfarer. You should know, the dead do not have an abundance of patience! My soul won't rest until you open your purse and put some fucking silver on the ground!

speaker: Dead Body
en: Wayfarer? Where are you going? Get back here!

speaker: Dead Body
en: Ah! Now I can rest in peace in the land of the dead and all that. You can go, wayfarer. Go ahead. No need to stay!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah! What is this? An entrance.

speaker: Eivor
en: The voice of the dead! You appear much livelier than I expected.

speaker: Swindler
en: I tried to swindle you, so what? Life is tough! It's good business being a dead man.

speaker: Swindler
en: No need to get angry about this.

speaker: Eivor
en: This belongs to the living!

speaker: Swindler
en: That's mine! I swindled hard for that! Give it here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now you are truly dead. Speak all you want.

speaker: Jotun
en: Skami! Speak to me! What has that bastard done to you?

speaker: Havi
en: Who has caged this Jotun?

speaker: Jotun
en: An Æsir? It is a dire day when even enemies must be friends. But I must beg for your help. A hunter lives in a house nearby. He has become crazed, and now he preys on his fellow Jotnar. He has captured and beat my love, and soon he means to skin him like a rabbit! Will you have mercy and aid us?

speaker: Havi
en: Where is this hunter?

speaker: Jotun
en: Inside the house, asleep. Quickly, you must kill him before he wakes! He will have the key to this cage.

speaker: Jotun
en: I'll free you, I promise! I'll find the key to this lock!

speaker: Havi
en: A door in a wall? Is this the house she meant?

speaker: Havi
en: Well that wasn't there before.

speaker: Havi
en: A woman's hairbrush. Perhaps this hunter does not live alone.

speaker: Hunter
en: An Intruder! Die, Aesir! Get out of my house! Scum of Asgard! Trying to cut my throat in the night! You'll be my newest trophy!

speaker: Hunter
en: Stop! Stop! Take what you want, just spare me!

speaker: Havi
en: I am no thief. I am here to free the Jotun you have imprisoned.

speaker: Hunter
en: That villain? He's lucky I only caged him. How would you react if you found another man porking your wife?

speaker: Havi
en: Your wife?

speaker: Hunter
en: Aye. I've been waiting for her to return so I can thrash her. She won't be able to walk once I'm done.

speaker: Havi
en: You have imprisoned her lover, and you mean to beat her when she returns. I think I'll just finish what I started.

speaker: Hunter
en: Then you shouldn't have let me catch my breath, fool!

speaker: Havi
en: The key to the cage outside.

speaker: Havi
en: There's no need to die for your vengeance. Give me the key, and keep your life.

speaker: Hunter
en: You leave me little choice. Let that faithless wench have her pretty-boy, then. Here's the key.

speaker: Havi
en: The key to the cage outside.

speaker: Hunter
en: A curse on that woman. Sending an Aesir to do her dirty work!

speaker: Havi
en: Your wife has deceived me. I'll leave you in peace.

speaker: Hunter
en: Good. And leave that wretch in his cage. I'll deal with him later.

speaker: Hunter
en: Gods help her when I catch her. I'll skin them both alive.

speaker: Havi
en: The key to the cage outside.

speaker: Havi
en: The key to the cage outside.

speaker: Havi
en: It is done. The hunter is dead.

speaker: Jotun
en: Wonderful stranger! My everlasting thanks for saving me... saving us. Hurry now! Release him!

speaker: Havi
en: You're free to go.

speaker: Skami
en: My love. I knew you'd come for me. And your husband? Is he dead?

speaker: Jotun
en: He'll trouble us no more.

speaker: Skami
en: Then we can claim the house that's rightfully yours and begin life again. Let me rest awhile first, though. Everything hurts.

speaker: Havi
en: I have the key, Jotun, but I am not your assassin. Be satisfied with that.

speaker: Jotun
en: O, stone and soil! Now he will hunt us wherever we go! You have saved us and doomed us all at once! Hurry now! Release him!

speaker: Havi
en: You're free to go.

speaker: Skami
en: My love. I knew you'd come for me. And your husband? Is he dead?

speaker: Jotun
en: He still lives. We must make haste, away to our secret tower! Maybe he will not find us there.

speaker: Skami
en: As soon as I regain my strength, we will go. I fear I am too weak to move.

speaker: Jotun
en: O, you must try! He will not be long, I know it!

speaker: Havi
en: You lied to me, Jotun. You tried to have me murder your husband. Get the key yourself if you dare.

speaker: Jotun
en: A curse on all Aesir. Begone from my sight and never speak to me more.

speaker: Eivor
en: I mean to bargain with your husband, the king, but he's a complicated man.

speaker: Richardis
en: You are being diplomatic. Charles was not always as he is now. When he was a boy, he fell into bits of madness. His keepers believed him possessed and put him through a ritual. His conversion afterwards was sincere, though he gained a terrible fear of fire. When we met, he was honorable and pious.

speaker: Eivor
en: You sound proud of Charles. You loved him.

speaker: Richardis
en: Do I? Yes, in a way. But we have never been a normal husband and wife... in private.

speaker: Eivor
en: Does he not love you?

speaker: Richardis
en: It is not him. I could never be what he needed. But he is a man, and found solace elsewhere... often.

speaker: Eivor
en: The nun, Little Mother, was going to kill you.

speaker: Richardis
en: Perhaps. Her deliverance rituals were brutal and cruel. Few survived. Euphrasia belonged to a secret group that believes Francia has fallen into apostasy. She thought me possessed.

speaker: Eivor
en: The bishop Engelwin was part of this group, I think.

speaker: Richardis
en: You know of Engelwin? Yes. They call themselves Bellatores Dei, God's Warriors. And there are more of them.

speaker: Richardis
en: We have arrived. There is Bernard.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have brought me all this way to see a child?

speaker: Richardis
en: Yes. Charles has a son.

speaker: Richardis
en: Little Bear!

speaker: Bernard
en: Richardis! You're safe!

speaker: Richardis
en: God protects me. Never doubt that, child.

speaker: Richardis
en: Bernard, this is Eivor. A friend.

speaker: Richardis
en: Go now, and wash yourself. You've got more color on your shirt than on the canvas.

speaker: Richardis
en: He paints beautifully for a child, don't you think?

speaker: Eivor
en: He is better than many I've seen. Did you teach him?

speaker: Richardis
en: I do not have that gift. He got the ability from his mother, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is clear from the subject choice that he admires his father.

speaker: Richardis
en: Bernard does not yet know Charles' dark side. Thankfully, the boy is more like his mother.

speaker: Eivor
en: He called you by your first name.

speaker: Richardis
en: Yes, it seems odd for a child, I know. But I am not his mother. Nothing else felt right.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bernard is not your son?

speaker: Richardis
en: How could he be? Yet I love him as if he was. As I said, Charles and I were never that way.

speaker: Richardis
en: But he's a man, and a king. Naturally, he found other places to satisfy his appetites. From that came Bernard.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're hiding the boy from his father?

speaker: Richardis
en: Charles wants Bernard to succeed him to the throne, and Bernard wants nothing else but to please his father.

speaker: Richardis
en: That is why I must keep Bernard from him. He will lead the child down a dark path, one not meant for a good king.

speaker: Eivor
en: My agreement with Charles was only to return with you. The child need not be involved.

speaker: Richardis
en: And I will not let him be. Bernard knows to find a church if he needs help and I am not there.

speaker: Richardis
en: I must leave again for a while. When I return, I want to hear your Latin verbs.

speaker: Bernard
en: I know you're going to see Father without me. I'm not stupid you know!

speaker: Eivor
en: By keeping Bernard from Charles, you hope to prevent him becoming king?

speaker: Richardis
en: You misunderstand me, Eivor. Bernard must assume the throne, for the good of Francia. You see what Charles has become. Bernard is young, but will make a good ruler. One that will be more sympathetic to your people, also.

speaker: Eivor
en: If Charles wants the child, he will not be pleased to see you without him.

speaker: Richardis
en: I hope that is not true. Charles knows the Bellatores took me. He would be concerned. We have not been on good terms lately. But he sent you to free me. Perhaps he wishes to be reconciled.

speaker: Richardis
en: That bear is wounded.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait! If it is wounded, it is dangerous!

speaker: Richardis
en: It's alright. Shh. What have you done to yourself? There. God is with you. Be more careful now. Off you go.

speaker: Richardis
en: They are noble animals. She had given up. She is alright now, thanks to God.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are all bears so tame in Francia?

speaker: Richardis
en: All of God's beasts respond to love, Eivor. Even more so when they are hurt. In that, they are not so different to people.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have the gift with beasts. But you are speaking of Charles now. You think the same is true even of him.

speaker: Richardis
en: Especially of him.

speaker: Richardis
en: We are here. Charles' camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: I fulfilled our agreement. Here is your wife, the queen. She is unharmed.

speaker: Richardis
en: Charles...

speaker: Charles
en: My dear wife. Finally, you appear before me. You must want for refreshment after your long and complicated journey.

speaker: Richardis
en: You are still angry. It is for nothing, Charles. I have been as faithful to you as I have been to God. I am sorry for taking Bernard, but

speaker: Charles
en: Ah yes, my son. I thought by finding you I would find him, but I do not see him. Where is Bernard?

speaker: Richardis
en: Safe.

speaker: Charles
en: Do you remember the night we met? I've never forgotten it. The sky was clear and awash with thousands of stars. The night of our wedding, it was the same. I took it as a sign from God. I knew you and I were meant to be. You were in white, all purity and grace. I thought, "Tonight, I am not the prince. I am the luckiest man alive." How lucky to take a wife who fell so easily into another's bed. You did not take me as your man, but as your fool.

speaker: Richardis
en: Charles, no...

speaker: Charles
en: To our "marriage"!

speaker: Eivor
en: We had a deal.

speaker: Charles
en: O, do not be concerned about Bernard, Richardis. He is my son. Without your interference, he will find me.

speaker: Charles
en: And you, Northern devil, who presumes to sit at the negotiating table with a Frankish king. Here is your deal.

speaker: Eivor
en: You lied to me.

speaker: Charles
en: I did not lie, diable (devil). I said God would make it so. And so he has.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will take care of the guards. Stay hidden!

speaker: Eivor
en: Kings. Always saying what they do not mean, to get what they do not say they want.

speaker: Richardis
en: I failed to mention everything about Charles. I'm sorry. The truth is awkward, and I did not see the need.

speaker: Eivor
en: He believes you to be unfaithful.

speaker: Richardis
en: There is no end to his accusations. I hoped he had come to himself. Do you think he really meant to kill us?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. Now Paris will fall, Charles has made certain of that. Sigfred was right.

speaker: Richardis
en: Don't despise Charles. Like that bear, he may yet recover with God's help and become your ally.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not share your faith in your God or your husband. But you carry both with a rare honor.

speaker: Richardis
en: Thank you. That is a high compliment. For my part, I don't think God has finished with you yet. We were meant to meet. Now I must find Bernard. We will go to the Paris slums and aid the sick. Charles will not look for us there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must go meet Sigfred at the forward camp in Paris. I have a siege to prepare, and pride to swallow.

speaker: Richardis
en: God exalts the humble, Eivor of Raven Clan. You will see. Farewell for now!

speaker: Raven Clan Warrior 1
en: Who do you work for? Who is your lord? Use your tongue or I will feed it to you!

speaker: Raven Clan Warrior 2
en: Eivor, you should hear this.

speaker: Raven Clan Warrior 1
en: This bacraut (asshole) and his friends had the foolish balls to raid Ravensthorpe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are the others dead?

speaker: Raven Clan Warrior 1
en: A few. Most of them escaped. They did not damage much but made off with some of our gear. Should I get Randvi?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, she has enough on her table. I'll handle this.

speaker: Eivor
en: So... you thought you would play at vikingr, little man? Are you prepared to go all the way?

speaker: Saxon Prisoner
en: You won't get anything out of me, Danish scum! I'll never talk!

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Norse. What makes you think I want to hear you talk? Maybe I'll take my payment in flesh.

speaker: Eivor
en: Chop off his leg. It does not need to be a clean cut. No need to sharpen your blade.

speaker: Saxon
en: No! Please! Don't cut off my leg! It was Sir Edward who wanted your stuff! He paid us to do it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sir Edward?

speaker: Saxon Prisoner
en: He's the Earl of Westerna, or that's what he calls himself. Said he hates Vikings, your lot especially.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where can I find this Sir Edward, Earl of Westerna?

speaker: Saxon Prisoner
en: I don't know, I'm new! We were supposed to steal the gear, then meet at the longship west of Ravensburg. That's all I know!

speaker: Eivor
en: You can take him to Randvi now. Maybe we can trade him for a pig. I'm off to check out this longship.

speaker: Eivor
en: Our prisoner did not lie about this location. Fear breeds truth.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like they were planning to launch a raid dressed as Raven Clan... and blame us for it.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Saxons must have stolen this longship. They added our clan banner but do not know how to mount shields.

speaker: Eivor
en: This outfit is still in good shape. I'll reclaim it for our clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: This was a slaughter, not a battle. Their wounds are very precise... and familiar.

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 1
en: You there! What happened here? Who killed the sentries?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not me.

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 1
en: Is that a joke? You won't be laughing when I drag you before Earl Edward to answer for your incompetence!

speaker: Eivor
en: I would very much like to meet your Earl Edward.

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 2
en: Ah, Captain, I think that's a real Viking.

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 1
en: Drop your weapons, Dane, and submit to me!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm Norse. And you will die for soiling the honor of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Roshan
en: You are true Raven Clan. My name is Roshan, and we share a common enemy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sir Edward?

speaker: Roshan
en: The Earl of Westerna is a puppet, manipulated by one called "Al-Si'la", a fitting title given her duplicitous nature. She belongs to an order who employ disruption and strife to further their ends. Your clan is a tool in her schemes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have met such weavers of intrigue before. And those who oppose them.

speaker: Roshan
en: I would consider the enemy of my enemy a friend. Let me guide you to where you can take your revenge on the Earl.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lead the way.

speaker: Eivor
en: If this Al-Si'la seeks to wield my clan's honor as a weapon, she shall find it cuts both ways.

speaker: Roshan
en: Satisfy yourself with the Earl and leave Al-Si'la to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Perhaps this task is best left to one who is young... to one more familiar with these lands.

speaker: Roshan
en: I was killing her kind before you were off your mother's teat. The Earl's death will draw her out. Leave the rest to me. That blade you wear upon your arm, where did you get it?

speaker: Eivor
en: It was a gift. From my brother.

speaker: Roshan
en: Truly? Is he a

speaker: Eivor
en: A great warrior and traveler who discovered many things. And yours?

speaker: Roshan
en: Reclaimed after a long absence. The years without it were the hardest I've known.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your endurance is impressive for one of your years, and I meant no disrespect when I offered to kill the one you

speaker: Roshan
en: My blade has grown neither rusty nor dull. What I lack in brutish strength, I make up in quiet subtlety.

speaker: Eivor
en: I too can be silent when I choose.

speaker: Roshan
en: Ha! You may be exceptional among your kind, child, but I am a lifetime ahead of you in that.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you know of Earl Edward? Why does he hate the Raven Clan so?

speaker: Roshan
en: He blames you for the loss of his title and property. The very land where Ravensthorpe now stands.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was there for the taking, abandoned and uncared for. His quarrel is with those who came before us.

speaker: Roshan
en: It matters not to him. He hates all Vikings and will work with whomever will help discredit you and drive you from England.

speaker: Roshan
en: We will have a better view from atop this tower.

speaker: Roshan
en: That is where Al-Si'la and the Earl make camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: At Ravensburg no less. They will choke on their arrogance.

speaker: Roshan
en: Al-Si'la's gold has built up the fort's defenses. It will be no easy thing to penetrate.

speaker: Eivor
en: A challenge for some perhaps, less so for me. Do you know what lies within its walls?

speaker: Roshan
en: If I described what I have learned, could you picture it with your mind's eye?

speaker: Eivor
en: I can do better. Sýnin!

speaker: Roshan
en: Listen carefully. The Saxons within the outer wall are less disciplined, relying on their Viking attire to deflect curiosity.

speaker: Eivor
en: They will not notice one more Viking among them. I could use the outfit I took off the dead Saxon at the longship.

speaker: Roshan
en: Very good! Also, some Saxons are engaged in tasks which could help you blend in.

speaker: Eivor
en: What of the Earl? Where is he?

speaker: Roshan
en: Within the heart of the encampment, he plays at holding court. But in truth, Al-Si'la keeps him leashed like a hungry dog. The Earl's death must be loud and unmistakable. A clamor Al-Si'la cannot ignore.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, a silent approach with a noisome finish. This is your counsel?

speaker: Roshan
en: Is your mind capable of balancing two conflicting ideas while orchestrating this necessary distraction?

speaker: Eivor
en: I could kill the Earl a hundred different ways while composing a great song for the occasion. Do you have a preference?

speaker: Roshan
en: In the open, beneath that tree. Approach silently, then kill him in full view of his men. That will draw the spider out.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will create a commotion the gods could not ignore.

speaker: Roshan
en: Good. Will you now don the outfit you took from the Saxon imposter? To better blend with the rest?

speaker: Eivor
en: This disguise will help me play the imposter.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me consider the matter before I choose.

speaker: Eivor
en: I shall wear the Saxon disguise, though it be more... common than my usual dress.

speaker: Roshan
en: You look like a real false Viking. You will blend in admirably.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to be patient or risk rousing suspicion.

speaker: Eivor
en: What? You do not approve of my outfit?

speaker: Roshan
en: Your chances would be better if you dressed as they do. Why not wear the outfit you took from that Saxon?

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a point. I would draw less attention.

speaker: Roshan
en: A wise warrior is always open to good counsel.

speaker: Eivor
en: This disguise will help me play the imposter.

speaker: Eivor
en: I shall wear the Saxon disguise, though it be more... common than my usual dress.

speaker: Roshan
en: You look like a real false Viking. You will blend in admirably.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to be patient or risk rousing suspicion.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not need a set of clothes to proclaim I'm Norse.

speaker: Roshan
en: Ha! True. Everything about you screams it for all to hear.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to be patient or risk rousing suspicion. Perhaps I should put on the Saxon's outfit. Pride makes for a poor disguise.

speaker: Eivor
en: At least they got our colors right.

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 3
en: Did you hear the Earl? We're gonna be rich as kings!

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 4
en: Ha! I'll buy that promise when there's coin in my hand.

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 5
en: Why is the Earl so obsessed with the Raven Clan?

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 6
en: They took his land or something, I dunno. Who cares so long as we're paid.

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 7
en: Have you seen that foreign bird, Al-Si'la? I wouldn't mind a slice of that.

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 8
en: Way I hear it, she'd cut you ten ways to next week. Anyway, she rarely leaves that cabin of hers. Keeps it locked tight.

speaker: Eivor
en: This area is heavily guarded. I need to take more care.

speaker: Eivor
en: Al-Si'la's cabin. I will leave her to Roshan.

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: With the riches we earn from these Viking raids, I will reclaim my lands and we shall all live like kings! We must take care not to show our hand until my plan reaches fruition! All gold and silver belong to us! Any writings you find are reserved for Al-Si'la!

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: Do we want the Danes taking our women and ploughing our lands?

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 9
en: Yeah, we'll show those fucking Danes!

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: How many more boatloads of Danes must soil our shores before we wake up?

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 10
en: You tell 'em, Earl!

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: We do this not just for ourselves, but for our children! And the children of those children! And their children too!

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 11
en: Edward! Edward!

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: If you see intruders, deal with them most harshly!

speaker: Eivor
en: There is the Earl. To meet Roshan's challenge, I should strike from behind.

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: If this venture is to succeed... and it will succeed... people must truly believe we are Vikings! We must adopt the mindset of these murderous, thieving barbarians! We must raid them as they have raided our lands! It's not enough to simply look like Vikings. We must get inside their heads!

speaker: Eivor
en: You want to be Vikings? Are your ready to die like a Viking? I am!

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 12
en: The Earl is dead!

speaker: Saxon Mercenary 13
en: The Vikings are attacking!

speaker: Eivor
en: So much for subtlety... the Earl will be on his guard now.

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: A Dane is among us! A real one!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not let you tarnish the Raven Clan a moment longer!

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: I know what you are! You belong to the Raven Clan! You are a blight on this land!

speaker: Eivor
en: I failed to achieve the desired distraction. Perhaps some fire will draw Al-Si'la's attention!

speaker: Eivor
en: Run while you can, cowards, and never cross my path again!

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope Roshan did not see that, though she likely did.

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: A Dane is among us! A real one!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not let you tarnish the Raven Clan a moment longer!

speaker: Earl of Westerna
en: I know what you are! You belong to the Raven Clan! You are a blight on this land!

speaker: Eivor
en: I failed to achieve the desired distraction. Perhaps some fire will draw Al-Si'la's attention!

speaker: Eivor
en: Run while you can, cowards, and never cross my path again!

speaker: Roshan
en: It is done.

speaker: Eivor
en: Freyja's might! To be that deadly after so many winters!

speaker: Eivor
en: That was a glorious sight, wise one. It was as though Hel, Queen of the Underworld, descended from that tree.

speaker: Roshan
en: I think I felt her in my bones. And not in any comforting way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you...?

speaker: Roshan
en: I am fine, though I will pay for that glory later.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, now that your destiny is achieved, will you seek a more peaceful path?

speaker: Roshan
en: Al-Si'la was merely an obstacle on a long road. This is the real prize of the day.

speaker: Roshan
en: I'd retrieved it after I put that witch to rest.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it?

speaker: Roshan
en: The future. A seed to plant in Jerusalem.

speaker: Eivor
en: So the Fates are not finished with you.

speaker: Roshan
en: Does it ever end? And you? Are you satisfied to have achieved your vengeance?

speaker: Eivor
en: My greatest satisfaction is knowing that the honor of the Raven Clan is unblemished and that my people are safe.

speaker: Roshan
en: As it shall ever be, so long as you are their champion.

speaker: Roshan
en: Goodbye, Eivor Wolf-Kissed of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: I wonder if I shall ever learn more of her story...

speaker: Havi
en: Surtr and I, we crossed blades once. Back when there was nothing at stake but our pride... Of course, one day, he and I must fight again. I do not know when, nor why. Only that it will happen. And when it does, you must stand well clear. I will not risk my most beloved child getting caught in that fray.

speaker: Havi
en: Svartalfheim. Even after all these eternities away, I still hate the place. Yet it offers me the hope of revenge, sweetest of morsels. The realm is changed. But this is not Surtr's doing. It is something more. I must find Brokkr and Ivaldi. They'd better still have my Salakar nice and safe.

speaker: Havi
en: What? Has the shelter fallen? These Muspels are a plague!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 1
en: Help us, High One!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 2
en: Save us!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 3
en: Please help us!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 4
en: Rid us of these savages!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 5
en: Don't let any of them escape!

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive 3
en: Don't abandon us!

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Havi! You are back!

speaker: Havi
en: Yes, yes. One moment while I clear up this mess.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Damn Muspels, they came out of nowhere.

speaker: Havi
en: Where is the Salakar? Have you lost it?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Brokkr left the shelter yesterday before the raid even happened. Took the Salakar with him.

speaker: Havi
en: Where has he taken it!?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Since you went away he has become... erratic. The Salakar, it... it's all that matters to him now.

speaker: Havi
en: You should learn from his example. Now, where is he? Where?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: The other night he spoke of exploring the crater of Eitri to seek out more answers.

speaker: Havi
en: He takes the Salakar to Surtr's front door?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Wait! Where have you been these past few days?

speaker: Havi
en: Days? No matter, it is where I go that matters.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: And where is that? Eitri?

speaker: Havi
en: Wherever I can find vengeance.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Calm yourself, Havi. Collect your wits. An eye for an eye will leave us all blind.

speaker: Havi
en: What do I care of eyes!?

speaker: Vesall
en: Brokkr leaving before the raid even happened? Seems fishy to me.

speaker: Oglehr
en: So many... dead. My friends, my brothers, all gone.

speaker: Reihi
en: It was so sudden. We had no time to defend ourselves.

speaker: Havi
en: I must find Brokkr in Eitri's crater. The brave fool means well, but risks cheating me of my vengeance. What is it with these two brothers? One died sneaking after mead. The other now risks death by taking his job too far.

speaker: Havi
en: I see you, dwarf.

speaker: Havi
en: Brokkr! Where is my Salakar!?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Take it easy. It's right here. Nice and safe. Wanted to investigate something, but then I tripped and

speaker: Havi
en: Can you walk? No? Then I shall carry you.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Gentle. I ain't a bleeding sack of spuds, you know.

speaker: Havi
en: What have you learned of the Salakar?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Might just know how to use it. Of course, you going after Surtr... you'll most likely end up feasting in Valhalla.

speaker: Havi
en: Valhalla? It is for the feeble and blundering. No, I shall not die. Worlds may end. But, I, Havi, shall abide.

speaker: Brokkr
en: What about Sindri? You calling him feeble?

speaker: Havi
en: What would he be doing in... Ah yes, yes. He is there in Valhalla, of course. For one such as he, it is a great honor.

speaker: Havi
en: Now then, this looks like a good place to put you down.

speaker: Havi
en: So? Tell me of the Salakar's purpose.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Haven't a clue.

speaker: Havi
en: Can it kill Surtr?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Well, that ain't its purpose. But yeah, I think it can.

speaker: Havi
en: How?

speaker: Brokkr
en: It harnesses light. A lot of light.

speaker: Havi
en: That was Baldr's gift. To turn day to night and back. Is that why Surtr stole his hugr?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Yeah. The others, they're just for... balance. But, see, there is one more in there. Like Baldr's, incomplete...

speaker: Havi
en: Whose is this hugr?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Surtr's. An itsy-bitsy snippet, mind you.

speaker: Havi
en: I don't understand.

speaker: Brokkr
en: I think... I think if the Salakar touches Surtr, the two will... come together.

speaker: Havi
en: The Salakar is already complete. Nothing gets in or out.

speaker: Brokkr
en: A torn hugr will always try to reunite itself. His might just be strong enough to do it. If that happens, he will become the Salakar.

speaker: Havi
en: Then nothing can stop him!

speaker: Brokkr
en: Only if he can control all that light. But I don't think he can. His old carcass ain't made for it. It'll be like trying to hold the ocean in a single hog's bladder.

speaker: Havi
en: This thinking... How can I be sure you're right?

speaker: Brokkr
en: You ain't heard all me workings out.

speaker: Havi
en: Do you truly believe the coming together will be too much for Surtr?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Best try it when he's weak. Ideally dead. Not dead-dead, of course. Just normal dead. Before he wakes up all over again.

speaker: Havi
en: You've done well. Now give me the Salakar and leave this place. It is too dangerous.

speaker: Brokkr
en: I ain't leaving. I come this far―

speaker: Havi
en: Do as you're told! Friend.

speaker: Havi
en: I wonder... does Brokkr send me to my death? No. My destiny is Ragnarök. Far in the future. Not Svartalfheim.

speaker: Havi
en: Be strong, High One... Gorge upon these bitter fruits. Turn them into... savage victory!

speaker: Havi
en: Baldr... you will be avenged. That... that is my pledge.

speaker: Havi
en: No one... no one shall dare strike down the seed of Odin and live to tell the tale!

speaker: Havi
en: Here, fool! Your twilight comes!

speaker: Surtr
en: Still drawing breath!? I have a cure for that!

speaker: Surtr
en: Baldr squealed like a pig when I ripped out his hugr!

speaker: Havi
en: You won't squeal! You'll be too busy choking on your own sword!

speaker: Surtr
en: I will be master of all nine realms!

speaker: Havi
en: You're not even master of this room!

speaker: Surtr
en: I am Surtr, destroyer of worlds!

speaker: Havi
en: I am Ragnarök, destroyer of Surtr!

speaker: Havi
en: Die!

speaker: Brokkr
en: Hey! Give us a hand!

speaker: Havi
en: This is no place for dwarves.

speaker: Brokkr
en: I've earned my right to see this through.

speaker: Brokkr
en: I told you it would work. And there you were, doubting me.

speaker: Brokkr
en: I... I might've got it wrong.

speaker: Brokkr
en: This looks like it was just the key.

speaker: Brokkr
en: That, on the other hand...

speaker: Surtr
en: Half... a key. You... want the rest?

speaker: Surtr
en: Come... claim it!

speaker: Havi
en: You really shouldn't have come here.

speaker: Havi
en: You come and claim it!

speaker: Surtr
en: I don't run from the fire! I am the fire!

speaker: Surtr
en: There is no escape, little mouse!

speaker: Surtr
en: You hop well for a one-eyed toad!

speaker: Surtr
en: Are we not having fun!?

speaker: Surtr
en: Don't worry, maggot. I am right here.

speaker: Havi
en: So much for your grand plan, you fool.

speaker: Havi
en: You sought... to harness the power of the light. The power of my son!

speaker: Havi
en: It would've turned you into the wrecker of worlds. But in this feeble state... his light... will devour you whole!

speaker: Havi
en: I must return to the shelter and share the news of my triumph.

speaker: Havi
en: Smell that? The breath of liberty. My gift to you.

speaker: Havi
en: Why the sour faces? Would you rather remain fugitives―

speaker: Havi
en: Hyrrokin? So, the whispers were true. You were here in Svartalfheim all along?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: You have been busy, High One. Your vengeance floods the entire land like a raging river that has burst its banks.

speaker: Havi
en: Why are you here?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: I, too, bring a gift. Dread rumors from Asgard. Rumors you would have heard had you not been so... preoccupied.

speaker: Havi
en: What has Loki done now!?

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Escaped the cell in which you left him to rot. Unbound Fenrir. Awoken Jörmungandr. Rallied Hel. Now raising an army like no other. Clearly, he has been busy too. Of course, Loki is not your only problem. Soon, the gates of Muspelheim will grind open and its minions will emerge, demanding retribution for their fallen king. And let us not forget Suttungr in Jotunheim. Do you really think he will miss this chance to settle old scores? Your vengeance comes at a price, High One, and you and everything you hold dear are it.

speaker: Havi
en: So, there is to be a fight? I haven't lost one yet.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: You have heard of the Twilight Sword?

speaker: Havi
en: Surtr's blade? Destined to cut the sky and signal Ragnarök? I stuffed it down his gullet.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: As I came here, a great beam of light rose from that lone tower. Tore the sky asunder... Your doing I assume? It is you who ignites Ragnarök.

speaker: Havi
en: So it begins. By my own hand.

speaker: Havi
en: Hyrrokin, a favor please.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Have I not already done you one?

speaker: Havi
en: Not for me. For you. Go to the tower you spoke of. Within, you will find an elven marvel lying amid the ashes. Take it.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: Why?

speaker: Havi
en: It offers a way to deliver the one you have lost... yet seek to save. But first it must be emptied of those lost souls within.

speaker: Hyrrokin
en: I already have a plan to rescue my love.

speaker: Havi
en: There's always a better one. Now go.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: What is this trick? You don't care about her lost love.

speaker: Havi
en: I care about Baldr. If she can free him, even unintentionally, he may yet make it to... the other side of Ragnarök.

speaker: Havi
en: Ragnarök comes, yet I will abide. Though not as I am, and not in this body. I will not forget this life. Not one breath. I will always remember when Odin, son of Bor, father of Thor was me!

speaker: Havi
en: Well played, Loki. We shall have our fight. Soon enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will make my way to Wincestre. The letter asked me to meet a man in white at a house of God. And then recite this phrase. "When pride cometh, then cometh shame. But with the lowly cometh wisdom."

speaker: Randvi
en: A passage from their holy book, I believe. Interesting. Go with care.

speaker: Eivor
en: The seat of King Aelfred's power... where hog shit stains my boots. I will find the man in white in their god's house.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: You remember Mildritha from the bakery?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: The trollop who kneads dough with her bodice free and loose? My husband can't keep his eyes off her.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Ah, you'll be happy to hear Reeve Selwyn arrested her.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: Goodness! For parading her nakedness, was it?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O, I wouldn't doubt it. Probably the gaze of someone more important than your Egbert.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Wincestre mourns a good bishop. And a strong, virile man. May he find his peace with God.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: The Lord takes the best of us to sit beside Him.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Bishop Ealhferth? He is not with God. He is locked in the flaming crypt, where all heretics go.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Hush, they'll hear you.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be the house of their timid god. They built him a rich dwelling.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Even the mighty fall. And God's servant, the Bishop Ealhferth was mighty indeed in defense of his God. He was a man of surpassing vigor, well versed in the Bible, quick of wit, oxen-strong, meek as a lamb. But God called Ealhferth to sit beside him. And Ealhferth answered, his body gone to earth and his sister weeping. Mourning a lord far-known and beloved. I give praise to such a man, to keepsake his memory. Requiem æternam dona ei, Domine Et lux perpetua luceat ei Requiescat in pace. Amen.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: A Dane treads the cobbles of God's house. In search of Christ's redemption, I hope.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your Christ can wait his turn. It's you I've come to see.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: Is that so?

speaker: Eivor
en: "When pride cometh, then cometh shame. But with the lowly cometh wisdom." You know these words, and you know why I speak them.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: I do. But I am not yet satisfied that you are the one for the task ahead. As Jesus said onto Thomas, "I am the way, the truth, and the life." Speak the deeds of Christ in order. Only then will you cometh unto my Lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why deny the pleadings of an unwashed pagan who aches to know God? Take me as I am, and I will do your Lord's bidding.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: How great is the burden of learning for one so unworthy. But I see that no amount of instruction in the Lord's words will save your soul. Come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who am I to meet, priest? I cannot stand waiting in silence.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I must dance to your tune, tell me where to step.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: In books one may find such wisdom. We had many in England, before the Danes burned our churches. A few yet remain nearby. Or perhaps a more pious soul in need of charity will reward you with a lesson.

speaker: Baptism Story
en: For God's spirit breathed on the waters, and in the , Jesus was cleansed of all sin.

speaker: Eivor
en: He bathed in the river. So a gentle wash brings them closer to their god.

speaker: Resurrection Story
en: At his tomb the earth shook and an angel appeared asking them why they looked for the living among the dead. He has risen!

speaker: Eivor
en: He rose from the dead? A nice trick, and not easily done.

speaker: Revelation Story
en: On the mountain, He walked with His disciples. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became as white as the light.

speaker: Eivor
en: Their god brings them light ... just as Baldr does. Light as bright as the summer sun.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: Speak the deeds of Christ in order.

speaker: Eivor
en: On the mountain, his face shone like the sun and he became light.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: His Transfiguration.

speaker: Eivor
en: God breathed on the water, and in the Jordan River, he was cleansed of all sin.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: His Baptism.

speaker: Eivor
en: The women came with offerings. But they could not find him when they looked among the dead.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: His Resurrection.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have nothing for you now. But I will return.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: And Jesus said, "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness." Well spoken.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are the riddles done?

speaker: Eivor
en: That is not for me to decide, for I am not the one who summoned you. If you follow, I will lead you to him.

speaker: Eivor
en: I solved your riddle. Now all I get is silence? Who am I to meet?

speaker: Sigebeald
en: Thou art weighed in the balances... and found wanting. Perhaps you should try again? Speak his story. In order.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have nothing for you now. But I will return.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: Shhh. Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is considered wise.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yet men become wise by speaking with other men. They grow foolish when keeping to silence.

speaker: Sigebeald
en: Hush! Your prattling offends God's ears. We're here.

speaker: Unknown Voice
