en: May Christ, whose terror scares away the foul throngs, make with me a strong covenant. Was God's lesson instructive?

speaker: Eivor
en: I learned that your god fears death, just as mine do. Just as every man does.

speaker: Unknown Voice
en: Yet through our Lord we may achieve life everlasting in His glorious presence. Perhaps you missed that detail.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do all the priests in Wincestre have the same skill for drama?

speaker: Eivor
en: I learned that my gods and yours inspire tales of equal amusement ... they make me howl with laughter.

speaker: Unknown Voice
en: A dull answer. But a battle-blunted axe may yet be sharpened.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do all the priests in Wincestre have the same skill for drama?

speaker: Eivor
en: Do all the priests in Wincestre have the same skill for drama?

speaker: Eivor
en: You risk your life, Aelfred King.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I have invited you here to speak on equal terms. Do the Danes laws of hospitality not apply in Wessex?

speaker: Eivor
en: You gifted my jarl to that whelp from The Order of Ancients, the warrior Fulke.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Fulke was an enemy of Wessex. But it seems someone has already removed her threat from my lands.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you didn't hear it was me, you have now.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Impressive. The Order of Ancients has surely been crippled by her loss.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Fulke is a member of the Order as well? Hm. The wolves biting at my skirts grow craftier by the day.

speaker: Eivor
en: How much do you know of this order?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Only this and little more.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: This letter, signed by one who calls himself a Poor Fellow-Soldier of Christ, warns of a plot against my life.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Gallows, The Quill, The Seax. Three men eager to kill you.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Two, now. The Bishop Ealhferth is dead. He was The Seax, so far as I can tell.

speaker: Eivor
en: And a humble servant fo your God. That must sting.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Still, his death has strengthened Christian fellowship in Wincestre. I pray the death of his colleagues will do the same.

speaker: Eivor
en: So many lies in the name of your God. Perhaps he is not strong enough to help you.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: My God is the Almighty. But my enemies are numerous and my throne is fresh. There must be no trail from these murders back to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have faced warriors like me many times before. And many times you have been lost or been cheated. Why trust me now?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I have men in Lunden and Jorvik. Men who send me reports on the rise and fall of the tides of war. Not long ago, men and women of some influence were murdered in those places, in oddly specific circumstances. When I received this letter from our Poor Fellow-Soldier, it did not take long to work out why. I don't know your motive, nor what you hope to gain. All I ask is that you finish the work you have begun, before these fallen souls infest England further.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should let the Order kill you. It would speed our conquest of England.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: You may remove the organs of state, the cancer will remain.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should let the Order kill you. If I made it easy for them, they might even return Sigurd to me.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: I would return him to you myself if I knew where they were holding him. But Fulke's treachery has blindsided me as well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then promise me a reward I can sing about. A healthy king's weight in silver.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Very well. As much as you can carry. This morning, my reeve, Goodwin, was not at his post.

speaker: Eivor
en: A man you trust?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Goodwin was following the clues given in this letter when he disappeared.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where was he last seen?

speaker: King Aelfred
en: At his house, by the west gate. You may find something here.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Eivor. Compose yourself while you are my guest. My city is not a battlefield.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not yet, great king. But the day will come.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to find this reeve Goodwin.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: That Selwyn's got some stones on him, arresting Aelfred's man. Who rule in Wincestre, anyway? Is Aelfred king or not?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Well, you ain't, that's for sure. So keep your mouth shut and do as you're told.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Shut your mouth, yeah? Unless you want yours to rot off in the keep.

speaker: Eivor
en: Goodwin gone. And guards sniffing around. So where would they have taken him?

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone disagrees with Aelfred educating the people of Wincestre.

speaker: Eivor
en: Papers, thrown on the fire. Goodwin covering his tracks? Or the guards destroying evidence?

speaker: Eivor
en: Broken bowls, food scattered. They took him by force. There must be a garrison in the city.

speaker: Eivor
en: A violent struggle with the guards. They must have taken him to Wincestre's garrison.

speaker: Eivor
en: Another of The Quill's notices. The Quill's influence is spreading like lice. More writings from The Quill.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see you, little mice. Are you spying on me? Come here, I want to talk to you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: The Quill has eyes everywhere. Scarper! She's on to us. You'll get nothing from me. I'm as loyal as the king's hounds.

speaker: Eivor
en: The prisoners might know something.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Felling trees, chiseling rock from the earth. And for what? To build more prisons for men who steal apples.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 4
en: I was starving, my baby son close to death. Would you not steal to save your child?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am looking for the reeve (sheriff).

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Selwyn? That bastard said I stole an apple. He'll see me hang for it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Not Selwyn. Reeve Goodwin. Was arrested not long ago.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Aelfred's man, arrested? Now that's as funny as a dose of the pox. Seems no one is free in Wincestre.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thick wall and thicker guards. A place to keep a valuable man.

speaker: Eivor
en: Reeve Selwyn ordered executions for petty theft and mud-slinging. A husband and wife, to be carried out soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Evidence against The Order of Ancients. Stolen from Goodwin?

speaker: Eivor
en: Goodwin's research against The Order of Ancients.

speaker: Goodwin
en: A Dane in Wincestre? These are strange times.

speaker: Eivor
en: King Aelfred sent me, pleading from his bended knee to find someone.

speaker: Goodwin
en: I know Aelfred well enough to spot a bloody lie when I hear it. If he did send you, he was standing tall and proud.

speaker: Eivor
en: That he was. And you're the man I've come to find, Goodwin. Do you know why?

speaker: Goodwin
en: If I had one guess, to find the heretics from The Order of Ancients and bury them so deep, even God would need a shovel.

speaker: Eivor
en: So where do we start digging?

speaker: Goodwin
en: My research should help us. If they haven't burned it already, it'll be somewhere nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have your papers here, taken from the captain of this keep.

speaker: Goodwin
en: A marvel. History will name you the protector of Wincestre. A pricking irony.

speaker: Eivor
en: And not lost on me. Now let's go... before they discover their eel has slipped the hook.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's regroup beyond the walls.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll find your research. Now go, before they find their wolf has fled his cage.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's regroup beyond the walls.

speaker: Goodwin
en: I am grateful for your help.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a brazen move to arrest Aelfred's favored reeve.

speaker: Goodwin
en: This so-called Order are nothing but defiled shit-peddlers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shit-peddlers who have wormed their way into every crevasse of your country. They're dangerous.

speaker: Goodwin
en: I didn't catch your name, did I?

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor of the Raven Clan. Scourge of Mercia if that name doesn't rattle some recognition.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Well, Eivor, when our three heretics smolder on a heap of ash, we'll down a cup of ale together and share our distaste of Mercians like old friends.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfred believes at least one is dead. Your bishop Ealhferth was The Seax.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Bugger. Half of Wincestre is in mourning for that nun-groper.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found this nailed on a door. The Quill wields words like a knife.

speaker: Goodwin
en: A Disputation of Tutelage? Pretty chatter with poisoned intent. I will look into this more.

speaker: Eivor
en: One calls himself The Quill. Are words his weapons?

speaker: Goodwin
en: There were rumors of letters nailed up around Wincestre. It may be that one of these can tell us more.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Gallows. What do you know of him?

speaker: Goodwin
en: Must be another reeve, I'm sure of it. Only we have the power to mete out justice. And this one would walk with cocksure righteousness.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is Selwyn a name you know? He seems to have judged and executed many for little more than stealing ale and bread.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Gallows had you arrested. So he must command the law.

speaker: Goodwin
en: Reeve Selwyn?

speaker: Goodwin
en: Of course. That hedge-pig has brought down laws like a hammer on Wincestre. Executing sinners on spurious charges in the square.

speaker: Eivor
en: Could it be another?

speaker: Goodwin
en: He's the man. He's the only one who fits. End his terror, Eivor.

speaker: Raid-loving Husband
en: My love for you rises tall and strong, like the Tree of Life!

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: Do not promise me a mighty branch, then let me down with a tiny twig.

speaker: Raid-loving Husband
en: Freyja's beard, it has wilted again! I cannot stay firm when you talk to me like that!

speaker: Eivor
en: Does everyone in Alrekstad play their love-games so loudly?

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: No, it is just my husband. He cannot satisfy his wife.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah. Old age?

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: No, he is still young and fit. It was not always so. You could not keep us apart when we were raiding.

speaker: Eivor
en: He would plow you during raids?

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: Our first time was in the middle of a burning village... after a while, the crew made us stop. They said it was distracting.

speaker: Eivor
en: Love can burn brighter near death. Have you tried revisiting these memories?

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: Ja, but talking about it is not the same. I need to feel it. Smell it.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, you need to bring the excitement of the raid into your bed.

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: You could help us pretend we are raiding! That will make my water flow! Come, we must tell my husband.

speaker: Eivor
en: I was only... Well, all right.

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: Grab your weapon, you big, strong vikingr! Today, we raid!

speaker: Raid-loving Husband
en: A raid? Now?

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: Join me in the blood-dance! Fill me with your battle lust!

speaker: Raid-loving Husband
en: O ... yes! Yes! Let us go viking! Maybe you could start by breaking things?

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: And scream as you do. Like it is really happening.

speaker: Raid-loving Husband
en: It is ... amusing, but not arousing.

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: Ja, it does not feel real enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe you need more fire, like your first time.

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: Yes! Burn down our house! Burn it to the ground!

speaker: Raid-loving Husband
en: That did it! I am as hard as Heimdall's tower!

speaker: Raid-loving Wife
en: Then ram me like the Valgrind Gates and enter Valhalla! Take all the plunder you want, vikingr! Take us also, and let the love-hunger consume you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Another time, maybe, but I will help myself to your chest.

speaker: Havi
en: This dream of yours, Baldr, do not fret. How can it be a vision of death when you are immune to death? As for Ragnarök, it lurks far in the future. And when it comes, you have my pledge. I will safeguard you and all those we love... Ragnarök is not for us. It is for everyone else.

speaker: Frigg
en: Hurry! We are nearly there!

speaker: Havi
en: Peace, Frigg. It will do us no good to arrive at our enemy's doorstep exhausted.

speaker: Frigg
en: Surtr has our son! Fair Baldr, fallen to treachery! Does that mean anything to you?

speaker: Havi
en: It does, and Surtr will pay a heavy price for it. But we do not serve our cause by reckless haste. The tyrant of Muspelheim acts with purpose, and I would know the web he weaves before I'm caught in it.

speaker: Frigg
en: So speaks one who never nursed our babe at the breast, nor held him as he slept! You were warming your wife's bed while I nurtured our son.

speaker: Havi
en: You were only too keen to send him to my care, and Freya's, when the call of adventure became too great to resist. Now dampen your heart-fire. Captive he may be, but there's nothing in the Nine Realms that can harm Baldr.

speaker: Frigg
en: There is one thing. Pick up your heels!

speaker: Frigg
en: Baldr was too mighty to be captured by force. I sense Loki's hand in this.

speaker: Havi
en: As do I, yet still the wretch refuses to confess. That is why he waits in fetters for our return. Chained by my own hand, as I chained his son.

speaker: Frigg
en: As he has chained ours in turn.

speaker: Havi
en: If he is truly conspiring with Surtr, he will know my everlasting wrath.

speaker: Frigg
en: Will he, Havi? Or will you forgive him once again, so he may wreak more misery upon us? You love your dear blood-brother too well, when he has brought you nothing but pain.

speaker: Havi
en: We have brought each other pain.

speaker: Frigg
en: Havi. Look.

speaker: Havi
en: Burned. Their corpses left as food for the crows. A dark omen indeed.

speaker: Frigg
en: Come. There is no time to waste on the dead.

speaker: Havi
en: We should have done more. We should have rallied the whole of Asgard when the Muspels invaded Svartalfheim.

speaker: Frigg
en: And you should never have let our son come here!

speaker: Havi
en: He sought to prevent this war. Was that not a worthy goal? As for Asgard... The Builder's treachery was still fresh. We needed to rebuild, honor our dead. There was little appetite for further conflict.

speaker: Frigg
en: I recall you said the same when Surtr invaded Alfheim. Now the elves are no more.

speaker: Havi
en: Now you dredge up ancient history?

speaker: Frigg
en: You should have intervened, Lord of Asgard. Then and now. Instead, Surtr has grown too bold, and our son may be the cost of it.

speaker: Havi
en: Do not say so, Frigg. We will find him yet.

speaker: Frigg
en: What have they done? The city lies in ruins!

speaker: Havi
en: This is worse than I thought. They've put this land to flame and sword.

speaker: Frigg
en: Baldr!

speaker: Frigg
en: He is nearby, Havi. I feel it.

speaker: Havi
en: You feel it?

speaker: Frigg
en: The bond of mother and child. Something you will never understand. Now follow!

speaker: Frigg
en: Where is he? That way! Maybe this?

speaker: Havi
en: These buildings stand hollow. No one is here.

speaker: Frigg
en: Then we have nothing to fear. There! Inside that house!

speaker: Frigg
en: That building! Hurry!

speaker: Havi
en: I see no sign of Baldr.

speaker: Frigg
en: No, but the essence of him lingers. It is stronger here than before. Do not slow, Havi! We are on his trail!

speaker: Havi
en: If this instinct is true, let us follow it further.

speaker: Frigg
en: Where are you, my son? If they have harmed a hair on your head...

speaker: Havi
en: Keep faith, Frigg. We will find him safe, you'll see.

speaker: Havi
en: This city broods beneath a cloak of uneasy silence. Where is the enemy?

speaker: Frigg
en: Concern yourself only with our son. He is close, I feel it now!

speaker: Frigg
en: Oh! He was here! The smell of his skin, his hair. It's as if he left but a moment ago!

speaker: Havi
en: There may be other signs. Keep watch. I will look upstairs.

speaker: Havi
en: What is this place? What happened here?

speaker: Frigg
en: Dried blood. Could it be his?

speaker: Havi
en: Mistletoe... They know.

speaker: Havi
en: Who wrote this? Was it you, dear brother?

speaker: Frigg
en: Havi! They are here! The enemy is upon us!

speaker: Havi
en: Muspels! Frigg! I'm coming!

speaker: Frigg
en: Where is my son, demon?

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: He waits at my master's pleasure, there. But maybe not so fair as you remember.

speaker: Frigg
en: Havi! More of them! Gorge your blade!

speaker: Muspel Warrior 2
en: You will burn, Asgardians!

speaker: Havi
en: Your grave yawns to greet you!

speaker: Frigg
en: They have him in the keep, Havi!

speaker: Havi
en: Then let no lackey of Surtr stand in our way!

speaker: Muspel Warrior 3
en: Kill the Æsir scum!

speaker: Frigg
en: Havi! Here they come!

speaker: Muspel Warrior 4
en: You will never reach our master! This city will be your tomb!

speaker: Frigg
en: These fiends are coming from everywhere! How many more must we face?

speaker: Frigg
en: Keep going! We are nearly there!

speaker: Frigg
en: ...Baldr?

speaker: Surtr
en: Ah, Havi, you came. As I knew you must. It's been too long since you and I crossed blades.

speaker: Havi
en: Then let's make this the final―

speaker: Surtr
en: Don't worry, High One. Neither you or I are fated to die today.

speaker: Havi
en: Each injury you have done my son, you will feel them tenfold!

speaker: Surtr
en: I feel nothing but your empty breath!

speaker: Surtr
en: Do you falter, Lord of Asgard? You should never have come to my hall.

speaker: Havi
en: I will close your mouth with steel!

speaker: Havi
en: Your dark ambitions end here, Surtr! Surrender my son to me!

speaker: Surtr
en: Keep talking, High One. Your blows are as weak as your words.

speaker: Frigg
en: Havi! Behind you!

speaker: Surtr
en: You look like you could do with a lie down.

speaker: Havi
en: Frigg...

speaker: Frigg
en: Uh... Frigg... No...

speaker: Surtr
en: You'll want to watch this.

speaker: Sinmara
en: We must kill the High One.

speaker: Surtr
en: He is not fated to die today.

speaker: Havi
en: ...My boy... he... he lives...

speaker: Riddler
en: A young and handsome peasant's daughter. She seizes me, red, plunders my head. O dear me no, what am I thinking?

speaker: Riddler
en: Four dilly-dandies. Four stick standies. Two crookers. Two lookers. And a wig wag.

speaker: Riddler
en: Dark were their tracks, the path very black. Swift was its moving, faster than birds. Yes, yes that's it.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are you doing here, in the middle of nowhere?

speaker: Riddler
en: Ah, a visitor for Chad the Bewilderer, the most radiant and rakish Riddler. Do you have the wits to bet me? There is cake in it if you do.

speaker: Eivor
en: For cake, I will answer any mind-tease you have for me.

speaker: Riddler
en: My head is forged with the hammer, hurt with sharp tools, smoothed by files. I take in my mouth what is set before me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Iron is forged with tools? And a keyhole could be a mouth of a door? A lock and key?

speaker: Riddler
en: Wonderful, your wit sparkles! But still... another one.

speaker: Eivor
en: A murdered man cut down by a hammer? He swarms with flies, and would bring earth into his mouth?

speaker: Riddler
en: Ah, a fine guess. But not the right guess. Another, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: A fish? They're caught with flies, and are caught on a hook when they bite upon it.

speaker: Riddler
en: A fish? A fish? No, no. Let us try another.

speaker: Riddler
en: I saw a strange thing, wonderful of shape, singing in a tavern. Its beak underneath, stood upon splayed legs that cannot walk.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birds sing and have beaks? And fly rather than walk.

speaker: Riddler
en: They may choose not to walk, but walk they can. Wrong, my friend. Let us try one more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Something that sings? A musical instrument? The bladder that whines and wheezes through pipes? Bagpipes!

speaker: Riddler
en: Very good! A tricky one, that few but the sharpest needles can sew. Now, the final test.

speaker: Eivor
en: Many sit in a tavern, and a stool has legs?

speaker: Riddler
en: But do such things sing? Have a beak? No. Perhaps the last one will be easier to fathom.

speaker: Riddler
en: With my roof of tears, I am driven far and wide on my avenging path. When I shake the forest, I rumble the fruit from the trees.

speaker: Eivor
en: When a giant walks through a forest, the rumble of his footsteps fells trees!

speaker: Riddler
en: Ah, but when has a giant stood beneath a roof of water? Perhaps you are not up to the challenge.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tears, anger, vengeance suggests someone wronged. The despair of a spurned lover can rattle the earth?

speaker: Riddler
en: Ha! A tragically romantic guess that speaks much of you. But no... that is not the right answer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rain covers the earth like a roof. And the rumble of thunder and lightning can shake acorns from a branch. A storm?

speaker: Riddler
en: You are brighter than the sky-lantern!

speaker: Eivor
en: Confusion hounds me, speak it again?

speaker: Riddler
en: Your wit outshone my words. And such a feat deserves three cakes! But unfortunately, I do not have any.

speaker: Eivor
en: So the cake was a lie?

speaker: Riddler
en: Do not pout. Have a reward much more worthy of your talents.

speaker: Eivor
en: Goodbye, Chad. Your riddles were a fun diversion.

speaker: Riddler
en: Stay a while, read some more of my scribblings.

speaker: Riddler
en: You are brighter than the sky-lantern! A worthy effort, friend. But some meanings did not find you.

speaker: Eivor
en: And my cake?

speaker: Riddler
en: Long eaten. But take this instead.

speaker: Riddler
en: A terrible display, friend. And now the sweet treats will go uneaten.

speaker: Eivor
en: So the cake was a lie?

speaker: Riddler
en: Not so, sadly you just do not deserve them.

speaker: Riddler
en: I do not get many visitors. Your presence sparked my mind. A rare thing out here. I wonder, will we ever tire of such wordplay? Will the riddles of England die with me? My grandfather built this turf maze. I might leave this place one day, and move to with my riddles.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nightshade grows in graveyards. No shortage of those in Christian England.

speaker: Eivor
en: Nightshade has a distinct stench. Like this. Must be near.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's enough nightshade. Foul-smelling herb. I should meet Bjorn.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bjorn, here as promised.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your nightshade.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Good. It has the power we need for the coming ritual. Nearly done.

speaker: Eivor
en: The skalds say Odin on a tree much like this. He lived, though. Most die.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Yggdrasil the World-Tree, Odin's gallows. The place where life and death are one.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Ride with me, Raven. The seidr (magic) awaits.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Berserker brew hits hard. It may open your eyes to the spirit realm. It may turn you into a savage beast. Whatever happens, face it without fear.

speaker: Bjorn
en: How are you called, you bear-skins, you wolf-shirts, you tasters of blood? We are the shield-biters, wall-breakers, born in battle's flood!

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you fight for, you bear-skins?

speaker: Bjorn
en: You wolf-shirts, you drinkers of blood?

speaker: Eivor
en: We fight for glory, we shield-biters!

speaker: Bjorn
en: Wall-breakers! Born in battle's flood!

speaker: Bjorn
en: Raaaaugh!

speaker: Eivor
en: Raaawr!

speaker: Eivor
en: I've been close to death many times. But this... this was different.

speaker: Eivor
en: Feels like a Jotun kicked my head in.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Tis glorious, is it not?

speaker: Eivor
en: Berserker brew... does not... does not agree with my belly.

speaker: Bjorn
en: But you live still! Can you feel the power of bear's blood coursing through your veins?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, but you... You were a bear.

speaker: Bjorn
en: And the bear-power courses through me still!

speaker: Eivor
en: I am ready. Where to?

speaker: Bjorn
en: The Mercians who slew my wife cower in Beodoricsworth. We shall kill them all! With me!

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor ... Sigurd wishes to speak with you. He is quite agitated.

speaker: Eivor
en: Has something happened?

speaker: Randvi
en: You will want to speak with him yourself.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor. The time has come. Our time.

speaker: Eivor
en: Our time for what?

speaker: Sigurd
en: My final glory awaits.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your final glory ... I fear to ask what that means.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Do I not speak plainly? My time in Midgard is done. I wish now to see the hall of my ancestors.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you wish to die, it will not be by my hand.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I do not speak of death, Eivor. I speak of life! Life and glory everlasting! I know I have been in a fog these last few weeks. I know I speak words you don't fully understand. But I only ask you trust me once more. On my final voyage. Back to Norway, to wish my father farewell, and achieve my destiny.

speaker: Eivor
en: Back to Norway? I need to discuss this with Randvi.

speaker: Sigurd
en: If you must. I will await your answer, down by the docks. Do not keep me waiting.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Have you spoken with Randvi? Are we ready to leave?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will. Have patience.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be time to return to Norway. Sigurd's eager to see his father and ... and beyond that, I do not know.

speaker: Randvi
en: I have heard ill news about Styrbjörn in the past year. If you go, go with care.

speaker: Eivor
en: We'll leave now. And return as soon as we're able.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. And be safe. Both of you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd...

speaker: Sigurd
en: Shall we, then, Eivor? To Norway... and well beyond.

speaker: Eivor
en: To Norway, then.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Good, good! Lead on.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have a few things to take care of.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Please, Eivor. Be quick.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: If Sigfred has his way, there will not be a single Frank left in these hills by winter.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: He hates them, that is certain. Did you see him crush that soldier's neck?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Wolf-Kissed! Here!

speaker: Sigfred
en: How did you find me? Where is Toka?

speaker: Eivor
en: Toka guessed you would be here. She is still at Melun looking for your missing watch.

speaker: Sigfred
en: I lost Engelwin, but this soldier told me he is heading for the church nearby. Come. We can go through the slums.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Gah! Even from here I can smell the piss of the slums.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigfred, I mean to stop this fight from coming to England. I must meet with Charles.

speaker: Sigfred
en: For what? You cannot bargain with these thralls! Have you forgotten my fallen brother Sinric?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, and that is why I must try. It is why I came to Francia. If I kill Engelwin, I want you to help me get an audience with the king.

speaker: Sigfred
en: There is no reasoning with you, Wolf-Kissed. You are as wild as your namesake.

speaker: Odo
en: In our veins run the blood of holy kings and conquerors. The Northerners may have numbers, but we have God!

speaker: Sigfred
en: That is Odo, Count of Paris and right-hand man to the king. Drumming up support for his army, no doubt.

speaker: Odo
en: Our courage and honor will not fail us, no matter how hot the fight. We will overcome this evil, as we always have.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Self-important as always. The one next to him is Gozlin, Bishop of Paris and a fearsome warrior... for a Frank. Those two are for another day. You have to get to Engelwin, and to do that you have to find your way into the church. The answer is down there in that stink.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is not much to go on.

speaker: Sigfred
en: If it was easy, I would have killed him myself already. You have an advantage. You are unknown to these... people.

speaker: Odo
en: The raider Sigfred is almost at our gates! And what does he want? What the Northerners always want: blood and silver, yours and mine.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Me, they know quite well already. Someone down there knows something. All you have to do is get them to tell you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have your word. Once this is done, we find Charles.

speaker: Sigfred
en: As you say, but work fast. I cannot leave Melun unguarded long, and this Frankish stench already turns my stomach.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Three guards? Insulting. I will deal with them, while you find Engelwin. He is hiding in his church. Will you sneak in, convince one of his own to aid you, or cover the streets with blood?

speaker: Eivor
en: As you would?

speaker: Sigfred
en: They deserve no less. But you are the Wolf-Kissed. You do not need my advice. So what will you do?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find my own way.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Count Odo is the protector of Paris, the king's man, and he has told you the truth! You cannot trust the Northmen to do anything but be Northmen... because that's what they are... Northmen. This is not the first time they have come and it will not be the last. But we must make it the last. Because at the last... it is up to us!

speaker: French Man 1
en: Damn these nobles, always talking down to us. We don't hear a word from them until there's trouble.

speaker: French Man 2
en: Let him speak!

speaker: French Child 1
en: Bread or coin. Bread or coin.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you the owner?

speaker: French Woman 1
en: Owner... that's such a naïvely hopeful word. What can I get you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to find the bishop.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: The bishop? I can tell you he's not in this mud pit, my friend. He wouldn't risk ruining his royal sandals. There is a priest who does the bishop's numbers in here at times. Last I saw, he was talking to a table of soldiers.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a good crowd.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: If you mean tables of soldiers drowning themselves in wine at my expense, then yes, it's good enough. It might be better if not for that old drunk over there crying about the bishop to everyone who'll listen. I'd send him away, but to be honest, I need his business.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thanks for the help.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: You look the kind that enjoys a good complaint. You'll be back.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wine loosen lips as well as ale. Someone at the tavern might know something that'll get me into the church.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Someone needs to report back to the bishop, tell him the nosy scribe is taken care of.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Well, not me. My cup isn't empty yet, and that bishop makes me uneasy. For a "servant of God," he has a terrible temper.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could look for the scribe at the plague district, or see if someone here knows something more.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's two good leads.

speaker: French Man 3
en: What does a bishop and his soldiers want with my daughter? She's a good girl. Never did wrong. She's all I got!

speaker: Eivor
en: You mentioned the bishop.

speaker: French Man 3
en: He took her. My daughter! She's gone. She's a good girl. Never any trouble. She wouldn't steal anything.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who took your daughter? Was it the bishop?

speaker: French Man 3
en: The bishop's soldiers in the slums. Said she stole the bishop's silver, that she has a devil and needs deliverance. Wassat? Wha'd you say?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find your daughter here in the slums, and she will help me find Engelwin.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is two good leads.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could look for the drunk's daughter at the slums, or see if there's more to learn here.

speaker: French Man 4
en: God himself holds you over this pit of hell, like a spider held over the fire. Your own wickedness makes you heavier than lead. You have offended God infinitely more than a stubborn rebel ever did his prince, yet only his hand keeps you from falling. O sinner! You hang by a slender thread! The flames of divine wrath flash all about you! Awake now and fly from the wrath to come!

speaker: Eivor
en: Now to find the scribe.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am looking for a priest. He works for the bishop as a scribe.

speaker: French Man 5
en: The bishop! I do not know about that. One of the nuns might know. I do not know anything!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm looking for a priest who helps the bishop with his numbers. A church scribe.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: You as well? He's popular today. It must be serious if it's bringing you all down here. We don't get many visitors.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone else was looking for him?

speaker: French Woman 2
en: Guards from the city. He didn't seem too pleased to see them. They got to arguing, then all left towards the sewer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me where the sewer is.

speaker: French Woman 2
en: Just over the rise. Be careful though. With all those plagued bodies, it's not clean and smells to high heaven.

speaker: Eivor
en: The sewer opens here. The soldiers must have taken the scribe inside.

speaker: Eivor
en: Agh! That is the stench of death.

speaker: Eivor
en: The bodies here are decayed and falling apart.

speaker: Eivor
en: This body has rotted in the water. It's been down here a long time.

speaker: Eivor
en: Blurred by the water, but this is a list of some kind. It must have come from the scribe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Plague corpses, just as the nun said. Floated here from somewhere ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Argh, my mouth is sour with the filth.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is a priest's robes. This must be the scribe.

speaker: Eivor
en: A list of numbers that show Engelwin mishandling tithes. The scribe discovered the bishop was stealing money, and it got him killed. This is a watchword. "Job 1:21." It will help me gain entry to the church.

speaker: French Woman 3
en: Is that another one dead? O, it's not natural.

speaker: French Man 6
en: Don't touch it! It's the plague for certain.

speaker: French Woman 3
en: It's not just the plague. That's four in one day. It's a bad omen. God help us!

speaker: French Soldier 4
en: Stop struggling!

speaker: French Woman 4
en: No! Let me go! I don't want no deliverance! Leave me alone! Help!

speaker: French Woman 4
en: Help! Don't just stand there, help me!

speaker: French Woman 4
en: It's not safe here! This way!

speaker: French Woman 4
en: That was close.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're welcome. Your father told me the bishop took you.

speaker: French Woman 4
en: My father? Yeah, the bishop's soldiers. I didn't steal nothing neither! Then they wanted to give me deliverance.

speaker: Eivor
en: You stole from the bishop? That was bold.

speaker: French Woman 4
en: Well I just said I didn't, didn't I? Well, I didn't take no silver. It was just a little church key.

speaker: Eivor
en: I want that key.

speaker: French Woman 4
en: So did the soldiers, but you are too late. I sold it to bandits in the sewers. They got it cheap too!

speaker: Eivor
en: My reward for helping you is to fight bandits.

speaker: French Woman 4
en: You are welcome. Good luck, the sewers stink. I have to get to my father before he is thrown out of the tavern again.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be the sewers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fresh tracks. Bandits must be close.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rats! They're small, but their teeth are sharp.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Why must we guard the stuff, and they get to go up top? I'm tired of the stink.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: We are new, what do you think? That key and the other stuff is worth a fortune. It cannot just be left unguarded.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Well, I better get up top tomorrow. I've forgotten what fresh air even smells like.

speaker: Eivor
en: These goods have been packed for travel. The bandits are smuggling.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: What luck! Everyone knows the bishop has rooms packed with silver and valuables.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: We might have to take care of that girl. She's the only one who knows we have the key.

speaker: Norse Man 3
en: Get in and out of the church first. Then we deal with that little rat.

speaker: Eivor
en: The key has a Christian cross cast into its bow. This is a church key.

speaker: French Soldier 5
en: Sorry, we're closed down here. Try your luck back upstairs.

speaker: French Man 3
en: I thought I'd lost you! But here you are, back safe as ever. Thank God Almighty!

speaker: French Woman 4
en: Of course, Papa. But you have to stop drinking so much. It does you no good.

speaker: French Man 3
en: You're back! Where were you? Thank God Almighty! I was so worried.

speaker: French Woman 4
en: O, Papa.

speaker: Eivor
en: The guards here are heavily armed. I should be careful here.

speaker: French Soldier 6
en: The tithes are collected and accounted for.

speaker: French Man 7
en: Excellent. Where are the man tasked with the other matter?

speaker: French Soldier 6
en: Ah... they have not returned yet, Father.

speaker: French Man 7
en: What? It has been hours. If they are in their cups at the tavern again, it will be their heads. See they report to me as soon as they return. The bishop's very keen to know the matter has been dealt with. Now, back to your duties.

speaker: Eivor
en: The church appears closed.

speaker: French Man 7
en: It's the plague. We're still receiving tithes, however. God will receive your offering too, Northerner.

speaker: French Man 7
en: How did you come by this watchword?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is it not enough that I have it? Or would you like to question the bishop about his business?

speaker: French Man 7
en: Strange that he told me nothing of this, but... of course. You may pass.

speaker: French Man 7
en: Let the Northerner through.

speaker: French Soldier 7
en: I'm watching you, Northerner. Be about your business quickly.

speaker: Eivor
en: There must be a way I can get in.

speaker: French Man 7
en: Only those on urgent business for the bishop may pass.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could be on such business.

speaker: French Man 7
en: If you were, you'd have mentioned the watchword. But you haven't. So you aren't. Come back once the plague has passed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to get through.

speaker: French Man 7
en: As I told you, no one can enter due to the plague.

speaker: French Man 8
en: Every one of you has sinned and fallen from God. And why do you sin? Because something inside you compels you! Only God can burn away the darkness in your souls. Go to his altar. Seek deliverance while it may yet be found!

speaker: Eivor
en: Whatever deliverance is, it sounds grim.

speaker: French Woman 5
en: Did you hear that priest? He was talking about deliverance again.

speaker: French Man 9
en: They are always talking, usually about offerings. You would think God himself was poor if you listened to him.

speaker: French Woman 5
en: Hush! Don't say such things! You'll be taken for a heretic, and sent for deliverance yourself.

speaker: French Soldier 8
en: Count Odo fights with the might of God, and Gozlin fights with a mighty sword... Together, they fight whenever, while Charles don't fight and just gets bored...

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to find Bishop Engelwin. Do you know where he is?

speaker: French Man 10
en: If you are here for deliverance, you have a long wait. My brother has been upstairs waiting for hours now.

speaker: French Man 11
en: That seems a lot of money, but I shouldn't have looked. The bishop and the Bellatores serve God. That's the end of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is behind this door that it needs a guard?

speaker: French Man 11
en: This is private. Only those appropriately robed are admitted beyond this point. Return to the main area of the church.

speaker: Eivor
en: The guard mentioned a robe. I should find one.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is an impressive hoard for a bishop. Engelwin serves more than the church alone.

speaker: French Man 12
en: It can't be right. Bishop Engelwin didn't say anything about this. Why are they screaming? What do they do in the basement?

speaker: Eivor
en: This robe is well made, and looks ceremonial. It might be useful.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you here for deliverance?

speaker: French Man 12
en: Yes... I don't know. I want to be close to God. But those screams don't seem right. Does it seem right to you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your deliverance ritual, is it with Engelwin?

speaker: French Man 12
en: Yes, he does it alone. I'm next in line and I... I don't think I want this.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could take your place, and see Engelwin for you. Then you could leave. Tell me what I must do.

speaker: French Man 12
en: You need a robe. They won't let you in without their special robe. Then you go down to the corridor and talk to the priest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Give me your robe.

speaker: French Man 12
en: My robe? They gave me one but I didn't put it on. I left it somewhere around here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will find it and take your place. You should leave now before they call for you.

speaker: French Man 12
en: Yes... yes, you're right. As soon as my nerves settle.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be the robe I need. It is well made.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have a robe already.

speaker: French Man 12
en: O, right, yes. Just make sure you are wearing it when you go in. They won't let you in, otherwise.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will go to the priest now. You should leave.

speaker: French Man 12
en: Yes... yes, you're right. As soon as my nerves settle.

speaker: French Man 11
en: I see you are ready for the ritual.

speaker: French Man 11
en: Take this key. Prepare your heart and when you are ready, enter through this door. The bishop is waiting for you.

speaker: French Woman 6
en: Welcome, traveler.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your eyes are covered, yet you see me.

speaker: French Woman 6
en: Justice and innocence are both blind, yet see more clearly for it. Find them, light the way, and see the treasures of God. God is light, and in him is no darkness at all. The way through darkness to your deliverance is clear when it is lit by God.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a riddle. The way to deliverance ... that must mean Engelwin.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is one. The nun said "lights." There must be another.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is two.

speaker: French Woman 6
en: Justice and innocence light the way. Without them, we are blind.

speaker: French Woman 6
en: Naked you came from your mother's womb, and naked you will return. Enter here now, naked and alone.

speaker: Eivor
en: Engelwin.

speaker: Engelwin
en: It is always this way, deliverance or death. Another soul for the Day of Judgement. All thy judgments are just. Amen.

speaker: Eivor
en: This disguise may not be convincing up close. I should keep my distance from the guards.

speaker: Engelwin
en: Only those who know God can truly know beauty. And to truly know God, we must suffer. This is a paradox, and is itself beautiful.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is more than just greed. Engelwin is gathering a war chest.

speaker: Engelwin
en: You must enter the pool. We cannot begin until you are cleansed by the ritual water. Come, my child. Like the priests of old, you must be cleansed by water before approaching God. Step into the pool.

speaker: Engelwin
en: Come. Do you know why you are here, child?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes.

speaker: Engelwin
en: You have been chosen for a great honor. Yet being chosen is only the beginning. What we do now won't be pleasant. Remember, the Lord has said, "Unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required."

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I remember.

speaker: Engelwin
en: Others have shown themselves... unworthy, as you have seen. My hope is you will fare better.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will.

speaker: Engelwin
en: Your confidence speaks well of you. Once we begin, we cannot stop. I will not heed your cries. Your soul depends on it. The devil will not endure the pain, so you must. Do you understand?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I understand.

speaker: Engelwin
en: We may discover in the pain there is a delicious pleasure. God himself grants it as a mercy to aid us in the struggle. Now, make yourself ready. Disrobe and do not leave the pool until I grant you leave.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am to be unclothed?

speaker: Engelwin
en: Do not be concerned for modesty. Once you comply my guards will leave, and we will be alone for the ritual.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very well.

speaker: Engelwin
en: Guards, leave us.

speaker: Engelwin
en: Very good. You have made the correct choice and now, we will begin. Accept, I beseech thee, this freewill offering, O Lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your offering is accepted.

speaker: Engelwin
en: You are an imposter! Guards! To me!

speaker: Engelwin
en: Touch not the Lord's anointed, you ungodly heathen.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not be naked.

speaker: Engelwin
en: You must disrobe for the ritual. My guards will leave us alone once you do. It will be just you, and me, and God. But I warn you, if you do not comply my guards do not bear their swords in vain. Now disrobe.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not be naked, you loathsome draugr (ghoul).

speaker: Engelwin
en: There's an intruder! Guards! Guards, to me!

speaker: Engelwin
en: I cast you out, devil! I will purge you! God fights with me, heathen!

speaker: Eivor
en: He had a strange key and a strange chest on him. I should find a way out of here quickly, before he's discovered.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Is it done?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And have you laid poles of hazel and composed your poems for the coming victory?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm here to speak with Geadric.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Go on then. Your master awaits.

speaker: Eivor
en: Still dreaming of your precious stone?

speaker: Sigurd
en: It's not dreams that led me here, Eivor. I've had visions. Prophecies from the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: Visions?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I'll sacrifice to Týr this day. The Lord of Justice. The harbinger of flawless victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, what prophecies?

speaker: Geadric
en: Are we ready to assault the castle, Eivor? The signs and portents read well.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll return when I've destroyed enough of Eadwyn's men and supplies.

speaker: Geadric
en: We'll be ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maintain the fyrd. I'll return when the time is right.

speaker: Geadric
en: As you say, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Hush, Eivor. Our sacrifice must find its way into the ears of the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: We both fight for the same end, do we not? Let us put our differences behind us, Brother.

speaker: Sigurd
en: My difference is what is at stake here. My difference is all that matters.

speaker: Eivor
en: You don't believe that. I know you don't.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've been foolish, Sigurd. Scampering about like a bewildered child.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Don't wield your jaw-lightning over me. I asked for quiet.

speaker: Eivor
en: And I refused it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Time has passed and our blood has simmered. Will you talk with me?

speaker: Sigurd
en: When the battle is won, we will speak at length. Not before.

speaker: Geadric
en: Eivor. Are you ready to begin the assault, now?

speaker: Eivor
en: We are ready. Give the command.

speaker: Geadric
en: Good. An' let's be quick about it. My scouts tell me a force of King Aelfred's men is on the march. Let's end this before that flap-mouthed pudding has a chance to hit back.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Bring down the drawbridge!

speaker: Sigurd
en: It's open!

speaker: Eivor
en: Take the castle!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Spare no one!

speaker: Sigurd
en: She's through there!

speaker: Basim
en: Eivor! Get to the portcullis!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's open!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Pour through, men!

speaker: Eivor
en: Find Eadwyn!

speaker: Eadwyn
en: Fight me yourself, coward.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lady Eadwyn!

speaker: Sigurd
en: She has bodyguards.

speaker: Eivor
en: Eadwyn! You won't get away this time.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: Foolish Dane! I will send you to your sad supper in Valhalla.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: A reward in silver for each dead Dane!

speaker: Eivor
en: There's your wages.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: We will use your flesh as mulch for our crops!

speaker: Eivor
en: Go to your god, wherever he hides.

speaker: Geadric
en: You've felled the lofty lady!

speaker: Eadwyn
en: Do what you must, Thegn of Dungheaps. As one loyal to her shire and her people, I know which of us God favors.

speaker: Geadric
en: Eivor bested you. It's for Eivor to decide your fate.

speaker: Eivor
en: Heal her wounds, dress her in rags, and send her out onto the heath in exile. You are banished from Mercia. Without family, without rank, without friends to comfort you.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: I will walk the road until my feet are bloody, dreaming of cutting out your rotten lungs.

speaker: Eivor
en: You fought with honor and purpose. For that I put you in Geadric's care. He will see you're treated well.

speaker: Geadric
en: I will, so long as you recant your friendship with that pot of warm piss, King Aelfred.

speaker: Eadwyn
en: Agreed.

speaker: Geadric
en: Take her away.

speaker: Eivor
en: I fulfilled my promise to you, I trust you will do the same. An oath between our people?

speaker: Geadric
en: Aye, you've done us well, Eivor. I thank ye. And if you ever need the like, I'll do what I can.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will. Count on it.

speaker: Geadric
en: I'd be quick about plundering. King Aelfred'll be on his way, and he won't be alone.

speaker: Informant Note
en: My Lady, We have followed your wishes and kept a sharp eye on the Dane blackguards that darken our lands. I send this horseman to tell you, honored Dame, that those same Danes have been seen in the company of that damned heretic Fulke! She has somehow escaped, it appears. As I write, they are headed toward the abandoned tower where her cunning friend (no longer a thorn to us) was lying low. Your humble servant

speaker: Letter to Lady Eadwyn from Aelfred of Wessex
en: Lady, I remain prepared to support you with soldiers and supplies, should the need arise. –Aelfred Rex

speaker: Fulke
en: It's here somewhere. I know it. It must be.

speaker: Sigurd
en: My mind is ariot with hope.

speaker: Fulke
en: You see? The markings of the Ancient Ones. The Isu, the gods begat of gods.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I... I have seen this somewhere. I know these words. I...

speaker: Odin
en: One who stands at a threshold should take great care to look around...

speaker: Odin
en: ...For who knows what foes lie in wait, in the halls beyond.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have passed through this doorway once before. With Sigurd. In a dream.

speaker: Odin
en: Not once. A thousand times.

speaker: Eivor
en: A thousand?

speaker: Basim
en: What does it say, Sigurd? Does it speak to you?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yes, but the words are... fogged. Shadowed, and yet I... I feel their meaning. And the ash tree! I see the great Tree of Life. Her boughs reaching... skyward... opening the way.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor. I am more than I appear to be. So much more.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is wicked magic, Sigurd. Dark ' (magic). Do not listen!

speaker: Sigurd
en: No. This is real. This is everything.

speaker: Geadric
en: To the walls! To the walls!

speaker: Geadric
en: Aelfred's come! King Aelfred of Wessex! Marching up the rise with a mess of soldiers!

speaker: Eivor
en: Have we time to escape?

speaker: Geadric
en: The men are spent. We've not a chance in blazing Hell.

speaker: Sigurd
en: A parlay, then. We must call a parlay. I will speak... and the King of Wessex will listen.

speaker: Sigurd
en: As I understand, King Aelfred, your name is not spoken with affection here in Mercia.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Yet I am close enough to Wessex to hear myself praised from morn 'til twilight.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Return to your singing subjects then! And leave the affairs of Mercia to the Danes.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Not 'til your are safely out of hearing.

speaker: Basim
en: Offer an exchange, lord... You can (unintelligible)

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Please. No secrets here.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Let's end this here, my lord. Let's exchange men. My best warrior for yours, to prove peace.

speaker: Sigurd
en: After which, you leave Mercia, and we fall back north of river Ouse.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: These terms are fair. Wolfrich! My war thane, you will go with Geadric, brother.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Name your man.

speaker: Basim
en: Sigurd Jarl. I offer myself...

speaker: Sigurd
en: Thank you, Basim.

speaker: Fulke
en: King Aelfred! Wait.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Paladin Fulke? Are you with this company?

speaker: Fulke
en: I was, my lord. To recover from Eadwyn what was mine by right.

speaker: Fulke
en: Sigurd is the only man you need. He's worth more than twenty other men. He is the son of a king.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Traitorous snake!

speaker: Fulke
en: And his heresies are profound, my lord. He claims to be a living god.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll gut you, troll-woman!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Shush!

speaker: Sigurd
en: I'll gift myself to you, King Aelfred, 'cause it is not my fate to die by your hand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brother!

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Have faith that the Lord God watches over you all.

speaker: Fulke
en: This man is dangerous, my lord. Let me hold him.

speaker: King Aelfred
en: Do what you must. But treat him with care.

speaker: Eivor
en: By all the gods, Basim, what was that?

speaker: Basim
en: I will shadow them. They shall not get away.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you make of all this, Geadric?

speaker: Geadric
en: I'm no philosopher, but by my lights, a fellow who give himself o'er as hostage has as much sense as a pile of bear droppings.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a wise man.

speaker: Havi
en: The height of this mountain displeases me. If this were Asgard, I would have had my people flatten long it ago.

speaker: Havi
en: They'll need to dedicate an entire saga to this climb alone, the size of this mountain... Best I don't slip and break my neck. That would not do. Ragnarök will have come and gone by the time I reach the peak... I wonder, who will bring the final twilight upon us?

speaker: Glod
en: Answer me, you sniveling, useless bastard!

speaker: Havi
en: What's this now? Could this be the son of Surtr?

speaker: Glod
en: You defy the almighty Surtr? I will tear you apart, Einar.

speaker: Einar
en: No! No, there is no defiance! I am loyal to your father, I swear!

speaker: Glod
en: What did you say?

speaker: Einar
en: Urk! Glod, p-p-please...

speaker: Glod
en: Excuses, scholar! Pathetic! Make the relic work!

speaker: Einar
en: I... I am trying, lord. Please.

speaker: Glod
en: Trying? Trying?! You are failing! Are you so eager to die?

speaker: Einar
en: N-no... I will not, will not fail you... but, but I cannot revive the relic without the

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: I saw claw marks in Glod's chamber, like he's been bedding a troll or something.

speaker: Glod
en: You have failed me for the last time!

speaker: Einar
en: You don't understand! Urgh!

speaker: Glod
en: Now it lies dormant. Useless. The only means to awaken it

speaker: Einar
en: I've searched everywhere! B-b-but Ivaldi's records are a mess! Rest assured, I will

speaker: Einar
en: The purpose of

speaker: Gldd
en: The only purpose it has served is drawing out vermin.

speaker: Einar
en: No no no no!

speaker: Havi
en: Gentlemen. Ladies.

speaker: Einar
en: Gah! Oh, my leg...!

speaker: Einar
en: Have to... get away... agh! Ow!

speaker: Einar
en: Agh. Damn it all... mmph!

speaker: Havi
en: Tell me, where did the son of Surtr take the relic?

speaker: Einar
en: I don't... I can't... just... look! Who are you?

speaker: Havi
en: I am Havi of Asgard. I hold your fate in my hands. Answer me, before the room is swarmed and I leave you to the Muspels.

speaker: Einar
en: No, no! I can help you. You saw through the portal Glod opened, yes? You saw the vault? I can get you inside. I can!

speaker: Havi
en: I am listening. Best you are swift.

speaker: Einar
en: The vault, it's sealed with an ancient magic. But I can get you inside.

speaker: Havi
en: You can help me get the relic?

speaker: Einar
en: Yes, yes, but that is not the prize. It is what happens within the vault that can truly shape our fates!

speaker: Havi
en: They will be upon us soon... Can you walk?

speaker: Einar
en: I-I don't think so.

speaker: Havi
en: Very well.

speaker: Havi
en: Time to move.

speaker: Einar
en: Great. Great!

speaker: Havi
en: You said you could be of aid. Tell me how, traitor.

speaker: Einar
en: Would you stop calling me that! I may well have worked for the Muspels, but that does not make me a traitor!

speaker: Havi
en: You wrestle with reason like a rabbit wrestles a boar. I can see through lies before you even think of them, traitor.

speaker: Einar
en: Oh, piss off.

speaker: Havi
en: Carrying dwarves is fast becoming a habit.

speaker: Einar
en: What?

speaker: Havi
en: Never mind.

speaker: Einar
en: Just get me off this accursed rock. Oh, for crying out loud...! I'm going to die on this bloody rock...

speaker: Einar
en: Could you please just focus on the matter at hand!

speaker: Havi
en: The Muspels are afoot.

speaker: Einar
en: This day gets better and better!

speaker: Havi
en: Don't die. Stay here.

speaker: Einar
en: Then do not increase my chances! Oi! What? Where are you going?

speaker: Einar
en: Havi! What are you playing at?

speaker: Havi
en: We have company, traitor.

speaker: Einar
en: Stop calling me traitor, you horse's arse!

speaker: Havi
en: Let's go. Time to move.

speaker: Einar
en: I was better off with Glod, wasn't I... Great. Great!

speaker: Havi
en: Let us find somewhere fit for a discussion.

speaker: Havi
en: We will be safe enough here.

speaker: Einar
en: Are you mad? This close to the mountain? Surely the Muspels will find us.

speaker: Havi
en: Then you'd best tell me what I need to know. Quickly.

speaker: Einar
en: Listen to me! We can't stay here.

speaker: Havi
en: I need answers, now, traitor.

speaker: Einar
en: Do not call me that! I had my reasons! Not that you'd understand such an abstract concept as 'reason', you mad, spiteful half-blind

speaker: Havi
en: Choose your next words carefully. They may be your last.

speaker: Einar
en: They have my boy. The Muspels. I only did what I did to save him, you see?

speaker: Havi
en: You save him, I'll do anything you ask. I'll... I'll damn well walk you into Glod's vault myself.

speaker: Tyra
en: Stop!

speaker: Einar
en: My... my boy...

speaker: Einar
en: Oh my boy. What have they done to you?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Get off me. She wanted your life spared, not me, you backstabbing stack of shit.

speaker: Havi
en: Silence! Baldr would never dare speak to me in such a way. You've lost your eyes. You want to lose your tongue as well? Three dwarves is three more than I'd planning on rescuing. Can any of you fight? Of course not. So, I must find other uses for you.

speaker: Havi
en: You. Owe. Me.

speaker: Einar
en: We have much to discuss. But... we need to get this one into the Vault of the Ancients.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Are you...? Do you have any idea what you're saying? To do that... you'd need...

speaker: Einar
en: A Sunstone, yes. And very precisely augmented. Lad, if this is what it takes to drive out the Muspels...

speaker: Fritjof
en: Then it must be done. Alright.

speaker: Einar
en: There is a Sunstone that watches over Onarthorp. Bring it to me, at Hvergelmir Mylna, and I shall forge that which we need.

speaker: Havi
en: Must I do everything? Very well.

speaker: Havi
en: Wise words, indeed.

speaker: Einar
en: The Sunstone watches over Onarthorp. A small market town, long abandoned. I'll meet you at Hvergelmir Mylna, and we shall forge the Sunstone into a new form.

speaker: Havi
en: I watch. You forge. I will bring you the Sunstone.

speaker: Fritjof
en: My sight, I... I think it's returning. I... I can't believe I told you to kill my father.

speaker: Havi
en: Everything he did was all for you, you ungrateful cur.

speaker: Fritjof
en: That doesn't change the fact that he did those things though, does it?

speaker: Havi
en: Enough lip, or I'll take your sight for good. I have practice in tearing out eyeballs.

speaker: Havi
en: This looks to be the place. Dull as dishwater but... safe, once. A simpler life... One that has been denied to me, thanks to Loki. Not to mention my own occasional foolishness. Only one thing watches over this tiny village. That statue.

speaker: Havi
en: Nothing. But whatever stone was here has been carefully removed. No scratches nor scorches. So it was not taken by Muspel hands. When I was a child, my brothers and I would rob the fairies. Such innocent times. I remember how the fairies sometimes got wind of our approach, and would try to hide their treasures. Fairies, dwarves. They all think alike... I must search the nooks and crannies of this village. Leave no stone unturned.

speaker: Havi
en: There you are. Now, let us see what Einar can do with you.

speaker: Einar
en: Havi!

speaker: Einar
en: I was starting to worry you may have met with resistance.

speaker: Havi
en: Those who resist me are not long for this world.

speaker: Einar
en: Indeed. And we are not short of foes in this area, so I'd be glad for your company. Come, my workshop is close.

speaker: Havi
en: Here, Einar, your Sunstone.

speaker: Havi
en: This is where you worked, before the Muspels invaded?

speaker: Einar
en: One site of many, indeed. When the Muspels took Uldar, captured Fritjof, and my niece

speaker: Havi
en: Tyra?

speaker: Einar
en: Yes. I returned to the city. Worked with the Sons of Ivaldi, but to no avail. So, I allowed myself to be captured. Offered my services to Glod.

speaker: Havi
en: To rescue your son. There is more to you than meets the eye, Master Einar.

speaker: Einar
en: As you can see, it's been some time since I was last here. Now, if I may ask, what does the 'High One' of Asgard seek in Svartalfheim?

speaker: Havi
en: My motive is not so different to your own. A son to rescue. To do so, I believe I need the relic, though to what end remains a mystery.

speaker: Einar
en: I see. So you're not here to save dwarfkind?

speaker: Havi
en: If butchering Muspels in my path aids your cause, then I will not deny you my gifts.

speaker: Einar
en: You are most generous.

speaker: Havi
en: It has been said, yes.

speaker: Einar
en: Damn it all to Helheim.

speaker: Havi
en: What? What is it?

speaker: Einar
en: Havi, forgive me.

speaker: Havi
en: What? Do you fail me, Einar?

speaker: Einar
en: The Sunstone must endure incredible heat for me to render it into a new form. My instruments are no longer capable. I'm sorry.

speaker: Havi
en: Give it to me. I have the means to endure any heat.

speaker: Einar
en: Of course. When the process is complete, the Sunstone will shine brightly. Bring it to me then, and I shall finish what you have begun.

speaker: Havi
en: Big words from one so small. It will be done.

speaker: Havi
en: Now, to subject myself to the kind of heat that would kill all but a Muspel.

speaker: Havi
en: This had better work. If this is an elaborate deception, Einar's death will be considerably more simple.

speaker: Havi
en: Almost there. Just a little more...

speaker: Havi
en: It is done. The Sunstone radiates light and heat. Einar will know what to do next.

speaker: Einar
en: How did you... Ah, I know better than to ask.

speaker: Havi
en: Do you have what you need now?

speaker: Einar
en: Yes, I believe so. Let me see... ah! Still hot.

speaker: Havi
en: Will this work? Einar...?

speaker: Einar
en: Sorry. Sorry. I just... I've only ever read about this in the ancient scriptures. I've never seen it with my own eyes.

speaker: Havi
en: Can you get me into the vault or not?

speaker: Einar
en: I believe so. But... Glod is no fool. He'll surely have made preparations.

speaker: Havi
en: Let me worry about Glod.

speaker: Einar
en: As you wish. Now, if all has gone to plan, Fritjof and Tyra will be in position by the time you arrive within Uldar's Old City, the great cavern at its heart.

speaker: Havi
en: And you?

speaker: Einar
en: I must catch my breath and calm my nerves, but I will join you there as soon as I can.

speaker: Havi
en: See that you don't fail me.

speaker: Einar
en: Have I thus far?

speaker: Einar
en: I'll do as I have promised. The vault will be yours.

speaker: Einar
en: I won't let you down. Head for the Old City, within Uldar. Find my boy. I must rest a moment but I will join you there, and we'll finish this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Harald's colors. He is already marking his territory.

speaker: Dag
en: Marking? Gods, he's spraying like a horny pup.

speaker: Eivor
en: Harald may be young, but he is clever. Do not underestimate him. He came of age very quickly.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: You, there, what are you doing? If you wish to have words, come closer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you one of Harald's men?

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: I am. The king wishes to make a survey of the land he now rules. Nothing more.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me ask, are you one of the conquered? Did Harald take your lands as well?

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: No. My family has lived under his banner since the days of his father, Halfdan the Black.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well, welcome to Fornburg, warrior.

speaker: Eivor
en: How are you doing, Hytham? You survived a serious blow.

speaker: Hytham
en: I am mending. I will never be the warrior Basim wishes me to be, but I can serve my brotherhood in many other ways.

speaker: Eivor
en: With Kjotve dead, will you return to the south?

speaker: Hytham
en: We are going west, in fact. Basim is a tireless crusader.

speaker: Eivor
en: Get some rest before you set out, then. Injured men do not fare well on the open ocean.

speaker: Hytham
en: Of course. Thank you.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: You heard that Harald is banning raids in all of Norway?

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: I did.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Does that not bother you?

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: If we cannot raid anyone, they cannot raid us.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: O! A fair thought.

speaker: Svend
en: First they will demand taxes, and soon after they will be living in our homes!

speaker: Tove
en: Keep your voice down! They will hear you!

speaker: Svend
en: Fine by me! If those bacrauts (assholes) come to our door, I will carve them new shit holes!

speaker: Gunnar
en: How can I help?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will free you from this bond.

speaker: Gunnar
en: And I will be ready when you need me.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's Eivor. Open the door.

speaker: Alvis
en: Come in, but keep your voice down. You will alert Harald's men.

speaker: Tekla
en: Where will we live?

speaker: Holger
en: The English will fight back! The wars will never end!

speaker: Gudrun
en: Or they will push us into the Christian ways.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Quiet! All! Give me a chance to speak! Two days ago, we rid this land of Kjotve and his dogs. Yet today we do not celebrate. Today we cower under a cloud of fear. But it need not be like this. We are not the heel-trodden subjects of a boy-king! We are the Raven Clan. Our destiny is our own!

speaker: Tekla
en: Did you know about your father's oath to Harald?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I did not. And for that, my anger burns hotter than any man's here. But I will not let that drive me into despair. We cannot stay in Norway, not under Harald's boot, not without fueling more war. So we push forward. To newer lands.

speaker: Sigurd
en: To England! And there make a new home. A kingdom of our own.

speaker: Randvi
en: The Sons of Ragnar Lothbrok have been in England eight winters already. Is there any land left for a clan of our size?

speaker: Sigurd
en: More than enough, wife. Of the four kingdoms of England, only one is truly pacified.

speaker: Dag
en: I have no desire to wear Harald's leash. I like this idea.

speaker: Alvis
en: A for the ages, I agree!

speaker: Gudmund
en: It will take time and resources to build ourselves a new home. But the riches taken from Kjotve's raid would suffice.

speaker: Sigurd
en: No. That belongs to my father, as a fair compensation. In England, we must start anew.

speaker: Bragi
en: You would start us with nothing, in a land we do not know, among people who hate us?

speaker: Eivor
en: Kjotve's riches would go some way to easing our passage, Sigurd. I bested him. It is within my rights to claim his goods.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Our leaving must not be an assault on my father. It is a time of renewal for us.

speaker: Eivor
en: If we go, we will need all the help we can get. I saw we take Kjotve's spoils for our own.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I abhor such theft. But if this is what it takes to sway you to my cause, I accept.

speaker: Eivor
en: Styrbjorn will prosper by the generosity of his new king. Kjotve's riches belong to us.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you object, I understand. Let your father keep Kjotve's riches. England will have riches and cargo enough for us.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Good. I did not want this cloud hanging over us. It is a wise leader who considers the need of others.

speaker: Randvi
en: To England then, before the day is out. Pack what you need, but no more than that.

speaker: Eivor
en: And tighten your lips. The last thing we need is the attention of Harald's troops.

speaker: Eivor
en: How much did you hear?

speaker: Valka
en: Enough. A new path is revealed and your journey will be challenging.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will you not join us?

speaker: Valka
en: For my mother's sake, I cannot, but our threads will cross again before the final day. Until then, farewell.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: I don't like the way those soldiers watch me.

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: I find it flattering.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: You think one will marry you and carry you off to the capital?

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: Would he?

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: He would take his pleasure and move on, you moon-eyed magpie. Leaving you with a little soldier to raise by yourself.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, the wind favors us! We should set sail without delay.

speaker: Eivor
en: You made quick work of packing. Well done.

speaker: Randvi
en: The dream of new lands is a powerful lure.

speaker: Eivor
en: As is the promise of glory. But the act of leaving so beloved a home, there is a sadness to it.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Having doubts?

speaker: Eivor
en: No. Not at all. The die is cast.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Then let fate guide our journey. Are you ready?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am ready. Let us take to the water and leave unbothered while we have the chance.

speaker: Randvi
en: That chance has passed. Look.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fate flies on swifter wings than we.

speaker: Sigurd
en: King Harald's banner.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Sigurd, what is this assembly? What are you planning?

speaker: Sigurd
en: An exit, Father. As graceful as I can. For if I cannot be king in the land of my birth, I will start a new saga. In England.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Nonsense. Your place is here, Son. At my side. There will be other victories soon, other glories.

speaker: Sigurd
en: My choice is made, Father. Do not hope otherwise.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: It is easy to lose one's way on the road to glory. Do not let false victories blind you to what is true.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You talk of false victories to me, old man? A sad old bear who destroyed his honor with one bent knee? The further I sail from this place, the louder I will sing.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will be his anchor, lord.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: No, you must be his better half.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: May Ægir bless your voyage.

speaker: Sigurd
en: My choice is made, Father. Do not hope otherwise. There is nothing for me here. I must go make my name in the world.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: And you have plundered Fornburg's resources, I see. You leave nothing behind but your honor.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You left me no choice. I entered the ' (clan meeting) a prince. I left the son of a jarl.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: There are always choices, Sigurd. I will not stand between you and yours, but I do not accept it.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Seventeen winters ago, I opened my door to you, Eivor. And now... your only thanks is to rob me? I should have left you to the wolves.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Sad old elk. Do not carry his words with you to England. He brought this day upon himself.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know.

speaker: Dag
en: The time for tears is over, you weeping sacks of wool! Put some muscle into those pulls!

speaker: Bragi
en: Ration your strength, Dag. We have an ocean to cross.

speaker: Dag
en: All right, you lazy bacraut (asshole). Sigurd, what's our course?

speaker: Sigurd
en: The Sons of Ragnar established a settlement near the coast. We set sail for that. Bragi! Sing a song to lift our hugr (spirits)!

speaker: Dag
en: To rouse the gods! Inspire a mighty fart from Thor to speed us on our way!

speaker: Sigurd
en: An ocean lies before us, Eivor. And on its far side, a new kingdom awaits.

speaker: Eivor
en: You know England well from your travels?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I spend a season in their Kingdom of Mercia. A temperate land. Lush and wild. By now, the Sons of Ragnar will have claimed its heart.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do we mean to join their army?

speaker: Sigurd
en: They will join ours! In time, all of England will know of Raven Clan and the glory we brought to that fractured land. So to England, glory and destiny!

speaker: Eivor
en: To England!

speaker: Dag
en: To England! Or Valhalla!

speaker: Linco
en: I am fortune's fool! The one weapon that can fell a Muspel in a single blow, just out of my reach! If only a champion, a hero of great magnitude, would heed my call! And claim my weapon as their own!

speaker: Havi
en: What ails you, little one?

speaker: Linco
en: By the might of Ymir! You are Havi of Asgard, yes? I had heard you were afoot, but never expected to lay eyes upon you! It's my hammer! A mighty hammer, strong enough to tear a mountain in two. And by sheer accident, I tripped, and threw it out there. If you can retrieve it, then you may keep it, Havi.

speaker: Havi
en: A weapon of such strength cannot be ignored. Very well. I shall get it.

speaker: Havi
en: It is done. A trivial matter for the High One.

speaker: Linco
en: Yes, I can see the lava was no problem for you. But... Oh no! The hammer! It is damaged.

speaker: Havi
en: Damaged!

speaker: Linco
en: Yes, look closely... This crack in the shaft...

speaker: Linco
en: You have passed the trial, High One.

speaker: Havi
en: Trial? What trial?

speaker: Havi
en: Ugh, my head... What the Hel...?

speaker: Mikke
en: Oi. You. Come here, quick. Pssst! Hey! You there, Æsir! Don't draw attention, just get over here, before it's too late.

speaker: Mikke
en: Right, we've only got one shot at this, so listen, and listen good.

speaker: Havi
en: What are you jabbering about? Who are you? What's happening?

speaker: Mikke
en: Unless you want me to tell this Muspel who you really are, and while you're still helpless, I suggest you do as I tell you, and quickly!

speaker: Havi
en: Helpless?! You dare to threaten me?! I'll throttle you through these bars!

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: Shut up or I'll shut you up!

speaker: Mikke
en: There's no time to explain. I'll lure the guard, you grab his key. Get us out of here and I'll explain everything. Ready?

speaker: Havi
en: What?

speaker: Mikke
en: Hey you! Yeah you! Come here! I got some information your chief is gonna want!

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: Go on then, enlighten me. What drivel will you spout this time?

speaker: Mikke
en: Your mother spotted by last night, paid me a visit.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: She died years ago, fool.

speaker: Mikke
en: Yeah, well, uh...

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: You idiot...

speaker: Mikke
en: Idiot, am I? Surtr's your overlord, yeah? Reckon he might want to find the High One of Asgard?

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: Hah! The shit that comes out of your mouth.

speaker: Mikke
en: What if I told you that Havi is a lot closer than you think?

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: I'd tell you your execution is a lot closer than you think.

speaker: Mikke
en: I know where Havi is right now. Just come in here and I'll whisper it in your ear.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: The way you smell, I'm fine staying out here. You have something to say, then say it.

speaker: Mikke
en: I'm serious. Me and Havi, we're old pals. Go back years, we do.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: Every day. Every day I am forced to endure you and your horseshit. I honestly wish someone would put me out of my misery.

speaker: Mikke
en: Heh. Be careful what you wish for.

speaker: Mikke
en: Now then, get your things so we can leave. You'll catch a chill if you head out dressed like that. I mean, eventually. We haven't got time for funny-business. Grab your things, eh?

speaker: Mikke
en: You'll get nowhere without me! Let me out! Hey! Don't just leave me here!

speaker: Havi
en: Get up. We're leaving.

speaker: Mikke
en: Only if you promise to get me out. No matter what. I stay here, I'm dead.

speaker: Havi
en: Tell me what's going on or I'll kill you myself.

speaker: Mikke
en: The Muspels took me prisoner. Threw me in here. Now, on the other side of that opening is a hall full of lava. I can't get out, not on my own. But if you're in here with me... lava's not a problem for you. Not according to our mutual acquaintance.

speaker: Havi
en: The Jotun shapeshifter? The one who tricked me, told me of a hammer that could split mountains?

speaker: Mikke
en: Ah, that old chestnut! Look, you want the real hammer, pick me up, get me through the tunnel.

speaker: Havi
en: Fine.

speaker: Mikke
en: Yah! Ooh! Hot hot hot hot!

speaker: Havi
en: Shut up, or I'll drop you into it.

speaker: Mikke
en: Just, hurry up! Agh!

speaker: Mikke
en: Come, High One. Time to go.

speaker: Mikke
en: Smell that, High One? The sweet aroma of freedom. And we have you to thank for it.

speaker: Havi
en: What was your crime?

speaker: Mikke
en: Other than being a dwarf and fighting invaders?

speaker: Havi
en: Fighting invaders?

speaker: Mikke
en: I'm a blacksmith by trade... Just before the invasion of our lands began, I single-handedly armed an army. Bravest dwarves you ever saw. Clans dropping long-held grudges, joining to fight Muspels and the Jotnar. Anyway, all came to nothing in the end. I was locked up. Told they'd let me out if I made weapons for the Muspels... told them I'd sooner die. Now, about that hammer...

speaker: Havi
en: I know. Nothing more than a tall tale. And not a bad one.

speaker: Mikke
en: You did all this, knowing there was no mighty weapon? I see now why they call you the High One.

speaker: Linco
en: Haha! There he is! Safe at last, brother! I told you I would find someone who could help.

speaker: Mikke
en: Never thought I'd be so happy to lay eyes on that big ugly face of yours. You did well, brother.

speaker: Linco
en: Ugly! Hah! Have you looked in the mirror lately? Father should've dropped you from the cliffs the moment your tiny screwed-up face drew breath! It's good to see you.

speaker: Havi
en: Well well, the Jotun who managed to fool me. And you're brothers?

speaker: Linco
en: Aye, brothers from another mother. Our father was Travi, the famed dwarven explorer who travelled the Nine Realms.
