speaker: Mikke
en: Travi and my mother are dwarves. My half-brother here is half-dwarf, half-Jotun. We have a sister who is half dwarf, half Muspel.

speaker: Linco
en: And another brother that is... well... half-bear, but that's another story.

speaker: Havi
en: I see. Your father Travi was... very well-traveled.

speaker: Mikke
en: He kept himself busy, that's for sure.

speaker: Linco
en: You have our gratitude, High One. We shall drink to your honor for all time!

speaker: Havi
en: Enjoy your freedom, and stay out of trouble, lads.

speaker: Havi
en: This is how I overcame several legendary animals and the shapeshifters hiding in their ranks. I approached a group of beasts from downwind, and caught them by surprise. I travelled on, but in moments I was surrounded by beasts! Next was a battle to set a skalds tongue to stirring song! Once again, I had shown my prowess, and proved that none can defeat me!

speaker: Sigfred
en: To the palace! Fire and vengeance! Faster, faster! Catch them off guard!

speaker: Goll
en: Follow me, warriors! To Hel or victory!

speaker: Goll
en: Warriors, halt! There is a deep wrongness here. These dead. They are all Norse.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Where are those Frankish dogs? This silence gnaws my guts. Shields up and close ranks.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Forward! Spare no one, attack!

speaker: Eivor
en: They're too many. Sigfred, we must retreat.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Fall back, warriors! Fall back!

speaker: Goll
en: Come fight me, cowards!

speaker: Eivor
en: They're cutting us down!

speaker: Sigfred
en: Fall back! Fall back!

speaker: Sigfred
en: Damn the gods! I walked right into Odo's trap like a yearling elk.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not lose heart, Sigfred. Battle is a fickle goddess.

speaker: Toka
en: Uncle, it is worse. The scouts report that warrior priest, uh

speaker: Eivor
en: Gozlin.

speaker: Toka
en: Yes, he rallies a large force of Franks in the east, in that church.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Damn the gods. They will crush us out in the open. What do we do?

speaker: Toka
en: Our catapults could hit that church, but they have no way to aim.

speaker: Eivor
en: We should light signal fires on the towers. That will give the catapults something to target.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Yes, do it. I will get the wounded out and alert the catapults before rejoining you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. And I will take down this warrior-priest Gozlin before he rallies the Franks.

speaker: Toka
en: Eivor, keep up! We must light those towers.

speaker: Toka
en: Watch out!

speaker: Toka
en: Damn their aim! Where are they shooting?

speaker: Toka
en: Eivor! Climb up and light the towers. I will take out the guards below.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's one tower. Now for number two.

speaker: Eivor
en: The gates are down. Charge!

speaker: Pantomime
en: You there, help! Yes, you, the hulking barbarian! Please, help me!

speaker: Eivor
en: I remember you, the silent jester from the tavern.

speaker: Pantomime
en: You have earned my eternal gratitude. I assume you seek the war-priest Gozlin? Please, take the church key. It's brought me only trouble.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thanks. It seems you found your tongue, after all.

speaker: French Man
en: Hush, my son, you didn't see anything. You're scared, that's all.

speaker: French Child 1
en: No, Papa, I did! The big cross moved, it wobbled.

speaker: French Man
en: Perhaps it was a sign just for you. Now pray silently like Mémé taught.

speaker: Gozlin
en: Fear not, brethren! We are safe behind these stone walls, safe in God's house.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Safe? The Northmen have broken through the city gates!

speaker: Gozlin
en: And ran right into our trap. Even now, our warriors gather for my devastating counter-attack. We will crush them between the towers and the walls. We will slay them all and burn their villages! Now pray with me, good people. Pray to God and all the saints to deliver us from this plague of heathens.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Pray for what? A quick death? You have failed us, bishop!

speaker: Gozlin
en: We shall pray that King Charles and his army arrives to smite our godless foes. Have faith.

speaker: French Woman 1
en: You pray for a rescue from Charles the Fat? Truly, we are doomed!

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: The Mad King drinks wine while Paris burns!

speaker: Gozlin
en: O ye of little faith! I command you to pray with me! Our Father, Who art in Heaven, Hallowed be Thy Name...

speaker: Eivor
en: If that cross falls on someone, it could be deadly.

speaker: Gozlin
en: My God... is that a darkness... or a light... argh...

speaker: Eivor
en: Join your Nailed God in death, as you served him in life.

speaker: French Man
en: Hail, thou art highly favored, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women.

speaker: French Child 1
en: Dear God, also please let Socks-Paw be safe.

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: We should be inside, praying with Lord Gozlin.

speaker: French Soldier 3
en: Captain says we stay here and watch for our flag-bearers. If they fall, we fall back to the church through the front door. The men are jumpy. If the flag-bearers fall, they will desert.

speaker: French Soldier 4
en: Enough. Fall back, men, fall back!

speaker: Gozlin
en: You! You foul beast. You Northmen slaughtered my brother.

speaker: Gozlin
en: Now I shall wreak a terrible vengeance upon you.

speaker: Eivor
en: He stood in my way. Now you, too, stand in my way.

speaker: Gozlin
en: O Lord God, to whom vengeance belongeth, how long shall the wicked triumph?

speaker: Gozlin
en: Die, heathen!

speaker: Gozlin
en: God give me strength!

speaker: Gozlin
en: No! This cannot be. God, heal me!

speaker: Gozlin
en: Lord, into Thy hands I commend my spirit...

speaker: Eivor
en: To Hel's icy embrace I send thee, down in Niflheim where the dragon dwells.

speaker: French Child 2
en: Mama, I'm scared.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Clear the hall!

speaker: French Woman 2
en: Hush child, hush.

speaker: Toka
en: Come, Eivor. The fighting still rages through the streets. We need your strength.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Blood red wine for your drinking horn, my brother.

speaker: Eivor
en: How does this end, Toka? Killing everyone?

speaker: Toka
en: It is as I feared, the bloodlust is upon him. He will slaughter the whole city.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I can reach Count Odo, I can make him surrender, to stop this madness.

speaker: Toka
en: Sigfred's warriors have surrounded the gates to Odo's palace. With Gozlin dead, the streets are ours. We are moving the catapults to batter the palace gates down.

speaker: Eivor
en: There must be another way over, under, or around those walls.

speaker: Toka
en: Nolwenn once spoke of a tunnel in the southwest.

speaker: Eivor
en: One way or another, I'll get in.

speaker: Sulke
en: Buy yourself some luck! Live a charmed life! Do you want the favor of the gods? Or protection from them?

speaker: Sulke
en: Welcome, warrior. Sulke Silvertongue offers wonders from across the Nine Worlds! Rare objects! Priceless artifacts!

speaker: Eivor
en: And yet you have put a price on them.

speaker: Sulke
en: Everything has value, wise one, and I ask only a fraction of its worth. What would you say to a piece of Christ's cross? Snakeskin from Ragnar Lothbrok's death pit?

speaker: Eivor
en: These items do not look very impressive. Like this old shoe...

speaker: Sulke
en: That belonged to the first Christian Pope... or maybe it was a saint. It brings the blessing of their god.

speaker: Eivor
en: They would need it with that shoe... and there's an old leather strap...

speaker: Sulke
en: A shield strap belonging to the hero Sigurth when he fought... the great beast.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ja... my mother had one embroidered like that. And what about that helmet?

speaker: Sulke
en: That was the helmet Halfdan the Black wore when he died in battle. It will protect you and bring good crops.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is a lie. It was the helmet my father, Varin, wore the night he was killed.

speaker: Sulke
en: Ei... Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: I know you now, Sulke the Snake, and these are things from my old home. How much silver did Kjotve pay you to betray us?

speaker: Sulke
en: No silver! It was not like that! I was there that night, but I did not fight for Kjotve! I ran...

speaker: Eivor
en: Coward! I should cut you down!

speaker: Sulke
en: No!

speaker: Sulke
en: I did no harm!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will judge that!

speaker: Bodyguard
en: Gahrr!

speaker: Sulke
en: Leave me alone!

speaker: Eivor
en: You will answer for your actions!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your treachery ends here.

speaker: Sulke
en: Please, I never betrayed Varin. On my life! I was frightened and I fled, and when I returned, everyone was gone or dead.

speaker: Eivor
en: And yet, you looted our dead. Bartered the ashes of their lives.

speaker: Sulke
en: It was all I could find. I sold nothing for a long time. But the weight grew too heavy, and I needed to eat... to survive.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is not living. Without honor we are worse than beasts and have no hope of a better life beyond this realm.

speaker: Sulke
en: This world is all I know, and this life all I have left. Would you take that from me? Take anything you want from my shop. Take everything. Just let me live.

speaker: Sulke
en: May the gods grant you better luck than I have seen!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sulke will stay within the city. He finds safety within its walls.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Bring it back! Please bring it back! Bad birdie! When I get hold of you, I'm gonna punch you right in the beak! That's my mother's, not yours, you stupid bag of feathers!

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened, little one?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Mummy's ring! I just took it out to look at it and a mean bird snatched them off me!

speaker: Eivor
en: What were you doing with your mother's ring?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Someone borrowed it, and she asked me to get it back. But now, it's up in that tree, and I can't climb that!

speaker: Eivor
en: There is the bird's nest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Something fell from the nest.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Here, you! Take your hands off my property! That ring is mine. Give it back, I say!

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you the girl's mother?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Stepmother! My husband gave me that ring. My stepdaughter stole it from me! She's been a plague to me ever since I married her father! When all I've tried to show her is kindness!

speaker: Eivor
en: She says you borrowed it from her mother.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Her mother is dead! O! Perhaps it did belong to her once. I didn't know.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your new husband gave you his dead wife's ring?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: We do not have much. I will not spurn a gift from a good heart. He is a fine man, and I love him dear. But his daughter will never love me. Not while she still pretends her mother is alive.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is his ring to give, and yours to keep. May your love hold true. I will speak to the girl.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Thank you, stranger. You are kind indeed.

speaker: Eivor
en: The ring belonged to your stepmother. You never told me that.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: It's not hers! She'll never be my mother!

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not think she is trying to be. Your mother is dead. You must accept that.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: I don't want to talk to you anymore.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let the girl have the ring. It is all she has of her mother. Do this, and new bonds may grow between you in time.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: You are wise, stranger. It is hard to give it up, but ... it belongs to her more rightfully than I. Take it to her, please.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have your mother's ring. Be careful in the future. We should hold tight to what is precious.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: I saw you talking to my stepmother down there! Did she try to take it off you? What a warty old dragon!

speaker: Eivor
en: She agreed that you should have it. Be kind to her, little girl. She is trying her best for you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: I suppose. I'll speak to Mother about it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Farewell, then.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me more about Ledecestrescire. I should like to join Sigurd soon.

speaker: Randvi
en: He traveled to a town called Repton to meet Ubba and Ivarr Ragnarsson. As I hear it, they are on the verge of exiling the current King of Mercia, with the hope of installing a king of their own.

speaker: Eivor
en: A bold endeavor. I should be there to help, however I can.

speaker: Randvi
en: I think you should.

speaker: Eivor
en: I won't keep them waiting.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. I will send word to Sigurd and the Ragnarssons, pledging your assistance. If I were you, I would go by ship. Repton is quite a distance north on the river Trent.

speaker: Eivor
en: Repton. Sigurd should be here with the Ragnarssons.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: No! No! Ah! P-please!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Stay still.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Who stand before Ivarr Ragnarsson? Are you Sigurd's drengr (courageous warrior)? Aygor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor. If you keep that up, you'll stain the floors.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eh. The place could use some color.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who are they?

speaker: Ivarr
en: All spies. Dressed to look the part of a peasant. Got feisty. Pitchfork. From this rabid little one.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Was a time when you met and slew your enemy on the field before they could dream of things like sending spies.

speaker: Eivor
en: And now we sake hands and make deals.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Not my thing.

speaker: Eivor
en: I figured.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I love them whipped, weeping, and reeking of piss. Hey!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Good boy.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You're free, Saxon piggy! To run amok through the Mercian fields.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would have let him down easy.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Hm. Follow me. I'll give you the tour.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you call this place?

speaker: Ivarr
en: I call it The Shithole. To the Mercians, it is Repton. Their most revered kings are buried below the church. Imagine their weeping when we drove them out!

speaker: Eivor
en: You plunged your knife deep into the heart of this kingdom.

speaker: Ivarr
en: That is right. We've got a number of Saxon nobles lined up with their lips puckered, ready to kiss our asses. The only holdout is King Burgred and his war-thegn, Leofrith. But my brother is brewing a plan to deal with them.

speaker: Eivor
en: I take it that's where we'll find my brother.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Right. Talkers they are, Ubba and Sigurd. Might want to dig the wax from your ears.

speaker: Tonna
en: Don't play me for a fool, Ubba. I know Burgred's sent a your way.

speaker: Ubba
en: Enough of your noise, Tonna! We have plans to devise!

speaker: Tonna
en: I'm not going anywhere, bacraut (asshole). You have the king on his heels because of me! Because of my men!

speaker: Ubba
en: For which you were paid! But that price does not change because you caught a whiff of our hoard!

speaker: Tonna
en: You forget, I am a sellsword. I ask for what I please, and I take what I'm owed.

speaker: Ivarr
en: If I wanted to hear you talk shit, I'd gouge out your tongue and shove it up your ass. Now, fuck off.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Haggling over silver is a bad look for the son of Ragnar Lothbrok. But worry not, Ubba, I have the warriors you need.

speaker: Ubba
en: If this is one of them, my worries have vanished.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor! Wolf-Kissed. You have come at just the right time. Ubba and Ivarr hare are hunting a king.

speaker: Ubba
en: And when we've caught him, we mean to crown another. Our own Thegn Ceolwulf here.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: It's not a role I begged for, but it's what Mercia needs just now. A man to fairly rule both Saxons and Danes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you have what it takes to be king?

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: One day, I hope. As it stands, we at least have an understanding.

speaker: Eivor
en: It sounds like you'll be a king in name only. A puppet.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: I am doing my part. I hope you have come to do yours. We are going to need all the help we can get for what lies ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can't imagine the current king is too happy about all this.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Burgred is furious, of course. But this is our new reality. And I don't want to sit idly by while he drags our kingdom through the dirt.

speaker: Ubba
en: The king has refused our offers of peace. Ceolwulf means to change that. He'll be a new king for a new England.

speaker: Sigurd
en: For now, Burgred is holed up in his fortress at Tamworth, making a final stand.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Another shithole, only further south.

speaker: Ubba
en: We've held a siege there for weeks, to no effect. So no more knocking. Now we batter the gate to splinters. If we take Tamworth, remove Burgred, and crown Ceolwulf... come morning, this shire is ours. And Mercia soon after.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Yes, remove. I cannot stress that enough. Burgred is not to be harmed. My legitimacy as king hangs on this one simple fact.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You rob all the joy from war, Saxon.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Not every victory needs to be marked by the slaughter of a king.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ah, but it is much better.

speaker: Sigurd
en: His request is fair, Ivarr. And we will honor it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolwulf betrayed his present king. Maybe tomorrow he betrays us too. Why trust him?

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: How can I answer that with any hope that you'd believe me? I only want what is best for the people of Mercia. And I want what's best for my son. In Burgred's Mercia, where Danes and Saxons murder one another daily, it's not possible.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is a good plan, brother. I am ready for the coming fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolwulf's right to be cautious. If he shows mercy to Burgred, the people have reason to trust him

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: My thinking exactly. And the quicker we act, the more lives we spare... on both sides.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is a good plan, brother. I am ready for the coming fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is a good plan, brother. I am ready for the coming fight.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Agreed. Yet remember this. Whatever you stand to gain here, so do we. An alliance between my clan and Mercia's crown.

speaker: Ubba
en: See this man installed on his throne and you will have it, I swear.

speaker: Eivor
en: The bold Sons of Ragnar bellow to sound the spear din and the thunder of shields. So let fall the arrow storm. The battle begins.

speaker: Ubba
en: Ah! You never said this one was a poet!

speaker: Ivarr
en: I need to piss.

speaker: Ubba
en: We have a forward camp just north of Tamworth. Will you go with us?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Lead the way.

speaker: Ubba
en: Take in the sights of Repton if you like. We will be at the docks when you're ready to go.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: I'm glad you and your brother have come. If only to bring some measure of calm.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ease yourself, Ceolwulf. We all stand to benefit. And you'll be remembered for this, for years to come.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: For all the wrong reasons, I fear.

speaker: Eivor
en: A lively town. Quite a lot to see here.

speaker: Ceowulf
en: I'll gather my things and meet you in Tamworth as soon as it's over.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: So some of us are staying behind as I hear it?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Half the army's already in Tamworth, and we've now got help from the south. It's our lot to look after this place now. To protect her.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Shame. I wanted to see the look on Burgred's face when we stormed his fortress. Now we'll just hear big tales, told by drunken heroes.

speaker: Ubba
en: Sail southeast. Bring the men to the gates of Tamworth. We'll flood the fields, and Burgred shall weep at the sight of what the future holds for this kingdom!

speaker: Ubba
en: Eivor... is your axe sharpened?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm ready for the spear din.

speaker: Ubba
en: And the thunder of shields, yes! It's good to have you with us.

speaker: Eivor
en: To fight beside such legends is an honor. I've only heard tales of your conquests. Now I get to live them.

speaker: Ubba
en: We'll weave our sagas together, thread upon thread.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Come on, boy. We'll forge a man from your softness, hammered on the anvil of war.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: One does not need to fight to be a

speaker: Ivarr
en: Move! Move!

speaker: Ubba
en: Calm, Ivarr. The fight's not here.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Aye. The fight's not anywhere to be found in this boy.

speaker: Ubba
en: A boy who happens to be Ceolwulf's son. Why is he not in his quarters?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Our future king wants a battle hardened heir. Time he proves his worth, don't you think?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not yet crowned king and already grooming his successor. That shows some boldness

speaker: Ivarr
en: Right. And bold kings need bolder sons.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can't be an heir if he's dead, Ivarr. Can he wield a sword?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I've had some training. I only... I don't want to kill anyone. These men are my friends, my countrymen.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Relax, little king. They won't call you friend now. You can thank your father for that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Throwing a boy who stinks of fear to a pack of wolves is not the best way to train him. Are you sure that's what Ceolwulf wants?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Mm... he left it open for interpretation.

speaker: Ubba
en: Ivarr...

speaker: Ivarr
en: He comes with us. And should anything happen to this little sprout, I will bear the punishment our future king inflicts.

speaker: Ubba
en: He'll want to remove your head.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ha ha! You hear that, boy? You die, and I'll have to kill your father too.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Mount up, Eivor. It's a long ride to Tamworth.

speaker: Ubba
en: You'll have to endure my brother. He always finds new ways to humor himself.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll keep that in mind.

speaker: Ubba
en: And both eyes open.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You smell that, Ceolbert? The stink of jealousy. Of our budding friendship, I think.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is Ceolwulf's son doing in Repton at all?

speaker: Ubba
en: It's Ceolwulf's way of proving his loyalty. And there's no safer place for a traitor and his son than the middle of a pack of Danes.

speaker: Eivor
en: Safe from who? You and Ivarr seem to have brought this shire to hell.

speaker: Ubba
en: The s are with us, the common folk. But Burgred still has his soldiers all over Mercia. They're devoted to him. And they'll die defending him.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Your voice, Eivor. You sound different than the brothers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good ear, lord. Most in England cannot tell the difference. But not all Danes are Danes.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: From where do you come, if I may ask?

speaker: Eivor
en: North of the Dane Lands. A place called Fornburg, in Norway.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I didn't know there was land north of there. What are the people like?

speaker: Eivor
en: You ever see a herd of sheep follow each other off the edge of a cliff? They're like that. The ones who remained, anyway.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Couldn't have said it better myself.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Was it a mass exodus from Norway then?

speaker: Sigurd
en: It was. Norway is now the province of a young king. Harald by name, a boy wise beyond his years.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Are you not angry that he has displaced you and so many others?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I was... for a time. But our weeks at sea have softened my brow-fire. If I am honest, I realize I quite admire King Harald. By words and weapons both, he had pacified the country I call home. For the first time in any man's memory or any skalds song, Norway has one king. Just one. And that is quite a feat.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: That is impressive, truly. England is half the size of Norway, and yet we have four kings for our four kingdoms.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You see? How could I not be impressed? No, Harald is a good man with grand ideas. I can see that now.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I am only six years his junior, and have yet to see my first battle. I cannot imagine the skill and cunning he has.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Your first battle is coming, young Ceolbert. From this day on, you may see rapid progress.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I'm not sure I want so swift a rise.

speaker: Sigurd
en: In truth, Ceolbert, it is my father who bears the heaviest of my anger. Not King Harald. My father gifted my birthright to Harald without my consent or knowledge, as easily as if he might hand over a barrel of mead. It was not merely a deception, it was a betrayal of trust. The prick of which still stings me.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Be it a blessing or a curse, family is always first.

speaker: Sigurd
en: A good line, boy. Were you not an ', I would hire you as my skald.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Skald... it sounds something like ', our court poets. Is that what you mean?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Right again.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Fascinating. The harmony between our words and yours is quite something. As if we were distant cousins, separated by an ocean of time as well as space.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I like the thought of that, I do!

speaker: King Burgred
en: Look at these pagan rats! Ravenous, unseemly beasts, teeming over holy ground!

speaker: Leofrith
en: Have a care, lord. These pagan rats outnumber us.

speaker: King Burgred
en: I can see that, fool! What do we do about them!

speaker: Leofrith
en: I advise we strongly consider their demands, lord. We won't survive a fight.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Is that you, Leofrith? How quickly you recover. I'm beginning to wonder if it is a man or a god beneath all that armor.

speaker: Leofrith
en: A man of God stand before you, Ivarr. Proud and resolute.

speaker: Ubba
en: That's Bugred's war-thegn. Killed a dozen of our men in an ambush along the river Trent. It was Ivarr's axe that stopped him.

speaker: Ivarr
en: That is a poor description of a perfect thirty-yard toss.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Enough jawing, heathens! Speak your piece.

speaker: Ubba
en: We've come for your crown, lord.

speaker: Ivarr
en: With or without your head attached.

speaker: King Burgred
en: I admire your ambition, pagan. But what you ask is impossible. No Dane ever has or ever will occupy Mercia's sacred throne.

speaker: Eivor
en: Would you settle for a Norse? We're not as gentle, but we're much better poets.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Norse. Dane. Dog. You're all the same to me, all godless.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not to worry. We have a Mercian of our own.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Ceolwulf, you mean? Whan I've done with you lot, I'll execute that foolish thegn for treason!

speaker: Eivor
en: The Ragnarssons are the least of your worries, Burgred. The Raven Clan now sits upon your southern border.

speaker: King Burgred
en: And who might you be?

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor of the Raven Clan, here with Sigurd Jarl. We are friends to these men, and foes to you.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Well, you've chosen your friends poorly, though that's to be expected of a lowborn Dane.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Oh, I've heard tales of the Raven Clan. I see their leader, Sigurd, among you.

speaker: King Burgred
en: And you are Eivor, the one who helped the Danes in Grantebridgescire. Destroyed poor Wigmund.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Then you see why you should choose your next words very carefully. For here stand four of us who wield such power.

speaker: Leofrith
en: My king, may I suggest a more measured approach to this

speaker: King Burgred
en: I grow weary of this palaver. You have trampled our lands, toppled our monuments. We've given you silver. Fed your people. And yet in spite of this, your encroachment on my kingdom continues. No more! We will die defending what is our, whatsoever the cost.

speaker: King Burgred
en: If you want my crown, Ubba Ragnarsson, you must pry it from the hands of my bloodless corpse! Man the walls!

speaker: Ubba
en: Back to the camp. Round up the men. We're taking Tamworth tonight!

speaker: Ubba
en: Eivor, tell the captain we're ready to march. Ivarr and I will round up the men. Do you know your way around a battering ram?

speaker: Eivor
en: I've seen them in action.

speaker: Ubba
en: I want you at the helm of ours. You're strong and agile.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll be there.

speaker: Sigurd
en: As will I.

speaker: Ubba
en: I'm eager to see you fight, Eivor. Show us old wolves a thing or two.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor... first one to Burgred gets to string him up by his dangly man-wattle. Then jab him in his fat head.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's get through these walls first, Ivarr.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Let's make short work of this, Eivor. England is a big place.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Lord, light my way...

speaker: Letter from Ubba Ragnarsson
en: Vegh, Following this letter will be three fleshly slaughtered hogs, twelve baskets of fruit, and twenty kegs of ale. Have a feast. Light fires. Bellow loudly at the stars. Announce yourselves to the Rat King of Mercia. He will not sleep this night. None in Tamworth shall.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Who are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm with the Ragnarssons. It's time to roll out the battering ram.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Burgred wanted a fight. Now we'll give him one. Are you ready to march now?

speaker: Eivor
en: It's time to capture a kingdom.

speaker: Sigurd
en: What are we going to do about him?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert... something wrong?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I know these men, Eivor. I've supped with them. Not two weeks ago, Leofrith showed me how to wield a greatsword. He's a friend.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Friendships end. Often at the end of a spear.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: It cannot be that cold. Least of all with Leofrith. He is only following orders.

speaker: Eivor
en: When the march begins, find an empty tent and stay there.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Do not think me a coward. I'm not afraid of war. I do not want to kill my friends.

speaker: Eivor
en: There's no other way. Fight or hide. It's up to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Destroy the gate!

speaker: Ubba
en: Slaughter the soldiers! Leave the king to me!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Forward! Push forward!

speaker: Eivor
en: Gate's down! Push through! Push through!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Burn the houses to cinders! Leave them no place to hide!

speaker: Sigurd
en: What a tale to weave into our sage. Look at us, side by side with the Ragnarssons. We're a long way from Fornburg, Eivor. This... this is our destiny.

speaker: Eivor
en: The path is blocked. We must destroy that barricade!

speaker: Eivor
en: Protect the ram!

speaker: Eivor
en: Cut down their marksmen and elites! Or they'll thin us out, one by one!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Saxon blood feeds this land, and it is we Norse who march all over it!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Burgred! I'll find you, you little rat! Do you hear me!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's over, Burgred! Lay down your weapons and surrender.

speaker: Ubba
en: Take three men and search the rear.

speaker: Ubba
en: Look around. See what you can find. I'll send for Ceolwulf... tell him we found a throne.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ah, that was a good scuffle, hm? But I did notice we were short one aetheling. Where was the son of our king?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert was around. It may be you missed him.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Your lies are just like you, Eivor. Big and bold.

speaker: Requisition Letter
en: Lord, I hope this letter finds you well. You have my gratitude and my promise that these men will not be called upon unless absolutely necessary. We continue to fend off the Danish incursion and will do so without respite. Æthelswith sends you her regards. She is well, though like my war-thegn, I wonder if she too has begun to doubt our ability to win this war. No matter. It is I who lead it, and I will defend my state to the bitter end.

speaker: Eivor
en: Burgred called for help. Enlisted the aid of powerful men... but who are these warriors he speaks of?

speaker: Letter to Maetild
en: My dear sister, I'm sorry I haven't written sooner. By now you've realized I won't be coming home at all. The Danes have pushed further inland, and King Burgred has done nothing but provoke them. As much as my heart is aching to leave, I cannot abandon my duty for fear so many people will die. As long as I'm here, I can protect them, even if it means giving my life. I know you understand. How is Roderick? Still can't believe the apple farmer's boy is going to make me an uncle. Your belly must be big now. I remember you saying if it was a boy, you'd name him after me. I pray every night that it's a girl. Your loving brother, Leofrith

speaker: Eivor
en: Seems Leofrith is at odds with his king, but bound to duty. A loyal man.

speaker: Royal Ledger
en: To the almighty king, We have an agreement, that is, if by the time this message arrives, is is still your arse that warms the seat of Mercia's throne. Here's what I know: The Ragnarssons have been speaking with one of your own, Ceolwulf is his name. Together they are devising a plan to overthrow you and install him in your stead. A Norse named Sigurd had arrived and allied with the brothers. An attack is soon to follow. Ready your men. As for your secret haunts, they are safe for now. But keeping them that way will cost you. I await your reply, only this time, send a more fair-faced envoy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hmm... a chronicle of payments made. Like a ledger. There's a symbol here... a clan emblem maybe? The brothers should see this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr, I've found a letter. There's a symbol here...

speaker: Eivor
en: Your men have any luck?

speaker: Ubba
en: Nothing. You?

speaker: Eivor
en: This. Do you know that symbol?

speaker: Ubba
en: Tonna's sigil. It seems she has been dealing with Burgred as well, the wretch.

speaker: Sigurd
en: She was the mercenary barking at you in Repton, yes? She is playing both sides of this war.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: She could have told him anything. Sold him secrets. About me, about Repton, our plans.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Why bother with all this pageantry? Fashion a new crown and stick it on your melon. There you have it, you're the new king.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: That is not how it works. Not in Mercia.

speaker: Eivor
en: We have Tamworth. Burgred's on the run. You're the king in all but name.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: It won't matter. So long as Burgred is free, the people will call him king. He must abdicate his crown to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tonna is our only lead. We talk to her, find out what she knows.

speaker: Eivor
en: You were one of Burgred's thegns. You must have some sense of where he'd be.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Burgred had his secret haunts, but he never told me of them. Kept me quite in the dark... for good reason, I suppose..

speaker: Eivor
en: Tonna is our only lead. We talk to her, find out what she knows.

speaker: Eivor
en: We're wasting time. Tonna is our only lead. We talk to her, find out what she knows.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I would sooner launch my face into my axe than face her.

speaker: Ubba
en: That might improve her impression of you.

speaker: Ivarr
en: We have the same father, Eivor. But his mother was a sow.

speaker: Ubba
en: Meet us at Tonna's camp when you're finished here. And bring your patience.

speaker: Ivarr
en: And your axe!

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: Eivor... a word, if you would.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go, I'll catch up.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I will join the brothers, Eivor. Meet us at Tonna's.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: My son told me what happened earlier, with Ivarr pressuring him to fight. He said you intervened.

speaker: Eivor
en: You would be mourning your son if I hadn't. He's not a fighter.

speaker: Ceolwulf
en: No, but he should be. By trial or by training.

speaker: Eivor
en: He'll come around in time, but keep him from Ivarr if you can. He's the furthest thing from a mentor.

speaker: Erriff Champion
en: I'll put you in the ground, Viking!

speaker: Eivor
en: Lugh's spear. A true warrior's weapon.

speaker: Eivor
en: This looks like a piece of a map. Vagn will want to see this.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: You'll get nothing out of me. Nothing!

speaker: Soma
en: Insects like you would not be crawling out of the muck if Wigmund wasn't hurting. Talk!

speaker: Eivor
en: Something has happened...

speaker: Soma
en: Eivor. The plan worked. One of Wigmund's captains. Caught him sniffing around Duroliponte. Remember, you don't need to kill him. Have fun. I'll be planning our next move in the longhouse.

speaker: Birna
en: Little boy, little boy. Where is your daddy hiding?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Godless heathens. Grantebridge is the province of Lord Wigmund of Walden. The city is rightfully his.

speaker: Galinn
en: Poor soldier. Doesn't know what heathens do to men of God like him. Hasn't heard the stories it seems.

speaker: Lif
en: We can educate him. Look at those ham hands! Could make a nice pair of gloves!

speaker: Birna
en: And his heart! A heart that beats in a lad like this? Feed a family of six for a week!

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's cut his throat now and water the orchards with his blood.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: No! Sweet Lord no! No, no! He's on the Isle of Ely! Ealdorman Wigmund! In the monastery. I swear!

speaker: Birna
en: Hm. Thought that would take 'til the next morn. Let's tie him up and let him rot away.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Fucking Dane half-wits! The Lord will smite you from this land. All of you! May God have mercy on

speaker: Galinn
en: That home-thieving snake might have cast a curse on us. I couldn't risk it.

speaker: Birna
en: Christians don't curse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wigmund's on the Isle of Ely. I'll tell Soma what we've learned.

speaker: Soma
en: Eivor. What did Wigmund's little man have to tell us?

speaker: Eivor
en: Wigmund is at the monastery on the Isle of Ely.

speaker: Soma
en: Hiding among the church mice. I'll need to plan our attack. But I won't face him while the traitor he commands is still under my roof. So what have you learned?

speaker: Eivor
en: I need more time to think.

speaker: Soma
en: Of course. Feel free to search the shire for more clues. And speak to anyone you wish.

speaker: Eivor
en: You there. Did you see anything strange around Grantebridge before the attack?

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: I didn't. I was in the longhouse, drinking with Birna and her men all night. She can really put it away!

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you see anything strange on the night of the attack?

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Hm. Come to think of it, I noticed one of the longships wasn't where it usually is. It was beached further north, on the riverbank.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where was this?

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Northeast of here, along the shore. It's been a few days, though. May not be there now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hail. Did you see anything strange on the night before the attack?

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: I saw someone run from the outskirts of Grantebridge to the shore, just before the fighting started. Too dark to see who.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you see anything the night of the attack?

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: Only Lif! Fighting bravely. Did you know Lif carves a poem in each of his longships? He's a craftsman and a wordsmith!

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are these longships now?

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: Lost in the fog of the Fenlands, sadly. If I could reclaim them, I would. To return his works of art? He'd be so grateful!

speaker: Eivor
en: To be sure. Good luck to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did anything strange happen before the attack on Grantebridge?

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: I saw two Saxons riding past the city while I was on guard. One for the Meldeburne monastary, and one toward Utbech. I think they were messengers. Didn't think anything of it since they weren't coming here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma was smart to build this tunnel.

speaker: Eivor
en: A painted cross...

speaker: Eivor
en: This tunnel leads to the longhouse. The traitor marked it with a yellow cross. Then opened the way and led them in.

speaker: Eivor
en: The traitor must have exited here with a few more, heading away... towards the riverbank.

speaker: Eivor
en: A trail of yellow paint drops...

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone hauled this bucket of yellow paint all the way down to the riverbank. They quickly painted a longship beached here. Then they sailed off. With allies to help crew the vessel.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: It's a good longship, but powerfully ugly. Why's it splashed all yellow like that?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Danes and Saxons, sailing on the same damned boat. The world is going weird.

speaker: Eivor
en: This longship is splashed with yellow paint. A quick job. Why would it be painted a different color than the others?

speaker: Longship Inscription
en: Pathed by a , a destiny writ, Clear in his vision, rigid his grit.

speaker: Eivor
en: This carving references Galinn in verse

speaker: Eivor
en: This longship was ambushed by bandits. The survivors ran into the fog, pursued by half the party, while the other bandits looted it.

speaker: Galinn
en: Eivor. This is a surprise.

speaker: Eivor
en: I was wondering...

speaker: Eivor
en: The visions you've had about you and Soma, how do you interpret them?

speaker: Galinn
en: A piercing question. Hm. I believe it means that Soma will lead me to greatness, however difficult. That she is linked to my destiny.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why were you at death's door when Soma found you?

speaker: Galinn
en: I left my clan to pursue my vision. I don't remember much. The sacred plants addled my memory. But I was hungry for more visions. You may not understand. But Soma does. She knows the gods have a plan for me and that following it is worth any risk.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found a letter to the Saxons from Wigmund. It says not to attack any longship painted yellow.

speaker: Galinn
en: Strange. Only Lif would have the tools to alter the color of our longships. Something to ask him about.

speaker: Galinn
en: Was it yellow? I don't recall. You could ask Lif. He's our shipmaster.

speaker: Eivor
en: Did you see anything odd when the attack began?

speaker: Galinn
en: I did. I saw a wave of Saxons appear in the heart of Grantebridge as if by magic. Odd as wings on an eel. I fought ragged to the brink of death, from one night to the next. You saw the end of it. Wolves almost took me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Somebody let the Saxons into Grantebridge's secret tunnel, Galinn... I believe there's a chance that it was you.

speaker: Galinn
en: I fled a harrowing attack, cutting down Saxons and praying a Valkyrie would take my men when they fell. You pick at me like a scab. And I won't have it. Be happy I don't strike you down for adding a sour note to my battle song.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm trying to find who betrayed Soma to the Saxons. I could use your help.

speaker: Galinn
en: I wish I could help. The night of the attack, I was meditating on the shore, far from prying eyes. I was alone that night. And until Saxons appeared, I didn't see anything out of the ordinary. I hope that's enough.

speaker: Lif
en: Eivor, you look like the wind had fled your sails. What's going on?

speaker: Eivor
en: I was wondering...

speaker: Eivor
en: You told me you often disagree with Soma's orders.

speaker: Lif
en: I do. But I follow them. It's my duty to this clan, to my jarlskona. A man's honor comes from his acts, not his wishes.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you feel when Guthrum named Soma the steward of Grantebridge and not you?

speaker: Lif
en: If being honorable were easy, we'd have no evil men. It it something I... I wanted, sure. But I am a man of honor above all.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found this odd letter telling Saxon forces not to attack any longship painted yellow.

speaker: Lif
en: I've never painted any longship yellow beyond a few small touches. It's expensive. I know of no such letter.

speaker: Eivor
en: You said your yellow paint was stolen before the attack?

speaker: Lif
en: Aye. And yellow's not an easy pigment to mix, let alone acquire. I was furious it was stolen.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found your yellow paint barrel near the river.

speaker: Lif
en: Did you? It was stolen from my workshop not long ago.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found it on the riverbank. It was empty.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did the night of the attack play out, from your view?

speaker: Lif
en: I was working in the shipyards. Next thing I knew, the city was burning from the inside. Then Soma led our retreat.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone told the Saxons about the tunnel under Grantebridge, Lif. There's a possibility it's you.

speaker: Lif
en: You insult me, Eivor. The night Grantebridge fell, I was working. In the shipyards. I could already hear fighting by the time Soma gathered me to retreat. I was nowhere near where the Saxons came in. I hope that's enough for you, Eivor, because we're finished here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lif, someone showed the Saxons the longhouse tunnel. Where were you when the attack started. What were you doing?

speaker: Lif
en: When the fighting started, I was in my workshop, decorating a sail for our allies in Grimsby. Without my yellow paint. By the time Soma gathered me to retreat, the city was under attack from within. I was nowhere near that tunnel. Nowhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: These bags are Birna's. Packed for a long journey.

speaker: Birna
en: Well, you're not the regular Sunbeam I've come to know. Something weighing on you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I was wondering on a few things...

speaker: Eivor
en: It must ache to serve under someone you love so deeply, one who doesn't love you back.

speaker: Birna
en: Some days, the pain hits hard. I need to press my hand into my heart to keep it from digging through my chest.

speaker: Eivor
en: You were a smuggler. Some would say that's not a trustworthy past.

speaker: Birna
en: And water is wet, what a surprise. I'm an opportunist. I see a chance, I take it. It's helped Soma so far. She knows what I am, what I was. But she trusts me. Who would better know the difference between a joke and the truth?

speaker: Eivor
en: I found a letter telling the Saxons not to attack a longship painted yellow.

speaker: Birna
en: None of our longships are painted yellow. I don't think...

speaker: Eivor
en: I found your things packed for a long journey. Were you planning to travel?

speaker: Birna
en: If I had betrayed this city, I'd be gone now, wouldn't I? No, I stayed. I'm happier near Soma with a broken heart than far away with a heart still longing.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened the night of the attack?

speaker: Birna
en: The people were at peace. A beautiful night, fog and all. Then came the Saxons, all around, and Soma roaring like a great bear. When she called a retreat, we ran for the longboats, aiming to regroup in the swamps. It was an ambush, no more, no less.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birna, Grantebridge was not taken by fluke. Someone showed the Saxons the longhouse tunnel. And there's a possibility it was you.

speaker: Birna
en: I was drinking under the noses of dozens that night. I would never betray my people. We're done here. And it'd be good for your health to take a walk, away from me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Someone in the city led the Saxons through the longhouse tunnel. When the fighting started, where were you?

speaker: Birna
en: Drinking with my warriors in the longhouse. When the Saxons came, I fought. I couldn't have shown anyone the tunnel. Eyes were on me all day and night.

speaker: Soma
en: Did you find enough clues in Grantebridgescire? Are you ready to choose the traitor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Birna is in love with you. Unanswered love is a volcanic emotion.

speaker: Soma
en: Birna has always been unpredictable. But she's a warrior grown. She does not let her emotions guide her actions.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birna was drinking in the longhouse when the attack began. Others can attest to that.

speaker: Soma
en: Hardly the behavior of someone expecting an attack.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birna used to be a smuggler, hardly an honorable life.

speaker: Soma
en: There is honor among even the lowliest of men. Danes know that better than most.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birna was packed for a long journey the night of the attack.

speaker: Soma
en: You think she wanted to leave us?

speaker: Eivor
en: I think she was prepared to leave, that's certain.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lif wishes he had stepped up to lead... and to be where you are now.

speaker: Soma
en: Lif has a celebrated place in my clan. As a shipbuilder, he is without peer, and he knows I know this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lif told me he was working in the shipyard the night of the attack.

speaker: Soma
en: The shipyard is exposed and far from the tunnel entrance. Not the ideal man to lead Saxons into the city.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lif disagrees with how you run Grantebridge.

speaker: Soma
en: This city thrives under me, as a bustling port for his longships, for instance.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lif told me his yellow paint had been stolen.

speaker: Soma
en: Yellow is a troublesome color to make. He was upset when his stores were stolen.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found an empty barrel of yellow paint beside a longboat launch. Yellow paint was used to mark a boat the night of the attack.

speaker: Soma
en: An odd time for a fresh coat of paint. But that's his work, is it not?

speaker: Eivor
en: Galinn puts his visions above everything... to the point of fanaticism.

speaker: Soma
en: Visions are like clouds. Each person sees a different meaning in the shape, and Galinn sees an important meaning.

speaker: Eivor
en: Galinn had no alibi. No one can place his location on the night of the attack.

speaker: Soma
en: He's an odd one, that man. But he is a man, not a toddler. He doesn't need a constant watch.

speaker: Eivor
en: Galinn told me he was near death when you found him and saved his life.

speaker: Soma
en: Yes, people thought him cursed. He was adrift in deep water. But don't we all deserve a guide back to the shallows?

speaker: Eivor
en: I found Galinn's longboat painted hastily with yellow paint on the day of the attack.

speaker: Soma
en: Why would he mark his longboat differently from the rest of ours?

speaker: Eivor
en: A local said they saw someone running from the outskirts of the city to the river, just before the attack.

speaker: Soma
en: Did they recognize the person?

speaker: Eivor
en: No, they couldn't be seen in the fog. But whoever it was, they knew something bad was coming.

speaker: Eivor
en: I found a message meant for Saxon forces. It said not to attack any longship painted yellow.

speaker: Soma
en: There's no yellow on our longships beyond some small details... if there's a yellow longship in the Fens, I want to know.

speaker: Soma
en: You... you told me you found yellow paint on Galinn's longboat, didn't you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your secret tunnel had many footprints nearby, and its mouth was painted with a yellow mark. Whoever betrayed you, they did so by marking the tunnel entrance, then opening the way to let the Saxons in.

speaker: Eivor
en: I already know who I suspect.

speaker: Soma
en: Your instincts must be strong if you're so quick to judge. So who is the traitor?

speaker: Eivor
en: That's all the evidence I think we need.

speaker: Soma
en: You've been thorough... Who is the traitor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Galinn betrayed you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birna betrayed you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lif betrayed you.

speaker: Soma
en: Are you certain?

speaker: Soma
en: This will be the hardest thing I have ever done. Stay close by me Eivor. I will need you.

speaker: Eivor
en: How to you plan to deal with this?

speaker: Soma
en: As a leader must...

speaker: Soma
en: My family, my inner circle. Today we make sure what has happened to us will never happen again. We end Wigmund's life. But not all together. For you cannot survive the winter with a rat in your larder.

speaker: Soma
en: Galinn. You have betrayed me, Galinn.

speaker: Galinn
en: I haven't! Soma! You're the key to my life. You must lead me to my destiny. Carry me to the summit of victory!

speaker: Soma
en: Do not warp was is real with the stories you tell yourself. I have seen no signs of your destiny.

speaker: Soma
en: What I have seen is my people slaughtered, my city befouled, and your delusions fueling the destruction. How dare you think your destiny, your greatness, outweighed all of ours?

speaker: Soma
en: He believed too much in faith. And not enough in us. Take him away.

speaker: Soma
en: Birna. You betrayed me.

speaker: Birna
en: No. Wait. I could never. Never!

speaker: Birna
en: My heart grew so warm here, in spite of the cold.

speaker: Birna
en: You do not love me as I love you. But love is not possession.

speaker: Soma
en: You love me, you admire me.

speaker: Birna
en: Even under your blade... I would do anything to stay here with you, anything.

speaker: Soma
en: You would do anything to get an edge. Say anything to spend one more day alive. It's how you served me so well...

speaker: Soma
en: Lif. Galinn. Take her away.

speaker: Soma
en: Lif. You have betrayed me, Lif.

speaker: Lif
en: Soma! That's not true!

speaker: Soma
en: A grown man should have a better grasp of his jealousy. It must not drive him to madness and destruction.

speaker: Soma
en: But with you? Every one of our warriors, our slaughtered people, are dead because you couldn't be where I am now.

speaker: Lif
en: I have only ever served you, Soma! I would never betray my clan. My family! I'm a man of honor!

speaker: Soma
en: And ambition...

speaker: Soma
en: Wigmund took you from us long before I ever raised my blade. Clear the body.

speaker: Soma
en: I feel as if I have torn off my own arm.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wigmund deserves death, but killing him won't make your family whole again.

speaker: Soma
en: You think I don't know? This is for those who follow! To join me is to take an oath! To break it is to suffer!

speaker: Soma
en: We make camp on the outskirts of the Isle of Ely. Join us there.

speaker: Odin
en: She carries the weight of leadership on one shoulder and the bonds of her people on the other.

speaker: Eivor
en: Now that she's lost one, she walks lopsided. It will take years of toil to rebuild those bonds with her people.

speaker: Odin
en: Yet she is unburdened now. Lighter. She is a leader, not a friend, Eivor. Her mistake was thinking she could be both.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Ah! Warm draft coming from that grate. Feels nice.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Smell nice? Because I just got done pissing in it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Well, you're an arsehole, you know that?

speaker: Strange Sounds
en: It is likely my mind playing tricks on me, but I swear the grumbles from that grate sound like a person often times. Certainly no one can be living down there, can they?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Eggs! Eggs! Eggs! Eggs! You deaf?

speaker: Eivor
en: Say that again?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: You heard me! I need eggs. Viper eggs. Crusty little shits won't go away. This is my land, I was here first. So as I said, bring me viper eggs, and I'll make sure they leave and never come back.

speaker: Eivor
en: Provoking snakes is not how I planned to spend my day, but that could change.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: A reward, yes, I understand your meaning. Bring me the eggs and it will be done.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Yes! O! More. More viper eggs.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: O... that's much better. Getting closer... now. I can feel it. More eggs. More!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Ooah...! Yes!

speaker: Eivor
en: I knew I would regret this.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: That nearly turned my insides out. O, I wish I could see the stir I've caused above.

speaker: Eivor
en: My reward, before I choke to death.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: As we agreed. Well? Have you nothing to say after such a forceful breaking of wind?

speaker: Eivor
en: It blew me away.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: O, God! The smell. I can't!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: O, my throat! It's like someone has poured salt in it!

speaker: Eivor
en: I can see Modron ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: How far has the search for me stretched?

speaker: Modron
en: Far enough to say it's best you stick to the countryside and wear that disguise. But Tewdwr's body has not been found as yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: Modron, well met.

speaker: Modron
en: Guards! Someone save me! A murderous Dane is here to sever my head from my neck. You could have told me of your plight earlier. We are both friends of Brigid, and I know you would do nothing to jeopardize your friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: The night was full of drink and merriment. I do not remember much, but I had no quarrel with Tewdwr.

speaker: Modron
en: A sorry tale. Did you learn anything from Halewyn?

speaker: Eivor
en: He gave some herbs to a man from Cudd Lladron. Name of Gwilim, he was drinking with Tewdwr and myself.

speaker: Modron
en: Cudd Lladron is the Welsh name for the Thieves' Warren. It's atop a hill west of here. I can lead you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I owe you a great deal for all your aid. You did not have to trust me.

speaker: Modron
en: Tewdwr's fate is to my interest as well. This is a troubling development that I hope to get to the bottom of.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let us make haste then. I must find Gwilim and regain my honor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would like to look at these sacred stones before we depart.

speaker: Modron
en: The old gods whisper in these stones. I've had my fill of their secrets. Tell me when you are ready to leave.

speaker: Modron
en: Are you ready to depart?

speaker: Eivor
en: This forest, and all Glowecestrescire, feels untamed. I feel as if I have ridden my horse through a door to another world.

speaker: Modron
en: Aye, there is old magic here. Old magic that would be snuffed out by Tewdwr and his Church.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tewdwr did speak of reformation. Do you think that's why he was targeted?

speaker: Modron
en: There are many who would claw their way to the top. Tewdwr's disappearance could be the work of any.

speaker: Eivor
en: But you are a witch, open to wisdom from the gods. Have you seen anything?

speaker: Modron
en: I see much smoke. Are there any rival Danes passing through who could have done it?

speaker: Eivor
en: If it were rival Danes, we'd have heard their horns by now. We are not a humble sort.

speaker: Modron
en: Blunt tongues and sharp axes.

speaker: Modron
en: Cudd Lladron. The Thieves' Warren... this is where I leave you.

speaker: Eivor
en: You'll find somewhere safe?

speaker: Modron
en: There is a shrine nearby. If you've need of me, then meet me there. Gods, old and new, go with you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Learned this from one of the Daughters of Nimue. They're blessed in holy healing. It should help with the pain.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Thank you, Feran. You've been a great comfort.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's Tewdwr's voice. So he lives!

speaker: Eivor
en: That must be where Gwilim is hiding.

speaker: Gwilim
en: O, shit.

speaker: Eivor
en: O, shit is right.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Eivor! You're alive!

speaker: Gwilim
en: Have mercy! I were under orders! Ealdorman Cynon! He gave us coin to dispose of Tewdwr.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then he should demand it back. Shit sellswords you are. Cannot kill a single man!

speaker: Eivor
en: You made a poor choice in scapegoat, Gwilim.

speaker: Gwilim
en: And we thought that... if we kept the lad alive we could squeeze Cynon for more coin. To keep his secret.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why would Cynon pay to have Tewdwr killed? He is to be his successor.

speaker: Gwilim
en: We en't ones for details, the less we know, the better, yeah?

speaker: Eivor
en: You chose to extort the man, but you have no basis for the crime? You are imbeciles.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cynon's meeting his end in the wicker man at the end of the Samhain celebrations.

speaker: Eivor
en: You look like a man who lies to save his own skin.

speaker: Gwilim
en: I look like a man up to his neck in sheep shit. Please, I'm telling the truth!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell it to your god.

speaker: Gwilim
en: Look, we wasn't gonna kill the lad! We've come to like having him around! Tell her! Tell her we've taken care of ye!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Cynon did this? Why? I've done nothing−

speaker: Gwilim
en: O gods, is he dead? Wake up! Wake up! Tell the Dane I've hand-fed ye like a baby sparrow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Move, fool.

speaker: Gwilim
en: Ah!

speaker: Gwilim
en: Look, Eivor, we're mates right? Had drinks together? Remember the chickens?

speaker: Eivor
en: Speak again and I'll take your tongue.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Tewdwr'll need to see a healer, this lot've been smearing dung on his face. But I've been held for ransom by worse men.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you for your aid, then. And try not to get held for ransom a third time after you flee.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Thank you, stranger!

speaker: Tewdwr
en: When I awoke in this demon lair, I feared the worst.

speaker: Eivor
en: Save your strength, Tewdwr, it's a long ride.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Cynon, he ordered my death? I don't understand. He's been like a father to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will ask him myself.

speaker: Tewdwr
en: I was mulish when he spoke of the pagans being just as we. Living in kindness, under the law of many gods. One face, many faces. It matters not. We are all blessed to be alive in His glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: This scrape has changed you, Tewdwr?

speaker: Tewdwr
en: Changed me. Change the dressings...

speaker: Eivor
en: He's hot to the touch, and his mind fades in and out, but he lives.

speaker: Modron
en: Perhaps a sickness of the blood. Shame, shame. He was captured by the men there?

speaker: Eivor
en: They claim to have been hired by Cynon.

speaker: Modron
en: Cynon did this?

speaker: Eivor
en: I know not why, only that he gave them coin to dispose of Tewdwr. You can see how well they saw to that.

speaker: Modron
en: They were alike once. The boy and Cynon. God-fearing Christians arguing the nature of life with me. But he softened.

speaker: Modron
en: Men do great evil to cling onto power, and save their skin. Perhaps he means to put Tewdwr to flame in his place?

speaker: Eivor
en: Does not the rite demand the leader?

speaker: Modron
en: If he made the lad's body ealdorman, then it would still be right to sacrifice.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then he's not safe until I've dealt with Cynon. Can you tend to his wounds?

speaker: Modron
en: I am a very good healer, but if the gods want him to join them, I cannot stop their will. Eivor, what will you do with Cynon?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll gut him. Death and dishonor is the punishment he deserves. All legacy destroyed.

speaker: Modron
en: Cynon may be ill and aged, but his sword arm is strong. He'll kill you first if you let him. Do not let him.

speaker: Eivor
en: My blade is imbued with the blood of gods and armies. I fear not a single coward.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will reveal his sins. Let his people decide if he deserves an honorable death.

speaker: Modron
en: The man tarnished your name and you would let him live?

speaker: Eivor
en: Shame for shame. Not even his god will welcome him when I'm done.

speaker: Modron
en: You are resolute then. Then may you ride as .

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, Modron. And please, take care of Tewdwr. I must get to Cynon before the festival's end.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Friend or foe?

speaker: Eivor
en: Friends, peace. I was told you might know where the Britons bring in their supplies.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Are we your friends, Dane?

speaker: Eivor
en: I woud have it so.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: After years of blood and gore, looting and burning, forgive us if we don't trust a Dane.

speaker: Eivor
en: In Rhodri we share a common enemy. My only wish is to destroy his supply line and bring him to the table, begging for a truce. Once we have peace, you and your kin will no longer walk this land in wretchedness.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: What you say is good sense. Very well, Dane. Here's what I know.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I imagine you've known sword, fire, and death. That you have lost those close to you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: All of us have.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have known that pain. It brought me to England to start anew. But Rhodri and his Britons stand in my way, as they stand in yours.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: I understand you well. Perhaps I spoke in haste.

speaker: Eivor
en: As a Norse, I know I have little right to ask for your help. But I'm fighting to bring this war to an end.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: If you're truly fighting that devil Rhodri, I'll tell you what I know.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: The Britons move their goods through Dhustone Quarry. See that tower to the south? That's the Hill Gate Remnants. Further on you'll find the stone quarry.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Hold a moment. If you need extra help...

speaker: Eivor
en: I may...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Good Mercian men are working in that quarry. They all fought for thegn Merton. If you find yourself in a pitched fight, call out his name in praise. The workers will rally to you.

speaker: Eivor
en: "God bless Thegn Merton." Understood.

speaker: Farewell Letter
en: Arleigh, it's up to you to look after your brother and sister while I'm off fighting the Britons. You're the oldest and you've a good head on your shoulders. I wish your mum was still with us, but alas. Begging's your last chance. Watch that Osred and Inga don't get into too much mischief. Da.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dhustone Quarry, filled with Briton supply carts. Once I burn those, it will push Rhodri to peace.

speaker: Orlaf
en: Let me out. I want to fight these bastards.

speaker: Eivor
en: Deorlaf asked me to free the prisoners to strengthen our .

speaker: Report - Prisoner Labor
en: Ynyr, We've put the captured Saxons to work in the quarry. They are bitter because we killed their leider. I have never seen men work so slowly. I will increase punitive measures until they cheer up. -Cymen

speaker: Eadric
en: For the love of Saint Cuthbert, free me!

speaker: Eivor
en: These men will fight for us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sciropecire needs you.

speaker: Eivor
en: God bless Thegn Merton!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: For Thegn Merton, lads!

speaker: Eivor
en: Merton's men, fight with me!

speaker: Report - Prisoners Taken
en: Ynyr, We have captured some Saxons as you ordered. They do nothing but shit and complain. Request permission to cut their throats. -Cymen

speaker: Eivor
en: The quarry south of the tower? Thor must smile on me today. I have already destroyed the supplies there. Thank you for your time.

speaker: Eivor
en: There we are. The quarry and Wenlocan, both done. That should shake Rhodri to his senses. Now to Wesberie before Ivarr causes more problems.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's done. Off to Wenlocan Outpost and the Briton cargo.

speaker: Sigurd
en: There she is... England. Our new home.

speaker: Dag
en: Not a patch on Norway, but we'll make this land our own soon enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am glad to see any land at all. And will be happy to have my feet on solid ground again.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We must not rush our landing. All you see here is Saxon territory. The Kingdom of Mercia, largely unpacified. There will be eyes watching us from the trees, with bows drawn and traps set. We must be wary. Randvi! Dig in your oars! All standing!

speaker: Randvi
en: Have you spotted something?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not yet, but let us go ahead to clear the path of any dangers. Then follow our lead when the sun brushes the horizon.

speaker: Randvi
en: Understood! May Thor bless you all on your way! We will see you soon!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Sail on!

speaker: Dag
en: Yes! I am ready for whatever these green-thumbed fairy folk have to throw at us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, do the Sons of Ragnar know that we are coming?

speaker: Sigurd
en: They do not. But they will not scoff at our visit. Of the four kingdoms in England, the Sons of Ragnar have settled only one. The rest is ripe for the taking.

speaker: Dag
en: Do we mean to join their army?

speaker: Sigurd
en: No, no. We will speak with them, get the lay of the land. And carve this country into as many pieces as we see fit.

speaker: Dag
en: Look ahead there. Is that what passes for a town? Plain brick and a single rune to their timid god?

speaker: Sigurd
en: That rune is called a rood, Dag. The cross upon which their god was sacrificed. It sits atop a monastery, a place of worship.

speaker: Dag
en: That cross killed their Christ, and now they display it in worship! Bizarre.

speaker: Eivor
en: We carve idols of our gods and make wishes before them. Like our sacrifices to Odin the One-Eyed.

speaker: Dag
en: But we do not worship the wolf that kills him! That is the difference.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Whatever strangeness we see in these Saxons, they must think the same of us.

speaker: Dag
en: The hammer! Now there is a symbol worthy of a god. A bolt of lightning would take that cross clean off!

speaker: Dag
en: Look there! What are they doing?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ritual drowning.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Baptism, Dag. Are the ways of Christians really so unfamiliar to you?

speaker: Dag
en: Not at all! I simply forgot. And someone has to keep the conversation up. It must be priests and worshippers alone in that place. We could storm this port with ease, sack it without breaking a sweat.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is there much in the way of treasure there?

speaker: Dag
en: Always! They shape precious metals and cut jewels to their gods. There will be a fortune there!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Later, Dag. There will be time enough for raiding once we have settled.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Come to! Stop the boats! Pull up over there. The way forward is blocked by a chain spanning the river. We must remove it before pressing on.

speaker: Dag
en: A chain? Can we cut through it?

speaker: Sigurd
en: It's too thick for axes. But there must be a way to release it somewhere in that camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will go.

speaker: Dag
en: And I will be right behind you!

speaker: Sigurd
en: No, Dag. You stay here. Should trouble come our way, I want you defending the ship.

speaker: Dag
en: A good idea. Send out the arrow and keep your sharpest axe at hand, eh?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Something like that.

speaker: River Chain Blockade
en: After conducting several trials we have found that these naval chains will hold against even the most durable Danish longships, so long as the mechanism remains intact. Several more blockades will be constructed in the coming months and are to be installed on the rivers leading inland. This is our best defense against any forthcoming incursions. It is imperative that the blockades be maintained and kept operational at all times. Any failure of function is to be reported immediately.

speaker: Eivor
en: This chain is huge. And poorly anchored, it appears. I might be able to shoot it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Done. The path is clear.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The chain is away! Eivor, back to the boat! We should be close now. Barring any more surprises.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Fine work, Eivor

speaker: Dag
en: I say we go back, Sigurd. Give those dogs a good knock-around and take whatever treasures they have. Easy pickings.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not today, Dag. We press on until we reach our goal. We cannot afford another surprise. Now be on your guard. It should not be far.

speaker: Dag
en: Gods, I'm ravenous! I hope they have food and ale on hand when we arrive. You should have sent word ahead of us, Sigurd. To get something on the spit.

speaker: Sigurd
en: If Halfdan, Ubba, and Ivarr Ragnarsson are lacking food in England, then all of us will starve. Have no worry.

speaker: Dag
en: Ah, I can see it now! A suckling pig, tender and juicy. And ale as gold as the treasures that we failed to steal back there.

speaker: Eivor
en: A man of simple pleasures, aren't you, Dag?

speaker: Sigurd
en: And he is happier for it. For my part, I look forward to standing in the footsteps of the giants that built this land.

speaker: Dag
en: What giants?

speaker: Sigurd
en: The great Romans and their empire, giants of a forgotten age. They held dominion here, long ago, and their ruins dot the landscape. Every brick and stone tells a story of conquest and glory, and now they are rubble and ash.

speaker: Dag
en: Ready to be remade! We will rebuild their empire, brick by brick! And ours will not crumble to dust.

speaker: Sigurd
en: All things end, Dag. Ruins are not a warning, they are a testament.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Look there, just ahead. Where the Sons of Ragnar make their camp.

speaker: Dag
en: At last. To find our feet on steady ground.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, hold back. Something isn't right.

speaker: Dag
en: Good eye. There is too little movement for an army. Only tents and a few men.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not the army we hoped to find?

speaker: Sigurd
en: No... let us get a closer look.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those are not Norsemen. They are too ragged and soiled.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We should proceed on foot, lest they spot the boats.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag and I will go together.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We all go. If they are friends, I wish to meet them as a jarl. And if they are foes, then we fight them all, together.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Who are these men?

speaker: Eivor
en: They speak with twisted accents. English, no doubt.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Dag, Eivor... on me.

speaker: Eivor
en: The River Champion is defeated. The Legacy of Saint George is won!

speaker: Vagn
en: This is why we found each other, Eivor! That I would lead a true warrior to a deserved prize!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you believe this did once belong to this sainted man, George?

speaker: Vagn
en: Who can know? But it is pleasurable to think so. I say we should believe it! And you know, there's probably more where that came from. Keep raiding, I say. Never know when you will stumble upon another legend.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Eivor, I'm pleased you came.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Welcome to the estate, old friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thegn Aelfgar. It's an impressive amount of land you oversee.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Quite right! I often get lost swimming to my island in this flowing sea of wheat.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are flush with land and crops, to be sure. You're a brave man to flaunt your riches from this lonely hill.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: It's not bravery, it's trust. I trust that the respect I've earned keeps Saxon and Dane alike from temptation.

speaker: Eivor
en: You said you had something to show me when we last spoke. What did you mean?

speaker: Eivor
en: It's more a lake of wheat, I think.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: I beg your pardon?

speaker: Eivor
en: If we're to be friendly, Aelfgar, you should laugh at my jokes.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Ah, yes. You Danes and your sense of the absurd. It's marvelous, quite marvelous.

speaker: Eivor
en: You said you had something to show me when we last spoke. What did you mean?

speaker: Eivor
en: You said you had something to show me when we last spoke. What did you mean?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Ah, yes, I did. Observe...!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: This fine specimen belonged to our ealdorman, Hundbeorht, before his untimely passing. He left it here when we last hunted together. I now wish you to have it.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a beautiful weapon. Finely crafted. Thank you.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: I thought you might like it!

speaker: Eivor
en: This has the feeling of a bribe, Aelfgar. Are you trying to win my favor for some reason?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Bribe you? Heavens no! This is a simple gift of thanks. For solving the mystery of Hundbeorht's disappearance.

speaker: Eivor
en: If this belonged to the ealdorman, shouldn't it go to Hunwald next?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: I suppose so. But I thought you a more fitting recipent. You'd know how to use it.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Now, now, take it and come hither. I have a rousing hunt planned for the two of us.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Leave aside talk of politics and shiremoots. Let us enjoy the fruits of my land together.

speaker: Eivor
en: We're hunting or fruit-picking?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Both, if you like! Whatever you fancy! I'm generous with the yields of my estate, as you will see.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: To be plain, Eivor, a great bear has been badgering my estate for weeks. I must do away with it if only to prevent a future tragedy.

speaker: Eivor
en: You brought me here to hunt a bear?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Yes, and I'm so pleased you agreed to come! I suspect you know better than most that I have what it takes to lead this shire. Though its line of kings is all but ended, the people of this land still teems with life, with promise. But today, this shire languishes. It needs the guidance of new blood.

speaker: Eivor
en: Like me.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: I'm sorry.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm the definition of new blood. It may be I should put my name in for ealdorman.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Ah! There it is, that dark sense of humor. Blunt as a hammer, eh? Like the one carried by your ... your thunder god, the, ah ... I don't recall the name.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go on.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: What I mean to say is, I enjoy the company of your people. Or people like you. What little I've seen of them. And I don't care what stuffy fools like Herefrith or Hunwald say. You Danes are damned decent people! Not dense at all.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kind of you to notice.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: I remembered when the Danes first arrived, not long ago. The locals were terrified. Not of being raided, but of their spouses being seduced away! With all your perfumes and braiding and grooming and... bathing, even! How novel!

speaker: Eivor
en: I hear you Saxons bathe once a year, whether you need it or not.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: It's true! We are learning as we go. Between washing and braiding grooming, where do you people find the time to raid and ravage!

speaker: Eivor
en: We sleep less than Saxons.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Sleep less! My goodness.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are we hunting, Aelfgar? Or is it your hope that I'll braid your hair?

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Hunting, definitely. The bear's lair should be nearby.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Ah, my old friend, Grim! How wonderful to see you here! What a pleasant surprise.

speaker: Grim
en: What surprise? I came as you requested.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Yes, and how is Grimsby? How are all the other Danes?

speaker: Grim
en: I can't speak for all Danes ... but I am well. And itching for a hunt, as you made plain in your message this morning.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Yes, that's right, very good! Speaking of Danes, I'd like to introduce you to Eivor. Perhaps you know each other, as one Dane to another.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well met, Grim. Glad to have you along.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm Norse, actually. Something you might learn by asking. Well met, Grim. Glad to have you along.

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't be frightened, Grim. But I believe Aelfgar has arranged for us to meet.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: O, goodness, I've been discovered. But it's nothing untoward, I promise. I'm an honest man, and I believe that all people should live together in harmony. That's all.

speaker: Grim
en: Hail Eivor. Did he lure you here as well, with the promise of a hunt?

speaker: Eivor
en: He
