speaker: Aelfgar
en: Yes, hunting a bear! That's the point of all this, we're hunting. I promise.

speaker: Grim
en: There's a cave up the hill there. Seems a likely place for a lair.

speaker: Eivor
en: If the beast is as large as Aelfgar claims, it'll take all three of us to bring it down.

speaker: Grim
en: I'm game. Let's get a new fur cloak, shall we?

speaker: Grim
en: There is all manner of beasts in this forest. If we don't find the bear, we'll find something worth our supper.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: I have a divine rule over the land on my estate. God shall provide, have no worry.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is the threshold of a beast's home, there's no doubting that.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's not a bear... Wolves!

speaker: Grim
en: Ach, wolves! Ravenous troll-steeds.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Wolves everywhere, and not a bear in sight.

speaker: Grim
en: Aelfgar? Eivor? There's something you'll want to see here.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Is that ... that's smoke! My God! My estate is burning like a twig!

speaker: Eivor
en: Soon to be a sea of fire.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Eivor, you're skilled enough, and I can't tell you how to handle this, but ... please, by God, help me with this!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm in this fight with you! A clutch of puny Mercians don't frighten me.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: My people are fleeing. They must get to safety.

speaker: Grim
en: Someone waited until you were away to set your world aflame.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll send them straight to Hell, the marauding menaces!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: The crops, the fields! They're burning the food!

speaker: Grim
en: Food's no good if there's nowhere to eat it! The houses burn, Eivor!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Where is Aelfgar? Bloody Dane-lover? Search every last house, then burn them when you're through!

speaker: Grim
en: Die!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Take the thegn! Kill the rest.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Burn this Dane-lover down!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 4
en: Burn it all! Down to ashes!

speaker: Grim
en: Mercian dogs!

speaker: Eivor
en: The men who'd see you burn are dead. Let's get these fires out.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Agreed!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: What a mess. A sea of ashes. I thank you, Eivor, for doing what you could.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a man of many riches, Aelfgar. You can rebuild.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: To be sure. But I do not look forward to the toil of...

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Sweet Lord in Heaven. The bear has returned!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Away, beast! Away! You won't trouble me any longer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfgar, careful!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: There, you see? Didn't I promise you a rousing hunt! Brilliant, simply brilliant!

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor. A word of note... Someone has set up shop outside. A trader, I believe. When you can, ask him his business here. He seems to represent a larger guild. The Child's Eyes. Or the Eyeless Children?

speaker: Eivor
en: Eyeless children?

speaker: Randvi
en: No, that cannot be right. Ask him yourself.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Good day! A new customer!

speaker: Eivor
en: Whether I am or not, I am the one you will speak with. Randvi tells me you are... merchants?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Ah! Hello, hello. Are you the leader of this bustling encampment?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: We come on behalf of the Thousand Eyes. Vendors of uncommon goods and exotic treasures from all corners of the world.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: If you need it, we have it. If we don't have it, you don't need it. Such is our pledge.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see. And is this child with you?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Child?

speaker: Unknown Voice
en: Child?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: My friend, you look upon the Master of the Thousand Eyes! The head of our guild. A legend, a hero of the people, and the richest merchant west of the ! You look upon... Reda!

speaker: Eivor
en: He means... you?

speaker: Reda
en: He does, Eivor Wolf-Kissed. It is a pleasure to meet you at last.

speaker: Eivor
en: How have you come to know me?

speaker: Reda
en: The Thousand Eyes have one thousand ears as well. And word travels fast.

speaker: Eivor
en: You seem... strangely familiar.

speaker: Reda
en: Perhaps we have met in another life. But, most likely, I have a common face.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what is it I can do for you, or you for me?

speaker: Reda
en: It's quite simple. For a fee, I can connect you to a shadow market that stretches from the dunes of Egypt to the moors of England.

speaker: Eivor
en: What sort of fee?

speaker: Reda
en: It varies with the item. But there is a small hitch.

speaker: Reda
en: Through this market, all prices are paid... in opal.

speaker: Eivor
en: A striking color. It it rare?

speaker: Reda
en: Rarer than an honest man in England! You must keep your eyes open for this mineral! It has great value. Now look here! Browse what wares I have on offer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Interesting... what a strange color it has. May I hold it?

speaker: Reda
en: You may hold it and keep it, Eivor. A gift from Reda for your immeasurable hospitality. Now look here! Browse what wares I have on offer.

speaker: Reda
en: Nothing for now, no matter! My selection changes daily. You will soon find something you like.

speaker: Reda
en: An excellent choice. And a lucky one too. For nothing in stock lingers very long. My selection changes daily.

speaker: Reda
en: Now that you are friends with me, you are also a friend of the Thousand Eyes as well!

speaker: Eivor
en: And what does this mean?

speaker: Reda
en: Observe my outfit, note the scarf I wear. As you travel, you will meet many of my associates, clad in these same vestments. These are my people, my other Eyes. Seek them out for trade or contracts. Oblige them and you will earn a tidy sum. And I might even feel inclined to reward you myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: An interesting offer.

speaker: Reda
en: Good to hear. Now if you will excuse us, my apprentice has a tent to secure.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are staying here for a while, I suppose?

speaker: Reda
en: O yes, and you needn't even thank me! We would be honored to call this our home. Good day!

speaker: Havi
en: Allow me to recount one of my glorious battles with my cunning brother Loki. Ahead of me I saw what I knew to be my prey... and I struck! Thus my tale concludes, in glory and honor!

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Iva! Iva, wake up, you fool!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: He can't hear you. Passed out cold.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: She's right. You can tell by the pool of piss around his ankles, see? He won't come to for a while.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: It's alright. We'll wait. That way he can watch while we skin you.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Never mind, Iva! Stay asleep! Sleep!

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: O! It's you!

speaker: Eivor
en: You two again? Bent over the barrel of another adventure, I see.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: This is his fault! I told him they looked like bandits, but he insisted on cheating them out of coin. We need to leave. Some of them went to fetch firewood. They will be back any moment.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is no "we" in this. Your brother, your problem.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: What! No, please. Look at him! He is deadweight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Deader weight soon. You should hurry.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: If I have to carry him, we will never make it out of here alive. Please!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your brother is lucky I like you. There may not be much between your ears, but you are not the problem here.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Thank you? Erm, this way!

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Think again, Saxon filth! There is no besting these Sons of Ragnar. Soon the world will know us by name!

speaker: Eivor
en: A sleep-talker. Just what I needed.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: See this? Do. You. See it? This blade was forged by Grundel... Grundel Thundersmith! Greatest of all blacksmiths. One nick and your life essence will shoot out of you like a geyser from the depths of Norway. You laugh. Am I a joke to you? Do I look like a jester? That is what I thought! You will think again before laughing behind my back! No one laughs at me! No one!

speaker: Eivor
en: Cast him aside when this is done. For your sake.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: This is far enough. You can put him down.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: There they are! After them!

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Look there!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay close to me!

speaker: Eivor
en: This is where we part ways.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Yes! My... my thanks. Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop thanking me and listen closely. This life does not suit you. There are people out there who would kill you over these petty squabbles.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: This I have realized...

speaker: Eivor
en: If your idiot brother hatches another one of his glory seeking plans, take your fist and slam it right between his eyes. Or better yet, punch him in his cock. He will listen.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: Punch his cock. Yes. That should get the point across. Thank you... Err, you will never see us again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: What-what... what-what-what did... Ah! We made away with the coin, didn't we? Poor fools never suspected us, but we are more clever than we look, eh!

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Where are you going, Brother? You must tell the details of this great victory.

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: I am going home!

speaker: Eivor
en: Vagn. Well met. The Champion put up a good fight but their lance is now rightfully mine.

speaker: Vagn
en: Well done, drengr! Where were you when I was a young Jomsviking?

speaker: Eivor
en: When you were a young Jomsviking, Rome still controlled these lands!

speaker: Vagn
en: You continue to delight me, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: The champion had a scrap of a map on them but I've never seen this terrain. It looks to flow from the North Sea.

speaker: Vagn
en: North Sea, hmm?

speaker: Vagn
en: I have it! This is Francia. Here, let me mark the river on your map. The Romans called it Renos but the locals call it the Rhine.

speaker: Frankish Champion
en: You've made a poor decision coming here, pagan dog!

speaker: Eivor
en: The Rhine may be long and treacherous but she couldn't hide her riches from me! I took this sword off their Champion.

speaker: Vagn
en: You continue to impress.

speaker: Havi
en: The Old City lies within the heart of Uldar, as does my prize.

speaker: Dwarven Captive 1
en: You! Leave! You have no business here!

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: They will sing our song, brother. We shall bring Surtr the one-eyed head of Havi, and become lords of Muspelheim!

speaker: Muspel Warrior 2
en: Shout of your success when the deed is done. Until Havi is dead, shut your gob. I'll wager that old goat still has some tricks to play on us.

speaker: Havi
en: Einar said Fritjof and Tyra would await me, somewhere beyond these gates.

speaker: Fritjof
en: How was I meant to know he wasn't really a traitor? We're all experts in bloody hindsight, aren't we?

speaker: Fritjof
en: I acted on what I had heard at the time. And he was working with the Muspels. Technically speaking. So, in a way, I was right.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Oh, will you give it a rest. We got there before Havi killed him. No harm done.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Fine. You got us there before Havi killed him.

speaker: Fritjof
en: So learn to speak the common bloody tongue. You understand it well enough.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Look, would you just... just stop. I'm getting a headache from all of this. It's hard enough with my eyes still getting back to normal.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Finally. You made it.

speaker: Havi
en: Careful. It sounded like you doubted me for a moment. What of your eyes? Are they mended?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Getting there. Recovering, thank the gods.

speaker: Havi
en: You're welcome. Now then, show me what to do with this augmented Sunstone.

speaker: Tyra
en: Einar?

speaker: Havi
en: Alive, last I saw. But old, and slow. We must begin without him.

speaker: Havi
en: Do you know what must be done?

speaker: Fritjof
en: My father is the expert in these ancient relics, but... how hard can it be? Now, place the Sunstone here.

speaker: Havi
en: Surely it cannot be so simple...

speaker: Fritjof
en: No, this mechanism... what was it... I think, yes, we need more light to converge here, on this spot.

speaker: Havi
en: Leave it to me. Stay out of sight.

speaker: Havi
en: See what the light reveals. Yet the Sunstone still hungers. More light is needed.

speaker: Havi
en: It is working! Einar was right, haha! The Sunstone must be satisfied. Now, the relic will be mine.

speaker: Fritjof
en: The Vault of the Ancients.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Couldn't have said it better myself.

speaker: Havi
en: What is wrong? Why isn't it opening? Is there something wrong with the mechanism?

speaker: Fritjof
en: Yeah, about that. I'd feel a lot more confident if my father was

speaker: Einar
en: Help!

speaker: Havi
en: Get to work. I'll stretch my fighting arm.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 3
en: Stop them! Kill the dwarves!

speaker: Fritjof
en: Where have you been? Any idea what we're doing?

speaker: Einar
en: I have the scripture right... right... here...

speaker: Fritjof
en: You bloody lost it!?

speaker: Einar
en: You may have noticed I was being bloody chased!

speaker: Einar
en: Yes. Right. Um. I did read it. I think I can remember it. You two, follow my lead. Son. If this all goes belly-up...

speaker: Fritjof
en: Shut up and focus. Now is not the time.

speaker: Einar
en: If this is to be our last stand...

speaker: Fritjof
en: Dad!

speaker: Einar
en: I'm proud of you. Both of you. That's all.

speaker: Fritjof
en: It... it's working! It's bloody working!

speaker: Einar
en: Finish the job before celebrating, you two.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Right, right.

speaker: Havi
en: It is done.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Took you long enough.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: By Ymir's armpit, what are you doing here, you one-eyed shitbag?

speaker: Havi
en: Seeking a relic. It's somehow grown more wrinkly and ill-tempered since I last saw it.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Fuck off. Ooh...

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Looking for this, I'd wager?

speaker: Einar
en: The mighty relic!

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Piece of junk. I took out all the good stuff already.

speaker: Einar
en: Wha... wuh!

speaker: Havi
en: Then we shall take our leave.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Quickest way out is through the front.

speaker: Havi
en: You look like you've been to Helheim and back.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Glod may be a mongrel bastard, but he knows how to torture a dwarf, that's for sure.

speaker: Sinmara
en: What do we have here... The 'High One,' stealing again? How unbecoming. And with his little friends... My stepson takes his mongrel eyes off you for one second, and look at this mess... To think his father expects him to rule Muspelheim one day.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Oh no, no-no-no. She's one of the bad ones. She's the

speaker: Havi
en: She's nothing. But she has Frigg's blood on her hands, and must pay. Find another way out.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Uh... the way we got in. Quick!

speaker: Havi
en: Get to the shelter. I'll see to her.

speaker: Sinmara
en: Promises, promises.

speaker: Sinmara
en: If you're going to fight, fight! You cluck and clash like an old hen! Fight as if you really want your son back!

speaker: Havi
en: What do you want with Baldr?!

speaker: Sinmara
en: Your anger makes you clumsy. Did you care for Baldr's mother?

speaker: Havi
en: Had it been an honest fight, Frigg would have bested you!

speaker: Sinmara
en: You're improving, Mad One. Almost worth my effort.

speaker: Havi
en: Give me my son and I shall torture you only a little!

speaker: Sinmara
en: All I shall give you is death!

speaker: Havi
en: That's right, you mewling quim! Run back to Surtr!

speaker: Havi
en: The Shelter. I must speak with Ivaldi.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Did you end her?

speaker: Havi
en: She escaped.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Come. I've been cooped up long enough.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Of all the faces I left behind in Asgard, yours is the last I expected to see.

speaker: Havi
en: You sound disappointed.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: I'd have preferred you sent a buxom Valkyrie wearing nothing more than a mischievous smile!

speaker: Havi
en: And carrying a barrel of the good stuff.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Now you're talking! But... when I saw you in the palace, through Glod's portal, well, I knew you'd come for me. Thank you.

speaker: Havi
en: Anything for a friend.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: My gentle jailer rescuing me from a far worse jail. It's almost poetic.

speaker: Havi
en: You dwarves never did understand poetry.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: The sky is high, wood is good, and Havi is still an arsehole. How is that for poetry, you miserable shit?

speaker: Havi
en: About as good as you smell. Now, I have a use for you.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: "Havi has a use for me." Words to chill the blood. Still, you know we dwarves give nothing away for free.

speaker: Havi
en: Do you breathe fresh air? Or the stench of Glod's torturers?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Keep your eye in its socket. What will you have me do?

speaker: Havi
en: Wait.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: What?

speaker: Glod
en: Vermin! Thief! Face me!

speaker: Havi
en: Be warned... I will finish what you start!

speaker: Havi
en: Is that the best you can do?

speaker: Glod
en: I shall have your head, and present it to Lord Surtr!

speaker: Havi
en: You should have stayed away, beast!

speaker: Glod
en: The age of Muspels begins with your death.

speaker: Havi
en: What did you do to my son?!

speaker: Glod
en: None shall survive Surtr's wrath!

speaker: Havi
en: Surtr stole my son. Now I have killed his. A small step towards justice.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Wished you had let me get a few kicks in. Bastard almost ate me once.

speaker: Gunborg
en: Then it is over? The Muspels will be in disarray.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Not while Surtr is in power.

speaker: Havi
en: Tell more of the relics, and what you did with them. What happened in the vault?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: What do you think? Glod tortured me. Commanded me to revive the relics, then extract their magic so that Surtr might use it in some way.

speaker: Havi
en: And you could not?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: How fucking dare you. 'Course I could. But not for a shit like him. Of course, Glod was too dim to see that I was dispelling the magic rather than storing it. And as soon as I knew you were coming, I gutted the relics, rendered them useless. So no mighty weapon for that prick, Surtr!

speaker: Havi
en: It is unwise to underestimate such an enemy.

speaker: Havi
en: But... you were short-sighted, Ivaldi. I could have made good use of that magic.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Well, if it's items of power you seek... during my imprisonment, I heard rumors. Surtr is building something. Something small yet very, very potent. And highly valuable to him. So valuable that if it were to fall into your hands... you might do some real damage here, I think.

speaker: Havi
en: Music to my ears. That is... intriguing.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: I will seek wisdom on the subject, more ancient and advanced than even my own. But first, I must equip myself with some decent tools. Starting with a hammer, and maybe a chisel or two... There is a dam in the north of Vangrinn. Huge bloody thing. Almost completely frozen over.

speaker: Havi
en: I... I know of it.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: South of the dam, there is a workshop. Perhaps it remains in good order. When your travels are complete, you will find me there.

speaker: Havi
en: I will come when I'm ready.

speaker: Havi
en: You made it back, then. And without anyone needing to be carried.

speaker: Tyra
en: ... (Reckon it's my turn to get carried somewhere, eh?)

speaker: Havi
en: What did she say?

speaker: Fritjof
en: She said you're welcome to carry her off.

speaker: Havi
en: Another time, perhaps.

speaker: Einar
en: Thank you, Havi, for wounding the Muspels here. And for liberating the three of us.

speaker: Havi
en: You know it was not my aim.

speaker: Einar
en: That does not change our gratitude.

speaker: Havi
en: Be well, you three.

speaker: Havi
en: You did well, Einar. A true scholar. You have surely earned your people's trust once more,

speaker: Einar
en: Honestly, it matters not. So long as Fritjof is out of their clutches. You must understand better than anyone.

speaker: Havi
en: That I do.

speaker: Havi
en: Mighty Tyra. Yours shall be a saga for the ages. Even if no one understands a word.

speaker: Tyra
en: ... Havi.

speaker: Havi
en: My thoughts exactly.

speaker: Havi
en: Fritjof. Breaker of vaults. Seeker of relics. The blind one who now sees.

speaker: Fritjof
en: And you're only half an arsehole. Not bad for a one-eyed Æsir.

speaker: Havi
en: Be well. Know you're welcome in Asgard. We have mead that will drive you blind all over again.

speaker: Fritjof
en: Yeah, maybe I'll give that a miss.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Njal will taste Mercian blood!

speaker: Eivor
en: Show me what you can do, berserker!

speaker: Bjorn
en: For Alfhild! Rawr! Yee-ahhh!

speaker: Bjorn
en: Show yourself, cowards!

speaker: Eivor
en: To me, Njal! Bjorn!

speaker: Bjorn
en: You killed her! My Alfhild! Why?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: I've always wanted to fight a berserker. And a white bear rug will make a fine trophy.

speaker: Bjorn
en: It's done. Let's leave this blasted place.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bjorn! Your enemy has fallen. You have your revenge.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Yes. But now I fear I must ask you one last thing, should you be willing.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is it?

speaker: Bjorn
en: Njal is tired. I will tend to her beneath the tree where this all began. Please, bring her some of her favorite flowers. They look like...

speaker: Eivor
en: I know the ones. I'll gather them and meet you beneath the gallows tree.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Stay strong, my child. Bjorn is here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw some of Njal's favorite flowers growing behind the gallows tree.

speaker: Eivor
en: His wife's grave. No wonder he visits this tree often.

speaker: Eivor
en: Flowers for Njal. Now to meet Bjorn beneath the gallows tree.

speaker: Bjorn
en: I brought her here. Where it began. Where it ends.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand.

speaker: Bjorn
en: They hung my wife in this tree and buried her among its roots.

speaker: Eivor
en: A grim and undeserved fate.

speaker: Bjorn
en: We took Njal in as a cub, she and I. No children of our own. Now both are gone, yet I remain. Dear Njal. You were always at my side, for the better years of my life. Why must it end like this?

speaker: Eivor
en: We strive for fame, and glory, and good deeds. Naught else can we do.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Yes. Even the gods will die.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Nornir stitch our dooms and none may go against the thread.

speaker: Bjorn
en: We are but single threads, and who knows what pattern they weave.

speaker: Eivor
en: Njal sleeps at the All-Father's feet tonight.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Yes. They let loyal hounds into the Hall of the Brave. So Njal too is there. With Alfhild.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Nornir stitch our dooms and none may go against the thread.

speaker: Bjorn
en: We are but single threads, and who knows what pattern they weave.

speaker: Bjorn
en: Before, you asked if I would join your clan. I am ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. There will be a place for you on my longship and in my clan.

speaker: Bjorn
en: I shall sing of Alfhild and Njal during our travels, sing of their deeds. And I will carry their names into battle.

speaker: Eivor
en: When you are ready, follow the River Nene to my settlement. We shall welcome you as a brother.

speaker: Bjorn
en: I will be the berserker of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: Welcome, Bjorn. May you find a new home here among the Raven Clan.

speaker: Bjorn
en: I hope to. And I will start now.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is the stench of rot in the air.

speaker: Eivor
en: "Notice to All Under God's Eye: Wrath has come to our fair town. Be gone or be doomed."

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Stop! Not a step closer!

speaker: Eivor
en: There is nowhere left to go.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: P-please, don't hurt me!.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why are you here alone?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: I remain with my family. The Withering is taking them, but I do not wish to abandon them.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Withering?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: A disease that often goes unnoticed until it is too late. The whole village had it. It destroys the mind and heightens the aggression in an individual, and ultimately, the poor soul is rendered catatonic.

speaker: Eivor
en: Leave here, child. Your family will soon go, and this village has nothing for you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: But... Papa... Mama...

speaker: Eivor
en: They will find peace in death. Live for them, they would want that.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: I... I... Y-You're right. I cannot hold on any longer to what is already lost. I will go.Here, a key if you want to check on the sick, yourself. If I'm to leave, I can't face them again.

speaker: Eivor
en: This town leaves behind a bitter legacy, but such is the way of this world.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: My head... it swims... a fairy... no... a demon!

speaker: Eivor
en: The stench. They've endured much, it seems...

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: My head... it swims... a fairy... no... a demon!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Breathe, just breathe easy. I... I'm sorry...

speaker: Eivor
en: One's duty to family can be ruinous.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm... a list of names, ages... all killed by a plague. "The Withering."

speaker: Eivor
en: It will not save them, but at least it might ease their suffering.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see you have eluded the grasp of death.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: It is you, Dane! The one from the village. Aye, God saw it fit to spare me their fate. I repay his glory now, healing those here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take care.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Lord above! What are you doing! Stop!

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Eivor! We will march upon Armagh immediately!

speaker: Eivor
en: This place smells like a brewer's hut.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: I will blood eagle the with my own hands! I will blanket the North with the skull of petty kings.

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough! If you charge into Armagh like a berserker, they will crucify you like their Christ.

speaker: Azar
en: I am sorry to tell you, my king, the siege weapons you requested are being held by Armagh.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: Hel have that abbot! Those weapons were to show of the strength of Dublin's new king.

speaker: Eivor
en: Forget about shows of strength. Cast your fortunes with Flann. The will be a powerful ally if you back him now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are these weapons coming from? Who is supplying Armagh?

speaker: Azar
en: A shadowy web of pirates run by a druid cult. They roost along the northern coast, looting and trading in equal measure.

speaker: Eivor
en: These druids, do they call themselves the Children of Danu?

speaker: Azar
en: In fact, they do. Led by one they call "The Seed." Now that you have their scent, I wish you a good hunt.

speaker: Azar
en: If there is nothing more, my king, I will return to my shop.

speaker: Sichfrith
en: I will gather what forces I can, wherever I can, and join them to Flann's. Together, we will avenge my father.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a strength that comes from him. When you find that, men will follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: These would be the arms dealers Azar spoke of. I must approach carefully.

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks like they do good business here.

speaker: Eivor
en: So the abbot leads the Children of Danu. Both druid and bishop, what god will greet him at his death?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Grandfather's wallop is like none other. All it takes is one.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: His fist is a glorious basher of fools, full of great big scars and old dried blood! One day I'm gonna be as strong as Grandfather! I'll wallop the heads off oxen!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: He uses his powerful wallop to protect us. O, his legend grows with every day!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: O, such a fine wallop it is...

speaker: Eivor
en: Little ones, what is this wallop you speak of?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: It's our grandfather. And be careful unless you want a walloping.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am certain my might could clove his wallop.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Many cowards have said the same! He uses only one fist. One wallop. Boom! Like a wolf howling with its knuckles!

speaker: Eivor
en: Well...this wallop has me curious.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Ha! Good, destiny is coming to your plate. Grandfather, there's someone looking for a walloping!

speaker: The Walloper
en: Hello. Yes, I have overwhelmingly powerful strength, but it is not worth talking about.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you are drengr, we should tell stories of battle, swill a cup of mead around a hearth, and share our wisdom.

speaker: The Walloper
en: You want some wisdom? Don't become a hero like I have. I'm cursed with this wallop.

speaker: Eivor
en: These children have me curious. Your calm demeanor even more so.

speaker: The Walloper
en: I beg you. There is no need for this to go where I feel you think it should.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: You best depart unless you desire your face become a fist cave.

speaker: The Walloper
en: Children, stop saying such things. I do not want to use it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I truly wish to see this wallop. I will break it with my humble fists.

speaker: The Walloper
en: Ugh...Neither of us will enjoy this, I am afraid.

speaker: The Walloper
en: I'm tired. Don't say I didn't warn you. The disappointment you will feel, I also feel.

speaker: Eivor
en: There you have it. As promised. Banal victory for me and my wallop. Still unbeaten. Why, God? Come back if you want an endless taste of my endless victory. I know I don't want you to. If you want the wallop, it will ruin your life. It has ruined many already.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hej. I have returned.

speaker: The Walloper
en: I see. I suppose you want to see the wallop?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, it is time. I want to experience this wallop.

speaker: The Walloper
en: This is a sad moment in time. Hold on to your teeth.

speaker: The Walloper
en: And so goes my day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Down you go.

speaker: The Walloper
en: I have never been bested before. I am shocked! Stunned! I never thought it possible. You have thwarted my wallop. You may have access to the treasure my wallop has sadly gifted me over the years. Various awards for bashing skulls. I feel liberated of my legacy. Now I can live the normal life that has forever eluded me. Thank the heavens!

speaker: Eivor
en: The treasure he promised.

speaker: Ubba
en: You did better than your tight-lipped man here. He'll never say anything again.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: We've told you everything. Won't you let us go?

speaker: Ubba
en: That depends on what happens here.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: What do you think? By land or by water?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: We take a boat in there, it'll cause a stir.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Is that a bad thing?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor, there you are.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's with the prisoners?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Men from the fortress out on patrol.

speaker: Ubba
en: We squeezed them. Burgred's not here. It's his queen they're guarding, Æthelswith. They must have separated after Tamworth.

speaker: Eivor
en: I heard as much from Ceolbert in Ledecestre.

speaker: Ubba
en: Ceolbert? What was he doing there

speaker: Ubba
en: Ivarr...

speaker: Eivor
en: Too long a tale for now, but he's fine. I sent him to Repton. What's the plan here?

speaker: Sigurd
en: It won't be long before someone comes looking for these men. We need to get inside and find Æthelswith.

speaker: Sigurd
en: It won't be long before someone comes looking for these men. We need to get inside and find Æthelswith.

speaker: Eivor
en: Capture a queen to find a king... it might work.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Only one way to find out.

speaker: Sigurd
en: See if you can get any more out of them. Me and Eivor will take care of fetching Æthelswith.

speaker: Ubba
en: Odin guide you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The Saxons won't welcome us through the front door. We could find a quiet way in, or we can take your longship. I'm beside you either way. Ah, Eivor, I have dreamt of this day.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of scouring the shire in search of a king?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Of going a-vikingr! With you! With our brothers and sisters! Conquering new lands. Forming lasting friendships. And if it takes chasing some weasel across a new land, so be it. I am right where I wish to be.

speaker: Eivor
en: As am I, brother.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We'll do this the vikingr way then!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Soldiers barracks. Æthelswith might be here.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You three, scurry.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Lady Æthelswith, I see Burgred has done his best to hide you away. But what is lost must always be found.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Let my handmaidens walk free of this place. They have nothing to do with our quarrel.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You hear that, Eivor? Noble. Selfless. This is the sort you must strike a bargain with. A woman of quality. We seek only your king, lady. Tell us where Burgred hides, and we will leave without an ounce of blood spilt.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Please... I-I don't... I don't know.

speaker: Eivor
en: Effective, Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: She's only naive to her present danger. But she will soon understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait... Those are the hands of one who washes linens... a servant.

speaker: Eivor
en: She is a decoy.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Guards! Come quickly! The Danes, they've found me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Watch the handmaidens! I'll follow Æthelswith.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Over there! Soldier by the road! Help!

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Stay away from me! My husband will send you all to Hell!

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Stop what you are doing at once!

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite clever, Your Ladyship. You are certainly making us work for it.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Keep your hands off me, pagan!

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you lost your sense of hospitality?

speaker: Eivor
en: I regret asking...

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Let me go! I demand it!

speaker: Eivor
en: After what you put me through? I would have to be mad.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Do you understand what you're doing, pagan? I am the Lady of Mercia! You're wasting your time. I won't talk. Not to you, not to any of you barbarians.

speaker: Eivor
en: You may reconsider, if only for your people. For who knows how many more may die at the hands of us barbarians?

speaker: Æthelswith
en: You don't frighten me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then you are a fool.

speaker: Ubba
en: Lady Æthelswith... you have seen better days.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: God will sear your soul, heathen! If He can find it.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Quite the catch, Eivor. She is as much a poet as you.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Where's my Kadlin? What have you done with her?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Your handmaiden, you mean? The brave one dressed in royal finery? She's in chains with the others.

speaker: Ubba
en: I'll take them back to Tamworth. Get them talking.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: If she has so much as a scratch on her...

speaker: Sigurd
en: I will inform Ceolwulf. He might have some ideas on how to get through to her.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will meet you there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll go to Ledecestre. Ivarr may have had better luck.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd... what about these prisoners?

speaker: Sigurd
en: We've got what we need. Let them go.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should see what needs to be done around the settlement.

speaker: Eivor
en: These offerings should satisfy the gods, the boat is full. I should return to Sunniva.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Eivor! You've shown yourself to be an inspiring leader. Look at the bounty you've gathered. It's time to make our offering.

speaker: Eivor
en: I enjoy our little festivals. A day where an escaped pig is our biggest worry is a good day.

speaker: Sunniva
en: I can't believe Braun got you to fetch his pigs! You shall have the honor of lighting the flame, Eivor. Come find me when you are ready.

speaker: Havi
en: Really, Baldr? How many times must you ask about the elves? Fine, I will tell you once more. They were brighter than the sun, and their understanding of the sacred hugr was far beyond even my own. And then, one day, the news came of what Surtr had done to them... Even Loki wept. As for their knowledge of the hugr, it now resides solely with the Lord of Muspelheim.

speaker: Havi
en: If Surtr has a heart, I shall put it to the test. Surely his beloved daughter's life is worth Baldr's freedom? The dwarves at the smelting camp... maybe they can help me hunt down the little princess.

speaker: Havi
en: That stink... Smells worse than Ivaldi's Forge back in Asgard. Let's see what these dwarves can tell me about Eysa.

speaker: Bumnoli
en: No, no, no! What is... What... Argh!

speaker: Havi
en: You toil as if tomorrow will never come. Is this the pace Eysa demands?

speaker: Nisdelle
en: It keeps her pesky rodents off my back. Keeps me fed. Well... barely. At this rate I could eat a troll.

speaker: Havi
en: I imagine the hunger pangs hit quite frequently here. May I offer you something to eat?

speaker: Nisdelle
en: It would surely help keep this "toiler" going.

speaker: Havi
en: I have something that will sate your belly, and hopefully rouse your spirits.

speaker: Havi
en: I do not have any food to give you yet.

speaker: Nisdelle
en: That's a shame.

speaker: Nisdelle
en: Ah! It is you. Have you returned with a hearty meal?

speaker: Nisdelle
en: How can I repay such a kindness?

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa is a common enemy of ours... and I'm looking for her.

speaker: Nisdelle
en: Hah. Common enemy is right. If I had it my way, I would bash her pretty face into scalding goo. Sadly she has not returned for me to try my hand. And I do not know where she has gone.

speaker: Havi
en: Is there anything you can tell me?

speaker: Nisdelle
en: Hmm. I get the growing sense you mean to confront her.

speaker: Havi
en: Forcefully.

speaker: Nisdelle
en: Then do have caution. Eysa can use magma to treat her wounds. Quite quickly, I might add. She always has a silky fresh layer on her skin.

speaker: Havi
en: I'll have to remember that.

speaker: Nisdelle
en: If you see Eysa, you will give her my friendly regards, won't you?

speaker: Havi
en: You and I should talk.

speaker: Dwarven Captive 1
en: High One? Is that really you? What are you doing here?

speaker: Havi
en: I've come looking for Surtr's daughter, the one they call Eysa. I hear she frequents this place.

speaker: Dwarven Captive 1
en: She makes her rounds. Comes to see that we are working as best we can.

speaker: Havi
en: What is all this work for?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 1
en: Who knows? She brings us the ores. We extract the metals. They go to Surtr for whatever it is he so desires.

speaker: Havi
en: And what is she like, this Eysa?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 1
en: Get on her bad side, and she'll bark her threats. But so long as you keep on the straight and narrow, she is... tolerable. Ensures you are well fed and healed of your wounds. Sets the bar high for a Muspel.

speaker: Havi
en: Where might I find her now?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 1
en: I do not know, but you can try your luck around the kiln.

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa appears soft of heart. For a Muspel.

speaker: Havi
en: I am looking for the one they call Eysa. Does the name mean anything to you?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 2
en: It means I should not be talking to you. Nor should any of the others. Now go, before you land us both in hot water. Hot magma, more like...

speaker: Havi
en: Can you spare a moment?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 3
en: Piss off, one-eye.

speaker: Bumnoli
en: No, no, no! What is... What... Argh! (coughing) This is bad. This is very, very bad!

speaker: Havi
en: Huh, friendly...

speaker: Havi
en: Are you all right?

speaker: Bumnoli
en: Move away! I need to fix this or I'll lose the whole batch along with my head! (coughing)

speaker: Bumnoli
en: Think, Bumnoli, think! If I could just free that damned trap. How can I loosen it?

speaker: Bumnoli
en: Ymir's beard! It works! It works!

speaker: Havi
en: As good as new.

speaker: Bumnoli
en: You have done me a great service. I could kiss you!

speaker: Havi
en: I'd prefer you use your lips to tell me where I may find Eysa.

speaker: Bumnoli
en: Eysa? What business does an Æsir have with a Muspel princess?

speaker: Havi
en: I have a... quarrel with Surtr. His daughter will help me rectify it.

speaker: Bumnoli
en: And how do you plan on that? Eysa may come off as a young cub, but she does have a dark side.

speaker: Havi
en: As do I. Can you tell me where to find her or not?

speaker: Bumnoli
en: Not exactly. The resources we receive come from a mylna, but I haven't got a clue which. Our blacksmith, Glamnic... Eysa took some of his workers with her. He may know more. But have caution. Last I heard, the guards are making an example out of him.

speaker: Glamnic
en: Come now. That is enough, is it not? Please! Let me out!

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: Any longer and we may have to scoop you out with a spoon.

speaker: Muspel Warrior 2
en: Oh, I would hate to have to do that...

speaker: Muspel Warrior 1
en: He looks as though he can handle it. What do you reckon? A tad longer?

speaker: Muspel Warrior 2
en: Wouldn't hurt. Ensure the message is fully understood.

speaker: Glamnic
en: O! What are you doing?

speaker: Havi
en: Getting you out of here. Now keep quiet.

speaker: Glamnic
en: Quiet? My arse is on fire! Wait! You can walk over magma!?

speaker: Glamnic
en: Agh! Don't leave me here, you oaf!

speaker: Glamnic
en: We are in the clear, I think! Put me down. Put me down!

speaker: Havi
en: Are you okay?

speaker: Glamnic
en: I owe you my life. Those Muspels were prepared to let me bake to death.

speaker: Havi
en: You are in no debt to me. Though as it turns out, I have need of your help.

speaker: Havi
en: You are in no debt to me. Though as it turns out, I... I have need of your help.

speaker: Glamnic
en: Me? What can I help you with?

speaker: Havi
en: Putting a stop to this invasion.

speaker: Glamnic
en: I am listening...

speaker: Havi
en: I know Eysa oversees your work, and I need to find her. What do you know of her whereabouts?

speaker: Havi
en: I know Eysa oversees your work. I need to find her. What do you know of her whereabouts?

speaker: Glamnic
en: Nothing more than which way I saw her leave. It was... east. Though, interestingly, she took a bunch of my people with her. Diggers. Maybe she is scouring another site.

speaker: Havi
en: That is helpful. Farewell, and keep safe.

speaker: Glamnic
en: At last! O, relief!

speaker: Glamnic
en: Go east. That is where I last saw Eysa headed.

speaker: Havi
en: I would have a word with you.

speaker: Durrigor
en: An Æsir? You... you should not be here.

speaker: Havi
en: I'll only take a moment.

speaker: Durrigor
en: Please go. I do not want trouble with the guards. They allow me to speak only when reporting to them, and them alone.

speaker: Havi
en: I should disguise myself as a Muspel.

speaker: Havi
en: Do not react. It is I, the Æsir.

speaker: Durrigor
en: Wh-What? That is quite the disguise. If Loki is giving lessons, tell him we could use his expertise.

speaker: Havi
en: I have him locked away in a dungeon cell for roughly the next thousand years.

speaker: Durrigor
en: Ah... So then, what brings you? You have not come to lend your hand in the muck...

speaker: Havi
en: I'm looking for Eysa. Can you help me with that?

speaker: Durrigor
en: Surtr's daughter? Haven't seen her for some time now. She's got her minions keeping a watchful eye on us though. What I can say is that wherever she goes, she makes it a point to forge large magma pools. Seen her do it here. Walks around in them. I hear she can even move through them.

speaker: Havi
en: Something to look forward to.

speaker: Durrigor
en: Crafty, she is. If you see any liquid-fire pits, it may be proof she is nearby.

speaker: Havi
en: I will keep an eye out.

speaker: Havi
en: Some other task has stolen Eysa's attention as of late. If she is distracted, that will make capturing her all the more simple.

speaker: Havi
en: I wonder how Eysa feels about uninvited guests.

speaker: Havi
en: Everything a Muspel princess could ever want.

speaker: Havi
en: What is this?

speaker: Eysa
en: Are you lost, Æsir?

speaker: Havi
en: That depends. I'm looking for someone. I was told I might find her here. Maybe you know her? Muspel. Around your age. Goes by Eysa. Father's a... how shall I put this... a vainglorious fool who thinks himself a god.

speaker: Eysa
en: Never heard of her.

speaker: Havi
en: Then you will not mind if I stay awhile, dip my toes in one of these soothing fire baths...

speaker: Eysa
en: I have a better idea.

speaker: Havi
en: Oh!

speaker: Eysa
en: Turn around, go back from where you came. And please do mind your step.

speaker: Havi
en: That is no way to welcome a curious outsider. Care to put that away?

speaker: Eysa
en: Why? Afraid I know how to use it?

speaker: Havi
en: I'm sure you can use it. Passably well... But then I would have to kill you.

speaker: Eysa
en: Don't worry. You won't.

speaker: Havi
en: Lay it by, Eysa. There is an easy way out of this.

speaker: Eysa
en: Now where is the fun in that?

speaker: Havi
en: That pendant. It gives her the same gift as her father. No matter what I do, that pendant will give her life. I mustn't let up. I need to stop Eysa before she can use her pendant. I must overwhelm her, prevent her from healing.

speaker: Havi
en: Let's keep the baubles out of it, shall we?

speaker: Eysa
en: Oh, no, the godly gloating. Smite me, I cannot bear it.

speaker: Havi
en: If I were you, I would save the tongue-wit for a more appropriate time.

speaker: Havi
en: I saw no such trinket on Surtr, yet he too has a problem with dying.

speaker: Eysa
en: So that was you in Eitri. What squabble had you trading blows with my father?

speaker: Havi
en: He has taken my son! And now I'll give your father a taste of what he has wrought. Move. So that I may trade his child for mine.

speaker: Eysa
en: You clearly do not know my father.

speaker: Eysa
en: Your son... Baldr, I assume? He has something my father needs. And if that is so, Poppa would sooner see me dead than give in to your demands.

speaker: Eysa
en: If you want your son back, you will need something far more precious than me to barter with. Me, his own daughter, I simply will not do.

speaker: Havi
en: Then there's no longer any need for you to draw breath.

speaker: Dwarven Captive 4
en: Eysa! We found it! We fou—Oh!

speaker: Havi
en: Found what?

speaker: Havi
en: What have you found?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 4
en: Er... Eysa would not want me to say.

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa is no longer here. I am. Havi of Asgard. Lord of Frenzy. And you are in full control of my temper.

speaker: Dwarven Captive 4
en: A-a-a mural. Eysa believes it may help her gain entry to an ancient vault. It is in a cavern. That way!

speaker: Havi
en: So long as Surtr lives, my son will be his prisoner. But how does one kill that which cannot be killed? If death is not his weakness, then I must find something that is.

speaker: Havi
en: The mural Eysa was searching for should be somewhere in this cavern. She believes there is something interesting here... I need to see what it is. I could use Loki right now. He always had a nose for treasure hunts.

speaker: Havi
en: Found your mural, Eysa. Let's see now...

speaker: Havi
en: Elven symbols... a few of which may allude to peaks, or mountains.

speaker: Havi
en: You. Can you read this to me?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 5
en: Me? Er... I, uh, I can try... Elven runes are not something I can decipher with ease.

speaker: Havi
en: You will fare better than I, and that will have to do. Any mention of an ancient vault? A door? Secret entrance, maybe?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 5
en: No. Er, but I can make out this, see... two great mountains to the north... the sun and moon above...

speaker: Havi
en: That's it?

speaker: Dwarven Captive 5
en: Regrets, Æsir. We are simple diggers. Not experts of things writ long ago.

speaker: Havi
en: Not to worry. You have been a great help.

speaker: Havi
en: The vault is located between two great mountains to the north. I should search there.

speaker: Asta
en: Nnngrrrr! I, the great summoner Asta, call to you, my noble steed Skinfaxi! I know you are deaf, but hear me in your soul!

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not think the horse can hear you.

speaker: Asta
en: That horse can't hear anything! So, how does he-- Uh, how did father do it then? The horse always comes when he summons it. Father was a good horse summoner, I'll have you know. I will rise in his stead!

speaker: Asta
en: Rnnngh! Vrrrrghh! To me, I decree! If not your ears, may your essence hear me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Easy, girl.

speaker: Asta
en: Hah! My summoning worked!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your horse is a little unsettled but safe.

speaker: Asta
en: I, Asta the Great Summoner, first of her name, thank ye.

speaker: Eivor
en: Next time, summon a bridge.

speaker: Asta
en: If father were still alive, he'd be proud of me. Wouldn't he, Skinfally? Wait, what did I call you earlier?

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe the horse will have a better life now.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You! You little rat! Come back with my horse!

speaker: Asta
en: Uh-oh! Let's go, Skinfaxi! Follow the wind!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Gah! Stop! Stop!

speaker: Asta
en: Hey! Where are you going? That's my horse! Stop, you thief! You dirty horse thief!

speaker: Asta
en: Skinfaxi, no! You're a monster! Once I master the summoning arts, I will banish you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me about Jorvik. Hytham says there are three more targets there.

speaker: Randvi
en: If that is true, you are in luck. Our old friends Hjorr and Ljufvina have made their homes in Jorvik. Both had status and influence in Norway, so they may have valuable insights into the city's politics.

speaker: Eivor
en: That would make my work easier.

speaker: Randvi
en: What say you then?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will go now. Do you know where I might find Hjorr and Ljufvina?

speaker: Randvi
en: When entering a new city, it is best to ask around the ports. The people there know more than the average peasant.

speaker: Eivor
en: This must be Jorvik. The Order of Ancients lurk in its streets and alleys. My old friends Hjorr and Ljufvina live here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hjorr and Ljufvina settled near the harbor. Someone should know where to find them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hey, friend. Could you help me find some of my people? I am looking for Hjorr and Ljufvina.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Hjorr... I know him. Are you a friend?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Then you will get no help from me or any of the other merchants for that matter. Now if you do not mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hmm. Bitter. Has Hjorr wronged him somehow?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am looking for some friends. Been told to ask around this harbor. Ljufvina and Hjorr.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: A whore? Sure, I know plenty!

speaker: Eivor
en: Of that I am certain.

speaker: Eivor
en: Little one, can you help me? I am looking for some friends. Do the names Hjorr and Ljufvina mean anything to you?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 1
en: Mmmmm... I think I know that name. A woman. She's from Bjarmeland.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very smart.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Boy 1
en: She sounded funny, so I asked her once. Hope it wasn't rude of me. You'll want to speak with the dockmaster, Grigorii. I've seen him talking with her before.

speaker: Eivor
en: My thanks.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: And what about me? What about my wares?

speaker: Grigorii
en: You can have your wares back when you pay the docking tax.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: On whose authority do you impose a tax?

speaker: Grigorii
en: By order of the Council of Jorvik. You can take your issues up with them.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: O, I shall! And I think I speak for the rest of us when I say this isn't over.

speaker: Grigorii
en: Move along now. We run a clean dock in Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must be the dockmaster.

speaker: Grigorii
en: What gave it away?

speaker: Eivor
en: Everyone hates you.

speaker: Grigorii
en: As I just explained to your friend there, if your wares have been seized, take it up with the council.

speaker: Eivor
en: These merchants are not my friends, but I'm looking for some. Hjorr and Ljufvina.

speaker: Grigorii
en: You know Hjorr and Ljufvina? What business do you have with them?

speaker: Eivor
en: We know each other from Norway. Bid farewell to that land, but not to old friends.

speaker: Grigorii
en: You may glad to hear they fare quite well in Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: It does not surprise me. They are driven. And so am I. Now, I would like to see them again.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're sticking your nose where it does not belong.

speaker: Grigorii
en: I'm a dockmaster. Being inquisitive befits my line of work. Keeps things under control.

speaker: Eivor
en: You'll find no trouble here unless you seek it. I only want to speak with some old friends.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I know them, and you seem to know them too. Point me in the right direction.

speaker: Grigorii
en: In a manor surrounded by flowers. That's where Hjorr and Lfujvina live.

speaker: Grigorii
en: How about some coin for my trouble?

speaker: Eivor
en: How about I cut out your tongue?

speaker: Grigorii
en: Forget I said anything!

speaker: Eivor
en: A manor. Hjorr and Ljufvina have done well for themselves.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Keep your coin pouch close to you, there are pocket thieves around lately.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Huh! They can try.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: I cannot wait for the Yuletide feast! Snow, wine, food... It truly is the best time of the year!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: Have you gotten gifts for your family yet?

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: The third crate of mine taken this week, and with no explanation.

speaker: Norse Woman
en: Rules are rules, but I wish they would tell us why.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here, this is their home.

speaker: Eivor
en: The place has been ransacked. And this body... it's not Hjorr or Ljufvina.

speaker: Eivor
en: Scattered scrolls. The thief was looking for something.

speaker: Eivor
en: There was a struggle here. Looks like it continued outside.

speaker: Eivor
en: Blood, but no body. Which way did they go?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this one of the thieves? Hmm... the trail continues.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Blood of Tengri! Riders of Bjarmia!

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Who is that? Come closer, now!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's... it's me, Ljufvina. It's Eivor.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Eivor? What... Who sent you? Are you with them?

speaker: Eivor
en: Breathe, Ljufvina. You are rattled. You know me. I am a friend.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Are you? You show up here, like this... These people tried to kill me!

speaker: Eivor
en: I heard there was trouble in Jorvik. I have only come to help. On my honor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Cast your suspicions or be ready to kill me, because I will not raise my weapon against you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can we deal with this later? It's not safe here.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: I am sorry, Eivor. I did not mean to doubt you. It has been a tense few weeks.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who were they? Why were they after you?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: They were after this.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: I do not know what it is, but these men were ready to kill me for it.

speaker: Eivor
en: "A Poor Fellow-Soldier of Christ."

speaker: Ljufvina
en: You know him...?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have seen a letter like this before, in Lunden. This city is in great danger. Where is Hjorr?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: At the royal hall. I will take you there.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Pull up your hood, we may not be safe just yet.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: This way. They are still looking for me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hide low. We can slip past them.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: She can't have gotten far. Look around.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Come on.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's go.

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Have you seen a Bjarmian woman? Answer well if you know what is good for you.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 5
en: I... I haven't seen her, I swear.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Did you hear something? Keep an eye out.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Look, over there... Is that her?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: More of them, just there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep your head down.

speaker: Eivor
en: Out of the shadows now.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not see any others. Let's keep moving.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: I think it is safe now. Gods, Eivor, your arrival could not be better timed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Call it fate. I had hoped our paths would cross again, though I imagined a calmer reunion.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: We fled one problem only to find ourselves embroiled in another. While King Ricsige is preoccupied with a money shortage, a group called the Red Hand has been imposing their will.

speaker: Eivor
en: The ones who attacked you?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Yes and no. They are bandits, but someone is controlling them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Look no further than the names in that letter. Killing them is the reason I am here.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: But they are coded. They could belong to anyone.

speaker: Eivor
en: The sludge in the streets often drips from the gutters of the halls. When in doubt, look to those in power.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: You mean the council? Hjorr is on the council.

speaker: Eivor
en: That works in our favor. Someone we can trust to find the answers we seek.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Yes. We are nearly there.

speaker: Hjorr
en: It pleases me to see you, old friend. All are welcome here in Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is good to find you well, Hjorr. Both of you.

speaker: Hjorr
en: What are you doing here? You have not come all this way for the Yuletide.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have come to warn you, old warrior. About a rot in your city. Three figures, corrupt and dangerous. We should work together to bring them into the light and kill them before they come to power.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: However I may help, I am ready.

speaker: Hjorr
en: Slow yourselves. Eivor, we cannot just go running around the city poking and prodding and killing at will.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: They nearly did me, Hjorr!

speaker: Hjorr
en: What!

speaker: Eivor
en: These people sent the Red Hand after her, ready to shed blood in your streets to keep themselves a secret. But they failed.

speaker: Hjorr
en: This is the letter that was sent to our home. The Needle, The Firebrand, The Vault.

speaker: Eivor
en: They belong to a group called The Order of the Ancients. These are their assumed names. Our leads.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Listen to her, Hjorr. She has dealt with their kind before.

speaker: Hjorr
en: Corruption has seeped its way into Jorvik. But King Ricsige's hands are full, which means my hands are full. Counsel on this matter will fall on deaf ears.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not want his counsel. All I have told you stays between the three of us. But you should introduce me to the king. I will need to align with him if we are to go about this freely.

speaker: Faravid
en: The Picts are winning this war. We should be scraping together every ounce of silver to procure food for our men.

speaker: Audun
en: Understood, dear Faravid, but we also have a responsibility to our townspeople. The Yuletide must go on.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Enough! The more you argue, the more my head hurts.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Hjorr... I was not aware we had company, the likes of which I did not approve.

speaker: Eivor
en: King Ricsige, I am Eivor of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Well, Eivor of the Raven Clan, as you can see, I'm in the middle of something. Hjorr, perhaps for a lack of better judgment, deems it necessary that you interrupt. Why?

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a problem in Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this how you greet all the strangers who walk through the doors? Or just those who mean to help?

speaker: Hjorr
en: Forgive me, lord, this is

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor of the Raven Clan. Don't bother, I know well who you are, Ricsige. You have a problem in Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have a problem in Jorvik.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Yes, I'm looking at it.

speaker: Eivor
en: A problem that nearly got my friend killed. Ljufvina was attacked by the Red Hand. They raided her home, destroyed her property, and chased her through the streets.

speaker: Audun
en: Those bloody scoundrels again!

speaker: Eivor
en: She survived. But the Red Hand has been a growing problem here of late.

speaker: Ricsige
en: And what is your stake in this? Are you some sort of wandering mercenary?

speaker: Faravid
en: No, this is Sigurd Jarl's drengr (courageous warrior). Took our old camp by the river Nene as I hear it. I am Faravid, war chief to Halfdan Ragnarsson. And this well-fed wastrel is Audun, High Reeve of Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have seen rebel groups like this before. They sit and wait, and the moment you lower your guard, they spring up like weeds. If left alone, they will take Jorvik out from under you. Not what you want. Not what Halfdan wants.

speaker: Audun
en: O dear...

speaker: Ricsige
en: What do you want?

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me what you do you know about the Red Hand, and I will rid your city of them. You can go about your affairs.

speaker: Ricsige
en: They've been sticking their hands in coffers around the city. Targeting nobles, merchants, and anyone else they can throttle.

speaker: Audun
en: And they are growing, as you said. I would rather not be worrying about them come Yuletide.

speaker: Faravid
en: This is not something we can afford to ignore. If we do not have the means to deal with the Red Hand, we should let Eivor.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Do what you can. But do it quietly. I do not want the public alarmed. Hjorr... send funds to procure food and ale for Faravid's men. And make sure there's enough left over for the feast.

speaker: Hjorr
en: But it's as I said, we don't have

speaker: Ricsige
en: Find it. I have spoken.

speaker: Hjorr
en: He tells me to find more silver. Where, in a dragon's hoard? Come, I will take you back to Ljufvina. She will know where to begin.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I cannot tell if that went the way you had hoped.

speaker: Eivor
en: It went well enough. Ricsige will stay out of my way. No one can argue, that the Red Hand must be dealt with. Speak a word of this to no one. The circle of trust must stay between the three of us.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: You will forgive me for stepping away. I grow weary of those pissing contests.

speaker: Hjorr
en: My love, I am sorry for what happened. I should have been there.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Nonsense. You have your duties to fulfill. Besides, a few bandits is hardly something to worry over.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I am only glad you were not harmed. Eivor, I will be around if you need me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Once you catch the tail, you do not let go.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Old habits die with a struggle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hjorr has changed. Softened.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Politics. It takes the Norse out of a Norse.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am happy for him. You have made something of yourselves here.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Perhaps.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you have there?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Christian texts. The gospels. Ecclesiates. The Revelation of John. The Red Hand steals all they can find. We may run this city now, but the Christians must still be allowed to worship as they see fit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Seems the Red Hand disagrees.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: What's more, Audun is worried they will come for the archives next. Between this and all the uproar at the harbor, I would say we have some leads.

speaker: Eivor
en: What does the Red Hand want with Christian texts?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: That is the question. Whatever it is, there's no length they will not go to retrieve them. They have even burned people alive who refuse to hand over what they demand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is the largest collection of texts in the city?

speaker: Ljufvina
en: The archives, but they haven't yet been so bold as to attack it yet. Audun keeps a close eye on that place.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will try my luck there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I went by the harbor when I first arrived. The dockmaster looked wary when I asked about you.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: That does not surprise me. He's been using Jorvik's money shortage to increase taxes. As if he's ordered to by the council. Hjorr would never wrong the people like that, even if Ricsige demanded it. The dockmaster is a thief and a liar.

speaker: Eivor
en: A man in need of a throttling. I will have another look around the harbor.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Try the trade depot. It is where he is holding the merchant's wares.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will get started at once.

speaker: Eivor
en: No, I need you here. Listen to the voices in this hall. Look for any signs, changes in behavior, anything.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: I would swallow a horse heart to join you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know, old friend. Your loyalty is why I need you here. I will return when I find something.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Can anyone hear my cries? Please help! This brute has me trapped in this sultry tower.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Shut your mouth. A lady you may be, but here, you are my prisoner. And you will do as I say.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: I'm trapped! With no means of escape. So helpless. O, I need someone, anyone!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: A challenger approaches.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O bless!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Step back, Dane. I am sworn to this lady, and unafraid to kill the likes of you!

speaker: Eivor
en: If you're going to hold someone against their will, it would be wise to gag them.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: I am Thegn Tarquin. Lady Annis belongs to me! I told you to leave, Dane rat! The lady is mine!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: You must fight for me with all your heart, for if you fail, a lifetime of gloom awaits me!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: No more! I yield! Find another champion, lady!

speaker: Eivor
en: Strange...

speaker: Eivor
en: It is over. You can come out now.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Tarquin? My thegn, what has happened?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your captor fled. Felt a little soft for my liking. What are you really doing in there?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O, God, no! It was only a game. A romp! My dear Tarquin, how could you!

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw a man holding you against your will.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: All a part of the seduction! O, God! You really thought my life was in danger? And you risked your own...you, o, you are so brave. A fine protector.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me you are joking.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Please, you must fight for me. Who knows what lurks below? What vile people might come to harm me! I need a protector, stout and resolute! Please, stand guard below.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I do, will you come out?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O, assuredly.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Just...stand at the door below. That will place you directly between me and any bad, bad men. Perfect, I feel safer already.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Wait. No! Come back! You must fight for me. I am in a perpetual state of danger and must be protected!

speaker: Eivor
en: Trouble coming.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O, good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Real trouble. Keep quiet

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: O, woe is me. A king's daughter who has run away from her royal house with all of its rare jewels in tow.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Huh. Well now...I'd say that's worth a look.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ugh.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: A courageous traveler has come to my rescue! Please, Lord, guide their hand! Help me, O savior! Rescue me from this dastardly man!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Yes! You've done it again! I think we are destined to do this forever.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think it is time I take my leave.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: Are you still there? My savior? O dear...

speaker: Skjaldmær
en: Ahh! No!

speaker: Havi
en: The divided shieldmaiden doth live! Or suffers a kind of half-life!

speaker: Havi
en: I am reminded that the rules of death are different here.

speaker: Skjaldmær
en: No! No more... There's little of me left...

speaker: Skjaldmær
en: I'll fight you... I'll fight you... while there's breath in me yet!

speaker: Havi
en: I am not your butcher, but I will cut you down if I have to!

speaker: Havi
en: Her will was strong. She deserves a better fate.

speaker: Skjaldmær
en: I am not your thrall! My thoughts are my own!

speaker: Havi
en: I take your life to preserve my own... but I think you'll be the better for it. What purpose drives you? Is this a curse, or some hellish design?

speaker: Havi
en: She has been made whole... Fighting completes her!

speaker: Havi
en: Stay your hand, shieldmaiden! I'm not your tormentor.

speaker: Skjaldmær
en: I know that now, and I thank you for making me whole.

speaker: Havi
en: A painful favor, but fruitful in the end. How did you come by this odd healing ability? Is it a quality of this place?

speaker: Skjaldmær
en: I was human before Hel... changed me. She didn't wield the instruments but her will doubtlessly guided them.

speaker: Havi
en: Warriors who grow stronger through death would make a formidable army. Are there many more like you?

speaker: Skjaldmær
en: I know not. I feel parts of my memory have been hacked away. But I'll not forget my debt to you.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: My head aches... Argh..."

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: By all the bacrauts (assholes) of the world, what ails my mind? Must be a hangover. Argh...

speaker: Axehead
en: Over here, good warrior.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hej, stranger.

speaker: Axehead
en: Excuse me, I have a slight pain. Do you notice anything on my head? It's an itch or a cut that simply won't go away.

speaker: Eivor
en: It appears to be a... a battle scar.

speaker: Axehead
en: Ah, as I suspected. It must be from my most recent battle. You should see the other man. He got the worst of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Worse than... I suppose its possible, yes. If he is headless.

speaker: Axehead
en: My arms are numb from battle. Does it need any dressing? Do you think it is a serious wound?

speaker: Eivor
en: Good drengr, you have an axe in your head. It is grim. I will take it out, but you will surely head off to the next realm soon.

speaker: Axehead
en: Ah. Valhalla, it is. I appreciate your candid response. Now I prepare myself for the sights and sounds of the Corpse Hall.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will relieve you of the pain it gives you. Send you down the Bifrost.

speaker: Axehead
en: It is time.

speaker: Eivor
en: I feel it is a small wound, for a warrior as great as you. Nothing but a twig stuck near your brow.

speaker: Axehead
en: Ah, yes, thank you for telling me. And your keen eye on discerning a fellow great warrior.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can take it off, the twig, if you like.

speaker: Axehead
en: Of course. When you have a moment, just brush it off.

speaker: Axehead
en: You know, there is a great meadhall nearby. We could go there and reflect on our greatest exploits. Nothing finer than an endless night of drunken glory to make you forget all of the dishonorable fops in this world. Just skalds and warriors full of mead and story-greed. O, yes, let me weave you a hero's from dirt and spittle. This one blustery battle-day, I was inside a shield wall... and my wife entered the shield wall... nude... and started singing... O... We were so young... so very nimble in our hugr (minds) and our ways...

speaker: Eivor
en: All your enemies have been slain. Now you rejoice.

speaker: Faravid
en: Eivor! Welcome, join me in drowning this golden drink.

speaker: Faravid
en: You made it, come have a drink.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're a few horns deep already.

speaker: Faravid
en: Yet still floating! Tell me, how did my old friend like his goblet gift.

speaker: Eivor
en: There were other things on his mind. Your man Ulf, for instance. He died protecting the spoils he stole from Halfdan.

speaker: Faravid
en: Ulf! Poor Ulf. I told him to mind your tongue, but he wags it like a slobbering dog.

speaker: Eivor
en: He gave your goblet little more than a second glance. He rants and broods in his high tower.

speaker: Eivor
en: Was Halfdan always so easily riled?

speaker: Faravid
en: No. Riches and glory have shaped him into something new. He's not the same man he used to be.

speaker: Eivor
en: The songs of skalds and the glint of silver can turn even the best of us.

speaker: Faravid
en: He was a fierce man in days past, but he has lost the bite he once had. He's too careful. He ruminates and hesitates.

speaker: Eivor
en: A jarl is owed the spoils of war, to spend as he sees fit. So it has always been.

speaker: Faravid
en: That may be so, but Halfdan hoards our wealth for himself, sharing neither gold nor glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this place? I expected an army, ready for warcraft.

speaker: Faravid
en: This was our first camp in Northumbria. I came here with Halfdan and his brothers, Ubba and Ivarr. We besieged Jorvik and put King Ælla in the cold ground. Those were good days, now too far gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is all this?

speaker: Faravid
en: My share of the treasure we took from those distant days. I buried it here for a rainy day. This bag is heavy with silver. Enough to pay for an army. Come, race me to Jorvik, Eivor! Remind me of the glories long gone!

speaker: Eivor
en: You're too drunk to win a race.

speaker: Faravid
en: Then have a drink. Make it fair.

speaker: Faravid
en: What's keeping you, friend Eivor? Waiting for spring?

speaker: Faravid
en: Best not fall off your horse.

speaker: Eivor
en: See you in Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your horse can smell the ale dripping from your mouth. You frighten her.

speaker: Faravid
en: It warms my heart that you're concerned, but Hulda and I can hold our drink.

speaker: Faravid
en: Fast, Eivor! Ride like Sleipnir's hooves!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your horse is slow and her rider's drunk.

speaker: Faravid
en: The gods love a fool!

speaker: Eivor
en: Fly, my friend, fly. Show Faravid our arses.

speaker: Eivor
en: Having trouble keeping up?

speaker: Faravid
en: My horse must be deeper in the cups than I am.

speaker: Eivor
en: The mead gave you luck, that's all.

speaker: Faravid
en: I offered you enough mead to best me. No excuses!

speaker: Eivor
en: What are we doing in Jorvik? You haven't said.

speaker: Faravid
en: Paying a visit to our kept King Ricsige, long may he reign. I haven't enough men to beat the Picts alone. But with Ricsige and his fyrd, we'll finish them off.

speaker: Eivor
en: You would bring a puppet king into this fight, but not your jarl?

speaker: Faravid
en: Shhh. Keep this to yourself. The streets have ears, the windows have eyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I did not agree to this level of deception. You should have told me this before.

speaker: Faravid
en: Eivor, my friend. If I described my full strategy, we might never leave the campfire.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'd prefer the light of a fire to the darkness of your plans. Don't do it again.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Things are better now, are they not? Ever since Audun

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: Shh! Speak not that blasted name!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I've been afraid to touch even a drop of wine since the Yuletide feast.

speaker: Norse Woman 3
en: One more reason to stick with ale.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: I wish Yuletide happened every month... the daily slog kills me.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: Not if it happens the way it did last time. Ugh.

speaker: Faravid
en: Wait. A favor I must ask of you. Make no mention that Halfdan is ignorant of our plans. It's better this way.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you mad? Ricsige answers to Halfdan. You put this man in grave danger if he defies his master's will.

speaker: Faravid
en: Ricsige cannot defy orders he has never heard, no? Trust me, I will take the blame should our plan fall apart.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Eivor the Wolf-Kissed. And Halfdan's cup bearer. What a curious surprise.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope the day finds you and Jorvik well.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Yes, we scrape by. With what little we still own. But this new war should make wealthy once again... until our tribute is taken.

speaker: Faravid
en: I smell the bile on your breath, king. Do not forget who is in charge here.

speaker: Ricsige
en: O, do remind me, Faravid. Yesterday, it was Halfdan. But today I hear whispers that you are leading the charge. I am confused.

speaker: Faravid
en: Yes, you answer to Halfdan. And now he orders one final strike on the Pict stronghold at Magnis.

speaker: Ricsige
en: To make war with the North on such a scale will require a hefty amount of silver and a large force of men.

speaker: Faravid
en: My soldiers and silver are pledged already. I expect the same from you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have given my aid as well. The battle must be decisive.

speaker: Ricsige
en: I see. And you have these orders from Halfdan in writing, yes? From the great man himself?

speaker: Eivor
en: Not with us, but you can rest assured that Halfdan has needs of you. He expects a swift victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: To be clear, King Ricsige... Halfdan knows nothing about this attack.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Nothing at all? That's unusual, Faravid.

speaker: Faravid
en: Eivor is mistaken, Lord King. I was given Halfdan's personal assurance that you would volunteer your troops. He expects as much. But Halfdan is ailing and tired. Let us not burden him with more worry, but please him with a swift victory.

speaker: Ricsige
en: I'm sorry, Faravid, but duty compels me to refuse. Without strict orders from Halfdan, I will not risk the lives of so many.

speaker: Faravid
en: You deny me?

speaker: Ricsige
en: I do. To gift you an army puts my wealth and reputation at risk. That's not what Halfdan wants. He needs a strong and loyal king.

speaker: Faravid
en: You presume to know what Halfdan wants?

speaker: Ricsige
en: Hearsay is not enough. For all I know, this is another of Halfdan's tests.

speaker: Faravid
en: The greatest snake in Northumbria, that Saxon is. But we need his army to take Magnis.

speaker: Eivor
en: And we'll have it, if we falsify orders from Halfdan ourselves.

speaker: Faravid
en: You would do this? Draw up fake orders and pass them off as real?

speaker: Eivor
en: That's it. And I know just who to speak with. Hjorr of Jorvik. He'll know what we need.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Without Halfdan's formal approval, I cannot help. It's too great a risk. And, after all, he is my ally. You understand.

speaker: Faravid
en: I should break your arms for that! What were you doing?

speaker: Eivor
