en: I saw no reason to hide the truth. Ricsige is a Saxon puppet. He has more to lose than you and I ever will.

speaker: Faravid
en: That serpent cannot be trusted, Eivor! If he tells Halfdan of our plan, our victory is at risk. Our victory is for Halfdan's own benefit. We will secure Northumbria for him, along with the gratitude of all its Saxon and Norse subjects.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine. If we falsify orders from Halfdan, Ricsige will accept them. Hjorr of Jorvik could help.

speaker: Faravid
en: Good. Hjorr's favorite alehouse is nearby. Seek him there.

speaker: Faravid
en: Picts rampaging through our lands, while the Saxons do nothing!

speaker: Ricsige
en: The Picts are an eternal problem, plotting beyond the wall, so I doubt

speaker: Faravid
en: We conquered all of Northumbria! Never doubt a drunken Norseman.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Ale costs more than bread! Things were better under Audun.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Hjorr, this crowd won't listen to reason.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Give us your coin, you bloody robbers!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hjorr... just where I hoped you would be.

speaker: Hjorr
en: Eivor, gods! You have come at the right moment.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Right then, what's this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Go home or get hurt. But you won't bother my friends.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: I'll bother who I please, after I brick your face to the brains.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Eivor, always the fighter.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Winter's chill slowing your bones?

speaker: Hjorr
en: Thank you, Wolf-Kissed. Those men will wake up soon enough.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: With greater sense, I hope. What brings you back to Jorvik?

speaker: Eivor
en: Secret errands to Halfdan. I need an army of men to face the Picts in the North.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: What happened to the silver you took from Audun? You could hire a band of sellswords with that much.

speaker: Eivor
en: It won't be enough. We need Ricsige's Saxons at our side. Any fewer would be a death sentence.

speaker: Hjorr
en: Has Halfdan planned an attack he cannot afford? That's not like him.

speaker: Eivor
en: To be clear, Faravid made this plan. Not Halfdan.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Does Halfdan know of this plan or...

speaker: Eivor
en: He doesn't, but he's given me leave to act as I must, for reasons I cannot share.

speaker: Hjorr
en: Yes, we've heard the rumors. And all our messages have gone unanswered.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you aid with some trickery? Help me forge a set of orders from Halfdan himself. To force Ricsige's cooperation?

speaker: Eivor
en: You'll be taking quite a risk. You have my thanks. We can meet outside the Royal Hall after you have the documents.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Eivor! Join me for a drink.

speaker: Eivor
en: You both seem to have settled well in this city.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Yes, we do enjoy the comforts we have here. But I still think about Norway... the cold and the warmth.

speaker: Ljufvina
en: Stay on the road safe, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I try to.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Audun, we remain loyal. Things were better with you around.

speaker: Hjorr
en: Here, take this forgery and pray that King Ricsige sees nothing amiss. I trust you know what you are doing.

speaker: Eivor
en: Straight from Halfdan's hand, as you see.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Hm. Yes, yes. Well, if Halfdan's loyal mules have pledged to fight... Still, my help will come at a price.

speaker: Hjorr
en: I-if you're speaking of coin

speaker: Faravid
en: I remind you that your soldiers are mine.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Halfdan's, my good man. Halfdan's soldiers, for these are Halfdan's orders. Correct?

speaker: Ricsige
en: But I jest, I jest.

speaker: Eivor
en: All is in order, then?

speaker: Ricsige
en: If Halfdan commands, I shall raise my fyrd. And you shall have your fighting army.

speaker: Faravid
en: Good. Get them marching at once. This must happen soon.

speaker: Ricsige
en: As soon as they are mustered, Lord Faravid. And no sooner.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Eivor. A moment with you?

speaker: Faravid
en: I'll meet you at Stenwege.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Faravid is Halfdan's man. So are the Hemmings of Snotinghamscire, as are we here in Jorvik. But not you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't like talk that dances around thorns.

speaker: Ricsige
en: For whom are you fighting, truly?

speaker: Eivor
en: We all fight for Halfdan, and for Northumbria.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Loyal to the bone, aren't you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I fight for myself, and my people.

speaker: Ricsige
en: As any great leader must.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am on your council, Ricsige, King of Jorvik.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Quite the charmer, you are. But you jest. We all know in whom the true power lies.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why ask me of loyalty? What are you seeking?

speaker: Ricsige
en: An innocuous question. Loyalty is a word that slides off the lips like honey. Sweet to the taste, but never lingering. There are things simmering in Northumbria, hidden even from you. Take heed and have a care.

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: Have you been brought by Njord to send these sun-bleached bones to the bottom of the sea? Do you have the courage to face one thrice-cursed by fate?

speaker: Eivor
en: Salt-licked soldier, you've... lived here for some time.

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: I call to Njord, Lord of the Sea, till my throat bleeds with grief, but he only sends fish and other things to sustain me. And now you have come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why do you complain to Njord like this? And what has it to do with me?

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: I scorned the gods and pitched into the sea for my arrogance. Thorgest thought me dead and sailed off into legend.

speaker: Eivor
en: The old King of Dublin? That Thorgest?

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: Send me down into Njord's cold embrace. I can't simply give myself to the waves. Will you give me an honorable death?

speaker: Eivor
en: You will sleep with sea-serpents this night.

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: I will not make this easy. I must earn this death.

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: I pledge this death to Njord.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your death.

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: Whoever falls first.

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: You must cut deeper. I was Thorgest's strongest.

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: Ah, it is like when I fought at Thorgest's side.

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: This is my day, do not let me down.

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: At last. A fisher once told me I would find peace near the sea. Yet know, another sad survivor of Thorgest's crew still walks...

speaker: Hogne Sea-Tossed
en: I had a dream. I was in water... Lough Neagh. I felt Thorgest there. With his prize...

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: Dead! Dead! And dead! You can never eat too much death!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop, drengr. Have you lost your wits? Why berate a man long dead?

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: This soldier promised deathly peace. He claimed he'd bested foe after foe, each left more dead than the last.

speaker: Eivor
en: He is dead himself. You cannot kill him better.

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: I sailed with the mighty Thorgest! I deserve my place in the great hall! An honorable death is all I ask. Could you, stranger, could you give me a just fight and, at long last, release me from this cursed life?

speaker: Eivor
en: You have suffered mightily. You deserve a seat next to Odin.

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: Let it be so!

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: Come. One of us will find the great hall.

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: Much more promise than the others. You do not fight like a dolt.

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: I begin to weaken, stranger. It is now that I am most dangerous!

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: Valhalla calls. But I shall not die easily!

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: Well done, stranger. I am the last and largest of Thorgest's drengir. He who lies at the bottom of Lough Neagh.

speaker: Blud the Giant
en: You have released me, clever stranger. Another of Thorgest's crew, such as I, survives. I long to see him at Odin's feast.

speaker: Eivor
en: The mighty Thorgest. A fitting remembrance.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is the barrel of mead, friend?

speaker: Braun
en: A seer warned me of a vision she had where I was a frog drowning in a vat of mead. Haven't had a sip since.

speaker: Eivor
en: So instead you're guarding empty pens?

speaker: Braun
en: I was hoping no one would notice but the pigs I bought for the offerings got loose after their cart crashed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see where this is going. You want me to find and kill the pigs and bring back the meat.

speaker: Braun
en: What? No! No. They need to be alive for the offerings. Can you go gather them and bring them back?

speaker: Eivor
en: And how would I go about doing that?

speaker: Braun
en: The farmer I bought them from said that if you whistle, they will come running. If they trust you, they will follow you.

speaker: Eivor
en: This feels like an errand for a child. Is Bertham not around?

speaker: Braun
en: Please, Eivor. Norvid gave me some of his tokens. They're yours if you bring back the pigs.

speaker: Eivor
en: Very well, Braun. I will find your lost pigs.

speaker: Braun
en: Thank you, Eivor! May the gods favor you!

speaker: Eivor
en: This looks like the crashed pig cart. Tracks show they ran into the forest.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here they are. Now to whistle and hope they trust me. I wonder how the farmer trained the pigs to follow a whistle?

speaker: Eivor
en: Come on, pig! It's like you don't want to be offered up to the gods! It's an honor, I assure you.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's raiding season and I'm shepherding pigs through the mud. Maybe Dag was right.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's one pig returned. I'm still not clear why he couldn't do this. Two fat piggies playing in the mud. That should be all of them. Eivor the Pigherder.

speaker: Eivor
en: Here you are. All your runaway pigs back in one piece.

speaker: Braun
en: Thank you! These boots are new and I couldn't bear the thought of them covered in mud! O, I have your promised tokens but I think you've also earned the right to choose which god will receive your offering.

speaker: Eivor
en: We offer this to you, Lady Freyja. May you grant us many riches on our raids.

speaker: Ubba
en: Your turn. She won't talk to me.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor will handle it. Go on.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've exhausted my friend Ubba here, but I'm wide awake. Maybe tell me where Burgred's hiding and let him rest happy.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Never.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stone-faced and tight-lipped, all for a king who hides like a cowardly , too scared to protect his family and his people.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thirsty?

speaker: Æthelswith
en: My husband does what he must for Mercia. How could he do otherwise, knowing that even his closest friends could betray him?

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Give that traitor, Ceolwulf my message... he may win this earthly battle, but the Devil has won the war for his soul.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolwulf is a Mercian doing his best to find common footing in this new land. Seems to be the only true Mercian by my reckoning.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: I spit on him. Whatever life he makes in Mercia will be built on the graves of the nobles who gave their lives to defend it.

speaker: Eivor
en: The longer you drag this out, the truer that becomes.

speaker: Eivor
en: He stabbed you in the back, true. But the people of Mercia are scared, and Ceolwulf offers them a balm for that fear.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: I spit on him. Whatever life he makes in Mercia will be built on the graves of the nobles who gave their lives to defend it.

speaker: Eivor
en: The longer you drag this out, the truer that becomes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't care how you feel about Ceolwulf. But he will be king. It's only a matter of when.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Burgred is king. Elected by the and anointed by God.

speaker: Eivor
en: My lady, I know what the losing side looks like. And you're on it.

speaker: Eivor
en: We've taken Repton, Tamworth. Now Templebrough and Ledecestre.

speaker: Eivor
en: With each victory, your hope for peace recedes.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Yet Burgred has what you do not. The loyalty of his people. Good men. Faithful men.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who? The thegns and ceorls of Mercia? No, No. Only Leofrith remains loyal. And he too will fall.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Yes, goodly Leofrith. He will die defending his king. And win or lose, he will send a hundred more of you to Hell!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor... Your Ladyship... do not mind me. Only here to count my spoils.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: O, God!

speaker: Eivor
en: Pigs have to eat, my lady. The trouble is, it takes a lot to sate their hunger.

speaker: Eivor
en: Only a matter of time before they finish those and sniff around for fresher meat.

speaker: Ivarr
en: And the smell of pig shit after this? Hoo!

speaker: Eivor
en: Out, Ivarr! Now.

speaker: Ivarr
en: All right, all right. But if you mean to stay, mind the smell after they finish this.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I would not stick around too long. The smell of pig shit after they pass this is something dreadful.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: M-my God! Get me out of here! Please!

speaker: Eivor
en: Talk now and we'll draw you a nice, warm bath.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: You... you are asking me to betray my husband! How can I do that?

speaker: Eivor
en: If you don't, you will betray countless others. In legend, you may be remembered as the king and queen who abandoned their kingdom in its darkest hour. But there will be peace. This is Ceolwulf's promise, and it will be honored. You have my word.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Does the caged bird sing?

speaker: Eivor
en: Burgred is hiding in an old crypt to the south, where the Alne and Arwy rivers join.

speaker: Ivarr
en: A crypt... now tell me this is not a sign from the gods.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a long way to carry a king. The three of you must clear a path back to Tamworth. Where can we meet?

speaker: Ubba
en: Bring him to the bridge at Venonis. It's a straight line through. We'll deal with any trouble there.

speaker: Eivor
en: The heads were a nice touch. I'm not one for spectacle, but it got her talking.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Spectacle? That's just me.

speaker: Eivor
en: How many more times will I have to curtail your spectacles, Ivarr?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Spectacle? That's just me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Heavy guard for a musty crypt. It cannot be the dead they're protecting.

speaker: Eivor
en: He's got to be down here. Where are you hiding, Burgred?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: My lord! Intruders!

speaker: King Burgred
en: What's going on out there!

speaker: King Burgred
en: No... no no no! It can't be. Stay back!

speaker: Eivor
en: That's a bread knife, my lord. Do you mean to butter me?

speaker: King Burgred
en: Stay back! Back, I say! I'll fight you!

speaker: Eivor
en: If you insist.

speaker: King Burgred
en: You'll have to kill me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Luckily for you, it won't come to that.

speaker: King Burgred
en: This kingdom is mine! Mine!

speaker: Eivor
en: Time to go, my lord. We're late for the crowning ceremony.

speaker: Letter From Burgred
en: The situation has turned dire. The filthy Danes have taken Tamworth from me! I am trapped, hiding in a muggy crypt with no telling when I may resurface. This is unacceptable! The fate of Mercia now lies in the hands of my thegn, Leofrith, but I have no faith that he can succeed. He is a loyal rat, nothing more, and is now best served as my human shield. And so, for this matter that must be resolved with the utmost urgency, I am writing to inform you that I have called upon your loyal hunters. And rest assured, you have my promise that this favor will not be forgotten. The Lord King of Mercia

speaker: Tonna
en: There! I want that Dane cleaved and butchered!

speaker: Eivor
en: Tonna..."

speaker: King Burgred
en: Help!

speaker: Tonna
en: You crossed me, lovely dove. Did you think I wouldn't find out?

speaker: Tonna
en: I'll send you back to the Ragnarssons in pieces. Our fates are weaved together, lovely dove! Let's finish this now! You and me!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hel watches over you now, lovely dove. That settles that.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Agh! Get me off this thing!

speaker: King Burgred
en: Agh! Get me off this thing!

speaker: King Burgred
en: Y-you think you've... won? You haven't! Leofrith... I sent him away with orders to destroy you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quiet.

speaker: King Burgred
en: The mess you're in... you don't know the half of it. You're a blight on this world! The whole lot of you! A rancid disease! You don't deserve Mercia.

speaker: Eivor
en: To the victor the spoils, my lord. You must win Mercia to deserve her.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor! This way!

speaker: Eivor
en: We need to go. Fast!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Right behind you.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Burgred, you old beauty! I hardly recognized you there.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Agh! Put me down!

speaker: Ivarr
en: The only way you go down is with a rope around your neck.

speaker: Sigurd
en: They'll be coming for him. Stay alert.

speaker: Ubba
en: Trouble ahead. Go, we'll cover you.

speaker: Burgred
en: Help!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor, stick his face in the horse's ass.

speaker: Sigurd
en: More of them.

speaker: King Burgred
en: To me, my soldiers! I'm here!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: They've got the king! Don't let them get past us!

speaker: Eivor
en: Here we are. Look familiar?

speaker: King Burgred
en: No... no... you, you Godless slugs. You won't get away with this.

speaker: Ubba
en: Change has come, Burgred. All that remains is a coronation. A with the lords of Mercia.

speaker: Æthelswith
en: Burgred, my love!

speaker: King Burgred
en: My lady! Are you injured? Did they hurt you?

speaker: Æthelswith
en: No, no. I'm fine.

speaker: Eivor
en: Move along, lord. Your king awaits.

speaker: King Burgred
en: Your death will come, Danes. Your end was writ the moment you came for me. I have made damned sure of that!

speaker: King Burgred
en: The Zealots will know your names soon enough. No matter where you are, or how far you travel, they will hunt you down!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Enough of that, you squeaking sparrow.

speaker: Ubba
en: Let my brother be the lunatic of Tamworth.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Zealots... what does he mean?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ignore him. Desperate pleas and prophecies, nothing more.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Walk with me, Wolf-kissed. We have some time before the ceremony.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: What's the password?

speaker: Eivor
en: What? Just let me pass.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: No, that's not how it works! You need to say the password!

speaker: Eivor
en: Apple?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Yes! Welcome, valued customer!

speaker: Eivor
en: Raven?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Ooo! That's better than the one I came up with! Okay, it's Raven from now on. Come in!

speaker: Eivor
en: Get out of my way.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Everyone says that! Fine, spoilsport, on you go.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Welcome to the Tiny Black Market, traveler! Come and browse our treasures!

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are these treasures? I see only odds and ends.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: That's what you think! These three items here are true treasures! We have this special shoe, a shell of all the colors and a petrified worm! Which one do you want to look at?

speaker: Eivor
en: Why are you selling a moldy old shoe?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: This shoe has magical properties. You'll see when you put it on. We stuffed some paper in it to keep it from wrinkling, so you get the paper too.

speaker: Eivor
en: All right, I'll take it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: And the paper inside comes for free! Bargains galore at the Tiny Black Market!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Anything else?

speaker: Eivor
en: This shell looks pretty.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: It carries the whole ocean in it! Truly!

speaker: Eivor
en: Really? I doubt that.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Just place it next to your ear and you'll hear it for yourself!

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a fine thing, regardless. I'll have it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Yes! Another sale!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Anything else?

speaker: Eivor
en: That petrified worm looks a lot like a stick.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: That's because this worm is more than eighty bacrillion years old! Whoever carries it will live forever! Unless you lose it. Then you turn to a pile of dust.

speaker: Eivor
en: That is a powerful enchantment indeed. I will take it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: May you live till the moon falls from the sky!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Anything else?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have better things to do than play this game.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Awww! Fine, then. Come back when you're not being such a grump-bags.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: Anything else?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: You bought all my treasures! Thank you!

speaker: Eivor
en: And never was a coin better spent. Farewell, little one.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's this? The paper inside the shoe has writing on it. Perhaps this is a treasure after all.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Whoa! Look at all this silver! You sold everything?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: I told you! Next, bring your grandmother's tooth. I'll get a fortune for it!

speaker: Toka
en: Wolf-Kissed! I hope your head does not ache like mine. What a night. But we should leave for Francia soon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Pierre.

speaker: Pierre
en: Ready to leave for Francia when you are.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am ready.

speaker: Eivor
en: Francia, the land of Charlemagne and the bitter prize of Ragnar, who sacked Paris for a fortune in silver and sorrow. Now a new king rises, uniting Franks against Norse in open battle, and casting angry eyes towards England.

speaker: Eivor
en: I must stop this mad king from sending war across the sea. Already his armies assemble, and crows gather again over Paris.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham. Now that you and Basim are settled, what will you do?

speaker: Hytham
en: We have work to do. Starting in the cities of England.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham... Randvi asked me to see you. About finding friends in the cities of England.

speaker: Hytham
en: That's right...

speaker: Hytham
en: Lunden, Jorvik, Wincestre... all three are infested by members of the same order to which Kjotve belonged. But their reach extends much further than this. Of all the lands on earth, I believe England is the most overrun.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do they cause here the same turmoil Kjotve caused in Norway?

speaker: Hytham
en: Not just turmoil. They spread a plague of delusion, teaching men and women to abase and abuse themselves in exchange for power.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have strong feelings about this.

speaker: Hytham
en: Of course. This is the sole purpose of the Hidden Ones. To liberate the body and spirit of man from any unnatural shackles. But we have not operated in England for over four centuries. Since the fall of the Roman Empire, the Hidden Ones have not had a presence here. This absence has given the Order of the Ancients ample room to grow and thrive. Our task will not be an easy one now. But with a bureau, Basim and I could begin our work. If you have the time and spare resources to build one, we would be most grateful.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will see what I can do.

speaker: Hytham
en: This will make a fine space for my work, Eivor. Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well if your work benefits us, I will see that you keep it for as long as you live among us.

speaker: Hytham
en: I believe it will, for we have a common cause against our enemy. They have dug their claws deep into England. Eradicate them where they are strongest and the alliances you seek will be far easier to come by. In Lunden, they now operate without restraint. If you were to eradicate them, the city would be in your debt.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will talk with Randvi about your idea. Get her thoughts.

speaker: Hytham
en: Good. Yet before you do, there is something else. A gift I wish to share.

speaker: Eivor
en: A gift?

speaker: Hytham
en: I cannot show you here. Will you walk with me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will. Lead on.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hear a heaviness to your breathing, Hytham. Does your wound still trouble you?

speaker: Hytham
en: It does, I am afraid. There is a pain in my chest for which I have no remedy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rest easy then. So long as your mind stays sharp, you will recover.

speaker: Hytham
en: Of course. Though I am reluctant to displease my mentor.

speaker: Eivor
en: You would risk your health and your life to please Basim? That I do not understand.

speaker: Hytham
en: I should not expect you do. When we first arrived, I noted a shadow of suspicion in your eyes. A doubt, a wariness.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that a question?

speaker: Hytham
en: No. Only an observation.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you well enough to steer this boat?

speaker: Hytham
en: I am, have no worry. It is only prolonged stresses that exhaust me. My energy runs low rather quickly.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what is this gift you wish to give me?

speaker: Hytham
en: It will not come from me. It is a gift you must give yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: More riddles. What fun you are.

speaker: Hytham
en: Let me say it another way. My gift is not for giving or taking. It is a way of living.

speaker: Eivor
en: Still no clearer.

speaker: Hytham
en: It is a thing better demonstrated than described.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I will wait.

speaker: Hytham
en: Forgive my jest. This gift we call a Leap of Faith. It is one of our Brotherhood's most sacred rites. It is not a tool we use against our enemies, but an act we embrace to strengthen our resolve. Like your meditation, it centers our minds, steadies our hands, and purges fear from our hearts. And more practically, it aids our movements, in flight or in stealth.

speaker: Eivor
en: You call it a leap. And we are climbing a rather steep hill...

speaker: Hytham
en: There it is again, the shadow of a doubt. Nearly there. Our destination is there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I suspect you mean to throw me off this cliff. Is that it? Please tell me if I am near the mark.

speaker: Hytham
en: And spoil the surprise? To perform the Leap of Faith, you must give yourself over to something greater.

speaker: Eivor
en: The gods?

speaker: Hytham
en: Yourself. Embrace the hope that death will not come before you are prepared to meet it. Believe this and you will fear nothing.

speaker: Eivor
en: Our deaths are prefigured, weaved into the fabric of the world. To fear this would be a waste of worry and tears.

speaker: Hytham
en: Good. Then your mind is already attuned to my lesson.

speaker: Hytham
en: I will leap first. On my word, you must follow. Lean into your faith, into your strength, and take flight.

speaker: Eivor
en: You want me to jump? From here?

speaker: Hytham
en: Yes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I would sooner grow wings and fly away. Thank you for the lesson, but

speaker: Hytham
en: Wait. And watch.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham! Pig-headed fool, are you injured?!

speaker: Hytham
en: You see? My faith proved stronger than my fear!

speaker: Eivor
en: And that loam cushioned your fall!

speaker: Hytham
en: Eivor, I have not seen this side of you before! Do not feed your fear, conquer it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hmph. I have seen my death in a vision. It was not here, not today.

speaker: Hytham
en: Eivor, are you well? Eivor? Speak! O dear. This is not how I foresaw things. Not at all. Dear God, Basim will have my head for this!

speaker: Hytham
en: A perfect fall. And how did it feel?

speaker: Eivor
en: You spoke true. It was madness and vigor, a purging of fear. A gift I give myself. I see that now. Thank you for showing me the way.

speaker: Hytham
en: Of course. And thank you, Eivor... for hearing me out.

speaker: Eivor
en: You called this Leap of Faith a sacred rite. Do all Hidden Ones practice this same ritual?

speaker: Hytham
en: As far as I know. It is a rite of initiation that dates back to just before the birth of the Christian Jesus.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you hoping to initiate me?

speaker: Hytham
en: I might try if I believed you would join. But that is not my purpose in England. Basim and I are hunting larger prey.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Order of Ancients.

speaker: Hytham
en: Yes. You remember the medallion you took from Kjotve's body? That is their symbol. They are a plague, one we hope to purge from this world. Like us, they act in secret. But their aim is to rule the world, not free it from unnatural fetters.

speaker: Eivor
en: The desire to rule is not unique to this order. Sigurd and I want the same. A land to call our own and the honor that comes with it.

speaker: Hytham
en: Do not compare yourself to such people. The Order has no honor, no principles. No humanity. Yet they sit on a great many of England's thrones. If you seek to pacify England for the safety of your clan...

speaker: Eivor
en: ...then it may be in my interest to give you aid. I understand.

speaker: Hytham
en: You desire alliances. We seek to rid England of its deepening rot. Where these hopes meet, our cause does too. You may think this land ruled by harmless jarls and bumbling thegns, yet look more closely and you will find a deeper threat. The Order's invisible hand touches all. It shapes everything, instilling its poison into every level of society. From the lowliest fishmonger to the richest merchants, from wealthy thegns to useless kings, The Order has corrupted all.

speaker: Hytham
en: Basim has given me one task here. To locate and eliminate The Order of Ancients in England, in whatever dark corners they reside. If we work together towards this end, it will benefit us both. You will have greater influence over the kingdoms of England.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you will have more medallions to count.

speaker: Hytham
en: Exactly. You should begin in Lunden. I have credible reports that The Order is working now to seize the city.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will speak with Randvi about this.

speaker: Hytham
en: And while you are there, be on the lookout for our symbol. Centuries ago, the Hidden Ones had bureaus built around England. There were six, I believe. If you can find them, search them well for documents bearing the same symbol. It will greatly aid my studies.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will. Thank you, Hytham. For all of this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Edyt, there you are.

speaker: Edyt
en: Something you need?

speaker: Eivor
en: I was considering going back to England.

speaker: Edyt
en: Really? The nightmares are still plaguing my people.

speaker: Eivor
en: We must go. There are matters I must take care of in England right now. I will help your people later.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're right. I will stay and end these nightmares.

speaker: Eivor
en: Edyt, how are you?

speaker: Edyt
en: Concerned. The nightmares are still plaguing my people. Would you like to return to the Isle of Skye to help them?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's set out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not right now.

speaker: Groom
en: Doves on a wedding day spell luck... But an eagle? Nothing but doom, nothing but doom.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you alright? I'm here to

speaker: Groom
en: An eagle! An eagle will bring ruin to us all! I saw it in a dream!

speaker: Eivor
en: I won't get much from him. The nightmares certainly seem bad here.

speaker: Cursed Skye Civilian 1
en: It started with a bird's eye view... No! No.. An eagle's eye view.

speaker: Eivor
en: You. What can you tell me about this nightmares everyone is having?

speaker: Cursed Skye Civilian 1
en: Tell you?! Tell you?! I don't need to tell you about them. They will come for you soon enough. These nightmares spread like a plague. Worse than a plague! Sickening your mind...

speaker: Eivor
en: Vivid, but not useful.

speaker: Bride
en: No beauty sleep before my wedding? And dreams of my ex-lover ruining it to start a fight? Was it a dream or... a premonition?

speaker: Eivor
en: Is everything all right? You seem−

speaker: Bride
en: Find the warrior woman with the braid! She is our undoing! Stealing our dreams!

speaker: Eivor
en: A warrior with a braid? That can't be Randvi. Where is she?

speaker: Bride
en: At a church Northwest of town! That's all I saw in my dreams. Find her and please, let me sleep.

speaker: Eivor
en: Strange. Valka did say her vision was cloudy. Was she seeing Randvi in this aura? And a graveyard... Or as Valka put it, a scene of death.

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka was right. Randvi!

speaker: Stranger
en: No.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you are?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your opponent.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So is this Randvi good with an axe?

speaker: Eivor
en: She is. Much better than you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eh, I prefer a spear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You favor other weapons, too. Where'd you get that blade?

speaker: Eivor
en: You talk too much.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like there are some things to talk about.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine. If we must.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, "opponent". Do you have a name?

speaker: Eivor
en: Eivor. I take it you're one of the Hidden Ones?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not exactly. But I admire their work.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you're not going to talk straight, let's go back to fighting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not a Hidden One, but I have friends that are. And often, my goals align with theirs. I assume the same is true for you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. I've made friends with the Hidden Ones and I agree with their goals.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then perhaps we might have more in common than we thought.

speaker: Eivor
en: While I appreciate their gifts, I'm not sure I trust fighters so cloaked in secrecy. I prefer more direct methods of battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Clearly.

speaker: Eivor
en: You haven't told me why you're here. After coming all the way from... where?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've travelled so much, it's been a long time since I've been from somewhere. But the Greek world was my home long ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I came here looking for an ancient artifact that's causing this island a great deal of trouble.

speaker: Eivor
en: You mean the nightmares? A seer told me that the person I'd find amidst death on this island was causing them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The same one that mistook me for someone named Randvi? Maybe your seer is having an off day.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're telling you're not responsible for all these bodies?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I watched these people tear each other apart out of madness and lack of sleep. It's the artifact I'm looking for causing all of this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Normally, I'd be quick to track it down but this fog is making things... difficult. Almost impossible.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you're so easily blocked by a curse, how do you expect to deal with the realm of spirits and dreams?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A curse? You know the secrets of this land well, then. I

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you hear something?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, no. Listen, something tells me we should work together.

speaker: Eivor
en: And what exactly is telling you that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The obvious! You want to stop the nightmares and I want the artifact causing them. Help me get rid of this fog so we can find it.

speaker: Eivor
en: After such a strange encounter, I'm really meant to believe you're not causing the nightmares?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I swear to you, I am here to stop them.

speaker: Eivor
en: We can work together. For now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Give me a hand over here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. Here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're quite strong.

speaker: Eivor
en: You should know. I had you cornered in that fight just moments ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And an even stronger ego to match. Not surprising.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What an interesting church. In all my travels, I've never seen one quite like this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you here to see the sights or get rid of this fog?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have to take in what I can. It's not as if I plan to stay long.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nice work! The curse is fading. It'll be much easier to find the artifact now. Glad I let you tag along to help.

speaker: Eivor
en: I did most of the work. You're getting on my nerves, you know?

speaker: Kassandra
en: These close quarters probably aren't helping. Let's find a way out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're crazed from lack of sleep—just like the men I saw tearing one another apart earlier.

speaker: Eivor
en: Better take them out before they take us down, then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Cold, but I agree.

speaker: Cursed Skye Civilian 2
en: Eagle Bearer! You caused this! You're responsible for our suffering!

speaker: Eivor
en: Was he talking to you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They've been driven to madness. It's just nonsense. Watch out!

speaker: Cursed Skye Civilian 3
en: You're treading on the wrong god's land! We will purge you of it!

speaker: Eivor
en: It really seems like he's addressing you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The madman? We're dear friends!

speaker: Eivor
en: It really seemed like someone was talking directly to you in the fight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The artifact I'm seeking does cause strange things to occur. But I should track it more easily now that the fog is gone.

speaker: Eivor
en: As if a foreigner could search these hills.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ready to commit to being my guide?

speaker: Eivor
en: I didn't say that. If I'm going to help, I need more information. Like what exactly is this artifact you're seeking?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The less you know about it the better.

speaker: Eivor
en: The better for you, you mean. You want me to trust you, no?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The artifact is an object of great power left here by old gods. Left on the island, it could wreak havoc on the world.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why aren't we under whatever spell or curse this artifact seems to have placed over everyone else?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It is difficult to explain, but artifacts like this can affect people differently. Many are corrupted by them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perhaps we are of a similar... strength. But even if we're not having nightmares, we should still be wary of its power.

speaker: Eivor
en: If this artifact is ancient and was left here who knows how long ago, why is it suddenly causing problems now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Loki got bored?

speaker: Kassandra
en: So serious. Truthfully, I'm not sure. These artifacts can be activated. Maybe someone tampered with it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: After all, many are drawn to its powers. It tempts them.

speaker: Eivor
en: How exactly are you planning to track it down?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave that to me. Finding these artifacts has been my calling for some time now. I've developed a knack for tracking them down. With the aura gone, it should be even easier to find.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's not waste time. What's our next move?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now that this fog is gone, I should be able to better track the artifact's location. Before that, though...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going to take another look around the church. See what I can learn of these foreign lands. Meet me in Tobhta?

speaker: Eivor
en: It'll take more than studying one church to become familiar with this island. But fine. We'll meet again soon.

speaker: Azar
en: Drumlish has joined our trade network. Their dyed cloth is among the finest. They are able to produce the seven royal colors.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where I come from, dye is used for tattoos.

speaker: Azar
en: In Shiraz as well. Here, Drumlish cloth will brighten any heart.

speaker: Azar
en: Illuminated gospels have arrived from Lisdurrow thanks to the new trade post you claimed. I am impressed.

speaker: Eivor
en: You doubted me?

speaker: Azar
en: I meant the manuscripts. Their crafting is magnificent.

speaker: Azar
en: I am reading the books you procured from Dysert. I see why you went to the other end of Ireland to get them.

speaker: Eivor
en: I took the trade post without knowing the cargo. If the books are good, so much the better.

speaker: Azar
en: For people who believe in holy scripture, these books are worth more than gold.

speaker: Azar
en: Thanks to you, Ardmel joined our trade. Their sweet honey will lure our most demanding merchants.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is honey so valuable?

speaker: Azar
en: It is liquid gold! But luscious and sticky.

speaker: Azar
en: Thanks to your efforts, the jewels and ivory from Port Auley now grace our stocks. Is there anything you cannot do?

speaker: Eivor
en: The list is long.

speaker: Azar
en: I find that difficult to believe.

speaker: Azar
en: Athlone has begun to send us excellent ale. From experience, I can tell you this is dangerous cargo.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've never seen a shipment of ale reach its destination without losing a barrel or two.

speaker: Azar
en: My crew knows the cost of hitting the stocks. Everything will ship and we shall reap riches. With ale to celebrate!

speaker: Treasures of River Berbha
en: was a virtual representation of one of Eivor Varinsdottir's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Treasures of River Dee
en: was a virtual representation of one of Eivor Varinsdottir's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vagn! I return to you victorious and as the new owner of Lugh's armor!

speaker: Vagn
en: Very impressive! Not too bad for just another myth, eh?

speaker: Treasures of River Exe
en: was a virtual representation of one of Eivor Varinsdottir's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Treasures of River Severn
en: was a virtual representation of one of Eivor Varinsdottir's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is all this?

speaker: Thyra
en: A new Yule game to test your skills: Twirling Targets. You shoot as many spinning targets as you can, as quick as you can. Care to give it a go?

speaker: Eivor
en: Put a bow in my hand.

speaker: Thyra
en: Take a moment to center yourself and then go! Freya's love! Incredible shooting! Glad I bet on you to win this! By Odin's eye, you shoot well! You make this look easy! You make your ancestors proud!

speaker: Thyra
en: You're half the way there, Eivor!

speaker: Thyra
en: Time's almost up!

speaker: Thyra
en: You've done it! You've achieved perfection. I did not think I would ever see such a score.

speaker: Birstan
en: No troubles bestir your heart, do they, Percy? All you think of is what next to eat. How I envy you. There, there, old hound. Hold faith, for soon we'll be hunting. A man, his dog, and the outdoors. What greater pleasure can there be than this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Birstan. Estrid said you'd be here.

speaker: Birstan
en: Eivor, dearheart! You who drew back the bow of Eros and reunited me with my one true love.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have your thegns asked why you do not look for Estrid?

speaker: Birstan
en: Pish! They have asked, yes. I said it was hopeless. Then I lay upon my couch sobbing and wailing. A pretty show.

speaker: Eivor
en: That may not be enough.

speaker: Birstan
en: Tut tut! The winds are soft upon our faces, and I am far from the whispering doors of Colcestre. Come, let's hunt!

speaker: Eivor
en: What are we hunting now?

speaker: Birstan
en: Boar! A majestic animal, don't you think? Driven by a fierce fire, blazing eyes, and sword-tusks.

speaker: Eivor
en: I once knew a strong-armed shieldmaiden who rode a boar into battle! She named it Bristle-bold.

speaker: Birstan
en: How wondrously strange! Your tales are worthy of the hearing. We'll not ride our boars but eat them! A feast in Alfida's honor.

speaker: Eivor
en: A feast for your mistress? Birstan, if this ruse falls apart, King Aelfred will strip you of your title. Our alliance would be worthless.

speaker: Birstan
en: Have no fear! I shall be discreet! We will eat and sup at my hall with a few friends and family. It is there our friendship will be sealed.

speaker: Eivor
en: So soon after Lammas. Will people there not recognize me?

speaker: Birstan
en: No, you are just one more Dane! And in that chaos, who remembers anything but the screams of dear Estrid?

speaker: Eivor
en: These are your lands. I trust in your judgment. And how is Alfida?

speaker: Birstan
en: She is a firebrand! We have rekindled our love as if we were teenagers. Even Eluric is a welcome addition. A younger brother to me, yet more alike to a son. The things I should like to teach him. Ah, this is the spot, the best boar here!

speaker: Birstan
en: Look at that fat hog! He'll make a delicious roast. They are fearsome beasts. But tasty! Come on, the feast table won't fill itself! I shall suck the scrumptious marrow from your bones, you porcine devil! You will serve my love well, hog. A haunch worthy of her arrival.

speaker: Birstan
en: My bow-arm aches! We did well, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: A good hunt, Birstan!

speaker: Birstan
en: And enough for one day I think. Even my thegns will not go hungry with this catch, and they are as voracious as wolves snatching at my carcass!

speaker: Eivor
en: They may give you grief, but I've been nothing but amused. They're a welcome change to warring jarls and piss-sodden politics.

speaker: Birstan
en: You have brought us all true happiness, Eivor. I thank you, from the bottom of a heart full up from joy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birstan, the heart-hound who sought his true love by searching the sad haven of his memory and finding her there.

speaker: Birstan
en: Beautifully said, my friend! Beautifully said. Come Percy, you hapless hound! Barely a boar worried, I do not know why I keep you in my employ.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Our lord is back! Gather up, men! Let's go collect the fruits of the master's hunt.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are your plans for Essexe and your family?

speaker: Birstan
en: There is much that is new in this old fling. Alfida is changed... the girl I fell in love with lies behind years of hardship.

speaker: Eivor
en: And Eluric?

speaker: Birstan
en: A soft lad, but with a heart as stout as his sister's. Their closeness does them both credit. The way he looks at me is often strange. His eyes furtive and downcast, like a hound waiting for his master's crop. It worries me, to be honest. Can I be both a brother to him and love to his sister?

speaker: Eivor
en: Give him time, Birstan. He had his sister to himself all his life.

speaker: Birstan
en: Yes, yes. But tell me, Eivor. Did you succumb to my flighted bird's charms? She can turn one atremble with her eyes.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're talking of Estrid?

speaker: Birstan
en: Do not be coy. It does not suit you.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not coyness that keeps me quiet, Birstan. We grew close. I won't say more.

speaker: Birstan
en: Fair enough. I should not pry.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you jealous, Birstan? After casting her aside?

speaker: Birstan
en: Of course not! I could not be happier. I only wondered... for her sake.

speaker: Birstan
en: All that to say, I am only glad she has found a chance at happiness again. Lord knows I could not give her that. But these are grim thoughts, and I will not let them lay their cold grip upon me. Tonight we feast and celebrate!

speaker: Birstan
en: Home and hearth never used to stir the soul as the hunt did. But now my Alfida is here, all is changed.

speaker: Alfida
en: Birstan! You promised we would never be apart, not for one waking or sleeping moment! And already you're sneaking out to hunt!

speaker: Birstan
en: For the feast, sweetling. We owe our mutual friend a great debt. One that I promised to repay over suckling pig and ale.

speaker: Eluric
en: Sister, have you forgotten where you are?

speaker: Alfida
en: I have a right to happiness, Eluric! Or am I to play nursemaid forever, you ungrateful pup?

speaker: Eluric
en: Happiness, yes. But you embarrass yourself nightly, heaving and sweating with this ham hock!

speaker: Alfida
en: Hold your tongue, boy! Lest we both speak our truths!

speaker: Eluric
en: What truth have you to speak? That you've returned to this fickle man who abandoned you years ago for a a Frankish pet? A woman he paid this Dane to abduct in that Lammas shadow play?

speaker: Eivor
en: Mind yourself, boy.

speaker: Eluric
en: Or that you let him sniff and paw you and take him to your bed on a promise of nothing? The whole of Essexe whispers now! He's married still, his wife freshly stolen, and you are no more than... than his...

speaker: Alfida
en: I am the mother of his child, you whelp!

speaker: Birstan
en: Child? Alfida...?

speaker: Alfida
en: Please, my boy, I...

speaker: Eluric
en: I will never forgive you for this. Never!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: My lord! Joyous news! God smiles upon us this very day! Estrid has been found by Aelfred's men. They ride to her rescue as we speak!

speaker: Eivor
en: I will not let this plot be undone.

speaker: Birstan
en: Nothing is safe until they are away to Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will fix this, and one day I will call on you, and you will come.

speaker: Birstan
en: You can count on it, my friend.

speaker: Alfida
en: I wanted to tell you, so many times.

speaker: Birstan
en: Hush, angel. Do not fret so.

speaker: Alfida
en: He hates me. What have I done? We must go after him!

speaker: Birstan
en: He will not stray far, lamb. Much has been said this day. But if... if he is my son... our son... we must believe he will return to us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you leering at me, lord?

speaker: Aldrich
en: You, Birstan's hired Dane. Do not think what you did went unseen. Yet tell me one thing. Is Estrid safe? And happy?

speaker: Eivor
en: She's happy, that much I know.

speaker: Aldrich
en: Good. Now leave. And if we meet again, you will fall by my sword.

speaker: Eadred
en: Estrid should have ruled this land, I would have followed her anywhere.

speaker: Eivor
en: Estrid is so close to freedom. I hope I am not too late.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rollo! Aelfred's men have found you!

speaker: Rollo
en: What? How can this be?

speaker: Eivor
en: Lork, stand by Estrid, guard her with your life. If she is taken, all is lost for us and Birstan.

speaker: Lork
en: Come, lady. It would not do for them to take you back. Watch out!

speaker: Rollo
en: Lork! Odin, no!

speaker: Rollo
en: What? Found us how? Were we betrayed?

speaker: Eivor
en: Gerhild, you protect Estrid. If she is taken, all is lost for Birstan.

speaker: Eivor
en: They will skewer us like suckling pigs!

speaker: Gerhild
en: Saxons! We have your whore-queen! Come take her.

speaker: Rollo
en: Gerhild... you fetid blood-blister! Was it you?

speaker: Rollo
en: Treacherous she-wolf! Damn you!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Release the woman, Danes! If she's unharmed, we may let some of you live.

speaker: Rollo
en: Here come the bastards! Protect Estrid, prepare the ship!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Kill Rollo the Imprudent!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: Stop that ship from sailing!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Look to the north! More Saxons!

speaker: Estrid
en: Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Estrid. I promised I would free you of your life in Wessex. Francia awaits your return. Go now, with Aegir's blessing.

speaker: Estrid
en: I will miss you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: When winter is past, summer will come and wind you in a flowered skirt. For you are beauty and shall not wither.

speaker: Rollo
en: Goddess Freyja, give me more of that!

speaker: Eivor
en: Come. Take care of her, Rollo Stoutheart. And if you find yourself on England's shores again, I will expect you in my hall.

speaker: Eivor
en: Estrid!

speaker: Rollo
en: Gods! Gerhild the traitor? I should have listened to my gut! I always hated the way she carried herself, glared at me. This is my fault, Estrid. Mine alone.

speaker: Estrid
en: Stop chiding yourself, Rollo. You could not have known it would come to this.

speaker: Eivor
en: Can you move? I can pull the arrow from you, but I fear what pain it will cause.

speaker: Estrid
en: I can stand... If I can lean upon you, Rollo?

speaker: Rollo
en: If we stay here, we die. Come, sweet bird, I'll take you to the ship, and we'll tend your wounds. You will see Francia yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: When winter is past, summer will come and wind you in a flowered skirt. For you are beauty and shall not wither. Take care of her, Rollo Stoutheart. And if you find yourself on England's shores again, I will welcome you in my hall.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. They are safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Estrid's wound was grave. But she'll live long enough to see the shores of Francia. If only that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Birstan got his end of the bargain, and Estrid is to Francia. I should return to Randvi.

speaker: Eivor
en: Raided. Someone has been here.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Barely two days since we took the sword and now, gone! Bah!

speaker: French Soldier 2
en: Merde... I blame Herbric. He must have been sleeping at his post that night.

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Now he sleeps in Hell, well deserved.

speaker: Eivor
en: Scattered swords on the ground... the thieves must be looking for a weapon.

speaker: Eivor
en: A letter, and a map. The thieves left evidence. They stole an Ulfberht sword? If rumors are true, that blade is made of crucible steel. Might be worth looking for.

speaker: Bo
en: Beautiful... simply beautiful... mine, only mine! It was worth it. Truly, it was. For you belong only to me. Me! Only me! Ah, my friends, I weep for you. You should have let me have it!

speaker: Eivor
en: That sword you hold, the one you stole from the camp

speaker: Bo
en: We stole. These men and I. But there is only one sword and can be only one owner. Týr's Hand is now mine. My dear friends, my brothers, my kinsmen! They coveted it, but I could not let them have it. No... I had no choice...

speaker: Eivor
en: An Ulfberht sword, made from crucible steel. I've never seen one up close. It sells for a large amount of coin.

speaker: Bo
en: There is almost no price that can match the sword. It has both immense power and beauty. Once you wield this sword, you will understand. Though that will not happen. If you want it, there is only one way. We must fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Look at me. Look well. Do I look like these men? Make the wise choice and give me the sword.

speaker: Bo
en: I am looking. I am seeing. I... No. I killed my brothers, I must have it. Else it will be all for naught...

speaker: Eivor
en: They are gone, and you deserve no respite for betraying your kin. Leave the blade, walk away, and never appear before me again.

speaker: Bo
en: Beautiful... simply beautiful... mine, only mine! It was worth it. Truly, it was. For you belong only to me. Me! Only me! Ah, my friends, I weep for you. You should have let me have it!

speaker: Eivor
en: He killed his men. His brothers, his kinsmen. All for a sword.

speaker: Eivor
en: Would you not part with it for a hefty sum of coin?

speaker: Bo
en: Týr's Hand has no price! It is priceless, an object of the gods! But... how hefty are we talking?

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite hefty.

speaker: Bo
en: Then I shall accept. I will take the coin and live for my brothers. Now, leave me.

speaker: Eivor
en: The one and only way it shall be. We fight.

speaker: Bo
en: Your confidence is heartening, but you chose wrong, friend. None can hope to hold against this master-crafted blade!

speaker: Eivor
en: Give up the sword and you can walk away with your life.

speaker: Bo
en: You think me afraid? Look around you! These were my brothers, my friends!

speaker: Eivor
en: You would die for a piece of metal?

speaker: Bo
en: Fool! This is no ordinary metal! It is mine!

speaker: Eivor
en: Now to take the sword for my own.

speaker: Eivor
en: A fine weapon. Heh, I should probably not let Toka see this.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Did you consult the volva?

speaker: Sunniva
en: And were your questions answered?

speaker: Eivor
en: Some questions were answered. Others I must answer myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you think there is a place for Vili in our settlement? He expressed a desire to live and work with us.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Will he not be jarl of this shire before the day's end?

speaker: Eivor
en: That remains to be seen. Some are more eager to see Trygve in the high seat.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Eivor, Trygve has no intention to lead. He feels duty bound to follow his master into death.

speaker: Vili
en: Absolutely not! My father would never allow such foolishness!

speaker: Trygve
en: How else can I honor my jarl, old as I am? This is no country for me. The future is yours, Vili.

speaker: Vili
en: The flames of this pyre will burn for my father. You must live! I forbid you to follow him into death. I will not let you sacrifice yourself!

speaker: Trygve
en: Do you forbid me as a friend, Vili? Or as our new jarl?

speaker: Vili
en: As a man who would see you come to your senses!

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili. Trygve. Each man wears one of Hemming's boot, with both men unwilling to seize the other.

speaker: Odin
en: Does the world need such useless, dithering men? Why not stake a claim yourself? Take this shire for your own.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not my place.

speaker: Odin
en: Your place is anywhere you lay your head, any hill you summit, any silver you take for your own. Do not limit yourself to niceties.

speaker: Eivor
en: Snotinghamscire deserves a leader to admire. A man the people can trust. Most love Vili, and he loves them. But he lacks the will to be a leader. He could learn... but does he wish to? And Trygve... sturdy and wise and loyal to the legacy Hemming Jarl left behind. Almost to a fault. But he is old and his thrill for living has fled him. Hardly inspiring.

speaker: Vili
en: You cannot! I will not allow it!

speaker: Trygve
en: I am not asking for your permission. Only your forgiveness.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods, Eivor. Put a stop to this fool's death wish.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is no small decision, Trygve, and not without great cost. The shire will be diminished without you.

speaker: Trygve
en: But I... I have nobody left. My life's purpose lies dead upon that pyre.

speaker: Vili
en: That is not so. When people looked to my father for guidance, who did they see him turn to for counsel?

speaker: Trygve
en: Hemming Jarl was my rock. Yes, I gave him counsel, but he made the hard choices.

speaker: Eivor
en: If Hemming were here, would he not urge you to wield this wisdom for the betterment of all? And was your vow to serve Hemming Jarl unto death? Or to serve his legacy in life?

speaker: Trygve
en: I will stay. You have wisdom, Eivor. More than I could have guessed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Trygve has no jarl to serve, Vili. He's free to set his own course to the ocean's edge, to trade this world for the next. As are you, Vili. Our lives belong to us.

speaker: Trygve
en: Thank you... thank you, Eivor. Vili, do not misplace your anger on friends who speak what they believe is truth.

speaker: Vili
en: Do as you must, Trygve. I... I will miss you, old friend.

speaker: Trygve
en: And I you, my boy.

speaker: Trygve
en: I must prepare myself for the flames. Body and spirit.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hm? Sunniva?

speaker: Sunniva
en: Picts were spotted moments ago, lurking in the thicket. Vili gave chase.

speaker: Eivor
en: Arse-Stick, he should have roused me first. Show me where he went.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Let us wake the others. The dark is lousing with Picts.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can take them on myself. Tell me where.

speaker: Sunniva
en: They're not far. I'll show you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell no one of this. The last thing we need is a dozen more bodies for Hemming's pyre. This will be a fine tale to tell after the Althing. But until then, we stay quiet.

speaker: Eivor
en: The nobles are too drunk to join this fight. It would be a slaughter on both sides.

speaker: Sunniva
en: You know best, drengr. Just... take care, will you?

speaker: Sunniva
en: His rage has consumed him, Eivor. All this anger, this sadness, it has truly taken form.

speaker: Eivor
en: Arse-Stick was never one to temper his emotions. This was bound to happen. I should have been more vigilant.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Do not blame yourself, drengr.

speaker: Eivor
en: He always had me to watch his back. As children, and again now. If this rampage is what he needs to rid himself of the sick that binds him, I will at least make sure he does not hurt himself.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Thank Odin, he has the mighty Wolf-Kissed as his shadow.

speaker: Eivor
en: There are things we do for family, Sunniva. No questions asked. For you, I would have done the same. For any of Raven Clan.

speaker: Sunniva
en: We know, drengr. That is why we are sworn to you.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Here, Eivor. This was where Vili saw the scout killed and then charged after the enemy ahead. I will head back to Hemthorpe and make sure our ravens stand vigilant. Return to us safely, drengr.

speaker: Vili
en: Eivor? Perfect. I could use your edge right now.

speaker: Vili
en: You dare disturb these days of mourning!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stop, Vili. They're gone. It's done.

speaker: Vili
en: Bah, I've seen roosters fight with more spirit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oddly enough, so have I.

speaker: Vili
en: That sound. Is it thunder?

speaker: Eivor
en: Footsteps.

speaker: Vili
en: We need to fall back. Follow me. Quickly!

speaker: Vili
en: Thrilling, was it not? Just like when we were children, getting into trouble and getting away.

speaker: Eivor
en: Save your honey-words for when we get out of here alive, Arse-stick.

speaker: Vili
en: A moment to catch my breath.

speaker: Vili
en: Ah, by Thor's Thunder-hammer... that quickened the blood!

speaker: Eivor
en: Wild and reckless. Like our first battles together. Remember, the island north of Stavenger?

speaker: Vili
en: I do. Kjotve the Cruel trained his beserkers there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Great lumbering fools, foaming at the mouth. We taunted them from the tree tops.

speaker: Vili
en: And the drunk one, remember! Naked at the morning! Froze his cock off trying to find us!

speaker: Eivor
en: Then fell to humping a snowdrift.

speaker: Vili
en: Were you glad to hear from me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I did wonder what trouble you had been up to. But I smiled at hearing your name. And I wondered if you had taken after your father. If you were now leading your clan.

speaker: Vili
en: Well, you have your answer. I'd sooner take after a troll and leave this clan in your hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: That I will not do.

speaker: Vili
en: When my father was named jarl, he had no one to help him and still he triumphed. But I am not my father. I... I simply want to roam. Do you think Sleipnir would be content bound to a stable, no matter how glorious it may be?

speaker: Vili
en: Hey! What is that for?

speaker: Eivor
en: You have friends, Vili. And what about Trygve? And me? And your clan?

speaker: Vili
en: Of course, I know that.

speaker: Eivor
en: You can't roam forever. Keep that in mind. You are surrounded by those who love you. And that will not change unless you push it all away.

speaker: Vili
en: You... you speak a truth I understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Troll-faced, arse-stick.

speaker: Vili
en: A chicken draugr? Is such a thing possible? For that does not seem possible!

speaker: Eivor
en: Voda too! A water infused with fire. I do not lie.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your father's death aside, Vili. This has been... good. Fun, even.

speaker: Vili
en: Do you ever wonder what might have happened if we had not been separated by the North Sea so early in our lives? What adventures we would have had. The raids, the battle, the glory. I even think about what we might have been to each other.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have, fondly. And often enough that it sometimes seemed you never left. Maybe you never did.

speaker: Vili
en: I... I want you, Eivor. Your warmth. Your touch.

speaker: Eivor
en: Like this?

speaker: Vili
en: I cannot say how I feel tommorow, Eivor...

speaker: Eivor
en: Shut up, Vili.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili. You know that... that this was a momentary heat. Just a flickering flame.

speaker: Vili
en: Yes. We let our passions set sail, just this once. I should get back. Rest. The funeral will still be there when you wake up fully.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili... no. That will not happen. I'm sorry.

speaker: Eivor
en: Get some rest, hey?

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you going?

speaker: Vili
en: O, with so much on my mind, I haven't slept a wink. The funeral. The thegns. I should get back.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. I'll see you there.

speaker: Eivor
en: No. I never dwell on our past that way. I find it slows me down to a crawl. And I'm not made for crawling.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll think I'll turn in. Long day ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you going?

speaker: Vili
en: O, with so much on my mind, I haven't slept a wink. The funeral. The thegns. I should get back.

speaker: Eivor
en: I understand. I'll see you there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Vili... gone already. To prepare for the funeral I imagine.

speaker: Lif
en: This priest blows as much air as a hailstorm! He cannot be allowed to keep spewing.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Did you sail through a storm? You never mentioned.

speaker: Lif
en: Eivor! A fine day for being out, no?

speaker: Eivor
en: Soma said I would find you here, Lif. What's your plan?

speaker: Lif
en: We're ridding the world of a priest who spouts praise for the ealdorman, and funnels into Wigmund's coffers. So the plan is this... We sneak in, gut the priest, and return to Soma. That'll get Wigmund steaming.

speaker: Eivor
en: How did you come to join Soma's army?

speaker: Lif
en: We came to England together, sailing under Guthrum. The Great Summer Army the Saxons called us. When Guthrum left for Wessex, Soma stepped forward to lead. Something I would have liked to do myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: What would you do if you were the Jarl of Grantebridge?

speaker: Lif
en: I would run the city my own way. I would not give Birna and Galinn's opinions equal weight.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you not trust them?

speaker: Lif
en: I wouldn't say that. It's more... Birna's boots are stuck in the mud. And Galinn's are in the sky. If death were bearing down upon us, I worry neither would have what it takes to carry us through.

speaker: Eivor
en: You were there when Guthrum made Soma the steward of Grantebridge. How did that feel?

speaker: Lif
en: Good fortune for her! When Soma took hold, the silver started flowing, and the people started dancing. She knows trade. I do wish I had been bold enough to put myself forward, to take on the burden and honor of running a city. But that is beside the point. Soma is my jarlskona, and I am her sworn man. No act of any god will change that.

speaker: Eivor
en: As a master shipbuilder, what does your work require?

speaker: Lif
en: Patience and love. I know each of our vessels as a parent knows their child. But building ships needs silver too. The hard wood, the tough fabrics, the expensive paints. The yellow I use, for instance... that must be imported. A high price for a happy color. I'm certain that's why someone stole my paints some weeks ago. Blasted thief.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good conversation, Lif. Now, let's take down Wigmund's man.

speaker: Lif
en: Too right, too right. Wigmund's whelp awaits his reward. My warriors will distract the Saxon forces at the gate. You and I will find the priest.

speaker: Lif
en: You know, I would much prefer a more straightforward approach. But for you, I'll try something new.

speaker: Eivor
en: How kind. Now keep your voice down.

speaker: Lif
en: Now this is how I like it! None of this skulking around nonsense!

speaker: Eivor
en: Wigmund's priest is in the church.

speaker: Lif
en: Well, well. I may be a heathen in the Saxons' eyes, but this church is lovely. I know good craftsmanship when I see it.

speaker: Lif
en: Ah! Look at this structure? The trees they must have hewn, the devices they must have used to lift stone! Solid work.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you in the midst of a conversion, Lif? Shall I steal a small cross for you as well?

speaker: Lif
en: No! Never! Can't a craftsman drool over... other... crafts?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Lord Wigmund of Walden carries with him the blessings of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ! We may be chopped, roasted, and eaten by these pagan cannibals. But our lives have meaning if they end in his name.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Guards! Help! Help! Wigmund should have killed you all off the first time!

speaker: Lif
en: The priest's lies will not poison the shire any more. We should leave.

speaker: Letter from Wigmund
en: Father Cuthbert, I want to thank you for your continued support. I must say I am charmed by your pupils. They are endowed with an obedience that I suspect can only be attributed to your wisdom and guidance. Please, continue sending them my way. It pleases me to speak with such spry young men, eager to learn about the Order of the Ancients. There is much for them to gain and they are welcome to follow this great cause. Wigmund

speaker: Eivor
en: Well struck. We made short work of Wigmund's man.

speaker: Lif
en: That we did. You've proven yourself an asset to us. I'll see you back in Grantebridge.

speaker: Eivor
en: Does this stir your thirst for battle, Randvi?

speaker: Randvi
en: It does!

speaker: Eivor
en: There is nothing for you here but death!

speaker: Dag
en: Go to your graves!

speaker: Randvi
en: For Raven Clan!

speaker: Randvi
en: Their numbers are flagging! Press on!

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Kill any who stand in your way!

speaker: Eivor
en: Who sent you to die here?

speaker: Randvi
en: Only a few cowards left! Drive them off!

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: No survivors! Burn them to the ground!!

speaker: Eivor
en: You will meet only death here!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is that the last of them?

speaker: Randvi
en: The rivers are clear. If more were coming, they thought better of it.

speaker: Eivor
en: By their colors and markings, I believe they come from . But with none left alive to spill their secrets, we may never know why.

speaker: Dag
en: Here is one!

speaker: Dag
en: This vermin was crawling to the river, hoping to float away!

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Have mercy, friend, and you may find an ally with us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mercy is earned by the quickness of your tongue. Where do you come from and what is your quarrel with us?

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: We are settled... in East Anglia. Newly arrived... and hungry for silver.

speaker: Eivor
en: You drifted off course. This is Mercia.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: As we were ordered.

speaker: Eivor
en: By whom?

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: You bore me.

speaker: Dag
en: Useless hound, scratching your ass in search of silver. Put an end to this one.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your silence earns you no kindness, Geat. So I will ask you once more. Who sent you?

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: The wind sent us. And the rivers will take us home.

speaker: Dag
en: He begs for death, Eivor! Give it to him.

speaker: Randvi
en: Or send him home with a warning. Let him tell his people what death awaits them, should they sail this way again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go. And do not return.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: I thank you

speaker: Eivor
en: This is not mercy, it is death deferred. Whoever sent you, warn them of the slaughter that awaits should any return.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: O, what tales I will tell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Send one of your scouts to follow him. We will find

speaker: Eivor
en: Dag!

speaker: Dag
en: To show mercy would endanger us! Soil our reputation as cowards! This was the only end possible!

speaker: Eivor
en: We could have learned something by tracking him. Now we know nothing.

speaker: Dag
en: Sigurd would have acted as I did. That is all the justification I need.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd is not here to make such a call. But I am. And if you cross me again, he will know about it.

speaker: Dag
en: I see you, Eivor. And I know what you are.

speaker: Randvi
en: Put no stock in what Dag says. His bluster may be loud, but it blows softly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Get this cleaned up. Then we will talk of next steps.

speaker: Eivor
en: May there be one who mourns you at home, for we will not.

speaker: Randvi
en: Eivor, I could have sent my scouts to follow him home. We might have learned something.

speaker: Eivor
en: The price of such disrespect is death, Randvi.

speaker: Dag
en: Just as Sigurd would have done.

speaker: Randvi
en: I cannot devise a strategy if my advice is ignored.

speaker: Dag
en: To let that man live would announce to the world that we are soft and cowardly. Now these wayward Danes know to fear us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Forgive my haste, Randvi. But Dag is right.

speaker: Dag
en: For once you see clearly. I beg the gods that it continues.

speaker: Randvi
en: We should clean this mess, and move the bodies from the camp.

speaker: Eivor
en: Agreed. Then we talk of our next steps. Together.

speaker: Letter from Soma
en: Eivor, You entered my mind today. I was thinking about how I felt when I lost Grantebridge. The anger. The doubt. You helped me reclaim my city, but you did more than that. You helped me reclaim what I had lost in myself. Today, my people, my city-- they are stronger than they've ever been. And I am a proud leader once more. Soma

speaker: Eivor
en: Ceolbert? Are you well?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I am, but... I wish I could have risen to the challenge put before us. Instead of hiding here in the longhouse.

speaker: Eivor
en: You were exactly where you needed to be. Defending the people. And yourself.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I know, I just...

speaker: Eivor
en: Our forces outside were sufficient. And your father would have many unkind words for me if anything had happened to you.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I know, I only wish my father's long shadow didn't darken my prospects here. I want to learn from you, not watch you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no doubt. Next time, then.

speaker: Hytham
en: Eivor, again your people impress me with your skill. The invaders barely stood a chance.

speaker: Gunnar
en: Ha! Those invaders never stood a chance. Not when you are armed with Gunnar's handiwork.

speaker: Saxon Bandit 1
en: Oi, what's this? A mess of filthy Danes befouling our riverways?

speaker: Saxon Bandit 2
en: You there. Give us your name.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I am Sigurd Jarl of Fornburg. And you are?

speaker: Saxon Bandit 2
en: Men who do not take kindly to Dane invaders creeping into our camp. You'd best move along, pagan. Spare yourselves a slaughter.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You threaten Norsemen with a play of swords, and expect us to cower?

speaker: Dag
en: I have been eight days at sea without a drop of blood to whet my axe. So spare the chatter, bacraut (asshole), and draw your weapon.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Let's finish them.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier
en: Kill these heathen bastards!

speaker: Sigurd
en: You had your chance to turn away! And it passed you by!

speaker: Dag
en: Like a blade through butter!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Have a look around, all of you. I want no more surprises.

speaker: Eivor
en: Right. I will check the longhouse.

speaker: Dag
en: Thought I would find at least one of those fools squirreled away somewhere.

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: These folks know nothing of tending to their weapons. Careless fools.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Eivor... look at this.

speaker: Eivor
en: A noise trap. Might be something inside. I will have a look.

speaker: Yanli
en: W-wait, who are you? Are you with those brigands as well?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd! Dag! In here! Those men had prisoners.

speaker: Yanli
en: You there, untie us! Let us walk and we will not hurt you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite bold in those bindings. I like your spirit.

speaker: Rowan
en: We are very agreeable people, I promise! You need not kill us.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Peace, friend. We have no need or wish to hurt you. What are your names?

speaker: Yanli
en: Yanli. I'm a merchant, not a bandit like those others. And this is Rowan.

speaker: Rowan
en: R-Rowan, that's right. I'm a stable hand, that's all. I keep horses and... well, I did. 'Til those brigands sold them off.

speaker: Yanli
en: They meant to sell us next, as slaves to the nearest bidder. But I'd rip their eyes out before I let that happen.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And how did you find yourselves here?

speaker: Yanli
en: We came to trade with the Sons of Ragnar, at Halfdan Jarls asking. But they were gone when we arrived.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Unbind them.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You know the Sons of Ragnar?

speaker: Rowan
en: Aye. Sold many a mare and stallion to the brothers. Good men, always paid me fair.

speaker: Sigurd
en: From the look of this camp they've been away for some time. Where will you go now? What will you do?

speaker: Yanli
en: Rebuild my stocks. Start anew. I have friends and allies across the land to aid me but... it won't be easy.

speaker: Rowan
en: Every town and village needs a stable. To keep horses fit and trim. I'll find my footing again. Somewhere.

speaker: Dag
en: What are you thinking?

speaker: Eivor
en: That we could use their skills as we get settled. Having access to trade and someone to tend our mounts would be a boon.

speaker: Sigurd
en: My thoughts as well. Any friend of the Ragnarssons is a friend of mine. Right, Dag?

speaker: Dag
en: Whatever you think is best, Sigurd.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yanli, Rowan... I am Sigurd Jarl of Fornburg, son of Styrbjorn. This is Eivor... and Dag. Both of you are free to go, but more than welcome to stay, if you are willing to pull your weight.

speaker: Yanli
en: We'd be happy to. If only to get back on our feet.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Then let it be done. The Raven Clan welcomes you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: From strangers into friends into family.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The others have arrived. Come.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have a good feeling about this place.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Honored family, friends... welcome to your new home!

speaker: Eivor
en: A camp... overrun with bears.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Psst! Here, I'm over here! Odin's beard! I-I can't move, it hurts. Hurry, before they catch on to my ruse! I'm here, here! O... I'm going to be bear-feast...

speaker: Norse Man
en: Praise Odin that you found me! But be still, we are in the lands of the ferocious tree shakers... My wounds hurt deep. If you could carry me to safety, kinsman, I would be indebted!

speaker: Norse Man
en: H-hey! Where are you going? You can't leave me here! P-please!

speaker: Norse Man
en: Slowly, slowly now...

speaker: Eivor
en: You are safe now.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Thank you, thank you, kinsman. I was so helpless against them. I even tried to use a key I found as a weapon. The brute swallowed it! Now I will never know what that key unlocks.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how did you come to be stuck here?

speaker: Norse Man
