en: My friends, the Toothbreakers, were with me, but we were separated when I went searching for what my key might open. I ended up snooping around that abandoned camp, and that's when they showed up. Bears! So many bears. I must catch my breath...

speaker: Eivor
en: You are safe now.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Thank you, thank you, kinsman. I was so helpless against them. I even tried to use a key I found as a weapon. The brute swallowed it! Now I will never know what that key unlocks.

speaker: Eivor
en: And how did you come to be stuck here?

speaker: Norse Man
en: My friends, the Toothbreakers, were with me, but we were separated when I went searching for what my key might open. I ended up snooping around that abandoned camp, and that's when they showed up. Bears! So many bears. I must catch my breath...

speaker: Eivor
en: He has nothing more to fear.

speaker: Einherjar
en: Your curses cannot touch me! Your weapons will not harm me! I will bathe in your blood!

speaker: Havi
en: Warrior! Put reins upon your battle lust and ride it! Do not be ridden by it.

speaker: Einherjar
en: I do not know your face, but I know...

speaker: Havi
en: Yes, think. What are your last memories?

speaker: Einherjar
en: I remember the fire-fog filling my throat... wading through a sea of blood and meat... a spear piercing my heart...

speaker: Havi
en: And then the Valkyries plucked you from the Helvger, which leads lesser men to Hel and brought you here, to glorious Asgard.

speaker: Einherjar
en: Asgard? This place is truly like no other... and... this is not a dream? Am I supposed to fight you?

speaker: Havi
en: We will fight together and become part of the greatest army ever assembled. But first, go eat and drink among the gods. Take your place in the Hall of the Slain. Your bravery has earned it.

speaker: Einherjar
en: Thor! Storm-Bringer! I offer you my blade! ...Odin! Raven-Feeder! I give you my life!

speaker: Eivor
en: A crowd... something is happening.

speaker: Odo
en: Just know, Charles will never honor a bond with you Northerners. Unlike him, my word can be trusted.

speaker: Toka
en: Ha! You are no more than a wounded dog at my table, looking for scraps.

speaker: Odo
en: How dare you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait!

speaker: Odo
en: Eivor, finally we can talk sense. What of Richardis? Did you encounter Charles?

speaker: Eivor
en: Richardis survived a trial by fire. The flames never touched her.

speaker: Odo
en: And the king? Did you do as I asked?

speaker: Eivor
en: I fought Charles, but he still lives.

speaker: Odo
en: Merde! We had an agreement. Where is your honor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Be careful, count. Things changed.

speaker: Odo
en: Just the opposite. It is as it always has been with you Northerners. All lies and doublespeak.

speaker: Odo
en: You made no promise to kill the beast, and maybe I was fool to ask you. But tell me you did not take the king's word over mine?

speaker: Eivor
en: Richardis had her own ideas about the future of Francia. I grew sympathetic to them.

speaker: Odo
en: After all I have done to keep her safe from him...

speaker: Eivor
en: She convinced me that her plan was sound. She meant to... subdue the king. Truly, she has a spell over him.

speaker: Odo
en: This is your plan for the long term safety of your people?

speaker: Eivor
en: She will ready the boy Bernard to be the next king of Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: I was not convinced at first. She begged that I should take pity on him.

speaker: Odo
en: He would have never done the same for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe not, but when he was at my mercy, I did pity him. Richardis swore she would take him away to a secluded place. He will be gone from power. She means to groom young Bernard to be his successor.

speaker: Odo
en: He is yet a piglet!

speaker: Eivor
en: You should be glad, Odo. Charles is gone. He'll not bother you any more.

speaker: Odo
en: Maybe. But I won't stand by idly and watch this kingdom crumble any further.

speaker: Odo
en: At least we can drink to Charles being... subdued.

speaker: Odo
en: Let us go! We have work to do.

speaker: Toka
en: What do you think he will do?

speaker: Eivor
en: Odo will look for Charles. And if he can, he will kill him. But Odo's anger could be his undoing.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odo will focus on rebuilding Paris. I just hope he does not grow bitter in the doing.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not know what he will do now.

speaker: Toka
en: I will have Pierre's eyes on him for some seasons to come.

speaker: Eivor
en: A wise step.

speaker: Toka
en: Can Richardis really keep Charles from returning to an active kingship?

speaker: Eivor
en: That is the wager I have made. And the lives of my clan depend on it.

speaker: Toka
en: They can depend on more than that. You still have me.

speaker: Toka
en: I will be sure to send word should Charles slither out of whatever pit Richardis has put him in.

speaker: Eivor
en: Richardis yet lives. Charles does not.

speaker: Odo
en: And when Francia's nobles back me to be their next king, you can count on a pact of friendship between us, Eivor the Wise.

speaker: Odo
en: That makes today a day for celebration!

speaker: Toka
en: Skal!

speaker: Eivor
en: Skal!

speaker: Odo
en: Santé! (Cheers!)

speaker: Odo
en: It has been curious to know you, Eivor. You are as enigmatic as any Northerner I have met. Here's hoping there are more like you.

speaker: Odo
en: I must go now and attend the throne. I wish you a safe journey back to England.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your greatest challenges lie before you, Count Odo. I hope you have the strength.

speaker: Odo
en: As do I.

speaker: Toka
en: Is it wise to put our trust in him?

speaker: Eivor
en: You can bargain with him, Toka. I know it will be strange to ally with someone Sigfred hated so. But he will keep his word and

speaker: Toka
en: I know, I know. Leaders drink the wine and so on.

speaker: Eivor
en: You were listening.

speaker: Eivor
en: You should not trust Odo, or any other leader in these lands. Not fully. Odo's duty is to his people.

speaker: Toka
en: As is mine.

speaker: Eivor
en: And as long as your ambitions do not cross his, there can be a reprieve from the bloodshed.

speaker: Eivor
en: The future is a mystery. Whether Odo will even attain his ambition is unclear.

speaker: Toka
en: Then... how am I to proceed?

speaker: Eivor
en: I cannot tell you that. You are the leader of your people now. Your instinct will determine their future.

speaker: Toka
en: I have much to consider.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay true to your honor and bring glory to your people. If you do that, you cannot fail.

speaker: Toka
en: I will send word should the Franks grow an appetite for England again.

speaker: Eivor
en: To your relations with Odo, consider returning to him the lands that Charles pledged to Sigfred.

speaker: Toka
en: No. Those lands are compensation for the hardship he has caused us. Odo kept Paris. That is enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: You sound more jarl-like all the time.

speaker: Eivor
en: And now I must think of my own people, whom I have been away from for too long.

speaker: Toka
en: Before you go, have this. It was my father, Sinric's. The second-best leader and teacher I have known.

speaker: Eivor
en: It has been my honor.

speaker: Toka
en: I hope to lead as well as you do, Eivor. If ever you hunger for more Frankish cheese, I will be happy to share.

speaker: Eivor
en: Farewell, Toka.

speaker: Havi
en: The prophecies of the Nornir are as clear as daylight. The Æsir are doomed. All Asgard is doomed.

speaker: Havi
en: Repeat the last passage.

speaker: Urðr
en: Brothers will fight one another and kill one another.

speaker: Verðandi
en: The home of the gods turns red with gore.

speaker: Skulð
en: It will be an age of storms.

speaker: Urðr
en: An age of wolves.

speaker: Havi
en: Not this! Further along... the foretelling of a wolf, a great beast.

speaker: Verðandi
en: The wolf Fenrir howls terribly before the gates to Hel.

speaker: Skulð
en: The beast will break its bonds and run.

speaker: Havi
en: And my part. What about me?

speaker: Urðr
en: Then comes the second great sorrow...

speaker: Verðandi
en: ... when the Havi goes to fight the wolf...

speaker: Skulð
en: ... and falls to Fenrir.

speaker: Havi
en: And falls to Fenrir! It's there you see? You have foretold my death. Your Havi will die.

speaker: Urðr
en: We speak what we see.

speaker: Verðandi
en: We know your fate, your destiny.

speaker: Skulð
en: Have you gleaned enough, O Wise One?

speaker: Havi
en: Fate governs all humankind. But I am the Defier of Death. I am not bound by these forces.

speaker: Urðr
en: All threads are measured. Everything dies. Even ancient Ymir, whose fertile carcass gave birth to the nine worlds.

speaker: Havi
en: You three spin our destinies as a thread in fabric. But threads may be unraveled by snags and catches.

speaker: Skulð
en: Not all can be foreseen, but loose threads can be rewoven or restrung. At day's end, the tapestry will be preserved.

speaker: Havi
en: Why struggle and fight if we are but threads stretched between anchored points? Without hope, life is a prison, not a gift.

speaker: Verðandi
en: Life is the music that comes from playing those threads. That is what lifts our spirits and fills our hearts.

speaker: Havi
en: I am no string to be plucked or tied! I am the High One, the Lord of Ecstasy, the Enemy of the Wolf. I am eternal.

speaker: Havi
en: Riddled words only cloud my thoughts. A storm is brewing, not in the clouds but down below. Does our final battle draw near? Is this how Ragnarök begins?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: The Havi returns to lead us to victory!

speaker: Týr
en: We must devise a strategy to deal with these invaders, Thor! You cannot smash your way out of certain death!

speaker: Thor
en: Who crushed the skull of Thrymr, King of the Jötnar? Who slew the Gargantuan with a flaming ball of

speaker: Týr
en: Ja, ja! And it was all well done! But the past is settled. It is our future we must decide!

speaker: Thor
en: You don't decide the future, you strangle it! By Mjölnir, I will hunt down these invaders to the ends of Asgard if I must!

speaker: Freyja
en: And leave our halls undefended? Without your hammer, we'll soon be overrun!

speaker: Thor
en: More danger, more glory!

speaker: Thor
en: Búri's balls! We are Asgardians! We don't skulk around like elves. We fight!

speaker: Freyja
en: We are fighting! For our homes, for our people. But some problems can't be solved with the hard end of a hammer!

speaker: Thor
en: Name one!

speaker: Týr
en: Havi! Break our stalemate.

speaker: Havi
en: What is this, another invasion?

speaker: Týr
en: Warriors from Jötunheim! They attack from all fronts.

speaker: Thor
en: While we sit on our trembling hands and scratch our bums!

speaker: Freyja
en: Not so, Thor. Many Æsir have been sent to the four corners of Asgard, leaving we four to defend the Great Hall.

speaker: Thor
en: Havi! Lend me a score of your warriors and I will lead them into Jötunheim myself!

speaker: Freyja
en: We cannot afford such a loss. The Einherjar (champions) must hold back to defend our city.

speaker: Týr
en: I would bring them here to hold the Great Hall itself. This invasion is too large to spread ourselves around.

speaker: Thor
en: All this prattle solves nothing! Battle or death!

speaker: Havi
en: Silence, all of you! We will take the fight to the enemy before they cross the Bifröst.

speaker: Týr
en: Well said, Raven-Feeder! Name those who may fight beside you!

speaker: Havi
en: I need only one. You, Týr, Lord of Justice. We'll gather our forces and scatter the enemy like grains.

speaker: Týr
en: Yes! I will fight as a thresher through a field of wheat, Mad One.

speaker: Havi
en: I need only one. You, Thor, Lord of Thunder. Together we'll cripple the enemy before they grow too bold.

speaker: Thor
en: Rouse every warrior who can hold axe or hammer! We're hunting Jötnar (giants) heads!

speaker: Havi
en: I need only one. You, Freyja, Queen of Asgard. Will you fight at my side?

speaker: Freyja
en: I'm with you, Havi. Let the Bifröst shimmer with the blood of their dead.

speaker: Havi
en: The rest of you stay back to protect the Great Hall.

speaker: Havi
en: Were any creatures among the jötnar? Draugr? Trolls... or wolves?

speaker: Freyja
en: What troubles you, Havi?

speaker: Týr
en: Does your far-sight tell you something?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: More invaders! They gather at the Bifröst bridge!

speaker: Týr
en: Where's Loki? He should be guarding that door!

speaker: Havi
en: Warn the others. The fight begins.

speaker: Týr
en: I'm with you, Havi. Let's deal out some punishment.

speaker: Týr
en: They're pouring in from Heimdall's tower! We must clear the bridge!

speaker: Thor
en: Mjölnir! It is time to crush!

speaker: Thor
en: Einherjar! Here is the battle you died to attain! For Havi. And for Asgard!

speaker: Thor
en: Jötunheim scum! Welcome to your doom!

speaker: Freyja
en: Come Havi! Tonight we drink and swive! But now's the hour we prove our might!

speaker: Freyja
en: If they've breached the gate to Jötunheim, someone must close it!

speaker: Thor
en: Mjölnir! It is time to crush!

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Lead us to glory, Havi!

speaker: Havi
en: Warriors, with me! The rest of you, guard the Great Hall!

speaker: Havi
en: With me! I gift this battle to myself!

speaker: Týr
en: They cloud our senses with enchantments!

speaker: Havi
en: Kill them, and their illusions die!

speaker: Thor
en: Einherjar! Bring the Havi your blades! We'll drown our enemies in blood!

speaker: Freyja
en: Jötunheim magic! It conjures a concealing mist!

speaker: Havi
en: My steel will shred their illusions.

speaker: Havi
en: Blood for Asgard! Say hello to Jörmungandr!

speaker: Jötun Soldier 1
en: Kill the Æsir! Burn their halls!

speaker: Havi
en: Cut them down!

speaker: Thor
en: To Helheim with you!

speaker: Thor
en: You break too easily!

speaker: Havi
en: Not while I stand! Return to your Jötnar masters!

speaker: Havi
en: Loki was charged with guarding this gate, and yet it was left open.

speaker: The Builder
en: Please! Have care! I've done you no harm!

speaker: Havi
en: What's that?

speaker: Loki
en: You've done us no favors either, Jötunn (giant).

speaker: The Builder
en: Wait, no, you're mistaken! I'm no Jötunn. I was only passing through from one land to another!

speaker: Loki
en: Would your song be the same if the Jötnar had won this fight?

speaker: The Builder
en: Yes, of course, of course! Are you calling me a liar?

speaker: Loki
en: Havi! I found this one lurking in the shade, shying away from battle. Shall I extract some teeth to get him talking? Or pluck out an eye?

speaker: Havi
en: You were told to guard this portal, Loki. What happened?

speaker: Loki
en: The portal opened, and these soldiers came bleeding through. So I sent warning straightaway.

speaker: Loki
en: And I captured this one, the soggy-jowled sheepherder.

speaker: Havi
en: What is your name, stranger?

speaker: The Builder
en: I'm called the Builder by most.

speaker: Loki
en: He wants your name, not your trade.

speaker: The Builder
en: If I have another name, it's not within my memory. Builder it's been for as long as I've been... building things.

speaker: Havi
en: Do you come from Jötunheim?

speaker: The Builder
en: I do, or I did. That is to say, I passed through. But I am not of that place, which pleases me well, for I hated it.

speaker: Havi
en: Had you any dealings there?

speaker: The Builder
en: As a builder, yes, for a time. But they took a dislike to my methods, which are... shall I say, magical in nature.

speaker: Havi
en: And what can you build that would impress me?

speaker: The Builder
en: I work with stone, wood, metals, whatever is at hand. And I finish by infusing my work with subtle charms and wishes.

speaker: Havi
en: Did the Jötnar benefit from these charms and wishes?

speaker: The Builder
en: O, for a time, for a time. But you and I both know, the Jötnar are a dull and desperate race.

speaker: Havi
en: Why have you come to Asgard?

speaker: The Builder
en: To balm my bruised ego, I'll admit. The Jötnar did not appreciate my skills and crafts.

speaker: Havi
en: And you thought we in Asgard might?

speaker: The Builder
en: Was it wrong to believe you and your kin possess a wisdom beyond measure and could recognize such a rare opportunity?

speaker: Loki
en: Havi, when someone gifts you a horse, you ride it. I'd put a bridle on this one.

speaker: Havi
en: Is that right, Builder? Are you a gift horse... or a secret curse?

speaker: The Builder
en: Neither, High One. I am only a tool. One with hopes to be well used.

speaker: Havi
en: This portal has been a source of misery for some time. I want it sealed.

speaker: The Builder
en: With respect, this is not the only way the Jötnar can enter Asgard. May I propose a more encompassing solution?

speaker: Havi
en: Quite a coincidence that you came when you did. At the tail end of a brutal attack.

speaker: The Builder
en: That I came when I did was by design. I have been among your enemies for so long, I know how they hunger for your demise.

speaker: Havi
en: We have tried all manner of barriers, and still we are breached. What makes you think yours could keep out giants or worse?

speaker: The Builder
en: I have been among the giants, learned their weaknesses. My shield will succeed where yours have failed.

speaker: Havi
en: And what do you want in exchange for this shield? Other than your freedom?

speaker: The Builder
en: I must give that a thought, a very deep thought. It would not be a simple task, and I do have my reputation to consider.

speaker: The Builder
en: If you doubt me, I could offer a demonstration.

speaker: Loki
en: A demonstration, yes. And if he fails to impress... we hoist his skin as a sail.

speaker: The Builder
en: I'll accept these terms with a last condition. I would need water from your Well of Urðr.

speaker: Loki
en: What do you know of our sacred well?

speaker: The Builder
en: It's a place of great power and vital magic. A source of spirit. It's the water there that will power your shield.

speaker: Loki
en: I'll collect the water, Havi. Keep this one clear of our sacred sites.

speaker: Havi
en: Loki, halt.

speaker: Havi
en: I will go to the well. You must find this Builder a clearing for his display.

speaker: Loki
en: No, no, it's no trouble, Havi. The damp and the dark appeal to me.

speaker: Havi
en: Go with the Builder, then return to the Great Hall with news of our next step.

speaker: Loki
en: As you command.

speaker: Loki
en: An interesting offer.

speaker: Havi
en: A curious coincidence.

speaker: Sunniva
en: We've brought back the fist fighting tournament!

speaker: Eivor
en: Good. It's been too long. Any changes from last time?

speaker: Sunniva
en: We have added new rules to make it more challenging! After each round you win, you will earn tokens. You can leave with those tokens or bet them on your next fight and earn even more!

speaker: Eivor
en: And if I should lose that next fight?

speaker: Sunniva
en: Then you leave with nothing! The greater the risk, the more the reward.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see now how it's more challenging.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Ready to fight?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Are you ready for the next round?

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. I'm ready.

speaker: Sunniva
en: I give you your champion. Eivor of the Raven Clan!

speaker: Eivor
en: I have completed the contract.

speaker: Reda
en: Excellent work, my friend! You impress me more and more every day. Here is what you have earned.

speaker: Pierre
en: Eivor! Over here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Pierre. What is this about?

speaker: Pierre
en: We have a shared interest... you in resisting Francia's Norse-loathing loyalists, me in getting paid.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those do not seem connected.

speaker: Pierre
en: I am working with a rogue band of men and women across Francia who tire of the chaos Charles' rule brought. Their numbers are small. Few are foolish enough to resist well-equipped loyalist forces.

speaker: Eivor
en: You do not believe in their cause?

speaker: Pierre
en: I do not, but they do. This is where you come in. Help them, and you will have ample reward for your effort.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is strange that you support them while believing their cause ill-fated.

speaker: Pierre
en: What kind of monster would I be to dash the hope they hold in their hearts? Anyway, there is profit to be made, and only a fool ignores that.

speaker: Pierre
en: How can I help? What do you want to do? So, what will it be?

speaker: Eivor
en: What have you got for me? Show me what is available. What do you have?

speaker: Pierre
en: Nothing to your liking? Well, you know where to find me when you change your mind.

speaker: Pierre
en: Back to England?

speaker: Eivor
en: To England.

speaker: Pierre
en: Off we go then.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will stay for now.

speaker: Pierre
en: Fine with me. Food and drink are better here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll be back later.

speaker: Pierre
en: Well, you know where to find me if you change your mind.

speaker: Pierre
en: Well done, Eivor. I expected nothing less. Magnifique! (Magnificent!) If you want do more, I'll be here. Good work. Let me know if you're looking for more to do.

speaker: Pierre
en: Mon Dieu! Stop this infernal mewling, else I swear I will turn you into soup!

speaker: Eivor
en: I did not take you for a lover of cats.

speaker: Pierre
en: I am not. One of the rebels picked it up during a mission. Nearly cost the fool his life.

speaker: Eivor
en: Animals are true-hearted. That cat will be a loyal companion to the end of its life.

speaker: Pierre
en: I doubt it. Felines are crafty, sly. They follow their own agendas, much like myself. Once he has had his fill of food and drink, I predict a quiet disappearance. Speaking of disappearances... the loyalists grow fewer. Our missions are going well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Am I detecting some sentiment?

speaker: Pierre
en: We are making small change, but it is not enough... and it matters not, so long as we make a profit.

speaker: French Man
en: Pierre! Don't forget, it's your turn to feed Fantôme today.

speaker: French Woman
en: It is always Pierre's turn. And he'll sooner jump into the lake than forget to feed Fantôme.

speaker: Pierre
en: Shut up, both of you.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am surprised to see that cat still here.

speaker: Pierre
en: It will not leave, and it takes up space. It does not help that Dero and Enna find amusement in how attached it is to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your little band of rebels is growing.

speaker: Pierre
en: Funny. But truthfully, they grow stronger with each victory, as does their confidence. They are bolstered by our victories. And it's easier to convince new recruits to join.

speaker: Eivor
en: Soon this hideout will not hold them all.

speaker: Pierre
en: We will face that when the time comes. For now, we fight.

speaker: French Woman
en: It's Eivor! Come join us!

speaker: French Man
en: You too, Pierre! It is time for merriment!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this a celebration?

speaker: Pierre
en: In a way. A break, for all our hard work. Come, drink with us.

speaker: Eivor
en: The place is starting to look more like an alehouse than a rebel hideout.

speaker: Pierre
en: We call them taverns here, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Careful, too much wine and a man's heart is laid open for all to see.

speaker: Pierre
en: Good people! I do not make long, flowery speeches.

speaker: Pierre
en: What I want to say amounts to but a few words. We have arrived. A toast! To us, and to Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: ' You have become softer than the cheese you love.

speaker: Pierre
en: I did not have any hope for this movement when we started. Or rather, I did not want to have any. A small group of armed peasants against, what, an army of trained soldiers? But now...

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not through numbers that victory is gained, but in the hope and courage of those who fight.

speaker: Pierre
en: Bah. Hope is an ugly word. But, mon Dieu, they made me... feel.

speaker: Eivor
en: "For friends last longest, if fate be fair, who give and give again."

speaker: Eivor
en: A verse from the , words of wisdom we follow.

speaker: Pierre
en: Poetic, for a bad for a collection of blood-thirsting raiders.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham asked that I travel to Lunden. What do you know of it?

speaker: Randvi
en: A wild city, one that Halfdan Ragnarsson tried to claim for himself, years ago. But it resists all attempts to be held.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hytham claims that the city was overrun by a strange cult. The Order of the Ancients. He asked that I tracked them down and kill them. Doing so may help the honest people there, and earn us an ally in the process.

speaker: Randvi
en: In a city so chaotic, it is worth a try. Approach by the north gate, and start asking around.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will.

speaker: Randvi
en: Good. I await your return.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Cripple Gate of Lunden. Might find an official worth his salt here.

speaker: Stowe
en: I beg patience, all! We'll have this wrack cleaned up in no time! Keep it steady.

speaker: Stowe
en: Here you are, love.

speaker: Stowe
en: Bear up, Master Hamme, you'll be on your way shortly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Something of a shepherd, aren't you?

speaker: Stowe
en: It can feel that way, aye. Can I help you with something?

speaker: Eivor
en: Who governs this burgh? I would like to speak with him if I can.

speaker: Stowe
en: Ah, the governor Tryggr. A good and fair Dane, come to Lunden four year back.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tryggr.

speaker: Stowe
en: Aye. Most hours of the day, you can find him at the old villa, dealing with all manner of knavery.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Stowe!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Avgos wants his cut of the summer harvest, shit-! What's the hold up?

speaker: Eivor
en: We're talking.

speaker: Stowe
en: Gentlemen, the farmers of Mercia have paid their burden already. If Avgos wants more, he can petition for it.

speaker: Norse Soldier 1
en: Petition for it? Well, you can tell that old mud-merchant

speaker: Norse Soldier 1
en: that if he wants his apple... He can bob for it.

speaker: Stowe
en: That belongs to Master Hamme, Sir.

speaker: Norse Soldier 1
en: Bob for it.

speaker: Stowe
en: That is filthy.

speaker: Norse Soldier 1
en: Bob for it!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this kind of noise common to Lunden?

speaker: Stowe
en: No, we've a quiet day, once in a great while! Try not to kill anyone, eh?

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: I'll wear your face as a skull cap, Stowe!

speaker: Stowe
en: Watch your head there!

speaker: Eivor
en: Eyes on your own foe!

speaker: Stowe
en: God'n Heaven, you fight like the Devil's stolen your bread.

speaker: Eivor
en: You give some hard knocks yourself.

speaker: Stowe
en: You don't finish fights as well as you start them.

speaker: Eivor
en: Was that a fight just now? It looked like you were trying to comb that man's beard.

speaker: Stowe
en: Roald, be a good lad an' prick the names of those that pay their food tax, will you?

speaker: Stowe
en: Right then, you've some dealings with Governor Tryggr, was that it?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll have dealings with any who can deliver a fair friendship with my Raven Clan. If that's you, then all the better.

speaker: Stowe
en: Ach, no. Tryggr's your fellow. I'm the shire reeve (sheriff) of Lunden's westerly half. I keep things ordered and fair.

speaker: Eivor
en: Shire Reeve is not a name that rides easy on the tongue.

speaker: Stowe
en: Reeve's my title, sorry. Stowe's my name. Stowe of Lunden.

speaker: Eivor
en: A burly name for a burly man. I like one who can hold himself in a brawl.

speaker: Stowe
en: To walk tall in Lunden, a man must know how to swing his fists.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not empty praise I give.

speaker: Stowe
en: Well, your candor is ... appreciated.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take me to your governor, Stowe. He sounds like a man worth knowing.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is good to meet you, Reeve Stowe. Lunden sits on sturdy shoulders.

speaker: Stowe
en: To be fair, I'm not the only reeve. There are two of us now, and the governor to boot. We do our best in these times, wild as they are.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take me to your governor, Stowe. He sounds like a man worth knowing.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take me to your governor, Stowe. He sounds like a man worth knowing.

speaker: Eivor
en: Right, then! Station filled, flock shepherded. And off to Tryggr we go!

speaker: Stowe
en: And what can I call you. Humbler of Thugs? Dane-hammer?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor of the Raven Clan. We have a settlement to the north, just off the river Nene.

speaker: Stowe
en: Well, I owe you a great debt, Eivor. You're a worthy ally.

speaker: Eivor
en: So, this is Lunden. A city built by giants.

speaker: Stowe
en: So they say! She's an old place, and surly as they come. But there's a mystery here I quite adore. I was raised here, in fact. Learned the scriptures of Christ's apostles in Lundenwic, our Saxon borough just past the western walls.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're not a priest, are you?

speaker: Stowe
en: No, I was raised by them. And for a penniless bastard, I turned out pretty well.

speaker: Eivor
en: A penniless bastard, and now Lunden's fearless Reeve.

speaker: Stowe
en: Well, it's Tryggr who saw something in me. He judges not the circumstance of my birth. His two hands, left and right, are me and a Dane-born soldier, Erke. Erke's an orphan of the last Viking horde to put down in Lunden for a season. Two or three years back now, it must have been. It's through Tryggr I met Erke, and now we reeves walk the city like parents looking after our children. A native son and an imported Dane, see? Lunden's a city built of many pieces.

speaker: Stowe
en: Wait, something's wrong...

speaker: Eivor
en: Iron on the air. This blood is fresh.

speaker: Stowe
en: These were good men! What's happened here?

speaker: Stowe
en: God, no! No, no, no!

speaker: Erke
en: It took three arrows to kill him. The next twelve were an insult.

speaker: Stowe
en: O Lord, deliver these men where the light of thy countenance visiteth and shines upon them.

speaker: Erke
en: We've no need for outsiders, Stowe. It's a private matter.

speaker: Stowe
en: There's no cause to be leery. Eivor had my back in a brawl at Cripple Gate. More thugs from the garrison.

speaker: Erke
en: Hm. You must be a real broga to hold your own against those shithogs. It's time to fetter those men, Stowe. It can't go on like ... like this.

speaker: Eivor
en: If this one had a head, you'd be calling him Tryggr, yes? Your governor?

speaker: Stowe
en: God above, the man is dead! Some respect, please.

speaker: Erke
en: We'll get along well, you and me.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must be Erke, Lunden's second reeve.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a serious attack. Were they after you as well?

speaker: Erke
en: Now that's a fine question, isn't it?

speaker: Eivor
en: You must be Erke, Lunden's second reeve.

speaker: Eivor
en: You must be Erke, Lunden's second reeve.

speaker: Erke
en: Erke Bodilsson, yes I am. Are you telling me this gut-bucket called me second reeve?

speaker: Stowe
en: First in the east borough. And a man I'd trust with my life.

speaker: Erke
en: Stowe's never been a good judge of character.

speaker: Stowe
en: Erke, this is Eivor. She came to meet with Tryggr, to seal the bonds of friendship with her clan.

speaker: Erke
en: He would have welcomed you heartily. He was a trusting man. And that got him here.

speaker: Stowe
en: Have you found anything?

speaker: Erke
en: I just arrived. The killers left a letter on the body there.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll have a look around.

speaker: Stowe
en: Tryggr had men with him at all times. How could the killers get through?

speaker: Erke
en: They must have been known to him. Well enough to get close without suspicion.

speaker: Stowe
en: Good and holy Christ, that could be most anyone. He governed this burgh!

speaker: Eivor
en: This letter. Someone wanted us to see it. "From Rome went an order of heretics who worshipped the relics of a time before Christ."

speaker: Stowe
en: Erke, this was the letter he told us about. Said it contained fearful news about Lunden.

speaker: Eivor
en: It warns of three such heathens who have infiltrated Lunden. His killers I expect.

speaker: Stowe
en: O, dear...

speaker: Erke
en: What is it?

speaker: Stowe
en: Dirty notes from a mistress... sorry, mistresses. In Tryggr's desk.

speaker: Erke
en: O, yes. The old man had a wandering hand and eye.

speaker: Stowe
en: I didn't know. I didn't think...

speaker: Erke
en: He didn't want you to. It was his secret to keep.

speaker: Stowe
en: Find anything?

speaker: Erke
en: Besides enough blood to repaint the city's faded bricks? No.

speaker: Stowe
en: I can't make head or foot of all this. I just... I just can't.

speaker: Erke
en: Look at us sitting on our laurels, while Eivor does all the work.

speaker: Eivor
en: Three sets of footprints leave. Two average and one massive.

speaker: Eivor
en: A barber-surgeon's tools. Sharp and precise for easy butchery. Must've been what was used to free Tryggr's head from his neck.

speaker: Eivor
en: I don't envy this man's death. Hang on, there's something in his hand. This was not Tryggr's seal?

speaker: Erke
en: Nay, it looks Roman in origin. Must've been on a letter he opened.

speaker: Eivor
en: It must have been significant to this guard for him to grasp it even in death.

speaker: Stowe
en: Mayhaps it's what got him killed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I think I have a clear idea of what happened here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tryggr was shot where he sat, probably as he read the letter. One of his guards grabbed the seal and tried to escape. He didn't make it. A second killer found him first. He met his end at the noose, lifted by the bigger man. A third attacker took his eyes... then came for Tryggr's head. Symbolic maybe. Headless leader, eyeless guards. The killers were without fear. This kill was a message. Their footprints leave together, three sets, heading back to the courtyard.

speaker: Eivor
en: The letter mentions three heretics, named only by monikers. The Leech, The Arrow, The Compass. Signed by someone calling himself a Poor-Fellow Soldier of Christ.

speaker: Erke
en: Poor-Fellow Soldier. Odd name.

speaker: Stowe
en: Three names, three killers. As you said.

speaker: Erke
en: Baldr's sack, it could be anyone in Lunden. Who can we trust?

speaker: Stowe
en: Only the people in this room, I fear.

speaker: Eivor
en: Even that would be unwise, until we know more.

speaker: Stowe
en: The Arrow is described as a pugnacious Dane invader. That describes too many in Lunden.

speaker: Erke
en: The Leech hails from Wessex. Lunden is home to many of them as well.

speaker: Eivor
en: And The Compass, a Frankish captain.

speaker: Stowe
en: Less common, but no face comes to mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: What is this symbol here?

speaker: Erke
en: I recognized that from the Mithraic Temple. I passed it on the way here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Mithraic Temple, is that a church?

speaker: Stowe
en: A church, heavens no! Mithras was a pagan idea, a so-called god beloved by the ancient soldiers that built this city.

speaker: Eivor
en: This temple is in plain sight? How far from where we stand?

speaker: Erke
en: It's the skeletal remains of a place of worship, just a stone-skip away.

speaker: Eivor
en: This Temple is our only strong lead. I would like to see it.

speaker: Stowe
en: Our city is overrun by cowards. We may be next to fall if we don't resolve this sick fermentation of hate.

speaker: Erke
en: I've told you, this city answers to blood and power. We should serve as such.

speaker: Stowe
en: I can't leave him like this. He's... I need to...

speaker: Erke
en: We'll get the Church to see to it, Stowe.

speaker: Stowe
en: No, no it should be me. I must ready him for judgment.

speaker: Erke
en: I understand. Only get some air from time to time. It reeks in here. Shall we, Broga?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: The guards have been murdered!

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: To arms! Defend Tryggr!

speaker: Erke
en: Well, now the locals have caught a whiff of this fetid mess. The Temple is yours to explore, Eivor. It's to the east of here. I must wear my Reeve's face for a time.

speaker: Erke
en: Keep away! Keep away! The fight is over! Town hall will follow soon!

speaker: Eivor
en: Should the reeves change their minds, I will have to gut them and put a puppet atop Lunden's throne. But, Stowe seems a good man. I will trust his word.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Temple of Mithras, well-guarded for a tangle of old ruins. I need to find the entrance.

speaker: Recruitment Orders
en: Arrow, We must increase our strength to stage our coup. Drum up some support from the layabouts at the West Market. Archers are needed in force. We need them to man those new springalds you're so enamored with. I will return when you send word of your success. Compass.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Compass holds sway over the others. He's ordered The Arrow to recruit archers in a market to the west. Worth a visit.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tools for a surgeon, finely crafted. Like we found in the villa. And there's a letter here, arranging payment to a blacksmith.

speaker: Eivor
en: Messages between The Leech and The Compass. Healing. Gutting. The Leech is a strange one, but The Compass calls the strikes.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've got enough to go on for now. Erke and Stowe must see all this. I see more bloodshed in Lunden's future. At least, Sýnin will feast.

speaker: Stowe
en: It's worth knocking on a few doors, that's all I'm saying!

speaker: Erke
en: Tryggr wasn't killed because you want to plant a few trees and fix a few roofs in Lunden!

speaker: Eivor
en: Looks less like a meal for crows in here.

speaker: Erke
en: Eivor. You bring good findings, I hope.

speaker: Eivor
en: A few sheets of vellum, notes between members of a secret society. The Order of the Ancients, they are called.

speaker: Stowe
en: Order of the Ancients. Doesn't sound any bells in my head. What's their purpose?

speaker: Eivor
en: That would take some time to explain. But know this, that I'm here to kill them. In Lunden, it seems The Compass is the head. The Arrow and The Leech are his hands.

speaker: Erke
en: Pet names and secret orders, what a crock! Do we know anything we can act on?

speaker: Eivor
en: The Arrow is a Dane who has seen his share of battle. His name suggests he's an archer.

speaker: Stowe
en: I'd bet my knuckles he's the one sowing discord among the Danes that shelter in Lunden.

speaker: Erke
en: If it were me, I'd hide among my ranks. Surrounded by other fighting men.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Arrow has orders from The Compass to recruit soldiers at a market in the west.

speaker: Stowe
en: I know the very place.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Leech has need of flesh. Been looking for thralls, though I can't say why.

speaker: Erke
en: We've found a number of dead down by the quays lately. But not thralls alone. Some of the missing we find again in several places, cut to pieces.

speaker: Stowe
en: Good Lord, Erke.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Compass is a mystery. He's mentioned often, but there's little to go on.

speaker: Erke
en: Said he was a Frankish captain, did you? To find him, we'd have to mark the ships that came and went along the Thames.

speaker: Stowe
en: Captains are a transient sort. It may be he's far away, keeping quiet.

speaker: Eivor
en: That may be. But would he scream if we cut off his hands?

speaker: Erke
en: O, you've a filthy mind for strategy.

speaker: Eivor
en: We kill The Arrow and The Leech, then sit back and wait. Let The Compass come to us.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's not waste any more time. We will find The Arrow and The Leech. Killing both should drag The Compass back into port. Stowe, I'll catch you at the Western Market.

speaker: Stowe
en: Count on it.

speaker: Erke
en: And I'll make for the quays. There's another few bodies there to fish out of the muck.

speaker: Eivor
en: It could be The Leech is back at work.

speaker: Stowe
en: God be with us, friends. Go in His name, and be protected by Him.'

speaker: Ciara
en: Aililiú! Eivor! I am glad to see you.

speaker: Ciara
en: I reckon Flann and Bárid have found common ground, seeing as you're still here.

speaker: Eivor
en: They have.

speaker: Ciara
en: Ara, and how much of your charm seeped into that conversation?

speaker: Eivor
en: I merely showed the High King I'm a Norse he can trust.

speaker: Ciara
en: It's more than that. You've certainly left your mark here. Sure, I think Flann is fond of you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is he the only one?

speaker: Ciara
en: You're not shy, are you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Just perceptive.

speaker: Eivor
en: Flann has ambitions. I am the means to achieving them. That is why I am here.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're kind to butter me, but it's not why I have come.

speaker: Eivor
en: We need to curry favor with as many kingdoms as we can. Flann said you could help with that.

speaker: Ciara
en: Aye. The kings of Ireland have long sent their grievances to the High King's court in hopes their pleas be heard. Their problems range from petty squabbles to larger issues. I've taken the liberty of sifting through them, choosing the ones that might illicit the best response.

speaker: Eivor
en: I see. The bigger the favor, the bigger the reward.

speaker: Ciara
en: There you have it. Keep an eye for pigeon coops. That's where I'll leave any noteworthy tasks. Help solve their woes, and the kings'll pay tribute with the men and supplies we need to invade Ulster.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfway there.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, Orlog. I know this game well.

speaker: Alwin
en: Eivor! Do you want a match?

speaker: Eivor
en: I didn't know you played.

speaker: Alwin
en: I learned it from a Norse merchant and I've become quite good. I'd even say I'm the best player in Ravensthope!

speaker: Eivor
en: A bold claim. I assume you're ready to back it up.

speaker: Alwin
en: Always! Shall we play now?

speaker: Eivor
en: Let's do this, then.

speaker: Alwin
en: Prepare yourself, Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Too easy.

speaker: Alwin
en: You have shamed me, Eivor! Can we play again so I can try to get my dignity back?

speaker: Eivor
en: What awaits in Eurvicscire?

speaker: Randvi
en: Halfdan Ragnarsson, Conqueror of the North, sends his greeting. He wishes to meet with Eivor Wolf-Kissed personally.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan Jarl. I have heard the man's name so often, I feel as though I know him already.

speaker: Randvi
en: He is currently tangled in a war with the Picts of the northern hills. I suspect he wants your council. Or your axe. If you are keen to meet him, he asks that you join him at his war camp. I have the location here.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will go at once.

speaker: Randvi
en: With caution, Eivor. Eurvicscire is currently at war with the Picts, a proud clan that lives just beyond the Roman wall.

speaker: Eivor
en: Signs of battle.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hard fought on both sides.

speaker: Eivor
en: The battle climbed into the hills.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Hey, who's that?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Everyone all right?

speaker: Faravid
en: Help the wounded. And get every man's name. We leave none behind.

speaker: Faravid
en: Well met, Eivor Raven-Friend.

speaker: Faravid
en: Now there's a face I've seen before.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid. We met in Jorvik, the Yuletide feast.

speaker: Faravid
en: The Yuletide massacre, I remember. What brings you here?

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan Jarl, he summoned me. Is he near?

speaker: Faravid
en: He was, but the Picts hit us hard. We were separated.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fresh attack, from the hills!

speaker: Faravid
en: Circle round! Watch your backs!

speaker: Eivor
en: Picts. They won't be happy to see the likes of me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Odin take you all!

speaker: Faravid
en: The Picts are just ahead. Lead the way and we'll watch your back.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you wounded?

speaker: Faravid
en: I'll live. But my men...

speaker: Faravid
en: If we die today, tonight we drink with Odin. Either way, we claim victory.

speaker: Halfdan
en: For Thor!

speaker: Halfdan
en: For Ragnar!

speaker: Halfdan
en: For Halfdan!

speaker: Halfdan
en: You owe me your life, old friend. Once again.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan Ragnarsson, we meet in the forge of battle. Surely a good sign.

speaker: Halfdan
en: I don't know you. One of Faravid's new dogs?

speaker: Eivor
en: I am Eivor of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Eivor, yes. Down in Mercia. Kingmaker with my brothers Ivarr and Ubba. And Finnr in East Anglia. From the tales I hear, I feared you might be taller.

speaker: Eivor
en: That's not a fear you feel often, I imagine.

speaker: Halfdan
en: So you answered my summons. But the timing is poor as you can see. Too many here are spent ... battle-sore ... thirsty. Faravid. Have your men build field pyres for the dead.

speaker: Faravid
en: At once, my jarl.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Not here. Not now.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Then to Donecaestre for a victory feast!

speaker: Faravid
en: The oldest son of Ragnar Lothbrok, so he says. What do you make of him?

speaker: Eivor
en: Heroic display. He makes a powerful first impression.

speaker: Faravid
en: Just the way he likes it. Welcome to Eurvicscire, friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: Well met, Faravid. I was hoping your jarl would be as welcoming. But I suppose I must earn his trust.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kings and jarls, bishops and earls, I've met them all. Halfdan is but a man like all the rest.

speaker: Faravid
en: He conquered East Anglia, took Northumbria for his own, and sacked Lunden. What warrior could claim more?

speaker: Eivor
en: Winning battles is easy. It's winning trust that brings an end of war.

speaker: Halfdan
en: What I think does not matter. I'm interested in what his men think of him. Is he honest, trustworthy, loyal?

speaker: Faravid
en: Is that why you've come here? To earn Halfdan's trust? To find a seat at his table?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have my own table. What I want is a bond of friendship between the new lords of England.

speaker: Faravid
en: Among whom you count yourself, I suppose.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is an ally I seek, not a master.

speaker: Faravid
en: Well, there is one Lord of Northumbria.

speaker: Faravid
en: You heard the jarl. Take the gear and start digging.

speaker: Faravid
en: He's at Donecaestre, the towering castle by the river.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Roman giants outdid themselves with this fortress.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where would Halfdan Jarl hold court?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Please, Lady Moira. My wife grows ill.

speaker: Moira
en: I will attend to her soon, I promise. But Halfdan needs me now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you a nun? I thought nuns dressed like geese.

speaker: Moira
en: Nothing of the sort. I am Moira of Wyke, Halfdan's herbalist. He is an ill man, and I do what I can to give succor and hope.

speaker: Eivor
en: I saw him fight. He was in fine health then.

speaker: Moira
en: Thanks in part to my soothing tonics. Would you pardon me?

speaker: Halfdan
en: We crush them in spring. No sooner. That is the plan.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Yet my people suffer day by day

speaker: Halfdan
en: Your people? Do you rule a shadow kingdom under my nose?

speaker: Ricsige
en: Our people suffer from these brutal winter raids.

speaker: Ricsige
en: This war must end, that is my first concern. The time to strike is

speaker: Halfdan
en: Is when I say we strike. Halfdan's hammer protects this land. Tell my people that, King Ricsige.

speaker: Ricsige
en: As you wish, my lord.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Who is this? Come closer.

speaker: Eivor
en: Halfdan Ragnarsson. My sword-arm answers your call.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Thank you for your tribute, Eivor Wolf-Kissed. Your battles and deeds are well known to me.

speaker: Halfdan
en: And you are the Hero of Jorvik, so sing my skalds.

speaker: Faravid
en: Not just any hero. Eivor brought order to the city when King Ricsige could not.

speaker: Halfdan
en: They say you rooted a gang of thieves and traitors.

speaker: Eivor
en: Not alone. But I led the charge.

speaker: Halfdan
en: You gifted my silver to the karls and ceorls of Jorvik.

speaker: Eivor
en: To men and women who needed it most.

speaker: Halfdan
en: A foolish choice. The coin never left King Ricsige's treasury.

speaker: Faravid
en: The silver Eivor recovered there now pays for our war with the Picts.

speaker: Halfdan
en: It is wasted fighting Picts. It should be put to better use.

speaker: Eivor
en: I try never to regret the decisions I make in a time of war.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Agreed. To second guess ourselves would only stall the victory. I don't regret sending Faravid to lead our strike against the Picts... in spite of Eivor winning the day.

speaker: Faravid
en: Eivor and I felled them, Halfdan Jarl, so you could sweep in, stab a few cold corpses, and claim a glorious victory.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Old friend, your jests hit like Odin's spear, always on the mark.

speaker: Faravid
en: I would not be here without your hammer, great jarl. Please accept this, your share of the loot we won today.

speaker: Halfdan
en: A thing of beauty. Frankish, I believe. What do you think, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: A fine piece of work, fit for the lips of a king.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Or a man who makes kings.

speaker: Eivor
en: A cup is a cup. What matters is the brew that sloshes inside.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wine goblets are for Roman kneelers. Give me a horn of mead any day.

speaker: Halfdan
en: There's wisdom in the one, Faravid.

speaker: Faravid
en: By your leave, lord, I must return to my forward camp. It's a long, cold ride.

speaker: Halfdan
en: A two-faced, smirking glory hound...

speaker: Eivor
en: My lord, in your summons you said

speaker: Halfdan
en: Shhh, not here, not now. Dance, sing, and fill yourself with ale, then meet me atop this tower of stone.

speaker: Halfdan
en: There I will weave a tale of friendship and treachery. A tale as old as the world.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Not here. Let's get away from envious ears.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: Only a fool makes a long war in winter.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: He should drink good honest mead, not that bitter Frankish wine.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: You? Care to test the speed of your fists?

speaker: Eivor
en: Fair warning, ceorl. My fists have hammered nails and strangled sharks. Still care to brawl?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 1
en: Swift and strong you may be. It's the one most righteous who wins the fight.

speaker: Eivor
en: You fought well, warrior. But here your legend ends, bound to no name.

speaker: Eivor
en: Feeble.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Here, Dane. Try your luck at throwing bones.

speaker: Eivor
en: My luck overspills like the ocean's tide. Only fate will keep me from winning.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 2
en: Then come and see! What fate do these dice hold for you?

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Warrior! You can swing an axe, but can you lift a horn?

speaker: Eivor
en: As Thor swallowed the ocean, I can lift many horns and drain them too.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: A bold claim! I'll drink to that.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've put off Halfdan for too long. Atop the tower of stone, he said.

speaker: Ricsige
en: How true! I shall send a strongly worded note in protest.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Soldier 3
en: But sir, I'm told Halfdan can't read.

speaker: Eivor
en: King Ricsige...

speaker: Ricsige
en: Ah, Eivor. We have missed your wit on the Jorvik council.

speaker: Eivor
en: I attend in spirit.

speaker: Ricsige
en: Would you lend us your wisdom now, if possible? We are at pains to determine how to deal with the northern Picts.

speaker: Eivor
en: Meet iron with iron, that is the way.

speaker: Ricsige
en: And this feast is how the Danes prepare their blades?

speaker: Eivor
en: We fought well, and won. Tomorrow we will fight again. But we must always make time for celebration.

speaker: Ricsige
en: I defer to your expertise. Hacking, hewing, and the like. Enjoy the feast, counselor.

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: But Faravid is the one out there fighting.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Dogs don't beg for silver. Dogs don't yearn to be jarls. But I'm a wolf. No, a wolf king.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Ah, Eivor. Come, let me show you a wonder.

speaker: Halfdan
en: All this. We conquered this. He and I. Together.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've earned great fame, won many battles across England.

speaker: Halfdan
en: But not alone, no no. Björn Ironside, fearless Ubba, Ivarr the Boneless, Sigurd Snake-in-the-Eye. Great warriors all. My brothers.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gold is good and battle better, but glory never dies. Forever it lives in the hall of heroes, high on valor's steed.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Together, we have conquered. Together with my friends, my clan. Faravid above all others. One sword is not an army, Eivor. Even a hero needs loyal friends. I have never lost sight of that. Never!

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you room for one more among those you call friend?

speaker: Halfdan
en: What does friendship mean to you, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: Friendship goes beyond words. It is a solemn bond, a chain unbroken.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Spoken like the volur. It is indeed a kind of magic.

speaker: Eivor
en: You wriggle like an eel in a basket, Halfdan. What has caught you?

speaker: Eivor
en: It's but a name for an alliance. What matters is keeping your oath.

speaker: Halfdan
en: A hard way to see the world. Hard, but fair.

speaker: Eivor
en: You wriggle like an eel in a basket, Halfdan. What has caught you?

speaker: Eivor
en: You wriggle like an eel in a basket, Halfdan. What has caught you?

speaker: Halfdan
en: Friendship can also spoil, like rotten meat. After all these years, he dares to bite my hand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Faravid? He seems a good and loyal man.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Seems, yes. As a bright sky in winter seems warm. But rumors fly of little men plotting treason in the dark.

speaker: Eivor
en: Have you proof of his treachery?

speaker: Halfdan
en: Not yet. That is where you enter my saga. Prove this for me. Discover if Faravid has been disloyal. Then we shall talk of oaths.

speaker: Eivor
en: Start me somewhere. Give me something to go on.

speaker: Halfdan
en: You see this? From a sea unicorn. I filter my mead and wine with it.

speaker: Eivor
en: I've heard of such beasts. They swim below the ice, beyond the world's edge.

speaker: Halfdan
en: And their horns protect against poison.

speaker: Eivor
en: You believe Faravid wants to poison you?

speaker: Halfdan
en: I fear he has tried. Countless times. And failed them all. You don't believe me, but I know the man. His gifts of wine. His easy smile. His envy. His plots. Learn the truth. Dig up... unearth this treason.

speaker: Eivor
en: Why trust me with such a task?

speaker: Halfdan
en: Jorvik. You stopped the ill deeds of Audun and his swarm of rats. You can do the same here.

speaker: Eivor
en: Like a good sword, honor has two edges. I'll help you.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Faravid has left the feast already, heading for his camp upriver. Join his war band. And behind his back, dig.

speaker: Eivor
en: And if I find nothing? If he's a good and loyal man?

speaker: Halfdan
en: Even better, even better.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fair enough. I will find what I find, then return, my friend.

speaker: Halfdan
en: Don't let Faravid fool you. He's hiding something.

speaker: Maximilian
en: If I find one crack—That statue is as fragile as the rest of my collection and costs more than the hovel you call a home!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Just a clay man with his cock out, ya nutter.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have a friend who needs that little Roman man you have. Octavian of Lunden.

speaker: Maximilian
en: I've a guess who your friend is, and no. Osbert cannot have his greasy pedestrian fingers on something so exquisite.

speaker: Eivor
en: Osbert?

speaker: Maximilian
en: O-ho, that is delicious. Yes, Osbert. A name fit for a poor failure. It'll cost a cow's weight in silver to get it in his hands.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fan of Rome, I see? I am too. Unique methods of torture. Crucifixion, . But, where I am from, we have The Eivor. Nose lopped off, skin flayed, teeth carved out to wear as a necklace. Then left to the birds. How much, again?

speaker: Maximilian
en: Uh, free of charge. Let me just grab it for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Heh, I'll have to take this back to Osbert.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll give you the filthy silver.

speaker: Maximilian
en: O-o, that is... thank you. Well. I should hope so! You may take the legionnaire.

speaker: Eivor
en: Heh, I'll have to take this back to Osbert.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not leaving Lunden without that sculpture.

speaker: Maximilian
en: Then you'll just have to return with more coin, Dane.

speaker: Eivor
en: I need to keep Maximilian distracted and out of the way if I am to steal the statue.

speaker: Maximilian
en: Crawling back for the legionnaire, I see.

speaker: Norse Child
en: Odd jobs for coin! Odd jobs for coin!

speaker: Eivor
en: I have an odd job, and can pay you coin. I can pay you even more coin to not ask questions

speaker: Norse Child
en: You sound like my father. What do you need? If you try to chop me up to bits, I'll scream.

speaker: Eivor
en: I just need you to keep a man busy while I take back something he stole from me.

speaker: Norse Child
en: If you pay up front then, deal. But, we need a signal. For if he's coming, and for when you're all clear. I'll make this noise, caw-caw, if he's coming your way. And you make it when you've got the thing.

speaker: Eivor
en: This noise? Ca-caw!

speaker: Norse Child
en: Close enough.

speaker: Norse Child
en: Greetings, lord. I 'heard you buy things the giants left behind.

speaker: Maximilian
en: Romans, yes, but go on.

speaker: Norse Child
en: Ja. Well, my father, he found a great deal of these things by our house. Coins and heads 'n' stuff.

speaker: Maximilian
en: He's found actual busts? What level of damage? Have you found any emperors? Which ones?

speaker: Norse Child
en: There's one with curly hair and a big nose There's one with a chin like a brick. There's a lady with a wreath around her head.

speaker: Maximilian
en: What was that noise?

speaker: Eivor
en: Heh, I'll have to take this back to Osbert.

speaker: Maximilian
en: Hang on. I must inspect.

speaker: Eivor
en: Argh... Ca-caw! Ca-caw!

speaker: Maximilian
en: Enough babbling, someone is in my home!

speaker: Norse Child
en: Run! Caw-caw! Caw-caw-caw!

speaker: Eivor
en: Great work. Try to keep out of trouble.

speaker: Norse Child
en: I don't make promises I can't keep. But, you paid me in full, so I won't break your knees.

speaker: Maximilian
en: What are you doing! Get out of my house!

speaker: Eivor
en: So Ceolbert has traveled to Sciropescire.

speaker: Randvi
en: He has, into a difficult situation. The Shire has been mired in a long war with Rhodri, King of the Britons. Ceolbert hopes to negotiate a peace with the Britons of the west. A difficult task for one so green.

speaker: Eivor
en: I hope your tutelage has prepared him well,

speaker: Randvi
en: Indeed. But I think it best if you supervise these talks. If Ceolbert can make this work, we will gain a valuable alliance.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll make my way to Sciropescire.

speaker: Randvi
en: I am relieved. He and Ivarr should be in Quatford just now. You will find it along the Afon Hafren River.

speaker: Eivor
en: If Ivarr is with him, I will certainly be needed.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Your King Rhodri's in there, begging on his chubby knees for peace!

speaker: Briton Warrior 1
en: Peace? Who wants peace?

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Rhodri's nothing but a stinking pile of sheep dung.

speaker: Briton Warrior 2
en: This isn't your fight, Danes. Go back to the sea.

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: You come over here and say that!

speaker: Briton Warrior 2
en: Come on. Take a swing at me. A good swing.

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Your sorry king wants peace.

speaker: Briton Warrior 3
en: Poor Danes. So far from home. Who's with your wives now, eh?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: We've had nothing for days.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: Nettle and turnips. It's all I could find.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Smells good, that.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman
en: There you go, young man.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Curse this war. Say your thanks, Bertwic.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Thank you, ma'am.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Come on, boy... ha!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Aaah, oof!

speaker: Ivarr
en: You wouldn't stop a lamb. Come on!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I hurt my shoulder.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Shake it off!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Ha!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Don't hold back. Follow through!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Aaaah!

speaker: Ivarr
en: And...

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Oof!

speaker: Ivarr
en: To your feet. Up! You keep moving as long as your body will follow. Whoop!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ah ah! Not half bad, boy. But be fierce. Dirty. Strike at my balls!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr, are you training the boy or tormenting him?

speaker: Ivarr
en: One will lead to the other in time.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Eivor, well met. You received my message, and just in time. Our negotiations with the Britons have not yet begun.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will be at your side when they do. Is there anything I should know first?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: The venerable King Rhodri is here. I am to deal with him directly.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Rhodri is desperate for peace, ever since we captured his sniveling brother, Gwriad. Sounds like a man coughing up snot. Gwriad ap Merfyn!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Rhodri waits at the church nearby.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who speaks for Sciropescire in these talks?

speaker: Ceolbert
en: The last ealdorman was killed in battle. Bishop Deorlaf is standing in.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Until we get this wet whelp installed! That is his father's wish.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I find the idea of leading a shire on my own quite... quite terrifying.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's a grave thing to be ealdorman in a time of war, Ceolbert.

speaker: Ivarr
en: He will piss his pants first thing, that's for certain.

speaker: Eivor
en: Don't fret until you have taken up the ealdorman's title. Too many things can go wrong between now and then.

speaker: Coelbert
en: My father thinks me fit already, I shouldn't want to disappoint him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr will toughen you up. But watch your back. He's a wily one.

speaker: Ivarr
en: It is always the same with me, boy. When things get too quiet, I throw daggers.'

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I'll be on my guard.

speaker: Eivor
en: As future ealdorman, you should speak in the talks as well. But with humility. Rhodri is a king and will expect to be treated as one.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Rhodri will want us to get down on our knees and sniff the rosy wind blowing from his ass. I know the man.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've met him?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Met him, fought him. He gave me this nick here.

speaker: Ivarr
en: He gave me this nick here. Maybe I can give him one back. Remind him some call me King Killer.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be you should stay behind, Ivarr. That's not a recipe for a good parlay.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I'd like you both to be there. To guide me, to judge my fitness.

speaker: Eivor
en: Give us your word then. Your blade stays in its sheath.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Eivor, don't make me laugh. We both know what my word is worth. But sure, I will let you do the talking. Probably.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Excellent. Now... to the church, I think. Our guests await.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: It's not far, just across the village. We've been at war with the Britons for coming on two years.

speaker: Ivarr
en: The Britons had the best of it, 'til me and my berserkrs plowed through their ranks and chased Rhodri's brother into a ditch.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: That's why Rhodri's talking peace now. It's thanks to Ivarr.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I am going to enjoy seeing him squeal, the old oak. Not nearly as much as taking him down, though. That would seal my legacy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your legacy?

speaker: Ivarr
en: As King Killer. They do not all get away like Burgred did, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep the peace, Ivarr.

speaker: Ivarr
en: What has become of your preening brother?

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, my brother. We parted. His road is unsure.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have not seen him since we were together in Ledecestrescire. I am left uneasy when he is away.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You are better off leaving that sauntering pole in your wake.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Our Bishop Deorlaf and King Rhodri are ensconced in the church ahead.

speaker: Eivor
en: These houses of Christ. They're all so hard and cold.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Yet within is warmth. The Christian God unites King Rhodri, Bishop Deorlaf, and myself. On His ground, peace will be made.

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Briton cowards! All of you!

speaker: Briton Warrior 1
en: Suck on yellow snow! Filthy Danes. We'll festoon our halls with your entrails!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: Come on, then. Let's have at it.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: Captain Ynyr! Explain to the good bishop our position.

speaker: Ynyr ap Cadfarch
en: Yes, my sovereign. Bishop Deorlaf. We are deaf to offers of peace until Gwriad is returned to us.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: The king's brother is

speaker: Ivarr
en: The king's brother is a moldering sack of cow dung.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: You. I know your face, your stench. Ivarr... the one they call Boneless. Did I not gift you that scar myself?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ah! You did, and I mean to gift you a gash, you reeking piss pot. In your fat fucking skull!

speaker: Eivor
en: Hold! both of you!

speaker: Eivor
en: My lord, this is Ceolbert, the future ealdorman of this shire and the son of Ceolwulf of Mercia.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: This green stripling? Ealdorman? You couldn't piss without help, boy.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rhodri. You've wasted your men's lives in a fruitless war. Ivarr need not show respect to you.

speaker: Angharad
en: This Dane is deluded! How dare you speak to my husband in this manner

speaker: Eivor
en: Now is not the time for keeping grudges. We're here to smooth a path to peace.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Peace, peace, peace! Not with this bag of Briton slop.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: On that we are agreed..

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Now, now, calm everyone. Good faith is all I ask.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: You know my demands. Until my brother Gwriad walks free, peace between us is impossible.

speaker: Ivarr
en: He is lucky he can walk at all! Fell on his own blade fleeing from us!

speaker: King Rhodri
en: I will soon help you fall on yours.

speaker: Angharad
en: Husband. Keep your head. It is in our interest to find a way to peace. All of us.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: First, my brother.

speaker: Ivarr
en: First your head on a pike. Then the runt goes free.

speaker: Angharad
en: Husband! No!

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Enough! This is a house of God! Let us take some few minutes to gather ourselves, shall we? Eivor, to me.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: I do not know you well, but Ceolbert believes you a steady head. We need such a one.

speaker: Eivor
en: It may be too late. I see the crows of war gathering.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: I have a hefty sum of silver. Speak to the people here. If the silver will help one bring us toward peace, offer it to them.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: These talks are stalled. I fear the upshot.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do not fret. You will be ealdorman yet.

speaker: Eivor
en: King Rhodri.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: What is it, Dane?

speaker: Eivor
en: I wish to help you to peace.

speaker: King Rhodri
en: I will not talk of peace until my brother Gwriad, is returned to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you first agree to peace, he will be returned. Would a sum of silver help overleap this difficulty?

speaker: King Rhodri
en: I cannot be purchased with looted silver, Dane. Stand away.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Talk, talk, talk! All we do is talk!

speaker: Eivor
en: You are with Rhodri, yes? One of his advisors?

speaker: Ynyr Ap Cadfarch
en: I am that. Ynyr ap Cadfarch by name. Address me proper.

speaker: Eivor
en: Tell me... soldier... do you still hold sway with your king?

speaker: Ynyr Ap Cadfarch
en: He consults me for his every decision. If I push for war, he will agree. If I argue for peace, he will follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: Peace is our desired end. Is there a chance that some silver might lead you to counsel your king in the same direction?

speaker: Ynyr Ap Cadfarch
en: A sack of silver? For me? Hm. Yes, I might amend my advice to Rhodri for a tidy sum of shining metal. Yes.

speaker: Ivarr
en: We should settle this with blood, not pretty words.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lady. Let is get past the anger and find our way to an agreement. What is your husband's greatest concern?

speaker: Angharad
en: The royal treasury has been depleted by the war. This brings immense strain to Rhodri and his every decision.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I could provide a boon of silver, would that guide your husband way from the war?

speaker: Angharad
en: A replenished treasury would certainly help my husband come to peace.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ahh! Enough of this nonsense!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Lock the doors. Murder that sweating pig and have done with it.

speaker: Eivor
en: If I could find you silver, would that quell your bitterness while we seek peace?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Peace. Is that what you think is going to happen here? I told you, I know this bastard.

speaker: Eivor
en: Will silver quiet you?

speaker: Ivarr
en: It may, it may not. I would have to see the silver in my hands to know for sure.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are Gwriad, are you not? Brother to King Rhodri.

speaker: Gwriad ap Merfyn
en: So I am. And a bruised pawn in your bloody game.

speaker: Eivor
en: How do you stand with your brother?

speaker: Gwriad ap Merfyn
en: My brother loves me well. Yet he can be slow and stubborn. Were I king, I'd have played all this quite differently.

speaker: Eivor
en: What if you had the chance?

speaker: Gwriad ap Merfyn
en: At the crown? I would leap at the chance to rule. But a man needs wealth to bring down a king. Nobles must be bought, you understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: I make no promises, but I may be able to find you the silver you need.

speaker: Gwriad ap Merfyn
en: Under what terms?

speaker: Eivor
en: Knock Rhodri from his throne, withdraw all Briton soldiers from Sciropescire, and never again threaten this border.

speaker: Gwriad ap Merfyn
en: If you speak true, I would make that bargain gladly.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should report what I know to Bishop Deorlaf.

speaker: Letter to Bishop Deorlaf from Ceolwulf
en: Revered Bishop, It is my intention to install my son, Ceolbert, as Ealdorman of Sciropescire. However, he is yet young and untested. I ask that you, good Bishop, stand as ealdorman and exercise all attendant powers until such time as my boy grows into himself. At which point, you shall return to your God-ordained duties. Ceolwulf, King of Mercia

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Eivor, my friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: I asked around as you suggested.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Have you come to a decision? To whom have you given the silver?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have yet to make my decision.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Please, don't tarry.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take this. Spend it as you will, and tell Rhodri his best path is peace.

speaker: Ynyr ap Cadfarch
en: You have a bargain.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are a wise warrior. Perhaps the silver will become available.

speaker: Ynyr ap Cadfarch
en: Hmph. And you, go take a shit and let me know how it turns out.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ynyr.

speaker: Ynyr ap Cadfarch
en: You again. What of the silver you spoke of?

speaker: Eivor
en: Lady Angharad. Take this silver. Do what you can to calm your husband.

speaker: Angharad
en: I shall. The Kingdom of Gwynedd thanks you.

speaker: Eivor
en: If such a boon comes, I'll consider your words.

speaker: Eivor
en: Dear lady.

speaker: Angharad
en: The treasure you spoke of would help bring us to peace.

speaker: Eivor
en: Damn your eyes. Here is the silver. Do with it what you will, but do not upset this chance at peace.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I did not know you were so foolish with coin.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Silver! Good. I can bludgeon Rhodri to death with how heavy a bag I have.

speaker: Eivor
en: If there is any silver to be had, I'll think about it.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You do that.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Now you dangle silver before me? Are you so frightened of the Britons that you fight your battles with wealth?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Back again, eh? Brought any treasure with you? I will see that it is well spent.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take this silver, depose your brother, and you'll rule with our support.

speaker: Gwriad ap Merfyn
en: His blood will gush at my first opportunity.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will see about the silver.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gwriad.

speaker: Gwriad ap Merfyn
en: Are we in league, Dane? To buy me a throne? What say you?

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Eivor, my friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: I spoke with more people.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Have you made a decision at last? Ivarr is increasingly agitated.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Captain of the Guard will advise Rhodri to sign the agreement. Peace will be yours.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Let is pray Rhodri takes his advice.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lady Angharad will use the silver to bolster the royal treasury. That will reassure and calm Rhodri.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Ah. A wise woman indeed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I gave the silver to Ivarr for his assurance that he will stay calm.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: I have yet to see Ivarr look calm.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rhodri's brother will use the silver to take the crown himself, by force.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: He promised rebellion? Are you sure this was wise?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your silver's in the hands of one who wants it most. Now pray to your god it does some good.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Rhodri! I see you mocking me! I challenge you! Single combat. Now!

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Ivarr, no!

speaker: King Rhodri
en: Boneless Ivarr. Spineless, toothless, gutless. You cannot kill me! A dragon will be my death as my seers have foretold!

speaker: Ivarr
en: And your brother? Does your destiny guard him?

speaker: Angharad
en: Gwriad!

speaker: King Rhodri
en: By God Almighty, I'll

speaker: Ynyr Ap Cadfarch
en: Get them to safety. Go! Quickly!

speaker: King Rhodri
en: Kill the Boneless one! Paint this chapel with his blood!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr! What have you done?

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ahh! Now that is vikingr diplomacy! Show the fuckers who the real warriors are.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Ivarr, you have scuppered the peace!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Do not be fooled by peace, boy. It is just an empty voice between axe blows.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Dear Lord, this is a massacre!

speaker: Eivor
en: We have no choice now but to fight our way out of this.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ah! A good test for you, boy!

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Lord, forgive us.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Stay close, Ceolbert. You watch my back and I will pull the knives from yours!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Dear Lord.

speaker: Eivor
en: Stay here where it's safest, bishop.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gwriad won't need this silver now.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Help me with this fucking door!

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Rhodri's fled! It's war!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Briton cowards. I am Ivarr, King Killer!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: For Mercia!

speaker: Eivor
en: There are more at the river!

speaker: Norse Warrior
en: Gut them!

speaker: Briton Warrior
en: Kill the Danes!

speaker: Ceolbert
en: Good God, what carnage. We must let Bishop Deorlaf know that the battle is done.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You did yourself proud, ætheling.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: This was not a battle we needed, Ivarr.

speaker: Ivarr
en: When you are king, Ceolbert, you won't need battles. You will crave them.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: You murdered Rhodri's brother, you beast! Our one chance at peace is lost!

speaker: Ivarr
en: Peace with Rhodri is as likely as you dying a virgin, bishop. It won't happen. He is too canny, too vile.

speaker: Eivor
en: You nearly got Ceolbert killed, you boneless flap of leather.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Ah, the diplomat speaks what she really feels.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fail us again, Son of Ragnar, and I'll send you back to Repton without your limbs.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's done is done. We must plan our next moves before the Britons regroup.

speaker: Eivor
en: Ivarr has a point. Rhodri showed us nothing but contempt. Peace was not to be written today.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You see, ætheling ? Eivor understands. There can be no peace with these backwards Britons.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's done is done. We must plan our next moves before the Britons regroup.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's done is done. We must plan our next moves before the Britons regroup.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: They will retreat to their great castle, for certain. It's well-nigh impregnable.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Then we starve them out. Attack their supplies. Watch them beg for death.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Dear God. More death, more war, endless refugees.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is our only way forward, Deorlaf. You know the territory best, how can we hurt them?

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Well... for food and supplies, they stockpile cargo at Wenlocan Outpost, down south of Quatford.

speaker: Eivor
en: I came across Wenlocan earlier. I've taken that cargo already.

speaker: Ivarr
en: Well done, drengr (courageous warrior).

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Rhodri has another secret supply line. Ask those among the refugees near the river. Those who have fled from occupied villages.

speaker: Eivor
en: Rhodri's Britons will strike back long before we can.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Indeed. They will send Ynyr and his soldiers. They train in Wesberie, west of the ruined tower.

speaker: Ivarr
en: You do not need me to hold your hand, Eivor. I will head to Wesberie, scout around.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I know your methods of scouting. It always leads to swordplay.

speaker: Ivarr
en: I'm as regular as tidewater.

speaker: Ceolbert
en: I shall go with you. If only to get an honest accounting of our situation.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll meet you both in Wesberie then, once I've done some damage. Until then.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: One last thing. We'll need a ' before our battle's done. Try to free any captives you find. They'll swell our ranks.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good bishop.

speaker: Bishop Deorlaf
en: Have you made progress, my friend?

speaker: Eivor
en: Some. Have no fear.

speaker: Toka
en: Welcome to Francia!

speaker: Eivor
en: What? No sniveling emissary from King Charles to greet us?

speaker: Toka
en: Believe me, Wolf-Kissed, you will feel the warmth of his welcome soon enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: Their mad king did this?

speaker: Toka
en: We all had a part in it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Gods. This is what he would bring to Ravensthorpe.

speaker: Toka
en: It is. We are almost there. But we cannot take the longship around Paris as the Franks' bridges block the way.

speaker: Toka
