en: Our village is inland. We will take the horses from here. The others will follow on foot.

speaker: Eivor
en: Is there danger of an ambush?

speaker: Toka
en: Not this close to the water, and not at night. Sigfred has done his work too well.

speaker: Pierre
en: I will finish unloading the ship. You two go ahead.

speaker: Toka
en: Many thanks, Pierre.

speaker: Pierre
en: And Eivor... there is something we should talk about when I arrive at Melun. Until then, ride safe.

speaker: Toka
en: Mount up. The ride is not long.

speaker: Toka
en: How will I face Sigfred? He entrusted me to gather axes. He wants me to lead one day, but I failed even this.

speaker: Eivor
en: The failure is not all yours, Toka. Jarls are ever busy with their own concerns.

speaker: Toka
en: Ah! Just give me strong ale and a good fight. What else matters?

speaker: Toka
en: Frankish scouts. They have been watching us closely of late. What do you think it means, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: That Sigfred has not finished his work yet.

speaker: Toka
en: Sigfred will not be finished until there are no more Franks left to fight. Scouts have been gnawing at our heels ever since Charles forced us from the North.

speaker: Eivor
en: He pushes hard against your people. You might have to lead sooner than you expect, Toka.

speaker: Toka
en: I may not be the best one to do it.

speaker: Toka
en: I see the longhouse. We are almost there.

speaker: Toka
en: It is strange to be back after so long. I thought to return with an army.

speaker: Toka
en: Welcome to Melun. We should find Sigfred.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Toka! You have returned! All went well, I hope. Are the others you brought coming behind you?

speaker: Toka
en: I need to find Sigfred.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: Of course. Well, you will find him where he always is.

speaker: Toka
en: Ah yes. He will be at the burial grounds, staring into the mist. It is where he begins most days. This way.

speaker: Toka
en: Our burial grounds. Sinric... my father lies there, with the others. We should go.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is something ... calming about this place.

speaker: Toka
en: It is a beautiful land, or would be if it was not filled with Franks. There is Sigfred. You go ahead. He may not be happy to see me return with so few allies.

speaker: Sigfred
en: I will not rest, brother. We are almost there. Your honor will be redeemed, I swear it.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigfred?

speaker: Sigfred
en: You came, Wolf-Kissed. Good.

speaker: Eivor
en: You knew it was me?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Pierre sent word ahead. Your axe will be a boon to us.

speaker: Eivor
en: I heard your axe has been busy as well.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Yes, I have slain many on the open field with honor, as Odin intended.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is our way.

speaker: Sigfred
en: But it is not their way. The Franks dragged our jarl Sinric from his bed, and gutted him like a coward. They did not even bury him, just left his body for the animals to take. I raised this mound for him.

speaker: Eivor
en: You want me to join your side against these Franks.

speaker: Sigfred
en: There is no side! There is only blood-debt, and vengeance, and Helheim for those I split with my axe.

speaker: Eivor
en: I know of blood-debt, and vengeance. When the time comes, Sigfred, you will have my axe.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Good. It is as I hoped.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am sorry for your sword-brother, Sigfred. Odin himself will grant you your vengeance. But my first duty is to my clan.

speaker: Sigfred
en: That is a fair saying, when you are in England. You are in Francia now.

speaker: Eivor
en: How dangerous are these Franks? What do they want?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Do you not understand? They want us as Sinric, dead and dishonored! But I will teach them what honor means.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Now, we will feast, and I will tell you of my plans for Paris.

speaker: Sigfred
en: This is Vidarr. A more noble beast I have never known.

speaker: Eivor
en: The god of vengeance. It is a good name.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Many Franks have met their end beneath his iron hooves. He hates them almost as much as I do.

speaker: Eivor
en: You placed a carving at Sinric's grave.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Sinric won it from me in a ' when we were children. It is Eikthyrnir, who watches over Odin's hall in Valhalla. He was holding it when I found him. It was the only way I knew him after the animals had gotten to his body.

speaker: Toka
en: Ours will be the greatest raid since Ragnar sacked Paris, and brought longships full of silver back to King ! We will fill our warchest with silver and our mugs with mead! Blood and glory! Skal!

speaker: Sigfred
en: This is not just about silver, Toka!

speaker: Toka
en: He hates being disturbed while he eats.

speaker: Eivor
en: You know, Ragnar returned with more than just silver.

speaker: Toka
en: More than silver? What was it? Swords? Precious jewels? Wine!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stories... of a dead saint defending Paris. Horik was so awed, he freed the Christians and executed his raiders.

speaker: Toka
en: Really? That does not sound glorious.

speaker: Engelwin
en: "Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good to thee." Kill the heathens. Bring me Sigfred's head, and that one as well. Leave the stripling alive to tell of it.

speaker: Toka
en: The what!

speaker: Sigfred
en: Bishop Engelwin. This is a good night.

speaker: Eivor
en: O, shit!

speaker: Eivor
en: Horses give them advantage, but it will not be enough.

speaker: Sigfred
en: Where did Engelwin go?

speaker: French Soldier 1
en: Mmmphhh... mmph.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigfred, wait!

speaker: Eivor
en: What did he say to you?

speaker: Sigfred
en: Toka, see to the wounded, and find the watch! They should have warned us of the attack.

speaker: Toka
en: I told he doesn't like to be interrupted while eating.

speaker: Eivor
en: We needed that soldier alive to question. Wild heart, level head.

speaker: Toka
en: O, I like that!

speaker: Eivor
en: Where is Sigfred going?

speaker: Toka
en: My guess is to find that bishop, Engelwin. He hates him above all others. It was he who killed Sinric.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, his sword-brother and your father. I am sorry, Toka.

speaker: Toka
en: Nothing has changed. If anything, the attacks grow more frequent, as you see.

speaker: Eivor
en: Randvi was right. I have to stop this before it reaches Ravensthorpe.

speaker: Toka
en: Pff! Unless you can convince their king to surrender, you may have to kill every soldier in Francia.

speaker: Eivor
en: If we take Paris, many of their soldiers will die. Charles knows that. The threat of it will force him to negotiate.

speaker: Toka
en: That oath-breaking coward will never meet you! Even if he does, his word is worthless. Better to kill him.

speaker: Eivor
en: Then I will meet with Charles and see if he can be negotiated with.

speaker: Toka
en: Their king? That pork-bellied coward will split your skull when you turn your back. Better to kill him than to trust him.

speaker: Eivor
en: This battle will not be won with axes. I must find a way to meet Charles, and convince him not to attack England.

speaker: Toka
en: Remember, Charles murdered . He will not honor his word. Better to kill him.

speaker: Eivor
en: The problem is bigger than one king, Toka. I must talk to him. It is what my clan expects.

speaker: Toka
en: You may be right. But I am not the one you will have to convince in the end.

speaker: Toka
en: If you kill Engelwin, Sigfred may be persuaded to help you find Charles.

speaker: Eivor
en: You begin to think like a jarl, Toka.

speaker: Toka
en: Twice our scouts followed Engelwin to the slums south of Paris. When you are ready, that is where Sigfred will be.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will meet Sigfred there, and return when Engelwin is dead. Then we will find Charles.

speaker: Havi
en: Listen now to the tale of my first meeting with the Lord of Muspelheim! As I made my way onward, I saw Muspels lurking ahead of me. I attacked in a battle-fury! Soon enough, I chanced upon a fearsome Muspel, glowing with inner fire!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Baa-lessings for the season! Yule goats! Made with care! Baa! Baa! Quality yule goats for the winter! Get them while they last! Would you like to baa-uy some expertly made yule goats?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: A yule goat for your silver?

speaker: Eivor
en: Where are these toy goats, child?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: I keep them safe elsewhere. My sister and I made them, and they are finest in the land! I'm not sure about being the finest. But I do love them, every one! Baa!

speaker: Eivor
en: If you have one in the likeness of , I will take it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Wow! Thank you! I did it, Sis! I sold one! I did it!

speaker: Eivor
en: You will find a buyer, young one. But not right now.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: If you ever change your mind, come baa-ck here! The warmest winter to you!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Sis! Sis! I did it! Someone bought a goat!

speaker: Eivor
en: What about my goat? Where are you going?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: You'll be so happy, Sis! Someone bought a goat!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Sis, this nice stranger bought our goats. I miss you, Sis. Especially during Yule. I hope wherever you are, there are plenty of woolly fluffy goats to keep you warm!

speaker: Eivor
en: Sister? This is your sister?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: We made the goats together! But the cold took her last winter. I promised her I would continue selling our goats. She said they can bring warmth into the hearts of others. Here, it's yours. I hope it will keep you warm on your travels! Goodbye, nice stranger!

speaker: Eivor
en: Rest, spirit. Your legacy lives on with your sister.

speaker: Brokkr
en: These are the finest tools you'll ever lay eyes on!

speaker: Ivaldi
en: The finest? I've forged better in my sleep!

speaker: Brokkr
en: Yeah? Is that why you were snooping about in the ruins of the old workshop?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Only because the Muspels stole everything I had, dimwit.

speaker: Havi
en: Good to see you're getting along.

speaker: Havi
en: So Brokkr, do you accept your duty?

speaker: Brokkr
en: Don't have much choice, do I? Last thing I need is a godly smiting up me arse.

speaker: Havi
en: Let this be the start of a beautiful new friendship.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: To study the Salakar, I'll need the very best of tools. Too bad this workshop is lacking.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Bugger off. I got more stuff here than you can wag a finger at.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Doubt it.

speaker: Brokkr
en: If you find something you don't know how to use, just ask.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Ha! I'll be giving you lessons on how to use your own―

speaker: Eysa
en: Bickering dwarves. How unusual.

speaker: Havi
en: Eysa, you return.

speaker: Brokkr
en: What? You deal with a fire nymph?

speaker: Eysa
en: Not this again.

speaker: Havi
en: What news do you bring?

speaker: Eysa
en: My stepmother is stubborn. I cannot push too hard or she will grow suspicious.

speaker: Havi
en: She has no interest in a trade?

speaker: Eysa
en: Interest yes, but not yet the will.

speaker: Havi
en: I don't understand.

speaker: Eysa
en: The Salakar is all but indestructible. You, on the other hand, are not.

speaker: Havi
en: She assumes she'll catch me, kill me, and retrieve the Salakar.

speaker: Eysa
en: Time is on her side.

speaker: Havi
en: Then I must strip her of this illusion... If I were to make a nuisance of myself, one that cannot be ignored...

speaker: Eysa
en: Sinmara prepares to lead my father's next major invasion.

speaker: Havi
en: But if I were to disrupt her plans... it may force her to the bargaining table.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Sounds risky to me.

speaker: Havi
en: I once plotted and carried out the murder of Ymir himself. What do I care of risk?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Well, since you put it like that...

speaker: Havi
en: Where must I strike?

speaker: Eysa
en: At Afalvat Mylna, my stepmother develops a strange army. At Jöfurrsmida, she breeds beasts of war. And finally there's Drekathorp, her supplies hub.

speaker: Havi
en: I'll deal with all three.

speaker: Eysa
en: In the meantime, I shall return to Eitri. I will send word once my stepmother has become more... amenable.

speaker: Havi
en: I'll return when I'm done. And I will expect answers regarding the Salakar.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Alright then, where do we start?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: If I knew that, I wouldn't be here!

speaker: Brokkr
en: Miserable sod. We best get on with it then.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Yes, you just follow my lead.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Who put you in charge?

speaker: Ivaldi
en: You were once your brother's apprentice. Now you are mine.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Apprentice!? Are you having a laugh? This is my shelter and my rules!

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Then we are truly doomed.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: To solve this task, we must put our minds together. Well, my mind, and whatever you call that thing between your ears.

speaker: Brokkr
en: Piss off. In all our time together, I never had no complaints from my brother.

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Mjölnir?

speaker: Brokkr
en: It wasn't my fault! Everyone knows that! Everyone!

speaker: Ivaldi
en: Of course it wasn't.

speaker: Havi
en: I have work to do.

speaker: Havi
en: So this is where Sinmara creates her mysterious army.

speaker: Havi
en: Not even Loki could dream up such twisted aberrations of nature!

speaker: Havi
en: Do you weep yet, Sinmara? This is just a small vengeance for what you did to Frigg.

speaker: Havi
en: So, this is where the she-demon stores her precious supplies...

speaker: Havi
en: Soon Surtr's warriors will have grumbling bellies, and only sticks with which to fight.

speaker: Havi
en: Why wait for Ragnarök? I bring my own.

speaker: Havi
en: Unleash the beasts!

speaker: Havi
en: If there are more, I must release them too.

speaker: Havi
en: It is done! The pigs run wild!

speaker: Havi
en: Without these plans, no further beasts can be bred. No more piggies for you, Sinmara!

speaker: Havi
en: Once Baldr is free, he and I shall feast on the roasted flesh of these mighty pigs!

speaker: Havi
en: Now Sinmara will negotiate. Baldr for the Salakar... and then, together, he and I will steal it back.

speaker: Eivor
en: What happened here? And what befell the driver?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Huh... There's a bear in here who wants to eat my face. I would quite like it subdued, please. Hello? I can hear you out there! Aren't you going to save me? If I die, it'll be your fault, you know. Do you want that on your conscience? Do you?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Perhaps a chokehold would do the trick? Be gentle! I don't want it bruised! Use the flat of your blade!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Did you kill it? You weren't supposed to actually kill it! Get in here, now! I want a word with you!

speaker: Eivor
en: Your gratitude is touching.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Gratitude? That was my prize fighting bear you killed. How am I supposed to make my living now?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is thanks to me that you are living at all.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: O, thank you, Your Majesty! Please accept my eternal loyalty for condemning me to abject poverty!

speaker: Eivor
en: I should teach you some manners.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You can take your manners and shove 'em where Odin can't see. Let's do this, you filthy Dane!

speaker: Eivor
en: Stilling that bitter tongue was a service to all.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm sorry. You seemed like you were in danger.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: Sorry? Sorry won't feed my seven children. What am I to do now?

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe pick a smaller animal to abuse next time. Farewell.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: How am I going to feed my children now that my bear is dead? Without my bear, all I have is my winning personality. O God, I'm doomed. That cursed animal! Trying to kill me! I should have it beaten it more while I had the chance.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're welcome. Enjoy life as a beggar!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: You've ruined me, and you don't care. No one cares. What a world, what a world!

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe pick a smaller animal to abuse next time. Farewell.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man
en: How am I going to feed my children now that my bear is dead? Without my bear, all I have is my winning personality. O God, I'm doomed. That cursed animal! Trying to kill me! I should have it beaten it more while I had the chance.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wedding preparation's in full bloom.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 1
en: Come come, the wedding is soon to start!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child 2
en: How grand!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 1
en: A beautiful and worthy celebration, my lord.

speaker: Oswald
en: Thank you. May this feast set a spirited tone for East Anglia's future.

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor, I'm so glad you've made it! Just like you to keep a king waiting at his own wedding.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yet, I arrived in the end.

speaker: Oswald
en: A part of me worried you wouldn't.

speaker: Eivor
en: I told you I'd see you crowned. And now here we are.

speaker: Oswald
en: Without you, I'd be dead. Another wasted hope for East Anglia.

speaker: Eivor
en: You look good, Oswald. Like a man about to marry a more powerful woman.

speaker: Oswald
en: Do I? Because I'm nervous as hell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of all the battles a man can fight, the war against himself is the hardest to win.

speaker: Eivor
en: I came for the food and the mead. Is there a wedding as well?

speaker: Oswald
en: There is, there is! You won't be disappointed by what Elmenham has to offer.

speaker: Eivor
en: You look good, Oswald. Like a man about to marry a more powerful woman.

speaker: Oswald
en: Do I? Because I'm nervous as hell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of all the battles a man can fight, the war against himself is the hardest to win.

speaker: Eivor
en: You look good, Oswald. Like a man about to marry a more powerful woman.

speaker: Oswald
en: Do I? Because I'm nervous as hell.

speaker: Eivor
en: Of all the battles a man can fight, the war against himself is the hardest to win.

speaker: Finnr
en: I hereby name you man and wife. And as man and wife, I name you...

speaker: Finnr
en: Oswald of Elmenham, first of his name, the rightful king of East Anglia... with his Lady Valdis, soul, fist, and beauty of this land.

speaker: Eivor
en: You've done it, steward. A king now sits on the throne of East Anglia.

speaker: Finnr
en: Don't leave yourself out of this song. We did it together.

speaker: Eivor
en: Back to your dreams, then. Of fire and Helheim.

speaker: Finnr
en: I lost my way some time ago. Hard to say when. I don't want to be here. I never did. This was Halfdan's dream. He ordered me to see it through. In my dreams, I'm sailing, remember? Wind in my beard, salt on my lips. I want that life again. Whether or not I find it, only time will tell. Until then, let us feast, drink, and forget our pain!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: A Dane? Leading a Saxon army?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: Better than her brothers too. She charged into battle without fear.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 2
en: She stormed Burgh Castle, brought Rued to his knees. And let Oswald hold him for trial?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 3
en: I could hardly believe my ears either.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 4
en: It was Oswald's wishes.

speaker: Brothir
en: Eivor, care for a challenge?

speaker: Brothir
en: Eivor! Wolf-Kissed! Gaze upon my pots. They stand so strong! Unbreakable at this distance, no?

speaker: Eivor
en: They are not, Brothir. My arrows shatter whatever targets they strike.

speaker: Brothir
en: Even after draining so much mead? Succeed and you shall be rewarded!

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep your eyes open long enough to witness this, you drunken lout.

speaker: Brothir
en: Yes! That's it! As with everything, an easy task for the Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Eivor
en: Barely a challenge.

speaker: Brothir
en: Impressive! Impressive! Here, as promised. Now go enjoy the party.

speaker: Brothir
en: Time's up! You've been bested at last.

speaker: Eivor
en: A waste of my time.

speaker: Brothir
en: Mead and pots confound the Wolf-Kissed! When they write your saga, I'll remind them of this embarrassment.

speaker: Eivor
en: This is beneath me, Brothir.

speaker: Brothir
en: And you're no fun! It took so long to set those pots up, and I... Ooh... ale.

speaker: Eivor
en: Maybe later, Brothir.

speaker: Brothir
en: Eivor!

speaker: Eivor
en: Still waiting for me to break your pots?

speaker: Brothir
en: Yes! No one else will entertain me. Come on! Do it!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I've never seen this church look so beautiful.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 5
en: Oswald designed it himself. Handpicked all the decorations here.

speaker: Unfinished Verses
en: Valdis, I have never heard a name such as yours. But it brings to mind the flowers of my— Dear, Valdis, you are our Queen now. Together we will bear the fruits of— Valdis, you are the sole captor of my soul, my burning ember, the igneous

speaker: Oswald
en: ...so I told the Dane, "You get the wool while the Saxon gets his milk." They'll trade with each other, and when the time comes, we will make it into a good stew for everyone.

speaker: Valdis
en: You like sheep?

speaker: Oswald
en: I hate it, actually. When we make that stew, you can have my bowl.

speaker: Valdis
en: You think in such a strange way.

speaker: Eivor
en: What do you make of this Christian ceremony?

speaker: Valdis
en: Finnr is no priest, but he did the job well enough. And as far as wedding ceremonies go, I intend this one to be my last.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald is a good man.

speaker: Valdis
en: He is. If not for you, I would have lost him. Thank you, Eivor.

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor! The festivities have only just begun. Enjoy yourself.

speaker: Norse Man
en: Behold! How light-footed I am!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: You're as light-footed as a bear in a birch tree!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: These are the moves of Elmenham!

speaker: Norse Child 1
en: Large walker! Join us, large walker!

speaker: Eivor
en: Ah, my small walkers! I see that you are enjoying yourselves.

speaker: Norse Child 2
en: Of course! There is plenty of cake for walkers all around East Anglia now, both large and small!

speaker: Broder
en: Skal, Eivor! Let's have a drink!

speaker: Broder
en: Your fist is without ale! Let us address that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Surely a special kind of mettle is required for drinking before the new king.

speaker: Broder
en: A mettle not unlike your own!

speaker: Eivor
en: To Odin and his endless glories.

speaker: Brotder
en: And the new king of East Anglia! May his reign be long and good!

speaker: Broder
en: Not bad, Wolf-Kissed! I wager you couldn't drink more than me if you tried.

speaker: Eivor
en: A fool's wager.

speaker: Broder
en: A challenge nonetheless. What say you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will drink you under the table.

speaker: Broder
en: Confident are you? Let us see how you fair against the Ale Beast of East Anglia. And we'll make it interesting. Put your silver where your mouth is. What say you?

speaker: Eivor
en: I accept.

speaker: Eivor
en: Silver? Such tiny ambition. Do this for the skalds (poets) that will sing songs of our superior bellies.

speaker: Broder
en: Then let our guts live forever in their tales. Come, let the making of a legend begin!

speaker: Eivor
en: I could use a drink and shame you all at once, Broder. But not right now.

speaker: Broder
en: Eivor! Drink, come drink!

speaker: Eivor
en: Still here, drunkard?

speaker: Broder
en: Waiting for you! Come now, accept my challenge.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could use a drink and shame you all at once, Broder. But not right now.

speaker: Broder
en: Eivor! Drink, come drink!

speaker: Eivor
en: Still here, drunkard?

speaker: Broder
en: Waiting for you! Come now, accept my challenge.

speaker: Eivor
en: The ale here... it's strong. But I am stronger.

speaker: Broder
en: Aye, stronger than me. You drink as well as Valdis. Now that I would pay to see!

speaker: Eivor
en: Speaking of payment, where is my silver?

speaker: Broder
en: Here. Well earned, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll (hic) get you next time.

speaker: Eivor
en: This ale is strong, Broder.

speaker: Broder
en: Hah, but I am stronger! Better luck next time, Wolf-Kissed.

speaker: Broder
en: Now, you owe me some silver.

speaker: Eivor
en: Fine, take it.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 6
en: Skal? Is that what you say?

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Yes, to celebrate. Skal! Drink more!

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: Look there, Finnr on the roof!

speaker: Norse Man 2
en: The road to Valhalla does not run that way, Finnr!

speaker: Norse Woman 2
en: He's been up there a while.

speaker: Finnr
en: Eivor, Eivor. Some sweet wine for a sweet swine. Come join me!

speaker: Finnr
en: The Saxon god wanders somewhere up here, does he not? I haven't seen him.

speaker: Eivor
en: They like to say he moves with mystery.

speaker: Finnr
en: Look, the moon! It moves untroubled now. But one day, it will be eaten by a giant wolf, and the nights will be black forevermore.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you all right?

speaker: Finnr
en: I tasted glory once again! And it was good.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm glad to hear it. Now

speaker: Finnr
en: I always felt like or , chasing and trying to fulfill Halfdan's wishes. But now I've caught my Sun and Moon... I've got them and I... I don't know.

speaker: Eivor
en: You can let them go. Sail to a further shore.

speaker: Finnr
en: My longship's in Valhalla! Or don't you remember, Fire-Starter?

speaker: Eivor
en: Come on. Let's get you to solid ground.

speaker: Finnr
en: Hm! Everything's spinny.

speaker: Finnr
en: You're very stong.

speaker: Eivor
en: Y-you're very large.

speaker: Finnr
en: Sorry for this, Eivor. I've had one last glory, I should be happy. I am happy. Thank you.

speaker: Eivor
en: It need not be the last.

speaker: Finnr
en: Not the last...

speaker: Broder
en: The boar represents fertility. Did you know that?

speaker: Eivor
en: As does Freyr. What's your point?

speaker: Broder
en: You impress me, Eivor. Your battle wisdom, your strength of character, skilled in so many ways. Yet I wonder. Is there any skill of mins that I could impress upon you?

speaker: Eivor
en: Even a fool has something to teach, whether they're aware of the lesson or not.

speaker: Broder
en: Aye, aye. but I could show you how to wield my... plough-sword.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be plain about it, stiff-spear. You want to lay with me, is that it?

speaker: Broder
en: That I do. Will you follow me? To a place more comfortable?

speaker: Eivor
en: A good plough-sword is a rare thing. Lead the way.

speaker: Broder
en: Gods...

speaker: Broder
en: That's worth a verse or two in some skalds song. I'll remember that for all time, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I shall as well, Brothir.

speaker: Broder
en: Brothir? I'm not Brothir! Búri's balls! You thought I was my brother?

speaker: Eivor
en: To be honest, I did not think at all.

speaker: Broder
en: All day long, all I hear is Brothir this and Brothir that. How strong he is, how handsome. It's always Brothir, Brothir, Brothir...

speaker: Eivor
en: I will too, Broder.

speaker: Broder
en: The sagas are never this good. This night remains glorious.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sorry, friend. I am hear for mead and merriment. Nothing else.

speaker: Broder
en: Wait, did you hear... Did my brother just call me? I think he... You know, I should go. Brothir?

speaker: Eivor
en: Sheath your plow-sword, Broder. I'm not interested.

speaker: Broder
en: Ah, you thought... No no, I wasn't serious. Come on now, drink and be merry!

speaker: Eivor
en: Well ahead of you, friend.

speaker: Broder
en: Wait, did you hear... Did my brother just call me? I think he... You know, I should go. Brothir?

speaker: Eivor
en: Have another horn of mead, Broder. It's brewed with clover and raspberry, they say.

speaker: Broder
en: Did you hear what I...?

speaker: Broder
en: Mmmm. Yes, it's good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Keep that up.

speaker: Broder
en: Wait, did you hear... Did my brother just call me? I think he... You know, I should go. Brothir?

speaker: Eivor
en: Enough fun and games. I should see how Oswald is doing.

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor, I'm about to address our guests, and I'd like you to be there.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's been a worthy ceremony so far.

speaker: Oswald
en: And have you had enough fun yet?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm ready to hear you address your kingdom.

speaker: Oswald
en: Good. Come, come. Join me.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not yet finished celebrating. I'll come find you when I'm done.

speaker: Oswald
en: Take your time. It can wait.

speaker: Oswald
en: Friends, honored guests. We've pushed through hard times. It seems like all we've known is loss. And suffering. But it is not conflict that binds us. It is compassion. May we always favor compassion, even when our enemies refuse its boon. So... to my Dane friends and neighbors, I give thanks for the bravery you have shown during our collective struggles. And for my fellow Christians, may we continue standing as examples of our Lord's grace. Lights in the dark. I see East Anglia's future right here. Right now. In all of you, Dane and Saxon alike. To our future!

speaker: Broder
en: Still a bit soft on insults, but the king has courage.

speaker: Oswald
en: And to Eivor, without whom none of this would have been possible!

speaker: Valdis
en: On behalf of East Anglia, let this ring be proof of our loyalty to the Raven Clan, and all they have done for us today.

speaker: Oswald
en: Would you have any words of wisdom for us?

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald – you would not have been my first choice as king. Nor my second. I thought you weak, bendable, without resolve. But not all men are as they first appear. I came to see that Oswald's heart is amongst the largest I have ever known. He is sturdy, he has wisdom, he has courage. All qualities worthy of a man to be king. He is the king East Anglia deserves, and the king you need. To the good King Oswald!

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not one to bask in the glow of another's triumph. But I'll say this: East Anglia is safe. Under his protection, under his guidance, under his wing, the good king Oswald will keep you safe for many moons to come.

speaker: Eivor
en: To the good King Oswald! Skal! (Cheers!)

speaker: Broder
en: To Oswald!

speaker: Brothir, Eivor, and Crowd
en: Skal!

speaker: Oswald and Valdis
en: Skal!

speaker: Crowd
en: Skal!

speaker: Finnr
en: Okay, everyone, the bridal race starts now. Remember, you all have to lose to the bride and groom!

speaker: Brothir
en: Quick, brother!

speaker: Broder
en: We can't lose to Oswald!

speaker: Broder
en: Must you win at everything?

speaker: Brothir
en: You lost!

speaker: Eivor
en: It was a beautiful wedding, Oswald. Like you said it would be.

speaker: Oswald
en: Thanks to you and everything you've done here.

speaker: Eivor
en: It won't be easy putting the pieces of East Anglia back together. But you won't be alone. Saxon and Dane have banded together in your name. You're the right man for the throne, and they'll be with you.

speaker: Oswald
en: Thank you, Eivor. I don't know what to say.

speaker: Eivor
en: Everything I've done here was for my clan. Their safety is my night's good rest. You know that feeling, I'm sure.

speaker: Oswald
en: I do.

speaker: Eivor
en: East Anglia needed a leader. I simply helped put the right one on the throne.

speaker: Eivor
en: When we met, I spoke of an alliance. Will you hold to the oath you made?

speaker: Oswald
en: I will. Consider East Anglia a friend of the Raven Clan.

speaker: Eivor
en: There will be a day when I come calling.

speaker: Oswald
en: Goodbye, friend.

speaker: Eivor
en: Until next time, great king.

speaker: Finnr
en: Steady all. And ready yourself for the wedding race, the king and his bride against all!

speaker: Norse Soldier
en: My king!... He... he

speaker: Rued
en: The sheep you left to guard me have been shorn! Oswald! King of the sheep-fuckers! Show your eyes!

speaker: Eivor
en: I challenge you!

speaker: Oswald
en: I accept.

speaker: Rued
en: No square. Only sweat and blood!

speaker: Eivor
en: He may be wounded, but do not let your guard down.

speaker: Oswald
en: Let's settle this.

speaker: Rued
en: I will bury you, Saxon! I'll take all that is yours!

speaker: Oswald
en: Should a king show mercy to one so malevolent? So cruel?

speaker: Oswald
en: I'll not give you the satisfaction of a good death, for my God forbids such cruelty. Therefore you are outcast, from this moment on.

speaker: Rued
en: You have won! My life is yours.

speaker: Oswald
en: Your life is God's.

speaker: Rued
en: Raaaah!

speaker: Oswald
en: Now go, leave my kingdom and never return.

speaker: Broder
en: I do not understand this Saxon religion.

speaker: Brothir
en: Oswald is a coin, one side mercy, the other courage. There are few like him, I'll admit. Saxon or Dane.

speaker: Finnr
en: Such a strange display. Courage and restraint like I have never seen. With all that's happened, with all the chaos Rued wrought... still Oswald found reason to spare him.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a strange thing.

speaker: Finnr
en: A remarkable thing. From what inner spring does such kindness run? I'd like to know.

speaker: Finnr
en: With my duties here fulfilled, I now choose East Anglia. I fight for you, my king.

speaker: Oswald
en: Rise, old friend. You're embarrassing me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be well, Finnr. Your choice is a bold one.

speaker: Eivor
en: You continue to surprise, Oswald of Elmenham.

speaker: Oswald
en: Thank you. When we first met, I made an oath. I promised you an alliance.

speaker: Eivor
en: You did.

speaker: Oswald
en: You'll have it. So long as I draw breath.

speaker: Eivor
en: Till next time, king.

speaker: Eivor
en: Oswald is king, and a king must have a champion. I will fight in his stead.

speaker: Oswald
en: He challenged me, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your fight is bigger than this, Lord. You must rebuild East Anglia, plank by plank. And a dead king cannot keep his oaths. Let me finish this.

speaker: Rued
en: Oswald, you gutless ' (cowardly) swine! I'll slay the Wolf-Kissed, then hang you with your own tongue.

speaker: Rued
en: You! Always getting in the way. East Anglia can burn for all I care!

speaker: Oswald
en: I wish it had not come to this. So much death. So much anger.

speaker: Eivor
en: What's done is done.

speaker: Oswald
en: You're leaving now?

speaker: Eivor
en: I should. Your wedding should be a day of peace and happiness. Today I lack both.

speaker: Oswald
en: Eivor. You've done East Anglia a great service. I promised you an alliance, and now you have it.

speaker: Eivor
en: And one day I will need you to make good on that alliance.

speaker: Eivor
en: I should find Finnr. Say goodbye before I leave.

speaker: Eivor
en: Broder.

speaker: Broder
en: Eivor. You will be missed.

speaker: Eivor
en: I gave you a few good memories to keep.

speaker: Broder
en: That you did.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take care of your king, Broder. He will need you in the years to come.

speaker: Broder
en: Are you sure? Or just guessing?

speaker: Eivor
en: Take good care of your king, my friend. He will need you in the days ahead.

speaker: Broder
en: Aye. He will live without fear. My brother and I will see to that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Broder, look after Oswald, will you?

speaker: Broder
en: Aye, he is family now. And I could not be more proud of him. We have you to thank for that.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take care.

speaker: Broder
en: The old soft-heart has guts. Strange I never saw it until now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Brothir. Oswald is in your hands now. Protect your king. And call out to my banner should the need arise.

speaker: Brothir
en: Aye, Eivor. Without a moment's hesitation. Travel safe.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will, friend.

speaker: Brothir
en: We met in a play of fists, Eivor, and now look at us! Fast friends!

speaker: Eivor
en: Valdis.

speaker: Valdis
en: Will you not stay a moment longer, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: I should not linger. My banner-folk await my return.

speaker: Valdis
en: I understand.

speaker: Eivor
en: Take care, Valdis. You fought well, and won yourself a worthy king.

speaker: Valdis
en: I did, didn't I? Take care, Eivor.

speaker: Valdis
en: Thank you, Eivor, for making today a reality.

speaker: Oswald
en: A dream come true, like none other. Thank you for everything, from the bottom of my heart!

speaker: Oswald
en: I'll send a message to Halfdan in the North. He'll be please to know that a king now sits upon East Anglia's troubled throne.

speaker: Finnr
en: Ah, greetings, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're missing the festivities.

speaker: Finnr
en: I've had my fill.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's as much yours as it is Oswald's.

speaker: Finnr
en: I was a crumbling man, Eivor. Before all this I thought I'd died a tired old failure. But now, my heart burns bright, with newfound fire. I want to live hard, die fierce.

speaker: Eivor
en: Glory cares not for age, Finnr. Sail with me. My ship could always use a wise head and a strong axe.

speaker: Finnr
en: Together?

speaker: Eivor
en: Together.

speaker: Finnr
en: I'll gather my things.

speaker: Finnr
en: What a celebration!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Woman 7
en: It's good that Oswald married a Dane. I'm tired of fighting.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 4
en: I know, Mother. Maybe peace is the way of things now.

speaker: Thor
en: Gaaah! A good fight! But I wish there were more!

speaker: Havi
en: The sky itself shatters before your might, Thor!

speaker: Norse Warrior 1
en: Death to all Jotnar!

speaker: Norse Warrior 2
en: Asgard belongs to the Æsir!

speaker: Norse Warrior 3
en: We are undefeated!

speaker: Norse Warrior 4
en: Glory belongs to the fearless!

speaker: Norse Warrior 5
en: We are proud to serve you, Havi!

speaker: Norse Warrior 6
en: Your fame will live eternal!

speaker: Norse Warrior 7
en: Our strength is unmatched!

speaker: Norse Warrior 8
en: Asgard will never fall!

speaker: Norse Warrior 9
en: A good blood-harvest, Havi!

speaker: Havi
en: My thoughts are clouded with shadows of doom. Even this peaceful valley seems to hold hidden dangers.

speaker: Havi
en: Wolves. I should slay every last one. No prophecy shall bind me.

speaker: Havi
en: The Well of Urdr. Not even I know all your secrets.

speaker: Havi
en: The sunstone has been moved. The light's path has shifted.

speaker: Havi
en: These caves run deep. Nidhogg and his serpents have been busy.

speaker: Týr
en: Havi! Loki said you'd be here. He told me of the Builder's request, an offer that gives me great worry.

speaker: Havi
en: Why was this passage blocked? Has someone been here recently?

speaker: Týr
en: Do you hear me, Havi? This Builder is a stranger to us. We know not what he intends.

speaker: Havi
en: I am the King of Asgard, Týr. Do not question my desire to protect her.

speaker: Tyr
en: Calm, old friend. What's needling you?

speaker: Havi
en: I have known you, Týr, longer than any in Asgard. And I trust you as a brother. But my present worries, I cannot share.

speaker: Týr
en: I understand. The burden of kingship must often be shouldered alone.

speaker: Havi
en: Strange omens and wild portents. Something evil is stirring. And I cannot always sift the truth from what is false.

speaker: Týr
en: Far-Seer, you have sight beyond us all. I have no doubt you will prevail over what troubles you.

speaker: Havi
en: The Nornir told me I would die at Ragnarök. They described the scene of my passing.

speaker: Týr
en: All but a few will perish in the final battle, we know this. Yet we will die well... and live again in great and glorious tales.

speaker: Havi
en: I will need your strength in the coming days. To anchor me, to challenge me, to pull me back from the abyss should I teeter.

speaker: Týr
en: And I will, as long as breath fills me. So I must caution you, step with care in this place. What happens here may ripple through the fabric of the nine worlds.

speaker: Havi
en: The well is sealed. Someone labors to keep me out.

speaker: Týr
en: Perhaps it is meant as a warning.

speaker: Havi
en: I will take it as a challenge.

speaker: Týr
en: I recall there being more light in here.

speaker: Havi
en: These sunstones are meant to guide the light, but the path has been diverted.

speaker: Havi
en: What if an invader was trying to weaken the well's defenses? Are we meant to intervene?

speaker: Týr
en: The integrity of this sacred place must be preserved, but whether we be a bane or a boon remains to be seen.

speaker: Havi
en: There are two targets the light must strike, but only one stream.

speaker: Týr
en: How do two farms share one source of water?

speaker: Havi
en: By splitting the stream.

speaker: Týr
en: You've done this before, Havi.

speaker: Havi
en: Once or twice.

speaker: Týr
en: I doubt the Nornir will appreciate our visit. The curious are not welcome here.

speaker: Havi
en: We'll have come and gone before they feel our presence.

speaker: Havi
en: Now that the light is split, the streams must find their way home.

speaker: Havi
en: The light has found its mark. The stone is lit.

speaker: Týr
en: The well is open to us.

speaker: Havi
en: I will lead.

speaker: Týr
en: Take what you need, and do it quickly. We should not linger.

speaker: Urðr
en: Havi, break our stalemate.

speaker: Verðandi
en: They like to spin in silence.

speaker: Skuld
en: It is done.

speaker: Havi
en: Týr?

speaker: Havi
en: Careless little pup. You shouldn't be here. Where are you? There's no wolf alive I can trust...

speaker: Týr
en: Havi, stop!

speaker: Havi
en: Out of my way, Týr. I'll suffer no wolves in Asgard!

speaker: Týr
en: This is a sacred place. Killing here is forbidden, you know this Havi.

speaker: Týr
en: Has your mind fled you? You act as though possessed by the spirit of another!

speaker: Havi
en: I am the Many in the One, Týr. The Yeller, the Spear Charger, the Masked One. I am Long Beard and Shaggy cloak. I am the Wanderer and the Striver. And now I am the Foe of the Wolf. Nothing can change this now.

speaker: Týr
en: Whatever mind drives you, Havi, you mustn't kill here. Shed no innocent blood in this sacred place.

speaker: Havi
en: My mind is my own, Týr. But you pose a curious thought. Could one mind usurp another's? The hugr (mind) of one in the body of someone else?

speaker: Týr
en: Are you drunk on these waters? Take your flask, forget the wolf, and let us be gone before the Nornir weave us a pair of shackles!

speaker: Havi
en: The Nornir warned me... a wolf will be my doom at Ragnarok.

speaker: Týr
en: Will you slay every wolf in the nine realms to sidestep this fate? Ridiculous!

speaker: Havi
en: Take this beast, I want it caged. I would have every wolf and dog in Asgard caged if I could.

speaker: Týr
en: To ease your troubled mind, I will do as you ask. We need you focused for the coming war.

speaker: Havi
en: Thank you, Courage-Bringer, for your steady hand.

speaker: Týr
en: When one descends this deep, there's no going back up.

speaker: Havi
en: Then the only way is further down.

speaker: Loki
en: When a thought enters your head, you're not afraid to take the plunge!

speaker: Havi
en: Loki?

speaker: Loki
en: How was it in there? All is well?

speaker: Loki
en: Hello! Havi! Over here!

speaker: Loki
en: You entered the well, did you not? And you found what you were looking for?

speaker: Havi
en: I have a skin of sacred water, yes. Is the Builder preparing his demonstration?

speaker: Loki
en: How did the well look? Peaceful? Calm? Quiet?

speaker: Havi
en: What are you driving at, Loki?

speaker: Loki
en: Driving at? I'm only curious. The well is a wondrous place, I wish I could see it for myself.

speaker: Havi
en: There was a wolf cub with us, trespassing on sacred ground. But Týr took care of it.

speaker: Loki
en: Took care of it? Is he dead?

speaker: Havi
en: It should never have been born into this world.

speaker: Loki
en: O, what have you done? What have you done!

speaker: Havi
en: Týr convinced me to spare it, against my better instincts.

speaker: Loki
en: Ah, yes. To be sure, intellect should overrule our instinct. Týr knows this well.

speaker: Havi
en: The wolf lives. But Týr will cage the beast at his hall. I want no free wolves in Asgard.

speaker: Loki
en: Ah, yes. Good. A wise decision, Havi.

speaker: Havi
en: I wanted to kill it, but Týr stayed my hand.

speaker: Loki
en: Týr is pragmatic, and it serves him well. You should heed him more often.

speaker: Havi
en: I asked you a question, Loki. Is the Builder ready or not?

speaker: Loki
en: The wolf, Mad One! What have you done to the wolf!

speaker: Havi
en: The beast lives for now. Test my patience further, and I may fashion a cap from its coat.

speaker: Loki
en: There's no need, Havi, no need. I only worry about the purity of the well. That's all and no more.

speaker: Havi
en: Now tell me plainly. Where is the Builder?

speaker: Loki
en: In a meadow, not far from here. Your raven may find the way.

speaker: Eivor
en: What a strange place. Who could have known this was on the Isle of Skye?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look alive! There are more coming!

speaker: Eivor
en: I had this under control.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Under control? Looks like you were about to get skewered.

speaker: Eivor
en: I can defend myself. You didn't need to come.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Admit it. You missed me.

speaker: Eivor
en: Let me rephrase that. You shouldn't have come.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know my presence make things complicated...

speaker: Eivor
en: These people are attacking me because of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know, I know! Can we talk about this once they're dead?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should have been honest about my presence activating the artifact. I'm sorry. And I know me being here makes reaching the artifact harder.

speaker: Eivor
en: Harder? No one would be trying to kill me if you weren't here right now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know! But trust me, you will need my help once we reach the artifact. These people are nothing compared to its power.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm not getting rid of you, am I?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry. I'll grow on you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen mechanisms like this before. I'll get the light working. You direct the beams to those plates near the door.

speaker: Eivor
en: So I can move these. I see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One down, one to go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There! It's opening!

speaker: Eivor
en: Finally.

speaker: Eivor
en: Those pots and weapons are so strange.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're from my land.

speaker: Eivor
en: What are they doing here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's an illusion caused by the artifact.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you being near it?

speaker: Eivor
en: That mask looks unique.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've torn many of those masks from the faces of cultists. Even knowing they're illusions, to see all these things from my... my...

speaker: Eivor
en: Home?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have a home. Not anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That can't be... Phoibe.

speaker: Eivor
en: Kassandra, what are you doing? Come. You said yourself all this is just an illusion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need a moment.

speaker: Unknown
en: Honor our blood long after we're gone...

speaker: Eivor
en: Kassandra!

speaker: Eivor
en: All that trouble for this?

speaker: Eivor
en: You keep it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Admit it, we make a good team.

speaker: Eivor
en: You're not so bad to work with, after all. Terrible at following orders, though.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give me a little credit. It's my first time working with another person in... I don't know how many years.

speaker: Eivor
en: I could've handled it myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Please, I practically saved you.

speaker: Eivor
en: For a foreigner, you're certainly as stubborn as a Norseman.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I might have become stuck in my ways after working alone for so long.

speaker: Eivor
en: That must get lonely.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It does, from time to time. But it's the path I'm meant to walk. Anyway, I should get going. It's not good for me to stay in one place long. Thank you for your help. Truly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Wait. The Norse celebrate their victories. And since in the end, you did help... Why not come out for a drink with me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I... I don't know about that. It's not really good for me to be seen by too many people.

speaker: Eivor
en: If everyone drinks enough, no one will ever know you were here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. What can it hurt?

speaker: Eivor
en: Hopefully your head tomorrow morning if we have a great time. Meet you at the longhouse in Kiltaraglen?

speaker: Kassandra
en: See you there.

speaker: Sigurd
en: So strange... little has changed, but it feels unfamiliar.

speaker: Eivor
en: Our few years abroad have shaped us more than all the decades we spent here, Brother.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And it's bloody cold. Colder than I remember.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This is Harald Fairhair's kingdom now, every peak and fjord. It pains me to say it, to think it even.

speaker: Eivor
en: And our father his fool, the poor man.

speaker: Sigurd
en: It is a role he chose. He bent easily, and broke in half. Do not pity him.

speaker: Eivor
en: No.

speaker: Sigurd
en: For many moons, I could not sleep, always thinking of his betrayal. The horrors I wished upon him. He deserves nothing but shame now.

speaker: Eivor
en: Put it out of your mind, Sigurd. There is no need to hound the old man.

speaker: Sigurd
en: No, he must taste the same foulness that I taste. He must know what glory he missed by staying here, the lapdog of a conqueror.

speaker: Eivor
en: You want to speak with him?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yes. Face to face. I will tell him the truth.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Alrekstad. It thrives. In spite of our father, no doubt.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you sure of this?

speaker: Sigurd
en: I will say what needs to be said.

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you fear his rebuke?

speaker: Sigurd
en: O no, I crave it. It may be the old hound has lost his bark.

speaker: Eivor
en: Or it may be you will light a fire beneath him. Inspire him with tales of our glory.

speaker: Sigurd
en: If I do, I'll stoke that flame until it burns.

speaker: Sigurd
en: What was it Randvi said? Our father spends his days in the meadhall and his nights on barren planks of wood?

speaker: Eivor
en: That's right.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We'll search the meadhalls.

speaker: Eivor
en: I remember one nearby. A sad hole where men soak their unhappiness.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We should look there.

speaker: Eivor
en: We come empty-handed. Not even a gift to offer.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Rats don't appreciate gifts. They sniff and lick them, without care.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are chipper, Brother.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: That poor soaker he never leaves.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: From sunup to sundown, he just sits there, staring into his horn.

speaker: Norse Woman 1
en: Once, just once, I'd have him take a bath.

speaker: Norse Man 1
en: He was a king once, that one. You'd never know by the way he sulks.

speaker: Eivor
en: We should go. Look at him.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Father...

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: S-Sigurd...? My son... Eivor... by Odin's blessing! Come and let me look at you both!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Stop. That is far enough.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Blood of Týr, what happened there? A grievous wound you have. Are you well?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Far better than I look, I assure you.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: This... this calls for a toast! Your journey has been long and cold. A drink to warm your blood!

speaker: Sigurd
en: We are not here to drink or make merry. Only to look upon the wreckage of a once great man.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: And then what? Make new war against King Harald? Stake a claim on his crown? Is that your wish? To sow more chaos here?

speaker: Sigurd
en: You are absurd, old man. What could possibly interest me in this frozen backwater?

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Interest you? You robbed me of my wealth when you left for England. I presume you would do it again.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not my idea...

speaker: Eivor
en: You left us with nothing when you pledged for King Harald. We took only what we deserved.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I heard rumors that England was infested with kings already. I thought maybe... maybe you would return here to ...

speaker: Sigurd
en: I have cast aside all dreams of kingship, Father. A much greater end lies in wait for me.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Hmph.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I have returned for one reason only. To say goodbye. And to thank you... for your colossal failure.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Failure?

speaker: Sigurd
en: As a father, as a king, as a man. For without it, I would not have discovered my true self.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: My failure, as you call it... my oath to King Harald... was the only sensible path forward for a man in my situation.

speaker: Eivor
en: It was your right to pledge your crown to another. And I know you did what you thought best, for the safety for our clan.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: As Harald's forces advanced, I knew we did not have the strength to oppose him. We were too disorganized, too weak. With a son ever absent, always off raiding in some far-flung land, never concerned with the duties of kingship... what choice did I have but to pledge my allegiance to him? A man with ambition and an army to match it.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Absent? I only acted as the son of a king must! To earn your riches! To bring you glory! To praise your name!

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: The people of Constantinople had no use for my name, Sigurd, I needed you here!

speaker: Sigurd
en: Listen to this weeping old goat!

speaker: Eivor
en: There was nothing sensible about your betrayal. Sigurd should have been king. You robbed him of that.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Who did I betray? A son was never home? A selfish boy with no sense of leadership? An arrogant drengr!

speaker: Sigurd
en: You lie! I have led numberless men into battle! And countless ships on raids across all the known world!

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: You talk of kingship as if it were a matter of counting the notches on your axe. But to lead means so much more. I passed my crown to Harald because he was a man who understood the challenge put before him. Unlike you...

speaker: Sigurd
en: You pathetic worm...

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd! This is not why we came.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Plans change.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: As do hearts.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not this one.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: And you, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: And what you have done with yourself since? Drink heavily and weep for what might have been?

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I have... I have worked hard to broker peace across our land. To spread Harald's message of unity.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I heard you sleep beneath Harald's bed, always at his beck and call. And that he uses your gaping mouth as a chamber pot.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: You make light of my service to a great and powerful man. Is that how you treat those who serve you, Sigurd?

speaker: Sigurd
en: You pathetic worm...

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd! This is not why we came.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Plans change.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: As do hearts.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not this one.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: And you, Eivor?

speaker: Eivor
en: I wish you whatever peace you may find in this new life you have found.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I did not find it, Eivor. I chose it... the only way forward that did not lead to more violence and death and grief. Your father would have understood. He died to avoid a similar fate. To save his family, at the cost of his reputation.

speaker: Eivor
en: No. My father... he... he was...

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: He loved you. That is all.

speaker: Sigurd
en: nonsense! I've heard enough.

speaker: Eivor
en: You are a coward. And I have no room in my heart for cowards.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I find it hard to believe you have a heart at all, Eivor. Ever reckless, ever foolish, you could have been the one to guide my son to a better and wiser course. But you could hardly control yourself. Always putting your own glory above the welfare of your clan.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You're leaking piss and vinegar, old man! Can you not smell your own bitterness? Coming here was a mistake.

speaker: Eivor
en: You should have told us of your plan to bend the knee to Harald.

speaker: Sigurd
en: And spared me the shame of seeing my father debase himself like a gutted pig.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Y-you are right. I owed you the truth, and for that I am sorry. But I will not apologize for what I did.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Then I have nothing left to say to you.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Sigurd... From the day you were born, I wanted nothing more than to pass on my title, my land, my people... to you. But one year is never like another. And with the passage of time, certain truths appeared... unavoidable. Ours was the last kingdom in Norway to resist Harald's advance. To oppose him would have been our deaths.

speaker: Sigurd
en: You do not know that. We could have fought back.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: We could have, yes. And suffered countless deaths for no other reason than to protect our pride.

speaker: Sigurd
en: We will never know the truth because you were too afraid to risk it.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: Look after him, Eivor. And if you have the chance, lead him back from the edge of the abyss.

speaker: Eivor
en: He is my brother... not my dog. Be well, old man. And serve your king with honor.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: My son, please...

speaker: Eivor
en: Sigurd, wait...

speaker: Sigurd
en: I have spoken my words and he has spoken his. And from this clash came bitterness. What more need be said?

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I wish you well, Sigurd, in spite all that has happened. I hope you find what you seek. And that it brings you peace.

speaker: Sigurd
en: It will. Our destiny awaits. Do not linger long.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I know you love him, Eivor. I know you trust him. But don't follow him blindly into darkness or despair.

speaker: Eivor
en: You have spoken your words and Sigurd has heard them.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: What happened to my son? What turmoil did he see that took his arm and darkened his mood?

speaker: Eivor
en: He saw his father for what he truly was. A coward who faced his enemies with more honesty than he did his family.

speaker: Styrbjorn
en: I was a father to you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have no father.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This sad business is finished. And good riddance. And now we sail for further shores... to my true purpose. To my destiny. To the end of my road.

speaker: Eivor
en: I will follow you as far as you wish in this world, Brother. But if you mean to take us further... I may reconsider.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I do not think you will, Eivor. I think you will marvel at what I have to show you.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Mm...

speaker: Eivor
en: Still dwelling on your father?

speaker: Sigurd
en: Not at all. I was only reflecting on my visions. Wondering at them... how present they are, like memories of yesterday.

speaker: Eivor
en: Describe them for me, your visions.

speaker: Sigurd
en: My earliest was of a large door, embedded in ice, far north of Hordafylke. The Saga Stone, embedded at the top of its arch. As the visions grew stronger, the door opened, revealing many things. The life tree Yggdrasil. The golden fields of Valhalla. And the faces of our gods, all of whom called me friend, brother, warrior. I felt at home among them. Warmed by their love.

speaker: Eivor
en: You suffered so much pain at the hands of Fulke. It may be your visions are only dreams or... hallucinations.

speaker: Sigurd
en: No, no. My visions began long before Fulke. Before England even. And it was Basim who told me to heed them. They are real, Eivor. And this is no mere foxhunt. Where I take you now, few men have ever seen.

speaker: Eivor
en: We have come a long, long way in search of a hazy vision. Sigurd. Be careful.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Good, Eivor... I would not lead you blindly into the unknown. Have faith that what I know is true, and where we go is real.

speaker: Eivor
en: You should know... you are not alone in this. I too have had visions.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Have you? And what did they foretell?

speaker: Eivor
en: It is hard to say. I've seen Odin leading me into shadows. I've seen spinners weaving wild destinies from pools of blood. I saw the great beast Fenrir, the branches of the world tree, and a man with...

speaker: Sigurd
en: Go on...

speaker: Eivor
en: Valka warned me of a great betrayal. But what form it takes, I cannot say.

speaker: Sigurd
en: I see...

speaker: Eivor
en: I hold to my oaths, Sigurd, you know that. Betrayal is not in my nature.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Of course not. You are as stalwart as a pillar of stone.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Come now. My destiny awaits.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The of Ægir bless our passage.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes. I feel a great calm as we cross these waves.

speaker: Sigurd
en: This ordeal with the Elf King, Aelfred. How far have you pushed him? Does he bend? Will he break?

speaker: Eivor
en: Guthrum's army will be chasing him across Wessex now. With luck, he'll push Aelfred into the sea.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Strange how these earthly concerns seem so distant to me.

speaker: Eivor
en: But we've gained so much in England. And we stand to win even more.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The Christians are hardy foes. They see one man above who holds the axe. One man higher than us all. That is a powerful fuel.

speaker: Eivor
en: We hold our own axe. We swing it where we may.

speaker: Sigurd
en: The woman, Fulke... in my time with her, as painful as it was... she showed me things. Things so strange and wonderful, I am almost grateful for her treachery.

speaker: Eivor
en: What she did to you was cruel beyond measure.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Yet, with every snap of the flail, with every scar, with the loss of my arm... my visions grew stronger.

speaker: Eivor
en: If you can find the good in that, fine. But she was as mad as the ocean is wide.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Even the mad ones can offer wisdom. Their Jesus was an odd fellow. Now half the known world loves him. And no one believed us when we were young and we chiseled our plans under table in meadhalls. Not even my father.

speaker: Eivor
en: There is the Sigurd I know well. Can we not return to England and finish together what we began?

speaker: Sigurd
en: No. Forget all that. The future is forward. A great wealth awaits us.

speaker: Eivor
en: I am with you, Brother. Until the end.

speaker: Eivor
en: A white rage stands in our way.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Keep moving forward!

speaker: Eivor
en: Do you know the way?

speaker: Sigurd
en: As I know my own mind! We will cut through this winter sheet like swords through straw, do not worry.

speaker: Eivor
en: To perish on a lonely fjord, we'd be the shame of our clan.

speaker: Sigurd
en: Ha! That we would.

speaker: Eivor
en: The shiremoot will start soon. I should return to Lincoln to see that it goes well.

speaker: Eivor
en: Acha. Is everything ready?

speaker: Acha
en: The shiremoot will soon begin. Will you join us, Eivor? We'd be comforted by your presence.

speaker: Eivor
en: Yes, I'm curious to see this shiremoot for myself. I will follow.

speaker: Eivor
en: I have other things to attend to.

speaker: Eivor
en: When will the vote begin, abbess?

speaker: Acha
en: Twelve able lords of Lincolnshire have already cast their stones. But they have reached a tie. Four votes for each man. It not falls to you to break this impasse.

speaker: Eivor
en: Me? By whose order?

speaker: Acha
en: You have earned the trust of our three candidates, it seems. Even our bishop has found a certain fondness for your hardy spirit.

speaker: Eivor
en: It's an important vote for your people. How would you counsel my vote?

speaker: Acha
en: I value competent and righteous leadership. Not foolish friends in high seats.

speaker: Eivor
en: Anyone but Hunwald, you mean?

speaker: Acha
en: I love Hunwald as I love my own kin. But I would not put a stone in his care without fearing of the safety of both.

speaker: Eivor
en: Aelfgar and Hunwald were attacked recently. And your bishop remains fearful. It's clear someone wants this stopped.

speaker: Acha
en: They tried, yes. But they did not succeed, praise be to God.

speaker: Eivor
en: I kept them safe. Not your God.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is not an easy choice to make. But I will choose with care, I promise.

speaker: Acha
en: I pray that God guides your vote today... and not the Devil, as I fear.

speaker: Eivor
en: How are you, lord?

speaker: Earconbert
en: Have I heard aright? That you have come to break us from our deadlock?

speaker: Eivor
en: I have, lord. Have you any advice before I vote?

speaker: Earconbert
en: Lord Hundbeorht was a bold and honest man, if somewhat reckless. I see the same qualities in his son. Therefore, Hunwald is my man.

speaker: Eivor
en: King Ceolwulf's attendant, aren't you?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Aye, the king sends his love and support. Whatever happens here today shall have his full blessing.

speaker: Eivor
en: He's learning fast. Good man.

speaker: Eivor
en: Grim. Good to see you again.

speaker: Grim
en: A hearty hello, drengr (courageous warrior). Seems Britain is getting quite used to the idea of Danes stalking her shores.

speaker: Eivor
en: Where do you fall in this contest, Grim? Aelfgar is a friend of yours, is he not?

speaker: Grim
en: He is, and a good man as well. But I cast my stone for the bishop.

speaker: Eivor
en: The bishop? That's an odd strategy.

speaker: Grim
en: These Christians are easy to nudge about. So desperate they are to avoid a good fight, they'll agree to most anything a Dane says.

speaker: Eivor
en: Good evening, Aelfgar.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Eivor, I hope it's not untoward of me to solicit your support. But I do need it. The vote is closer than a cat's whisker.

speaker: Eivor
en: It is a difficult choice, Aelfgar. Know that I won't make it lightly.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Good, good. But let me say unreservedly that I am the man who will lead Lincolnscire into progress and victory.

speaker: Eivor
en: I do not doubt your convictions, lord.

speaker: Hunwald
en: A vote for Hunwald will return the house of the ferocious swan to its former glory.

speaker: Eivor
en: How fare you, lord?

speaker: Hunwald
en: My prayers are fervent and my will is strong, Eivor. If I am ealdorman, I will bring joy to this shire!

speaker: Eivor
en: There's more to good leadership than merrymaking. You must be strong and stern, and willing to take risks.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Of course, of course! Strength and wisdom and fortitude and all that. I shall rise about the peat moss of mediocrity! Have no fear!

speaker: Eivor
en: That's good to hear.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bishop.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Eivor. I must thank you for your fearless participation in our moot.

speaker: Eivor
en: I'm surprised to hear you vouched for me, bishop.

speaker: Herefrith
en: I surprised myself, to be honest. But I felt it would be a good test of God's faith in my judgment. Under my guidance, this shire is crawling back from a decade of lawlessness. God knows the love that lives in my heart for the people of Lincolnscire. I pray now that he guides your hand accordingly.

speaker: Eivor
en: Quite a gambit, bishop. Mad enough to work, it may be.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Well then, I thank you, for what it's worth. God go with you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Three men, three possible futures.

speaker: Odin
en: Which of these sad puppets will dance best when you call upon them?

speaker: Eivor
en: It's not for myself I must cast this stone, but for my clan. Who will serve us best in a time of true need?

speaker: Odin
en: You can never be certain where you stand in another's heart. Choose only for yourself.

speaker: Eivor
en: All three have strengths and weaknesses.

speaker: Eivor
en: Though tinged with arrogance, Aelfgar is competent and wealthy. He'd be a good ealdorman ... but a faithful ally?

speaker: Eivor
en: I choose Aelfgar. He's sturdy and competent, and his wealth will be a boon.

speaker: Eivor
en: Hunwald is not the most cunning or clever, but he has heart and spirit. Both go a long way in times of need.

speaker: Eivor
en: Lead your shire with pride, ferocious swan.

speaker: Eivor
en: The bishop can be stuffy, and wallows in Christian piety. But he is the wisest of the three and has already proven himself.

speaker: Eivor
en: Herefrith it will be. He knows what it means to lead. And he'll carry on with no trouble.

speaker: Acha
en: It is decided. By the grace of God, the new ealdorman is Lord Aelfgar of Lincoln.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: God has spoken, and his voice is a clarion call. As your ealdorman, I will work to better this shire, to foster peace between its people, and to serve our king. I bless you all.

speaker: Acha
en: Let us all raise our cups. A toast to our new ealdorman.

speaker: Acha
en: It is decreed by this lawful shiremoot that the Ealdorman of Lincolnscire shall be... Son of our dear and departed Lord Hundbeorht... Lord Hunwald of Lincolnscire.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I... I don't know what to say. I thank you, deeply, madly, humbly. What more can I say... I... I don't know... I miss my father. I'd sooner see him standing here, than... well, I will do my best. For each and every one of you!

speaker: Acha
en: Let us all raise our cups. A toast to our new ealdorman.

speaker: Acha
en: Our Lord God, through his infinite grace and mystery, has spoken... And he has spoken with a ringing voice! The Bishop Herefrith shall be Lincolnscire's ealdorman.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Thank you, one and all. God's blessing go with you.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Psalm seventy eight, seventy two. "David shepherded his flock by the integrity of his heart, and guided them by the skill of his hands." So I shall lead, with heart and hand as one. God bless you all.

speaker: Acha
en: As all well know, this shiremoot's decision is not final, but advisory. It now falls to newly anointed king, Ceolwulf, to ratify our choice. To this end, we need not worry. Ceolwulf is a friend to Saxon and Dane alike, and he is sure to approve the results. Our good and noble friend, Aethelswith

speaker: Herefrith
en: A septic rot has overtaken this shire! A sickness for which there is only one cure!

speaker: Acha
en: Your Grace, what is this?

speaker: Eivor
en: Nobles of Lincolnscire, stand fast!

speaker: Herefrith
en: For the glory of the ancients! Leave none alive!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Herefrith, you rat!

speaker: Eivor
en: Steel yourself, Hunwald!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Mother of God! Another battle!

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Hold steady, ealdorman. Grab any arm you can!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Ah! God deliver us from this evil!

speaker: Hunwald
en: Men of Lincolnscire, stand firm! Defend your ealdorman! Kill these traitors!

speaker: Eivor
en: Is this how their god welcomes a new ealdorman?

speaker: Eivor
en: Bastard bishop. What's his endgame?

speaker: Eivor
en: Your troubles begin early, Aelfgar.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: We'll find and kill that man.

speaker: Hunwald
en: To think such carnage could happen in Lincoln.

speaker: Eivor
en: The grief-tosser can't have gone far. Raise a ' (peasant army) and march against what men he has left.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Agreed.

speaker: Aelfgar
en: Hunwald, will you fight with me?

speaker: Eivor
en: I will. For the sake of Lincolnscire, I bloody will.

speaker: Eivor
en: This one's gone. Find those who still draw breath.

speaker: Eivor
en: Polish your arse, Hunwald. The ealdorman's seat is yours. As your war counsel, I suggest you waste no time in catching this grief-tosser. He won't be far.

speaker: Hunwald
en: We should first bury our dead... no?

speaker: Eivor
en: That choice is yours to make, ealdorman.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes... yes of course. We'll bury our dead, then raise a fyrd (peasant army).

speaker: Acha
en: I'm at a loss for words. A trusted man of the cloth. I will pray for these martyrs and tend to the remaining wounded until the last man walks free.

speaker: Eivor
en: Be well, Acha.

speaker: Acha
en: And you, Eivor. May God or... or the gods... protect you.

speaker: Eivor
en: The Valkyries have little to choose from. So many innocents cut down.

speaker: Earconbert
en: Herefrith, the bog rat, the shit-eater! The Devil has him, that's plain to see.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Bloody murderer. Our shire... what remains... my heaven awaits.

speaker: Eivor
en: Go easy on the mead, lord. It's a long ride to Grimsby.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I'm only sniffing it. I seem to have lost my thirst.

speaker: Eivor
en: Herefrith was the right man for the seat, Hunwald. He has influence and respect. Something you have yet to earn.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I know. I've always known. I think I wanted this only as a means to remember my father.

speaker: Eivor
en: There are better ways to honor his memory. Like a drink and a song.

speaker: Eivor
en: I couldn't back your claim to your father's seat, Hunwald. You're a deep-feeling man, but this work is beyond your skill.

speaker: Hunwald
en: I know. I've always known. I think I wanted this only as a means to remember my father.

speaker: Eivor
en: There are better ways to honor his memory. Like a drink and a song.

speaker: Eivor
en: This city, with these people... it's not where you belong, Hunwald. You're a Dane at heart. Go to Swanburrow and live well.

speaker: Hunwald
en: Yes... that's true. Thank you, Eivor.

speaker: Eivor
en: We'll speak again soon. I have an alliance to secure.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Eivor... you have gifted me a great honor, one I hope I can repay.

speaker: Eivor
en: One you must repay, as our tradition demands.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Name your need.

speaker: Eivor
en: I want your holy word that Lincolnscire will be a friend to the Raven Clan, through the thickest and darkest of troubles.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Yes, of course. Have no doubt. We are friends, you and I, from this moment forward. Only call and I shall come.

speaker: Eivor
en: Thank you, bishop. Take care of your sheep.

speaker: Eivor
en: And shear that one from time to time. For his own good.

speaker: Eivor
en: Abbess.

speaker: Acha
en: I applaud your judgement, and thank the Lord he saw fit to clear the clouds of doubt from your mind.

speaker: Eivor
en: You could just give me the credit for how I cast my vote. I did not see your god pick up a voting stone.

speaker: Acha
en: But he has not cured you of your heathenism, I see. These things are sent to try us, I suppose.

speaker: Eivor
en: Bishop and ealdorman. Those are two high titles for one man to hold, Herefrith.

speaker: Herefrith
en: Rest assured, I carry both with ease. The Lord saw fit to grant me the strength and clarity I need to rule this shire. You turned out to be an excellent tool of the Lord's will. You don't understand what an honor that is, but perhaps in time you will.

speaker: Mysterious Voice 1
en: Traveler! You have strayed onto cursed ground. Your life is in peril.

speaker: Eivor
en: Who's there?

speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
en: We are the wisps of the swamp. Leave all you have as tribute, or you will never see the sun again!

speaker: Eivor
en: Spirits? We will see about that.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Give up your treasures and we will release you from the fog!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Not that way! Go back or be lost forever!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: They've found us, lads. No sudden moves, all right?

speaker: Eivor
en: Here are the mysterious wisps. So you and your fellows like to scare travelers into giving up their valuables?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: That's right! We're peaceful like that. Wouldn't hurt a fly, me!

speaker: Eivor
en: You tried to rob me!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: A sorry necessity. We three were left homeless after your country folk, er, burned our village to ashes. Now we do what we must to keep body and soul together. Here, you figured out our trick. Can you help us?

speaker: Eivor
en: Help you?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Just a few pointers! How can we improve? Be more effective ghosts, so to speak?

speaker: Eivor
en: I'll make you into real ghosts, you thieving scum!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: We'll see about that! Hoof it, lads!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Don't chase me! Alden's got the most silver!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Edgar, you craven coward!

speaker: Eivor
en: Why don't you hang up some bone dolls from the branches? A man would be scared witless coming upon that in the fog.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: That's a fine idea! We'll do it! Here, you deserve a few coins for your help, at least. Thanks, traveler!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: So, who knows how to make a bone doll?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: Can't we use twigs or something? Bones make my skin crawl.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: That's the idea, idiot.

speaker: Eivor
en: Your petty schemes do not interest me. Be thankful I leave you with your lives.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: O, we most certainly are that. The Three Wisps salute you, and bid you safe journey from our swamp.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 1
en: I miss the days of selling whelks down by the shore. The smell of the sea. Not like this rancid old swamp.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 3
en: Chin up, Edgar! You're a wisp now! The ghost with the most! Flaunt the haunt!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Man 2
en: Are you ever unhappy, Alden?

speaker: Diary of Winchell the Robeless
en: By the holiest of virtues, please Lord, give me the strength to forgive my foes, for I struggle to do so. Many moons ago, I told them that You O Highest Above would never judge one of Your creatures unfit. I told the many nobles of Grantebridgescire: Tryeth the airs of Him with no skin-blockers! All of our lives were not meant to be abdicated by the walls to our bodies. Henceforth we have all been nude, yet these crows go home clothed, perform Witans and moots clothed. Aelfred must disrobe even, he joined us once when he was ploughing his servant. I pray forgiveness and guidance. God Is Great.

speaker: Decree against Winchell
en: By decree of the many nobles of Grantebridgescire, and the hundred and the witenagemot, the Various Thegns of this, Boudicca's Pond. We no longer allow the presence of the usurper and criminal Winchell the Ursurper. He is forbidden from speaking or holding court in our waters for the nude and privately so. He should be removed by force from his rock. A nuisance to us all. Signed, The Merry Nobles of Grantebridgescire

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Please, don't sting me. Because you will die and I will cry. Ow! Ah! Ah... Get away! Don't come near! O! Surely you can spare a little honey? No need to get so maddened.

speaker: Eivor
en: If the bees bother you, boy, maybe do not stand so close to their hive?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: But I need honey! Just a little. It's for my friend. It's all she likes to eat.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
