en: My friend loves honey. She has a very sweet tooth. She's so gentle and kind, but if she doesn't get her honey I don't know what will happen. I only want to scrobble a little. They have plenty to share. I've tried poking it with a stick, but it riots them up something chronic.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: You got the honey? O, thank you! That looks delicious! Leave it on that rock and she'll be right along.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: The rock is just over there by the tree. Hurry before she comes.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Come sit and wait with me. She'll be here soon.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Winifred looked after me ever since Mother and Father died. She's my best friend. The other children tease me. Sometimes they throw stones to shoo me away and call me the grubby watcher in the woods. Winifred saved my life, I was curled up on the grass praying that God would take me too. And she scared the wolves away!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: There you are, Winifred! I got you honey!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Winifred, my bestest of bears! Any day spent with you is my favorite day. So, today is my new favorite day. This kind stranger got you some honey. What do we say? Thank you? All that honey must have given you quite a thirst.

speaker: Eivor
en: Are you really all right out here on your own, little one?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Silly! I'm not alone, with the very best of bears by my side. Goodbye, and thank you! Come on, Winifred. Shall we walk to the lake? Maybe we can splash in the reeds?

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Here you all are! All my friends together! Isn't everything just perfect?

speaker: Eivor
en: A strange fellowship. But then, friendship can often be found in unexpected places.

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: Please don't hurt my friend! They're all I have!

speaker: Anglo-Saxon Child
en: No! You killed my friend!

speaker: Havi
en: How are you and these folk getting on, lady?

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive
en: Better now that I see there is an Æsir among us. You'll free us from the clutches of that red witch, won't you?

speaker: Havi
en: Who do you mean?

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive
en: Eysa. Daughter of Surtr. She has taken our people. Please, All-Father. You must help us. Enlist all of Asgard if need be. Please.

speaker: Havi
en: What else can you tell me about this Eysa?

speaker: Dwarven Fugitive
en: Only that so long as she is out there, we will remain down here. Help us. Speak to Brammer. If he is still able to string a sentence together. That drunkard.

speaker: Brammer
en: Who will join us in merriment? Come. Come, all! Where is my drink?

speaker: Lom
en: Which one?

speaker: Brammer
en: Ah! Ha! Right...

speaker: Lom
en: This eve I will pour my favorite drink. It is called "a lot."

speaker: Brammer
en: Easy, Lom!

speaker: Lom
en: What? I am not as think as you drunk I am.

speaker: Havi
en: If there's anything to learn from these dwarves, it will take great patience on my part.

speaker: Brammer
en: Look around. There's got to be a tankard we can tongue a few drops out of.

speaker: Havi
en: Don't let me interrupt you.

speaker: Brammer
en: Lom... am I pissed or does the All-Father stand before me?

speaker: Lom
en: Er... both?

speaker: Brammer
en: This... this is good! The Wise One will surely help solve our problem.

speaker: Havi
en: Let us help one another. What exactly is the source of your grief here?

speaker: Brammer
en: Rhymes! Rhythm! O, we could use your poet's heart.

speaker: Havi
en: My what?

speaker: Brammer
en: Your words. Your gusto! We, the greatest of the Sons of Ivaldi, are in need of a fitting end to the song of... well, our end!

speaker: Havi
en: I am here to understand how you might help me strike back at Surtr.

speaker: Brammer
en: Strike back? Nonsense. Besides, it is not only he we must contend with, but his kin. His daughter, Eysa, stirs above, snatches up our people, works them to death.

speaker: Lom
en: An unwinnable war. All that's left to do is eat, drink, shag, and seal our legacies.

speaker: Brammer
en: Exactly! But, as is clear as day, we have drunk ourselves to Hel and no rhyme sticks the way it should. So! It must be you who completes the song of our saga. Mine and Lom's.

speaker: Havi
en: I will hammer the end of your with the strength of Mjölnir.

speaker: Brammer
en: Yes! What spirit!

speaker: Havi
en: That is not why I've come.

speaker: Brammer
en: Of course it is. Fate has brought you here.

speaker: Havi
en: My poetry on your saga? Are you certain?

speaker: Brammer
en: Why else would you be here?

speaker: Lom
en: We are to be remembered and revered by all.

speaker: Brammer
en: Yes! With Havi among us, we must adjust the final verse. Listen closely...

speaker: Brammer
en: To the depths of Svartalfheim, great Havi came, met with dwarves he knew not by name.

speaker: Havi
en: In search of warriors without remiss, instead found cowards who reek of piss.

speaker: Havi
en: Led by their wallowing, their pitiful groans, I could see they had peckers but found no stones.

speaker: Havi
en: A tall tale they asked to spin in their favor, a sad little saga whose truth is much graver.

speaker: Brammer
en: Er, not quite what I was thinking. Let's try

speaker: Havi
en: You call yourselves the Sons of Ivaldi. Why? To shit on his name?

speaker: Lom
en: Brammer, I don't think he means to lend his words to our song.

speaker: Brammer
en: Go away, Lom!

speaker: Brammer
en: Your words carve a deep wound. But they are true enough. Each day we see our numbers dwindle. Friends go out and do not return. The choice to forget is... alluring.

speaker: Havi
en: Surtr has stolen my son, and I do not have the luxury of forgetting. You said Surtr has a daughter?

speaker: Brammer
en: Yes. Clever. Cunning. Commands an elite swathe of warriors. She oversees Surtr's operations here.

speaker: Havi
en: Where may I find her?

speaker: Brammer
en: There is a smeltery up the road. The dwarves there may know.

speaker: Havi
en: I'll go there, see what your people know. With luck, I can trap Eysa, trade her life for my son's. Thank you, Brammer. Now tend to your people as a true Son of Ivaldi should. They need you.

speaker: Brammer
en: I will.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Eivor! I have just the thing for you.

speaker: Eivor
en: Sunniva. Norvid told me you had set something up. A fighting competition?

speaker: Sunniva
en: The greatest fighting competition this land has ever seen.

speaker: Eivor
en: Any rules?

speaker: Sunniva
en: Yes! The rules are simple. Fight, drink, fight! And remember, Eivor, the more participants, the bigger the pot. If you ever any willing fighters, bring them to join in! Now! Are you ready to begin, my powerful friend?

speaker: Eivor
en: You know I'm ready.

speaker: Sunniva
en: Just like in Norway! A knock-down Yule brawl!

speaker: Sunniva
en: Let us celebrate ... with fists!

speaker: Sunniva
en: Bring the kids! The fight is about to begin! A battle to rock Asgard itself! Who here wants to see blood sport? Two Norsemen enter, only one leaves! 'It's not midwinter without a good fight! It's a Yuletide brawl!

speaker: Sunniva
en: She bested every fighter in the ring and drank enough to kill a mid-sized ox. Eivor! Champion of the Yule Brawl!

speaker: Sunniva
en: Well fought, Eivor. Let us do this again next year.

speaker: Eivor
en: Norvid, the settlement looks quite ... festive.

speaker: Norvid
en: The Yule celebration is here! It's midwinter, Eivor. Time to drink, fight, and compete in hopes of a bounteous harvest. Jólnir, the Yule god, smiles on us. The days will soon grow longer, my friend. It's all a glorious rebirth about to begin.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you did all this?

speaker: Norvid
en: Not exactly. On a scouting mission, Sunniva and I met a group of uh ... we call them "revelers". They did most of the work. Sunniva's manning the fist-fight tournament. All in good fun! Meanwhile, I have opened my own shop. Rather than silver, we use what I call Yule Tokens. I made them myself.

speaker: Eivor
en: They certainly look ... homemade!

speaker: Norvid
en: Thank you, yes! Now! Before we begin our celebrations, we need to get the brewery and the cattle farm ready for the Yule Feast.

speaker: Eivor
en: And you'd like me to do that, I suppose.

speaker: Norvid
en: I would! And since I'm so fond of you, have some Yule Tokens! I expect to see you at the celebrations later!
